_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: I liked Momodora: Moonlit Farewell and I believe I mostly got my money's worth.I use the following approach for rating (1-5) for each category and in general:1.	Badly done / Don't bother2.	It's functional but barely / Only if you like the genre or the gameplay3.	Average but it works / It's enjoyable but has issues4.	well done / You will probably like it5.	Perfectly done / Buy it even if you don't like the genreAtmosphere:Compared to the previous game, this feels different, brighter and not souls-like. Yes, it is still dark fantasy (impending extinction event), but it manages to avoid the typical tropes of every cookie cutter dark fantasy souls-like game I’ve been seeing for quite a while now.Having said that, I did find the environments and the enemies a bit mismatched. You tend to be mostly underground and many of the enemies didn’t really feel they belong there. Regardless, it’s quite well done and I give it an extra point for avoiding the aforementioned tropes. 4/5Story:I found the story straightforward but rather generic. There are barely any cryptic pieces which you have to put together and then read a blog to understand what happened (which is a plus in my book), but on the other hand, it boils down to “something happened, go investigate” and then “you are the only one who can save us!”. It's serviceable and I don’t really need more than that. 3/5Graphics:There is a significant upgrade on the graphics compared to the last game and it stands out as one of the better art in metroidvania games. It’s not the best out there, but the developers put a lot of effort and it shows.However, I found that the effects of your attacks can become greatly overbearing and many times you lack the clarity as to what is happening, not being sure if you took damage, dodged successfully or where the enemy projectiles are. It is so prevalent, that I must take a point off. 4/5Sound:Unlike with graphics, I barely paid any attention to the music which severely failed to capture my interest. At some points (mostly during boss battles or ambushes) it turns into the “epic with lots of piano” kind that in my opinion plagues many Japanese games. It tries to be epic but it becomes comedic with how trite it is. I can’t convey enough how much I dislike this kind of music in games!Sound effects are also nothing to wite home about, they are serviceable and lo-fi (which is intended obviously) but they are no more than that. 2/5Gameplay, general:You move slowly (more on that later). You also have a stamina meter. It’s horrible and I don’t think I’ve liked it in any game that I have palyed. You need stamina to be able to run and dodge but it manages to make traversal a bit tiresome. Your character’s health is a bit of hit and miss, in that you may end up with 1500 HP at some point (starting at 200 or so), but some enemy attacks can easily take half of that away. Damage given/taken and HP tend to go along with the progression, making it essential that you go for the secrets that grant you health, damage & stamina upgrades. If you don’t, the game becomes way too difficult.You can equip sigils, that grant you some passive bonuses (e.g. increased damage) as well as companions that apparently offer you some perks, such as intermittent healing or extra attacks on enemies. I found the effect of the sigils relatively subtle (with some exceptions on the latter half of the game) and the companions… well, they are there, but they don’t really make an impact.I found the boss fights to be relatively easy, but that’s because ranged attacks tend to be better than melee ones. Weirdly, the difficulty of bosses is not linear, with the last few ones being way easier than I’d have expected, but that’s definitely partly an effect of some of the equipped sigils. However, your stamina and slow-moving speed make the boss fights a bit more tedious (rather than difficult) than they have to be, but then again… you have a bow. It does less damage but gives you way more time to dodge and avoid taking any damage yourself.As a result, bosses are for the most part an exercise in attrition, you have to stay patient and keep attacking (in contrast to having to wait for an opening to do damage that you see in other games) and to make sure that you heal yourself every now and then.In short, stamina sucks, upgrades are necessary, optional items are nice to haves and bosses are manageable. 3/5Gameplay, exploration:There is a bit of backtracking needed to get to most of the secrets though many of them will be found during your standard exploration. Backtracking is needed because for some of them you need the abilities you unlock later. That’s standard fare, sure, however the map layouts tend to be very mazey and this makes it a bit tiresome, but not really a pain.You generally have a good idea of where to go next, although at a couple of points I was lost. Keep an eye out for the map and any room openings to unexplored areas! In general, I liked the exploration, but it felt slightly less enjoyable compared to Kingdom Shell’s (which I reference because that’s the game I played right before this one), ignoring that game’s tendency to make you feel lost most of the time. 4/5Gameplay, platforming:Coming from Kingdom Shell, I was shocked as to how slowly you move. Your character seems to carry a lot of weight and the stamina meter does NOT help matters. However, the platforming feels quite solid, especially when you get some movement upgrades, allowing you get to manoeuvre pretty effectively. 4/5Closing comments & overall:4 out of 5. The game is definitely an improvement over the last one and I managed to finish it in under 9 hours, secret-hunting included. I detest the stamina and movement speed, but you get used to those quickly. Boss fights tend to overstay their welcome a bit, but the game mostly avoid souls-like tropes which is a plus. The price could be a couple of bucks lower, but that’s no biggie.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: A tight metroidvania action-platformer. Mildly challenging, cute cast and what I found to be a compelling story that manages to stand on its own without having to play Momodora 1-3, and even without "Reverie Under the Moonlight". Short but sweet, fun soundtrack, beautiful art/sprites and tight controls.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic game and that's my review! Momodora is the latest, and maybe last game in the Momodora series. From its humble origins as a weird Cave Story clone, it's gradually evolved and become more and more polished. It shows that you don't necessarily need gimmicks for good game, just to do it well. Moonlit Farewell is a mostly linear action platformer, with some mild metrodvania aspects, but while you do have an open map, you are mostly gently steered towards where you need to go. There was a brief period towards the middle when the open map worked against it for me and I got a bit lost, but careful examination of the game eventually showed me where to go. The default difficulty is not too hard for a clumsy gamer like me, but does require some attention. There are not what I call puzzles as such, but some jumping challenges occasionally. The game is about 10 hours long but you may take longer if you are hunting down all the last items or play the post-game challenge modes, or replay at higher difficulties. For presentation, the game is pixel-art style and it is beautiful. There are lots of lovely details in the maps and also in the animation. Game speed is medium to slower side and I found the movement to be precise. The beautiful music compliments the story and action segments. No surprises, no single thing that you may call 'exceptional', but as an entire package it is sublime.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Goodbye MomodoraThis game reminded me of Ender Lilies even though it has almost nothing in common. It was nice, tight, and a good 10 hours of metroidvania fun. Cute anime girls, cool bosses, dreamy music; I adored a lot of things about this game. The Sigils could have been space out better because I was doing alright throughout most of the game. Late game I got 3 sigils back to back and became an unstoppable monster, kinda flattened the endgame. Bombservice ended Momodora well and I will follow them to their next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game.  But 108% in about 7 hours is kind of meh, IMO.  I've never played any other Momodora games so I'm not sure if they are all short games.   I liked the story a lot. The movement was a little slow for my likeing, and the abilities were your typical Metroidvania style.   The cards/sigils were a good addition.  My least favorite part, except from the length, was the map.  For the most port the map shows you all the rooms with "secrets" or items.  There was very little back tracking and when you need to, you know exactly where to go, so not much exploration or trying to figure anything out.I would recommend playing if you have a little bit of time. Also I wish the difficulty was a lot higher. most bosses are very easy to read and can easily be one shot.Really like the music, and background graphics, but character development could be improved. 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: A nice send-off to the Momodora series. Beautiful sprite work and very engaging combat and movement. Decent story, though not as compelling or interesting as Momodora. My only real complaint is that the game felt rather easy. I died all of twice and went a long stretch not feeling challenged. Some of the sigils break the game a bit, so if you're looking for a challenge, feel free to ignore them.If you enjoyed the other games, or are in the mood for a really solid action platformer, give this one a go. You'll have a good time for 10 hours or so.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, short and fun. In terms of exploration, there's not a ton in the way of metroidvania backtracking; most collectibles can be easily acquired the first time you see them, with only a handful gated behind movement abilities. All collectibles are also marked on the map, so a 100% guide is totally unnecessary.In terms of difficulty, even on normal (the hardest option available in a new game) it's not particularly challenging, either in combat or platforming. It should be fairly accessible for any platformer fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Thoughts after spending 10h in the game:- Is the game feels good after RUTM?: NO- Is the game worth playing by itself?: YES- Is the game has well-designed characters with its own stories and let player dive into the interesting world?: YES- Is the game fight system well-balanced?: 50/50 (mobs are perma-stunned if you were able to get close to them, most bosses are SUPER-EASY to fight and EASY-RUSHING, some locations and mobs make it difficult to see thats happens on the screen, most of SIGILS will not be used at least once ())- Is the game satisfy my with its visuals?: 50/50- Is the game satisfy my with its music?: more NOT than YES (I am super fan of some themes in RUTM and think its kinda step back in Moonlit Farewell. .)- Is the game offers challenging gameplay?: NO (just artificially created)- Is the game offers some unique mechanics or some innovative ideas?: NO- Do I recommed the game afterall?: 50/50 () - this game for Momodora fans and for metroidvania-fans who looking for a game to play. If you are a newbee in metroidvania-games I recommend you to start with another title.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: The supposed finale to the Momodora Series is here and it's just about everything I expected it to be: A 10-ish hour Metroidvania with great art direction, and decently polished combat and traversal. If you're familiar with BombService's previous titles like Momodora Reverie Under the Moonlight (RUtM), or Minoria, then you'll feel right at home here. While the story is not the most granular in terms of depth, it has enough beats and moments that ground you as a character into the world and motivate you as a player to continue exploring the world. It references events in previous tiles in the Momodora Series and ties it all together to a resolution. That being said, it does try to adjust the story so that anyone who jumps in to the series with this one won't feel lost... To varying degrees of success. You won't feel lost, but you definitely feel like there is more that went on before you start the game that you missed. Little has changed for combat, with the bespoke bow, leaf, making a return as your main tools. But beyond losing the charge up for the bow in Reverie Under the Moonlight, the general kit has remained intact. Healing is now based on an MP Gage that resets at save points. Most "power-ups" take the form of sigils that you find as you progress through the world. Each sigil takes up a slot in your inventory and modifies how a specific part of your toolkit interacts with the world. As mentioned before, combat is rather similar when compared to Reverie under the Moonlight. I'm not sure if it's just me, but boss battles also feel a little more straighforward than I remember from previous titles. But that is just my observation. No good or bad connotation to it. Take that with a grain of salt, as you'll have to make your own assessment, should you pick this up yourself.Lastly, This is a Momodora game. The play time is not egregiously long, and the barrier of entry is rather low when compared to other metroidvanias. I'd say that is a good thing, because nothing really overstays its welcome. That being said, I always feel like I want more from them.Ultimately, I recommend this game. If you're a Metroidvania fan, this is for you. If you want to dip your toes into Metroidvanias, this is also for you (heck, even RUtM too!). If you're a Momodora fan, this is definitely for you (but I am sad that this will likely be the last). Cheers BombService. Looking forward to whatever you guys make in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: If you know what you're here for, youll enjoy it, so i enjoyed it. If not, pretty standard metroid vania with decent aesthetic, though not too much innovation. love some of the basic quality of life stuff that the series has improved on, but its hard to recommend this to people familiar with the genre. Good for newcomers, pretty forgiving
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: I played Momodora: Reverie Under the Moonlight, and expected this game to be the same but with different enemies. THAT is NOT the case. This game gives the player more movement upgrades that are fun to explore with and dodge enemies. There is also a new "magic system" with sigils one can equip to get different abilities instead of equipping certain items like the past games. Although the combat system seems easier, with constantly stunning enemies, I still find this game very fun. I did find the bosses pretty easier to beat than in Reverie as well. The music and the pixel art is as gorgeous as ever! (PLUS you can pet the many cats in Koho). I highly recommend this game and will be playing it many times, like I have Reverie.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played and liked Reverie, this is an easy recommend because the gameplay is largely similar.If for some reason this is your first Momodora, it's a by the books metroidvania. Gameplay is tight and responsive, relatively light on backtracking and you get new abilities at a fairly modest rate. Most bosses are pretty good, although you can certainly outscale the difficulty of the game if you get all the upgrades.Art is good, Soundtrack's not memorable, but it was inoffensive. A solid game overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me curious enough to go back to play all the other previous games, and what a journey that was! I would recommend any fan of this game to try out the others, though Moonlit Farewell is certainly the most polished game in the series.Besides the incredible environments, hard-hitting OST, and fine-tuned gameplay, this game is easy to get lost in. You can explore to find all the collectibles, battle the bosses under a time trial after beating the game, and replay the game in new modes. It was a wonderful experience that I will come back to whenever I want to lose myself to the game's serene atmosphere. Whatever direction the series is planning to go, I honestly hope it keeps up this level of quality, if not better!If I have any complaints, it would probably how absurdly abusable the late game combat can get with the right combination of sigils. From having a setup for endless chance-on-hit extra attacks that block everything on the screen, to having an extending healing and invincibility whenever you use your bell, it really changes the meta of the game. I kinda prefer how the game was more about carefully dodging and countering attacks. I actually lost my first Hardcore run after walking off the stage during the final boss, because I couldn't see where I was during a combo! Anyway, this game is a grand celebration to the Momodora series and how far it has come since being a game inspired off of classic Nintendo games and Cave Story. I certainly enjoyed it, and come back whenever I need to feel nostalgic again.*Alrighty, with the latest major content update, I got more than I bargaineded for with the new boss :'D
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: As a Momodora fan I had high expectations from this game as the last installments were awe-inspiring, and I was not disillusioned. It has epic music, beautiful sceneries, and awesome characters.Unlike many metroidvanias that sin of allowing the best upgrades just to be used in a battle or two, this game features an , which adds more fun and entertainment. To be honest, I was a bit disappointed in the fact that I would not get cool secret items upon beating a boss without taking damage as in RutM; however, on another note, the new sigil system indeed allowed me to play "in my way" and I ended up loving this system as much as RutM items. It is somehow inevitable to compare this game with RutM, since RutM was simply a masterpiece; nevertheless, this game has features of its own that are as good as the ones present in previous games. Supporting the Developers statement: this game indeed can be well enjoyed without having played the previous games; however, it is great to meet again characters from previous entries, so it is a win-win for both previous Momodora fans and new players.I really hope this is not the last entry for the Momodora series and I am looking forward to play future installments for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: I spent several days after this game came out binge playing every other Momodora game, starting with RutM, then Momo1-3 to come play this game. The flow of story and characters, seeing names of NPCs that I had interacted with in previous games, places I had gone, and events in the aftermath of prior games I was greatly satisfied at the end. While maybe one of the easier final bosses of the series, I still felt accomplished at the end and thoroughly enjoyed the entire experience even reaching 111%. Whether you're coming from RutM or you've followed the series through, I honestly think you'll love this game. Hell, even if this is your first Momodora game it's a fantastically made Metroidvania. I look forward to seeing where the series goes from here, if we continue following Momo or if we start to see the evolution of other characters and their journeys in this world.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell the developer is getting way more refined, this game has everything I wanted more out of Reverie. It is definitely a much more polished game, awesome to play-through.However I felt there was something missing in this game from Reverie. There's cooler enemies, cooler zones, cooler abilities/upgrades, but something isn't there. Maybe environment? The more-eviler zones were great, I loved the fairy castle, but all the other zones weren't as striking. Reverie had this unsettling feeling everywhere in a different way each zone.I really wish they would get more open areas instead of just hallways, there was some sections in the forest like this but they were still too small.If you haven't played this series, honestly recommend starting with the previous title Momodora: Reverie Under the Moonlight FIRST and this second. I really enjoyed this game and I'm glad I followed its development. Though as always I wished it was a little longer.Back to shilling this series til the next game!
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: I remember Reverie a little more fondly than this one. I can't tell if it was actually better or just nostalgia. This game is still good, but I wish there was a little more optional content other than the optional content which exists post credits. The fact all the secrets spare few are visible on the map removes a lot of the mystique of exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: I've never been much into metroidvanias, I didn't care for any of the metroid games I've tried such as metroid dread but i played both of the momodoras on steam and I enjoy this game.  The vibes are good, no idea whats going on in the story so far and I don't know that that's the strong suit of this game but the core gameplay combat and movement feel great.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: I cautiously suggest this game if it looks good to you but know that this game is EASY!!! A harder difficulty should be included and I would imagine most people would prefer playing on that setting. Why is it so easy LOL? Such a good game otherwise. And no I'm not a tryhard sweaty player and I'm not even that good at games.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly as far as metroidvanias go, you won't find anything crazy here. I enjoyed my time while playing this, it was short and sweet and I had fun. I felt like normal had a good balance of difficulty and if someone new to the genre were to ask for a recommendation, I'd probably let them know about this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: The Negative thing first:I really didn't like the combat, your normal attacks move your character forward, sometimes into the hitbox of other enemies or off cliffs. You can't dodge roll mid-air which would be really helpful against certain enemy types and their placement. Traps still damage you when you dodge roll trough.BIG COMPLAINT: After you clear a room and move back in, the enemies instantaneously respawn, which is really unrewarding, so moving past them and not to fight them does the same thing (except you won't earn money from them, but you can get enough money from fishing anyways so you don't have to bother with that).The enemies should only respawn when you hit a bell, bells are the checkpoints. (for example, like in dark souls)I played on normal difficulty and the best combat strategy was to just face tank enemies and heal afterwards (after i reached mid game and had enough upgrades). It was not challenging, but that’s not a point I want to complain about because I didn't look for a hard game, but the combat movement didn't feel good (as i described in my first point).Also the Companion System is kind of useless, I only used the Exploration Companions for more passive income.The positive things:Map is very nice, it marks every area where you still have something left to explore, that's really nice for completionists.Graphics are awesome and very lovely; background music is great to listen to.Story is nothing exceptional, it’s a bit to melodramatic with the over-the-top shaking text bubbles, I would only use such things when you REALLY want to make a point, but not in every other conversation.FazitI play a lot of Metroidvania so I am always a bit harsh. The first 3 hours where frustrating to deal with because of the combat, which nearly made me quit, but when you have enough upgrades, it became more of a button mashing game (there are two types of game a like, permanently really challenging, or braindead games where you feel like a God and nothing can stop you). This was for sure number 2 after a certain point.I took me about 7:10 to finish the game to 109% (I don’t want to bother myself with the last few collectables I am missing because I can’t find the map parts I missed). I read all texts and talked to nearly every npc.For 12 € the game was Okay, I hope they improve the combat (smoothen it) if they ever plan to make another part of the series. I will not actively look forward to it, but if steam ever happens to recommend me the next part of this game series, I will buy and play it.Thumbs up from me because the game was made with a lot of love!
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: This one is an odd case as it is by no means a bad game. I do feel like its a little underwhelming compared to their previous entry Reverie Under the Moonlight as far as gameplay. Bosses felt very easy, exploration felt kinda linear in comparison, was a little disappointed to not see active abilities return, magic felt like the only purpose it had was healing, and I wasn't a huge fan of the new stamina system. All that aside, the art is amazing, the game feels great, the story is cute. I would still recommend this game overall, but I just think it doesn't bring a whole lot new and takes away things I liked in the previous entry.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Obviously at the time of this review I have only played a short time, but as a returning fan of the series I want to share my initial thoughts.Firstly, I love RUtM, the last Momodora game released in the series. It's not a big game, but the controls are crisp and responsive, the boss fights are short and sweet and the visuals are fantastic for a pixel game.Moonlit farewell has added some new systems and some nice sharp new visuals, but I fear some things have sadly been lost from the last game. The controls no longer feel sharp and responsive, the lack of hit stun on your attacks strips away the satisfaction of a fight and you are no longer rewarded with amazing signature items for clearing a boss hitless, a trope that I had come to love from RUtM and Minoria.All this to say, I appreciate what Bombservice are going for with this new game, but I fear so far it falls short of RUtM as some of the charm and snappy combat has been lost in the sauce.I'm leaving it with a positive review regardless because of course I haven't played this title enough to leave a final opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, short but fairly tight experience. I would say that on the challenge side, this game is not particularly challenging on a first playthrough and it is fairly short but I consider those both good things as there is an arrange/hard mode playthrough available after game completion (I haven't done these). Overall though, great spritework, music and tight controls. A fun initial playthrough. On the negative side, I would wish for some more variance/ ambiguity in the level design. It was fairly linear/straightforward and easy to collect all the various powerups for hp/mp/stamina.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: A great follow-up to Momodora: RutM that aspired to be twice as ambitious in it's art and animation. This is a gorgeous game. You're also in for a straightforward, inoffensive metroidvania with a cool videogamey story. I only beat the game on its normal difficulty, but unsurprisingly there are additional difficulties to play through if you're in the mood to revisit the game or to just jump right back in. That means you could get a solid 10+ hours of the game and there are some decent challenges in store in the post-game and alternative difficulties!
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most well rounded Metroidvanias out there. There isn't a single dull moment. The combat as good the movement feels great and progression is super smooth. It never truly blows the mind with any one thing in particular but that's hardly a complaint when it gets everything across the board so consistent. It's wicked pretty the soundtrack is great there's no reason to not get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: If you crave some good platforming and metroidvania action, you can't skip Momodora: Moonlit Farewell. Despite it apparently being the last game in the series, I think it is a great entry point for newcomers and a beautiful love letter to the fans.With Moonlit Farewell you can expect: beautiful pixel art with fluid animations, excellent combat, some nice platforming, tons of collectibles and thick anime girls. The music complements the atmosphere perfectly, transitioning seamlessly between dynamic, somber, oppressive, and moody tones as needed, enriching the overall gaming experience.Since Hollow Knight, other metroidvanias have adapted their versions of charm system, and this game is no exception. Here we have cards called Sigils that allow players to tailor the difficulty and play style to their liking, adding a layer of customization to the adventure. Some have little to no use, others can provide some essential boons, that directly tie to this game's difficulty. I played on normal, and it was quite challenging at first because you don't have many options to heal, and even regular enemies can kill you very quickly. However, mid-to-lategame, you can find Sigil combinations so overpowered, that I basically facetanked many bosses, without even bothering to dodge.Clocking in at 8 to 10 hours for a completionist run, Moonlit Farewell offers a well-paced adventure. While the post-game content includes a boss rush and another difficulty mode, a couple more areas would have been a welcome addition.In summary, Momodora: Moonlit Farewell delivers a simple, elegant, and polished metroidvania adventure.Recommended9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: A really great Metroidvania all around. play well, sounds well, have fun designs, no bloat at all, enough fun option to play with, well geared difficulty, it's the full package. A very easy reccomandation for anyone that remotely like metroidvania. And be sure to check the rest of the momodora serie while at it, all the games of the serie are worth the play!
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: This is a top-tier Metroidvania. It's short, sweet, doesn't withhold the fun traversal from you for overlong and has some of the least limitations on it's movement mechanics I've seen. This, simply put, makes traversal a joy instead of a chore. Regain your double jump after you bounce off a wall? Genius. The soundtrack has some real gems, there are some fun postgame things to do and a neat bonus mode after you beat the game (and a masochistic one which deletes your save file when you die, great for some I'm sure!)I wouldn't classify this as a hard game but it does have some challenging bits for sure. The power fantasy from a few of the late game combinations is ecstasy. If you like Metroidvania's, you owe it to yourself to play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: GAH DAMN! Not only does this game look amazing but it plays just as good. This is my 1st Momodora game and I'm glad this ones a banger. I enjoyed the succinct and playful world. Some metroidvanias have way to many rooms with not enought enemies to face or secrets to find. Every unlockable and secret I found was extremely useful. I found a combination of perks that promoted and supported my playstyle. You won't go wrong picking up this gem, especially if you loved metroidvanias with gorgeous pixel art.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible sequel to one of my favourite games of all time.What this game nails is atmosphere. The beautiful pixel art, the area and character design, the lighting effects and the wonderful soundtrack all combine to an experience I was very happy to be lost in. And I mean that somewhat literally, as this is a metroidvania. If you love exploring then I highly recommend this game.And if a funny anecdote is what'll pique your interest: This game made me respond to a boss' second phase with "finally, gender equality."
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: a bit different from momodora 4 but not for worse. in terms of exploration i might put it a bit higher, the map is easier to navigate and there's a bit more distinct variety in areas, as well as a full arrange mode to spice up a second playthrough if you want more. takes some notes from minoria but notably only on the things that worked or had potential to work, which does lead to its overall feel being very different from momodora 4, notably just in the fact that on a basic level it's not as brutal as that one could be, more of the challenge is set aside for self-enforced challenge runs. but being more forgiving and accessible as a stylish action game can have its own appeal so it's hard to call that a negative, and the tools to make it harder for yourself if you want are handed over pretty early. on the whole, it's the most polished game in the series. i had a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell’s Gameplay is Goat’d. The pixel art and music are Goat’d. The story? Functional… and that’s Goat’d. Even if you think it’s too easy you can play it again on Arranged and Hardcore difficulty. Not only am I recommending Momodora: Moonlit Farewell, but the series as a whole. Play them, NOW!Honestly the only thing I wanted was to be able to play Isadora too.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell is a great send-up to the Momodora games that came before it, building off of previous installment's worldbuilding and characters. It also maintains the visually striking pixel art style of Reverie Under The Moonlight.However, I felt the combat was poorly balanced (too easy on Normal, far too punishing on Hardcore). There was a notable lack of interconnectivity between zones in the game - a problem I had with the previous installment in the series as well.Moonlit Farewell was enjoyable enough and its Arrange mode has some real promise for anyone interested in a second playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: an excellent sendoff for the momodora series. it's just a bunch of great metroidvanias. RutM and this one are definitely the best of the five but they are all worth playing. very stylish and impressive pixel art, fun gameplay and legitimately interesting stories across the board. you can feel the various games that helped inspire the series all over the place, and it just seems like a great amalgamation. anyone who likes the genre should absolutely play this.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game. before playing this game, i played one of the previous games (reverie under the moonlight) and ive got to say this game is a massive jump in quality and lore. the pixel art was amazing followed by the Visual effects, it really made everything feels so lively and punchy, there were points were there was a lot of clutter causing a silly death but it ended up being funny so i don't mind. the music and sound effects were quite good as well, having some really nice music to accompany the exploration and i never got sick of any of the tracks. the lore was actually surprisingly good with only a couple of exposition dumps which were at least complimented with cutscences, and for any die hard fans there are log entrys you can read. now some things i didn't enjoy, the boss ai is quite bland as they dont actually react to what you do they just follow a loop of the same attacks which makes them quite easy once you get there pattern down, the game has not much in the way of build variety i found one build that i liked and never changed it after that which isnt the worst but i would have liked to have seen a bit more. and as of writing this i have 110% completed my save file with only a few things to clear up but traversing about the map to gather collectables with a lacking fast travel is quite annoying. overall a really great game with a cheap price tag for the quality.and if any of the devs are reading this please please please add an extras, with concept art and behind the scences stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: I have not played any of the previous games in the series and found it to be a pretty good metroidvania. While playing mostly feels familiar it is still a good execution of the genre. Combat feels good, bosses are for the most part enjoyable (if a bit easy), good selection of abilities and sigils (this games version of charms from Hollow Knight), platforming is not a big focus but what there is is solid. I would say it is a pretty good introduction to the genre, overall easier (and shorter) than many other games in the genre and also has an easy mode, but those looking for a challenge might be disappointed (There is harder versions of the bosses that can be fought at the end of the game but I have not done that yet). The map has a question mark wherever there is a collectible (with a few exceptions) making it fairly to get almost everything. Good pixel art and animations, and the story and characters are decent. Overall a solid metroidvania for those new to the genre and those looking for a short and (mostly) relaxing experience.Also works well on steam deck
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this title. It is a successor to Reverie und the Moonlight, which I also enjoyed. It follows the same game design approach with outstanding pixel art, good combat with great gameplay variety, a world that can be thoroughly explored without taking up too much real world time, and bosses that are more fun and interesting than hard and grindy.  I felt the companion system was underdeveloped and the sigil system was really nice. Although the later sigil combinations can completely break an already easygoing game. Overall it's a charming pixel art gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Another installment of Momodora series. and another great game.While not the longest, you can really feel the heart and effort the team put into the game, with little to no major bugs and quick patches fixing existing ones. Beautiful character graphics, backgrounds and animations all work really well on building the atmosphere together with great soundtracks you can hear as you explore the enviroment in the vicinity of Koho village and in the palace high above, as you uncover the mystery behind ringing of the bell.Graphically an upgrade to previous installments, with only somewhat funky thing being character's spring animation (she swings her arms way too much) and double/wall jump (being just a 360 degree spin of character graphic). Apart from that everything is beautiful.Audio is on really respectable level, both the background music, as the sounds of characters, hits and attack indicators.The story is rather easy to follow and is not extremely complicated, but I think for Momodora it's a good thing. It wants to tell you a tale that you can be engaged in, myself I was really dragged into it, and was really thrilled and excited about what would happen next. Since the story is rather eqsy to follow you don't really need to wonder where you should go next, as it's both in dialogues and hints on the map rather clearly stated where you should no. With that said the game really rewards you for exploring since the very beginning, as it also shows rooms, where there is an item to collect, be it a stat up, a collectible fairy or a sigil.Speaking of sigils, they are modifications to your character and you can equip up to 5 of them by the end of the game. There is quite a bit of them, some help you explore more smoothly, some are defence or offence focused, but pretty much all of them have some use, depending on what your needs or your playstyle are.While the enemy variety is not the biggest, and some enemies are just copies of enemies from previous games, they usually pose a threat adequate to your progress when you meet them first.For the last thing: special enemies, the so-called bosses. While there is quite a handful of them, almost none of them feel pointless or are boring to fight. There is maybe like 2 bad bosses in here, and final boss is not one of them, which is really great compared to previous installment. The final boss in this game is really engaging and while not the hardest of them all, he can pose quite a threat. Overall with the ending, I think he makes a satisfying finale for the game.tl:dr Game good, graphics pretty, audio good, bosses fun, a little bit short. 8/10 from me, definitely worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely gorgeous game. Art, animation, and music are all beautiful. Good difficulty if you aren't used to its type of combat. If you are experienced it can be a bit easy, but first time through it feels awesome getting new abilities and blasting everything away. There is a variant mode available after beating the game once that I haven't tried, and plenty of ways to challenge yourself if you're looking for more replayability, but the main game coming in at around 10 hours is well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell lived up to my expectations. I played one of its prequels a number of years back and was impressed that this one took me about twice as long to complete! So that was a nice surprise. Overall I like the way this game treats its combat system with the sigils you can swap out and try combinations. It can be tough but like most metroidvanias you can overcome adversity by learning how to dodge attacks and playing conservatively. I may even come back and try out the bonus mode which seems to be a sort of Second Quest.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: momo is so precious i cried. reverie under the moonlight was one of my all time favourite games, and now this joins it up there with the greats. the new sigil system allowed me for so many options in how i played towards the end i was constantly swapping to try out new things. spritework is as fantastic as ever, while i still think momodora 4 is the better for a quick sit-down-and-play, this game is much better to really soak in and appreciate with all the different upgrades and progressions you can make in it.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Finished in Normal mode, and played Momodora 4: RutM before this.Story is alright, nothing wrong with it, though unlike previous games this only has 1 ending which is a shame. They do provide you with lore for Momodora 1-4 in the form of Notes, but for what the game is trying to achieve in scope, the story is good.One of the aspects I was looking forward to for this game, blew me away with how good some of the Boss music and BGM can be (especially the final boss, that piano and drum slaps)Animations and sprite work is a great, very similar to RutM. I'd say if there are sequels to come this pixel art style is probably what I'm looking forVery fluid, it takes some getting used to but once you get the first two movement abilities it gets much better. Animation lock does take out a bit of the score but otherwise if you know the limitations of your control over Momo this feels nice to play.Perfect dodging feels nice to perform, though there are times I abused the invincibility frames it gives to wham on the boss. Sigils are nice too, they give a small push to how you want to play. Overall, good. 8-9 hours depending on how quick you go through and if you decide to complete achievements, which is lower than I expected. Endgame stuff does bump it up an hour or two. At least it wraps up quickly and doesn't drag on. Some parts of the overworld (looking at you, Meikan Village) can feel BS at times, but it's mostly fair game. Most of the bosses can be beaten in 1-3 tries, but they're not the most difficult compared to RutM.Momodora Moonlit Farewell is a great game to spend a week on. If you're looking for the difficulty RutM brings you might want to save that expectation for Nightmare mode at the end, or wait for a Nightmare mode if the dev plans to bring that sometime in the future. Would recommend buying it when on sale (10% or more), but buying as-is is totally fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it - just like the rest of the series.Good fun all the way through - the graphics are nice, exploration feels rewarding, the bosses are intimidating, and new stuff is unlocked at a fairly fast pace, so the game never gets boring.If I have any complaints, it's maybe that the Aegis Sigil is overpowered, and means I could tank all bosses after getting it, and didn't really have to dodge attacks any more. Game just got a bit easy at that point, but it's not a big deal. Meanwhile many sigils just seemed inferior to others and never got any use from me. So the whole character customization part of the game felt a little bit imbalanced to me.Another minor thing I would have liked to see is character portraits during conversations - like in Cave Story etc. The characters are cute and it would have been neat to see them express a bit more emotion.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Hey, Rdein. Know that I'm proud to be following this series since Momodora 3. It's very dear to me and this game specifically helped me through some rough times. I was really excited for this game and it ended the series on a high note while also being a love letter to the franchise. I know how some negative feedback can affect you, and how game development is exausting, so If you keep developing games or not it's up to you. But in case you want to stop know that you went out with a bang, this game is incredible. Everyone at Bombservice did amazing. This is indeed the best farewell it could've been.PS: You probably won't remember but a few years back I asked you on Twitter if Momodora 3's trailer theme (aka Momodora 1's Stage 8 theme) had a extended version, and unfortunately there wasn't. So imagine the biggest smile on my face once I heard it in the game at -that- moment.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: I played Momodora: Reverie under the Moonlight back in the day, and I never thought a short but sweet metroidvania could have been made better than that.Momodora: Moonlit Farewell proved me wrong. It ticks all the right boxes for me, striking a perfect balance of challenge and fun without overstaying its welcome and a story full of lovely characters; all with a gorgeous presentation both in its pixel art and soundtrack. It's a game made with love and a perfect end for this lovely franchise.Plus when you pet the cats they stretch their body in order to meet your hand. If that doesn't make it a 10/10 game I don't know what will.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting characters and beautiful pixel art, a bit lacking in terms of difficulty tho IMO. It felt like I kinda breezed through the game on normal learning very little about timing on boss moves kinda just dodge rolling through everything with my noncommittal attacksFinding all the collectibles would also be more rewarding without the question marks or the map, but I could totally have played with those off so that's on me
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: It's good, and it's an all around improvement over the previous game I played in this series. Less of the things I found annoying in the prior game are in this, so I loved it. Tighter controls and gameplay too. It's a metroidvania, with some soulslike dodging, although without the minmaxing and builds to deal with. Overall, the game is good in that regard, simple and sweet. As a matter of fact, simple and sweet is probably the best way to describe the game, as any other company would have crammed it to the brim with things until it was overcomplicated and not fun. It's fun exactly because it is simple and sweet.Story? It's nothing great or grand. It's just some teenage girls on an adventure to stop bad guys, with many of the bad guys being ladies who you will smack with a giant magic leaf until they die. Is it a game about cute girls doing cute things? Kinda, but it's an actual action adventure game. Smut? No. Sure, tons of hot monster girl enemies to smack with a magic leaf, but it isn't a Rule 34 game, and good on the devs for not pushing that. Sure, you smack a giant snake lady with giant snake lady boobs to save some adorable little fairies, only to see the big booby mega fairy that is their queen, but honestly it there is no sexual posturing, nor fetish pandering. It's never as strong as the content in Dark Souls 1, and also with far less fidelity, so it's not bad. It's not even a PG-13 experience, although it dips near close at times. Honestly, it's actually less lewd than Shantae, because Momodora doesn't have a belly dance.However, it's something like a 90% a female character cast. If something has a discernible gender, chances are that it's female, although there are a couple bosses that are definitely male. Yeah, much like the previously mentioned Shantae games, which is also a metroidvania platformer, so I guess the comparisons are many between them.I guess I also answered about graphics in the last paragraph, but if you want an example, just look at the Steam page. It's exactly as shown. I like the general style.Oh, and you can headpat the cats in town and there is an achievement for it. This made me very happy.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell isnt a revolutionary metroidvaniaBut it's gorgeous, with an amazing OST, and incredibly tight gameplay and design that makes it well worth playing for anyone who is even a slight fan of the genre.The game doesn't overstay its welcome like a lot of metroidvanias do, beating it at a brisk 8 hours is perfect for me, but I could see that being a turn off for some people.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It's ok, nothing amazing or great but overall ok. Decent metroidvania with decent combat, ok world, and alright story, if a bit short, but the price matches that. A few bugs/issues, but first week of launch, hopefully they'll have it all tightened up soon.Long form:Ok, I'll say that I LOVED Momodora: Reverie Under the Moonlight, it was short, but good. The atmosphere, the feeling of the world, the story progressing and the setting were all... good. Nice, interesting, had a good feel, the world was varied, enemies interesting, some great boss battles. Overall it had a very nice experience. And they nailed the combat down to the point you can (and I did) beat it on a no hit run. I came here after playing that one, and hoping for more of the same, or even perhaps better... Unfortunately it just isn't, at least for me.First of all, the world and art. The art is... ok, the world is... ok. It looks alright, but it doesn't hit me... or feel amazing or really interesting or like there's some great story or parts for me to just focus on and look at here. The world itself is... mostly just Forrest, repetitive forest with generic tiles you explore through, with no real rhyme or reason as to why the terrain would be shaped like this, or where you're going or what you're doing. The enviornment simply doesn't, in 90% of the game, tell a story or feel important. So it feels a bit hollow, the part I personally don't love random forrest levels, or sea shell filled levels didn't help. RUtM did a nice little forrest intro level. Short, sweet, didn't outstay itself for the story/feel it could offer. Here. it's just so much forrest, without major points of interest or stuff there to see. So the world feels mostly dull, final areas town was ok, but still felt like the enviornment, enemies, etc... weren't telling a story as you explored, just all preset to taken over town and once you saw the start that was more or less all there was to see through the rest. So ya, the art is ok. But didn't have anything that really left an impresion. Same on the characters or bosses. The arts ok.. but the design or styles or actions of most... don't really feel unique or cool or interesting enough to leave great impressions that stick with me after the fights. Push for more over the top horror things, more extreme beasts... or more sexy snake ladies or demons, take whatever style/idea you have, and push it and give it character so it leaves a solid impresion as a unique character from this game, and not just a generic snake lady, demon, monster, etc... So again, ok art on the technical side, but overall feel of the games art and world was lacking, especially compared to the last one IMO. It's just, ok.Story. Well, it's pretty simple and straightforward. The problem is again the world and environment and enemy design itself all doesn't really feel like it contributes and helps tell the story, so it feels like set dressing, rather than a world to seep into and get engage by. And that means a simple story comes off as... just simple. So it's ok, but again no real strong impression by the time I'm done. Though a few question still the game doesn't answer about why a few key things happened, or were the way they were.Combat. Probably the best part of the game, but still not quite up to Momodor: RUtM imo. For the most part it's pretty good and tight, though there do seem to be some input/queuing bugs that happens sometimes when inputting more rapidly. Most notable one that's happened many times (especially on the final boss) is the one where you tab dodge, and then push stick the other way, and tap dodge again... but you keep rolling/dodging in the first direction. In this case that's off the edge of the arena to your death. Fun, restart a 3 phase boss fight because of an input issue. When redoing on nightmare for the boss rush, this killed me four out of seven times. Just got in the habit of not dodging on those and playing it more slow, not quite how the buss rush rates you since it wants speed. So, some issues, mostly stand out on that fight with the ledges you fall of and instantly die at, but most of the game it felt mostly ok, or on the tougher fights I was more rapidly inputting stuff at, at least less sever when an issue happened. Games out first week now, so hopefully this won't last long. Now, the more important part I feel is... enemies, enviornmental traps/factors, and player unlocks. Many enemies are ok, but others are... designed in some ways or placed in ways that just aren't... fair, or fun in all cases if you want to no hit run. Wouldn't recommend that for this game with how it's set up. But oh well, most won't care about that as long as they can power/heel through those encounters and generally you can just fine. The biggest issue I had was player side of combat was less... interesting, engaging, complex... compared to the previous game I've praised so much. That one had more interesting core combat, moves, and items. Here, you're basic combat moves are all pretty simple an straightforward, and then you just get some card/sigils or something, that do passive effects. And while they are useful and sometimes powerful, they don't really change combat and how it feels or add to the complexity or type sof actions the player can take. So overall it felt again more simple compared to the previous RUtM experience. Not bad, still overall good and decent, but not quite great and as engaging as before.So in summary, still an ok to decent little metroidvania. But it won't be sticking around in my memory as a standout quite like Momodora: Reverie Under the Moonlight did, on basicly any account. Only thing it's got going for it is that's it's probably longer, but when it feels a bit more padded out with bleh terrain tiles or stuff to achieve that bigger world and longer play time, I'm not really feeling it. The other one was super short, but because it rewarded multiple playthroughs and challenging yourself, I didn't feel it was a negative there. So ya, ok, but not something to jump at if you came here hoping for more of the last one. It's got a very different atmosphere, feel, and somewhat different combat style.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Really well made as always, and way better.I think "as always" is enough to say. So precious.If you are not played the series and dither over to buy, I recommend to play RUtM first. 5 USD is almost free.* Controls : Like RUtM, well fitted for level design. one of the best controls as 2D platformer, in my memory* Difficulty : Fair difficulty even in hardest one.* Graphics : No need to say. Well animated, adorable and cool, but dogs not included.* World & Lore : Most detailed in the series (at 2024)
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful pixel art animation, smooth gameplay nice music. Metroidvania elements and exploration are solid as well.The game is on the shorter side though, less than 10 hours. Additionally the bosses are wayyy easier than they have any business being. (coming from a normal mode playthrough)Having played Reverie Under the Moonlight I love the see the dev teams progress in smoothing out their gameplay and finding an incredible art style.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: I've only finished the normal difficulty first playthrough at this point. Pretty great! The sigil system gives you a reasonable amount of wiggle room to customize your build. Movement feels good without making you overpowered. Map is decently large. Without being too daunting, so once you've cleared an area of required objectives, cleaning up any remaining collectibles is pretty breezy. There are no longer bonuses for defeating bosses without taking damage, but given the larger number of bosses, and the few sigil builds that necessarily require taking damage (and how few players probably engaged with boss drops in previous games), it's an understandable removal.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Momodora have always been a great franchise that I love, from years ago when my PC could only run small games to this day with the last game of the franchise, it always have been fun and warm my days and this game is part of thatHad lot of fun exploring every nook and cranny of the map, meeting with characters that I love and having epic battleIf you like Metroidvania or played Reverie Under the Moonlight I highly recommand playing Moonlit Farewell
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, and I recommend it to... well almost everyone but especially fans of metroidvania.The second to second gameplay is fine tuned, it's reactive and dynamic, with clear tells of the enemies attacks. It's well balanced, not too easy, but also not overwhelmingly difficult.As for the exploration, it's also very good. The movement abilities are used well with the environment, and the map is just the right size, not too big so it's manageable to backtrack and explore, and not too small so it doesn't feel restrictive. Add to that pretty art and good music, and it's a very good time for 10 hours of playtime or so.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: The final entry in the Momodora series and honestly this is the best game of them all. Momo and Dora return from Momodora 3 for one new adventure together, an important relic has been stolen and thus the demons are returning wrecking havoc on the world and thus is up to Momo to find out what happened and saving the land. The first thing you notice about the game is how it looks, it's absolutely fantastic, every zone in this game is just stunning and the pixel art is incredibly expressive, accompany all this with the usual masterful soundtrack and you are already in for a great experience. Not only the world is more vibrant than before but there are a lot more of people to talk to, sidequests secrets to explore and the notes section also shine light on the timeline of events of the entire series and it felt rewarding for me after playing through the entire series. The credits sequence with the screenshots and updated sprites for all the main characters of every game was also incredibly charming and cute and gave everything a great sense of finality. The improvements are not only in the presentation the game takes everything Momodora Reverie Under the Moonlight did and just upgrades everything. The movement is better giving us a run button and a wall jump making exploration fun as hell, the pacing of the fights also got faster your attacks have more combo potential your dodge roll is also quicker and snappier. It still feels deliberate in the movement and as usual the bosses will deal a LOT of damage to you if you're not careful but this frantic rhythm gives us some of the best battles in the series. I don't know if we are ever getting a new Momodora game in the future, everything in this game makes it feel like this is the definitive end, but honestly this is probably the highest note the series ever reached so I can't think of a better way to go out. Check these games out all 5 of them, you won't regret it
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Momodora Reverie under the Moonlight is the reason i grew to even like Metroidvanias as genre, and now, Moonlit farewell is a reminder as to why i love them. The game is in general just a fun and cosy time from start to finish. It's visually gorgeous and the music sounds stellar, in addition to improved combat and world traversal compared to the Rutm, Also i would probably spend an ungodly amount of time fishing if there was a DLC of sorts to flesh that part out more, just saying.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Bit safer and more streamlined than the last game but it was absolutely worth the wait. The sigil system is really fun, the boss fights are cool, the level design is great albeit linear (dont think there was a single room i hated), and its short enough to have great replay value while not feeling like a waste of time.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Not all the way through, but this is a masterpiece of a game. It has emulated within me the same sense of wonder, mystery, and expanse that Hollow Knight managed to without being at all derivative. Not to mention the sheer beauty of its artwork and landscapes. Expertly crafted. Truly a work of art, I am only hoping this game is longer than I expect it to be so I can enjoy the discovery of the world for as long as possible. Best game in the series by far, a true privilege to see this developer blossom from Momodora 1 to this absolute masterpiece. Godspeed.Edit: Just finished the game. Excellent. My only complaint would be: seeking out all of the secrets makes the second half of the game very easy. I found myself easily tanking/outhealing even the final boss, but I was very thorough to complete each area I was in as much as possible before moving forward, even backtracking to complete some areas before I believe the game expected me to (you unlock fast-travel pretty late, probably when they expected you to return.) The secrets are all quite easy to find, all marked with a ? on the map. There is a hardcore mode, but I worry this won't really fix the problem, just punish you for carelessness. If you want a difficult challenge, I recommend maybe skipping some upgrades. Otherwise, despite the lack of late game challenge, the world was just so enthralling and beautiful I found myself not even caring. Then again, I haven't done the final challenge just yet. Perhaps this is where a fully upgrades save file will be truly challenged. In summation: A beautiful experience highly worth your money, but may not be as difficult as you are expecting, especially coming from the last entry in the series. Then again, you can always place constraints on yourself. Thank you RDEIN!
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. This was a great followup to MoMo reverie. idk if I was garbage on reverie or this game was shorter. but I had alot of fun.thoughts. I dont like searching through maps for things I have NO CLUE where they are. There needs to be a marker feature.so i can mark places ive been and so I can make places I wanna go back to.I cheesed a few bosses. the big bee was very easy to cheese.I dont like being surprised by some of the bosses with moves that kill me or put me very close to dying. and then having to play on my back foot.hurtboxes for bad guys way better in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this game a few minutes ago. I have played the other Momodora games in the past and was excited to play through this one.I had a lot of fun and the music is amazing the listen to, including the final boss fight. The controls worked fine with me and I didn't have any slowdown or glitches that others have reported.If you are fan of Metroidvania. you should pick up and play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: I have been impatiently waiting on this game to drop and I have not been disappointed one bit!  The music, art style and game play all feel really good.  The story is simple and has a few twists I didn't see coming and I really enjoyed it.  Overall, I have to say that I've had an absolute blast playing the game and look forward to hitting 100% achievement progress!
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Highly polished controls, great pixel art, and a cute aesthetic. The difficulty selection is granular, considers things other than just health (such as tighter required timing) and presents a tough but fair challenge, borrowing some ideas from Soulslike games.This whole series exudes the charm and quality of its creator's tireless effort. I can't recommend it enough.You can also pet kitties. 11/10
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: While a good game, this Momodora doesn't live up to just how good Reverie Under the Moonlight (RUtM) was after the final quality of life patch.  This one's still good, and worth a play, but just doesn't have the same combination of everything working together almost perfectly.Moonlit Farewell is a good bit larger and longer, and also a good bit more linear than RUtM.  I really liked how you could go 4 different ways in RUtM after reaching Karst city, and do most of the major tasks in any order.  Routing mattered as you needed to balance what upgrades, active, and passive items you'd need to progress.  Moonlit Farewell only has a small non-linear segment, while everything else guides you along a certain path.  You can take detours to get sigils and collectibles, but nowhere near the extent of the how wonderful RUtM's progression felt.  The large number of collectibles, and the large number of mostly minor sigils also makes it feel a bit too large compared to previous titles.Movement skills include a double jump, a dash (but no air dash), a wall jump, and the roll you start with.  Later on there's an upgraded temporary jump and attack powerup.  While it's a bit more than the movement in RUtM, the movement skills are spread out a bit further apart.  Movement in general feels a bit slower in general, plus the dash consumes stamina.  This makes movement and the world feel a bit slower and larger to get from one place to another.Artwork and music look and sound great, though some bosses get very busy with effects.  There is an option to help reduce that which I appreciate.  You can also disable screenshake, which I also greatly appreciate.  That said, a lot of areas are dark, and contrast can sometimes make things difficult to see.  Close to half the game is very dark with a small aura of light around you.  Difficulty isn't too bad, a few bosses I had to do a few tries to get their patterns down.  Most aren't super reaction-focused, which I'm also glad about because of my age and slow reaction times.  Unlike RUtM, there are no bonus rewards from no-hitting a boss, just an achievement for your first no-hit.  This does mean you can play more aggressively and just damage tank/heal through some encounters without worrying about losing out on a significant upgrade.Unlike RUtM (and Minoria), there are no active skills/spells.  Every sigil is a passive effect.  You start with 2 slots, and can slowly find more slots up to 5.  These come in VERY slowly.  A lot of sigils are very minor boosts or modifications to your "build", and you only have one loadout (so you can't set multiple loadouts for different purposes and easily switch between then, you have to individually disable and enable the sigils you want).Overall, I did enjoy this title but found it to be a bit of downgrade compared to RUtM.  Still worth a purchase, just after you get Reverie and play through it.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: This has been a fantastic Metroidvania so far. The mechanics feel really good, although I find the changes to the arrow mechanics to feel like a bit of a downgrade. The environments are beautiful, and the story is engaging. Will update my review upon completion.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Great little metroidvania. Cute art, fun characters, and fun upgrades. Loved the references to Reverie Under Moonlight, which is one of my favorite metroidvanias of all time. I was hoping it would delve into more of the bleak atmosphere of that game, but I can appreciate this for a more lighthearted fairy tale with occasional dark patches. Great OST, and the pixel are is absolutely incredible.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: Moonlit Farewell is more of a mixed bag than Reverie Under the Moonlight, but still well worth the purchase and worth playing. The game is quite linear. Which isn't as much to my taste, but isn't necessarily a bad thing so I don't hold it against the game.The movement without the Sprint ability feels a bit sluggish. It costing stamina that drains rapidly and refills glacially leaves traversing and especially re-traversing the world feel not so great. At least not until you find the  This is a shame because moving while sprinting actually feels fantastic, especially with the excellent animations. I can't help but feel like the stamina system should either be divorced from sprinting, or removed entirely. If you go through the game without skipping a gross amount of optional stuff, the combat is pretty much trivialized near the end of the game. It's not my preference, but it is still fun. It does feel a bit nice being so obscenely powerful and indestructible.The biggest stand out here is the artistic design. The characters and environments are all looking fantastic. Big shout-outs to the  boss. I love that one. The art and music there are excellent.-The MP system is underutilized, only being used for healing (extremely good use) and some optional sigils (imo a complete waste). -Money is next to worthless and any Sigils/Companions that give you more money are therefore worthless. -Companions as a whole are really not useful. -Death-warping back to your last bell is such a ridiculously useful time save over and over again, it should have just been something you can do at will. -Secrets you have to find, and then wait 10 minutes to actually collect... why?Ultimately the game falls short of Reverie Under the Moonlight in a lot of ways. But falling short of nigh-perfection is no shame, and this game still holds its own as a fantastic metroidvania well worth your time and money.Also, you can pet the cats. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Momodora: Moonlit Farewell

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm not the type of person who writes reviews, but as the Momodora series fascinates me in a unique way, I couldn't help but give my compliments.Momodora: RUtM is my favorite game, I used to say that the only problem was that it was too short, haha. The story, characters, gameplay, music and impeccable art are all part of this game and couldn't be better.Then Moonlit Farewell came and, surprisingly, managed to take the quality standard of its predecessor and raise it even higher. With new mechanics, new stories and the gorgeous art as always.If you like Metroidvania and a beautifully made pixel art, you must give a shot to this game.This game is truly a masterpiece and I'm proud that it has the Brazilian blood in it.P.S.
