_childDocuments_.review: *as for the time of this review, I haven't finished the game, as I am too busy with making every setup work perfectly- beautiful idea- the gardeners are adorable- will tire you if you keep practicing the same throws over and over again- you grow plants- the frog- beautiful music composition as you progress on the levels- very cozy...none I can think of that is a fault of the game.(it's mostly just me getting dizzy after playing too long *shrug* )it is a very easy to learn game, however it takes quite a bit of practice to make the gardeners act as perfectly as you think they could work.i enjoyed every single bit of the game I have played so far, I did not enjoy disconnecting my brain from my body after getting too hooked with the game x-x'I have a bunch of levels to do yet, but I have a lot of fun by perfecting every single gardener I can place!my little brother has a lot of fun with the robots and playing around!it is an absolutely adorable and cozy game, If you can play this game please do!it has also perfect regional price for my country as of the time of this review!9/10!get it if you can!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: At times it felt like the developers had invented a whole new genre & era in gaming.On paper it's just another production based game (in the vein of "SpaceChem", etc), but doing this in VR—by way of recording actions, adding them to time loops, etc—it becomes a completely unique gaming experience, and one of the best uses of Room Scale in gaming to date. (even though Room-Scale isn't strictly required).And even though the game is itself unique, it somehow makes it easy to imagine other realms of gaming coming to us in the future (as well as other non-gaming related software/tools). Great fun. Great food for thought.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful!Just enough story not to be bored but still cozy and interested.Loved the music room. Spent WAAAY to long in there playing music by myself. Love the First person automation thing. Very intuitive!Found myself trying 100 times trying to get one knife throw just perfect so i could cut down the number of robots needed. Can definetly see myself in an open ended first person automation game.The first room with the yellow pumpkin fruit was bugged (i think) for me since the hatch was already open without having to pay with fruit juice?
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very nice puzzle VR game and probably one of my favorite VR games I've ever played. All of the different properties of the fruits you use along with the different tools and skills you have to "solve" each room really create a very nice progression system. I'm pretty sure this is the first Steam game I actually got all of the achievements for, and most of those achievements come with meeting the highest throughput goal for each challenge, which involves making or harvesting the most amount of fruits per minute possible while using the least amount of clones possible. It can be really tough trying to figure out how to meet those goals sometimes, but it's always a fun sort of challenge and I can sincerely say that seeing a full assembly line of clones of you, knowing that each one of those clones represents you at a certain point in time... it's really unlike anything I've experience before in a video game. I highly recommend this game, even if you don't want to sink 18 and a half hours into it like I did. It probably only takes 8-10 hours to beat if you're playing casually, and I really do think it's worth the $25 price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it! Cute story w/ great voice acting + a unique puzzle mechanic, maybe a bit on the short sideIt's fun to see how "human" the clones feel just from the subtle movements they register from youI'd highly recommend it if you enjoy puzzles or factory/automation gamesHoping there will be a sequel some day!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: A cute game, and the core principle of the gameplay is quite entertaining. Here you have a decent story behind the decorations, narrated through dialogs, and the visuals are... as i said - cute. Vr controls are only via teleport and snap turn, which are not favorable to me if i have a choice, but i get it - it's safer for vestibular system, and implemented as a default in most vr games. As for the duration of the game - i think it's more or less of correct duration, so you dont get bored by the main gameplay and the game can end gracefully.P.S. By the way, Transpose is another title with similar mechanics, but quite different visual style, if you liked building a chain of actions with clones, you could try it as well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very high-quality VR game. Art and music are outstanding; the Clocktower feels inviting and relaxing just to be in, which lends an enjoyable atmosphere to the whole experience. Writing and pacing are tight, interactions are polished (the level selector in particular is great; it's satisfying and intuitive and all-around demonstrates a great way to do VR menuing), and puzzles are well-designed, if a bit on the easy side. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Cloning yourself into little robots to solve puzzles appears to be one of the most addictive things to do in VR! I love this game and felt compelled to support the Devs by leaving a positive review. Expect your brain cells to get stretched but not in a frustrating way, I mean, you can't get frustrated at puzzles involving fruit and robots that looks like Jonny5 from the classic 80's film, Short Circuit ! Amazing ! highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful puzzle game with a cloning mechanic that feels super intuitive to use. Music is lovely, story was touching (with some great voice acting), and a very pretty aesthetic. Making unoptimised loops with a bunch of funny interactions is a highlight for me personally, but recording the same throw across the room dozens of times to save one clone for optimisation purposes is also a treat.I was a little disappointed by the lack of environmental interaction beyond game-required objects since I find that to be a really immersive factor in VR games (can't pick up mugs, hand phases through plant leaves etc.) but that's a nitpick really.Overall, I consider this a must-have VR game. I hope they make DLC or a sequel for this. Regardless, I'm keen to play whatever else these devs put out!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun VR game that you can take at whatever pace you'd like since efficiency isn't rewarded with anything but achievements. Messing around with really efficient conveyor belts of bots is just as fun as making a super long chain of yourself passing down fruit. Each puzzle has it's own personality based on how you acted it out and it's really cool to see!Biggest issue the game has is that it's short. If you aren't going for achivements you can probably beat it in 5 hours. I got 9.5 by getting about 70% of them with me giving up because this game makes it really annoying to re-make puzzles due to how strict the timing between clones is. There's also no mass reset button that I'm aware of. The puzzle solving gimmick also never really gets expanded upon. The variety comes primarily from the puzzles themselves introducing new obstacles, but you never get anything that makes you reframe your approach to this mechanic. Which is fine if the intention is to not make it too complex. It just started to wear itself out on me while I was trying to go for the achivements.Dialogue and story is just pleasent, really. Overall chill game that I really enjoyed the gimmick of almost all the way through!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely delightful and beautiful VR puzzle game. It feel's like a beautiful combination of Opus Magnum turned physics sim mixed with a rhythm game!It tells a charming story in a beautiful world and has just the right amount of challenge! Optimization is easily the funnest challenge, but it's a comfortable 10 hours of creativity and fun. Would love to see where it goes from here!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that I was an early adopter of VR and have been largely let down by most of the experiences VR has had to offer; however, this is easily my favorite VR title of all time. It completely justifies its choice of medium, and feels wonderful to play.The Last Clockwinder is a cute puzzle/factory game that lets you record your actions and play them back on repeat, and tasks you with solving puzzles by creating clones of yourself to assist you in doing so. The difficult curve is immaculate, and, as somebody who optimized almost every single puzzle, it felt like the perfect length to me. The story is cute, doesn't in the way, and yet the entire game oozes personality in the best way possible.Only complaint that immediately comes to mind is that if you don't have a large area to move around in, some of the puzzles will be significantly more fiddly.10/10, would recommend to anyone who enjoys puzzles and has a decently large VR play space.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Such a charming VR experience. I loved every moment playing this game. The voice acting is superb and the music and sound design are incredible. Playing feels intuitive and effortless. I found myself laughing out of pure joy and excitement after setting tight sequences between the gardeners. I wish there were more content - it was all over a bit sooner than I had hoped.Play this game if you ever have the opportunity.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so fun! Automating clones of myself Kobe-ing from across the room is just so satisfying. Then on the sidelines creating cheerleader clones to keep all the Gardeners motivated! I'm not terribly far into the game but so far and the gameplay mechanics are just so much fun. The story has been pretty good so far but is secondary to the great mechanics. I don't know how the game ends but I'd love to see more content along these lines.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: extremely well made, polished, and high quality game. its the best wholesome content game in vr right now in my opinion. very challenging, and is 100% based on timing and your ability to catch, and manage people (gardeners) effectively by creating time loops. ive encountered very little bugs, the only one being when i set up a perfect loop in say, the luft apple research room, when i come back its not timed up the way it should be, the way i left it. otherwise, this game is fantastic, and although it doesnt have a very long story line if you blow through it, any achievement hunters will want to create maximum efficiency rooms, and thats where the real hours are spent.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful 4-6 hour experience in which you automate the assembly and delivery of questionable fruits. This time, however, instead of conveyor belts, you automate the process with timed clones of yourself!An excellent game that made me think, smile, and swear when I inevitably hit my wall when throwing something from one place to another. A quality VR experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's a puzzle/automation game where you record clones of yourself to grab, manipulate, and throw things to set up an assembly line.Pros:Exceptional art/environment designFun gameplay, including challenges to make high-throughput levels with a limited number of clonesEntertaining audio-log storyCons:The game is pretty short; ~3 hours minimum, ~6 to 100% itThere is no option to disable the 'black flash' when turning or moving
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful automation/puzzle game which works beautifully in VR. The physics interactions are really solid and you get a fantastic sense of achievement when you get a bunch of your little gardeners working together. The only downside is that because of the amount of reaching and throwing you end up doing, I have punched the wall more playing this than anything else! That however is very much a me problem, not a game problem! :) As of writing this I've just finished the story and I'm really looking forward to going back to work on the challenges. Beyond that the graphics are really clear and vibrant and the story and voice acting are really endearing. Overall this is one of the best VR games I've played. Easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful example of a game that needed VR to exist. Something like this just wouldn't work with a controller or keyboard. It is not perfect, it has quirks, but the core gameplay is very unique and fun.There was one thing that almost ruins this game for me personaly: the little keycard things you use to unlock new rooms, the way they're hidden throughout the environment and required to progress is such an achilles heel for me mostly because i'm partly blind but mostly because i didn't come here to explore this place i came for time-clone cooperation-based automation! In tandem with that, i'm not a huge fan of how this game structures its progression. I was hoping for more of a Zachtronics flow where you're given a clear problem to solve, and the tools to solve it, and when you solve that problem you're given a new one. Sometimes this is what we get and these are the most fun parts in my opinion. The less-fun parts are the object-hunt segments and, i'm sorry, the story is incredibly one-note so far. I never did read much of the stories in Zachtronics games either. I don't feel like these types of games benefit from having a bunch of backstory and lore. But that's just me. Overall I am invested in how the gameplay evolves and having a lot of fun with the robots / clones. Good purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has really bad motion-sickness, Clockwinder was exactly what I wanted out of VR. I love narrative experiences like Gone Home and Tacoma, and being able to experience such a cute story in VR was very fun for me. The fact that such a good story was coupled with some honestly incredible physics puzzles makes this a 10/10 for me. Though the game is rather short (I finished this game in just under 5 hours) I would say that it's worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Has quickly become one of my favourite VR games of all time - the environments are exceptional, the sound design pleasing and the gameplay incredibly satisfying when you get to sit back and watch it all play out in front of you. It's very clear the love and dedication that went into this by the devs. My only hope is that DLC or  mods extend the experience as I would love to simply have more of what's already here!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Really good and fun puzzle game, comparable to something like Maskmaker (which I also enjoyed).How you solve each level is very open to interpretation and it doesn't hold your hand too much. You can also redo areas if you think of a way to increase the efficiency of your clone team (though it is not required). The game has optional efficiency goals to obtain which act like skill levels. It is satisfying to watch your assembly line working efficiently, so there is some motivation to attempt them, especially if you are at all OCD. You learn the backstory of the place though tape recordings that you find and also though conversations with an NPC, which gives the game some depth. Funny, I never found out why the clock needed to be wound in the first place though, or what would happen to the world if you failed (perhaps I missed that dialog).   The game has a cool looking art style that is not graphically heavy, so it should run well on lesser machines. The sound is very well done. I played through a couple levels on a Reverb G2, but the tracking seemed worse than usual for some reason and that hampered the gameplay a bit. Performance was good as it ran natively on WMR (bypassing steamvr), but I was unable to use any steamvr add-ons because of that. Without a turn-counter and play space centre marker, I got my cord tangled up pretty fast as you need to move around and turn a lot. After that I switched to a wireless vive-pro and the game was much more enjoyable. Quest2 users should definitely play this without the link cable. I got about 10 hours of gameplay which never felt repetitive or boring.  Not only do you need to figure out how to solve each level, but it also requires some eye-hand coordination and practice to pull it off. I felt it well worth the price and would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a puzzle game or just as a break from the usual fps games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: i had alot of fun playing this game and i might still come back to for the achievements.  its not super long but it is very fun and it feels like you are makeing factory production lines but made entirely out of clones of you. it is a facinateing mix of carefully planning out what to do and then skillfully executeing it. you can pull of crazy stunts and throw things around but you only need to pull off each action correctly once. it is very satisfieing to watch your creation at work when it is finished
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: i recommend this game 100% to anyone who is considering to play it, or wants a good VR experience. the game was short and solid, story is a good experience and is not too complicated, very straightforward and easy to understand. also, the OST was amazing, as it really added the extra sauce to the experience, it could not have been more perfect. please play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game from design to execution with a compelling story.  My only issue is the length of the game for the cost.  For full completion of the game and all achievements, you're looking at around 6 hours with little to no replay-ability.  Don't get me wrong, it was a very fun and engaging 6 hours with a great variety of puzzles and challenges.  However, I feel like this might be worth waiting for even a small sale.  If you're interested though and you don't want to wait, please don't hesitate.  You won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes it's hard to put into words what VR can bring to any particular style of game that's new. The Last Clockwinder, conversely, manages to bring something to VR puzzling that's hard to put into words and somehow very old and comforting.You're not quite sure what to expect going in but the way the game unfolds the premise gently, the lovely opening cinematic and that first careful exploration into the dark and unknown, the wonderful way you start to explore its gentle introduction to the main mechanics of the game and how it rewards your curiosity without overcrowding you while making the puzzle gameplay the focal point with little distraction is very refreshing.You're often left, after receiving some information, wondering what's next. That sounds bad but the answer is never hidden from view, even if it's something unfamiliar and alien. Your natural curiosity takes over. It's just a different environment you learn to read as you adjust to it, it feels familiar and comfortable but strange. It says here's this world, we don't need 500 collectable logs to make you feel like you're in a real place which is so great, there's no attempt to artificially slow down the player while providing the full experience literally at your own pace.The storytelling mostly via audio and short transition cutscenes is non-intrusive while usually allowing you to keep on doing whatever you were doing meaning you don't need to stand around forced to just listen for minutes at a time like in other games, weaving a bittersweet but heartwarming tale of someone exploring a cherished childhood past through older, wiser eyes and uncovering the secrets they were too young to understand. A couple of times already it made me feel a genuine wistful nostalgia for a place I've never been, something no other game (VR or not) has yet achieved.Exploring the clock tower from the "world" mechanic is just mind bending enough to hold wonder while being intuitive enough to make sense, even though in context it doesn't as the various rooms are brought to you, or are you brought to the rooms but the scenery stays the same outside? Whatever the case, it works well.I've not even touched on the actual gameplay here which is exactly the kind of innovation and originality we needed to see in the VR space, the way the music builds with each clone recorded and combines instruments to create a unique tune brings an immediately noticable joy to making progress in the puzzles and keeps your brain engaged while you're problem solving, always trying to find the harmony with your gardeners.I'm surprised by the ability to revise and fine tune the mechanics and how much of a simple joy it is to time things properly, the timing is intuitive when when it's your body doing it and it brings something strangely human to your robot copies that imbues a recognisable personality.If you value originality in your games, play this game and play it right now. For years puzzle games have been resigned to the bargain bin or just redressed old concepts in new clothes but the problems thrown at me in this game so far are genuinely innovative and challenging without it ever not being obvious what you need to happen. I look forward figuring out the rest of them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Atmosphere and voice acting are excellent. Gameplay concept is unique and has exciting potential, but the execution leaves something to be desired. Overall still recommended, and even a must-have to experience this unique application of VR.Starting the game and seeing the initial gameplay mechanics was thrilling. It brought to mind games like Spacechem or Infinifactory that take a concept and explore every corner of it to deliver 100+ hours of gameplay. Clockwinder, however, doesn't wring out its automation mechanics the way those other games do.  It offers maybe 8-12 hours of gameplay if you optimize every room, within reason. Unlike those other games, the available gameplay blends well into a short, captivating story with stellar voice acting. Clockwinder isn't trying to be an endless automation game, it feels more like the automation mechanics are a vehicle with which to deliver the story.Even though it isn't a hardcore automation game, automation is the core gameplay, and Clockwinder's implementation of that gameplay has some issues. To summarize the gameplay execution issues: a room whose automation worked when you left it may not work when you load the room again. The record/replay mechanism isn't 100% deterministic. Compared to Zachtronics-type games this slight randomness is deeply unsatisfying. The non-determinism makes the game feel "messy".In addition to non-determinism, there are a few other issues that contribute to the messy feeling:- If you delete a robot at the right time, the game will record that you are using 1 fewer robots before it registers the impact of removing that robot on the throughput of the room, allowing you to cheese some of the achievements. I did this accidentally while attempting to achieve the top result in a room, which robbed some of the satisfaction of eventually doing it properly.- The player's manual, non-recorded actions can contribute to the computed throughput of a room for the purpose of reaching throughput goals. Again can be used to cheese goals, even accidentally.- For many rooms, luck is the only way to optimize robot count past a certain number. For example, one robot _could_ grab and blindly throw several things to precisely the correct locations in 1 tick, but the chance of pulling that off is extremely low.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game and this is a great idea for a VR game. It reminded me of those time clone puzzles in Ratchet N Clank but you use your clones for automating fruit collection. This game can be very short and sweet, probably like 6 hours if you're just looking to finish it, but I found it much more fun to go for the challenge production rates. They doubled the amount of playtime for me. They are far from necessary, so you can just relax and make your own solutions if that's what you're looking for. There were two bugs that led to some frustration. One, sometimes the connected fruit would clip outside of the press machine leading to inconsistent output. It didn't happen too often, but when I was really close to a solution for max output it really irked me. Two, I'm not sure if this is really a bug but when I was trying to reach peak output with the Luftapples they would get clogged in the roof tube. I had to have a clone shove its hand into the tube to declog every 4 seconds, but that wasn't a consistent solution. I thought maybe this was intended and was to discourage sending too many to that pipe, but a lot of the planter box positions and the limit on the amount of clones seemed to suggest this was the intended solution. Maybe I'm just a fool, but I couldn't think of any other ways to reach that last challenge output. I still ended up reaching the final challenge output because when I switched rooms it forced all of the luftapples to get shoved into the pipe at once and that counted.You can cheese a few challenges by just amassing a bunch of fruit or pellets next to the output tube and just dumping them all at once. I didn't think that was very fun and I preferred to find an intended solution, but to each their own. In the immortal words of HungryBox, "We take those."The story was sweet and I found myself going out of my way to find all the tape recorders and to listen in on all the Levi chatter.I whole heartedly recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun VR puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty short. It took me about 4 hours to beat it, and spent some more time after beating the story to further optimize my farms. The gameplay itself is fantastic, and the story is fun as well. I would have like smooth locomotion and smooth turning as options, but teleport and snap turning are fine enough for this game since the important stuff, which means setting up your clones, happens while stationary anyway. fine tuning the location of your clones can be a little clunky with teleport, but it's not too bad.I had a ton of fun with the game, so I don't feel like I spent too much, even if the game was pretty short.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing, seriously. It's cozy without being cheesy, the core puzzle mechanic is executed beautifully, and it allows for tons of creativity. The story is told through voice logs and conversations over a radio. Solid voice acting performances, and dialogue. To the devs, if you read these: please make more games/dlc using this core mechanic. The efficiency-centered game play is a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Its a very nice and unique game. I enjoy the core mechanic very much. I hope more devs are coming up with new innovative ideas like this. Its really worth the experience. It also has a nice story to go along and the graphics are super cute. I hope they will make a DLC some day, to provide more content.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Clever and engaging puzzle game with a beautiful atmosphere, setting, music and voice acting. I was also impressed with the accuracy of the physics - at least, things went where I thought they would when I threw them! I really wish there were more levels but for the price point the content feels just right. There is also decent scope for replayability by optimising your loops in each level so I expect more hours of playtime in my future!Kudos to the developers for finding a workaround for virtual desktop in just a few days, they didnt have to do that, but it shows massive respect for the playerbase.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This was a neat little VR game. If you like automation and puzzle games, you will get your money’s worth here. The story isn't too bad either, although the focus is on the unique gameplay mechanics.I'm writing this review on 06/05 and finished the game after about 5 hours. It's missing a few nice quality of life features, such as resetting the room or restoring a room to its last functional state. At the same time, there are some VR jankiness and audio issues. But none of that would cause me to not recommend the game. Only the challenges in the rooms I will probably do later, if such updates are still coming.In the end, I can only hope that more will be done with this mechanic. Perhaps even a full factory automation game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing concept, great execution, plays really well, fun puzzles that make sense. Art style is beautiful yet simple. Only way i could see improvement is with locomotion support instead of just teleportation and some in world interaction (like picking non essential objects up, but thats just me being picky)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Even though it costs 21€ and gives you 5 - 7h of playtime, that playtime is SO fun that it's worth it. And when you've completed the game, you can just load your save and make all the previous farms much faster with less gardeners to keep you entertained (Or just restart the game). It is one of the best VR games I've played. And all the reviews so far (60) have been positive.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played a little bit of the game, but I'm already super charmed by this game. The basic mechanics are simple yet very effective, the voice acting and world building is phenomenal and I love the style of the levels itself.Some things I would like to see improved, it would be the lack of settings regarding locomotion. I'm one of those people is perfectly comfortable with smooth gliding locomotion, but teleportation makes me uncomfortable.Also, the initial "intro" puzzle with the glowing sticks is a bit confusing (though not terribly so), as it doesn't quite seem to match the actual game-play it's trying to teach. I would skip the door puzzle and instead teach the player just by having them do the 3-levers pipe puzzle with the gloves.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 2 hours in and I'm loving this game! Gameplay is super smooth. There's no time limits so you can progress casually through the game if you like, making simple lines and letting the seeds slowly accumulate to unlock the next level.   The challenge is when you're trying to make your line of robots really efficient (each floor has optional efficiency challenges); I find myself recording the same few seconds loop of me trying to grab objects out of the air, stick them to another object, and throw to the next robot, for example. It's really satisfying when it all comes together. Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10Pros:Fun automation and plenty of achievmentsAmazing story that leaves you wanting moreLots of levelsCozy room design and graphics that give that warm vibeYou can make the bots do whatever you wantpuzzle gameSmall dev team listens to feedbacksupports Virtual DesktopDifficulty curve is perfect Completed levels give you the satisfaction you craveCons:i played this game for 6 hours straight and now my throwing arm hurts
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very fun and immersive vr experience the art and game design are unique and amazing and game play keeps you going trying to figure out how to solve the puzzle and the idea of setting automatic systems means every level could be beaten in any number of ways Overall 10/10 game and is a must buy if you wanna try something new or are brand new to vr
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is incredibly fun. I bought it because of the concept and I am having fun trying to complete the challenges, whether it's having one robot throwing a ton of fruit as fast as possible to make it so I have as few as possible or restarting one to get the perfect throw. This is a game I hope to 100% someday and I really hope that the Devs do more, either with this game or make more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I don't leave reviews but this game is a gem. I love automation and factory games, and this one has such an interesting way of doing it and it really, really works. The controls are simplified VR (Teleport movement only), but it's still so very good. If you like automation or factory games, and you like having a great reason to use your VR headset, buy this game. We need MORE of this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: I love factory/automation games and this game perfectly transports that fun into VR with a super cool idea. Creating a perfect clockwork of a bunch of clones of yourself is both mentally and physically challenging. Sure you could have three clones hand the produce down to the output shaft, or you could have one clone yeet it across the room. The self-induced chaos and comedy that can ensue from this simple concept is magical. Presentation is also top notch, with shockingly good voice acting,  and the game runs smoothly and without any glitches so far.Finding good VR games is hard these days, but this one's a real gem!
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Basically one of the chemistry themed Zatchtronics games, but less programming and more physical interaction. And also a botany theme and very nice little diorama levels.In addition to the mental challenge of the puzzles (nothing too extreme, at least so far), there's a physical challenge here too. Like Zatchtronics games, you get rewarded for speed and minimal use of gardener robots, which requires not only careful planning but well recorded motions for each robot. If you need to pass something to the other side of the level for example, you might play it safe and slow, passing it along a chain of 3 or so robots, or you could play it dangerous and try to make the perfect recording of you tossing it straight into the chute from the other end.This personal touch to each robot's motion gives you an extra feeling of satisfaction, as the robots throw and assemble everything in perfect fashion, knowing it took you like 30 tries to get that one perfect recording for each of them.If you like these kinds of factory line puzzle games and want to see a really cool new take on them in VR, this is a must play. The story is quite nice so far too.NOTE: If you have both Oculus and SteamVR installed, and SteamVR is not set as the default OpenVR runtime (check the developer settings in SteamVR), the game will not start with an odd message about your headset not working. There's a few more minor bugs, e.g. I somehow teleported the phone's switch about a meter from where it should be, but nothing massively game breaking. I'm writing this very shortly after release so I imagine these could easily be addressed with some small bugfix updates.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the most fun in VR I've had in the last year or twoThe gameplay so far has been addicting. Its a interesting mix of catching and throwing objects, single player teamwork, and a little factory line optimization. Often challenges are straightforward, you know what you have to do you just have to find the best way to do it, and have the skills to carry out your plan. It rewards both strategy and coordination, while also allowing you to have fun and progress at your own pace. Also the throwing physics are spot on. With unique gameplay, a cozy environment, and voice acting that is both fun and immersive. I can easily recommend The Last Clockwinder.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Clockwinder is one of those unique VR games that is both extremely satisfying to play, and has gameplay that only really works in a VR setting. By setting up short recording loops, you can pass, assemble, and throw objects to other cycles of yourself, creating an automaton factory that's entirely your own motions.As you progress, the quantity and efficiency of your work plays a part behind the scenes, where finished items will continue being made across "levels". This gives a great additional reason to revisit areas and optimize, as it increase the rate of progress later on.All of this is wrapped around an interesting story fleshed out through player dialog and audio logs, with a pleasant art style that complements the nature themes of the game world.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Clockwinder

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun, having a blast, only problem is the every loop(Bot throw rotation) fps drop.  If that could be solved I would be very pleased (I don't believe its hardware, I'm running a RTX 3060 Ti). Made a entire system only to discover a more simple way to do it.  The game runs, and looks great otherwise, I always wanted a game where you have clones that mimic your moves and do stuff.  I don't know how much content there is so far, but I hope there is, or could be a challenge mode (something of that sort).  With a little polish, this game could be one of the best titles to date.  The simple and welcoming art style helps make the game calm, and enjoyable.  Many, (including myself) are waiting, and hoping for a big, cool VR game to exceed expectations, but any attempts made usually boil down to "It could have been a screen game".  While this game could work as a screen, it wouldn't have been as engaging as it is in VR.  The fact that you have to actually throw the fruit, and catch it while being locked with a time frame to do it gives pressure, while also improving your ability to time stuff.  The game comes down to a understanding of surroundings, instead of a understanding of a keyboard and mouse.Spoils!!!!!My favorite part so far is the when you have to catch all 4 dew drops on a fruit (the way I did it at least) then throw it over to a catch bot who holds it over, then the knife bot goes, WOOSH, and it just works.  So fun and moments like that make the game amazing.For those who don't want to read a essay,8/10  Really gives a push on the brain, and body. Really fun, cool game, and plays well (polished).  (only big problem) If it would stop having frame drops at bad times I could maybe make my shoots.Additions-  The float fruits can be very buggy, and one of the pipes will not accept the fruits over filling the pipe.  Loading screens are well hidden with the changing of platforms.Post game- Great story, very charming.  I like how many ways you could go about doing something in this game, but it is very short.  Taking my time with this game gave me roughly 10 hours of content.  I hope their is eventually more content, maybe even a dlc with new plants, and more crazy levels.  Since this game is made in unity, I can not wait to see what crazy mods are made for this game.  custom levels, or even more fruit could be very interesting.  While I know some had problems with teleport, and snap turn, this game was small enough that it actually feels better playing this way (smooth turn would be nice though).  The flying fruit could be very buggy, one minute lining up perfectly, the next unsynced.  This game has high potential to have more content added, and would be a shame if it was just a quick "That was cool!" and move on.  There also was a lot of areas that just felt lackluster, and could be beat in a few minutes which was sad.Final Final- 7/10 wish there was more, but was one heck of a experience GO PLAY IT NOW!!!Extra- This feels like Animusic as a game, just the way the robots move and look, and I love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying that i am not defending Capcom adding DRM. That being said:There is a TON of misinformation floating around about Capcom's Enigma DRM, and many people are just blindly believing whatever they read on Twitter, then spreading that highly questionable information further and passing it off as proven fact.The truth of the matter is: Capcom added this DRM literally months ago, and absolutely nobody noticed. Do you know why? Because it didn't actually affect performance, at least not to any noticeable degree. It sure is weird how all of these people complaining that their performance is suddenly way worse, somehow didn't notice this supposed markedly worse performance for multiple months until they finally read about the DRM months after the fact, don't you think? Again, this was added MONTHS ago, and nobody started claiming that their performance plummeted until AFTER the news about the DRM spread and it had already been installed for months.What actually happened is that Capcom patched RE: Revelations, and the patch screwed  up the game massively. When people were poking around that game afterwards they THEN finally noticed the DRM, and then some shmuck who pays for a blue check on Twitter equated those issues with RE: Revelations to the Enigma DRM when the issues were in fact caused by the patch.Has it been flagged as malware by some antivirus programs? Yes. Does that definitively mean that it actually IS malware? No, it does not. A lot of things cause false positives, and there are numerous people/videos out there that have run tests and found that it is very likely just a false positive (Mutahar, for example). Are there reasons to be leery? Sure. Is there actually any objective evidence that this is harmful malware? No.Does it suck that they added this? Yes. Has it been blown wildly out of proportion, and are people spreading and buying into a ton of misinformation because they just believed whatever they read without actually looking into it further? Yes.I'm not defending it. I'm not saying definitively that it isn't an issue and/or isn't malware. But i AM saying that people need to calm down, look at the actual facts, and stop spreading hysteria and misinformation and passing off unfounded claims as objective and proven facts. (Btw, for what it's worth: i have played numerous Capcom games on here over the last few months, and have noticed absolutely zero difference in performance on the games that i have played.)*prepares for everyone to tell me that i'm a shill or a moron or whatever other toxic nonsense this attempt at reason will inspire....

_childDocuments_.review: Edit - 11/19/2023 - Time for the Proper ReviewAlright, hundo'd both Stadiums so time for the proper review. First, the old games are good...except the variety here means that unless you are a generalist then getting all of them (like in the bundle) is going to get you games you don't like. Heck, I'm a generalist and I still didn't like some of them. But all these games got reviews throughout history, so let me tell you about the Stadium "wrapper". It's a bit overdone in places and underdone in others. While the simulated Arcade is cool an all, I have to say that most folks who want retro games are more likely to want something less...resource demanding (both in RAM and storage space). I'm personally fine with it (tho I would have done it differently), but I think the best play would have been to make it more optional. Maybe like a side feature instead of the main interface. Next, you get a limited number of quick save slots (32). Not bad, but "other" ways to play old games offer unlimited quicksaves. Next, the Stadiums are a shining example of why you don't set your game's default settings to something controversial like "Simulated Cabinet View Mode". I WROTE A GUIDE TO SHOW HOW TO MAKE THE GAMES LOOK LIKE NORMAL GAMES AND NOT SIMS OF CABS. The fact that I felt it was worth it to write a guide telling how to do it should give you an idea of what's next: obtusely designed GUI. It looks pretty, sure, but it is not intuitive, even to exit the Stadium. It can be figured out with some effort, but a GUI shouldn't take effort to figure out. There's been standards for decades. And then there's all the things the game doesn't tell you despite all the tutorials it overloads you with when you first start playing. Like the math for the CASPO points, which varies per game. Or the hard caps on gain per session (that changes depending on the bonus theme of the week). And so on. These things should be knowable and spelled out...but probably not in quite so an intrusive and overloaded manner as the current explanations.Now, personally, all these are pretty forgivable. The games run fine (on my rig, at least) and, except for when I had way too many windows open while trying to find a guide for a game older than me, there were no noticeable problems with actually playing. (Which is more than I can say for far too many retro ports that were (in those cases) blatant low-effort cashgrabs). And hindsight is 20/20 and I'm sure the Devs did their best despite whatever rot any higher ups tried to force on them. Badly made deadlines, unreasonable demands imposed more by the marketing department than actual players of games, unhealthy working hour demands, and so on. The industry is full of it and I'm sure this had to endure it too. A few instances of "not enough time to think things through" shouldn't be a deal breaker but I will still take points off for it.Lastly though, the price. Hoo boy. If you look at the reviews over time, you might notice references that don't make sense. This is because of how the bizness dept handled things. Or mangled things, really. The games were released as DLC. That's actually fine since it means you can pick and choose what you get instead of the standard Collection price where you are required to pay for everything including junk you know you will hate. BUT! The way the DLC was released is where things get bad. They didn't release them all at once. They bundled them oddly. They changed the way they were bundled multiple times. The used the Steam Package pricing setup instead of the Bundle pricing setup in some cases, meaning if you owned some of the DLC already and bought a package you would be paying for stuff you already had and would not get anything for it. (Bundles have been a thing for long enough, stop using anti-consumer Packages please.) And at time of writing, there's no bundles at all now? Why?  Ugh. Never seen a Bundle pricing arrangement get removed before, or even just replaced as many times. I don't understand what is going on with the bizness decisions here.Oh, and let's not forget the decision to split the Stadiums. Why do it? Is it a problem of File Size, maybe for consoles? A matter of how a contract was written somewhere? I'm not upset I had to get all the Cheevos for both Stadiums instead of just for one unified Stadium since I needed the time to understand all these old games had to offer and cogitate what a Minimum Passing Grade for a Retro Game Wrapper/Port/Emulator Thing should be judged on AND what a good price would be. I'm just super confused.Anyway, in all, I give the Stadiums a Genuine 100% "Mixed" Review, complete with a Like for  Stadium 1st and a dislike for 2nd Stadium because that's as close to a Mixed Rating as Steam allows. The games together are "Mixed" because tho the games themselves are as good as they've likely ever been, I doubt any individual player is going to love all of them (tho that matters less since the Bundle pricing is gone, but it still matters enough since the rating is for the Stadium as a whole). The Stadium gets a "Mixed" rating. It runs the games without problems (that I can tell), it can do most of what the...*ehem* "other ways to play" can do, it did the decent thing of bringing older games to newer hardware for the enjoyment of all and preservation of history, and it offers some decent additional content like points leaderboards and such. But, it doesn't have online play, the bizness decisions have been inexplicable (and frankly concerning), the interface is unintuitive & more than most seem to want, and why did they not sell all the music tracks instead of just a couple?100% Mixed.Pre-Lim Review Starts Here:Soo, this is just a prelim review. I'm still working one my review for the first one, but I noticed here there were lots of people complaining about "Microtransactions" and such like. Now that's not actually an issue. Lots of people don't want all of these games. They only want a few, based on whatever it is they like. Like shmups. Or they maybe can't afford all these games, even with the Package Discount. And these are all FULL games, not some trashy costume, or in-game currency, or even actual Arcade pay-per-play mechanics or whatever. This ain't "microtransactions" in the way that deserves to be reviled and buried in an unmarked grave. It's an almost wholesome selling model that makes sense for a massive collection of diverse games it has to offer, and this would almost be very consumer friendly.Edit (7/1/2023): Well, dunno when or why they changed the package to a bundle, but they did. But I'm leaving this as negative for now until I can actually get time to check the game out properly.

_childDocuments_.review: Good- A lot of the games hold up well. Options to make the game more accommodating to modern audiences are appreciated. The games run well. Thoughts- After 38 hours of gameplay, I can say that this package might not be for everyone. If you’re an enthusiast of the medium or a fan of Capcom’s arcade glory day? Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium is well worth your time, and I would say it’s worth it to check out most, if not all, of the games. Many of them may not have held up as well, but even they hold some value as a time capsule. Video games have come a long way since the heyday of the arcade – but that doesn’t mean we have to forget the medium’s roots after all. Capcom certainly isn’t.

Once you are in the game, you are s.o.l.No Key binding, which means, if you are playing on a computer and you want to use the directional keys instead of WASD, you can't (For reference I play the Puzzle Fighter game).Third. I only use a keyboard for games, but even if I did use controllers, I can't for the life of me figure out how to adjust the settings (it gives you an option to select what type of controller you will use when opening up the first time, but it appears to be a one time menu from what I can tell).Fourth. The game wants you to feel like you are in an arcade playing, which means you are looking at a cabinet with boundaries and it mimics a bubble view of thick rounded glass. You are even given 3D camera view options (you know, in case you want to look around a fake mock up of an arcade while you are trying to play a game???) Ideally there would be a mode to transition from Classic view to....idk, not classic view? Maybe allow the gamer to choose what kind of experience they want?Lastly, I have not found a way to pause the game and the music is not great (It's loud and obnoxious like being in an arcade, which I guess is the point?) _childDocuments_.review: Okay, first thing to address:There's a lot of people saying that this collection is harming the Capcom Fighting Collection's viability. It's not. The purpose of this collection and the CFC are radically different. If you want a competitive online experience complete with matchmaking and rollback netcode, this is NOT the collection for you, you want the CFC. Period.-This collection, however has fun casual features such as rewind and speed change and has a breadth of fun titles to either relive or experience altogether.The collection has incredible variety, from shoot 'em ups, to racing, to puzzle. I made sure to purchase the full pack, so I can't say how well the ala carte method of only having access to a few games at a time, but I never had problems with games not being unlocked or the technical issues griped about in some reviews.-This collection is fantastic for having a relaxed evening with nostalgia, if you're a fan of arcade games and arcade collections, this is a no-brainer.

_childDocuments_.review: A very polished compilation of old arcade games, classic or niche. The arcade background really sells the retro ambiance and preserves a bit of the original context. CA2S has a solid line-up of games, way better than the first compilation in my opinion (I personally spent most of my playtime in Mega Man 2). For the games themselves, the emulation runs perfectly and the extra features (save/load, rewind, speed change) are well appreciated. The challenges and leaderboard also add plenty of replay value. A very great way to experience a part of video game history!So, why do I not recommend this game? Well, there's a high chance that a game-breaking bug just wipes your save data and prevents you from playing further unless you reboot your computer. In a game that encourages grinding and playing for several days straight (one of the achievements asks you to boot the game for five days in a row), it can be very demoralising to lose 7 hours of gameplay for no specific reason, but it becomes really annoying if it happens a second time. I'm willing to take the responsability of the bug, I should have been more careful with the autosave, but game data should not corrupt this easily.Sadly, this small detail is a dealbreaker in this otherwise flawless compilation of games. If you don't mind playing russian roulette with your save file every time you close the game and manage to overlook this issue, it's a really good package. Otherwise, I cannot willingly recommend a broken product with an issue that could have been fixed with a simple flag check to prevent the player from quitting the game while it's autosaving.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium: A Fresh Collection of Retro Gems with Modern EnhancementsIntroduction:Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium takes players on another nostalgic trip through Capcom’s arcade classics, delivering a second wave of retro hits that defined the golden age of gaming. This collection features fan favorites and lesser-known gems alike, wrapped in a modern package with gameplay enhancements that make revisiting these timeless titles feel as exciting as ever. Free with the download is SONSON, a beloved classic, and it's just the beginning of an arcade experience that offers plenty to rediscover.Gameplay:The heart of Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium lies in its diverse collection of classic arcade games, each offering its own unique challenges and gameplay style. Whether you're fighting enemies in co-op with a friend, navigating shooters, or enjoying other retro genres, this collection caters to every arcade fan. The gameplay stays true to its original design, but modern quality-of-life features elevate the experience: rewind mechanics let you fix mistakes instantly, save states allow you to pause and resume anytime, and speed adjustments give you the power to control the pace of play. Whether you’re reliving your childhood or diving into these titles for the first time, these improvements make the games more approachable while keeping their core difficulty intact.Graphics:Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium captures the authentic arcade look with detailed 3D-rendered arcade cabinets and customizable display settings. Players can tailor their visuals to their liking with scanline filters, aspect ratio adjustments, and screen effects that simulate the glow of old-school monitors. The pixel art of each title is lovingly preserved, keeping the vibrant colors and intricate sprites intact. It’s an immersive visual experience that makes you feel like you’ve stepped back into an arcade, but with just the right amount of polish to appeal to modern sensibilities.Conclusion:Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium is a fantastic follow-up to the first collection, offering both veteran gamers and newcomers a chance to experience Capcom’s retro catalog in a new light. With gameplay-enhancing features, customizable visuals, and online leaderboards to keep you engaged, this collection feels both classic and fresh. Whether you're competing for high scores or simply looking to relive the magic of arcade days gone by, *Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium* delivers an experience that's well worth your time.Rating: 4.5/5 - A Retro Collection Done RightSummary:Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium builds on the success of its predecessor, offering a new wave of classic Capcom arcade titles with gameplay enhancements that make them more accessible than ever. The addition of modern features like save states, rewind functionality, and speed control allows players to enjoy these retro games with a fresh twist. Whether you’re in it for the nostalgia or looking to conquer leaderboards, Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium is a stellar continuation of Capcom's efforts to preserve arcade history while making it fun and engaging for today’s players.

_childDocuments_.review: So... Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium is another collection of 30+ Capcom Arcade Classics. And like the first Stadium, I really enjoy it for what it is. I had a problem with the first Stadium where my game would randomly freeze for a few seconds every so often while I was connected to the internet, and 2nd Stadium doesn't do that to me. So I'm gonna go into pros and cons, but before I do I'm gonna address a big elephant in the room...Many have taken notice that Stadium 2 has 6 of the same games as the Fighting Collection, such as 3 Darkstalkers titles, Super Gem Fighter, and such and it only released a month after Fighting Collection. If you just wanna play these games, you should get the Fighting Collection as it has a bunch more settings you can play around with such as improved controls, online play, and easy-to-select secret characters. Stadium only has Rewind, Speed Change, and Invincibility. I don't recommend you go out of your way to get those overlapping games on their own unless you just wanna have a complete Stadium set or mess around with Invincibility. If you already didn't have a copy, then maybe, but for these games, Fighting Collection is superior.-32 classic arcade games that are mostly fun-Customizable settings, same as the first Stadium-Improved Time, Score, and Special Challenge Modes (This got ported into the first Stadium too)-Invcincibility Setting DLC for all 32 games, and it was free when I got it this time!-Rewind, Speed Change, and Infinite Coins if you want them-No online multiplayer, Remote Play Together is your best bet.-Came out 1 month after the Fighting Collection with half of that collection's library-Any altered assets from 1st Stadium and Fighting Collection still altered here-Overlapping games from Fighting Collection have more options than their Stadium counterparts

_childDocuments_.review: '' is a virtual arcade with tons and tons of classic games from the company  all to which sculpted many of our childhoods and were maybe even the reason why some of us became gamers. Coming from someone who's played a lot of games in their childhood, I'll be honest and mention that  didn't play a vital role in it. I grew up playing mostly  games alongside a few other titles but among them  some  games calling '' and ''. Sure I wasn't great at them but hey, I found them to be pretty fun.It's unwise to think you'd be able to play all the classic  games in this one title but it's an arcade! It clearly states that in the name so what gives? I never had the luxury of going to an arcade as a kid, being bombarded with ensembles of seizure inducing lights and sounds which obviously a virtual environment couldn't replicate but being able to explore different arcade cabinets to play some games I've never even heard of before? What could be better?Unfortunately curiosity killed the cat in this case as the entire arcade is anything but amazing. You have a virtual arcade to which you're locked on a selection screen while hyped-up techno music and flashy lights fill the room as well as your eyes. There is a very generous amount of games in the arcade's roster but as you all know, you can't play them all. You can't play  of them except one, '', a 2D sidescroller where the goal is to clear 20 sections while collecting food and shooting baddies for points. It's alright I guess, all you do is move between 5 or so platforms while trying to survive long enough for the game to eventually end. I'm also aware that the description on the store page gives a vague implication that all the games are paid DLC and that '' is the only one that's free but damn, just one?Now what makes this disappointing? Well for the obvious reason: you're only given one freebie while every other game is locked behind a paywall and not a cheap one either.  per title. That's right, games developed around the same time  became a thing are being digitally sold for 6 damn dollars. You might say that's not a lot and that 6 dollars is exponentially lower than most games sold today but we're talking about games older than most active users on . On top of that, these are games with little content in them given their age and if I have to be brutally honest, if I had to pay 6 dollars just to play '', I can't say I'd be happy either.One can make the argument that it's better since it's structure functions very similarly to other games such as '' and '' where you only buy what you want and I agree, it works to an extent but I still can't comprehend why they couldn't have just sold it like what  did with their classic games collection. Maybe it's just the fact that I prefer games being sold all together as one since it feels more complete instead of the company looking like they're trying to milk as much money out of you as they can and trying to sell you each of them singularly at inflated prices.I have nothing against this type of structure since it gives players the freedom to buy what they want not having to pay a larger sum for a collection of games they may not be interested in playing. In fact, it isn't all bad as there are other handy features included in the arcade that you wouldn't normally have access to like a fast-forward, slow-mo and even rewind feature to make games you're playing easier in case you make a mistake. There are also save features as well as customizable skins for arcade cabinets to give your virtual arcade a bit of personal touch. On top of that there are different difficulty and challenge modes adding some more variety to the game in addition to multiplayer which at the moment is sadly local only. It's actually not bad and is a little something extra for those who actually enjoy playing ''.At the end of the day it all comes down to preference but it sure makes the "Free" price tag on the store page look a lot less appealing.As mentioned the arcade gives you plenty of control over the game with the ability to change speed and rewind time making even the hardest games a cinch. But for the one game that you  play, all I really have to say about it is that well, it works. It's not great but it's not bad, it's... retro. It definitely plays and feels like a retro game and I think that in itself adds to the charm. The game itself is pretty hard even on the normal setting but for a game released back then, it's expected. The arcade has lots of menus and controls making the entire ordeal just to navigate around it pretty damn confusing since most of the controls are different than what most PC gamers are used to.This is definitely the type of title you'd use a controller for as it clearly caters to controller players rather than keyboard and mouse players (rightfully so). So if you're heading into this with keys and a mouse, expect at least a bit of confusion even if you don't plan on buying any actual arcade games.For the arcade, it looks pretty nice with the appropriate flashing lights and 80's vibes with neon lights strewn about. Although I can't say much for the games since I haven't played any of them besides '', I'd imagine they look exactly like if not better than their original counterparts. Overall, the arcade pretty much looks like what I would have expected it to look.Imagine a party with music blaring out into the streets along with lights illuminating even the darkest of shadows. Now imagine that music being kind of decent but once you decide to check the party out, you realize all you can do is drink punch and doing anything else that's fun will cost you a fiver. That's basically ''. I can at least say the music and sound effects  accurately represent those you'd hear in an arcade but once again, they don't really stand out. I'm just glad it didn't cause me to scramble for a mute button.Sadly more disappointment covers the floor of the infamous  arcade because there is no online play. The potential to play classic co-op games online with other people is flushed down the toilet as  made the wonderfully dumb mistake to exclude any form of online play. Sure you're able to play together with someone in a physical space but what are the odds of a two people being equally interested in this title and wanting to play the same game that this arcade just so happens to offer? The bigger demographic is clearly online but for some reason a massive game company with more than enough resources and workforce can't seem to understand that. Just goes to show, you should leave the gaming industry to gamers, not people who most likely have never held a controller in their hands.'' is a very limited virtual arcade game where you can only play 1 free game while the rest are locked behind a very stingy paywall. Although it's fairly easy to tell that there's only one game available to play for free, it isn't directly acknowledged that you can only play one game unless you put two and two together. It's like going to an arcade but only being able to play one game. It's sad. That being said though, it still offers the ability to just buy what you want rather than spend more for things you don't want along with extra features that make playing a tad easier. All in all, it comes down to preference but I personally am not a fan of this type of structure for games. This game isn't really "free".

_childDocuments_.review: The Capcom Arcade Stadiums tend to get a rather eh rep, and some of it was deserved up to a point in time, but honestly, I think now these are great ways of playing Capcom's arcade greats. They're especially fun when trying the challenges!Do they devalue Capcom's other collections? Honestly, no. I think the point is for these to have a different focus from stuff like Capcom Fighting Collection's online VS play - you can still do that locally for funsies, but you get the most out of practicing your favorite games and recording your all-time best runs for the world to see - and for other players to challenge! Sure, the bot plague extended to these compilations a bit, but let's be real: I would NEVER count those lazy clowns in anything competitive. If you can beat real people's challenges, that's worth some pride.Parting words: I hope that someday we can get more compilations of games that include spinoffs of fan-favorite game series. Seeing the MegaMan arcade games rereleased for the first time since, what, *freaking MegaMan Anniversary Collection of all things* is seriously awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda got scared from the numerous negative reviews making it sound like there's something defective about this collection.Then Humble Bundle had both Capcom Arcade Stadiums in a bundle and I jumped for it. Both stadium 1 and 2 work and play fine on my PC so I have no idea what the negative reviews are on about.... Except the ones whining about DRM - THOSE are from communists and software pirates who hate the idea of DRM and want anything with it to fail commercially. These complaints don't even make any sense given if you wanted to play every game in this compilation (and more) without DRM and for free, you can do so with MAME. Honestly, I don't think anyone would know the DRM is there unless they tried to pirate this collection which, again, is just 'why?'To the 1 negative review where they couldn't get the game to start: Capcom Arcade Stadium 2 uses RE Engine to fully render a mock arcade, so if you're trying to play this on a potato, that's probably why.Outside of that, the only people I'd expect to be angry with this compilation are purists who would predictably get mad the NA ROMs aren't 100% original using the Japanese titles likely due to stupid copyright/potential political reasons:Hissatsu Buraiken = AvengersGanu Sumoku = Gun.smoke (this better be because of the ancient TV show and not idiotic political takes on the word 'gun'. And yes, its called gun.smoke. The . between gun and smoke is the most important letter of them all)That being said, I'd also expect anger over most of the games from Capcom Arcade Cabinet being recycled for this collection. Although, to be fair, the ROMs in Arcade Cabinet were tampered with and their behavior wasn't 100% arcade accurate. Stadium's ROMs seem to be 1:1 arcade perfect, although some games have been censored/edited.This collection includes lots of features I don't care about to emulate the arcade experience: scan lines, filters, CRT deformation and the like. Who cares? I like the rewind feature though.The selection of games in this collection is a bit of a mix of good, bad, and obscure. I'll list the Capcom arcade generations and call out some of the better games:- There are lots of pre-CPS board Capcom games here. Capcom knew how to make games at this time, but not how to make them good or enjoyable. This time period is from Capcom's inception up to 1988. Most of these games were also in the Capcom Arcade Cabinet collection, but they're mostly unmolsted for this collection. Most of them still suck, aren't fun, and are frustrating. Strangely, most NES versions of these same games are much, much better.1943 Kai : maybe the only standout from this era that is actually pretty goodTiger Road : another some people seem to like. I don't care for it.- This collection also features a bunch of lesser known, obscure, and b-tier games from Capcom's CPS1 generation (1988-1995). The advent of CPS 1 in addition to suddenly knowing WTF they were doing is when Capcom made a name for itself in video game arcades where most of these games wound up being good and fun (if not also unfair to take in lots of quarters):Magic Sword - A classic. Its hard to explain this game. Its like a D&D inspired side scroller.The King of Dragons - Basically a mash up of Final Fight with D&D. Back in the day, I never saw this in an arcade, ever. Only on SNES.Knights of the Round - Basically medieval Final Fight. This is perhaps my favorite Capcom game and was basically in and out of arcades in about a year never to be seen again. This is like the 4th time I've stupidly bought this game in a Capcom collection. I don't care because I like the game so much! The concept of having the Knights of the Round Table evolve as they level up where King Arthur becomes a walking suit of bronze armor that uses a giant spoon to beat up medieval fair actors just works and never gets old for me.- The CPS2 generation (1993-2003) games found here are all lesser known/L@@K R@R3. Their rareness and obscurity is not an exaggeration. Unless it was a huge game with a known title, you wouldn't see many of these show up in an arcade. And if you did see a b-tier CPS2 game, it didn't last long. Capcom also cracked down hard on bootlegging/piracy with CPS2 to the point every board had encryption keys kept alive via a battery. When the battery ran out of power, the board would commit sudoku. The security was so robust for these games, it wasn't cracked until relatively recently by people who then dumped 100% playable ROMs to MAME. A blessing since you didn't see many of these games appear in arcades back in the day, and you likely won't see any in a vintage video arcade today.Saturday Night Slam Masters: YES! This was another game that was literally in almost every arcade in NA when it came out, and pretty much disappeared from them all at the same time about a month later. Playing it again now, decades later, I'm reminded how the CPU AI makes this game not fun at all; its unfairly good. I'm also reminded how I was angry with the SNES version for not letting you play as Scorpion in single player.... Only to discover this was also the case for the arcade version; you can pick him in tag team match tho. And he's the only guy I wanted to play because he looks like a bad ass ninja while everyone else looks like a giant doughy drunken gweilo.all 3 Darkstalker/Vampire Savior games : I consider these all rare. When it came to arcade fighters from Capcom, most arcade curators picked Street Fighter 2 over anything else so I only ever saw a few DS 1 and 2 cabinets in NA arcades and never saw 3 ever. Darkstalkers 1 is a shameless ripoff of Street Fighter 2 but the others are actually pretty good and unique fighters.Super Gem Fighter Minimix : This is maybe the dumbest game ever made, but I found it so. much. fun. It looks like Street Fighter 2 for kids, but plays like something intended to be goofy and not serious in a very Japanesy way. I actually saw this in one NA arcade once, its a lot of fun.Mega Man The Power Battle & Megaman 2 The Power Fighters: I don't believe either one of these ever found their way to arcades outside of Japan. Its kind of what you would expect for a Megaman game adapted for the arcade; its just boss fights. Its not bad. I imagine it would have done well in NA if given the chance.All 3 Street Fighter Alphas : By the time these came out, Street Fighter 2 had played itself out so nobody was playing and NA arcade operators weren't very interested. Not much of a loss. 1 was very meh. 2 was better, but still meh. Then Capcom went overboard with Alpha 3. 3 is pretty good, but it was still a wash and hard to find in arcades.Hyper Street Fighter 2 Anniversary : Man, I forgot this existed. So do arcades. Literally a blink and you missed it arcade release. Sadly, the arcade scene in NA was simply dying at this point. This was Capcom's last CPS2 game.I think that's about it for this compilation. Both Capcom Stadiums depress me greatly reminding me of a much better time in my life when arcades existed, the games were awesome, and you could have a hell of a time on a few dollars. Its not like now where if you can even find an arcade, its like 2 lame 10 year old+ driving games and a bunch of garbage redemption/ticket games. The sadness I feel deepens just entering the fake arcades the Capcom Arcade Stadiums feature. These things.... They just don't really exist IRL anymore. :CThe other sad thing is you will NEVER see Capcom put out a compilation with their games featuring licensed properties. So no Willow, Aliens Vs Predator, Cadillacs and Dinosaurs, anything Marvel, no UN Squadron/Area 88. The D&D collection is still somehow available. You are also denied the best SF game of them all: Street Fighter: The Movie. These games are the best argument for MAME since some of these games are Capcom's best from a time they 100% knew WTF they were doing.

_childDocuments_.review: The game most likely will not run out of the box and you will get the "D3D fatal error" thing before it crashes during the start up. Tl;dr - you need to disable Steam Overlay for the first time running and other intensive software, especially the ones that use a lot of full screen tricks because they will cause the fickle-af boot-up sequence to crash. For example, you can cause it to crash by closing Opera browser while it is starting.NOTE: These start-up crashes have nothing to do with display drivers and they are most likely caused by the non-secured and volatile way the program loads data during the start-up process. It is most likely that the loader fails by software issues and that causes the D3D initialization part fail when the whole program crashes underneath it. It is about loading and saves. If other software writes or reads the disk hard during the loading sequence, the game will crash with a high probability. It is extremely shoddy programming.Another thing is that it creates the initial settings file only after starting up and it starts you with a high resolution borderless window and high detail settings that you most likely want to change for extra stability.The only thing I can recommend this product for is playing that free SONSON game while using Rewind - it is a difficult game. Other games such as the Street Fighter II and such games are notoriously censored, making them the worst iterations of those games and not worth the money.If they fixed the start-up issues and uncensor the games they are asking money for, I might consider giving this one a recommendation. Before that happens, Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium will act as a proof for why being a paid customer gets you screwed over with certain publishers and how you should stop buying until they prioritize an authentic game experience over irrational piracy control measures and social politics.EDIT: 1.I  did run "sfc /scannow" (in Win10 command prompt), though it most likely did nothing.2. The issues might be called the failed implementation of acquiring the system privileges for disk reading and writing. Some people have issues with fresh installs because the game creates a settings file only after successfully starting up. This issue is worsened by heavy disk-usage by other programs (or their parts such as Steam Overlay) that causes crashes during even later start-up sequences.The start-up problems could be made worse by installing the game onto a non-OS disk drive (OS drive = Windows is installed on it) i.e. usually other than C: on Windows systems. That is because when you install onto a non-system drive with possibly different hardware, that can cause delays that that time out and crash the Capcom Arcade 2nd Stadium process. That is what happens when you do not make your program resilient the volatility of resource management.
