_childDocuments_.review: I was enjoying this. The backtracking to hunt down places to "remember" the lore of items was a nice bit of progression and fun... to a point. There is no fast travel, just some reasonably speedy elevators that aren't very convenient, and you can set a "home" beacon to travel *back* to, which is far from convenient. This turns backtracking into a commute and a chore.The point where the game broke me was when I discovered there was a max level of 99. And not much respec.I was hoping for a game where, as I played, I'd be making the world feel more alive, and less pixel-rotted... and... that's not really what you get.While the max level and "Oh no, I broke my character?" made me stop for a day, and locate a workaround... I don't think I'm going to use it. I just... everything about this game just feels like it will only get worse and less interesting, not more.I saw the sword from Transistor, and realized how many things were just... references to gaming culture that didn't have anything to say about them. The lore didn't seem to be going anywhere or painting an interesting tapestry... just...When telling a story, one sets expectations, makes promises to the audience, and keep them. This isn't promising much. There's no sense of a cohesive narrative that's going to explain Sonic's shoes and rings fitting in with Link's shield. And if you need it to unlock the lore on your equipment, it's not an easter egg, that's part of the world. It's just... not doing anything interesting with the premise, the setting, the mechanics...And I picked up *all* the Yakuza games on GOG for, like, $35. It's not fair to compare an indie title to that franchise, but it *is* competing for my free time, and I *did* give this my money and a chance... and it just didn't mesh.Kudos tho to some excellence in game design:Elevators that move swiftly, and near-instantly if you're not on them. Respects the player's time.Clues for unlocking rememberances indicate if you've been to the right zone, if you have the abilities you need to access the right part of the level... that's a decent way to keep players from getting overwhelmed with the search.The Consumer boss's dancing combat animations are a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ treat. And as someone who danced in younger days, it really does telegraph the next attack sequence pretty well.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply Soulslike.Combat wise very similar to Dark Souls series.Thematically it's a world that is gamefied in terms how that universe works and gone horribly wrong because of heroes not wanting to sacrifice themselves anymore, and you're there to fix it or perhaps not.Most areas are based on other games or well known franchises. The same goes for loot.An example of loot inspirations: Thief (Garrett), Halo (Chief), Horizon Zero Dawn (Aloy), Zelda (Link), Disney (Scrooge McDuck), FF7 (Cloud). Has loads of inspirations from soulsborne games too.Also don't forget about the snarky narrator who belittles you, hinders you, or helps you and then regrets few seconds later, and goes back to what worked best.There are few npcs questlines, and they can be missed, and killing one npc can end other npcs questlines too, or you can miss them literally by going to a boss too fast and you'll actually end up glitching the npcs, so you can't interact with them at all.Though mind that, you can get only 1 end achievement per character, but you can still continue on playing in that world and see the other end that's available, though you can easily save edit it.There is sadly no way to reset your stats at the moment, also no new game plus.But because the savedata is so easy to edit, you can do it yourself for both.Reset storylines, unkill npcs, get duplicate weapons or armor pieces (armor though can get buggy when one set is remembered and the is unburdened), reset all the loot that can be picked up, reset scripts, reset boss fights, change stats, or change level to keep on leveling even if the normal limit is only lvl 99.I basically made my own ng+, after missing almost all npc questlines, and remembering almost all items, missed all the secret places, and seeing two basic endings, sit on the throne and/or sacrifice yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could, I would rate it as mid, but I have to chose so negative I guess, it's not that bad but it is pretty boring and repetitive, they did the whole DS1 thing where you can't teleport to bonfires so you will spend a LOT of time walking, speaking of walking, they for some reason chose to make your run pressing down the L stick? I know there is an option to toggle run but most players won't see it and spending 30 mins with your thumb mashing into your stick is painful. Next the enemies, I wouldn't really call them hard, more so annoying, especially the ranged ones, there are (imo) Four difficult (non-boss) enemies : The werewolves,  the knight that commands the cobold(?) miners, the teleporting shadow monsters in the ending/tutorial section, and the bucket head with the spear specifically (for some reason the hit detection on his attacks starts BEFORE he actually does his attack animation).Next onto the main reason anyone plays souls-likes, the bosses, frankly, they are BAD, the most difficult boss in the game is THE FIRST ONE(the grinder), yes even more difficult than the final boss, for some reason they gave him three phases, which would't be a problem tbh if like 12 enemies didn't also spawn in the third phase. Apart from that one you will die for sure like 2~4 times on every other boss, you are far more likely to die to a regular monster on your way to the boss, than to the actual boss. Next the worst thing about this game, the level design, idk who they hired to do this but they ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up, never mind the countless texturing/OOB glitches, there are several areas where you clearly should be able to get through, but you can't, an entire area that's pitch black (you can light it if you have the torch, but I finished the game and never found a torch lol), there is also another area of low visibility (the wilds), where you have to light four beacons to progress (basically Farron keep from DS3) EXCEPT that to reach beacon two you NEED to light beacon one first, otherwise there is a mist that insta-kills you, this entire are is also littered with the most annoying enemies in the game, goblins that run away, attack from range and shape shift into random objects, and skeletons, soooo many skeletons. Speaking of enemies being annoying, they will follow you to the ends of the earth and their hitbox is often bigger than it seams, so they WILL block your path in the many narrow areas withing the game.Then we have the reward for all the adventuring and killing: the itemsthere are many, but few are actually useful, I completed the entire game with the starter shield and I never had enough magic stats to use anything other than the basic throwing star, so I didn't, I played this game as a melee fighter and that was the only ranged thing I used and in my experience using it, I would say actually trying to play this game as a ranged focused character (which btw is magic ONLY, lol no physical bows or anything) would be terrible. The lock-on in this game is ♥♥♥♥ and you will often be faced with multiple enemies and many enemies that run away, and in that case you will hit where they were before instead of your attacks tracking them. Another thing with the items this game introduces, the remembering mechanic, my advice, don't bother. The effort required to find the correct place based on a vague hint is not worth the small stat boost and special skills(which you will never use because they are ♥♥♥♥), you will also often need to pay to actually get this and souls in this game are hard to come by as it is. Later on in the game you unlock the ability to "unburden" items, which gives you the extra stats, but no abilities or cool flavor text in the description, but its free and you don't have to spend hours looking for a specific place. I finished the game having used a total of three main weapons, the starter sword, a dagger, and another dagger, so for me remembering items was mostly a waste of time and souls that I could have used elsewhere.Now, The One thing I hate about this game the most. THAT quest, if you played the game you KNOW which one, basically a character tells you to give an item to another character and if you don't do it before advancing to the next area, whelp they just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ DIE. ALSO REMEMBER WHEN I SAID YOU CAN'T TELEPORT, WELL THE DISTANCE YOU NEED TO WALK IS NOT AT ALL INSIGNIFICANT, IN FACT IT'S QUITE LONG, SO YOU WILL DO ALLLL THAT AND THEN, YOU LEARN THERE'S ANOTHER CHARACTER WHO WANTS YOU TO GIVE ANOTHER ITEM, TO THAT EXACT SAME CHARACTER, AND YOU WILL HAVE TO WALK, AGAIN, FOR LIKE THIRTY MINUTES. OH MY GOD.  I skipped this and got shamed by an npc for doing so but I am not doing all that, thank you very much. 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's OK. An in the middle, competent souls-alike with an interesting setting and story that's good for about 3/4 of the game but really drops the ball in it's latter stages.It's issues do appear way before the disappointing end sections with the lock on function that sometimes doesn't quite work or refuses to select targets close to you when approached by multiple enemies, wonky AI pathfinding that frequently catches itself on scenery and walls, and regular enemies with fast combo attacks that tend to power through your own attacks. Sometimes I wonder if enemies even have their own stamina pools as they can let off a series of attacks with very little cooldown in between (the werewolf is an example of this and one of the most frustrating enemies to fight in this game).Other issues I encountered is a lack of proper fast travel until very late in the game and an increasingly interconnected and confusing level design as you progress through the story that can leave you running around areas for ages trying to remember where a particular shortcut is and where it leads. There is no map and very little in the way of signposts.Despite that I did enjoy myself for most of the game. The game starts to creak a bit when you get up to the Moat of the Stolen Crown where you are forced to traverse down a path littered with many (breakable) objects and lots of werewolves (that often get stuck on said objects). It was alright again until you get up to Start of Sequence where the game devolves into traversing through long sections of very tough enemies and deadly narrow pathways above endless voids. It doesn't get better afterwards.

No complaints there.)- Some pretty strict quests that are easily missable (which might be by choice since they tend to be sensitive in other souls games too)

_childDocuments_.review: Its a pretty decent take on the Souls like genre. Its handled in a pretty clever way and its a really nice touch.I havn't found any bugs or glitches and the AI is pretty well done. The combat is smooth and responsive but also your making deliberate choices within its framework.The voice acting is decent enough but the actual dialogue was rather grating and i didn't find the humor hitting any notes.The story was rather forgetful and i was not impacted by it. Which is unfortunate because it really could have done something special.The level design is pretty good and getting around was easy enough to figure out. But there were moments where i found myself wandering aimlessly.Other than the art direction your basically playing Dark Souls 1.There's not a whole lot to say about the game as its not terribly unique.But if you like the genre, then this will probably be right up your alley.Overall, it is a good game and is fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so since the humor is so hit and miss for so many people, I'm just going to elect to ignore it as far as my review goes.  Combat in the game is pretty much your standard affair for a souls-like.  Which is to say that it is good.  I did have problems with hitting targets when not locked on, but for the most part, it was fun exactly as fun as you'd expect.  But holy hell, the interconnectivity of the world is insane.  It feels like you can get anywhere from anywhere else pretty fast with how many different ways the world loops back in on itself, and that's awesome.  That little dopamine rush of opening a door and seeing a location you've previously been happens a lot.  But what I think is the most outstanding thing about the game is the remembrance system.  All weapons and armor  you get comes in this low res version.  And there is lore on these items, like most souls games, but it's even more important.  That gear needs to have it's memories restored, and you're given hints on where you need to do this.  Even at bonfires, it'll give you an indication on how many items can be remembered in the area.  Restoring the memory of a weapon or armor set not only upgrades it to a higher res graphics style, but you get tangible increases to the weapons and armor sets stats.  And on top of that, the game will track AND reward you for the total of items remembered, which is super ♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool.  I feel like the game's worth trying just for this mechanic alone.  But yeah, for at least me, the humor was either good, or just kind of whatever.  But like I said, not judging the game on that.  I do think Souls fans should give this a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty well-polished. Most of the time it glitches it's intentional, as it plays a lot on the meta idea of players transcending the confines of their design. It's a decent game and I'm glad I played it. That said, the only thing that holds this game back from being great is the pacing, so I'm going to detail my gripes with it to help you determine whether you're willing to put up with them or not. The game is funny, has a lot of references to random video games, and is an overall fun experience, but you have to take the good with the bad if you want to have a good time with it.This game's map is pretty huge to the point that it kept going even when I thought it would end. And then it kept going and going and I asked myself, "why?" The game just kinda flattens out at the climax, drawing out the suspense for seemingly no reason. At least this comes from me only paying loose attention to the lore. So the middle and end portions of the game were slow in terms of pacing. What made the middle section slow was the limited fast travel system. You can basically set a "tether" checkpoint on any 'bonfire' you visit, but can only ever have one active at a time. This game has such a huge number of shortcuts and branching paths that my attention span and memory were constantly at maximum capacity trying to figure out where everything was. Remember, you can only ever have one tether active at a time, so you'll be doing a lot of backtracking. Putting the game down for a few days and then coming back to it would be fine, only until I had to backtrack for whatever reason.. As for myself I kept forgetting where all the shortcuts were to the point I had to go through three entire areas on foot just to find the place/thing I was trying to find.If you have a great memory or take notes on the Steam overlay you probably won't have as much of a problem going from place to place like I did. Even if everything went smoothly for you though there are many drawn-out sections that could be a lot more impactful  if they were shorter. This game is very DS1-like in its backtracking, but with a very limited fast travel mechanic. If you can get past possibly getting lost or forgetting that one out of a hundred shortcut that saves you twenty minutes of time, you'll have a blast with this game. This game is a rough gem that most souls-like fans will enjoy so long as they understand what they're getting into.Also, idk if it was intentional, but I love how one of the bosses makes fun of how ridiculous the Elden Ring boss wind-ups are.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall i would rate this game 6 elden rings out of 10.Usually roguelikes try to bring their own ideas into the genre, leaving the core untouched. This is not about this game, the developers tried to copy Miyazaki as much as possible(the game has a canonical level and quest design). With only one their own idea -  remembering. Almost all objects store memories of themselves in special places, and when you go there, the object remembers its past and has better stats and new skills. This turned out very well.There are few unique movesets\enemies in the game and they are poorly designed, often you will wait for a certain attack from the enemy and only then hit (hello werewolves) or you will often meet the same enemies only in recolor (less often in different skin) and with more hp. In the late game, enemies have problems with hitboxes, especially when it comes to parries.

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful adventure, lovingly-crafted by people who appreciate the good ol days of gaming, and understand how to weave a troubling but humorous tale.It's a little rough around the edges, sometimes intended, others not (less than 4 game-breaking issues in my entire playthrough - restarting fixed with no game loss).  Combat is basic but souls-ish, although the stagger-on-hit can be frustrating at first.The ingenuity of finding items, reading clues, and fully unlocking the items is tops.  It makes every weapon interesting, even if you never plan to use it in combat, and every piece of armor tell a story, even if you never plan to wear it.It nails the souls formula, right down to the frustrating "swamp" (forest in this case) section, but push through dear gamers, the second half of this game is full of fun and even cooler items!  solid 8/10, even at the very reasonable full price this is worth your time!

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool game! It starts off kind of rough because the game can feel a lot like the 2014 Lords of the Fallen where you get hit and are stunlocked into the next week, but once you get some levels, armors, and just general acquaintance with game feel it gets real fun. The "remember" system is also incredibly cool! Really enjoyed it! My biggest complaint is that the game is no very funny, it ends up being more reference heavy than parody. Like seeing sonic's shoes and the Green Hills Zone in the distance isn't funny, nor is trains, cows and dumb narrators. I do love the premise, where you are a corrupted play character returning to a soulslike game world that the players had ruined for the npcs with their greed and the world is slowly regressing back into a pixelated soup, but I would rather have had a story focusing on that with more original content with the occasional wink or nod towards something cool rather than just straight up having the master sword or buster sword. Oh well, definitely fun! Hope the studio makes another!

_childDocuments_.review: It's an exceptional "dark souls 1 - like" for the first 8 hours.Then the quality nosedives really hard, throwing good level design and balanced enemy placement out of the window. I could not finish it because of this.It's got some unique ideas and systems that improve on the framework of a souls like.Combat is solid, very methodical, so don't expect it to be as fluid DS3 or elden ring. But all enemies (except in late game) have clear telegraphs.Memory system is a good way to engage with the world, making you soak up the details. I just wish I could filter the inventory in some way so I could quickly see undiscovered items.Nitpick would be the accesibility of some important npc's. The world is really well interconected, but without teleporting it's not fun if you have to make a long run just to get to the shop or a forge.

_childDocuments_.review: You know, I have been searching for a game like this for a long time. I just finished the base game, and it was a fantastic experience. While the leveling system is much like games such as Dark Souls and Elden Ring, the new stats that were introduced make it feel like its own game.  The remembering mechanic is fantastic, and the weapon variety is nice. Overall, a great game. 10/10Edit:After 75 more hours, I cannot recommend this game enough. The Devs clearly put a lot of time into this, and no amount of raving can convey the message of "Go play this game right now!" enough.Edit 2: So, I bought the DLC, and I'm putting that review into this one because I can't figure out how to put it into the DLC's store page. Anyway, the DLC is great! It allows people who have completed the game more than a few times to experience something new, while not intruding on the base game at all. In fact, I think that the time when the DLC is introduced is placed specifically as to prevent characters from becoming too strong for the base game because of it.  There were a few glitches, but I hope that they will be patched out soon, and the rest of it is so good that I barely even noticed these minor bugs. It also has a fantastic final boss, which can unfortunately only be accessed if you complete the Innocent's questline first. The other two bosses were good, but the real standout fight is definitely the ending fight. Overall, absolutely a recommend for anyone who already owns TLHoN, but I wouldn't buy the base game because of this DLC. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: (game not completed at 30 minutes and refund requested) (short version) I can see why the reviews are mixed, I was waiting with baited breath to play this game and was extremely excited to buy and play it.  Unfortunately upon playing the irritation of unpredictable hit boxes, no iframes after damage, and the ability for basic enemies to stagger/chain kill you in 4 hits was my quit moment.  I enjoy a souls like game however this is not the one for me.(long version)Too many unpolished issues. I don't want to say the game is too difficult because I've played and have beaten several souls like games already. The major issue that I can see that will get worse is the staggering hits that can be chained with no iframes to make a recovery. _childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: A fun Dark Souls clone, with some weird game design choices and a confusing world.The game plays exactly like Dark Souls. Specifically, the janky original one with questionable hitboxes. Expect to grit your teeth as your toothpick weapon misses a stick figure by a pixel, which causes your death by a clobbering. That was quite common, playing a dexterity build.Once you get used to this, the game flows well, and starts strongly. The world is pretty cool - the references, though mostly low-hanging fruit (Master Chef, huh duh), are actually pretty funny in places, and the mix of pixel and realistic is done well. The sound design is decent and the music is alright.However, there' are a few things that bothered me greatly.- The bosses were fairly mundane (well, the ones I could fight, more on that in a sec). None were very challenging and were mostly just people. No dragons or giant monsters or anything.- The world was confusing to navigate. Dark Souls does a fantastic job of cyclical level design, i.e., opening shortcuts to connect the world together. Nostalgaia does this to an extreme level, to the point where the world feels like a maze more than a set of paths. As a result, I got lost frequently.- Limited warping. The tethers (read: bonfires) in this game can be set and warped to. However, you can only do one at a time. For example, I set a tether at the village, then wander off to the forest. If I rest at a tether, I can then warp back to the village, but I cannot warp back to the forest!Why the developers thought this was a good idea is beyond me, especially when the item remembering (which is an excellent idea) promotes backtracking. There are plenty of weapons/armours which I realised where to remember them, but didn't bother because it'd be a 5-minute walk in the wrong direction. Silly.- MISSABLE BOSSES. This one is particularly stupid, especially in 2023 when we have decades of game design telling us this is a terrible idea. Some bosses are locked behind a particular sidequest that you can miss if you don't pay attention and backtrack when needed. If you do miss it, you don't get to do the full ending, period. This includes a boss in the DLC - you won't be allowed to fight it if you haven't done this missable sidequest.Despite these frustrating design decisions, I can say I enjoyed my time in Nostalgaia. Hopefully, the devs take feedback to heart and think about what would make the game/future games more enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game with a friend in 11 hours.Both our thoughts were that it's very janky in some spots, but overall it's pretty damn great.Fun combat, clever world that links together in a nice way, lots of diversity in the environments. The skills have been streamlined from something like dark souls, but there's a lot of different build variety. There's also a ton of secrets and areas to find. The game really can be janky in certain spots. Poor hitboxes, poor attack telegraphing, annoying difficulty spikes in certain areas that are only made worse by jank. I'm not downplaying the jank, I just don't think it sours the whole game.It's been a long time since I've bought a game and smashed through it in a few sessions, so I'd heartily recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: As many have said before me, Last Hero of Nostalgaia is a satirical spin on the soulslike genre that introduces unique mechanics while building on what makes the genre so popular in the first place. However, there are things that I’ve seen that have somewhat soured my positive experience.✅  The Narrator is a great part of the game, and I found myself chuckling at whatever he threw at me. Whether it was random events to hinder my progression or him just sh*tting on me constantly, it was always a welcome addition to my playthrough.✅  The world is bleak. Even though the game is satirical and doesn’t take itself seriously a lot of the time, it’s very apparent that those who live in Nostalgaia have either gone insane or are pixelated chunks of depravity. As I was walking through Nostalgaia, I found myself wanting to save it even more.✅  The remembrance mechanic is the most unique take on weapons in a soulslike game I’ve seen. Solving riddles and finding where you need to go to make your weapon better is a breath of fresh air from the typical upgrade system that you see a lot in other games.✅  There are many unique characters that add to the lore of the world. I can’t add much to this as I could give out major or minor spoilers.✅  I did not expect this game to have voice acting, let alone great voice acting. ✅  I’m a huge fan of the original Dark Souls, and the combat in this game fits that to a T. However, I understand that there may be some people who don’t find that style of combat fun.❌  I have no knowledge when it comes to actually programming and creating a game, so I do not know whether it’d be incredibly hard to add a NG+. This won’t be one of my major issues, but I feel as if the addition of a NG+ would encourage me to play the game more.❌  Not all of the NPC questlines are convoluted, but some questlines will really, really, really test you. ❌  I started the game as a STR-based character and then switched to a DEX-based character as none of the weapons felt as if they had weight to them. Some weapons swing slower, but none of the "heavy" weapons felt heavy at all.❌  There are many moments in the game that make you feel really good about finding a shortcut to a tether, but I noticed a lot of shortcuts that either didn’t need to be there or led to a tether incredibly far away from where you were heading. I didn’t find myself creating a map in my head that would easily help me understand what shortcuts would get me where I needed to go.The Last Hero of Nostalgaia has satiated my hunger for soulslikes. It’s fresh, it’s challenging, and it’s unique. I recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of my favourite games of all time. I thought it was going to be a funny joke souls-borne game, but it kinda surprised me for how good it actually was!The controls felt pretty smooth unlike some of the other souls-borne games that feel a little janky, the remembering system is very unique, I liked the way they set an atmosphere for each area that I went to, I loved the subtle references from different series throughout the game, good humour, the bosses were fun as well as being very challenging, there is so much to explore, a great story with unpredictable outcomes, and the soundtracks were a bop. But, there were some issues as well.The game was a little buggy, like I sometimes get stuck on stuff and I can't move, then I get absolutely destroyed by multiple enemies at once. Or when I go to climb down a latter I would get stuck in a running animation and I had to restart the game. I also did not like how you couldn't fast travel to different areas of the map which was a little frustrating, since the map is so huge, especially when I had to backtrack to restore the memory of items. Although, the game did give you a bunch of shortcuts to get to certain places so it'll get deducted half a point. After a certain point, I felt like the bosses were getting easier where I was getting them on my first or second try, which kinda took the fun out of it, or maybe I just got gud. Also, uhh. Unbreachable Maw and Lair of the Adversary.. We do not talk about that part of the game... Ong, I was about to lose my mind venturing through those areas.Other than that, I'd give the game a solid rating of 7.5/10. If you wanna become Samus, while holding a light sabre in the right hand and the Hylian Shield in the left, then I absolutely recommend you to play it yourself! 👍

_childDocuments_.review: is a brief, charming, and challenging romp through a Souls-like adventure that pays homage to everything from Super Mario to Soul Calibur. I've played video games as an enthusiast since I was three years old, and making my way through Nostalgaia simultaneously spoke to the wonderstruck child in me and engaged the experienced adult that most games nowadays fail to grab. has nearly everything great about the first three Souls games. The only thing I truly notice missing is being able to roll from knockdown, which was added in Dark Souls 3 and was one of my favorite additions to combat, but only as a sort of icing on the cake. TLHoN still has the rest of the cake, and it's just as delicious, if not even  delicious, than it ever was when playing Dark Souls 1 and 2. The main thing to watch out for is how a group of enemies can dogpile you and stunlock you from full HP to death if you're not careful, but - barring only one exception with a Heavy Knight that I can think of - it's the classic "If you died, it's because  made a mistake that Souls games are known for. Nostalgaia carries that forward by having an excellent enemy variety, each with a reasonable moveset that you can memorize after only a couple of encounters.But talking about the combat is only to guarantee you, new player or Souls-like veteran, that it  fun to play. As far as  it would be unfair of me to call TLHoN anything short of masterful, even in its brevity. Yes, brevity, TLHoN is not a long game, but it truly doesn't need to be.  is the standout feature of the game, and, if you pay attention, it can make the game's somewhat short length feel historically long, as you piece together everything that led up to the classic, Souls-like "dying world" that you inhabit. Remembering items manages to feed you everything from hilarity to sorrow, based around what happened to this item and its wielder. The items, along with the rest of the world of Nostalgaia, are truly  even after the person who wielded them is dead and gone, and it lends a refreshingly-unique sense of depth to the world, connecting you personally to even the weapons you wield, knowing that they - and, again, the world around you - will remember what you've done long after you're gone, too.If you're concerned about the "meta-humor" in this game, don't be. The references made and even the characters that are practically just name-swapped and copy-pasted into the lore are all tastefully done, and in such a manner that the history of video games entirely seems to seamlessly fit into the lore of this world as  video gaming. There was never a moment that an allusion to a well-known and established character felt like a cheap, wink-wink-nudge-nudge stealing of credit, but rather a respectful working-in of the legacy of characters and games into this game's world, which serves only to broaden it; never to denigrate either the source or how this game uses it.I deeply, strongly recommend The Last Hero of Nostalgaia, and, whereas I've seen some reviewers forget, I'd like to remind everyone: This is not a AAA title. This is a labor of love, and it does what it's trying to do very well. Don't go in expecting Dark Souls 4. If anything, go in expecting something more akin to TRON 2.0, which, for those who know it, is similarly steeped in a warm love for the material it's borrowing from.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm baffled.Who would've ever imagined a game with a DS1 gameplay, a Paper Mario-ish artstyle, a The Bard's Tale / Stanley Parable humour, tied together with a truck load of retro and not so retro gaming references. Turns out Over the Moon did, and it's a blessing.The references themselves were enough to keep me playing. I wondered if some games I grew up playing would eventually get their love in this game... and I kept being excited to see them appear. I mean, a Runescape ref ? Come on man OF COURSE I'm whipping out this bad boy.Now don't me wrong, this isn't a flawless game, but it's extremely refreshing. I was bewildered throughout my roughly 12 hour playthrough. Most journalistic reviews of the game already point out the flaws: some bugs here and there, the game is relatively short, the weapons aren't as varied as in Dark Souls... but I don't think this is what this game is about. It's fun, funny, and remarkably polished in the gameplay (except those overhead swings man come on I locked on the enemy don't make me miss).If you like Souls-like titles and humourous games, this game is definetely worth the try.Also Kirby butt.

_childDocuments_.review: Nostalgaia is a game that I don't know why is so much underrated, because it's actually good. Imagine Darks Souls with Stanley Parable and Devolver`s humor. It's literally how this game is. Gameplay and combat are pretty decent, the environment design is pretty cool. But my favorite thing about this game is the references about other games (you'll see). Multiplayer focuses on 2 player coop, so if you are interested, try to get a friend to play with you. Also it is crucial that you pay attention to the details of this game, like sidequests and npc conversations (if you have trouble knowing where to go, don't hesitate to look on the web about it, like Dark Souls, this game has a weird way to follow side quests that are utterly important to the game's story).7.0/10

_childDocuments_.review: A hidden gem. For any souls-like fan this game is a must play. The best piece of work that developers besides From Software were able to add to the genre. The world design and how all the places are connected to each other is simply astonishing. Gameplay wise it's very, very similar to Dark Souls 1, but thanks to its unusual premise and "Item Memory" mechanic The Last Hero of Nostalgaia really stands out as something unique. What a great surprise this game was. Great job developers, you really captured the essence of what makes Souls series so much fun and gave me exactly what I needed to quench my thirst for souls-like game. Can't wait for your next titles.

The balance for legit all of the spells felt off, the basic magic spell you start with just shafted legit everything else besides the spell that just held basic mobs in place.  The ammo cost for the spells was way too high for the damage or ability they do. and the 3rd boss i dont even remember and i finished the game today and i dont even remember who the third boss was or what she did.  all i know it was a girl in a dress.  and the boss after that the areas before him became so tedious and annoying, losing the merchant so no more buying upgrade materials, ammo, or anything else that you missed before he went rabid, Just became annoying and tedious. Overall im glad i played it would give it a 7/10 for these indie experimental souls games.TLDR, very tedious mid-late game but overall a good experience 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Nostalgaia was strangely compelling from start to finish. It shed new light on what I value in a soulslike by being weaker in some regards than other soulslikes that I haven’t finished, but still being one of the only non-From Soft soulslikes that I actually finished. Most surprisingly, I would say that the combat was competent, but not what hooked me, which is usually what I point to as the most important aspect of a soulslike for me. The combat has some fun twists which I appreciated, such as a more varied parry system that rewards the player differently based on how risky they choose to play, but ultimately the combat felt like something I was only engaging with to get to the rest of the game that I was actually enjoying.One of Nostalgaia’s biggest twists on soulslike combat was how it changed the luck stat, as it functionally adds a whole skill tree of random benefits that are unlocked as you level the skill, but the way this increased the dependence on luck sometimes left a sour taste in my mouth. Especially because they put caps on the benefits you can receive from luck in a way that prevents you from fully breaking it. For example, the game caps your crit chance (which is determined by the luck stat) at <50%, which led to many instances where I would die because I would fail to crit 4 or 5 times in a row, and my non-crit damage was insultingly low because I had dumped a majority of my levels into luck. This may feel like I’m asking the developer to save me from myself, and to a certain extent I am. The way luck works in Nostalgaia made me wonder if this sort of system isn’t in From Soft games because they recognized that it feels bad in a way that doesn’t jive with the intense difficulty.The actual combat encounters were also a weaker element of the game. The regular enemies were fine, but the bosses really showcased the weaknesses in the AI. Pretty much any enemy in Nostalgaia is easily cheesed one on one, they walk straight at you and attack in ways that have clear tells and openings for retaliation. Now, this is fine to a certain extent, and definitely preferable to completely unreadable and seemingly random behavior I’ve seen in much worse soulslikes; I absolutely would not have finished this game if that had been the case. However, the predictable and opening-laden animations did make for somewhat boring fights that I rarely needed to retry. (aside from failures caused by the aforementioned RNG woes)What kept me coming back to Nostalgaia was its charm. The somewhat jokey worldbuilding of a game which is degrading due to its playerbase (or lack thereof) is fun, but more importantly it is played straight and treated with import by the NPCs that live in the world. The references to other games are occasionally corny, but generally cute and take a backseat to the original worldbuilding and story being told. The mechanic of reuniting gear with its origin in the world to increase its power was a fun way to pace out the combat gauntlets to avoid them wearing out their welcome, and it was also a great way to showcase what is perhaps Nostalgaia’s greatest accomplishment: its world design.The world design is one area in which I think Nostalgaia matches From Software’s library. Nostalgaia demonstrates its confidence in its world from the get go by having very limited fast travel, while still encouraging a ton of backtracking. The world of Nostalgaia is demonstratively contiguous, with all the fun of the original Dark Souls or Elden Ring, where you can see some fantastical location out in the distance and watch as it gets closer until you find that you’ve reached it. It even has a similar vertical shape to the original Dark Souls which allows it to be chock full of shortcuts which tickle the brain every time you find one. The fast travel is largely unnecessary because by the end of the game you can travel between one end of the world and the other in a few minutes, despite the original trek taking hours.I was also fascinated by the art style of Nostalgaia; the intermingling of billboarded 2D pixel art and 3D models with varying levels of detail. It nailed the aesthetic of digital decay that the game was going for, and the game played with it in fun ways like having vampire enemies which start out 2D but upgrade to 3D models after successfully biting you. Unfortunately, the art style consistently left me wanting more; both the 2D and the 3D art felt very derivative and lacked a personality of its own aside from occasional bits of stand out character design and architecture. The combination of the styles still gave Nostalgaia a unique aesthetic that I won’t forget, but I still felt like it could have been taken further with component parts that were as original as the combination.Ultimately, the key reason I still recommend this somewhat mixed bag is its length. It took me about 15 hours and I was somewhat completionist in my wandering around the world. I did a fair amount of backtracking and exploration reuniting over 50 of the weapons and armor sets with their origins. (something you really only need to do with the specific armor and weapon you personally use) I would recommend it if a more abridged soulslike experience is something you would be interested in, and if combat isn’t your #1 priority for the genre. (although who knows, maybe — like me — you’ll be surprised to find it doesn’t bother you)

Another is the weird progression of difficulty, some areas I have been able to get by scott-free, but is then followed up by enemies that can 2 shot you at 1100+ health that have marginal windows to fight back.Another big problem is the seeming lack of NG+, unless I missed something that tells me about it, I can't find any option to move to NG+, which is a shame because I would love to play through it again.Though these issues don't stop me from having a great time playing it

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Dark Souls 1 despite it being a little clunky?Do you enjoy an interesting parody that is both funny and add it's own spin to things?Well then you should try this game.The style of transition from a stylistic 2d pixel art to full 3d models is pretty well executed and unique.I'm sure something like it has been done before, but definitely not like this game.I won't go too in depth here as I'm writing this for the steam awards. But I've already dropped 10 hours into this game and I am loving every moment spent.There's even 2 player coop with a bit of a twist. Instead of being able to send in your friend an unlimited number of times off to their death and then constantly resummoning them or relying on them to dish out the damage.In TLHoN you have to actually participate in the battle, because if your friend dies, you also die.That's right, you don't share a healthpool but your lives are tied together once you team up.But hey, on the plus side, you can also progress together.I personally recommend this game.If you need another Souls-like in your life while you wait for the next Elden-Souls-Borne, this game will help hold you over till then.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: I am sorry, we are sorry.I played the whole game with my girlfriend and it was a BLAST, the game is fantastic, the level design is super cool and enemies and bosses are well balanced as in a classic soul game, we loved every hour trying to search around the maps killing enemies, farming souls and unlocking secrets, until...The game just keeps losing everything, from a certain point the narrator won't be so present as in the first part of the game and suddenly everything just becomes empty and easy, the whole last level is just a bunch of cool rooms with one type of enemy .The last part seems finished in one day, unpolished and empty spaces that left us completely dead inside since we really loved all of the game and I feel cheated, I undestand the small studio and I appreciate the whole effort because for a good 80% the game is really cool but since it is not so long (we passed a lot of time searching for every passage) an ending like this is just sad.I recommend the game for 3/4 of it, but it is like the best party of your life and when you are on the edge to kiss your crush you puke and pass out.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If there was a mixed rating I could give this game, I would. While I enjoyed the experience, your mileage will vary based on knowledge of video games and how much you like Souls-like games. There are better Souls-like games mechanically and narratively, but for $25, it's a worthwhile adventure that does what it sets out to do.GOOD- Story: A meta story about video games, the characters, and, in directly, the players who play them. While goofy and referential, it's a sincere story with surprisingly serious discussion of themes like destiny vs free will, class dynamics, and if the ends justify the means,-Unique Puzzle Mechanic: Like every souls game, much of the lore/story of the game is conveyed in the environment and items. In this game, the equipment you pick up has lingering memories of their previous owners and each one has a hint for you to unlock the lore and full potential of the weapon. Its an interesting way to get the player to care about the item and the world as each weapon is functionally a character. Plus, you get passive, character-affecting bonuses for helping the weapons remember.- Good atmosphere and aesthetics: One of the conventions of a "Souls-Like" is a world in decay and this game sells that aesthetic pretty well. You will encounter destroyed towns with ominous writing in blood, poisonous forest with demon ritual taking place, and dark dungeons with pained screaming periodically playing in the ground. The game does enough to sell the seriousness of the environment while making it very obvious that these are cliches.  BAD- Gameplay feels like a derivative of Dark Souls. Attacking and dodging feels sluggish. Despite having different weapons from different games, every weapon feels exactly the same. Weapon Skills are minimal and ineffective. For example, swords and great swords get an AOE spin attack that does less damage than a light attack, longer recovery than a heavy attack, resource dependent, and does not stagger enemies on hit. With the exception of Luck, you offensive stats (Strength, Dexterity, and Source/Magic) don't offer any variety in benefits. This has resulted in just taking a random sword and just light attacking my way to victory. In a post-Elden Ring world, its difficult to look past an RPG of this kind lacking build diversity.-Unpolished: Crits causes the game to occasionally drop to 0 frames, textures and the skybox will start to flash singular colors, enemies will get caught on stairs and door frames while allies will T-pose during boss battles with multiples phases and levels.-Navigation: The game has a fast travel system and an abundance of short cuts. You can set one beacon (the game's bonfire/resting spot) as your headquarters, allowing you to teleport back to that spot from any other beacon in the world. Some items have you going to the other end of the world to unlock their memory and this system makes engaging with the memory mechanic more tedious and unenjoyable than it has to be. I feel like the better idea would have been to make all beacons a fast travel point.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Hero of Nostalgaia is a perfect mix of met gaming industry humor, and challenging souls-like combat. The story is fun-loving and offers a great twist to the "main character" trope, starting with an amazing character customization. TLHON brings a terrific new system to the game as well with their remembrances. A large portion of the shields, weapons, and armor come with a scavenger hunt-esque riddles that points you to a location in a specific area of the world. When you find the location, you can "remember" said item, boosting its stats and potentially unlocking hidden abilities. It's incredibly clever, and leads to an attention to detail while you make your way through the areas. Not to mention that a large majority of the items are subtle and not-so-subtle references to many other beloved games.There are two major flaws with the game that are big enough to warrant mentioning - however, I would not be surprised if they are addressed and fixed with time, given the responsiveness of the developers in the discussions for the game. I will list them in order of most-frustrating to least.First, there are a handful of NPCs in the area that each have optional quests throughout the game. Some of these quest-lines are tied together, so if you miss the beginning of one and beat an area boss, that quest-line and any subsequent quest-lines (to my knowledge is all of them minus two) are now locked from being completed.Second, the quests above give rewards to the player - runes, equipment, etc. There are two paths you can take to side with certain NPCs. Either one you choose, it locks you out from receiving the other quest rewards, and therefore locks you out of completing either the Collect All Armor, or Collect All Runes achievements in the same run. I believe that can be solved by implementing a NewGame+ mode that allows you to keep what you have collected, and finished the achievements with one character.As a third non-major issue I personally had with the game, I did not like the Tethering system with the beacons. Being able to only teleport to one location led me to a LOT of time backtracking to remember certain items. Even though the world is very well connected and there are a lot of shortcuts, I found it to be a little too time consuming to be fully enjoyable. I understand the Devs have mentioned that that was a key design that they chose instead of being allowed to teleport to any lit beacon, but in practice it was not enjoyable.Overall, I would 100% recommend The Last Hero of Nostalgaia. Whether you are a fan of souls-likes or not, it is a fun, yet semi-complex game that has captured my attention and become all I could think about in the week that the game has been out. After three completed play-throughs, have a large majority of the achievements as well, but need to step away until either the above issues are handled, or a comprehensive guide is created by some Hero.I look forward to returning to this game in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun. I was hoping I would like it after seeing the first trailer and playing the demo. And my hope was not without merit. I've been playing for a bit now and I'm only about halfway through. There's so much to explore; items to find and lore to discover. I love the sarcastic narrator, the various NPCs and their quests, and the creepy atmosphere in some parts of the game. Besides the bosses, a lot of the other enemies have some interesting fight mechanics that are fun to figure out. The game is punishing but fair; there were a couple of times I died and lost over 20,000 memory, but after a bit of grinding I was able to get it all back and level up. If you're worried about difficulty, play as the mage/sorcerer class and that helps ease the difficulty as you can fight a lot of the enemies from afar. Overall, solid 10/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fantastic. The story is relayed very well through environmental storytelling and the Remember weapon texts. There are several side quests int he forms of Remembering weapons as well actual NPC based sides. its also chock full of references to various adventure / RPG titles, but not in a "HAH HAH HERE IS A REFERENCE" but woven into the backstory in meaningful ways. The combat is very dark souls III as opposed to Elden Ring. the magic system could user a few more spells. there are plenty of armor sets and the weigth PERCENTAGE versus weight NUMBER makes mixing and matching much easier to math out.TL:DRThis is a fantastic, solid, charming indie soulsike with great writing and solid combat. Defnitely a recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Due to the $25 price-tag, I would recommend.  TL:DR; There is a lot of good quality and witty things about this game. There is also an equal amount of frustration and disappointment in the design. Examples of those decision. Cap player level at 99, with such a low level cap, you barely get to put points into any stat. On top of that the stats scale slowly so adding points barely helps in progression. The remembrance system is really cool, but also super tedious, and necessary to your own progression (To improve upon the system, I would have had an aura glow around the character when an item is ready to "remember"). To make things fun, they should have had the tether points unlock, so then it wouldn't be as tedious to go to back to places for the remembrance system. Yes towards the end of the game the whole map tends to "connect", it's still an assload of walking and fighting. On top of that there is no newgame+, so there is no second play through you can do to go back through the game with the item already in hand for remembrance.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game! This is not your ordinary souls-like rip off. The controls feel great, which is not something that can be said for a lot of these type of games. There are a few hit-box issues with certain move-sets but the devs are aware and working on it, so hopefully once that is fixed that'll feel great.The story is packed full of funny one liners and references. I tried to keep a notepad with all of the references I was spotting but I gave up counting when the references started piling in at above 20 different games.One mechanic that I really like is the relic memories. Each relic (weapon, shield, armour, etc) has a memory tied to it. If you read the lore of the relic it will give you a clue of a location that the relic is tied to and if you find this location you can "remember" and the relic will tell you about its owner. There is lots of really fun and cool references and story bits in this. I really like how this encourages exploration and it adds a bit of a puzzle element to the game. This is a must have for anyone who has been into gaming for a while. If you are not a souls fanatic, don't worry because it isn't as difficult as the souls game but you still get that great souls feeling from it. Strongly recommend.Edit: nominating this game for best story-rich game!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really good humorous take on the Souls series. I would say that there are definitely glaring flaws, especially after the first major story thread (this involves the King), as the game just turns into an unfun frustration at that point, and you can kind of see that part of the game is also just really really rushed.There are also some very frustrating bugs, like interaction with objects not registering, or just hit-regs on enemies in general -  but they'll be ironed out I'm sure.Another thing I kind of had issue with is getting around in the world. I get that they wanted to try out a massively connected world, but it gets very frustrating trying to go to the right place, especially when there's no indicators of what area you're going to when you're taking a shortcut. You can't fast travel between the beacons (bonfires) btw, only to a point that you've "tethered" to, which is kind of pointless when you get items that take you to a last rested point anyway. (I get that it's for backtracking, but in a first play session you don't know when you need to backtrack)But the game is still good! Tight ass controls, the lore system and unlocking powers from "remembering" weapons is super cool and interesting, the storytelling is funny etc etc. So I'd still recommend it if you can ignore the flaws mentioned above.

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Hero of Nostalgaia is an amazing souls like that feels like The Stanley Parable Narrator got bored and decided to vacation in Lordran needless to say this amazing combination has both entertained and challenged me. Without spoiling to much, the game has lovable references and mechanics with an interesting lore under its surface and for the most part it all feels very much alive. My only fumble thus far has been that I could not name my character HelioBlade because of Hel being in the name, so I instead took inspiration from the game and named my character "Hack_and_/" this game deserves a glowing 1000/10 rating I wish I could rate this higher than steam would allow.

_childDocuments_.review: All I can say is WOW! I played Elden Ring when it came out, and it got me to start playing every Souls-Like I could find. Recently stumbled on this due to NerdNest on Youtube (Great channel by the way for Steam Deck discussions) and at first I was like "No way." But after watching some video on it, and now playing around 3 hours of it, it is absolutely brilliant. I've only just reached the resting spot by the mines, but wanted to go ahead and review because I can tell this entire thing will be a masterpiece. I am playing on Steam Deck, and it runs flawlessly. I hope it gets the green check-mark before long. This game looks a bit weird at first site, but its a full fledged Dark Souls, with a comedic narrator. Give it a try!As for complaints... I have only one... The sprint button should be something else. On a controller its funky, but on Steam Deck its even more funky to reach up there and hold it down.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Hero of Nostalgaia

_childDocuments_.review:
Nostalgaia, the world of videogames, is collapsing backwards into a mysterious pixelation, with every particle of fidelity bleeding away. Oblivion seemingly awaits even our most cherished gaming memories. But as the lighting dims and frames diminish, with the world on the brink of extinction, hope emerges to fight back.

As the most hideous pixelated hero to ever spawn in Nostalgaia, you must fight through an army of its mindless inhabitants, while being jeered by a cynical narrator who despises your very existence.

The Last Hero of Nostalgaia is a satirical action-adventure, driven by a dark story, set in an incredibly rich and complex world.

Featuring hard but fair combat that fans of the genre will relish, along with full character customization, unique battle armor and engaging narrative mechanics rich in lore, The Last Hero of Nostalgaia's twisted and wicked tale is prepared to send you headfirst into almost certain death around its every vertex.

name: Choo-Choo Charles
detailed_description: Wishlist my multiplayer prison escape game! About the Game Charles is a bloodthirsty train, and you need to destroy him. Navigate a massive play area in your trusty old engine. These winding tracks are treacherous, so you'll need to plan each mission carefully. Be wary when traveling on foot, or switching the track's direction; Charles might be waiting for you. Upgrade your train to fit your needs. Go looting or complete missions to find 'Scraps', which can be used to turn your train into a death machine on wheels. Get help from the townspeople. Help out the settlers in return for high powered weapons, and other items vital to Charles' destruction. Fight Charles to the death . Complete the main questline, and summon Charles to a mortal duel. If you’ve gained enough strength, firepower, and skill, Charles may finally meet his match.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: games good but too short, wait for a saleI beat the game in less than 3 hours, and got all but 1 achievement in that time.It's a good game although the price is kinda steep how long it is. I get this game took a little over a year to make by a single guy so i'm not gonna over commit to making the price a key point here, but i would recommend getting this game on sale if you can.Bugs:so the only major bug i dealt with was opening my map and all of a sudden im in the middle of nowhere and my train is  still going, usually the train stops when you jump out, but i guess the code for that is a hollowed out cylinder around the train that you can jump over, somehow.This is also where i learned charles follows near the train and not the player, thats really the only reason i could live long enough to hunt down my own train and hop aboardthe second and least impactful bug was a lighting issue underneath the bridge you plant 8 explosives on, for some reason the second coming of christ was happening and i couldn't see where to plant the bomb without burning out my retinas.mechanics:there are plenty, most of which have already been shown off even in the trailers, but i want to put a pin in sneaking for a minute. It feels incredibly under-cooked, there's no exposed meter that you can use to know if the cultists can see you, they  just, see you. and since you never get a weapon that isn't connected to your train, you're better off making a b-line to whatever your objective was and run back to the train, and since they can easily corner you, you're more than likely going to die since there shotguns hurt, alot.I think the dev knew this since dying really isn't a punishment, that most scrap i've lost from dying is 3 and by the halfway point, i was basically loaded and my train fully upgraded.upgrading is very satifying, except maybe weapon damage, never really felt like i was doing anymore damage at level 1 than i was at level 10, but i can understand why, if maxed out damage did too much, the final boss would be a joke, which is kinda funny since its a meme game with a slenderman mission. all-in-all tho, the upgrading felt good, especially speed, you're zooming by level 4Speaking of weapons, the only ones I ended up using, at least in the final boss section was flamethrower and rocket, one to slow, one to damage, works great. u just gotta be quick to switch them out.The way you get the weapons is pretty nice too, but some of those optional quests are just so slow to trudge through, im looking at you witch. Thankfully they reward you a ♥♥♥♥ load of scrapfinal thought:Could this game be more polished, absolutely, but it's better quality than a lot of AAA games i've played in the past. so congrats dev, you're already doing better than most. keep it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Choo-Choo Charles

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR Version: Short, sweet and to the point. A fantastic little horror game. 9/10 The game is a great time start to finish. Charles is terrifying. The island is fun to explore and the sense of danger that comes with leaving the train knowing he could shamble over the horizon at any moment never left me.A personal favourite detail is how, organic Charles felt. It never felt like he popped up just for a cheap scare. Often I would hear or see him roaming around in the distance and he'd just wander off and leave me alone. But other times he would notice and give chase. I never got the feeling there was some invisible timer counting down till his next attack.The only complaint I could give is the stealth sections felt a bit clunky at times. Simply tapping the sprint key would mean they'd spot me from miles away, but then they could walk within inches of me with no cover and not notice at times. Not a massive issue, just a tad frustrating at times.Overall: This game is simply fantastic. I loved every minute of it. It was short but it didn't outstay it's welcome and get tedious. And the scare factor never wore off like other games I've played. It stayed tense from beginning to end. Highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Choo-Choo Charles

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes, you want a deep and complex psychological horror that burrows into your very soul, reframing your entire perspective on the world.Sometimes, you want Choo-Choo Charles.I'm not going to lie. This game has its issues. Visual things like the fact that the characters' mouths don't move and the stealth gameplay leave a lot to be desired. But this game is clearly a labor of love and the person (yes this was all mostly done by one person) who made it clearly had a LOT of fun bringing their vision of Charles to life, and was completely unashamed of that. That's more then I can say for most AAA games these days. And the parts of it that are bad are often excusable. For instance, he probably tried to do the lip syncing at some point but found that he just wasn't up to it - he couldn't make it look right. He then made the decision to not do it at all. Not having people move their lips while they talk is weird, sure - but horrific lip syncing would have looked worse. It takes guts - and brains - to make that sort of decision. Dude's got good instincts.The only real complaint I have is the afformentioned stealth game play. A lot of people don't like stealth game play, and I'm actually not one of them. When it's done well it can really exhilarating for me. But I didn't like it here and the reason for that is just how awkward it was. For instance, maybe this was just my impatience, but the enemies were often timed in such a way that they'd appear as soon as I thought the coast was clear. But the biggest suggestion I have is a way to deal with the enemies. It doesn't even have to be combat, but once you sneak past a guard it would be nice to not have to worry about them anymore. I keep talking about the bad, and I forgot to mention the whole REST OF THE GAME.  Choo-Choo Charles is at once horrifying and hilarious. You'll be talking to the Pickle Lady about her Pickle Mission and suddenly the bellow of Charles' whistle will break through the night and his bloodstreaked face will climb the hill on its ambling spider legs. This is a fairly occurance. Plenty of references to other horror games litter the world, but they're done in a tasteful way where if you didn't recognize them you'd just think it was just another part of this weird, strange island. Charles himself, as the centerpiece of the game, deserves to be commented on. A meme come to life, he embodies the mix of terror and humor that this game goes for. He is always a possible threat, and hearing his whistle when I wasn't prepared for it filled me with legitimate panic on more than one occasion. A horror game that can do that is doing something right, and one that can still keep those moments scary with all the whackiness around it is even better.My suggestions for the next game would include a knife that can only be used to stealth kill guards you've sneaked past, more guns, and more train customization. Imagine if you could choose a pattern for the colors on your train!TL;DR: Don't expect any AAA quality graphics or deep and compelling lore - though there is an interesting story to find if you look. But if you're looking for a good laugh and a good scream, possibly at the same time, Choo-Choo Charles has got you covered. It's a simple labor of love that knows what it wants to be an is not ashamed to be it.[[Edited because this got some attention and then I realized that I never properly finished it]]

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine how sick it would have been if none of the trailers or marketing for this game had shown what Charles actually looked like and only alluded to it being a murderous train. Sure it wouldn't have had as much hype behind it, but dang would that have been such a great horror reveal if we didn't know what to expect.
_childDocuments_.name: Choo-Choo Charles

_childDocuments_.review: You know what? This is damn fine.This game is remarkably well put together for a fresh indie release. Game is solid. No bugs worth mentioning, game mechanics are clearly explained with plenty of time to get to grips with them before Charles starts coming for you, the atmosphere is ominous, the locales are unique enough to be individually identifiable, and combat is tense. The game's whole premise is inherently ridiculous, and it leans into that while playing it dead straight (most of the time).Basically, game good, worth money.
_childDocuments_.name: Choo-Choo Charles

_childDocuments_.review: It's short (beat the game with 100% achievements in 3 hours), but was a good time. The game could use some optimization as frame rates were inconsistent. Stealth was easily cheesed by just running back to my train and gunning down goons with my machine gun. Overall, I had fun with Choo-Choo Charles and hope to see more from this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Choo-Choo Charles

_childDocuments_.review: This was Such a fantastic game! So well made with a really great story and addictive, fun gameplay. The premise is you are sent to this huge open world to kill a terrifying spider train called Charles and you have to use all means necessary to do this. There are loads of side quests to do to collect scrap which can upgrade your train. Other missions including finding weapon parts to gain New weapons for your train to help with the main fight. The gameplay loop is really addictive. Travelling around the world in the train does not get old and the fact that Charles can come and attack at moment is terrifying, the use of sound that is used when he is close really makes this such a tense . Unnerving but fun game to play! This is definitely one of the more polished horror games I have played this year. I didn’t encounter any bugs or anything. Such a fantastic addictive experience. Great job devs! Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Choo-Choo Charles

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of hype behind this game. I am sure a lot of us have been following Gavin for a while and his journey on developing this game. Very impressive for a solo developer who is all self taught at that. For that reason, I think a lot of us will ignore the game's shortcomings. But just note, it is a very short game. Took me about 3-4 hours and I did all the side missions, but some people completed in 2 hours. I will add that it does get repetitive and the missions are very basic.. However, I think the build up for the final showdown was worth it. Very impressed with this developer's dedication. He clearly poured his heart and soul into making this while taking suggestions from us players at well, and keeping us involved/updated ion the journey. $20 is a bit steep imo, but I am happy to support the developer and if $20 will make or break you, wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Choo-Choo Charles

_childDocuments_.review: Choo Choo Charles is an all around fun game. There is definitely some mechanics that could use some work but I had fun completing all the side quests and collecting all the paints for my train. Some things that could use some work are the sneaking mechanics, maybe if a crouch feature was in the game to actually make me feel like I was sneaking around. Also having no attack really makes you feel powerless which might be intended by the developers but almost feels like a bad thing while playing the game. The goons chase you forever once you are spotted and it feels like you have no way of getting away, that's where a melee option might be useful. I enjoyed the side quests, most were pretty easy but still entertaining. I found it pretty amusing the NPCs didn't move their mouths while speaking.  And finding all the paint cans around the map was a good end game task. I enjoyed my play through and lets just say I wont be completing the game on nightmare that's for sure!!

_childDocuments_.review: Good fun little, creepy horror game. Open world, so you can wander all over the map. Very simple graphics, with some surprisingly advanced options (DLSS for example and it supports ultra-wide and has a FOV setting.), make this game moderately easy to run.  Controls are very typical so no issues there. The train driving is actually a lot of fun. I am not really in to stealth, but really you don't have to be too stealthy in this game, you can just charge through like a bull in a china shop and survive - mostly! The biggest danger is when you turn around and Charles is behind you. There's real chance you're going to fall off your chair, screaming!There's not much to the game, it's small and short, but it's still a lot of fun. I would love to see more maps. Replayability is pretty low really, I suppose, so you have to decide whether the price is worth a good few hours of creepy fun or not. Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Choo-Choo Charles is a game by Two Star Games about a person who's hired to come over to an island to murder a killer spider train named Charles who's been terrorizing the populace after a mine owner/greedy capitalist Warren Charles III (hinting at something maybe? Who knows) accidentally (or maybe on purpose) digs up monster eggs which woke up an ancient evil. You're job is to kill the monster by any means necessary, mostly involving a moving train and a machine gun/any weapons you pick up. You go around completing quests that involves stealing three eggs, finding a hidden stash of pickles, finding 8 Pages hidden in a forest (yes a Slender reference), and others I won't bother to reveal, all while collecting scrap and upgrading your train to match up with Charles himself.That's it for the story for the most part, you can mostly find other pieces of the story by picking up notes hidden around the island which tells of cult worship, Warren's expeditions, and the obsession of the local Pickle lady. As mentioned before, you can complete quests and get scrap and new weapons, as well as collect scrap all around of which there's enough to find before you finish the game. You can also collect paint cans to customize your murder train. And basically that's the loop, drive around in a train, complete missions, and etc. Honestly overall, I like it as a game. It's on the short side (excellent), it's a novel concept with a funny premise, and there's enough lore to make it somewhat interesting. You can tell that this was an indie team of one or two people and for what they had they made some unique and interesting. The sound design was creepy, and graphically it looks good. Like I don't honestly have many negative things to say other than the stealth isn't really that good. In certain areas around the island a cult led by Warren himself have stationed themselves and to me it turned into "Get their attention, run to the train and shoot them, then run back and pray to god". Other than that, I can't think of anything else that's really bad for the life of me. It can also certainly be scary as hell (though kind of frustrating) when you're a bit far from your train and that motherf u c k e r flies in out of nowhere and stomps your booty hole in. Another complaint I guess I can throw out is the price, 20 dollars isn't bad but I'd say wait and get this on sale, especially considering sometimes it feels barebones.Positives:Unique conceptInteresting, albeit not too much loreKiller Train bondingSound Design/Graphical Presentation is goodShort SideNegative:Stealth SucksA bit high for the priceTo finish it off, yes it's a small indie game and can it feel somewhat empty sometimes? Yes it can. But I like what they have here, and I know they can expand it to make it even better in the future, but for what we got now? It's pretty good and I enjoyed my time. Shout out to my G Wrathne for getting me the game. If you want to check out the development cycle behind this game, I'd suggest looking up Two Star Games on Youtube:
