_childDocuments_.review: The story and art is phenomenal and draws you in. The game offers choices at every step of the way and they pull at your heartstrings. The choices you make during the story do matter and will determine how everything unfolds.This game is all about the story and setting and it hits the mark just right to keep you invested and wanting to progress. It's not the type of game I usually play but it sure is great for what it is. Definitely a must play if you are at all curious.The game plays out in partial day segments and the game auto saves after each segment concludes. You cannot save whenever you want but each segment is roughly 15 minutes long so it's not too long between autosaves.The game also keeps track of everything you do and every character you meet so you can refer to your diary to remind you of any details you might have missed. This is great as it not only keeps a record for you but also provides more detail and background to every aspect of the story which draws you into the game world even more.If I had one complaint it would be that the trailer for this game gives spoilers. Big Spoilers. wtf.8 out of 10
_childDocuments_.name: Gerda: A Flame in Winter

_childDocuments_.review: The title is Gerda: A Flame in Winter, however the gameplay is about Gerda: Saving Husband.It's a narrative game set in late WWII time, in a remote Denmark village where Nazi take control and the Resistance wants it out. The play style is like 11-11 Memories Retold, however you only control Gerda who's half German half Denmark, unlike in 11-11 you take control of people in different nationalities.There's a brief moment until Gerda's husband gets kidnapped by a bunch of Nazis. Then she is forced to join the Resistance because her hubby asked to deliver a message. The gameplay is about first choosing a location - without knowing which is which, and maybe to gain replay value, you are bound to miss-out something because you are informed events are happening at the same time. Then it is again about choices when you encounter German soldiers or Denmark civilians or Resistance.Everytime you make a choice in a conversation or action, the game judges you by (1)affection for the German or Denmark side and (2)favorable for people related. It is very confusing, as it always ends in one rise and one fall in each category, the consequence is unknown, leaving me wonder what is the best choice for Gerda, and the Resistance are cold and not helpful.The game is not exciting until the last chapter, when Gerda tries to rescue her hubby from the train which the Resistance determined to set a bomb on. Despite all the efforts I made I still failed, and others died due to related choices. I was in rage but now that I think about it, this ending might just fit the purpose of the game, showing the ugly fact of war where you tried your best yet still can't save the loved ones.This game is for some educational purpose, but not really well made. Still, I reckon the title as Gerda: Saving Husband is better, too many times she is going to give away the Resistance, and I don't see much patriotism in her.I rate this game 5/10, wish I've picked better ones.

_childDocuments_.review: Gerda: A Flame in Winter - ocena całościowa (10/10).Gerda: A Flame in Winter - overall evaluation (10/10).PL_______Rozgrywka - gameplay (10/10)Tępo rozgrywki, na samym początku wydawało mi się, że będzie wolno i nudno, ale NIE! Było zupełnie odwrotnie, tempo było przyśpieszone w odpowiednich momentach, a mechaniki powodowały, że nuda zamieniła się w ciekawe i podejmowane w afekcie decyzje! EN_______Gameplay (10/10)Blunt gameplay, at the very beginning I thought it would be slow and boring, but NO! It was quite the opposite, the pace was accelerated at the right moments, and the mechanics turned boredom into interesting and emotional decisions!PL_______Fabuła (10/10)Fakt, że fabuła jest oparta na faktach dodaje więcej kolorytu. Jeśli chodzi o mnie to mi fabuła przypadła go gustu, ale tutaj możemy określić, że jest to bardzo subiektywne. EN_______Plot (10/10)The fact that the story is factual adds more color. As for me, I liked the plot, but here we can say that it is very subjective.PL_______Oprawa graficzna (10/10)Tutaj powiem, tak „gra jest na tyle dobra na ile jej pozwolisz” i faktycznie sceny są tak przemyślane, że wyobraźnia pozwala nadać postacią odpowiednie rysy. Jednak taki brand graficzny jest zupełnie odmienny i mi bardzo przypadł do gustu! Znajomi, który oglądali rozgrywkę za moich pleców byli pełni podziwu jak można dopracować detale.EN_______Graphics (10/10)Here I will say that "the game is as good as you let it" and in fact the scenes are so thought out that the imagination allows you to give the character the right features. However, this graphic brand is completely different and I liked it very much! Friends who watched the game behind my back were full of admiration at how details can be refined.PL_______Ścieżka dźwiękowa (10/10).Gerda: A Flame in Winter zaskoczyła mnie oprawą graficzną, ale również oprawą  dźwiękową. Sceny i muzyka to współpracujące elementy, w krytycznych momentach muzyka podbija rytm i tępo gry. _childDocuments_.review: Gerda: A Flame in Winter:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Now a certified nurse, Gerda is returning to her small Danish village of Tinglev via train on a chilly winter’s night in 1939. The village is located only 10 kilometres from the German border, and its inhabitants are a mixture of Danes and Germans. Despite the upcoming war, Gerda is looking forward to Christmas with her family and the love of her life, the handsome Anders, a fine Danish mechanic. However, after tying the knot with Anders and getting through almost all the years of World War II, her life will suddenly be turned upside down in early February 1945 when her husband is arrested for being part of a resistant group. Stunned and scared, she has to find a way to save Anders by any means, but has only a couple of days to do so. Over the next several hours, you will walk in her shoes in a compelling story inspired by actual events in Gerda: A Flame in Winter.  Gerda: A Flame in Winter is an adventure with choice-matter mechanisms and multiple endings developed by PortaPlay and published by DON’T NOD on the 1st of September 2022 on the Steam platform. The game is also available on Nintendo Switch.First, I would like to congratulate the developers for such an incredible experience. I was totally grabbed by this game from start to finish. Every element in this game is done spectacularly well, from the story to the characters, the choices you have to make, the historical facts and the sound effects. For me, the standout feature is the magical artwork. Imagine playing a game from inside an impressionist painting; the canvas is a bit fuzzy, but you can still see all its details, capturing a place in time. I truly felt that I was sent back in time, experiencing the grief and the agonising decisions Gerda had to make. The crackle of vinyl playing on the gramophone, along with other carefully placed sounds, embellish the atmosphere.The game starts when Gerda is welcomed back from Copenhagen by her fiancé and father on Christmas eve in 1939. This particular act is a tutorial. It will show you how the dynamic relationship works based on your answers with the different groups of people (Danes and Germans), the Wehrmacht and the Gestapo (occupation) and the Resistance. For example, if your answers are more favourable towards the German people, you’ll gain a point towards them and lose points towards the Danes. The same things will occur whether you decide to make more decisions favouring the Resistance or the occupying forces. Gerda will also have mental energy points (Compassion, Insight and Wit), which you gain by choosing one of three specific statements at the end of each act when Gerda writes it in her journal. This will give you access to some sentences when talking to other characters. However, if you don’t have any insight points in your mental energy and a phrase is available while talking to another character, you will not be able to select it. You also have phrases that are followed by a dice icon. These phrases have become available due to points you have collected based on your relationship with the groups of Danes and Germans, Resistance fighters, occupying forces and the trust you gain from specific characters. You’ll also be shown how many points you need for an attempt to use these phrases and succeed. But bear in mind that it also depends on how the current discussion has evolved. So, if you use these phrases out of the blue, even if you have acquired enough points, it might not work, and Gerda might be in a little trouble. It is important to judge how the discussion goes. As mentioned, there are four acts per day. In the first couple of acts, you’ll only have one destination available on the map. But then more locations will become available for selection, and it is totally up to you to decide where to go. Always remember that your decision will be appreciated by some and will annoy others. You will gain or lose the trust of some characters, and some of your actions will cost lives.Gerda will also find objects at the destinations she will visit and will be able to use them to help her relationship with the other characters, convincing some and calming others. Every few acts, you’ll unlock historical facts that you can access in the Gerda journal, which are worth reading; it’s astonishing what people had to go through.  Stunning artwork, sound effects and soundtrack. The game is impressive in the story, artwork, depth of the characters and historical facts. And there are multiple endings, which gives you good replayability. Expect around eight to ten hours of gameplay on your first playthrough, depending on how fast you read or how quickly you decide which phrase to use. Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Amazing artwork and atmosphere+	Good sound effects, soundtrack, and voice over+	Great characters depth+	A compelling story with multiple endings+	Like a good book, you are intrigued to know what’s coming next+	Achievements.Negatives:~~~~~~~~ -	No trading cards as yetGerda: A Flame in Winter is like a good book. It will grab you from start to finish in all aspects. Just brilliant!9/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: Gerda: A Flame in Winter is a point and click style adventure game with many choices and consequences.  Aside from the standard "inventory" which can be used to unlock various choices and advance certain plot-lines, there is also a relationship system that gives the player a rating based on your responses to each faction and each individual.  If your rating is favorable, then some choices could become available with 100% success, or perhaps requiring a dice roll whose success % is based on a combination of your relationship attributes.  This all creates a dynamic, fluid system that is very intuitive.  In my play-through I tried to role play Gerda as best I could, but occasionally I gamed the game in order to enhance certain attributes I was lacking in.Combine this with a tense story and setting with high stakes and intrigue, and you have a winning combination.  Shades of gray abound in this tale.  It is nearly impossible to complete the story without characters being scarred mentally or outright killed.  Multiple playthroughs are definitely possible since you cannot explore all paths and encounters... that said for me personally I'm quite satisfied with just the one.My rating: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game which brings your more closely into the interpersonal conflict of those caught in-between in WW2. Not a game that requires hand-eye coordination or any quick reflexes, but it still tells a story worth being heard. I'm glad I played it. I just wish I could decipher how to download the soundtrack (which they claim is free), but I've been unable to do so. It's poignant and heartfelt.
_childDocuments_.name: Gerda: A Flame in Winter

_childDocuments_.review: Wauw, what a game. Such emotional storytelling. I've also learned something along the way with the "facts" tab giving some history lessons. I simply couldn't stop playing, I basically played the whole story in one go and tried to see every option, speak to everyone, explore everything, read everything in the "facts" and "folk" tabs. _childDocuments_.name: Gerda: A Flame in Winter

_childDocuments_.review: This game lures you into a thoughtful mindscape, where moral dilemmas are posed that many of our ancestors likely have had to go through during wars. It feels down to earth, personal and like something you can relate to. What I like about the game is its distinct ambience, the calm pace and the way it makes you think about different perspectives. As a bonus there are historial tidbits as you go along. There is one con I can think of. When reading about the characters as they are introduced, there is a section below, that reveals the secrets you have found so far. Those secrets are never reset. Meaning that you will always see them, even if you have begun the game all over. However all in all, I hope the creators releases more content like this. It is a gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gerda: A Flame in Winter

_childDocuments_.review: A true gem from dontnod. 10/10. Way better than LIS series. Dialogues are great, story is well written, characters are well made, visual style is beautiful, music complement the scenes, and the choices truly matter. So many possible outcomes make a very high replayability. One of the best games i've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Gerda: A Flame in Winter

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. Hooked me from the beginning. There are multiple ways to "succeed" in a conversation whether it's building attributes like Compassion, Insight or Wit through how you play Gerda, to dice roles building from your interactions and choices made during conversations with other characters. This game is heavy on the narrative which I love, and it offers player agency in making decisions on how you want the story to go. Yet, actions are never without consequences. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Gerda: A Flame in Winter

_childDocuments_.review: Many games on Steam have the "choose your own adventure" tag but not all of them truly deserve it. Gerda: A Flame in Winter is one that deserves this. My favorite approach to this genre, which is exploring gray moral areas also exist in this game and does it really well too, actually surprised me. Naturally, replay value is quite high. Another game like this with better graphics and OST would draw quite the attention I would say.

_childDocuments_.name: Gerda: A Flame in Winter

_childDocuments_.review: Such a good choices and consequences game based around the German occupation in Denmark (WW2). The game is easy to play but challenging enough for you to think twice about which of the factions you should rely on in helping securing your husband from being shipped off to a concentration camp.You can even avoid collaborating and go stray on your own path. _childDocuments_.name: Gerda: A Flame in Winter

_childDocuments_.review: I have spent adorable 10 hours in this game. The most valuable feature of the game is story telling. In fact, Gerda: A Flame in Winter can be considered as lower budget version of Detroit: Become a Human. It's replayable, plot makes several twists which are hardly predictable.Graphics in Gerda is debatable. On pictures/screenshoots it looks like a mess. Fortunately in the game it makes better impression. After some time i even started liking the style of the picture.Gameplay doesn't have any new insights. It just "make a decision" game which doesn't give you any challenge. You can consider it as a book where you can affect the main character and her environment. But story captivates your attention and it really suitable for slow, relaxing time spending.I definitely think that Gerda deserves bigger popularity than it has right now. But i think that price(10.5 dollars at the moment) restricts the amount of new players. For this sum you can get more well known games during steam sales.So, I would strongly recommend to give Gerda a try, especially if you can buy it for a lower price.

_childDocuments_.review: DONTNOD has once again blown me away. This is a very different direction for them, but I am excited to see more projects like this in the future. Their narrative and branching story power has served them in crafting a tear-jerking and unforgettable narrative. DONTNOD continues to put immense care and time into their stories and they are truly fearless.
_childDocuments_.name: Gerda: A Flame in Winter

_childDocuments_.review: Positives : Interesting take on WWII that isn't explored that often in media.Good conversation and interaction mechanics that seems to be inspired by minimalist pen and paper roleplaying games.Interesting characters.Good stylized art.Choices have consequences for the most parts.Pretty immersive narrative game despite hardly any voice acting (save for the narrator voice of course)Replay value.Negatives:Story kind of falls apart at some places where events seem forced regardless of choice. but maybe there is no point mentioning that since its not something they can fix. pretty typical in these types of games anyways.Can't skip cut-scenes. Bugs encountered:1 during diary choice where the audio didn't match the text option I've picked. but that's nothing gamebreaking.
_childDocuments_.name: Gerda: A Flame in Winter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of many faces. After playing the Life is Strange games, as well as Syberia, there are elements I really like about Gerda: A Flame in Winter, and others that I wish were further developed.- A WWII based story driven game is a great setting and it really ups the stakes of your choices. It's very interesting to have a Danish town as the backdrop, which is refreshing. The added history pages in the menu provide a context that enhances the gameplay. - The plot is easy to understand and you never get 'lost'. The skill system of  is a clever way of letting the player feel in control. Seeing answers crossed out because of previous actions is a good way of letting you reflect on your choices. - The music and narration really adds to the overall immersion. The music fits the story and swells when important decisions must be taken. The reflective tone of the narration fits the character of Gerda.- Quality over quantity. There are little to no filler or fetch missions. It helps to keep the story straightforward and on track. Each day is filled with purpose and determination. The price of the game delivers the amount of gameplay you expect. I felt the length of the game was good.- The visuals are a bit bland and lack detail. The painting-style is chosen on purpose, but the lack of expression in the characters (body and face) leaves too much for the imagination. The locations are basic and nothing out of the ordinary. This felt like a missed opportunity, but the team clearly put most of their efforts in the game mechanics, which is fair.- Results of previous actions are not always visible and sometimes ignored. It is clear that some missions are meant to follow each other, but now and again you help someone and get acknowledged for it, only to be shouted at in a mission you chose to do a little later. Nothing major, but noticeable.- Forced consequences. Sometimes the game seems to push you in a certain direction by showing some thoughts Gerda has. Going against that almost always ended up in unwanted consequences, e.g. someone dying. This is part of any choice-driven game, but at times you are more thinking about what the game developers have set-up next. instead of making a decision that fits the character.These are all minor issues and the overall game experience is very pleasant. I hope there will be a sequel with a new historic based setting, and further character development.
_childDocuments_.name: Gerda: A Flame in Winter

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable choice-based game that tests the players wits, as well as their conscience. The interconnected nature of seemingly inconsequential actions and dialogue can come back to save the player, or haunt them. The various outcomes that are possible make this game replayable.The characters are engaging, three-dimentional and, in some cases, surprisingly relatable. Gerda: A Flame in War, made me wonder what kind of person I would be in occupied Denmark.
_childDocuments_.name: Gerda: A Flame in Winter

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful little game. Well written with lots of room for replayability/making big choices. I wish we got a few more dialogue choices that didn't impact stats, but just allowed us to tailor how Gerda reacted to certain situations. At this price point, definently pick it up if you enjoy story/choice focused games.
_childDocuments_.name: Gerda: A Flame in Winter

_childDocuments_.review: i was surprising shocked about how deep this game is and loved it , i however did run into a few bugs mainly triggers around the extra dice roll game dialogue you sometime can get as a option that cause the game to freeze so i had to reload it , but thankfully it has a good save system and you never lose more then 5 min at most.if fact soemthing good came from one of these freezes , i know weird huh let me explain , i had a radom event come up on my way to a main story mission that was in the road and i only realized it had random event because of the freeze , when i had reloaded it was a entire different event on the road soo no where have i seen it stated this game has random different events giving this game great replayability. not only can it change with the choices you make but its the few random events you can run across that  make this game even more of a gem, i will look forward to replying this game and watch this company for new games in the future !
_childDocuments_.name: Gerda: A Flame in Winter

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved it! I had high hopes about this one, not only because I'm a big fan of DON'T NOD and their games in general, but also because WW2 fiction and war games that aren't about fighting. I love when you get to see the "normal" life behind the battle zones, and I've been excited about this game for months to the point that I was worried I'd end up disappointed. I wasn't. I loved every minute of it. I adore the art style, it fits the setting and makes even the more gruesome and violent scenes less intimidating, and as with the other games by DON'T NOD, the choices sometimes made me need a moment to breathe before managing to pick one. I love games where your earlier choices make a difference, and it seems like this one will have a bit more depth when it comes to those choices than LiS did. (Thankfully. I love LiS more than anything else but the ending was... eh)I'd say this game is a mix between This War of Mine and Life is Strange, so if you like either or both of those ones (both amazing games that you should play if you haven't), then you'll absolutely love this! Thank you DON'T NOD and PortaPlay! I can't wait to see what you'll bring us next!
_childDocuments_.name: Gerda: A Flame in Winter

_childDocuments_.review: Walk the path of Gerda as her quiet life is turned upside down during the World War 2 occupation of her small Danish village. How far would you go to protect your loved ones?

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game with an EXTREMELY well told story. Every twist and turn made me jump from my chair and yell WTF. Highly recommend and the music is just PERFECT suspenseful when it needs to be, and it kicks into high gear when a "oh sh*t" moment happens. Everything about this game is just so well done. Please if you like interactive stories and mysteries, get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: ORWELL: Keeping an Eye on You this is not, but it is a satisfying game for the time it sticks around. My primary complaint, as is shared by many others, is that I want more. The entire game can be completed in just over two hours and many of the tools you are provided with you will only use once. The entire game feels like a chapter one, and I was invested enough in it to hope that there would be more. I'll leave this one on the backburner for now, but if more comes, I'll be there for it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: I feel conflicted about recommending this game at full price.Excellent writing meets little player agencyEngaging environment meets short gameplaySound design and bgm are well done.Unskippable cutscenesSoftlock bug if you figure out puzzles before you are supposed toOverall it is more like a movie you need to do something in order for it to proceed and some light puzzles.For a first release this is still a strong showing, and I hope to see a sequel to The Operator, featuring longer play time and branching choices.This game is a one-and-done story on rails, so figure if you want to pay full price for that, and expect about 3 hours of content.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended? Yes and no. While the game starts off strong by giving you intrigue and possible connections between cases, the ending provides almost no answers and felt kind of abrupt as if its leaving everything up to a sequel. The gameplay scratched an itch for a more interactive & immersive point-and-click game, which is why I would recommend it for that portion. What I found to be the biggest flaw with the gameplay however, is that at certain points you get to ask important questions, but instead of getting answers you get responses that simply refuse to give you more info. All-in-all a short, fun, immersive, yet also strangely unfulfilling experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. I love mysteries and crime shows, and this made me feel like I was actually in one of those shows. It's really well made, has some fun puzzles to do, and a twist that I was not expecting. Totally recommend this game. I can't wait to see where they take this game, and totally looking forward to more.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun puzzle game!  Worth the 13$ I picked it up for. I did 100% in only 4.7 hours. The Operator is a story game with puzzles that is a linear experience.I think it had a lot of cool aspects that I wish Bureau 81 leaned into.For example the terminal is only used for like 1 puzzle. The art direction of the game is really  cool as well. It is rendered in Unity but with the effects on the "videos" it looks like CCTV which is nice touch for a detective game.Overall it was a fun experience and if you were a fan of Her Story, Unheard, or those FMV detective games you will enjoy this one.  8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing experience this game is.A well written story with excellent pacing, and also very good voice acting. It features amazing sound design that really cements the suspense and excitement that this game portrays so well.The gameplay is simplistic, but shows a lot of thought and care in its design.You play with a virtual tabletop where you'll navigate files, folders and the chat-system you utilise to communicate with agents. You'll be scanning pictures and videos for details, and cross-check data with the company database that lists any person you can identify with a full name or via face recognition, among other things...As I finished the game I was filled with a hunger for more. And the systems implemented in this game leaves nigh limitless potential for future projects based on the same concept. I loved every second playing this game, and I hope to see more from this developer in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so fun and always kept me guessing throughout the whole thing. Please give it a try because there are so many twists and turns you wont wanna put it down. I started playing at 11:30 last night and i blinked and suddenly it was 3 am! This game is quite short and only has about 3-4 hours of playtime but it is very worth it and is very interactive throughout!

_childDocuments_.review: Great little story game. Can't wait for more  . Well worth the cost even if a few of the mechanics are only used once. It made me want for more of the base gameplay so if anyone knows of more like this let me know! Only thing I would suggest probably would be being able to skip forward in dialog/cutscenes might be nice for going after achieves
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10 - Soft recommendation (Buy on sale).This is a very short game, you'll be done in 3 hours if you're competent at basic puzzles ~ less if you spam the hint feature.This is an investigation game, where you're an operator in the FDI (or FBI really), and the investigative features boil down to clicking on images and connecting evidence when asked to do so. There's the odd puzzle, but it isn't particularly difficult ~ the hardest part is a timed segment, which you can get around by pausing the game, as all the information remains on screen anyway.Really, you're here to play this for the storyline, which is a fairly predictable conspiracy laced, X-files, deep-state mystery. The twists are fairly obvious, but the execution of the story beats/elements are lacking. It feels as if the story would have better served from being a bit longer, given more time to stew a bit. There's unnecessary padding, in full blur cut scenes that take place between each 'day', and they seem to exist either for 'atmosphere' or more cynically, just to pad the game out so you go over the 2 hour refund mark. (Your mileage may vary, they did nothing for me but waste time.)For £10, it is... okay? At best. There's one ending, as far as I know, so there's little reason to replay the game. As a one-shot experience, it is decent, but I think it is better on a deeper sale, something around £5-7 maybe, as this is such a niche experience, it doesn't really do anything new.If you're an X-Files fans, or someone who loves conspiracy theories, lizard people behind the scenes (or a flat-Earther, whatever), you'll be right at home here. Otherwise, it is a fairly basic investigative game that doesn't quite nail the key plot points to take it beyond being simply decent.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: The game is extremely immersive once you get a little into the game. I recomend a headset and to turn off all lights around you to immerse even more. I am not into games like this I primarily play shooter games or combat but it really got my attention. The game also tells a great storyCons: there was one mission where all I did was miss 1 name and that was quickly mentioned and it caused me to have to look up the answer because the hints werent enough. i got to where i needed to be without looking it up but i couldnt select the right thing Overall/ TLDR:  8/10 great game, great story, no bugs, 3 hours of gameplay. WATCH THE CREDITS, TRUST ME

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so far. I haven't finished a game yet. Actually, I don't want to finish soon - want to be enjoyed as long as possible. haha. Anyway, the combination of a story, gameplay, nice music, and immersive atmosphere makes me feel like I am actually stepping into the FBI. I highly recommend!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: The game has potential but it is way overpriced for how long it takes. Will take 5 hours tops if you take your time to get all of the achievements. Also unfortunately it seems like the game is very linear, there are a few decisions you can make but I doubt they would change much to the ending. Also, there is a plot twist that is supposed to be a huge reveal and that I unfortunately saw coming a mile away, and I think most people would too.Also, there is a terminal in the game, which is a neat touch, but it has some bugs (some commands that are listed in help don't work like they should) and it is never used besides typing commands that you are told to type. I was initially very excited about it but ended up disappointed that it doesn't have much use.** Spoilers below **For example, at some point you are given a command to call someone by typing their IP in the terminal, so I started writing down everyone's IP since I thought it would be useful later and I would be able to call them, but no. 99% of the notes I took in the notepad ended up being useless because the game's story lacks depth.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: A great, Orwell-like, game. The writing, visuals and story all fit perfectly together and give you a super immersive experience. The game is not very long, but it'll definitely leave an impression on you. The price is a little on the high side in comparison to the game length. But nonetheless, I'm super glad I bought it and I'd buy it again and recommend it to anyone into puzzles, story driven or dystopian games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game and it's atmospheric detective style. I want this developer to make more, but this time take as much time as they need and develop a much longer game. All the good games seem to be real short as of late and I get that the developers are usually just starting out or do this in their spare time, but if they're willing to make a much longer game....say around 60+ hours worth, I'd gladly pay for it if they put it into alpha or whatever whilst they still develop it. These guys really know how to make a great mystery/conspiracy game and I want them to make another or rather continue this story and make it way bigger. Great job Bureau 81!
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic thrill, without spoiling much, I've spend 4 hours feeling like an FDI Operator, helping those agents on the fields. The role playing is incredible, the puzzles smart, and the story well crafted. The soundtrack adds to that immersion.The lenght is ideal, it does leaves us wanting more, but is just perfect for what the game wants to achieve.Congrats to everyone involved, you've made something truly special.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game is a 3-hour long visual novel with not-that-meaningful choices, good music and sound effects, narration, and an interesting but short linear story line. 0 replay-ability.The nice things:The first playthrough of the game is amazing, but there are a few nick-picking things.Finally, if you have finished the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: I was truly, genuinely hoping that this would hit the same itch as the Orwell series, but this game was unfortunately, an utter disappointment. It is too short for it to be anywhere considered good, this feels like an overpriced demo than a full game. I expect it to get multiple expansions to make it worth the investment, otherwise.... Stay away.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler - Started off Great then the ending happened and felt like a waste of time, pretty much everyone dies or gets sent to prison, while the secret bad guy organization gets away Scott free with no repercussions.I hate when games try these Gotcha cliches where they have a big twist that's supposed to make you feel something, but in the end all it does is prove how big of a waste of time it was, because everything you do doesn't matter in the slightest.if the game had multiple endings where it felt like your choices could give you better endings than maybe I would enjoy this game more, but since that's not the case I'm left disappointed and frustrated about the time I wasted

_childDocuments_.review: This game was fun, relatively short if you are able to solve the puzzles pretty quickly, and they arent major brain busters. The asthetic and vibe of the game is really fun to be immersed in. And i hope they do a second one.I wish it was longer however, and one thing that might have been cool is to have the "cutscenes" in between segments to have been animated cutscenes or something like that.Over cool game,
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyed. Is it short? Perhaps, but that's subjective. Is it linear? No, it's narrative driven, there's a distinction. Is it memorable? Absolutely. You could spend the (reasonable) asking price on a nice meal instead but it won't have anywhere near the lasting effect you'll get from this. Definitely looking forward to more from this series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: There comes a time when a game captivates you in a way nothing else quite does.I've helped with the development of over 40 games. I've streamed easily triple that number. This game is special in a way little are.Everything in the way this game was presented was done with care. Little details, things you will miss, things you will find, dialogue you will expose.You are here for an engaging story, that has a lot of enjoyable game elements. The way that the game doesn't handhold you and lets you figure things out for yourself is wonderful, the timed element? Absolutely excellent. I've felt unease in a videogame only four times, and this was probably the longest. To the devs, truly, thank you. That was exceptional.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Very immersive story, with interesting visual choices (and I mean this in a positive way!). Loved the plot twists and how the puzzles were constructed. There was no part of this well written story that were boring, so I would definitely recommend! I was looking to spend few hours at a game involving crime investigation, puzzles and action, and was not disappointed. Well done Bureau 81!Only two remarks I have
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: One of the reasons I play games now for as long as I have is for its story and I liked this game's premise starting out because it had a lot of potential, However the one thing I particularly love about a video game's story over a book or TV show is the immersion and replay value, however the story was too short and linear for that. It should've started with the first few cases being separate from the main case to build onto the story and flesh out more connection with the characters. That way at least the ending would've had more of an impact than a cliffhanger that doesn't really support a sequel to be had whether the developer wants to make one or not.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo during the steam fest thing and I was hooked.It's hard for me to explain why it's  so good, it's just is.The puzzles, the game play, the subtle music, the story, the overall fuzzy feeling I got when playing it... just *chief kiss*I imagine it's not for everybody, but if it looks like something you might like, do yourself a favour and buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: It was definitely a rollercoaster! This game was a fantastic experience that felt incredibly realistic. I had so much fun, and I’d highly recommend it if you’re looking for an engaging, interactive investigation experience. I managed to guess most of the plot twists, but the ending still took me by surprise. The only thing I’d change is adding more cases beyond the main one to make it even better. Overall, though, it’s a must-play!
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Good, but far too short.   When the game had finished, it felt like I had just completed the tutorial, I was just getting the hang of all the things I had access to... and then it... ends... abruptly. The quality is amazing, but there is just not enough content.   Just enough content to put you over the 2 hours refund window, but not enough to really be worth it for the price. I was going to give this a thumbs up, but I think I'll stick to my first though of a thumbs down... Zero replayability (other than achievements) and just enough content to stop people refunding... I don't want to see more "released" games like this on the market.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: I was hooked from the demo and brought the game the moment it released and have no regrets. The game although somewhat short has a great storyline, I absolutely love the format of playing on the PC, accessing databases etc. The voice acting was great, and the twists and turns in the story kept me interested the whole time I did finish it in one session because I was having so much fun.Great job by the developers, I have my fingers crossed for DLC or a part 2 or something similar, 100% recommend :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: What puzzles it had were ok, nothing special. But the real problem is that there are so few of them. The dialogue choices don't really matter either, with some being as purposeless as "Understood, Agent" vs "I understand, (NAME)". Makes me wonder why they were put in at all. Rather short game. What substance it had was nice, but there was so little of it. Add that to the , and I can't recommend it, especially at its current price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game, but too short and easy. Very atmospheric and immersive. Interesting ideas which could be MUCH more explored (most of the puzzles/concepts are used only once). Story is predictable like an X Files episode, but with some cool moments. Hardly no replayability as there's no randomness.I'd very much like to see a much more expanded (and randomized) sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Enhance! It's a short, immersive, detective game, best played with headphones on for the music. While sometimes the music is a bit too intrusive, it's very good, especially the ending (keep watching all the way through). _childDocuments_.review: Maybe my expectations weren't set properly but I was going into this game hoping to fill the shoes of an FBI operator : - Analyse photos, videos, samples- Search and match data accross differents sources- Analyse piles of documents or suspects conversations- etc.in order to make some deductions and help ongoing investigations. This is what you get for the first 25% of the game. After that, it slowly shifts into a narrative driven experience, where your choices don't matter (the game is programmed to end one way), the scenario is at best foreseeable at worst blatantly cliché. All the investigation mechanics that you were taught are thrown out the window and never used again. The scenario felt like drinking room-temperature water. It's uninteresting, not particulary pleasant and completely forgettable. Overall it feels like a huge bait and switch

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Immersion: The narrative takes the lead in the game. As we solve puzzles and analyze evidence, an intriguing story unfolds with unexpected twists. _childDocuments_.review: The game is a fun story, in a "operate a computer" setting. You can feel a bit hacker-y and competent. Visuals and Audio are appealing and immersive. The game is voiced for all characters that require being heard (there are some pure-chat-interactions).The story itself if obviously the heart of the game. It doesnt get bogged down in the whos, whats and logistics of things. Some plot points seem predictable, but there are some rather cool reveals.If you ever thought you wanted to jump into the deep end about the "what could be" of US-Government Law Enforcement, this will be a fun ride. The game is quite short, taking me about 3.5 hours to complete with repeating a certain part twice (about 20 extra minutes). The game having this length is POSITIVE. It doesnt overstay its welcome, features introduced are unique in their own way and operate smoothly. Give this game a try, I think this developer should try his hands at another game of this type.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunate to release a game like this in-between the Golden Idol game, as it makes look like it could a smilar type of investigation game. This is not really the case, even though you could really batch it with it and Obra Dinn as point & click made for people prejudicied against point & click, The Operator have more stronger emphasis on its narrative over the actual case solving.This probably no biggest departure between what you could expect compared to what the game delivers so it's probably what needs to be the clearest : this isn't some X-files case solving about solving stranges cases and chasing aliens, this is short narrative game. While I kinda wish it had more filler cases, that would require to use all the different tools to solve, it's clearly outside the scope of this game. The story itself is a very typical thriller, to the point is possible to get where it's trying to go just because the trope used are that common and maybe it would a problem if this was a visual novel.The obvious gimmick here is the entire game is told through the screen of a computer, a very limited dispositive that get the most out of the very conventional plot. This may sound dismissive thriller are very codified type of story, that's part of the interest in even saying "this is a thriller", the same way I expect to see a group of young people sharing their sob stories and their way to save the world in my J-RPG. So how do you make something like this interesting when you can't hire Keanu Reeves to do cool stuff on screen ? What the Operator does is giving as little as possible. Low quality camera footage, damaged photography, unreliable testimony, chat windows and a lot of phone calls, an quick acces to a lot clues but very little interaction with the actual narrative. Backed-up by the dynamic soundtrack, this game creates some pretty sincere moment of tension. Especially when the main character position matches the player playing the game, good for immersion even if you don't emphasize too much with the character (I didn't really, sorry).I do think this game overall is a bit short and lack a bit of substance as an investigation game, but is a narrative game really dedicated to its theme.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to feel like you're an investigator for the US government in an agency like the FBI or CIA, this game puts you there. It's more than a visual novel, but less than a full-fledged world with practically infinite choices.Even so, it feels full and like the choices matter. Definitely some memorable moments in this. I would like a full-fledged game with many choices and outcomes, but that would deserve a higher price tag. This is what it should be for the price, and isn't too short.The story is solid and engaging. Having worked in the government, I can say this is idealized a bit, but is definitely not ridiculous compared to crime shows. I was surprised at several points in the plot, and the way you discover the protagonist's situation and that he encounters is solid.However, there are a few things that make it a bit realistic. It is set in the early 90s, yet the "FDI" (not FBI) have the capability to "enhance" photos like Stable Diffusion can now. There are cell phone towers and tracking, but not many people used cell phones in the US back at that time, and the ones that did had big Motorolla boxes the size of a lunch box they plugged into. They were technically mobile, but not very. The cell phone antenna had to be attached to the car roof with a magnet. And it cost over $100/mth. Sure, it wasn't uncommon for business people, and really rich people had somewhat smaller mobile phones, but still.Also, in the boot screen, it shows a version of Linux that is "x86_64", but 64 bit didn't become really common until around 2007.However, you can forgive these small foibles since you can consider the game as a parallel universe world; very similar, but slightly different, like how you work for the FDI instead of FBI. Perhaps in this world, they had a decade or two jump on us in technology.I thoroughly enjoyed this and hope they put out a longer game with either more choice or perhaps getting to play more characters, or a single protagonist through a longer story arc. When it comes down to it, my only complaint with this game is that there wasn't more of it. That's a good complaint to have if it matches up with a good price, and it does. Good luck to the dev team now and in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: I had a great time with this game! These were some very creative puzzles incorporating a fantastic user interface that simulated real work/casework very well at times. It captured the fantasy of working for the FBI or, as they called it, the "FDI" wonderfully.  The audio cues for the "ah-ha" moments were so well placed as you filter through the evidence provided by characters who were supportive and also dumbfounded with you as the mystery unfolded. If you are into crime mystery and puzzles with a few great story twists, get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who works with people working with customers through calls, i always wanted to see a game with a point of view as an operator, because it can be a stressful job. Long story short, I like this game for that, plus the fact that you can compare data like 'paper please'.Also, the story has a good suspense. I remarked it had many similitude with another investigation game ( government heads hiding human experimentation program), but the suspense and the music will give you the shiver Althought i need to say that the game really feels a bit incomplete at the end. _childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: The game kind of struggles with what it actually wants you to do and who it wants you to be.To get started: I really wanted to love this game, because I like researching and playing detective. However you are given a set of tools and expectations to be resourceful, while actually non of it works outside the main storyline. As a package it is nicely crafted and for a while it has you engaged, but at some points it expects you to really take control and go beyond the objective ... but only in the exact path the developer(s) have set out for you. The developer(s) haven't realized that it becomes very frustrating, very fast that the game doesn't allow you to explore or make combinations other than that what they exactly have programmed you to do. So encouraging you to think beyond one case, but at the same time limiting your possibilities very much gets your frustrated easily. Sure there is a subpath that you miss sometimes, but you only miss it because all your other attempts to try something different aren't supported (like you can't call anyone on your own or analyse something that isn't supposed to be analyzed). If you don't have any room to play / experiment, you stop doing it and than at some point the game will make fun of you and point out that you have missed something.Same goes for the dialogs. The game keeps asking you to select an answer while none of it really matters, it is all linear! Again it learns you to make choices, but the choices don't matter so why are they even there than? Just for a single different line of text to go back to the main story path again?I'll try to give it a go some more when I am less frustrated. But for now, it has got me fed up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: I can't in good conscience give this game a good review, but I also can't give it a poor review. It's times like this I wish Steam had a middle-ground review option. This game was very fun and scratched an itch I didn't know I had. However, labeling it as an investigation game or describing it the way it does is misleading. Yes, there is some investigation, but there's really only one singular crime to solve. The storyline is very linear and easy to guess. If it were marketed as a game about solving a singular crime, that would be accurate, but it misleads you in the description by stating, 'Investigate mysterious crimes. Use cutting-edge FDI software to dig for clues, solve puzzles, and uncover the truth.' This is incorrect. You only use most of the 'software' exactly once, after implying you should read the extensive manual that comes along with it. This is a game that you could probably finish within 2-3 hours, which also doesn't justify its price. Honestly, they could have dropped the mid-tier storyline and just made a game along the lines of Criminal Minds or CSI, where you use these tools to try to solve cases, and it would be infinitely more fun. I know I'm probably the outlier here with my review, and I will say I did enjoy what they had, but it just wasn't what they promised in their wording and descriptions (maybe I misunderstood some stuff, who knows). There does seem to be an open door for expansions in the future, but if they're along the same timeframe as this game and offer only 2-3 hours of playtime, they should drastically reduce the price because as it stands, it felt like an expensive tech demo.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Coming into the game, I wasn't expecting a lot. I saw the trailer and some screenshots a while back, and saw the price and decide, eh, why not, at worst, I can refund it right?Golly gee gosh, what a great decision on my part. This is one of the best games I've had the pleasure of playing yet this year, it's incredibly well-paced, has very fun mechanics that rely on your ability to read and digest a wide volume of information, and most of all, it has an incredibly compelling story. It's hard to synthesize exactly what I enjoy about this game without any major spoilers, so I'll just say this. If you like a game that needs you to think critically for a couple of hours? It's for you. The music is also exceptionally good, and I'm hoping it gets released somewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic detective/investigation game where you play as a phone operator for the FDI (definitely not the FBI). As you help agents in the field, you start uncovering some things you shouldn't...It's short and sweet but the story is intense and full of great reveals. The presentation is fantastic and the puzzles are tricky but not so hard you get bogged down. Everything is well paced and executed. The voice acting and script are great.Without spoiling, an end-credit scene hints at more coming. I really hope we get more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this is one of the best indie story-driven games I've played in a LONG time. Fans of the X-Files will absolutely love this. I haven't been so emotionally invested in a short game since Papers Please. My only "complaint" is that I finished the game in 2.5 hours. Was it worth it? Yes! The only thing I wish is that it had more random missions with field agents that weren't related to the bigger story. I loved the mechanics of detective work from analyzing footage to using lab equipment. I would love to see additions in the future with just random cases popping up. I'm sad it's over because it'll never hit the same as the first playthrough, but absolutely worth the price. Super immersive (must play with headphones!) and great gameplay mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: This was honestly an experience. As short as it was (only took 4.2 hours), it subverted what I thought the story would've been, and instead gave me a really interesting plotline that went full-circle in so many ends! Kudos for such amazing writing, storytelling and unique gameplay-narratives.Though, the gameplay did start feeling stale after the 3 hour mark, it kept itself varied and narratively interesting enough that I never felt like I had to go away for a bit to detox. _childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: A great little narrative game, short but very good. The story is engaging and immersive. The game play is challenging but not impossible - it's very rewarding when you figure out a puzzle. The sound design is absolutely excellent and fills in a lot of the gaps left by the simplistic graphics, especially in the scenes that take place "outside" of the FDI software program. I definitely recommend playing with headphones and no background noise. And there's a fun, exciting twist at the end that got my heart pounding. I highly recommend this one, especially if you enjoyed games like Orwell and Need to Know.
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10 - amazing build-up that doesn't live up to first impression (wish Steam had a neutral as it would have been more realistic); Day 1/2 are 9/10, Day 3/4 are 4/10PROS:- atmosphere- intriguing first half- feels engaging at early investigationsNEUTRAL:- game time - on one hand the price is fair for it, but on the other hand the game feels like it's missing bits after about half point mark - which means it would benefit if it was a bit longer- writing is all over the place ranging from great/clever to cheesy in a bad way (characters especially)CONS:- about last third of the game; denouement is abrubt and feels like devs wanted to execute too many points too fast which culminates with general feel of rush writing and ending that just doesn't live up to what ingame Day 1 and 2 have set; investigation results felt like a letdown- no replay valueIt's a solid game that won't be for some people, but for the fans of style, I'd recommend it on sale. Personally, I'm looking forward to their next game as there's so much potential here but also so many opportunities to execute better in their next game. Will follow Bureau 81's future projects.

_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: A 1990's-era X-Files-inspired game, you play as the titular Operator, one of many multi-talented personell tasked with assisting the agents of the Federal Department of Investigation (FDI), the fictional counterpart to the US FBI and, eventually, uncover a strange conspiracy.The voice acting is excellent, really bringing life to all the characters. The puzzles are all logical and clever, especially if you keep track of prior cases.The story is also excellent. It's only ~2 hours long, but it feels much longer than that, not because of padding, but because it manages to pack in a lot of meaningful intrigue and story beats in those 2 hours. It also has some excellent twists.Would definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the games where I wish there would be a "Meh" option.I plaid the Demo and was looking forward to the games release as this sort of "operate and solve puzzles from your PC" ones are much to my liking. Unfortunately the game itself was quite linear, very few and quite easy puzzles and the story sort of foreseeable. _childDocuments_.review: I grade The Operator A-. This is an excellent investigation game with a great premise and fantastic presentation, including the music. While it doesn't have Hollywood-style hacking, given that its setting is in 1992 and you're working in a government alphabet agency, the developers nailed the look and feel of a stripped down government UI. Even right down to a part where you use an even  computer and the visual area changes from 16:9 to 4:3. Nice touch.The story is very well written. I didn't detect a single typo or weird turn of phrase. A lot of detective games here on Steam are made by non-English developers, and so they tend to get wonky in localization. The Operator does not have that issue. The story is almost entirely logical and internally consistent, and it was fun to experience.The only thing is the story's wheels fell off at the very end. While the story beats and twists were a bit obvious, the final hard twist -- though it was presented really well -- makes absolutely no logical sense even within the context of the world that is presented to us. I come away from it with a lot more questions, but not the good "What are they going to do next?" kind. It's more the "Why did the basic premise happen in the first place?" kind. Unless there was some subtlety I missed, I can think of a thousand reasons why the first step of the plot shouldn't have happened, and that sort of makes the ending a little bit of a letdown.But don't let that dissuade you. I'm happy to have bought the game and supported the developer, especially because the gameplay was excellent. I really enjoyed the act of investigating as a government agent and having tools like face-scanning and an omni-database just a mouse click away. Don't get me wrong, I enjoy games with hacking -- whether Hollwood hacking like Orwell or more script-based hacking like HackNet -- but it was really fun to be an agent for the "other side" and just have some improbable tools at my fingertips. If there is a sequel, while I hope the writing makes a little more logical sense, I really encourage the devs to keep the gameplay just as it is.

_childDocuments_.review: I gave it a thumb up although I'd have liked to give it a thumb "middle" if something like that existed on Steam. The reason is that while I loved the presentation, the music and the idea itself, it suffers from the same illness as 12 Minutes or Zero Time Dilemma: it starts great but the story gives you a plot twist just for the sake of having a plot twist at the end of the game. It looks cool and all while you're playing but as soon as the game is over... All I could think of was "what was the point of ?"I don't want to go into spoiler territory, so I won't say anything more about the story. It's reasonably priced and it's pretty entertaining all in all, even if the puzzles are not difficult. So that's why I think the game deserves a chance despite the story.Finally, I want to add that I see some comparisons with Obra Dinn or The Case of the Golden Idol. Make no mistake: those two games are masterpieces. This one is pure entertainment. It feels like comparing Drive with Fast and Furious so to speak. For me, a better comparison would be the two titles that I mentioned at the beginning of the review where the surprise factor is more important than a coherent story.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this game is short.. It takes about 3-4 hours to complete, but the game tells the story it wants to tell in that time so it´s fine.  The story is fine. It starts of strong, leaving you as the operator to figure out what you are doing and why you are doing it.As soon as the story picks up the pace, the game is beginning to get more and more predictable. Sure, it makes sure to tell the story in a convincing way, but if the player has had any contact with books that follow similar plotlines or watched a few "rogue agent fighting conspiracy" movies you know where the plot is going and how the game will end. Ending was fine, a bit disappointing because the cut was fast and hard and resulted in a cliff hanger. To me it feels like the devs wrote a story thats about 10 hours long and just cut the game in half when they had the opportunity to do so, preparing the player for a future sequel.  Pretty good, especially the main menu music. But not memorable. Just nice BGM. Not really worth paying for the OST imo but who am i to decide.For me the games strong points are the art direction or visual direction in combination with the player interacting with the desktop. It really immerses you in your role as the operator and you really feel like you are investigating CCTV footage and sifting through documents to find small clues. The game really takes you out of this illusion by having to click the objective and then clicking the requested information. Not a fan of that, could have been integrated in a more smooth and immersive way. Audio design is great too, the voice acting feels believable enough and the sound effects are accurate and synced well. Nothing really to complain about there.Overall it is a fun, short and interesting game with a few flaws that can be overlooked. Wait for a sale before you buy it though, for 3-4 hours of playtime it is just a bit too much (About 1€/$ per hour of playtime should be standard imo).

_childDocuments_.review: It's a short game, true, but I'm an absolute sucker for these little detective games. I played the demo during NextFest and instant-locked it for buying when it came out.  If you've played A Hand With Many Fingers, I think this game scratches a similar itch. Loved the story, really loved the voice acting (Agent WALKER/PENDELL/SKINNER all standouts).  Game does a good job of mixing up the challenges from case-to-case.  Honestly a criticism might be that you just dip your toe into a lot of things (chemical analyzer, for example) and then quickly move on to the next case/thing. It might have been nice to have more opportunities to use the stuff...but am I describing padding? Game moves too fast to ever wear out its welcome. I will say the post-work/out-of-computer videos dragged, a bit, by the end of the game.  I understand it as an aesthetic choice but those bits weren't for me. The narrative is tightly focused and the game is pretty on the rails; neither is a particular negative for me but I can understand people might want more agency.  As I mentioned earlier, the game is quick to play.  Time to complete is low, which was a disappointment.  Still a firm recommend as I enjoyed the game a lot, but per dev comments there's no reason to replay it given the singular narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: The game puts you in the shoes of an FDI operator (ingame version of FBI), helping field operatives behind a computer screen.There's a huge conspiracy you stumble into, aided by a hacker.Without going into story spoilers, I saw the "twist" from the very start, obfuscated by a small wrinkle that doesn't actually play into the story at all unfortunately.The game leaves many loose ends, and ends rather abruptly and is rather short overall (playtime 4,4 h on steam).After finishing it it was obvious the game was very constrained by budget, and story wise seems the devs bite off more than they could chew or had much bigger plans for it. For that reason, the game kinda ends on a cliff hanger and your "choices" don't really matter, there is only one ending- my bet is that they want to make a sequel if this sells enough copies.With all that being said, there is some amazing atmosphere, voice acting and tense and well written moments to experience in this. I'd love to see what the devs would be able to cook up given more room/time/money/people to breath and spread their wings.I recommend it to people that like these desktop/hacker/operator type games - you can compare it to watching a really interesting thriller at the movie theatre - both in the cost of the game, and time playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a well executed game with a quality UI and sound design. My only criticism is that the developers took a lot of care into designing the game's computer mechanics but then do not give you very many opportunities to use them. I was looking forward to a puzzle solving/detective type experience where I could piece together clues and solve cases, however the game's story quickly takes center stage; just as the tutorial section of the game ends, and you think that you'll now get to work on a wide variety of cases, you come to realize the entire game is more or less a guided experience through a conspiracy story. I personally was hoping for a more subtle, open-ended experience that focused on case solving, where the conspiracy itself could be discovered by a clever player gradually and then pursued as a personal choice. What is offered is entertaining and engaging, but those looking for a good detective experience will be somewhat disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only giving this a thumbs down because I believe this is marketed incorrectly. I loved the game for what it is, a visual novel. But this is not necessarily a detective game, and I'd argue not even really investigative.The game follows one story line, and kind of fools you into thinking your choices matter when they really don't. For example, I attempted every dialogue option to not work with HAL, but that didn't matter, I had to work with them anyway.The tools used are awesome; facial recognition, Human Database, lab analysis. But we only use some of these things once or a few times at most.Don't get me wrong, the story is fantastic, and I genuinely loved my time with it. I agree with a lot of the other reviews that this should be way longer, but overall, I think the game is marketed incorrectly which is where I can't recommend it. I, and it seems a lot of others, went into this with the idea I would be solving multiple cases, using the technology multiple times, maybe even an endless mode where there's multiple variations of possible cases. I do think it's a great game, the immersion into the FDI computer is fantastic, the art style/graphics are perfect, everything ran smoothly. I mean genuinely top marks across (most of) the board. But it did leave me wanting more, I really dislike that we only used some of the tools once, and my choices didn't matter. All that being said, I absolutely would purchase another game from this dev.

While it's not too hard, it's challenging enough to keep you engaged. (And if you get stuck, there's a pretty subtle hint system.) Also, huge round of applause for the writing and the voice acting. It's top notch, considering this is an indie game.Overall, this is a strong recommend. I have my fingers crossed for a direct story sequel (and hopefully a longer playtime too.)  But I also wouldn't mind seeing this style of gameplay being used in other situations. For example, an emergency services operator dealing with a serial arsonist, or a private security company operator dealing with a series of break-ins. The possibilities are endless!

_childDocuments_.review: While a very polished and well-crafted experience, this game has a number of fatal flaws that undermine and eventually irrevocably cripple your enjoyment of it.  Firstly, it's incredibly short.  I do understand that this tends to be the case for these kinds of games, crafting content for them is much more effort intensive than it is for other genres, but even by the standards of other games in this genre, you get very little playtime compared to its cost.  This is further exacerbated by a complete lack of replay value, as the story is completely linear and has no alternate endings, though there are a few pieces of content not central to the story that the player can find through their own initiative.  If you take nothing else from this review and do decide to buy the game, buy it on sale, the existing content doesn't really justify the price point.To get into the real reasons this is a negative review, as money alone wouldn't have been enough to get me to write this, we need to first revisit the game's linearity.  The game does provide the illusion of choice, but none of the choices the player can make matter, and acting as though they do will inevitably see the game yanking on your leash and railroading you back to the single story it wants to tell.  This linearity continues to the mysteries that form the game's content, as they are designed so that the player is forced to solve them linearly as well.  Rather than providing multiple angles of attack, players must solve one specific part of a mystery before progressing to the next one, so for the most part you don't get that feeling of everything coming together as multiple clues and leads snap together into a single image, though there are exceptions to this.  I can't get too much into the ending without spoiling players, but it was abrupt, unsatisfying, and served to terminate any remaining sense of agency I had.  Everything I had accomplished was undone in an instant, in a way that felt, frankly, disrespectful and contemptuous to me as a player.  The entire point of a game, the thing that fully differentiates it from other forms of media, is that the person consuming it has agency, is not simply a passive observer but actively engages with and shapes the piece of media that they are consuming.  Of all the games I've played, this embraces that principle the least, and suffers for it.The ultimate sin of The Operator, however, the one no detective game can be forgiven for, is its predictability.  I am in no way talented when it comes to mysteries.  When I play a detective game, read a mystery novel, or watch a movie in those genres, I am generally unable to put together the pieces ahead of time and figure out the twist before it is presented to me.  This was not the case with The Operator.  I was able to determine most of the major narrative twists well ahead of time, because they were fairly obviously telegraphed.  There were a few that were well done, and there were some that would have been very good if other obvious elements hadn't telegraphed them ahead of time.  Anyone playing this game will likely figure out its main narrative twists well before they are presented to the player, and that is truly tragic.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't really recommend this game for the price being asked.The Operator has a lot of good things going for it, the premise and story are interesting and the puzzle gameplay keeps itself fresh so nothing feels tedious. Special mention must be made about the high quality of the sound design - both the voice acting and the choice and timing of the music stings are excellent.The biggest problem with The Operator for me is that it all falls apart just as it was gaining momentum. The last set of puzzles lack the sense of discovery from earlier, the game abruptly ends leaving a bunch of unanswered questions, and you're left feeling like nothing you did mattered.This feels like the kind of game that should have multiple endings or changes caused by the player decisions, but there is nothing like that here. This is a specific story that you're being taken on a ride for - one with a pretty obvious "twist" - and no replayability.If this was a prologue or chapter one of a larger game I would feel more favourable to this, but in its current state I wouldn't recommend this unless it's at least half price.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm pretty conflicted regarding my thoughts on this game, if there was a neutral review that would be my rating. On one hand the game is very polished, especially for an indie game. It's OST really sets the mood and switches at the perfect time to give you goosebumps. The mechanics are pretty fleshed out; providing a decent challenge while also not being so hard that would require one to search up guides on them. The story is also really thought out and you will get invested into it very quick.The unfortunate problem I have with this game is that it's extremely short. You can tell by the average 3 hour playtime in the reviews. Additionally all the content + mechanics that the game will throw at your are pretty much in the trailer. (There's only like 10 cases in total) Additionally, all game choices seems to not divert things from the main ending, which means that the game is not very re-playable. There may be some secrets as hinted by the credits achievement or that can be activated by a certain specific sequence of events, but they aren't readily accessible and would require probably some video tutorial guide.And that leads to the big question, should you buy the game? I honestly can't say in good faith that it is worth it to buy the listed price ($14 USD). If you have a good amount of spare money to spend on games, then go for it. But for most people, I'd recommend holding out on purchasing the game unless it has a heavy sale.

_childDocuments_.name: The Operator

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the Game after ~3 hours, so it's short.That said, it had the most intense gameplay moment of my LIFE! That alone would warrant the recommendation. But it generally is very well made.It feels like being the protagonist in a mystery thriller movie, has a really good and tense atmosphere.There are more puzzles in the beginning, while it's much more story-driven later on, which I find a bit sad, as the interface/gameplay/tools have so much potential for amazing, complex, intertwined puzzles, but the actual game barely touches the surface of them, they remain rather seperated from each other and thus are rather easy to solve if you concentrate.I would've liked more intricate puzzles, with more steps inbetween to get to the final solution, and generally more puzzle parts. On the other hand, the simpler puzzles keep you from getting stuck for too long, so that the story never stops developing, and that generates a thrilling experience of you being on the hunt to unravel a mystery with you doing the thinking and "your" agents in the field getting you the necessary evidence and info.I'd give it a solid 7/10, could've easily gotten a 9 if it just had a bit more puzzle "meat" to it. Can't stress enough how good the puzzle solving feels and how strong the story is presented. But it really needed like an additional chapter before the finale begins, with a chunk of more difficult problems to solve. The way it is now leaves you with wanting more.Absolutely worth the price though.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with the obvious as soon as you start the game : the sound design, musics, sound effects, ambiance and voice acting are *gorgeous*. And it gets better with time.Yet I'm debating to put a thumb up or down. On the one hand, it's original and well made with an impressive level of finition. On pretty much every aspect.On the other hand ... I don't believe a game is the proper vector for this experience. The gaming aspects constantly break the immersion (at least for me), which in turn ruin any tension or engagement towards the plot, as I view it from a game point of view. For instance, you're in a conversation with someone, yet can take the time to do whatever background checks you want and the person will kindly wait as long as you want before you answer. All of this make the events less impactful emotionnally. I'd add to that a deep insatisfaction with the ending (not as much the content of it as the unfinished business that stops abruptly), and the frustration of sometimes not doing the things right, but still having to deal with the consequences. Yes, it's more immersive, but it makes the gaming experience more frustrating, and I don't want to restart the whole game, so I have a feeling of unfinished business. Not in a branching story game way, more like losing a level but having to go on instead of restarting.To sum up in a single sentence : the gaming aspects are in the way of the immersion, and the immersion is in the way of the gaming enjoyment.+++ Sound design++ Global quality and realism+ A few good ideas and tools thrown into the mix for variety- The end, with multiple untied ends- Too short, with a lack of reusability of the tools and 'sandbox' aspect (you're very handheld at all times)-- The inadequate mix of immersion and gaming
