_childDocuments_.review: I love Megaten games and have played nearly everything that's been released since Devil Survivor 1 on the original DS + most of the PS2 games. This review is my first impression after getting through the first 3 story dungeons.Playing the game on Very Hard for my first playthrough and I'll say I'm enjoying the challenge it offers that restricts you from using items (although it is very trial and error not knowing any of the bosses the first time around) with just enough customization to help you prepare and enough side-content in between if you find yourself struggling/underleveled. Battle system is not press turn, but there's enough customization to compensate and make things a bit more interesting (equipment/comp upgrades/demon fusion/Mistiques that boost parameters of a certain type of move/etc). The characters are interesting and consist of adults that act like adults (elevated by the voice acting, the English VA's did a great job). The banter between the party members and the battles are probably the most enjoyable aspect of the game for me. Music is good overall.Onto the bad stuff, the dungeon crawling is incredibly bland and sluggish. I don't get why they had to tie many mechanics of dungeon crawling like finding item chests/heal spots/and especially demon negotiation to demon recon (where monsters in your stock just stand in random spots of the map to offer you one of the 3) it makes discovery/finding things a whole lot less interesting. Figue as a navigator seems really unnecessary with how simple encounters in this game work (the monster is 3 feet in front of me I don't need a navigator to tell me what's right in front of me) The Soul Matrix dungeon (of which there are 3 of the same dungeon for each of your party members aside from Ringo) is tedious/boring, it's like Shin Megami Tensei IV Apocalypses final dungeon times 3 with a lot of nothing and is a major missed opportunity. These things alone dampen the experience a pretty good amount and makes it kind of difficult to recommend to everyone kind of player.Despite being pretty mixed on this game and a little hard on it, I'm still finding enjoyment from the game. The cyberpunk setting and the battle system/characters are what help's this game stand out. I can only recommend it if you're craving something that isn't Persona or Shin Megami Tensei (though borrows things from both games), are looking for a JRPG with an adult cast, and are piqued by the cyberpunk setting/theme while not too peeved by the underwhelming dungeon crawling.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of Atlus's weaker title but it's not that bad to be honest. I do enjoy it from the start until the ending. The game feels like its rushed for some reason and you can tell that this game doesn't received the 'Persona' treatment budget from Atlus. Anyway, I'll get straight to the point. One thing I would like to praise the game is the UI and graphics. Being made with Unity, they managed to make this game smooth in terms of performance and stability. Also, the UI feels a lot modern and fits with the game's settings. I really like it a lot. Another thing are the characters. Very well development and memorable. Each of them are really enjoyable to watch with Ringo being my favorite SMT's MC up to date. Yeah. She's that good. OST is your typical Atlus's which are top tier. Story line feels is practically linear as you only have one goal without anything to interfere. Game play is very friendly towards returning and newcomers of the series. It's easy to mastered and you won't be having much of hard time unlike other SMT series.However, the dungeons are very very bad. it's dull and boring. Most of your time are wasted on the dungeons figuring out where the **** you are going. I have to search for a guide as I'm keep getting teleport to the same place. Really frustrating.Other than that, I think it's alright. Definitely worth checking out if you're a fan of the series but I don't recommend with the actual price. Pick it up on sale or something. Overall, I'll give it a 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I just wanna say before really starting that i've never really got a chance to play any of their other games like P5R on PS or SMT and im basically a newcomer to trying out Atlus games.(EDIT at the bottom of review)The game is just fine. The characters are fine, I personally enjoyed their stories and their hangouts learning about them. The combat is fine, my problem with the combat is the "Sabbaths" the game does after every, single, time, you end your turn. After about 100+ battles I wish I could just turn it off. Its just annoying after a point, I don't care how flashy they look, they just extend how long my turn goes on for, when I just wanna grind some mobs and be done with it. you can skip them but you cannot actually just disable the cutscene for them because of abilities some demons can get. Having to mash the skip button just to skip the cutscene for it is really driving my gears.Dungeons, my problem is the soul matrix. It is boring, I don't like exploring it. after doing the second instances of everyones Soul matrix for the first time and finding out there were 5 for each character not including Ringo (15) total with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ teleport system they introduce HEAVILY after the second one was so mind numbing. Unless you have a certain skill that you obtain from Milady which makes Ringo run faster while exploring dungeons your going to be looking at the soul matrix alot if you wanna get specific character skills. Other dungeons are fine, something else to look at.DLC, Please don't buy them unless your a crazed Atlus lover, I won't tell you how to spend your money but please just don't because I already blew mine on it just because I bought the pricier version of the game. The booster item pack is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, cheats locked behind a 7$ CAD price tag and it gives you guaranteed level up items for both your demons and your characters along with items that sell for a really good chunk of coin. The plus side of this is you can disable them dropping in the settings. Don't use them unless you wanna ruin the first playthrough of your game being overpowered.The bonus story pack should have just been apart of the base game, I don't know why it isn't and its locked behind a garbage 13.49$ CAD for how little it adds to the actual game. the content itself is fine. The character it adds is a joy. It also gives you access to a dungeon locked behind the dlc, which consists of a 11F tower that is just a copy and past for all 11F's basically. Just run circles, get to the next stairs, repeat.The bonus demons, same thing as the booster pack. essentially cheat codes locked behind a ♥♥♥♥ paywall of 17$ CAD.Demons with crazy good resistances and stats, along with really good moves. and they allow you to summon them regardless of your level so you could essentially start the game with a lvl 90 Demon if you wanted.Costumes & BGM pack, I enjoyed the music more then the actual costumes. The game only has one soundtrack for fighting basic fights not including bosses, the extra BGM at least spices up normal monotonous fighting if your grinding. The costumes are just ok. Definitely not worth 17$ CAD tho. Also can only see outfits in combat.Useful item set is free.  just adds a difficulty that limits your use of items in battle, and some early free stuff.If you can get past the boring parts of the game its a alright game. the world is great. The dungeons are fine to explore, (other than matrix but to each their own) I recommend at least the base game. The DLC however I do not recommend buying. Ever.Bonus - Loading screens take a long bit and there is a lot of them. If you go into your settings and look for "Loading screen tips", change it to either "Display (Button advance)" or "Hide" to change your loading screen times from 10-12 seconds to about 1-2 seconds.Edit - I have long since beat the game and I can say that I just felt meh, I ended up reaching a point where I thought "Can the game just end already?" because I was bored out of my mind. My original review still stands, but I don't like the game, it was fun for the time until I got bored of the dungeons, and the ending made me go "Thats it?", I would recommend trying their other successful games rather than this one. You would probably get more satisfaction playing any one of their other games, I felt like I just wasted my money.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd somewhat recommend Soul Hackers 2, but with many caveats. I've played every single Persona game and almost every SMT game ever released. I've played games made by Atlus for a long time, and after the resoundingly high note that was SMT V, I had really, really high expectations for Soul Hackers 2. What I got was a very middling JRPG that's stuck between being an SMT game and a Persona game but is good at being neither. This game is a prime example of style over substance. It looks really, really nice. It has one of the best presentation out of any megaten game. However, the gameplay, dungeons, and quality of life aspects just aren't there. Pros:-Great artstyle. Everything just looks very aesthetically pleasing, from the characters to the environments, the demons, the visual effects, etc... The colors really pop and look vibrant no matter what is happening on screen. The character models are not only very sharp and expressive, but they also move really well. From a presentation perspective, I can't fault Soul Hackers 2 at all. It just looks really good.-Interesting story with solid characters. Midway through the game, the only thing that pushed me forward was the story. It shared some loose connections with the original Devil Summoner and Soul Hackers that I appreciated, and it was nostalgic to see the world of these games again after so long.-Great atmosphere and setting. The writers really kept the atmosphere of the original Devil Summoner games alive in this game, portraying this gritty, dangerous world full of demons and intrigue. Again, this may be because I've played the original Devil Summoner and Soul Hacker games, but I instantly liked the world of Soul Hackers 2. -I like Ringo a lot. Cons:-The gameplay is noticeably worse than the most recent Atlus entires. It's like we've regressed 10 years since Persona 5 and Shin Megami Tensei 5 came out. This game feels like a PS2-era game that was released in 2022. Gone are press turns or anything that makes megaten combat remotely enjoyable post-nocturne. The combat in this game trying to be more like Persona's combat but it's somehow much slower paced, less complex, and less satisfying. It plays like a very generic JRPG combat system, which is already a dealbreaker for me when it comes to JRPGs, but even more so when it's a megaten game. In addition, demon negotiation has been completely gutted. You can no longer even talk to demons in battles. The only way to recruit them now is through an RNG mechanic that occurs when roaming the dungeon, and when you do get to talk to them they ask you for only one thing and will always join you if you give it to them. It's like they only included demon negotiation for the sake of having it, and only put in only the minimum amount of effort to make it functional. It's a very gimped version of a very long-standing megaten mechanic, and I have no idea why they made it this way when even games released 10 years ago had it down pat. -The dungeon crawling is really, really tedious. Ringo moves really, really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slowly and the dungeons mostly consist of very barebones corridors that you run straight down to get to the next boss or story moment. There are barely any gimmicks or variations in scenery. These are some of the laziest, most tedious """"""dungeons""""" I've seen Atlus put out. Hell, even Megami Tensei I and II on the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ NES had some dungeons with more variety than Soul Hackers 2. The game also only has 2 tracks that it reuses for every dungeon in the game. 2 tracks. You remember how each dungeon from any Persona game, or even each dungeon from the first Soul Hackers game had a unique theme? None of that is here. In fact, the dungeon music in this game became so mind-numbing after 20 hours in that I just turned the music off and played my own music. I almost dropped this game a few times because of how unbelievably ass the dungeons were. All my above complaints wouldn't even be so bad if only Ringo had a sprint button that I could use to speed through it all, but they decided to make her jog like my grandma after she just had a stroke. After having played through the sprawling maps of SMT V or the complex, multi-layered dungeons of Persona 5, it's really, really hard to slog through this game's sorry excuses for dungeons.-The loading screens are atrocious. You get a 5 second loading screen every time you change locations. It may not sound much but keep in mind that this happens every. single. time. you. change. locations. If you need to go shopping at 3 different stores, go grab some quests from the quest lady, then go fuse some demons, then go back to base to rest up, then go back to the dungeon to keep exploring, that's 7 loading screens in the span of 5 minutes. How is this even a thing? SMT V had massive open levels that were like 30 times the size of any one map in Soul Hackers 2, and there were barely any loading screens at all in that game. Conclusion: I'll give Soul Hackers 2 a 6/10, and I'm being generous. I wanted to like this game. I liked its presentation, its world and story, but if you strip away all those things, it's a very clumsy and mediocre JRPG sitting on the shoulders of giants. It's not even sitting properly up there; it's just half-heartedly dangling one leg off the side like it doesn't fully know what it's doing. My main problem with this game isn't that it's not Persona 6 or SMT 6, but rather, it executes some of the most basic aspects of being an Atlus game quite poorly. I'd only recommend you get it when it's on sale or if you're a big fan of Atlus and their games. Even then, set your expectations somewhere around the middle of the pack. Then you'll enjoy this game much more than I did.EDIT: After I've finished the game and sat on it for a while, I'll knock the score down to a 5. The story was actually quite good right up until the very end, where it went straight to ♥♥♥♥. The final dungeon was also like a final ♥♥♥♥ you to the player. The enemies suddenly got a massive level spike, forcing you to go back and grind, and the """""gimmicks""""" that they threw in were, as with any other gimmicks in this game, thrown in for the sake of having gimmicks and padding the dungeon out rather than being a fun or interesting challenge. The DLC mission is also a joke. It's one of the most barebones Atlus DLC I've ever played. SMTIV Apocalypse and SMTV had some of the coolest DLC the franchise has ever seen, so Soul Hackers 2 once again is the lame child in Atlus' family of games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like it was made by whoever was leftover from working on the persona ports at the atlus offices.Soul Hackers 2 is probably the easiest megaten game out there from my experience, but if you're unfamiliar with megaten games as a whole, it might give you some challenge. That said, I don't recommend this as your first outing as it'll give you a bad first impression on what to expect going forwards.The good:The setting and presentation are nice, lots of style to be had if you're a sci-fi nerd and need a change of pace from your average cyberpunk dystopia. (Not that the dystopian aspect isn't explored at all)Character design is stellar, especially for the important shop keepers you return to throughout the game.The voice acting well done for the human characters and the jack frost monsters.And the story is by far the games best strong suit.The bad:Simply put, this game overstays its welcome by a long shot.If you're B lining it for the story you might not feel anything beyond the occasional grind wall for neglecting side content.However, being a completionist, or 80%ist, the game is littered with busy work that can feel more time wasting than interesting.by the 30 hour mark, you've already seen all there is aside from the stories conclusion.Dungeons easily feel like stretches of land with nothing to do in them aside from fight, but you'll start to avoid combat after a while as the only time the game tests you is through the "target" series of side missions.These missions start out fun, helping you come up with clever ways to beat the fight like a puzzle, but eventually feel like a gotcha for not investing in a monster who can use a particular skill. made worse by the fact, the hardest target missions, require abilities you don't "need" for anything in the base game.its not hard because you can't use your head, its hard because you happen to not have the answer with you, and you'll have to then spend the time to go bad and rebuild a particular monster to have the move.The sad thing is, these will be the things that get you killed in almost every circumstance. the fights run on a timer where if you take too long, they'll throw out a move that insta kills the party. I can still count on two hands the amount of times I died to fights normally.On the target of dungeons, the thing that finally got me to write them off, almost every late game dungeon relies on putting long hallways with rooms that have multiple teleporters everywhere. one or two, ok. but when five dungeons do the same thing back to back, thats not challenging. thats mind numming. made worse by the fact they all look the same.Demon negotiation is all but nonexistent in this. Now you just find you monsters throughout the dungeon, the demon will show up, ask for something slightly more demanding depending on how many of the said demon you've killed. they then join you no question.the voices for the demons outside of the jack bros series aren't fitting either. recent game gave them good voices, but now suddenly ones who normally sound refined and calculated sound crazy and silly.what version should you get?either the deluxe or ultimate edition. get them on sale. don't pay full price for any version.the inclusions either version provide make the overall game easier to swallow, especially with how low the price point has been getting on sales lately.Final verdict: 6/10TLDR: its OK. but thats it. don't bother trying to 100% it. Don't make this your first megaten game either.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the first Soul Hackers about a month ago, I'm somewhat conflicted and underwhelmed. There was so much potential I have imagined with the direction they could have taken this series in, but in the end, this is a half-baked SMT game that was not given nearly as much budget and attention as it needed (and it shows), despite being sold as a full priced 60 EUR game.Now for context, my experience with the SMT franchise as of writing this review is having played the entirety of IV, a bit of IV:A, around 3/4 of V, the first Soul Hackers recently, Tokyo Mirage Sessions #FE, and Persona 3 and 4.The sabbath mechanic doesn't add much depth to combat, "1 More" from Persona and Press Turn from SMT3 onwards works much better and gives the player much more choice, this is simply just "more damage at the end of the turn with an optional bonus if one of the demons chosen for sabbath has a sabbath special skill". The fusion animation is very disappointing, and the fusion system in general seems fairly limited in terms of inheritance. Dungeon design, oh god the dungeon design, someone fire the guy that made these atrocities, most of the "dungeons" in this game is literally endless empty copypasted corridors with 0 atmosphere with nothing in them, and Ringo moves so damn SLOW through them until you get Milady's sprint ability. Going through Soul Matrix in this game over and over again to get your companions new abilities and find out more about their backstories is torture, the environment is so bland. Only the last dungeon in this game looks like someone put at least a little bit of care into the actual design of it, but it's still kinda meh.Main story writing is nothing special, although it gets the job done, I guess the companion conversations are one of the few redeeming things that make this game enticing, although for that alone you could just look at a youtube compilation of these.Side quests are horrendously boring generic MMO fetch quest grind, but honestly, this is the case for every Atlus game ever, including P3/4.The OST has a few standout pieces, but is fairly weak to the other SMT games I've played.Also, there is absolutely no demon negotiation which is really an SMT staple, and that's very disappointing, only being changed into I want your money/item/HP/MP - Yes/No selection.It might be worth it to get this game on sale, but definitely not for the full price, if you've already played all the better SMT games and are still looking for more.Personally I would recommend IV as a nice introduction to the series instead (V is more accessible because Switch, but imo has horrible writing and terrible level scaling in combat implicitly forcing you to grind and eventually me quitting halfway), the first Soul Hackers once you get into how the mechanics usually work, because even despite its age, it feels surprisingly modern, especially the 3DS port. And if you want more of the mushy Social Links stuff, obviously go for Persona instead, 4 Golden has been out for years, and 5 Royal is just around the corner for PC.

_childDocuments_.review: It's... an Atlus game. I'd recommend it, but understand what you're getting into.The most popular genre example I can make is Persona 3 FES, The Answer. In The Answer, which was an expansion to the original Persona 3, the entire "game" was dungeons and minor story sections. That was it. No social links, no slice of life, no sidequests, nothing else. You went from dungeon to dungeon, midboss to midboss. The combat of SMT and its spinoffs has always been strong, but it gets to the point of staleness.I would compare Soul Hackers 2 to The Answer with slightly more story content.There are two types of dungeons - story dungeons, which exist as real-world locations, and the Soul Matrix, which is an isolated Tartarus- or Mementos-like series of dungeons that all share the same aesthetic. The dungeons are not procedurally-generated, so once you've cleared an entire map, you're good. However, each type of dungeon only gets one audio track, so you will be hearing the same two tracks for hours on end. And there are also no changes to battle themes apart from what you get in boss and midboss encounters.You get your full party early on and then don't get any more members for the rest of the story. The five lead characters (four party members plus the navi) are somewhat one-note, but still interesting enough. The party members engage in playful banter during battles that also serve as audio cues in case you're not paying attention to weaknesses or resistances. Because you're dealing with five characters, instead of eight or nine like in Persona, there's a stronger, more consistent sense of comradeship among the team.The plot takes a lot of time to seriously get going and has the potential to turn people off early on out of boredom. Once it does, late in the game, it's just as exciting as other good Atlus games. However, it relies very heavily on MacGuffins, and changing the rules of said MacGuffins on the fly, which is super-tropey and may also turn people off. There are also instances where no-name characters show up like they're insanely important figures in the story only to never be seen again after one or few appearances.The combat is the highlight and is very strong... Some of the challenge bosses are like puzzles that will take you several tries to figure out. Hitting an enemy weakness builds a counter which results in a large AOE attack every turn. As you progress through the game and gain party member skills, you can rack up insanely large counters, resulting in a crazy-satisfying attack.The game is obviously lower-budget compared to something like Persona 5 or SMT 5, but thankfully it is still polished with minimal noticeable bugs or performance issues. I did not purchase the DLCs, and my review of this game does not take any of them into consideration.Again, I recommend it, though understand that it's a very, very, very combat-focused game going in.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into SMT or Persona, this game is for you--but let's be clear, it's NOT those games. Every SMT game is trying to do something different. The mainline Shin Megami Tensei games, like Nocturne, which is on Steam, are going for sort of these big, apocalyptic spaces, telling a story of how the world was ended and must be remade by killing God. Persona games--at least the ones that are on Steam or coming to Steam--are all about high schoolers getting into big stuff where you end up killing God.Soul Hackers--whether the original Saturn game, the PS1 game, or the 3DS remake--is more of your standard first person dungeon crawler. Think Grimrock or something, if you're not super familiar with Japanese dungeon crawlers (they share the same roots: the Wizardry games!). It dealt with the anxieties about technology leading up to the new millennium, so it was all "what if an MMO ate people?" and "what if spirits used technology to invade our world?" It was really cool, and if you have a 3DS, I think it's really neat.While the lineage is a bit nuts, Soul Hackers 2, which is technically Devil Summoner 3 (Soul Hackers 1 is Devil Summoner 2 basically lmao), is standardized into the third person of SMT and Persona now, like SMTV or Persona 5. It shares the same demons. It's not even exactly a followup to the technohorror of Soul Hackers. The budget's lower than Persona 5 or SMTV, and you can see that in the game.But it's FUN. Really awesome game, especially with the massive QOL patch they did that includes dashing while running! Cool story, interesting twist on the press turn system (though I still prefer press turn). But because it's LIKE the other games, it is not EXACTLY the other games. It's doing its own thing. Demon negotiation? Sorry, now your demons go find other demons for you to recruit. Victor's back with the compendium, and fusion is more like what you've come to expect from newer games of the series.Basically... it's... like, it's own thing. It's a cool, dark JRPG about preventing an apocalyptic event. It's a game where your friends eat pizza and for some reason have two massive jars of mayonnaise on the table. It's a game with some really good voice acting (Ringo is superb), great character designs, and so on.But like, hey, the budget's a bit lite. Expect most locations you visit to be relatively small--Kabuki-cho is represented here, but instead of Yakuza's Kamurocho, it's a single street with shops to visit. The Soul Matrix dungeon, which is absolutely massive, only has one aesthetic--even the much smaller SMT3 megadungeon had a mere five kalpas, and Persona 5's Mementos, while absolutely huge, was mostly procedurally generated mazes. I love them all, but these are more classic puzzle dungeons--deliberately designed and very specific. They just have... exactly one aesthetic. While there is story to them, and some fun fights to be found, don't expect a huge budget that would allow a ton of graphical variance.If you set your expectations correctly, you're going to have a great time.I'm getting near the end, and my current save has me at about 40 hours. I've done all the side content I could find--and the neoseeker guide got me thinking I have done ALL the side content. I haven't done the final DLC superboss yet, and I'm approaching the end of the story.Good game, fun time. Probably best for people who love SMT; I'd recommend you play Persona 5 first to dip your toes in, and then maybe SMTV on switch (or when it comes to steam, which will hopefully be soon).

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is a very good follow-up to the first Soul Hackers. It carries forward similar themes relating to technology, as well as adding its own things to the mix. The characters are downright amazing, forming (in my opinion) the best SMT cast. The music is wonderful, composed by the same person as the Nier series, and the anime looking style is done really well in 3D, probably the best I've seen. The plot as well is wonderful and has ample emotion and suspense throughout.The game isn't perfect however. While the combat is good, it is a tad simplistic compared to main-line SMT, though if you're coming over from Persona then it'll provide some good tactical challenge. The dungeons for the most part are not very good, especially the soul matrices. Despite these gripes, I would argue that combat gets very fun once you get in the swing of things, and as a time waster while watching something, the soul matrices are quite relaxing.Despite the downfalls of the game, I would still rank it extremely highly, as the positives far outweigh the negatives. Definitely something you should check out if you're a fan of Megaten, or RPGs in general.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is a really solid cyberpunk JRPG. Its greatest strength are its characters, all of whom are very likable and have had their own traumas that made them grow into who they are, and they very frequently have an air of moral ambiguity to them, even when you wouldn't initially expect it. The dialogue is hip and modern, and yet, unlike Persona, which is hard not to compare this against, more adult to fit in line with its characters all of which are adults.Combat is your standard turn-based fair, but instead of the typical bonus turn from older Megaten press turn titles, you get a bonus attack of varying power depending upon how many times you exploit the enemies weaknesses. I appreciate its long winding dungeons; in some ways they're reminiscient of the dungeon crawlers in the series early titles, which could be very mazelike. This game is no different, though admittedly it takes a while for the dungeons to become more complicated and interesting. Eventually you get teleport puzzles and other environmental puzzles, but early on a lot of the maps will be very samey. Once you get past that though it really gets going.The game is very pretty and its music is pretty solid too. Animations during cutscenes can sometimes be very good, a step up from older Megaten titles.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but I just couldn't in the end.The premise and start of the game was interesting. I enjoyed Ringo immensely and how she interacted with Milady, Arrow and Saizo. I loved the cute little lines the demons tell you when they're out on recon in the dungeons. All of the dumb filler lines were great. The soundtrack for the last dungeon slaps hard. There were many different types of hee-hos. I really loved Milady. The EN and JP voice acting was amazing. That's all I really have to say that's positive.Now the negatives is just a long laundry list of stuff that really disappointed me as a longtime SMT fan. For one, the story was just so lacklustre and short. It only felt like the game was long because there was just so much filler. Everything related to the narrative picked up at the last dungeon and I got myself worked up only to find that it was the end. They could've done so much more with some of the characters and their backstories, especially Arrow. Throughout my playthrough of the game, all I could think about the entire time was "wow, Ishikawa Kaito really was typecasted for Arrow" because he was just so bland even with all of those later-game background revelations. The last dungeon could've easily been the midpoint of the game, but it just wasn't and I felt like my hype was for nothing. I hated the Soul Matrix designs and found myself immensely frustrated trying to figure out the 4F/5F of everyone's matrices. I felt that the game was really grindy and annoying, even though I was playing on not Hard Mode. I'm not a huge fan of whatever Persona-esque battle system is used (I'm a press turn stan). Overall, the game just felt rushed. I felt like I got half of a game and that they could've done a lot more with it. I'm not sure if it's even worth playing. If you played the original Soul Hackers, I think you'd be disappointed with this.

_childDocuments_.review: Apparently my steam review was way too long so I'll put my extended, full thoughts on my pastebin, though my starting and closing thoughts should serve to give a general opinion on what I think of this game, and why I gave it a positive ratings despite some faults: Soul Hackers 2 is definitely not the big budget, 10-year development-time ATLUS title of the likes of Persona or mainline SMT. In fact, it is also not very much like the previous Devil Summoner: Soul Hackers game at all. It is also not a game of  quality per se,  I will have to disagree with a lot of the negative reviews here, and agree with a lot of the people giving it a positive review because of two key points: The plot and characters. (as well as the fantastic work on the English dub by ATLUS as always)It's well-known at this point that mainline SMT, Persona, and even brand new IP titles like Metaphor Re:Fantazio by ATLUS take a long time to develop, release, and get localized. In fact it is quite often a point of contention and discourse in the Megaten community. A lot of people are tired of the constant Persona-related spinoff titles (even if I'm not) when they want to meet a new cast of characters and experience fresh plotlines without wasting years and years waiting. A lot of fans were asking for a narrative from the perspective of an adult cast, for a budget title that isn't as big as the 100-hour long Persona/mainline behemoths... Among many other things often requested by the community.And it is clear that Soul Hackers 2 was meant to be a title to meet all of that, and in some aspects, it does. It's a budget title that should be celebrated, not derided and shunned as it has been by some strange whim of the community, so that we can get more titles like it at a more frequent pace instead of having ATLUS put all its chips on the decade-long projects and endless Persona spinoffs. We need more budget titles like these from ATLUS again, with unique concepts and perspectives willing and able to take risks to let us explore new worlds and meet new faces more frequently.And I think that Soul Hackers 2 should and does accomplish that goal perfectly. If I can get more titles like it to tide me over until Metaphor Re:Fantazio comes out after having waited for it since 2017 (6 years now!). Then I will welcome it with open arms, support it, and hope ATLUS decides to do more of these types of titles in the very near and recent future. It seriously bothers me to no end to see the Megaten fanbase complain about all these things and hate on this game (when it was clear some didn't even finish the admittedly long tutorial) which has many of the things they've asked for a long time; just because it doesn't match their expectations on what Soul Hackers game should be. For superfluous complaints such as the difference in art style and plot to its predecessor as opposed to actual flaws with the game; when it shows so much promise in the future of ATLUS side titles we could have, that we could return to.  When we used to get a spinoff with a unique take on the SMT formula in the form of a new IP every few years consistently.Perhaps one day in the future people will be able to look back towards this title for what it is, what it was, rather than by what it wasn't. And perhaps ATLUS will be able to take lessons learned from developing this title to make some more quality middleware AA titles for us to enjoy more frequently. I do hope public perception of this game grows better with time, and if you decided to read this or try the game out yourself, that you enjoy your time with it as well just like I did despite its faults, as a little diamond in the rough with plenty of personality... and soul.   -  Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: this is a good game. i like all of the characters, the dialogue is good, i'm a fan of the gameplay systems the music is very solid. soul hackers 2 is a game between the styles of persona and mainline SMT, but while it does lean quite a bit more into the mainline end of things, i think if you're using this as a bridge between the series, it's much easier to cross it starting from the persona side. there's a lot of little exclusive things its missing from a mainline game that a persona players wouldn't pay much mind to being missing, such as demon negotiation and more in-depth dungeons. as someone who stems much more from the persona side, while i can't say that those systems were replaced by anything more interesting, i will say i didn't mind as much that they weren't present. the characters are definitely the best part of the game for me. there's only 4 party members, but all of them get generous amounts of attention, are expanded upon in an interesting way, have actual conflict between them, and don't get neglected as their arc passes. the 'hangout' system to interact with your party members outside of the main story also feels satisfying and paced well. ringo as the main, fully voiced protagonist was done fantastically, and i never felt like she did or said anything a player would disapprove of, while also staying interesting and multi-faceted. the main cast being all adults also served and improved the story, and its refreshing to not have to play as a bunch of high schoolers in a jrpg.i did enjoy the story a lot, i think it played very well into the characters backgrounds and over the course of the game, had an interesting message and made the game more memorable to me. there were motifs throughout that constantly developed the characters even more, showing different sides of them as the story struck their nerves. i'll concede that the overall story was pretty predictable, but there were moments that did genuinely surprise me without being ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. speaking of which, the story did not rely on an "i have amnesia but i will suddenly be able to remember an important plot detail in the third act" moment, which is a plus.there were some definite downsides of the game though, some that i sympathise with, and others that didn't affect me much but i understand. one of the bigger ones is a DLC with a "bonus story arc", which i genuinely cannot defend. the arc itself i believe is great, but the fact that it's day 1 DLC with a significant amount of story content is a bit ridiculous. granted, it is just a side quest that isn't directly mandatory for the main story, but it is by far the most in depth side quest in the game. the dungeons seem like the biggest complaint, as they don't have many grand set pieces, can be repetitive and even maze-like. while i believe all of those aspects, it didn't impact my experience as much, as that's usually something i'm not too interested in anyways. this combined with the demon negotiations being absent is probably more ignorable if you're predominantly a persona player (tartarus moment). i will defend the sabbath system to the death though, it's fun as ♥♥♥♥ and gets expanded upon with skills, it's awesome. overall, i love this game a lot. i played it a while ago and it's still lingering in my mind. it's small scale comparing to other jrpgs (even by atlus alone) but its style and lack of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ moments makes it both memorable and respectable (and fun) enough to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Remember back in the 90's when Square was trying something different with every new Final Fantasy? Set classes in IV with rigid party structure, back to the freeform classes of the Onion Knights in V, magic decoupled from characters first in magicite, then materia in VI and VII? That was, for me, an exciting time. Who knows what Square will do next? (Oh, Junctions. Oh well, IX will do something different!)This feels like that for Atlus, who have a habit of most of their games, really since the 90's, feeling kinda samey. Shin Megami Tensei will be apocalytpic explorathons (since V nixed dungeons mostly), Persona will be social sim with decent dungeon and a fun, dumbed down version of SMT's press turn. Catherine will be...  weird. Etrian Odyssey will be boring (sorry, guys), Trauma Center will be impossible to play in docked mode, and 13 Sentinels will be... developed by Vanillaware and just distributed by Atlus. (but seriously, play 13 Sentinels, guys)Since the one-two punch of Persona 3 and SMT Nocturne brought us One-More! and Press Turn, Atlus combat has mostly looked like variations on those. Which is fine. They're great. And every time they deviate from that in ostensibly a game in those series (Strange Journey's Demon Co-Op, TMS's Encores, and now Soul Hackers' Sabbaths), there's an outcry.So I'm going to be that weirdo who says I like Sabbaths. I don't think they're better than Press Turn (SMTV still has my favorite moment-to-moment combat from an Atlus game), but it's nice to see something different in an interesting way. It's less braindead than Encore and feels more satisfying along the lines of Demon Co-Op, especially as things get more complex later in the game (once you get 10+stack Sabbaths things are typically more interesting). And the way systems are spread out, between Mystiques, weapon upgrades, Soul Matrices, and demons, there's enough fun interlocking stuff to keep things interesting, and I can definitely see new game + being worth doing.The story is simple, straightforward, almost basic at times, but I haven't yet been absolutely insulted by it. What it mostly allows is for character interactions, which is the real bread-and-butter of the storytelling here, and which keeps me interested in what's happening. Grabbing a drink at the bar, sharing a meal at the safehouse, or digging into their secret, repressed traumatic memories are all opportunities to get to know these cast members and really feel like a part of the group. Even your navigator, Figue, and incidental side characters like Raven have piqued my interest enough that I pay attention to new info about them. Having onging questlines involving the shopkeepers is also a great idea, as it gives these potentially throwaway NPC's some staying power as characters (think the collector manikin from Nocturne). The world has stuff going on. It's a cyberpunk world, so a lot of what goes on really sucks. And it's glorious.The real let-down for me is dungeon design. If you count the three soul matrices as a single dungeon, since they all share a tileset, and the two subway lines as two different dungeons... which also share a tileset, there hasn't been much variety in dungeon designs. I'm not done yet, but I feel about 2/3 of the way through, and repetitive dungeons have taken up much of that time. Once I'm IN combat, or out of the dungeon, things are great, but wandering the hallways is a drab, repetitive, boring experience made somewhat worse by the semi-random placement of scouting demons (which replace item chests, healing points, and also allow you to recruit demons).Overall, the game is very fun, and despite its flaws, I definitely recommend it. Unless you're a real diehard fan of the sort of bright cyberpunk that feels like it's trying way too hard to bury its dystopia (but trust me, it's there), it may be worth waiting for a sale, especially given the absolutely predatory practices regarding DLC, but I am glad I preordered the game proper, if nothing else to let Atlus know that yes, some of us are interested in PC releases of their products.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is a solid, enjoyable game worthy of the Atlus name, and while it suffers from too much mediocrity to be a fantastic game, it does offer a fun, focused, and accessible entry point to the storied Atlus catalogue. While there might be minor critical quibbles for Soul Hackers 2, there may be major content concerns for the conscious gamer.While sketching this review and listing my dislikes, I wrote, tongue-in-cheek, “It’s not Persona 5 Royal.” As much as I enjoyed Soul Hackers 2, it didn’t compare to Atlus’ pièce de resistance in many areas. It’s a good, fun game, but it’s not going to make anyone’s Game of the Year. The story was decent, with two or three twists, most of which I saw coming. The combat was basically identical to any other Atlus game, and, while it’s good turn-based combat, it didn’t really do anything different or unique. The music was always fitting to what was happening on-screen, but it was never attention-grabbing, unlike P5R’s OST, which has some absolutely banger tracks. To me, the most outstanding parts of Soul Hackers 2 were its character design and its pacing. Everything else was good, but not amazing.Everything about Soul Hackers 2 makes it a perfect choice for someone’s first Atlus game, and I highly recommend it as such. The game gives you a taste of what Atlus games are like, but without the commitment to a 60+ hour slog. Veteran JRPG fans or Atlus fans might find Soul Hackers 2 lacking in areas, but on its own, Soul Hackers 2 is a solid game

_childDocuments_.review: I was very excited and hopeful for Soul Hackers 2 since it was the first time in a long time we got a brand new Shin Megami Tensei series spinoff, and could be the title that would bring forth new / revive some old SMT subseries. While the game is good in some aspects, it's tainted by some very glaring cons that make it a drag to play at points. It's hard to give it a positive rating, so I'm going to say I'm very mixed. Here's why: The game itself visually looks well with the vibrant color palette and character designs, especially Ringo and Figue who serve as the main character and sidekick, who look very well done with the cyberpunk-ish look and style.This game's cast, which is an adult cast this time around instead of younger teenagers like the Persona series, is a good bunch with their own distinct backgrounds, personalities, motives, etc. Each character is perfectly fine, and I had no complaints on how they handled them. It's not one I would vaguely remember many years from now, but they were an interesting bunch. The main character Ringo, she is easily the best part of this game. They actually went with a protagonist who isn't silent this time around, and I hope it's not the last time due to this games' mixed reception. She was very like-able from the beginning, and is easily the best character by a landslide.The story itself was alright as well, with the different side characters this game offers and events. The antagonists were very bland though IMO and weren't nothing to write home about. I will throw in a big con about the story however here. The biggest gut punch about party's backstories (Arrow, Milady & Saizo) if you want to learn them, you have to go through the 'Soul Matrix', which is the most bland and uninspired dungeon I have probably ever witnessed in an JRPG. More on this later on exploration. Now time for the points I am either mixed on, or very much despise about the game: The combat itself at first is okay, the sabbath system is essentially the "All-Out Attacks" from the Persona series, except some demons can acquire skills called "sabbath skills", that usually tack on extra damage or ailments to the enemy. The skill variety is what you can expect from an SMT game, but certain demons have their own unique skills that are just not in the game at all. The biggest one being Yoshitsune, who's unique skill is 'Hassou Tobi' which is a big part of why he is a sought after demon to recruit/fuse, is just not there. This was a slap in the face when I realized this, and is very jarring since we just got SMT V less than a year ago and these skills including that one are all there in that game? The combat after a while becomes a cake walk, especially since it isn't the press turn system and you can hit enemies that resist/null certain affinities and not get penalized for it. The COMP skills however, I can say I thought was a good addition and made it a bit more interesting and made you want to go after since they can increase damage and affinities which are huge to have for later. The OST is nothing too special, certainly not even close to touching Shoji Meguro or Ryota Kozuka works by any means, but it was fine. They let MONACA, who have made the music for the Nier series, handle the soundtrack instead and while there are some tracks that are good, they aren't any that would stand out that I would listen to over time after playing. The best piece I would say is the game's main theme "Hopeless Call". I wouldn't say there are any BAD battle themes, they are all decent but not too memorable like mentioned. Now finally for the exploration / dungeon layout - which is BY FAR the WORST part of this game. The dungeons are very linear and get to be a drag to get through, especially since there isn't a dedicated DASH BUTTON. A bit later on, you start to acquire these skills called "Map Skills", which can make these more bearable but still a chore since you spend a bit of MP to activate them and have to constantly refresh them. One of these skills is "Assassin's Footsteps" I believe it's called which served as this game's run button for dungeons / open areas, which runs out after a short while and costs 10 MP each time to use. Why would this be locked behind a skill for crying out loud? Persona 5 had a dash button for dungeons and that game came out years before this. At the time of me typing this, they announced on October 3rd 2022 they are releasing a patch for the game that adds a dash button and other fixes that will be released sometime in November I believe. I can respect them for at least going back to correct it, but it's too late for many who have already played it and moved on, myself included. The demon negotiating, which is a big staple of the franchise, has been completely watered down here. Within dungeons you send out the demons in your current stock to "recon" the area, which they usually turn up with an item either for restorative purposes or for a quest, or just straight up restore your HP/MP. It's completely randomized, and these recon demons are also how you recruit new demons to your party. Again, it's COMPLETELY randomized which demon it selects, but it usually is according to the current dungeon difficulty/level. The thing is, instead of the demon asking you questions unique to itself, as well as asking for either Macca or items, it only asks for either ONE item or Macca and it joins you simple as that. Recruiting this way that's completely randomized as well as brain dead frankly was very uninteresting. Continuing from my last point about dungeon layouts... The 'Soul Matrix' I mentioned earlier, which is required to go through for the main story to an extent, but further if you want to learn more about the party members, is the main culprit with awfully linear and repetitive these dungeons can be. Each floor for each character looks the EXACT SAME, but are laid out differently and end up getting more complex with random warps and such as you progress further up. These are so bad that I started to believe they were auto generated with how straight forward and boring these got. This itself is the biggest con of the game for myself and many others I can see. And to wrap it up, this game brings back more "Day 1 DLC", similar to the sort SMT V had, but it is infinitely worse here. The biggest part of being an ENTIRE SEPARATE STORY ARC locked behind it. The game itself it pretty short for an SMT title, so why would they cut this out and not leave it in to add some more depth and side quests, when the side quests in this game for the most part are just fetching something and skipping dialogue just to get to the reward? The DLC also includes bonus demons as well, including Satan and Mara. The other two are costume packs and booster items, which are okay and should've been the only two. The costume packs are different outfits for the party you will recognize from older Megaten titles, and include some unique music tracks depending on which you wear. You cannot see these costumes outside of battle however. I own the DLC, which I regret greatly after playing. I went and spent my time getting all the achievements the game has to offer to get my moneys worth at least. If you are interested in buying the game as a Megaten series fan, or even just a fan of JRPGs, please wait until this game is discounted to AT LEAST half off. Looks like it's currently at $45 USD at the time of my review, and the highest tier, the "Digital Premium" edition listed at $58.49 instead of $90 USD retail. At least the highest tier which includes everything is under $60, but it's still not worth it even for that price.

_childDocuments_.review: A strange inversion of the standard SMT formula in that it`s more plot focused than the persona series with a more broadly relatable cast (though if you`re over the age of 25 that isn`t saying much) the gameplay however is a underwhelming experience of slowly trudging through functionally the same dungeon. The sabbath system is essentially just a less impressive all out attack from the persona games and isn`t really the game changer it was marketed as. The characters however are at least moderately interesting with the protagonist Ringo being the easy standout, but not one honestly worth slogging through the game for. _childDocuments_.review: Seems like a pretty solid middle ground between a more "traditional JRPG" approach like persona, and a mainline SMT game. The demon's as equipment approach provides more customization and Flexibility than you'd get in a persona game, while keeping a small, focused party of developed characters that an SMT game's mix and match monster party's have to rely on nonplayable story NPCs to have. Instead of the extra turn mechanics or knock down into all out attack combos of the other games, elemental weaknesses in this game build up an aoe attack that scales based off of each attack targeting a weakness, instead of an all or nothing approach. The enemies do not get this feature, but can still ambush you, which is a legitimate possibility based off of their spawning patterns.The dungeon system works pretty well, with your demons popping up around the map for a chat and a quick mid-dungeon recovery or gift, and the sword swing letting you knock down map enemies without starting a fight unless you intentionally run into them afterwards in case you just want to keep moving. This game also has "high risk" enemies (sort of like persona Q's FOEs), that cannot be knocked down, but can still be pushed away if you want to run past them.The bonuses for leveling a demon enough to learn all of their skills provide a nice little pseudo 'job' system, and I'm curious to see where this system goes later in the game.Non gameplay things: Pretty art, enjoyable characters, solid music. Animated portraits in dialogue is a nice touch. English voice acting is pretty good, though there's a kind of disconnect in RIngo's voice acting outside and inside of battle. Her battle line's seem higher pitched or something? Maybe I'll get used to it. Anyway I'm hoping for more PC releases of SMT games in the future, and this is a pretty good one so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes changing an established formal can be good, other times it's annoying. Soul Hackers 2 is a strange mix of both. For new-new comers to the series, many of the changes may seem weird, but nothing annoying. For anyone else whose coming off the heels of SMTV/any other SMT game, they can put a real damper on your enjoyment.For starters, you can't recruit demons via talking anymore, only through demon recon and it's random too. This means that 8/10 any time you recruit a demon it's one that you already have. With how rare demon recruit nords are, it's a MASSIVE waste of time. Even more so when you're trying to farm.Fusion skills have also changed, now skills can only be passed down if the new demon has an affinity for it.  Which, the game does a poor job of telling. But the biggest change is the (lack of) press turn, this changes battles on a fundamental level. In other games, you would avoid hitting a demon's resistance because it would mean losing you're extra turns. Now? It doesn't matter! Not only does hitting a demon's resistance not affect turns, it still does a good bit of damage. Thankfully, the characters, music, and setting more than make up for all this. This is not a game you buy at full price, this a game you get on sale. Oh, and the DLC is terrible, all of it full stop. Don't pay for demons that are main stays of the series and the exp items break the game. The costumes don't even show up in the overworld.

The attacks and demons are similar from the SMT games so you can  leverage the knowledge from this game if you go onto others. Enemy HP and damage is scaled similarly to the player's which makes healing and targeting weaknesses important. One of the joys of the game was finding out a new demons weakness. The story is pretty good, some background story elements are assumed based on the conversations  but it's not necessary to show.. The dialogue for sub quests and inter party banter is very good and gave me chuckles while being serious when the setting called for it. _childDocuments_.review: An old fashion JRPG warts and all after my heart.Good old Atlus giving us another dose of that sweet sweet persona goodness with a different twist. That being said I again find myself getting all ground out from the game and having trouble tracking down resources needed to maintain parity with the bosses. That is to say, beating regular enemies isn't a challenge. The bosses tend to come with some very particular sets of rules or are just way stronger and get to move multiple times a turn however never after losing a boss did I feel it was impossible there was always more I could do to improve my chances. Improving my relations with my fellows, gathering materials for better equipment. fighting and gathering demons for fusion. I however always find myself at a deficit of levels/XP. Enter the Side quests. The "Requests" are very bare "go do!" quests. Why? because it's a game dummy. That isn't to say the game doesn't make some attempts to veil this but clearly someone felt the game was lacking or may indeed be lacking some sort of balance that this addresses but to me it seems more shoe horned in because other games in the genre have an exhaustive list of side quests instead of any sort of game play or narrative reasons but I may be off base on this one. Maybe it's just me but I'd like to see something more out of side quests than another way to get EXP and non-unique/common items. Side Quests don't flesh out characters, They don't add narrative, and are essentially a thing you pickup for the EXP bonus while you are grinding. At least for me, I'd rather just get more EXP from the bad guy PIÑATAS instead of catalogs of things I need to do, just slows the game down. It does however make me appreciate personas time system as a creative restriction on developers to keep the story moving along.

_childDocuments_.review: I have two really major problems with this game. The story, and the Sabbath system but they are so fundemental that I cannot bring myself to recommend this game. The story is easily the worst of ATLUS's games I ever played - and I played a bunch: SH1, SMT 3-4 + 4:Apo, Strange Journey, Devil Survivor 1-2, Persona 1-5. You'll be rolling your eyes pretty much every cutscene be that from extremly big plot holes or character over-reactions. The titular Soul Hack from the first game, was brought down from mystique, epheral to convenient ressurection switch - which can be turned on or off whenever the plot needs to somehow push forward.Characters themselves are good, though they are at their lowest during the main story events, and are at their best during the hangouts scenes. Now onto the second issue - the Sabbath system. This system is basically an equivalent to "win more", that is if you are winning by exploting enemy weakness you will hit again at the end of player turn. The problem is, that this system doesn't work well with any other battle system mechanic. First, if you setup your team correctly and have a wide spread of elemental skills you will pretty much wipe the enemies even before Sabbath will have a chance to hit. Ok, you can utilize it by not using your last character's turn if you have a big stack count enough to save some MP - but that's it. In comparision, in Strange Journey we had a similar system, but one with very important difference - that attack was immediate, and was also connected to demons alignment system which enemy could counter. I won't go into details how Persona or SMT systems perfectly blend their mechanics into their own battle systems - but one thing that connects them is that the mechanics can also be used by enemy, therefore making their mechanics integral part of the whole battle systems that player needs to play with.All in all, it's sad because the game really has some good music and interesting aesthetic but is brought down by some fundamental flaws. The way the game was published wasn't really helping it either. For most people it was a new franchise which they weren't sure about. Yet the developer/publisher decided to move content into Day 1 DLC. The situation is even worse because the game itself is very short compared to other ATLUS's games, and the price tag is set to AAA games standards - initial price was the same as Xenoblade 3 - released a month prior - which has a lot more substance and content.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is best described by being good enough, but the potential was there for an outstanding JRPG. Atlus showcases that they price their games equally, but they are not made equally.Before I review this game, I want to stress that the patch from 17.11.2022 fixed the game in one important aspect: Soul Hackers 2 was too slow.Pacing of a game is difficult, and sometimes one single big change makes or breaks a game. In this particular case, the game changer was adding a fast battle function and the ability to sprint. Before that, everything was too slow in the game, it made dungeons and at times even dialogue something to endure. Forget New Game +, which becomes barely unplayable as there is so much dialogue which needs to be reexperienced. Just to make a comparison, how much faster the game is:How Long To Beat was saying that the main campaign needs 40 to 60 hours for the main campaign and 70 to 80 for 100% achievements. With the changes, I needed 47 hours for 100% (including the story DLC, which makes grinding easier).There you have it, the game sucked at release. Imagine just needing to spend two times the time in a dungeon for no reason except for Atlus not adding running and fast battle speed in a modern RPG, not to forget no cutscene skips.Soul Hackers 2 was motivated by the so typical business tactic: Overpromise. Underdeliver.Pretty good, actually. The original Soul Hackers and Soul Hackers 2 are only loosely connected and while the callbacks are subtle, they work out quite well. But honestly:Who even played the original Soul Hackers or its remaster on the 3DS?If Soul Hackers 2 could not stand on its own legs, it was doomed from the start. And well, stand it can, after being given the crutches called patch.Soul Hackers breaks with many SMT conventions which help the game a lot. It takes the personal interactions from Persona and makes the main character a talking and spunky woman who does extremely well in interacting with the main cast. The problem is that there is not enough narrative depth, as most characters are one dimensional, if they do not belong to the main troupe. If the game did more with its cast and maybe allowed more varied interactions than just talking, it could make this an outstanding cast. Wasted potential, a motive which touches every facet of the game.Leading to the big thing: main story. It is good, at times even surprising in how it acts out. There are only singular outstanding moments, but it keeps the audience engaged for the course of the game.Atlus has two modes: Either design a complicated and skill rewarding JRPG which stands as a titan among the genre. Or simplifying it although no one asked for it.Soul Hackers 2 is the latter, but this does not speak of the quality, which is good enough. Instead of summoning demons like in the original Soul Hackers, Soul Hackers 2 decides to take the Persona route and every character is Joker/Yu Narugami/Jesus who can equip any demon to gain stats and their respective offensive and defensive capabilities.If an enemy gets hit with an effective effect, a counter goes up. At the end of the round all counters are consumed and deal bonus damage. That was it. That is everything that Soul Hackers did. And it works surprisingly well as hitting weaknesses still feels very rewarding and there are decent risk vs reward calculations in going for max stacks to finish a fight faster. At least in specific cases as there is another problem within that design choice:The bonus damage granted by counters is extremely high. There is no reason to not hit weaknesses in any scenario. Did I mention that it is AOE? Well it is and this makes it even more broken. Better not to speak of strength builds, they do not exist. Magic is too strong as it boosts four different elements while physical attacks only have two possible elements. In short: Math says that magic demon is superior, because they are more likely to be able to hit weaknesses for counters.All in all the gameplay is good, it is still an Atlus JRPG, but good is disappointing, if one considers what Atlus recently created. No Atlus JRPG without dungeons. They all suck. Every single one. They range from miserable to okay. Boring slogs of running through corridors, simple puzzles and, not to forget, trial and error. The main story is good enough to carry the momentum and at least kept my interest, but I dreaded going through a dungeon.There is this problem called: solution and implementation.Solution is the step-by-step plan to solve the problem. Implementation measures the methods (and time) to implement it. In Soul Hackers 2 finding the solution is often exceedingly simple, implementing it takes too long. Where is the creativity, smart riddles or anything like that? Even the original Soul Hackers from 1997 had better dungeon design. In general, I go the opposite route, I list the positives for a game and then rip it apart. But Soul Hackers 2 can’t be ripped apart, because especially bad stuff is what it lacks. Yet it need more good content.Creative dungeon design, challenging combat which is also fair, more focus on character and environmental storytelling, more cyberpunk than just lip service.I enjoyed my time with the game and characters like Saizo (a standout character) will be remembered, but I wish that Atlus really gave the development team more resources.Currently, Soul Hackers 2 is too similar to the quality standard of Digimon Cyber Sleuth, a game from the PS Vita and remastered for the PS4 and PC from 2015.Soul Hackers 2 is a game that can only described as mid. As soon as the price tag reflects the quality, it is a perfectly adequate game, but for 60 dollars and day one DLC, Atlus asks too much. A weak thumbs up of disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: A dungeon crawling JRPG that sees you take control of Ringo and her party of devil summoners as they set off to prevent the end of the world. It's part of the megami tensei series so those familiar probably know what to expect gameplay wise to some degree.It has more of a focus on your party members, learning more about them as you watch them clash with and confide in each other, and I was really fond of the party and this aspect as a whole. I'm also really fond of the designs of both the world (outside the dungeons) and characters. I still feel like the game could've expanded on NPCs outside the antagonists and the world itself. Most sidequests aren't that interesting to tackle and aren't good for much more than character tidbits but the writing can feel shallow, and there's not much for the few characters with a proper name and design like the shopkeepers. Some plot elements are also a bit questionable but not overwhelmingly so.This is a megami tensei game and that means you'll be recruiting, fusing and summoning demons to use in battle. Well, you won't exactly be summoning them, this game uses a system akin to Persona games before 3, with each member being able to "equip" a demon and use its abilities, take on its strengths and weakness and have their stats boosted. There's no restriction to what demon each of them can use, but each party member can only equip certain tiers of enhancement items and choosing demons with skills that benefit from those items is ideal. The demon roster is decent, it's mostly nice to see some of these in full 3D, lots of cool designs as usual. As you can expect in battle you'll need to carefully consider your party's composition and the enemy populations of whatever dungeon you're going through to make it through in one piece. Mostly you just want demons that can hit their weaknesses hard, and as always the fusion system gives you an interesting way to make the most powerful demons you can.Unfortunately the actual dungeon crawling part of this experience is also its weakest. To start with outside of the final dungeon the visual variety is very lacking and they aren't very interesting. You've got shipping yards, subways, an office building and... that's it. Well, there's also the (mostly) optional Soul Matrix, but it's the biggest in the game and all of it has the same cubey cyberspace look. Most of it doesn't feel like it reflects the game's flashy, futuristic cyberpunk style, they could be in any modern game really. In terms of how they're laid out they also aren't that interesting to navigate, kind of feeling at the same time simplistic and tedious to get through, even worse when they're involved in side quests.For the Soul Matrix specifically, the issues start with how it's explained: in-universe it's 3 dungeons that represent the connection Ringo has with each of her teammates, built from their memories. That sounds like a pretty cool concept with lots of room for interesting theming inside the dungeons themselves. In reality though, all 5 floors of all 3 of these dungeons look the same, the only difference being you'll see events for their respective characters in the appropriate place. They also aren't that much more interesting to explore and the sidequests for these are the same 3 kinds for each floor for each dungeon. Defeat some number of a specific enemy, that can be annoying when it just won't show up (at least enemy groups containing it are marked), collect a specific item from around the floor, and fight a powerful gimmick enemy with some restrictions (which can be an interesting challenge at least). They are all optional but a few of the item collecting ones at least you will need to unlock fusion for each Mitama, something you'll want if you plan to take full advantage of the fusion mechanics. Exploring the soul matrix is also how you enhance each character's passive abilities.Another thing I'm not too fond of is the demon recon system. Supposedly you send your demons out to scout and find useful items and information for you, but in the end it's just a way to reframe finding an item in a chest which I'd honestly prefer over this, it's not like your demons have that many personalities or things to say. It's also part of the much simpler replacement to demon negotiations, and you also just can't speak to demons mid random encounters anymore.Some other miscellaneous gripes: The Sabbath system looks very cool, but the (skippable) animation is overkill for something that'll be playing constantly because it's really easy to trigger, generally just strike an enemy's weakness, and doesn't feel like it adds any strategic depth. Characters are way too chatty in battle, having a line even for every menu option you hover over. The enemy warning system is pointless and sometimes annoying. The soundtrack feels too limited. Attack effects and animations in battle feel lackluster. Risky enemies are your best source of XP and money but it still doesn't compare to how much of a chore they are to fight. Autobattling or fast forwarding in battles still feel too slow. I wish I had a much longer lasting version of Estoma or a way to autokill weak mobs...Overall it's kind of hard to recommend so I suppose I won't, there might not be many people, interested in MegaTen or not, that could overlook its significant shortcomings for the parts that are good.

_childDocuments_.review: I was on the fence for reviewing this game for so long because I wanted it to succeed. But after months dreading to return to it, I just gotta get it off my chest. Atlus rushes a RPG to further boost sales. It seemed too good to be true that two Atlus games came out in the same year.Gameplay: Fun for the hardcore turn-based rpg players. For all others it will come off as a grueling dungeon crawl slug. I love a good grind but this game made me rethink that.Levels/Worlds: Very nice designs, just wish they were a bit shorter. After a point everything looks the same and there isn't any events to liven up the rest of the crawl.Characters: Ringo is obviously the strongest character, and it is nice to finally have a main character with their own personality. That being said at some points she's just too good? Too strong? It is clear they put all of their focus into the main character as the side characters are nothing but their tropes. Your side members exist just so you have the 4 party scheme of persona. Honestly you could go a more mainline SMT approach and that would take the bland characters out of the spotlight. Figue was my second favorite but the story reduces her to the sidelines for no reason other than a spoiler reason at the end of the game with very little pay off. ♥♥♥♥ the bird, easy to spot a cash grab mascot and this is the most bland attempt yet. It is just a drone for Figue and is tied to a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ mechanic.Voices: Being unable to turn off the notifications of enemy awareness is too taxing. I get the use, just let me turn it off. I played the game on mute after a point just to avoid it. YOU HAVE BEEN SPOTTED, YOU HAVE LOST SIGHT OF THE---, YOU HAVE BEEN SPOTTED. I played with the english dub voice acting and I'm sorry for them that they had to voice this game but at least they tried.Graphics: I thought this was the area the game would struggle in but this is where the game performs. Everything is visually appealing and smooth, I think the cell shading helps but I could see where someone who hates anime style with a passion would get tired. Atmosphere: The game really hits the bright neon notes and a striking visual backdrop, but after a while things start to look the same. I wish there were areas that weren't as future or fantasy to show just how much things have advanced but every square inch screams "FUTURE FUTURE FUTURE"Story: Interesting to a point. They really push the "technology has exceeded further than humans know what to do with and no new inventions will ever exist again" and then it just pretends we didn't discuss that for over half the game. For a society that has peaked, we don't see anything new from our world that could exist. It is a modern day world with a futuristic coat of pain and cyberpunk just ain't my thing.Grind: Too much without DLC, Too easy with DLC. I like a good grind but other than the numbers going up the battle abilities are story progression locked and you only get a certain amount. Hope for 30 hours you were planning ahead! Which is another thing, imagine if this game was over 30 hours long and you still had to grind just as much. Makes me shutter. If only they spaced it out to a 100 hour RPG with better pacing.DLC: Absolutely required. Can't beat the game without it. Shameless cash grab.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, the best way to describe this game is: Wasted Potential. Everything in it has potential to be incredible, but it seems that the budget only allowed it to be mid. Incredible character design that's not well explored because of the weird 3D models' animations (like Ringo's hair clipping through her clothes); Incredible storyline that's not well told because the storytelling feels just... Weird (it feels like the game was supposed to be about 45h~50h long instead of 25h~30h); Beautiful dungeons with bad and outdated map design that just feels boring by the end of the game; And worst of all: full of paywalled content, it makes no sense to have a demon DLC or a single extra story costing that much, specially as they were available when the game was out.I truly wish this game could be what it was supposed to, I wanted to see its full potential and ejoy it even better, but at this state, it's mid at its best.

They will spam it and it'll become impossible unless you Level Grind or have MP recovery skills which are rare. One of the items being DLC. The restriction of items definitely pushes the game difficulty up alot. It wouldn't be so hard if every damn DLC/Challenge boss didn't have this move.Even SMT Nocturne was 10x less tedious than this. I even resorted to using EXP DLC because of how much grind you need to put into this for some of the toughest enemies they toss at you for no reason. Almost none of the Recommended levels match up after level 30.Also the quests become tedious by the halfway point. There's just too much RNG to it and just too much running around the same exact areas. Lots of them sharing same bland designs too. Anything that has to do with the Axis is just awful. They could've EASILY made it one dungeon but no, it's 3 lifeless ones that have several quests each which take forever. You need whatever you can get on Very Hard.Still despite all of it's problems, it sits at a 7.5 out of 10 for me. It definitely has its flaws but it's still a enjoyable RPG but man it shows it's issues once you see them.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:  - Ringo, a voiced female protagonist with a fun wisecracking personality.- The main cast is pretty well designed and voiced.- The story is pretty standard prevent apocalypse, save the world cliché of the Megaten games, no plot holes from I've seen.- Nice visual design portraying the cyberpunk setting, it could very well be an anime movie.- Music is great as usual for the Megaten franchise.- Gameplay is pretty similar to the Persona games where you control 4 party members each equipped with demons adding their stats and skills to your repertoire. If you only want to get one DLC, get the Booster Item Pack, it makes the game a lot less grindy.
