_childDocuments_.review: I dunno whether to recommend this game or not! I have a love/hate relationship with this game.I personally really adore Ringo as a character (She's a fully written, full voiced character which is awesome and hopefully ATLUS does this with future protagonists) and I really like Saizo, Milady, and Arrow too. I like the soundtrack with the opening theme being my favorite song from this game and it's cool that Keiichi Okabe composed the soundtrack. I found the world itself to be interesting, but not as much as the original Soul Hackers' world. I like how this game has a full adult cast and I super enjoyed their many interactions between one another! These characters are not friends and it took until almost the end of the game for your group in-game to truly "be friends" or at least get along well, and I know throughout the game they'll sometimes have a nice chat but a lot of the times when they're together they will have arguments of some kind (Arrow and Milady are a big example of this) and this is because they these four characters have no choice but to stick together and stay as a team to get through this even though they don't want to! They basically aren't friends and are forced to be together and overtime these characters develop more, and I honestly love all this about these characters. They're nothing like the usual characters who join you on your adventure in jrpg's and rpg's where everyone in your group is just super nice and wants to help you on your quest without question, with everything being hunky-dory. However, as for the things I do NOT like about this game: Let's start with the Soul Matrix. It feels pretty bland and uninteresting, the music is always the exact same which is a real shame. I don't like how no matter how deep the places goes the Soul Matrix always looks the exact same and it doesn't have any sort of variety to it. I also feel it drags on for far too long as what also doesn't help is the fact there's import story stuff tied to it and the player is required to completely explore the entirety of each Soul Matrix to unlock everything the Soul Matrix has to offer, including the story stuff. When I mentioned "Each Soul Matrix" I mean that there's three Sectors in the Soul Matrix. There's the Arrow Sector, Milady Sector, and the Saizo Sector, and each look and play the exact same but the only differences between them is that each sector has it'd own story stuff like cutscenes etc (for example, Saizo's Sector is focused on Saizo) and while I do love these three characters (ESPECIALLY Saizo) I honestly feel the Soul Matrix drags on for far too long and according to some players, the Soul Matrix became too much for them overtime and they didn't want to do them anymore which is a shame because of the story stuff that's locked behind the Soul Matrix is actually good important stuff for these characters from what I remember experiencing but I fully understand these players decision. I personally did not mind the Soul Matrix too much but yeah I honestly understand other people's  criticism. Another thing I don't like about this game are the many dungeons (and not to be confused with the Soul Matrix. that too is a dungeon but it's a single overly large dungeon with randomly generated layouts). These dungeons are more bearable than the Soul Matrix, HOWEVER these dungeons are very uninspired, uninteresting, and boring but sure you could say the dungeons of the original Soul Hackers were "not good" however I truly believe those dungeons had much more thought put into them plus all those dungeons in the original Soul Hacker's had great interactions within them, and I feel Soul Hackers 2 is absolutely brought down not only by it's dungeons but also how all interactions within those dungeons work. Something I should also mention about Soul Hackers 2's dungeons that I didn't enjoy is that it's dungeons lack puzzles or at least any good puzzles.Overall, I have a love/hate relationship for this game. There's things I wish had more thought put into (like the soul matrix, dungeons, and puzzles) and things that I believe are fine the way they are (like the main characters the player is with throughout this game, and the voice acting) and plus it's a good game in my opinion but there are things which hold it back from being great and the dungeons/soul matrix may turn away other people from playing this game, especially with how much talk there is about them online and to be honest the soul matrix is the worst part about this game for me.For me this game is a 6-7/10 rating for me, at least! It has pros and it has cons, and because a lot of the time spent in this game is through the Soul Matrix and the many Dungeons explored in-game, It's a hard sell in my opinion. I feel this game is the perfect example as to why fun and overall great dungeon design in any game is super important and that bad uninspired dungeon design/dungeons is not good for any game.Even though my review says "I recommended this game" it's a review that's both positive and negative.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is a tricky game to discuss in that it openly invites comparisons to another game it's very much not trying to be. The original Soul Hackers, so far as I can tell without having played it, was a fairly standard Shin Megami Tensei game, albeit with a more cyberpunk setting. Soul Hackers 2 sidelines SMT's trademark demons and most related mechanics, instead treating demons as equipment for the game's mostly human party members. This comparison ultimately does the game a disservice, as while a more conventional follow-up would perhaps be more welcome, it does a respectable if uneven job of standing up on its own. The human party members are endearing, the game's sabbath system is quite satisfying if not particularly deep, and while the new demon recon mechanic doesn't quite make up for the sidelining, it does function as a clever way to give those demons a greater presence. The game's biggest genuine fault is that the dungeons' designs are generally lackluster, in terms of both aesthetics and layout, and for a game that's spent mostly in dungeons, that can drag the game down considerably.Giving this game the Soul Hackers moniker may have been a misguided choice, but this is a fun if flawed JRPG. Maybe get it on sale, though.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game whose shortcomings can be heavy to some.Important context: I picked up and played this game after the Quality of Life patch was added.I feel this is important as I believe a lot of negative experiences stem from things the patch addressed and fixed.This includes things such as:1. The Dash Button.   The dungeon designs are "dated" and very hallway-esque. This isn't a problem for an older person like myself who grew up on hallway-rpg designs from the PS2 era but it's worth mentioning all the same. Without the speed-up from the dash feature, I can see why the hallway designs would be annoying. This also allows you to more easily avoid random encounters when you're just trying to go from point A to B.2. The Fast Battle feature.  Animations at normal speed can last a bit longer than needed, especially the unusually long delays after an attack has finished. After you've seen everything so many times you just want to get through the battle as fast as you can without pausing for every animation, which is fixed with this addition.As for the actual shortcomings of the game as mentioned in the header, it all really just comes down to the DLC.The DLC questline is an entire story that supplements the main-story in a way that feels incredibly impossible to just separate and sell as an individual dlc. Between the new character, the added lvl 95~99 fight and leveling area, and the story itself being as important for context as the nibelheim flashbacks were for FF7, it's hard to recommend this game without the story DLC, which then leads to me saying:Wait for a sale. Not for the quality of the game itself, but because the the extra story DLC is important and I highly recommend you wait for a sale to justify the price of the main game + the dlc.Another minor issue is that the other iconic demons are in another DLC pack- and a major character from Soul Hackers 1 is in that dlc pack. This feels like a major step back from other SMT and SMT-Spinoff games which have better ways of including the previous games' protagonists.With that out of the way, I'm going to just end this review with a Pros and Cons list for simplicity.+Solid JRPG Story+Stylistic Design+Character Design and Character Personalities +Pacing and Flow of both story and gameplay(leveling, upgrades) is smooth.+Sabbaths are an interesting eye-candy mechanic that's both quick and satisfying to stack up.-Terrible DLC decisions-Overall Demon List is Lacking-Because they ripped the DLC story from the main game, there's a massive waste of opportunity with the DLC character who should have been integrated into the main story.-/+ If you have any idea what you're doing with fusion, you'll have an omni-negate demon for every member that covers everything they need by level 60 if not earlier. This could be a positive or a negative depending on who you ask so I figured it was worth mentioning.Either way: Get this game, it's great. Just wait for a sale because the dlc story is important.

_childDocuments_.review: If you can get this game at a decent price then I can comfortably say you're in for an experience that, while somewhat flawed, is still very much worth your time.There are a few things that I must address before going in-depth:While I didn't encounter any bugs or glitches, myself,  Atlus announced there is a patch to add some general fixes and QoL updates coming in the near future, so these issues may be fixed by then. I did the following for the best personal experience:-Under "Loading Screen Tips" set it to either "Hide" or "Button Advance". For whatever reason this shortens load screen times drastically.-Lock the frame rate to 60fps, as apparently higher/uncapped rates can break some animations.-Adjust the camera settings so Ringo is focused in the center and the camera zoom is further away.-Lower analogue stick sensitivity, as Ringo can be a little slippery to control.Soul Hackers 2 is a game I can say I personally enjoyed, but I can completely understand why others may be underwhelmed or disappointed by the final product. The fact that the first Soul Hackers is such a cult classic among RPG fans may also play a role in this game's mixed reception. As far as Shin Megami Tensei games go, it is a very mellow experience that has a lot of the pieces the series is known for but doesn't necessarily go very far with them, and as a result the game lacks the sense of scope that players familiar with the series may come to expect.If there's one thing I'm certain Soul Hackers 2 does very well, it's the presentation. The game is incredibly stylish and beautiful with its futuristic city environments, character designs, UI and VFX, as one would expect from a modern SMT/Atlus title. The music is also great with the Opening Theme, Weapons Shop, and the multiple Battle Themes being the highlights for me. The voice cast is also full of very solid performances. Outside of looking and sounding great, it's the rest of the game, itself where one's mileage may vary.As far as writing goes, I found the interactions among the main cast to be very enjoyable. Each party member is well fleshed out and they play off of each other very well, with Ringo and Saizo being my personal favourites. The other major characters also have some good interactions with them as well when it's their turn in the spotlight. The actual story, though, is rather lacking as far as JRPGs go. It has the pieces there to be something great, and there are a lot of compelling elements, themes, and interesting ideas that SMT is known for, however it feels like for most of the game that the story progresses just for the sake of moving the plot along.For most of the game I was more compelled to see the interactions between party members and piecing together each of their backstories and how they weave together, rather than being attached to the main plot. It was only really after the major twist regarding the main antagonist that I began to feel like things were really picking up and felt engaged to continue the story, and that's roughly three quarters into the game. Fortunately I do believe the game had a satisfying enough finale and a great final boss to go with it.The other thing that I feel a lot of people will be hit or miss on is the gameplay. Soul Hackers 2 is, in all intents and purposes, a Megami Tensei game, but it's a relatively simple Megami Tensei game. The core gameplay loop that makes SMT so addictive is all there: you explore dungeons to recruit demons, and eventually fuse those demons together to create stronger demons, allowing you to explore more dangerous dungeons. The battle system also features the series' trademark affinity system, with each demon/enemy having their own strengths and weaknesses against the different damage types in the game. It's one of personal favourite systems as far as turn-based RPGs go.On top of these staple features, battles in Soul Hackers 2 features the addition of the "Stack" system. On top of dealing bonus damage, attacking an enemy with their weakness grants a Stack. At the end of the player's turn Ringo performs an AoE attack and deals damage based on the amount of stacks gained during their turn. It's a very simple system, though in comparison to other battle mechanics present in other SMT games, it can feel rather shallow by comparison. Even as you progress through the game and gradually unlock more perks and abilities, the Stack system doesn't provide as much strategy to battles as the "Press Turn" system in mainline SMT or the "One More" system in Persona.While the battle system can feel hit-or-miss based on your preferences, the layout and dungeon design is probably the game's lowest point in nearly every aspect. While not necessarily bad (for the most part) they are considerably boring. Dungeons in Soul Hackers 2 go back to the maze-like hallway design of older RPGs and don't really bring anything interesting to the table. Compared to other recent entries in the series like SMT V's sprawling environments and Persona 5's unique palaces, it leaves a lot to be desiredIt also doesn't help that the environments are rather bland. The Soul Matrix, the area where you will likely spend most of your time leveling up and grinding, features 15 different floors, each one with the exact same music and background visuals (not even a change in colour scheme) and it gets very samey, very quick. The main story dungeons don't fare much better either, as they all boil down to the same idea of "abandoned urban environment" (two of which are abandoned subway lines) and all share the same music track, which detracts from giving each one their own sense of identity. The only exception is the final dungeon, which feels very distinct and interesting and features a unique music track that adds a lot to the atmosphere.All in all, the best way I can describe Soul Hackers 2 is that it's a very good game to introduce newcomers to Megami Tensei as a series. It features all the core elements and gameplay loop in a way that's easy to get the gist of. It isn't brutally difficult like Mainline SMT, and it isn't a massive time sink like Persona. It's just enough to give players a taste of everything this truly unique franchise of RPGs has to offer. That being said, do I recommend getting this game at full price? No, not really. I would still say wait until it goes on sale for like half off. If you can get this game at a decent price then I can comfortably say you're in for an experience that, while somewhat flawed, is still very much worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: >>****Game runs flawlessly on the Steam Deck on high > very high stable 50+ FPS using latest GE Proton version****<<Steam Deck Performance - 10/10PC Performance - 10/10Gameplay - 8/10Graphics - 5.5/10Style & Sound - 10/10Story - 7.5/10>>**To start off, this game is NOT Persona, and is not part of that series, despite being SMT.  This game is from a part of SMT that is far closer to its original incarnations as a dungeon crawler.  If you are expecting Persona, this isn't it. **<<Music and art style are really high points here and make up for  the otherwise rather basic graphics that this brings to the table. That being said, those basic graphics are also somewhat of a blessing, as it gives the game incredible performance on the Steam Deck and any middle-range PC system. On my main desktop with a 3080...not so much. Gameplay is about what you expect, though it has less emphasis on demon hunting than I expected of it, as most SMT games have a pretty heavy emphasis on the demons.  This game has a lot more emphasis on the characters themselves which is an interesting twist compared to other games from this branch of the series.  Combat is varied and tactical and is a real highlight. It is turn based but highly customizable. Storyline is heavy, with lots of cutscenes and voice acted dialogue. Characters are very colourful and charming, story is bright but with a side of strange nihilism, many of the characters you meet and recruit are people who were murdered, if that gives any indication of the tone of the world. Overall I recommend this game for fans of SMT, if you enjoy classic SMT and dungeon crawling you will enjoy this. If you're expecting the next gen game to max out your high end PC hardware with AAA big budget graphics and massive open worlds....well, you wont find that here. This is a JRPG through and through, so as long as you set your expectations properly you wont be disappointed.My biggest gripe with this game is that the DLC is sort of BS. Overpriced and silly. It's worth noting this game also has Denuvo anti-piracy, which I think is also unnecessary and punishes legitimate customers for buying games. If these things turn you off of the game, I wont blame you for it.A recommended buy when on sale or if you can find it for less than the $79.99 asking price elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s alright. There is a part of the game where, once you complete a dungeon that takes place in a subway system, you have to go right back into another full length subway dungeon. This is just bad game design, plain and simple. Revisiting dungeons is fine when these visits are spaced out enough as to not make the player bored, but there was no effort made to space these dungeons out at all. Additionally, the Soul Matrix is bland and uninteresting. It’s just a sea of blue cubes meant to be all hacker themed, which is fine, but the Soul Matrix is meant to be done over the course of the game. Nothing about this dungeon changes at all between floors, or depending on whose Soul Matrix it is. This is only two dungeons I really had a problem with, sure the others weren’t super interesting but they were at least fine. I liked the dungeon where you kept getting into forced encounters that drained your MP, as it forced you to defeat the group of enemies with limited resources. In terms of combat, the combat system was fine. It was fun enough, but not as fun as mainline SMT or Persona. The main thing is Sabbath attacks that occur at the end of every player turn if you strike a weakness. Each attack that strikes a weakness adds a stack to this attack, and you can unlock ways to get more stacks depending on the element used or by certain commander skills. There is some satisfaction in getting very high stacks and dealing some massive damage, though the damage never seemed really significant to me, even when using every demon in my stock. Though maybe that’s just me, either way it’s still fun, but that’s all there really is to the combat. Other than that it’s SMT. The story was alright, definitely a step up from SMT V. I haven’t finished the story because frankly I got bored once I had to mandatorily revisit the Soul Matrix, so I can’t comment much on it. There are some twists and turns, the characters are enjoyable (except Mimi), and the English voice acting is aight. Again, haven’t finished the story because again, boring dungeon made me bored. Grinding in this game isn’t bad at all, as the meal system provides meals that can give you even more EXP from fighting higher level enemies. Meals can increase stats or buff your party in some way, and wear off when you leave whatever dungeon you enter. These meals aren’t hard to get, and you’ll likely end up with more than you need just from your allies giving them to you. The meal system is pretty neat and adds some level of strategization when preparing for a boss. There’s a hangout system where, after certain events or sidequests, you unlock a hangout event where you get to talk to one or some characters at the bar. These are kind of neat, but if you don’t care about them you don’t have to do them. Overall this game is just alright. Buy it on sale if you’re interested as this game isn’t really worth the $60. I haven’t covered every element of this game, mostly just the things that stood out to me as good or bad. It’s an alright game but it could have been better.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot to love with Soul Hackers 2, the music, the setting, the characters and the story stands out from the usual defeat god ending which plagues a lot of the Shin Megami Tensei games. The Sabbath/Stack system also adds a new depth to the turn based formula, rewarding players for exploiting weaknesses by having a special end of turn attack damage all enemies based on how well you performed.Now with that being said, the start to this game is brutal. Incredibly slow, tutorial heavy and railroady. You don't even get to sprint in this game. Around 5 hours in you could potentially unlock a slight jog as a skill but that's the best you'll get. Also the biggest issue for me is how some elemental affinities have been removed. This makes the majority of demons feel the same, which has always been an issue with the Shin Megami Tensei games.Even with these issues though I would still recommend playing Soul Hackers 2 however you will need a little patience in the first couple of hours.For my full Review of Soul Hackers 2 check out my video here:

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 feels rushed under-cooked in almost every regard. The story is stretched paper thin, and the game time is padded to death due to difficulty spikes and ridiculously expensive upgrades that force grinding. The dungeons are vast hallways of emptiness, and what little unique designs exist are reused immediately.The combat system seemed interesting on the surface but it's incredibly shallow. You start with no ability to swap demons in battle and each demon can only use 3 moves. Eventually  you can be upgraded to allow swapping and up to 6 demon moves. You also end up with passive perks that end up funneling your party members into specific elements. Some of the passives can be used to fight more creatively, but its still not much. Saizo can be upgraded to have a chance of stunning enemies when he uses gun attacks. Ringo can have a chance of going twice. Milady can unlock a 0 sp almighty move that can restore sp. It's really not much.The most unique battle mechanic is the "sabbath" end of turn attack. You increase its power by hitting enemies weaknesses and then at the end of the turn it unleashes. But that's it. You have one unique mechanic at the cost of much better battle systems.There are 3 dungeons in the Axis that are all the same boring padded dungeons5 dungeons in the real world and 3 of them are slightly altered versions of the others.The dungeons themselves are shockingly empty. The only thing you MIGHT see is your demons sitting around offering items or negotiations for other demons to join you. The game is pure grind. Grind to level up because every stat point matters. Grind to get money because EVERY upgrade is outrageously expensive.Probably my biggest problem with the game is the disappointing story. I can't explain it all without spoiling it. It started off fine and had one good small twist but then it keeps going and gets really dumb. The jrpg genre is typically known for its really good stories so I don't know who dropped the ball here.I do not recommend this game unless it's on sale and you're out of other rpgs to play.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I'm using the version of the game including all DLCs. Like I usually would have done, I cheesed it and level grinded my party to 99 early on, so I've been able to auto-battle most stuff. This was made easier by the fact that one of the DLCs lets you toggle the dropping of level-boosting items from each encounter, but I would have done the same thing even if it took me longer, so it was really just a timesaver. A friend who's also playing it has taken about the same amount of playtime to reach where I am now while barely using the DLC content, so I imagine it must not be that difficult of a game compared to mainline SMT.Story, and especially characters, are top-notch. I never want to play a silent SMT protag again after this. In contrast to Persona (except P2:EP), all the main cast are adults and have adult problems and deal with them in a mostly-adult manner. I played with the English dub, which was excellent, although I'm planning to do NG+ with Japenese audio to compare. The graphics are also excellent, in my personal, amateurish evaluation. The music - done by MONACA, the people who did the music for the Nier series and Drakengard 3 - is also great, aside from one or two tracks that I felt were repetitive. The weakest point is probably the mostly-optional side-dungeon design, which is very same-y. The layouts of the dungeons are fixed, and early dungeons are pretty straightforward, but later dungeons have gimmicks. All in all, although I haven't beaten it to 100% completion yet, I like the game a lot and would definitely recommend it!If you're starting out, however, you'll want to adjust certain options in the config menu from the title screen before you start, since you won't be able to actually access the in-game menu until partway through the tutorial level. Namely:-Set Ringo to center instead of left screen-Make the camera distance further from her-Set Loading Screen Tips to display (button advance), which will remove 90% of load screen time

_childDocuments_.review: Starting this off with the fact that I normally enjoy Atlus RPGs and will defiantly be picking up Persona 5 and 3 when released with my previous experience being with Persona 3,4 and Shin Megami 2 which were amazing games that I got hooked on instantly. Saying that soul hackers 2 wasn’t the case from the beginning and is now the same if not worse 30 hours in.The first key point for these types of games for me is generally the story and characters with a mix of good combat mechanics that come together for an enjoyable experience. With this game, the biggest problem is, that it all feels stale and bland with the story being simple boring and overall super predictable from the base story or the side story from learning the characters' pasts through the dungeons. The characters in this game also fit the story point of being one-dimensional and just not interesting at all not keeping me there, with this being one of the few games where I was just skipping through the conversations. Dungeon design is extremely simple which is honestly the case for Persona 3/4, but these games stem from the generation of the ps2 while this game is a 2022 release a lot of the dungeons feel the same as walking down a tunnel or corridor and being generally outdated. The graphics are ok for this type of game but seem very pixelated even at max setting at 1440p but are passable, I guess as the game's performance seems good across the board using a 3080 and on the steam deck (do not change the resolution or get locked out for 24 hours recommended to play at high for best overall experience).The one point of the game that stands out over everything else would be the combat that again is like previous games which were good anyway but includes a stacking system that isn’t partially new or amazing but is a nice addition. Demons and monster collecting is enjoyable and fusing but again is something they’ve done well through their franchises and as such is good in this.After getting to the 30-hour point heading into the last arc with all the side quests to this point done apart from the 4th-floor matrix collection quests that are honestly unenjoyable I’ve decided to drop this game as overall it’s just extremely boring and hasn’t grabbed me at any points, so I honestly wouldn’t recommend this game even at £30 which is what I spent and not at full asking price with the day one DLC implementation being embarrassing (if you haven't just go and buy persona 4 or wait for 3/5).

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, but looking at other reviews, there appear to be some misconceptions/misinformation.- First off, if you bought DLC, you DO have it. You will NOT be able to access some of it until LATER on in the game (which makes sense because some of it is higher level than what you start as.) You do not need to buy DLC to enjoy this game. If day one DLC upsets you, don't buy it. I also want to point out that you can get the game cheaper on sites like Fanatical if the price is putting you off from it. - Under settings, you can turn on the unlimited XP and gold items after each fight if you have that. I had the option to do this pretty early on. The game doesn't tell you this.- I do not have my Steam Deck yet, but some people are posting about issues with it. I don't see where this game says it is Steam Deck verified, so play at your own risk.Now, onto the actual game review. It's pretty good from what I have played. _childDocuments_.review: You're probably going to regret buying this at full price. I enjoyed the game, quite a bit, and I still regret buying it at full price. It starts off somewhat rocky, but after it lets you off the leash, the game becomes really fun. And then after a while, it just becomes disappointing. Although I have to admit, I was disappointed right at the get-go.If you were expecting a sequel to Soul Hackers 1, from the words 'Soul Hackers' and the number 2 in the title, then you'll be disappointed. This game owes more to persona 5 than any game in the devil summoner series. Whats the difference you might ask? Devil summoner games are usually first person dungeon crawlers where the player starts out weak and then evolve into a gun toting, sword swinging, demon summoning badass. Soul Hackers 2, meanwhile, is a 3rd person dungeon crawler where you fight demons as a party of 4 unique characters who deepen their friendship over the course of the story. Sound familiar? But that was only the start of my disappointments.The artstyle of the game is really good. Very pretty, good character designs, the works. The thing about it, though, and it might take you a while to realise this, when it comes to graphics, the game is pretty ♥♥♥♥. The environment looks pretty dated, character models don't emote very much, and they recycle almost all of the attack effects. Animation is pretty weak in general in this game, the most notable example being Ringo's walk cycle. It's rather stiff and somewhat awkward, and since she's the main character, this is probably going to end up bothering you a lot.Voice acting is pretty alright overall. The 4 leads have pretty decent voice acting, but Ringo's voice acting is just a bit off. Most of the time it'll be fine, but there's certain times where the quality dips. And again, since she's the main character, this is going to end up bothering you a lot. Music is alright too, not really any notable tracks.The gameplay is normal SMT fare, with the notable absence of light and dark instant kill spells. That means that random mobs won't randomly one-shot you, which is nice, I guess, and that's about it as far as gameplay differences go. Dark spells are debuffs, and they also do damage and exploit weaknesses so it's not bad. Building up the 4 characters is also pretty engaging, because the materials you need to upgrade them aren't always found in the same dungeon, so you'll upgrade different affinities at different times. You'll never really need to farm if you keep up with axis unlocks. The axis is the main side dungeon, basically, and you clear it out for some pretty nice character buffs. The issue with the axis, though, is that you'll be going there a lot, the scenery never changes, and it's used to pad out the rest of the game. The main issue with Soul Hackers 2 is that it's really not a long game, but it makes itself feel like it's much longer. I have just finished the game with 60 hours, 50% of which was spent in the axis, 25% I spent on loading screens, and probably 25% I spent in the actual story and story dungeons. There's just not a lot of content, and around the halfway mark, you'll notice things repeating themselves. As for the story itself, it's alright. There's a really actually quite solid (if somewhat cliche) twist in the lategame, sandwiched between 1 ok twist and another twist that's pretty poorly built up. The characters are alright and they get more fleshed out over the course of the plot, though they start off pretty one-dimensional. I'd give the story a passing grade, for whatever it's worth, considering you won't interact with it much. Though I should note that I almost didn't bother finishing the game because it was just so samey by the end dungeon, but I figured I might as well have just bitten the bullet.Overall, this is kind of a disappointing game for something that has the balls to say that it's full price. If you really want to play something like this you might as well just play Persona 4 Golden, which has more content AND a better story, and it's only about a 3rd of what Soul Hackers 2 is selling for. If you really, really, really want to play this, I'd wait for a sale. This isn't really a must-play game, especially considering P5R is coming out on PC in october.

_childDocuments_.review: A handful of flaws, but a solid game otherwise.If you go into this game with the lens of it's not gonna be as great as mainline SMT or Persona, it's actually quite fun. I loved the characters, thought the camera work and animation were wonderful (on top of the fact that, according to what I've seen, this is the first game where ATLUS ACTUALLY ANIMATED ENGLISH LIP SYNCING, HELL FREAKING YES), enjoyed the combat (though some of it needs work, namely enemy balance and the amount of grinding you need to to), and the story was nice and had plenty of good writing in it.HOWEVERIt is far from glorious. Some of the dungeons (especially in the endgame) are horribly designed and made me legit look up a guide just to navigate through them, which for basic map design with zero puzzles should not happen. The game forces you to grind a lot, which is thankfully easier to do with the character Axes areas, but it's still a drag. And I played this game before they released the QoL update, which took over TWO MONTHS to come out and adds damn near necessities for a JRPG, like a freaking RUN BUTTON.It has its flaws, major and minor. But the people who say it's the worst thing ever are very much exaggerating it. I enjoyed the game as a fresh, new experience, using the demons I loved from SMT and the gameplay design of ATLUS I've known for years. I think it could've been great, but some of the decisions they made regarding endgame stuff and the flow not really having a hook to it (I lost motivation to play this game 4 times over the course of 2 months, most good games I finish I only lose motivation to do so one time, if at all) shot the game down in the end. Again, it's still good, but could be a lot better. 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The good: It is more STM sub series finally onto PC and not as some console exclusive, fun combat.The expected meh: comes with the series: Being a STM sub series it can be grindy for certain things like "oh you want this upgrade well you need 5 of these items from this enemy in this area, there is a 10% chance you get the enemy you need and then a 25% chance you get the item drop you need and you have to do it till you get all 5.The unexpected meh: The dungeons are just like the early games of the series of being basically copy paste which you expect in a randomly generated map, very samey. Which if this was released after say Persona 3 then yeah it would be expected but with more modern STM and sub series games having much better maps going back 10 years of updates is unexpected.###UPDATE###NOTE: The god awful loading times are a result of the loading screen tips, if you disable the loading screen tips the loading times are almost instant and if you switch it from auto next tip to button press next tip then you can also skip the way to long load screen, which in turn makes this "The bad" I have a feeling that maybe the options of "auto/button press/off" maybe had a translation flaw but the wording in the options makes it sound like it is between "off/ auto going to next tip/ button press to next tip" and not "off/ auto exit loading screen after too long of a time/ exit the loading screen almost instantly but only after pressing a button so you can see the tip before it goes away". Either way just turn off auto advance and select either "off" or "button advance" and the load times are perfectly acceptable.### END UPDATE###The bad: The ungodly amount of load screens to do any preparation, and even on my quickest SSD they are not short load times either, a good 15-20 seconds which may not sound like much until you realize "travel to weapon shop" load screen, "travel to accessory shop" load screen travel to item shop, load screen, travel to the equivalent of the Velvot Room load screen,  go to safehouse to recover MP/HP load screen, and when you teleport to a shop you don't teleport directly in you teleport outside so each time includes a few short load times as well.The ugly: Multiple demons locked behind DLCAll in all I am enjoying the game because I love SMT style combat, but boy does it have some weird design decisions. I will say recommended under the pretense that you expect a good-ish game from an otherwise great developer and do not expect the same level of care in this series as their bigger name Persona sub series. It is fun to play, it is worth a buy but it is not a "must buy" either, it needs a lot of optimizing and re balancing before I would say you need to play it but it is not a THPS5 cash grab dessaster, it still is a fun game even if flawed.

_childDocuments_.review: As no doubt most reviews by now mention, when you first launch the game go to config -> gameplay and change the loading screen prompt either to button display if you want recaps or to none. None will change your loading screen times from roughly 8 to 10 seconds down to near instantly.Additionally worth mentioning is that the lack of costumes outside of battles can be fixed very quickly and easily with  mod. Keep in mind there are clipping issues here and there, but that's on Atlus. Not the modder!Now on to the actual review.If you are used to the length of Persona games you will be disappointed. Soul Hackers 2 takes as long to beat as your average mainline game. The game has 2 endings and a NG+ mode. Keep in mind, all NG+ does is add a few tougher quests and is intended for those that don't want to save scum to see the second ending or play the game on a tougher difficulty again.My first playthrough has been on  and while I enjoy the difficulty spike, some of the game's features don't account for the difficulty. You will find yourself biting your teeth out on Risky Enemies (always 10 levels higher than you) and foes going into enraged mode during challenge fights due to turn limits that don't take the lack of damage or HP sponges into consideration.Instead of the press turn system you are used to you are greeted by a stack system that deals damage at the end of your turn instead of letting you go again when you hit a weakness and depending on Ringo's abilities as well that of your demons unlocks additional perks such as free healing or applying status effects on enemies. I for one welcome the change in the formula and enjoyed my time with the system and trying to find ways to make full use of it.The story follows a more mature theme and unlike the depressingly lack of depth SMT5 had, the writing is servicable once again with characters being fleshed out. Albeit predictable at times, you will build an emotional connection not only with your party members but foes and temporary guests alike.The biggest downfall and gripe you should have with the product being sold to you comes no doubt from the atrocious DLC policy. Opposed to the claims Atlus made (companies lying, what's new?) the story dlc starts as early as you getting access to fusions and a recommended level of 8. The chain continues through the entirety of the game and is not limited to post game content at all.Not only does the boss demon pack break the balance of the game being readily available in your compendium without Macca charge or level restriction attached, it cuts out prominent and popular demons you normally find in any SMT game as of late. Nemissa being a part of it felt almost as dirty as seeing a stable meme like Mara being a selling point.Costumes should have been useable outside of combat by default and having to rely on a mod to fix the laziness of the developers isn't something to be happy about either.All things considered, the base game is well worth it's money especially if you bought it from one of Atlus' trusted partners. The premium edition is vastly overpriced and while I don't entirely regret shilling out for the DLC it will leave a lingering taste of salt and regret over cut content in my mouth for a while. Whether or not you speak with your wallet and avoid the dlc is your choice.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad I waited for the QoL update so I could sprint through dungeons, because oh my god is the dungeon design tedious. I hope you like long, blue-tinted corridors because that's essentially all you're getting. You'll also be revisiting most areas multiple times if you plan to do all the sidequests/get the "good" ending.Battles are your standard Persona/SMT style turn-based combat, so unless you're very into those you won't get much else out of them.I mostly play JRPGs for the characters and the story though, so I'd have been able to forgive the lackluster dungeon design if I really loved those. But I didn't. Saizo, Arrow, and Milady were all fine. Not particularly exciting, although it was nice that they were adults who had adult lives. Ringo... was not as great as I was led to believe from all the reviews. Not offensive in any way, but not particularly great either.That's about all I can say for the characters. I loathed Figue, but that was almost a given. The story and worldbuilding made no sense. Everybody just blindly accepted the exposition dumps about an all-knowing AI, the conflict was basic and unnuanced, the final villain and their motivation made me roll my eyes (although the villain before that wasn't any better). It seems very clear to me that Arrow was meant to be the protagonist at one point, with how the story centered around him as much as it did, but he wasn't any more fleshed out than the others.I also wish I'd gone with my gut for the "normal" ending. Doing all the dungeons and sidequests just for that cheesy "good" ending was not worth it. It was actively worse than the normal ending for me. But I guess by the time I got to that point, I just so done with the game I wanted everything to burn. Incidentally, you can't do everything on the first run. You have to do a NG+. Which I will never touch.

_childDocuments_.review: This is how I like it. It's how I roll, okay? I enjoy crawling dungeons. I'm a dungeon-crawler kinda guy. I'm borderline and hypersensitive and what not, and thus I absolutely love miles upon miles of twisting and turning corridors, repeating similar battles ad nauseam, things that occupy my fingers and the ever-terrified lizard part of my brain so I can distract the mammal part of my brain with the music and finally let my human-brain ponder things almost the same way the normal people do. Having said that, Soul Hackers has actually managed to tire me out somewhere around the finale. And, mind you, some time ago I've spent 200 hours plus crawling Mary Skelter and loved nearly every second of it. And there was Legend of Grimrock just before that. And Vaporum. Have I already mentioned I was into dungeon crawlers?My problem with Soul Hackers is not that it involves an abundance of dungeoning. That's is one of the things  I came here for. The minor issue is that most of the locations are not particularly inspired. Shipping districts with lots of crates, abandoned construction sites, subway tunnels. All of these mercilessly recycled. There are at least two dungeons of each of those kinds, all of them consisting of multiple floors. But the absolute beast here is the Axis. It's a (mostly optional. But if you know your Shin Megamis then you must realize that skipping optionals is not an option) Gibson's cyberpunk virtual reality themed dungeon consisting of 12 (more on NG+!) mazelike floors that all look exactly the same. And if that wasn't enough, they employ an extensive use of portals when you reach the final levels. Not one or two portals per level but a sizable archipelago of islands interconnected by a network of teleporters that not necessarily make an immediate sense, require the memorization of where they lead and sometimes don't allow going back without taking a lengthy trek or teleporting entirely out of the dungeon and starting over. Luckily, there are a few fast travel points that somewhat remedy the situation. And as far as I know there is no separate map besides the mini-map projected onscreen as the party crawls.The thing is, I owe it to Shin Megamis a lot on lots of grounds and music is one of them. See, when it comes to such lengthy campaigns it is inevitable that sooner or later, and with the notable exception of Yakuzas, I will get bored with the soundtrack and switch to an external provider. And as fate would have it, it is always over the final dungeon of a Shin Megami game that I discover some of the best tunes. I've got Tanooki Suit from Persona4, Jess and the Ancient Ones while running kalpas in Nocturne, Sulfur Giants on a loop four or five hours straight, and Hackers had me discover Rave the Reqviem. But this was supposed to be a paragraph about Hacker's music, right? It's fine and dandy. Fits the mood, and stuff. Go, check Jess, Tanooki and Reqviem out. The characters are medium-lovable. Their backstories are the same old. There are also some heavily questionable, logic-bending actions towards the conclusion of the story, some unnecessarily theatrical screaming and some traditional JRPG exaggeration. But besides that, they are actually charming. During my 60 plus hours with Hackers, the way they interacted, hinted and commented each other's actions during the battles never got old. The little events in the local bar (the game has over 40 of those) while rather predictable, were still fun to witness. And the change and development they all undergo during the events of the game is - if you're willing to listen to their stories - actually quite impressive. Also there's Ringo, the game's protagonist and one of the better Shin Megami characters. First of all, she is not your typical SMT silent lead. She has both voice and personality. She is witty, upbeat and curious. She is also basically an anthropomorphized splinter of a macrocomputer superconsciousness overseering the humanity and there is a graceful explanation as to why such an entity would basically downgrade itself to meat and bone. L-l-look at you, Shodan, how the tables have turned...Also! The demons are really well written. There is this clever, little gimmick that instead of looking for the chests lying randomly around the dungeon, you send your demons out and they wait for you with items around the map. The Vile family deserves a special mention with their "Uhh, this thing will absolutely help the team.. W-w-wait how long have you been standing there listening?! DON'T tell anyone or I will have to kill you!" lines. You know, Viles? The evil guys.Also! Also! Most of the sidequests are of the standard go / kill / fetch variety but some of them are wrapped in a truly brilliant narration. Just forget the whole koala gig, it's better that way. I did. In all honesty, I have no idea what this koala business is all about. Found it in my notes for this review, reminding me to forget about it.            It's a Shin Megami, what did you expect? The mechanics are solid, there's hundreds of demons to be caught, and the usual rock-paper-scissors of the elements is present. If you know your SMTs you'll be at home and if you don't, you'd do best by starting somewhere else. P4 or 5 preferably, maybe Nocturne. Basically, any other main game. This one is for the folks who have drained all the other possibilities and still want more Atlusverse. Anyways. Hackers is slightly on a lite side. It's easier, more colorful and definitely less edgy than your usual SMT. Yes, of course there's the fate of humanity at the stake, but it's somewhere in the background. It's definitely not as soul - crushingly dark as Survivors or Nocturne. That is, if you find the complete extinction of humanity on a Biblical scale dark, I realize opinions may vary on this one. Nonetheless. The battles are significantly less challenging than I'd expected. Take the Sabbath mechanism. Every time a party member hits demon's weakness, it adds to the stack which in turn results in an all-out attack performed by the end of the turn which occurs when all of the party members finish their actions. Moreover, there is no similar punishment for enemies hitting the party's weaknesses. And, while I am far from calling it a hindrance, saving is available at all times outside of the battle.      Sixty hours plus cut short, Hackers is the definition of a mixed bag. Sure, it's only a solid Megami, but that's still a viable way of wasting some hundred hours of your lifetime away. Yes, it's not a legendary like Personas or Nocturne. Or Strange Journey. It has its ups and downs, but there are some really nice ideas and honest, heartfelt moments every now and then. Still, the DLCs are coldheartedly greedy and atrocious. If he was alive, Freud would definitely have had a thing or two to say about locking Mara inside a paywall cage like that. Best course of action, 60% discount or higher, no DLCs and only if you've already completed Nocturne and at least one Persona. I have spoken.      * had no idea for paragraph tiles, used the names of my playlists As always, thank you for reading this farand, as always,

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 feels like an Atlus game from 15-20 years ago, not a brand new game that just released in 2022 at full price AND with a day one DLC.The story has been okay so far. A nice mix of sci-fi + SMT esoteric fantasy stuff. It's not been anything too interesting so far, but that might change later. Characters are fine for the most part, with Ringo being a major standout with how great she is (especially with Japanese VA). In terms of storytelling and character development it's a major step above SMT, but (aside from Ringo) never quite reaches the heights of Persona or Atlus other story focused works.The aesthetic is great. The neon cyberpunk styles and city is a cool setting. The OST is good overall (but again, still falls a bit short of Persona or SMT) and the cutscenes are all really well doneThe gameplay is simplistic yet fun. The big twist with the game is that with every weakness you hit on an enemy, you get a "stack". At the end of your turn, you unleash every "stack" as a massive attack. It's very satisfying. If you're an experienced megaten fan you'll probably find it way too easy, as enemies never take opportunity attacks on you, nor can they build stacks like you can. This makes SH2 a good entry into the overall series, but might leave experienced fans a little bored.Now, the issuesFirst, Soul Hackers 2's dungeons are AWFUL. Genuinely some of the worst dungeons I've had to suffer in a JRPG in a long time and it feels like a massive step back for Atlus. Remember Persona 5's amazing palaces? Or SMTV's open world design? Well, SH2 goes back to old Atlus dungeon design: long, narrow hallways with no decorations, no interactable items or treasure chests, no puzzles and LOTS of dead ends and backtracking. It's terrible and mind numbingly boring.On top of that, Ringo moves so, so slowly through these hallway dungeons so not only are you bored out of your mind because there is nothing in the dungeon besides you and some easy enemies, but it takes twice as long to get through as it should.It actually blows my mind. I've seen 30 year old games with better dungeons than Soul Hackers 2. I've seen DS games with better dungeons than Soul Hackers 2. The fact that they just threw in maze like, dull empty hallways and decided to call them "dungeons", then charge 60 dollars for it is an insult.Which brings me to the second major issue: the price. Soul Hackers 2 is not a 60 dollar game (70 dollars if you decide to buy the day one DLC), nor is it anywhere near the quality of other Atlus titles. This is very much a throwaway game made by Atlus' C team (supposedly the same guys that made TMS) while the rest of Atlus works on Persona 6.If I had paid 30 or 40 dollars for this, I would have likely been willing to overlook it's issues. But I paid 70 dollars for the deluxe edition because I was expecting the general quality and polish you expect when you buy a game with the "Atlus" logo. This isn't even in the same dimension as ANY of the Personas or SMT's. It feels cheap and half-assed. It's the first Atlus game I genuinely regret buying.Overall, it's not a bad game, but its really not great either. Maybe worth it if you can get it at a steep discount, or if you're really hungry for more megaten, but I wouldn't recommend it otherwise

_childDocuments_.review: I am rewriting my review as I've beaten it and am no longer in my honeymoon period for this game, alongside me just feeling the original was not that good in the first place. A quick and short answer for me is "Buy if it's on sale and you're interested".In personal opinion the story and characters are very solid and well-built. They don't ever feel like an annoyance nor make me want to roll my eyes, which was something i was terrified was going to happen pre-launch. The combat in this game is an altered form of SMT's typical combat: Instead of the staple "Press Turn" fighting, it's instead normal turn-based with the added element of "Sabbaths", which is a large attack based on the accumulated Stacks you got from exploiting weaknesses. The system itself feels very one-sided and unfair, which made this game typically easy even in hard mode. It would be slightly better if the opponents could do the same, at the very least the summoner bosses, but none do that as it's a plot element that Ringo is the only one who can. It can be exploited even more as you delve farther into the Soul Matrix's of each character as you get Stack bonuses too. Recruitment is also something different, as there isn't talking options during battles; instead, you recruit them in the field from your other demons finding them. I think this system is ok in all honesty: it's incredibly easy to recruit them in this game, as almost all of them only need a singular item to be completely fine with joining. The music was honestly very good throughout the game, however there isn't many tracks in it(which is probably why they have a music dlc in the first place). For the most part you should be expecting to hear the same few songs alot.Dungeons in this game are very straightforward and sometimes incredibly annoying once you reach the third floors and beyond for Soul Matrix's. Something to note as well is that there's no treasure boxes in this game, you only find items from your demons.Quests can be very binary in which it's basically either just a slaying mission or a collecting one.A complaint i can also quickly think of is how animations can look very stiff and unnatural.Despite a lot of the flaws this game is presented with, i still thoroughly enjoyed it throughout the duration i played. It definitely feels like they needed to at least delay it a bit more to sharpen the edges it has, but it is what it is. The game gave me alot of similar charm to the original SH which made me really happy too. I can recommend this game if it ever gets a sale, but you should probably avoid the DLC as nothing is really needed and it's all very overpriced for what it is.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot to complain in this game, but I'll be somewhat brief by focusing myself on the major thing that can at least allow you to endure the rest of the game. Like, for example, their previous game: Shin Megami Tensei V; which had an enjoyable (but still flawed) battle system, while having a mediocre (if not nonexistant) story. A disappointing game, yet not one I dropped. For your information, I played a fair share of Shin Megami Tensei and Persona titles already; my review will be based on these standards and knowledge. Let's talk "battle mechanics".Shin Megami Tensei/Persona games are reknowned for their iteration of the PressTurn system, be it variations of it, or unique branches like the OneMore system in Persona. Mechanics that allow you, AND your enemy, to accentuate the need of utilizing weakness to capitalize the number of turns. Discovering weaknesses, focusing on them, multiplying turns, disabling theirs of the adversary, but also available for your enemies... In short, a double-edged, (variably) complex but rewarding system, that can be used by you OR your foes; an equal foot for everyone.Now, Soul Hackers 2, and the Sabbath mechanic: hit weaknesses to boost an obligatory "big" attack at the end of *every* turn. That is all. No real variation, nor an enemy version. Not something to plan, but something automatic, and one-sided. A sadly simple and boringly linear mechanic that becomes uninteresting and impressively repetitive by the 10th fight. Adding to that the (pretty cool but) annoyingly long animation —and I repeat: EVERY turn— that you will start to —by the 10th fight— to skip. And that, is why I can't bring myself to continue this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is the definition of unfulfilled potential.This game is what you get if you take the modern Atlus formula and boil the elements down to their most barebones, basic forms.  Demon negotiation is here, but instead of being able to talk to demons in combat and persuade them to join you, you'll get the chance to recruit them occasionally in dungeons by just talking to one of your demons who found them for you.  And instead of having to discuss things with the demons, they just state a price up front (sometimes that price is free) and you can pay it and they'll always join you, or you can say no and they leave.  There is no way to mess up or fail negotiations, and the demons are always 100% honest.Remember social links from the Persona games?  Well, what you have here is "soul level", which is a number that can go up to 100 (200 in NG+) which you can increase by making dialogue choices during the story or during hangouts at the local bar.  It doesn't matter which dialogue choices you pick, the only thing that happens is that one of your party member's soul level will increase.  Your party members are supposed to have opposed philosophies but there's never any friction outside of what's already scripted.  Not even a "X didn't like that" message.  The bar hangouts are likewise disappointing.  They are mostly inane chitchat.  There just isn't much narrative meat to them.The press turn system is here... mostly.  But it's been simplified too.  This part is a bit of a mixed bag.  The hama and mudo instant death skills are gone, replaced with the "ruin" element that deals status effects.  This could be an interesting shakeup to the formula.  But combat is too easy for it make much different.  Instead of getting extra turns for hitting weaknesses, or knocking down enemies and preventing them from acting, what you get is a mechanic called the stack counter.  As you hit more weaknesses, your stack counter goes up, and at the end of the turn your demons pull of a big attack called a sabbath that does damage to the enemies based on how high your stack meter is.  It's kind of like an all-out attack ala Persona 5, but without the strategy.  It's basically free damage at the end of your turn.  There are some tough optional bosses that make good use of this mechanic but otherwise it trivializes combat entirely and offers nothing in return.That's the story of Soul Hackers 2.  Everything has been simplified to the point that the game doesn't really feel like an Atlus game.  It feels like a generic JRPG with a sprinkling of Atlus's usual elements here and there.  All the rough edges of an the Atlus formula have been smoothed away, leaving behind something bland and not that interesting.  This isn't a bad game per se but if you're played a few SMT or Persona games in the past this is going to feel lackluster in comparison.  I would recommend this primarily as an introduction to the series, or maybe even JRPGs in general.  Otherwise, though, Soul Hackers 2 doesn't have enough to leave a veteran player satsified.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually went into this game rather hopeful about it, despite its mediocre reviews. After playing 50ish hours and getting all the achievements, I can confidently say that my hope was completely misplaced. Giving credit where credit is due, I actually really liked the characters, at least those in your party. Their interactions are all pretty solid, and each character has a decent amount of development. The optional bar hangout events are a fun little way to show off more of each character separate from the main story. Ringo is a really good protagonist, and I really appreciate the characterization that comes with her being an actual character rather than just a silent representation of the player (don’t get me wrong, I love the Persona protagonists but the change of pace is nice). The music is also really good (with one caveat that I’ll mention below). There are a lot of very solid songs, especially ones in the various shops you can visit. I also think that the stack system is an interesting idea, and definitely distinguishes itself from the “one more” system in Persona or the “press turn” system from Shin Megami Tensei. I also absolutely adore how in-depth fusions are in this game, and all the functions for searching made fusing demons incredibly convenient.And now for the bad. The story is very uninteresting, and at times felt like a genuine chore to get through. Nothing interesting or unique in the slightest. The dungeons are also pretty darn terrible. By themselves, they are *okay*. However, combined with the fact that each dungeon uses the same generic theme, they all feel exactly the same even though they were in different locations. I cannot emphasize enough just how much worse off the game is for this. I compare this aspect of the game to another one by Atlus; Shin Megami Tensei III: Nocturne. That game has a unique theme for most of its dungeons, and that gives each one a very unique identity. Every time you enter a new location, the music changes to reflect this, and it gives each area a very unique and distinct feeling. Now take Soul Hackers 2; where all of the game’s dungeons share the same song. Each location feels incredibly similar and it makes the entire experience of playing through the dungeons very tedious. The optional Soul Matrices (which are unfortunately required for all the achievements) are also very boring; they all take place in the same location with the same generic song and with no interesting or fun puzzles to make playing them feel interesting. Progressing in these Soul Matrices offers skills to choose from, but the game is easy enough where I never felt I needed them.I wanted to enjoy this game. I really, really did. But for a game made by Atlus, a studio whose games I always love, it all felt so generic. The pros were heavily outweighed by the cons, and the game was downright miserable at times. The only enjoyment I had while playing this game was from the TV I was watching at the time, and that is very disappointing to me. I wouldn’t recommend this one unless you 1: get it at an extremely low price on sale, and 2: are extremely bored with nothing better to play.

_childDocuments_.review: It was ok, nothing special to me. Some plot twists here and there, but I didn't get caught up in it, something feels off. Maybe I felt like it was a standard anime, with some drama, characters fighting and then laughing together etc. I thought they were pretty generic from the trailers, they build up during the story though and Saizo is my favorite, I liked his story more but this is personal. Arrow got me at the beginning because I underestimated him a lot. Milady is ok aswell. Ringo is a MC with a fixed name and dubbed, which is great but I felt like something was off, maybe because she didn't have a background (explained story-wise but still..) and she's more self confident than the others, so I think I would have preferred a mute character like Joker. Figue seemed useless to me, even if she gets involved a lot in the story later on. It could be bigger, there are only a few small areas and some shops but it kind of works. I liked the night and futuristic atmosphere, specially the arts from the shops and the characters in there. Karakucho is my favorite area since it's bigger and you can feel the city. I also liked a lot the idea of the bar in Shinsando, you can meet your friends there and it resembles the social links in Persona but after a while it gets repetitive because it's limited to that, with the same animation of them taking a beer and drinking, while in Persona you can meet up in so many different areas of Tokyo and do different things. But I don't mean this game should have social links like Persona, it just does it way worse. Having played some other Atlus games, I think they did 2 great things through their games: the dungeons in Persona 5, where you get detailed palaces with parkour, air ducts, safe rooms etc and the ones in SMT3, labyrinths full of traps where you can get lost, with poisonous floors or no light and even some ingenious boss battles where you have to understand what's happening and think outside of the box to beat the enemies, aside from just weaknesses, strenghts and counter skills (EG: finding the only one enemy with a shadow on a full moon or the statue with no reflection). In this game, world dungeons are ok, more SMT like specially in the subway ones, where's a series of opened walls closing when you cross them and triggering others to open, and the ward municipal tower where there are some floors and a puzzle with elevators you can switch, but that's it. The rest of the world dungeons are just small and flat themed areas with some blind corridors. And you spend most of the time in the Axis dungeons, where you walk on squares suspended in the air and the only funny part about them is the area with random teleports where you get lost a lot and the challenge is to explore everything without getting lost. But that's something SMT3 did way better and SMT5 even worse in its only 2 dungeons, so I'm worried about that. I mean either do them well or don't put them in the game, otherwise it gets boring. It seemed pretty good to me. The comps upgrade system gives you all the passive abilities in exchange of money and materials found inside the dungeons; mystiques enhance your skills, halve mp costs or add ailments to normal skills, they are obtainable by leveling up demons or by scrapping the ones you don't need anymore. I didn't check if they were making an actual difference, but the numbers were there so they sure did. As always well done. I played it in english and the quality is the same of other Atlus games. Checking the game folders I also noticed they actually put lip sync folders for both english and japanese dubs. I expect a lot from Atlus soundtracks, I loved both the dancing vibes of the Persona series (that got me dancing on my chair for over 110 hours of gameplay) and the darker themes and ambient tracks featured in the SMT main series, that allowed me to better feel the apocalyptic atmosphere. Since MONACA was involved and they did a fantastic job in Nier, I was hyped a lot. But they obviously adapted their work to Soul Hackers 2 and there I lost the one thing I knew for sure I would find in an Atlus games. I mean, it fits well in the game's universe but I think their games are also unique for their soundtracks and I couldn't say the same about this one, with some exceptions. Leaving behind the awful experience with the missing costumes & bgm pack (digital premium editions in particular) that luckily has been fixed some days after release (I was almost getting through the end of the game without them), the only bug I noticed is the end walk animation being tied to the fps. If you cap fps to 30 it's how it's supposed to be, but with higher frames like 60, or 144 in my case, when you release the left stick Ringo keeps moving onwards by a lot. But it's not a big deal and the game should be otherwise bugs free. I have to mention though that there are still some rare cases of people that haven't got that dlc yet. Going through the Axis dungeons you unlock some background story scenes about Arrow, Milady and Saizo. But you just see the holograms of the characters involved like in Code Vein and I can't get to like this way of telling a story. It's an ok game, surely not great as it really feels it was a low budget production. But not that bad either. I recommend it to people without great expectations, but as a big Atlus fan I can't recommend it, they can and usually do way better than this. Since it has been produced by the same team from Tokyo Mirage Sessions, a game I avoided for the same reason, I guess it all makes sense.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted like this game so much. _childDocuments_.review: Objectively speaking, Soul Hackers 2 probably isn't a good game... But I just can't get myself to give it a negative review...Soul Hackers 2, has some great characters, an interesting setting, and a pretty interesting premise for a story! Plus the soundtrack in my opinion is a solid A tier! Not quite up to the Atlus standard in my opinion, but still has a lot of bangers that I listed to very often even after I've finished the game!But the dungeons man... The They gotta be THE most boring and mechanically frustrating things I've had to play in a looooong time. Which is a shame since you're gonna spend most of your time in them...They all look basically identical, and most of them have the same song, and then you have the navigator constantly making noises about enemy statuses, that you have no option to mute (as far as I know).And the Soul Matrix, each party members "unique" dungeon, is the worst example of that. Each floor, for each character looks and functions the exact same, and then later they also throw in portals into the mix, that you don't know where they will teleport you to, making traversing them even more frustrating. But the worst thing is that they are not really optional, since, to get the true ending, one of the things you need to do, is to complete each characters dungeon. But at the end of each dungeon, you get some honestly really cool and challenging boss battles! Which in my opinion are solid highlights of this game, making the dungeons kind of worth it in my opinion!As mentioned previously, this game has some good characters! And those boss battles are usually pretty personal for them, making them feel very climactic! Or, maybe good concepts for characters...?Since, I like them, but also feel like they are very underdeveloped? Either way, I enjoy them! But really wished they where given more time and attention, since the game is kind of about them? Anyways, I was first very skeptical on Arrow and Figue, but Figue ended up being one of my favorites! Not to mention the protagonist herself, Ringo! Ringo is such a treat, and is super entertaining! And her dynamic with all the party members is very fun to watch.And the story is cool at first, as long you don't give it that much thought, because as soon as you do, the logic starts to crumble and fall apart real fast.Another thing that I like in this game though, that I personally haven't seen done that much before, is that as you finish some side quests, the party members can actually comment and talk to you about what their opinion on that matter was, as you unlock a conversation with them about it at the bar, once the quest is finished. It makes the side quests a bit more worth it in my opinion, as it fleshes out the characters a little more, and makes them feel like their own individual people.The side quests themselves on the other hand, aren't that great... I mean, some of them have their little side plot going on, which is fun to follow up upon as you get more quests from those characters, and can even meet them in the overworld, and hear their opinions on the recent story events. But most of the side quests basically boil down to "find the thingamajig" or "fight someone somewhere", meaning that yet again you have to go out to the right dungeon, and mess around until you by some mere chance find the thing you where looking for. It takes so much timmmeee, and is not very fun! The "collect this amount of this item" quests are by far the worst though in my opinion. because one time, I was either doing something wrong, or I had THE worst luck imaginable as I had 5/6 items I needed, but couldn't find the 6th one for literally 2 HOURS. Since the chance to get that item was random. Plus, the game overall lacked a lot of polish in my opinion... Small things like, the main menu theme not looping correctly, everyone spamming voice lines for each little move they do in combat, or the foot step noises not being synced to the animations (Since, sometimes the sound doesn't match the visuals), or when story events aren't being reflected by the music, like, when something sad happened/is happening, and the characters are sad because of it, but the music is still happy and funky in the background. I know they are all super small things, but they add up, and kind of break the immersion quite a lot. As you can see, my opinion on this game is a very mixed bag. Plus, I haven't written a review before either, so, I apologize that this is kind of a rambled mess. But, despite everything, if this game has sparked your interest, I'd say give it a shot! But please, spare yourself, and use a guide or something to just get the dungeons (and quests if you wanna) done and over with faster, and I hope you will enjoy the characters, boss fights, and the music! Because as I said, I'm really glad that I sticked with it! I had some great moments playing it, and Ringo, Figue and Saizo will be living in my head rent free for quite some time I think!So yeah! Here's hoping that Atlus doesn't get too discouraged by this games performance, and tries to make more games outside of the mainline SMT and Persona series in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: Balan Wonderworld literally has a higher user rating than this now. Is this game really worse than that? Sure the dungeons visually are a mess but the character development, the combat, the story, I think are pretty good, a lot of the themes are very mature and reflect things people go through in real life. There's a few glaring flaws with the dungeons as I mentioned, the walk speed and fusions feeling limited in potential. Combat is also fun with how customization for each of the characters work. It's not a terrible game. If anything I think people had there expectations set on a successor to Persona 5 Royal, if you go into any game, comparing it to another. your almost always going to have a bad time. Soul Hackers 2 is a fun experimental game made as a revival of a 25 year old franchise. It's not trying to surpass Persona 5, or Shin Megami Tensei V, just being it's own thing and try something different, while appealing to older fans of the series. feel free to keep hating it if you want, I enjoyed my time with the game, and I hope whoever reads this found something they liked too.  If you do genuinely hate the game, your opinion is yours to have, and I'm sorry you feel like you wasted your time and money on it.Personally I liked the complexity of the dungeons, visually they failed i agree, but i liked actually having to "solve" the later dungeons. there's that 'ah-ha!' moment when finally progressing that made them really satisfying to work through. the 1 way door mechanic in the subways felt like a more fleshed out version of what they tried at the end of Shin Megami Tensei V, as well as dungeons from the PersonaQ games, all i ever hear is people hating how complicated the dungeons are. but that's strictly a personal thing, and not a 'flaw' of the game. If the layouts were the same but each of the soul matrix's had unique and striking visuals with there own music and themes would you still hate it? The demons could have also been replaced with chests, but instead they chose to show us demon's from our party, a lot of people tend to overlook this but it was kind of cool getting to see Ringo standing next to your demons and interacting with them. Also I personally enjoyed the DLC story, it's not connected to the main plot at all aside from just a hint of extra context for the ending, even then it just feels like a filler episode, extra fluff. it doesn't takes anything away from the game not having it, but for those who like the game it's a nice side story that's fully voiced and fun to play through while adding an extra dungeon to explore, and adding some of the hardest fights in the game for those who really want to push the limit.I just find it strange that this game is literally getting a worse overall rating than Balan Wonderworld. At least this game works well, even if it's flawed. feel free to leave a comment if you agree or disagree or want to bring up something I missed.
