_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is a pretty good entry into the ever expanding library of the SMT series. It'd definitely following the trend of becoming more "Persona" than previous SMT games, but still manages to deliver a worthwhile experience.First off, and the biggest draw of the game to me, the characters. Most of the time, SMT doesn't really focus on its cast, they serve their purpose, and have their quirks to them, but generally, SMT is about the gameplay. Soul Hackers 2 is not like that. While the non-essential story characters are incredibly flat and forgettable, the core party and those close to them are incredibly memorable and fun to watch. The chemistry between Ringo, Arrow, Milady, and Saizo works really well, and every scene they're in is a joy to watch. The story is more interesting than your standard apocalypse scenario because of how well the characters are all written, and it makes you feel for everyone on all sides. It's hard to make all of your characters likeable like this, and you can tell a lot of effort went into making the cast a lot more three dimensional than your standard SMT cast. However, the writing only gets you so far in an RPG like this, hows the gameplay? Well, its definitely a lot more simple than most other Atlus RPGs, this isn't too terrible, and allows the game to be a lot more accessible to new players, but if you're a hardcore SMT gatekeeper, you'll likely be disappointed. The move pool is drastically smaller than even Persona's, and demon move slots are limited to 6. Fusion is super streamlined, similarly to SMT V, with compendium fusions being carried over, reducing the tedium of filling out the compendium again. Dungeon exploration is standard enough, with one major problem. At the time of writing my original review, RINGO WAS SLOW AS ♥♥♥♥. They mercifully added a run button a few months after the game released, and while I'm sure its a nice quality of life booster, it doesn't save the frankly boring and generic levels. With the exception of the FINAL AREA, the levels are the same 3 recycled subways, office buildings, and blank voids repeated over and over and over again, making it a huge drag to get from one story beat to the next. I really like the story here, but I'm not going to lie, some of the mid points made it really hard to continue. Luckily, these dungeons tend to be short, but with them composing most of the game, and feeling twice as long with the lack of anything interesting, they are definitely the games biggest weakness.Now, lets say you've read my little textwall, and the game sounds interesting to you. As you scroll back up to the buy button, you might notice this game has a lot of DLC. Now you're thinking "Hmm... should I buy the deluxe edition???"No.The DLC is a total waste of money. At best, you get a couple side missions that are a nice distraction from the main game for a little bit, and at worst you're spending an addition 50% of the main game's cost to completely ruin the game by instantly being able to hit level 99 with infinite money, and getting a couple neat (but totally useless) costumes. If this is like your favorite game ever and you just really wanna show your love for it, go for it I guess? But really, these are nothing more than a scummy attempt to scrape more money away from you by ripping content from the game day one that really has no business being DLC to begin with.Overall? I had a good time with Soul Hackers 2. The gameplay is pretty lacking for an SMT game, and the DLC is pretty lame, but the characters and story are such a great time, and the general aesthetic being so appealing and easy to get sucked into, that it almost carries the rest of the games weakpoints. I think this makes a great first SMT game, especially if you're looking something closer to Persona. If you're a bit more of an SMT veteran, this may be a bit harder of a sell. If the story looks cool, or you just wanna see everything this series has to offer, it's far from a terrible game, but other games in this series significantly outshine it. 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the least engaging megaten game.Story feels rushed. It's just moving from point A to point B, and at point B a big story moment happens, nothing happens in-between. Even SMT5, the game with THE HAT SCENE, has a better spine.And it really surprises me how so many people claim that the characters in this game are good. While they get their development, it's extremely predictable. In the end it's not like their beliefs actually matter, there is so little conflict they might as well just make all the characters best friends who always agree. And when it comes to picking a dialogue option the game literally tells you who likes your answer, not even persona does that.Oh and it's not a sequel to soul hackers. It does not have the world building, characters, art direction, gameplay, themes or anything even in the style of soul hackers. It doesn't matter if they have soul hacking or name a character Kuzunoha, it is clear this was not made as a follow up to any devil summoner game, especially not soul hackers, and all the terms were just shoehorned in.The gameplay is so bare bones it's not even worth trying to learn the details. It's literally just hit enemy weaknesses and get an all out attack. Didn't hit a weakness? Well you're gonna deal 5 damage, even with high stats. Because demons don't matter half of the time. Fusion should only be used to get the next level of elemental spells for your party, no need to think about stats or costs. I got past the halfway point of the game I'm pretty sure, and I barely fused any demons, because they don't do anything. 90% of your stats are tied to your character, the rest 10% is from your demon, they get added up, so it ends up just like SMT5, only your character level matters for scaling. And the dungeons are just hallways. Just dark tunnels, rarely any quirks, and no secrets at all. You could argue that is what dungeon crawling is, but actual fun videogames have engaging events and reward exploration. In this game you just walk into a bunch of dead ends until you get on the correct path. It's actually insane how much detail they put into shopping areas you rarely visit with a bunch of NPCs and stuff that serve absolutely no purpose. Yet they can't make the player interact with a dungeon environment. Hell, they literally had to add the option to sprint in an update since the dungeons are such big snoozefests.It's not as bad as persona 3, but it's still a disgrace to soul hackers and the megaten franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2, itself as a game, does not deserve the review beating it has taken. As a bridge between social sim Persona and Hardcore JRPG SMT, it does quite well. A solid 8, not groundbreaking but a fun time.The main focus of the story is Ringo and her crew travailing a horrible stagnant and stale corporate future, in order to save mankind from causing its own destruction.The gameplay is standard SMT/Persona fair, turn based combat plus creature collection. Its not particularly hard if you have any JRPG experience and tends to border on being too easy.The world and dungeon design is not that good tbh. granted it sets the tone of living in a corporate and stagnant city , with a thin veneer of glamour masking the hollowed out reality of a post industrial city. Yet this boils down to a lot of corridors in train tunnels and empty corporate buildings when dungeon diving. Except the Soul matrix part of the game, which is more like long pathways in "cyber space" and teleporter puzzles. I enjoyed the soul matrix until I ran into those puzzles. I wish that they were just number/colour coded. My advise is save before you jump.On the down sides, its a bit short, the teleporter puzzles suck and thats about it. I even liked the music , even if it was limited it wasn't grating. HOWEVER the DLC practices are obscene. If it wasn't for the high prices it could almost be forgiven, but locking away series regular demons was too much, it felt like whaling. Costumes and extra missions are one thing (not great behaviour, but all too common ) but that was a step too far.Other notes is that this port runs ok. You will get stutter on your first battle of that play session, but other then that its not too noticeable, when running around and such.Overall I did enjoy my time with it and 100% completed it. I liked the combat chatter from team mates and the enemies making the characters have bags of personality. I enjoyed the style of the character design and the music. The story is So-so to good, with great character moments thrown in and some good voice acting from Ringo and Milady's VA in particular. I look forward to any sequels that may come.I would say that this game is easily worth its money at £30 or about that. I wouldn't bother with the DLCs at all. The challenge battles arn't worth it, though the character introduced is fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Atlus resurrected the cult classic 90s MegaTen game, Soul Hackers, for a sequel which is perhaps the most by-the-numbers, and predictable RPG they've released in fifteen years.At its core Soul Hackers 2 revolves around traversing some of the most thematically bland and uninspired dungeons, defeating enemies in a so-so variation of Press Turn combat and making your way over to the next round of story dialogue, much of which tends to be filled with unnecessary exposition. Throw in some half-hearted MMO sidequests too - the game has to rely on this as a crutch to make the dull dungeon crawling more palatable. The above would be digestible if the narrative was actually interesting, but it isn't. Soul Hackers presented the writers' bold 90s vision for what a connected future might mean for society. While I don't mind the loss of the hard boiled detective atmosphere that permeated its predecessor, Soul Hackers 2 is meant to be set in an era where data-driven AI has become sentient, but it does almost nothing interesting with it, at least in the 13 hours I've played so far. The world itself might as well be set in the present day. If you're going to spend your precious time on an RPG, or even an Atlus game, you can do much better than this. There are simply more interesting, more memorable games by the esteemed RPG developer which are worth your time over this uninspired sequel.

The OST also does not hold up compared to the original (the opening theme is a banger though but nothing reaches that level).The bond building (their persona attempt) is pretty bare bones. You just grab a beer with them, dialogue choices in the story, do the summoner requests, and clear out the soul matrix. It's pretty mid but if you like the characters you will enjoy that.The characters are all just ok. I like Ringo, Saizo grew on me, and Milady. Everyone else is pretty whatever and the story itself isn't all the great but just fun to go through. Compared to the og SH and most SMT games it holds up fine. I hate that Atlus locked up the Nemissa skin behind a dlc though (which i wasn't going to buy because I knew I was only plaything this once).Overall, the game is fine. Nowhere near as bad as people made it seem but it just doesn't have that soul hackers feel i was hopping for. If you look up all the characters, music, world, UI you will see a clear winner in aesthetic choice. This doesn't mean the original is a fantastic game, but pretty cool for what it was. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I would not recommend this for someone getting into the SMT genre because it is a bad representation. If you've played other SMT games and are expecting something similar to those I would also not recommend it (DO MORE RESEARCH). For the truly brave that want something different (perhaps worse imo) then I think you could consider this game it just feels very unfinished to me. I have not played Soul Hackers 1, I played a bit of the remaster and it didn't really interest me so I do not know if it's a good successor to that game.Just for some background, I've played a bit of SMTIII Nocturne, finished SMTIVA, SMTV, Devil Survivor 1, Devil Survivor 2, the upgraded versions of those games as well, Persona 4 Golden, Persona 5, Persona 5R, Persona 5S and I am near the end of this game and I don't know if I can finish it. I consider myself in between a casual and hardcore for this genre at least the modern version.For a modern game it feels really bad, more specifically unfinished. I'll try to not go into the specifics of the story, but most of the game play is mapping around the dungeon, fetch quest via talking to demons, and talking to your teammates. I struggled coming up with a third point cause it's mostly the first two. The dungeon experience is straight out of Persona 4 or SMT4A but worse because they make you do more with the same movement and those games came out in 2008 and 2016 respectively. The puzzles in Soul Hackers 2 are just infuriating and inconvenient, the maps are plain, and walking around just feels like a chore. The movement and attacks also feel clunky, while it's not important in a game like this I thought I should point it. All this just screams to me that it was rushed because there is practically 0 depth to the dungeons.Another issue I have with this game is the overworld. It feels so empty. It's pretty much the shops to get items, interact with teammates, demon fusion, quest shop, and restaurants for food. A lot of things are tied to character interactions which honestly they are all pretty bland.Moving on to the combat... it feels unrewarding. The press turn battle system has evolved into sabbath attacks which replace bonus turns for more damage at the end of your turn, which can be modified with different abilities but most of them suck imo. I feel like this is move is bad because it restricts a player's choice. It only allows you to get more damage down as opposed to healing or buffing yourself again which feels worse to me. It's not like this helps with resource management either because your MP pool is so big plus you can always just leave, heal, and come back.Another issue for me personally is demon fusion. You are restricted to 6 skill slots with I think 0 amps for specific elements, although these come in the forms of augments for your comp which can be debated on whether this is good or bad. I think this discourages you from swapping demons too often as you only have so many augment slots and they are also linked to farmable materials + money. There are also far fewer elements in this game than say Persona or even SMT which means easier element coverage but also demon variety seems lower. Also money is painful to farm, I have the DLC and it's still rough fusing demons, so I couldn't imagine what it's like for people without.Side Note: RIP Hassou Tobi you will be missedAs someone else said in their review it's like a mix between a Persona game and SMT except it does both poorly.End of gameplay stuffPOTENTIAL SPOILERS MAINLY JUST TALKING ABOUT CHARACTERS AND HOW BAD THE STORY IS IGNORE IF YOU DON'T WANT TO KNOW ANYTHING Characters:StorySide Note/Rant (PROBABLY A SPOILER)Idk this was a rant cause I was really excited for this game, it looked cool like Persona 5, SMTV had some great combat imo, and I had an itch for a new SMT game and this just didn't scratch it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a somewhat decent core of a game here, however I feel like the negatives outweigh the positives so I can't really recommend it.Starting with the battle system, I have to say that it's merely alright. It's the standard "hit weakness, do more damage" fare that you'd see in most other modern MegaTen games, but the press turn system is replaced by the pretty boring Sabbath mechanic that lets you do damage at the end of your turn depending on how many weakness you hit during it. Seems decent on paper, until you realize that it doesn't really do that much, and it's actually pretty useless against boss fights.The COMP upgrade system is rather unimpressive, and all it does is encourage grinding enemies for the necessary materials to buy your upgrades. The upgrades themselves are also pretty boring, and the most exciting thing you can unlock is Commander Skills which are special abilities you can use every few turns in battle that do useful things for ya, like increase your Sabbath stacks, swap demons etc. Every other upgrade is generic "do more damage" or "you can now equip higher tier upgrades". Overall very underwhelming.The story is very average and predictable. The characters are very barebones, and the ending is so basic you can see it coming 10 hours into the game. The first Soul Hackers game at least had great characters to carry the story, while this one doesn't even have that. There's really nothing special to write about here, the story is kinda just... there. The side quests are on par with the main story, and kinda just exist. In a way they're worse than the main story, because you will often find yourself getting asked to go back to the same dungeon you were asked to go to 5 times already to fetch yet another item from yet another random demon. There's 2 particular dungeons, both of which are almost identical looking subway lines, that you are constantly asked to go back to over and over again because the game just doesn't have anywhere else to send you.Finally, what I think is the worst part of the game: the dungeon crawling. 80% of the action takes place in what's called the Soul Matrix, which is a set of 3 dungeons of 5 floors each, which are . It's literally a series of almost untextured corridors floating in a void of nothing where you constantly get spammed by enemies every 2 steps of your way, and your reward for beating each floor is a tiny bit of story dialogue that they could've easily fit anywhere else. I think a good comparison to the Soul Matrix would be the final dungeon of SMT4 Apocalypse, for folks who have played that one. Just a large section of literal nothing that takes needlessly long to complete.I kinda focused on the bad here, but there  things to enjoy here. The combat, despite being simple, is still fun. The boss encounters are mostly enjoyable. The fusion system is as fun as ever.Unfortunately, for every little good thing the game does it does 5 other things poorly, so it's just not worth the time.Play Soul Hackers 1 instead, as this game has nothing to do with it anyways other than share a title.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are coming from a Persona series perspective, here's what I can tell you. The gameplay is closer to P4, but slightly simpler. There is no schedule mechanics, so if anything is similar with P5 Strikers in that aspect. You can and should build relationships with your party which is easy. Overall the game is good.If you are wondering about negatives, there are few in my opinion. The party doesn't grow beyond a total of 4 members. The dungeon(s) that are dedicated to party members are generic in design (literally all look the same). You acquire the full party pretty quickly at the start since the story depends on having all 4 during the whole time (this may be seen as a negative to some).In terms of DLC it is mainly cosmetic with 3 exceptions. 1. is a side mission DLC. 2. is a demons pack DLC which is probably the one that annoys people the most. 3. is a boost pack, which doesn't automatically break the game since every boost is actually an item so you have full control over when to use it. It can be useful if you are stuck, but generally the money boost is the one that may make the most difference without actually breaking the game.

_childDocuments_.review: very good and cooledit: thought i'd add more to my review considering that the above is kinda basicthe interactions between all the party members both inside and outside of combat are really refreshing for this kind of game, having party members comment of each others actions in game play and in story/hang out segments having their own conflicting beliefs but working together regardless is great as opposed to the average homogenised jrpg average of "yeah we're all really good friends trust me, we said so out right in dialogue". The main character of Ringo was a treat, despite the multi-choice dialogue it really feels like she's her own fleshed out character who exists to be more than just a self insert for the player.The story is you're average jrpg "save the world kill a god" kind of thing but mainly stands out with the theme of characters attempting to strive for the same goal via opposing means which comes together in multiple boss fights.gameplay wise, the sabbat system all though interesting, doesn't hold up as well as either the press turn or one more system of smt and persona respectively, all the idea of chaining weakness explanations for a bigger burst of damage was interesting kind of like the demon co-op attacks of strange journey, fails to really reach the same levels of depth as the other systems, really just summing up to "do more damage with weakness and crits = do more damage". Otherwise, i really appreciate the ability to fully customise the party's moveset and elemental affinities, allowing you to customise your parties' comp down to the buttons to rip that boss a new arseholeOverall, this is a great game though maybe not as unique as it's predecessor the OG Soul Hackers or other SMT entries, the story, characters and the customisation available for your party makes it a cut above your average JRPG.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as Jrpgs go this is a very good game. Ringo is a very good protagonist I much preferred her over the persona main characters for the most part. The story was as you'd expect its a cookie cutter Atlus experience but the game did have some amazing moments I just wished some parts of the game were more fleshed out and other bits should have been streamlined, the pacing was a little iffy at times but peak moments were amazing.The demon fusion and character customisation is amazing as expected and the game has its own unique twists not offered in the other games so even if you're tired of the same Megaten stuff you can build your team and strategise differently.The ost was pretty good especially the event and boss themes, unfortunately you'll likely get sick of hearing it by the end.My main problem with the game is the dungeons, they get extremely repetitive and by the end I just ran through avoiding all battles and the final area was pretty disappointing to me I almost couldn't be bothered to finish it, the battling and story overstayed its welcome which was sad because I felt like I did want more of the game, just not what I was given.I still suggest if you've not played any Atlus game before, play a different one first, this is not the best they can do. If you want a challenge I'd play SMT instead the game got easy even while being underlevelled on hard. But if you're more there for the story and not dungeon crawling I'd definitely recommend! Just pick it up on sale if you can it's gone 50% off a few times.

The textures, effects, lighting shadows, etc. Seem fine enough but they all have an early Ps4 game feel to them rather than a game that just released. No idea how long the development was on this title. Ultimately, I am enjoying the game and will probably finish it. However, for anyone with a medium to low income, I'd say wait for a sale because this game doesn't seem to do anything to warrant a triple A price tag.Edit September 5, 2022:I have now finished the main game and the little DLC completing *most little side stuff and achievements along the way. In my opinion the worst part of this game by a wide margin is the Soul Matrix. If you're at all interested in completing all 5 floors for each character you're very likely to spend more time in the Soul Matrix then the rest of the entire game combined. Considering that it basically looks the same on all 5 floors, with the addition of teleport pads on the higher floors, it is very, very tedious. The second worst part of the game is the DLC dungeon "Hachigaya Training Field". This, much like the Soul Matrix but arguably worse since it's most the exact same floor duplicated over an over is extremely tedious. The actual Lost Numbers story and the character Nana is pretty fun and adds to the game but, this dungeon was super lazy. It could have all but 1 of it's floors removed and would pretty much be the same dungeon. In a nutshell, those 2 dungeons feel like pitiful attempts to add playtime bulk to a rather thin game that is asking a triple A price. The actual characters imo, are somewhat endearing however, 2 of them--I won't spoil much--just grow too quickly and end up acting about as off the rails stupid as I could imagine. The whole game feels like it takes place over the course of just a few weeks and it just doesn't track at all with the character progression for those 2. There needs to be like a whole middle of the game added to this game.For people complaining about it being compared to Persona or Shin Megami Tensei get real... Even Atlus immediately threw Persona content into this game. Besides that, as far as the genre goes the easiest other games in the genre to compare it to are Atlus's other IPs. While this shouldn't be another Persona or SMT it should be comparable in detail quality or superior even now that Atlus is a much more successful studio than when they were developing P5. The Joker costume for Ringo imo, is the way to go, I super dislike her vanilla outfit. Some of the Persona 5 music is being reused here but, that's not a bad thing, frankly the original music for Soul Hackers for me personally is a let down. Otherwise, it's a fun if a bit generic JRPG that feels like an early PS4 release despite being a 2022 release. If you've played hundreds or even just dozens of games in the genre you'll see tropes everywhere some bad some fine. I'd say wait for a sell unless you're a big JRPG fan that has money burning a hole in your account and you've already exhausted Steam's list of JRPGs that are better than this game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a shame this game's catching so much venom!From my perspective, as a willing supporter of those who create and publish works like this, Soul Hackers 2 is a slick, fresh, modern take on the long running Shin Megami Tensei / Persona Universe. The characters are compelling, the Japanese voice acting is superb, the localization has done a fine job with the challenges faced by translators. The art work and style are excellent, consistent, and well-used in conveying the tricky bits involved in AI personalities interacting with Human Beings.Any experience you've had with all those previous games in the SMT/P series carries over well into finding your way around this piece of world building. And yet, remarkably, it feels fresh. Well done, authors, artists, and Atlus! My own time with SMT goes back to the PS Vita and Nintendo products of that era. I'm thoroughly enjoying this game! One thing I've noticed with this particular battle system; in many turn-based team battle settings it often feels optimal for your team members to gang up on opposing targets, eliminating them one by one - for each one quickly eliminated, that's one less source of incoming fire.Not so here! Instead, it seems to be preferable to spread the damage across as many in the enemy group as possible, to bring their HP count down across the board, so that when Ringo lets go with a Stack Attack you can wipe out multiple targets in one swipe. Very interesting. Battles in Soul Hackers 2 take on a completely different dynamic from a lot of other turn-based battle system games. It feels fresh and interesting.Now, there are technical aspects to the Denuvo Digital Rights Management (DRM) solution that some folks object to as a matter, to them, of principle. Perhaps they feel they should have the right to copy and redistribute software freely, despite that specifically being prohibited by the Terms of Use they've agreed to by installing and starting the software. What we purchase is not the software, but the limited and specific rights to use it, under license. Copyright laws vary by nation but are established with consistent intent to protect the rights of authors and publishers of creative works. Those rights are not cancelled simply because someone doesn't agree with them, any more than your right to speak would be cancelled if I didn't agree with you.Like the game? Want to try the game? Buy the game. if you're offended by the DRM implementation, then return the game under Valve's Terms of Use and get your refund. But please don't tear down or trash-talk a game or a game publisher simply because they've taken steps to protect their rights to a creative work.Does this trash-talking happen to every game that employs Denuvo DRM? If so, that's an injustice against the authors and artists. And while we're at it, the level of piracy in the present world is a plague upon any creative house trying to produce and publish copyrighted work in a sustainable way. Want less noxious DRM? Stop downloading copyrighted works from piracy sites.And none of this has any bearing on the merits of this work as a game. I've been enjoying it very much, and feel anyone who's enjoyed previous excursions into this universe will probably enjoy this one as well!So thanks again, authors, artists, composers, musicians, and publishers! My life is enriched by your creative efforts, and I'm glad to support them!Addin, now at  65 game-hours,,,Still a strong recommend for this one! I'm actually playing it in parallel with Persona 4, 5, and Soul Hackers 1 on the 3DS. It's turning into quite the late Autumn/early Winter binge here, and I'm thoroughly enjoying it!Some folks say the Soul Matrix levels are tedious, or overly plain: Bah! Look at them on a decent monitor, they're a nice rendering of the idea of a synthetic reality - and their design from a game architecture standpoint is just fine. The stairs come along when they need to, the gates are well-placed, the story-reveals are meaningful and significant, if you just let the story do its thing on you; there's really no problem here.So in sum, at this stage, this is a game that belongs in the SMT Universe. There's room in the world for Golf, Croquet, and Frisbee Golf, too!

_childDocuments_.review: Having finished Soul Hackers 2, I want to say I have mixed feelings on the game.To begin, It's clearly taking influence from SMT games while mixing in elements of Persona (Sabbath's being similar to All Out Attacks from Persona 5,  hang out events, etc.) but never fully commits to going the extra mile to make those features truly fulfilling imo. I think the strongest aspect of SH2 is the story and characters whilst the gameplay is a bit slow it also picks up towards the end when you have all your upgrades. The problem is some of the design choices that were made towards this game which felt like a massive slog for most parts of the game. For example, Ringo (The main character) does not have a designated run button but rather she just kinda lightly jogs around the field and that feels like a slog to me personally. (You get an ability to speed it up but if it's an ability which can only be unlocked by doing an optional dungeon). I think the other disappointing aspect is the level design as everything is flat and not very creative. There isn't much variety and when there is some change it all comes towards the end of the game and kind of is short in general. The lack of complexity for the dungeons kind of makes everything feel bogged down and there were times I felt really bored in the 50 hours I played. But I kinda dragged through it because the story and characters were really charismatic imo.So even with these caveats I'm giving it a recommend? Yes, because I had an evidently good time with it but at full price of $80 CAD I don't know if it's actually worth the full price of admission (Kinda wish Steam had a sideways thumbs in this case) but if you're looking for a solid JRPG when this does go down in price, keeping in mind with the downsides, I think it's a pretty good game.TL:DR Decent JRPG with a strong story and characters but falters with weird design choices that went towards the game. Recommend getting on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Initial impressions: The trailer art style is semi deceiving. Initial impressions set my expectations to something close to Tokyo Mirage Session however the lighting and shading work lends it somewhere closer to a noir comic book like style. If you enjoyed PS2 Megaten games (like I do) the game navigates kinda similar, in a close up 3rd person view. The controls are a bit difficult and throw you off but they aren't intolerable. The combat system is highly controversial, and I can't say for late game, but initial impressions are interesting to say the least.People are disappointed that Press Turn isn't the system that Atlus went with, and while I also enjoy press turn this was to be expected even before the games release. Devil Summoner games (which this game should fall under) tends to be Atlus's test bed for different combat systems. Devil Summoner 1 and Soul Hacker has its loyalty system, Raidou Kuzunoha has its real-time battle system, and Soul Hacker 2 has the Sabbath system. Its sort of like 5's essence system and 3's magatama system. The player character gains the affinity of the demons they have selected and use demon skills during their turn. The player doesn't summon the demon to the field, rather they use the demons skill directly, and if the skill is especially effective against a foe the demon will stick around till the end of the round. At the end of a combat round the demons engage in a Sabbath and inflict extra damage against the enemy party. The side effect of this system is characters can only summon 1 demon each, a maximum of 4 per party. Its a far cry from the 4+ party characters and I can see it leading to less complex party set ups compared to Soul Hacker 1, but once again this isn't the first time Devil Summoner has limited the active demons in a player party. It's not the worst combat system but I can see why many don't like it compared to the other games. I enjoy it (as of writing this) but it's worth knowing this is the main gameplay for this game. The combat animations are exceptional, all characters have a stylish aura and demeanor (yes even the guy in the hoody, he looks cooler in person than in the trailer).People often ask why Soul Hacker 2, rather than Devil Summoner: Aion or whatever. Besides Soul Hacking being a main story mechanic it probably has to do with its themes being directly connected to Soul Hacker's. Where Soul Hacker's main themes and setting was all about the exponential growth of technological capability and how the explosion of tech in the 90s was rapidly changing the living standards of all people, Soul Hackers 2 directly follows it up with modern days continued technological growth and yet somehow the stagnation of human living standards. Even if tech is still getting better as the years have gone on we as people haven't been greatly changed. Not in any utopian way that the 90s had envisioned it atleast. Only time will tell if this theme is fully realized but I can at least understand the Soul Hacker 2 monicure.TLDR/Conclusion;I'm not saying this is the best game or even one of the best. Its probably not going to break new ground in the SMT fandom in terms of story or gameplay, as many have pointed out in there own Reviews. However I see very little reason as of now to not recommend it to people who enjoy SMT and Atlus games in general. If you set your expectations to that of a decent, if simpler take on Devil Summoner I doubt you will be disappointed. I see very little reason to by the game full priced and with DLC. I only did it because I like to support Atlus's game developers. I honestly have never played a bad Atlus game. Many tedious and some that were kinda boring, but never bad. Play on Hard if you are familiar with Atlus games (its closer to other Atlus games Normal, and remember there is a Very Hard that should be closer to the expected Hard mode).

_childDocuments_.review: Two cyborg waifus created by a super secret artificial intelligence attempt to stop a culturally stagnant humanity from killing itself via demons. The setup is more exciting than the actual plot itself. The twists and turns follow your typical JRPG playbook with every  coming from a mile away. One noteworthy inclusion is that the MC, Ringo, is fully voiced. While not the worst thing in the world it's hardly anything special and Ringo herself can be funny despite some of the cringe writing. You'd think a sequel to Soul Hackers would have demon summoning and recruitment, well you're wrong bucko! The series is now a persona spinoff complete with lack of demon party members and recruitment. Instead you equip one of your four human party members with a demon and they use the inherited spells and abilities. Recruitment is handled in the most brain dead way possible, you walk around and find them randomly. You simply give them what they ask for and if your level is high enough they're yours. You'll be hunting for demons randomly placed in dungeon maps so boring and empty you'll get persona 3/4 flashbacks and they aren't even randomly generated maps! Combat is one of the worst in the series thus far! Instead of the one more time system where a strike with an enemies weakness you get build your "Sabbath" charge. Some hits can add more than 1 per attack if you hit hard enough or use a commander skill to boost them. At the end of your turn your demons come out to smack the enemy. You or your enemies hitting weaknesses do not give/take away turns unless it's status related which makes the combat extremely easy and boring. In an attempt rectify this they added the commander skills from SMT strange journey REDUX . There's also social links, but they're for the party members only and suck.Actually nearly fully featured other than lack of ultrawide because Japanese indie devu pwease understandu. Might be worth it on sale if you really want to play every mid JRPG ever made. I'd personally avoid if I was you tbh.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 + SMTV with an identity crisis and a $15 budget. Not very good to say the least. Not terrible but not good either, very much a 6/10 game. In terms of it being an SMT Game its like a 3/10 for me. Simplifies most of the core gameplay and appeal of Both Mainline SMT and Persona to the point of it being completely dumbed down and losing most depth. Not to mention the game honestly feel kinda janky and somewhat lacking an identity. This was definitely made by Atlus' C team who couldn't decide what the game was supposed to be and focused too hard on blending SMT and Persona to the point that they forgot the core concepts and appeal of both, giving us a game that doesn't match the appeal of either. It has some things to like like character designs of an alright cyberpunk aesthetic but all of it is bogged down by some of the worst dungeon designs and combat I've seen in an SMT game. I hope you like running through empty corridors with no variation and hearing your party members speak literally any time you open any menu in combat (Seriously i don't know how that made it into the final game the way it is) plus the whole "Sabbath" System isn't nearly as fun or engaging as something like the press turn system or the 1 more system. Atlus tried to reinvent the wheel when they already have combat and dungeon designs mastered. I don't being negative as SMT and Persona are some of my favorite franchises ever but with this trying to be a hybrid of both it has massive expectations to live up to, even without those expectations this is still just a very meh game at best. If you are Persona fan reading this and you are looking to get into Mainline SMT this is NOT the game. Play either Nocturne or SMTV, I'd also recommend SMTIV and SMTIV:A if you have a 3DS still. All of those game are significantly better first entries into mainline SMT imo. If you are are a Persona fan looking for more Persona you will be disappointed. If you are an SMT fan or a fan of the OG Soul Hackers you will probably be even more disappointed. Overall i sadly wouldn't really recommend it to anyone and doubt this game will even be mentioned a few years from now. Hope Atlus can learn from this and this flop doesn't discourage us getting more SMT spin off games but i'm not super confident considering Persona being the money printer that it is.P.S. Haven't beaten the game myself but watched a friend of mine play through the whole game past where i was because i really couldn't be bothered. 7 hours was more than enough for me because the same blue-grey boxy dungeons gave me a headache.P.P.S. ATLUS ♥♥♥♥ OF WITH ♥♥♥♥♥♥ DAY 1 DLC LIKE THIS. It doesn't get much lower than locking fan favorite demons behind a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ paywall. Hope all of this has been a bit of a rude awakening for them when it comes to their future DLC practices as well as just making games that actually appeal to their core audiences.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is disappointing.It's stylish. It's "the sequel" to one of the weirdest SMT spinoffs, giving it a lot of room to experiment without being bound by past titles. If I were to describe to you the story or some of the events, it has a really, really interesting concept, and the cutscenes and characters are visually distinct and fun, with solid performances. It also has a few incredibly nice quality of life features (props to whoever decided to have an icon pop up over enemies in the field you need to take on for quests! That saved me so much time!).But this game feels like it was made on a budget of about $50 and all the coffee the team could ask for, Long stretches of the game are running through multiple "separate" dungeons which consist of the same tilesets. (Two of them are the most egregious, feeling straight up identical, including reusing their opening area.) The vast majority of gameplay is technically optional, being identical gray voids which will ask you to rerun the same three quests no less than FIFTEEN TIMES (this sounds like a joke, this is not a joke), but for the power curve or having any kind of money on hand, you'll want to take these on. Just using the demon compendium is massively grindy and more expensive than ever, and if you try to go without it, recruiting demons is more RNG-based than the series runs on*. I hate saying it, but the GAMEPLAY portion of this game feels unfinished and cobbled together from the assets they had on hand when deadline struck.I completed this game, I even got the "good" ending, but I feel like nothing sums up how soul-sucking this game is that the content was so bare-bones, and the cast dwindles so fast with named character deaths, that I kept thinking I was coming up on the final dungeon over and over for the last 12 hours of my 33 total runtime, because I didn't see how they could draw anything more out of what remained. (The fact that the final chapter is basically only hinted at in one scene and then actually contained more lead-up in the DLC campaign makes me suspect that the DLC was content removed from this base game to have ANYTHING to sell.) I will never call anyone who says they enjoyed this a liar, but I'm cautioning any single person reading to stay the hell away.Also I just realized at the end of this I literally cannot recall the soundtrack to this game. Not a single track.* Oh, you think I'm joking, or this is hyperbole? You need to do the following to recruit a demon. 1. Find one of YOUR demons in the preset 'search' points in the dungeon. 2. Hope that the demon has the recruitment icon over their head, not "key item", "item search", or "healing" instead. 3. Talk to them and hope that it's a demon you want or haven't already got, a thing you can't tell from a distance or until you engage. 4. There's one final bit of RNG in that now you have to do the bargaining step from other games, taking their requests until satisfied as usual. If any of these steps fail, return to 1. Have fun filling out a team.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate this rating system.It's hard to give this game a "not recommended" when in fact, the truth is somewhere in the middle. It's not a bad game at all. It's also not spectacular if you've played other games in the SMT universe. This game is a Cyberpunk interpretation of a SMT game. The world is quite interesting and the characters are well written. But just not enough time and effort was put into the game that it needed.To summarize, the game seems like it had a great blueprint with a lot of potential on paper, but due to a shoestring budget or other reasons, the game was never given the chance to blossom. The world while interesting, is bare bones. You are not told enough about the events that led up to the world you are now inhabiting. There aren't any Social Links/Confidants (Persona) to flesh out the world. Instead, you have one place that you can meet with your party members where you accumulate "Soul Points" in order to unlock gates in their respective mini-dungeons. The mini-dungeons of each character are repetitive and predictable.  Speaking of the dungeons, they are also mundane. Each dungeon plays the same, and while they might have small differences in size and scope, they are essentially the same kind of place and suffer from severe repetition.The story had potential but felt incomplete. The story, which is good on paper and could have had some really compelling moments, was held back by some instances of clumsy writing and the main event scripting which felt a bit rushed.The only place the game shines is the gameplay. It's good ol' SMT Devil Summoner gameplay. The gameplay does all the heavy lifting for the game because otherwise, I would have gotten bored and stopped around the 20th hour. So much potential wasted. If you have never played a SMT or Persona game and can get it on discount, then you should pick it up. Otherwise, save your money and wait for the next Persona game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one to recommend. If you're going into it for the story experience with some nice characters and voice acting with a serviceable battle system and a decent-to-good presentation, I would recommend this game. However, if you asked me to describe what I did for most of my 40 hour play through, most of what I describe would sound mediocre and not worth sinking time into. It rides that middle line really hard between recommending and not recommending.I'll get the bad stuff out of the way first. As many people have mentioned already, dungeon crawling in this game is repetitive, and frankly, bad. It feels tedious going through both the main story areas and the Soul Matrix (which is this games Tartarus or Mementos), and you are often expected to go through each of these areas several times to complete side quests or to level up your characters/fill out your demon collection.  I always have to put something on in the background, whether it's music or Youtube videos, because these dungeons are so mindless and boring. What's worse is that the further you get in, the more that dungeons incorporate new mechanics that only serve to waste more of your time, such as teleporters that don't function how you would expect them to that often times teleport you in the opposite direction of your goal. Unfortunately, this is where most of my play time came from, and what you have heard about the dungeon crawling experience from everyone else is true. Dungeon crawling is punctuated by the battle system of the game, which is perfectly acceptable, if a little boring. In my time with such games as Shin Megami Tensei 3 and Persona 5, the combat in Soul Hackers 2 feels far simpler, and mostly boils down to "use attacks that are good against weaknesses". It honestly feels a lot like modern Pokemon games, except more challenging. I was able to get through the entire story and most of the Soul Matrix with this strategy in mind on normal difficulty, though I wouldn't be surprised if the harder difficulties required you to incorporate more 4D chess into your strategies. It's an inoffensive combat system, but it's hardly something that's a main draw for this game. If you have played any SMT or Persona game, you will feel right at home, but don't expect anything revolutionary or progressive about itThe worst part about this game? The DLC, and how much it actually affects your experience. In the final few hours of my play time, I decided to purchase the BGM and Costume pack, as well as the "Booster Item Pack". Neither of these pieces of DLC were worth it, especially in the case of the BGM pack (how are you going to charge 13 dollars for music that already exists and a few costumes?). For the booster pack, this DLC is basically a god mode, allowing you to max out all your characters, AND demons, AND your in game wallet, and all you have to do is give 5 dollars to Atlus. I thought it was bad when Ubisoft added XP boosters to Assassin's Creed, but the booster pack for Soul Hackers 2 compromises every challenging encounter in this game and makes an already mindless game EVEN MORE mindless. This alone was getting me close to not recommending this game; it's obvious they cut out content from this game to sell it back to consumers on day 1, and Atlus (along with every other large video game company) needs to stop this crap.However, after thinking about my experience after playing this game for 40 hours across about 10 days, I realized that I enjoyed myself enough to warrant being satisfied with my experience once the credits started rolling. For those that wanted more of a Shin Megami Tensei story experience that revolves around adults as opposed to high school kids, I have to say that this was a nice, engaging story with a good cast of characters. Of course, this is mostly subjective, so it's difficult to sell this game to someone on just narrative alone. I will say, if you are into melodramatic anime-style JRPG's, you will really like the story, characters, setting, and just about everything that surrounds this game aesthetically. In particular, I want to give kudos to the voice cast for this game; most of the dialogue in this game is fully voice, and the English voice actors do a great job (gold stickers for both Ringo and Milady's voice actresses).Ultimately, my conclusion is that I do recommend this for those that want to see a cool story in a cool setting. If you don't think that you can stomach hours and hours of dungeon crawling, don't pick this up. Either way, I would highly recommend picking this up on sale and NOT buying the DLC. Another caveat on that: if you've never played any other SMT or Persona games, play those first. Persona 4 Golden is also on Steam, is way less expensive, and way better in general. Once you're balls deep into Shin Megami Tensei, then you should give this a shot. I know the optics around this game aren't exactly glowing, but I still had a good time going through the main game and helping Jack Frost kill a bunch of random demons 5 different times.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird one for me to review. It's basically the most "meh" JRPG in recent memorie for me, one that might just edge out into a fun but likely forgettable romp if you're a fan of Atlus's style of JRPGs like I am. Also, this game basically has nothing to do with devil summoners (likely why they removed the subtitle) or even Soul Hackers 1 (a devil summoners game) despite the concept of devil summoners existing in-world, as this is mostly subverted from the very get-go and your devil summoners even react to how they're not really acting like normal devil summoners anymore... most of your human opponents do, but it's ultimately kind of pointless fluff the way enemies are presented, though.That's okay, I guess. but I kind of wish it was a true devil summoner game... the other characters aren't all that interesting and imo it would have been better to have Ringo (the MC) be a classic devil summoner on her lonesome, summon demons directly, and just have her use soul hack to resurrect whatever character is to become the current story arc's central figure. Instead, you stick with a 4-man team forever and much of the game focuses on them while very lightly touching on stuff like what a human soul really is and what it means to be human.Unfortunately, it regards to that, there's just a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of wasted potential so far that has me really frustrated. This isn't new for JRPGs, which usually take a pretty shallow approach to concepts like good and evil. It's by intent; a lot of JRPGs share tropes with anime (specifically stuff like Naruto, Demon Slayer, Dragon Ball Z, etc), and shōnen, which is what that genre is called, is literally targeted at young boys. That's why a lot of JRPG MCs are young teenage boys, and why the stories never touch on darker or more mature themes like many western RPGs commonly do.But Soul Hackers 2 has an entire cast of adults exploring what it means to be human as well as the nature of death and the human soul... Not a child in sight (technically), and yet the game immediately and forever shies away from any meaningful engagement with those concepts. There's even an early joke about getting addicted to soul hacking (the supposedly emotional process that brings the dead back to life), so it's all shallow and lighthearted. Anyway, the game's leads are the same guys who did Tokyo Mirage and you can really tell... so yeah. At least the story premise here isn't laughably ridiculous from the start as it was in their last game.While not outright terrible (writing is fine, voice acting is good), it all adds up to a kind of meh storyline and you never really end up caring about any of the characters. The game also looks pretty simplistic and doesn't have very extensive scenery or dungeons, though the individual character models are well-done. I've never once been awed upon entering a new area or dungeon.Combat remains Atlus's best strength. It's probably what you'll enjoy the most, and there is a crapton of it. Unfortunately, there's a really repetitive, drab Mementos-like area (for those who come from Persona 5) that doesn't really add many twists (looks the same, pretty linear, all the quests involve just killing enemies or boss versions of normal enemies, etc), and boy does it get old and tedious after 5 seconds.Overall, it's a decent JRPG that I think true fans of JRPGs will view as a game with more positives than negatives, as most of those negatives are also things JRPG gamers have long dealt with. It's not an outright terrible game, and can serve to fill in time gaps in between what I would consider far better JRPGs (Persona 5, The first Crossbell Arc Trails game, etc), and if you play western RPGs too, there's probably a lot better upcoming options out there too depending on tastes.I'm going to give it a thumbs up, but I'm going to finish by saying this will never be a must-play and will probably be forgotten by the end of the year, and it's definitely never going to be considered one of Atlus's best games.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished it a few minutes ago.I loved the cast. Ringo is way more likeable than I initially expected from the trailers. The rest of the main cast is incredibly likeable, too. I've always found myself not fond of some main cast characters in other SMT games, but Soul Hackers 2 made everybody very likeable. _childDocuments_.review: I rate this game a 7.5/10. If you expect something of persona or mainline SMT quality, this game is not it.Overall I enjoyed my time with this game but it has some major flaws keeping it from being a 8/10 for me.This game is supposed to be a budget title and you can see it ingame, which is why I don't recommend buying this game at 60 dollars if you're not a huge Shin Megami Tensei fans (Go grab P5R instead if you haven't played it).What I like:- The characters. Ringo is a great main character with actual personalities- Progression system is fun with a lot of customization opportunities- Sabbath and commander skills are neat ideas- Stress-free combat for casual players like me (but it can be too way easy at times)- The game respects your time by allowing you to save and quit anywhere- A few great tracks with huge Nier vibes, as expected from Monaca- Good story, not great but it's a breath of fresh air from Persona and SMT games- 40 hours main story, a good length for this gameWhat I don't like- The dungeons. Even though I'm used to navigating bad dungeon designs (looking at you Tales of Berseria) it doesn't mean that I give them a pass, especially for a 60 dollars game. By the end of the game I just spam Assassin Steps to rush through dungeons.- The lack of variety. This one is the biggest flaw for me. In Persona games, the randomly generated dungeons change overtime in terms of soundtrack and overall theme. In Soul Hackers 2, there's only 1 track for Story dungeons, 1 other track for Soul Matrix, 1 track for every single story boss, etc.- Combat is too easy with every single enemy advantages removed from hitting your weak points- Demons and some materials require a lot of running around and pray that RNGesus will give you what you actually want- Skill inheritance isn't explained very clearly. I still don't know how they pick which skills to inherit by the end of the game.- ♥♥♥♥♥♥ DLC practices. Atlus keeps trying to hammer in the worst DLCs possible in their games and I don't support this one bit.

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes me wonder why Steam still doesn't have a "Mixed" option.The only reason I am giving "Recommended" is because it is a 6.5/10 game for me (so it's above 5/10).Basically it's a very average game with nothing too special going for it, as it feels a downgrade compared to the other SMT and it's spin-off titles. I'd pick (and emulate) any other title before playing this one, unless you really need an easy and accessible title to get into the better games in this franchise.For the positives, gotta say that the graphics and the boss battle OST are great, and if Atlus need to learn something from this game, is that having a MC with personality and voice actor was a real positive change. Also the QOL features like fast-forward button and skip sabbath animation made the game much more smoother and better to play, helping the gameplay be more enjoyable.The other stuff though were very underwhelming, like the dungeons, battle system change from press turn to sabbaths (and demons becoming "just stats"), and the story and the characters were cliche and made no sense in some situations, despite the setting was promising and had some good ideas. Also the side quests were annoying as most of them require you to repeat cleared dungeons that already weren't great in the first place, so it makes the game even more tedious and I didn't bother finishing them, and even gave up on the "extra story" dlc because of it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is for 0.01% of people. It's been lambasted and given mixed reviews by basically everyone, including MegaTen fans.While I understand their opinion and can see where they're coming from - I'm here to tell you that this game... is actually good (if you fall into that 0.01%)Essentially, this title is a strange hodgepodge of classic SMT and more modern Persona-like character interactions.If you came here for Persona, you'll be sorely disappointed when you find a different battle system and significantly less side "activities" and social links. If you're here for SMT? The battle system seems simplified at first and might scare you away from the lack of press turn (but is actually harder than SMTV on hard and Nocturne, excluding BS encounters), and some anime-isms might irk you.What really makes this enjoyable is that classic "average rating game" nostalgia that those familiar with Dreamcast/PS2/1, etc era are familiar with. When dungeons were total BS mazes and you could get hardstuck on fights if you weren't prepared. Lower difficulties unfortunately do this game a disservice. It's bizarre to me that the designers would make a game with classic dungeons designed to troll you and throw in "easy" mode combat and other things to try to get non-rpg gamers, when none of those people would EVER enjoy this dungeon design. You have to be a very specific type of person to enjoy these "monotonous", labyrinthine, teleport-heavy, one-way door dungeons. If you're that 0.01% that likes mapping and being trolled? This one's for you. The combat on Very Hard is surprisingly good. You'll get your ass beat far more frequently on bosses than SMTV hard, etc. Going in blind, you're forced to get your ♥♥♥♥ rocked, learn the mechanics. rebuild your team, and repeat quite often on bosses. It's arduous and annoying, but satisfying once you make a full party and get the rhythm going.  Every turn, you're swapping demons on your party members, issuing commands, holding sabbaths, and so on with little room for error. Normally, during SMT games, you eventually become absolutely broken and steamroll the game. This doesn't really happen on Very Hard, as the lack of items, exp falloff, and high difficulty forces you to constantly change strategy and team members/builds.The story is average and fairly predictable, but Ringo as the MC makes for a refreshing change of pace. (it definitely feels like Arrow was supposed to be the MC at some point and the story was hastily rewritten).If you're here because you liked Soul Hackers 1 (or the rest of the Devil Summoner series) - unfortunately, this has very little to do with those outside references, NPCs, etc.If you happen to be the extremely rare type of gamer that likes difficult RPG combat that challenges your teambuilding, and don't mind essentially doing the same dungeons for hours repeatedly, or revel in traditional teleport troll dungeons (a la Strange Journey, but less visually interesting), this one's for you. This one's all about the boss battles and classic bs dungeons. If you're anyone else... this game will probably be an unfun, painful experience (and that's ok because game variety is good and not everything is for everyone).

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this isn't Atlus at their best, but they still delivered an interesting game.It's pretty good if you want a simpler game where you can take your time with progression and grind levels in dungeons.It's fascinating to hear the protagonist speak and to witness how expressive she it. Normally Atlus protagonist tend to be silent, but not this one!Ringo is actually a pretty big selling point for me, It shows what Atlus can do with a fully voice protagonist and I wish they would do it again in the future.Music is pretty good and memorable, the map is also very appealing style wise, graphic wise it does lack a bit.The turn based combat is very similar with other modern Atlus games, so while they didn't evolve it much in this game , they did bring us a good combat system.Game also has a pretty good run time at around 30 hours, but the dungeons are very simplistic, it's literally just a bunch of hallways that stretch from one end to another and they all look the same, you may also choose to run away from enemies or engage with them.You do that until you reach the next bit of story and then your repeat this exact process in the next place.That's why most people are mixed about the game and so am I.It's not a bad game, just very repetitive still if you want to grind and make powerful allies while trying to clear the story, this is definitely worth it at a discount. I would not recommend the game at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has pros and cons, but if you like JRPGs or other games from the Megami Tensei universe I'd say this is worth the buy on sale. I got it on sale and have no buyer's remorse.Pros: -Characters are well written and the story is immersive. -Not too grindy, farming is relatively easy as you progress-Decent challenge on normal, not punishing but without sufficient level grinding and strategy you can get beat down, especially by Aion's optional bosses.Cons-Freezes on Steam Deck a lot. I had to exit the game and reboot it every so often.-Dungeons can be a bit of a slog, especially the soul matrixMatter of personal taste-It didn't have any music tracks that REALLY slapped, like "One More God Rejected" from Shin Megami Tensei 3, but some people might enjoy the soundtrack anyway.-Sabbath system in my opinion, while fun, is not as enjoyable as the Press Turn system from Shin Megami Tensei, especially compared to SMT5 or SMT4A. However, once you learn how it works, team building around it ends up being pretty rewarding.Overall I'd say it's a B game, good not great.

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely a divisive entry in the Devil Summoner series. If you walk in expecting gameplay in the likes of the original Soul Hackers or of the Raidou Kuzunoha duology, you will be very disappointed. This gameplay is more along the lines of other Megami Tensei games, namely Shin Megami Tensei: Strange Journey and Tokyo Mirage Sessions. Though I wish Soul Hackers 2 had dungeons on the level of Strange Journey. This game is definitely worth it at a discount where you could score the complete package at $30 at most.

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks pretty and has some really good music.The story is simple, but builds up hype at the right moments.The combat and progression are great, which for me was really the main reason to play.Unfortunately the dungeons didn't really seem all that interesting.The sidequests were also mostly time wasting fillers.I was also a bit disappointed by the lack of fusion power spikes, I generally felt that my demons were sometimes weaker after fusing them.Overall I really liked the game, 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. The characters and story are definitely the highlight of the game. The characters are very likeable and have a lot of depth. The story has some very emotional moments and some good twists. The battle system feels kinda like an extension to Strange Journey's battle system. The game's biggest problem is the dungeons all feel the same, mostly because almost all of them have the same music. However I feel that the pros outweigh the cons. The game feels like a combination of SMT and Persona and in a good way. The way that you learn about the different characters feels more like part of the rest of the game than Persona's social links. Soul Hackers 2 is not perfect but it is a fun game with a lot of heart in it. Also don't worry about buying the lost numbers dlc, you're not missing much. If that didn't exist I bet this game would have better reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game gets an unfair comparison to Atlus' giant franchises like SMT and Persona. I personally like the story, the characters and their motivations. The dystopian cyberpunk atmosphere was done right. The music is a bop (special mention to COMP Smith and Battle of Devil Summoners). Character and Demon designs are beautiful and very stylish. Sabbath system doesn't bother me that much, in fact, I like it and it's a breath of fresh air from SMT's Press Turn system and Persona's 1-more system.Now the actual downsides of this game, for me, are the dungeon designs. They're... boring. They're just hallways, nothing very special. There's teleporters but that's it. Soul Matrix's dungeons were the worst, especially on floors 4-5. Lots of teleporters to teleport you on God knows where. You gotta memorize where they go or write it down, else you're going to be stuck to that floor for a while to the point that it gets frustrating. For Lost Numbers DLC, it was alright, I guess. I liked Nana and her story. However, the DLC Dungeon is once again, the worst. Every floor was basically almost the same. Also, same as the other dungeons in the base game, there's nothing very special with it. It was a drag all the way down to the last floor.As for other DLCs, they offer nothing except some "conveniences" and fan-service to other Atlus games. If you like costumes and custom battle BGMs, then get them, otherwise they're not really essential.Overall, I have issues with the game, mainly on dungeon design, but still, I really like it.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Persona but not SMT, so my perspective comes from there. I've also never heard of Soul Hackers 1.Pros:- Genuine protagonist. Ringgo is great, especially when compared to Joker. Everything else in that world has so much personality it always felt weird the protag didn't. As I say, Ringgo is good fun.- Simplified mechanics. This isn't a Persona or SMT game and it didn't seem to be trying to be. It's essentially a new IP and an introduction into the way Atlus do things. It works really well with that mindset. It's also far less of a time investment than Persona.- The stuff Atlus usually nails. The world, shops, people. Yeah, they nail them as usual.- Persona 4-esque dungeons. I didn't really get on with the palaces and liked the re-grindable dungeons from 4. This is closer to that but without the demon of procedural generation. Being able to chill out and fight demons is nice.Cons:- Hardcore fans might be turned off by the simplified mechanics. The Persona/Demon fusing is barebones in particular.- Simplified soundtrack. The battle and dungeon track are both good, but I didn't miss an 'S' there. You get a song for every battle and a song for the dungeon, that repeat. - Default camera controls are DREADFUL. Change 'em.I enjoyed it in the same way I enjoyed Scarlet Nexus, but there are two sides to that coin. I recommend trying it if you want to try the Persona/SMT mechanics but don't want to jump into the massive rabbit hole those IP's represent. Also, please create actual protags in future Persona games Atlus! You've shown us you can do it!

_childDocuments_.review: There's a reason why all the negative reviews are complaining about Day 1 DLC and Denuvo:It's because the game is actually really good and these meta-concerns are all there is to complain about. Tons of side content, combat is just complicated enough to keep you thinking strategically, Hard mode is actually hard and requires effort.   With the side dungeons, quests, food, collectibles and etc. it almost seems like there's too MUCH distracting from the story at times. Definitely not a lack of things to do. The story seems decent so far, though I'm just getting started on that. Dungeons are of the simplistic style that Atlus is known for, but they are pretty and not oversized. The game runs well on my moderately-good PC. Put as simply as possible, if you're a fan of Atlus JRPGs in general, there's no reason you wouldn't like this one in particular.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Get this game if you're looking to play a Megaten game but you simultaneously don't want to play an SMT or a Persona game. I don't think this game deserves most of the initial hate it got, but it doesn't do anything groundbreaking on it's own.Pros: +Story and setting are interesting+Ringo and the crew are a great main cast of characters, Ringo especially is a great protagonist.+Upgrade system.+Great demon fusion and unit customization, par for any Megaten game.+Commander Skills, Sabbaths, and Demon Recon make it unique compared to other Megatens.Cons:-Dungeon design is bad, outside of maybe the final area. -Demon negotiations are simplified.-Some aspects of the story/setting could've done with a bit more fleshing out.-No Press Turns/One More in combat (Subjective, I personally didn't miss them b/c of Commander Skills but others may not like this)-DLC is not worth it at full price

_childDocuments_.review: Many who need this might not see it, but the steam cloud saves are broken and will corrupt your game. In order to fix this, screw around in the main menu (start new game, exit before selecting difficulty, open config, mess around in it a little, go back to title, etc.) and eventually it will somehow uncorrupt your save. I saw that this worked for multiple people online and I can confirm that it worked for me too. I hope this helps someone who fell into the same "trap" as me. On another note, this game runs well on steam deck although I haven't been able to get mods to work (such as DLC costumes outside of battle).

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because I wanted to know why it was so disliked, and luckily I still have no clue. The game is fun, the combat is nice, the difficulty is fine, and the characters are likeable. I'm getting the idea that the people who disliked this were just Persona fans who were upset that it isn't Persona, and Smt fans that are upset that it doesn't have a little "Shin Megami Tensei" above or below the title. I've seen people complain about the variety of the dungeons, but honestly that's also fine. In Persona 5 you spend hours in a palace with like one theme throughout the whole place. As someone who went back these past 2 years and played as many Atlas games as possible from smt 1 to 4/4a, and Persona 3-5. Is it Digital Devil saga or Smt 3? Maybe not, but it's a bit more enjoyable than the DS/3DS games and I absolutely loved all of the DS/3DS games. I highly recommend this game, especially for Smt fans looking for a game with just a little more story/character interaction, but not an overbearing amount, and Persona fans looking for a game with more gameplay, and less planning/hanging out in it.

_childDocuments_.review: There have been issues with the DLC content based on where you have bought the game and/or DLC. Be advised that not all DLC may work correctly at the time of the writing. This game runs decently on Steam Deck but latest stable and Proton experimental will have effects displayed incorrectly or visual effects missing. The power draw for me was quite high so don’t expect long battery life at this point.I enjoyed the game, it’s fun Atlus rpg with pretty fun battle system. It’s not Atlus’ most expansive game but if you enjoy Persona series and other Atlus games it’s well worth the time. I recommend this game.Soul Hackers 2 is next in line of the Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Summoner: Soul Hackers series. The game’s story does not really connect to the first one’s story, but there are mentions here and there. You can jump in this game without feeling like a lot of things are missing. If you are familiar with other Shin Megami Tensei games or the Persona series, expect to see lot of familiar demons from the series.The game is typical Atlus dungeon JRPG. You advance the story, do sidequests and roam dungeons while defeating enemies in turn-based battles. The battles follow same principles as other Atlus RPGs, hit the enemy’s weakpoint to deal with them quickly. The difference this time is the Sabbath-system, where each time you hit enemy’s weakness, you gather “stacks”. After your team’s turn is over, you will unleash Sabbath attack based on those stacks. For run of the mill battles, you also have auto-battle feature.The story is pretty standard JRPG story, nothing exceptional, but for most part it will keep your interest up with side-quests and some interesting concepts. I for one enjoyed the different setting and more mature characters and lack of the usual high school shenanigans.The game runs quite well on PC. Your graphical options include the typical display modes, an FPS cap with 30,60, 120, 144 and unlimited varieties, vsync option and your average “low, medium, high, very high” settings. For Anti-aliasing and depth of Field you can either enable or disable the options. Unfortunately, the game does not offer clearer AA options. The sound options allow you to se volume levels, select sound device and change the voice over language from Japanese to English if for some reason you want to do so. The game allows you to set your key config and supports a wide range of symbols from different controllers from xbox controller to Dualsense controller as well as a keyboard + mouse controls. The game does not feature any accessibility features apart from subtitles and message speed, which is a shame.For gameplay options you have some basic options such as different difficulty levels and camera positions. You can also change the BGM options for battles.The DLC is mostly cheats and some regrettable choices. The Booster item Pack essentially is cheats and the accessories included with the costume DLC are very strong. Bonus Demon Pack includes some iconical demons from SMT series, such as Mara and they will be very high level and available for free. The Bonus Story Arc is a separate set of side quests with its own story that you go through alongside your main quest.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite all odds and all the bad business practices surrounding this game, I honestly had a good time and that's due in large part to the really great cast. I played in the eng dub and everyone really brought their A game to this. Dungeons may feel same-y, but honestly they give you a lot of necessary tools to mitigate that with map skills you unlock in the matrix. Story, while done before, is bolstered when following the entire cast in all the hangouts and extra world building. I'm always a sucker for these types of futuristic settings too, and the techno vibes were great.But, honestly, most important thing I gotta highlight is Ringo. They made a stellar protag worth following and I hope this can serve as a blueprint for future games to start including voiced protags with personality. It doesn't ALWAYS have to be that way of course, but I'd love to see it again in a future Atlus title. Here's hoping, especially with all the enjoyment I found following Ringo.
