_childDocuments_.review: After plaything almost 2 whole playthroughs and getting all but 5 achievments, I feel like I can finally take the time to review this gameI'll give a summarized version, and an extended version of this reviewSummarized: It has good visual presentation and voicework, but falls short in every other categoryMAJOR MAJOR SPOILERS BELOWExtended review:Oh man where do I start...? I'll start with the positives I guess.Pros:-Soul Hackers 2 has some really nice visual designs and presentation, I really liked the aesthetic overall, the whole cybery futuristic dystopia is nice, as well as the character designs themselves, be it the main cast or the extra shop owner characters like Victor or the quest giver Madam Ginko, the designs are top notch-Demon Fusion is still fun to do, although it feels pretty much unchanged from other games, so nothing too interesting, but at least it still works as intended-Game doesn't have any massive bugs (that I'm aware of) and runs fairly smoothly-Music is alright, nothing too spectacular given ATLUS's track record, but passable-Voice work was really good in this game, in both English and Japanese-Saizo is kinda based sometimesNow onto the bad...we're gonna be here for a whileCons:-Small nitpick to start, the default game options are godawful, the default camera angle and FOV make exploring dungeons a nightmare but thankfully you can change that. Same goes for loading screen tips artificially inflating load times, they can be disabled thankfully-Characters are really boring in this game, genuinely some of the most forgettable characters in any game I've played recently except Saizo, and he's just alright at best, the only memorable part about Arrow, Milady, Figue, Ringo, Raven, and so on, are their visual designs, otherwise they have nothing that makes them stand out, Arrow being generic anime good guy, and Milady being the "tough girl who refuses to open up, but has a soft spot for children" as her entire character, Raven ends up being a "morally grey" villain who wants to save these orphans by...destroying the world?!?! It doesn't make sense and is hardly morally grey, it's just bland-Story is very very VERY generic anime, and very very forgettable, starts with standard megaten "apocalypse" plot, but it tells you everything important within the first 2 hours, like Yatagarasu, Phantom Society, the Covenants, summoning the Great One, yadayada, it shows its hand right away and then barely builds on it at all, the numerous plot twists are all predictable and fail to make me care about what happens next. Like, the whole Soul Hacking thing barely even comes into play throughout the entire game, only like 6 times in the ENTIRE story is Soul Hacking even used, 3 times for your party members, 1 time for Arrow to give the purple covenant, 1 time failed with Figue and Raven, and 1 time to rescue Figue on one of the endings.All the story exposition happens in one of two locations, the safehouse, or the orphanage, and very rarely in the Axis itself.The whole story revolves around gathering the covenants to stop the end of the world...that's it. The individual character stories are pretty bland as well or just handled poorly, and speaking of being handled poorly, character stories happen in the Soul Matrix or during the hangout scenes at the bar. The Soul Matrix sucks major ass, and the hangout scenes aren't engaging enough to be memorable, which only further hurts the memorability of the characters. The game has 2 endings, both are similar and neither of them are very interesting, effectively leaving things off virtually unchanged from the start of the game. -Gameplay: I'm gonna split this one into two parts, Dungeon Crawling and Combat.    -Dungeon crawling: Oh man this is by FAR the worst aspect of this game, having to explore and return to the various "dungeons" as they barely qualify as.This game has multiple boring dungeons, between the shipping areas, the subway lines, the towers, and the Soul Matrix, the only one that felt even slightly different was the final dungeon, and it still sucked hard.The shipping districts are just small containted areas, nothing special about either of them, West or East shipping districts.The Subway lines are just that, abandoned subway lines with almost nothing of interest except for this one door puzzle that goes away after you beat it, and there are 2 of these identical subway dungeons for you to mindlessly roam around in.The Ozaki Hope towers are a smidge more interesting, with the elevator puzzle, but that's about it, otherwise it's the same mindless roaming around, aside from this one segment where you go through the vents as Mimi, the little owl navigator bot, which is extremely slow and still have to deal with enemies while doing so.....it sucks, plain and simpleThe Municipal tower is this weirdish dungeon with doors and "teleporters" that transport you either up or down depending on the flow of the water...and that's it.Soul Matrix, the dungeon you revisit the most because there's 1 for each character except ringo, so you have 3 identical dungeons, that boil down to doors, telporters, and a second version of teleporters....yay....I just listed eveything unique between all of the dungeons, now here's the flaws they all share.All of them are enormous, long, spiraling empty halls with nothing to do except fight or run past enemies....which makes exploring them not only very tedious over the course of the roughly 60 hours of main story progression, but very boring as well.On top of having boring empty halls for every dungeon, enemies spawn every two seconds, forcing you to stop and swat them away, wasting time.Actually progressing through these dungeons really sucks when you realize that Ringo moves slower than a paralytic grandma who just got shot in the knees, and the only way to speed her up is by using a skill that costs 10 MP to speed you up for like 20ft worth of distance, which you can only unlock by progressing Milady's Soul Matrix....Also the navigator is insanely annoying, someone invented a mod just to shut the navigator up...that much should be self explanatory.Combat: BUCKLE UP ♥♥♥♥♥♥ BECAUSE THIS RANT IS GONNA BE MORE INTERESTING THAN THE BATTLE SYSTEM-Battling: You and your party members can each equip some gear, augment mistiques, and a demon eachcombat is turn based and lacks the fun aspects of other smt games, like the press turn system, or even the baton pass from Persona 5, and 1more function from Persona 3 onwards. Instead you are rewarded with a Sabbath for hitting weaknesses....which is just damage at the end of your turn to all enemies....for doing the normal thing...so the gimmick with combat is a non interactive reward for playing the game normally....lame...and you can only upgrade it through having certain demon skills or stack bonuses applied, but it fundamentally remains the same.      There's no sabbaths for enemies either, so the enemies are always at a disadvantage to you, which is an oddity for SMT and Persona, as enemies could take advantage of both Press turns, and 1more in those games.      Light and Dark skills are gone entirely, replaced with Ruin, which is basically just ailment moves that also deal damage...      Without any sort of interactive gimmick, battles become really boring, especially with the removal of Demon Negotiation putting the final nail in the coffin, it just devolves to hitting the weakness and moving on, no strategy or tactics in any capacity.With a lack of strats, progression just becomes a boring grind.I have more I could say, but I can't fit much more into this steam review, so here's my final verdictGame has good visuals and presentation, everything else is ♥♥♥♥, and I can't recommend it, even if you're a longtime fan of the series. 2/10, don't buy it, even on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent SMT game better then expected. The twist to the all out attach mechanic is definitely interesting. It's been a while since there was stacking (somewhat like SMT4). Battle system is not that deep and there isn't really all that much to do in the over world but compared to SMT V there's still something.Hopefully the patch comes out and fixes the issues with encounter rate and character movement speed.The game is overpriced with day 1 DLC. 100% should not have broken out the side story and extra demons into dlc.Definitely a lot of review bombing going on here especially from people who have only played Persona or started gaming in 2010.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished at 60 hours, which is just about the perfect length.  This is a fun Persona spin off game that I really enjoyed despite some issues. There’s no cringey high school setting, no children protagonists, minimal social link BS and no pervy dialogue…right there, it’s a gem.The combat was fun and strategic without being over complicated or difficult, but definitely some difficulty ramp-ups on a few bosses.  I liked the characters and was invested in them and their stories.  The main story was decent and it kept me entertained.  It’s quite different than the Persona and SMT games, and I guess that’s one reason everyone is crying about in the reviews here.  Me? I am glad it’s so different. Unfortunately, the game has an ugly, copy ‘n paste dungeon problem that tries to ruin it all…the soul matrix in particular, with its horrific teleporter puzzles that plague the later levels, are the worst.Still, I enjoyed fusing and leveling the demons and just about every other facet of the game. I totally recommend it if you wish your Persona games were less silly high school cliques and more intense "save the world" stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Soul Hackers 2

_childDocuments_.review: I believe that a lot of people of people who post negative reviews have mostly played main-line SMT/Persona games, which, as high-budget productions, strive to excel at every aspect. Soul Hackers 2, as you may guess, does not, but I can confidently say that I became attached to the characters and was deeply engaged in the gameplay and preparation of my whole party for tough battles. As a mid-budget game it had to cut some corners - in this case, those are dungeon level designs and and side-quests. As one person on twitter said "if you didn't mind Persona 4 dungeons for 100 hours, you won't mind Soul Hackers 2 dungeons for ~50 hours". And side-content is just bare-bones, but luckily non-essential for the most part. I do not regret money nor time spent on this game - the protagonist Ringo is also one of the best among Atlus cast. That being said, if you expect a Persona 5-like behemoth, maybe just wait for sale until it gets to 40$ and go for it :). P. _childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the game. Had a few issues but overall a good game that does a lot of things better than a lot of other recent Atlus games. First off, the graphics. I love the visual style of this game. Its like P5 with its comic book aesthetic, but dialed to 100. The colors pop out very well. All the characters look extremely vibrant. My greatest praise goes to the demons. While using the same models as P5 and SMTV, with the use of colors and textures the demons look better then they ever have been. Going back to P5 after this makes that game look kinda dull. One thing this game does worse than P5 though is the UI design. P5 still clears this game in that sense, but the UI is still miles better than SMTV. The music is also very good. Its not as good as the previous atlus game, but there still are a lot of good songs. The jewelery shop theme, all three of the boss themes, and the hideout theme come to mind the most. The reason for lack of songs is probably budget. Now for gameplay. I am going to get the negatives out of the way first. The dungeons suck. But, they arent as bad as people say. People went through p3 and p4's dungeons, and never complained, even though they were way worse. And do not tell me those games are old so its okay, all the Atlus games that preceded p3 and p4 had way better dungeons. While the dungeons in this game are bland mazes, they function as a place to do combat, which imo is amazing. The combat in this game is amazing. I know people complained about human party members, but this game does them perfectly. Demons in this game function like Personas. You equip them to party members and they give you stat boosts, skills, and elemental affinities. How this is different than the modern Persona games is that finally every party member can change out their demon. In P3 having mc being the only one with more than one persona worked because of the AI party members, in p4 and p5 it sucked. All the party members might as well not be there as there is zero customization to them while the mc just does everything. It is so lame. Instead SH2 works like the older persona games, where you only have four party members who are all extremely customizable. Not only can each member freely use any demon, you can also customize them by increasing their elemental affinities and giving them accessories so each party member feels different. This customization goes into the gameplay as it really does have that SMT feel of making the perfect party to fight the boss, making it very satisfying. Managing your demons by fusing them is as fun as ever, especially since they brought back smtiv's fusion search functions. Ringo's Aion skills also add a lot of strategy. They allow fast swapping out of demons like in Persona, but puts a limit on it so its not OP. Another Aion skill is increasing stacks, which segways into the main battle mechanic. The Sabbath system. In this system when you get a weakness you build a stack. At the end of your turns you summon a demon for each stack and you can do an all out attack for a lot of damage. I really like this system since it becomes a puzzle for getting the most stacks. Later on you will unlock Aion skills and passive upgrades which give more stacks depending on if certain conditions are met. It becomes a puzzle to see how high you can get the stack. Now for story, I will keeo it brief to avoid spoilers. I really liked it. Its simple, has good twists, and is very personable to the characters. The characters are all interesting with their motives, and the writing quality is a leaps better than P5's (p5's writing is doo doo so ig its not a high bar). This game avoids p5's writing pitfalls by not having mean spirited humor, making all characters equally shine, and also being more concise. Characters mostly do not repeat the same plot points a million times. I also find the plot point of most people yearning the apocalypse interesting. Is it the best story ever told: no. But imo the plot still clears smtv, and persona 3-5.Overall I recommend this game. My only issues are the dungeons, and I guess the lack of budget. The side content also has that feeling but it still reinforces the satisfying gameplay loop. Another issue is the dlc, which is disgusting I agree. I still think the base game is good enough though, also p5 had 80 dollars worth of dlc which had even more overly priced costumes and op personas but no one cared for some reason. In short, if you like the gameplay side of smt with fun battles, and if you like simple but satisfying stories, you will probablt like this game. Most of the issues are budget issues, and overall I was able to look past them. The hate is overblown for this game, reminds me of the TLOU2 hate, where people were more mad because the game wasnt what they were expecting. If this game interests you, please play it.

_childDocuments_.review: is this the best megaten game out there?nois is truly worth $60?probably not.but do i love this game anyways? absolutely. The combat is the classic weakness system megaten is famous for, although it does deviate with the sabbath system rather than the press turn or one more combat system, but its still just as rewarding. By downing enemies using their weakness or getting a critical hit, it adds to the sabbath counter, in which more and more demons can participate and deal extra damage, as well as some having sabbath skills that allow for extra moves being able to be pulled off (extra damage, health/mp restore, etc).The characters are also, well, full of character! They do fall a bit cliche at times, but Arrow and Milidy's constant bickering, with Saizo just in the backround trying to stay neutral was pretty amusing, and Ringo's initial snarkiness at how primative humanity is was always fun. In fact, Ringo in general is just a fun character who calls everyone out on their BS.Honestly, the only thing i can really say the game was lacking in were the dungeons. I wasnt expecting Persona 5 levels of design, but the long corridors lead me to think that the dungeons were originally going to be randomly generated (ala persona 3/4), especially the SOUL Matrix, the "mementos" as it were of the game. Other than bland dungeon design though, the game might be a tad on the shorter side (no side content start to finish being about 6-7 hours, doing only the manditory 1st floor of the matrix and minimal demon fusion), but on a "normal" playthrough, its probably going to take around 9-10 hours, especially when counting in the DLC.Overall, i give the game a 7.5/10Its fun and enjoyable, but not for everyone. the game had a small budget and it shows, but it does everything it can with that budget.$60 is totally worth it, but hey, it doesnt hurt your wallet to see if it goes on sale for ~$40.

_childDocuments_.review: as of 20 hours into the gameStory/Character: 5/5Aesthetic/Graphics: 4/5Combat/Gameplay: 3.5/5I personally love this game. It fits nicely into what I was looking for and my experience with the SMT series but I can see the caveats a lot of players have with it. so I think it's best served to just say who I think will enjoy this game. Who I think would enjoy this game: Soul Hackers 2 seems to be ATLAS targeting new adult fans of Persona. The story is less shy about treating you like an adult and all of the characters are adults themselves. So I think the person that is going to get the most out of this title are people looking for something a bit more mature than Persona 5 but are relatively new fans of the franchise. Explanation of scores:ATLAS at this point has a reputation for love-able and memorable characters, and Soul Hackers 2 is no exception. The characters all have endearing chemistry and great well written banter that makes it easy to get attached. The most standout example of the characters and writing is our protagonist Ringo who is just as active and well, if not better, written a character as any other in the game, a notable and welcome departure from the silent and self-insert protagonists we see so often in RPGs in general. Aesthetics wise Soul Hackers 2 delivers on what it offers. A bright and colorful cyberpunk world with a high quality soundtrack. The set pieces and aesthetics of the game are clean, well constructed, and have a memorable identity and flare. Meanwhile the soundtrack delivers on the style we're used to in the Persona franchise, albeit without the catchy vocal tracks. The only draw back for the looks and aesthetics of this game is the volume of aesthetics. Soul Hackers 2 shows its more limited budget in stretching the assets it has, however those same Assets are not wanting for quality.Soul Hackers 2 is a distinct flavor of the SMT franchise while also borrowing elements of the persona series specifically with it's social gameplay elements exploring side character stories. As far as SMT games go the combat is familiar and different enough that newcomers to the SMT style of games will find a distinct different flavor of combat vs recent entries such as Persona 5 but veterans of the SMT franchise may feel it doesn't stand out compared to other games from the series.

_childDocuments_.review: 7 Hours of gameplay opinions and tips:     - Very approachable for newcomers, a good entry for veterans but may feel a little oversimplified at times if you're used to the difficulty curve for SMT/Persona/DS games     - English voiceover is okay, but Japanese audio will make the game feel less awkward     - Agreed. Day 1 DLC is a pain, bought the extra story DLC and so far it has made very little impact on gameplay. Would love to see Atlus/Sega atone for this sin ;)     - Default settings for the game are terrible, fix your camera, text speed, etc ASAP when you start the game     - Music is solid     - Demon merging system is nice and simple with the new "search fusion" filters     - Character upgrade elements are an interesting take on the "Glory" mechanic that SMT 5 intoduced to the franchise     - Dungeons haven't been anything special but they haven't been a pain either     - Story is actually pretty good. Cutscenes and dialogue are a lot more lengthy and slightly less interesting than SMT 5 in my opinion, but if you're the kind of person who likes long storylines you'll like this one.     - So far I think a $40-$50 price tag would have made more sense for this game on release day since it does feel a bit watered down for a SMT/Persona/DS game but honestly you can justify buying it for $60 if you're pretty diehard on the franchise and want to play it ASAP and want a solid PC option until P5R gets ported.Overall I do recommend playing this game but perhaps waiting for a sale or solid free DLC drop if you've been on the fence about buying it. It doesn't quite justify the price tag just yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is another title in the long line of the Shin Megami Tensai umbrella collection of games and another entry in ATLUS's commitment to bringing the games over to the PC market overtime for past releases and same day release for newer content.The immediate comparison people will attempt to make with it being a SMT title is to Persona 5/5 Royal. The only real comparisons you can make are the demons you can summon/recruit and a giant stretch to the hangouts you get with each party member at the bar in the city and the occasional dialogue choice that gives bonus points to their relationship level. The "Soul level" of your party member is required to delve deeper into their own personal dungeons, which are sort of just bland and uninspired grey looking "mindscapes" with no differentiation between your three party members. As you progress you unlock gates, as long as you have the required soul level for them, which gives you a little more backstory into that character and gives them an unique passive or usable ability.Your party is limited and small, four total, and you get all members around 15-20 minutes. You really only do one very small dungeon with two people and meet the third at the end of that and the fourth immediately after in the city you visit. While it's a staple for most RPGs to have bigger parties that you end up getting new members well into the game and have to switch out members if you want to level them but Soul Hackers confines its story into these four protagonists and their involvement in the storyline.The overall story is basic. Make sure the big bads don't summon their big angry god to rewrite humanity. Anyone who has played a SMT title knows that's just how things go. Where you get involved is how the characters flow into the story. The ideals they hold, their different paths they took in the Summoner world and how/why they're working together now. It does delve into some serious stuff, but that's par for the course for a SMT title.The gameplay is standard SMT fair. Turn based combat, use demon abilities to hit weaknesses, weaknesses build up a gauge which stacks up and at the end of your turn does damage based on the stacks and resets. You explore fairly simple, cityscape type dungeons for the most part and they're not too hard to go through. The only real challenge/annoying aspects is the last dungeon and certain floors of the protagonists personal dungeons that have warp elements to them which, if I'm being honest, had me looking for a map after 15 minutes of getting nowhere. While in the dungeons, your demons will be in random areas with something to give you. You can recruit demons from them, they can give you items (and notably key items that unlock more hangouts to get more Soul Points for certain party members), or heal you a bit. Depending on the difficulty you play on, you can burn through the game in probably 40-50 hours while still exploring all the areas to try and get everything."Well that sounds like a very neutral and bland sounding game, so why recommended it?" Thank you for asking, random internet person.It's not a really a bad game. Nor is it a great game. It's a 7. It's just a generally good, relatively simple RPG. Being a SMT fan as a whole, from the mainline # series to all of their spinoffs on varying consoles and handhelds, it satisfied the itch of a SMT title. For what it does and tries to do, it does it well. If you jump into this because you finally got to play Persona 5 Royal, or even Persona 4 Golden, expecting all SMT titles to be that way then yeah you'll probably be disappointed. Soul Hackers 2 is its own thing, as is the other spinoffs like Persona, Raidou, Devil Survivors, Digital Devil Saga, the mainline #'d series, Strange Journey, etc. You also don't need to play the original Soul Hackers because this has nothing to do with that one at all.The latest patch added some much needed quality of life elements as well, most notably faster dungeon movement and battles.

_childDocuments_.review: . but: If you've come from SMT or the Persona Series, you'll be very disappointed with Soul Hackers 2.- The combat starts slow and boring, but it gets good and interesting mid-late game.This game is also grindy as ♥♥♥♥, which wouldn't be a problem if the combat wasn't boring. The boss you are supposed to fight at the end of the first real dungeon (the Central Line one) is lvl 34. If you didn't grind, or just did a couple of fights and you are at hard difficulty, you'll face them at lvl 20. I'm not kidding, I've spent 10 hours griding to complete that fight, finished it and activated the DLC Forbidden Scriptures to gain levels without griding for the next dungeons. At hard you also get a pityfull amount of money, which makes it even harder to fuse demons. But activating the DLC items also feels awful, because within an hour of griding, you can reach lvl 99 with a character and have 5M yen to spend on whatever you like.I wouldn't mind the free lvl up demons, but the free lvl up summoners are straight up broken and unbalance the game very fast.Oh, and all non-story bosses have a hidden turn limit. If you don't kill them by their 5th turn, they will one shot you. Even if you can beat them by repeating a strategy over the course of 10 rounds. So not only you have to grind to be on level, you also have to be over-leveled to beat those bosses.- The Story is SMT meets Persona. Not espectacular, not bad either. Pretty mid. The characters are good tho.It's meh. It's the same quality as a the game itself. It gives a little bit more info about parts of the main plot tho, and it intertwines with it in a very good way. If the missions didn't have the "DLC" tag right next to their name, I wouldn't have noticed that that story line wasn't part of the main game.Really good. Had only 3 crashes which all happen after skipping the intro title, when loading the main screen. Idk what triggered them, but I didn't lose any progress, or time. I just alt+f4'd it and restarted the game.If you saved before a boss fight, quit the game, open it again, and imediatly fight the boss, there's a clear freezing frames issues because the game wasn't expecting to load a fight so fast after being loaded in.Ah, there's an option under the Gameplay settings. There are fake load screens. The game loads VERY, VERY fast, but if you have the "loading tips" option enabled, then between every load there'll be a 5-8 sec "load". If you disable it, the load times will be instant. This is an issue because you spend a lot of time running to and from different parts of the city, so disabling it does save A LOT of time.I LOVE THE FAST BATTLE OPTION. I WANT TO KEEP SEEING IT IN FOLLOWING GAMES.I missed and I love that Ringo (MC) has both a personality and agency. It is very refreshing to see. I wish future games do this as well.I love I don't go to a game over screen after the MC is killed. The MC has party members, let them revive them. I wish this was in future AND previous games.Why I ask myself is how are the party members able to use demons? According to the story, the summoners lost their ability to summon demons because now Ringo controls them, so they need her to summon their demons. But if Ringo dies, then they are still able to use them.I do think that the MC dying should impact the fight in some way because they are the heart of the team, and having your party members unable to use their demons is the perfect excuse to have an implicit timer to revive Ringo as soon as possible if she dies during combat.But, I like not instantly losing to a one shot ability that I couldn't predict.I bought it at a discount and I don't regret it, but don't pay full price for it.Copium that Atlus will see that people bought it, finished it, and they will choose to release P6 or SMT 6 the same day on PC and console.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler Free review.Let's be honest no one here has played the original soul hackers game and no one cares. What people care about is a good JRPG with great dungeons and even greater story. Sadly this ain't it chief. Soul hackers 2 is plagued by a predictable story, boring lazy dungeons that frankly just waste your time, static characters, and Cash grab DLC. The only saving grace of this game is the amazing characters designs and well built world, But you don't really get to explore the world so it doesn't matter. This game is pure cash grab that felt like there was some sense of passion earlier but quickly muddled by the need for money. If you had high hopes for this game like me, or was hoping for another amazing JRPG by Atlus, boy are you ready to be absolutely disappointed. So lets break open this baby.Dungeons and GameplayThe dungeons in this game are literally walking simulators with enemy encounters. If you thought death stranding was a boring walking sim, this is worse. Dungeons all look the same, either some sort of subway or the matrix. There is only 1 dungeon that's even some what appealing to look at and its the final dungeon. To be honest these dungeons are worse than P4. Large areas with loops and turns that take forever to get through and ringo walks like a slow ass grandma, yeah i fell asleep while exploring the dungeons. Puzzle don't seem to exist in the world of soul hackers because every dungeon is the same walking sim ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. What's worse is there's a section of a dungeon that becomes random encounters while not being able to see ♥♥♥♥ because camera controls are limited. enough is enough and i've said enough about these horrible dungeons, Battles and encounters on the other hand aren't that bad. It's your typical smt/persona TB battle system. Target weaknesses apply debuffs and buffs. The sabbath system, while a bit simple is really fun. Finding demons with unique sabbath only abilities is always fun. Commander skills feel a bit overpowered at times but being OP is fun. Difficulty doesn't really exist in this game. It's overall a very easy game with some systems that let you feel OP. The one Negative about battles is probably ruin. instead of having abilities that do specific debuffs, ruin abilities do damage while applying debuffs. Ruin kinda breaks the balancing of all area's excluding bosses(Bosses are usually resistant to ruin all together). So gameplay is fun.Story and Characterssince this is spoiler free i'm just gonna keep this section short. The story is predictable, BUT NOT BORING just predictable. Some aspects of the story don't make sense and character development is weak. some characters are ruined by events in the game and i don't like it. Saizo is the only saving grace of this game. The character I thought i'd absolutely hate is the most dynamic character. Most of the characters in this game are fairly static till the the last few hours of the game, and the ending feels rushed. Overall its a mediocre story about human emotion and the characters are fairly static till the last hour. Also the ending feels rushed and pacing is all over the place, like all JRPG's.ConclusionI don't have to tell you that the world of this game is amazing. I don't have to tell you that the character designs are amazing. That's probably why you're here. The overall game isn't that great. The dungeons are just walking sims with rpg battles, and the story is a weak one with static characters. Don't play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: So I bought this game looking at the 'mixed' reviews and thought,: 'its an ATLUS game, it should be good right?'Now I know why a lot of people hate this game.I'll list a few positives first.1. The fusion search function is great, wish the other persona/smt games had that.Now the negatives that really outweigh the positives.1. The normal attack is within the skills tab. You might think this isn't a big deal, but when you're grinding and trying to make levels using only attack, it becomes irritating to take full control and use it. I know that there is an option for attack constantly, but sometimes you don't want all your guys to attack at once. It's funny but this one design choice made was irritating, although this is the smallest issue out of all of the others I'm going to list.2. Maps/dungeons are poorly designed and waste of time. There are plenty of LONG hallway dead ends, and having to turn around and run another long hallway is boring.3. Monsters spawning randomly, although you can knock them down with the sword, they are irritating while you're trying to navigate the horrendously designed maps. Then there is the purple monster who is always many levels  ahead and will chase you down if it sees you. It's like the design is made to slow you down on purpose because the game lacks content.4. The game lacks content, is short and only made longer by the above irritating design choicess.5. Side Quests are fetch quests almost exclusively.6. Characters and story are not that interesting. Characters have personality sure, but it's not interesting and character growth is limited.I have to say that even the boss battles are underwhelming, as well as the villains. You're not missing much by skipping this game.

_childDocuments_.review: To sum up the review im about to post: I think If you come into this game accepting it for what it is and not comparing it to other Atlus games, It's not a bad game. I'd give it a solid 6.5/10. A good majority of the criticisms about this game will probably be centered around it not being enough like Persona or SMT; but as its own stand alone title it's not bad..some of the issues I have with this game are as follows;1.Kinda pay to win. - First of all... Day 1 DLC??? I bought DLC with the game and I found out that as a level 15 I could summon a level 90 demon. On a normal occasion when doing fusions, it's impossible to get a demon higher than your level. I understand that you could easily just NOT summon them, but I know a lot of people wont really enjoy the game for what it is because they'll cheese it as much as possible. I also feel like this game will lose some replay value due to this as well. 2.Fight mechanics- There is not really a system to hold people accountable for any combat whatsoever. You can literally hit most enemies, knock them down and run away. In fights It never seems beneficial to be conservative with your MP because you can always go back to the safehouse as much as you want without the story progressing to rest. 3.Current state of game- Without making immediate adjustments to the game it feels like an Atlus game I would have played 10 years ago. After making some camera adjustments, It felt a little better, but it just doesnt feel up to par with most of the other current 60$ games to be released. I would 100% buy this game for 40$; but buying it for 60$ doesnt feel quite right. 4.Graphics??? - 95% of this game is really graphically amazing. I think the stylistic choices made for this game carry it quite a bit. The only issue I have with how the game looks is just that some of the textures look like this game was made for the switch, and not for a new console with improved graphics. 5.Story- I dont feel like there's a huuuuge amount of development in this game. Its probably better than SMT for sure but not persona if you /had/ to compare it to others. It just feels like you know where every avenue of the story is going :(ALL OF THIS BEING SAID; No. I dont dislike this game. I think this is worth a buy if it were 40$. It feels like a game made by the B team for sure, but I dont regret my purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets a lot of hate, some warranted and some not. It still has fun SMT gameplay and still has demons you can fuse, albeit they reduced the amount of demons in this game since SMT V. At the same time, this game has a lot of “one step forward, two steps back”.I believe a lot of hate from this game comes from it being so tonally different to the original Soul Hackers and from the graphics of this game not looking too great, which I would agree with to an extent.It still has many similarities they put in this game from the original, such as “Zomas” returning and it even the Bomb status ailment, which doesn’t appear in any other Persona or SMT games except Soul Hackers as well as Club Cretaceous returning with Madame Ginko who appeared in the original Devil Summoner and Soul Hackers 1. Devil summoner factions also return such as the Phantoms and Yatagarasu. Vision Quests return too, but the only issue is they’re not as exciting as in the original Soul Hackers.I wouldn’t be surprised if some of the developers who worked on Soul Hackers 2 played Soul Hackers 1 when they were young, but they couldn’t do much except for references due to a tight budget and the hand they were given.If you want to play Soul Hackers 2 for the SMT and Persona gameplay, I’d say go for it. But be aware that they heavily “persona-fied” the combat. So unlike the original Soul Hackers, you now control 4 human party members who equip demons that you can change at anytime (this was a big disappointment for many people especially since SMT V released and had demon party members). Why couldn’t we get the protagonist, 2 human characters, and 3 demons? Why did they do only human party members in a game spinoff where you always recruited the demons directly? They just made SMT V as well, why couldn’t they re-use those assets?Also, “zomas” return in this game (zomas are unique artificial demons, you fuse them with regular demons to create very unique demons), but unfortunately you cannot get one in this game – it’s enemy exclusive which was extremely disappointing. It’s worse that they made it enemy exclusive rather than just not including them to begin with. But you know why of course, it’s because it would take too much effort to make one nowadays. It’s so sad because they make many references to how zomas are made from the original games, such as showing Dolly Kadmon which was a vital ingredient for the creation of zomas, which only made me even more depressed.You don’t “knock down” enemies like in Persona, instead each time you hit a weakness a “Stack” counter goes up, and after the round of combat is over you unleash an all-out attack (called a Sabbath stack) which deals damage based on how high the counter got.You can upgrade your party members’ COMP weapons to deal more physical damage or to get other bonuses, such as making the stack counter go up for healing party members or for dealing critical damage. My criticism is that you can’t see demons attacking directly anymore unlike in SMT V or even Persona games but you can see them during the stack Sabbath attacks.The optional quests have fun optional bosses to fight too, but narratively the quests don’t have much substance to them. One criticism is that the quests don’t have objective markers, so you’ll have to wander through entire old dungeons to find who you’re looking for.The plot of this game is also, admittedly, very boring and dry! Again, it sounds like it’d be a fun game, you have all the factions of Devil Summoners fighting each other and demons, you need to save the world, and people control demons through computers! But the way they handle the narrative and exposition is just awful. There’s so many flashbacks that are not fun to watch and there’s a lot of repetition.As well, without spoiling specifics, they kill off so many characters as soon as they’re introduced (even off-screen) and then do flashbacks, but what’s the point anymore – the character is dead. And it’s not just once, they keep doing this numerous times in this game! There was one character that is heavily foreshadowed in the game who, if you played old Devil Summoner games, is a pretty big figure from a fancy devil summoning background, and guess what happens? Killed off-screen.I kept face-palming at the numerous bone-headed decisions they kept making, it’s as if they were intentionally trying to make their fanbase mad. It’s not even like the plot of the game was rushed – the plot of this game is detailed and they clearly spent a lot of time writing it and editing it, but it’s just bad and not entertaining at all, kind of like Fire Emblem: Fates’s horrible plot.All of the dialogue is voiced extremely well, but the actual lines of dialogues written are in such a long-winded way for some reason. At first, I laughed because I saw streamers who got codes for the game early skipping all of the cutscenes while they were livestreaming and I thought to myself “Damn, maybe these people stream FIFA all day or something and can’t get into JRPGs”, but when I played the game for myself I immediately understood why.Another criticism I have regarding dungeons is that there’s no treasure chests, so exploring doesn’t feel rewarding anymore. Sure you’ll find your demons who will give you money, items and introduce you to other demons, but you can actually grind these infinitely by running up and down, they don’t feel unique like treasure chests, it makes the game feel grindy and repetitive.The demons have material drops in this game compared to other SMTs, so you now need to grind and defeat thousands of demons to gather the materials needed to upgrade your COMP and get new skills for your party (these are on top of the skills the demons they equip give them, they’re not necessary at all but they can be helpful). I think I’d prefer just having COMP upgrades cost more money and having the demons drop money, rather than having to track down drops all over the place and having to grind a specific demon for hours just to get the one last material I need for an important upgrade.The navigator in this game is pretty annoying too and talks way too much. Having encounters on the map be “generic red monsters” also goes back to how SMT4 and SMT4A handled encounters (in fact it’s even worse because in those games they’d actually have different enemy models depending on if it was a giant demon, a dog demon, a male/female humanoid demon, etc, so you could tell which enemy you were facing, whereas in this title it’s always the same generic red monster chasing you or a powerful generic purple one).Another issue with this game is that although I agree that 30-40 hours needed to complete it is reasonable, but the pacing is odd and generally very slow. I won’t spoil anything, in the endgame area the plot really picks up, but as soon as it picks up steam it dies and ends the plot quickly. There’s two amazing bosses after the “sea dungeon” who have big plot significance, but they go out the window and you go to the final boss quickly after to wrap up the plot. The game had the potential to have an exciting plot, like having devil summoner factions fighting each other or having a bunch of devil summoner groups work together to defeat some big bad demons attacking the city, but they didn’t go for that route.So use this as your criteria if you want to decide whether this game is for you or not. I definitely wouldn’t recommend this game as your starting point into SMT games though because of the many criticisms I have with the game’s story. I do believe the game is just a tad underrated, but granted most of the hate is genuinely deserved. If you’d rather watch the game, I have a full playthrough of the game with all routes, all quests, NG+ quests included, Nana DLC, superbosses, and endings below on YouTube.

_childDocuments_.review: I know this game tends to get way too much hate, and while i can see many of the points made, i can agree with a lot of the flaws mentioned. If i were to get straight to the point the games rating is a solid 7.5 out of 10 for me at least.  The things i agree with is that the games dungeons are just so boring and have nothing to really force you to go out of your way and explore. above all that, some of the maps are unnecessarily huge and spawn rates of enemies kinda suck. Last but not least, the dlc. to have a day one 40ish dollar dlc is just crazy for us all. and for the extra story the only nice thing about it was its boss fight being difficult. To me, that's really all i "HATED" about the game.    You'll get a lot of people saying "oh this game is way too "anime-like" quite honestly one can argue its just the art style change that forced this argument cause all atlus games are quite anime like and soul hackers didn't lean towards the smt story style but rather the persona styled story. I can easily say this game shines where it needs to, and kind of helps you forget about all of its flaws. The characters are great and so is their development. The story is not perfect but it is quite good and i don't really see it being as bad as some people make it out to be.  All in all, soul hackers will not be as bad as some reviews make it out to be, you'll be getting yourself a game with a great story and characters that'll really grow on you/will come to love, if you could get over just simply crawling through a lifeless dungeon and the irrelevant (at least to me) art change from your typical smt/persona games you will be in for quite a nice ride!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  Don't hate this game for its creative or gameplay decisions. Hate it for its technical failure. In other words: this is a fun game until it stops working. All I get upon starting the game now is eternal loading. Not recommended unless the issue gets fixed.THE FULL REVIEW (spoiler-free)  Most of you have probably already got your info on this game from Megaten youtubers, so here I will mainly touch on things they didn't, or on points I have a different view on.THE GOODStory & Characters  You play as Ringo and three other party members to prevent the apocalypse in a futuristic and apparently stagnant but comfortable society. The plot has three major twists which I found engaging enough to keep me wanting to play. Ringo has a positive and playful personality, and I would love to befriend her IRL. Opinions on the other three party members vary across the playerbase, so make your own mind up. However, they still come across more alive in general than P3's cast (SEES); you can feel both the camaraderie and animosity in SH2. As for Figue, she is wife material; that is a fact!Art Style The game has a captivating art style and fresh character designs (within Megaten at least) and it pulls it off well.  The colours pop out very nicely in the whole game without being garish, whether it's on a bright environment like the hub worlds or sabbath attacks, or  the subtle specks of colour in the light signals and yellow lines in the dark subway tunnels. The menus are stylish but not overly so. I like the helpful skill type and weakness/resistance icons. Too bad the text is so small, and you cannot enlarge it in the config at all.Music  Most tracks are just fine, but there are a few bangers. They are: Mansei Realm, Safehouse, Battle, Boss, Soul Matrix Boss, and the opening theme Hopeless Call. See also Soul Matrix section. Combat  The battles are easy in random encounters, but harder during the bosses from the mid-game onwards, and hardest during risky (mauve) enemies. The latter category is used to grind for high sums of XP and money. A good balance in difficulty overall. (I played on Normal all the way.)The main principle in SH2 is the stack and sabbath system. Strike an enemy's weakness to add one of your demons to the stack. Once all your party members have their turn, all demons from the stack you made do a free, all-out attack on the enemy. The more demons in the stack, the more damage you do. This applies only to you; the enemy does not do stacks on you. Another important change is that aliments are now a big deal, while are buffs and debuffs less so, so you should take ailment skills, vulnerabilities and resistances seriously when making your demons and constructing your party. Learn to exploit this to your advantage and you'll have such fun!  Shield spells (as well as buffs ad debuffs) work on all allies/enemies (so, you know: properly!) which is a definite plus. Critical hits, unfortunately, do not result in extra turns, unit later in the game as an optional, unlockable, in-game upgrade to your comp weapons. Overall the stack and Sabbaths make for a fun combat system. I like the build-up to each sabbath with the demon silhouettes and increasingly thick mist and colours. The sabbath attack animations are thrilling and satisfying to watch. I've only ever skipped them twice out of over 100 times.Soul Matrix  This is a semi-optional dungeon you must complete if you want to unlock more character abilities (summoner skills). Many players have complained that the Soul Matrix is the same visually and musically throughout, and while I absolutely see their point, it's not all bad. The music and atmosphere are very serene outside of battle, and I love to admire the shimmering effect on the floor or background blocks. I advise you to stop and smell the roses. Admittedly, the blocks and BG could at least have been differently coloured for each character, and maybe the hue could have changed the further you progress. Nevertheless, I'll still gladly take the Soul Matrix over Persona 3's Tartarus any day for the positives I've mentioned.Demon Personalities  Atlus have always tried to flesh out the demons' personalities through their dialogue in the Megaten games I am aware of, and SH2 builds on this trend. The demons in SH2 have text archetypes and voice archetypes to give you an idea of their personalities. Some of the voice archetypes which stood out to me are: the Valley Girl (Mermaid, Apsaras), the cocky and mischievous male (Gremlin, Andras, Cu Chulain), gay male (Mokoi, Mothman), caring older sister or governess (Silky, Valkyrie) and scumbag male (Pazuzu). They did interesting things with Mothman and Pazuz. Info on them below in their own sections.Unfortunately, these are for flavour only. The excellent demon loyalty mechanic from SH1 is gone. I'm not joking. Demon loyalty was fun in SH1 and half-arsed in the Raidou games.Mothman (minor spoilers)A certain mothman stalks you throughout the apartment block dungeon to drain your party's MP before absconding to leave you fighting his increasingly tougher possy (nothing you shouldn't be able to handle by then). Mothman may use the gay voice archetype, but you know that one gets ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. He is a real player. God bless you, Mothman! When you finally catch up to him, he has three of his fellows with him. Throughout the dungeon I kept thinking you would take him/them out in a boss battle similar to, but even more satisfying than, the cat in Eternal Punishment's TV studio dungeon, but no. They are destroyed for you in a cutscene. [sigh] Never mind.PazuzuAtlus has always been good at writing downright scummy characters when they intend to, and in SH2 this honour goes to Pazuzu. He is the objective in a semi-optional sidequest from Aion. His lines are voiced and let you know that although he is powerful and speaks in a refined manner, he is nothing more than a bully. If you have a shred of decency in you, you'll make it your obligation to take him out. Great job, writers. Another Pazuzu appears in the Ash boss fight and uses the poison mist mechanic which was fun.THE BADDemon negotiation  It is overly-simplified. It works, but it's better in Nocturne. Then again, did any Megaten veterans complain about buying demons in an auction in Devil Survivor?Text Size  The text is much too small, and there is no way to change it. We went from nice and clear in P4G, to OK in Nocturne, to unreadable unless you put your spine into shrimp mode for the unvoiced dialogue in SH2. Please rectify this ASAP,  Atlus. I'm sure it would be much easier than sending Mr. Tomigawa round to fix my back every time.The technical problem  All I get upon starting the game now is eternal loading. I can't even get the title screen anymore. And this was all of a sudden after playing the game some 135 hours. The solution someone suggested on the Steam forum did not work for me at all even after verifying all of my local files. I cannot even say to wait for a sale, because this may happen to you at any time. Whether you buy it cheap or dear, what good is a game you cannot keep playing?CONCLUSIONWhat a shame. Apart form the one bug which makes the game unplayable, the good definitely outweighs the bad as long as you can play the game in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: Feel like putting this out right now while I'm still finishing up my playthrough, probably postponing it till the upcoming QoL patch but I feel like there's stuff that needs to be said before then:Overall, aside from the trash day 1 DLC that Atlus pushed out, the game itself isn't bad. The game is just... different. I was one of the people who pretty much knew as soon as the trailer dropped that this ain't gonna be Soul Hackers part 2, or SMT or even Persona. It really felt like they were trying to be different but chose an existing name to use for some reason when it barely connects. If you ignore the fact this game is called "Soul Hackers 2" there's a lot that can be enjoyed here, but... Overall the game is a solid 8/10. It's not lifechanging but is much better than all the doomsayers that gave the game a 55% mixed rating on Steam. The game feels very persona 2-esque with characters developing with or without the interference of the main character and everyone's ability to use any demons with some caveats so if you enjoyed Persona 2 specifically then this game may be right up your alley.I wouldn't say that the game feels rushed, it just has some weird design flaws that are thankfully going to be fixed with the upcoming patch. Overall, while I agree that the game has flaws in many aspects: dungeon design, QoL and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ day one DLC, the game still does tons of good despite all this. Hopefully a lot of the negativity dies down once they release the QoL patch (expecting them to make the DLC be free/cheaper is pretty unrealistic but will also help a lot).

_childDocuments_.review: Ringo is a fantastic protagonist and the style of the game is very cool, but that's about where the positives for the game end. Combat is surprisingly clunky, slow, and uninspired, especially if you've ever played any other SMT game, the plot is very character-driven but with some of the flattest characters imaginable (except Ringo, who does her best to save it), and most of your playtime if you want to do sidequests will be filled with backtracking huge, generic, and rather boring dungeons. Aspects of the plot are so bad that it feels like parody at times, which would pull me out of it if I had been engaged with whatever was going on in the first place. While I personally enjoyed playing this game, I could not, in good faith, recommend you spend more than maybe $20 on this. It's just worse than SMT V or Nocturne or the upcoming Persona re-releases in almost every way.

_childDocuments_.review: I both love and hate this game. 80% of this game you will spend upgrading your characters. No, not by grinding, but by exploring the literal MANY mazelike maps that you must navigate to find the areas to open doors that you must have a high enough bond with your characters to open. Like similar Shin Megami Tensei style you get to use a variety of demons with each character, and customizing your characters is super easy and someways fun. But upgrading your characters sucks. Imagine in Persona 5 that you had to go through mementos to unlock the skills you get like "follow up" or "assist" BUT you had to go through all of mementos over and over again for EACH CHARACTER. That'd be super frustrating right? That's the reality that this game is. The graphics are great, the story is good, and the voice acting is good. But some of the choreography and sound effects just feel like they're missing or weirdly put together. Only really in cutscenes though. The characters are super likeable and i live for hanging out with them, because i love them a lot. But this game is NOT meant to be played unless you have a 2nd computer screen to watch anime, youtube, etc because the Axis = Mementos takes up a LOT of time. Keep in mind i've played 32 hours i'm pretty sure i'm near the end of the game, but i'm not doing side missions, BECAUSE it takes so long to do the Axis.The worst part of the side missions is that there are no map markers. Meaning you have to explore the dungeons you visit ALL OVER AGAIN and these maps are BIG. Think Shin Megami Tensei big. For those that only played persona, imagine all of each part of mementos was all one floor. Yeah. That'd be very tedious to navigate. AND THERE IS A LOT OF BACKTRACKINGThe plus sides of navigation are that you can smack enemies around and run past them, you have an ability to get rid of lower level enemies but it doesn't last long. I just can't recommend this game at full price. It goes on sale at $20 i've seen and i think that's MORE than fair. But to be honest this game is only Good. Not great by any means. There are some game mechanics that are literally used twice then never again. (at least as far as i've played). The game needs quality of life updates. At this point i'm just playing the game because I bought it on release being the atlas fanboy I am and when you pay full price for a game that is only really worht half the price, you better ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ finish it.;tldrDon't buy this game unless it's on sale & you have a second monitor to watch/listen to something. Also for the love of god use the DLC this game will be annoyingly grindy without the "Sell items for money" dlc or the "stat upgrade" dlc.Edit: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ THERE'S A BAD ENDING TO THE GAME! You can't even get the good ending unless you New Game+ the game?! Now it's a good thing it has new game+ and customizable options to change things in newgame+ but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that's 35 hours of gameplay I did SPEEDRUNNING halfway

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I got  attention, I think this is a great SMT game, and, like every other entry in the series, have it's pros and cons.Let's start with the :- The gameplay is classic and that's a good thing, I love the weakness exploitations and with a great addition: the sabbats.- Ringo and Figue are the best IA protagonists, and at first I thought that this could be a bit cliché, but the more I get into the game, the more I liked them.- The game theme is a bit unclear but, once you get through the final steps, it gets more evident and I absolutely love it. I just wish it were a bit more clear, but I think that one is on me!But in every light, :- They try to make a group connection out of the members but they didn't feel like one. Maybe this approach is a bit more realistic than the classic JRPG where completely strangers come agross adversity and became friends. This group feels more like co-workers that tolerate the other one for the job's sake.- The Soul Matrix is, in my opinion, dull and empty. There's no use of it beside getting hacker's skills and learn just a bit more about the group.- And, the most irrelevant, but kinda in point with the game title: this is no sequel to the first one. There are no common elements, even if they trying to tell us that there are (and no, getting Nemissa as a demon with paid DLC is no connection at all). Even the connected terms "Soul Hacking" and "Vision Quests" are nothing like the originals. This could get a complete different name as the Devil Summoner saga and nothing would change.In general, I love the game's theme: . I just really would love that Atlus could've pour a bit more budget, but in general, this is a good start to revive the SMT flame and I hope they can play a bit less safe in later games in the saga, as once they did!
_childDocuments_.name: Soul Hackers 2

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I beat it. More on that below. The main paragraph here still applies.Buy on sale if you really need an SMT hit. It's not bad, but they brought in a lot of persona influence and it feels like some weird middle ground between mainline and persona. Nothing wrong with the core gameplay loop, just a bunch of small things that drag the whole experience down. I wouldn't pick this as someone's first SMT game either.No way Atlus looks at this, but Fog Breath's description is wrong. It says it lowers all stats, it actually only lowers attack/accuracy.Good news: looks good, combat is surprisingly interesting (although I'm at level 20 so who knows about later), battle transitions in dungeons are snappy. A lot of Raidou love (PC port where).Things I would love options for but don't expect: Remove the danger alert owl in the top right, he clashes with the background, is real noisy, and provides little useful information. I can hear when the demons spawn in...Lower the amount of in battle dialogue, they are giving xenoblade a run for it's money and I've already given up and muted character voices.Let me walk faster. Please.Let me just warp into shops and save a load screen. Even on PC, on an SSD, it's ~5-10 seconds to load the area the shop is in, then enter the shop, buy my items and another load screen to leave. God help switch players.Similarly, let me use safehouse functions from the map field. Spare me the load screen to heal.Major whine: Main cast is main girl and 3 walking anime tropes. That wouldn't be a problem except a fair amount of this game is running their social links and helping them through their trope issues. So you know how their characters will work out, it's just waiting for the plot to catch up, and until then angst. --- I have now beaten this. I'll keep it basically spoiler free.This was a surprisingly short SMT game. My profile says 55, I'd peg more around 45, I got distracted and idled a fair bit. That is also ignoring the 5 hours I spent wandering around quest locations looking for a doohickey, and the hours I spent half awake in teleporter mazes.Not sure how I feel about that, it didn't feel like the game got compressed or anything, it's just a shorter game. Except one way teleporter mazes where I can't mark the map, those suck. I hold by my original opinion: buy if you really need an SMT hit. Skip the DLC, even the extra story DLC, I assure you the extra story isn't worth 10 bucks.Things that fixed themselves: You can unlock an ability to run faster. Shame you get it pretty deep in the game, it lasts for maybe a minute, and costs 10 mp. It also requires some very specific ability choices.The cast's anime character tropes get resolved pretty fast all things considered. Mostly because the game moves fast but still.You also get an "instantly leave the dungeon" spell. Very good.Things I am now confused about:You can get equipable items that buff damage types, IE +50% fire damage. No such items for physical/gun damage... Why?It has the SMT5 thing where you are constantly low on mana, but the game really wants you to spam spells to activate sabbaths. So lots of safehouse trips to top up...DLC demons get 1 free compendium summon, so you could just grab Satan from level 1 and steamroll.The mistique thing is a real cool concept, to make you specialize what spells people are using. In practice to optimize sabbaths you want to zap the enemy with what they are weak against, so everyone is blasting the same spell type. So besides when you're farming the risky spawns for XP, or you die to a boss and are party rejigging, it doesn't see much play.Things I really grew to dislike:There is a final alignment choice. I thought it would be determined by which party member has the highest soul link. It's actually SMT5 where they just ask you in the final dungeon which ending you want. It also appears to be 1 of 2 options, although I didn't reload to find out. I'm not even sure why the choices I picked gave me my ending, or why I should care.I wasn't exactly enthralled with the plot, but I was actually expecting a twist at the end, just because it felt like nothing happened. Nope, that was it.You can only recruit demons by fighting them, then hoping you have a map event to recruit them. Makes it a PITA to drum up fusion fodder. Certain items and killing them with sabbath damage helps but you still don't get to pick who you want.Fusing demons is also a pain, because demons have at max 6 skill slots, and are very restrictive as to what skills they will take. Not only are you trying to optimize the end result, you're also optimizing the intermediate demons so you can actually pass on skills you want.The mind dungeon/Tartarus is... real dull. All the objectives in there, also real dull. Long, same looking, and teleport mazes.A real lack of scenery variety. You go to the docks twice, the sewers twice, and the office building twice. Only the last dungeon looks even remotely interesting.Big whine: some sidequests are basically: go to location X, find dude Y, do something. They don't mark where dude Y is on your map. Those 5 hours looking around dungeons to find dudes? I am not kidding. My advice, is look in the box rooms near teleporters, or when available use a guide.
_childDocuments_.name: Soul Hackers 2

_childDocuments_.review: Overpriced but still kinda fun. All the criticisms are valid. I barely recommend. If Soul Hackers was a riff on the earlier SMT formula, this is certainly based on SMT4. 3D environments, requests, etc. I couldn't help think of other games in the greater series when playing this.The core feeling I got was Tartarus from Persona 3. I remember many, many hours of running around and grinding and without the cheat DLC, I'd sure be grinding SH2 right now. Two major problems are it reminds me of P3P, where most of the fun exploration was replaced by menus, and that many of the dungeons end up being blind teleporter mazes. The story reminded me of Strange Journey not for any thematic reason, just it barely existed and the party members were basically "Stupidly selfless" good, "Rage Against the Machine" evil, and "I'm not getting involved" neutral. Similarly, the choice of endings (if there is one, I'm unsure) is a pick-a-path in the last 15 minutes of gameplay.Combat is overly simplified. Now weaknesses just add to a meter that does more damage at end of turn. It loses a lot of complexity and people interested in deep SMT tactical battles are out of luck.It is graphically very nice and the voice acting is above average. I can see where the money went, but this is very much Atlus' B series, with their A price. I guess I had almost 28 hours in it, but as the game went on, I needed more and more frequent breaks. That's not the way things should be. I don't want my time back, but this is "Pad playtime by grinding: The Game." Get it on sale, and be sure you're interested in grinding and obnoxious mazes. If you're expecting Persona 5, you'll be very disappointed. If you're expecting Strange Journey or Devil Summoner in 3D, that's less likely to end in heartbreak. But that price point.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game with tempered expectations and really enjoyed it. As a fan of DRPGs and Atlus' PS2-era output I felt right at home, and the QoL updates fixed a lot of issues. Pros and cons:+ Great all-adult cast of relatable companions+ Ringo is an amazing protagonist+ Some good gimmicks in the dungeon navigation+ Navigating between dungeons, shops etc. is snappy+ Fun core loop+ Battle system is easier than many SMT games but still has depth+ Not too long (50h avg. doing all optional base-game content)+ Great music++ Disco jacket- Low budget is apparent in dungeon visual design & character portraits- Character designs look like they all came from different games- Extremely predictable JRPG tropes in the plot (YMMV)- Some plot points felt too sudden or forced- Soul Matrix is a bit too large & monotonous

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR This game could of used another half a year of development. Wait for a sale or better yet dont buy and support this  kind of practice selling unfinished games. Also not a fan of the DLC practice of cutting out Demons and extra story content.Pros Good music and mature scifi story and likeable characters. Good old SMT goodness, Dunno where people are getting these 30-40 hour play times, Im 56 hours in and just at the final boss.Cons extremely bland dungeons copy paste designs. Teleporters are not fun in the soul matrix Floors 4+.High level demons don't learn any repel or absorb skills besides what they innately have that's been a staple in most SMT style games for demon fusion was a letdown for me. Could of easily added them in and replaced the plethora of dekunda and dekaja filler skills demons learned. They really messed up the compendium prices for demons. The costs get ridiculously silly. Some of the Aion directive requests fights have 3 turn limit to kill said boss demon or it almighty wipes your party out mechanic was used way to often for different requests. Buff and debuff skills besides the aim and dodge boosting/reducing skills were very nerfed and hardly useful i found even with the mystique that boosts buffs and debuffs by 5%. The dlc Demons  are a slap in the face to us and should have been in the base game. Mara's Multistrike to Devil survivor players doesn't quite work as you think it would. Its still the most powerful phys skill in the game that attacks 3-7 times hits boosted based on your agilty but doesn't hit all enemies 3-7 times. It can't be passed down to other demons via fusion. Theres also Masakados unique skill Oneness of body that works like charge but guarantees you will crit with you next Phys attacks as well. Also can not be fused onto other demons ,would of made for a nice new charge skill to put onto demons would of been a welcomed feature. At least they made the animation unique instead of this next travesty.Satan gets a ability called  Megido Arc. Sounds baddass right? It is but the animation of it is just a copy pasted megidolaon. My $1.50 pay to win demon i was looking forward to seeing when i hit level 90 to fuse better skills onto was lazyfied into what it is currently. Also theres a scarcity of high level demons to fuse compared to lower levels i noticed. There were times you needed to go up 4-5 levels to get the next demon to fuse. (Level 70-99 range)Iconic Demons like Metatron not having any Unique attack skills like his Fire of Sinai was also a letdown.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game's aesthetic, story, characters, and music were cool, the game's combat and dungeons felt basic and bland and doesn't have any interesting features that makes it as unique as any other Megami Tensei games. The DLC is overpriced and the extra story was alright but not necessary, and the quests are so boring to do. I wanted to like this game, but the best parts of this game was everything that wasn't the game.

_childDocuments_.review: With 98.8 hours clocked in, 40 out of 47 achievements and on the Normal Difficulty, I have officially beaten Soul Hackers 2, what a great and exhausting journey that game was, but very much worth it, I can highly recommend it to both casuals and SMT fans with the highlight of the game being it's amazing and super satisfying combat and affinity systems, hitting weaknesses has never felt this good. Mid points are low amount of dungeons with a lack of variety, sure it's cyberpunk but Metro System 3 also doesn't look any different than Metro System 1 did, and there's 2 identical shipping district dungeons, soul matrix is nice and absolutely huge but digital cube aesthetic is very overdone, low points are the music and bugs, the soundtrack is very small and none of the tracks really stand out, except the final battle theme, that said none of it is grading on the ears either, game really needs better multi monitor support, would constantly change screens even though I'd set it to a specific one in the settings. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice game. In gameplay, compared with other megaten games, it is a lot faster (specially with the last update to walking and fighting), getting you up very quick in a lot of things, including helping you a lot in the fusion side of demons and how to get them. Plus, Ringo and Saigo are some of the best characters in the megaten franchise by a lot and the ideas of Aion is interesting.The negative part is the plot, which is a lot more simpler with no Law/Neutral/Chaos sides, the demon will join you or not basically if you want or no, (they basically have no agency). Plus, while in the main quest and sidequest you would get to 65 level aprox the "secret boss" you need to grind a lot to get to an apropiate level to fight them/have demons that can hurt them (which was a lot faster than i expected) and i expected more sidequests to get to that level, but at that level the only thing to do was grinding. Plus, Yagataratsu vs Phantom Society ideas are less...hmmm....edgy and more. And the price of the DLC, i can't forget that.At the end of the day, i recommend the game. I want to see Ringo again, but i would like a deeper plot.
