_childDocuments_.review: The hate I hear from the game because it doesn't compare from the first Soul Hackers game. after completing hard difficulty first walkthrough because a challenge is always fun. I did have fun however noticing its flaws, played few other well known Shin Megami Tensei titles, Soul Hackers 2 didn't exactly grasped me like the first Soul Hackers. What makes Soul Hackers unique from other SMT titles and Persona? Firstly, we all know Status Aliments is a common thing however one Aliment "Bomb" is only in Soul Hackers. To see it back in Soul Hackers 2 made it exciting, as well for demons in a unique race name "Zomas" that was later mention in the story. However I knew the "Demon Compendium" didn't have a whole lot of demons like SMTV, not even ONE "Zoma" to fuse for. The hype for it died down for it. A returning character from the first Soul Hackers, and Devil Summoner came in and that was "Madame Ginko" but in all honestly, I just wasn't hype for it unfortunately, same applies for Yatagarasu and Phantom Society. Vision Quests are back but I find first Soul Hackers to be more entertaining. The characters from your party are great, the voice acting is fantastic. Saizo has relationship problems and shows how being a devil summoner messes/changes your life, which made me love a lot. Milady is cold, hides information from the group, eventually later gets expose on some stuff but all of that would've been solve if she just opens up to them a little more, especially since the dire situation everyone is in. Arrow is average, don't hate him, don't love him either. Couple moments where I was hype for him. Ringo has amazing personality and succeeds serving as a protagonist that always puts a smile on my face. Picking out choices as her is great to see her reaction. Voice acting amazing. Figue unfortunately didn't get enough screen time until the climax happens, eventually making me dislike her. Other adversaries that oppose Ringo and the gang are good, Iron Mask and his Zenon was good, both of their looks awesome. Without spoiling much, his writing could've use some work, but I love seeing him whenever I got the chance too. Story felt/is repetitive since the first person that died, and this kept going throughout. It was horrible because I'd really love to see more about the characters, how they got there, how they die ETC. If they did this, it probably would make me care about the characters lot more and get an understanding what sort of motive they wanted to aim at. Ichiro onda for example since the beginning, his slight shown of Braze made me want to know more about him, along with Arrows Sensei. The Developers love having their characters say "Soul Hackers". The day one DLC was a disaster, especially when they announced DLC from previous Soul Hackers cosmetics, a favorite character, and well known demons that SHOULD'VE already been in the game BASE. So no thank you. Gameplay; unfortunately it wasn't challenging. Hit a weakness, hit more weaknesses, you deal more damage from what's known as "Sabbaths" or "Stacks" if you're only a persona fan, basically an "All Out-Attack!" move. Yes, the battle is that of Persona look, you get four party members equip with demons with little stuff. Landing a improper move in battle, they don't punish you for it unlike SMT or even PERSONA games. You just get rewarded for it as long as you have a demon to block that move incase the enemy reflects on it. You don't lose a Stack, the enemy doesn't get stronger, NOTHING like that, so then the battles just feels.. well.. boring. Sometimes I wish it was just Ringo or with Arrow and Four/Three other demons which you don't see in battle unless its a Sabbath. If it had more actual team building, it would've been more fun, but Soul Hackers 2 just didn't have any sadly. No momentum/flow at all. If it were to have first Soul Hackers battle system, battles would've been NUTS. Little interaction with characters like reviving an ally, making jokes during battle was entertaining. Some may find it annoying, it can get old but I personally didn't mind. Customizing your COMPS was actually really fun for me! Dungeons; My god where do I begin. It was very repetitive, boring, last dungeon looked appealing. I disliked the Soul Axis dungeons, the portals were disgusting. I had to look up a guide online in order to pick which portal that would lead me to a gate. This made SMTV exploration look like a masterpiece to be honest. The Matrix doesn't chance at all, not even giving a little personality base around the character you wish to visit. Heck if they even add a red color in the background, I'd notice a little difference. The Music was the same thing, Matrix, if an enemy ambushes you, regular battle theme, EVEN when facing the bosses. I really wish it was different, R.S maybe having a hip hop battle theme, those bosses have the same music, god even Iron Mask bro. Missed Opportunity like how? It's a SIN. Dungeons hardly have any traps, and not enough puzzles. It sucks. Navigator to warn you enemies near by was super annoying. If they just left it out and keep a signal on right corner that changes colors showing you're on the clear or not, I'd be happy for cause I can see game, thank you. Anyways, lots of repetitive stuff in this game. I feel little emotional by characters but wasn't enough. I knew not to expect much from Atlus making 3D. I don't know how they didn't do it well on this one despite making great sellers in the past SMT that are 2D. I'm more emotional on that than the game itself. Please do better Atlus, I know you can, it's just not this one sadly. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite Atlus game I think. The combat finds a way to incorporate the idea of having a party of characters fighting together without being as repetitive as Persona thanks to the ability to actually change the demon associated with each party member. It mostly feels like an in-between of SMT and Persona, being both an ensemble narrative cast of protagonists and a game about making nice with demons so they'll help you in a fight. It's the same combat as most every Atlus game, once again being a little simpler than SMT V's additional turn system but more in-depth than Persona's All Out attacks.Mostly though this is the first Atlus game where I care about the characters and want to see them interact and develop as friends, including the protagonist, who has a distinct character as opposed to the blank slate types that you often see in Atlus rpgs. Oh also they're all adults and there's no weird adult/child romance stuff, so you know, that's a positive.Anyway I just think it's the best JRPG this company's ever made so it's a bummer that this might be the last one since it doesn't seem to have done well.

_childDocuments_.review: What frustrates me the most is how Atlus has messed up what could have been the revival of another good spin off (the other being Persona) of Shin Megami Tensei.Atlus prioritized style over substance. The characters are extremely like-able, really well written and the art is super cool and visually pleasing, but it is clear that the gameplay was an after thought in most departments. There is some complexity not seen in any other game in the series, some additional systems only introduced in this one, but it's not enough to make-up for the slog that it is in the end.The dungeon design is awful, I've seen better in SMT 3.  The OST made me go insane, every dungeon has the same background music, WTF were they thinking?I recommend this only for the characters and the story. Oh and Ringo's butt.
_childDocuments_.name: Soul Hackers 2

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is a dungeon crawler, an old school dungeon crawler. It is similar to games Atlus released on the 3DS or maybe the PS2. If this sounds like a bad thing to you, stay away from this game because it is not the new big jRPG release by Atlus. It is not Persona or SMT6, it is not a big new shiny thing either.If you read the PS2 statement and it did not bother you AND the fact this is being sold as a full price release -which could buy you the big new shiny thing I mentioned earlier- isn't an issue for you, then this game is good. I enjoy it a lot.The story is good and delivered at a nice pace. The party members are very nice (they are very grounded, which to some might be boring) with different facets of personality and relationships to the enemies and each other. The dungeons are sprawling mazes, some of which really required me to pay attention to which warp led to what portion of the map and while grueling to explore sometimes gave me a real feat of accomplishment when completing them since it really feels like the dungeon is kinda fighting you back, making itself difficult to navigate through. Really wish we had more visual and music changes during the dungeons though.Combat is nice (please, play it on hard!! This game's hard is easier than SMTV's normal!!). The bosses have a puzzle approach to them with multiple phases, contrary to SMTV, which felt like every boss could be beaten by just tanking and hitting weaknesses and keeping buffs/debuffs up. The Sabbath at first seems lacking depth but as you get more COMP upgrades and Soul Matrix skills it shines quite a lot, making possible some strategies I couldn't see happening on normal Press Turn.tldr: Soul Hackers 2 is made for a very specific type of people that wants a dungeon crawler with grounded characters and a overall old school experience. It does not try to do anything really new. It was made within a budget and you can see it with the very samey dungeon designs, the fact that almost every dungeon or that every boss uses the same music track. It is still a good game in my opinion.♥♥♥♥ Atlus and their DLCs practices though. Also, a lot of the problems with this game come from its pricing. If it was being sold as a $40 title, everything would make sense. $60 could get you at least one of the upcoming Persona ports which are all better than this game. It could get you Xenoblade. It could get you the eventual SMTV port. Atlus and Square are really trying to get back to the old days, releasing a bunch of lower budget niche games which are all cool but almost never cool enough to justify the full price tag making the game compete with titles it can't win against, sending it to fail.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does so many things right that it's a shame that the final product is weighed down by bad decisions and poor performance. Story and characters are interesting, voice-acting is great, art direction is cool, but the gameplay is too thin and a step back from more recent SMT games. Taking away the extra turns from hitting weaknesses and replacing it with the Sabbath system has dumbed down the strategy greatly. It's just hit weaknesses, get free damage at end of turn, repeat. Add to that the limited move list for every demon, little variation in enemy encounters, and it just feels like a mobile game; a far cry from the strategy and careful balancing in the core SMT or Persona games. Beyond that there are the side quests, which are MMO-style fetch or kill affairs. Boring, uninteresting slogs, every single one. Under-cooked is the term that came to mind. Occasionally a dungeon will spawn an elite or treasure enemy, which are basically pointless because the elite enemies are just regular demons that are 5+ levels higher than the party and the treasure monsters were regular demons that you can't ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hit no matter how much you buff your aim. To top this off there are strange quality of life issues. When moving around town protagonist Ringo will take a few slow-down steps after the player releases the stick like she just sprinted the hundred meters. Navigating to the world map can not be cancelled, a selection must be made, and from there a load screen. And the load times for a game that has smaller maps and poorer graphics than SMT5 on the Switch are longer than they really should be. Overall this is not a horrible game, but a decent one done poorly, something I don't expect from the series or publisher and will probably be my most disappointing game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a longtime fan of the Megami Tensei series. I've played nearly every game since I started with Persona 2 on the PS1. While I am not yet finished this game, I am really enjoying my time with the game so far, and I am fairly confident that other fans of the series will find something to enjoy here as well.First, the gameplay. This game evokes a similar feeling to older entries in the series. Press turn is notably absent, replaced with a more traditional turn-based combat system. Your team takes their actions, hitting enemy weaknesses to gain stacks, which are consumed at the end of your turn to deal extra damage to the entire enemy team. There is not much strategy beyond just hitting weaknesses for some extra bonuses, but some skills and abilities unlocked later in the game provide some stack interactions that add some much needed texture into the combat. Navigation of the combat system uses a similar menu layout as found in Persona 5, and it feels snappy and responsive. Combat is surprisingly fast paced due to the ease of menu navigation, coupled with short animations, and there is almost a musical rhythm to it that feels very satisfying. Overall, while I would prefer that the combat simply used the press turn system, it is more than a serviceable combat system as it is.The next core part of any Megaten game is the demons. Unlike a more traditional Megaten title, your demons do not join you in battle. Rather, they are equipped to your human party members in a manner similar to how it works for the main characters in the Persona series. During fusion, you have the ability to reassign any skill in the skill pool, including a demon's base kit. This means that you get quite a bit of flexibility when fusing. It seems that demons in this game only have a maximum of 6 skill slots. While that may seem like it reduces the overall possibilities for a build, that ends up basically not being that relevant. Your party members each are able to equip passive skills that affect various properties, so the end result is that you will still have access to at least 8 skill slots that affect your combat prowess.I actually quite like the exploration and dungeon design as well. There are a few clever contextual mechanics and puzzles sprinkled throughout. There is one dungeon where its unchanging aesthetic makes it visually boring after a while, but I think it is a relatively minor complaint. I liked how you basically never need to bother with combat unless you want to, and can just focus on exploration. I found myself simply knocking enemies away in the dungeons with my sword and running past them, then catching myself up by using the rubberbanding exp gains to level myself up right before a boss by doing some side content. Yes, the dungeons have been more interesting before. I personally think the design of SMT dungeons probably peaked in Strange Journey, but what we have here is still more than enjoyable, if just a touch on the easy side.The fusion interface is one of my favourites ever in terms of both ease of use and presentation of information. There is a fusion search feature with many search options, including a compendium fusion option that allows you to automatically summon and fuse a fodder demon from your compendium. It also allows you the choice of summoning either the base demon for cheap, or your customized entry for the full price. I've already spent a solid chunk of time just fusing things for fun, and I imagine I will spend quite a bit more.This game is also beautiful to look at. Just like Persona 5, it oozes charm. Rather than a picareseque roguish style, this game draws its art direction from its more cyberpunk oriented roots. Characters are visually distinct and really stand out, thanks to some brilliant designs from artist Shirow Miwa. Coupled with the outstanding art direction, the music is also impeccable. The soundtrack blends a variety of genres, from dubstep to power metal, once again highlighting the techno roots of the cyberpunk aesthetic. I particularly enjoyed the COMP Smith track. The guitar riff in that track calls back to Digital Devil Saga, making for a nostalgic trip back in time.I tried to stay away from much in the way of trailers ahead of time, and I was expecting that the protagonist, Ringo, would be an emotionless doll like so many other AI characters in anime-adjacent media. That is surprisingly not the case, as she is a lovable ball of sass and sarcasm. Alongside Ringo, the other cast members are all likeable as well, gradually opening up their backstories over the course of the game, and their constant banter is both believable and adds some levity to an otherwise dark story. I am playing the game using the English dub after having forgotten to change it before I started the game. I ended up being pleasantly surprised by the voice acting and delivery of lines, and have been largely happy to keep it on English voices.So far, the story is fine. There is nothing head-turning here, but what is here is done competently. There is a plot about some secret conspiracy to destroy the world and remake it using the power of some MacGuffins. Pretty typical Megaten faire. I assert that plot has never really been the strong suit of the series anyway, and that so long as it is inoffensive, it serves its purpose well enough as a means to an end to move us from dungeon to dungeon, where the real fun takes place.Overall, I really have been enjoying my time with the game. I don't think it's perfect by any means, but I take comfort in its relative simplicity. I also accept that this game is not going to be everyone's cup of tea. If you became interested in the Megaten franchise through Persona 5, this game probably doesn't have much of what drew you in. If you're someone who really just likes a classic JRPG, this is like a Dragon Quest game with a splash of Megaten paint on it. I know people are hungering for anything at all like Persona and getting disappointed that this isn't it, but games like this are great too. It's comforting and beautiful in its simplicity, and a genuine love letter to days past and the games of old.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this game today so i'll review it before getting all the achievements and then come back and see if i made any errors.story:This is a very good generic RPG ("generic" doesn't mean "bad"). though, it felt more like "Soul Hackers 2 (part 1)" than "Soul Hackers 2". this game feels more like it only introduces and develops said introduced characters, and doesn't leave much outside of it. typical Atlus... can't do a game unless it's over 80 hours long full of meaningless fluff.the story at the last dungeon was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ AWFUL. some "dude" influences "good girl" and "good girl" becomes "eeevil girl"... _childDocuments_.review: It's like Persona except you're all adults so the only time you get to hang out is over a beer between work shifts.Okay now for the actual review:This game's combat system is heavily based on that of the most recent Persona games, there are no rows, alignments or temperaments to think about when assembling your party, instead there are four fixed party members who are essentially all given the ability of a Persona protagonist to "equip" a demon in order to use its moveset. Each party member has an affinity for a specific element and so pairs up better with some demons over others.The combat itself is even more persona-like rather than resembling the original Soul Hackers, with the initial combat interface being instantly recognisable as the one from Persona 5. The main gimmick of this game's combat system is the Stack system which grants you a extra attack at the end of each turn whose damage is determined by how much you can exploit enemy weaknesses. Unlike systems from previous games in the series, enemies cannot use this system against you, leading to the combat system being balanced in the player's favour.Older SMT games will allow for demon negotiation during combat, the replacement for this system is something I will go into as part of the next section.Fans of older SMT will be happy to see that maps quickly become fairly complex, they are by far not the most intricate in the series but in later areas are satisfactory. Dungeon crawling consists of free 3d movement of your character rather than tile-based first person movement of older SMT games, as a result moon phases and magnetite "demon rent" systems have been scrapped.The traversal in Soul Hackers 2 has been made to be very streamlined and forgiving, to begin with, encounters are no longer at random, instead taking another feature that recent Persona is known for (yes I know they didn't invent this) where encounters are visible in a dungeon and can be avoided. There are also a number of field abilities that you are able to unlock including one that I missed on my original playthrough which allows for sprinting. Since finishing the game I have learned that this is now a default ability after an update, thank god.Saving is allowed at any time in any location and fixed terminals allow warping between different points in each dungeon, An early field ability allows instant escape from a dungeon to the map screen in exchange for 1mp, this eliminates concerns of managing your resources while deep into a dungeon as you can leave to restore your stats at any time with little consequence.Rather than chests or much of anything else to discover for yourself in dungeons you will instead encounter demons that you have recruited standing around, speaking to them will allow you to claim either an item, or recruitable demon. While unique, this is quite a shallow system.Item discovery is randomised, with a chance of being consumables or upgrade materials of common and rare varieties. The locations of quest items are mostly randomised, goals often being "collect X item in area Y" requiring you to walk around aimlessly talking to demons until you find the required number of quest items.The negotiation system in this game is a negotiation in name alone, there is no real failure state to recruiting a demon; you speak with them, they name their price, you say yes to recruit them, or no and then they leave.This game has a very modern interface, as mentioned previously the basic battle controls you will be interfacing with are pretty optimal, making use of all of a controller's face buttons rather than a tedious linear menu like other SMT games.It is clear that Atlus learned some lessons from their HD port of SMT3 to Unity, the resulting game is quite a decent PC port supporting high resolutions, framerate capping options up to unlimited, and many options for graphical settings.Affecting their PC ports since P5 Strikers is poorly implemented anti-aliasing, I substituted this for the AA from nvidia's control panel and it looks fine.Loading screens are almost nonexistent, but a pause was added to loading screens so that the tips can still be read. this pause can be disabled in the settings menu.One major port issue is that running above 60fps can cause running acceleration to bug out, this does not affect balance but can feel odd. - Present (English and Japanese) - Atlus game (good) - Atlus game (very good)While overall I would rate the music of this game highly, I am at least a bit disappointed that it does not quite feel like a successor to the style that Soul Hackers 1 went for, what we have instead still sounds great but is a bit closer to something from Ryota Kozuka's work on SMTV. That said I hope we get some high quality uploads on streaming platforms soon as I am a big fan of some tracks. - BadThere is some great music in this game, and each area you visit of the city when picking up quests, upgrades, or items in between dungeon runs has you encountering a number of them which never got old for me, the majority of your time however is spent in dungeons which - with a mere two exceptions, all share the same dungeon theme.While the dungeon themes are dynamic in that they transition to a more tense version of the theme when an enemy is in pursuit, this still means that this long dungeon crawler is spent mostly listening to the same song on repeat, this is especially a problem when the theme starts from the beginning after every battle encounter.Speaking of battle themes, there are a few different boss themes, but for regular encounters we only get the one, and due to the lack of demon negotiations within battles, there is no negotiation theme either. Given that the regular battle theme is by far the one that will play the most, this makes the DLC which adds music from previous SMT games something I would strongly recommend.Possibly my most controversial opinion on this game is that of the character designs for the main cast, which I have strongly disliked from the moment they were first revealed, they do however grow on you after a while of playing, and once again with DLCs the cast can be dressed as characters from other SMT games in order to fix their goofy outfits.The visuals are otherwise great, demons are high quality and environments are very stylised even if the dungeons are repeated tilesets.The story was alright, better than SMTV but nothing special. The main cast are fleshed out a lot with lot of scenes of dialogue explaining their backgrounds, there are some plot heavy sections, these can be skipped easily on repeat playthroughs.There is some connection to the Devil Summoner series (mostly some names and the use of COMPs to summon demons), there is little to directly tie this to SH1 plot-wise. The nature of Demons and COMPs existing is never really a focus unlike the last game.I think this game easily could have been named Devil Summoner: Aion instead of SH2 and might have been more successful for it, no knowledge of SH1 is needed to enjoy this game.Gameplay = Simplistic and easy but excusable due to being streamlined and satisfying.World = Pretty and sounds good, fleshed out by a ton of dialogue.Plot = Mid-tier for a SMT game, good enough.Recommended for fans of dungeon crawlers & monster collector games.Not as convoluted as other series entries but main mechanics like battles, exploration, and demon fusion are present. This is a decent first entry for someone trying to get into SMT.Game is quite expensive for what it is, relies on DLCs to cover up flaws that would be more of a pain otherwise. I would suggest picking up the deluxe edition from a key site if possible, or wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Not as bad as some people are making it out to be.Soul Hackers 2 is awkwardly sandwiched in between the release of SMT V, and the re-releases of the Persona games. It was never supposed to be a huge 70+hour JRPG, it's supposed to be a rather experimental, smaller JRPG for Atlus to see what works and what doesn't, similar to how they operated with the Raidou games, Strange Journey, DDS, and hell even the original Soul Hackers. I think a lot of people placed unrealistic expectations for SH2 to blow things out the water, when instead it's probably the most solid 7/10 game I have played in recent memory.It's essentially a Persona game with more stripped back combat, and it even tries to mimic the Social Link system with its own 'Soul Level' type of deal amongst the main cast. I think it's quite fun, and is a cool hybrid between SMT and Persona that feels like a 'lite' version of both series. Here lies the problem though, I think this game would be perfect if you have never played an Atlus JRPG before, but I don't think I would ever recommend it as someone's first game considering various other Atlus projects do it so much better. It's the Soul Hackers 2 paradox.If you're looking for SMT level of difficulty, unfortunately it's more on the Persona side of things, as the game itself is fairly easy. And due to it taking influence from Persona, the dungeon designs are rather bland and consist of you running down hallways to find the route to progression. It's confusing to me seeing people hate on the dungeon designs, and then recommending people to play Persona 3 or 4 instead. Are you alright? The dungeons in this game are very similar to those found in P3 & P4, and I feel like the emphasis on the dungeons being mid in this game is overblown.The OST could have been much better though, a lot of the tracks here are forgettable. I feel like a game with a futuristic aesthetic they could have had some off the walls type of music going on here, but instead it's rather mellow and reminiscent of things you've probably heard before. But regardless of that the game is still fun, and while I don't know if it's worth £50, I still feel like I can recommend it to anyone curious, or to fans of JRPGS. Maybe wait for a sale and you'll have yourself a fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: I will give this game a thumbs up, as the game is not "bad" and I did have fun, just taking a step back and looking at things objectively.Really disliked how rushed the story was.  It was dungeon after dungeon without any breaks for proper character developments or subplots (excluding soul matrix and requests).  Character moments, while I did find them really enjoyable and heartwarming, were too short and too few.As the main story is extremely rushed, there is no time or incentive to fully utilize items such as the augment/arcana mystiques because by the time you grinded enough to get them, you would already be reaching the end. Combat is okay.  I preferred the old press turn systems from older SMT games.  Delivers more of a challenge and a reason to fuse properly.  Without enemies being able to gain extra turns from exploiting ally weaknesses, there really is no point in stressing trying to get coverage because you can just heal the next turn.On a technical level, the game runs smooth on my laptop, but I noticed that Ringo's hair tended to spaz out when she runs.  I've checked with many other users and they also said the same thing.  This isn't a major problem as some players did not have it happen to them.Dungeon design is really disappointing.  For a "cyberpunk" world, the dungeons revolved around dark, gloomy, old installations.  Dungeons also have the same old puzzles most of you guys know such as, collecting keys to unlock doors, defeating mid-bosses to get items and teleporting through portals. Speaking about cyberpunk theme, despite the main city being designed nicely, you are unable to really explore the city.  When you're in the city, the game becomes a "side scroller" where you just run back and fourth to the store you want to visit, and that's all.  No exploration within the stores or whatever, it just shows up an item screen.The soul matrix is really a slow burn, it does look good however.  If you aren't a fan of backtracking or running a long distance, you would probably find yourself skipping alot.DLC review:-Lost numbers is alright.  It's really just a few more quests.-DLC demons are alright.  They have unique skills, but you can't pass them on via fusion. -Costumes are beautiful, just that you can't wear them outside of battles.  Not even while traversing dungeons.-Stat boost items are sort of a waste because you can grind for highest stats, but once again if the main story is so short, what's the point?To end the "review", I would just encourage future players to wait for sale to get this game, because it is not worth the SGD$120 I paid for.  The game has good moments, but the moments are quickly taken away due to how rushed everything is.  There were many promising character developments wasted.  Mini spoiler:The man you see in the trailers, only really appears for a few quick battles and that is all.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an Okay game. That's disappointing to write, but I did have higher expectations for this game. However, as a non mainline game, Soul Hackers 2 kept my interest enough while Persona 5 got released on PC. I wouldn't play it a second time now that Persona 5 is out, but I'm glad I finished it. It was lacking in story, yet it it did have interesting characters, Saizo being my favorite of course. It also had demons and gameplay that you'll easily get familiar with if you ever played any Shin Megami Tensei or Persona game. I definitely wished it was more developed regarding the dungeons, which are repetitive and aesthetically boring, and customization, which just boils down to using the highest stat item and paying for the DLC if you want your characters to look different.  All of that said, the game is addicting for someone like me who loves playing Shin Megami Tensei and Persona games. I love grinding, listening to the music, and seeing the visuals and the interesting characters. It maybe needed more time of development to make it feel more unique, but as it is, I still recommend the game if you never played any of the other Atlus games I mentioned. _childDocuments_.review: I think it's a shame that I cannot give this game a “mixed” review because even though the game looks eye-catching, I don’t think that Soul Hackers 2 sets a good example for either series (SMT or Persona) nor does it feel fulfilling to play as a game after Soul Hackers (3DS), despite not needing to play it beforehand.There’s a few things I really appreciate that were done well with this game:- Leading is Ringo and Figue’s designs. Matching suits with altered personal touches: a cybernetic jacket for Ringo and leggings for Figue. It sets them apart as main characters for sure (or rather main character and sidekick but we’ll get to that later), because no one else is an AI overlord turned humanoid. - Another thing I think was handled well was the character's individual skills through the usage of Mistiques and COMP Upgrades. Each character has an affinity the game starts them with but the game gives you free reign on switching that around and crafting the team as you see fit, granted you have the materials.- The final thing I want to praise, is more of a Quality of Life thing, but it's the ability to essentially Demon Search when out in the field. I got about two thirds of the way through the game before I realised it was a thing but it saves so much time. By going through the menu and into enemies list, if you have the demon you need to fight for a request there, you can hit them with the “search settings”.  Now when you’re out in the field, if the demon you’re looking for is in the encounter that's appeared, that encounter will get a little target mark over it. The bigger bonus is that you can assign more than one demon with the search setting at the same time which is amazing for people who like to bulk complete quests.The big gripes that I have with the game are as follows:- Dungeon design is beyond bland and the Soul Matrix is the biggest offender. Endless blue/purple sea of platforms. They change the puzzle design per person and per floor, but not the look or the musical style of somewhere that is supposed to represent your party members. If Aion can literally make Figue and Ringo, then the place that’s supposed to be the soul of a person can look a little more interesting than some floating platforms and broken stairs. This point also leads into another minor annoyance I had with the game, the map. Or rather the lack of a dedicated screen for a map that I can interact with, while yes, if nothing has spawned I can stand for an indefinite amount of time and look at the map, I don’t want to do that. I want to look at the map in a way where I can see it all and not have to keep fiddling with it so I can see what I’m running into and not have my entire screen obscured. Additionally, why can’t I pin points of interest on the map? There have been some Aion directives I wanted to go back to later but because of the amount of teleporting bullshittery, it's hard to get to and from certain locations or even memorise the route to get there. Green teleporters are one thing but the red ones really take the cake and admittedly, ended up with me putting the game down for an entire week before I reluctantly picked it up to finish the main story. You fixed this issue with Strange Journey Redux (3DS), and backtracked here. Why?- Why do I have to pay with MP to run faster? At the time of writing this it was announced on Oct 3 that there will be a dash introduced and Assassin Steps will be shifted into the role of Estoma+ essentially. Why does it take a patch for this to be implemented?- The load times have been a point of contention for a lot of people and I agree. God forbid you’re upgrading your party and you forget to buy equipment and you have to back out of one place and go somewhere else? Why not have most, if not all, of these available Karakucho? Another big offender with time wasting is going to the Axis. Why is there not an option to go straight to the Soul Matrix as opposed to having to go through the notions of walking past Flamma every. single. time. - Battling is so SLOW. Again, also going to be patched in, but in a game where you have long animations, constant fighting and possibly grinding, whether it be for levels or items from certain demons, speed up buttons should be the norm at this point. Again, you did this in Tokyo Mirage Sessions (Switch) with speeding up the session mechanic, but decided against it here with the sole exception of being able to skip sabbath animations. On that note,- Sabbaths are also beyond underwhelming too. You lose out on Persona’s “All-Out Attack” feature or SMT’s “Press-Turn” system. Literally either of these would have worked better in this game than sabbaths and I think Press Turn would have been the way to go, as it would have added far more difficulty to the game as opposed to making every enemy HP sponges. - You have NG+, but are still required to sit through the tutorials despite having completed the game at least once already. Who decided that?TLDR: I don’t think this is a good game to start with for people new to the whole franchise because it does too much of both sides (Persona and Shin Megami Tensei) and does neither half as good. It’s an alright play for those familiar to the franchise, and a roundabout decent game for those just looking to play for fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not new to SMT games, but I've never played the original Soul Hackers, not have I played any of the Devil Summoner titles. That being said, I went into this pretty much treating it as it's own title, not holding it against any of the other related SMT games. To keep it short and simple, it was a decent game overall. The gameplay is okay, the demon encounters are.. frequent, the available demons and fusions are sufficient enough to make it through the game without major struggle. However, the story and it's pacing are far from perfect. I enjoyed the story, but there  is so much nothingness happening for the first half of the game, and then the story suddenly goes balls to the walls and gets interesting. Unfortunately, many players will probably lose interest before that point, especially when you consider that some of the dungeons are absolutely miserable. It's clear that some of them are designed to straight up waste your time and artificially prolong the game. If you can bear it until the end of the game, you will definitely be satisfied, as the story and everything does have a very good (and very Atlus-y) payoff.

The biggest issue I had was the overall design of the game. They combined cyberpunk with magic/demons and it just feels disjointed at best. Maybe the reason I loved Persona so much more was that the characters felt more real and grounded, not like in this game where everyone has a super eccentric personality and dresses like they were standing in a paint shop when the store exploded.Also, the disaster of dialogue that makes up battles almost had me muting the game. Literally even scrolling through targets will make people shout out "helpful" hints. _childDocuments_.review: Despite mixed reviews, I'm loving this game. It's just a really nice time. I can see where the negative comments are coming from, but for some reason or other, the lack of polish doesn't really bother me. I also bought it for 65% off with all the DLC, which I'd recommend.Soul Hackers 2 is in a weird place in between Persona 5 and SMT5, and having played and disliked both of those games, I find that Soul Hackers 2 gives me (personally) the exactly correct amount of character driven narrative to keep me moving forward, without getting itself in my way. The battle system is straightforward but the gameplay feels rewarding. It's less deep than both P5 and SMT5, at least it has been for the 30-ish hours I've played of it, but it feels nice to interact with the systems. The environments are repetitive and there is a lack of enemy variety, but I just kind of don't care? The game works for me.The thing that really makes me come back to it though, as opposed to Persona 5, is that when I boot up this game, I actually _play_ it. I get into combat, I explore areas, I fuse demons, I complete side quests. For the 30-ish hours I've played it, I actively played at least some 27h of those. Meanwhile, 30-ish hours into Persona 5 and I wasn't even halfway through the second dungeon and I'm pretty sure at least 20 of those hours were spent reading very well written teenagers being freaking annoying and stupid. I'm sure there is an audience for that, but that ain't me. Meanwhile, Ringo has been on Earth for 1 day and has already resorted to heavy drinking to cope with the amount of crap she has to deal with... and that might the most relatable bit of characterization I've ever seen in any Shin Megami Tensei game.Soul Hackers 2 also lets me actually listen to Last Surprise, which, bewilderingly, Persona 5 Royal refuses to.

_childDocuments_.review: What a disappointment. I mean, a JRPG with cyberpunk anime aesthetics that seemingly implements some social mechanics, as a Persona enthusiast how possibly could this not be appealing after all? Well sadly, it turns out this game doesn't live up to my prior excitement.There's actually not much to say tbh. Soul Hackers 2 isn't especially bad imho, but it isn't exactly good either. Getting straight to the point, Ringo is an amazing character, but that's about the only good thing - in fact, she pretty much carries the entire run and ended up being my sole motivation for actually finishing the game. Aside from that, this game is basically sheer blandness as you will go back and forth between a very few enclosed areas, going through corridor "dungeons" (as in actual corridors...) and completing your typical boring sidequests. Characters excluding Ringo are decent enough, but the very limited social aspect didn't quite lay the ground for actually empathizing with them - well, you certainly will at some point, but in regard to storytelling and character development, Persona 3 did it 10 times better 16 years prior. There's indeed no such thing as social links in this game, rather you will encounter occasional hangout events at the usual place which will eventually allow you to unlock combat skills for each member of your party - and tbh, while this will still give you some hints of lore about them, it's much more the foresight of that end objective that made me actually hangout with my party. As for the story itself, it is very timid in its intentions, thus very predictable.Fortunately though (or maybe not), Soul Hackers 2 is an SMT entry so it has inherited from the series' good old mechanics, namely turn-based combats and demon fusions which are both as effective as ever. To be fair, someone who isn't familiar with SMT would probably be able to show more appreciation towards this game since said mechanics are overall well thought out. Then again, I wouldn't even recommend this to newcomers as there are far better options available out there if you're willing to dive into the SMT series.So yeah, Soul Hackers 2 basically is a very lacking game and comes off as a lazy attempt at making something refreshing. While I still enjoyed it at some point, I just can't help thinking that Ringo just didn't deserve that game.Edit: typo.

_childDocuments_.review: I never posted a review for a game before because I feel like everyone is going to have a different opinion about a game regardless. However, I am going to have to make one just for this game in particular. So pardon my lackluster compositional skills. I feel like this game gets a lot more negative criticism than it deserves. So here's my take on it as someone who has recently gotten into the series starting with, of course, Persona 5. From there, I went on to play Persona 3, Persona 4, Persona 4 Golden, Persona 5 Strikers, and SMT3: Nocturne. I also played some of the non-RPG titles like all of the Persona dancing games and the fighting games. So that is where I am at in terms of the series. If you have been into the series for quite some time, then chances are that there are a lot of elements of this game that are going to turn you off and you are not going to like my review so may want to stop reading right about now. However, for those of you who are relatively new or are on the fence about this game due to negative reviews like I was, I feel that you should give this game a chance even if you have to wait for a sale. Gameplay: This game is actually pretty damn fun - mainly because it still has that addicting SMT gameplay. In terms of difficulty, this is probably the easiest out of any of the SMT games that I have played as it is pretty easy to get demons that can resist any element. There plenty of side quests in addition to the main quest even though they don't really get anywhere that interesting in the end, but offer additional combat and rewards that can help make the game even easier and unlock certain dungeons/maps. If anything, I think this adds accessibility to the game especially for those that are not familiar with the SMT series or are not fans of the difficulty spike in certain games of the series especially towards the end. Those of you looking for that challenging SMT gameplay may want to skip this one. I'm personally into both the challenging games and this accessible level of difficulty for this game. There is also new game+ available so that adds some replayability to the game too. I personally don't do new game+ stuff anymore since I have limited time for video games these days. Story: It is your typical JRPG trope-filled prevent the end of the world with the power of friendship kind of storyline. The characters are pretty likeable in my opinion although a bit flat. They help make the atmosphere feel pretty chill unlike Nocturne where everything feels empty and depressing (yeah, I know it is supposed to be post-apocalyptic) even though some people are into that. To each their own.Art Direction: I like it. Personally, not a fan of the other SMT games with the gothic doll-like artwork so it was not hard for me to like the artwork in this. Environment/Level Design: Other people seem to think that the dungeons are repetitive or tedious. If you think that the level design is repetitive, then you need to play Dragon Age 2. If you think that the maps in this game are tedious, then you need to play SMT: Nocturne. Music: Pretty good, but not Persona 3,4, or 5 level of good. Performance: This game never had any form of instability and it never crashed for me. I feel like it was optimized well for the PC and I had smooth frame rates the whole time. The game did not seem to be graphically demanding in the first place evidence being that my GPU fans did not activate when I played this game and I am rolling with a 5600xt with a Ryzen 7 3700X when I played it. If you are into ratings, then I would personally give this game an 8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the problems the game had at the beginning like fusion skill inheritance which was really strict at the beginning, no dash that wasn't a skill, ui problems, and some other issues have been fixed so thats not an issue anymore, the biggest problem of the games is that it doesn't know what it wants to be.Let me explain i'm a Megaten fan and i have played most of the games including ones that are still Japanese exclusives, so i have experience with the series, why i said that this game doesn't know what it wants to be, because Atlus tried to make a Persona/SMT middle ground game that is a good entry to start playing the franchise which i do believe it succeeds, it also fails to attract previous fans, the game is not as Difficult nor as grimy and dark than main SMT games and also it has some social elemets like in Persona which not every main SMT fans like, and the Dungeon design is middle of the pack is not really bad but also nothing stellar.And for Persona fans is the opposite, even if the game combat system is a simplified version of SMT and Persona combat system, the difficulty is higher here than in Persona, and something that is the selling point of the Persona series is the social element of the game where you need to make bonds and frienship with a cast of characters in order to get abilities or just for plot reasons, which is in this game but is heavily simplified with just conversations with your party member.Taking that aside the combat which is the focus of the game, is actually really good an strategic, even if its a simplified version of the SMT and Persona combat system, when you hit a weakness instead of giving a "One More" or a Press turn it gives you an stack, and every time you hit a weakness the stack keeps adding, at the end of the turn the game is going to make a super attack which the power is based of how big your stack gets, also Demons can get special abilities that can Trigger when that super attack is done, the combat is simple but is still fun, strategic and challenging, is still a Megaten game so even the regular mobs can just destroy you if you aren't prepare.About graphics i have no issue, the game looks really good and the art style is just really good, the plot is good is not something revolutionary and is kinda generic but at least it has some interesting twist and the premise is interesting, the characters are interesting nothing out of the ordinary but good nonetheless the soundtrack is top tier like with every Megatnen game so no problems in that departmetI recommend the game because i like it and i genuinely believe is a good game, but the lack of a clear identity and also that most stuff in the game is just fine, i do believe the game is not a mediocre game but with how high quality SMT and Persona is, it just feels that it could be better, we  know that Atlus can gives something better if they had a more clear goal with the game instead of just making a SMT, Persona entry point.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I don't think the game deserve its price tag and day one DLC which is quite minimal content, dungeons are uninteresting after some time, in game currency could've been managed better especially the devil summoning prices which are ridiculously expensive, bosses fight are not as fun because they give you one shot mechanic which pretty much force you to learn 'Sabbath' but then again after fusing demons, you pretty much want to avoid summoning them due to its price making it significantly difficult to have optimal devil lineupsI wish I can stay neutral in my review, I want to recommend this game but there are a lot of flaws that will keep people away, including myself. The gameplay itself was enjoyable at first, I was playing at hard mode for 20 hours or so but then I decided to go back to normal because how they treat some boss fight, especially some optional boss challenges. Some optional boss challenges have mechanics where they will one shot you after X turns, which is extremely frustrating if you face them under levelled. Pretty much every boss, you will need at least 1 heal bots and sometimes they get rid of 1 character on optional bosses, I find it almost impossible to beat boss on first try (unless you are over levelled) which is usually what I've always aim to do when playing Persona.Another incredibly frustrating things are economy in this game, I've been going through dungeons facing almost every single one enemy that I encountered and I only have barely enough for one or two accessories and upgrades leaving none to summon devils. On top of that, the price for summoning devils are ridiculous reaching up to 300k at level 20-ish, the more you levelled them up, the more severe the price hike gets. You can either choose to get a couple of weapon upgrades or one devil summon, I would always choose to upgrade my weapon because devil always ends up getting fused anyway.Dungeons are also very uninspiring, it's closer to what we had in Persona 3 and Persona 4 where dungeons are pretty much almost the same and I think we can also compare it to Mementors in Persona 5. I would imagine this as playing Persona 5 without the main dungeon, only going through mementos and the area is significantly larger without much challenges. I liked that they replaced treasure chests with Demon Recons but they essentially are the same thing.I will update it as I go my playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: So first off, let me state that Soul Hackers 2 IS NOT PERSONA in any way shape, or form! If you need to have this game compared to something from Atlus, the closest match is Tokyo Mirage Sessions #FE Encore for the Nintendo Switch. They are very similar in design philosophy, battles, etc. So now that is out of the way. Let's get to the pros and cons!Pros-- Future Cyberpunk setting (think Cyberpunk Edgerunner aesthetic mixed with SAO anime character design)- The cast of characters (the cast is small but has enough variety and personality differences. Character growth also happens as you do more side quests and activities with them, as well as advance the main story.)- Combat is fun with a twist to the usual Atlus-style combat systems that we have come to expect from things like Persona. - No knowledge of the previous game is needed at all.- Music and Voice acting are all good and fit the setting and themes.Cons-- Combat-heavy game (If you are more for story over gameplay this game may not be for you as there is a TON of dungeon crawling and combat with a little section of the main story thrown in at various points.)- Difficulty Spikes (certain areas can see a sharp increase in difficulty.)- Side quests (Kill X many things, Fetch this, there are some story bits that try to make them at least entertaining. However, the biggest problem is all the backtracking to previous areas to complete these quests.)      So is Soul Hackers 2 the next big Persona franchise Atlus is hoping it would be? Nah, it is more the Tokyo Mirage Sessions #FE Encore just available on every platform now. It is a decent game as long as you do not come in expecting Persona 5 Royal, or Persona 4 Golden. You will get a competent JRPG with some unique things going for it, I would give it a 37/50 (or a 7.5/3.5 for your more traditional game score people)

_childDocuments_.review: Best way I can describe this game is SMT on training wheels. This is the easiest title in the franchise from what I've played. As much as I love the game, please buy this game when it goes on sale. For what it contains, it is not worth full price. A shorter than usual JRPG, with lackluster dungeon design, a rushed story, and some lacking side content.Is it bad? Not in the slightest! If you can muster through dungeons similar to Persona 3 and Persona 4, then by all means try this game! Soul Hackers 2 is a visually stimulating game with an incredible cast (Great dub by the way), and flashy combat that took inspiration from Nocturne, Persona 5, and SMT5. Even though the story felt a bit rushed, I was still longing to see what would happen after each major event. Albeit, a bit predictable, but engaging nonetheless. Oh, and not to mention that Keiichi Okabe's studio Monaca (Nier, Drakengard, Tekken) worked on the OST, which by the way, is full of bangers!

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game. The level curve is a bit lower compared to other Shin Megami Tensei games so you might not end up using your favorites but if the story really grips you then you probably wont care too much anyways. The Soul Matrix felt a bit like an extremely long version of SMT4A's final dungeon which was mostly a bad thing but the Soul Matrix is optional content for the most part. I played the game entirely without DLC and it felt complete enough as a whole at the end which was nice but it is still sad to see how much day one DLC Atlus is still trying to push. Overall I would recommend this game to JRPG fans of SMT or to JRPG fans as their first SMT.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game not only as a SMT game but as a JRPG as well. The story and characters are pretty well done and I love how the the four main characters relationship evolves as the game plays out. The Bar Heidrun is a location you can go to to have "hangout events" with some of the squad and you can learn more about them as people and see them interact with each other on a more personal level (some times) outside of the main story. The game is quite easy actually (and I played on hard) as it's designed to make sure you don't really have to worry about dying and you can freely grind  for the levels and macca you need and honestly calling it "grinding" is a bit of a stretch as the game sort of throws exp at you. Battle System itself is simple and has enough mechanics to make it interesting but I wish certain elements were either still there or done better. Personally though I found that the battle system kind of dragged until mid close to late game phase when the demons became more interesting in their skill slots and having certain upgrades for your COMP and passives your characters can learn from the Soul Matrix. Dungeons are awful and boring as all hell (especially the Soul Matrix my god) and the lack of variety in regards to the dungeon music is a sin but the OST itself is good (well I like it at least). DO NOT BUY THE LOST NUMBERS DLC it's low effort and a scam tbh I didn't even finish nor do I really care to because it has what is the worst boss I fought in that game. The boss is bad not because of poor design but because there is a sheer lack of putting any effort in it's design to begin with and the main game has some interesting bosses. For PC performance I had no hiccups at all while playing this and it was a smooth 10/10 experience for me personally so maybe Atlus can port they're other games with better success in the future.Overall for me I recommend this game whether you are a megaten fan or even if it is your first game in the franchise it has enough elements you keep you a engaged and due to the game designed around making sure you can comfortably  level up, fuse and upgrade your COMP as necessary people shouldn't really have to much of a difficult time with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: 4.5 StarsThe game has a 5-8 hours tutorial depending on skill level, however towards the end of it combat and the Soul Matrix/Level system is an amazing upgrade to the Confidant system from persona, Soul Hackers 2 uses the Sabbath system which is an interesting evolution to the Press and One More system of previous games, your team can equip demon's similar to personas in Persona 2 and at the start of the game you earn "Stack" by hitting weakness similar to Press or One More however at the end of your entire turn the Stacks turn into an All-Out Attack called "Sabbath" where you summon demons for each stack earned (Pendulum Summon style from yugioh), as you progress the Soul Matrix and leveling your teams Soul Levels you earn more ways to gain stacks eventually gaining the benefits of the previous Press and One More systems, this makes it so you have to earn the overpowered exploits of the systems prior to top it off on Hard and in mid game, Elite and Boss fights start to use these systems against you as well.Story: 4 StarsTaking a classic of AI predicted the end of man and putting a really good twist on it, SH2 takes place about a decade after Soul Hackers and the events caused by Spookies story. Though unrelated to the previous game the world very much is the same world though we don't really address alot of the politica in SH1 that was setup in the World, Basically an Almighty AI calculated the world would end if 2 specific people are killed, your mission is to prevent their deaths and save the world. You end up being too late and have to Soul Hack Arrow to bring him back to life and from their you go on a Steel Ball Run chase to collect the corpse parts.....I mean to collect the Covenants to prevent the Antagonist from collecting all 5 and using them to summon the Great One and end the world.Graphics: 3.5Very basic Anime JRPG graphics of the 2020s the game offers very little customization and the antialiasing is kind of poor. (I run a 3060 GeForce RTX, with a Ryzen 7 5800x and 64GB of Ram) while i get a real stable 144+ FPS without needing vsync the lack of additional options makes me feel less in control of how the game looks.Audio: 4OST is pretty good, if you got the DLC though the new soundtracks added are alright (kinda sad I can't blast Mass Destruction during battle) also if you get the DLC unless Persona 5 or P5R you get to select the BGM during battle in gameplay settings and don't have to rely on what outfit Ringo has equipped.DLC: 1The day 1 DLC that has everyone in a fritz is honestly utterly optional the only major concerning one is the  Number's Chaser which adds a Side Story for you to progress side by side with the main story and due to Atlus' habit of Royal/Gold/FES editions not including DLC you will more than likely have to rebuy this DLC when this gets the Rerelease (if they even rerelease it considering the backlash they are unnecessarily getting.) The biggest reason i'm ranking it so low is you can tell all of it is just content that was not complete at the game going gold deadline and they had this content almost done so they decided to finish it between the Going Gold time and Release time to give us Day 1 DLC. The reason i strongly believe this is 2 series signature Demons/Personas are in the day 1 DLC Satan and Mara, the 2 have been in every base game to my recollection of an SMT title (outside of Digital Devil Saga) to date.Updated notes: Game is Persona 5 levels of easy and it is surprising a short campaign based on where I'm getting bored, the mystery and conclusion just doesn't feel great. While I enjoy returning to a standard story and gameplay for SMT, this is definitely leaving much to be desired, would recommend getting on discount as a bundle.

_childDocuments_.review: I adore the Megami Tensei franchise. I love the sweet anime-like wholesomeness of the Persona series and can't get enough of the poetic hopelessness of the mainline SMT titles.Soul Hackers 2 is the first spin-off title in the franchise for the last decade that is not Persona. I can't emphasize how big that is. Every fan was over the moon when ATLUS announced that a sequel to the long-forgotten Devil Summoner: Soul Hackers is coming out soon.I truly wanted to love this game. Even if it wasn't up to par with P5 or SMTV, I still wanted it to perform well enough so we could get more spin-offs. However, it saddens me to say that Soul Hackers 2 feels like a game that predates P4 or any modern ATLUS title. The game has so many questionable design choices in the name of streamlining that it's no longer fun. For a game called Soul Hackers, very Little soul can be found in its dungeons and levels. I never went in expecting a meticulously designed game packed with content like P5, but I expected something that would make it stand out. So far, I haven't been able to find it, and I doubt I will ever be.I cannot recommend Soul Hackers 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Great entry in the SMT franchise. It shines brighting when it comes to their characters, if you do most of the sidequest and their little hangouts events you are really gonna be missing the main cast by the time de credits role. The story is quite decent too, it quept me invested right to the very end. The places where this game is kinda mediocre is in the OST and the dungeons. The OST tends to be the highlight of other entries but in this it left a lot to be desired (good thing is you can play other games' battle music if you bought the costume DLCs). And when it comes to the dungeons it's not particularly bad but it feels cheap, you get 2 tower buildings, 2 warehouse district maps and 3 underground train complexes, a lot of re used assets. At least you get a completly new layout for the dlc and final dungeon. SMT is mainly a dungeon crawler so a lot of the oldest games used to have very samey dungeons so it's not that terrible but a little more variety is never bad...Overall I really enjoyed the experience, the lovable characters makes up for it so I'm gonna be getting that 100% achivement soon, I really recommend playing it even if it has it's flaws.PD: The opening is such a banger!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this to anyone looking for a fun diversion in SMT spin-off style as well as those who, like myself, are hoping for a Strange Journey pc port/sequel. Controller is a strong recommendation, as well a FOV settings changes. Game runs alright on linux, a little taxing on the steam deck - and both have minor graphical glitches. Soul Hackers 2 seems to struggle in reviews do to what it isn't. It isn't a new persona, or digital devil saga, or most assuredly not a new SMT mainline entry. It isn't a classic-to-the-series dungeon dive and it isn't you vs law or chaos. I still find it quite enjoyable for what it is - a game with SMT-like mechanics and references with decent combat, graphics and play loop. Having completed the first playthrough on hard, everything I have seen indicates it to be a prequel to the original Soul Hackers, but only in setting. Gameplay is much more like the recent Persona 5, at least in exploration and combat, though most battles are easily trivialized with overgrinding. Default style is something like cyberpunk-lite, like a split between modern styles and edgerunners cosplay. I used the DLC to set most of my characters in Persona 2/Devil Summoner outfits, so there is flexibility.Story and setting, while similar to the original Soul Hackers, has an approach that reminded me more of the Devil Survivor games. The finale was somewhat touching, though not nearly on the scale of some of the other entries in the series. EDIT: Forgot to add that, if anything, I found the OST to be a bit of a weak point. The original Soul Hackers is up there with Persona 2's OP in my mind, whereas this is a mellow and fine soundtrack nothing really struck me.

_childDocuments_.review: Imma be very honest. This game is very disappointing. TLDR, this is a overpriced 6/10 game that should be R400( $20) MAX. The amount of content in this game is lack lustre. Persona 3, Persona 4 and SMT 3 Nocturne, games released in the PS2 era have more content than this game. I actually found myself doing other stuff like browsing the internet, talking to family/friends, ACTUALLY doing my job during Xmas while this game was running because I got that bored. So if you are reading this review, do not purchase the game OR The DLC. Its not worth unless its less than R400( <$20). ESPECIALLY THE DLC, it doesnt add anything worthwhile in my opinion. Even the DLC costumes are ass for the most part. Now for an attempt for a review. Imma try keep it short. Gameplay:This game, lacks content and poorly tries to make up for it by forcing you, the player, to GRIND. But GRIND without clear or obvious EXP exploits like in prior games or as a example Dragon Quest with their metal slimes. So bosses and mobs feel like Tanks that can ♥♥♥♥ dmg but in a repetitive way. Even getting demons/making demons is a mission since you are capped by your level, so you feel it more. To add more perspective, I got I think 2/3 into the game and have completed every sidequest available but 2. This includes the Aeon stuff( trying not to spoiler and I likely misspelled Aeon but idgaf). I felt VERY restricted because I can not dish out as much dmg/healing because my demons did not have stronger abilities. 6/10 because I actually have a life outside of my pc, my pc is not my life. Story:The story is a joke. Like on the surface, it makes sense but if you actually think about it for 2 seconds, you realise its actually moronic and the main villian should not be succeeding as much as he is given the situation. To use an example, its like Green Arrow vs Batman or Hawkeye vs Iron Man. Yea both parties have no super powers but Batman and Iron Man will WIN NO QUESTIONS asked cause $$$, resources and cause they are Batman and Iron Man. But somehow the story paints it that Hawleye and Green Arrow are bodying them and have a chance. Lmao nope. 2/10 cause story is nonsensical.Characters:Imma be frank, Saizo alone will make me want to finish the game because he not only comes off as likeable but the only character in the game with social skills and a fountain of actual life experiences. 2nd to that is Ringo's jacket. That jacket be fly ngl. The designs of the NPCs that sell you stuff is 11/10. They could actually shuffle with the main characters the way they look so good :).  Everyone else is meh or okay or decent but . So Character design, 9/10 because there were misses. Characters overall, 2/10. Saizo made carried the game for me. MC chicc is alright( but again she's supposed to be Batman/Iron Man lore-wise but she getting clapped by her bootleg) Music: Sleep dude, maybe the final boss music and outro track would be killer but music was just mehmeh/10Overall, dont be a fool and buy this game at release retail price. wait until its on special for 1/5 of its cost. Again, Persona 3,4 and SMT nocturne have MORE CONTENT than this game and better execution. Old school games almost 20yrs in age are better than the most recent Atlus game. Thats sad♥♥♥♥ it, this game is 4/10 and its 1 of those games where I suspect the actual ending will be pretentious while using fancy words to make it seem grander than it is. ♥♥♥♥ this game, I genuinely wanted to like it and the only expectations I had for it, was that it would be a good game. Not a great game, or a terrible game, but a good game for me. Its also worth noting that only 30% of players at the time of this review got to the point I was in the game if you are looking at the steam achievements and 10% actually finishing the game. So player retention and engagement is definitely an issue for this game. Edit: I relaunched and uninstalled the game 3x to give it a fair chance to redeem itself. This game is not balanced late game and I would recommend players play the game in Ez mode. Again I have finished prior Atlus titles but why am I getting oneshot in 1 turn by enemies or bosses despite buffs and debuffs. The Risky enemies gimmick is ver stupid too. Its the games main farming tool but its basically as hard as boss fights and you would more often avoid said fights because you can die in 1 or 2 turns.2nd Edit: Eventually reinstalled and finished the game, the true ending of the game is locked behind New Game + where you need all 3 characters to have an affection rating of 100 or above. ♥♥♥♥ this game, this is some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up levels of padding.

_childDocuments_.review: ***SOFT RECOMMENDATION // WAIT FOR A SALE***Pros:-Fun combat. While I miss Press Turn & One More from other sub-franchises, Sabbaths are fun. I just wish critical adds weren't locked behind upgrades and were in the system by default. Demon inheritance is a thing, but not every demon can learn every element. It's a shame, because the attribute system in SMTV seemed like the most fun way to balance demon builds. Beyond that, if you like MegaTen combat, you'll like it here too.-Great characters. With how goofy most of the cast looked, I wasn't expecting much; perhaps that's why was blown away by the quality of the character writing. Each character has a unique perspective and character traits while still feeling reasonable why they'd help Ringo and without feeling one-note.Cons:-Ringo moves very slowly through dungeons. There is a speed boost skill you can get early on, but it doesn't last very long and is tedious to repeatedly activate.-The dungeons are boring and repetitive. There aren't many dungeons in this game, and the ones that are feel very short and bland. There are two in particular that I consistently had to check against quest and demon locations because I could not tell them apart visually. MegaTen games typically have some interesting dungeon puzzles; there are only two of such in this game, and calling them puzzles feels like an overreach. They can be bruteforced very easily, and don't feel satisfying. I'm not asking for Nocturne-level warp dungeons, but a little more content would have gone a long way.-The story is apparent within the first half-hour of gameplay. The character writing carries the entire game on its back.-This game only feels loosely connected to Soul Hackers. There are a couple of character references and Soul Hacking happens. That's it.-The music is serviceable. Disappointing when compared to Persona 5 and SMTV, the latest entries in the other two major Megaten franchises under Atlus' belt.All in all, if Atlus was attempting to make Devil Summoner the third pillar in their roster, they failed. This game was underfunded, lacking in distinct content, and generally feels like it could have used more time in the oven.DLC Rating:-I have no opinion on costumes. It's pricey, but honestly changing the battle theme to the original Soul Hackers one was worth it to me.-Demons being such expensive DLC-- ON LAUNCH-- is criminal. This game already wasn't given enough budget or time to come out well, and bad launch-day DLC practices only hurt this game even more.--Lost Numbers is okay. Nana is a fun character, but all other associated content is either very short or insanely repetitive. The only highlight is the .--Ring-ho should not have been DLC, much less locked to the DIGITAL DELUXE EDITION.Recommendation: The game is fun, but not worth the $90 Atlus is asking for what feels like the "full" game. I still recommend buying it, but only with a good discount during a steam sale. Do not touch the DLC unless its discounted, and even then only buy The Lost Numbers.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of the Megami Tensei games, and this game is one of those special cases where I refer to it as a "flawed masterpiece"The game is good, but it could have been better. It has a great setting, soundtrack, characters, and an interesting story that keeps the spirit of the other Devil Summoner games, even though it is not a direct sequel to the first game while still being in the same universe. My main complaint with the game were the dungeons. They all felt the same. A lot of the exploration felt stale and it just felt slow a lot of the time, but what made it somewhat good were the various bosses at the end of each one.Another part of this game that I have mixed feelings for is the combat. The combat steps away from Press Turns and 1 Mores from other Megami Tensei games, and tries to come up with something new. It kind of works, but it just feels a bit lazy from Atlus with this kind of system.Overall I recommend this game, and there is a lot of valid criticism for it, but that just allows Atlus to learn from their mistakes and create something all fans alike can enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is not bad per se, but for an Atlus RPG, it is baffling.Graphics are "allright", doesn't support ultrawide gaming, but runs decently on a 1070 with maxed settings. Graphic design is good, but environments are rather boring. Dungeon design is SUPER boring; soul matrix is the biggest eyesore, but the fact that the only uniquely designed dungeon is the very last one is telling of how much this title needed more time in the oven.Story is forgettable, super predictable, and the main cast is not interesting enough to warrant the long-winded gameplay segments.Music slaps in its own right.Gameplay is boring, unbalanced, and disrespects your time. Main combat gimmick is super boring (more damage), and could be saved by the later introduction of sabbath skills. Elemental attacks are way stronger than its physical counterparts. The idea of having materials bound to upgrades is fine, but I do not understand why Atlus chose unique raw materials per demon, so if you miss an upgrade, you have to backtrack and farm.If this is your first Atlus title, welcome to one of the best core RPG gameplay loops in the industry.If it is not, then just play Persona 5 or SMT V once more.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Hackers 2 is a aesthetically beautiful JRPG with fantastic VA, hilarious dialogue and stylish memorable character designs. SH2 adds some cool new mechanics to the mix while also adopting from older Megaten games in the series, most noticeably Persona series. The one negative thing I will say about Soul Hackers 2 is that the dungeons are pretty bland visually which is a real shame considering how incredible of a job Atlus did with SMTV dungeons. However the layout of the dungeons is pretty standard fair for Megaten series as a whole.
