_childDocuments_.review: I've only grasped the first few dungeons, so I'll give my review out so far.I have not played the previous Soul Hackers title, only Persona and SMT titles, but from what I've seen so far: You play as Ringo, an AI agent created to prevent apocalypse, maybe that's why it seemed like the plot feels a little too rushed. Right after the prologue, Ringo would automatically thrown to a dungeon in order to start her mission of saving the world from the apocalypse. The goal is to save a certain someone whom later joined in on her party, Arrow.Meeting Arrow would give the player the mechanics of the 'Soul Hack'ーWhich is a skill unique to Ringo where she could 'hack' a soul in order to revive them from death. Once Ringo saved Arrow, it was then revealed Arrow had a connection to the other characters that later became the rest of the party members. This would all be done in just It is unbelievably fast if compared to Persona series in general.So far, I don't really see the appeal of the character dynamics other than Ringo and Saizo's (And when Ringo picked the Saizo's preferred options)ーThe quirky answers are amusing. But then again, it's mostly because it reminds me a lot of the quirky answers Persona series has.As for the party's dynamics (as far as this review goes), the current atmosphere feels like they're only characters bound by the same reason of "being revived by Ringo" and currently shares the same goal. But other than that, I have yet to see connection between each of the party members.Now onto Ringo and the other AI agent called "Figue". Again, for me, their dynamic felt a little too rushed for my comfort. They are both AI that was born on the same moment, with different personalities. In-game, they should only know each other a day or two, but the game made it seemed like Figue had known Ringo for a long time by worrying every each one of Ringo's actions like a doting parent. For me, it seemed incredibly stupid. So it's a bit hard to have attachments as of this time of writing.The graphics are phenomenal, especially the character models and designsーI fell in love the moment I first saw the trailer (esp. knowing Shirow Miwa is the character designer. I have loved sensei's design since 7th Dragon 2020), and it was actually the reason I bought the game in the first place.The UI is clean and attractive as well. However, my only complaint so far would be the design for each dungeons. It felt so empty if you compared them to the Persona series.The gameplay felt a little bit too repetitive with no real consequences (I play in Normal difficulty).With no in-game days mechanics, you can go back and forth between the dungeons and the safehouse with no consequences other than your meal buff effects wore off the moment you leave a dungeon.Again, I have not put in enough hours to give an overall verdict, but putting all my impressions so farーI would say only to get them if the game is on a discounted price (I bought the Digital Deluxe edition and for me it's honestly pricey. I would not say it if the game is otherwise worth the money). Just buy Persona if you want a much more fun ATLUS game experience with that much amount of money.

_childDocuments_.review: So this was the game SEGA teased in their last survey earlier this year. TLDR: Overall, the game is amazing, a perfect intro to Atlus. a story that is well put together and about mid length compared to most JRPGs. Turn based, and has elements from SMT and Persona. You do not need to play the first game to understand this one. It is a stand alone title. Worthy intro to Atlus games and will set new players up to how Atlus creates their games. Basic enough to understand and then moving into SMT and Persona, getting a much more refined experience from those titles.------------------------------------This game is actually really good and a nice side project from Atlus. Newcomers to Atlus games should definitely give this game a try as it is about 1/3 in length compared to their mainline series of Persona and SMT and the mechanics are basic and unrefined in SH2 compared to the other titles. SH2 will take roughly 30-40hrs to complete vs their bigger titles which are upwards to 100hrs+. Vets of Atlus games should not be comparing this title to the bigger ones because it isn't a mainline series for them. Obviously it is going to be much more basic and comparing it to P5 is just being disingenuous and unfair to Atlus. The first ever turn based JRPG I played was (yes) P5 back in 2016 on PS4. It got me into this genre as turn based in not an easy mechanic that many players like due to how it slows down game play, atleast for me. But Atlus does it right somehow. So I know where some of the vet players are coming from when feeling the need to compare this title to it. Then went and played P4G and even FF10, but I haven't played an SMT game yet though.Starting off, the game runs very well and you can actually play it on release compared to other devs >_>The story line is fully voiced and is fairly deep, though with sometimes feeling a bit rushed and cliche in JRPG tropes. But doesn't detract from the game all too much. The characters are unique and likeable, and you can build rapport with them to increase their personal story lines and get more background info. The game features various things from other Atlus titles, such as summons/compendium and upgrades/items for your team. The worlds are not the most detailed, but it gives off such a nice cyberpunk vibe and is detailed in an anime aspect. The music...Atlus scores another success in my personal opinion. My favorite, the over world exploration BGM, is calm and relaxing and I can see myself listening to it on a YT 10hr track lol. The dialogue is humour at times and brings a smile, especially that first boss, which had me face palming in both cringe and laughter. The bosses and enemies in early game are super easy. The game practically hand holds you until you get to where you get your 2nd team member. Then teh difficulty pushes you off the bridge and you will find yourself getting more challenged. Not so much in teh trash mob aspect, but teh bosses. They tend to exploit your weakness more by design and also pack a punch as well as can take a hit. I spent an hour trying to brute force my way through [redacted] in Subway Line 14 as I was too stubborn to go back and level up more before getting some nice RNG and beating the boss. After that, I made sure to prepare more. The game will crush you if you are under leveled, even by 1 or 2. So grinding may need to be required at times, which isn't too bad as the game is generous in handing out exp.Now for some of the negative things I've noticed which are actually not a whole lot, and that proves that devs can for the most part, release a polished game to the public and not play damage control. -The game has a weird brief auto walk after you stop moving for Ringo to come to a complete stop. It is annoying at times and should just be taken out of the game.-There are some minor rough edges on mainly the characters themselves when viewed up close in cutscenes. Nothing too drastic and for the most part, unnoticeable.-VERY minor stutters when moving around in the over world. lasts about 2-3 seconds. Infrequent enough to not warrant a negative feedback.Lastly:The default settings may need to be changed for some players, as they are super clunky and make the game feel much slower. Consider changing these settings when you get the chance:-Chat Speed to Instant (voice lines tend to finish before the text)-Camera Speed (turning the camera is super slow)-Camera Distance (Ringo defaults to taking up a good portion of the screen)-Camera Tracking to OFF (Allows you to actually control the camera more fluidly)-Using a controller (unfortunately, yes - M&K is perfectly fine, but feels clunky at times)As well as any other settings to suit your needs.

_childDocuments_.review: Guess I´ll keep this short. The overall experience was around 6/10 in my opinion.After finally getting my hands on and devouring Persona 4, I decided to check and see what else Atlus has been up to. I´d never even hear d of Soul Hackers before this and from the demo footage it looked kinda cool. Now it´s 60 something hours later, and my opinion boils down to a resounding ''meh''. The story itself starts of well enough, introducing interesting concepts and showing a fair bit of promise. Unfortunately it seems content to never really explore some plot points, there are a fair few cases of loose threads just being left hanging, and by the halfway point it seems as if the story was being rushed violently to it´s conclusion. The characters likewise show a lot of promise, and in true Atlus style there are a few systems in place to help the player spend time with and get to know them better. Unfortunately I never found myself becoming invested in any of them, and any character motivations came of as fairly dull at best. There are a fair few things to enjoy about them on the surface, but when you begin to dig there really isn´t to much to find.As for the gameplay itself it should be nothing to unfamiliar from Persona, although it felt more akin to Shin Megami Tensei. You have a fairly decent hub world to explore, various NPCs to interact with, quests to complete, it´s all here. the demon summoning allows for a fair bit of customization, depending on the situation at hand and a persons playstyle. Each character has strengths and weaknesses that can be offset to a degree, but never enough as to remove their individual identities. There is a bit of an issue of character dialogue getting quite repetitive, and that problem unfortunately persists throughout the entire game. I found myself playing the game more with the sound turned off during the more grindy sections, with the final boss suffering badly from this problem.Main story line is relatively straightforward and easy to track. Most all of the plot twists that occurred are anything but subtle, although I will give the game props for one or two that did catch me by surprise. The side quests are your standard fair for these kinds of games, but I will give props for the NPC´s actually being given character development. A fair few will give multiple side quests of similar nature, but with an overarching story all of their own the progresses along with the main story.I could speak of this game further, but as a whole this feels as though it is one is a hit-or-miss kind of situation. I can´t say I enjoyed it particularly, but that does no mean the game has no redeemable qualities. Far from it. I would say if you´re a fan of Atlus´ other work, I´d say you should think about giving this one a look. Definitely not one I would recommend paying full price for, but do pick it up when it goes on sale and give it a whirl. I can´t in good conscience recommend going out of your way to complete it, but if you just stick to the main story and a few side quests, I believe it should help to kill a few hours.It by no means should be compared to it´s siblings, but taken as it´s own thing. An interesting venture into exciting waters, but ultimately it seems more interested in floating on stagnating waters, rather than raising the sails and catching it´s wind.I would love to see what this series could become with some time and a fair bit of polish.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 - The SMT (Shin Megami Tensei) series may not be for everyone, but as a fan of turn-based JRPGs, I thoroughly enjoyed this game. If you're also a fan of the genre, it's definitely worth purchasing, especially when it's on sale. The game boasts a solid story, which seems like it draws inspiration from The Ghost in the Shell series. The characters each have their own personal traumas, which can be explored through the Axis, similar to Persona 5's Momentos level design. The game's artwork and sound are both exceptional, and the battle system, while different from previous SMT games, is still enjoyable, particularly with the addition of Sabbath actions that allow for customization and special actions that can be taken per turn that require some planning to make the most of out in boss battles. The character customization is a highlight, with the combination of augments and demons allowing for individual strengths to be maximized, individual characters affinity to be increased, and accessories and meals to buff the team.However, the level design is lackluster, with poorly thought-out mazes that feel tedious to navigate. Boss battles are particularly punishing (as expected, I played the game on hard), requiring grinding that can disrupt the pacing of the story, although this is typical of SMT games. Overall, the game offers a challenging and enjoyable experience, with its art, story, characters, battle system, and customization all impressing. While the level design may not be the best, it's a great follow-up to the original game and references it in subtle ways, but falls short in similar ways the original did.

_childDocuments_.review: Many small issues and a few bigger issues.As of 2022/09/11, several game crashes are still in the game with no word I've found on fixing them or acknowledging them.If you have loading tips on, especially on auto, it significantly increases your load time.Game is not optimized well. (Whether or not Denuvo has a part is unknown). The game has an abnormally long starting load. This seems to be mitigated somewhat by disabling tips on load screens, oddly.Premium Costume DLC and Preorder DLC was broken for several days.Some missing QoL, such as the ability to cancel fast travel if you accidentally activate it and the inability to fast travel to certain locations.Not a huge minus, but some content is locked behind NG+Certain things are tedious, such as clearing "New" quest marks.Recruiting new demons feels a bit too much RNG based, particularly at the start. This is mitigated later in the game, but initially, you can kill 100 of a demon and end up getting a different demon that you've never encountered before despite the game suggesting that more kills = higher chance. This is on top of recruitment events already being somewhat random. Limited battle music options. (You can choose one song or random, you can't select which ones you want).Game auto-pauses when you switch windows, so you can't even do things during load screens.Some QoL stuff is locked behind active skills with relatively short durations and cost MP.Some of the keyboard controls are somewhat awkward and seem to be designed for controller, such as scrollbars not acting as scrollbars.Minimap options are somewhat limited as you have zoom in, zoom out, or disabled. There is no partial minimap option or real minimap transparency options.There are times where the text log just doesn't work.Battle speedup is locked behind Auto-Battle and only works if activated before the attack. There is no visible option to have the speedup activated separately.In one section of the game, you have forced camera angles. In one spot, because of camera angle swapping, it is very difficult to move as the controls keep changing due to the angle swapping.And more.

_childDocuments_.review: I used to be a big SMT fan, or the SMT blanket of games, but not as much recently. My favorite game of all time is the first Persona. I was really disappointed with the direction the series went with social links in 3 on. I mention this in case just knowing that helps you decide if you agree with me or not going forward.As far as Soul Hackers go, and the first Devil Summoner...I dabbled with them, but didn't get far because of the language barrier (back when they were on Saturn). They both became more of collectors items. So I can't really compare this game to the first...but what this game came out to was pretty impressive.The combat system feels pretty standard of the series, but I really like the benefit of stacks from hitting weaknesses. I am always targeting weaknesses and keeping a balance of spells, so this is just adding icing on the damage cake.Also the way social links are handled in this is so much better than the other SMT games i have played. It doesn't feel like it is trying to take over like in the Persona series. Its subtle...leaving the game, exploration, and combat as the main focus.I've seen others mention areas being boring and bland...and that there are a lot of cut scenes, making it more of a visual than a game. I haven't gotten super far into it (around level 22 currently), but I haven't felt like I have been spending more time watching than playing...and the areas do look the same, but it didn't seem like a distraction or disappointment to me. I grew up on areas looking the same. Thankfully there is an on screen map to help. I remember the days of NES exploration where that wasn't present.I guess if I could sum this up is that this probably won't be the best game you have ever played....or even the best game in the "SMT blanket series". But it doesn't leave a bad taste. It is enjoyable...it might not be the most amazingly detailed game ever, but neither is my favorite game of all time. Persona is over 25 years old and I will still play it today. Would I still play this 25 years in the future? I think I would. And that by itself says a whole lot....

_childDocuments_.review: Played just about every SMT Mainline and spinoff there is, such as DDS, Devil Summoner, including the first Soul Hackers, at least the 3DS port if not the Sega Saturn original. Knowing the first, I was pleasantly suprised. I was hoping they'd bring this sequel more up to speed with the other current titles, and so they did.The story is surprisingly compelling, though there will be a lot of dungeon crawling pretty soon into the game. More than some people might be used to. If I'd compare this title to any other in the SMT Universe it would actually be Persona Q probably.In a nutshell, I'm really having fun with this one, even though it is a little on the easy side. I like the traditional press turn system, which has unfortunately been replaced with the sabbath system. In a nutshell, for people familiar with Persona and SMT: Instead of getting extra (half) turns for exploiting weaknesses, the party collects "stacks", one per exploited weakness, later more possibly with some passive skills. If there is at least one stack at turn end, it will trigger sabbath, which is essentially an "All-out" attack, and it gets stronger the more stacks there are. This actually makes the game easier in a way, but it just feels a little less satisfying to me. It's not horrible though, and I think it's quite alright that they experiment with their combat system a little.For anyone who likes the SMT Franchise and doesn't mind doing a lot of dungeon crawling, they'll probably appreciate the title as I do.

_childDocuments_.review: I've finished this game twice now, once on the PS5 version and once on PC. Obtained true ending on both.For context, Megaten has been my favorite video game franchise since 2015, and Devil Summoner: Soul Hackers is one of my favorite games in the entire franchise. When Soul Hackers 2 was announced in early 2022, I felt a combination of optimism and skepticism going into this game. On one hand, I was so happy that ATLUS was making a new Megaten game that wasn't Mainline SMT or Persona, which still gives me hope that there will be future games for other Megaten spinoffs (devil survivor 3 PLEASE)On the other... this game looked like a very big departure from the first game. It took awhile to *somewhat* get over that hurdle for me, but once I did (and after going through the game twice), I can say that - while flawed from a dungeon crawling perspective, I really enjoyed my time with Soul Hackers 2.In my opinion, I think that the best part of this game is the story, which might just be the best Megaten story since SMT IV. The main party of this game are some of the most charming characters I've seen from ATLUS, and Ringo might just be my favorite protagonist in all of Megaten. She's wonderful. The plot is simple, but works very well throughout most of the game due to solid writing and great voice acting. Furthermore, I appreciate the emphasis of Detective Work throughout the game, which is seen throughout all of Devil Summoner. While this doesn't feel like a Soul Hackers sequel in my opinion, I think this game works great as a Devil Summoner title (should've called it Devil Summoner: Aion)The combat system called "Sabbath" is similar to the demon coop system in Strange Journey, and while it starts of slow, it really does open up greatly the more you progress through the game. While I don't think it's the best combat in Megaten, I find it to be very solid on its own and remains fun through the rest of the game.The same cannot be said for the Dungeon Crawling. As a whole, these might be some of the worst dungeons in all of Megaten. The Soul Matrix (the game's optional dungeon which provides very powerful upgrades and additional story for the party) is the biggest offender to this. Boring designs, repetitive music and visual design, large amounts of dead/open space, etc. The main story dungeons also suffer from these issues, although as the game progresses, there is slightly more variety in both music and visual design. After the November Patch, dungeon crawling is less annoying with the addition of a sprint button, but this only mitigates the bad dungeon crawling. Coming directly after SMT V (where the open areas of Da'at had really incredible level design), it's crazy how much of a stepback this game was.Overall, I really enjoyed my time with this game. Soul Hackers 2 goes on sale often, so if you're a fan of ATLUS or are just looking for a solid JRPG, I do recommend buying it! Although reception and sales were middling for this game, I do hope for future titles in Megaten that aren't Mainline SMT and Persona. Personally, I think it's likely with how well SMT V and the P5R ports sold, so I'm looking forward to what's next from ATLUS.

_childDocuments_.review: Really wish there was a neutral option on Steam, but since there isn't, I'll just settle for a recommend only because I did find myself having more fun than not. That being said, this game just doesn't feel complete. Not in the way of playability (bugs, glicthes, etc.), but more in a sense where it doesn't really have enough polish.I've played plenty of the other SMT games, so honestly I just bought this game because I'm waiting for P5R to release on Steam and I had already beaten P4G this year. With comparisons in mind, I really like the difference in combat in this game, the main difference being that attacking weaknesses won't stun enemies, but instead adds up to extra damage at the end of your turn, which itself can be modified in a bunch of different ways. As a result, getting hit is guaranteed, and it forces you to choose between offense and defense more than before. Other than that, its essentially the same, but for me, that was really just what I was looking for anyway. Upgrading weapons is a tad too grind-reliant, as it requires materials on top of the currency. All the options do allow for making more specialized builds with each character, but unfortunately they don't amount to much more than more damage for particular types, just first of the reasons why it doesn't feel like it had gotten the full polish treatment. As far as plot and characters go, the game does a fine job. I actually really like the characters, as they really aren't as morally cut and dry as the other games, so seeing them interact with not only each other but with your dialogue options is a pretty fresh feeling. Ringo is genuinely really funny, and even if the other characters are kind of tropey, I thought it was not really distractedly so. The story is just okay, its main problem being far too predictable (and at the time of this review, I'm a little more than halfway through it). It feels more like a plot you would get when your in your second draft; you've got the basic premise, maybe some things to spice it up, but you haven't reached the point where anything truly engaging has been added. The absolute BIGGEST problem with the game are the levels (or dungeons, whatever you might call them). Straight up, they are bad. Compared to other SMT games, they are incredibly uninspired, with them being simple mazes at best to infuriatingly gimmicky at its worst. They aren't even interesting on a aesthetic level either (other than the Soul Matrix, which acts as each companions side-quest dungeons). TWO of them are just subway systems with literally nothing going on. This was definitely the biggest problem with the game, and it is actually disruptive at time considering its not only the way to actually progress, but as mentioned before, they want you to actively grind for upgrades, too, so coming back to them is bound to happen. Even worse, for some reason you can't see the missions you accept in the Soul Matrix, so you either have to remember, look up what they were, or get lucky. The levels were CLEARLY not thought out enough, and its kind of baffling at times. All in all, its a fine game, but its unfortunately marred by potential not seen through completely. The fact that the main story on average takes somewhere near 30 hours to finish compared to the near 100 the others have says a lot. In a weird yet disappointing way, Soul Hackers 2 feels like the side game to the side game, and while I would love for them to come back to this, they have to put in more effort. Overall, like a 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are  fan of PSP/PS Vita/DS/3DS style JRPGs you may like this. Its very small in scope like the portable JRPGs, small areas, a lot of transitions between those small areas. I'm sure a lot of the Demon models have been taken out of other Shin Megami Tensei (SMT) games as well as it seems they have the same animations. The game play is not that much different from those JRPGs too but it feels really good. This game was also mainly played on my Steam Deck too so that has helped.The world design reminds me a lot like Digimon Story Cyber Sleuth (DSCS), more so the way they designed the digital areas of the game, the rest is just your JRPG version of future Japan that has been in a lot of the portable era of games.Character design is fun and looks like a lot of Japanese sci-fi games that have to do with sci-fi  future, yet again reminding me of DSCS. Its the generic group of JRPG protagonists with flashy and flamboyant cyberpunky clothing. The voice acting in English is good but your standard fair from the portable era of games. I didn't play the original Devil Summoner: Soul Hackers so I can't compare. The battles are fun and flashy with great animations. They don't quite work the same as the other SMT games so it took a bit getting used to.  You don't use Demons as summons in this game the same way, you use them as essentially programs in your weapon which decides what attacks you can do and what your weakness and strengths are. The attacks are very similar to what the demons would do in the other SMT games. The demons in this game don't have the same weaknesses from other SMT though so I had to relearn some of what I knew from other SMT games. Demon fusion is here, and pretty much similar to the other SMT games. If you have played any of those portable are games the dungeon crawls are the same, a lot of back tracking a lot of small areas with a lot of transition. You see the demons in the world and can knock them down like other SMT games and get preemptive attacks. The dungeons are kind of bland like the portable era games.The main plot is a mystery story with your group mainly acting as detectives. You pick up cases from a few people in the world or from a quest giver that then will send you to people in the world. Most quest haver you returning to areas you have already traversed to find a glowing item, killing a certain demon or a certain amount then returning to the person you talked to then returning to the quest giver. The more you do, the higher you level up for the quest giver and get newer quests. It can get tedious and repetitious.

_childDocuments_.review: Buy it on saleSoul Hackers 2 is overall subpar for an SMT entry: plot and worldbuilding details are glazed over without serious consideration or development, dialogue is repetitive and shallow, and the characters feel hollow and unlikable. Serious themes such as death, sexuality, and divinity are handled callously and the cutscenes depicting them are often slow and lifeless. The environments are repetitive and boring, npcs and quests feel uninspired, and the dungeons don't feel worth exploring. Characters and demons themselves LOOK good, I just can't understand the gap between their looking straight out of Persona 5 while running around environments that look ripped from SMT 3 Nocturne.The combat is worthwhile, but the Sabbath system feels gimmicky and the dialogue between characters makes me cringe. I would rather have a team of just demons over these gloomy losers. The leveling feels really off: unless you're stopping to fight every mob, you're going to be super under-leveled while progressing at an organic pace. The Soul Matrix is straight-up a bad time. The side-quests feel like content for the sake of content, which I would expect from a lesser JRPG. It's like a checklist to clean out these horrible teammates' souls by witnessing their trauma and having a conversation like "that was messed up but I see why you wanna get the bad guy" over and over. It makes me more claustrophobic than Mementos from P5 or Tartarus from P3, and might stop me from ever finishing this game. Lastly, a matter of personal preference: I usually play SMT games in Japanese, but the subtitles are really lacking in this one so I'm playing with the English dub so I understand what my loser teammates are whining about in battle. If you're a Subs > Dubs guy like me, you understand it's a bad time.

_childDocuments_.review: If you haven't played an SMT or Persona game, this is not the place to start.That said, it's actually a pretty good RPG in my opinion. It's a surprisingly good sequel to Soul Hackers 1 too, which is one of my favorite RPGs. I wasn't sure what to expect at first, as the preview trailers didn't remind me much of the first game and the game wasn't a first person DRPG like the original. They actually nailed the tone and atmosphere pretty well somehow though, and there are a lot of similarities to the first game that really solidify it as a proper sequel.I enjoyed the game, but depending on your expectations you might not enjoy it as much.The current mixed rating is pretty harsh, but not entirely undeserved. The DLC situation is pretty inexcusable and I hope Atlus isn't quite so brazen next time. The game itself is pretty solid, despite the lack of polish in some areas. I think it's a great sequel, all things considered. Most of the issues/shortcomings can be chalked up to the development team working with an unfamiliar engine, and maybe some unrealistic player expectations. I would cautiously recommend this game, but not as an introduction to this amazing series.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the most expensive edition on PS4 at launch and had mixed feelings after finishing the game. Forcing you to level grind for a few extra mins/hours.   - The dungeon designs are so bad. _childDocuments_.review: I want to point the fact that this was a positive review. Then around the 40th hour in the game I simply broke down because this game is a complete waste of time. every single mechanic of this game is made to waste your time for nothing and story and background environment, as every npc, are basically nothing and there is no worth to go on with the story.For reference, I played EVERY smt\persona game into existence, yes included the old famcom megami tensei, so I know what I am doing here.This is not a good SMT game. It’s a bad entry point for a newbie of the series, it has NOTHING to do with the original Soul Hacker except some citations all around and it’s the worst story and npc.Regarding the setting I will never understand why they put the "2" here considering the original soul hacker game is the ending chapters of two old series (the raidou games and the devil summoners). If you don't want to explain everything it's relatively fine, but this is an entry point in a story that goes on from FOUR games in two different series. Atlus simply solved this excluding everything coming from the original game and putting the name just for marketing purposes. Just reading till this if you are a SMT fan you have your full for not buying the game.Now back to the game.The dungeon design is the WORST I’ve ever seen. The dungeons are all the same and the soul matrix is simply the worst thing that they could ever thought of. Instead of a single labyrinth they decided to split in three parts, and every part has four enormous floors. Too bad that those parts are the same empty space with only the floor to walk into. The floors have the same monsters and object, the only difference are the minibosses. You will stay A LOT around here for mmo fetch tier quest with no interesting rewards, the miniboss sometimes unlock some fusions but nothing more. The normal dungeons are subway, offices or dock area, recycled every time. The shop hubs are tiny and poor designed. This game coming after Persona 5 and in 2022 this dryness of environment is terrifying lazy. It’s like playing into a beta version or some modeling kit.The battle mechanics is classic SMT with come late persona’s qol, but there is no progression nor new mechanics. The thing you do in the tutorial dungeon is the same thing you are doing for all the 40-50 hours needed to end this pain. There is absolutely NOTHING as progression, only numbers that go up. The MC carries the game like Atlas, but the other npcs are NOTHING. Their personal stories are really lazy and predictable but the worst experience is doing hours of the same labyrinth, the same four demons, running and running spamming assassin’s steps cause you are TIRED, just to have two or three lines of conversation and that's all. The game tries to build mystery but in the end the characters story and the general story is NOTHING. I know perfectly that the SMT games take a while to gear up but this takes the consideration to an insane extreme. This is why I decided to put a negative review. I sit through the immense NOTHING of the personal stories, boring side\fetch quests with two or three dialogues and nothing else, hoping there was something better in the end.Well, there isn’t. All the situations are solved with some stupid deus ex machina (yeah I know that that’s basically what the two MCs are but it’s SO LAZY), personal motivations fall behind and everything turns to I have to find a thing to find a thing to find a thing. They put some kind of bait and switch in the fourth floor of every NPC labyrinth but to reach it you have passed 30 to 40 hours in game hungry for more, and that’s basically the only surprise\reveal you can expect because all the other stuff you can easily predict or they are so phoned in that it’s offensive, from a narrative standpoint.The plot starts to gear up in the LAST dungeon and it's solved like it's late for work. _childDocuments_.review: I’m a big MegaTen fan, but I just couldn’t do this one. Soul Hackers 2 has some good ideas and has some of the aspects that I love from this series, but ultimately, I was unable to finish the game and it felt like a chore to get as far as I did.The game starts with an almost forty minute cutscene sequence and that kinda sets the tone for the pacing here. It is slow, monotonous, and one of the laziest JRPGs I have played in a while which really hurts to say given the studio that it’s coming from.The dungeons are quite literally just connected hallways and small rooms, there is VERY little actual variety there and the devs couldn’t even be bothered to include chests or other physical treasure to find. The exploration is limited to dead ends that sometimes have one of your demons standing by to hand you an item.It doesn’t even take that long to get that bad, because by the second dungeon you are literally walking on floating hallways and rooms in cyberspace. It is the most basic of JRPG dungeon designs and is something I would expect from a student project, not a full-fledged AAA production from a respected studio.I wouldn’t say the story has been terrible so far, but it has hardly done anything to hold my interest. It’s your typical JRPG sci-fi with just a bit of edge to it, kinda reminiscent of Scarlet Nexus, but a bit more narrow in its focus. This is good in some ways, but given the already slow pacing, it’s a bit of a pain as you wait for things to build up and the sheer number of cutscenes included here does not do it any favors.The only thing I outright enjoyed here would be the combat. It’s your usual turn-based combat, elemental attack types, strengths, weaknesses, bunch of items to use and upgrades to equip, and my favorite element from this series - the ability to recruit demons and fuse them together into stronger ones.All of that is some good stuff. Granted, it doesn’t really do much to elevate it further than that, but at this point I will take what I can get from this game.Outside of that, there’s nothing else really to note here. It’s a roughly 30 hour JRPG with okay graphics, okay music, and fun combat, but absolutely awful dungeon design, a monotonous gameplay loop, and a story that leans more towards boring than interesting. I had planned to finish this one up for a full review, but honestly, I just can’t see myself burning any more time than I already have here.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot I can say about this but I'll try to keep it brief:Soul Hackers 2 is a more simplistic SMT entry in gameplay. It doesn't quite have the depth of games like Persona 5, SMT 5, or Strange Journey, but it has a much more focused story. The mainline SMT games are overly edgy alongside trying out new mechanics that generally don't always work (Smirk + Companion in SMT4), making it a good JRPG gameplay experience but not a strong character-driven experience. Side games like Strange Journey have excellent dungeon designs, but the story is often driven by ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who won't ever compromise, always going to a "the law/chaos ally goes to overwhelming extremes." Persona has been the series that often doesn't fall into those pitfalls by focusing on Social Links instead of Law/Chaos, but the gameplay is designed to often be unfocused, with a lot of your limited days going towards raising friendship points to attempt to get to the next breakpoint in a social link, and you often end up only experiencing a portion of the social links, which are the highlight of the character development. You effectively get familiar with the characters you already liked, and don't see the full story of ones you didn't, which can heavily impact your opinion of said characters.Soul hackers 2 stays focused on its relatively small cast of 5: Ringo, Figue, Arrow, Milady, and Saizo, plus a few characters that are close to that cast, about one or two characters per. They also have a few side characters with a short quest line that does help flesh out the problems with a technology driven world. You get a pretty good development on the group as a team, rather than just dating sim between mc and one other character. That's a big advantage of a focused story.Now the dungeons do suck. They're pretty barebones, and the game is low budget and that's noticable. The animations aren't super amazing either: Ringo's hair clips on her jacket from very early on and the soul hack dive animation is pretty clearly reused in a super noticable way. The demon roster isn't big and the Macca system is pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Comp upgrades are a bit boring where there's much less tradeoffs than in other games (i.e. status weapon with 1 damage), and there's not as much flexiblity with each character as certain ones are locked to doing certain actions better than others. It streamlines it for newer players, but it also limits the depth of gameplay for older players. Sabbaths are boring and you can't have the animation on skip by default for some reason (?). They still haven't figured out that modern turn based combat should have a fast forward button like Bravely Default did, without tying it to auto-attack. They don't tell you what you need to do the True End. These are all valid complaints that don't necessarily need comparisons to just other SMT games. The story also isn't the newest thing ever, but I think what a lot of people miss is that it's not about what the story is about, but what route the story takes to get to its plot points. I think you don't need to write a new story every game, just a relatable and meaningful experience on the path of the story. It's about how much you like the characters. After all, if we were rating SMT games by just the plot, most of them would be the same general story in the "big picture."

_childDocuments_.review: It's decent. 7.5/10Its decent, but playing this right after Persona 5 hurts its score.Persona 5 had fast combat animations, great soundtracks, good pacing, and interesting maps.Soul Hackers 2 combat feels slower, soundtrack not memorable, a lot of side quests, and the 'soul' dungeons are all the same maze like style. Pros:The world is a futuristic japan with demons summoning being the normal.Main characters are fairly cool and their story unravels as you play.The shops owners are like side characters with their own side quests and stories.Side quests are quite interesting for lore, world builder, and store owner stories. Con:Combat is not snappy and feels slow. There is a speed up option that doesn't feel nice to watch, but it does help.Initiating combat is odd. You need to swing at the enemies model and then walk up to it to start combat. I get its there so you can skip battles (swing but don't touch), but feels odd.Map list is ehh. Its gets long, and theres not indents to help quickly locate city or store options.Weird default settings. _childDocuments_.review: Edit2: Well, the game is going to get an update which will speed up the game a bit. The run speed will still be the same (you just no longer go to a menu now and then), but being encouraged to fight more due to higher battle speed would solve both tedium and material grinding. So the main issues are (probably) gone and I'd be more eager to recommend this game. Well, if I actually got to TRY these changes. Too little too late, Atlus.Edit: I have beaten the game and am editing this review, but I'll keep the old one for anyone interested. I played on Hard from start to finish and have played the whole 3DS SMT library, as well as Personas 3-5 for any comparisons I'll be making. Also, I had to leave the game on a lot recently while playing, so the playtime is inflated by a few hours, and I didn't buy any of the DLC because Atlus is getting too greedy.This game was a rollercoaster. On one hand, most of the main and sidequest bosses as well Risky Enemies were great fights, and I think this game has some of the better gameplay design in the series. The difficulty slowly drops off, but not as much as some of the other games (like SMT4 or Persona 4G and 5, which just drop and keep dropping past the first few hours), and I think it was just enough for me to keep the postive review. Barely. On the other hand, the random encounters are as simple and boring as ever, which wouldn't be as much of a problem... if the battles weren't so slow, and you didn't fight so many of them. I know SMT5 added an option to skip animations by pressing the button again, why the hell is that absent here?You might be thinking to yourself, "Well I'll just avoid the battles", which is what I did most of the time. Well for one thing, you need materials for your COMP upgrades - in order to get "Skill II", you need "Skill I", so you'll need to go back and fight anyways, or be like me and just not have fun with the better Mystiques because you can't use them. Secondly, this is where the dungeon design comes into play - it's ♥♥♥♥. I mentioned it in the old review, and most people point it out, but nobody really points out WHY it's ♥♥♥♥. It's not just because it's linear with barely anything to interact with - Persona 3 and 4 also had that, and I didn't suffer nearly as much there. No, the problems are 1. There are only FOUR TRACKS in the whole game, two of which only play at the very ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ end of the game, while even Persona 3 at least had variations of one theme, and 2. Ringo is so S L O W, even when you get the speed increasing skill early on (which should've been the default, and it would still not be enough) Other games had the decency to make your character zoom pretty fast and/or have smaller, more compact dungeon design. This one doesn't.As for the story, it's about the same as I stated before. It's alright. There was a twist that I really enjoyed, and there were some good scenes with the main cast, but overall it's nothing special.Honestly, if Atlus fixed the tedious parts - dungeon movement speed and battle animations, primarly - or a mod addressing was released (I know somebody used Cheat Engine to speed up the game, which sounds like just the thing - but I learned too late to bother) I think this would be one of the better SMT games, and I'd recommend it at full price for fans, as before. Unfortunately, you're better off waiting for a discount, and maybe try another game in the series first if you have no prior experience with Megaten. OLD REVIEW:I WAS going to give this a negative review, but... eh, sure. It gets decent after the slow start.If you like JRPG gameplay and are fine with bland, very simplistic dungeon design, then this game is alright. If not, you'll want for discount, but it should still be ok if you want to try a Shin Megami Tensei game a bit closer to mainline than Persona, and SMT3 looks too aged for you. I'm still early into the story (will update this review if I remember) but it's enjoyable enough, if only for the main characters' banter and small talk. It's not good compared to other games I've played, including SMT, but it's not like Steam has many of the latter far. The combat is pretty good and challenging anyway, which is good enough for me. A lot of people miss Press Turns/One Mores from other games for hitting weaknesses, but in my eyes those mechanics negatively affected game balance or boss design if not handled right, so I'm fine with them gone in spinoffs. SMTIV lets you steamroll everything past the first 2 bosses by snowballing buffs while Persona bosses are boring and rarely do anything with elements.I will say the beggining of the game is boring as hell. I thought that maybe it was because it's too long and full of lore exposition, but in hindsight, I think it's the opposite: the game tries to show you all the main characters, their motives, positions, most of the town NPCs and what the main story will be about all within the first hour or two. As a result, a lot of the explaining and introductions feel half-assed. It helps get to the combat and gameplay faster but it just makes the early story unnatural. I feel like it's getting a bit better with its pacing later though.I also thought I'd hate the character design but it quickly grew on me. Saizo best boi.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not my ideal SMT game, but it is better than most of the series' historical titles.The music is great.  Normally I don't like voiced protagonists in RPGs, because my enjoyment of the game as a whole is marred by what the protagonist says.  I actively want Geralt, Eloi and Tiny Tina to die horribly in a hurricane with sharks,tigers and a nuclear bomb thrown in for good measure.  Ringo is enjoyable -- but I would still prefer silence. But I prefer gameplay over story, so take my opinion for what it's worth.As SMT titles go, the battle system here is "meh".  Not the best, but not overly tedious.  I miss the press turn system and feel like this system is a downgrade.  But it generally avoids the kinds of problems that could make Nocturne "the opposite of fun", where you have to spend 30 minutes incrementally grinding away at the health of a boss only to find out you lost the race and have to start over.What is an improvement over many of the titles is that you can swap out any of the main characters' demons both out of battle and during.  That opens up a lot of options for dealing with difficult situations.Overall, I'd give it a 7.5.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun RPG with a nice battle system. I don't think any of the mechanics are as deep as some of the other Atlus games, but that is isn't a bad thing. The game is streamlined but not hand-holding or infantilizing. The story is very character focused but the characters are actually quite charming. It's also nice that each dungeon gives you something to pay attention to story wise-- that keeps the pacing tight.  The combat is generally fairly smooth and while the dungeons themselves are surprisingly plain, these are probably (overall) also the least annoying dungeons in SMT (or offshoot) game in a while. The game does a good job at keeping you focused on the story and advancing while also allowing you to grind if you'd like. It is an easy time if you are looking for a traditional (character) story focused JRPG.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with Soul Hackers 2 and would overall give it a thumbs up.  It's the usual as far as turn based weakness exploiting SMT combat goes - so if that's up your alley you're likely to get some good mileage here.  The story is pretty well done and the voice acting is phenomenal.  The game is also short enough to where the things that bothered me didn't get out of control, but there are some noticeable issues for sure.-Dungeons are bland and barely vary throughout the entire game until the last dungeon.-You will hear the same 4 songs for 90% of the play time.-Lots of content that should be available with the main game is gated by NG+.That third point is the most frustrating to me.  There is a mechanic in place where certain answers to situations will increase your link to a party member, which in turn governs how far you can venture into their psyche which functions as another dungeon to explore as well as fleshing out their characters further.  There are a finite amount of these points available per playthrough, so playing multiple times to see it all is required.  The game also only has one real route through the main story so everything else will play the same, making the whole process even sillier.All that being said, I DO still recommend the game.  It's not the strongest offering from ATLUS but it's far from weak, and especially worth picking up on a decent sale.

detailed_description: Comparison Chart TEKKEN 8 - Deluxe Edition The Deluxe Edition Includes: • TEKKEN 8 • Playable Character Year 1 Pass - Additional playable characters: Eddy, Lidia, Heihachi, and more - 3-day Early Access for DLC characters - Avatar Skin: Kinjin • Character Costume: Gold Suit Pack - 1 costume per each playable character (32 total) TEKKEN 8 - Ultimate Edition The Ultimate Edition Includes: • TEKKEN 8 • Playable Character Year 1 Pass - Additional playable characters: Eddy, Lidia, Heihachi, and more - 3-day Early Access for DLC characters - Avatar Skin: Kinjin • Character Costume: Gold Suit Pack - 1 costume per each playable character • Avatar Costume: Classic TEKKEN T-Shirt Set - 32 designs • Avatar Skins: Kazuya, Jin, and Jun About the Game GET READY FOR THE NEXT CHAPTER IN THE LEGENDARY FIGHTING GAME FRANCHISE, TEKKEN 8. • 32 FIGHTERS FOR A NEW GENERATION Completely redesigned character visuals. Elaborate, highly-detailed models built from the ground and high-fidelity graphics break the limits of new-generation hardware by adding a new weight and atmosphere to TEKKEN’s signature battles . Vivid environments and destructible stages combine to create an overwhelming sense of immersion, creating the ultimate play experience. • NEW GAME, NEW RIVALRY Fist Meets Fate in TEKKEN 8. Holding a record for the longest-running video game storyline, the TEKKEN series begins a new chapter as TEKKEN 8 continues the tragic saga of the Mishima and Kazama bloodlines , and their world-shaking father-and-son grudge matches starting from 6 months after the closure of the last match. The story of Jin Kazama's growth and determination marks a new chapter in the timeless saga . • THRILLING OVER-THE-TOP BATTLES EMBODYING AGGRESSIVENESS & DESTRUCTION The new battle system, Heat , dials up the aggressive nature of battles , while maintaining the play feel and tactics unique to the TEKKEN series. The intensity of battles is greatly enhanced by the destructable stages. Unleashing super move-like Rage Arts is sure to enthrall both players and spectators alike. All of these hard-hitting mechanics come together to make TEKKEN 8 the most exciting installment in the series to date! • ENJOY YOUR TEKKEN LIFE! In the new single-player mode Arcade Quest , craft your own unique avatar and embark on your new TEKKEN life. Battle your way through a variety of rivals across multiple arcades as the story unfolds, all while mastering the basics and practical skills in TEKKEN 8. Unlock a variety of customization items for characters and avatars as you progress. *In addition to this edition, Deluxe Edition and Ultimate Edition are also available. Please be careful not to purchase the same content twice.

_childDocuments_.review: [UPDATE] Oct 6, 2024So in an alternate universe, we should be boycotting T8 for banning Chinese and Russian players, right?[UPDATE] Feb 29, 2024Still recommend the game, but have to chime in on the fact that the Tekken Shop and the way it was implemented is the WORST possible approach they could have taken. Minimum purchase of 500 coins for $4.99 with each costume costing 400 coins is outrageous. 1:1 item purchase would have been forgivable, but they just had to piss people off and add Fortnite coins, didn't they? Tekken 8 would have been easy GOTY contender for its quality and its release would have been 100% flawless if not for the shop. Sad times.By no means am I Tekken master nor am I a fighting game maniac. But as a gamer who is familiar with almost every genre, I try to play every fighting game I can get my hands on. It's safe to say that I at least know the basics of fighting game mechanics and what it takes to "get better." In the recent years, with the help of my best friend from high school, I've had a chance to learn the ins and outs of games like SF6, Dragon Ball Fighterz, MK, and even some anime fighting games. As a result, the more I invested, the more I learned. The more I learned, the more I enjoyed the games. I grew up with the OG Playstation and Tekken 3. Now, 20+ years later, what a great time it is to be alive: to witness the eighth installment of the Tekken series.In the fighting game genre, I think we can all agree that if the game is fun, the game is already great to a certain extent. Back in the day, that's all that mattered. Now, we've got other categories to consider like amount of content, cosmetics, replayability, updates, etc. But let's face it: when it comes to Tekken, no one can deny that it's the legend among legends when it comes to the bare bones. They solidified the game and introduced the new heat drive(?) system. They went the same route as Street Fighter 6 in that they brought the "special style" for newcomers - akin to Modern controls in SF6 - to just press buttons and enjoy the game for what it is. Of course, we all know that this will only get you so far; and to really delve deep into Tekken, one needs to get the kids' gloves off and play like the Tekken legends of old (lol) to learn combos w/ manual inputs and understand what you're actually doing. Regardless, there are many ways to enjoy the game by whatever means necessary. The game perfected the Tekken recipe and it is indeed the best Tekken to play in 2024.Two things that were noticeable: companies know that a lot of players are not as hardcore and excited to play online/ranked so it feels like they implemented a strong Ghost system for players to enjoy in the long-term, especially those who deem themselves "less competitive" like myself. When it comes to replayability, I think this is a good way to enjoy the game further past the story/arcade modes without stressing out about playing online. Second, the special style allows players to "see" what certain characters can do without lifting a finger, really. Well, maybe using your thumb to chain simple combos but it definitely makes the character bust out the flashy stuff on the fly.Tekken's story is beyond disappointing, and this has been the case since T4. It's your average hero beats villain, angel vs demon routine that every Tekken has brought so far. No real character development, no real stakes. Just a Jin/Kazuya fest as usual. I have this lowkey feeling that the writers have this hard-on for making the Japanese characters look cool and have the characters that represent the rest of the world be their side pieces, but this might be just minor politics at play and wouldn't really bother me.... IF THE WRITING WASN'T SO SUBPAR. $20 says AI technology can do better for Tekken 9. Then again, every anime series post-2010 has had similar subpar storylines all over the place so.. I guess they just lack creativity and prefer to take the "safe" way when it comes to stories (just like Ubisoft).[UPDATE] Feb 15, 2024Upon further analysis, the customization in Tekken 8 is the best in the FGC. Beats the likes of MK1 and SF6 out of the water. Still would like to see more accessories, as we had in the T6 days, but from what we've seen people around the world come up with these past few weeks since launch, the potential of creating various characters from different franchises is astounding. Do they plan to release more accessories and outfits in the future? If so, are they gonna be paid DLC...? Case in point, the customization options that are available at launch are underwhelming to say the least. I don't know why I was expecting to feel more excited to see the likes of T6 and TTT revived. But I might have gotten my hopes up a bit too high. At least we can make LEON from RE4? Cyberpunk for Jin? A bootleg Kenshi from MK for Victor? GOKU FOR LARS?Arguably the best Tekken game of all time, for veterans and newcomers alike. The biggest compliment I would like to throw is that in a game industry where we're used to companies releasing unfinished games to rake in the $$$, Harada and his team really took their time and sweat blood and tears to bring Tekken 8 to a near-perfect state before unleashing it upon the world. Also really looking forward to how Knee dominates the tournament scene once again.Yeah, I think I'll be sticking with this one for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Have been playing Tekken since Tekken 3 from back in the days when it was originally released. Played Tekken 7 for more hours than I care to admit(it's thousands) and had multiple chars in the highest rank, one of which is Dragunov, which is one of the worst characters in T7.If you're reading this, do not buy this overpriced piece of garbage game. Below I'm going to explain why from different perspectives: casual, nerd, competitive player, fan of the series, technical perspective.The game is an absolute abomination no matter what perspective you view it from.Let's start with a perspective of a new casual player. The problem for new casual players is that the game has very big banalcing issues and gives too much advantage to the attacking player. And once you get out of the very very newbie category that only have a few hours in the game, you will run into a lot of bad but not so new players in orange-purple ranks that abuse the imbalances in the game and the counterplay to them is too hard for most people and especially for new casual players. So you end up not having fun, because once you get attacked, there's very little you can do to effectively defend. In fact, in many situations all you can do is to guess between a low and a mid mixup. And even bad but not new players will abuse those situations all the time, because the game gives easy access to big mixups for bad players.And let me tell you, I've seen just this with my own eyes where my friend ragequit the game because of this. And teaching her how to deal with it requires her to learn advanced things such as fuzzy low parrying in neutral, ducking strings on reaction, stepping strings on reaction, option-selecting multiple options by SS~blocking and SS~ducking, using better spacing together fast keepout tools and using them well, block and whiff punishment. Yes, those are good things to learn, but in a well-designed game, a reward from hitting it and a counterplay to that is directly proportional to how hard it is to do. So, if it's a very easy to access running move with big plus frames on block, it should be as easily to beat by either just ducking or sidestep blocking and then launching it. That's not the case in this game. What's happening in this game is that some moves are virtually impossible to counter(such as Azucena wr3,2) and when Azucena hits that wr3,2, she starts a casino and you can option-select anything and is forced to guess. That's not fun to play at a casual level when you can't do anything. Not fun to play at any level.Now let's view it from the nerd and competitive player's perspectives. There are so big imbalances in the game, that it's too hard even for top professionals like Knee and Arslan to overcome. Let's see the examples:Speedkicks "My issue is with the people who wouldn't be good at anything win".Arslan(the best player in Tekken history) "This game is for noobs".Kokkoma(one of the best players in history next to Arslan and Knee) "We are all in casino". This implies that the game is very random and there is no real skill needed, and specifically that you can't overcome worse players with skill: the game gives too much and a good defender player can't do anything to win vs worse players. So we're just all in a casino and bet."I think it's actually superficial that the concept of Tekken 8 is aggressive. It's just a simple 50/50 mindgame."Last but not least(#2 best player in Tekken history), Knee basically says the same.The point here to take is that the game gives for the attacker very easy and undeserved access to best mixups of their character. And that's what you want as a player and that's how you win in Tekken: you want get access to the best mixups and then you want to mix your opponent up with them. The difference between Tekken 6 and Tekken 8 is that in Tekken 5 the access to mixups was harder to achieve and also the mixups were much less strong. I'll give you a few examples. Bryan. In Tekken 6 qcb3(hatchet) was +2 on hit and tracked worse than in T8. Yes, +2. In Tekken 8 it's +5 on hit adn tracks much better both sides. What it means is that in T6 the attacker had the advantage, so Bryan could overmash your buttons but didn't have as much of an advantage and couldn't catch your steps with jabs. Also, the tracking on moves in T6 was worse than in T8, so the defender could avoid many more moves of Bryan than they can now in T8. Now in T8 hatchet tracks both sides and it's not steppable when a good player uses it: just don't do it at point blank and delay the input a tiny bit and it will track both sides and is unsteppable. Then it gives +5 on hit and if you try to attack after it, Bryan threatens to frame trap launch you with b,f+2, so attacking after it is pretty much out of the question. Also, if you want to step, there are many more moves that track now in T8 and will catch you if you try to step after qcb3 on hit: 1,2, d/f+1, d/f+2, d+2, qcb3, qcb4 just to name a few. This basically means that the attacker has options to punish and launch the defender big time for doing any option: either attacking after qcb3 on hit or even just sidestepping. This basically leaves the defender one real option: backdash. And backdash, well, it's nerfed in T8, so that all Bryan attacks will reach the defender no problem.This gets us to the simple 50/50 casino game, because all that's left for the defender is to backdash and do nothing, and now the defender gets mixed up by a Bryan with big 50/50 moves: qcb3, qcb4, u/f+4, b+1.Or another example, Dragunov wr2. In Tekken 6 it was +4 on hit and remember, moves in T5/6 had much less tracking than moves in T7/8. The defender could sidestep and avoid the wr2 itself, and punish it on whiff. Also, on block it didn't do any damage in T6 and the fact that it was +4 on hit meant that Dragunov can't frame trap you with d/f+2. This meant that the defender has an option to press quick moves such as jabs without risking of getting frame trap launched by d/f+2.Also, because it was only +4 and moves had less tracking in T6, the defender could step and avoid Dragunov attacks such as: 1; 2,1; d/f+4; d/f+1; d/b+2; b+4,3; b+4,3; d/f+2; etc.On the other hand if you mashed, Dragunov could overmash you and punish you for attacking at minus frames with moves like 1,2,1; d/f+1,4 and d/b+2,1. But then if you want to step or backdash, Dragunov on the attacking side has option to either chase you with forward dashes or realign himself with the sidesteps and then attack, but the point here is that then Dragunov would lose his plus frame advantage, because he'd first have to forward dash or sidestep to realign with movement, because the moves themselves didn't track.This created a deep game where both the attacker and the defender nave options and can choose how they want to play.Now, in T8 Drag's wr2 is +6 on block and does chip damage. If the defender presses even something as small as a jab, Dragunov can launch with d/f+2, which goes against the archetype of the character, which is supposed to be poker: death by a thousand cuts with pokes: 1; 2,1; d/f+1; d/f+2; d+2; ws4; etc. Then they gave Dragunov d/b+3+4 hatchet kick that tracks one side, +7 on hit and 23 damage. This leads us to the exact same problems as I described above with Bryan's qcb3 hatchet and also pretty much the same to what I just described with Drag's wr2.The point is that the game is dumbed down so much that it's not real Tekken anymore, it's a dumb 50/50 casino simulator, just as those top players described.Then, there is also a crime that Bandai Namco is committing nowadays: they falsely copyright claim people on YouTube for showcasing the game with mods. Uploading a video of their game on YT is fair use. Mods is simply not Bandai Namco's property, so they falsely copyright claim the videos, which is a crime.

_childDocuments_.review: Several months after the game's release, the game has burned all of it's good will on release due to the post-release content and support of the game. They released a cash shop in a full-priced, $70 game after reviews were written, a battle pass full of reused assets, and decided you can't practice against DLC characters if you don't own them in the replay feature. I've been a long-standing Tekken player and back then (before Tekken 7), they would release a complete, feature rich game without any greedy monetization practices. Gameplay-wise. is fun casually but heat (aggression mechanic) needs to be dialed back as it forces guessing games with the opponent with many heat smashes/moves having massive advantage on block and losses usually comes from guessing incorrectly. There's no defensive counterplay for heat at the moment which leads to very gimmicky gameplay in ranked sets. Defensive play is punished with chip damage too. Also, the way the game handles people disconnecting from ranked matches is very poor as you don't get the points you would have won and there's virtually no penalty from disconnecting yourself. TLDR, fun casually. Avoid for bad monetization practices and aggression is dialed up too much that it forces guessingEdit: Now they charge you for longstanding franchise characters as DLCEdit 2: They don't include all new stages in the Season pass. You have to pay extra for it

_childDocuments_.review: I think people need to look at this game realistically:PERFORMANCEDecent. The benchmark tool does a great job, but you might still need to check a replay with many effects to see if you drop frames. Speaking of dropping frames, the game lags in the character select menu, it's pretty silly. Most anti-aliasing options look pretty bad, either in motion or in general. Since Bamco added DLSS, they could have also included DLAA. The animations during gameplay are not always fluid, even though the game reports 60fps. It becomes even more apparent when you turn off V-SYNC.GAMEPLAYI mean, it's TEKKEN, it survived as the only 3D fighting game because it's good. The design is "AgGrEsSiVe", so be prepared for people to mash, act out of frame, mix you up and cheese at every opportunity. There's little time for breathers. Ranked is pretty stressful, since the people still playing are mostly veterans who are not afraid to unleash their lifetime experience of set-ups on you.ONLINEDecent, but not great. Rollback works pretty well when it wants to. If you only accept 5 bar wired connections, you will have a good experience during matches. That is, when you get matches. People like to disconnect and/or refuse rematches. How long are the wait times? It depends. There's some people saying you need UPNP/Port forwarding and/or a static ip address to have access to everyone in the queue. Nobody knows, it's not like there's an official guide or anything.MONETIZATIONThe worst. Every bad practice is here: premium currencies, premium shop with oddly-priced items, battle pass, "premium" version for anything and everything. It's very in your face, very annoying and Bamco knows it. And it will keep doing it because people will still buy. The in-game shop might not even be safe from game save corruption and people still buy. It's the same with DLCs: pay to play characters, pay to lab their match-up, pay to play on a stage, buy this, buy that, etc.ADVERTISINGWhen it's not pushing aggressive monetization, Bamco pushes ads for their collabs. I'm almost convinced we got a Times Square stage just so that we can get the joy of real-life ads during matches. People at Bamco say it's to fund the game, but it still feels so cynical to milk your audience for all their worth.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it bangin?YesThere is no fighting game I have played that has captured me like Tekken 8 has. From the beautiful character models and animations to its fast paced offense focused gameplay, Tekken 8 has taught me self improvement in its systems and I have taken those methodologies into other games and aspects of my life. This is my favorite fighting game of all time (excluding smash ultimate but that gets its own tier). The online in my opinion is very consistent and out of 700-800 matches I have only been disconnected a handful of times, but I am on a wired connection so mileage may vary. The core gameplay is simply fantastic and as someone with minimal Tekken experience, but plenty of fighting game experience, it is so so so much fun.Microtransactions?YesThere is no game I have seen that has a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ battle pass than this. Absolutely terrible avatar cosmetics that will never be used and 3-4 decent character cosmetics in a 60 double tiered battle pass. The final reward is literally just the female version of a male cosmetic thats already in the game and the majority of the cosmetics are from Tekken 7. Very disappointing, but hopefully with more time they can make the next one not complete ♥♥♥♥.Steam deck?YesYou definitely need to turn the graphics down to low-medium range to get a consistent 60 fps, but I have been able to take my steam deck with me to campus or the laundromat and learn combos on the fly. I have only tried online matches a handful of times and they were okay but I wouldn't recommend it being your primary way of playing online.TL:DRThe game is phenomenal with great gameplay and characters but has the worst battlepass of literally any game I have ever played. If you buy the game do not support the battlepass in any way. Just enjoy the learning process and watch yourself improve as you climb the ranks. Also steam deck is pretty chill on low settings.

_childDocuments_.review: As the 8th iteration in a fighting game series with no previous cargo truck simulation titles, Tekken 8 is quite a surprising but refreshing twist in the development of the franchise. It seems crazy at first but what the game designers at NAMCO did is truly genius! The creativity required for this level of cross genre mashup is beyond my cognitive grasp, but I will try to express my feelings at least. Each round the players take each other on a frenetic, dopamine/cortisol infused race, where the goal is to unload the cargo before the opponent and bury him in it before the the same is done to him. The game is balanced by the capacity of each players truck and the speed and fluidity of the unloading system. A must try for all genre mesh-up fans.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: DO NOT BUY THIS GAME AT FULL PRICE, EXTREMELY GREEDY MONITIZATION PRACTICES FOR A $70 GAME.This game is priced at $70, yet it’s riddled with microtransactions, similar to free-to-play games like Fortnite. It feels especially frustrating for a full-priced game to adopt such a monetization strategy. On top of that, they’ve begun charging separately for content that was previously bundled together. For example, the stage that was released alongside the Heihachi DLC is now being sold separately. In the past, when you purchased a DLC character, the corresponding stage would be included. This change feels like a clear attempt to exploit the popularity of Heihachi by charging more for content that was once part of the package.The decision to split the character and stage into different purchases reflects a shift towards a more profit-driven approach, prioritizing short-term gains over long-term player satisfaction. It's disappointing to see a beloved franchise adopt these tactics, especially when the upfront cost is already so high. The overall direction feels greedy and anti-consumer. I strongly recommend against buying this game at full price—wait for a sale or until they address these issues.

_childDocuments_.review: The perfect example of a textbook fighting game. Each character has their own style that suits how you want to play and has so much detail and variety in each of their movesets, it can take years to master just one character. And although it may be off putting to be annihilated, playing and learning more about your character and what they are capable of makes losing feel rewarding. The game also offers tips and punishes in the replay mode which should be a staple in any fighting game going forward.The game is most definitely not beginner friendly. If this is your first Tekken game (as it is mine) you will need to be labbing combos etc for hours and hours a day to keep up with players. That being said, there are options for new players such as auto combos and also a really good story mode for those who are looking for more casual play.Customization options are completely unmatched. Unlike other games (sf6) you can change almost every aspect of your playable character in game to make them look however you like. This results in moments where you load into a game to find our your matched against ninja or optimus prime.Tekken 8 is huge for fighting games. Content wise and gameplay wise, it completely puts Mortal Kombat 1 in the bin and it is a huge competitor to Street Fighter 6, if not, already better on launch.Cons:- Tekken 8 graphics are very very good. Issue with this, is that it can be hard to run at times. There are good graphic options but a fighting game needs to be run at a solid 60 fps AT ALL times to maintain competitive fairness. This is due to attacks and punishes being based on frame start ups etc, so when you play the game for the first time on ultra settings and you get an fps drop, this could lead to an entire round lost.- With the addition of crossplay, you may have console players playing using wifi, although this is fine most the time, this can lead to unplayable matches. Rollback netcode doesnt fix everything, and when a player is using terrible wifi, your match will be slowed down into a slo mo fight which is just horrible to play. However, the game does tell you if your opponent is using wifi before matching with them. - The Tekken lounge is a cool addition and feels like a bit of a quickly added in thing to match street fighters hub. Things to do in the Tekken lounge are quite limited and does feel a bit pointless for the most part.9.5/10
