_childDocuments_.review: Tekken has deteriorated rapidly from what it once was. A game of classic fighting has gone down  the road of entertaining those who cannot stand 0.3 seconds without dopamine which is provided with easy inputs and strong and easy comeback mechanics. Gameplay flaws-It forces you to be on the constant aggressive where a select few characters are undoubtedly stronger than the rest of the cast which encourages said audience to play them. Defense, which is admittedly one of the harder qualities to master is no longer needed as even if the opponent were to block, some characters have insane chip damage + frame advantage, there is very little counter play. Side stepping is also busted and does not work on 70% of the cast since tracking of many characters moves is completely busted while others are disproportionately disadvantaged. As a result of said comeback mechanics, it offers poor level knowledge + game-play to get to outrages levels of ranks which are not proof of their real skill of the game. With two very strong comeback inputs, you can very much delete 90% of the opponents health. Tekken 7 was poor, but tekken 8 takes the cake. People often favour characters who are 50-50 on aggression. The counterplay is guesss correctly or lose half your health. Again, counterplay such as side stepping which would, depending on match up, be a good counterplay measure. But again, no longer works.  That last true tekken worth playing is Tekken 6. It will take you 1000 + hours to counter this degree of comeback spam that you would have to invest heavily into the game to get past such gameplay. I miss Tekken for what it once was, this certainly isn't it. Microtransactions and Roster: Dont get me started on the microtransaction-pathway the publishers are going down. They have sold out. You would have to pay to get outfits that they are recycling from previous games which you once would unlock simply from playing matches. Half of the cast aren't used due to imbalances in match ups. They for whatever reason prefer to release 20 characters on release and purposely add later characters at a premium cost to use. You cannot play them without buying them-- even if you wished to learn more about them in offline practice mode.... therefore unable to learn how they are used/played to counter them. Its  a pay to win scheme upon character release. New characters are much stronger than the rest of the cast... of course... its a selling point.  Previous tekken games would give you a much wider selection of characters to use upon release. For example: Tekken Tag 2 had 53+ characters.. + another 6 that were free to download.. Online Matchmaking:Most people 'plug' on loss which means the win you so rightfully deserve is invalidated as the opponent purposely disconnects their computer to void the loss. They are not punished for this and as a result, is a common occurance. People with a clean-looking record before matching will purposely do this on a promotion match just out of spite. I had it on countless occasions.  The number of ranks has decreased, meaning people or more squished together. Therefore, there is less consistency of the level of people you match up against. Strong players are able to climb the ranks on newly played characters and walk through those who aren't at their level. Once they reach a certain rank, they will repeat it. So if you're not playing at Tekken King Rank (Top 0.21%) you wont progress. The number of players doing this are rampant. please visit this Reddit Link for rank distribution:Long time tekken players such as myself are no longer playing. If you want little work + high reward, this is your game. If you want to play something that is a testament of skill, i recommend going down a different fighting game lineage. Such as Dead or Alive or Street Fighter.

_childDocuments_.review: tekken has always been the hardest fighting game and tekken 8 is no different.i am here to enjoy that learning experience as i have with the other tekken games. however, this game to me never feels rewarding and is far too stressful to play for any meaningful amount of time in one sitting. this is a huge problem in a game as complex as tekken, in such a game, you want the player to spend long amounts of time learning in each sitting but due to the core systems in place within this game and the lack of infinite rematch the players including myself no matter how hard i try struggle to be motivated to learn nearly as much as with previous games (this obviously excludes pro players and content creators).As with all other previous tekken games i can get my arse handed to me and still enjoy myself get demoted several ranks even and still enjoy myself but this game truly feels so dense, every character feels the same for most of the round due to heat which ironically was intended to boost character personality and while i see character archetypes boosted during heat i ultimately feel (due to heat smash and dash that which are the core components to heat) that all characters feel overly oppressive, doubly so due to chip damage. Personally i would like heat if heat smash and heat dash did not exist and the game design was focused around using heat to boost characters specialities which is what i thought heat was being sold to us as before release.to summarise, the game simply is not fun at least for me to learn and i suffer major burn out which is what i have never experienced with any prior tekken game, tekken has always been complex and tekken 8 would have inherently been a complex game due to characters being more specialised and the natural tekken charm of an increased movelist each game. But adding heat has made characters homogeneous for a significant portion of each round whilst adding to the complexity of the game.possible solutions- (likely) tone down heat in bits over the entire lifespan of the game- (hopefully) make heat once per match as opposed to once per round- (i wish) remove heat dash & heat smash

Whether I was playing online matches or attempting to enjoy the single-player modes, the lag persisted, creating an infuriating gameplay environment.The constant lag not only hindered my ability to fully immerse myself in the game but also made it challenging to compete against opponents effectively. It's disheartening to see such a fundamental aspect of the game, like server stability, fall short, ultimately detracting from the overall experience.Despite Tekken 8 boasting impressive graphics, diverse character roster, and engaging gameplay mechanics, the persistent server issues overshadow these positive aspects, leaving me deeply disappointed. Until the server performance is improved and the lag is addressed, I cannot recommend Tekken 8 to fellow gamers who value a smooth and enjoyable gaming experience.In conclusion, Tekken 8's potential is marred by its subpar server performance, resulting in a frustrating and ultimately unsatisfying gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Tekken used to be fun.Now it's devolved into this sad shell which is merely a mirror of corporate greed, the former spirit and vision of the game is now completely gone.They've added ingame shop for a fighting game months after release as well as a battle pass. Battle pass in a fighting game. It's full of skins for your avatar, which are completely useless, who even goes into the online avatar lobby? I've never been there. I played fighting games for their flow, difficulty and fun of them, not for customizing my online avatar and showing off.The story is completely pointless. Previous iterations of the game except for T7 used to have an okay and at least slightly interesting story. The character endings in T8 also feel completely void of heart, like they just animated something for the sake of each character having a short video.The customization is super lack-luster, they have stripped roughly 50-75% of previous game's outfits and items, likely to add them into the item shop later. They're also severely cracking down on modders - why? It's what made the game fun, having custom titles and more visuals, or adjusting the stages to your liking - the lighting on some of them can get annoying as you can barely see the characters if their outfit has a matching color.As previously, the game is riddled with pluggers and bad connections, for whatever reason they are not banned though? I am forced to play against people with 2-4% disconnection rates because nobody has lower  rates than that. I've even seen 14% disconnection rate trying to match me several times, why are these people not banned?There are also people who have 4-5 bars of connection and the game plays at super slow motion with them, you literally can't even input a string of three buttons because you'd have to delay each button by a second, give or take.But the worst offense is the way the actual fighting has turned out to be - I personally thought a little more agression would be okay, however the game plays completely different now. It's no longer about how do I open this guy up, or how do I fish for a counter hit. It's how do I make this guy stop pressing buttons, when do I press at all? It feels like almost every move leaves people on plus frames. Plus they added the dumb heat smash moves, where each character has several variations, all of them of course leaving you crushed, so if you hated rage arts, now there are two of them essentially.And lastly the biggest gripe I have with this game - execution used to feel rewarding. Now that the game is more accessible, it's extremely dumbed down. You had to work for combos that dealt more than 75 damage, you had to practice for hours, learn the optimal combos and everything. Now every character can do 90 or more in an OPEN SPACE with no walls just with their heat. This has also killed some uniqueness of characters - remember how Lars or Dragunov could do wall to wall on really long stages? Now almost every character can do that. Now every character can pull off at least 130 damage combos without rage art, just with the silly wall quirks and bounds. And of course, everything is obviously very unbalanced. King can literally take a third of your health with a single grab that you cannot tech - because counter-grabs are a thing now. Nina can shoot at you? Victor also shoots at you. Devil Jin has projectile chains that lead into serious damage combos. Every other character has some stupid power up that glows below their health bar. Kazuya and Devil Jin have a plethora of laser ranged attacks that are viable. Victor's and Yoshi's sword hits do like 25% of your full health bar damage on natural hit, and they also deal insane chip damage - and yoshi also heals on hit with that, because why not. I thought we'd leave all this 2D bs behind in T7, but it's only gotten worse. I miss Tekken, this isn't Tekken. It's a glorified mash-fest made accessible to as many people as possible pumped full of micro-transactions to appease the newer generations.For clarification, I was a Tekken Emperor in T7 and got to blue ranks under 25 hours of playtime in T8, so I'd like to imagine my points are a little valid.

_childDocuments_.review: TEKKEN 8 is a total package worthy of being at the top of its series, if not in the fighting games genre overall.The game comes with a plethora of modes for players of all kinds to experience and enjoy.The conclusion to the epic Mishima saga is set in this game's story mode, which has been going on for so long and it's a roller coaster of a ride (quite literally!). Jin is the main focus here, and if you're a fan of Jin in particular you'll be quite happy. I think the story mode is made for the fans to enjoy because of all the touches and (tasteful) fan service scattered in. Cutscenes are animated nicely and they made real good use of the soundtrack (more on that later).The Arcade Quest mode is also catered to single player minded players which can be a great tool to teach them TEKKEN basics while having fun simulating playing at arcades. It is very well done and nicely thought out, effectively gamifying the learning process.TEKKEN Ball is back since TEKKEN 3 but they added some more modern gameplay elements to it to keep up with the gameplay changes in this game which is nice. You can play online with friends as well.The customization is really good. You can unlock items from Arcade Quest as well, which is a nice incentive to make progress there. You'll find a lot of creative ideas implemented by players everywhere and you can take your design online to show everyone your creativity.The online experience is a mixed bag. I like the idea of the lobby system which makes it fun to roam around and have conversations with players in the chat. You can also type in your language in the chat which is super nice. As for the matchmaking it takes a while to find a match sometimes. Not sure if it's how the algorithm is written but it's inconsistent. A rework could be needed to help improve reliability. Also netcode is good except for when the connection is not stable. Other games tend to rollback much smoother than this game, but I personally had more good connections than bad ones. It helps that the game indicates if the opponent is on WiFi or is having performance issues. Crossplay also works which is great to have on day one.JUKEBOX! The feature is implemented very well, you can create playlists featuring your favorite music from all previous TEKKEN games as well and have them play over any stage or even change the character select theme. Practice mode is awesome and fully featured. You can also use the replay feature to watch your replays and take control at any point to help you learn from mistakes or try to recreate situations you had in a fight as a really awesome learning tool.Graphically the game is a big upgrade from TEKKEN 7. Character models were recreated with more detail and better textures. Stages look beautiful, down to the lighting. Sound effects in general are great, most have been replaced with new ones and they sound punchy. I like them a lot.Mechanically I like the new Heat system changes. It adds a new layer of oppression, which is the general theme of the game thus far, and it allows the aggressor to keep pressuring. There will be a learning curve in the mid to high levels on how to deal with this sudden pressure for the duration of the Heat Gauge and especially that TEKKEN now has chip damage. With that being said, combat feels exciting, looks great even while spectating. I am sure the team will keep the game alive with balance patches every season to keep things feeling fresh.The launch characters have a nice selection of fan favorites along with some new faces like Victor, Reina and Azucena. They are very cool additions to the roster and if that's the kind of quality they're aiming for I can't wait to see the DLC characters in the future. No complaints here.Overall, I think this game deserves to be on the top of the franchise. The mix of content found is made with love and aimed at every type of gamer. Competitively it seems to be the most exciting TEKKEN has been for me in years, and hopefully with more years to come as they've shown with TEKKEN 7's lifespan.Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're an actual Tekken fan, Do Not Buy!  What Tekken 8 makes up for in graphical fidelity, it sorely lacks in fluidity and strategy.  Be prepared to be bombarded with animations that take you out of the fight and gameplay, while the camera focuses on either you or your opponents face every 5 seconds!  (during every pvp, online player or ranked match!)  Tekken 8 is a hybrid of all the worst aspects of fighting games these days.Just under 60 hours worth of gameplay, unlocked everything, completed all modes, played online, got my favorite character to Mighty Ruler, and unfortunately, I've lost interest.  I'm no Tekken pro, however, I can hold my own and enjoy a good online fighter.I've owned, completed, and enjoyed all of the Tekken games that have come out.  Tekken 1 thru 8, and Tekken Tag Tournament 1 and 2.  While Tekken 8 is a decent fighter, and perhaps beginner friendly, this particular Tekken installment is much more of a button masher and rewards spamming far more than any Tekken before it.  It's odd really.  There is a fundamental layer of Tekken-gameplay underneath the nice new graphics, but the technical aspects of Tekken 8 seem to have taken a step backwards.  T8 does encourage a more aggressive playstyle, but also slips up in it's precision, accuracy, and execution.   Character Hit-boxes are all over the map, and moves that should have whiffed end up landing (both for and against you).  It's quite jarring considering the controls and gameplay felt much tighter in Tekken 7 *(after numerous updates of course)*.  I personally believe that Tekken 5 (Dark Resurrection) was the height of the series, and while I've always curbed my expectations with regards to sequels, Tekken 8 is a looker, but lacks the precision and polish of the past three games in the series.  The lack of precise attacking and hitting makes the overall gameplay more frustrating than fun.  This is coming from someone who used to enjoy the learning curve of distancing, dodging, and counter-attacking.  Unfortunately, it seems as though every single character in the game is affected by this lack of precision this time around.  I know it's not just me who thinks this either, because a few other regular Tekken players I've played with have noticed this as well.Anyway, aside from all of that, here's what Tekken 8 has to offer:- A Cringe worthy Story Mode  (Tekken fans know what they're getting here)- An episodic Mode where you get an intro and ending Cutscene for each Character (better than Story Mode).- Tekken Ball (Actually an interesting, if a little basic, game of Pong using characters and their movesets)- Arcade Mode (It's Arcade Mode... does what it says)- Arcade "QUEST" Mode (a mode with another story that seems to be geared toward 3rd grade children. (!?!)- Super Ghost Battle Mode (Probably the most interesting new addition of Tekken 8)- Online Player and Ranked Matches (connection quality seems to be better, but the spammy gameplay and hits that land, when indeed they shouldn't have, seems to be worse).- Online Lounge (Where you can take your silly looking character Avatar and...  hang out).- A LOT of missing characters.  Expect a Plethora of future DLC!- Last but not least, a downgrade in character customization.  Not a big deal, but people should know.  (UPDATE: Less than a month after release, all kinds of Pay For customizations are released.  I have over 67 Million Gold in game now with nowhere left to spend it...  bought all the customizations that don't cost real money in the game, what now?  Good Job Namco!)I get it, this Tekken was made mostly for newcomers to the series.  I wouldn't say that the gameplay excludes Long-Time Tekken fans, but it certainly does feel like the series has forgotten its roots.  It's by no means a bad fighting game, but as far as gameplay goes, it just does not feel as tightly controlled or as rewarding as Tekken 4, 5, 6, 7, or even TTT2.  That's my opinion though.Normally I'd put a few hundred hours into any new Tekken that I pick up.  However, at just over 50 hours and after completing everything the game has to offer, with regards to Story, Arcade, Ghost Battle, Collectibles, and Achievements, I've pretty much had my fill.  The online play, which is normally where I'd spend a few hundred hours has actually made me want to go back to Tekken 7.   I personally can't recommend Tekken 8 based on the fact that it has lost some of the refinement that made all of it's predecessors control and play so well.  Seriously, those magical homing hits that reach an opponent when they actually should have whiffed, ruin this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Tekken 8, the latest installment in the legendary fighting game franchise, delivers an exhilarating experience that surpasses its predecessors in every aspect. As a fervent fan of the series, I found myself utterly captivated by the seamless blend of stunning visuals, refined gameplay mechanics, and diverse character roster.Visually, Tekken 8 is a masterpiece. The graphics are nothing short of breathtaking, with meticulously crafted character models, vibrant environments, and fluid animations that breathe life into every punch, kick, and combo. From bustling urban arenas to serene traditional dojos, each stage is a visual feast that adds depth and immersion to every match.Gameplay-wise, Tekken 8 strikes a perfect balance between accessibility and depth. Whether you're a seasoned veteran or a newcomer to the series, the game offers a variety of modes and tutorials to suit every skill level. The controls are responsive and intuitive, allowing players to execute complex moves and combos with precision and fluidity. The addition of new mechanics and techniques further enhances the strategic depth of combat, ensuring that every match is a thrilling test of skill and reflexes.One of the highlights of Tekken 8 is its diverse roster of characters, each with their own unique fighting style and personality. From iconic veterans like Jin Kazama and Kazuya Mishima to fresh faces like Yumi and Akio, there's a fighter for every playstyle and preference. The inclusion of guest characters from other franchises adds an extra layer of excitement and unpredictability to the roster, ensuring that every matchup feels fresh and exhilarating.In addition to its stellar gameplay and presentation, Tekken 8 boasts a wealth of content that will keep players engaged for hours on end. From engaging story modes and challenging arcade ladders to robust online multiplayer and customizable tournaments, there's no shortage of ways to enjoy the game's thrilling combat and competitive spirit.Overall, Tekken 8 is a triumph of fighting excellence that exceeds all expectations. With its stunning visuals, refined gameplay mechanics, diverse character roster, and wealth of content, it sets a new standard for the fighting game genre and cements its place as a timeless classic. Whether you're a longtime fan or a newcomer to the series, Tekken 8 is an experience not to be missed.

_childDocuments_.review: So I am not really one to leave reviews on games unless I really enjoy them or there are heavy issues that need addressing. This is a mix of both. I can't really say I hate it, but I can't say I enjoy it fully either. I am fairly new to the Tekken scene, this is my first Tekken game where I actively participate in online matches and events, so bare with me. I know I am not a die-hard vet of this franchise but I do enjoy a good fighting game whenever I pick one up.With that in mind, this game is made easily accessible for newcomers, like me, and has a pretty good tutorial to get you going. I main King, now chill TF out before you start throwing shade my way and give me a chance to explain plz, and I use him mainly for his simplified moves and flare of his character, I am in Tenryu at the moment as well with him. I'm more of a brawler-type than a grappler when I play him, because his chain throws are very hard to pull off, especially when there are numerous guides on how to easily break them, so it makes each match and opponent feel like a puzzle to solve that can either be exhilarating or ♥♥♥♥♥♥ when going against Lilli's, Xiaoyu's, Zafina's, or Jun's imo. At that point it's just you trying to figure out how to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hit them when all they do is dance around the arena and dodge all your attacks by doing that stupid crawl or duck-like movement. Breaking your knowledge of what you built up to that point when playing the game.I had a fun time with this game, that is until the game literally breaks itself with it's glitches or frame advantaged characters. I can't begin to tell you how many times this game mis-inputs or an opponent dodges with the absurd hit boxes in this game. You can either be too far or their frames are better than yours so they dodge a hit that clearly touches them, or you get launched due to them grazing you by a hair strand. It will then turn into a clown-game where your ass gets juggled to oblivion until all you HP is reduced to zero. Then, it's the spamming of chain combos whenever you go up against Reina's, Xiaoyu's, or Lilli's and then it's just never your turn when they get you with their long reaches from their kicks, etc. Don't even get me started on Victor or Eddy. Of course there is the fight pass as well, which I don't understand why you don't get that for free when you purchase the Ultimate Edition, it's just beyond me at that point and just corporate greed ruining another game which is the new norm.Overall, this game is great, I have a good time when facing new opponents and their style of fighting in this game, but when you face a player that literally uses the same combo as the previous player, then it just becomes repetitive at that point. I enjoy the competitive community, but I don't like the cesspool of constant toxicity when it comes to criticizing the flaws of this game. They then proceed to say "git gud" or "choose another character" or some ♥♥♥♥. There are a few moments when it's just good fun but too many moments where the player base is just toxic. This game needs some serious balancing and tweaks to make it a little bit more balanced, and not a juggling game. There are too many characters with movesets that break the game and though the game is good at introducing you to the world of Tekken, the skill ceiling is just too high for people that are just checking it out for themselves, that not even the "Special Style" can help ease the pain of seeing your ass go flying after getting hit with that Mishima uppercut. Again, this is just my two cents, I still very much enjoy this game, and I will continue to keep playing so that I can improve, but I am not sure if I would recommend this game to the casual fighting gamer, unless they are willing to spend hours getting their asses handed to them by the frames and unbalanced game play.EDIT: Side stepping just does not work. At all. You can dodge perfectly but they still get you by a pube hair. I apologize if I sound like I am just complaining about everything in this game, but cmon man.The misinputs are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying. I feel like I am fighting the game, not the opponents.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying I haven't played online due to Fatal Errors. However. I will add my thoughts once everything is good!From the days in 1995 to run down the hill to pop quarters in the machine at the pizza shop, to getting this as one of my first games on PlayStation 1 for Christmas the same year. Tekken has always been in my top 5 in fighting games. The clash of fist, heaviness of kicks, and the rumbling of throws have made this a mainstay for most of us in the FGC. Fast forward to 2024, and Tekken 8 has graced us with its presence, proving once again that the Mishima family dysfunction is the gift that keeps on giving.Graphics: 10/10 - Seriously, Just Take My Eyes!Tekken 8 is a visual feast – it's so stunning that even your character's jaw would drop if it could. From the flawless character models to the mesmerizing stages, the attention to detail is like a meticulously crafted sushi roll. Perfection.Story: 15/10 -  Jin's Daddy Issues - The Sequel We Needed!I cant give too much without spoiling the story. However, I can say that this game is a love letter for us Jin fans. Finally, our brooding protagonist takes center stage, dealing with more Daddy issues than a therapist on speed dial. However there is more growth in his character beyond that as well as a journey to redemption. The story kept me wondering what happens next. It also made me need Tekken 9 ASAP! final battle? Oh, it's like a chef's kiss via kick to the jaw but with added drama and martial arts action.Gameplay: 9/10 - Punch, Kick (its all in the mind), and Unleash the Pandemonium!As always there is your traditional Tekken style gameplay with you left and right punch/kick buttons. A new addition is new Special Style mechanic which you can change on the fly. This is similar to the modern controls in Street Fighter 6. When active you have buttons for specialty moves, air combos, power crush, low attacks, and Heat Smash. This feature will make it easy to play with those who want to play but are into fighting games or that little cousin that comes over who uses the 3rd party Mad Catz controller (Bonus points if you know the one). Rage Arts make a return which are the amazing super moves that only activate during low health. They are gorgeous to see and very powerful. In addition to Rage Arts, Tekken 8 introduces the new Heat Smash feature which is the successor to Rage Arts. Think of it like a baby version that you can use when needed. Heat allows you to unlock new moves, do chip damage, extend combos, and heal some health. It utilizes the Heat Gauge which allows up to 3 uses, but once its depleted you can no longer use it that round. Another decent feature is the Arcade Quest mode which allows you to learn your characters while pushing the difficulty up bit by bit. Training mode has combo challenges, punishment training, and save states which allows you to play out certain scenarios to learn how to best deal with them.Music: 10/10 -Beats as Strong as a Roundhouse Kick!The soundtrack of Tekken 8 is a musical journey that rivals a mixtape made by a DJ with a black belt.  Menu music sucked me in as much as the piano music from 7. The Character Select Theme took me for a ride like MVC2. Arena and Yakushima are two of the best. Pave your Path is another good one! There were many throwbacks thrown in as well like Snow Castle from Tekken 5 DR. You can also choose which music to set for the game in the jukebox menu which is a nice thing to have.Conclusion: Tekken 8 - A Knockout, Literally!Don’t just walk, run! Tekken 8 is a masterpiece that demands to be in your gaming collection. If you spot a friend playing, don’t be shy – demand a tag-in, even if it means using Parsec for remote play. And hey, if you have a fighting game fanatic in your life, surprise them with Tekken 8 - it's the gift that keeps the punches rolling and brings fire to old rivalries. This is a must-buy for Tekken fans and a definite addition to the FGC. Embrace the chaos, and let the Mishima drama unfold in all its glory!

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun for a while, but the more I learn about the new way of playing Tekken the less I like it. They seem to have surgically removed most of the prior games sources of accomplishment, the worst of which is probably easy slides and simplified dss for Law, but there's just a ton of these dumbing down changes. The heat system is fine as a concept, but paired with damage on block and rage art it's just too much stuff. Most of the battles are more animations, resets and counters, burning meter for advantage and free mixups than actual "proper gameplay". It really feels like someone decided Tekken needs a new direction and steamrolled through with all these changes without stopping at each one to see if they actually are an improvement. Some of the changes are good though, particularly the new backdash speed that helps new players out a lot that were limited to moving with sement bolted to their feet in the past. Also the added frames on whiff.The former games had a really good thing for them in terms of progression. With Law as a prime example, he was infuriating to deal with as a new player with his flips and sweeps, so the player has to learn to deal with and be rewarded by wins and a feeling of accomplishment. Good Law players were also infuriating to deal with, not because of sweeps and flips that is easy to deal with that experience but because of dss, which is a hard thing to master but really hard to deal with for the opponent if used well. It's a perfect balance. In T8 new players can do easymode dss and new players has to deal with both flips, sweeps and dss, which they do by just burning meter and rage arts; an unfullfilling win or infuriating loss.Kazuya is the same, scrub kazuyas are linear, unsafe and simple to deal with, but good Kazuyas can incorporate good movement to negate the downsides. Now he has safe mids, good tracking and easy execution electrics in exchange for meter, and so is really just another Jin, or Dragunov, or whoever, there's very little difference beetween character in this game as they decided to fill up everyones weaknesses, so everyone plays the same; a steamroller hoping to steamroll steamrollier than the other steamroller. Even Ling steamrolls, wtf?Outside of that the game is terrific. Animations are way better looking, practice mode is great, ft3 mode in ranked is great though I miss a function to invite a player to play in casual directly from the win/loose screen.

_childDocuments_.review: I say this not just as someone dissuading you from playing Tekken 8 but from the entire fighting game genre. If you've been thinking of trying a modern fighting game just realize that the good days are gone. _childDocuments_.review: I've never been a huge fighting game fan. There's something about SF, MK, and others that have never really jived with me. But I've always loved Tekken and Soul Calibur. There's something about their combat that I have always loved. It's the same thing here for 8. The fighting is as fun as ever for me, and the story mode is ridiculous in such a fun way. Looking at it compared to past games though, and I can't help but feel like this game was purposefully made worse for profits. There was such a small number of cosmetics at release, and a month later, it became clear that this was on purpose so Namco could sell those skins later. They've released some old costumes from past games, and it's $4 for each character. Plus a $10 dollar battle pass that ends up having a couple of interesting things in it, but that is about 5% of the total content. They tried arguing that they need all the extra money because of the updated graphics and their fight lounge. This game is 100 GBs, 40 more than 7. The fight lounge is a 3D server meant to facilitate a couple different online fight modes. Both are pretty pointless in my opinion. The game does look great, but I have never been one to think that graphics add anything too substantial. Not to mention the other games I've seen with this level of graphics which are not nearly this size, and I just can't believe that it's all necessary. The fight lounge is cool, but it's essentially just a way to try and make menuing seem less boring. Plus the 3D avatars almost definitely meant just to sell more cosmetics. (You can dress up your avatar just like Xiaoyu, just 4 bucks.) Then there's the fact that a single dlc character is 8 dollars. A dlc character that came out a little more than a month after release which just reinforces to me that he could've been in the game, but they wanted to sell him for the extra money. This is a great game saddled down with every single method they could think of to bleed more of your money out of you. Don't let them do it.

_childDocuments_.review: Here is an honest review from someone that only cares about the player vs player experience, the game is really good, best Tekken overall for me ,do not listen to the haters and just try it for yourself. Let me explain the pros and cons:PROS:It improved lots of bad things from tekken 7 in terms of gameplay, in 7 every character had very good counter hit tools and basically the optimal gameplay was to defend backdashing, do safe pokes and try to land the counterhit, and every character played like this. In 8 they fixed this by removing a lot of universal counter hit tools and also its a more aggresive game thanks to nerfing backdash and the heat system.It also removed completly death combos from the game and I feel like it doesn't have characters as broken as tekken 7 had.Character designs, Instant rematching, loading times, access to replays with integrated tips, graphics, online conectivity and so on are excellent.CONS:Bandai Namco implemented an online store, battle pass and all the monetization practices you can imagine, it doesn't give you any advantage in terms of gameplay since everything is cosmetic but this is the reason why the customisation of tekken 8 is the worst until now. I guess this are the current practices in the industry to monetise an online game and I dont really mind it, I just don't buy any skin in any game but i don't see the problem in doing so.Season Pass: They sell a season pass that includes the 4 character they are going to release over the next season which last one year. Its fine for me until this point, what I don't really like is that this doesn't include the new stages, you will have to buy the stages a part. To me feels like they trying to milk every euro they can from us, personally I'm not going to buy any stage and I encourage you to do the same in order to vote with your wallet and make them reconsider this strategy.I think you cannot see the replays if you don't own one of the characters in the replay, and in addition to this you cannot use those characters in practice mode in order to learn how to fight against them. Even though I think is perfectly possible to enjoy the game without this I also think this is a ♥♥♥♥ practice and i don't see any reason to not make this possible, I don't think this limitations make people buy the characters, on the contrary it just upsets the players and can make them quit or not wanting to play the game.Game does't have infinite rematch in quick matches, i get that ranked mode should stay as FT2 but the only way to play long sets with someone is if you invite someone to a lobby or joining public lobbies, i think we desperately need an infinite rematch quickplay option.Game still new and needs some balancing or tweaks in some systems like heat since I feel like sometimes feels to powerfull but Im sure they will work on that during the years and the game will only improve from here and its already quite good.

_childDocuments_.review: I've spent over 300 hours in this game, and have had plenty of time on Tekken 6 and Tekken 7 and was able to play them for years, yet I'm already bored of this game play and I'm going to put it down for a while.Hopefully balance patches will fix this issue in the future, but for now, it's just not it. You have completely busted characters like Feng, Xiaoyu, Jun, Azucena and DJ. While you have other characters who require no knowledge of the fundamentals like Azucena, Alisa, Victor, and Dragunov. It's 2024, there's  reason for this many characters to be brainless and/or overtuned, SF6, KI hell even MK1 doesn't have this many characters were you can play with your brain turned off, it's unacceptable. The developers and directors are trash. Half of the time they communicate with us it's for things that's not even relevant, and they refuse to take actions on things that actually matter. Example time. Again, it's 2024 and not taking actions against pluggers and people who alt+f4 is not only ridiculous, but also stupid. Now the rank system is completely out of whack and we have people who are in purple/blue ranks without even knowing how to  play the game. It makes people not even want to touch ranked, and no, banning one streamer and saying you have an excel sheet doesn't do anything nor does it solve the issue. One time I even saw a reddit post about Tekken 6 punishing pluggers.  How laughable. We've been given two CBT's before the game released, so there's  reason there should be this much imbalance. Especially since most characters were in and half the top tiers were in (Jun, Xiaoyu, Azu, Feng) yet despite the advice from the community, they did nothing for the most part. Before the shop was introduced, Harada tweeted that the team wasn't able to implement old outfits into this game because they "wouldn't look good in today's graphics." Whatever tf that means. Yet a week or two later, we get old outfits like King's Tekken 2 outfit, Xiaoyu's Tekken 4 outfit, and Kazuya's Tekken 4 outfit. This director is a man child. It's clear he doesn't know anything about Tekken and the direction it's going, then he questions why he gets backlash and gets defensive and cries when people don't agree with him, he never aged since elementary school.Tekken has to be the only fg that built their game to be offense only, and boy was it a bad idea. 20% of the time you'll find yourself in a position where you weren't even able to fight back, and thanks to the heat mechanic, you're always forced into a 50/50 and have to eat a potential 80% combo, this is Tekken, combo damage was always high but making it more 50/50 based was bound to be a bad idea. Throw RA's just for the middle finger cherry on top. Whatever though, the devs and directors don't know how to play anyway.You all knew this was coming. There's no excuse for this one, why does a 17 year old game (T6 and TTT2) have better customization? It feels like we're always taking one step forward and two steps back.Again, for the third time,  and the netcode just isn't as good as other fg's that released not too long ago. It's so bad that playing against Wi-Fi players is just impossible. I played last night and tried to play against a 4 bar  Kazuya. Never again. No wonder Tekken tournaments are always offline.The Tekken community honestly has the biggest ego I've ever seen in a fgc. Mfs will pick op characters and go yolo while you're trying out a new character you've clearly never played before. Then they'll ki charge at the end and one and done. It's just baffling, yes there can be toxicity in other fg's but Tekken honestly takes the cake for being the most toxic. She ki-charged and waited for the 10 seconds then left. This sugar mommy has brought out a new evil in people.Yeah, this game has a LOT to fix, and a long way to go at that, I'll be taking a break because I'm just not having fun nor does it feel engaging, and honestly you should too if you feel the same way.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game but there are also reasons not to. If there is a mixed option for a review, I would choose that. This is a Tekken game that is very different and it shows a lot in the gameplay with the added new Heat System. It forces you to be aggressive but at the same time, they nerfed the movement and defense. A very stark contrast from T7 which focuses more on defense and punishing the player's mistakes by having solid fundamentals. T8 gameplay usually falls into poking then who gets into Heat Mode first and then activate the Heat Move. Maybe this only applies into my current rank but that is just the gameplan of everyone I encountered. I was originally a defensive player because I came from T7 but holy hell I get punished for playing that way most of the time. Movement is not the same so sometimes there are moves that jail the hell out of you and then force a 50/50 and this is more prominent when using Heat. I like it but at the same time I wish the transition to this new gameplay was smooth. Movement and Down Parrying were my favorite things in Tekken and it is very sad to see that it has a very little reward now.My second gripe would be the battlepass and the costumes. STOP SHUTTING DOWN THE MODDING COMMUNITY FOR GOD'S SAKE!!! THE BATTLEPASS AND COSTUMES WOULD BE THRIVING IF YOU ARE RELEASING GOOD PRODUCTS. The Battlepass sucks, they just locked some outfits for female and male characters and the costumes are not really worth it since other costumes were FREE FROM THE LAST GAME. I didn't buy any microtransactions because you can see how they wanna milk the players.I recommend this game despite of my gripes because the gameplay is fun. You can play this game with friends and have a great time even if it is not perfect. Maybe I am just optimistic but there still upcoming patches that can change the gameplay and I am very excited for that. Defense Patch is coming soon so I hope that would be a good one. TL;DR: Game is fun but can improve a lot more and it contains rubbish microtransactions for customization items that were free from the previous games.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, pretty bummed out about the whole experience so I am giving this one a thumbs down for now.Technically, it's been a bumpy ride – lots of us are hitting snags with crashes, random disconnects, and just a shaky online experience in general. I've been getting booted out way more than I'm fine with. That alone is a massive bummer, but that's not where the fun ends, sadly. The gameplay balance feels way off, and the character lineup doesn't help. Remember how much flak Rage Drive and Rage Arts caught in T7? Well, T8 decided to throw in this new heat mode system, which honestly feels like it's causing more harm than good – it's making combos drag on forever and hands out beefy attacks like candy, making fights feel less about skill and more about who can hit the big button faster. And don't get me started on some characters being way too strong compared to everyone else. It's like they're playing a whole different game.And if you're trying to bail out of a losing match online by hitting that ALT+F4, guess what? No consequences. Yep, no system to keep quitters in check. Customization's a joke too. Wanted to make your fighter stand out? Good luck with that; options are super limited. The story mode's got some flashy visuals and it's kinda fun in a cheesy B-movie way, but don't expect much from the character stories. They're pretty meh. On the bright side, there's a decent mix of stuff to do, both offline and online – definitely an improvement from T7 there.

_childDocuments_.review: 60-70€ for an alpha/beta test build made by a predatory company. All the "feedback/critique" you give the devs don't matter as they'll do the opposite instead or continue whatever BS they had planned in the first place. I only got ~30 hours on the game due to the unfun nature + MANY issues with the game (excluding local gameplay hours at a friends place, VS mode) but still so few hours despite the game being out for some time now (should speak volumes of it's state). Most "positive" reviews you see the game get are from people who played the game during the "hype" phase. Either that or they are used to Alpha tests :D Jokes aside, it honestly confuses and shocks me to see the game have so many positive reviews.Pros:+ Fun singleplayer story mode (for fans)+ Training mode with lots of options (punishment training, replay etc)Cons: - Limited and poor customization choices compared to previous games.Lots of skins, costumes etc have been removed so that they can sell you it instead. You can also not mix-and-match full-body outfits the way you want with other pieces.The menu is horrible as you have to go through 10 different button clicks and loading screens just to preview an accessory. - Predatory (Content locked behind Paywall etc)70€ price tag yet sells u DLC characters, has an in-game Shop with Microtransations and a Battlepass. The shop btw sells you mostly re-used skins/assets that used to be FREE in Tekken 7 and some older costumes from previous games. They also decided to take down modders since they provided these "skins" for free before the shop was implemented, how else would they sell you the same content? What's funny too is that modded skins are client-sided so it's not the exact same as an actual ingame skin that you get to show-off vs other players... oh well. Oh and some items sold in the shop even have limited uses (such as fireworks ~10 time use). Moving on. You CAN NOT practice / replay-train / punishment-practice vs DLC characters UNLESS you've purchased and own them (this has been a thing since Tekken 7, they never learned). There is NO 600 coins option in the shop to buy the batlepass, you need to buy 500 coins minimum (twice). SCUMMY PRACTICES!- Bad Online / Versus gameplay (optimization, network, player-experience etc).While VS somewhat works, Online however DOES NOT work 70% of the time. Each match is a gamble on whether you'll have a lag-free match or not regardless if it's wifi, wired or 4 to 5-bar connection between you and your opponent. When you do find one, they usually quit mid-match or do not bother rematching having you spend a lot of time in loading screens and playing half matches. Every few other match lags which is intentionally caused by players using steams inbuilt screenshot feature (F12) to lag-switch you or unintentionally cause due to the opponents bad hardware or network connection. Oh and there is no permanent re-match option in-case you do find a decent match.- No Anti-Cheat or Anti-Plug (match leaving) punishment/system for Ranked or Normal online matches. People can cheat, leave a Ranked/online match whenever they want or do anything they want without any punishment at all. INFACT you are the one that gets punished since they DO NOT lose points when leaving a match, instead you get a "loss" or winstreak loss and they get to keep their points. - Dumbed-down Gameplay (Heat mechanic, new/old moves, aggression-gameplay focus aka game direction etc).You'd think they'd surpass Tekken 7s gameplay with new "better" gameplay, yet instead we get something much worse. For each added good change or new good addition to the game comes 10 worse ones introduced. While they did fix a few issues from Tekken 7 such as Side-step (dodging) not working properly. They also added more issues to the game.They claim to want to promote new-player experience and make the game available to everyone no matter the skill, yet the way they approach it is wrong on every front. There is an easy-mode button layout option in the game that has limited options and lots of downsides however it's an option for newer players to use instead of playing traditionally aka the way you're meant to play. BUT for some reason it shows EVERYONE in the match that you are using it, making new players face even more disadvantages and "shame". FEW characters have shortcut inputs to some "hard" moves that deal less damage in return, to help new players execute hard inputs. YET for some reason only VERY FEW characters have this. They clearly didn't know which direction to go when it came to helping new players get into Tekken or fighting games in general, hence leaving you with a bunch of half-assed options. Good luck new players, at least there's training mode haha... NOW let's talk old mechanics and moves. They removed Counter-hit options on many characters (magic 4 etc), nerfed Low-parry damage and few other things, which is fine btw and reasonable. BUT... then for some reason, they decided to buff normal combo/wall damage, LIMIT other gameplay options, and add in two Instant-click 50 damage options to the game. For some reason they removed Rage-drives (combo extender/starter special move) while keeping Rage-arts (one click, 50 dmg special moves) in the game. Most moves have become safer on block (rage arts, heat moves etc) and Rage arts especially got buffed (less -frames on miss/block) which means that you now have less options and weaker ones available if you manage to block one and there's almost no risk to using one now. Hyper armor on top of it almost being a safe move on miss/block = unbalanced and stupid. It's even worse since Rage-drives are gone now, leaving rage-arts as the only option meaning you'll use it almost always.Most moves/grabs track even though they shouldn't even though there are actual tracking moves in the game. Other moves JAIL which leaves you blocking more than evading moves, and moves now do CHIP damage on top of that. This results in harder/less Side-stepping, despite buffs, and other evasive options not being an option most of the time. Blocking now losses you the game.They introduced a new gameplay mechanic called Heat while also focusing on a more aggressive gameplay YET forgot to balance defensive/evasive options and defensive gameplay. Every match is now button mashing at it's finest and one or two 50 dmg (1 click) button spam. Aggression takes over the game as MOST moves and abilities now leave you in +frames, meaning you get to continue pressuring and spamming your opponent with moves while they get to spectate the match as they slowly die.Heat also helps on this front by enhancing your character with stronger versions of their moves/stances with more +frames, more damage, chip etc. While in HEAT you always have a 50 dmg (1-click) button to keep them on their toes and steal the match leaving little to no counterplay or exciting gameplay. Entering heat mode using a heat-engager move also heals you if you connect it, which heals "grey/chipped" health.Because of each of these "changes/additions" the gameplay ends up becoming repetitive, stale, boring and easy (easy in a bad way) as less skill is required, less options are available and things turning out the same almost every match (no variety or exciting different matches). Activate heat, button mash with your super boosted moves while chipping your opponent, hit one or two 50 dmg moves with Heat or Rage art and repeat.Charactes don't matter as much as each one play similarly due to the "new" mechanics forcing aggression down your throat. Weaknesses and strengths of a character don't matter either as each match relies on the same tools, every character is technically a "rushdown" now. It doesn't matter if you are new or a veteran, the gameplay plays similarly for both.3D is the new 2D apparently. Thanks for reading and Cya in 10-20 patches, perhaps the game is fixed by then. One can dream... :(

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:* It's Tekken 7 but prettier, definitely the best-looking current generation fighting game* Story mode is solid, and the character episodes are back to having fully animated CGs* The soundtrack is generally better than T7's* The new gameplay mechanics are addicting as all hell (stage interactions, Heat changes), albeit some characters' Heat mode can be a little too strong* Newcomers are pretty cool design-wise (Reina is without a doubt the best Tekken newcomer in a long time)* Netcode is much better than Tekken 7, but still has a lot of hiccups compared to Street Fighter 6. Crossplay with consoles also ensures that this will have great playerbase health until the next title releases* Arcade Quest is Tekken's first functional foray into new player onboarding and it does a great job at it* 32 characters on launch, there's one character for everyoneAll in all, it's almost a complete package if not for the fact that Miguel is missing from the roster.CONS:* Huge minus for the horrible system of managing pluggers/hackers. Tekken 7 has dealt with this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for years and they've somehow managed to make it worse in T8, what with broken disconnect rate percentages and still no handling for pluggers (if your opponent disconnects while you have a win streak, your win streak will break but your opponent will neither be handed a loss nor point deduction, so basically there's no punishment for leaving).They really, really need to fix the plugging plague. Murray and Harada are too busy faffing around and arguing in bad faith on Twitter without actually doing anything to address this problem.* Ranked system is very frustrating. You lose more points from higher-ranked players compared to losing to players that are lower in rank.* Deducting points for the degenerate design incarnate that are Azucena's WR3,2 and Victor's...everything. Game balance is completely all over the place, given this is Tekken's first multiplatform release without a prior arcade release, but yeah, some characters are absolutely broken. Dragunov, Jun, King, Azucena, Devil Jin, and Xiaoyu are the most ridiculous characters on release* PC version is pretty well-optimized, but since it doesn't force a benchmark test before playing online, bad performance on either side can completely screw matches over if either player is running it on a potato PC, especially since the game is more graphically demanding. Lots of reported PC crashing too.* Tekken Shop is pointless, and now they've added a battle pass to Tekken. They also added it after game release, which is an absolute scummy decision to avoid rating changes and reviews commenting on the microtransactions.* Customization system is a little worse than T7 since full body outfits can't be separated into top/bottom segments and you can't mix and match them, aside from the fact that there are less parts/options than T7Solid 8/10. It's a great game that will probably have long legs thanks to crossplay, as well as better netcode relative to its predecessor. I cannot give it a higher score because it's literally broken (no handling for pluggers, plus the occasional crash and disconnect), and they're monetizing the game as if it was an F2P title. It's scummy to put in microtransactions after release without announcing it beforehand.

However, it's quite obvious that Namco Bandai is not one of them. _childDocuments_.review: I enjoy the game with some caveats. I am ultimately giving this game a thumbs down, but I do plan to still play it regularly. A major bias I have is that I like attending offline tournaments and I happen to live in an area with a very active offline Tekken scene (Southern California). Despite the bias, this review goes over the game as a PRODUCT. I personally have the tolerance level to wait for further balance updates since vanilla releases of fighting games have been insane in the past, BUT it’s important to recognize modern consumer expectations. THE biggest offender is the inclusion of microtransactions. The UX is littered with advertisements for the in-game shop which is such in poor form and downright predatory.This is the first Tekken game to not go through an arcade iteration before its console release. Tekken 8 went straight to console.The game balance is all over the place. At the time of this review (v1.08 patch), tournaments have shown that Dragunov is clearly the strongest character and that some characters’ heat options are better than others.Personal bias - I cannot ignore that a part of me wants to say “just let it rock” until next season. I mean, players of older fighting games had to do that, right? Before the patching era of games. However, to say that on its own is to ignore the fact that standards have drastically changed over the years and the times have changed.We need to ask…how ARE these patches? Some have been really good for the game, such as v1.05, which removed the homing property from command throws and made manual Heat activation (Heat Burst) very linear. Patches like those show that Namco is paying attention to some degree. However, there have been some questionable patches such as:-          v1.03.01: Making Azucena wr3,2 even harder to punish (later fixed), making Lars DEN3 +5 on block (making sidestepping much weaker)-          v1.08: Heihachi patch. When facing Heihachi, Devil Jin’s rage art does NOT remove grey health from Heihachi AND time continues to tick during the rage art cinematic. Again, this is ONLY when Devil Jin is facing Heihachi. I don’t even main Devil Jin and I feel bad.The change to Lars’ DEN3 was made so that SEN1 couldn’t be interrupted with Rage Art. The end result is making Lars having a forced 50/50 and limits the opponents’ ability to sidestep. This was a massive oversight all because of a move, DEN3, that the Lars player doesn’t HAVE to do. It’s not THE worst change ever since DEN3 itself is ultimately a slow move, but what’s more important is what the change represents – the questionable play testing in the Tekken team. Moreover, the rage art bug in v1.08 is especially bad to me – I don’t know how something like that isn’t caught, especially since it revolves around a character, Heihachi, who is the main highlight of the patch!In the end, the player is left with the impression that the Tekken balance team is inconsistent. When it’s a good patch, it can be impressive. When it’s bad, it’s a pretty low valley. It’s hard for consumers to know if the game is heading in a good direction.Not to mention the new Heat system - many Heat scenarios force a 50/50. This wouldn’t be as bad if the risk to activating heat wasn’t so low. Activating manually gives 10s of Heat. If through a Heat Engager, 15s. This 5s difference isn’t enough of a deterrent. At times, it’s not necessary to use all 10s and it’s better to spend Heat immediately. If the player is smart, getting countered with a low/throw when activating manually won’t happen too much either. With Heat being THIS easy to access, and the 5 seconds difference not being enough of a deterrent, Heat is just simply dominant in any given round and feels overtuned.Why do I still plan to play the game then? Because there IS still core Tekken, that being movement, at play. There are still neutral interactions before the heat stuff happens. Sidestepping is more important to this game than Tekken 7. To say heat ALWAYS decides a round is disingenuous but heat undeniably is a major variable. My personal bias still thinks it’ll be alright eventually and I can ride it out. For the average consumer, the time to wait for a new patch may simply not be worth it.I’ve reached the God of Destruction rank, the highest online rank, with Jun. During the journey, there were some undeniable flaws in its system.You get a large point bonus if you win three matches in a row against opponents who are +/- 1 of your rank. Conversely, you receive a large point penalty if you lose three in a row. The idea of point bonuses, especially for the early ranks, is fine. However, this should not be present in the higher ranks. Ranked is a first-to-2 (FT2) in Tekken 8. I actually don’t mind FT2 – it helps me to discern typical FT2 strategies (valuable info for tournaments). It also helps in ensuring that I play multiple opponents who have different playstyles.The problem lies in the reality that in the higher ranks, the pool of players becomes smaller. If I happened to get the same opponent in ranked that I knew how to beat consistently, getting those extra points feels cheap and undeserved. Farming is boring to me because I play to learn, not to farm. If encountering the same player is inevitable in the higher ranks, then the bonuses should be removed to ensure the assigned rank is accurate. If I got the point penalty, to me personally, it was fine because I value the experience. But if the bonuses ever go away, then so should penalties.As a consequence, because of bonuses, I think there are simply not enough ranks in the system. There is rank inflation already. Also, the God of Destruction rank encompasses still a wide spectrum of skill levels.All of this is somewhat of a moot point to people who are purely dedicated to the idea of playing to learn because they’ll keep playing whether they get a bonus or a penalty. Just some stupid game points at the end of the day. The problem is that the ranked system doesn’t encourage players to embrace the idea of liking to lab. Streak bonuses may make players feel like they’re better than they really are (and consequently not lab). Streak penalties may make players frustrated regarding the rank and may encourage them to quit due to the game’s inability to provide an accurate assessment. This is a frustrating point because I think Namco did such an excellent job with the replay system, which is an invaluable tool for learning. Clearly they want people to know how to play the game (and especially evident with the easy-to-understand Heat mechanic), but they just need to foster the online environment that encourages that attitude and demeanor.The cherry on top: a third-party website ( provides a more accurate assessment of someone’s skill level than the in-game rank. Go check it out – it uses a comprehensive ELO system. I take the rating on that website more seriously than I do the rank system in the game. Isn’t it telling that I would rather rely on something outside of the game if I really want to assess where my skill level is at?The game is littered with advertisements and promoting a battle pass. The nickeling and diming is extremely disappointing. The situation with the Heihachi stage is especially bad since the communication was not clear at all. People who bought the Deluxe/Ultimate edition didn’t get the Heihachi stage – what a joke. Namco has since apologized and are offering to have the winter stage be included for Deluxe/Ultimate/Character Pass owners and giving 500 Tekken Coins for everyone. But due to the intense push for microtransactions and random merchandise (through collabs w/ Nike, Gentle Monster, etc), it’s difficult to know if their attempt to be consumer friendly will continue. This section in this review is not as long as the rest, but it is the game's worst offense.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a colossal disappointment, there are severe netcode and balance issues that require urgent adressing. Seems everything that made previous TEKKEN games good has been changed for the worse. This review will only cover core gameplay problems, not gonna discuss TEKKEN 8 business model here, which is unpopular to say the least.TEKKEN 8 is, sorry to say, a laggy, unbalanced, dumbed down spamming festival. - This game forces you to play online, there is nothing to do vs CPU other than a mediocre story which emphasizes 2 characters that much that Ive had enough of them for a lifetime- Half of the online games you play will have enemy connection so bad it will seem like you have 10 FPS and is practically unplayable, even though you will limit your search to best possible connection - Players frequently ragequit towards the end of match when it is becoming obvious they would lose because there is no penalty whatsoever for doing so- Features and game modes like Treasure battle have been removed... why?? in the previous game you had both online rank and Treasure battle rank, here unfortunately you only have online rank, the offline play would keep many players coming back, myself included- The gameplay itself is horribly unbalanced, certain characters have overpowered moves which stun block, take 25%+ health on hit, have extreme range, arent side-steppable because it will still require you to block, and players, of course abuse it massively. Also damage between same type of hits varies, making it that some characters deal twice as much damage for the same key pressed (you can easily see which characters are op by looking at character overall usage charts)- Developers state that this game is all about "aggressiveness", but in practice it has become all about spamming, once someone gets near the wall it will take a damn miracle to get out since you will be constantly spammed by enemy attack, most of which will even block stun you- I once tried button mashing a character that I literally have no clue how to play and dont even care about, got 3 wins out of 5 games by spamming keys - Who in their right mind made "ultimate attacks" and finishers impervious to counter attack, all the player has to do is press ONE KEY and it will ignore all enemy attacks completely, launching an attack that will erase 1/3 of your health, it should be high risk-high reward move, this encourages cowardly gameplay not aggressiveness!- They introduced health regeneration, doing above stated OP moves will on top of everything recover a significant portion of health on hit, yet another tool for noobs that encourages usage of such unbalanced moves- This game reduced the distance between opponents after hit and added new moves like heat smashes which results in you flying for half and hour once launched in the air while the opponent unloads same set of moves over and over again- Moves like chain throws which required speed and correct execution, have again been dumbed down to 1 button mash guessing game, not to mention king now grabs even in air, behind his back, 20 yards away, you get the idea, most of which again take 1/3 of your health - Customization was surprisingly poor compared to tekken 7, but 2 months after release came the answer why, which you can read in almost every other recent review - Maps and music were imo better in TEKKEN 7, luckily you can at least use previous games music and select it for certain stages so lets give this decision a thumbs up - They added and put a lot of attention to in-game avatars that noone asked for or really cares about- Character "episode stories" in the offline section are the copy-paste model of the same mini-tournament consisting of few battles, there are only a few characters who use a different, but yet again copy-paste model, come on people, couldnt the "episodes" have some content in them??CONCLUSION:There is nothing worthwhile to do offline, this game only forces online play, where you will experience lag, frustration over how noob friendly this game has become, spam and more spam, and occasionally egomaniacs who will come and trashtalk on your profile because they lost at their own spam game. All you have to do is launch your opponent in air twice, your opponent can go on vacation in the meantime, come back and he will still be flying in air, and after 2 of such combos game is over. In fact, regardless of the business model behind the battle pass, if it wasnt for the concept it gives, I would have long ago uninstalled this game because there is literally NOTHING to do other than the horrible online experience. And then I get the pass, looking to do some missions to unlock customization items, and what do you know: missions are " play 50 online matches", " win 25 online matches"....I strongly recommend you stay away from this travesty and save your nerves for something worthy.

_childDocuments_.review: Story itself isn't really that interesting, but there's a lot of effort put in it to make it a fun display.  It could have used more matches than five, could get a little harder at the end as it doesn't feel like a real game mode but something to do for casuals. I don't like that idea, I think even casuals would like to overcome some challenge, which would make them more likely to play online. Nevermind that, they could actually advance characters' storylines instead of repeating the same old feuds. So there's not much really new, would absolutely be more fun if you had no idea what Tekken is, I guess. But it's way better than Tekken 7 at the very least. , eight battles that are a lot more challenging, but I don't really see why you would play it again after you've seen it once, especially when there's Super Ghost Battle. Of course they are still not the carbon copy of the player and act slower, but they use similar tactics and make similar mistakes, so it is a very useful tool to break down the opponent's patterns.  Streamlined a lot of characters' game plan, added Heat as a last resort for choking newcomers and turned it into an actual fun mechanic so it isn't a burden on experienced players, the practice mode is great, being able to watch replays is great, you can even take control during a replay to try a different approach, it's really amazing how much thought they put into it.  It still doesn't break down everything, but at least it is character specific and gives you a good idea of what to expect. It's nice if you're someone who never played a fighting game and want to avoid studying a video game. It gives you the basics however it still won't teach you everything about your character, or about actual bastard plays people make in Ranked., while I think the visuals are cluttered and Rage Art cutscenes are annoying because it forces you to watch a customized anime character do a bunch of generic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ whose shameful creator is surely jerking off during that whole minute,  Turtling is not unbeatable anymore. You can sidestep, power crush, throw, and most importantly use explosive moves like King's or Paul's punches to stagger the enemy and put pressure on a blocking player or fish for openings. There's still a lot of times when it feels unfair, like when a character pulls up with something in a confusing mix-up, a trap for you to lower your guard to punish you for a simple jab, and spams that because it's the easy thing to do, but I do not think a fighting game can ever be truly balanced without being boring.

_childDocuments_.review: Tekken 8 is another modern fighting game which unfortunately I need to leave a dislike. The greed just took over the video games companies but it's getting to another level and it's not just Tekken. I remember a times when I could buy a game for 5€ (and even 1€ for a BUNDLE PACK WOOT)... Then for 10€... Then for 20€... Then around 80€ for a video game that has battlepass extra payment and DLC stuff? Sorry but everything has it's limits - and that's my review about the pricing policy... VERY NEGATIVE. However the price is only one piece of cake. Let's talk about the gameplay...The gameplay is similiar to older Tekken series with implementation of some new flashy moves and heat system. The "strategy" was kinda reduced to promote a bit of a more aggresive gameplay. The characters are much more "aggressive" now but their combos are weaker and easier to execute. The great example is the reworked Eddy Gordo. Eddy has the ability now to perform a very high damage combos by pressing only one button meanwhile his gameplay and tactics has been lowered down, he can't lay on the ground anymore, his poke is worse, there is no sense to hold the distance now and he has no "baits" or atleast I didn't found any. Now he is just a close-combat focused spam character like most of the characters in the game right now... But it's not an Eddy review, It's an game review, right? So let me add that most of the characters does looks like that. Just pure close-combat pressure and fight, no variety at all. It can be fun for a while or fun for the beginners (there is even a support-system that does let beginners do the combos with pressing one buttons) but in longer way it's very unfun and it's in general worse to the game than good. The game gets boring quicker because most of the battles looks the same... Cool and flashy but boring.They added too much unecessary things and they took away too many necessary things. The engine is good but there are some unecessary paths that the game went into. Game is focused on close-combat spam rather than KIND OF "strategy" that it used to be in older Tekken games. Beginner-support system aka press one button to do a combo unecessary in my opinion and the game is overpriced plus has some DLC and extra microtransactions like battlepass. The game generally is fine... I mean... It has potential but... There are so many wrong things that could be easily changed for good...4+/10 (honestly very MIXED review rather than NEGATIVE but there is no way to leave a mixed review)

_childDocuments_.review: Game is kinda solid if you forget about the issues with the competitive integrity & the scummy behaviour of developers/publishers (don't know who's the greedy bastard in this scenario). The game is priced around your typical AAA title, which isn't a surprise for such established title. The disingenuous part comes when they announce MTX into the game after the initial hype has ended, so the initial sales aren't hindered. The game has worse customization options than their predecessors, which kinda explains a lot now if you think about it, I wonder where all the work went. The shop itself would be a bearable introduction, $4 for whole customs isn't, in the end, a lot, but the game is infamous for their practices with DLC gatekeeping features. What I personally fear of is that the competitive integrity is not a priority for the developers, as milking money from loyal fanbase is the real purpose, which could lead to FOMO & other psychological manipulation (e.g. making new DLC characters unbalanced to force community to buy them). Tekken shop will offer free stuff aswell - which is gonna be just further advertisment for their partner deals with merch production companies etc., so don't expect any content of any real substance for other than the paid currency (this is dig at the already existing game currency that is completely useless as base customization is lacking).Technically the game is a decent step up, feels smoother & even the netcode seems to be slightly better. Technical design brought improvement with heat system, on the other hand some characters lost a lot of their tools and have been replaced with additions that are in certain scenarios more detrimental - poor/no balancing. Same goes for the bugs that were present since day one and haven't been fixed since. So far we had only one patch with few fixes & balances - a really minor one. Yet we had to deal with so many partner deals/ads and introduction of MTX. Currently the game is, at the competitive level, broken, so if you are looking for competitive game to play, I would advise you not to buy the game yet, or you could end up buying overpriced training tool, where you can't lab against broken DLC characters unless you upgrade your training tool. Perhaps after they milk some more money they will finally finish patching the characters they just skimmed over & solve the plugging issue.
