_childDocuments_.review: i dont know how this gem of a game isnt more popular. it was a joy from start to finish. tight platforming, great art style and music, and all around one of the best 2d platformers i have ever played. huge thanks to the devs on this one, promenade deserves all the praise. buy it and tell your friends. more people need to play this.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truely charming !The overall ambiance is incredibly enjoyable, with each area meticulously designed and uniquely themed yet seamlessly blending into the overall joyful atmosphere. The musics is great, perfectly complementing each environment and significantly enhancing the overall experience.Traversing through young Nemo's imaginary world briefly transported me back to those tender moments when every cloud seemed nothing more than a giant cotton candy.Moreover, the name of the game is a stroke of brilliance; it encapsulates the essence of the experience - a period of time specificly designed to enjoy what is surrounding you without any other aim than simply having a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the best platformers I've ever played, and a truly innovative experience!For casual players, it's a very pleasant ride, and for speedrunners, everything is done to make our task easier, and the challenge is really stimulating.The music is very pleasant, the art direction super refreshing. I really recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: 100% the first world and onto the next... already feel compelled to write a review. Others have already likened it to klonoa but more dynamic, and pointed out how unique the experience is and I must second both of those things. It's a 2d platformer game like you haven't played before, and if you like 2d platformers, puzzle platformers, or 3d platformers then it is a must play. It obviously isn't 3d but follows the design philosophy of 3d platformer collectathons more than it follows the typical 2d platformer design - explore the open levels and collect away! It's an itch I developed since I played a smw rom hack "demo" with a similar idea, and I finally get to scratch it! It really makes me wonder why more 2d platformers haven't explored this type of design
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: I've finished the 4 first level 100% and I really love it so far :)Great work :)EDIT :I've finished a 100% playthought (Still need few steam achivement tho)Honestly as far as platformer goes, close to a masterpiece.Gameplay 10/10- Perfect difficulty scaling, and well brought- The endgame content is very hard, but definitly doable- Extremy accurate input management (when you fail, you know it's your bad)Art: 9/10- Cute DAAudio: 8/10- I love the music- SFX prety nice
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: This game does what good games used to do: gives you a few well-polished core mechanics, then turns you loose in a world to explore and experiment. There's so much to discover here, you'll feel overwhelmed. But the good kind of overwhelmed, as the sense of wonder and excitement at having another nook or cranny to stick your head into never goes away. I'm genuinely impressed by how engaging, charming, and deep this game is.P.S. Steam Deck compatibility is great. I haven't had a single issue.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a while since I've picked up something I'd consider a hidden gem or something I've beaten the algorithm to play (last was probably Helltaker). Sure I've played some less known games before in modern time but I had never seen any discussion of this and seeing the trailer and the reviews on steam being in the double digits, my curiosity was peaked.WI went in thinking would it would be a nice looking Braid equivalent game but the game plays way more like a good translation of a 3D platformer collectathon onto the 2D plane. A while I was slightly worried at the beginning the controls would be stiff, they really become quite fluid and the slow walk becomes more justified when time trials become relevant. Although I had to think a bit, I had no issues doing what I wanted and finishing up the game when I wanted to. The music is also nice and breezy, in the style of a David wise, and I'll be adding the soundtrack to my personal collection if it's available.I think the key thing here is the 2D collectathon. I'm always looking for good ones to fit in between bigger games so If you like classic 3D collectathon, I'd recommend at least keeping your eye on this for a sale as i don't think I've found a better translation in 2D. Exceeded expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is criminally underappreciated, not by the people who have played it (look at the reviews and you'll see many more like my own), but by the enormous number of people who haven't. If you like collectathons, platformers, puzzlers, or just good video games, then you will enjoy Promenade. Give it a try. There was not a single moment that I was bored during my 16 hours of playtime. There were a handful of times I was a little annoyed (specifically the maze in the haunted house...), but bored? Never. There is always something to do, and those somethings are always right within reach. All you need to do is roll a little to the right or left and you will find another item to collect, another gap to leap across, another puzzle to solve, and always another. This is the type of game that makes you want to play it, not only because of the amount of things to do, but because of how crisp doing all of those things feels. There isn't much higher praise I can give than that. If your game makes me scroll through my probably-too-long list of installations, past the games I've already poured dozens of hours into and would gladly and mindlessly pour more, past the dozen other new games I have yet to open up and maybe never will, to its page, with that big green button that reads "Play," and even then, when I still have the chance to say "screw it, I'm just going to play some more Risk of Rain 2," even then, if I plug in my controller and hit play to return to your world and explore every inch of it, beating all the objectives and clearing all the achievements in the process, then you have made a darn good game. Even better than that, you have made a fun game. People don't play enough of those these days. Hats off to you guys and gals over at Holy Cap. I hope to play more games from you in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: I am genuinely shocked this game hasn't got more attention since its release earlier this year. This game consistently gives out Nintendo developer vibes through it's innovative puzzles and platforming mechanics that are always involving. Completed in around 10 hours but will definitely be going back to find the remaining pieces.The only real issue I encountered during my play through was the lack of fast travel to previously explored areas. The great elevator is good for travelling between larger worlds but I sometimes had a hard time finding a sub level where I was missing several cog pieces.Do not hesitate on purchasing this game and giving it a try. Works great on Steam Deck as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly don't have too much to say about this game other than it's good. It has a nice aesthetic, movement feels fluid, and the environments are varied enough to keep you interested all throughout your playthrough. Progression is achieved by solving simple puzzles or overcoming individual challenges to get the game's collectibles, which is where its correlation to Mario Odyssey comes from. I do think that some of the collectibles are more annoying to get than others, but majority of them are straightforward enough to figure out. As a minor complaint, I don't really care about the game's story; in fact, it's so unimportant that it might as well not even be in the game. Ignoring that, though, this is a really solid platformer and if you're a fan of collectathons, you might want to give this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Very chill platformer. Nothing is really difficult but the different mechanics feel fresh.You can see how the game also has been thought of for speedrunning with many shortcut in level design and animation cut mechanics. Not the best game of all time but a 10/10 for what is trying to achieve. I can only recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let Promenade fool you, behind it's cute and artsy graphics lies a challenging platforming and puzzle game. Get on an adventure and master the different tools at your disposal to collect gears and climb up the great Elevator. Promenade is an adventure game that rewards exploration with a ton of hidden secrets that you'll get clues for by fetching the lost pages of a journal. With multiple areas to explore, each bringing their new set of ideas and mechanics to platform will make your journey to the top an exciting experience to find out what mysteries lies in this world. If you love to explore, some challenging platforming and cute octopuses then this gem is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: SHORT VERSION:Promenade is a beautiful 2D collectathon platformer that excels in the creativity of its objectives. It's not particularly difficult, but the novelty of many of its goals kept me engaged. While there are optional challenges that tested my dexterity, I definitely recommend this to people who enjoy relatively easy and calming action games.LONG VERSION:MY PROGRESS:I've completed every level and gotten every item in the game. I also beat the developer times in every time trial.STRENGTHS:- CREATIVITYThis game had a lot of surprising twists and clever uses of its simple and accessible mechanics. Examples include grabbing a planet from a mobile and placing it on a star map so that you can hop in a spaceship and visit, carrying a puzzle piece to the place it fits in the background, or climbing frozen cliffs by making snowballs and throwing them down.WEAKNESSES:- SLOW WALKINGThere is a roll that gets you around a lot faster so I'd advise getting used to that quickly. Otherwise the basic walk is too slow for my taste.OTHER POINTS OF INTEREST:- LOW DIFFICULTYThis game is relatively easy, so it is generally a relaxing journey. However, there are some later levels and optional challenges that bumped up the difficulty. That said, there are better options if you want to be overwhelmed by controller-snapping rage.OVERALL:- This is platformer manages to be really creative in offering a variety of goals without being particularly difficult. If you're fairly new to platformers or just want to chill this is a strong recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: A rather delightful platformer that progresses in challenges and introduces new mechanics as you rise up through the giant elevator.  There are a handful of locations that feel a bit more puzzle oriented, but overall it's an immensely enjoyable journey through the game as you run into so many different locations.The platforming captures some of the best parts of Super Mario World and the grappling mechanic made me think of the original Bionic Commando.  The way you grab enemies to progress through the levels reminds me of Kirby's Dreamland.  In short, the game manages to pull some of the best parts out of classic platformers to give us a fun time.Graphically the game feels like it's going to be pretty memorable many years from now.  It has a slight Adventure Time look to it, but I think the game stays pretty unique visually throughout.  There's a great amount of love and care put into this game, and it's a platformer that is absolutely worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: When I first played the demo, I was unimpressed by it. The art style was nice, and I liked the idea of a 2D platformer playing like a collectathon 3D platformer, but the moment to moment gameplay wasn’t amazing. The main character moved too slowly for my liking, the music of the pirate level was underwhelming, and I disliked how throwing enemies at enemies wasn’t as fun as in any of the Klonoa games. But given that the game was the only 2D platformer I ever played outside Klonoa to have a “pick up enemy and use them as a double jump” mechanic, I gave it a wishlist. I thought it could be better when fully released.After playing the game for a bit, I’m shocked by how clever it is. The puzzle design is way better than I expected and once you learn how to use the roll for speed (and unlock the grapple hook type ability), the platforming is fun to master. I would still like a pure run button (needing to do a roll for a speed boost is fine but feels more complex than I would like) because the default walk is slow.The level design is good, the platforming is fun, and the puzzles that require rethinking how to get one thing from one side of a level to another make me feel like I’m smart. Highly recommend to anyone who is a fan of 2D platformers. While I wasn’t impressed by the demo, I still highly recommend playing it to get a good idea on the type of game it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: I had LOTS of fun playing this game! It's full of surprises and secrets, and it is a good challenge to get all the cogs!If you liked the demo, it just gets better and better!It'd be really good though if the devs managed to fix the stuttering of the background when it moves. It required some concentration to kinda stop being annoyed by it.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: The game's art style gives me Yoshi's Island / Yoshi's Story kinda vibes. But the game play stands more on its own just as a great platformer. You go around levels collecting golden cogs which allow you to fix the great elevator and ascend to the next level/world.The music, the art, the movement are all fantastic. Some of the platforming challenges in the game are pretty tough despite the cutesy look.Neither of the bosses have been at all tough so far, so that would be the one downside. That could change as I continue to play.An absolute delight of a game. I really hope more people check it out
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Promenade is a charming, colourful, challenging and fun 2D platformer; as a lover of Platformer games, this is one of the best and most difficult games I've ever played!This soundtrack, sound design, level design and rhythm are so well thought out.The level design in particular encourages exploration, thinking outside the box, rewards you for persevering and doesn't punish you for getting something wrong.The level design is very intuitive, as you go through they introduce new mechanics, gives you some practice and then puts them all together in the main boss battles and challenges. There are some things that can be frustrating, but nothing that would make someone rage quit.The character design are also very cute and well deigned.If you love platformer/puzzle games you need this in your library, I would recommend getting the physical edition as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10I enjoyed every single one of the 10 hours it took me to 100% the game. The Holy Cap Team put an incredible amount of love and passion into this platformer. At the time of writing, there's not a SINGLE negative review for this game yet, and I hope it stays that way, because there's also not any significantly negative thing I can say about its design!In fact, I think this game's greatest strength is that you're never going to be bored while playing this. Throughout the entire experience Promenade constantly gives the player new environments, mechanics, and activities to accomplish. It gets gradually more challenging, but enjoyably so - I really felt like I was getting better at their systems, and there's no moments where I felt like the game became too easy or too hard with the tools I had. It's just pure fun.If you enjoy 2D collectathons, you really should be wishlisting or buying this, because this gem shouldn't stay hidden.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing puzzle platformer that follows the rule of adding a new design idea in every level, adding up to a beautiful and very creative "greater-than-the-sum-of-its-parts" gem of a game. Really cool art, atmosphere and sound design as well. A few sweaty fingers challenges after you reach the ending will help you stay longer in a world you won't want to leave.This is one that shouldn't fly under the radar ! Come join the Promenade :)
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game. From the art style to the sound design to the physics/gamefeel to the creativity of the puzzles, it's a masterpiece in almost every conceivable way. Easily one of my favorite platformers, not just in recent memory but in general. I'm currently working on 100%-ing the game outside of my Twitch channel but have been asked to at least broadcast it on Discord by people who just can't get enough of it. This game is really something special and an experience I'll be talking about for quite a while.Feel free to check out my playthrough atIf I could pick one nit, it would be that it's possible to misinterpret a particularly anticlimactic moment as the end of the game, when the actual end of the game is wonderful and moving. If you feel a sense of "Uh, was that all?" consider the visual indications  to see how you might progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game during the beta and I played it again with pleasure when it was out.It is a good platform game, dynamic, well reacting to command, generous in game design and exploration.It is an independant game treated with a lot of care by a small relentless team. Musics are simple let enjoyable and adequat.The artistic direction is an obvious other strengh of this game.And last but not least, many easter eggs are present because it is a game which love other games and gamers. <3Delight yourself !
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Really unique and fun game. It's like they mixed a 3D platformer's goal based objectives with a 2D platformer and it works so well. The movement is also really fun and ranges from very basic running and jumping to chaining together combos and being able to do some really fancy stuff. Highly recommend to anyone that enjoys platformers of any kind.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Such an incredible game!Every mechanic it introduces is fresh and polished, and there is no shortage of said mechanics either.The collectathon structure allows for so many different kinds of challenges that there is something for everyone, and the requirements are lenient enough that you can progress easily while skipping sections that don't appeal to you.Then the several creative steam achievements are the icing on the cake, it has been a while since I played a game that was so fun to 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game in about 7hrs with 135/180 cog pieces and the five octopuses freed. A very fun old-school platformer with gameplay similar to Klonoa mixed with collecting cog pieces similar to stars in mario 64. There are some fun new ideas for platforming and unlocking the other abilities completely changes the game, giving you new options for traversal. Some of the time trials can be quite difficult but not impossible. This game is for sure built with speedrunning in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely worth the price. A beautiful collect-it-all puzzle-platformer in which you will appreciate the great freedom of approach given to the player in every situation, guaranteed by a varied and dynamic movement system that always rewards experimentation and refinement of the mechanics. If it plays like a cross between a faster Klonoa and a Super Mario Wonder, the design and cartoonish style might remind you of Scribblenauts.  Fans of the genre will definitely want to pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Such an unexpected gem, has some definite Nintendo charm (maybe not Nintendo-level polish) but in terms of level design, platforming mechanics, clever gimmicks and thoughtful interactions, Promenade is top-notch.Despite having levels the world feels open and connected and the game has some really nice bail-out features like cancel the race, go back to home world, doesn't punish you for exploring or make you backtrack in a needless way but it could use a detailed map with markers.Also, I appreciate the fact that there are no words, no long drawn out backstory, no exposition through dialog, it shows the story in small which doesn't bog down the experience, bravo devs.Works well on Steam Deck with XBOX One controller, animations are fluid, if you liked DKC and Mario Galaxy then you'll probably like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. It's like mario odyssey except 2D instead of 3D. I think it's better than mario odyssey too. It's extremely polished and feels great to play. The collectibles and levels are all a lot of fun. Promenade is in my top 5 indie games of all time, for sure.My play time:8.5 hours to beat the game the first time12.5 hours total to collect everything24 hours total for all the achievements (a lot of the extra time was for the 2.5h speedrun achievement)
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: I was gifted this game by the Developers themselves, not sponsored at all. I didn’t expect much going into a free game from a new studio, but I was extremely pleasantly surprised. This game is full of charm and delight.You have very limited movement options, and the game knows this, using it to its advantage. Every single enemy you can bounce on, hook you can grab, is placed in such a way that getting from A to B becomes an interesting and fun puzzle in its own right. But once you understand the platforming, you can start the adventuring. This is a collectathon in 2D. And that might sound limited, but you’d be amazed at what you can do in the limited space. I’ve helped snails find love, raced penguins across the world, flown a ship in space and many many other things. It’s incredible and I never got bored.If you liked 3D collectathons like Mario Odyssey, or loved the 2D platforming of Celeste, I’d highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: I have played just a few minutes of the game (the tutorial and the first "level"), but first impression in really good. Great art style, controls and gameplay. The story seems interesting (but it's too soon to judge).Edit: I have finished the game. The gameplay gets even better, the story is really interesting and I really liked the way it's presented. The level design is incredible. It kind of feels like a 3d mario game (like super mario 64 and odissey) but in 2d and it works incredibly well. If you like platformers this is a must have, and even if you don't, this is still a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game and a refreshing experience from passionate developers who put their heart and soul into creating it.The game offers a wonderful gameplay, be it for casual players or hardcore gamers, thanks to jump mechanics that get gradually more complex.Led by beautiful graphics, the environment varies greatly from a level to an other while offering many hidden secrets to find.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

_childDocuments_.review: Go on an adventure in a world packed with secrets helped by your friend, a poulp with many abilities. Explore, solve puzzles, wander across dungeons, blast through races and much more in this game inspired by the best 3D platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Promenade

name: ZERO Sievert
detailed_description: The world has ended. ZERO Sievert charges you with scavenging equipment across multiple areas, all set in an atmospheric fictitious post-apocalyptic Eastern Europe setting. Your base of operations, the bunker, is filled with traders, modding stations, and areas to make your own, providing you with progression across your excursions into the wild. Once you’re out in the wilds of the wasteland, however, the situation becomes a lot less secure. Across the five biomes of the game, you’ll initially be armed with little more than a gun and a bottle of water, after which point it’s up to you to recover items, take out bandits, and most importantly, get back alive. And be warned ; the nuclear fallout may have impacted some of the local wildlife… A wasteland to explore Procedurally generated maps make every journey different, with ever-changing hiding spots, loot locations, and layouts. With over five maps to explore, be sure to adapt and learn each one's secrets to get in, get out, and get better. Full weapon modification Hunt in a way that suits your playstyle, with over 35 unique guns and 150 mods that can be combined to make you the biggest threat in the wastes of ZERO Sievert. Create a weapon that suits your style or focus on stats to become the ultimate hunter. Looting and questing Multiple questlines guide you through the world of ZERO Sievert. Through talking with a range of characters you’ll slowly unravel information and lore about the world that’s been left behind. Alongside this, there are more than 100 different items to loot which can be used to craft new items, upgrade your own base, and trade.

short_description: ZERO Sievert is a tense top-down extraction shooter that challenges you to scavenge a procedurally-generated wasteland, loot gear, and explore what’s left of a devastated world. When the odds are stacked against you, you’ll need to do more than just survive...

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing the game since its very early stages of development, and I've played it periodically after every major update. Now, with the game finally finished and after putting in a few hours, I can say I still love it. It has a very specific appeal, so it's definitely not for everyone.I think the game's biggest strength is the knowledge progression you gain as a character. At first, you're wandering through the forest with nothing much—a mediocre gun and no idea how to navigate. What’s worth picking up? Should I engage this person? Are they friendly? Where does this lead? You’re afraid of everything and everyone. And rightly so—if you're not careful, you can die in an instant. Especially in Hunter mode, where you lose all your precious gear upon death, being careful and knowing when to act make you feel powerful, like a true survival veteran in this game.I have to say that if you're playing on lower difficulty, the gear progression is quite fast; you can get high-level armor and weapons in no time once you know where to look (looking at you, Lazar). However, the game offers a wide range of weapons to experiment with, and I find that gunplay against higher-level sniper/DMR opponents can be thrilling. You have to use grenades, flashbangs, and strategic positioning to get the drop on these guys. They can two-shot you through almost the entire game.To sum up, I really enjoy playing the game on Hunter mode. I'm so happy the team managed to complete it despite all the challenges, including the war. I hope you guys are doing well, and thank you so much for developing such a great piece of digital entertainment. Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun and I'd recommend playing it, but I think it has some wrinkles that need to be ironed out.  The amount of time required to loot anything is ridiculous. Considering all the containers and bodies you loot, that's a lot of dead play time spent just sitting around doing nothing but waiting for items to load.  I understand the point is to make looting risky because you can be attacked, but right now its implementation is absurd.  There has to be a better way than making 2/3 of the play time on any map just idle wait time while being effectively locked out of any actions.EDIT: I had another paragraph talking about the severe lag I was experiencing with this game.  After watching the MSI AB overlay for a while, I figured out that my laptop's CPU was throttling and it needed a good cleaning and reapplication of thermal compound.  After that the game runs smooth for me.  Sorry for initially blaming the game, it was just really noticeable for some reason.  I would still recommend playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Zero Sievert is a top-down pixel graphics shoot-and-loot extraction game. Right now, it's exclusively single player, and aggressively early access. If you buy this game now it's because you're along for the ride, not wanting to reach the destination. You follow a standard rogue-lite path: go on a mission, get some gear, kill some baddies, finish some quests, come back. If you die, your progress is reset to the beginning of the mission - the stakes are low. Because of this, the game is more like a roguelite than it is Tarkov. In fact, the similarities to Tarkov basically begin and end at the setting and the gun, armor, and ammo mechanics (like armor pen and ammo switching). If someone says "ZS is a Tarkov successor" ignore them - they are wishing it was. I personally have not found enemy accuracy to be insane. Maybe I'm playing differently than other reviewers, and enemies certainly aren't chumps, but I don't really get zonked out of nowhere by aimbot NPCs much, if at all, without it being my own fault. Yeah - if you run up to an enemy they will shoot you in the face. Turns out that guns are actually pretty accurate. Who knew. Overall if you buy right now (Dec 2022) you are going to get maybe 30% of a game. I am personally enjoying that 30%. You may choose to wait, and that's reasonable. But I think when it's 100% done it's gonna be a classic gem.

_childDocuments_.review: This genuinely used to be one of my favorite games, and I loved watching it come along through several patches, and despite its various quirks and flaws, it was challenging, fun to play and yet open and invited replay without rancor. Then this latest patch came along, and the devs duly warned us all that this would come with a save wipe, so I braced my end-of-content character for deletion and the starting of a new adventure. Several problems became rapidly apparent, some have already been mentioned by others, but this is my experience.-The disparity between the amount of reputation gain per quest and the amount of reputation to unlock what was before affordable gear at this point in my run is irritating. While I understand the intent and even the in-universe flavor reason for gatekeeping certain items, it's somewhat ridiculous that I'm going to be denied a backpack upgrade I could have easily bought twice over by now.- While I understand that in accordance with the new reputation system, the Green Army is no longer Neutral, but actively Hostile, this makes the early game MUCH more punishing than it was previously, when it might have been possible to rest among the green army soldiers like a clownfish in an anemone, or even lead enemies into them. Even as a fairly seasoned player, it was a frustrating start for this reason. Worse, the quests that presumably earn enough green army rep to make them stop shooting you likely comes well past the point you've stopped running from them, and being constantly shot at does not endear a faction to a player.-I personally have been unable to access the makeshift camp, even after jumping through several needless hoops in order to visit it at all, as the game simply hard crashes in a manner identical to the others. Which means I now have several quests that cannot be completed, and presumably am locked off from the reset of the levels forever. -In addition to this, not only do most of your quests now come from the Networker (which, whatever, but I had previously felt a connection with the barman and the Doctor and such as characters, so I was sad to see them lose that element.) and one of the initial quests immediately broke. For the quest Scientist Work 1, you're supposed to place an analyzer near a fire anomaly. Fine. Except, every time I tromp down to the big yellow circle on the map and find the big field of fire, there is no prompt for placing the device. At all. Anywhere inside or immediately around the circle. Anywhere. At all. I have searched, run through fire, died several times, all in an attempt to find the right place, but to no avail. Even with the other quests I've been able to complete, this has hampered my progress significantly.-For whatever reason, Blinks, an enemy previously seen several levels hence, are now in the Forest. Presumably, next patch will bring Big and ArminFor all of these reasons, Zero Sievert has lost a lot of the shine from its radioactive apple, at least for the moment. I have not lost faith in the devs, this game is still being developed, and sometimes missteps are made. Hopefully, they will listen to their fans, fix what wasn't broken before, and let us return to a freer Zarkov. I look forward to the day I can delete this review, and leave a positive one.

_childDocuments_.review: I have requested a refund as of this time. Don't get me wrong, I believe that this could be a good game, and most players might enjoy it. The following is a list of reasons as to why I don't enjoy this game.- Minimal Tutorial for new players, with no explanation to core gameplay mechanics and stats. - Everything one shots (or does too much dmg) and that would be okay if I could see them before they see me, which given how line of sight works, it wont ever work. - Starting missions require you to overload on weight if you want to do any looting, which removes the fun of having extraction. - The player is not introduced to the extraction locations in a way that makes sense (only hiding it on the map with 0 in game explanation, and often extraction points are just an invisible zone with no in world structure associated). - Art style is good except you need to be able to spot enemies on the edge of the screen, which can limit the strategy you can use because of dense follage. - Ranged scope mechanic feels unnatural. - Character mechanics such as sleep (and where you can sleep) are entirely unexplained except for the in game "tutorials" which acts closer to a wiki, and is barely introduced to the player. - Nighttime is brutal, and can be encountered before the player even works out sleep is a mechanic. - The Tutorial and starting area (bunker) need to be much more welcoming to the player, and ensure that they have all of the skills and information they need before departing. - Finally, while the gameplay loop is fun, locking upgrades behind such a large item requirement means that the first unlocks require you to ignore the games starting missions, get lucky in loot and enemy spawns, and on top of all of that, require the player to work out mechanics that could very easily be explained and or walked through with the player.All of this being said, I have played the game for under two hours, so maybe I don't have a full perspective on the game. However, I feel that this is the most important time for a player to understand how the game works, and if new players are not welcomed into the game, I feel that there isn't any content that I will be comfortable approaching.I love the concept, and I think the execution works in some ways, but ultimately I don't think this game is for me, as much as I would love it to be.

Instead of making small tweaks to balance their guns they killed the fun consistency of the guns in favor of Sudo-realism and forced diversity.  This has had the opposite effect. _childDocuments_.review: As a long time Tarkov player and a huge fan of the Stalker series, also a sucker for pixel games, I loved this game. I been playing the game since Kickstarter. However I cannot recommend this game at all in its current state. First of all, content. The game has been released for almost 2 years now, but all the devs been doing is tweaking and fixing bugs. Yes fixing bugs and balancing the game are very important, however there is almost no new content being added to the base game since its Kickstarter days.  5 maps in total and almost no new weapons or new quests except some holiday events. "The Bunker" or the game's main hub still has tons of unused space and placeholder assets.The devs fixing problems that never existed in the first place.The UI before the recent update worked perfectly, now they felt like a mobile game with very buggy inventory UI. Sometimes item can overlap each other in your stash, or sometimes you cant stack a stackable item.  The AI for some reason feels dumber and dumber each patch. I played on the Survivor difficulty but human enemy AI are not any smarter from Rookie difficulty since recently patch. On the other hand, monster AI is just unfair. Ever since Alpha the monster AI have a problem where they will sprint around the player in circles and snapping on to the player when they attack since most of the monsters are melee. This caused the player to just mag dump on them only to find out none of the shots connected and dies due to the need to reload. The devs never fixed this issue and seem to be fine with it even alot of people have requested to rework the monster AI in their discord.The devs seems to constantly tweaking core gameplay mechanics that should not be touched, because I literally feel like i am playing Enter the Gungeon, except with non of Gungeon's fluid movement.I really want to give this game a positive but i can't. if you plan on buying this thinking it is going to be a 2D tarkov, dont. It is not ready until 1.0 or at least til full release.

_childDocuments_.review: What a great game. Honestly. It's definitely early in the production timeline and there is a lot to be fleshed out, but the content that is within the game already is GREAT. It's so good, that I completed as much as I could in this game, and now I'm downloading Stalker: GAMMA to try and scratch the itch this game created. I am SO excited for this game to continue it's development, and it's going to be SO good. The developer definitely has a passion for this genre and spent a lot of time to make sure it feels good and is authentic to this looter shooter post-apocalyptic (F)Russia. Pros:It's a great mix between Tarkov and Stalker is how I would explain it. It allows for the hard punishment of instadeath if you play too recklessly, without the loss of all your gear. It takes a long time to get good gear, and even when you are basically at the top of the food chain, it takes one wrong turn to end up in a camp that will wipe you from the earth in 2 seconds flat. Super rewarding and very difficult in a good wayCons:A few glitches here and there, DON'T GO TO THE SWAMP, I spawned in and I literally could only access the railroad track, the rest of the map was water with like 3 islands in the top left, and I couldn't make it to the extraction. A few quest lines feel WAY too tedious at the early part of the game but I'm sure balancing will be completed later on. You'll mostly spend time in the forest and bandit camp. Once you can access the mall you'll pretty much be near end game, otherwise you'll get one shot immediately and won't play the mall lol. Final thoughts:Great game, worth picking up right now for sure. Solid 10-20 hours of game play, and worth supporting the developer to get an early start at a game that should have some fantastic payoff once it's all finished.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access:“Greed” would be a great alternative title for this game. I’m sure there are plenty of reviews comparing ZERO Sievert to a budget Tarkov with elements from Stalker but at it’s core it feels like a gambling simulator. You get tasks from various people littered throughout the bunker and you venture into one of several different maps to collect items to fulfill said tasks. Assuming you survive long enough to find the item or items a question crosses your mind, “Do I leave now or do I collect more loot?” Become the Rat Lord you always wanted to be. Carry a pistol with only 15% health and 10 rounds in hopes you can kill a bandit with a rifle with the same amount of health with little to no ammo. It doesn’t matter, like everything else you will just sell it when you get back. Constantly collecting rare items and money until you purchase some nice armor… and then do it all over again for the next upgrade. It’s Early Access and it isn’t perfect but it’s lots of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I first found out about this game via Splattercatgaming covering it last year. Haven't played to game enough for an in depth review, at least, not the finished product, I did play the alpha that was publicly released from dev last year and I liked it. Since then the old PC decided to visit the boneyard and so I hadn't played it since because by the time I got my new rig the alpha was gone. So, I sat and waited and bought it the day it came out.All I'm seeing with the EA launched product is a game that's far more developed than many 1.0 games out there from other indie's and AAA games. There's nothing wrong with the controls, the pixel art is charming and, sure, it's still rough around the edges to a certain degree, however, dev is passionate and updates frequently and listens to input, I don't see that slowing down any time soon. I like the game, the issue is I really suck at it lol. I'm used to top down point and shoot sorts of games, but this is a different beast of a game. In most pixel art games that'd seem similar the goal is the same as a twin stick shooter, point, click to fire, kite, repeat. ZERO Sievert? Absolutely not. I mean, yes, you CAN, however if you expect that to get you very far you're in for a very big surprise, you'll probably biff it within a minute. Why? Stealth factors. I've never played escape from Tarkov or the S.T.A.L.K.E.R.  games, so, IDK which of these the sorts of game mechanics I'm going to mention come from, so, keep that in mind, however: The reason you can't just run and gun is because this game accounts for things like Line of Sight (LOS). Not just LOS of trees/objects, but also LOS as a result of high grass, etc. The enemy is just as deadly or more deadly than you. In my case that's more deadly because I totally lost the muscle memory I gained from the time I played the alpha. Some might be turned off by my above description, which, okay, that's not a bad thing, you're probably looking for a twin stick shooter or something similar that's more arcade-y, that's not this game. This game has survival mechanics and crafting mechanics, has place holders for a faction system and has procedurally generated portions. It's pretty full developed despite it being just launched into early access and, a twin stick shooter is not. Moreover, there are a few unique mechanics I haven't seen down in other top down games (really, it's a huge list, but here's an example), when you mod a scope onto a sniper rifle, it moves the cursor down range and brings up a huge reticle shaped like your scope allowing you to find your target and click them, in this mode bullet speed is instant, so, click, target dies, move to next target. I don't think I'm doing it justice with that description, but, that's my best. I've never seen something quite like it in a top down pixel art shooter and it's quite functional if you're hidden from enemy vision. I could go on, point is, the game is tough as nails and requires you get used to the difficulty, think on your feet, conserve ammo, think critically on risk v rewards and improvise/adapt/strategize. You don't want to, say. jump right into a map to complete an objective for someone at the base and then try to 100% explore the map early on, you'll die super quick. In my case, an unseen sniper got me one time, a second pack of wolves I didn't seen the second time after I dropped an adjacent pack of wolves, and too many regular rando enemies with AK's that I hadn't scouted for me to feel comfortable admitting to. So, that's my review thus far, graphics are good for the style they're going after, sound is decent and music can be good, but is still under development. You can rebind things to meet you fancy and dev even has a slider at the bottom which checks to see if your keyboard is qwerty/azerty or something else, I thought that was pretty cool as I've played games that hard code certain keys like everyone has an AZERTY and yet more that hardcoded certain keys assuming everyone has a QWERTY. That... is a final attempt to express the way this dev thinks, it's these small little touches that tailor the experience or allow you to tailor the experience that shines. That and dev has responded a few times to Splattercatgaming covering the game, each time they did they were full of excitement that someone found their game good, and, ya know what... the games industry needs such passionate indie devs. Will update as I play the game, but, if a unique survival top down pixel art gem with some base building and crafting that punishes even the small mistakes but rewards derringdo mixed with tactical thinking, there's a good chance you'll feel right at home with this gem.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game in its current state, with an even more promising future as additional content or complexities are added.  As extraction shooters continue growing in popularity, ZS does an excellent job presenting the format from a top down perspective.  I love Tarkov, but the cheating situation in FPS games right now is untenable: this is PvE, so the only thing I need to worry about is procedural RNG and bag space.  As is typical of most PvE games, ZS allows you to choose your own unique play-through difficulty preferences.  To maximize replayability, I play on Hardcore mode losing all items on failed extract and making the gameplay more meaningful and immersive.  Message to the devs,Great job so far! Here are a few wishlist requests that I believe would push this game over the top:-Create urgency by making the raid extraction time-limited based on the player's radiation levels.  Each raid map would have a small but persistent radiation gain in addition to the other triggers that influence the radiation levels.  The player would be forced to consider the risk/rewards of extending the raid experience at the expense of not being healthy enough to reach extract, it would increase the importance of preraid preparedness, and create strategic considerations of item benefit trade-offs.  Most importantly, this simple modification immediately connects the gamer to the title of your game (0 Sv).-Make the maps larger in scale (x2) and apply a spawn probability % to all non-essential sites and non-active quest NPCs, so that the raids are more random and unique.  Add an additional, conditional extraction point nearer to the center of the map.-Hide the key sites on the unexplored portions of the map.  Only reveal contextual, or incomplete location data.-Modify the camps so that the number of  NPCs is somewhat random (instead of 3 NPCs all the time, make it at least 2 and up to 5).  -NPC bosses, should be rare, rich, and challenging.  Consider adding a countdown of days before a respawn after a boss kill to prevent boss farming, and maybe a less bountiful loot table.-Increase the probability of higher geared wondering "Hunters", with unique loot tables.-Add achievements, make several of them rare and challenging.  And finally...-Openly engage the modding community.  Some of my most memorable gaming experiences have come from modded games.  Your fans have great ideas, some of them enjoy programming games (for free).  Pick the best mods and include them as part of future releases/DLCs.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: Hate to say it but most recent patch complete ruined the game. Excessive radiation storms, broken rep system that requires insane amounts of grinding, and lack of quests for factions that have any meaningful rewards.The concept of a rep system is great as a way to keep players from getting high tier gear too quick, but the way it was implemented gives pitiful amounts of rep for completing quests while locking even mid tier gear behind insane rep requirements. Not to mention that missions for a faction will be rep locked, with no way to actually increase your rep other than daily's that only give you 2-6 rep. No one wants to grind 50 daily quests just to unlock the next faction mission. And with rad storms happening more frequently, you'd better hope you have an envirosuit to negate thhe storms, or at least anti-rad injectors. But any suit worth a ♥♥♥♥ is rep locked, as are injectors, and there are ZERO missions to build rep with Scientists for far too long, well after you're tasked with missions on Makeshift Camp/Industrial/Swamp, which have at least a 50% chance of having a rad storm when you spawn in. Get used to running right to exfil. Some lesser issues like AI aimbot, anomaly/mutant damage are certainly real but are easily overcome with skill and playing slow.This game is really great and I'd happily sink another 50 hours into it, but the devs HAVE to sort out the issues the community is having less they plunge the game into death and obscurity. I was really excited to start a fresh hardcore save with the most recent patch but its clear I'm gonna wait it out till ♥♥♥♥♥ fixed, as is most of the playerbase.

_childDocuments_.review: It's really 3 different games, at least it feels so. It is solid 10 hours of fun, if you don't mind the grind it's more like 20-40 hours, which are unfortunately less intense than the start. It's a game based around intensity/action density, which by trying to prolong it's playtime lessens it's core aspect. It's sad, but I had fun and would therefore recommend it anyway.That artificial prolonging of the game divides it into 3 stages that feel and play different.First stage is "paranoic level". You know nothing, you have no equipment, you can die form 2 shots and you die half of the time when fighting grouped enemies. Your goal is to hide, to scrap all leftovers and jump paranoicly after any suspicious sound is made. Really intense, immersive, free and fun.Second stage is "Why, tell me why!? level". You're no longer paranoicly scared, you've learned most of key signals (sounds, enemy looks, location characteristics) and unfortunately reached the grind wall... You have all the money you can have, but you can't buy better armor, because you don't have exp, you can't enter most locations because they're locked after filler quest (you don't know even which ones). You grind, grind, grind in hopes to see what you dream of. Though some of that grind is not that bad, even fun sometimes, it's literally worst part of the game. You either end the game here or are pacient enough to reach third stage. This stage is little boring and repetitive, but at times also intense and fun.Third stage is "Am I a boss here? level". You've grinded your dream set, unlocked most of location quests and reached 4th experience level allowing you to access most of the game content. You know most of the game patterns, you have enough experience to know when to run and when to walk slowly, you can "finally" finish all the game content, which happens to be quite hard and new/not repetitive, which makes game once again intense, fun and either really satisfying or really tilting when you stupidly die. It's very similar to the first stage, but a little more tactical at it's core.

_childDocuments_.review: Zero Sievert is a good game in its own right - mechanically sound, stupendous performance, incredible sound design, and impressive graphics for what it is. I really enjoyed my playthrough of the title. I particularly enjoyed the difficulty options that really let me pick how I wanted to play the game, as well as the feeling of growth and development as I slowly accrued wealth, skills, and better gear. The slow power creep that you get to enjoy, the finding of components and attachments for guns you have yet to unlock, playing with the various armors that the game offers to find out which one suits your playstyle best, fiddling with the different skills and specializations - all incredibly fun. I unabashedly enjoyed my time with the game and would recommend it to anyone who likes extraction shooters and doesn't mind playing them in singleplayer where Kibba is the only hacker you have to deal with. Twin stick shooter + extraction shooter = match made in heaven.The problem? Most of Zero Sievert's world building and mechanics are ripped from popular contemporaries. Whether it is coincidence or not, Zero Sievert *borrows* quite a bit from Stalker and Escape from Tarkov. Obviously given the russo-influences that is to be expected to an extent, but anomalies are really only found in Stalker and the variety of lootables from Tarkov are more or less 1:1 represented in Zero Sievert. Again, this is not really a problem given than Zero Sievert is more or less sold as a combination of those games with one less dimension. Food for thought for sure though.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun twin stick shooter with a heavy focus on looting. fairly difficult, the enemies are just as lethal as the player and a few shots can end a run if you have bad armor. individual runs are quick (10-15 minutes) and there is decent progression in the hub area. New skill system recently got added that encourages using all the different weapon types, which is nice since all are pretty viable and add a good bit of variety to gameplay.Lots of inspiration from games like Tarkov and the Stalker series. Hub area full of quest NPC's and optional upgrades crafted from random loot found in missions; merchants whose inventory you unlock by gaining favour; mutated animals and zones you feel out with thrown bolts, that kind of thing. _childDocuments_.review: This game is very satisfying to play. _childDocuments_.review: This game is what I was hoping Tarkov could be when I first saw it back in the day.  Extreme difficulty, solid RPG mechanics, and a progression system that takes you from feeling powerless to being an unstoppable juggernaut destroying everything hostile that you come across.  After my first 10 hour session however, I have some issues with the game.      The death/reset mechanic is odd to say the very least:  Losing nothing and being reset on death with the notable exception of in game time is just odd, but also frustrating if you had found something rare.  There are strategies to minimize this, of course, and I'm not looking to have it changed, but it's definitely more obnoxious than I was expecting, and definitely should be kept in mind when starting out the game.  Death is frequent, sudden, and you should always be expecting to die.      As for things that DO need to be changed, I have only one issue.  I've had enemies spawn inside walls 6 or 7 times in 10 hours, which wouldn't be a problem if the walls stopped them.  The walls that enemies are stuck inside pose 3 problems: first, the enemies can't move and so make no noise.  This has led me walking into melee enemies that ALWAYS cause massive damage and bleed on hit, with no warning that they're there.  Second, the walls don't block the enemies from attacking, leading to 2 deaths so far from being shot by an enemy inside a wall.  Third, half the time when I do survive a wall ambush, the wall acts as a shield, meaning I can't kill the enemy that's stuck and either can't progress or have to reset.     I finally had to take a break from the game after going into a cave area filled with bleed causing enemies and running into 2 of them stuck in walls in different places.  I play pretty smart, using sound to my advantage, but those 2 in wall enemies stuck me with 7 bleed stacks, completely using up the supplies I brought with me.  I was stacked to the gills to clear out this cave and I ended up getting reset by this glitch.  It wouldn't be so bad, but they can't move to make noise so I don't know they're there till i'm already getting multi-hit.  this game is an easy 10/10 if the dev can fix this, but this one glitch was bad enough to make me write a review and drop the rating to an 8/10.     Please be careful out there, the wasteland is not safe...

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little extraction looter/shooter that manages to bring the intense 'moment to moment combat' of a larger multiplayer game like this to a smaller scale, single player experience. The top-down pixel art style is delightful while the loading screens are dramatic and detailed giving the player a snapshot of what the world of Zero Sievert is like. Whether paying homage to older games like S.T.A.L.K.E.R. thru it's setting, or taking direct inspiration for it's, Tarkov-lite, game play loop. Zero Sievert is a fun little distraction. Well worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Still early in, but getting rolling. Pretty fun thus far. Still rough around the edges, to be sure, but it's early access and is sorta expected. Dialogue has grammatical errors, some dialogue options don't function with specific NPC's despite being available, big ol' "IN DEVELOPMENT" stickers here and there, etc. It's all minor stuff though, and the game plays well. Definitely Tarkovey in a lot of ways that are apparent just looking at some gameplay. Notably, you don't lose stuff on death outside of what you nabbed in raid, however. Dunno what I think of that, as it makes death a little inconsequential, but in the same stride death comes so quickly that I can't decide whether it's a bad thing. One way or another, it does feel a touch underwhelming to lose nothing and just go right back in. My only other complaint is that the dialogue is a bit... off. I'm no literary expert, but if I had to pinpoint what the problem is, I'd say it's that it's a bit too open with its expository dialogue. It feels very mechanical and overly direct. I hope they improve it as they continue development, as the atmosphere present in games like Tarkov and Stalker is a significant reason why I love them so much, and this game has the visual and gameplay to back it up if the dialogue starts pulling its weight. (On that note, make the Scav group themes work for more than a second or two before fizzling. I really dig it!)Gameplay is solid though, and I think it does a good job at giving info to players. Tooltips on ammo types and meds relieve so much of the headache involved in learning the counterparts in Tarkov, Gunplay feels good and snappy, with quick deaths and mostly quick kills. Non-human creatures move fast and offer an interesting alternative hazard to worry about. Scopes feel a little janky, and I think they'd benefit from an indicator for when the "lock on" that turns the weapon hitscan happens, much like how the crosshair turns color when LOS is blocked. As for the map design, I haven't ventured out of forest quite yet, but the partial randomization of threats and locale position is good. I think anomalies and radiation could probably have a little more impact though, as they're almost a nonissue unless you're collecting crystals. I'll likely update this section as I continue on and see more of what's on offer. I imagine that I could have problems with the system if it ends up being a linear progression of levels. Overall, even in early access I think this could be worth a buy if you want an extraction shooter that is singleplayer and isn't quite as punishing as alternatives.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to the hastily written reviews of others complaining about the gunplay and what not. The game comes with several sliders that you can use to adjust the game play to how you want it. Find that guns aren't doing the damage you want them to? Change the value in the games difficulty settings. The people that are leaving negative reviews have probably never played Tarkov or S.T.A.L.K.E.R before (which is what this game is based off of) and I think they are doing a phenomenal job with the game. The gunplay is fine. The ammo is what will make or break your guns damage just like in Tarkov or S.T.A.L.K.E.R . People complaining about how they "nerfed" guns seems biased. Every gun fills a role in a persons playstyle. Don't like a gun? Switch it up! :) They are balancing the guns to be more like there counterparts from the other game series' and I think that they are pretty accurate. The one gripe I will warn you about is to TURN OFF CLOUD SAVING. You can still save in the hideout by quickly returning to the menu and resuming the game. If you leave cloud saving on there is a chance that when you trade with an NPC it will revert your gamestate to the latest cloud save which will reset your progress. It happened to me about 10 times before I figured out that is what was happening. Until they fix that don't use cloud saving.Other than that this has turned out to be a very engaging and fun 2D tarky and S.T.A.L.K.E.R (gamma mod included) game.Good job devs :)

_childDocuments_.review: Going into a derelict, radioactive mall in full hazmat suit armed to the teeth with the most powerful sniper rifle on the market and a customized Five-Seven automatic pistol, murdering four people with lives and families and looting their corpses just for a bottle of Vodka. That's Zero Sievert.I've more or less beaten the game and am running out of quests to complete on my first save, and I can't recommend this game enough. It's kinda like if Tarkov and STALKER had a 2D baby. Sounds too good to be true, right? Well somehow the devs of Zero Sievert managed it anyway. The difficulty is extremely customizable, making it great for both casual and hardcore players. The gunplay feels great and rewarding, and you have to approach every fight with strategy. This is a great game. Get it.Now for feedback for the devs or whatever. Most importantly, OPTIMIZE THE GAME. I own a mid-end gaming laptop and the game barely runs with the rain and fog effects enabled. Secondly, nerf scopes. I'm a sniper main and even I think scopes are busted. Seriously, there's next to no reason to use traditional sights in the current patch, with all the crazy stat boosts scopes give. Thirdly, balance out the modding system. Most guns have attachment sets that are more or less objectively the best just because of their stats; I want a modding system where your gun shows what you like. More trade offs, less attachments that are stat upgrades of others, etc.. Also, please make the colors of certain parts customizable with paints. The best loadout for the SCAR-H is unbelievably ugly. Great game otherwise, keep it up!

_childDocuments_.review: If you have huge fps drops, it's likely because your windows decided it's better to use your inbuilt mini intel card over your actual graphic card... another user already commented on how to fix it in windows 10, so here's for windows 11:    1.Right-click the Windows icon in the taskbar, then select Settings.   2. Click System > Display > Graphics.    3. Select your app, then click Options. If you don't see it, go to your steam, right click on Zero sievert>properties>browse local files (where you see the .exe file)> copy this path    Choose your graphic card    Click Save.(source: XDA developers website and my own experience)

From the early struggles you find yourself getting steadily rewarded the more you play, and after about the 15 hour mark it starts to get easier as your equipment gets better. I love the different level designs and the quests although short do offer something of different value to the generic game play as the story slowly unravels. Out of all the places i would have to say that my favourite is the industrial zone. Though it can be chaotic with blinks coming out of nowhere and many fights breaking out across the map. I had one run where i stumbled across endless dead bodies, just gathering the loot up, and when it finally came for me to leave i got blindsided by a blink. However this left a bitter taste in mouth it didn't stop me from wanting more. There are still a few bugs in the game, some times the game will randomly close down on me and come up with a script that i have to abort. Other bugs are in game, where ghouls will be in the walls and invisible, yet they can still attack, and many times i have tried to use a medkit/food and it has taken the item but not healed or satisfied my hunger. Nothing really to stop my enjoyment though as i never had a problem with supplies through all of my runs. It is a great game though for the price you pay and something to fill in a void for a few hours when you aren't too busy. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks really promising. Even at its current stage, it is plenty addictive. The player has Home Base.An expedition could take anywhere from 5 to 20 minutes, which is almost entirely up to the player.Main Interests:1. Farming/Hunting2. Branching Self-Upgrade3. Base Upgrade (Limited Slots)4. Crafting (Cooking/Bullets/Healing Items)5. Weapon Modding6. Inventory Management (Space and Weight)7. Needs Management (Hunger/Thirst/Sleep/Toxicity)8. Braving Danger/Being Cautious (You die easily without armor, which you can't get early. There is no real penalty to dying though, except wasted time.)There are quite a lot of quests, which help players a lot at the beginning. _childDocuments_.review: The game has a pretty addictive game loop and it got me a solid amount of play time. for the price point I'd say its a good buy if you enjoy this style of game.As of writing, the main thing that has stopped me playing is largely lack of content.The first area (forest) feels threatening, has lots of places of interest and there are enough quests to keep a sense of purpose in engaging in that (real fun) game loop.After this things change - the story element quickly fades around the swamp area, it feels like it was not complete. Some of the zones also feel pretty empty. The Swamp and makeshift camp felt mostly empty with few points of interest.Pacing also flat-lines. The game starts of hard, its brutal. And there are a lot of things you need to collect and gather for upgrades: supplies are scarce and weight limits force hard decisions- but after a point the challenge dissipates and you tend to be ignoring most items you come across, with plenty of food and liquids stored up and mega backpacks - this changes the core game loop into a more looter shooter than the opening loop, which felt more "this war of mine" to me.Finally, it wasn't enough to stop me, but could be a problem for others - but a solid UX/UI pass is needed to make interacting with the game more intuitive. _childDocuments_.review: When the stars line up, this game is exactly what I want out of it: a top-down 2D stalker with weapon customization, inventory management and some fun fire fights. Putting together your guns is fun, you got plenty of options to experiment with different type of gunplay (though snipers have a clear advantage being able to shoot enemies before they can even see you.)But in the current balance of the game, it becomes a rather frustrating game the longer your play. Mid-to-late game enemies turn into bullet sponges that will absolutely shred your fancy armor (that you looted off a dead mob likely or bought) in seconds, despite it being identical to the enemy. Might as well wear paper to protect yourself cause your armor will break in a few hits and cost a lot to repair. And it happens a lot when exploring the Mall area and Zakov City. You turn the corner only to immediately die to a single salvo of guns from an enemy that requires basically an endless supply of grenades to kill efficiently. You kill a boss for a mission, only to be immediately gunned down by a sniper you can't see in the dark who uses a starter gun, yet it feels like they're shooting you with 120mm APFSDS rounds.After 30 hours on this game, I'm basically putting it down hoping for a balance pass on the armor of higher tier enemies & players.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll admit it, when I looked at this game and saw the Tarkov-esque gameplay loop, I was scared. The idea that you make one wrong button press and you've lost 100% of what you brought in and grabbed Is what pushes me away from those types of games, but ZERO Sievert doesn't punish players that hard. Every time you load into a level, you will come out with the equipment you didn't use (or all of it, tbh I wasn't paying that much attention to my inventory). If you die, you simply pop back out by the conductor and are free to go back into it. If you escape, then you get to keep what you grabbed and make progress to expanding your capabilities. The game is willing to let you gut most weapons, and the modification system is straight and to the point, this part gives you x accuracy and y recoil, and that's it. And from what I've gotten and from the look of the screenshots, this game is willing to give you the pieces necessary to make your gun look like it came from terminator if you wanted it to. Granted, I only have 1 hour of playtime as of writing this, but this is honestly very fun! I seriously recommend giving this a look if your interested in a soviet apocalypse.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright so lets hit the obvious points first:This game is Tarkov, with Stalker's environment, in singleplayer. Given the quantity of mods for STALKER, that should inform you about just how many people wanted to play something akin to this.This game is quite relaxing, while still having the high stress moments of Tarkov mixed in. You'll start looting a bandit only for his two friends to pull up and start shooting. The AI, while not relentless(mostly), will find advantageous positions and outflank your cover if you aren't aggressive enough. Mutants and animals are pretty lethal, you'll need to be both sparing with reloads and accurate with your shoots. The Art is appreciably unique. I quite enjoy the looks of the locations, and the little animations for healing/eating/shooting are *chefs kiss*.This is a game that will make you play slow. If you are a Hotheaded FPS junkie this game will repeatedly kill you, over and over. It rewards you for taking your time, for choosing your positions.TLDR: Singleplayer Tarkov with Stalker Elements, Excellent Gameplay, Excellent Artstyle, only missing component would be multiplayer(I can absolutely see this being S-tier if it arrives).

_childDocuments_.review: Solid so far - Keep in mind it's an Early Access game, and there's still some room for polish.Tarkov-like, but not quite as much depth - which is mostly a good thing. It's nice to have a less intense, single-player experience that doesn't demand as much from my PC.A few quick feedback notes for development (as of 11/25/22):Lag can be a major issue in the game world, particularly around radiation anomalies. It's a bit variable, but I notice it worst around .The weight of equipped guns does not apply to your character, allowing for occasional looting exploits.At certain points in the , I would randomly start taking damage and bleeding. I didn't see any enemies around, and wasn't able to see any "traps," but if I'm missing anything here let me know.Finally, a couple of subjective notes I have on what I think would make the game a bit more fun:First, increasing dialogue options would be nice. I'm an RPG fan, and while I get that this game isn't trying to be a full-on roleplaying game, I would personally enjoy it if there were some branching dialogue options and/or more NPCs had dialogue.Secondly, while I enjoy the semi-randomly generated maps on each raid, I think it could use some fine tuning. The extraction points often don't seem to fit well with where I was dropped off, so that I end up either having to bug out early, or I have to backtrack almost all the way across the map. Also, I think it would be interesting if not all features were present every time you went to a map - it's a bit of a double-edged sword, since it's nice to know I can always find certain features on a map, but I simultaneously feel like it saps at the potential variety in experience.Bottom line, I think for most people this game is worth it for $15, but if you're a big fan of Tarkov-like experiences and want to support a game in its development cycle, then I can easily see you getting your $20 worth out of this.

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, this is a problematic little game that has won me over with its charming pixel graphics. It's fun to play, but all these mechanics are just working against the player for no reason and it's bogging the game down as well. I think the devs just didn't have any game design experience, and if they do have it, then they have zero UX experience. I'll just note the main points here. Inventory system is not as good as it could be. Combat feels good but there are some enemies (mainly boars) that are too overpowered if even one ever gets close to you (hitting with their asses and doing spins in place). Reputation system is good but it gets bogged down by enemies and friendlies being too hard to tell apart (you either risk your life getting close or kill friendlies and lose reputation). Base building makes zero sense. You should just be able to swap out modules without having to destroy the previous ones (what we just throw an entire gym away?). Also, for what reason do we need to have them as an item and then use the item but we have to install the module as a level 0 module first? What? Why can't I just click craft on the crafting table and it enables the installation of the module, and I can disable / enable them whenever? It's just adding unnecessary grind into the game and punishing the player for no reason.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the vibe of Stalker and Tarkov, but like something that is a bit more relaxed and single player than Tarkov, then this game has you covered. It's a great looter-shooter / extract shooter in a top down perspective with a very enjoyable core gameplay loop. Go into a raid, grab what you can, complete missions, extract. I can highly recommend the Hunter difficulty (drop everything on death) because I think it makes the game last a lot longer and be more enjoyable with high stakes, but there is A LOT of options to the difficulty (think like Project Zomboid level difficulty options) so you can play how you want to. Also, the game is a masterclass in player-friendly design. At the home base you can instantly teleport between vendors so you don't have to walk everywhere. Carrying too much loot in missions will slow you down, but you can move normally even if overweight in the base. This game was perfect for me because I was looking for a less intense, single person Tarkov and that's basically exactly what it is, but it has it's own charm and some of the supernatural elements from something like STALKER. Best game of the year in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR because ♥♥♥♥ reading my awful grammar: It's a great, addictive game that lacks multiplayer or a real sense of tangible risk.Yeesh this game is addictive. So much potential for an indie title. Picking it up for the few hours I have, I can almost perfectly see the direction they're going with this and it's very promising. Pretty basic at it's core, survival looter shooter that wears it's inspiration quite apparently on it's sleeve. You have STALKER and EFT unabashedly wrapped up in a roguelite twin-stick pixel-art package. For the uninitiated STALKER is a game where you survive a nuclear post-apocalyptic Russian exclusion zone, fighting off rogue factions, paramilitaries, the actual military and local mutated wild-life (maybe humans). EFT on the other hand is a game that wears STALKERs inspiration on it's sleeve but in a different way, taking it's inventory management queues, more than anything. Instead you're in a more post economic apocalypse Russia where PMCs and bandit scavs duke it out for valuables and guns. And your goal as a PMC is to get in and get out with the most valuables through the extraction zones in each map. Zero Sievert takes a mixed inspirational approach, where it brings the theme and enemy palette from STALKER into a gameloop more akin to tarkov. You run in get all the loot run out and build a stash and hideout to reflect your playtime. The biggest difference here is that Zero Sievert has currently no multi-player mode to show for, which brings me to my next issue.The biggest gripe you could have with this game is it's lack of tangible risk. The most you might experience is a lucrative raid soured by a few well placed hunters near your extraction zone, or rad sickness throwing three bleeds at you when you're out of meds. Ultimately you'll just walk right back into the same map re-randomized like nothing ever happened. You'll have no loot taken, no detriment to armor or weapons, or even health, just a loss of in-game time.
