_childDocuments_.review: TLDR- The game is one part Stalker and one part Escape from Tarkov, but in 2d pixelart. It has limited content and some issues making certain progression useless, but is not a bad 20-30hrs for the price. If you like STALKER or Tarkov, you will like this.The Game- If you have ever played STALKER or Tarkov, then you know what this is. You go into a map, loot up, complete quests, and extract back to your base. There are humans, environmental hazards, and monsters looking to murder your poor character. Unlike Tarkov, the only thing lost on death is time, and the game is completely singleplayer. While it may have a Tarkov theme, it is much closer to STALKER in terms of gameplay loop. When you die, you just reset to the beginning of your raid and do not lose anything but time.Aesthetics- The 2d pixelart is great. Simple enough to understand what everything is, but still stylish. The sound design kept me completely on edge, even though I was playing a giant-headed pixelman. Not me obviously, but when Jeff plays the game, he jumps when a monster screams across the map, especially if it is dark and rainy. Probably because he has sheet ammo and does not know how to run backwards.  The aesthetics are an A+ for me.Mechanics- The game has a lot of in-depth mechanics to fully explore. Each weapon can be upgraded to have better ergonomics, recoil, flashlights, lasers, accuracy, and even scope mechanics. The scope system is implemented well with advantages and disadvantages, despite it being a top-down game. Different bullets either have high damage/low recoil or high recoil/ high armor penetration. However, there is a ton of room for improvement/balance. Basically, you have to have knowledge of Tarkov's armor and penetration system to really understand wtf 45 pen means, and the game does not really give you much info. I tried to explain it to Jeff, and he just got lost, but that is not anything new. Just take the highest pen bullets you have when you go into the mall. Also, the recoil and ergo stats of the guns do not make a big difference. I more mod guns to look cooler on my character. Jeff said A, but I say B.Content and "story"- Well, this is where Jeff says I need to give the game a pass because it is in early-access. BUTTT, the game is obviously lacking a lot of content. I mean, I am at max trader level, and have the second best armor in the game at 18 hours. I need some more stuff to do and reason to progress, but it is early access and maybe there is a little more content ready to come my way. The content is a mixed bag. Many quests, just like Tarkov, are like "blah blah blah, collect 30 nails, 3 crystals, and the magic of Christmas." There are some great quests, like kill giant monster that keeps murdering everyone or defeat a horde of ghouls. But mostly, you are going to be roaming around to find the one stupid friggin golden zibbo that refuses to spawn. Jeff does not know my pain, but anyone who has played Tarkov does. C+ (the + is an early access handicap).The need to get more bling- After the first three hours, the game gets really easy on keeping your character alive and getting "chadded out" as the youngins say. I found the some of the best attachments randomly after defeating the easiest boss. The quest givers seem all too happy to give me full durability weapons. The game balances weapon progression by making all guns found on the map low durability, basically making them jam so your character dies with his wee wee in his hand. You can jump through a bunch of hoops to craft repair kits, but you never need to cause the quest givers just give you full durability weapons like its candy, and we stopped giving Jeff candy after the "incident". Good armor takes a minute to unlock, and it makes you feel powerful when you get it, probably the better part of the progression. C+Base Building- Well, I am 18 hrs in, and I have had zero want of building up my base. I have basically unlimited money, and at no point did I think it was worth to go through the tedious task of gathering junk to fix a problem I never had. Jeff says he likes to build the bed cause it looks cozy, but I think it is just cause his bed is crap IRL. Well, like why would I spend an hour to gather items to build a kitchen when food/water has never been a problem? The game needs an overhaul to make the base good. It tries to copy Tarkov, but it just makes zero sense to grind a copious mount of junk for a game where you lose nothing when you die. D-The Fighting- Okay, I have a confession. Jeff recommended the game to me because he saw a streamer play it for an hour. Apparently, most of them had no idea you could just run backwards away from wolves so you don't die. The monsters are simple, but all different. I won't spoil what they all do, but Jeff is super scared by them all, even more than the... and I quote "mean hunter dudes." Fighting people in the game feels like a tactical experience. You have to pie corners, jiggle peak, snipe, ect. Well, the enemy has good AI that will take cover, push, search for you, yell stuff when you ambush them. The only ♥♥♥♥♥♥ part is that monsters will spawn in walls, making it where you cannot see them, then just kill you when you get close enough to the wall of death. Besides that one bug which only really applies indoors, this is where the game shines. A-Areas to Improve- Jeff told me "If you know so much, why don you make a better game?" Well, Jeff, I am glad you asked for my opinion. I love to talk about all the amazing ideas for the perfect game, and let me share them. I really think the game needs to make quests a little less grindy for the "collect 200 items." Like, okay fine, I have to do some mundane stuff early on, but most of the quests are like that. I want to see more narrative driven content, which the game does well when it does it. Also, make the ergo and recoil stats actually matter. This is not a game where if I do not put my crosshair on the head of a tiny pixel controlled by another overweight gaming manchild, I die. Making the character have a bigger spread for full-auto bigboy guns makes sense for having attachments matter. Also, make clean food less common in-raid and with traders, make full durability guns a rare big reward for actually difficult quests, limit the 0-60% durability repair kits to rare crafts, basically, give me a reason to upgrade the hideout and craft. Make me care about more than maximizing roubles per raid. Make radiation an actual hazard. For the love of god, make the game co-op!.... I could see giving me a penalty on death as a way to balance it, but some might call that ImMeRsiOn bREaKinG. Just do something to make surviving a challenge. Lastly, grenades and rocket launchers would be nice, even Jeff agrees.I always hate playing single-player games in early access. I feel like I will play the half finished game, then never touch it again. The game seems to have a lot more content planned, and is fun enough where I might pick it up again after I get bored with Tarkov's next wipe. Give me a co-op mode, and if you would just give it to me, I'd be nicer to Jeff.Rant over

ZERO Sievert is a post apocalyptic game set in a fictitious part of Russia.

The bunker ZERO Sievert: here you can accept new quests, talk to NPC, trade with vendors, manage your equipment and improve your base.

Maps are procedurally generated to ensure good replayability. The main points of interest will then be in a different location each time, but there is loot in everywhere in the map so be prepared to explore!

There are more than 100 different items to loot and you can use them to craft new items, upgrade your own base or sell them.

All this surrounded by a post-apocalyptic atmosphere that I will try to create as best I can.

name: Green Hell VR
detailed_description: How long can you survive in the Amazon rainforest? Green Hell VR is the most complex and authentic survival game for VR. The game faithfully recreates the dangerous conditions of the Amazon jungle. Alone and stranded, you will never feel safe. To survive, you have to face your weaknesses. Maintaining hunger, thirst, fatigue and mental health is going to be an integral part of your journey. Wild animal attacks and tropical diseases could strike you down at any time and out of nowhere if you are not prepared. Since you won’t get any help from the outside world, you need to craft your tools and weapons, learn how to build shelters, and heal nasty wounds. Story You are Jake Higgins, a famous anthropologist, who is thrown deep into the emerald and impenetrable Amazonian rain forest. The green hell. Surrounded by predators with only your trusty smartwatch, backpack, and the survival guide you grabbed just before leaving home, you will follow the familiar voice of a loved one through this endless and inhospitable jungle, unveiling bit by bit how you got there in the first place. What you discover will be worse than what you fought so hard against to survive. Realistic VR Mechanics Crafting - you find yourself lost in the Amazon with almost nothing, so knowing how to craft crafting is your best friend. The VR experience makes crafting even more authentic as you need to find the right elements and combine them to make tools, weapons, bandages, and more. Building - construct yourself a safe place to spend the night as sleeping on bare ground in the jungle may not be the best idea. Build a temporary shelter or find a perfect location, gather materials, and construct your base to cook what you found during your exploration, and to protect yourself from dangers lurking in the shadows. Healing - inspect your limbs, bandage wounds, and extract parasites. Experiment with different treatments to survive in the wild. You will discover plants and their medical potential by mixing them and making a brew. Be careful though, some ingredients don’t go together, and some... well, you’ll see. Food sources - you can hunt your dinner down, or you can choose not to kill animals. There are tasty and nutritious fruits like coconuts or bananas, a lot of unknown mushrooms, and plenty of plants, bulbs, and nuts to discover. These may be the sources of healthy proteins, carbohydrates, and fats, or they can have opposite effects! Be careful and stay healthy to survive. VR Was Made For Games Like This! With its vast mechanics based on natural movement and physics, and almost no visible UI and realistic gameplay elements such as your backpack and the map, Green Hell VR is highly immersive and gives you an opportunity to learn survival techniques in a harsh, demanding environment. Good luck! Unique Features Setting: deadly yet beautiful Amazon rainforest Human-made structures to explore Realistic body inspection Multitude of different animal and plant species Environment and body condition impact on your sanity Day and night cycle with various weather conditions Moving story rooted in modern reality Ranged and melee combat

It makes game is even bigger and feel very immersive. -It has more items and building options and a lots of additional props than standalone version which makes game rich. -Facing enemies is much challenging. -Overall play style is much realistic than quest. -The bag is free space which is very cool and nice But it's different than Into the radius. Also it's a big minus for Omni VR Treadmill and Natural Locomotion users. it's very simple thing. I hope devs fix it. - Rain graphic is really BAD. You did really well in the Quest version. the raining feels very real in it. but rain in this version, it's like an overlay on screen, not 3D at all very flat. it ruins whole game graphic fidelity. - Crafting is NOT good. Quest version is 300% better. it's very immersive and  intuitive in that version. but This one has much detail option to craft but process is worse than Quest version... _childDocuments_.review: Let Me first start off with the issues, since that's what everyone will read, including the devs and they'll have more motivation to address them, since I will remove them when they're fixed. I'll add things to this and my wishlist as I play the game so that others can reference them. Following that, I will post a wishlist of improvements that I don't consider bugs, but are quality of life.Followed by my impressions of the game.Issues/Bugs-------------------1. The smooth turning mechanic only seems to apply to the midline into the southern quadrants of the control stick. about midway and higher you do not turn, even if your stick is all the way to the edge. The way the index controllers are held, this feels like the controllers are not picking up input, especially when turning the direction of "inward" on the controller. this is extremely frustrating, and I would ask that you change it so that input in the northern quadrants of the control stick, also register as turns left or right when past a certain value on the x axis. 2. Occasionally, the walkie talkie will duplicate on your chest at roughly a 90 degree angle.3. Swapping to and from performance mode crashes the game without a warning. If a restart is needed, a prompt should show. 4. Swinging the machete too quickly passes through objects you intend to cut. 5. vignette settings seem to not save sometimes.Wishlist of improvements----------1. Make turn speed a clamped float with a max value about 1.5-2x that of your current fastest setting, rather than 3 discrete options. Since it is both a movement and vision controlling option and these are key to the game, I would like to fine tune my turn speed.2. Make the machete able to attach to the side of the backpack, over the shoulder, or at least face downwards. having it face back is awkward, and truth be told, I'd rather store it over one of my shoulders to be grabbed.3. Make the subtitles or walkie talkie dialogue attach to  the walkie talkie, in a grey box similar to how you pick dialogue options. That way if I want to read the subtitles, I can, against a nice contrast background instead of watching it jitter all over the place as I look around.4. Allow index users to select dialogue options with the walkie talkie hand thumb trackpad and press trigger to confirm. Walkie talkies are one handed for a reason.5. Index individual finger tracking. I want to flip off the natives and post to reddit to harvest butthurt.6. Add option menu to tutorial. It took me 5 minutes of fumbling to figure out that tapping the position button would bring up the menu, which I needed to increase turn speed because medium was slow, slow was turtle, and fast is not fast enough.Opinion/Review--------------Now that that's out of the way, let me get on with my opinion of the game.Right off the bat there was solid effort put into this port, which is extremely encouraging.It features:- Drop over shoulder looting and storage- a grabbable backpack -  IK driven arms- Picked up objects have physics and collide with other objects, and seem to somewhat simulate weight.- custom player driven mechanics for items (i.e, a handheld fireplow that you grab the stick and work back and forth to make an ember) very cool. - swing the machete at small trees to chop them down, and again at large sticks to break into smaller sticks- Release crafting items over schematics to add to recipe- hold food to mouth to eat- touch watch to change display (awesome)- draw on a whiteboard and eraseThe Graphics are good, but poorly optimized, which I don't blame the devs of the port for, or really, the original devs all that much for. It was made to look beautiful on regular flat screen, the tall and dense canopies of a rain-forest is taxing given the expansive nature of the map.That said, I have a 5900x and a 3080 FE running on the index, and I have the resolution on high, the quality on the lowest setting, and the textures at medium, and it still stutters occasionally. Any improvements to this would be greatly appreciated, as many don't have the stomach I have for VR and stuttering is EXTREMELY disruptive to enjoying an experience. The environment and ambiance are amazing. It makes me excited for what can be possible when hardware can render much more complicated scenes in VR. The tutorial is nice and well needed.The dialogue isn't the best, and there are some spelling and grammar mistakes on some of the notebook entries, but that's minor.  I am very excited for the multiplayer to this and additional polish and optimization, if it's within the devs abilities. I have noticed devs are reading reviews, responding and have noticed patches releasing.Because of all of this, I am endorsing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Green Hell is one of the most impressive Flat 2 VR conversions. After quite a few hours into it already, I can safely say that Green Hell VR is an absolute MUST PLAY (especially if you enjoy survival games).Green Hell is the full flatscreen game with no compromises (unlike the Quest version) - no content stripped or elements watered down (though multiplayer and the DLC content are coming later). Each flatscreen interaction has been completely redesigned for VR. It really is cool to see just how far a flatscreen game can be redesigned to feel like it was always a VR game originally and is a new bar for future flatscreen 2 VR ports.Let’s talk about graphics and immersion… I don’t think I’ve ever felt so immersed in another world in VR (maybe save Subnautica?). The graphics are absolutely jaw-dropping if you have the PC to run it at higher settings and it causes you to be completely sucked into that world - an open world you just have complete freedom to go, do and build anything.Note: The PC requirements are very high. Expect around an RTX 3070 to be min requirements if you don’t want to use ASW / motion smoothing (highly recommend VR Perf Toolkit with sharpening at 100% too). There’s also still a tolerable amount of “jank” still that you’ll need to deal with, but imo doesn’t take too much away from the incredible experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review in March 2024. I saw the terrible Steam reviews and I almost didn't buy this game. However, there was a Steam sale and I got this game at 50% off along with the flat screen Green Hell version. So I decided to compare the two versions. I haven't played the flat screen version yet at the time of this review.**Gameplay thoughts**The VR controls and the crafting system are really great and I'm really enjoying my time so far with the game. I got covered in bugs and my inner voices started yelling at me to give up but I kept playing and I made a fire and a nice shelter and even got myself some cooked food. It really feels like I am in the woods alone, losing my mind, and the only hope I have is my own. I spent $12 on the game and I think so far it will be a nice investment.**Performance thoughts**My PC specs:CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 5700XGPU: RX 6700 XTHMD: Valve IndexDefault settings gave me HIGH resolution and MEDIUM graphics settings along with Performance Mode ON.I played survival mode just to see how it performed so I could tinker with the graphics settings as I expected the game not to run that good, it ran fine. I got frame times between 15-18 ms on average. I noticed if I tried to boost the HMD resolution to VERY HIGH then I would see some stutters so I kept it at HIGH for my first play session. This allows running the Valve Index at 90 Hz by reprojecting 45 Hz to 90 Hz.What are my thoughts so far? Why is there so much hate in the reviews? The game engine Green Hell uses is Unity and I have played a number of Unity games in VR such as 7 Days to Die and Ultimate Fishing VR. Therefore, I can conclude that this game runs like all the other Unity VR games, not good but not horrible. You need to use mid tier settings due to Unity being Unity. If you like to tinker you can play around with Unity graphics mods, but the main issue is the way Unity handles draw culling, it is not optimized and this is most notable in VR titles that use Unity.It looks like a Unity VR game, Unity does a poor job in drawing scenes in VR. It is an engine designed for flat screen.Many people are complaining that this version is not getting the same level of updates as the flat screen version is, and although that is disappointing it isn't a big deal, get both versions on a Steam sale. I'm looking forward to playing flat screen Green Hell but I am loving this experience. Many negative reviews are unfair in my opinion.I've played Minecraft in VR and that makes me sick, this session didn't make me sick. The only reason I got out of the game was because my controllers died.*AFTER COMPLETING THE STORY MODE ~35 hours*I played some survival mode and then finished the story mode. In that time with the game I did run into a few performance issues. The magic fix for me is making sure all 16 cores are enabled in Task Manager->Affinity for GHVR.exe this will remove issues with CPU stuttering. For some reason, all cores are not enabled by default for this game. I also recommend using the OpenVR FSR mod that enables FSR for this game. With these two fixes the game runs pretty good for the entire story mode!

_childDocuments_.review: Green Hell VR is an incredibly immersive virtual reality survival game, those familiar with the original game of Green Hell will no doubt be able to imagine how challenging and entertaining this game can be in VR!Watch my first life in survival mode here: With amazing graphics that can go very high if you have hardware that is strong enough you will immediately feel at home in these beautiful jungle environments,but not without dangers of course, but for every danger there is a means to defend yourself, and all this in virtual reality is quite a job that you do not want to give up so easily.In story mode, you take on the role of Doctor Jake Higgins, an anthropologist who has been studying the Amazon for the past three years.Mia, his wife, who is also present will leave shortly after the start for a local tribe to observe them carefully, when it becomes clear that her safety is no longer guaranteed you as Jake will have to go to where she should be present ,throughout the gameplay, the game will also teach you all the necessary steps and basic functions so that you can explore and trade independently with the objects that are available fairly soon after the start.Green Hell VR is a virtual reality game like no other. You will have to pay attention to your surroundings.Watch my first session of story mode here: Memorize landmarks to avoid getting lost in the deep jungle, learn to distinguish poisonous plants from plants that can save your life, watch where you step because you are always meters away from deadly dangers! Just like when exploring food you will always have to be on guard and be prepared for any poisoning so that you can quickly undo this, it will also make it 'easy' to find out which wild foods are edible and nutritious is.During day and night cycles, live and breathe close to the awe-inspiring rainforest in this adrenaline-fueled VR adventure. Green Hell VR invites you to really immerse yourself in it, but it is still recommended to play the story mode before you throw yourself into the survival mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Green Hell VR is easily the best flat-to-VR port money can buy. In this review, I will go over the gameplay, visuals, and physics. Beginning with physics, I must admit I am very impressed. I would put the physics here juuuuust below saints and sinners, for the simple reason that objects become almost weightless when you aren’t holding them, and when you force grab an object it can send objects near it into the stratosphere (for example, if I grab a stick that is behind another stick, the other stick will be sent far, far away). However, the game has a very impressive weight system for objects in your hands, in which they really do feel heavy. Obviously I have to mention the thing that either sells or doesn’t sell a game to me: hand collision. I’m going to keep it simple. Hand collision is there, and it’s good. Visuals: demanding. Very much so. Thankfully, I use Virtual Desktop’s extrapolation, so I can basically ‘cheat’ my way into 120 fps with my 1060. Still, I have to have most of my settings at medium with performance mode enabled. Devs, you could either try to optimize the game, or lower all of the settings so ultra is medium (it’s a stupid idea but would result in a lot less complaining) aside from the performance side, the visuals are fantastic and immersive. You really notice how good the visuals are when you are constantly paying attention to see danger. That sort of thing in games is my favourite, when you aren’t just staring at a map. My one issue is some rocks have holes in them that causes the renderer to act strange. Gameplay-wise the game really shines. The original game was difficult and had a really good difficulty curve, but VR really makes you feel like you are learning how to survive in the jungle. The interactions with the items like throwing a spear, crafting, and especially starting a fire feel great.A few other things I should mention are the remarkable sound design and really good menu music. Overall, if you can run it you have to play it. It’s a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Played on the Valve  HMD/controllers.Please note, at the time of writing this, finger tracking for the Index is not supported.Green Hell VR is an open world survival game, ported from the flatscreen version by Publisher Incuvo (who previously ported Layers of Fear VR).I will start with , as I know its a question a lot of going to be asking about. The game manages to maintain a lot of the visuals from the desktop version and is quite well optimized. That is not to say you wont need good hardware to run it maxed out. I spent a bit of time playing with settings and so forth, and this is what I have found.Running with a 3090/12900k, Index (@90Hz) with SteamVR SS set at its default of 150%, the game needs to be toned down a bit to hold 90fps. God rays and ambient occlusion are very intensive and need to be turned off if you care about a consistent frame rate. I used 'High' res, and 'Very High' graphics, and moved up the sliders for draw/shadow distance to about 60%, this was the limit of keeping the game held at 90fps. The game wasnt terrible to play fully maxed out, as it stuck to 45fps and only certain types of movement (smooth turning) were unpleasant. And I do just mean, not terrible - so not great either - but it was better than trying to nudge up settings a little which would have my fps bouncing up and down from 45-90. As a further experiment, I found that turning AO to 'medium' while maxing out everything else allowed me to play *mostly* at 60fps (120Hz), but again, more than a few fps wobbles and Id just rather a solid FPS.Graphics menu (and settings used for 90fps):Dont worry too much about the fact that a 3090 isnt able to play this maxed out, here is a side by side of what my 90fps settings looked like against maxed out settings - And on a speculatory front, if the flagship (just months away) of the next gen is 60-70% faster, it will run this thing maxed out.As far as other hardware is concerned. I think Pascal is probably not going to cut it, maybe a 1080ti with very cut down settings (incl Steam VR SS). Since Turing was only a little better, 2080/ti is it for that, again with very cut down settings. Those on a 3070 or better should be able to run the game decently from middling settings (depending on your HMD res). I know some wont be pleased with that, but thats what it is and I think its reasonable for the visuals.Other than God rays and AO, the 'resolution' setting was the next most intensive option - so try a notch down on that if you are having performance issues. options:It supports smooth loco, teleport, and has comfort dials for different movements. Nice to see this. The game can also be handily calibrated (such a simple option, why all games dont do it I dont know) from a button press (hold), to recenter you and adjust for seated play. is excellent, I had no trouble believing I was in the Amazon! Plenty of detail, from the rustling bushes to the wildlife, you felt on edge and that you-vs-nature that you want from this type of experience.The game by all accounts seems to be an excellent port. Its content rich and those seeking a survival style game like The Forest etc will be right at home here. Im still getting into it, and should pay more attention to the prompts as I spent 10 minutes gathering palm leaves (why does a basic shelter need 26 of them and not use any other big fine leaves?! I think the devs are in bed with big Palm leaf - actually maybe even literally lol the bed also needs palm leaves) which I was dragging back 1 in each hand til I realised you could attach them together to carry ><; Also, small foul not being able to hurl a rock at a snake :(Green Hell VR is a fun time and well worth the price of admission.I got the game free from  VR curator group.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick and simple: Beautiful environment, fantastic gameplay, HEAVILY CPU bound (frame timing does not become adequate for a non-reprojected experience without at least a Ryzen 7 5800x, would recommend an even more powerful CPU)Update: Playing at forced half refresh rate of 120hz or 144hz yields a fairly stable relatively stutter free experience after the starting camp area, if you are willing to deal with the cost of high reprojection (50%+), artifacts, and ghosting. The character model hands were particularly disorienting. With this, I was even able to max the settings, and the visuals did look stunning. That being said, not even with the resolution harshly lowered in game and in Steam settings, and with all the graphics settings set to low could I get a smooth native 80fps experience. You basically have to use ASW or motion smoothing. It is the only way to play the game acceptably without incessant stutters, and actually looking good graphically. The gameplay is outstanding and the environment is very immersive. I will likely keep playing despite the performance issues and disappearing items bugs. The game gets a loose recommendation for doing most things right, but be prepared for bugs and poor performance.Original: The game performance is literal dog water. They need to update the system specs on the store page, because it is a complete lie as currently listed. At modest medium settings (the default), and even the lowest settings, I can't get the game to hold 80 fps on my valve index with a RTX 3080, Ryzen 7 3700x, and 32GB 3200Mhz RAM system. The "best" (using the term loosely) experience I got was with forced motion smoothing at 120hz, but the experience was still jittery and I got sick after an hour of gameplay, and I'm a 3 year VR veteran. The actual gameplay seems decent, but damn, it needs serious optimization for me to recommend. It also seems to be quite CPU bound as well. CPU frametimes are peaking constantly to 16ms+ while GPU frametimes are around 9ms at medium to low settings. I don't even think you'd have a good experience with a 4090 either.Maybe on top of optimization, more graphics options could help? Specifically, shadow resolution would be nice to edit. I would bring that way down to improve performance, or the ability to reduce the resolution of certain textures, as to not have to downscale the overall resolution to try and edge out a bit more performance without making the whole image look like a pixelated mess, which didn't seem to help anyway. Just a couple suggestions, but the performance overall definitely needs work.

_childDocuments_.review: This game WOULD be awesome except for one absolutely infuriating user interface choice that actually breaks the game. just like in the PC version of the game, your health, compass, stats, etc are tracked on your watch. you select various modes on the watch by tapping it with your finger. also like the PC version, you will need to sleep in order to replenish your energy, otherwise you will pass out in the mud and get covered in parasitic worms. the problem is, in order to sleep you have to select the sleeping screen on your watch by tapping the screen with your finger, then hold your finger to the face of the watch while a meter fills up to trigger the sleep action. but since the game cant differentiate between tapping the watch face, and holding your finger still against the watch face, you will spend an infuriating amount of time trying to go to sleep in a bed, or hammock while the watch just keeps cycling through screens endlessly instead of triggering the sleep function. this means, you cant avoid passing out in the mud and being plagued by parasitic worms and infections that guarantee you have no possibility of survival. you are lucky if after 15 minutes of struggling with the UI you get to sleep. much more likely, you will simply pass out, spend 5 minutes trying to sleep while the character you are playing keeps telling you how tired they are, before passing out again.so one of the most essential core game mechanics simply does not have functional controls, and while fixing this broken User interface issue would have been as simple as adding a button push on a controller to differentiate between the two inputs, the developers of this port apparently just never got around to caring enough about their game to fix it in the last year since it launched. it is that sort of unforgivably lazy failure to make a functional user interface that makes this game ultimately unplayable. which is a shame because it has so much potential otherwise. but if you want to experience this game, buy the flat panel version, and NEVER give this dev team money for the VR version that they clearly only slapped together as a quick cash grab.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: 7/4/2024 Full Review after completion: everything I said below was true. This is a great game. I would rate it an 8.5/10. The best survival game in VR. One of the 10 best VR games I have ever played!Here is my full video review: ----- Original Review Below: You can view my tips & tricks for beginners to Green Hell VR here: I'm honestly surprised by the negative reviews. If you like survival type games and VR, this is a must buy. In my opinion, it's one of the best survival games in VR (if not the best). Obviously, it's not perfect though. It does indeed have optimization issues and that is the biggest thing holding this game back. However, it's still very much playable and as long as you don't mind lowering graphical settings, it can be played at 90 fps (I did increase draw distance though because I hate pop-in).This game is challenging on story mode, Welcome To The Jungle difficulty (normal). However, you can try the easier modes or challenge yourself with the even harder modes or just go for the survival mode of the game (no story). I have died a ton already. WARNING: you may want to pick up a frog and kiss it, but just resist all temptation. I'm sadly and unashamedly speaking from personal experience. This is a very dense jungle map. There's lots of vegetation and animals and dangers all around. The amount of things you can interact with is really quite astonishing and the amount of things that can kill you as well. Watch out for ants!There's also lots of stuff to craft. You can make all sorts of tools & weapons, from medicine, to tents, to torches, etc. You'll need to keep tabs on food, water, fire, & your sanity. The story keeps you invested in story mode to go out there and explore. The game looks beautiful. You can swim, climb, jump, & crouch. Game is running on the Unity Engine. On my RTX 3080, I was getting steady 90 fps at first, but then after passing out my fps dropped to a 45 fps. I'm not sure why that happened. You have full locomotion, teleportation, smooth, & snap turning options, along with comfort options. You can choose between camera oriented movement or controller oriented movement. You can play this game comfortably seated.Like I said, I think this is one of the best survival games in VR, if not the best. I haven't played it enough to properly score it, but I do heartily recommend it for survival fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Well.... now I have a 4080 this is just stunning in VR.  with my 2080 it was a blurry mess and I couldn't really play.Incuvo have done a decent job of translating this, VR interaction is still a difficult problem. It could certainly do with some more polish, but for the most part I'm enjoying it. There are only two main issues, firstly the pace of the game is WAY too fast for VR.  A minute in the game is about 2 seconds. I'm sure this is fine when you are whizzing around FPS style with a mouse, in VR it's really not ok.  It can take you three hours to cook breakfast and find a few nuts. Secondly, your protagonist should NEVER have gone to the jungle.  He's completely out of shape, can't climb a small rock, doesn't know how to make a grapple from wood, eats and drinks three times more than a body builder in a day but still struggles to run more than 50 yards. The base story and the protagonist are what they are, but Incuvo could have an adjustment slider for how fast things happen, this would make this a far more enjoyable experience. _childDocuments_.review: Quite a faithful VR conversion. Obviously doesn't include the recent updates to the flat version. It wasn't advertised to have multiplayer at launch, which seems a poor criticism from others. It also doesn't have spaceships in it....?Good atmosphere and soundscapes, good options for tweaking quality and motion settings so it can run on a range of pcs and to you preferred movement types etc. You will die a lot at the start, but the difficulty curve is nice and satisfying. Theres a good selection of difficulty levels and a custom setting you can define yourself too. This makes it much easier to learn the game and what you need to do to survive. The discord group is pretty good too.Running on an i5/rx580+(8gb) and using the settings automatically applied at the start of the game, runs pretty smoothly. Couple of small bugs, but the dev team are great at taking feedback. Will be upping the graphic settings to see how far my pc can handle, but its definitely playable on lesser graphics cards.Map size is large, and the game provides a short(ish) story mode and a survival mode. There are 4 save slots so you can have 4 games on different difficulties or whatever which is pretty useful. Getting used to the bag system is tricky. The use of a crafting table which you can place anywhere actually feels quite a nice way of crafting. It encourages a little organisation. If you don't have time to place the crafting table to be able to make yourself a bandage before you die, then you were always gonna die from that injury. Things get bad fast when you're injured, sick, poisoned, wounded, etc. Its a pretty fun game that of course has some tricky bits, but that makes it so much more satisfying when things go smoothly.This review was added on the day of release after approx 3hours of gameplay. It feels like I've only just started, no idea how 3hours already went by!Pros:-Feels a true and authentic VR build of the original game-Immersive-Looks pretty-Good map size and selection of craftable items-Crafting table feels a good solution to crafting items in VR-Feels really fun to play-Definitely one of those games thats easy to spend a few hundred hours playing -Well priced imoCons:-Small bugs likely to be corrected in future updates-When its dark, its too dark to see anything until moonrise, although, this is more an "its hard" complain-Health status/effects are really hard to read-If you don't play the story first, there's no tutorial for survival (although quite intuitive)-It seems difficult to place items in the backpack and select items accurately (it seems the pointing hand needs to be perpendicular to the bag when held which is a fairly unnatural hand position, so things often dont align very well).OVERALL: Good little game great for survival and exploration fans. _childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend Green Hell VR.  Yes, I do.  It's graphically beautiful, the story is interesting, and there's a lot of game here for the money.  That said, is Green Hell VR making full use of what VR has to offer?  Is Green Hell VR completely without faults? No, and, of course not.  What follows is a critical summary of some areas of the game that I think could be improved which would raise this from a Recommend to a Must Buy.- The backpack system is unimaginative, tedious, and lazy.  Rather than an immersive and interesting interaction in 3 dimensional space, it provides a simple point and click Tetris experience which is actually worse than keyboard and mouse.  There's no reason for developers to fall back on stagnated interaction paradigms like this when VR offers innumerable options for interfacing with the world.  At the very least, get rid of the pointer and make me physically grab the items out of the backpack.  The sorting is helpful.  The utility pockets are helpful.  The point and click nature of the interaction is abhorrent and we as VR  players should expect better.  VR developers should want to build better experiences than this.  There's enormous opportunity here, seize it.-  The crafting system is dull and boring.  Drop items onto a table, and if they can be combined, a holographic shell of the item will appear which you simply grip and grab.  There's no actual physical crafting here.  Just drag, drop, grab.  VR can be so much better than this.  Yes, it would be hard, but there's an opportunity to make a truly beautiful and engaging experience in the crafting and sadly, this table experience is no better than a keyboard + mouse.-  The game simply doesn't run well on a Valve Index.  There is an odd dark halo around the periphery of the vision, as well as a general feeling of poor performance.  These issues are not present on Quest 2 over Air Link.  I wish I could provide more explanation than that, but it's not my job to test the various headsets.  Put an Index on and play your game, you should be able to see what I see in a head to head comparison with the Quest 2. -  Smooth turning seems to tank the frame rate. -  Hand / arm interactions look to happen at something like 15 fps.  This could / should be super smooth, but isn't.Incuvo - what you have here is a great game, but it could be a masterpiece.  If you care about making your game stand out, consider watching this video from Mr Voice VR:He goes into depth about the shortcomings of VR games and I think Green Hell VR is not innocent here.  There's plenty of room for this game to grow and I for one would love to see changes that lean into VR, and away from boring interactions which are better served for mouse and keyboard.A critical review, yes, but only because I genuinely do like this game.  I hope this feedback is seen as constructive.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first played this game, I had quite a frustrating relationship with it. It should be noted, I never played Green Hell at all, and I got to say I had one hell of a time with this game. It is VERY hard, at first. The tutorial is a joke, bottom line. It teaches you how to build a fire and how to make a basic bandage... that's it. Nothing else. You are then dropped into the game where you are forced to learn everything by yourself.... and death is one of them. lol. One thing that was helpful to me is watching some tutorials on YouTube and the .Other than the frustrating game that is 'Green Hell', let's focus on the VR game. Well, I will say, this game has it's moments, but there are some issues.This game performs horribly. I run on a 2080 RTX and I had to turn down my SuperSampling settings to 70% and had to reduce game graphic options to medium/low and even still, the game would chug around 30-40FPS so I had to force Motion Smoothing on and, since I use the Valve Index, I put my headset on 80FPS to get a somewhat playable/smooth experience. It did take some time to get used to the framerate, but once I did, I had a fun time with this game.Next up, is the overall VR interaction. Most people on here complain about the crafting system vs the Quest version. In the Quest version you are able to craft on-the-fly by putting objects into each other while holding the trigger buttons which makes for a very immersive experience. However, in the Quest version, the number of craftable items are limited.In the PCVR version, the crafting mechanic is quite basic. You have to pull out a crafting table from your notebook and then place items onto it to craft stuff. It is basic. The reason why the devs chose this is because they wanted to get the PCVR version of the game as close to the original as possible, meaning most, if not all, craftable items from the original game are available in the PCVR version.A lot of people are also complaining about the lack of multiplayer/coop mode. The original has a coop mode that you are able to play with other people to survive in the Amazon. This VR version lacks that. There is no multiplayer... well yet it seems. The devs did say they are currently developing it. However, there is no word of when this feature will be done.Another thing to note, the DLCs/free updates from the original game are also not present in the VR version. HOPEFULLY, this will be added to the VR version. I would love to have a pet Capybara in VR :)Even though there are issues, I really enjoyed this game, once I got used to the performance and the crafting system. There is A LOT of content here and it literally took me ~30 hours to get through the game (granted, I did take my time and built a few bases). Other than story mode, there is a survival mode and a challenge mode which I will be playing also.Bottom line, if you are looking for a VR survival game AND have the hardware to run this game, get it! It has LOTS of content and multiplayer is on the way, according to the devs!

_childDocuments_.review: updated 6/19/2022I changed this to a thumbs down. I can deal with a lot of thing- bad graphics,bad controls,the occasional shut down and restart, bad optimization etc.... But I WILL not tolerate a game that won't save. I could of built 5 camps for as many times I have redone just the one camp. I trow in the towel and quit. I do not understand why Devs are not all over this with a hot patch. Others are having the same issue so it is game related issue. With the other issues the game is having, not being able to save is just too much. Good Luck if you buy this game as it is riddle with issues and a good chance you only have 50/50 chance to save. ********************************************************************************************************I normally don’t play/review games until 3-4 weeks after they have been released(Wish I would have now!!). But I could not wait to play Green Hell VR. As I always wanted to try Green Hell in VR mode.      First, I like to say, my hats off to Incuvo. They gave a valor effort in the making of Green Hell VR. As far as game play went, outside of having to restart the game a few times, the game ran good(In Story Mode). No major hiccups that would make the game unplayable. In survival mode though, lots of work to be done there(lots of issues that make the game unplayable/hard to progress).  Graphics aren’t top notch, but just where you expect them to be in a VR game. Sound on the other hand, was outstanding. Swinging tools was flimsy and at times hard to use(Not a deal breaker). Lots of funny graphic moments as well, body 90 degrees out in front of me, my arm coming out my back, objects flying far away, head in my chest, stuff like that. Of course the only way to fix it was to restart the game.   The issues I did experience are:1.	Turning was not smooth, more of a stutter step.--Made me dizzy a few times. 2.	Can we talk about the rain?--Ugg pretty rough.. Black lines falling from the sky make the game look bad. 3.	Swimming! Avoid altogether.--Only when you have to. 4.	Crafting table, all I can say is what a mess.--I put too many items on the table and when I went to grab the item off, everything flew everywhere. Not Cool!5.	Using the bow needs some work. Just point in the direction of the target and hope you hit it. Not any good way to aim. Crosshairs/dot should fix this issue. I will give you thumbs up for the blood trail though, made finding the animal I shot in the leg easier to find.  6.	CAN WE PLEASE MOVE THE BOOK OFF THE CHEST???--When aiming the bow, I grabbed  that book so many times. Died quite a few times over this.7.	Combat, forget about it. Yes you can fight them( but until you become good with the controls, it’s a little tough) but if your just working away on your camp and something sneak up on you, your dead. And the bow isn’t that accurate. Normally head shots kill most things in one shot, here your lucky to hit them unless your standing on their head. 8.	Kept dropping tools or weapons I was using due to the grip format of the controller. This should be on a trigger/pad button if you want to drop. 9.	The airport still need work, Items would fade in and out(disappear), rain inside of buildings, birds landing on air and had to restart game due to the game didn’t recognized that I had picked up the climbing gear. 10.	Navigating the backpack was a pain, at the bottom where all the items are hanging needs to be spaced down a little further, kept trying to pick the grapple when I was trying to get dry leaves, for that matter any where there was clutter, it was a pain. I did however like how the backpack expanded. Nice.11.	In survival mode(WTTJ), at the drug camp, the game would not save, the saving icon just kept going around and around. This got pretty frustrating, loosing progress all the time. I know you need to save on a regular bases, but not to see if it still works. Had to close out game completely and start from my last save. What is funny though, if you quit and went back to the main screen and reloaded, you spawn in on an empty flat field, you could run for miles.  12.	And I would have to say the biggest issue for me was the controls. Awkward and clumsy. Should be able to customize controls. It was tough in the beginning, and got a little better towards the end, but not something I would want to do for long periods of time.  I feel that a X-Box/Play Station controller option would be better. I feel this would go along ways to make the game better. In conclusion:  I will give Green Hell VR a thumbs up, but still needs lots of work. While story mode seemed fine, survival mode had a ton of issues. In it’s current state, I don’t see a lot a replay value,(due to the controller issues) but at lease worth trying if you were a fan of Green Hell. Will see what happens when new updates come out. Might be worth trying again.(Even though I say this, I’m going to keep trying because I am a die hard VR fan, and with any luck the devs will fix most of these issues.)  I will say, the controls need some work for this game to get over the bad reviews. Tough trying to figure out controls while trying to survive, end up dead more often than not. = No Fun! All in all I would rate this game (in its current state) 6.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The real deal.Genuinely can't find much fault with the choices and direction Incuvo have gone with VR conversion. Until we reach the age where controllers and pressing buttons aren't a thing, we're stuck with highlighting objects and pointing in their general direction. Where they've succeeded here is that a lot of it feels very natural, more so than in it's near counterpart The Forest. Objects are more interactive given the nature of VR, after viewing a few things of the flatscreen counterpart, it's really quite obvious the developers have detailed a lot of the in game world objects to make the VR version more fun, By no means perfect, it would be more fun to do away with the crafting table and go full on bind a flint rock to a stick handle, but we're just not there yet with functional control methods and ad hoc VR physics models. The game itself is a frustrating ton of fun, a true learning curve cliff face if ever there was one, easily initially summed up by  shortly before just dropping dead or descending to frustrating death.Performance wise, at default on the G2/I7/3090, it ran absolutely fine. Everybody seems to have a different opinion, but those that are saying 12900k/3090 low graphics unplayable, that's certainly not my experience on the ever demanding G2 with it's never that great steam VR overhang. Even at the default settings (med/high) the game looks absolutely fantastic. A step up for a native VR title in a year 'wanderer aside' nothing matches this outside the PCVR mod scene.In a year of mostly mediocrity, PCVR deserves this one. Cheers Incuvo, long time coming, but you've delivered i think.

_childDocuments_.review: ---Edit---I have to change my review a bit. The game currently has a bug where if you have items in a storage box, they will vanish upon return. It's not all of the items but a lot of them. I don't like games that delete my progress. You can now salvage the rope you use to tie up big leaves, sticks and logs so that's good. All in all, I'd give this game a 3/5 in its current state (28 Aug 2022). If they fix the lost item glitches and make the crafting a bit less cumbersome I'd give it a 5/5. ---Oh my goodness, this game in VR is like living in a horror movie....and it's amazing! Throwing the spear is a little wonky, or may I just suck at it. The crafting table is a bit cumbersome to use but other than that it's a heck of a lot of fun. I don't really like needing to use rope (that isn't salvagable) to tie up big leaves for carrying, though being able to carry two big logs at the same time is nice. _childDocuments_.review: Graphics:The game looks beautiful and delivers a great feeling of presence. I would pay for just the menu. The rain, however, has not been improved since the demo which is a pity. The effect kind of does the job though. Some rock textures look quite blurry up close, but the general level of detail and the lighting are lovely. That being said I have everything set to max except ambient occlusion. I am using a HP Reverb G1 at 100 % steam SS, a fairly high resolution so to say.Performance:According to fpsvr I am getting an average of 37 FPS on an 3080 ti, i7 11700k, 32 GB, SSD, 'Performance Mode' off. Surprisingly, despite motion reprojection turned off the game still looks smooth to me. Maybe my eyes or brain are not fast enough. I did not get any motion sickness. Smooth turning by thumbstick feels like increments though. It would be nicer if this could be as smooth as looking around with your head.Controls:Almost unplayable with my WMR Headset unless I am doing something wrong here. By far the worst thing is trying to sleep by pointing at the watch. Unfortunately, pointing also switches between the various display modes of the watch. So before sleep gets triggered the watch keeps flipping to its other modes. This makes you pass out and pick up parasites leaving you to try again only in a worse condition. Absolutely unbearable. Throwing a spear does not seem to work at all, it either drops to the floor or ends up in the backpack. Item management in the backpack is a lot of struggle.  I could not figure out how to run. It's supposed to be left thumbstick press, I think. But this just brings up the Steam menu. Inspecting your legs is possible, but it takes a lot of practice to find the right spot on the touchpad to bring it up. Sometimes it is hard to find a spot which the game would accept for the crafting table even though the ground looks flat and even.Story & Gameplay:This could all be great. Having not played the 2D version I am looking forward to what to discover next. For now the controls lacking so hard costs me too much time to be able to experiment with crafting or building which I'm sure has the potential to be very satisfying. I am playing on 'Welcome to rhe Jungle' difficulty which I assume to be 'normal'. As time flies by very fast and your needs have to be met at a crazy pace, being held back by the controls kind of ruins it. It simply takes too long to do stuff. If they only patched the watch/sleep issue, I would get along I guess.I am happy we have gotten this very pretty and interesting game and appreciate some of the motion controls, but I really hope for a patch so I can play it the way it's supposed to be.Edit: I eventually found out that in order to trigger sleep without switching the display mode you just have to 'dip' the finger into the display of the watch rather than 'touching' it. While this is a huge improvement unfortunately, I also just ran into the saving bug with the saving icon animation continuing endlessly without saving. Happened to me the last 3/4 times I was building a basic shelter to save. As this is gamebreaking I will wait until this is patched.Edit: Seems like they successfully patched the not saving bug!
_childDocuments_.name: Green Hell VR

_childDocuments_.review: I quite enjoyed this one.  Well worth the price of admission.  There is some jank (as other reviews have mentioned), but the game has far more good than bad going for it.  A real and non-lazy VR version with: full motion controls, comfort options, support for seated play, saints & sinners style inventory, PC-quality visuals, 3D audio, lots of content, etc.  My first playthrough (semi-completionist) took me 39.9 hours.  I encountered no game-breaking bugs, and no CTDs.  As of the date of this review, here's the little bit of jank to actually watch out for: (1) if it freezes when you try to reload just quit to the main menu first; (2) your inventory can shift when you load, so just quickly check the ground in case something fell out.  If you like games like Subnautica then Green Hell is a must-have.  Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: After making a start in the story and setting up a decent mud-built house I can say this is an excellent game and ALMOST an excellent VR game. I have a 2080 and i7 12700f and it runs very well on high settings and a resolution of 2600x2600, but only when I use the VR performance toolkit to implement FOVeated rendering. The immersion is absolutely brilliant and the game mechanics/map size are better than almost all made for VR games. The downsides are some of the VR interactions. Grabbing stuff from your bag is a pain to do, items launch all over the place when you accidentally grab something from the bottom of a pile, putting stuff in your bag is a hit or miss and for some reason you can't see how full your bidons are so you waste clean water filling it up too much just to be sure. If they fix the water and bag situations this will be among my top5 favorite VR games for sure.EDIT: after 4 more hours I have changed my recommendation to 'no'. The reason is my game is becoming progressively buggier. In the last few hours, my character has developed a condition where he won't stop swearing. It's ''OH ♥♥♥♥, SERIOUSLY?'' and '' YOU STUPID PIECE OF ♥♥♥♥'' continuously on a loop which is funny at first but after an hour it gets incredibly annoying. I also can't carry multiple logs/sticks anymore, anytime I do at some point all but one of the sticks/logs will disappear. The mud filter gives clean water  when pointing at it, but when scooping from the reservoir the container holds dirty water. Vines became unlootable so I don't have rope anymore.I have stopped playing for now which is a massive shame. I hope these issues can get fixed, for now this is unplayable for me and it seems to get worse by the hour.EDIT2: changed it back to recommended because even with the game breaking every hour it is just too good to wait for patches.

I had to force quit my game 4 times, and tried to load my game 4 times but it was just stuck in the loading screen.  My specs are RTX 3080 12GB with a i7-12700.  I can ignore the optimization issues for now, but being unable to load my save game is a no no for me.  Until this is fix, it will be a thumbs down for me.

_childDocuments_.review: In my original review of this game, I was, for lack of better words, disappointed. The game ran poorly and had quite a lot of bugs, which lead to a bad first impression. Now, after the newest update, I'm glad to say that many of my problems with GH:VR are gone. Performance seems to be a bit better, and there haven't been any noticeable bugs in the time that i've played. Here's how I would review the game:Interactivity: 10/10, you can do everything that you can do in Green Hell, as well as a lot of unique VR only things. Not sure how much more interactive a VR game can get.Performance: 8/10, Runs well enough in my 2060, but definitely not as good performance as some other VR games. Seems to be pretty well optimized for a game of this scale.Bugs: 8/10, Many major bugs were fixed within only a couple of days of release, and I haven't found any bugs that can actually impact a playthrough yet.Developer Care: 10/10, they responded to reviews and took them into account when updating the game, not sure what else you could want.Story: 8/10, Not sure who plays Green Hell for the story, but if that's what you're looking for, it's pretty decent and seems to be the same scale as the flat version's story.Overall, i'd rate this game an 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Green Hell VR is the first step to a truly immersive survival environment game.A few improvements; When reaching your hand out to select an object, the invisible selection radius when pointing your hand is too small and sensitive. I often find myself standing there for a minuet, pointing my hand in all different directions trying to get the object to highlight so i can grab it. Same for selecting objects in backpack, when objects are too close together. The Global Lighting/Illumination seems off. Sometimes it feels washed out or dull but it doesn't feel as realistic as it can be. For those of us with higher end PC please make a realistic lighting setting. I've tried adjusting the brightness but it just reduces contrast and takes even more away from game. Other than that the game it great and I enjoy it very much. For those of us that played the console or original PC version its still very easy when you know exactly what to stay away from.4/5 stars

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely engrossing game so far but absolutely riddled with bugs & glitches. Way too many to mention , some very comical, like when I tried to light a fire & for no apparent reason shot myself about 200 feet in the air, way above the jungle canopy (& came down with one almighty crunch!) It also needs a LOT of optimisation, I’m running an i9-11900KF with 32GB Ram & an RTX3090 (24GB VRam) & am using my trusty Valve Index kit but I am only barely able to get a smooth framerate at 90hz, 200x resolution with “performance mode” activated, no AO at all & graphics settings on a combo of High & medium. There is definitely a really good game in there & the controls are just fine on the index "knuckles"& I will definitely be sticking with it as I'm having a lot of fun with it so far (despite the performance problems)  but I feel that it’s another prime example of a game that has been released waaay before it’s ready. I really hope that the dev's will be working hard on optimisation & bug fixing because it BADLY needs it. I do recommend this IF You have a powerful pc AND are happy to tinker around with the settings until you find something that works for you. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of the better VR games out right now.  The most obvious issue is the stability of the game as it can crash occasionally which, depending on what you're doing, can be phenomemally disorienting as crashes in VR are far more of an issue than on a flat screen.  That said, they ARE fairly rare.Graphics: 9/10.  The world, textures, objects, animals...they all look amazing.  The only thing that caught my eye were the models of people which seemed to be more made of clay than flesh.Sound:  Sound is easily one of the strongest parts.  From the beautiful areas to the insanity portions, it's absolutely riveting and you'll find yourself spinning in place to make sure that rustle-rustle wasn't a cougar.Input: The main issue is that control inputs are almost entirely locked and you can't really do significant rebindings for more than 5 actions.  You CAN change if grabbing something will automatically hold it, though I'd have preferred it to be a double-grab or something.Story: It's the green hell story so kudos goes to them, but it's good.Performance:  There are definitely occasionally issues where the game slows down neccesistating a restart but again, fairly rare.Overall, the pros outwiegh the cons, all of which can be fixed with optimization and patches from what I can tell.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Green Hell VR is too non-optimized to give a good review to, and the long, inconsistent story and total abandonment of PCVR doesn't help.I would give this a good review, I honestly would, but the excruciating load times mixed with the fact PCVR has apparently been abandoned, the story is entirely different across versions and so long that it feels more like a "travel through the Amazon" game than a survival game. Things you need to do are few and far between and it's already hard enough trying to manage your thirst, hunger and tiredness while traversing seemingly-impossible-to-overcome terrain. If it would get an update, a change to the story so it's consistent, even a bit of optimization, it could be redeemable. But the fact that no updates have released and the load times are so large that I feel like I need to sit down whenever it starts to load (5+ mins) means this game would need a LOT to be redeemed, maybe even a new dev team. It used to be good, Incuvo, it did. But you need to care for things doing well so they can continue to thrive.
_childDocuments_.name: Green Hell VR

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game and if it worked as "advertised" I would probably recommend it.. However it's just not the case... YET.. I hope it will be thou.It comes down to one simple thing:This should be sold as Early-access.. period.. it is simply not finished and cannot be called a "release" level product from any point of view. Had it been sold as early-access and the buyers made aware pre-purchase, I'd be totally fine with it as the developers do appear to be "willing" to work on it and polish it and also work with the community, which is great.. and would be perfectly in line with early-access expectations.The most glaring thing is the massive performance issues. There are some users who managed to "get it working" relatively smoothly (according to their own admission) - some on very extreme setups 3090's and the likes, others on low-end setups but also with low expectations, but then again people vary too and the levels of perception they have (we all know that "It runs fine for me" guy from all the forums who wouldn't notice reprojection if it was dancing infront of them naked).But, bottom line.. objectively speaking.. for what it is.. it is way too resource hungry on PC, period.. In my case for example, I'm running it on a system with an overclocked Ryzen 3800x all cores at 4.2 Ghz, 32 GB of high quality ram at 3666 Mhz and a RTX 2080 Super and a Quest 2 with cable link. I had to set it to medium graphics, thou I turned off "performance mode" (which btw feels like a very cheap and dirty trick to have to avoid working on optimizing things properly). In any case it's "playable" if you get used to it, it has alternating smooth sections with choppy sections.. (as a comparison, the Forest is kinda "notorious" as being an unoptimized port, however that runs circles around this game in terms of performance on much lighter hardware) On top of this, there are very "rookie" bugs, a prime example is smooth turning, which only works if you manage to send the game input only from the horizontal axis of the thumbstick.What does that mean?.. that if you even slightly press the stick diagonally and not perfectly left/right, turning will stop completely.. as such you end up with very jerky turning that gives you the feeling that your controller isn't working properly or your game is lagging and is just very annoying. This should have been something that any developer immediately picks up on in the very first stage of testing, cuz it literally feels like the controller's broken.. so either nobody at Incuvo ever plays with smooth turning, or they're somehow super lucky and their thumb was designed by Oculus or something and it's the exact length that it can do a perfectly clean horizontal axis input :) Again, this is something very reminiscent of early-access and would be somewhat acceptable there.Besides that handling objects is very clunky, you will make several attempts at grabbing things, till you're grabbing the thing you actually wanted so everything will take much more time and frustration than it should. I didn't get far in the story yet, but I've seen reports from others that a lot of the crafting recipes etc are also not quite working (again, this is "gossip" I haven't experienced it yet)Now, given the amount of bugs and the way it was released "unfinished" in my opinion.. I feel like the developers should be releasing patch after patch as you would expect with early-access games to quickly "plug" some holes they managed to figure out. I would rather have 10 patches a month with each of them improving something and making the overall experience that much better, than having the developer sit there in silence for a month or more. I also think that causes a lot of players to lose interest and stop waiting for fixes and move on to other games (thou again, that's just my personal opinion / assumption). Despite all of the above though, I do think this game has a lot of potential in VR, when it's running well it can be quite immersive and actually has the potential to make you forget it's a game from time to time (until you slap your wardrobe throwing a spear lol). I found myself listening for noises in the jungle, being a bit "scared" when I heard something from a bush or when I knew the night is near and I didn't have a fire or shelter nearby. I think these types of games somehow "make more sense" in VR.The stuff you can interact with, the various small critters, all the things you can eat (eww), being able to cut down most vegetation and such, it's all pretty awesome and it's all placed in a pretty neat way to where they seamlessly integrate into the environment, you rarely notice "barriers" between the environment and creature spawn points for example, especially if you're new and you don't know where the spawnpoints are.I never played the flat version so to me this is a completely "new" game, it does seem though that a lot of the positive aspects probably originate from the base game, which means that it's indeed a good pick from the developer to bring into VR. Not only that, the VR side of things also enhances it and gives it life, makes you be more curious and give it more patience.For example I really dislike "annoying / punishing / cruel / idk what to call it" games.. Basically the whole masochistic (beep)storm that probably got reborn into gaming with Dark Souls and then kept on blooming :D (back then I gave DS several chances and finally played to like the first boss and then I asked myself... "Why do people wanna do this to themselves?"). I feel like Green Hell would probably be the survival game equivalent of something like that to the uninitiated, and sure it gets way easier when you figure out certain things, but I think everyone would agree that the start for a new player can be very punishing. Yet... to my surprise, I don't really mind that in VR as much as I would otherwise!!I patiently struggled through the first 2 days, dying and reloading saves several times till I managed to figure it out and stabilize my character.Long story short.. it's a good game, but an unfinished game so I can't in good faith recommend it to people when I know most of them will struggle with its performance, get annoyed by the wonky controller bug or the clunky / laggy way of trying to handle objects. I would pick something "in-between" like a "maybe" or a "yes with some caveats".. or a 3.5 star rating out of 5... but Steam provides neither one of those options, so for now I'm going with a No, despite liking the game. If the game gets some updates and these issues get addressed, I'll probably come back and change it (if it's possible). I hope that's "fair enough" :)Cheers!
_childDocuments_.name: Green Hell VR

_childDocuments_.review: Game doesn't seem entirely stable, and even when it is stable it's not fun to play. I started the tutorial, immediately got stuck because of a glitch that prevented me from moving. Teleport movement didn't work at all, and I had to restart the game before smooth locomotion started working. One thing I noticed immediately is how short draw distances were. Even when I turned them up to maximum, shrubbery didn't appear until I was pretty close to it. "High" quality textures all look kind of flat and nondescript.  Sticks and rocks are all blobby. I can only tell what some objects are because of the text that appears when I point at them. Hand-dragging objects felt awkward too - could barely move a small log blocking my path. Sound felt weak too. If I'm standing in a rainstorm in the Amazon forest, I expect the sound of falling rain to be pretty loud. But it's like I'm indoors hearing a gentle drizzle on the roof. In the process of building a fire, I learned two things:1. Half the time when you try to put something in your backpack by putting it over your shoulder, you just drop it. 2. You should never take the option to do something with manual hand controls if you can push a button instead. Operating the firestarter felt really awkward because I wasn't really holding the pieces of it. Once I got to the end of the tutorial, I dropped to a black screen. It took me a moment to realize there was a cutscene playing on a movie screen behind me, so I don't know all of what happened there. After I regained control again, I decided I should build a shelter on the spot. The tutorial had not explained that I needed an axe, or what size tree I needed to make logs, or how I should cope with the fact that I had to pick up every stick 2-3 times in order to actually bag it. But I managed to get through all that, and was well on my way to making my first humble lean-to when I started having a glitch where the game would go to the pause menu every time I looked down. You spend a *lot* of time in this game looking at the ground, 'cause that's where all the sticks and rocks are. I restarted the game. Then my movement controls broke again. I restarted again. Made multiple axes, started looking around for likely trees, and then movement broke again. I spent so long trying to get going that by now, it was night in game and I could barely see anything. Why is the game-day so short? I barely had time to wake up and pick up sticks!Reading other reviews of this game, it's clear I didn't even get to the dangerous stuff. And now I've seen how much of a trial it is to do even the most basic survival tasks,  I don't think I want to. Go play "The Song in the Smoke" instead. That one has dinosaurs.

_childDocuments_.review: So good to get another full length VR game! Big props to the devs for doing such a great job with the port (although there's still a little ways to go). Sometimes it's a little fiddly and janky, but overall I'm having a great time. The survival system is much deeper than The Forest and there's a real sense of achievement as you survive each day, a little better than you did the day before. While some people have experienced performance issues, I'm on Vive with a 2080ti and have had no issues at all. It runs as well as any of my other VR games do, which is pretty impressive, given how lush the jungle is. Looking forward to becoming the apex predator in this jungle!

_childDocuments_.review: First let me say that I love this game. I beat it on PS4 and do not regret my time playing.I was so excited when Green Hell came to VR, and I want to be clear that the implementation is very good! The controls are good, the UI is good, the graphics are good, it all works well.That said, I bought this with the explicit promise that multiplayer would be coming to the vr version.That the publishers are still churning out updates on the flat screen versions but haven't touched this version since release is frustrating. That they promised features for this version of the game and have failed to deliver years later is theft.I will not be making purchases from this company again unless they can show that they'll keep their word about their products.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played TWD: Saints and Sinners, the controls are basically the same, which is a good thing as it's easier to grasp.I would say this game is very immersive that it will take a good chunk of your day just to "get started" so I would recommend to research on how to survive your first night or so before diving in. Days, in my opinion, don't last long at all and should be extended.For a newbie, it can be a bit intimidating because although they give you a short tutorial you really have to just think for yourself and figure it out which I think the original devs (Creepy Jar) intended. Instructions in surviving will not given to you on a silver platter. In saying that, the world is beautiful and life-like and it would be absolutely amazing if they implemented co-op (even though I would have no friends to play with lol) Disclaimer: Do not play this game if you get motion sickness from VR - after awhile you will get nauseous and will need to stop. I don't really have anything bad to say about this VR port, it works really well. However, in-game menu sucks. It's literally just a pause button. If you need to change in game settings like rotation speed for example, you need to close the entire game and reopen it to gain access to the options. This part was quite frustrating for me. At the time of writing, I haven't yet experienced any note worthy bugs.VR Headset used: Valve IndexAlso...The game is hard!

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game, although it suffers from some issues. As suggested by other reviewers, one of them is performance related. Using the Steam launcher will cause the game to stutter, even with high performance computers. However, the Oculus launcher seems to provide a much more stable experience. I'm willing to bet many of the technical issues of other reviewers could be resolved by choosing the Oculus launcher when pressing Play in Steam. Other issues are minor, such as lackluster rain graphics and janky backpack controls when grabbing items from it. Apart from that the game is an amazingly immersive jungle experience, that leaves you coming back for more!
