_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat I'll say I am biased to love this game based on my enjoyment of the "normal" version of Green Hell. This VR port is very well done, with the only real drawback being the graphics performance. That said, I played the demo months ago and the developers have  made a ton of improvements to the performance of the game. I'm running on a Valve Index (Native resolution, no SS) with an i7-8700k, GTX 1080, and 16GB RAM @ 3200MHz, and my settings are on Low/Medium, except for texture quality and resolution, which are both on High. I get a consistent 100+FPS and when Resolution is set to Medium I get well over 120+. I've not done much experimenting with the other settings, so I might be able to get more out of the game without too much of a performance hit. Focusing on gameplay, this port is really good. Incuvo have done an excellent job converting the physical interactions to work in VR. I'm early on in the Story right now, but two examples of really interesting physical interaction are making fire and washing mud off of yourself. Both (and others) of these interactions work exactly how you'd expect IRL. Such as with the latter, you pick up some water in the palm of your hand, and physically rub the other arm to clean it off. Interactions like this, rather than having things done "automatically" are what makes VR so cool. As of writing, I've built up a lean-to shelter and a fire, and narrowly avoided starvation when I managed to craft a spear and kill a peccary. This game is just as, if not more, immersive as the flatscreen Green Hell, and I look forward to finishing the Story in VR. I'm not going to give this game a traditional rating or anything, but as someone who loved the original and loves immersive, interactive, and narrative VR games, I highly recommend it for others like me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is REALLY amazing. The survival aspect, the way you build things, the exploration, all of it is really enjoyable, but I have had SO many problems that I cannot enjoy it. Firstly, after a single day my vision gets this weird black circle blur around it, limiting my field of view to a VeeeeeRY small circle directly in front of my eye, eliminating ALL peripheral vision. The point of me playing this game in VR is to be able to SEE the world from a more personal view, and limiting my vision destroys that. I have spent weeks trying to find a solution, trying in-game medicines or changing the settings, but this issue ALWAYS persists. It might be bearable on a flatscreen playthrough, but in VR it ruins the entire experience, especially someone who records their game such as me, as it blocks about 90% of my screen and creates unusable footage.I do NOT recommend this game, and will continue to criticize it until this singular issue is resolved in the VR version, or an option is added in settings to remove it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have spent almost 200 hours playing a non-VR version, and I was really looking forward to this one, expecting something  quality and immersion, but got a huge disappointment instead.Firstly, finger detection is a total disaster. I was playing on Valve Index. Middle, ring and small fingers are detected as one. Index finger is always straight, it closes only when pressing the trigger button in certain circumstances. For example, to press a button on the walkie talkie, I have to touch the button with my finger, but it doesn’t actually press it - to press it I need to press the trigger button on the controller, and in this case the finger stays straight in VR, even though it’s closed in real life.Picking up items? It’s not enough to close the palm, you actually have to press the trigger button too. However, holding the trigger button destroys the item, so you have to first press the trigger button and then release it.It all feels extremely unnatural.There are regular problems with interacting with the environment. Sometimes I cannot grab the stick lying on the ground, despite it being highlighted and my virtual hand touching it; sometimes some item appears in my hand that I was not even trying to pick up. I pulled up the backpack and made it hang in the air - after multiple attempts of trying to grab it and put it back on my shoulder, I closed the game. No matter where I was trying to grab it, there was either nothing happening, or it was picking up items from it.Crafting? If you are hoping for , you are in for another disappointment, as this is not the version available on Steam. I believe it’s for Oculus Quest only. _childDocuments_.review: More like BORING AS HELL.I really wanted to like this game, & waited, like everyone in anticipation for this VR release. Not only to play, but to create a series for my TY channel. Man, what a let down. Literally nothing got fixed from the demo. The rain effects are atrocious, the controls are so jank you fumble around trying to grab or place items in your backpack. You get some VR control options such as smooth turning & snap, however you only get 3 variations to choose from, slow normal & fast. You can't even adjust the speed manually!  When you do turn it's a continuous speed rather than how you move your thumb stick. Performance is pretty bad as well, even with a top tier PC, this is unacceptable. I thought No Man's Sky performed bad but this is the king of poorly optimized VR titles which is a bummer because it looks pretty nice but the game play is awful.Animals glitching through environmental objects, walking under water & just straight up disappearing. Which brings me to the crafting. Many people have said that the Quest version has a manual crafting system. I don't know, I don't have a Quest, but this version is point & click crafting style. It's nearing 2023 & the whole point of VR is to be immersed with full control of the environment & our hands - we still get button pressing to craft an item.Where's the innovation??No coop - yet. So I suppose if these problems could be fixed it might be an 'OK' game, but not in this state. I may just be nit-picking but there are way better games out there to play. I'd rather play The Forrest. But hey, I'm just salty.SALTY AS HELL!

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, I'd like to say that Green Hell (non-VR) is amazing and I was really happy to hear that a VR mode was developed by Incuvo.So, about the VR version:It's great!All the features from the normal game are here, you can even stack leaves and long sticks in your hands!The game feels realistic and the ambiance is even better, you'll be scared for real now :)I love equiping weapons and tools on my belt and shoulder, the backpack is easy to use.I love throwing spears and the house building is simple.The only downside is the crafting table and the cinematic in the game:I'd like for a stationary version of the crafting table, so you don't have to spawn one each time you get back to base.About the cinematics now: They are just videos from the previous game, rendered in front of you, getting you out of the game and letting you watch an "in VR" tv.However, I understand that it would have been difficult to animate it in virtual reality.I give it a 8/10I'll give a 9 when the multiplayer come out !Thanks Incuvo and Creepy Jar for those awesome games :)

_childDocuments_.review: From  post by the developer, I learned that this will not be compatible with the standard (flat) version of the game. This isn't mentioned in the sale page. I also didn't realize that they hadn't bothered to  implement multiplayer with release. But even if they had, that still wouldn't do me any good as the people I know who play GH do not have VR equipment and can't afford it. There are plenty of games out there that support standard and VR playing together. Many are even ports. Many included this in the base game long after the initial release as an update to the players instead of a cash grab. I get it, creating this content isn't free and this dev isn't the original, probably just someone the original publisher hired to port the game. They could have  included or planned for flat/VR compatibility. It feels like a cash grab because of how half assed it is. It is quite buggy so my earlier comment about it being unfinished really does still stand. On top of that releasing without multiplayer like halo infinite did was disappointing as such behavior is simply disappointing, at best. You'd think devs/publishers would have learned from the cyberpunk fiasco not to release unfinished games. I'm sure this was a "management" decision made by someone in charge that knows nothing about the process of creating a game and only got to that position because they knew someone and wanted to make their mark on the world, even if that mark is a veritable piss stain. The sale page didn't mention they hadn't bothered to include multi (unless you consider the only feature in the list noting Single Player to be accurate which I didn't as why would they only port part of the game? I guess that's on me for assuming it wasn't a half effort,) nor did it mention that they wouldn't create compatibility with the standard version. I shouldn't have to dig through forum discussions to get this information. I probably wouldn't have purchased it if this information had been offered upfront. And locking the FAQ thread where I found this information, as well as deleting any comments if there ever were any, is just messed up. Do you really think players weren't going to ask for multi with their standard version friends? VR equipment is expensive. Not everyone can afford it. Not everyone can use it even if they can. Compatibility between the two, especially when it was standard first, should be a requirement. Overall this is just disappointing. I had been looking forward to this ever since it was announced and well... here we are.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game but the short experience I've had wasn't really good..Performance-wise this game is okay. _childDocuments_.review: Review on the HTC Vive Cosmos EliteThis game does not offer enough settings for a VR game. There is no ability to customize the smooth rotation, and instead "Normal" which is way too slow and "Fast" which only sometimes feels right. The movement is also almost impossible with the Vive Controllers. Most VR games allow you to lightly hold your finger on the movement pad forward for motion, and point the controller in the direction you want to move. This barely works half of the time, and also horribly responsive. Another flaw is that there is no "left-handed" setting, which greatly helps the controls remain consist with every other VR game I've played. Having to swap using motion in left and rotation on the right makes the controls even more uncomfortable. Nothing about the "Comfort" tab in the pause menu is comforting.In regards to as a VR port of the original Green Hell, there's a few minor noticeable differences but none of which visually or mechanically make the game worse. I was disappointed to see that multiplayer and Spirits of Amazonia were not implemented yet, however this is fine as long as it's introduced in the future. The game is optimized well and performs well, considering I have a lower-end GPU and CPU.Overall, if you're left-handed and don't like rigid clunky movement and you own an HTC Vive Cosmos Elite, I do not recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: r7 5800xrtx308032gb ddr4Quest2VD/Airlink SSW/ASW on and offCompletely disappointed by the graphical fidelty and the performance. I get a smooth performance with high res, medium quality, performance settings on. But the game looks even uglier, than it looks with everything max out - and even with everything max out, it is NOT a good looking game, since there are a lot of blurry textures -mainly in the distance, but even on the ground). The best visual experience in this game by far is the starting screen when sitting at the campfire.Update (16.06.2022): Since you implemented Oculus RT, i gave it another shot.First off all:I can exclude now, that the issue of blurry textures is caused by the compression of VD/AirLink, since the behaviour is the same with the hp reverb g2. Oc, it looks marginally better, but it really is no game changer. The impression of "blurry textures" is still there. I think it is related to the relative short drawing distance. One example: when i am moving through the pool to the place, where the waterfall hits the pool (right after finishing the introduction) and turn around, you will see a little hill. From this point, most of the hill looks like a blurry, muddy space. When swimming towards this hill now, the vegetation on the hill start popping in slowly, piece by piece. The closer you come, the more is shown. Next thing is: With reprojection on, microstuttering is a real issue when smoothturning. Less (but still remarkable) in the hp regerb g2, significantly more with asw and airlink on the Q2 and with ssw on VD. The performance via air link seems to have improved a little bit by including oculus rt in the latest patch. (in comparison tho steam vr, that seems to be the only working option with vd at this point). Since you have made some progress, i wont refund again - but to me this is more like a bet on the future development - and i really hope, that you continue improving this game. I still could not recommend the game to others though.

_childDocuments_.review: This is surprisingly good I haven't played the flatscreen version however I did experience the VR demo way back but it had quite a few bugs, all of those seem to have been fixed and performance is really good.The story is quite short (it took me around 8 hours to complete whilst just focusing on the story alone which is quite short considering the price of the game but this seems to be on par with other VR titles these days though I did walk around in circles a few times before figuring out there are coordinates on the watch that help you navigate using the map lmao) but it is engaging enough to keep you playing and the voice acting really carries it along well.The VR mechanics are where this game shines, object interaction is definitely better than most of the VR games out there, First though there is some Jankiness when using the backpack sometimes grabbing things can be awkward at times but it isn't game breaking and the inventory management is generally excellent all things considered. the backpack is pretty good having external loops/hooks and multiple layers which add a sense of depth and inventory management, the grid however can be slightly frustrating but it isn't terrible and is much preferable over TWD: S&S's slot system.The survival mechanics are excellent you have macronutrients instead of a food bar which means no wolfing down excessive amounts of bananas, hydration is also important and the balance seems pretty reasonable, there are a myriad of ways to get sick, poisoned or injured and wounds can become infected if not bandaged or kept clean which means you always have to be alert and think things through whilst exploring which keeps you immersed.Graphically the game looks visually beautiful and runs great.If you are really into survival games this is definitely worth picking up

_childDocuments_.review: Cool crafting mechanics, pretty challenging at first (norm diff) but gets easier once you get the hang of it. Wish I played two notches harder in hindsight to stretch the experience, but might come back one day for that challenge. Haven't done most of the construction/crafting because there was no need on this diff. Literally could've evaded every conflict, curious whether you're more forced to fight on harder diffs.Story is great and the jungle is way larger than I expected. I rushed it a bit towards the end, but if I didn't I would've probably gotten 30-35 hours out of it without too much stretching.  That's without touching the challenge and survival scenarios. Played it on a WMR headset and it still felt pretty immersive. Only the grab aiming felt a bit off at times, but that might be a WMR issue. Can be played sitting down but can get a bit finicky at times and standing is just a much more immersive experience. Only wouldn't recommend this game if you're terrified by a 'stranded in the mysterious and dangerous jungle' setting.Could totally see a future sequel focused more on a multiplayer core with maybe Rust VR in the jungle kind of vibe? Maybe some procedural terrain generation in the mix? Would be awesome to explore new jungles, seek a pretty spot to set up camp, venture out when you have expanded your camp a bit, stumble upon other players' camps.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I wasn't expecting much, as most VR ports turn out to be janky at best and the Quest version wasn't really confidence inspiring. But the devs managed to retain the quality of the flat screen version of the game and in many ways improve upon it's mechanics.The immersion you'll feel in this game is incredible, I've caught myself holding my breath when diving under water. So far I've spent most of my current playtime in the vicinity of the starting Oasis building a base camp, so I didn't get to experience the story element of Green Hell, but I suspect it's directly ported from the flat screen version. This is great, because the story of Green Hell is one of it's strong points in my opinion.As for the cons I can think of 2 major things:1) The crafting system is a little clunky. I get that the number things a player has to craft in this PCVR version is much greater than that of the Quest version, but it would still be nice to get the Quest approach for crafting at least the basic equipment (axes, spears, bows).2) The game looks gorgeous, which sadly means it requires a slightly beefier PC to run it well. There are mods that help with the performance, but the stated minimum requirements are a bit to "minimum" in my opinion.TL:DRA great VR port of an outstanding survival game with continuous dev support for people with a slightly higher range gaming PC.

_childDocuments_.review: Green Hell VR is a beautiful and challenging survival simulation game. You play as Jake Higgins, a famous anthropologist. You are left alone in the jungle with no supplies, food, or tools. You will use real-life survival techniques to craft, hunt, fight, gather resources, and survive in the Amazon jungle.How long will you be able to survive in this demanding environment?The PC VR version of Green Hell features even more amazing graphics, more complicated gameplay, and an immersive environment. The Green Hell PCVR tutorial is pretty similar to the Quest 2 tutorial. It follows the same story and steps. The main difference is there is more complicated crafting in the PC VR version of Green Hell. Much more complicated.Green Hell VR on PC is extremely hard. That is exactly what it is supposed to be. Some users were disappointed with the “toned down” version that existed in the Quest 2 (some thought that one was too challenging). That will not be the case here. With an even larger map and more things to kill you, it can feel like you are getting nowhere. That is the fun of hardcore survival games.Full Review of both Quest and PCVR -

_childDocuments_.review: The game VR needed!!I have played this game for a short while, and I gotta say it is extremely interesting.. This game might be the best realistic survival in my opinion. But! I will not hide the flaws- Right from the start I was experiencing bugs and just a general stuttering experience.. I played this on both the Rift S and the Quest 2.Let's start off with the bad first: The game has many bugs that are seemingly so easy to catch its a real disappointment they didn't fix them before release. On just my first play through my tutorial bugged out and had me crafting bandage after bandage so the prompt will go away.. Items just flying out of your hand/inventory to never be seen again, text spinning, glitchy physics, and more that I probably haven't run into quite yet. All these issues are quite annoying but thankfully not game-breaking for me. If you are a VR player you probably already are numb to bugs anyway..And the good!!As I said above, this is probably the best survival simulator at the moment. It truly gives you the feeling of being stranded, in danger, and just an anxiety roller coaster. I love how the tutorial gives you the absolute basics for playing the game and then throws you into the deep end. It helps with the immersion of being in the jungle completely unprepared. I loved learning through trial and error, and the game gives you just enough information/feedback to continue your progress.I cant say this enough, I ADORE the physics in this game. As buggy as it could be, the fact that you need to put force behind your swings at a tree to chop it, being able to actually collide with your environment instead of phasing through everything is so breath-taking in this situation. It puts you in the moment, banging rocks together and poking a frog- all with extreme anxiety to find food for tonight makes this such an immersive game. All to get poisoned, which is another feature I love. Actually getting hurt, parasites, poisoned, and having to treat these.. I'm ranting a bit- but its simply because this experience made me want to pick up my headset again.I highly recommend you give this game a try. Yes, I do want the devs to actively work on this to help with the issues, but the content truly outshines its flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: As a new guy to the VR scene, my collection was lacking a survival title. The graphics are not too special on my 3060 Ti and there are some bugs (one hilarious one where my character routinely curses every rock and stick when I walk out of my camp, I would consider that a feature) but despite that there is so much going for this game. The sensation of making your own little two story stick hut which you physically have to climb if you wanna get up... so great, it really breaks my brain. Even the harrowing first time you forget your energy meter and wake up to a "creepy surprise you have to dig into". I was grossed out to the limit, the sensation was so intense. _childDocuments_.review: In my 2.7 hours so far in this game, I can tell you a few things. This is hands down the best VR game if you love immersion and the outdoors. There are a few issues concerning turning in game (I'm playing with an original Quest) and whenever I turn towards the right it sometimes just stops and gets annoying because I'm hitting my joystick constantly so I usually just resort to turning in real life. Another issue is spawning of items. I can almost never find coconuts (I have only found one and I've been looking for a while) which makes it almost unplayable. Another spawning issue is the stone to stick ratio. One game I found a bunch of sticks but barely any rocks and then the next game I had about 20 rocks with a total of 2 sticks, and only 2 small trees to cut down. Then the next issue is I couldn't cut down the small or medium trees with the rock alone which meant I could barely get a start. You can't throw objects onto snakes or other animals to kill or damage them (including weapons), you can only hit them when it's in your hand. If these are fixed than I have no doubt that this game will be a booming success and truly be an AAA VR game. Also good job on the graphics like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ they run well and look beautiful at the same time. One final issue is whenever I sleep is that my weapons disappear if they're holstered. They're just gone for whatever reason and if you load the game from a save and you have a weapon in your backpack, the model isn't there and you have to reach around for it. Those are the things that have spoiled the game mostly for me but entirely this game is awesome and extremely realistic for VR. Please fix these so the game because exponentially better.

_childDocuments_.review: Hell Yeah!, This game is Awesome! Is it Better than the Quest 2 Version..? Yes & No...The Quest 2 Version is lacking some content from it's original and graphics took a big hit!  They did a Great job overall, bringing the game to Virtual Reality! This PC Version is more of the ''Original Full Game'' brought to VR! It offers much more content and graphics look much sharper and detailed. However, All the great features they made for the Quest 2 Version did not make it to this PC port. For example, Crafting items, The Quest 2 had you rub materials together to create an item. While, in the PC Version you have to pull out a crafting table from your notebook every time you want to craft and create something. _childDocuments_.review: Awesome game - should run fine on most rigs after optimizing the settings. Using Valve Index, controls are somewhat cumbersome, but work. There's full locomotion (and teleport) and smooth turning (and snap) - moving direction can be set to hmd or controller. There's no finger tracking. The game is singleplayer, but comes with an interesting campaign. The game is only a 3.2GB download and 5.8GB install - but textures look nice, even though not being ultramersion res like Alyx and Boneworks. Performance actually is fine - maybe even great. I'm using Index SteamVR res 100%, 80 Hz (it all counts in this game), deactivated motion smoothing (seems to cause some strange stuttering when on), all in-game settings maxed, but ambient occlusion = medium. Using oc'ed RTX 3090 (Asus Strix), i9 10900K (10 cores/20threads), 32GB 3200 MHz ram.I mostly get 80 fps - runs great so far. The game looks awesome.72 fps in 144 Hz looks great too - another option if 80 fps is too much. Maybe even 60 fps in 120 Hz, but I did not try that.The game has a setting for res, so having that one maxed out and then increasing SteamVR res may lead to these settings being multiplied - so maybe better to keep SteamVR res at 100% and use the in-game res setting.Index using native Steam drivers may provide 20-30% more performance than other hmds needing additional drivers (when using same res) - so hmd may matter a lot in this game.The game does not support native Oculus drivers.I took some shots - find it all here:Btw, my settings:

_childDocuments_.review:
Green Hell VR is the most complex and authentic survival game for VR. The game faithfully recreates the dangerous conditions of the Amazon jungle. 

Alone and stranded, you will never feel safe. To survive, you have to face your weaknesses. Maintaining hunger, thirst, fatigue and mental health is going to be an integral part of your journey. Wild animal attacks and tropical diseases could strike you down at any time and out of nowhere if you are not prepared. Since you won't get any help from the outside world, you need to craft your tools and weapons, learn how to build shelters, and heal nasty wounds.

name: Meg's Monster
detailed_description: Welcome to the Underworld—a land of monsters and mutants who eat humans for breakfast. One such monster—a hulking ogre by the name of Roy—has no interest in eating humans. But one day, he and his best friend Golan stumble upon a lost little girl named Meg, and discover something truly terrifying: the moment she starts wailing in fear, a blood-red hue washes over the sky, and the earth itself begins to tremble and quake. That’s right: this small girl’s tears hold the power to bring forth the apocalypse—and the only way to stop it is for them to help find her mother so she can make it safely back home. Meg’s Monster is a short, story-driven JRPG with a big twist. Players control Roy, who begins the game with 99,999 HP and is virtually untouchable—but the real concern is keeping Meg safe, because if she starts crying, it’s game over for everyone. Players will have to master the unique mechanics and mini-games baked into each battle, all while protecting Meg and using her favorite toys to keep her pacified. Over the course of their journey together, Roy and Meg will encounter a host of quirky and colorful characters, all lovingly rendered in Odencat’s trademark vibrant pixel aesthetic that makes even scary monsters look cute. There’s plenty of drama and intrigue to be found here—and even previously defeated enemies can be befriended through optional sub-events. What begins as a relatively simple and heartwarming story about two unlikely friends ultimately expands into something much greater, as Roy and Meg slowly begin to unravel the mysteries surrounding the Underworld and themselves. The result is an emotional journey that, like any good storybook, will remain in your heart for years to come.

short_description: Take control of the Underworld’s grumpiest ghoul to help a lost little girl find her way home in this creepy-cute indie adventure. Just be warned: if she cries, the whole world dies.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this game in just a few hours, and in my opinion if I can finish a game in 6.5 hours and it still had this strong of an emotional effect on me you've done a fantastic job! I cried multiple times while playing, these characters are very sweet and lovable. I think the game is extremely worth it, and if you like games like Mother 3 and Undertale you would be missing out if you didn't give this one a try as well! I highly recommend this game if you have the time and funds, it's one of my new favorites! Thank you for the incredibly meaningful experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: A story of a little girl and her pet, William Birkin.My favorite part is when the monster says, "Shut up, Meg!"This game ripped my fu*king soul out of my body. It filled that Undertale-sized hole in my heart and left me yearning for more. It's like the most creative escort mission I've ever seen. Plus the art style and concept is to die for. Just such a great game, it’s an emotional roller coaster and just such a beautiful story that made me feel more than any book, movie or game I've experienced this year, I absolutely loved it. Story is awesome. Don't be ashamed to cry, it's totally fine.Meg’s Monster is a very touching game that at its most basic tells the common story of a very lonesome and closed-off person slowly becoming more relaxed as he meets another bubbly and affectionate person. It takes about four or five hours to finish completely, so it’s not a huge time commitment. The RPG elements are very light. Battles are turn-based affairs, but you don’t have a lot of tactical options so the route to victory is usually fairly clear. There are no random encounters, and every battle you fight is one dictated by the story’s needs. The combat is more like a puzzle than actual rpg. There's no grinding and if you die you can just retry, no game over backtracking. The battles are usually an extension of the story rather than a"chore" to earn more story.You will level up after certain battles, giving you a couple of stat boosts and an upgrade your HP. There’s no gear to collect, treasures to loot, or grinding to be done. There are several small locations you’ll visit at least a few times each, and a few overworld maps that stitch them all together. There are four or five sub-quests to complete, but otherwise you’re just playing through the main story.It’s a fantastic narrative experience. While it’s not the most mechanically rich RPG around, it’s not really trying to be. It’s here to tell a story, and it does so wonderfully. The characters are memorable, the plot is engaging, the presentation is sublime, and it’s on the whole just a hard thing to dislike at all. I haven’t been on an emotional roller coaster like this one in a while, and I’d highly recommend it to anyone looking for a touching story to play or the urge to cry like a b*tch.I would love for there to be a sequel but I know that it would undermine the games message and the ending so l am just going to sit here and enjoy my bittersweet candy.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: From the moment I played the demo, Meg's Monster captivated me. Now that I've played the full game, I can safely say it soared beyond all expectations I had. This game follows the story of a lost little girl, and the 2 monsters who are trying to return her home. A pretty simple concept, even the game itself acknowledges this, but what they do with it is amazing. The story has equal amounts heart, humour, and drama. I could not predict what was going to happen next, and it kept me engaged until the end. This game has a heavy focus on story and the few moments of deviation from the linear path is mostly areas you can revisit for additional lore. You will not be grinding at all, there are no default enemies, and the stats you need are all achieved through story battles. Most of the battles have gimmicks such as minigames to avoid damage or objects that can be interacted with. Paying attention to these as well as enemy dialog is the key to success here, and thus there's more of an emphasis put on strategy than brute force. Everything about this game is just perfectly artistic. The characters are carefully constructed, even Meg herself isn't just a two-dimensional "little kid" character but genuinely shows a lot of bravery and courage. Roy is a tough as nails badass who feels himself changing throughout the course of the story, and Golan is so much more than the "goofy friend" as it's blatantly obvious that he knows a lot more than he lets on. Even the NPCs such as the monster council, Paul, and Joey are all oozing with personality and the exceptional pixel art and music compliments the unique style of this game well.I cannot recommend this game enough. It is an unforgettable experience you won't want to miss out on.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: The tagline of the game is "If she cries, the whole world dies," but the one left crying is me.There's a lot I could say about Meg's Monster, but nothing I say could actually compare to how this game made me feel.I can't even bring myself to close the game yet, so I'm just letting it sit on the final screen. I don't know what makes me want to cry more; the story itself, or having to say goodbye to it.I love the characters. I love the music. I love the story.I love this game. Please play Meg's Monster. I'm glad I did.I hope you will be too.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: A heartwarming story, I cried. Twice. It'll feel good. Keep in mind two things if you come to play this game. First is that this is more of a visual novel than an RPG. I wouldn't call the combat system shallow, in that it's not a button masher and you will have to think. but don't expect deep combat. Approach each fight like a puzzle.The second thing is the story gets... I wouldn't say convoluted. But it does get a little dense, the same way a peanut butter is packed with calories; you might not realize how filling it is if you're not paying attention. The last 3rd of the story gets pretty bizarre to follow, and may require to suspend some disbelief. You'll have to take the game's word that sometimes there's a little magic that just goes unexplained in the world.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: What a delight! A fairly short but very sweet RPG that allows its mechanics to carry its narrative in some very effective ways. Combined with a localisation that nails the landing 90% of the time (there sure are some lines doing some very heavy lifting when it comes to exposition) I enjoyed the whole thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: Meg's Monster is a game that uses RPG mechanics in a somewhat unorthodox manner. In most fights, the protagonist Roy is in little danger of death, but the player can still get a game over if little Meg becomes too distressed by the combat. There's a fair amount of variety in those battles, with many enemies featuring unique minigame-driven mechanics or special combat options. In general, they're more like puzzle fights, but are quite forgiving.The game is driven primarily by its narrative, itself focused on the relationships between characters. The writing is well above average and there's plenty of earnest emotional content that doesn't rely on the manipulative tricks favored by some other games. Strongly recommended for anyone who favors storytelling in games.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, emotional story with excellent character writing and a good sense of humor. Fans of turned-based RPGs may be disappointed, as the gameplay largely takes a backseat to the storytelling. The unique 2-member party battle system may seem interesting but is very underexplored, the fights are easy and straightforward, and the whole game is very linear even with a few side quests thrown in there.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: The first act of the game starts off pretty slow and generic, but it is the second act of the game where everything comes together that this game truly shines. It is moments like in the second act of this game that I cannot praise enough as being the culmination of everything I feel games can do that elevates them as the most personable forms of storytelling possible. Just the simplicity of the fact that it's made clear constantly throughout the game that nothing can really harm you, and your only reach challenge is trying to make sure Meg doesn't cry, only for  It's such a poignant and emotionally charged moment. And then when If I were to just judge it "objectively" just purely on gameplay, it's a mediocre linear game with barebones combat. But it's usage of game mechanics to enforce and elevate emotional beats really sets this game far apart. I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Meg's Monster is a Beautiful and Heartfelt story, with so much charm.I was suckered in by the Mother 3 inspired art style, and the OST while limited has some pretty dang good stuff! The story that is told is rather simple and sappy, but I really ended up enjoying it. There is just so many cute additional visual details put in every minor scene,  which just adds to it's already insane charm and great visuals. The world and setting itself is actually surprisingly... messed up. I will say the game does have one pretty big plot contrivance, but the story that it does tell is REALLY effective in making you tear up by the end of it.The game is about as linear as story driven experience can be, but it was such a wonderful time that I loved playing through.Bonus Note: The game's WEBSITE is also not free from having so many cute and charming additional details too! I recommend checking that out too once you finish the game!

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like the game should have been longer or had more character development in certain areas to really have maximum impact, but it was still a pretty sweet story. "Undertale Lite" comes to mind, although it is it's own thing.Game is very linear with some small optional exploration (which is ofc what you want to do anyway ín a game like this, to get lore bits). Unsure why all that wasn't just mandatory.+ Nice artstyle+ Good music (although maybe repeated slightly too much)+ Accessible* Story seemed a bit convoluted but it still delivered in the end* Gameplay is put behind for the narrative/world building, there's an interesting fight mechanic but it isn't really fleshed out that muchIf you are looking for a story-focused game, this is fairly easy recommend on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t think I’ve ever flip-flopped on an indie as much as this one. It’s very clear a lot passion and heart was put into this game.  Sometimes I adored my time with it, but I also found it frustrating or even boring. Ultimately, I think for what I paid, it was worth it. But please wait for a sale.A very surface level comparison would be Undertale, with simpler combat and a worse story.Meg’s Monster’s main story problem is that it breaks one of the fundamental rules of story telling. Show, don’t tell. The game will often just dump huge amounts of exposition on the player, with no good story reason to do so, simply because the writer felt that the player should know it immediately. The ending really dragged as well, as heartfelt as it was.The combat is very simple, similar in playstyle to RPG maker games but even simpler than that. There’s nothing wrong with it, it’s just really easy.I really loved the mini-games. Being integrated into combat added a touch of flavour that it really needed.The art and story are clearly lovingly made, so like I said, wait for a sale. And only buy if it’s already up your street.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: This game was perfect in every way. The perfect amount of character building, writing, clever and unexpected plot twists, tear jerkers, etc. Just a masterpiece. True art in a nice little indie package. Absolutely worth the play, but have tissues ready, and have 5 or so hours set aside to complete it in one sitting, its worth it. Bravo to every dev that contributed to this. Its clear much heart was put into this.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good, though very different from what a lot of the promotional material is making it out to be. This is not in any real sense an RPG: it's a visual novel that gestures toward RPG mechanics as a narrative framing device. Mechanical play never progresses beyond what one would expect from the tutorial chapter of a full-fledged RPG, and it doesn't really have time to do so, because there are approximately 15 actual battles in the whole game, none longer than a couple of minutes, with the rest of its six to seven hour playing time being taken up by long, semi-interactive cutscenes. Fortunately, its writing is strong enough to make that work for it!

_childDocuments_.review: I cried, then put myself back together...and then I sobbed for an hour-or-so straight in the final sequences of this game. The ending is a masterpiece, and it truly sparked that "magic" when the gameplay and story come together in perfect harmony.What an extraordinary game. Go in as blind as possible -- it'll reward you, and it'll promise to leave a major impact.

_childDocuments_.review: Meg's Monster is a really good example of a short story game. It doesn't overstay its welcome, the mechanics and game itself never gets in the way of the experience and it does wonders in creating a world and characters with a short runtime.The only downside is that it's pretty much exactly what you'd expect. But if you're a fan of the whole 'grumpy monster becomes a dad' kind of story then it'll fit perfectly.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: Meg's Monster starts with a little girl, Meg, being dropped into a world full of monsters. You play as a big blue monster who serves as an adoptive father figure as he protects and comforts her, all the while trying to figure out what the heck to do with her. The narrative hook is that the girl’s crying can bring the end of the world. So not only do you have to keep her safe physically, but you also have to comfort her during battle to make sure her tears don’t cause the planet to explode. This is a pretty original concept and early on the challenge isn’t so much in beating your opponent, but keeping Meg comforted during the heat of battle.Combat takes place as a turn based battle affair with a few options: attack, guard, special attack, and play. Battles aren't super complicated but you can lose if you aren’t paying attention. I thought it was the right amount of challenge for this type of game.The strength of the game is the story which provides interesting character development for the big blue lug, Roy. He starts off living in a cave with little else other than “magic sludge” which serves as his source of sustenance. However, as he spends time with Meg, he and his surroundings begin to change. Getting furniture for his house, playing and comforting Meg, learning how to deal with a little human child when she falls and colors on the walls. It is a really nice story with fun twists and turns that keep you engaged in the story.My biggest complaint is that the pacing is a little weird part way through the game. Not to spoil too much but there is a section which serves as the climax to the climax. However, between climaxes things slow down a bit which is great to flesh out the characters, but also makes the pacing feel a little wonky.Overall, it is a solid recommendation from me! It serves as a tight, unique narrative experience with just the right amount of challenge to feel engaging during combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: A really good story-rich JRPG game! And what's funny was how I thought this would be those kinds of games with a short, but sweet story (Since, that's what they basically said in the description) that ends with a nice but bittersweet ending only for it to turn out being more like that Black Adam movie where the "end" isn't really the end and it just keeps on going and going and going, lmao. But from my time playing this game, it’s a really fascinating, emotional, and well written story, I'd say… With lots of personality, charm, and literally plot twists after plot twist after plot twists here and there. It also comes with themes that I personally liked, too, such as a monster-filled underworld (which, truth be told, kinda very reminiscent to undertale lmao), a monster turned guardian angel style character arc, and some what I'd like to call "cute-funny" style dialogues among the characters in the game. Gameplay-wise, its mostly filled with tons of walking simulators, clicking through dialogues, fetch quests, light puzzles and the generic JRPG style turn based combat with the usual balancing act between healing, defending, and attacking the enemies. Though, the game does try to spice things up on the combat with some more minigames and events within the fights as you progress along the story so as to not feel like you're just repeating the same combat over and over again… Which is probably a good thing for those poor attention span tiktok users, I guess.That being said, would really recommend playing this game if you're a gamer like me who's into interesting stories (especially if you're coming from the likes of undertale lol) and are into a quirky take on the typical JPRG combat genre!
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me feel so many emotions for the characters it's unreal. I struggle to find GOOD narrative games like this and this game is so simple yet I was sobbing at multiple points. This game is better story-wise than a lot of games that have come out in recent years.10/10.Thanks for the gift, @ebiggz <3
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: This was such a sweet game.  I loved it.It's not a LONG game.  I completed it over the span of about four hours.  But it was a wonderful experience, and I felt vague overtones of Undertale while playing through it, in terms of the notion of a child fallen down into a monster-filled underworld who then befriends everyone.  Every battle is essentially a puzzle: you need to dispatch your foe with a limited number of turns before you've expended all of your toys and your damage received makes Meg cry (and the world end).  It's a simple form of gameplay, but it worked well enough.  The soundtrack was serviceable, if a bit forgettable, and the art style was really cute.All in all, if you enjoy cute, sweet games like Undertale, you'll almost certainly enjoy this game about a child and her monster protector.  I heartily recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: If there's a middle option between Recommend or Not Recommend, that would be my choice. I did enjoy the story but I wasn't quite satisfied with how the story was told through a video game. I'd give it... well, maybe 7.5 out of 10 for the story but 2 out of 10 for the gameplay. The story was nice but as a video game, it was reeeaaally lackluster. If they say this is just a demo I'd believe them. But a full game? They really should've put more effort into it.First of all, I was very disappointed how bare-bones the world in this game was. You never had a real option to explore, it's always just from spot A to spot B and when you are in a map, there's nothing for you to check or talk to. There's no secrets to dig up or whatsoever. The optional stuff either felt too boring and unnecessary, or was just better left in the main story because it was basically an important part of the story. My second biggest complain is that for an almost visual-novel like game, the characters are criminally expressionless. Unlike undertale, in this game characters' faces don't appear in the dialogue box so all you see when they talk is their overworld sprite, and their faces hardly ever change. That just seems lazy to me on the dev's part. It wasn't fun for me to look at characters just standing there stoically when they talked and most of the time what they were saying wasn't that interesting or entertaining. Thirdly, the music and sound effects are just flat. Don't get me wrong, I think the piano soundtracks are beautiful, but that's all there is. The music is nice as individual pieces but flat as the whole soundtrack playlist of a video game. They tried so hard to set up this emotional atmosphere most of the time that there were hardly any changes in the mood throughout the game. That's why everything fell flat in the end or should I say the entire second half of the game. I just got too used to the music and vibe that it didn't work on me anymore even at the big climax of the story. Also, I feel like they didn't put any effort into the sound effects in this game 'cause I don't remember hearing any interesting noise throughout the entire game. I'd also like to talk about the visuals. Overall, the sprites and maps look nice. However, like I stated before, it feels flat and hardly ever changes its atmosphere when some dramatic or emotional event is taking place. For example, during the battle against the big bad final boss, the background of the battle was exactly the same as before when you fought some random grunts. Everything was pristine and illuminated by bright white light. It was just like an ordinary hallway not the battleground for an epic showdown. It was BORING and anticlimactic to look at. All in all, I'd say it's an okay game (well I did finish it instead of refunding) but that's all it is. I wouldn't call it a masterpiece. When I play a really good indie game for example Small Saga, I could tell the dev had poured their heart and soul into their creation. Welp, not this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: An exceptionally cute and sickly sweet game worth the experience tenfold~ If you're coming into this looking for more in-depth combat or gameplay that are as strong as the story itself, you might be a bit disappointed, but the story and characters alike are where the biggest heart of the of the game is from. _childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: A heartfelt story that visually might be very reminiscent of another game that features monster and human tensions, but it stands out with a nice focus on a set main cast that I couldn't help but just adore.Pretty good Pixel art, nice colour palettes that set the mood.With a mix of overworld sprites and more detailed combat sprites, the latter while not being the most animated compared to the former, I welcomed them to break the story from time to time.Combat.Every fight being unique, going the route of every fight is a boss rather than a random enemy.Most if not all of the fights have a unique THING going on to try and not be a repetitive turn based game, this is more expanded on in later fightsBeautiful soundtrack, hitting the right notes in the correct places, though I felt it's a little limited and not too memorable, but that's purely personal.The combat feels a little tagged on, while there is variety in the enemies you typically only fight once, game overs tend to fall down to extremely bad luck since you are on a linear path with no real options besides your established mechanics.How the player avoids a game over, I'd say it's at least unique, so a bonus for that.Despite having a world map, the game is purely linear (you are pretty much locked into your linear route too) With no real reason to explore any place further outside of areas being no more than 2-3 rooms large at most points.Side quests don't really add much bulk to the game play or plot, with one side quest being awkwardly placed tone wise and the other being multiple side quests that seem almost shoe-horned in to bulk up the plot and twist (or someone just REALLY liked a certain character idk lol)While I think the ending is certainly a nice one, some elements of the plot and characters could've been explored more, the setting of the world REALLY should've been explored more, certain plot points I have either missed or the game didn't bother to tell me.(If it's left up to interpretation then that's totally fine) I feel the game could've just been MORE that what it already is if it was given more time to work on rather than a nice little shortened story to get done in a few hours.Despite what I feel, I do think it was a cute little game, HoweverI would REALLY recommend one buys it SUPER discounted or just watch someone else play it, you will both share the same experience.I just don't think the price is worth a 5-7 hour experience.I'd like to recommend it but it's just lacking in content and replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: Well worth the $15 I spent on it! The JRPG elements are simplistic, but keeps it fresh as it introduces new elements throughout the game. The story and character development keeps you invested, with twists along the way; some characters you started off skeptical over you end up admiring. The quality of the music touched my heart (and I'm going to be purchasing the soundtrack). My only minor complaint is I felt some of the music got repeated a bit too much, and an extra piece or two could of helped with keeping the atmosphere fresh. Regardless, I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a small adventure to add to their Library! A wonderful introduction for me to 'Odencat'!!
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: This game was short and sweet, and it lived up to its "will make you cry" reputation for me.The path for the game is pretty set in stone with only a couple of "optional" things here and there, though a couple of those things are rather critical to the overall story.I thought the pace was good and kept me wanting to play more, to the point where I played it pretty much in one sitting. The pixel art in this is beautiful and the music is great to go with that.There is combat but it's rather simple, but not mindless. I did find myself KO'd a couple of times, so it's not like you can just button-mash your way through it, but you also probably won't find yourself frustrated by it.Overall, I thought everything came together very nicely in the end for this game and so far it's my favorite Odencat game to date!
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet game. _childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: A radioactive amoeba and the goblin king set out on a quest to help a little girl find her mom - because CERN is in charge of both waste disposal and wetwork - while making sure she doesn't cry because that is the neurolinguistic trigger for the amoeba's planet-cracking alter.11/10, I cried so much because that's what I do when a story is this beautiful and heartfelt. _childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: I certainly wasn't disappointed with what the the game had to offer in terms of story ALTHOUGH... the gameplay was really lackluster to say the least. Walking and 'exploring' in this game seems really pointless since there's max 2 rooms per area and barely anything to do in them. The turn based combat also wasn't super interesting at the beginning, it picked up a bit at the end so I'm not gonna say it was terrible, but if you're looking for a gameplay heavy game even for turn-based standards, you're in the wrong place my friend, this is more of a interactive fiction than a game. Speaking of, the story itself is the highlight here, albeit short, very engaging with unexpected twists and emotional moments, I highly recommend the game for people who don't mind the lack of gameplay features. One flaw in the writing that caught my eye I'd like to point out, was pacing, sometimes at the earlier moments the cutscenes feel rushed like there could've been more dialogue, but there wasn't.Story is what carries the game, but other than that the gameplay is so boring I cannot recommend the game, it's one of those games that makes you wish it was a visual novel instead. At least it's not long.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: Meg's Monster is a visual novel with minimal gameplay. Most of your time will be spent in dialogue and linear maps. The battle system is a bare-bones turn based RPG. Minimal moveset, no items, no stat customization, no resources. Occasionally these battles feature simple quick-time events or minigames. You will Game Over occasionally, likely through no fault of your own.So I would expect the story to do the heavy lifting. Unfortunately both the story structure and dialogue sound like what happens when someone is very familiar with tropes, but not how to use them effectively. Deus ex machina, inexplicable character growth, and chunibyo scientists that unironically say things like 'mua ha ha' feature heavily. The soundtrack is limited, and while the songs are quite good they grow old by the end of the first hour. The art style is similarly charming, but simplistic. Meg's Monster isn't an unpleasant experience. It might even be a fun way to kill an evening for ~$5, if you were looking for a mindless experience that keeps you moving from one scene to the next. But it wants to be something more than that and just... isn't. I purchased this game on sale for $11.99 US, and can't say I got my money's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, and I can tell that there was a lot of love put into the game. I do not wish to deter anyone from trying the game out. There is something to be said for the story here. But unfortunately the game does not live up to its potential.Without going into spoilers, I was primarily interested in how the story of this game would overlap with the gameplay, and I think the devs had a really compelling idea for how the two could overlap that just didn't pay off in the end. The gameplay isn't good because each of the battles is set up perfectly for you to win if you hit the right actions in the right order. They're way too scripted, and as such they are meaningless. I thought having the monster's HP and the girl's mood being two separate things to be worried about could be an interesting twist in turn-based combat. In practice, however, the monster's HP bar is just kinda for show, and the girls mood is the only thing you have to worry about. Toys are just potions, taking damage is functionally just taking damage. There's not actually anything new here gameplay wise. It just ends up being dumbed-down turn-based combat. :/And because this poorly executed combat ties in with the story, there were a lot of moments (especially towards the end) that should have hit me harder, and I could see what the devs were going for, but it just didn't feel as *earned* as it should have been. The story has some cool twists, some questionable story structure and pacing, but I can see why people like it.There's something really good buried under there somewhere, and I believe these developers will be able to express that sometime in a future game. Until then, I don't believe this game deserves an "Overwhelmingly Positive" on steam. It should be knocked down a few pegs--with love. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, this game is amazing. It's not too long nor too short and I don't believe I've lost interest playing the game at all in my playthrough.The story literally broke my mind at some points where I was beyond confused (In the good way, it made sense at some point). Although sometimes I kind of wish that it would've been a little more clear as to what specific things mean. I think while 95% of the game was great, the ending wasn't all too nice. Sure, it was still a great ending and all, but in no way does it allow for any way to continue the game nor really is it a happy ending which I kind of hoped for.I still did tear up at the end and multiple times in my playthrough which is pretty common with odencat's games at this point anyway. I would still definitely reccomend this game if you have 3-5 hours to play this game, you can always save and the game really isn't that difficult.Sadly you cant really do much after the ending. You kind of just can replay the game and I guess write a review and whatever. (This is why a different ending would've possibly fit better) I hope in a future update they'll make some type of true ending like they did with other games, the game deserves it.Overall the game is a pretty solid 9/10 for me even with the ending being not the best and the story being unclear at some points. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: A linear narrative which excels at emotive writing and story-integrated gameplay.  Meg's Monster alternates between interactive story sequences and simple turn-based combat.  Neither are particularly complex, although later segments integrate some minor action and puzzle mechanics.  A bit of poking and planning will carry you through, as they serve primarily to illustrate the story.  It aims to challenge but not overwhelm.This focused experience in a simple engine syncs up pretty well with the short runtime.  There is no grinding and no wandering.  It does everything it sets out to do and does it well, with nothing getting in the way and not much unexplored.Good for several hours.  Many world-building scenes are optional if the player decides they only care about the core story, and a chapter select is available upon completion.

_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: This game will punch you in the feels in the best way.  The characters, the main story, the music, all three were pitch-perfect. Going in, I didn't know what to expect besides a touching story, but Meg's Monster took many twists and turns and honestly blew me away. The only things keeping this game from being perfect are the gameplay, side stories, and lack of game world interactivity. The gameplay was far too easy and predictable. There are many different mechanics across the battles, but they are all firing on Beginner difficulty despite being boss-level fights. There is no in-game currency, so you never have to worry about depleting your potions, and an overworld map instead of exploring the world, so gameplay is very streamlined and straightforward but lacks the fun and freedom of discovery. Almost none of the items in the world were interactive (unlike similar games, the best of which add flavor and personality with fun and quirky descriptions). For these reasons, though this game is near and dear to my heart, I'm rating this a solid  I wish I could've spent countless more hours with Roy, Meg, and Golan, but the time we did have will always be a precious memory.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: Initially, the game didn't hook me in, but I kept playing and I'm glad I did, because it was worth the whole play-through.  The mechanics are simple and familiar, and the story is well-crafted and engaging, providing a worthwhile narrative journey. It ultimately delivers a satisfying and pleasant experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Excellent story.  The combat is pokemon style, but still remains unique. The last "battle" had me crying.  If you are a sucker for a story involving a strong seemingly emotionless being becoming emotionally strong, caring, & empathetic while giving you unexpected twists you will enjoy this.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: From the trailer to the demo I was sold on the game and liked what played. So I bought the game and loved every minute of it from beginning to end, it made be laugh and cry until the end. I love the pixel art style for the game is amazing and colorful, it almost remind me of Mother 3, especially some of the scenes and character designs remind me of that game. The soundtrack is also fantastic, and one particular song called "Wishing Star" had me crying my eyes out and stabbed in the heart right in the heart. The combat is interesting since Roy has already max out his HP and is build like a tank that most enemies seem like fleas, but the interesting spin on this is keeping an eye on Meg who has less health and could end the world by crying if her health is down to zero, so you have to balance between fighting and caring for this little girl. Thus making the combat more interesting, and her health gets bigger after each battle.This game may be short (it took me around 10 hrs), but it is a solid game and a lot of enjoy about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine you're Shrek but you end up taking care of a little human girl who fell into the monster underworld instead of befriending a dumbass talking donkey, and that the whole world is in danger of exploding if she gets too sad/scared/hurt and cries.It's a short, non-stressful, simple turn-based combat game that manages to be fun thanks to how it approaches its cute, heartfelt story and how it plays around with its simple turn-based combat by sprinkling some mini-game mechanics and funny dialogue. You can finish the whole thing in less than 4 hours and I enjoyed it a lot as a palate-cleanser between much longer and complex games.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more than its money's worth, even when not on sale.Behind the deceptively simple Pokemon/Earthbound-esque gameplay is an emotional story (some parts of it optional) that tugs on the heartstrings in both sad and happy ways. It isn't a long game, and also features in-battle quick-time events and a few puzzles to break up the usual flow of story/battle/story/battle etc.Usually wouldn't be so direct with a review:  but wishlist this and/or buy it ASAP if it sounds a tiny bit interesting.If you (like me) find it difficult to see what life means in your harder moments, this game is a beacon of hope for we struggling souls.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved it. It's a great story that was different from what I was expecting. The story is the game's best quality, but I can't say much about it because spoilers.The game has a simplistic combat system and few battles, but this is a deliberate choice in order to make each battle feel like a story rather than busywork. The battle system is very versatile and used to its fullest potential to make each encounter unique and memorable.Music is great and used effectively throughout the story. The pixel art style also looks nice, although I wish some things had more animation to them.There are some optional side content, but the game's length is still on the short side at about four hours, I would have liked more content with the quirky cast of side characters before things in the main story start to ramp up.Game ran extremely smoothly and I didn't encounter any bugs.Overall, I'd give this game a 9/10. If you're aching for a short game that tells a good story, this one is a great choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: A small masterpiece. Not so much for its gameplay, strange but very fun, but for the story it tells. It made me cry in both endings, really touching and deep. A really well done pixel style. The characters are really well fleshed out. Happy to have played it. Recommended for those looking for a well-told story, with two endings that turn you inside out. Game that touches you deeply, in your heart!
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this game in one sitting not too long ago. It's a decently short JRPG game with an amazing story, music, characters and pleasant-looking scenery of detail of the dark environments surrounding our characters. I haven't had a game like this that had me constantly tear-jerking so much near the ending of its game in quite a long time. It's a beautiful work of art that tells a down-to-earth story with a mix of silliness and seriousness that really deserves more attention to the general public.I've never played games like the Mother series before, but I was somewhat feeling nostalgic hopping into the RPG mechanics of the game, fighting intimidating, but fun and quick boss fights with the big blue brute and his little companion. It was always a blast mixing up your fighting style when going toe to toe with each new enemy. Easy to understand and isn't too overwhelming learning what you had to do to figure out a certain pattern when in battle.My only complaint is the game not being too "interactive" with its world environments when you have people like me wanting to explore more of the areas and click around on stuff, seeing what's interactable and what the characters think of their surroundings.Highly recommend playing and experiencing the game on their first go. 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this is one of the most emotionally resonant stories I've experienced in a long time. I don't want to say much about it because it truly deserves to be experienced spoiler-free, but everything from the narrative, to the characters, to the worldbuilding and dialogue is just amazing with maybe the best (if sad) ending I've ever seen in a video game.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: There are gripes I have with the pacing, and the combat could use more work. The optional events either don't pay off as much as I'd like, or are fairly important background information. The ending of the story is weirdly split up and depends entirely on a very vague plot-fixer element. I'm sure there's plenty of other issues here and there I could complain about if I felt like it.But I don't really care. Because at the end of the day, it has a few of those moments where a line of dialogue, or an animation, or a song, really *works*, and none of the complaints matter. The heart behind this game shines through clearly in the game's sort-of-two endings, and even if I think the steps along the way felt a bit rushed, that just means there's less time to wait until you get there.
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: The first half of the game felt like a fun walking simulator with a neat enough gimmick and if the game ended when the credits first rolled I would've said it was a decent 6/10 game that takes 2-3 hours... but then you get to the second half.The music boasted a wider variety of tunes with the council having some amazing boss themes, the battles turned into some decent little brawls instead of just being a disguised puzzle. Also the writing went from being mostly comedic to genuinely touching. The side stories were also nice little distractions and the characters were pretty good. The message doesn't go for something like "humans are the real monsters" or "it's a quirky indie game about depression" instead it's about the importance of memories and cherishing your time with loved ones.Also it has a fishing minigame so it's an automatic 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Meg's Monster

_childDocuments_.review: What an outstanding game. Every moment that Meg and Roy are on screen together, I have to hold back an audible “Awwwww…” because they’re JUST. SO. ADORABLE.I love this game. Between this and Mr Saitou, 2023’s really leaning into the “games that turn me into a quivering mess” sub genre. But seriously, Meg’s Monster is incredible. A game more than worth your time and money for some of the most charming, delightful and occasionally depressing moments I’ve seen in recent memory.Strongly recommended through and through.
