_childDocuments_.review: Despite how much I loved the previous games, I cannot recommend this one (at least for now)The way the Chapter/Story mode is done is extremely lazy - half the scenes are represented as slide shows, the other half has a 144p audioless cutscene playing.I really liked the "Sparking" aka "What if" stories in the first 1-2 chapters of Goku playthrough. They even had a "Sparking" indicator in the bottom (which for whatever reason had me really hyped to see what's gonna happen).The way  had me excited for the "what if's", especially later seeing  was really cool, but after that the "what if's" become really boring and lazy.I just finished the Android saga and the what if is literally .Sometimes you can't even differentiate if you're progressing the story as it was in the Anime or if it's a "sparking" story - I don't remember all the details of the series and the differences feel so small. Additionally, the "sparking" indicator all of a sudden stops appearing for some reason after around chapter 2.Most of the time story chapters don't even have any cutscenes or audio, half the time some of the "slide shows" are narrated, others aren't and I couldn't tell what's the criteria of which has or hasn't a narrator.Overall the "what if's" and the story itself seems to be implemented similarly to TWD: Destinies.The way the custom chapters and their creation works is sort of confusing - you can add an opening title, fighters, arena and a closing title and that seemed to be it. Unless I missed something, that seems kind of boring and useless.The character roster is indeed huge, but let's be honest - you will be playing a maximum of 10 characters outside of story mode, so to me it just seemed not as exciting.I have not yet tried any Online battles because I purchased the game mostly for the "What if's", so cannot share personal experience, but saw a lot of reviews pointing out "connectivity issues".

_childDocuments_.review: This game is kinda fun on the surface but once you dig deep it's really irritating to play. I've been playing the Tenkaichi series for as long as I remember and I have never thought I'd have to play a Dragon Ball Game with so many things to slow down the fight. With classic controls you have to deal with clunky controls when transforming or swapping characters, sometimes your special moves in classic controls will merge with the standard controls causing half of your special moves to be unusable, you have to hold the ki charge for about a half a second just to start charging your ki, and parries are so overused and come at no cost so you constantly have to fight around them. Along with glitches and hurtbox issues, this game is really iffy.First things I noticed were small like little to no audio cues on certain things like charging attacks. That was really important in the series because it gave you an idea of when something will break guard or how to time a perfect attack. Now that there's no sound to it, you have to play off of feel and while you can get used to it over time, the game is far too fast paced and flashy to really pay mind to the slight white aura appearing around you. The charge attacks don't really flow seamlessly into combos either which causes inputs to get scuffed or will have your charged attack get stepped easily. Another small thing I noticed was the removal of certain visual cues and mechanics in general. During a physical clash you can't really tell who's going to win the altercation because the attack combo doesn't show anymore. I understand that not knowing who's gonna come out on top is part of the fight but I personally would like to know who's doing better at an altercation. That's really the only clash I can speak on cause most of the clash minigames are extremely unintuitive and despite running into them on many occasions I simply can't understand what is going on. In previous games you would have to spam Circle/B to recover from a guard break, stun move, or charged attack. In this game I don't think they have that mechanic anymore since there's no visual cue to it. When your recovering from a guard break you can mash buttons to recover ki but it doesn't seem like you can recover from other things by mashing anything, so recovery just seems very unclear and once you get stunned you're really at the mercy of your opponent.The parries are a really big issue for me. At worst you waste 2 utility bars and knock them away with the opportunity for a special move and at best you get a perfect parry and drain some of your opponents ki. There's literally no harm in using a parry and I think they wanted the parry to be a big part of the game since the modern controls swap the old block button (Circle/B) with the parry button. While I don't get hit by every single parry thrown my way, I have to constantly maneuver myself around them and hit at awkward intervals because I know if I mess up I'll just get knocked back and work my way back in. It's the most boring concept known to man.A lot more of the beams track you down or count as grabs. SSJ2 Teen Gohan has both of these. His Super Kamehameha tracks like a madman and will chase you down so your options are either to take chip damage, risk a teleport, or waste two utility bars to knock it away. Knocking it away wouldn't be an issue if the Super Kamehameha didn't only take two bars of Ki. His Father-Son Kamehameha counts as a grab so at a certain range it's practically guaranteed. I don't really have an issue with that kind of mechanic but when these attacks move at the speed of light, take two bars of health, and can't be blocked, seeing them from so many characters is really annoying to deal with.The story mode is horrible, it's just a slideshow. That is all :(THERE ARE SO MANY GLITCHES OR HURTBOX ISSUES. Countless times there are moments where special attacks that charge the opponent will completely whiff for no reason and there are moments where my combos just wont move forward which will leave me at a disadvantage. I've had moments where my attacks would clip me through opponents and moments  where I can't use my dodge properly because I'm too close to the opponent and get caught on them. The game is extremely fast paced so I'm sure there's a lot more issues that I miss but these issues cost me a character and sometimes an entire match. I'm constantly having to fight against the game and the opponent just to squeeze out a win.This game has the potential to be really fun and I haven't ran into any extremely broken characters yet but there are so many things that just go wrong in any given match.Deleted the game on 10/23/2024, game is genuinely a waste of time.

_childDocuments_.review: Good : - Very good roster- Characters, animations, effects are gorgeous - Gameplay is fun but it has some flawsBad :- Story mode is pretty bad and short. Mix of cinematic and static/slideshow images. Even the videos are pixelated for some reasons. Lot of fights missing, some iconic scene are wasted. Remember first SSJ transformation of Goku, yeah you can forget that, it'll just cut to him already in SSJ form. You want to perform the father/son kameha against Cell as Gohan ? Forget that, you won't have access to the attack during the fight, it'll go in the slideshow. Many more cons but you get the ideas.- Menuing is awfull, nice screens but it's the worse ergonomic ♥♥♥♥ and 50% of the time you'll get some stuttering when switching menu. Oh you wanna personalize a character ? Ok then go to this tab, now you select shop/customize, you got a small cinematic on a tv, where you now choose between shop and customize. Let say you go to the shop to buy some clothes. Wanna equip that ? Ok you need to go back to the very first menu and select again that shop/customize menu, get the cinematic again, and NOW select customize. Who stupid ass designed this ? And that's just an example, wanna modify your control during training mode ? Nop you need to go back on main menu first and start training mode again to try it out.- Environments are mid (some texture are very ugly), they should have done it in a anime/cell-shading style as for the characters.- Game is not always fluid, even with really strong GPU you'll get some stuttering (4080 Super OC) + locked at 60 fps. I would have prefer a simplier environment more close to the anime for better artsyle + fluidity- That lead to very bad compromise. Shared-screen multiplayer is limited to one single map with lesser graphic settings. And that map is the room of spirit and time cause it's just empty and white. Laughable... You can forget inviting some friend to play with you at home.- Gameplay is fun but sometime unresponsive, some controls are weird, some move will work 50% of the time. Just an example, you press X + X + ↓ Y + ↑ Y to make you enemy fall and make a grab attack taking is leg and throwing him away. Sometimes it'll work, sometimes you'll just kikoha his face on the ground ( cause Y is also for kikoha attack ). - Bandai greed at its best with pre-release for people who pay more, and even worse with 2 different music pack if you wanna get some classic OST in game. Even if you pay 110 euros to get the ultimate edition you'll have to pay 30 more to get those. What a joke.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a step down from the previous games. I loved the older games and this one is definitely fun but it's definitely not worth it unless you played the old games and love nostalgia or are a hardcore Dragonball fan in general and even then, there are more fun Dragonball games out there. Feels like it was made by AI. The game's CPU is dumb and incredibly cheesable, it will get lost and can't find you when it's standing 10 feet in front of you sometimes. The story is... Well, let's say I'm pretty sure whoever directed the dialogue in this game has never watched the anime or read the manga to the point where it gets comical at times.. I was streaming the game to my friend (mildly knowledgeable fan) and I had to constantly explain why the game is telling him straight up nonsense, even he laughed at the characters coming to the same realisation twice in the same cutscene. Seriously the mobile games have more work put into them than this, even the super moves feel very low effort and wonky. The UI feels slow and responds weird, I have tried on both KBM and xbox controller, it just feels bad and poorly designed. The game lets you do custom battles vs. a CPU while you wait for an opponent in ranked, I'm not sure if it's because the game hasn't completely released or something I tried a few games with a few different settings and sat there forever without getting a match. The dragonballs do not feel rewarding. Bulma spams dialogue at you in the store just for you XV2 fans. The old playstyle of the tenkaichi games doesn't hold up as well compared to other modern games in and out of the franchise and it feels like it needs more meat.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the Tenkaichi series, you’re gonna love this game. It’s basically a sequel. The mechanics feel good, although a bit mashy, but there’s still some depth if you want to take it online and go up against other players. There's definitely a skill ceiling, not super high, but enough to scratch that itch for hardcore fighting game fans. How long it'll keep them hooked? I’m not so sure.For everyone else, this game is just awesome. The presentation’s solid, and the story mode isn't just the same ol retelling we've seen for literal decades now. There’s replay value since you’re encouraged to go back and unlock different story paths with episodes following many different characters giving perspectives we haven't seen before. Some of these alternate stories are really well done with full-on motion captured cutscenes. There’s also a ton of content, custom battle mode lets you set up your own fights with a backstory, and you can customize your characters. I could keep going, but you get the point.  There’s clearly a lot of love put into this game.Of course, there are some downsides. While the story mode shines, not every episode got the same level of care. For example, Goku Black’s saga feels pretty barebones compared to Goku’s. A lot of it is told through slideshows, which is a letdown. Honestly, I expected some inconsistencies with this much content, but I’m just glad most of it is solid. And then there’s the whole thing with the anime music being locked behind another paywall, even outside of the Ultimate Edition. That's just plain greedy. It’s frustrating they didn’t include it in the Ultimate bundle. Namco knows what they’re doing, and yeah, it pisses me off but at this point it’s what we’ve come to expect smh

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game.Its great to finally get a proper DBZ game after so many years. Poor efforts in Xenoverse 2, DBZ Kakarot, FighterZ can all now be forgotten. We finally have a game where we are (nearly...) playing the anime for our selves.========The Good========- Graphics on the Character models, Beams and smoke/explosion effects are fantastic. Literally like the anime it self.- Huge list of characters from Dragon Ball, to Dragon Ball Z, Dragon Ball GT and Dragon Ball Super, DBZ Movies========The Ok========- I grew up watching the Ocean/Funimation dub of DBZ. The voice work is good in parts and not so good in others. For example adult Gohan's super attack voice work does not match the mouth movements. The dub director should have really checked these things. ========The Bad========- While I praised the graphics in the good section, it was just the graphics on the character models and effects that are god tier. The real let down for me was the very dumb decision to use realistic 3D environments. Its super jarring to see anime quality models fighting in effectively a realistic mountain locations amongst others. The environments/stages should have been matched to the fantastic character modelling art style. I am  VERY let down by this and I dont even think mods could fix this. I would pay for a DLC to fix the crappy 3D real environments.- Weird pop in on the 3D environments. You'll notice during cutscenes and story the textures loading in, things link grass on the ground will pop int (I run of my SSD so should not be an issue)- Music. Sure they wont use the funimation dub but other Bandai games let you add a library of custom mp3's into the game or replace existing tracks. Very poor show here and limits the ability to enjoy the sound track.- Combat!? Super weird in the sense your counters have to be nano second perfect to pull of, it takes the fun out of the game for me. I have no plans to ever play this online and will only ever play offline. Recreating cool moments owning characters are too hard to recreate.- Story. Yes we've seen it many times but weird things like key moments being very short cut scenes (Goku's SSJ transformation vs Freiza), slide show presentations of other story parts and no narrator talking at times, just having to read text are a let down.========Summary========A great DBZ game for fans with some faults but it is the best DBZ game since Legend of the Super Saiyan on the SNES. It gets a solid 8/10. I am interested to see what sort of DLC will come in the long term and if quality of life features will be added and issues fixed.

The one thing we as kids loved about DBZ back then is missing from this game. And that is why I cannot recommend it. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DRDragon Ball Sparking Zero delivers stunning visuals and exhilarating combat, but it stumbles hard in story mode, feeling rushed and incomplete. If you’re here for PvP and fun online fights, you’ll enjoy it. But if, like me, you value a fleshed-out story mode, you might walk away disappointed.  ---I have mixed feelings about *Dragon Ball Sparking Zero*. On the one hand, the game looks absolutely stunning, and the mechanics are a blast to play around with. The fights are fast-paced and super fun, though the camera can get a bit janky at times, and in certain scenarios, button presses don't always seem to register as they should. Still, it captures that nostalgic Budokai Tenkaichi 3 feeling very well, which is a huge plus for me. And let me just say—PvP is really cool and something I’ve genuinely enjoyed.However, the story mode was a complete letdown. Without spoiling anything, it feels rushed, unfinished, and unloved. The only "What If" scenario that felt somewhat decent to me was Gohan's, but beyond that, it’s just disappointing. I can’t tell if they left content out to sell as DLC later or if the story mode just wasn’t their priority, but either way, it just doesn’t hit right. Much of the story is presented through basic slideshows, kind of like what *Ninja Storm Connections* did, which really takes away from the experience.I know this review might get a lot of hate because Sparking Zero is so well-received, and I can understand why. What the game does well, it really does well. But for someone like me who values a good story mode, especially for the "What If" scenarios, it was a big disappointment. Even Xenoverse 2 did the story better than this, in my opinion.I haven't tried custom battles yet since I’m waiting to see what other players come up with, but I’m definitely looking forward to seeing the community's creations in the coming weeks.So if you're someone who values what I value—mainly a rich story mode—then I wouldn't recommend this game right now. But if you just want a fun Dragon Ball game where you can enjoy online fights, then Sparking Zero will probably be perfect for you.

_childDocuments_.review: 1. Game is unpolished, weird bugs, bad lock on. Episode Battle (Story mode) is lackluster, a lot of fights missing for the protagonists that aren't Goku. The Slide Shows and in game "cinematics" look awful for the most part. Dialogue during episode battle doesn't continue unless you press a button, etc.2. Online doesn't function for a lot of people (Communication error - Game disconnects you)3. Gameplay is flawed and there's a lot of ways people can cheese wins by abusing objectively bad design choices by the developers (Sparking into ki blast spam, giants sparking and spamming dragon rush onto you, afterimage strike spam, instant sparking type abilities with no drawback, vanishing is too easy and you can go into vanishing loop until one of the players runs out of ki, and MORE!!!)4. 60 FPS cap in late 2024... - modding the game in offline to unlock FPS makes it so much better, but online will always be locked to 60 FPS5. Players can rage quit ranked online matches with 0 punishment and the person that gets quitted on doesn't gain their ranked points. That's right, rage quitter does NOT lose points or get punished and the person that's usually about to win and gets rage quitted on gets nothing.The developers should have taken a year extra at the very least to test their own game and improve it, polish it and add more content. A bad and lackluster story mode because the game is "focused" on online is not an excuse, especially when online doesn't even work properly. Also smaller issues: Changing between options in the game menu is slow and annoying, the non ranked lobbies are unnecessary and a waste of time, just give an option for instant matchmaking like ranked and make lobbies a different option. So many terrible decisions, I don't understand how no one in the developer team can see them.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★ - Great  16 hours  Normal  		• The combat mechanics are fast-paced and fluid and flexible, allowing for high-speed aerial battles and powerful energy attacks similar to its predecessors in the 'Dragon ball Budokai Tenkaichi' series.		• The character roster is a standout feature, offering a wide range of characters, their variants and their many transformations (Approx 85 Characters, 182 including the variations).		• The controls are responsive, but the combo system may feel clunky until you've had more time learning the system.		• There are a few difficulty spikes in the episodes, sometimes making battles frustrating rather than challenging.  		• The Goku Episodic Battles story follows a fast-paced retelling of the original Dragon Ball Z and Dragon Ball Super arcs but with a few alternate what-if paths. The other Character Episodic Battles focus on a handful of arcs for each character.		• Episodic Battles skip over smaller story beats to focus on the main ones. But as someone who didn't watch all of Dragon Ball Super, I felt like I got the general gist of the story that played out.		• Custom Battles allows you to create and play other people's custom one-shot campaigns which gives almost unlimited replayability to recreate fights that aren't previewed in the standard episodes or to make fights that are completely different. 		• Dialogue can be hit or miss, sometimes in translation, sometimes repetitive due to repeating key moves but is overall passable.		• There are some fun interactions between less-featured characters, particularly in what-if scenarios, though these moments can be few and far between.  		• The cel-shaded art style and animation does justice to the anime, with explosive energy effects that mirror the show’s iconic moments.		• Character models are well-detailed, though environments can feel bland and repetitive.		• It would have been nice if the retelling cutscenes were also in-game rather than just flash cards however due to scope of the game, I can understand why it was downscaled.  		• When in Episodes, Pause the game and go into Battle details to check the objectives. Alternative Objectives (Only allowed on Normal Difficulty) will send you to what-if scenarios.		• Skill Points (Big Blue number) will let you charge Ki to Sparking! Mode or otherwise use numbered abilities. It is work using these tactically in your fights.		• If the Up Symbol appears on your character, hold up on the D-pad during a battle to give you a menu to transform.		• If the reset Symbol is fully charged, hold left on the D-pad to switch to a different team member. In Episodes, you want to do this where possible to prevent knockout; a single Knockout will cause you to fail mission.		• Pause battle and check Explanation of Controls for buffs and specific character skills.		• Spend time in the Super Training mode to get a keen eye on individual moves, blocking, combos and dodges to get full acquainted with the combat.		• Multiplayer is fun but not beginner-friendly. It’s advisable to brush up on single-player modes before jumping into online matches.		• The game has some balancing issues, so expect certain characters to feel much stronger than others in both PvE and PvP.		• If you haven't spent any money\zeni, completing all of the Goku Episode should give you enough money to buy all purchasable characters.		• When Summoning Super Shenron, you want to purchase Characters or Ability Items. As they cannot be gotten elsewhere.		• Shenron and Namekian\Potunga Shenron Balls can be farmed by playing Offline Battle with the CPU (5% chance per ball). 		• Super Shenron can only be accessed 3-4 times. 1 from completing Goku Campaign, 2 from Future Trunks Normal and Alternative endings respectively and 1 from purchasing the Ultimate Edition.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fighting game, it almost excels. You can do mixups, callouts and counters. You can land combos, and then your opponent gets a few options to counter. They can block high and low, they can sidestep out of the way, and if they correctly call you out, you get stunned and they can combo you. Or you can grab them, or jump behind them, all of these have callouts that can punish you. There's also a resource you can spend to stop their attacks via revenge counters, mid combo, but even that can be called out if you counter it properly.So yeah, great game... At least... almost.Sadly, there's a game mechanic that literally ruins the entire competitive aspect of the game. It's called a super counter. Hit up and punch within some frames of the attack landing, and you do a super counter. These counters can be done at any time, regardless of position, regardless of attack, and regardless of resources. It costs nothing and gives you a follow up attack. To simplify it: There is literally no such thing as a combo. You literally cannot combo off of anything, because anything can be super countered at any time. All those mechanics I mentioned before? The high low mix? The timing counters? The resource counters? None of it matters. You have a free, perfect counter to everything that can't be punished. It breaks your opponent's combo even if they catch you with a huge whiff punish.There's no such thing as a punish.No such thing as a combo. No such thing as a whiff. You can just super counter out of it.It makes bots extremely frustrating to fight, as well. All in all, the game would be absolutely amazing if not for a single mechanic. The cutscenes are horrible, too. If you're not a Dragon Ball fan, you won't enjoy this. I know not everything HAS to be competitive, but the super counter also makes the fights look less like cool dragon ball fights. This, at the very least, ruins it for me, personally.I'd recommend it, if you either like Dragon Ball, or if it cost less than $40. At $70, this game is not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the Dragon Ball franchise, I grew up playing Dragon Ball Z: Budokai Tenkaichi 3, a game I absolutely adored. It’s hard to believe it’s been 17 years since that iconic title, and I never thought I’d see a sequel. Now, with Dragon Ball: Sparking Zero, we finally have a new installment that, while imperfect, has captured much of the essence of what made the original so special.Let’s address the elephant in the room: the game can feel unbalanced and at times a bit of a chaotic mess. The roster of characters is vast, but this comes at a cost. There are numerous transformations counted as separate characters, which can lead to confusion for people saying " OH WE HAVE 60 GOKUS! Yeah thats the beauty of the game. Additionally, the ranked mode has garnered criticism for being unfair. The amount of rage-quitting I've witnessed is disheartening—players quitting mid-match to avoid losing and subsequently preventing others from ranking up is incredibly frustrating. Yet, despite these issues, I can’t help but appreciate how much I’ve wanted a game that embraces this chaotic spirit. It feels like a worthy successor to Budokai Tenkaichi 3, and I genuinely love it for that.The story mode, however, leaves much to be desired. While it lacks depth and coherence, it shines in its inclusion of numerous "what if" battles. These alternate scenarios provide a refreshing twist on the familiar narrative and are undoubtedly one of the highlights of the game. They keep the experience interesting and allow for creativity in how the story unfolds.One major area where players seem to struggle is in their interaction with the game’s mechanics. There is a robust training mode available, yet many players seem hesitant to utilize it. Learning the intricacies of the combat system can significantly enhance gameplay and improve overall performance. I encourage everyone to take advantage of this feature—mastering the mechanics can make a world of difference.Regarding ranked matches, I believe a punishment system for rage quitting is essential. Implementing penalties for players who bail on matches would help create a fairer and more enjoyable competitive environment.On a more positive note, the custom battles feature is a standout aspect of Dragon Ball: Sparking Zero. It’s fantastic that fans can create and share their own unique battle scenarios, adding a layer of personalization and creativity that enhances the overall experience. This flexibility allows players to engage with the game in ways that resonate with their preferences, making for an even more dynamic gameplay experience.Dragon Ball: Sparking Zero is a game filled with potential and beauty. While it certainly has its flaws, the nostalgia it invokes and the opportunities it presents make it an exciting addition to the franchise. I’m genuinely thrilled about this game, and I can’t wait to see how it evolves. Here’s to hoping the developers continue to refine it and that the community embraces the spirit of Dragon Ball in all its Broken Messy nonsense!

_childDocuments_.review: Very unpleasant experience for the first few hours. The game starts by throwing you into a "tutorial" that doesn't actually explain any of the game mechanics and just forces you to press each button on the controller one by one. The problem with this is that most buttons have multiple context dependent functions, so explaining only ONE of those functions with NO CONTEXT is really not helpful. The in game "training" isn't much better and all the "assist" functions in the menus have NO EXPLANATION AS TO THEIR FUNCTION. The "details" of each of the nearly 10 ASSIST SETTINGS just allow you to toggle it ON or OFF with no real detail as to how each setting operates. It is a really enjoyable experience after the first 20 hours of figuring out how the game works, so be prepared for that if you're not familiar with existing mechanics from previous games.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to... relive the DBZ and part of DBS experience in a somewhat abridged format, broken into sections, from multiple different view points, with alternate story arcs, this game delivers on that in a really nice manner.I have never been very good at fighting games, but the combat is generally pretty fun. However what I do find frustrating is the bugginess of the combat. I've had multiple, upon multiple instances, of being in sparking mode, rapidly pressing X until I knock the opponent down. I will then try to use the ultimate attack and I start punching air instead of using the ultimate. Extremely frustrating, ya know? So let's say that's enough for you to just narrowly miss the timer for the alternate ending and the mission you're on is a timer. Wouldn't it be nice to be able to press start so you can back out to the main menu or show a retry feature? Sorry, you must wait till the programmers have deemed it necessary until you can use that feature. ALT+F4 is slower, so you're forced to wait. Ah, I know, I will hold in X to skip the cutscenes to make this annoying process faster! Ooooh, sorry, that too is buggy and sometimes it just won't work even though it is available (but it's not always available through the cutscenes).I can deal with bugginess, and I can deal with bad menus, but I can't deal with both in large doses. This becomes a real travesty when you consider the fun potential the story mode missions have for existing Dragonball fans.. On the other hand, once you understand how to get to most alternate story arcs is simply by "getting good and going fast", they all become trivial as long as the game decides to not get buggy on you.It's 2024 and developers still insist on ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ menu design and usability. We should be past this point.

_childDocuments_.review: Rarely play a game so much during its launch period (43 hours in 8 days and got all Achievements) so decided to write a somewhat lengthy review for once:Roster: Despite me being a weird who thinks Red Ribbon Saga is the best Arc in all of Dragon Ball and thus obviously being disappointed in the rep we get from the first 16 Volumes, which is just pre-23rd Tenkaichi Budokai Goku and some outfits for characters like Yamcha and Roshi, i'm still very impressed with getting such a huge roster at launch, that's genuinely comparable to BT3, a game that had two previous games to build off of. Especially was surprising to see pre Battle of Gods movies and GT having a decent presence, i very much expected them as DLC bait but a Budokai Tenkaichi game isn't complete without SS4 Gogeta so i'm glad we got them in base roster even if i'd personally trade most of movie characters for characters from the earlier sagas.Visuals: Not to much say here tbh, it's based off Shintani's style from DBS Broly which i personally love and they did a great job translating it into 3D imo.Single-Player: Easily some of the most fun i had with a story mode in a DB fighter, really enjoy the CPU actually using the in-game mechanics properly, reminds me a lot of Infinite World's CPUs which i also adored. There are still obvious shortcomings though, the presentation in the canon routes is lackluster, luckily they tend to be much better in the What-If scenarios which are the story highlight here, especially loved Trunks and Gohan's What-If routes, Goku and Frieza also get some very fun ones too. Haven't touched player-made custom battles yet or tried creating them myself but i did enjoy the Bonus Battles the game comes with it, they're pretty short but still fun alternate scenarios.The way you do character unlocks is also nice, you can just outright buy them with Zeni if you don't wanna bother with certain content but unlocks can also be done via story paths or even bonus battles and some via Shenron wishes, and if you used Zeni to unlock a character/costume you get the amount refunded when you do the story or bonus battle that unlocks themMultiplayer: Primarily played online so this will be just focused on that and uhhh... unfortunately its not a good experience rlly. There doesn't seem to much punishing against rage quitters so it's very common, i had my first rage quitter in only 20 battles. There's other issues too like non-existent Anti-Cheat so nothing stopping cheating and the game unfortunately also lacks cross play even though by now it's a standard in AAA fighters. More than that though what probably annoys me the most is this game having the worst Ranked player base i have seen in a fighter, i did 100 matches so far in ranked and could genuinely count on one hand when players did a full set, people always quit after 1-0, 0-1, 1-1, doesn't matter which way it went, it feels extremely rare to get a proper Best of 3 even.At least connections on average felt decent, though when it gets even slightly bad it does feel terrible and you won't be able to do basic mechanics like Z-Counters at all with proper timing.The worst of all though is that atm there is a bug where with Classic Controls you can't use the first Blast 2 at all when facing someone using Standard, really hope it gets fixed soon.Gameplay: Well its Budokai Tenkaichi so expect unbalanced as ♥♥♥♥ over the top combat with occasional camera issues, not much to say, its very much what you'd expect from the series.and Afterimage Strike is hilariously busted this time, Super Vegetto feels almost like a cheat code with it lmao.Unfortunately though the game does have a pretty blatant issue on PC, which is the Shader Stuttering, it's not the worst example of it since the game seems to share effects for a lot of stuff so you can compile them decently fast but it does suck every game/driver update you have to prepare for initial stuttering unless they fix it in one of the patchesRanted a lot during this review so maybe surprising i still recommend it, but i do think its genuinely worth it for the roster and visuals alone, especially if you have someone to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on my experience of playing this game from release and until today -- the day I 100% the achievements -- I want to say I really do enjoy the game. Most people on here are reasonably upset with the lack of communication and updates from the devs, but I want to say the only major flaw I have encountered was the button swap issue when playing online, and that is why my hours aren't insanely high. For some time, I went on hiatus until these glitches were resolved, but they had fixed the glitch at the same time as when Yajirobe was nerfed - whom I mained for a bit - not knowing tier lists or lack of caring for it.See, I have been paying attention to all Dragon Ball games since BT2 on PS2, and when this game was announced, and also being knowledgeable of the FGC, I was hoping people could relax with this game, because there was no balanced characters. So, when I did play Yajirobe taking out God characters and Fusions, I was grinning ear to ear. However, people cried, my character died, and I buried the game for a time.Now I just play characters that annoy people, like Pan, Videl, and a bunch of other lore weak characters. It's fun. I'm competitive to a point, but only to play the game the way I like it, not based on meta, so I don't get upset when people rage quit or use overused characters whom I'd assume are top tier.For the single player experience, I will admit most was a chore, and for the parts where I hoped they put more effort into the story, they flopped (looking at you SSJ Goku's first transformation on Planet Namek). Now where I actually paid attention and was pleasantly surprised was the What If bits, they were great and entertaining.The bonus matches that people created were hit and miss, but I can see some solid time put in there for those who were big on making YouTube fanfics with subtitles using Windows Movie Maker from eons ago. Keep up the good work the lot of you! I'd love to make a YouTube series of cool stories to showcase.I hope the game continues to have as much support as Xenoverse 2 is getting, and if sequels come maybe consider the Raging Blast 3 Fanwish Project approach. As of right now, I think it's bare for what the game offers, but I cannot ignore this game as a love letter to Dragon Ball fans.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat and the "what-if's" are the only upside to this game. Even then, both have their large downsides. Outside of combat, the cutscenes are soulless. Anything rendered with the in-game engine looks uncanny. Their eyes rarely move, and the only thing that really does move is their hair. Anything that's animated is in 720p. It would be easier to ignore this if DBZ Kakarot didn't exist and upstage them easily in both of these aspects. The difficulty is great. I love it. The combat is fun once you learn it. Every "what-if" has a lot of love put into it, and a few of them caught me entirely off guard like Gohan's. Couch co-op is ruined by only having one stage and terrible split screen. Online co-op is ruined by a lack of rollback netcode. I could let DBFZ get away with this 4 years ago, but this is a Budokai Tenkaichi game. They are FOUNDED on the premise of multiplayer. The entire franchise's legacy is multiplayer, and they failed to implement the most important feature for good connectivity. I can't tell what their goal was, but it doesn't feel like they accomplished it. It's not a good fighting game like FighterzIt's not a good Dragon Ball game like KakarotIt just falls short of the mark everywhere that it mattered.Edit: I completely take back my statement on the "what-if's" after playing through Goku Black and Goku's story. A. Half of them don't even make sense. So what if I beat Fused Zamasu in under a minute. He's immortal. How did I even kill him as blue Goku? If he dies he should just turn into Infinite Zamasu. It completely goes against the entire struggle of that arc. B. They're boring and repetitive. Every Goku Black "what-if" is just "What if Goku Black... won in ten minutes instead of eleven?" It's so dull. Every new ending for him is just winning in a different time. It's beyond bland. They could've done so much more, but they sacrificed quality for quantity.

_childDocuments_.review: Sparking Zero is pretty has pretty much everything you would want in a budokai game, as someone who has been playing the budokai series for years everything in past games is present and improved in this game in my opinion, other than the campaign (which is fine with me as the campaign has never been what attracts me to the budokai series). For a $70 game, the slideshow cutscenes and sparse use of VA dialogue make it feel kinda cheap, but all I really care about is fighting online and with friends which I think is done very well here, better than any budokai game to date especially with the graphics. One thing I am missing in sparking zero is being able to pull off ridiculous fusions, but for all the other improvements made I can live without the random fusions. My only complaint with this game is the netcode and destructible environments when playing online. Some maps seriously grind the gameplay to a halt with how slow they make movement and attacks, making it pretty impossible to react to things as they are happening and force to you telegraph your moves sometimes a good 5-7 seconds in advance because of how slow the gameplay is. I find this issue to be especially bad with the martial arts tournament map. As a result I mostly play on the time chamber map since it is completely empty and has no destructible environment to slow the game down. I hope this is an issue that can be fixed over time, because getting off an attack that does trigger the destructible or changeable environment of a map is seriously cool and adds a lot to the atmosphere of the fight in my opinion. As of writing this review there are a few particular characters that definitely feel unbalanced and hopefully that will be fixed with time and updates as well. Overall as someone who preordered the ultimate edition I am loving the game and highly recommend it even at full price to any fan of dragon ball, you will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for a real successor to Budokai Tenkaichi 3 for more than a decade and it's finally here. This game is a masterclass in fan service and passion. The graphics are excellent and most of the time the game looks exactly like the anime except for the deflated muscles. The animations are gorgeous (except for Jiren's goofy walk) and the effects are a sight to behold.I see a lot of people complaining about how the game is simple or not complex enough in terms of combat, how it's just a mash fest and requires no skill, but I haven't noticed that. Maybe it's because I'm a casual/bad player, but I find the combat excellent and immersive, but then again I loved the combat in Raging Blast 2 as well.I love all the secret pre-battle interactions between various characters, all the special grabs that only happen if you choose the right characters, etc.. There are many secrets to be discovered and there's a reason to use all characters.The developers are obviously quite passionate about the game and are constantly making changes/adding things based on players' opinions, which is sadly rare in the gaming world of today. I hope they keep it up and improve the game even more.All in all it's a 10/10 from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Go ahead, laugh at my hour-in refund. I guess at 28 I'm growing out of my ability to keep up with the newer fighting games of this younger generation. I cannot follow the ADHD levels of reaction time needed and complexity of inputs; everything is timed, and a lot of the bundled buttons make zero sense to where I can't keep up with the story A.I. Looks great, sure, love the roster and stoked to see who else gets released and added to it. But, I cannot play this game, it's like fusing together input complexity similar to Street Fighter and Tekken, just 3D and Dragon Ball themed with awful button mapping.Dashing, boosts, and steps should be their own damn button, vanish follow-ups should just be the desired attack button and direction instead of requiring ANOTHER button to teleport. Blocking and defensive vanishing was fine, no qualms there. All of these counters should be a simpler input paired with the damn block button, not scattered across the controller.Maybe I'm too hard-wired to expect Raging Blast 2 or Xenoverse style simplicity, but it is what it is. Buy this game if you want to tear your hair out to play a complex Dragon Ball game and play for hours just learning. Also, my first time recommendation is to lower the story difficulty for the first run. Great Ape Vegeta is a damn menace, and has the mechanic of hyper armor that Bandai loved in the Budokai Tenkaichi series, which pushed me away from those games then, same as now.Good luck, praise to you who can actually keep up, and farewell!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, however people saying it's the best game in the Tenkaichi series are just plain crazy or had their brain corroded from the 17 year gap between Tenkaichi 3 and this.The character roster is pretty lacklustre, yes "180 characters" but that doesn't really mean anything when at least 70 of those are different Goku and Vegeta variations and fusions. Take those out and the rest of the selection is pretty bland when compared to Tenkaichi 3. How did Spopovich make the cut yet we're missing stuff like Shin, Super 17, the Shadow Dragons, Tao, etc? Speaking of which, the game has no Dragon Ball representation at all aside from Kid Goku (and Roshi), what a joke.12 stages. 12. And mostly bland ones at that, with the best ones being World of the Kais and Namek. Several classic and iconic locations missing, such as Kami's Lookout, Glacier, Hell (Janemba), Space, Babidi's Ship, Mount Paozu, among others. Also no Ruined Planet mechanic, great.Story mode is short and also lacking, since it's missing 80% of the fights in the series, and you can only play through the story with a handful of characters. Yeah the what ifs are cool as always, but you can finish story mode in around 1 hour of playtime.I get that they want to release stuff as dlc later but the game as it is now feels very, very incomplete. Its saving grace is the online stuff, which is always fun. However if you're not playing online the game gets REALLY boring after 5 hours or so, which was not the case with other games in this series.I'd wait for a "Super Duper Ultimate Definitive Complete" down the line which includes all the upcoming dlc and stuff before buying this at full price

_childDocuments_.review: The Budokai Tenkaichi games were some of my absolute favorite games during my adolescence; needless to say I was very excited about their revival with Dragon Ball: Sparking! ZERO. The combat system is outstanding with several layers to it and techniques to master, the graphics look amazing and each fight is exciting, not to mention the incredibly diverse roster of fighters. Nonetheless, the campaign is a disaster. It's a slog to get through it all, with constant cuts and narrative structure that makes no sense (if you are not familiar with Dragon Ball's story, you will be lost), as well as cringy dialogue and over-exposition. But despite everything, it has some cool what-if scenarios and challenging fights that will test your abilities.

_childDocuments_.review: Sparking Zero is a game that feels like a warm embrace from an old friend. It's a neoclassical gem that seamlessly blends the nostalgia of the original Dragon Ball games with modern gameplay mechanics. The graphics are a visual treat, capturing the essence of the classic anime with stunning detail and vibrant colors.The gameplay is nothing short of exhilarating. Each match is a tense, nerve-wracking battle where every move counts. The characters feel incredibly responsive and powerful, allowing for fluid combos and devastating attacks. It's a game that rewards skill and strategy, but also leaves room for a bit of luck and intuition.What truly sets Sparking Zero apart is its ability to evoke a sense of familiarity while still feeling fresh and exciting. The characters are instantly recognizable, but they feel more alive and dynamic than ever before. The story is a love letter to the original Dragon Ball series (pretty short but consistant), filled with heartfelt moments and epic battles.In short, Sparking Zero is a must-play for any fan of the Dragon Ball franchise. It's a game that captures the spirit of the classic titles while offering a modern gameplay experience that is both challenging and rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: As a longtime fan of Dragon Ball and Tenkaichi 3, Sparking Zero is a blast from the past with a modern twist (disclaimer: I don’t typically write reviews, but I genuinely wanted to write this to help people on the fence with making a purchase).If you grew up with the fast-paced, over-the-top battles of BT3, you’ll feel right at home here as Sparking Zero does a fantastic job of preserving the core mechanics and chaotic energy that made the Tenkaichi series so beloved. The roster is huge, with tons of characters and transformations, just like the old days, and the fights are even more intense and cinematic. The devs did a great job taking what worked previously and improving on it substantially.The controls and combat flow feel snappy, making it easy to jump back into that classic style of play and I love that they implemented the two control options for different play styles. The visuals and animations have been given a beautiful overhaul on the Unreal Engine while still maintaining the nostalgic look and feel of the older games. That said, it’s not without its rough edges. I’m finding the pace of the story mode, so far, to be very fast and newcomers of the series may be lost at certain points. On the technical side, the AI can be a bit unpredictable with difficulty spikes, and the camera isn’t always perfect, especially in tight spots. But if you’re here for the nostalgia and the over-the-top action, these issues are easy to overlook and this is a easy recommendation.Overall, Sparking Zero is a love letter to the Budokai Tenkaichi series, and to Dragon Ball. Again, as a fan of BT3, I couldn’t be happier to see this style of gameplay alive and kicking again in 2024. It’s surreal seeing this game on Steam and I wish Akira Toriyama could’ve lived longer to see this game’s massive success, but I’m satisfied with my purchase and hopefully if you’ve read this far, you will be too.It’s not a perfect experience, but it captures the spirit of what made those games great and to me, this is already the best entry in the series (now if we can just increase the numbers of maps). If you’re looking for epic, fast-paced battles with that classic Tenkaichi flair, Sparking Zero is worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: What I like:I have been playing DBZ games ever since 1997 when DBZ Legends, DB GT Final Bout and DBZ Ultimate Battle 22 were released for the first time on Playstation 1 and ever since I've been playing almost every single game released of this franchise. I also played all the DBZ Budokai, DBZ  Budokai Tenkaichi, Xenoverse 1 and 2, Kakarot and FighterZ as well and always enjoyed the Tenkaichi formula the most out of all of them ever since Budokai Tenkaichi 1 was released. With that being said, I personally consider DB Sparking Zero to be the king of all Tenkaichi games to almost perfect and definitely recommend it to everyone who loves DB/Z/GT/S/D.--What I dislike:But no matter how good a game can be there are still some issues and set backs and I will mention them next:The story mode at first it feels lacking in drama and narrator telling the story in the background but as you get into it you start to appreciate it specially after you play the story chapter of Vegeta. The first person angle in the stories could've been better if it gave more angles and freedom to look around but it was an interesting touch only that it feels very limited and rigid but it gives a new dimension to the story at least.I believe the reason the story mode is the way it is, is because of the customize mode where you can make your own story with a whole editing option which takes a lot of time to make something good and upload it in the online for other players to play your made up story and share it and so on. Really adds a lot of replay value to the game.The combat is the best of all games but if you expect that each character will fight different then this isnt the game for you as they all use the same formula for combos and combinations. The characters are semi unique on their own with the different special skills and passive skills and visually but in combat is really not that unique with all honesty. Expect the same as all the other Tenkaichi games only better. During the combat its really hard to learn it at first even with the tutorial that sadly it doesnt tell all specially the most important part of the game which is being able to be released from "back shots" which is when you get locked in a combo as you are being hit from your back. You need to master the Super Counter which is Up+Attack button. The problem is that the game doesnt explain anything in depth on how to do it correctly and this is where most players rage quit the game. And even knowing exactly how it works, the game doesnt seem to really respond as you would expect specially in online as there is discrepancy in the connection. Its a whole learning curve and its mandatory because both players and the computer in high lvls will always do backshots.My mayor let down of the game is the offline PVP as the devs gave the excuse of having only the hyperbolic time chamber to play with your local friends and its because they were not able to work on some elements about the stages involving destructions in offline pvp  which sounds like excuses to me. On top of that its very common getting knocked back to unfocus your opponent and makes it tedious and hard to find them again in such big stage that is only mostly white with myst making it way too hard to find your opponent to refocus. It was so much for my friends that their experience was mostly negative and it was very frustrating for me to admit they were right with their critics.The other issues is that whenever you play online, there is a bug which remaps your controller if you are using "classic controllers" vs someone using "standard controller" and it confused the game to change your buttons mapping to make the special attack be the same button making it almost impossible to play. So if you play classic, you will feel forced to get used to standard as its what the majority plays. Hopefuly this has been noticed and fix soon.The game is clear in about a week if you really dedicate to it and once you are done the only replay value is the online and farming dragonballs that can be found only as a random loot after finishing offline vs cpu mode making it very very tedious and boring to collect all the dragonballs. I would've loved if they used the same way it was done in Xenoverse but its what it is.My other issue is that the game offers a lot of slots for clothes and empty space for accesories making you thirsty to think there are many unlockables as you progress and having you wanting more and leaving you with a lot of expectations to the customization but the sad thing is that there is almost to nothing to these elements. The only unlocks are characters, music, and cpu a.i. gamestyles. If the devs would've added as much variety in customization as Xenoverse 2 it would've make this game way way more lasting.And last but not least, while the action and special abilities feels pretty good and solid, after playing games such as Kakarot, most of them feels lacking. You have no idea how soft the Kamehameha feels when they hit the opponent. Its a nice touch there are clouds of dust and smoke out of it but the impact and the boom you would expect are very bland and light. Meanwhile in Kakarot they look and feel a lot more close to the anime both visually and in sfx. But there are other skills such as the Big Bang Attack that does feels powerful and strong.  Its also strange and very lacking how there are no planet destructions after a huge explosion such as Majin Vegeta's Final Explosion, something everyone was expecting to see in this game.---However these things that bother me about this game isn't really that much of a big deal and the game is still amazing as it is. I just only hope the dev team actually add more to the game and also opens up to include more stages for offline pvp.--Overall Score:  8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game, and I think it has potential!! I ,like many others, am a huge fan of it's predecessors. Tenkaichi 3 is still one of my favorite games ever made, and I think they did a decent job recapturing what made that game great. However, the game definitely has some warts, and numerous flaws. I think, if balanced correctly, it could be a highly competitive, and a viable game for tournaments and ranked play. It desperately needs to be balanced, and tweaked in several key ways though!!! There are a coupke characters that need some work as well. There are a handful of them that are blatantly and ridiculously overpowered, and the players who know how to use this handful of fighters have a massive advantage over the entire roster from the very start. These fighters need to be nerfed!!! Off the top of my head I know Z Broly, Android 19/20, Metal Cooler, and SS4 Gogeta need nerfs. Adjusting the counters would balance some of them so I would start with that, but they still need to work on this roster. I mentioned counters, and the priority/big fix should be the 5 counters. I think I have a way to balance all of them pretty easily. Super Counters are OP, mainly because it doesn't cost anything to preform them! Also, they cost some ki, but pretty much all of the vanishing moves are kinda broken.  However, if you 2X the ki cost of Vanishing, and make super counters cost 1-2 skill stocks, that would make the whole game play in a much more fair way. Also ki blast in general are an issue when facing certain characters. Which is why I would DECREASE the cost of revenge counters from two skill stocks to one, so that ki blasts can be countered more effectively, and the ki cost for them should be 2x as well. Implementing those changes as well as some other tweaks could make this game what it should be. The only other big thing I can think of at the moment is customization. To be frank I was offended when I saw the options for customization in this game🤣🤣 It is laughably pathetic!! Especially when you consider the options that you had in the predecessors to this game. I think that it can be fixed though and this game can be great just a couple of tweaks, and I think we could get there!! Solid 7 out of 10 game that could easily be an 8 and 1/2 maybe a 9 out of 10 if balanced correctly.

Sparking Zero is far less built-out than BT3 for that reason. However, I assume that DLC released over the next year will begin to rectify that situation.Consider this game and the impending deluge of DLC an investment. FighterZ and Xenoverse 2 are still supported years and years after their initial release. SZ is likely to be supported in the same way. However, if you want strictly balaned competitive fighting, go purchase FighterZ. And if you want highly customized OCs with depthful stories, go get Xenoverse 2. _childDocuments_.review: Look I went into this game after spending alot of hours on the BT 4 mod and being a fan of the raging blast games. So yes, I am bias as hell. I recently finished several of the story modes, just done with Trunk's and his might be the worse. I don't know for sure but I'll get to the point why.On the positives. + The new characters are fun to play as, from the super cast. I really do enjoy playing as them after all I had was modded stuff. + The custom battle mode is cool to play. It's a bet messy to work with (seriously just trying to have certain characters say lines is a hassle)+Clearly a lot of work in making this game in the camera work and in how it plays. They REALLY tried to make each Kamehameha look interesting+ The sparking episodes are a joy to be had. And gives some What ifs, that I generally wish we got instead, like Trunks staying in the normal timeline after his was wiped out.Onto the negatives, there's a lot!- The story mode is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mess. Let's take trunks for example, everything is skipped till the goke black arc. That means...No fight against the androids, no fight against cybrog Frieza, no fight against goku when he got to earth, no fight against vegeta in the time chamber, no fight against perfect cell, no fight against Dabora...wtf game.- the most insane thing to say but lack of characters. Great saiyan woman, no ssj2 for Super Trunks, 90% of the dragon ball characters, come on you could have given us dragon ball versions of tien, Yamcha, and piccolo at least. - Just really odd choices when it comes to the cast. Why do you even HAVE the new chibi Goku here, wouldn't it make more sense to add him as DLC with the other mini characters like vegeta and so on. Why is mystic Gohan not a transformation when it is treated as such.-  The moveset for some of these characters is so bad. Super Trunks has a pretty good base form. His ssj form SUCKS. Which would you like to use, the 3 bar purple beam or the 3 bar yellow beam...they do the same amount of damage!- Alot of great moves there were in the raging blast series is just not here for no reason, or lets you customize at least. Why can't Trunks have the moves he killed the androids. Why can't SSB Goku have the one inch punch?- no what if transformations raging blast gave us ssj 3 vegeta and Broly, meanwhile we still don't have golden Cooler.Those are just the problems I have at the moment. Do not buy this game, wait for it much later on when the DLC comes out and get it when the price drops. I honestly regret giving into the hype. Just settle for BT4 until this game is done cooking AND the modders get to have some real fun with it. Already I've seen people working on Vegeta ultra ego making it into the game.I spent more time with the game. It still sucks. Look, the biggest issue I can 100% say about this game is that it is underdone. It needed much more time to cook. How the hell does BT 3 ultimately come out to be a better dragon ball game compared to this, at least I can actually do the cool story moments there. I can't even do the Saiyan Saga Beam struggle between Goku and Vegeta in this game unless I make it myself.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to play PVP this game will be right up your alley.The graphics are amazing compared to where DBZ games started from. Key pieces of the story in episode gameplay were turned into slide shows.And I know these scenes can be seen by watching the anime. However, I would have preferred it in this format and graphics to see them again. How the ♥♥♥♥ can you turn Vegetas death in the Frieza saga into a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slideshow. And then Goku turning super saiyan the first time is also a slide show. WTF.What gets my blood boiling is the fact that they animated some things but these pivotal moments turned into slideshows. Either do one or the other, otherwise it looks like you are cutting corners. And that's exactly why they chose the slide show format for certain scenes.Additionally, one key piece about Tenkaichi that I enjoyed was hunting for dragon balls. It made the replay value that much better. However, in this game you unlock all of the dragon balls by completing certain challenges and you get to make your wishes. They did keep the rewards for wishes somewhat the same.Long story short: this is a watered down experience compared to it's predecessors.Combat is great. This one focuses more on timing and other nuances to provide skill based combat.Like I said at the start if you are looking for combat/PVP this is right up your alley but I was hoping for a Tenkaichi experience beyond the combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Never played a Budokai Tenkaichi game in my life, hated games like Fighter Z and Smash Bros, and thought I hated fighting games in general. This game was a welcome surprise and completely changed my view and opinion of fighting games in general. This game is a 3D arena fighter, and is a wildly different experience than Fighter Z and Smash Bros. There is a deep complexity to the mechanics that will have you practicing for hours trying to build the skills necessary not to get your ass kicked. The high skill ceiling with the depth of the ocean really culminates in a fascinating experience where you actually feel like a Z Fighter training for their next battle.If you are into fighting games, or just love dragon ball and want to hit your head against a few skill challenges, then I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: First let me say that I do not care for the online scene. I bought this game for the nostalgia and the hope to see interesting "what-if" scenarios that could lead into the Super timeline. If you are like me, honestly there are probably mods in Xenoverse that will give you that. The story mode and the branching arcs from the main timeline are so boring and not nearly as interesting as being the only thing of note to play if you are not trying to win online matches. From what I can tell, the want to give the community the ability to craft their own scenarios has hampered many instances of any creativity the "what-if" situations could have had as the story telling format of the scenes and goals for each fight makes it so that the game is just never engaging on how to get an alternate path. For about 90% of the alternate goals, it is just "beat this person/people quickly". There is not an ingame timer for any of these situations so it is either a guessing game if the condition has been met until the match is over and they deliver their dialogue. Another large negative to the story is the limited amount of battles for each of the characters. As an example, for Vegeta's story, you start on Namek, disallowing any changes from the fighting on Earth, Gohan starts in the Hyperbolic Time Chamber during the Cell Arc, and for some reason, the amount of fights per saga are very small skipping some fights, such as the Z-Figthers vs. Cell Jrs, most of the Ginyu Force fights, and many other tiny fights that help with pacing of the story and fights that allow for stuff other then the main encounters.I am hopeful that this is just a modern day game that will actually be decent to play through with updates and DLC that covers for most of the missing peices, but only because I have already purchased the game. Other then that, wait for discounts later down the road as right now, if you are here for some cool fan creations for fun what if stories, this is not the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best naturally cinematic games I have played, I say the same about Battlefield 1 but these are very different cases. I think Battlefield 1 creates it's moments using the sheer scale and destruction faced to show you how small you are and how triumphant you feel when you start to rack up kills. Here it feels cinematic in the sense of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ we're both transforming and we're about to clash the ♥♥♥♥ out of each other. I don't think I've played an anime fighter better besides when I emulated BT2 and even then this is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool, I don't think a game has had me more hype as a massive Dragon Ball fan it's good to see they didn't shovel out absolute slop with the mindset of "Dragon Ball fans will eat it up" because this game is very lovingly made.I like this game a lot, I like how the movement feels, how the combat feels, the defensive options at play, it's exceptionally solid and every time I win a ranked singles with Bardock I feel like the legendary super saiyan herself. I love how unbalanced it can feel at times because yeah, Broly and Babadi won't be on the same level will they? of course not, but it genuinely feels good in this game if you're able to outsmart and outplay a higher power level opponent, like Dragon Ball you need not only strength but the technique and inventiveness to think on your feet during battles, reacting to what moves an enemy uses and countering with your own as there are MANY ways to counter play and turn the tables at the drop of a hat. With that being said I do have some grievances and things I wish to see added although I doubt they will because as it is right now missing some things from older BT games it also feels "finished" as in I doubt the developers feel the need to add new content outside of the upcoming DLC.More maps for one, just a little more variety, but with more maps I would like to see a better lock on as, very rarely, but occasionally I have stared at an opponent and had to wait until they noticed me and moved in to attack for them to even register. I would like there to be more customization and costumes besides just destroyed variants, maybe other single player/online modes like in the older BT titles. I don't really know who's OP and who isn't, I've fought 3 cheesers and while I won against each of them they all sucked to play against but I know that'll be a problem regardless of the game and the nerfs so there I have nothing to say really, what shouldn't be a problem is the aforementioned leaving penalties. I think if you leave a match there should be a ban limit on ranked for a while, not sure how long but something to prevent the SSJ4 Gogeta from rage quitting during my combo. What I don't think is coming are free character updates, as much as I would love every few months or so a new character appearing in the shop being unlockable and it's someone like Monaka, Nam, or any of the characters from the Super Dragon Ball Heroes hellscape, I feel like with the large roster as is it will be seen as an excuse to not "bloat" an already massive roster in the hopes of having so many characters will make people not expect minor things to be added like bit characters from Super or OGDB as they already do cover a large portion of Super with some OGDB thrown in there but not a lot. If they do this? I'll be shocked and #happy but @ the same time I also think that doing so would bring about even more outrage from an already wavering playerbase who still argue about who's broken and what's cheese and a character who on launch will be used to find ways to "break" the game would probably put people into a form of soyrage.Despite all of this including the lacking singleplayer modes I think the game is incredibly fun and the only game I've bought at full price where I haven't felt buyers remorse whatsoever as this is maybe the only game to renew my faith in it with every round of play, in short, go buy it if you're a dragon ball fan, one of the best experiences you could ask for.

_childDocuments_.review: Zero fun.The what if/branching paths are so uninspired it would've been better to not have them at all. Some of the paths in fact just end and have no implications, for example if you fight Raditz alone and beat him that path plays out the saiyan saga with the difference being the Z fighters are still alive. Frieza then invades earth and if you beat him... that's it. There's no affect on subsequent sagas because apparently they don't happen on that path.There's lots of missing battles between characters that were present in literally every other dragonball Z game.There's no versatility involving combat, combos are always the same, you can't customise or swap out the skills of a character which means they get boring real quick. Transformations are 100% pointless because you can just start off as said transformation since that's a separate character and you always do in the story mode.Controls are god awful and clunky, the AI cheats with absurd reaction times and randomly gets free super armour even when being attacked from behind, which the game literally tells you that's a vulnerable point that can't be defended against.The characters themselves are so horribly balanced that there's absolutely no reason whatsoever to use anyone in Z, when all the Super characters are straight up broken.Once you've beaten the character stories, there's literally no reason to play the game. You've got the world tournaments but they're dull, and are basically just three matches. You can play online if you fancy getting disconnected and going up against fusion characters but that's it. Dragonball Z: Kakarot had an open world and optional bosses to fight, hell Budokai 3 had optional fights and small branching pathways, skills to unlock and levelled challenged. This pile of crap? Nothing. If this is what's in store for the Dragonball series then holy crap it's over, especially since people are meat riding this turd.P.S Great Ape Vegeta isn't tough, get gud.
