_childDocuments_.review: I love dragon ball. I love fighting games. I originally came here after around 2000 cumulative hours in Dragon Ball FighterZ. A lot of people are dissing this game because of the AI and the story mode, but that is hardly the issue, and can easily be chalked up to skill issue, but what I don't see in these reviews is someone actually discussing how bad the gameplay mechanics actually are from a fighting game standpoint, let alone an enjoyable gameplay standpoint. I will change my review when they actually fix these issues i'm listing, but I'm sorry to say that I don't recommend this game because the gameplay mechanics are genuinely terribly designed and here's why:Certain characters are broken: Yajirobe is a good example. He does decent damage, and can heal back to full an infinite amount of times and it only takes him 2 seconds total to do so. Of course, he needs skill meter to do so, but in a game where you're constantly dishing damage and getting damage done to you, the skill meter charges insanely fast, and Yajirobe can just heal to full after every knockback/knockdown. The icing on the cake is that it only costs 2 DP to run Yajirobe, so you can pair him with an OP character like Gogeta SSJ4 and cheese the entire game. You may argue this is also a skill issue, but with how dumb the defensive mechanics are in this game, it's so easy to get at least one knockdown/knockback and heal to full. A lot of characters also have unblockable supers that you can't even block/dodge or react to, so people will just TP behind you and spam unblockables that almost one-shot your character.Ranked is unbalanced. The DP system is an attempt at making a balanced ranked system in a tenkaichi game, but does not work because of how much characters can heal while tagged out. There is no concept of 'blue' health or 'temp' health like from FighterZ, which limits how you can heal. So if someone were to run Gogeta SSJ4 and Yajirobe, they can easily just tag Gogeta out and swap to yajirobe, spam sensu beans for a couple of minutes, and bring Gogeta back out to full health. This is the basis for almost the entirety of higher level ranked games. Too many defensive mechanics, and they need to be heavily nerfed: To list from the top of my head, there's 5 main defensive mechanics. Guard, Perception, Revenge Counter, Super Counter, and High Speed Evasion (TP). This isn't even considering defensive skills like explosive wave or afterimage that some characters have which gives you a get out of jail free card essentially. Super Counter is the most OP one because it can be done at any point in anyone's combo, regardless of whether or not the opponent is hitting you from behind. It isn't hard to spam Left stick up + attack button to hit it as well. You will get a full reversal for free, and in high level gameplay, you will never get in a full 'combo'. The most annoying thing i've been dealing with in higher level gameplay is infinite TP encounters, where your opponent will TP, and then you will TP their TP in a nonstop cycle until one person runs out of ki. It's genuinely boring gameplay and is terribly designed. It's funny at first, but once you end up in 20 TP cycles it gets old really fast, and is genuinely frustrating to deal with. Perception is also an inherently flawed mechanic, because you can HOLD block, and react with perception while still holding block. That means you can SIMULTANEOUSLY block and perception at the SAME TIME. The only answer is side step or grab but you can just SUPER COUNTER to get out of the combo that you should be punished with. NOTHING IS TRUE IN THIS GAME. The only thing that is TRUE in this game is that your opponent will counter you, and you will counter your opponent. You are never safe, and it's for all the wrong reasons. This game genuinely punishes you for making the right decisions and it's trash. The guard mechanic doesn't work very well too, as I find myself holding block fairly often, and guard tends to be unresponsive, specially during supers that you could normally block. The controls in general for this game are jank. Combos aren't real and this game punishes you for them. In high level gameplay, opening your opponent up in this game is near impossible due to the amount of defense mechanics in this game, and if you just so happen to get one combo off, it doesn't matter because they can super counter or revenge counter out of your combo. It's BORING. The entire gameplay loop of high level gameplay in SPARKING ZERO is guard, chip, counter, trade, guard, chip, counter, trade.Knockbacks lasting more than 2-3 seconds is not real in this game. This means that if your opponent knows how to tech out of a specific knockdown or knockback, then you cannot follow up with a super. It isn't real. Last time I remember, in fighting games, a knockback should allow the player to get a special ability/super off but nah, not in this game. Nothing is real Ki system is flawed. In high level gameplay, you're not charging, the enemy is not charging. Ki blast beats most character's charges, so what we end up doing is spamming ki blast whenever a player charges. That means that neither player is building ki, and both players are spending ki to prevent players from gaining it. The main issue here is that 'combos' (if you're lucky to get one off and dont get super countered in it) do NOT build enough meter. The only way to get supers off is if your opponent is in a vegetative state and lets you charge, or if you have an ability like high tension that lets you instantly build meter. That means that characters that build instant meter immediately outclass those who cannot. It's boring and stupid. Stun lock mechanics. As I mentioned before, in high level gameplay, nobody is letting you charge up. This means a lot of the time, you're going to have around under 1 bar of ki, and if you just so happen to block a heavy smash or a super and it breaks your guard, you will be stun locked for around 20 seconds. This is enough time for your opponent to charge all the way into sparking and one shot you. It's genuinely stupid, and I don't understand why it lasts so long. You can chalk this up to skill issue & bad ki management, but just consider that one sonic sway (frame 1 perception) removes about 1-1.5 bars of ki. Sparking Mode. Sparking mode is awful. Some characters have abilities that instantly put them in sparking mode, some characters are forced to charge in order to get into it, which we've already discussed is almost impossible to do in high level gameplay. Additionally, sparking mode provides far too much damage for its semi-infinite 'combos', which can only be beaten by super counter or revenge counter (but is still hard to do for the former). Additionally, a lot of players in ranked abuse the movement mechanics in sparking mode to immediately TP/dash behind you and spam unblockable supers that almost one-shot you. It's not fun gameplay, and there is hardly an answer to beat it if the opponent does it right. Best example is Base Super goku, who has an instant transmission  and an unblockable spirit bomb you that will one shot youThe camera is awful. In this game, you can only adjust your camera to the left or right while  you're focused on your target. This means that you can not look up/down, additionally meaning that if you opponent fast flies up/down, your camera will break like crazy, and you won't be able to see your opponent. Additionally, there's some odd bug in this game that causes your camera to break and lose your opponent when they're right in front of you. This happens a lot during beam supers that you've blocked, as well as when the opponent instant transmissions in front of you. in certain cases, it can also happen during after image, and is genuinely annoying to fix, as sometimes even when you're staring directly at your opponent, your camera does not actually "see" them and lock back onto them. It's RNG af and is a game breaking issue.

_childDocuments_.review: At this point, it's a refund. I have been playing the Budokai Tenkaichi series on PS2 so much and recently fired them up in anticipation of this game.After starting to play, this is a complete and utter joke of a difficulty. The AI can just overwhelm you with no way of blocking, they can spam specials without caring how high their KI bar is. What-If scenarios are locked behind this absurdly hard "default" difficulty, bc lowering Difficulty locks you out of secondary ways to win the fight and therefore unlock those what-if scenarios. Also the story mode presentation is very lackluster. Everything is delivered in slides with subtitles or short cutscenes. But it painfully underdelivers.I would have waited until Bandai releases a patch to this AI behaviour, but i rather play the classic games, bc in addition, the content of these older games is much superior than this. Apart from Story Mode, there are offline tournaments and PVP. That's it. That is the content they are offering the players for 70€. A story mode that is too infuriating, a tournament mode that is bog standard and a PVP mode if you just want to play mirror matches with the strongest characters. Or play with friends for the fun of it. To be positive, i'm sure the game can be fun when you just play unranked with friends. The gameplay does play smooth and can be a ton of fun, given the graphics that capture the feel of Dragonball. But i'm very frustrated how Bandai is basically screwing over singleplayer customers with a horrible story mode and severe lack of offline content

_childDocuments_.review: I have never been a competitive player, so I bought this mainly for the offline content. I really wanted to like it but I don't want to lie to myself.I am heavily disappointed with the story mode. Animations for character feel stiff and unpolished, the "alternate paths" are not really alternate and circle back to the normal path, the character select screen feels poorly made and honestly bloated, transformations should not take up a slot (only talking about User Interface here, I know they have different movesets).But the worst offender is the story being told through powerpoint style slides, with a fight in between. It just feels so bad. I wanted to be Goku when he transforms, I wanted to fight to the brink with Frieza, watch him murders Krillin and release the anger and transform while in game. Not watch it happen in a slide. I am not far enough to confirm it, but most likely every major event is told like this, my favorite transformation is Gohan going SSJ2 against Cell after Android 16 dies. _childDocuments_.review: Sparking:Zero offers a nostalgic, long-awaited reboot to the budokai tenkaichi series stocked with an impressive roster and fleshed out, vibrant landscapes. -This is a game I have been waiting for forever, it reminds me of battling with my brother on  BT:3 when we were kids. But sadly it is not the same, which is okay for the most part, and overall I love this game with all my heart and recommend it to anyone with interest in Dragon Ball or Budokai Tenkaichi type games. I still one specific personal gripe.The shift to a more competitive scene leaves a sour taste in my mouth and leaves room for unnecessary toxicity from the community, I personally play these games for fun and not an arbitrary ranking that takes away the games 'spark'. It would be a great ranked system if it wasn't the ONLY way to play the game seeing as the unranked portions of content do NOT have a "matchmaking" system like ranked does and instead uses 'rooms' akin to guilty gear or fighterz. This would be okay if the rooms weren't poorly designed. Allowing players over 8 slots for each room, which sounds amazing but the game pots for a 'king of the hill' method, knocking losers down to the final place in queue meaning that they need to wait potentially 30-50 minutes depending on game type to battle again. Again, this would be tolerable if not for the added effect of the games lack of activity within these rooms. Taking up to an hour just to find active players in unranked in every single mode. (Not to mention the ghost-town that is world tournament). This overall creates a dependence on the ranked portion of the game, as it is the only accessible content to me if I want to engage with the community. With that being said, and personal bias aside this doesn't have to be a bad thing. If you love ranked systems in games then this is a perfect game for you, I personally believe that ranked systems create a negative environment that serves to punish players for playing causing them to always need to be better than the next person. And yes, this is the essence of ranked systems and Gokus whole character inspiration. But this doesn't need to be your interpretation of the game as it is an incredible celebration of Dragon Balls lifespan and Akira Toriyamas (RIP) story. If you are a fan of Dragon Ball then this game is perfect, allowing you to re-create stories from your favourite dragon ball episodes in fast paced combat with stellar animation. Whilst allowing you to peer into alternate 'what-if' scenarios for the classic story. Overall, I recommend this game highly to anyone. I just went through the content too quick and do NOT enjoy the online portion in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: Feedback on Game Mechanics: A Call for ImprovementThe game has a great concept, but the mechanics surrounding defense and offense leave much to be desired. Currently, the use of ki is overly restrictive: breaking a combo, shooting a ki blast, moving, dashing, z-vanishing, and even sidestepping all consume ki. This creates a situation where players are constantly empty on ki, which can feel overwhelming.The intended rock-paper-scissors dynamic of defense is frustrating for new and seasoned players. While blocking, players cannot dodge, allowing opponents to circumvent defenses easily. Once an opponent gets behind you, you're left defenseless. Additionally, there’s no frame advantage at the end of combos, meaning attempts to dodge often result in being hit by ki blasts or follow-up attacks. Holding block leaves you vulnerable to back attacks, and while z-vanishing is a potential escape, it requires both ki and precise timing, which many players struggle with and tends to leave you getting hit in the face anyway even if you do manage to do the vanish they can vanish your vanish and it becomes a who got more ki war.Throws also fail to catch dodges effectively and feel sluggish, leaving players reliant on landing the first hit. If you miss, you face heavy punishment, losing 50-100% of your health from an opponent’s ultimate, which can often be confirmed from any knockback. Sparking is a huge problem with its infinite combo strings and high damage it gives.While the dp costs are interesting and is a feature I want to keep, anything beyond 5 mirrors lore-accurate speeds, making sonic sways or z-vanishes feel unmanageable, perpetuating an unfun loop where once you’re hit, you’re essentially “touched out.” A skill ceiling is essential, but the current tutorial lacks depth, forcing players to seek information elsewhere on critical mechanics like charging, blocking ki blasts, dodging, z-vanishing, and teleporting. making the idea of a skill floor almost non existant, you have to go to a whole nother area to get the rest of the tutorial.Overall, I appreciate the game’s vision, but it currently lacks the fun factor. Here are a few suggestions for improvement:Remove ki consumption for dashing and flying towards an enemy.Slow down all dashes to levels around dp 5 or 6.Make sonic sways not consume enemy ki.Consider keeping z-vanishing ki-based, but adjust the timing window to be more forgiving.These changes would create a more welcoming experience for new players while still maintaining challenge for higher-tier gameplay. By allowing players to utilize their movement and ki more strategically, we could encourage thoughtful combo building without the constant pressure of ki management. and as for the damage I talked about eariler hitting to hard, this will make it a lot easier to take less because most supers/ heavy attacks from giants take quarters and half chunks from your health.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like a dream come true. Countless hours that we spent on Budokai Tenkaichi games seamlessly transfer to the way this game works and even though it has been more than a decade since I last played those games, this game feels natural to play and almost as if no time has passed since BT3 . If you haven't played the original series, the game might require some effort to learn due to a lot of it being sort of complicated. But I assume that going through the tutorial and battle training mode should get you up to speed and ready to play in no time. While it is not exactly a pure fighting game (at least, not in the traditional sense of the genre), this game is one of the best anime battle games that I have played. If you played the original series on PS2 then I doubt that there any reason for you to not immediately love everything about this game (except for FPS limit which I am really hoping they address after the early access period is over) and I would say that it is worth getting at full price. The presentation and graphics are top notch and the fighting feels fluid (for the most part but there are some stuttering issues and FPS is limited to 60). If you remember the story mode of BT games, the story mode here is pretty much the exact same thing but far more elaborate now with more branching narratives and what if scenarios which are fun. And while I prefer online modes in most fighting games, this is a really fun mode and you can spend hours into it especially considering that this covers everything up until the recent anime seasons (I don't watch anime so I don't know a whole lot about how much content that adds but it should be pretty substantial). In terms of online, I haven't gotten much experience here because it seems to take a while to get a game (probably because of my connection not being optimal for playing with other players who aren't in the same region). But at least to me, the FPS limit is really annoying and it takes away a lot from the game for me to want to play it online (60 fps is criminally low imo). I really hope they fix this soon. Other than that, this game is a 10/10 for me. After like 15 years, finally getting a new entry in one of my most beloved PS2 game series with a lot of fond childhood memories associated with it that LIVES UP TO THE HYPE that I created for it feels unreal.

_childDocuments_.review: Pro-A Massive RosterWith 182 characters from Dragon Ball Z, Super, GT, and the movies, there’s something for every fan. Whether you want to play as iconic characters like Goku or niche picks like Turles and Baby Vegeta, the roster has you covered.-What-If ScenariosThe inclusion of "Sparking Episodes" lets you rewrite famous moments. Whether it’s Gohan taking down Golden Frieza or Vegeta avoiding Babidi’s influence, these alternate timelines make the story mode a refreshing experience.-Customization OptionsThe Custom Battle Mode lets you create dream matchups, adjust fight conditions, and even craft unique intros and outros. It’s perfect for fans who want to put their own spin on the Dragon Ball universe.-Stunning VisualsPowered by Unreal Engine 5, the game looks phenomenal. Every energy blast and Ultimate move is pure eye candy, staying faithful to Akira Toriyama’s iconic art style.Con-Repetitive CombatThe gameplay can feel formulaic, especially in single-player modes. Charging ki and cycling through Ultimate moves often becomes the most effective strategy, which can get stale.-Shared MovesetsSome characters feel too similar due to shared animations and abilities, which slightly diminishes the excitement of the larger roster.-Limited Tournament and Online OptionsThe game lacks variety in online battle modes and doesn’t offer robust tournament features. For a game that thrives on competition, this feels like a missed opportunity.-Server InstabilitiesOnline play is marred by frequent server issues, making matches inconsistent. Lag and disconnections can turn an otherwise thrilling battle into a frustrating experience.-Shallow Story CoverageWhile the game touches on Dragon Ball Super, it skips over earlier arcs, which might disappoint fans hoping for a comprehensive experience.My Rating: 8/10Sparking! Zero is a love letter to Dragon Ball fans, packed with characters and moments that feel ripped straight from the series. While it has its flaws—particularly in online play and repetitive combat—the sheer scale and customization options make it a worthy addition to the franchise. If you can look past its shortcomings, there’s plenty of fun to be had here.

The new mechanics add depth to the combat while still maintaining a low entry level and high skill ceiling. Rush attacks now have to be used as a combo finisher for a guaranteed hit and will most likely not hit if done raw. The lack of crossplay is certainly upsetting, but the dev team has been very cooperative and have listened to fan feedback, so I have no doubt it will be added eventually. The map restriction can be fixed with a mod that I'm sure will be made available, but it is still unfortunate that you have to resort to mods to fix this issue. _childDocuments_.review: Cant recommend. It's not what I wanted out of a Tenkaichi game. Wanted a nostalgic arcade fighting game that I could casually play and just have fun rewatching old stories and new whatifs. The difficulty ended up being very wonky, where some enemies just stand there and let you beat on them, even ones that should be "stonger", but then there are enemies that are supposed to be "weaker" that just start perfect inputing and taking half your HP away in a few seconds.  In addition to all of that, while not a dealbreaker, the menus are terrible—all of them. Navigating the main menu is clunky and terrible, taking noticeable amount of time for animations to play to move from one screen to the next. In addition to there not being a consistent way to move through said menus, hit A or hold A, hit B or hold B. Navigating the episodes for arcs and characters is equally terrible. Since you are forced to play a single character rather than play arc to arc, you play sporadic fights, skipping most of the arc and then jumping to the next fight. Which is fine for certain characters and their arcs, but even then it can still be sporadic. Then actually navigating the menu to select the fights is bad; the "pretty" visual style to select a fight where it shows the arena you will fight on is clunky. Navigating and playing fights that are whatifs isn't better. There are unskipable cutscenes, so if you fail to meet the whatif requirement, it forces you to the next available story fight in the arc rather than letting you retry, so you have to go all the way back out to character select then back in navigating slow menus and unskippable cutscenes. There is more that is disappointing and frustrating, but these are the major sources of frustration. If you think these won't bother you, you should be fine, but it just kept taking me out of the moment having to deal with all of it.Edit: Learned that there is effectively no progression, it doesn't affect episodes at all. Which means there is just inherently very inconsistent difficulty for the story missions. Also it turns out that the CPU difficulty in story episodes are the hardest CPU's in the game. The battle CPU even on the highest difficulty is considerably weaker than the CPU in episodes. The story CPU can and will perfect chain combos on you while input reading and performing multiple perfectly timed inputs in a row. Which the hardest battle CPU gets none of that.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best Dragon Ball game I've ever played. It's not perfect, Vegeta's campaign is like 5 missions compared to everyone else who gets at least double that. The What If scenarios are awesome for fans of the story, but it's not likely to suck in anyone new with it's telling of the story. The cutscenes and dialogue are super simple, and are done better in other games, especially Kakarot. What this game does well is the actual fights. It's hard to compare this game to anything other than Sekiro. It's not as unforgiving as that game, but the timing windows for parries, super-counters, vanishes, perceptions, and other techniques are very tight. Each fight is very cinematic and sees you crashing through buildings and mountainsides in huge arenas. You can go incredibly fast and blitz almost anyone in seconds if you are really good at the game, but I found some of the episode battles to be pretty hard. The bonus battles have some of the most challenging content in any game I've ever played... Still can't touch Beerus in his bonus battle...There is a ton of offline content to grind through, but that is all basically training for the online PVP modes. These are so much fun it's stupid. The custom battles have essentially infinite permutations and there is always a ton of tournaments to hop into. The roster of characters is somewhere near 200, which is insane and I'm sure they will be adding DLC for whatever characters they missed. Highly, highly recommend for any fan of fighting games. Basically a must-have for any fan of DB.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: What are you reading reviews for? Didn't you see the trailer? It's right at the top of the page. Click "Add to Cart" and join the fun!If you enjoyed the deep combat of the Budokai Tenkaichi games then this is gonna be one you wanna check out. It even has the option to use the OG control scheme. The game has a lot to offer. After about 20 hours I've barely made a dent in the main campaign because of how dense the game is. Just like the original Tenkaichi games there is a learning curve, so if you're looking for a pick-up-and-play experience, you might find the game frustrating. If you enjoy learning and getting good at a well designed and responsive fighting system then this is gonna be your jam. At default difficulty it is going to be more challenging than other titles like DBZ: Kakarot and Xenoverse, but that only makes it more rewarding when you finally do learn how to play.For returning veterans of Tenkaichi games this is gonna be an amazing, mind-blowing, experience. The combo chains are different from the older games, but that's not a bad thing in this case. The spectacle blows the game outta the water, and you can feel the genuine passion radiating from the game. It's very clear that everyone on the design team had a genuine passion for the game. Now if you'll excuse me, I gotta get back to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, the game isn't bad, it is somewhat good but lacking.My main reason for the negative is because of the price, do Bandai Namco think this is an AAAA game or what? What does adding A even means anyway? Being greedy and asking for more while giving less?For sure, there are lot of characters and stages missing.Only 12 stages to begin with is disappointing.Not including all characters from Dragon Ball (the original) and GT is a bit idiotic, lot of them are misising and sure, they could add them as paid DLCs but that's greedy, 150$ or a game that has barely any content, sure, if you lke having 30 different versions of Goku then you won't be disappointed for sure.I thought there would be more characters from the Super tournament, we can't really say that this game has more characters than Budokai Tenkaichi 3, even the Gods of destruction and the angels aren't there except for Beerus and Whis, i could give a long list of the characters missing but eh, hopefully they will add them through (free) updates at some point, also episodes and special missions of their respective series (original and GT)I'll make a list of the good and the bad, it'll be easier this way to understand.The good:- Gameplay is good, it could always be better of course, but it is good, better than the Xenoverse series in my opinion.- Offline tournaments are back, i'm not even sure if i could consider this a positive as it should have been in both Xenoverse games from the start but anyway.You have some to choose from and you can also customize your own tournament, so that's cool.- Unlocking stuff seems to be enjoyable.- Clothing tearing / damages is here and it seems to be for every or almost all characters- Stage destruction is interesting enough.- Effects are neat.- Conversations between specific characters (Goku vs. Vegeta, Cell vs. Frieza, Beerus vs. Frieza, etc...) at the beginning of a fight are cool, even though always the same and repetitive. - Transformations playable on both character screen and while in-game.- Interesting what-if missions, for example if you beat Cell as Goku, it'll be a different route, while on Budokai Tenkaichi 3, it would have been the same.- Custom battles is an enjoyable gamemode, and we're able to create our own custom battles as well.The bad:- Game sure is overpriced, i love Dragon Ball, but we gotta be honest about it, IT IS overpriced, Bandai are going crazy.- Lacking literally all characters from Dragon Ball (except Goku kid and Master Roshi, Krillin and Tien doesn't count as they doesn't seems to have their Dragon Ball versions), some from GT, some from movies and lot from Super.- 12 stages only at release, i don't know if this is a joke but honestly, it kills replay value by a lot. Even if they make DLCs, how many will we have by the end of 2025? 20? That still wouldn't be enough to even satisfy Dragon Ball Z.- Game optimization isn't so good just like other Bandai Namco games, seems they don't know how to optimize stuff, or they simply don't care. But it could be worst, it's not great, it's not so bad either.- Nobody speaks on dialogue during some story scenes (the pictures ones), a narrator like in the anime would have been great.- Some story scenes are missing, story isn't the strong point of this game.- Going through the map in Episode mode is a pain, it's way too slow and badly made.- Could have more What-If, some of them are uninteresting while some are more interesting.- Lot of lacking sagas, even Vegeta Dragon Ball Super saga isn't there, it ends at Majin Buu saga, why? Then the toxic community will say that "it's normal", people these days can't understand anything at all... - They missed the opportunity to make Trunks fight Buu in Trunks Episode.- Frieza soldier only have one skin which means the game has two different Frieza soldiers, the game definitely should have had more as it could add more replay value, either using it or only fighting against it.The "we'll see":- Will modding be available just as it was for Xenoverse 2? Being able to add new characters which would use their own slots, new stages, etc... without replacing anything? Hopefully so. Just for offline play.- Will they add some cancer such as EAC? Probably, hopefuly not, we'll have to wait and see.Note: Game isn't difficult at all compared to what some are saying, i have only used one character in every story missions in Goku episode without switching, only two times, once which it automatically switched to Trunks when the opponent had barely any health left and the final fight against Jiren and i have completed them pretty easily for the majority, even when fighting more than one opponent, same goes for the tournaments, all on normal difficulty. I'd say, i prefer this gameplay to Xenoverse, Xenoverse can be annoying.6.8/10 - Get the complete package when it will be sold for no more than 10$, it's an enjoyable game, but Bandai Namco doesn't deserve the money until they start respecting the players.This isn't even a completed game, you can love Dragon Ball, but don't be idiotic please, use your brain, this isn't good.And of course, the fanbase is once again proving how stupid they are, don't you guys want to use your brain once in a while?

_childDocuments_.review: I've always considered Dragon Ball Fighterz to be the best Dragon Ball game ever due to it being very faithful to the manga/anime, having a very beautiful 2.5D artstyle straight out of the anime with scenes that produce a lot of callbacks and fan service (dramatic finishers and intro's) and being accessible but complex enough to put hundreds of hours in. It is therefore crucial to compare Sparking! Zero to Fighterz: Sparking! Zero has the same pros as Fighterz while improving on, now outdated, Fighterz mechanics.The main gripe I had with Fighterz is that there weren't many transformations you could do (outside of cutscenes/finishers and the sole exception being Frieza with his golden form). This while I and many consider transformations to be the core of Dragon Ball (Goku going Super Saiyan for the first time being an enormously memorable moment).Sparking! Zero improves in this area by allowing transformations (and fusions!) mid combat. It is very cool to be able to play Gohan and your opponent being Broly (S) and feeling weak at first but after you transform you actually feel motivated to fight harder and beat your opponent, even if they transform into the Legendary Super Saiyan.The other gripe I had with Fighterz is the amount of and the destruction of stages. In Fighterz we've had only 1 extra stage that was quickly added after release, bringing the total to 14 stages. This amount is even lower when you realize that some of these stages are variations of each other. The true unique count of stages is 11. Sparking! Zero has 12 maps on release with more being hopefully added in the future. While this is on the low side, we need to realise that the stages are enormous and actually have destruction and weather/time effects built into them. They look beautiful and are actually impacted by your fighting. Fighterz had a small a destruction, and you could push your opponent to a different stage which was pretty cool, but nothing on this scale.Sparking! Zero might be a genuine contender for the throne that I totally recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Big Dragon Ball FighterZ fan here. It's not as deep as FighterZ, but there's still a nice layer of depth. I wish there was a bit more to the hand-to-hand combat, but it's fun the way it is.Unlike FighterZ, this game is accessible. You will find people of your level and will have a good load of fun.Still, there's a lot of clunkiness to the game, which, hopefully, will get fixed.-There's a weird lag at the start of every fight, when an opponent gets K.O.'d they just fall off without flair.-Sometimes, you get in this weird position where you ''can't'' reach your foe because they're just slightly above or below you, forcing you and your foe relying on teleports and button mashing.- The ''find your foe'' mechanic kind of sucks. Some abilities and character switching will cause you to lose sight of your foe, meaning that you have to find them using the right stick to turn the camera around, which spins in a very unnatural and clunky way. Sometimes, you can literally see your opponent but the game doesn't ''register'' the lock-on, making the game feeling very cheap.Still, the game is worth it to relive Dragon Ball's most gorgeous clashes with kick-ass super moves.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has moments where it truly shines, especially in the combat. When the fighting is good, it’s very good. The action is fast-paced, and there are flashes of the thrill you’d expect. But these moments of excitement are often overshadowed by the game’s many missteps. The story feels slapped together, told mostly through static images instead of proper cutscenes. It’s rushed and disjointed, with awkward pauses after every fight that break immersion. The cinematography is odd, and the writing feels hastily done, lacking the polish and impact Dragonball fans expect. The game’s visuals are hit or miss. While the character models have potential, their faces sometimes look weird, and the mouth animations are poorly done, pulling you out of the experience. The main menu UI is a cluttered mess, making simple navigation a chore. It’s not a dealbreaker, but it does make getting into the game less enjoyable than it should be. Combat is where the game excels, but it’s not without its issues. Animations can be unclear and hard to follow, making it tough to react in real-time. Certain sections of the game feel repetitive, even on the 'default' difficulty where spam attacks replace real challenge. Fights like the one against Vegeta are more frustrating than fun, with an unreasonable difficulty spike right at the start. But when the game hits its stride, the action is intense and satisfying. There are other strange moments that stand out, like the awkward talking animation on Vegeta when he's an oozaru. Then there’s Bulma in the shop screen, who just WON'T. STOP. TALKING, making an already cluttered interface even more irritating.The biggest letdown, though, is the treatment of iconic Dragonball moments. The lack of impact of Goku’s Super Saiyan transformation on Namek, for example, is a huge missed opportunity. These are the moments fans want to relive, and when they’re glossed over or mishandled, it’s hard not to feel disappointed. Despite its flashes of greatness, Sparking Zero doesn’t have the lasting appeal of classic Tenkaichi games it claims to have. I don’t see myself playing this the way I used to with games like Tenkaichi 3. For the price, it’s hard to justify sticking with this one when there are better options out there. That said, with some improvements or a strong modding community, Dragonball Sparking Zero could still become something special.Rating: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Awful experience. The CPU on single player are psychic, but aren't actually intelligent. If you sit still at the start of an episode match, they'll spam dash and kick air. If you go in to deal any damage, they'll immediately read your inputs and perfect parry or counter. The only enjoyable way to reliably beat the AI is to spam sparking, spam x and vanish counter their perfect parries. Otherwise, you're in a sparring match with a robot that knows exactly what you're doing exactly when you do it.This is only after you get the game running consistently, which in itself is painful. The game-speed is tied to FPS, at around 40 FPS, everything is in slow motion. EVERYTHING is rendered in 3D. The UI on the main menu is a handful of options (usually one or two) over a 3D modeled, completely rendered and animated background running constantly. If you swap over to the left or right to view the other two options they let you at a time, Goku dashes off and the game renders a completely new scene. This killed my frames, which in-turn slowed the game down. I could hardly even open to options setting to lower my graphics.The general quality of the game is awful too. The sound design especially is so choppy and broken. As an example, during super saiyan blue Goku's ultimate, his kamehameha charges for a split second, then the game goes almost completely silent. The camera breaks constantly, getting stuck in walls or the floor. You can't see characters you're locked on to that are just slightly above you, and you can't move your camera up or down. On the maps with larger structures, like the city map, I also tended to get stuck in the buildings with no way out. There's also a pretty common bug where you get stuck charging ki and can't do anything else. It's like no one play tested this game.The single-player is disappointing. Some of the what-if scenarios are pretty cool, but the way it's portrayed to you is so incredibly lackluster, it's lost. The entire story is presented to you in either short, poorly animated clips or just a slideshow of the exact events of the show that are completely rendered in 3D for some reason, removing all soul even screenshots from the anime or manga might have and also, similar to the main menu, greatly lowering my framerate. It also takes place on the exact same maps. Fight different characters on Earth? Same exact field/canyon. Fight a character on Namek? Same exact spot on Namek in front of Frieza's ship (except for the Frieza-arc's specific destroyed Namek.) It's repetitive. There's an entire roster of 180 characters, but only 7 characters have a story and only 2 of those have any fleshed out alternative paths. Most what-ifs are just a single scene if you beat a boss quickly or don't use a special move.And on the 180 characters, most of them are just air. 100 of them are Goku and Vegeta and the others are so weak and boring, there's no reason to use them unless you're joking with friends. If you do want to joke around online, then the best way to do that is ranked, because the unranked matchmaking is awful. Instead of randomly connecting you to someone else who's trying to play, like ranked does, you have to connect to a room that could have dozens of different players, and wait in line for your turn to play your quick 5 minute match. The other players can't even challenge each other while they wait. It's ridiculous. Playing ranked is just as miserable, though. You aren't allowed to have any fun playing ranked, you're supposed to sweat until you win. Want to play anything lower than 9 DP in single battle? Go ♥♥♥♥ yourself, here's 20 SSJ4 Gogetas in a row. Want to play DP battle so you can make a balanced team of all your favorite characters? Time ran out because it takes years to kill a character with 8 health bars and a heal. Who knew? The combat isn't even enjoyable enough to overlook these things. It seems enticing, but you can't actually combo in this game. You have 2 attacking buttons, and 4 dedicated to blocking and countering and dodging. The entire game feels like a QTE. Vanish counters are the worst example of this. They cost nothing to do, and they can by countered by themselves. If you play against anyone familiar with this mechanic, a good 30% of the match will be spent hitting right bumper at the right time while neither of you take or receive damage. And on top of that, the ACTUAL QTE's, the clashes, go off so quickly you often do them wrong before you even see them. The dash clash is the worst example. The attack button is the same one used to fight clashes. If you dash towards an enemy that also dashes and attack before they can, you've already messed up the clash and are punished for it. I really wanted to like this game, and I spent a long time playing it, but it's not worth it. If you're thinking about buying it, don't. If you already did, refund it.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game has great fighting mechanics, great visuals, and keeps the familiar roots of the other Tenkaichi games, it has several flaws that make it not worth buying at its current price tag.The first flaw being the lack of different skill sets between characters. Once you played four or five characters, you've basically played them all, and for a game to bolster a huge roster of a 180 characters, that is kind of disappointing. Granted, you can't expect every single character to be unique, but you could at least expect not almost 3/4th of the roster to not be a copy and past of each other.Another glaring flaw is the story mode and it's lack of dedication to the art and narrative. It is essentially a slide show and it is missing voices from the cast and the narrator. Navigating through the story maps can be frustrating as well. The "what-if" scenarios can be neat, but some of them are just a simple PowerPoint cut scene that don't even last  two minutes.And finally, the biggest flaw of all has to be the multiplayer. For those of you hoping to test your fighting skills against others online, you better hope you are in the 60% that are able to play online. Turns out there is a major problem with the system where people constantly disconnect right after the opening cutscene or partway through the fight. Despite all of the recommended fixes out there,  some people still can't fix the issue; those on PC seem to suffer the most. And if you are ranked fighting, that disconnection issue can get you banned if you disconnect too many times. So, as long as you don't plan on doing any online fighting, then this flaw can be overlooked, otherwise you will have to wait until Bandai comes up with a solution to fix it. All in all, the game in my opinion is not worth the price tag it currently has on it and should not be bought. However, if you're dedicated fan, or just have a love for fighting games and testing your mettle against others, then go for it. However, be warned, you're rolling the dice on how well it works for the competitive fighting aspect.

I bought the game for a fun, easy to understand arena fighter that had a complete package of solo and multiplayer content. But with the focus being on pvp, after a few hours, I just sort of tuned out. Again, pvp focus is fine. But I wanted more fun side stories, and silly meet-ups between characters, or original story content. But aside from a core story that takes a few hours, You have nothing to really do but play pvp. The defensive systems are cool when they work, but are so inconsistent, it's hard to be satisfied with them, especially with how the back-turned state is at the time of writing.TLDR: Purchase if you want a tight, complex arena fighter, with a focus on pvp. _childDocuments_.review: Beautiful Masterpiece <3Positives:Gameplay - Buttery smooth, feels familiar and new at the same time. I grew up on the PS2 games, and I played them to death. I'm doing the same with this one, it feels like an old friend. But there's new mechanics that switch things up, make it more interesting, and balances things out nicely!Story - I haven't gotten all the way through yet, only beaten Goku up to Buu saga, and then went back and did What ifs I missed. Getting through it at a steady pace as I record the game for my channel. The What ifs are HANDS DOWN my favourite thing. They really put in a lot of love and care, the devs know Dragon Ball and it's easy to tell they are passionate.Online - I'm so happy this game goes online, reminds me of the Raging Blast days when that was online. For the most part things run buttery smooth, I have it set to a connection range of 4 or higher and every match is great! When I have played Player Match with friends, depending on their internet/region there has been the very occasional laggy match. Everything runs in slow motion and it's not really enjoyable, but with my friends it's not too bad. We make light of it with banter. When you are loading into a ranked match and waiting to find an opponent you are able to play the game against the CPU while you wait. Which is really cool! So far I haven't really had much chance to play against the CPU as the wait times to find an opponent are extremely short. I usually find an opponent before the characters finish their intro dialogue, which isn't a bad thing!Custom Episodes - This is REALLY cool, you essentially get to make your own what if story mode missions. You have access to all the characters, you can change the camera angles during your own crafted cutscenes, as well as add subtitles. It is hard to find what you are looking for exactly given there's over 5,000 custom lines of dialogue, and you can swap around certain nouns, like character names and places. The filter system is a big help, but I wish there were more options given how specific I sometimes want a line. I made a very simple story fight and it took me 3 hours, and in the end it didn't 100% work as I intended. It's a learning curve for sure! The ability to set certain conditions, like when you or your opponent reach a certain health threshold you can set conditions to happen such as restoring health, or increasing the CPU difficulty. Giving access to certain moves previously locked off, or triggering certain cutscenes to happen. VERY cool, but complex. Thankfully they have a simple version as well as the regular version, just in case you don't want to put in all the extra detail. You can upload your creations for others to play and of course you can play other people's creations whenever you want. It has great potential and I know there's gonna be some AMAZING things made with Custom Episodes.Presentation - I'm referring to the menus and how you navigate everything. This... wow... I am blown away. Every menu has an animated background where the characters all interact with each other and talk to each other. As you switch menus, you follow Goku as he fly's to or teleports to the next menu location. Moving from iconic places from the anime, such as The World Tournament, to Capsule Corp, and even Kame House. Everything is seamless and and there's no loading screens either! Just a fantastic layout. My only personal gripe is the character select menu. All the characters feel as though they are ordered very odd. And compared with the past games, the select screen is a definite downgrade. I do like how seamless it is, once you pick the character it immediately puts you in the game with a smooth transition.Negatives:I have two MAJOR complaints, and the rest are so minor they aren't even really worth going into detail over.BIGGEST ISSUE - During Online play, there's this really annoying glitch that NEEDS a patch, PLEASE!!! Essentially, depending on your control scheme, (I play classic controls) If your opponent has "standard controls" it messes up your technique pallet. When holding down the charge Ki button, for classic it's "LT/L2" it brings up your technique pallet, so that you can do moves such as Blast 1 and Blast 2. These usually consist of "Blast 1" moves being some sort of energy attack, like the Kamehameha. And Blast being some form of rush attack. Now... the "GLITCH" shows the modern control scheme, or whatever the reverse is from the one you are using. And then shows that all my moves are the same. Rather than them being: Blast 1 (LT+Y) Blast 2 (LT+↑+Y) And Ultimate Blast (LT+↓+Y) They all instead say (LT+Y) And when pressing these buttons, it always defaults to Blast 2. Which for most characters is a rush attack. Usually Ultimate Blast works, despite it saying (LT+Y) but that requires going into Sparking! Mode. Which, if you know most of the player base, it's hard to do that, unless you have a character with a special ability which can trigger Sparking! without the need to charge Ki first. Basically my point is... it's a nightmare, and has definitely been a painful handicap whenever it has happened. Which has been about half the time if I am honest. PLEASE FIX!!!Second issue - This one is honestly not as big of an issue, but I just personally find it annoying. When your opponent switches out characters in Team Battle you lose "Lock on" and then have to search for them. To do this, you simply need look in the direction they are in, there's a visual and audible indicator that shows when you are looking at them. However... it kinda sucks. It doesn't work very well, I can be looking DIRECTLY at them and half the time it just doesn't work, unless they are close to me. If they are on the other side of the map or just a decent distance away, it struggles to lock on. Now... not to sound "too old." Back in my day, during the Tenkaichi days... the lock on would work VERY well. The moment you scan the environment, if the little radar at the bottom picked them up, it would lock on instantly. And all you had to do was hold a button down. You didn't need to look at them directly. I can see what they were going with when adding this feature back in, but it seriously needs a rework.Beside those two issues, I can't really complain! I LOVE THIS GAME! I shall forever support it. <3Sorry for such a LONG review, I like to get into detail about stuff. I doubt anybody actually reads this, but if you do. I hope you have an amazing day!Sincerely, a fan. <3

name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem
detailed_description: Welcome back to the world of Serious Sam in 'Siberian Mayhem' - a new standalone chapter in the adventures of 'Serious' Sam Stone. Make your way through the vast Russian landscapes on a quest to catch up with the traitorous General Brand, who remains one step ahead of Sam at every turn. The road is long, and there is oh so much to see. Co-developed by Timelock Studio and Croteam, 'Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem' presents an expanded look at a familiar journey full of forgotten stories, unexplored places, and Sam's trademark guns-blazing battles against Mental's Horde. Join the fight, comrade! WELCOME TO SIBERIA ...the heart of Russia. This place is huge, cold, and so unpredictable even the alien invaders feel lost. Travel through five new levels set in a beautiful and dangerous world, from Arctic coastlines and desolate forests to abandoned villages and a chilling ghost town. Siberia is large enough for you to fight & explore for as much as you want. BEASTS OF THE APOCALYPSE Only the strongest souls survive in Siberia, and Mental knows it well. A new set of dangerous foes and bosses join the Horde in 'Siberian Mayhem'. Including some of the most advanced and intimidating creatures you never expected to see. TEMPERED STEEL There's only one thing that stands between Serious Sam and his enemies - a gun. Treat yourself with a deadly arsenal of new weapons, from the legendary AK to experimental 'Perun' crossbow, and more! Do you want to cause death from above or become one with 50 tons of first-class firepower? New gadgets and vehicles are locked, loaded, and ready to fulfill your most destructive dreams. AT HOME AMONG STRANGERS When you think the journey is over and there are no more stories to tell, the universe gives you a second chance. Meet a gang of new outcasts and unexpected characters who will help Sam on his journey to Tunguska. Complete side-missions in order to uncover new chronicles these wild places uphold. And pay attention to your surroundings - the world itself can tell you something you never expected to hear. SIBERIAN MYSTERIES The lands of Siberia are huge, desolate, and full of secrets. Useful, silly, weird, familiar... you name it. Can you find them all?

_childDocuments_.review: Oh well... I will start this by saying, i did enjoy it but it's really short. Yes, i am aware it's just a stand-alone expansion, but still feels like there was so much more potential to it, potential that wasn't put into play.With some side missions and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around on the map i finished it in like 4 hours.If you're not a fan of the series or have some sort of attachment to the SS games, you might want wait for a discount on it.As an 'average winter enjoyer', i really loved the scenery, and i really wish the game had a photo mode, guess i will have to settle with some modding to take some captures from the game.Perun Crossbow is very powerful and satisfying to play with, it was probably my favorite weapon to play the game with (and finish it.. in like.. 4 hours...)The maps are big enough to strafe as much as your heart pleases, and fighting is awesome.Graphics seem slightly improved compared to SS4, BUT, the optimization is not very good.I like the idea of involving 'Tunguska' in the context of an alien invasion, because, in real life, there was a big explosion there in 1908, which sparked some interesting theories, even X-Files made an episode about it.What i am not happy about is that, in Serious Sam 4, there were huge problems with playing the game using DX12 (you'd get lots of annoying visual glitches), i was getting excited that maybe they fixed it in Siberian Mayhem (because trust me, there is a huge difference), but instead, they removed DX12 totally.They also added difficulty and multiplayer achievements again (Again with the ♥♥♥♥-measuring contests!)Cutscenes are too... cutty. Let me rephrase, in many cases there's no transition during dialogues, they're just cut suddenly, feels very amateurish.I'd say the game is good, but i expected some more, and it left me craving for more Sam.Am i happy or disappointed? Yes.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: Serious Sam 4 is great.  I will stand by that opinion.  Siberian Mayhem is more of the same, but even better.  It has snappier pacing, a far FAR better mech segment (one of the most fun mech levels in any FPS I've played honestly), a cooler sniper rifle, Roadside Picnic references, and a level that is basically Highway 17: Serious Sam Edition.  No, the performance hasn't been fixed, unfortunately, and if you really deeply hated SS4 this probably won't convince you otherwise.  But if like me you enjoyed SS4 a whole lot for what it was and want an expansion that takes the best elements and makes them better, definitely pick up Siberian Mayhem.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: The game has all the problems of Serious Sam 4, from performance to the absurd amount of overpowered things that make any balance impossible. Five levels isn't enough either, but now with survival missions and access to the workshop, lack of content should no longer be a problem.The level design, especially of the first two levels, has a quality level above Serious Sam 4. The first two levels are very interesting, they have varied situations and battles that remind you of the classic Serious Sam in the way they flow.The third level is more about exploration, as if it were a small "open world". I'm not a fan of this approach but it works well.The fourth and fifth levels are the more modern style where you use your overpowered tools to hold line against a bunch of enemies. In my opinion, this is the worst type of level Serious Sam has to offer and unfortunately it's the theme of the last two levels. Still, they aren't bad, they're just more on the braindead side of the action, but they're still fun with good moments.For fans of Serious Sam, it's another one of these imperfect games that has its charm and moments, so it's recommended. Also, I think it's more recommendable than SS4 for those who aren't a fan of the series and are just looking for an older style FPS.

Search and fight them!Jumping platforms... how the heck they even ended up there!? Ah, just survive!Ice skating episodes? _childDocuments_.review: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem is an amazing game made by modders that are extremely talented and blessed by the original creators of Serious Sam - Croteam. This doesn't happen often in the gaming industry and I think that the game should be praised just for that even if it was bad. Since it turned out great though it deserves a double-praise, an Oscar even or at least a medal...I had a great time with SS: Siberian Mayhem. It looks, runs and feels just like SS4 (that can be both good or bad depending on your preference) and just like in SS4 the humour was on point for me. The gameplay remains untouched and only some weapons were replaced due to the setting - the AR assault rifle for example got replaced by the AK and the sniper rifle by a crossbow. New consumables were also introduced along with a death-ray laser gun which absolutely rocks. In some locations I even thought that the environments were more detailed than in SS4 and the love for this franchise on the modders part really shows here.Unfortunately it wasn't all sunshine and rainbows. SS: Siberiam Mayhem is still plagued by the same performance problems of SS4. It isn't well optimized. Even on my relatively competant pc it doesn't have a stable frame rate. Also, even though this might be subjective, the final boss is not satisfying to beat and quite unfair. I won't spoil anything but beware that the final boss doesn't play by the rules of SS games. Every defeat feels cheap even though it has the most complex AI in the entire series and the fight as a whole is supposed to be this bombastic climax. It simply didn't do the trick for me.All things considered, SS:SM is an experience that matches the game it draws its inspiration from (on which it's also heavily based) and in some cases even exceeds it. It might be shorter but it's just as if not more fun. On a sale this is an easy recommend and definitely worth the price. There is also co-op so I can imagine that playing this with friends is going to be even more of a mayhem but I can't comment on that since I played in single player.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's one of the best Serious Sam game and deliver an unique experience, although it has its flaws and somehow performs even worse than Serious Sam 4, the content really worth it.INTROSiberian Mayhem is a standalone expansion for Serious Sam 4, it has new mechanics, weapons, enemies and vehicles, but the core of the gameplay remains untouched. It's harder and some sections are really challenging, with a good balance overall, the game also knows how to be brutally unfair, especially on Serious difficulty. It's not something that will frustrate you, except maybe an overuse of snipers enemies in some sections or areas where you don't have room to fight with enemies spawning above you. In the moment of this review, I had a single session of 5 hours of gameplay on coop, playing on Serious difficulty and with enemy multiplier set to 2X, as a Serious Sam veteran player, I will describe my experience in this game.TECHNICAL ASPECTSSpeaking about the technical aspect of the game, I can't say I had a really good time. It performed much worse than Serious Sam 4, running the game on low or medium settings didn't made any difference, and all I got was a constant low FPS, especially on fights. However even with this issue, I had no crashes or major problems.The game also presents a brand new menu, faster level loadings and a way better loading screen. Everything else seems pretty much unchanged, it's still a Serious Sam game.LEVEL DESIGNThe level design was what made this game so special. Every level is unique, beautiful and well detailed. Probably the curse of the bad performance is also the blessing of the game, with lots of small details that benefits the immersion in a way we haven't seen before in any Serious Sam game. Mostly of sections are based on fantasy instead of real locations, as opposite to Serious Sam 4, which brought memories of previous titles, when the militarism wasn't the focus of the franchise. This is definitely one of the best thing this expansion has to offer. I personally loved the third level and it's my favorite.BALANCEA game made by Russians must have the well known "Russian Balance", right? Well, sort of. The balance is good, sometimes unfair, but it's Serious Sam, it's something that many fans were missing. I confess that I was worried about it being too easy like Serious Sam 4, especially on the beginning, when you only had a shotgun, a pistol, and lots of enemies to kill, but without the urge feeling of danger. That felling started to change after you get your AK-47 riffle, and the game start to show its colours. If you like a difficult game, this one was made for you.SECRETSYes.I could end this section just with that word, but let me elaborate a bit more: You want secrets? You'll have secrets. This game has more secrets and easter eggs than every Serious Sam game ever had, and not only the simple and generic parkour secret (don't worry, there's still parkour secrets for you) but the most crazy and creative ones. And a side joke for any Timelock Studio member who's reading this, you owe the idea of using classic levels as secrets to Cockatiel Studios, it's their NFT now.NEW FEATURESYou'll play with new gadgets, weapons, vehicles, mech, and unique mechanics for solving puzzles, I loved every new addition in this game, everything was planned and work very well with the campaign, including the usage of gadgets, something I avoided on Serious Sam 4 because I couldn't feel the need to do it, but in this title you'll be forced to use if you want to survive, which makes them so useful and fun. There are a few new enemies that are also a great addition to the game, and speaking about enemies, you'll love the final boss.FINAL VERDICT This is a must play for every fan of Serious Sam. It's not perfect, it's not TSE 2, but brings so many good things that it's already special in its own way.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, going into this I had pretty low expectations considering how SS4 turned out, but after playing through it and beating it on Serious Difficulty I can confidently say this is the best modern Serious Sam game to date. There's a few negatives here and there which I'll be sure to touch on later, but let's talk about what makes Siberian Mayhem so great.First, the attention to detail is simply incredible. Arachnoids and Octanians will talk in their native language during combat, Octanians have a more significant military presence and genuinely feel like a key faction in Mental's horde, Technopolip Helicopters fall to the ground and explode violently on death, Harpies and Octanian Grenadiers have alternate attacks on higher difficulties to add to the challenge... and the list goes on.Secondly, the environments feel believable and help to serve the gameplay in a meaningful way. Ever since BFE, the series has struggled to balance out the more "modern" environments with Sam's classic gameplay, but Siberian Mayhem finally managed to strike a balance between the new and the old. During slower moments, you'll come across more detailed environments such as frozen over greenhouses, abandoned sheds with tractors still in them, fully furnished houses, orthodox churches, etc. However, when the combat starts to pick up, a lot of these environmental details are pushed off to the sides to allow for the combat to flourish. The combat arenas are still beautiful to look at, but they're functional above everything else, and I wouldn't have it any other way.Third, cool ideas that were introduced in SS4 are now fully fleshed out. Vehicles are back and better than ever, side objectives feel like self-contained levels with their own story and setting, gadgets are less frequent but are more varied, new and returning weapons feel good to use when dual wielding, etc.Fourth, da music. Do I really need to say anything? The main menu theme alone had me pumped to adjust my settings as quickly as possible so I could hop in and start playing. The OST for Siberian Mayhem is nothing short of legendary, it's short but oh so sweet to listen to.Fifth, the weapons! Most of SS4's arsenal returns but some of the more OP weapons/weapon mods have been replaced or removed (so long chainsaw launcher, nice to have known you). Luckily the new weapons more than make up for it, so let's talk about them.- First we have the crossbow. It straight up replaces the Sniper Rifle & Devastator by firing a hitscan beam that pierces through multiple targets and does heavy damage in addition to not having to reload. The downsides are it has a slow fire rate and low ammo capacity.- Next we have the AK which replaces the AR. It does more damage, has a tighter spread, and holds less ammo per mag. It looks good, sounds good, and shoots well; good gun.- Finally we have the Burner. It replaces the Laser Gun + Death Ray combo in a more balanced but equally gory way. It does pretty decent damage and on kill causes enemies to explode which in turn kills other enemies. It can absolutely shred through fields of fodder enemies and when dual wielded will cook through larger foes in seconds.Sixth, the new enemies! Not all of them are winners, but I hope to see them make a return in future Sam titles. - First up are Octanian Grenadiers which toss grenades and have an alternate attack where they toss out a rolling bomb that chases the player. They're not entirely new since they were planned for SS4 but still fun to fight nonetheless.- Next we have the Octanian Legionnaire. They're basically bulkier versions of Zealots but will sometimes be set up to guard other enemies, which is a neat mechanic I hope will return in the future.- Third up is the Draconian Burner. They're basically bulkier versions of Draconian Pyromaniacs that have better telegraphed attacks. In close range they'll slam the ground, at mid to long range they fire lasers that you either need to sidestep or jump over. They're a very cool addition to the enemy roster.- Fourth, the Aludran Microhopper. They're the first new enemy you'll encounter and are easily the worst. They appear in swarms, have unpredictable movement, and do loads of damage. I hate them with a passion.- Finally we have the best new enemy in the game, the Octanian Sentry Tower. They're one of the few area denial enemies in the game and serve as mini-bosses. They'll launch mortars, homing missiles, and have Miniguns to deter you from getting too close. They're actually pretty weak but can't be damaged until they overheat, where they expose their core for a few seconds. Their main purpose is to chip away at the player's health and create openings for other enemies to attack, and they're effective at keeping players mobile.So that's it for the positives, now let's talk about the negatives.First, performance is still an issue. Granted, the game runs much smoother than SS4, but there's still inexplicable lag spikes that pop up and there's a new performance issue that only Siberian Mayhem has where the game will literally freeze for a few seconds before playing normally again. This only seems to happen at certain points during the last 2 missions so hopefully someone at Timelock Studios or Croteam can fix this.Second, puzzles. I know what you're about to say, you only have to do a few puzzles and they're not required since they're only used for secret hunting, but they still don't belong in Serious Sam. They're kind of cool the first time you encounter them but on repeat playthroughs they grind the pacing to a halt.Third, invisible walls and death pits. Luckily there aren't many instances of these things but you'll still find yourself bumping into them from time to time.Fourth, inconsistent hitboxes. SS4 in general has really odd hitboxes for certain enemies such as Biomechs, Witch Brides, and Technopolip Helicopters where projectiles seemingly graze through their sides when it feels like it should have hit. Sadly this hasn't been fixed in Siberian Mayhem and the new Octanian Legionnaire enemy has hitbox issues where his armor effect seems to curve around to parts of his exposed back, making landing SSG shots needlessly difficult.And... That's it, wow. So yeah, if you can't tell I love Siberian Mayhem. It has some of the most enjoyable Serious Sam combat I've experienced in years and unlike SS4 the positives far outweigh the negatives. With that said I hope the negatives are at least looked into and that the performance issues are addressed in the future. I'd also love for cross workshop support with SS4 in the future and for SS4 to get some love in the performance department.It's immediately clear from the moment you boot up Siberian Mayhem that the people who worked on it genuinely love the Serious Sam franchise and have a keen eye for what made Serious Sam so memorable to fans in the first place. Everything from the secrets, combat, music, subtle world building, added details, weather effects, and map design are everything I could have asked for in a modern Serious Sam game, and Siberian Mayhem delivers it with such grace, integrity, and passion that I couldn't help but have a big dumb smile on my face the entire time I played it.Here's hoping improvements made to Siberian Mayhem get introduced to SS4 at some point in the future and cheers to the folks at Croteam and Timelock Studios that made this thing a reality!

_childDocuments_.review: Is it too wrong to say that my favorite Serious Sam game was not made by Croteam? I still have to refresh The Second Encounter and SS2 in my memory, but I'm kinda confident in that statement right now.Timelock Studio pretty much fixed all that could be fixed without making a whole new game.Like, believe it or not, this game has an actual style now. Every level is not baby's first attempt at making a map anymore. It's not lifeless barren wastelands filled with nothing but cheap copy-pasted assets. That's the first time since ... what, 2005? This alone makes a world of difference, but the developers didn't stop there.This game has actual exploration with actually cool secrets and really dаmn fun side-quests.Every other encounter is not "let's spawn nothing but a million kleers" anymore. There is one such encounter in the first level and I began to worry, but this fight is literally the only one like that in the entire game. What kind of sorcery is this?Even the story is kinda endearing to be honest.Look, it's still not a must-play masterpiece or anything, but I liked the hеll out of it from beginning to end. It's short and sweet and left me wanting more, That's a win in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, this stand-alone expansion is pretty cool. Timelock took most of the flaws of the SS4 & addressed them here in this game. The level design is better by a long shot, the new weapons kick ass, the atmosphere is there & many more improvements are present. The secrets are also more creative & feel Serious Sam-ish. It also contains one of the best final bosses I've ever fought in any video game. Finally, a boss that doesn't lazily spam minions.It's not perfect, though. It runs on SS4 engine, which means it carries over the issues, like poor peformance & small hitboxes.Balancing issues with some fights but nothing too major. They are doable at best.===========

The Hoover Board is by far the best vehicle in the game to drive around on specially that you can use the mouse to steer with instead of the arrow keys like the other vehicles.Best Final Boss than the last 2 games and looking forward to the workshop mods for this game.Coop is outstanding in the game with drop in drop out play as always.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun game, takes the best from SS4 and build upon it but unfortunately also keeps some of the worst parts of SS4. Overall a small step in the right direction compared to SS4Gunplay: Slightly better than in SS4 due to better level design and enemy placement. You don't have to hold S until you return half a level back due to overwhelming number of enemies and their tricky placement like in SS4. The new weapons and gadgets are pretty cool, but I still prefer laser to burner. New enemies are also really good.Story: Story? In a Serious Sam game? hahahahaPerformance: Arguably even worse than in SS4 due to changing weather effects and snowy areas. Scoping in with the crossbow cuts the FPS in half. Although that is not the fault of Timelock Studio, it's just the bad optimization of the original game carrying over.Soundtrack: Damjan did it again! Amazing soundtrack as usual.Level design: Still a far cry from diverse and wacky but clever design of TSE but better than in SS4 for sure. Secrets: WAY better than in SS4. More interesting and easier to find. I'm just hoping to never see those damn puzzles again. There should be no place for puzzles in a SS game, it kills the momentum so much.If you liked SS4 even remotely you're gonna love this one, you can tell it's made with passion. Good job Timelock Studio!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I've nominated Serious Sam Siberian Mayhem for Game of the Year. Yup. It was that good.Well. Can't say I was expecting a Serious Sam game this year but here we are. It's fantastic too.Serious Sam Siberian Mayhem manages to fill in quite a few gaps that SS4 wasn't able to fulfill.One of the most notable things that comes to mind with this game is quite simply the amount of polish and care put into each and every one of these levels. The side quests for an example. On SS4 they were mostly simple. They usually consisted of a small detour where you would be rewarded with a gadget here and there. Sometimes a weapon. Nothing too substantial though. Siberian Mayhem's side quests absolutely BLEW my mind. The amount of length and quality that each side quest brought to the table almost felt like an entire level of it's own. To put it quite frank. Most of these side quests featured really unique scenarios and sometimes even boss battles. I would've NEVER expected such attention to these areas of the game but they did it incredibly well.Not only this but there's a lot of subtle improvements within the game itself that SS4 lacked. Such as better sounds. More destructible environments. Various UI improvements. VERY creative easter eggs (almost on par with TSE to be honest). LOTS of throwbacks to the classic Serious Sam formula. We're talking classic battle arenas (massive rooms filled with various platforms and launchers to help accommodate the space followed by waves of enemies you have to kill before progressing), Several nods to prior games such as bringing back (and sometimes even remixing) classic soundtracks, MUCH bigger areas to fight the waves upon waves of enemies, as well REALLY in depth boss battles.This game blew me away. If you're a fan of the classic Serious Sam games (TFE, TSE, maybe even SS2), there is definitely something here for you. However it does still give the same modern feel that SS3 and 4 captivates on. So really. If you're just a fan of the series. Definitely pick this one up. I had a really good time with this one.
