_childDocuments_.review: So, I've just finished this game and this was AWESOME!   It feels like SS4, but it has something else...the atmosphere it makes feel all the game process in a new way.The gameplay was good, we got all our previous toys, but some new ones too and this time we had an opportunity not just to run in a mech, but to drive a freaking tank! The final boss suprised me a bit, it was a bit of a challenge (without gatgedts).   But the thing i like the most is the game atmosphere. The snowy lands, the buildings and the music. Serious Sam always got excellent music, but here we some insane ambient soundtracks. During all the game i felt some Witcher, Painkiller and a bit of Half-Life vibes. Another thing i wanted to mentions is the level design. In 5 chapters we managed to see wide snowy plains, refinery, urban structures, military objects, old slavic churches and houses, and spooky ancient slavic village! That place gave me creeps, xD. I cought myself that I'd like to visit such places in real life, and imo this means people behind this game knew what they were doing.   Also I am very happy that we got Sam from the future visiting us and telling about...hmmm...the new possible adventure! This Siberian journey was great, and I already can't wait for the next one. Despite some graphical issues I had, I think this game worths every dollar it costs. Another thing I like a lot is how Russia and russians are represented here, yes, a bit of a stereotype, but in a funny way, Everything was shown in a friendly way. Sam will surely remember this visit to Siberia and so will I.   In conclusion, will I recommend SS4 and SS4SM? YES!P.S. Croteam, please make a Painkiller skin for multiplayer xD.

_childDocuments_.review: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem is an awesome expansion to Serious Sam 4.I was very critical of the base game - it felt unfinished, directionless, but most importantly, it had very few of those signature Serious Sam moments. And I am very happy to say that Siberian Mayhem really does its best to make most of the SS4 formula. Most of the fights are frenetic, the vehicles are ridiculous (I mean, a mech with a chainsaw? Or a tank with a dash move?), the secrets are fun and imaginative, and man, that new weapon is really satisfying to use!Perhaps next time, the developers could get rid of the upgrade system and make running and shooting at the same time (and even dual-wielding) enabled by default. But other than this, even after two playthroughs, I had a lot of fun with this expansion and I really wouldn't mind if Timelock Studios would do another one!

_childDocuments_.review: This one is the best SS game since the Second Encounter.Beautiful levels, strong soundtrack, remarkable enemies,  great guns (AK is love).Even a lot of minor painful things from SS4 were fixed.I definitely love this game.BTW it's kinda short, and I would with pleasure pay any money for more content from same developers team.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: This is a sensational love-letter to the Serious Sam franchise and a condensation of all the best aspects of Serious Sam 4. It tells a great little side-story with fun characters, beautiful scenery and a refinement of the intense battles that the series is famous for. For those of us that cared about the story in Serious Sam 4, this campaign has some nice nods to it and fleshes out a few elements. The new weapons and enemies add some good tactical considerations and frankly the shorter length helps the pacing.I recommend playing on Hard, as this game is generous with inventory items (particularly if you're willing to secret-hunt) and they offer huge advantages in some of the bigger battles.Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: This has improvements over Serious Sam 4.  I liked how there are more secret areas you can find, which is more consistent with the classics First and Second Encounter.  The pacing is faster.  The ammo and armor loot is also more generous which also aligned more with the classics. In SS4 ammo loot seemed more scarce making the game seem more difficult.  There is generally only one new weapon which is the crossbow that shoots laser bolts, which admittedly seems a tad overpowered if not very fun to use though.Just like in SS4, I was not a fan of the parts with narrow corridor combat such is in city streets, but there were not as many of these at least.  Vehicles are back which I have mixed opinions on.  I like the ones where you use in big combat arenas such as the tank or the mech suit.  But the snowmobile and ATV seemed liked missed opportunities.  Overall I thought this was a bargain and satisfying for classic Serious Sam fans wanting some more of that classic gameplay.  I appreciated how Steam gave a bundle discount even though I bought SS4 last year.  I had no technical issues.  This was in good hands with Timelock Studios.  Maybe they can be involved with Serious Sam 5 and truly bring the series back to its former glory.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: A much more polished and fun version of Serious Sam 4. You can tell the team that made this know exactly what a SS game should be. The campaign is a bit short and at the moment there isn't any arena or survival modes, but what's here is really solid.  Performance could be better but after tweaking the settings you should be able to get it to run well while still looking great. Overall I would highly recommend this to anyone who loves this franchise.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: Serious Sam 4 was a bit of a cluster in terms of level design so it's good change of pace to see Siberian Mayhems main change is a drastically different approach to it. Siberian Mayhems campaign can be debated as being better than 4, it's less obnoxious in its story, there's less pointless areas.The side missions are utilized to have often interesting unique purposes. Some of the areas felt a bit ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ difficulty wise, which is honestly fine as SS4 was way too forgiving on Serious. Sadly Croteam and Timelock fail to get a game that runs optimally for the era it was made it, Serious Sam 4 is by no means a "looker" but it still runs terribly on my mid-low rig boasting a 1070 ti with 6700k. It's shocking being SS3 looks as good but runs far better. Still this is a hiccup of SS4 more than Siberian Mayhem as a standalone product. If you had issues with Sams 4 at a base level, you likely won't care for this but if anyone even saw a hint of potential its worth a shot. Siberian Mayhem is a fun medium length campaign that's straight to the point and cuts a lot of Sam 4s worst traits.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: Performance still leaves a lot to be desired but most of the issues happen within the first 20 minutes of launching the game and then dissipate almost completely (except chapter 4 which has horrible freezing for the whole level).This is a prime example of the kind of product you can get if you give a bunch of long time modders a stack of cash and then leave them to their own devices. Every single fight here is more fun and better designed than almost any in the base game. They're better paced and made up of better monster compositions while also being longer and larger in scale. Secrets are way more creative and involved too. You still have your basic hidden health and ammo supplies but there are also whole chunks of levels that count as secret optional areas and there's even a few different types of puzzle minigames, including a carbon copy of the Bioshock 1 hacking minigame. Bonus points for secret fights that are rewards unto themselves since they give you no* resources and a boatload of extra enemies.Finally, this expansion was hilarious. Lots of self-references, plenty of puns, and the dialogue after you kill the final boss is very nuDooM in its bluntness. I'm glad I didn't let SS4 turn me off of playing this. A patch to fix the Ch4 freezing and the texture pop-in would turn this into an A+.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: The game could do with some optimisation, though turning down the graphics to medium mainly had everything running well on my 1080ti & Ryzen 1600x. That aside, Siberian Mayhem is a hell of a lot of fun from start to finish. Even for someone like myself who hasn't played that much Serious Sam before. If only it wasn't pretty short.THE GOOD+ Pretty visuals with enough biome variety to not get stale+ Great level design hiding fun extras and secrets+ Large array of kick-ass weapons and power-ups+ Banging soundtrack+ Makes you feel like a crazy badassTHE MEH= The story won't win any awards, but that isn't what you're here for= Pretty short, but it means it's pretty much all killer, no filler= Vehicles like the snowmobile tend to get stuck pretty easy= The mech section feels a little jank (mainly the chainsaw); the tank section more than makes up for itTHE BAD- Perhaps not as optimised as it could beHere's hoping the team that worked on this entry get the opportunity to make more. Siberian Mayhem is a joyful experience armed to the teeth with sweat and the blood of a thousand enemies.

_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: Scraped a positive review but only just. Siberian Mayhem suffered from a few points. 1. It has no visual specatacle unlike the previous games. Even SS4 had Carcassonne and it was beautiful in the game.2. In SS4 the huge open areas had no reason to visit them. Bar curiosity to see anything was there. In Siberian Mayhem there are secrets dotted about. It means covering square kilometres on foot, systematically cross-sectioning areas. I am pretty patient with that kind of searching, but eventually I said ****-it, and gave up.3. Enemies seem to have had their damage rating altered. Like Scrapjack Rocketeers can sometimes go down with two rockets. It means confusing enemy kills and wasted ammo. Same with big mechanoids sometimes.4. The story ending doesn't make sense. It's like we need the next game for a conclusion. Fair enough but it feels off.Most importantly:5. There were just too many times when I was feeling bored. When I play Sam games I usually have a part smile on my face while playing practically the whole game. Siberian Mayhem was patchy in terms of fun. I'd be playing thinking "I'm bored". Then it would heat up and I'd get that, "I love it" moment, but it was too brief. It was kind of a mixed bag. Boring bits, average bits, and good ol' Sam fun. Level five however did redeem itself enough by being solid action. If you think £12.50 after 10% discount and discount for owning SS4 was 'too good to be true'. My five reasons above are why. Sadly it was a little too good to be true. Wish I had waited for a very slightly lower price.The positives. 1. When it gets going it's pure Serious Sam fun. Then again so was SS4 to me  - never got the reason why it got hated on. (SS4 was more consistent.) 2. Siberian Mayhem had areas of types never seen before. It felt inventive sometimes.I think the newer titles SS4 and Siberian Mayhem suffer from being RPG. Side missions for upgrades kind of doesn't work for me. Yeah am going to do all the content anyway. However why not just make it linear as it always was. No thinking - just playing.Do I recommend it? I think so. (16.1 hours to completion. 58% of secrets found.)

_childDocuments_.review: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem is standalone expansion for SS4. Chronologically it takes place between 14 and 15 missions of SS4. _childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: Short: a great addition to SS game series.Long... While original SS4 was good, this one is much, much better! It feels and plays better from every single aspect. Is it even legal? :)What makes this game so good:- Level design. Locations are interesting with great attention to detail. They looks better than in original SS4. Cool weather effects adds a layer of immersion.- Placement of weapons and enemy encounters: very well balanced, fun to play, does not feels overwhelming. And this is a full-blown game, not just some crappy add-on!- New guns are cool. New foes also cool. Every newly added piece is well-made and adds something to the game.- There are new combat vehicles as well.- As always, game got great music! And they are actually new tracks beside a couple inherited from SS4.- Some interesting easter eggs / side quests with pieces from Russian folklore.- Secrets are not limited to just jump-climb somewhere. There are very cool and interesting examples (no more spoilers here).- Detailed interior in houses. There are actual furniture from real life, especially that folding table sitting in the corner. :) It is a must-have gadget in every single post-soviet house - it is a piece of Russian's culture code. Well done!There are some downsides as well:- Now there is a physical fence around open locations.- Character's animations looks bad (like anyone cares).- New characters looks too generic and even uncanny.Final verdict:If you like SS game series even a little bit - this one is the best entry. At least in early 2022 (who knows what going to be released next?).

_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: More than a year have passed since Serious Sam 4 release and we suddenly got a standalone expansion called Syberian Mayhem. Nobody really expected it, especially considering the mediocre main title, crawling with bugs and issues. Surprisingly, despite using the same engine, this addon performs quite well and I didnt encounter any major problems during the campaign. The only issues were rare lags when game tried to spawn a large bunch of enemies and low volume of voice lines during combat. Does this mean the game is better than the original Serious Sam 4? Well, it really does.To begin with, though the game has only 5 new levels, each of them is big and detailed. They are like France level from Serious Sam 4 but much better in terms of design and playability. In addition to it, the developers added a bunch of new monsters and weapons, which make the gameplay even more diverse than in original. The last bost battle is one of the best in the whole series. It seems the developers also tried to apologize for the absence of the legion system in the major part of the main game, so now you're really fighting hordes of enemies on large open locations. Because of this the addon is also harder then Serious Sam 4 and gives you a decent challenge even on normal difficulty. Speaking about the rest, music is ok, graphics are fine, the story is a filler but has some nice jokes and references towards Russian culture. In conclusion, if you are a Serious Sam fan this addon is a must-have, if you like old school arcade shooters you can give it a try. I'm really surprised that after cranky 4th title, the developers managed to create such a great expansion! It feels just like playing The Second Encounter after the very first title!

_childDocuments_.review: "If Serious Sam 4 felt like poison to you, Siberian Mayhem is the antidote."SS4: "I have an empty lifeless flat countryside that looks like someone's backyard" SM: "What if it had thousands of paths to explore, bridges, waterfalls, rivers, mountains, huge trees, different biomes and buildings to raid and blow up!?!?"SS4: "I have a slow empty harvester sequence that gets damaged when you boop a little bush"SM: "What if the harvester was 5 times faster AND had a boost AND could shoot back AND didn't take any damage when hitting stuff AND there were 10 times more enemies on screen!?!?"SS4: "I have a big mech sequence that doesn't regenerate health and it's in a tight corridor"SM: "What if the mech was 3 times faster, had a freaking gigantic chainsaw, was set in an open field so you could actually move around and had 10 times more health!?!?"SS4: "I have a looooooooong campaign."SM: "What if it was shorter but actually good and filled with some actual content!?!?"__________________This is a MASSIVE improvement over SS4 in every possible way. It's mindblowing how good this campaign in when it's based off of SS4.I assumed this would just be "new levels and assets on the same engine" but I was pleasantly surprised to see that this has a lot of little QoL improvements.SS4 lacked SO MANY BASIC THINGS like impact sounds, destructible props, environmental sounds, dynamic skyboxes, real-time godrays/reflections, scripting etc... this game had not only all of these things, but also included new things like lens dirt and rotatable models in menus.It also fixed a few bugs which are still present in SS4 like the color option menu no longer turns pickups into glowing squares.Aside from technical stuff, the levels are absolutely fantastic! They're INCREDIBLY detailed, beautiful and huge, full of rewards for exploration and it has the best secrets in the franchise. Seriously, they're the most over the top Serious Sam has gotten.There's 5 levels in total but it'll take you a good 6-8 hours to beat this game, even more if you want to explore everything. There's even sidequests which you can totally skip and ignore but they are also quite long if you choose to do them, they're basically a whole extra little level within the main level, just optional but worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: This has great level and art design, interesting enemy encounters and high effort (on the part of the developers) secrets which encourage exploration MUCH MORE than a health pack on some ledges under the celling. Whoever ends up making the further entries to this series, I would like to ask them to make it with the same design principles in mind. After this, I did not feel burnt out on the series, but refreshed and ready to go for another 40 hours, c'mon, let's do Sam Carribean or Does D.C., whatever floats your boat, just don't lose this moment. With this density and variety of content, Sam really can get the whole oldschool shooter audience, not just Sam fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Most people already know what to expect from a Serious Sam game. _childDocuments_.review: Ran stuttery until i moved the game from a traditional hard drive onto an SSD. it did this because of the load times of textures and animations. -8.5/10-    When making a SS game, its hard to please everyone. most of the players are people who played the older games as a kid, or have some kind of nostalgia for how the games used to be. the developers of this version have done a generally good job keeping to the feeling of nostalgia while also bringing the fast-paced gameplay that the newer audiences want. That being said, I can see inspiration of games like  and the  series, but also bringing the chaos and horde combat that was prevalent in many of the early SS games.    Overall, this latest installment in the franchise is the best, in my opinion, from the last several years. i think that they've done a good job making the game perform well with very few bugs and maintaining that strong level design we used to see from the  devs. the game is worth the money they're asking, and I could very easily see this series becoming more popular if they play their cards right in the future.   A few things most people want to see is game optimization. Most people still use hard drives to store games, have older graphics processors, and are not looking to upgrade as they should in order to enjoy the games they want to play (a few examples of this would be ). For future games, i would focus on making the maps more tightly packed, or take away hitboxes that render from objects the player cannot interact with. this way, the average user will not have the issue of stuttering from loading unnecessary or overdetailed textures. really, this issue isn't that great, and the performance really should only be considered once your core fanbase is completely satisfied with the gameplay.   For future installments, another thing that keeps coming up is map diversity/open space. this is an issue, since the game has built a reputation for having an overwhelming amount of secrets and collectibles, and a larger map makes it easier to hide these things. As mentioned before, large, unfilled maps make for a game that is harder to play (from a performance and attention standpoint). a potential solution to this issue would be to make more vertical maps, that way the large, open field horde-style combat can be achieved, but also allow for the player to have a smaller map that is easier to load all at once, as well as giving the devs an environment to effectively hide the secrets that we all know and love easily. above all, i think the creativity and expressiveness the secrets give to the game are important, which is why this is just a suggested solution to a problem i think should be addressed in the design of the next game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting to have a potential GOTY contender so damn early in the year but yet here we are.Siberian Mayhem is essentially a standalone expansion for SS4 that acts as a director's cut or more so precisely as a "lost episode" of the very short russian third of SS4. The gameplay additions are great and the artistic presentation is honestly THE best the series has ever gotten.It is a short but SERIOUSLY sweet experience that i would absolutely recommend.EDIT: With the year ending and the steam awards asking to speak of our favorite games, i will say it. Siberian Mayhem is indeed my GOTY 2022. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I've played through the whole thing. It's a blast all the way through. Some people don't like the quirky NPC crew in this but I found them on the whole a massive improvement over the crew in SS3+4 combined. The combat variety is awesome, the layouts, the sidequests are like, actually interesting and more than "go down hallway, kill bunch of people, get power up that's probably not worth what you spent getting to it".The music is amazing, complete with new tracks, tracks from SS4, and remastered tracks (at least one) from TSE.  The minibosses were great, (The one when you turn on the power on a sidequest just delighted me greatly.) The new enemies are mostly fun, the hoppy guys can be kind of irritating but which ones that HOP aren't?All the new weapons are fun too. You get a heat ray that's basically just the death ray from SS4's upgraded laser gun, but it blows people up around the target, a lightning crossbow that's way more satifying than SS4's sniper, and the AK, which is just the tommygun reskinned as far as I can tell but it FEELS nicer so ♥♥♥♥ it. ORIGINAL:I'm not quite done yet, but as far as I've played this is some of the most legitimately surprising and enjoyable Sam content since TSE. Fun wonky arenas and surprise miniboss fights help break up the more standard killrenas, a mech segment that doesn't make me want to tear my hair out, and writing that feels more fun in general (so far) ; It's just a treat. Might update if suddenly they decide to make the game terrible in the next half, but so far I love the hell out of this.Also the new monsters are fun so far, the AK could just be placebo but it feels better than SS4's AR/tommy gun and the overall encounter balance doesnt feel as frustrating on hard compared to SS4.

_childDocuments_.review: Reminded me a lot of the first Serious Sam game.  Ah, nostalgia.  Large open spaces, lots of environmental flavor, plenty of secrets, and loads of traditional Sam fun.  The mech and tank were well done and fun.  On the negative side, I could almost complain that there could maybe possibly be a few too many weapons and gadgets.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: Played it through with my brother with 3 x enemy count, sometimes hitting 15 fps at minimum (Due to increased enemy count with ultra settings). Thing is, the ridiculous enemy count and stupid amount of lead, explosives, energy beams, bolts & cannon rounds you can output onto/into them makes this game so good even at low frame rates, wide open areas return and the intro from the base game is actually achievable in this fan made DLC.Well worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: A complete return to form for the Serious Sam series. Seriously. Serious Sam 3/BFE and 4 seem like jokes in comparison to the quality of Siberian Mayhem. The pacing is tight, the new weapons feel great, and the levels actually reward exploration instead of having numerous dead-ends. Plus the vehicle sections are pure ultraviolence magic. Seriously some of the most visceral fun I've had in ANY FPS in a LONG time.Most importantly, the game throws HUNDREDS of baddies at you in a way that feels way more congruent with Serious Sam TFE/TSE/2/TNE. I blazed through the single player campaign on Normal in about 6 hours - I definitely could've secret hunted for longer, and I'd really like to do a co-op playthrough with the 2x enemy multiplier! Game's a steal, and I highly recommend for a seriously good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Serious Sam 4, than I highly recommend to you this expansion pack: while short (~5 hours), it focuses on the best elements of the base game while improving things like level design and environments (such as blinding blizzard to direct flow of battle or fog for atmosphere).If you didn't like SS4, than Siberian Mayhem is unlikely to radically change your mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: Definately recommending if you enjoyed the base game. The expansion is a great continuation for the original game, expanding (heh) on some of the functionality that the base game sadly was underutilizing. Contains some cool bonus content for the fans of the old SS games as well. The game is short, but polished4.25/5
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: Potentially the most fun I've had in a co-op arcade shooter. Game is loud, in your face, totally aware that it's an over the top cheesy action game and horribly dad-jokeish. For $20 it was more than well worth the money. Yes there are some performance issues due to the number of enemies+particles+GFX. Overall if you've got $20 and an itch for an Doom parody that rivals Doom, buy this.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Tons of funCons: A bit shortTo me, Serious Sam's strength is in its level design. SS3:BFE seemed to change the design by adding more linear paths and less open bowl arenas. Which was fine, but when circle strafing is all you got (not double jump or dash), hallways and streets are only food for backing up. This game does a good job of presenting nice enemy combinations in different environments to keep fights fresh. I'd like to see the epic scenery of TFE and TSE return to the series one day, but this is a nice change of pace.

_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: A midquel set between the penultimate level and final level of Serious Sam 4 , Sam "Serious" Stone ends up at Siberia and does what what he does best: shooting a whole lot of aliens.Being made up of fans of the game, Timelock Studios did an amazing job with the game. Gameplay is still very solid. There's enough new enemies to the roster to help shake up the battlefield. Returning weapons feel great to use, as do the new ones introduced here. Writing and plot are still great, and so is the music. I would say its very much worth its price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game, I think it was way better then SS4. For the levels, I feel they were more fun to play through and I liked how much exploration they seemed to have in them, with me constantly going off the main path to check an area out. The new weapons were all fun to use, though I feel that the Burner was a bit too overpowered and that I was given too much ammo for it. The new enemies were awesome, but I feel that those tougher Zealot guys were a bit hard to kill because of their armor. The secrets were the best part, they were way better then SS4's and they felt really creative, kinda like something you'd see in the classic SS games or SS2. Overall, I think this is definitely an improvement to SS4 and there were a lot of moments that caught me off guard, the only problems I have with this are that there are performance issues and some of the fights can be very hard but I guess this is an expansion and usually expansions/DLCS are harder then the base game. Other then those, I think this is definitely worth its price and improves on most of SS4's flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: Serious Sam: Siberian Mayhem

_childDocuments_.review: Recommendation is solely based upon being BETTER than Serious Sam 4.The game itself is full of bugs; The worst of them is AI is stupid, like even worse than you remember from Serious Sam 4.If you go long range, you can pick them off one by one without triggering much response.Still has vast open areas with NO mobs in it, tho, it's way more "locked" in the openworld than what you remember from the "France map driving a tractor" in Serious Sam 4. A few new enemy types, and ALOT more funny "secrets" I was missing from the former game, heck this time I only got 50% cleared of achievements in the short gameplay time this game is. (I ran Normal Mode - 6 hours from beginning to credit with alot of free running around, so I recon standard players only doing objectives is more likely to run 4-5 hours unless speedrunning).I chuckled a few times with the new one-liners they provided Sam Stone with, actually pretty good ones!All in all - Basic FPS shooter, difficulty if you are used to playing either FPS games in general on Hard+ or Serious Sam on Hard+, pick a higher difficulty than you think you need. People on the stream thought I was playing on easiest difficulty, as the weapons are bloody overpowered for Sam in this game, hordes feel like... mere... puddles of mobs.Short gameplay - but has MP option (Not tried that at this moment, I just focused on getting basics done first)7/10 if you can get it on reduced price via a Sale,  6/10 if you pay full price.

_childDocuments_.review: For starters, the same thoughts as the original Serious Sam 4The single player company is wonderful. Multiplayer is good, but ONLY FOR 4 people? WHAT? WHY? For a computer in conjunction with an Intel Core i5-7400 + GTX 1050 Ti + 1x Kingston HyperX Fury Black (8 Gb), for some reason the game sets the minimum settings and the game still manages to lag and freeze, although the computer falls into the average according to the system requirements.BUTTimelock studio coped with the optimization of this piece of the Croatian engine and on such a weak PC, the FPS was about 75. In the most dynamic and busy moments, it dropped to 57, but this is not so critical. If the game is not streamed from such a PC, then it will not fall lower, but yes, you can lower it to 19 or even less. The main disappointment is that the plot seems to be canonical throughout the campaign, but at the end a wild twist is made because of which it is not clear where the canonical Siberian journey diverges from what the developers did. We are waiting for an answer to this question (yes, there are those who follow the plot lol)My final DLC score is 8.5/10 Great job!Mini Update for pacth 1.03SO MANY NEW SKINS FOR MP ARE MINDBLOW! Surviwal maps are awesome too! Love you Timelock studio <3

_childDocuments_.review: After beating the game, I believe this standalone expansion is a better experience than Serious Sam 4 and the launch is MUCH better!Pros: + Graphics are better than Serious Sam 4+ The Ui is better, since it has more variety of background art that fit the game (The main colour gives me vibes to the Second Encounter)+ Level design is amazing! + Easter Eggs are more fun to discover, and feel rewarding!+ The New weapons are REALLY fun to use!+ There are more fun gadgets!+ The vehicle sections are a major improvement and more fun!+ All bosses are fun the verse!+ Despite Serious Sam 4 trying to stay true to the classics, this one does a much better job!+ More replay value+ Serious difficulty is fun+ The story is funny and lightens up the moodCons:- Optimisation is still not good like with 4- Texture pop in's are more common in my opinionFinal Score: 9.5/10Overall, I've had a really fun and challenging experience with this game. It improves what made 4 good and even turns flaws into great features! I believe Croteam should still over look development to see how the future Serious Sam games go. However, Timelock Studio has proven they're talented devs and they should help with the future games! I still believe 4 is a great game, and one of my favourites within the SS series. But, this game... Is the game (Still can't top the classics).

_childDocuments_.review: short but sweet, takes 4's ideas and actually takes advantage of themif you liked 4's gunplay but hated the level design, id give this one a shot. i think its worth it for 20 bucks. my only real issue with the campaign are the puzzles because good lord they do NOT fit in a sam game. like not only are they not exactly engaging (moving cargo containers and bioshock-esque pipes) but they just bring the pace to a halt. it's great you actually get rewarded for them but i'd much rather be challenged with harder encounters than contemporary puzzles that are honestly unrelated to the rest of the gameplay loop sam is known for.performance is better than 4 at launch but still kinda crusty. turn on vulkan rendering and put ♥♥♥♥ on medium for a (somewhat) stable framerate.keep in mind too though that this is a sam game through and through, so it's lots of running backwards while pumping lead into hordes of enemies. not a whole lot on the thinking side. if you like that type of "turn your brain off" gameplay in an fps, this is for you. if not, i'd avoid this and the series as a whole lol.

_childDocuments_.review: As a pretty old time Sam fan, I gotta say, for Timelock Studio's first big project, they killed it. I have had a great experience playing Siberian Mayhem from start to end. The combat scenarios the player is pushed into are interesting and sometimes pretty difficult! I'm not quite sure how I feel about the new "Dog Frogs" as a sort of stand-in for the Marsh Hoppers of old, but they're a mostly harmless addition, so I cant be too upset.Oh, those new weapons? I cannot overstate how enjoyable they are. The new Gadgets too! The Perun Crossbow is an immensely satisfying stand-in for the classic sniper rifle, capable of gibbing even the biggest of enemies with a few well-placed headshots. The new laser cannon standing in for the classic laser gun is also immensely satisfying. I wish I had a little more time to play with it, but given it's power (especially when dual wielding it) I can understand its late introduction to the game. And not to mention the AK! Yes its more or less a reskin of the classic Assault Rifle, however it's damage stat is increased to offset its lower mag size from the 80 shots the AR got in Sam 4. Nothing gets better than hosing down hordes of Kamikazes and Gnaars with Akimbo AKs.My main issues come from some of the "crane" segments which slow the pacing of some levels down, probably a mechanic that was intended to be used a little more, but overall it's mostly harmless, if a little annoying.The game's performance is, admittedly, pretty bad. I dont have the best rig around, but it can handle gibbing mass hordes of enemies in other games, but in Siberian Mayhem, using the laser cannon against a large group of Processed causes my frame rate to tank. The texture pop-in is also a bit too noticeable, but I eventually was able to ignore it.Overall, I had a good time with this game. Sure, its short, but it doesn't overstay it's welcome, and that modesty is appreciated for a side chapter. I tip my hat to Timelock Studios. For your first big game, you did a really good job, even if some of the edges are a little rough!...Oh, if you see a guitar, maybe stop and give it a play. Trust me.

_childDocuments_.review: Free from the shackles of Croteam's development hell, a group of russian modders went above and beyond what it means to make a Serious Sam game in 2022. In almost every way this game is an improvement over its predecessor and I would argue the classics themselves. But a summary of the issues is that very little changed gameplay wise from 4. If you did not like how 4 felt/played mechanically then you will probbaly not be swayed.This game features much more refined and interesting levels, an amazing suite of varied encounters that are also on average more difficult than previous entries (especially early game), a most importantly it adds back many elements that modern sam games were missing. Prior to 3, serious sam was rather whimsical and didn't give a toss what kind of tonal dissonance it threw at you to make you laugh or what kind of evil tricks it would pull on any secret hunters. This was all pretty much removed come 3 and 4 as the games just took themselves too seriously to really go out of their way and introduce anything with any levity.In comes siberian mayhem and I just found a weird potion behind a waterfall that took me to a bootleg pyroland where I fought a mountain sized scrap jack who popped with 1 shot of the sniper. Or encounting a silly death stranding easter egg secret within the first 30 seconds of the game. The secrets and side quests across the board were made so much more memorable. For secrets it's no long always just some basic parkour trick you have to do, sometimes they can be multi level secrets, or play tricks with the level design. When it comes to side quests almost every single one has been memorable. In serious sam 4 I did side quests to get a few encounters, have some fun and may an upgrade, and move on. They were fine but frankly had almost no distinction from the normal gameplay that there was no reason to have them as optional quests. Just make the level 2 encounters longer!But Siberian Mayhem? Oh my god they make these quests memorable. More often than not it'll end in some unique gag, take you to a unique area that looks different, throw some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard encounters at you (it is optional afterall), and send you on your merry way. Sometimes they might have call backs to previous Sam games, sometimes they will end in an actually enjoyable boss battle with unique music and everything, and sometimes you might just get some fun gimmick.But while it goes really with the secrets and side quests, it's still just an expansion to serious sam 4 at the end of the day and the main story and aesthetic is still gritty realism. Though I do appreciate including more alien tech to the aesthetic as little as we see of it.In my eyes, this has been the best of both worlds. I really enjoy serious sam 4's faster gamplay and how fun the encounters have been, but now I can also enjoy that slice of the classics with how much more silly this can get between its side quests and secrets.

_childDocuments_.review: The TSE to the ss4 TFE1. The new weapons are great, but i was under the impression that we will get new weapons not replacementsThe crossbow is good, feels good, looks good, the orange color scheme and the behavior actually resembles the eraser from bogus detour, but not at the cost of both the sniper rifle AND the devastator, is this because it would be too similar? because really i don't think most players would careone suggestion would be to delegate the enemy piercing to the devastator, have sniper do massive bonus damage on weak points (small explosive in the bullets could be a justification) and have the crossbow pierce less in a line but with explosive bolts that stick out of enemies (or ground) can be manually detonated, or maybe arcing lightning a bit (since they're mentioned to be electrified) or proximity sensor explosive bolts that stick out and explode when another enemy is near, or... you get the ideasame with the burner, both it and the laser should be in, even just having different ammo pools would be enough to differentiate them with how different they feel, or a small tweak that has the burner beam doing less damage but add a small burn over time to enemies for a few seconds, really the minigun and the laser are also pretty similar so why not add the burner as well?and i really don't like that the autoshotgun is delegated to a secret, i thought that autoshotgun is going to become a staple weapon for the series like how devastator and c4 became after ss3 or the sniper after tse, it's also really helpful as it represents and option between 'oh a group of kleers/gnaars, lets whip out the shotgun' and '♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ THAT'S A HORDE BRING OUT THE MINIGUN'the AK is fine as the rifle is really the one weapon that feels appropriate for it to have variants, and the AK feels incredible, it's honestly the best AK i ever used in games, and i played a lot, if the weapon skin functionality stays for future SS games then the option for the AK should always be offered, it's that good!really don't be shy to give 3 weapons per slot in your games, even if some are similar, one could argue that having this many weapons makes them to clunky to switch but i'd say that even with half the current arsenal you're ♥♥♥♥♥♥ without hotkeys, get some future SS to have 3 weapons per all 9 slots the game deserves itthe gadgets here mostly have the same issue ss4 does but to a lesser degree due to the game being more stingy with OP battle enders, and the new gadgets are fun otherwise2. The new enemies are also greatThe hopper lizard thing may be annoying but it's a good type of annoying, the octanian variants are good and really demonstrate why the croteam should not be afraid to add more variants to their enemies than they currently have (just give just a new beheaded variant already, the yellow shirt bomber made many believe there will be more and people wanted that), and the turret is a good miniboss and makes me wish for ss2 style turret enemies to returnthe rollerball grenade especially (and the secret that spawns a ton of them, but they don't have their netricsa message why?!) just causes me to want the rollerballs to return, or be ported from last hopethe octanian raider is still not an enemy sadly, i feel ss2 style aircraft should also make a return in the futurethe only thing the game lacks (especially highlighted by the vehicle and open sections) are very large enemies like the highlanders and ss2 mechanical spiders, the tank section especially makes me wish for giant spiders, for some reason that i can't pinpoint the moment ss4 trailer dropped i had the image of a running boss battle with an enormous giant spider boss while in a tankthe boss isn't that good however, i feel that ss games are the best with massive, free roaming bosses with minimal scripting, and the massive maps of ss4 really would do well with bosses like that3. The new vehicles are great as well, both the tank and the new mech, the tank especially is something i wanted with ss4, though i feel that the tank is too slowthe other vehicles are also good, the snowmobile does it's job, as does that slow truck in refinery side mission (for what it's supposed to do it does the job well, it brings you back faster)though this really highlights an issue that was also present in ss4, there are either vehicles that you can't really fight on and mostly serve to transport you around or vehicles so OP they require their own section and outrageous enemy numbers, there's no vehicle that can fight and is an upgrade over going on foot but still fits with normal gameplay like the ss2 vehiclesi think the best bet would be to look at serious sam next encounter humvee, this is a vehicle that fits thematically with ss4 and one that isn't OP but still better than being on foot, this is a vehicle category that the games would really benefit from and enable more consistent and better usage of big open areas the game is capable ofthe hover scooter is also a step in the right direction, reminds me of ss2 vehicles4. The new maps are a massive step in the right direction, especially the bunker side quest in map 4 feels like the interior areas in TSEthe first 3 maps are examples of everything being done right, from the enemy placement to the secrets, from the map layout to the pacingthe last section of map 4 and the entire map 5 less so, if anything i feel the biggest problem with those is how incredibly tight they are while looking like they should be more open, especially the soviet apartment blocks don't feel that good when used for corridors this tighti guess most of my critique there is that the engine is capable of such open areas but the last map is actually pretty claustrophobic, and yes i know it's still comparable to the biggest, most open ss1 maps, i think part of this is that modern assets feel differently to the blocky old brushes and the fact that the game uses the NPC's as an excuse to throw more enemies at you while not giving you adequate room, really the encounters before the brigde when going around that park would warrant space similar to the kleer valley in metropolis in older ss gamesi could also say that some open areas in map 3 aren't as open as ss4 made me expect them to be, but to be honest without more ss2 style vehicles, powerfull weapons to thin the massive hordes instead of the OP gadgets that instantly delete them and giant enemies there isn't that much that can use themhonestly if there is one thing to take out from siberian mayhem, is that devs should never be afraid of experimenting and adding more variety to anything, even if something is similar to what was before, ss4 fell into a box when it comes to level design (but admittedly it's not as deep a box like the ss3 was in), siberian mayhem however mostly crawled out of it, now if the next ss crawls out from the box on enemy and weapon variety everything will be well, especially when the enemy variety box is already partially crawled out ofalso if some people say puzzles/tombs/interiors bad then they should not be listened to (but removing the darkness/widening the flashlight and not slowing down the player was a good move), and honestly the same goes with skills and gadgets, i fully expect ss5 to have skills and gadgets and i HOPE that they will be even crazier than here as long as they don't fall into a box of 'similar skills broken down into more skills' and 'either powerups or _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Dusk Diver 2 is a "more of the same, but bigger" sequel that largely succeeds.  If you enjoyed DD1, you'll almost certainly enjoy this one as well.  If not, probably not.  And if you haven't played DD1 at all, go buy it first.  This one assumes you're already familiar with the plot and characters.THE GOODFundamentally, the gameplay hasn't changed much, although the brawler action does feel a bit smoother in this one.  The biggest single change is that your party now fights all at once - all three of your companions are (almost) always fighting alongside you, and you can now freely swap between the four party members, who each have their own specialties.  If someone's tired of fighting as Yumo, this gives them some new options. You're still using Ximending as your home base, but this time you can also explore a few other areas of the city as well.  The overall 'open world' map is roughly 2x the size of the original.  Plus, there are MANY new dungeon types and areas to explore.  You'll still revisit dungeons from time to time, but there's far more environmental variety than in DD1.Plus the story is reasonably interesting, and the main cast is still highly likeable and engaging to hang out with.  And it's significantly longer than the first game as well - 20-25 hours to complete, and more like 35+ if you're trying to 100% it.However, I'd rate this one as "good" rather than "great," about a 7/10.  It does have a few issues.THE BADThe biggest problem is that, while you *can* switch between characters, you don't really have much reason to.  Yumo is still your best all-around fighter, with a fast-paced rushdown style that focuses on stunlocking enemies.   It's simplest to focus on leveling and gearing her up until the game becomes trivially easy.  I never saw a game over screen in my entire playthrough.  More than anything else, this really should have had SOME sort of mechanic which made character-switching genuinely necessary, such as in Genshin Impact or the last few Ys games. In addition, the quality of side-quests really hasn't improved.  Most of them are simple errands, usually with a couple battles thrown in as you run between checkpoints.  The issue is, they can now sprawl across multiple map zones, requiring several load screens to move around.  This makes them start feeling tedious.  At least in DD1, the map was so small that they never really felt like a chore to complete.I was also a little disappointed that there are fewer extra activities in this one.  No capsule machines, no fortunes, and even some of the little activities like going to the movies have been cut.  It's not a big deal, but I like those Persona-style hangout activities and I wish there'd been more.Finally, a warning:  When you finish the game, you CANNOT return to the game after the credits roll.  The final mission is a true point of no return.  (Although there is a NG+ mode.)  So if you're planning on trying to 100% the game, make sure you do it before entering the last dungeon.  This is odd, since the original game did let you return to the map after the credits.  Not sure why it changed.Overall, though, this is a solid sequel to its solid predecessor.  If you like the idea of a miniature mashup of Persona and Yakuza set in Taipei, with a charmingly quirky cast, give it a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Dusk Diver 2

_childDocuments_.review: You ever play a game and think to yourself, "Man, I like this core loop, the characters, and the world, but it all feels so budget! I hope the developers can do better next time."And in Dusk Diver 2, they did.From the copy-and-paste generic city streets of the one map to several vibrant, varied, and beautiful backgrounds.From the hordes of generic enemies you mow down Dynasty Warriors style, to a smaller handful of much more clever, powerful, and better designed enemies.Old characters that were just summons are now fully playable. Revamping of the combat system so you now have powerful, fun to use skills to swap in instead of just a hard-coded series of combos. You can play Le Viada and bring in her "Not A Gang" of fish underlings with ushankas, AK-47's, and vodka bottles to shoot Chaos Beasts dead.A legitimate heartwarming continuation of the first game, with backstories for the characters, explorations of topics and locations only hinted at before, and many bonuses for fans of the first game--I was really happy that the Little Lady clothing store got the big break it needed.It's not a perfect sequel. Some of the new systems I dislike, like the equipment system which feels superfluous. The plot is also a bit lacking in places, like the introduction and weight of the important new characters, especially higher ups who are intentionally evasive or suspicious but we never get much reason to care for them outside of their stereotypical, "They're the heads of these shady organizations, fear them!"But, I played this game nearly non-stop for the entire play time listed on this review. It wasn't a masterpiece but I enjoyed myself greatly.And I have high hopes for Dusk Diver 3, if they ever make one, because clearly these devs know how to improve, iterate, and make a sequel that shines brighter than the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Dusk Diver 2

_childDocuments_.review: The first game was a bit rough around the edges, but it was fun. Well, less is often more, and the second installment clearly shows it — while the original didn't outstay its welcome, the sequel struggles to keep the player entertained. The fights were improved, but now the whole city is riddled with combat encounters — I've managed to have effectively infinite resources and overleveled characters before reaching the half point of the game. There are a lot of quests, but most of them showcase nothing novel and are copy-pasted fetch missions. The inventory system was introduced to no avail, as there is little gain in managing it in a timely manner. Most of the side activities are so common, that the player's completion is counted in tens: win another ten fights, gather another ten crystals, etc."Dusk Diver 2" is not poorly designed, insanely boring, or completely broken, but I cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: For an updated review:---------------I don't know where to start.I went to 2019's Fancy Frontier and instantly fell in love with the fist sequel from the demo booth. The same with the 2nd sequel and here's my first hour impression:First of all, Dusk Diver's series forte lies in the combat. The 2nd series improves its combat further seamlessly into a freeflow form of combat than its prequel where you are going to feel a delay at the end of combo before chaining to your next combo. Second, still about the combat. And I salute and cheer for WANIN International for bringing out the feature that Dusk Diver fans looking for: Party combat. In Dusk Diver 2, Yu Mo/Player isn't fighting alone anymore against the horde of enemies. This time, Yu Mo is bringing up her squad together AT THE SAME TIME (At least with Uncle Leo with my progress so far) to thin the enemy gang, one for all and all for one style. Though, the ally AI could use better improvements as my observation during battle to test their efficacy, I saw Uncle Leo got beaten more than he could dish notable damage to the enemy. Still, the extra presence of your allied unit at the same time in the battle excited me and I am not done yet talking about the combat. Third, let's talk about the Break system. The devs took the Break system higher into the next level from the prequel and I am going to tell you how they did it in 1 phrase: FINISH HIM! That's right. In Dusk Diver 2, you can deal a heavy damage with your allied units on a specific downed target together with your friendly partner through the BREAK notification on enemies upon fulfilling the specific damage threshold. The cinematic effect during the animation, combine with the damage calculation give you the OOOMPH kick that motivates me to get the cinematic effect again. Why? Because the animation is satisfying and rewarding your reflexes. I could fill the entire review column just talking about the combat aspect so I am going to add another one. Another shoutout to WANIN International by adding the character switch feature. In Dusk Diver 2, player can switch to different characters other than Yu Mo, each with particular fighting style to keep combat from getting stale. The problem with Musou (無雙)  combat, is that the player will be using the same combo over and over again to clear the enemies and technical moves against boss/mini-boss instead of experimenting with different moves resulting in repetitive gameplay loop and Dusk Diver 1 didn't escape from this boring clutch. But not in the second installment where the player is given complete control to characters other than Yu Mo. From my progress so far, Uncle Leo is a slow hitting, high damage dealer crowd control character with a unique reloading mechanic, giving me more option to style my combat taste on my mood. Like I said, I can fill with another praise for the combat. After all, Dusk Diver's about combat, overpowering horde of enemies in satisfying freeflow fight but let's put that aside for a change of pace. The U.I is improved and stylized a lot in a graffiti style. For those has been to Xi Men Ding at Taiwan, the graffiti style from the U.I comes from local graffiti artworks around the walls of Xi Men and you can feel the love and support of the developer to the local community artist too. Exploration is improved WAAAY better than the predecessor and I am delighted to see my favorite Akihabara of Taiwan got mapped bigger, better, livelier into this sequel with improved NPC placeholders. My only dissappointment that still carries on from the prequel is the restriction of exploration in the normal Xi Men Ding. In Dusk Diver 1, there are certain areas those are off limits to players despite the allure and the call for the players to explore. One of them is the crossing across the next building. The problem persist in Dusk Diver 2, despite there's an action for player to move to the other building area but I still feel confined in a space rather than being able to explore the city to the fullest. But hey, you can now take the MRT ride to other locations now so one step at a sequel.I will update my review as I play longer but should you get this game in its full price at the 1st day launch?This game deserves every single of my money in its full price. P.S:Shoutout to WANIN International for making Yu Mo and Big Sis Vlada smexier in Dusk Diver 2, I love you guys. Thank you very much.

_childDocuments_.review: "If you liked Dusk Diver 1 then you'll like this because it's more of the same"I keep seeing this line or something similar quite a lot, with people saying the game is just "more of the same", and whilst it is basically DD1 with some improvements, there are also several instances where they made certain aspects WORSE than in the first game. There's a level of complexity as to how I feel about this game, because it IS a good game (which is why I've recommended it), but it also made me feel like I had to force myself to continue playing it in the end.When I played Dusk Diver 1 I felt compelled to play it every day that I had time whenever I'd got home from work, and whilst the game was shorter it kept me hooked BECAUSE of that. Dusk Diver 2 however felt like a friend that you met a year ago that you vibed really well with, and so you invited them over for dinner. After finishing dinner and having a good time, instead of leaving they pull out a sleeping bag and say "So we're good to hang out all weekend, right?". You like their company, but really wanted them to go home a day ago and now it's just annoying you that they're sticking around. Combat - Combat is very much the star of the show in DD2 compared to anything else, as it's better than DD1's combat in almost every way. With the added choice of playing multiple characters with their own unique styles, it ends up allowing you to play however you want. Each of the characters has a distinctive moveset where they each have things they're better at than the other, so whilst you CAN play one character for every engagement, you really shouldn't.Characters - Almost every one of the characters that I encountered from the base side characters from DD1 to the new ones you meet in DD2 were interesting in some way or another. Stylistically all of the characters which are part of the main cast have a unique look. Each character in the game seems to have their own ambitions they've got set out for themselves, and seem to actually live within the world of DD2.Soundtrack - DD1's soundtrack was already pretty good, but DD2 added some extra stuff like metal tracks and heavy electronic music for stages. I do wish they had used more original music rather than recycling part of DD1's soundtrack, but it's perfectly alright.Combat animations - With the animations outside of combat being so terrible I was pleasantly surprised when the in-combat animations actually exceeded my expectations. Everything feels properly done and has a level of flair which makes them pleasing to the eye, with each unique attack for each character having something in its animation which is there to say "I'm this persons attack". Unique movement mechanics for Viada when she's got water shells loaded, or electronic bats in Bahets guitar riffs, everything looks great.The Story - DD2's story for a lot of it was pretty standard anime cliche, though it did subvert my expectations quite a bit at a certain point. I neither liked it nor hated it, but definitely felt like the first seven chapters were much better than the five after it.Collectathon - There is A LOT to collect in DD2. Outfits, soundtracks, character illustrations, food items, shards, orbs. It's almost too much and feels somewhat monotonous to keep track of.Enemy variety - I WOULD say the enemy variety overall for this game is good, however you hardly ever encounter different types of enemies in certain areas. There's hardly any intermingling of enemy types, so if you're in an area where there's robots that's all you'll fight. If you're in an area with chaos beasts that's all you'll fight. Some of the more impressive enemy designs are used only once for a single battle and then tossed aside without introducing them into the storyline again.Sidequests - EVERY SINGLE SIDEQUEST IS BAD, and it makes me so irritated that this is the case because they didn't DESERVE to be this bad when there's so much personality and character charm for each individual character, and yet it doesn't seem like anyone cared and chose quantity over quality. Even important sidequests which are about character growth or their pasts are bad. DD2 has so many opportunities to capitalize upon a plethora of character traits for their side characters to make good sidequests. How about a "date" with Leo where the game teleports you from shop to shop and they spend a day trying sweets whilst he talks about himself? Or Viada getting Yumo to actually try being a model, having her try various dresses and so on and then talking about her past.Every single sidequest is bad.Animations outside of combat - For a $50 on release title it confuses me as to why these are all so very bad to the point where they make even makes Pokemon Legends Arceus look like a technical marvel of the same caliber as Crysis when it first released. There is one single cutscene in this game outside of combat which is actually well-animated, and it was the very last one, conveying more emotion in the one single 30 second cutscene than all others in the ENTIRE game. Character interactions when each character is standing near one another results in every character standing there like some sort of puppet without emotions.Hand-Holding/Tutorials - This game holds your hand and throws so many tutorials at you throughout the entire game that it almost feels insulting. For some things it's definitely needed, but for some things which really should've had a tutorial there isn't one, and for completely asinine things such as finding items around the city there are sometimes 3 page tutorials the game bombards you with. DD2 also throws tutorials at you whilst you're in combat, sometimes causing you to entirely skip them as a result of pressing buttons mid-combat.Support AI - Whenever you've got them actively set to participate in combat when not using a character, they'll often times just menacingly walk towards enemies and do nothing. You're almost better off not playing the game with your allies set to participate in fights so that all enemies focus solely on you instead.-Overall Score: 7/10.Worth $50? No. I'd suggest waiting for a sale.Closing Thoughts: Unfortunately Dusk Diver 2 feels like a worse experience to me than the original as whilst there are some improvements made it just overall feels like a worse package than the original. If you're looking for a decent combat-oriented game I would suggest it, but don't come into playing DD2 expecting anything exceptional.

_childDocuments_.review: This review breaks my heart to post.I absolutely love Dusk Diver. I picked it up for a few bucks off a Fanatical deal, and was surprised how much time I put into it...maxing out all the friend levels and even all the stores. It was a fantastic experience and a very amazing surprise to find.So What happened to Dusk Diver 2?Well...some times less is more, and you need to keep it simple. Dusk Diver 2 is the greatest example of this. This game is a mess of tutorials and "press this while you push this to do this". Perfect example: in Dusk Diver, but hitting RB with Leo equipped, I would do a nice hard crack to any baddies in my face. Now it is a disaster of "Press and hold RB, then press the button corresponding to the style of attack you want to do". So I have to learn all these attacks and how they are organized...keep it simple!!!And I don't know what the characters did...maybe walked through a pool of Krazy Glue, or put on their maple syrup shoes...but combat feels way slower in this one. Combat is more polished and smooth...at the cost of the speed and intensity that the first one carried. Just Dodge feel off now too. Also moves have way too much opportunity cost to them:  if you do this, then this bar will rise faster, but this stat will lower or gain less...The final let down is a weird one, and a lot of games might disagree with me on it: It isn't just Yumo this time around. Now you can get to switch between characters. Great!!! I like that....BUT WAIT!!! They fight with you during the quest. So whom you are not using are AI controlled. I hate that...i really do. Why? Because I have yet to find a good AI that uses half the brain power that a decent play would use. Instead of zoning, i watched the computer just get pounded on as it ran into 3 enemies with Leo head first and no plan.Its good to be back to Dusk Diver....and revisit the streets I know so well, but have never been to in reality. This series still makes me want to travel to Taiwan....but this game just doesn't have the magic like the last. Its not overly bad, and I will continue to play it...but let me explain why it will not get a thumbs up from me:Should you get Dusk Diver 2?- Well...do you own the first?    If not then no, you should not get Dusk Diver 2. You should get the first one and play that instead for a more enjoyable experience.- If you own the first, did you finish the first?  If no..skip this and go beat the first.- Did you finish the first and expect more of the same?  If so..then no, you should not get this game. It is the same but doesn't feel it. Play the first again.- Did you finish the first and expect something different from this?  If yes then maybe. Understand it is more polished but like going from Street Fighter Turbo back to Street Fighter non-turbo.- Have money to burn and finished the first?  Sure...why not. Get it and see if you agree.I don't want to leave without saying something good, because it isn't a total disaster game. It is ok...and it is beautiful and good to be back. Its just not as fun as the first. If it wasn't for my curiosity about how this story will go..I'd go back and play more of the first instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Now maybe it's just been a long time since I played the first Dusk diver but to start I wanna say it feels kinda slower? In combat I mean but not to it's detriment, so it's basically a lot like the first game but more, what do I mean? Well for starters characters from the prior game that were just essentially special attacks are now full on characters you can switch between in battle, there are more areas to choose from and walk around, attacks are more accurate than ever which I highly appreciate and it's just an all around good time and improvement, I said about the first one with certain things improved would make for a game I'd happily pay full price for, well they've done it and to make me feel a games worth full price is darn impressive in an era of quick heartless cash grab games with barely any real meat to them dood.Okay now onto the more detailed stuff, so the combat feels more refined now as I said, which is impressive with the addition of more playable characters I might add, the devs even did a great job of making them all unique, protag is a balanced melee fighter with a wide variety of attacks and the lightning element (This may stop an enemy from attacking) another is a defence/counter heavy fighter who's slow but high offence makes them an insane fighter if you play well, their element is fire which...oddly doesn't hurt enemies but instead makes them more susceptible to break, (Will explain that one in a bit) the third character has wider ranged hits and has essentially a bleed effect on their weapon but also timing to their attacks let's you do more damage and adds the bleed effect on normal strikes if you have good rhythm and finally you have a ranged character, very hard to master as the enemies love to counter long ranged attacks with rather nasty attacks of their own, they could have toned that down honestly but it's not the worst ever, their element is water, this slows enemies down both movement and attack wise dood.Combat flows nicely, it can be difficult at the start though and seem rather long as enemies seemingly have large health pools but as time goes on you get much stronger and you realise they wanted players to use their meter more (I'll get to that too) it also want's players to abuse the break mechanic, this can be activated from repeated hits or knocking enemies into a wall, you get a heavy, highly damaging attack in, free iframes (invincibility if ya don't know) and it even hurts enemies close by, essential for the more sturdy enemies if you want to end it quicker, enemies have decent variety too, even down to how some attack, one set of enemies truly terrified me to face off against every time I encountered them for their ferocity but also looked pretty cool, it made you play in very specific ways dood.Thought I was done with combat? Not yet! For you see I haven't mentioned special skills, there's a decent variety for each character, again all are quite handy and in fact all can also be set as a support attack, on top of that you have a burst meter that let's you power up and hit for some major damage, especially if you fill the new meter up to near full as it let's you then use a real cool ultimate attack, of which all characters have, the combat is real fun when ya get into it like that dood.Next onto food! So food gives you temporary buffs or even immediate effects at times but more importantly you have takeaway food, I think the idea is great! The execution less so, buffs last five encounters, typically you will have a few more than that in a non human world stage but you can only use them in a safe area, which you'd think means just out of combat which would have been ideal but instead meant save points or the human world, it's not like soul crushingly bad, it just feels wasteful in consideration to how many you can just stock up on and never use because you need to hit a save point, you already have a fullness meter stopping you from abusing it and the limit of three effects so it seemed a bit much dood.Next up is equipment and gems, they are a fun addition, armour can have up to three slots, as well as boosts to your stats, real basic but the slots let you put in gems that can substantially boost the players stats and give some handy effects, the only real issue being some are much better than others and often cheaper slot wise at that (some can take up to three slots) for instance 5% chance of not getting a status ailment is just plain wasteful, if it stacked like EXP or wafer (the alternate currency for other types of items) equipped to other characters it would be great but it doesn't so it sucks XD something to keep in mind for any dev 5% is rarely a good enough amount, that said the 3% health recovery on enemy down is great when there are so many enemies, weird they got that right but not the other dood.Music is great, nice variety to it but it could have done with one or two more tracks for particularly impactful moments of the story, although for the most important stuff they had some real good stuff for as every game should for their end game content, the story was interesting and the characters were very much themselves which is always a good thing dood.The costumes like before have name: Vampire Survivors
detailed_description: Vampire Survivors is a time survival game with minimalistic gameplay and roguelite elements. Hell is empty, the devils are here, and there's no place to run or hide. All you can do is survive as long as you can until death inevitably puts an end to your struggles. Gather gold in each run to buy upgrades and help the next survivor. The supernatural indie phenomenon that lets you be the bullet hell! Now with local co-op for up to 4 players! Supports mouse, keyboard, controller, and touch screen. Starting Tips Take your time to grab gems and items, they won't disappear. Get two or three offensive weapons at first, but focus on leveling them up one at a time. Armour and Luck are good starting power-ups to spend money on. Refund power-ups often, it's free, and try new upgrade paths. v0.1.0 release date: - itch: Mar 31, 2021 - Steam: Dec 17, 2021

You don't ever realise just how fun this game is until it's already too late, and you've been playing for four hours straight.10/10 will play more

_childDocuments_.review: You know what you're getting into with this game.  The concept is simple, the price is low, you've already heard of it, and you don't need me to explain it to you.  I picked up the game to try and 100% all of its achievements, blind (no foreknowledge of requirements, only using the Wiki if I had no idea what to do next).  Took me 40 hours to unlock the final character and get her achievement for 100,000 kills, which was the easiest one of all because she's so hellishly overpowered.  So... was it fun?Yeah.  The game has decent enough graphics, an above-average soundtrack, some actually pretty fun gameplay surprises, and even a bit of strategy when it comes to building.  Overall building is simple, and once your run is "solved" and you pass the point of clearly winning, the rest of the run can feel like a boring slog.  That's okay because the game lets you unlock several speed up and difficulty up modes that will bring the pace of the game back up to a fun/frenetic one at your choosing.  This isn't the time of game that I'm going to be relentlessly replaying like Risk of Rain 2 or Monolith, but it is a deceptively fun little Roguelite just the same.  I'd recommend it, even if you blow through it in a week like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: The quote "NEVER JUDGE A BOOK BY IT'S COVER" Has never been so true regarding this game.!!,For a game which has a price tag a little over £2 on Steam...Amazing!!, Please don't be put off by the graphics which I initially wasJust for sheer support to the production team behind the game the price is justly deserved and I would be glad to pay this just as a support contribution to the studio that produced it!!Ok, So about the game itself....It's basically an auto attacking game in which you control the character via mouse clicking (holding) which I didn't find very easy or the usual WASD which I found a lot better,The enemies incrementally get more frequent/stronger and as you kill more you collect xp tokens which in turn as you level up give an option of upgrades for your character ranging form abilities/weapons/defence etc, The game micro pauses so you can choose,You also have mini bosses that have a chance to drop loot chests which again can give a random upgrade towards your equipped weapons/skills making you stronger,You survive as long as possible until your sad demise, but wait!! , this is also a rogue-like game.All that earned gold carries into a coin storage that can be spent via an upgrade pool before you next attempt!!There are hidden characters/items etc for even more replay value.This is my first try at a review I hope this helps people make a choice to buy this game as I cannot stress enough the value per pence you get from this game,I have played for two hours so far and have streamed the gameplay via Twitch, £2 for 2 hours??? _childDocuments_.review: A new subgenre has been formed. For how inexpensive this game is, it's an instant classic in my mind.I had to go get and complete Nomad Survival before reviewing this fully and I can say I personally find Vampire Survivors to be better but not by much. I did not immediately feel this way, but after many battles - it has better skill combos that are more satisfying to use even if not always more effective or "better". I also appreciated the options in the maps for events or special items. This went a long way in replaying and achievement hunting - which was also a lot of fun to go through. This all said, I put more time into Nomad and I came out of all this feeling like it was worth buying and "beating" both of them. Vampire Survivors rarely slows down the deluge of mobs it throws your way but not without providing you with ample opportunity to level and skill up. As the enemies work to constantly surround and swarm you, you must strategically pick and choose which skills to equip and upgrade while you progress. Pick the wrong combos and you won't last very long. Pick the right combos and you could probably stop moving and could come out alive. Lastly, I'd like to shout out to the devs in that the game's controls are incredibly accessible and easy to use. You only need one hand and your character is always auto-attacking. It makes for a compelling way to go about a bullet-hell roguelike. This game is super cheap and super awesome. You should super get it.
