_childDocuments_.review: Update #2: It's quite simply -still- one of the best games I've ever played. It's packed with content and unlocks. The DLC is great. The music is great. The gameplay mechanics are great, especially when you unlock the game-changing/breaking mechanics such as Limit Break, Golden Eggs (increase base stats of a character), and Arcanas (ability/run modifiers for the current run). Curse is an excellent mechanic for crafting the tailor-making to your liking depending on the build you want to try and the character.I'll never tire of the experimentation aspect of this game. It's like a sandbox filled with cool and interesting tools for me to use and combine to my satisfaction. Amazing work. Amazing game. Go find some vampires if you can and destroy thousands upon heaping thousands of undead. I've literally slayed tens of millions of monsters now at this point with the occasional boss here and there.Update: This game is quite simply one of the best games I've ever played. If you enjoy min/maxing and experimenting with different builds, you will naturally find yourself running clinical trials thinking, "Okay, but what if I mix this accessory to increase projectile speed with that bouncing weapon. And then add this accessory to do reduce cooldown... And then... And then..." endlessly. The recently introduced Limit Breaker game mechanic only makes experimentation that much more engrossing by letting you over-level specific aspects of weapons that could be the literal amount of projectiles per tick/cast, the area size of its effect, the speed at which it travels, and so on. It makes every run different and lets me set wildly different goals. Sometimes I just like to focus on one specific weapon to see how badly I can wreak havoc on the baddies. I've done things... terrible things... that turned them into dust before they could even approach the edge of the screen.It's awesome.--What an amazing game for less than a gallon of gas. If you like destroying thousands upon thousands of enemies, Vampire Survivors will be your jam. There's more fun packed in here than most "triple-A" releases.You can expect gratuitous pixel death, interesting weapon combinations and evolutions, hordes, more hordes, and different characters that can encourage different playstyles. The transformation to weak hero into a god of death and destruction is satisfying every time, every run.This is already a great game with the potential to become even better through content updates. Even if the game received no updates at all though, it's more than worth its price. Can you survive 30 minutes, hero?

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 38.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: VS performs quite badly overall, and the first sign of that is a launch option called GPU Lag Fix. Regardless of your hardware, Vampire Survivors will eventually lag and stutter as an issue between its engine and the absolutely ludicrous effects, numbers, and entities on screen. That being said, lag is never really an issue for your raw gameplay, as at that point any semblance of actual input by the player is no longer required to progress and is merely an annoyance while farming. In the 54 hours it took me to finish with 100% achievements, the game never crashed, nor did I experience any gamebreaking bugs or glitches. However, the enemy A.I. is noticeably awful, and even as they generally just try to fuse their model with the player as a means of killing them, they still have a tendency to clip through terrain that should be inaccessible to them, like walls or pits, or get stuck on regular map architecture. There’s none. Vampire Survivors does not feature an overarching narrative but instead opts for a comedic and often referential approach in the little writing it employs. This is in the form of a bestiary that occasionally does feel like an attempt at some shallow worldbuilding but shouldn’t ever be mistaken for an attempt at a story. Besides the comedic writing, some maps leading up to the final map of the main game are designed to be surreal and toy with breaking the fourth wall as a means to engage the player. I quite enjoyed these small sections, although this approach seems to have been entirely abandoned for the DLC and is simply far too rare to recommend the game on the basis of them.VS can look quite good for what it is. Naturally, the game has barely any system requirements to begin with and is thus fairly limited in what it can portray in the first place. But despite this minimalism, characters, both the different PCs and enemies, look distinct at a glance and even have some memorable details on occasion.The music is surprisingly good and excels especially for different character themes; while not every unlockable character gets their own theme and thus stage music may or may not grow repetitive, the tracks that do stand out, like Pugnala’s ‘Red and Blue’ are stellar and worth listening to even outside of playing the game.The basic gameplay loop of Vampire Survivors is simple but actually quite engaging. In general, the player only ever controls their own character through the movement keys, while combat and aiming are done automatically. Enemies approach from all sides, and you’re merely trying to move in an efficient way so as to damage enemies, avoid damage yourself, and be able to collect dropped experience and items as you progress through a map. This makes the choice of which weapon to pursue more important in the early game, as it’ll tweak how you actively play the game. These may range from the knife, which shoots immediately and only in the direction you’re looking towards, to more defensive variants like the bible, which orbits around the PC like a shield. With early game, I am not referring to the early game of a single map but rather the first few hours in which the player has yet to unlock any of the more powerful items for their runs.These first few hours are genuinely quite fun and can even be reasonably challenging; however, I am wondering if this is something that the countless VS derivatives also suffer from: a ridiculous power creep that only ever gets monumentally more impactful with every unlock. These are tracked through a submenu and also equal the primary progression path for the player, besides unlocking the next map. The experience here is that once the player unlocks the ability or otherwise figures out how to evolve their weapons and starts to have just a modicum of an idea of just how VS works, it becomes a trivial experience. Aside from numerical concepts such as the effectiveness of weapons, there are aspects that are simply highly exploitable, such as, for example, the game fundamentally trying to achieve an entity density at any given point in a map. This means that strategies that could be conceived, like a movement build for kiting, are inherently worthless. Past this very early stage, VS coalesces into a gameplay loop that consists of setting up the most basic skeleton of the items you want by the end and past the first few minutes idling with little interruption, as the basic power level of the player is so ridiculously high that regular maps pose no threat almost regardless of what spawns—every spawn, naturally, also being entirely scripted. This doesn’t mean that interactivity itself isn’t present past that point; rather, the player is encouraged to collect items and secrets, which all just further this inherent problem of making the next map just a tiny bit less interactive than the one before.What it comes down to is that Vampire Survivors ends up playing like Cookie Clicker with extra steps. It evolves into what can only really be described as an idle game that has an annoying tendency to sometimes punish idling until you’re free to ignore virtually all of the game's once engaging mechanics when you get to the late game, when VS truly just becomes a game of picking your favorite near-immortal character and farming for endless amounts of stat bonuses you never needed in the first place to be just as effective. The DLC is particularly bad for this, as the maps are genuinely well designed and fun to play but simply end up serving as another brainless unlock as a victim of that exact same power creep.When I ask myself, Did I have fun playing Vampire Survivors? Really have fun, like in any other ‘regular’ video game. Then no. I didn’t. The first few hours are entertaining when there is still some sort of actual process of experimentation involved, but after that point, it deteriorates so quickly and so willingly into an idle game that I can’t really recommend it as a standalone experience. If you, however, are looking for exactly that: A more involved idle game—something to fill time with, say while playing an MMO and waiting for a raid to start or as a brief stimulant while working—then sure, it might be an experience worthwhile. I’d just question whether there aren’t better options available despite the already generous price.

_childDocuments_.review: A marriage between garlic bread and challah...it's about time this happened!You can use your favorite challah recipe or the one I've included below. The main element is the garlic mixture which can be used on virtually any dough (although I would be cautious using it with a super sweet recipe.As you can see, I rolled out each strand and brushed it with the garlic mixture. It's a bit fiddly and time-consuming. The other option is to just brush each strand and then braid. The flavor won't be as intense and it can be hard to braid when the strands are oily and slippery (it's hard to keep the ends together). But sometimes it's worth the saved time.I baked mine on a sheet pan this time and they came out wider and flatter. If you use a loaf pan (or there are oval pans specifically for challah), you will get a higher fuller look. Good news - taste is unaffected!For more about baking challah in general, and for a larger challah recipe, please see my Traditional Soft Fluffy Challah.Challah Ingredients:2¼ tsp. dry yeast (0.25 oz. / 7 grams)1 tsp. sugar1 cup warm water1 egg¼ cup honey3 tbsp. oil1 tsp. saltApproximately 4 cups bread flour (as always, add the flour slowly towards the end and feel if the dough needs more or less)Garlic Oil Ingredients1/3 cup extra virgin olive oil6 cloves garlic, crushed1 tsp kosher salt1/3 cup flat-leaf parsley, choppedOptional: flaked salt for garnishDirections:Whisk garlic oil ingredients together. Set aside.Dissolve yeast and sugar in ¼ cup warm water in a medium-sized bowl. Let sit about 15 minutes until thick and frothy.Add the egg, honey, oil, salt, remaining ¾ cup of water, and 3 cups of the flour. Mix until a loose batter forms. Add the rest of the flour slowly. You may not need it all, so go slowly towards the end. Alternatively, you may need slightly more. The dough should be soft but not sticky. Once the dough has enough flour, knead it well. You can do this recipe by hand or with a mixer (using the dough hook). Let the mixer do the kneading for you if you’re using one.Cover the dough with a wet towel or plastic wrap and put it in a warm place to rise for about 1-1½ hours. Dough should double in size.Tip the dough out onto your work surface and let it rest for 10 minutes.Divide it into six evenly-sized pieces. Roll each piece into a strand. Then take a rolling pin and roll the strand lengthwise so that it forms a long rectangle. Brush with the garlic mixture and roll-up jelly-roll style so that it reforms a strand. Repeat with remaining strands. Braid each three strands together, yielding two challahs. Brush the top of the loaves with more of the garlic mixture and sprinkle lightly with flaked sea salt (optional).Transfer loaves to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper OR two loaf pans. Cover and let rise in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes. Brush gently with more of the garlic mixture and place in the oven. OPTIONAL: If you prefer a shiny finish on your challah, brush with a beaten egg and then add the second layer of garlic mixture.Bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20 minutes. Remove from oven and brush again with the garlic mixture. Return to oven, lower temperature to 350°F (180°C) and bake for another 20 minutes. NOTE: Time will fluctuate depending on your oven and the type of pans you used. I used disposable aluminum pans - for real bakeware you may want to lower the temperature and/or reduce the time slightly. Loaf should be golden on top, and firm on the bottom.Remove from oven and as soon as possible (if you try immediately, they may break, so wait 10-15 minutes) transfer to a cooling rack and brush again generously with the garlic oil. If you don't have a cooling rack, you risk the bottom of your challah going soggy (this is a risk in general, but particularly with the garlic oil we've been dousing the loaves with. If that happens, put your challah back in the oven for a few minutes, directly on the oven racks (no pan). That will crisp up any soggy spots very quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: When it first came out in early access, Vampire Survivors was mostly praised for its unique take on the bullet hell genre and its surprisingly cheap price tag. Funnily enough, even though it was inspired by a lesser known mobile game, it became so successful that it unintentionally spawned a new genre called "Vampire Survivors-like".So, what exactly is Vampire Survivors? Vampire Survivors is a game where you control a character that does the attacking for you. It's kind of like an auto-battler, but you still have to move and dodge enemies by yourself. You then collect gems that were dropped by monsters, fill your experience bar and level up. You are given weapon/upgrade choices each time you level up, and you build your character the way you want. The goal is to survive the time limit. In order to do so, you need to become a killing machine, which is the entire point of Vampire Survivors. As mentioned in other reviews and comments, you become the bullet hell yourself.With its simple yet so addictive gameplay, achievements, unlockables, secrets and whatnot, Vampire Survivors is one of the best games on the market right now. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: It so damn addictive!  Literally sacked off a co-op game of Stellaris to play this by myself instead. Started playing at about 7pm and played through until 4.30am like some sort of lunatic on the first day. Anyway I've got all achievements for now so waiting for more content as game is still early access. As for the gameplay, it seems straight forward in that you move your dude across the screen and kill enemies and collect gems to level up. You don't even have to aim or press anything to shoot. You start off weak and have to kite the enemy around so you can circle back round to get the gems. The real skill comes in choosing your upgrade path. Every level lets you chose a weapon or buff, and then you can level up those weapons and buff, certain combinations then give you evolved weapons that are super powerful. But you only get 3-4 random options to choose each time so you might have a plan but then have to change it on the fly. You also earn gold which you can spend on permanent upgrades like speed, dps, area of effect, health, luck etc. But every time you level one up they all become more expensive. No worries though as you can reset your gold for free whenever and set up bonuses for a certain type of play through you have in mind. Finally you also have different characters to unlock, each with different skills and buffs and all start with a different weapon. The waves of enemies get harder and more every couple of minutes to max of 30mins where you get auto killed by the Grim Reaper but also get a 500 gold bonus for lasting that long. Currently there are only 2 maps but you can play them at normal or 'hyper' speed, with hyper giving you a bonus to gold. For the very low asking price (less than half a pint of beer) the game is well worth it and you'll get at least a good 20 hours out of it. It's still early access so hoping to see new mobs, levels, characters and weapons etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little Arcade Bullet Hell-ish Action RPG Rouge-lite.The game is quite minimalist, since your only input is 8-directional movement while automatically attacking. However, it's not an incremental/idle game or autobattler, since you have to actively dodge to survive and collect gold to progress. The "Rogue" element here is extra-lite; there is an element of random drops that will have you pursuing certain "builds", and a light progression system of permanent upgrades bought with gold from each run, but that's about it. Each run lasts at most 30 minutes. While I'd call it a Bullet Hell, it's not really a shmup/shoot-em-up - you are simply dodging the swarms of enemies that are spawning, while hoping your build has enough firepower to clear a path for you to dodge through. A few other classes and items eventually become unlocked as you obtain achievements. There are only 2 levels to play.That all said, it is surprisingly fun and original.

_childDocuments_.review: While on vacation I found myself wanting to play a casual game on the Steam Deck before going to sleep. So off I ventured into the wilds of the Internet in search of recommendation. Time and time again Vampire Survivors was being mentioned. Baffled was I, as I pondered the validity of such claims that VS is a casual game. I’ve never played a Rougelike or a Bullet Hell game and both terms seem to be the opposite of casual. Surely the Internet wouldn’t steer me wrong, right?As I gently pressed the power button, the Steam Deck warmed to my touch and began to gently purr in eager anticipation of vampiric slaying. I laid back against a wall of pillows and brought the glowing screen of the Steam Desk within view. I hopelessly maneuver around the main menu until I finally find the start game button and jump in headfirst.  I move Antonio around the screen as I futilely mash buttons trying to kill swarms of bats. I make it just past one minute before dying.“Argh! This is not casual!” But now I know that all I really need to do is move my pixeled survivor around which is nice since my furious button smashing tends to wake the Lady of the House.The next thing I knew, three hours had passed, 29 achievements had been unlocked, and the wife was sound asleep. 18 days later, 196 achievements were unlocked, 176 unique beasts destroyed, 173 items collected, 58 survivors found, and 16 secrets uncovered.Trying to review VS should be as simple as it’s gameplay and yet I’m at a loss for words. Did I enjoy unlocking all the things? Yup. Did I end up using the same weapons and passives by late mid-game? Indeed, I did. Did Queen Sigma make the game comically easy? Absolutely, but how else am I going to be able to reroll forty times until I can get Santa Water? ¯\_(ツ)_/¯Is VS worthy of your time and money? Of course it is.

_childDocuments_.review: More addicting than fun in the long run but beyond amazing before that tipping point.Roguelike/lite/whatevers that pull off the spinning plates act are always amazing. It's a seemingly simple task that actually requires insane attention to details and balance to remain fun. A select few pull it off and when they do the Overwhelmingly Positive ratings roll in. We all know them, and Vampire Survivors definitely joins the small club. But it's also its own animal.If you break down your gameplay timeline/investment in Vampire Survivors; The first ~10% would be pure delight as you steadily unlock characters and such while learning the game. Reaching new heights. Breaking records. "Completing" a run. Trying new levels and different item rolls. Then the next ~20% is grinding over the only difficulty hump. You hit your one roadblock. You have to adjust your focus to specific unlocks. Do a tiny bit of grinding. Figure out which character fits your style to do it. And then the final ~70% of your timeline is just pure addiction. You've reached the pinnacle already. It's just a matter of sitting through it X amount of times more to unlock the next achievement to unlock the next achievement to unlock the next... You're invincible. There's no challenge left. You're literally just playing to play and get that next dopamine hit from an achievement popping up in the bottom right corner.So while the spinning plates are balanced with care and the game is fun at its core. The only thing that keeps you around is addiction in its purest form. That's not to say your addiction isn't rewarded though. There are new wrinkles for each of those achievements you get. New levels. New bosses with mind bending ideas that seem genuinely "new" even 20hrs into a highly repetitive game. But again, you're more or less invincible. There's no threat to your runs for hours upon hours now. Even from the new stuff. It's just seeing that new stuff that's keeping you going. You aren't playing, you're just watching all the flashing colors and numbers. You cannot stop even though the challenge is gone. You're literally killing time just to see that next "new thing". That's where the ~70% bulk of the game is. Getting to that tipping point is worth it ten times over. The game is amazing. I threw down for the DLC before I reached the tipping point because it is that good and I wanted to support more. But I dunno if I'll even check the DLC content out at all. I'm ready to break the addiction! I think... Maybe just one more hit...Priced accordingly, I have no problems singing this game's praises far and wide. Plus I know most enjoy achievement hunting more than I do and this game has got that. I just wish the challenge/difficulty progression arc was as stretched as the achievement progression arc. Even just a wee bit longer. It coulda really, really been an all timer. But then again if we had the perfect roguelike/lite/whatever game made, there wouldn't be a reason to play any others. Stay safe, wear garlic.Plays great on the Steam Deck! I mean, you only need a joystick after all.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had my eye on Vampire Survivors for some time now. Always from a distance, though - at first glance, it looked like some unholy combination of one of those idle phone games and a bullet hell shooter. I'm happy to report I was (mostly) mistaken. Vampire Survivors is actually more of a rogue-lite defense game where you are the bullet hell.The gameplay starts off pretty simple: you select one of the characters (each of whom has their own default weapon) and the stage you want to play. The goal is to help the character survive a set amount of time (usually 30 minutes) by moving them around while they automatically attack waves of incoming enemies.Most enemies you kill will drop experience gems. Collecting the gems fills your experience gauge, and at every level up, you get to pick one of the 3-4 random weapons and items. Each weapon has a different attack mode, and most can be combined with specific items to create even more powerful versions.Collecting and upgrading weapons and items like this is the key to a successful run. Your character can wield up to 6 weapons, letting you combine attacks with different ranges and firing modes. This is especially important in the final few minutes of a run, when an endless wave of tough enemies is almost guaranteed to overwhelm an unprepared player.As you play the game, you'll unlock more and more characters, weapons, and items. Beyond that, you can also unlock powerful relics that let you tweak the game experience, permanent upgrades that apply to every run, and tarot cards that add special effects to your character and the stage you're playing in.Each of these adds a layer of complexity and strategy to what at first looks like a game where you simply have to move the character out of harm's way. Once you have some experience and a few unlockables under your belt, the game practically explodes with all the interesting combinations of characters, weapons, items, and add-ons you can play with.At the same time, this is probably the game's biggest flaw. Some combinations of items, such as Unholy Vespers, Gorgeous Moon, Infinite Corridor, or Phieraggi are objectively superior to most other weapons, especially during the later stages of a run. As such, you'll always try to get them if at all possible, which ends up making every run feel the same.All in all, despite the deceptively simplistic look, Vampire Survivors is a ton of fun. It will probably work best for completionists (after all, there are almost 200 Steam achievements to unlock) and players who enjoy the feeling of mowing down entire armies of enemies single-handed. Run around, mow down enemies, and survive. Interesting and addictive gameplay. Can become repetitive after a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access games have put me off ever since I grew tired of Subnautica by the time of its final release thanks to so many hours of playing it before the fully playable storyline was available. On top of that, there are Early Access games which never get finished, leaving players with a game they previously liked as they felt it "had a lot of potential. Many video games simply aren't well-suited to being played in developmental update chunks, and - even if a game is nearly finished - playing the game before the full launch will likely be a less enjoyable experience than one could have had with the final product with all the quality of life and polish one would hope for in said product. As such, I steer clear of Early Access games in general and don't believe I've bought one (outside of stuff in bundles) since Subnautica.Vampire Survivors is the exception to the rule. If an update comes out tomorrow or the next day, or even three months from now, I'm there. If it gets dropped by the developer and left "unfinished," it's not a narrative game and has so much content that it already feels pretty darn finished to me. I got over 58 hours out of it so far and had a blast the vast majority of that time (screw the Bone Zone, though...that level sucked). I've gotten all 127 currently available achievements, still have like 5 or more secret characters to earn when I feel like it, and have zero regrets from my purchase. This game cost me $2.99, and I haven't gotten this good of a deal since I bought a bicycle (a 12-speed or some such, I think?) at a garage sale for $3.00.Ordinarily, I would prattle on at length about a game, and go into the specifics, but the gameplay of Vampire Survivors is quite self-explanatory from just watching a few minutes of someone playing the game online. If you like killing lots of monsters, leveling up a bunch, getting tons of upgrades, and completing little tasks such as "reach level 99 as <character>" or "survive to the 31st minute on <map>" or "upgrade <weapon> to level 7" for fun little rewards which will further strengthen you for further runs, not to mention unlocking new characters for said runs, new maps, etc. If you want to feel something similar to this because you don't want to risk $2.99 on the game, you could always download "Holo Cure" for and play it for a few minutes. It's a free fan-made game with vtuber girls as the playable characters, but it's a decent intro to what Vampire Survivors feels like if you're unsure. I Holo Cure, thought "Huh, that was actually kinda fun," then broke the bank to buy Vampire Survivors for $2.99, and found Vampire Survivors to be far more enjoyable and engaging than the free game I mentioned. I am bitter and hard to please when it comes to a lot of video games, but this particular game has filled me with joy at a low cost. This developer has struck gold with this game. In my opinion, it's pretty darn fantastic for a game without a plot and with no characterization of the people in it. If this had been on the SNES back in the day, virtually every gaming household would've had a copy of Vampire Survivors. It's just that entertaining.

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire survivors is incredibly great, the value for money, art, sound, gameplay and progression. It’s all perfect. I was genuinely shocked after playing my first couple runs, I was very impressed to see the quality and engaging design that the game offers. The gameplay is very simple and traditional, your a small sprite that can walk around on a basic level with enemies coming towards you. It gets very interesting when you start levelling your character. The rogue like features really awesome and all the different items are drastically unique. Building up this kit of weapons and abilities is the selling point. It’s very easy to understand but you will need to put some thought in to progress past the early levels. The general rogue like systems are very traditional and they work great. The out of game progression is great and offers some new characters and levels. It’s simple but serves it’s purpose. The game does currently lack a story/purpose which seems to be coming later in development according to the early access details. The art is also great, it’s very retro but also has a modern twist which makes it generally makes the game more enjoyable and easier understand the game. All attacks are very nicely defined and all of the art has a very consistent colour palette and pixel amount. The art may discourage some people due to the style but It definitely feels modern. The sound is great it’s also just as retro as the art is. I don’t really have a major comments on the sound other than it’s really good and fits the game well. As for performance, to no surprise the game runs extremely well with zero performance issues. I’ve yet to even encounter a single bug. My final thoughts. as of writing the game is £2.09 at 99% positive so I highly recommend you at least try the game, specially if it’s on sale and before it’s price increases. It’s extremely cheap for what it’s offering. The game is missing some nice features like full screen and a good amount of options for all categories but feel these things will most likely make their way into the game eventually. Other than that I’d fully recommend you purchase the game. An outstanding start to early access.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I can remember I've loved garlic bread - it seems like there is nothing in the world as delicious and as simple. If I was given Garlic Bread to eat for every meal for the rest of my life, I would definitely die happy.Over the years, I've seen Garlic Bread being made in all sorts of ways - using butter and oils - cooking the garlic - using a brush the add on addition butter or oil. And I've come to know that these are all great ideas but you don't always get that amazing garlic bread taste you want. I've tried a few combinations, and found that this is definitely the most delicious.Some Facts: The Garlic Bread we know today is more of an American tradition, however it can be said that the Mediterranean people were the creators of the concept. They were known for dipping foods into hot seasoned oils especially oils that contained garlic.Ingredients: Italian Bread (NOT SLICED) Olive Oil Garlic Butter Oregano SaltQuantity: 2-3 Loafs of Italian Bread 10-15 Tablespoons of Olive Oil 10-15 Cloves of Garlic (Depends on taste and quantity of bread ) 3 - 5 Tablespoons of Butter 2-3 Tablespoons of Oregano (to taste) Salt to TasteI do not count calories or serving sizes. I eat because it enjoy it and I cook because I love it. Total Time to prep and cook: 30-45 MinutesDirections:1. Preheat the toaster or oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit. Take one piece of bread and cut it horizontally.2. Take a cooking brush and as evenly as possible - spread the oil inside, onto both sides of the bread for that great taste.3. Dice the garlic - Which should be evenly distributed onto the inside of the bread, again onto both sides of the bread.4. Place the bread in to an aluminium foil sheet.5. Place the bread into the oven for 8-10 Minutes at 350 degrees Fahrenheit. This is just to cook the oil and stick the garlic into place.6. Remove the Bread from the oven and place 1 teaspoon of butter onto the bread - the butter should be spaced out evenly so you get that butter taste with each bite. Then season with oregano.7. Place the Bread back into the aluminium foil and then back into the oven for another 10-15 minutes or until the bread it golden-brown on the outside.8. Once the bread is cooked - remove from oven and open the aluminium foil, let it stand for 2-3 minutes so it can cool down a little. Now cut the bread into even vertical pieces.Enjoy your garlic build :)

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivors is deceptively simple at its surface, holding a decent amount of complexity at its core. It's not exactly expansive, neither is it short of content. For a three-dollar game, it creates a nice middle ground. A game that you can actually sit down and finish. Technically, there are more things I could be doing, like gaining enough wealth to buy all the pre-game powerups. But instead, I sat down, and grinded for ten whole hours in a single day to get all 34 achievements currently in the game. Called it a day from there.I got up in the morning intending on wasting my free day away, and looked back at the clock, only to realize I'd put in almost ten hours. That should be enough to tell you that this game is gold, and in my opinion, has SO much potential. I can only really see this gem going up from here. As the game is currently, if you wanted to get all the achievements, that could be between ten and fifteen hours, maybe slightly less, depending on run RNG. For three bucks, that's certainly a steal.

_childDocuments_.review: Much has been said about Vampire Survivors already. If you're browsing the reviews, you probably already know that it's only $5 and it birthed an entire new genre. You probably have seen that the game is absolutely packed with content and the gameplay loop is as engaging as a brick of heroin. You've probably read how zany it can be and how ridiculous the builds can wind up.What I haven't seen written anywhere is just how consistently surprising this damn thing is. And while it's worth its price for any of the reasons written above, this is the one that made me sit back in my chair and go "Oh, no they didn't." And then they did. Over and over and over.As a roguelike, the game has a strict formula. You go into a level, you get stronger, monsters get stronger, you try to throw together a build, and they try to kill you, until either eventually you're overwhelmed or you ascend to godhood and slaughter all who displease you with nary a blink. It doesn't seem like there's a lot of flex in that pattern. And yet, somehow, there is. There are dozens of obscure events in this game that range from screen-filling bosses to punishing gauntlets because you fell off the map and into MissingNo's house. There are weapons that shouldn't be weapons, from emptying out your house of all the accumulated junk at your foes, to farting them to death, politely. There are characters who play so utterly differently from one another that even though they're doing the exact same thing, somehow, they really aren't. And every one of them feels like it's been cast and molded with love and innovation that bleeds through the screen. Sometimes I got a new unlock and thought it was bad, but I never thought it wasn't creative or interesting, or potentially some crazy new thing I could do a build around if I wanted to.This game screams with energy and creativity and love, and happens to be an excellent game that only costs $5 while doing it. I don't think I can possibly recommend it enough, and even if it does have some definite faults, I still can't think of a single person I wouldn't recommend play it, if only for the experience.Edit: And the expansions are great too. The first feels a little scant on content, basically one new map and the new weapons and characters are... eh? The second felt more fleshed out and had more of the creativity that I love about this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivors initially captivated me with its challenging gameplay, drawing me in with the promise of difficulty and intensity. I stumbled upon it after watching Asmongold struggle through it, and I was hooked by the sheer challenge.For a while, the game lived up to its reputation, providing a satisfyingly tough experience that justified every penny spent. I relished the endgame battles, especially the epic showdowns with Death every 30 minutes, a feat I accomplished with Leda just like Asmongold did in his video.However, revisiting the game left me feeling uninspired. While updates introduced some welcome improvements, such as upgrades for the clock lancet and laurel, they also unbalanced the game dynamics. The once intriguing Arcana mechanic lost its charm with the addition of scaling, tipping the scales too heavily in favor of the player.As I reached god-like levels of power in the endgame, the thrill of replayability vanished, leaving me with a sense of closure rather than anticipation. While my review may lean towards the negative, it's worth noting that I did spend 200 hours in the game, which speaks to its initial appeal. Despite its flaws, Vampire Survivors still holds a special place in my gaming library.

_childDocuments_.review: It's still in early access but, man, what a treat and find this early (pun intended) in the year. Vampire Survivors should run on a toaster so thankfully we can skip the technical details. It's a deceivingly 'simple' 2D autoattacker with a strong horror/monster movie theme drinking straight out of Castlevania and B-films of the era. Not much in the shape of story, it's pure mechanics. You're thrown into an arena and your goal is to survive up to 30 mins against increasingly brutal hordes of non-stop spawning mobs.You get a bunch of weapons at your disposal that you can upgrade as you level up, while randomly picking one each time you level up. That's where a rogue-like element shows up since you can mostly bet on getting the weapons and special effect items you get but it's all in that gacha/dice roll (props to the gacha theme since it's the embodiment of all gacha and you're not forced to pay real currency when you pick one chest!). You do get permanent upgrades that help you start in a stronger position but, still, it's not an easy task to reach the 30 mins mark. And what's your reward for doing so well? A swift death. Spoilers: death itself comes and takes you.There is a huge addicting and cathartic effect in planning a strategy as you desperately move around to position yourself and destroy some of the blatant Castlevania-like candles and flames for precious gold and items. Certainly a bit more entertaining than watching a cookie spin, right? The fact that it's compressed into 30 minutes sessions makes this an ideal pick up and play for those with little time to game. You're not demanded to sit through hours of non interactive cutscenes and dialogue, just pure raw, balls-to-the-wall auto-attacking.So, yeah, with that strong core of combining items and weapons to create your ultimate build, multiple characters to pick up from and the fact that it's still in development and is probably going to add even more content, yeah, surprise of the year and indie GOTY for sure. Gotta love when the stars align like this! Go get it now!

_childDocuments_.review: You know those moments in Roguelikes when you pick up a certain weapon, get a certain combo and/or get an ability where you know "This is it, this run is basically won" and you snowball your way towards Godhood and victory?This game is all about thatWhere in other Roguelikes it can be annoying that you can basically game-end the entire challenge of the run, in this game the entire goal of every run is to get so ridiculously unstoppable that you slaughter a Battalions worth of enemies in a few minutes and turn the entire screen into a living nightmare for your eyes and everything that stands in your way... and you don't even control your own attacks! It makes you feel like a force-of-nature, while only engaging with WASD and occasionally the spacebarTo further illustrate my point, let me paint you a picture: In one of my latest runs, towards the end of it when I had levelled up most of my equipment and evolved all the ones I could, I had basically become a walking giant buzzsaw, with a machine gun that shot out a dozen knives every quarter second, while having everything in a radious around me be flattenend by Orbital Bombardement and ripped to shreds by scythes flying out in all cardinal directions. The screen was completely filled with enemies, from top to bottom, nothing but Gribblies wanting to rip my face off and I was cleaving through them like a hot knife through butterAnd that wasn't even some stand-out Godrun or anything. Once you get a feeling for how to snowball your equipment correctly and survive to the point where you can become a walking Apocalypse, you'll be able to do this semi-regularly and take on even the harder versions of levels with confidence.It's ridiculously addictive, hits all the right spots in your dopamine receptors and is the perfect go-to if you want to sit back and enjoy the carnage

_childDocuments_.review: Aight it's been a while since I've written a review but I'm out of hiatus bc of this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ beautiful $3 gem. For the price of a family-sized bag of chips you get an addictive, challenging and wildly exciting bullet hell shmup where YOU are the bullet hell.Using iconic (a word I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ despise using, but in this case, it is objectively true) Castlevania-themed weaponry, you will fight against endless hordes of ever more powerful enemies and die instantly at 30 minutes. Unless the enemies get you first. They have no projectiles whatsoever. YOU are the bullet hell.With different characters sporting different abilities and a varied arsenal of weapons, you are playing dodgeball on an endless field while the items you gather either grant you an attack or enhance your other items, offering you a vast array of combinations of 6 attack and 6 "support" items. You get these items from leveling (which you do by collecting experience gems the monsters drop) or as rewards from boss monsters. You will also get gold which is used to puirchase other characters or upgrade the base stats of your character (think of it as having passive bonuses on top of your regular items).The first time I played this game I played ~6 hours straight into 100%, with different builds, discovering the different item combinations and all in all just grinding and having a great time with this game. Every update keeps me coming back and I more than look forward to what the future holds for it.All in all a great game, worth more than the price tag tbh. Much love to the dev, who keeps in touch with the community and constantly keeps tabs on updates and new features. An amazing Early Access title as it is. You can thank me (or ♥♥♥♥ on me) down in the comments below.v1.0 only made EVERYTHING BETTER. BUY THIS GAME.

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivors is a pretty good game, and it is also a pharmaceutical formulation of mechanics and audiovisuals already proven by other games to "work". Absolutely nothing about it is original: it's a world you're already familiar with (Castlevania), with rules you're already familiar with (every smash-hit so-called "roguelike", e.g. Risk of Rain, that's been pervading the indie scene), and a dash of lootbox & iPad slot game key-jangling, all laid upon a gameplay foundation that can be fully described in one (or two!) three-word sentences. But does originality and human sensory abuse matter? You be the judge. The fact remains that all of these elements are combined well, and are used to provide an intriguing challenge - sometimes easy, sometimes hard, always requiring a modicum of creativity. There's a modestly respectable distance between how a beginner moves and builds and how an expert moves and builds, but no more than that. Balance is surprisingly "decent", with some outliers. 15 hours in (across two days of ownership), and I still have a small list of challenges left. I've seen just about everything, but I'm still looking forward to doing those challenges. The journey of unlocking everything is compelling. I do not believe that this game is worthy of mastery once you have unlocked everything. But it's a nice journey, so that isn't a complaint.There's a reason that the ratings are so high, and it is that it's possible to dislike this game only through contrarianism, principle, or unmet preconceived expectations. Without those things, you are just left with fun. So, have fun! I also recommend it as an EA game because this could be the final version and I would still be quite satisfied with the purchase. It feels like version .9 when really it's only about halfway done. Cool!One thought I have is that if half of the fun of the gameplay is picking your items, and the entire item picking process is predicated on evolution pairs, are the evolution pairs truly intelligently designed to serve the gameplay? In their current state, they're restrictive and force the player to make cookie-cutter decisions. The way they currently are is acceptable for now, but I imagine that as the game and the playerbase matures, people will get sick of having to always get the armor if they want the runetracer, or tired of feeling like their run is spoiled if they can't get one. Some items are useless without their evo pair, and some items are so good that their evo pair isn't necessary.Item evolution is one of the best features of the game, and its most special, so I hope it is developed with care!

_childDocuments_.review: By popular demand, I now shift my focus towards a dark fantasy casual title I like to call, a veritable auto battler without having any chess elements to it. Vampire Survivors has been quite a sleeper hit, given its accessible price point, its premise and especially its predilection for short, action-packed gaming sessions tickling our heartfelt desires for instant gratification and self-fulfilment. The game has grown on me like a week-old beard and that was rather surprising since I rarely indulge into the casual spectrum of independent gaming on Steam. Nevermind playing anything on a mobile platform since I barely recognize most of those “entertainment apps” as being proper games worthy of my undivided attention. And yet here we are. Developed and published by poncle, Vampire Survivors is a stellar Steam debut with future ports for Android and iOS. There will be no escaping, though I welcome such titles as a much needed break from any other genre one might “default” towards prolonged sessions. Almost making me revise my previously mentioned stance on the majority of casual experiences.“Less is more” is an ancient and eloquent Greek proverb. It certainly applies to Vampire Survivors, since you don’t get much in the form of narrative development. Not even static introduction screens, as the only eye-catching artwork within this title, is its Main Menu.The story will conjure itself as you keep playing, pushing yourself in regards to that titular survival which is entirely dependent on a “rinse and repeat” type of progression. The Dark Souls pathos has transpired well into many other subgenres. One defeat too many, might still lead towards a well deserved victory once the necessary lessons have been applied.Dante’s Inferno. You start out weak and disorientated within a haunted forest. Suddenly you’re surrounded by vicious creatures seeking to devour your very life essence. Only way to stop these bloodsuckers is to stay on the move and place your trust into a curious assortment of spells and wards firing in any and all directions.Survival under such circumstances is aptly metered by a timer which is also acting as future warning of the impending doom. The deadly waves become bigger and faster, the foes are increasingly diversified. It’s only a matter of time until you’re engulfed by them, especially in the first few playthroughs.  The Phaser 3 graphics engine! That’s a rare one for my reviews, was almost certain it’s a variation of Unity until the Credits section settled this query. For all that seemingly endless fun it can provide, this engine still doesn’t properly follow the 16:9 aspect ratio, leaving “hollow edges” where the Steam Overlay messages glitch out. A minor inconvenience, at least the Overlay works as intended and I could capture those chaotic battlefields with my screenshots. The only HUD elements which can be hidden, are the damage numbers and I strongly suggest you leave those on for future reference in subsequent sessions. Performance can hardly put a strain even on first generation smartphones from the looks of it. Don’t expect any technical difficulties. In fact, I was able to push steady 144fps even when there were swarms of monsters by the thousands on-screen. The “Performance Mode” didn’t seem to do anything, I think it’s sort of an in-house joke like the 3D SCUMM rendering option for “The Curse of Monkey Island”. Mimicking the retro feel down to the severely limited selection of sounds. Mute them and blast some heavy metal in the background. “When the Doom music kicks in”, your survival skills will become truly motivated. You’ll thank me later.Simply moving around won't suffice in Vampire Survivors. You need to evolve your offensive capabilities and that involves picking up the experience gems dropped by fallen foes. With sufficient practice, you will learn to navigate those deadly swarms and collect XP at a steady pace, this in turn helping you increase the kill count. Thus, survival might almost become trivial, if not for the boss battles that clearly require more strategic thinking than just maintaining your distance from their attacks and spells. Use the environment to your advantage, though be wary of the enemies that can cross through most obstacles, since they're flying or have an ethereal form. The game does have “vampire” in its title, yet you shall face all manner of creatures from the fantasy genre. Some will prove quite difficult to cull. As predictable as those enemy types might become once you can associate them with the maps and timeframes you reach, a handful of random elements remain in place: your auxilliary spells and the special item drops.Keep an eye out for the chests with upgrade coins (they're highlighted with directional arrows), since these will help you unlock your first set of characters as well as stat buffs which carry over from one playthrough to another. The treasure chests must be your priority.As stable and comprehensive as it is, Vampire Survivors is still an Early Access title and that can only mean further improvements alongside new locations and challenges down its road map. I'll say again just how much I appreciate such indie titles that manage to take a minimal approach and turn it into something truly creative and decently priced at the same time. We live in an ever-shifting period of price hikes and constant inflation, but not all things must be overpriced and overrated. And even if you could play this game for half an hour and try to forget about it, once it caught your attention, you will soon begin to wonder how you sunk so much time into it, so fast. The true magic of certain casual titles going above and beyond the mediocrity of their peers. Looking forward to what Vampire Survivors has in store for us in the near future.+ Steam Trading Cards.+ Steam Achievements.+ Pleasant graphics, retro feel.+ Replay value through unlockables.+ Highly rewarding & addictive gameplay.- Limited and repetitive sound selection.EDIT: Added Steam Trading Cards.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Currently there are two games vying for my allocated gaming time slot: Baldur's Gate 3 and this. This is my first foray into "bullet hell" auto-shooters, so I really didn't know what to expect.Man, what a delight it is!I'm so far around a 1/4 into the game, but I've seen enough to judge. It's like a younger, more funny and sexy cousin of serious aRPGs (like Diablo or Grim Dawn). Yeah, it's arcade pixel style, but guess what: wanna try a new build to completion? Sure, go ahead! It'll take you max 30 minutes, and it won't require endless item farming and grind.The developers are so well adjusted to what the players want, that the answers to any problems I might have come right away. Like - "it's tedious to grab all those far-away items on each map". Wa-bam! Here's a solution. "I've ingested so many eggs I can't move straight". There's a pill for that. Etc. etc.Just pure fun.No qualms - recommended with both hands.

_childDocuments_.review: For $3, this is an absolute no brainer.It's basically a bullet hell but instead of bullets, it's all melee enemies. There is a very frustrating valley until you unlock some rerolls and skips, though. You end up unlocking a lot of good weapons, but a lot of them suck. The game LOVES to put you in a situation where you MUST choose your next weapon, and your three options are a knife, a clock lancet, or a laurel. It's absolutely infuriating if you don't have a reroll, skip, or banish. Because now your 12 minute run just ended to a level up.If I had any advice to a new player, it would be to buy the rerolls, skips, and banishes early. Also if you don't get a good first level up, just go ahead and restart.

And frankly, I love that it's a roguelike with a hard cap of 30 minutes.  For an adult gamer, it's kind of nice to be able to get something satisfying out of that short a period of play time.  I think the Castlevania nods throughout are fun and nostalgic, and the game being $3 for Early Access feels like a steal. _childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivors shines in the fact that there is no typical meta build, and having a wide diversity of characters to pick from to go for the build you want. Some roguelikes end up with build system that feel unrewarding and hard to scale, but Vampire Survivors' builds always ends up satisfying.Like most roguelikes, it can be a bit hard to initially understand the systems used within the game, but learning and understanding them is very rewarding, and is a very satisfying use of half an hour to complete a stage. Heck, even if you don't complete a stage, it's satisfying to know you've done the best you could in the round. Good action, fun systems and a blast to play anywhere you goEdit (for DLCs and Achievements):At this time I've spent 58 hours in the game, a lot of it was hoping to grab more achievements. Despite how it feels that 190 achievements is a massive undertaking, many achievements can be grabbed in one run and only a few are single-run kind of achievements (if you play it right). Hyper-mode has been a huge time-saver and the DLCs have added some fresh flare to the game itself. DLCs (if you haven't got them) add two massive maps that provide a diverse set of new weapons and new mobs. It's decently priced, and I'm sure I would've paid more for what this game has to offer. All in all, recommended game for the chill nights, or something afk in the background for those larger achievements (I'm looking at the mob killing achievements).

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful in its simplicity: You're dropped in the middle of a field (or library, or wherever), and all kinds of monsters swarm in from all sides; slow zombie style. Survive 30 minutes, and you've completed the level.The only controls you have are movement: North, East, West, South. There's no fancy roll-dodging, sprinting, or jumping here. Just you, moving at a walking pace that'll (just barely) outrun most of the things coming after you.You have weapons (a whole lot of them, in fact), but they're all automated. They'll fire off as soon as they're ready according to their natures (for instance, a whip will fire out in front of your character, in the direction they're facing; while an axe will arc up from your character, then drop down); all you need to do is manage your speed walking such that you're in position to take advantage of your weapons to kill off the horde on your heels.Killing monsters drops EXP crystals which you use to level up. However, unless you're killing them at literal point-blank, the crystals will just sit on the ground where they were dropped. The trick is to maneuver around the swarms, picking enemies off as you go, dodging around them so that you can swoop in to grab as many crystals as possible.Leveling up lets you upgrade current weapons or power-ups, or get brand new weapons or power-ups. What you get to choose from is random, so there's no one-build-to-rule-them-all that you can follow without fail - you'll need to assess what options are available, and when it might be better to settle for a weapon or power-up that you might not have wanted, since the other options would be even worse.Once you've upgraded things to max levels, you'll start discovering super weapons - these can be picked up from chests which drop from boss monsters; but only if you have the needed weapons and/or power-ups at max level already. Generally speaking, these are all crazy powerful; and getting several of them going at once can mean the difference between winning a stage and being overwhelmed during the last couple minutes.Once you've finished a stage, either in triumph or defeat, you'll get a summary of your run; then you'll earn achievements and/or gold coins. The achievements can unlock new items/weapons/power-ups/characters; while the gold can be put towards upgrades that persist between rounds.It's simple, it's fun, and it's a blast seeing your character transform from a dude with a whip to the walking embodiment of destruction in 30 minutes. It's also cheap!

_childDocuments_.review: Jones: I have loved you, how very much I have tried my best to give you the good life. In spite of all that I’ve tried, a handful of our people, with their lies, have made our life impossible. There’s no way to detach ourselves from what’s happened today. Not only– We’re in a compound situation, not only are there those who have left and committed the betrayal of the century, some have stolen children from others and then seek right now to kill them because they stole their children, and we are sitting here waiting on a powder keg. I don’t think it is what we want to do with our babies. I don’t think that’s what we had in mind to do with our babies. It was said by the greatest of prophets, from time immemorial, “No man takes my life from me, I lay my life down.”Crowd: Yeah!Jones: So, to sit here and wait for the catastrophe that’s going to happen on that airplane (it’s gonna be a catastrophe) … Almost happened here, almost happened, the congressman was nearly killed here… But you can’t steal people’s children. You can’t take off with people’s children without expecting a violent reaction. And, that’s not so unfamiliar to us, either, even if we were Judeo-Christian, even if we weren’t Communists. The worldly kingdom suffers violence and the violence is triggered by force. If we can’t live in peace then we must die in peace.Crowd: ApplauseJones: We’ve been so betrayed, we have been so terribly betrayed, but we’ve tried, and as Jack Beam often said (and I don’t know where he’s at right this moment, poor Jack), he says if it’s only worked one day, it was worthwhile …Crowd: CheersJones: Of what’s going to happen here in a matter of a few minutes, is that one of the few on that plane is gonna shoot the pilot. I know that. I didn’t plan it, but I know it’s gonna happen. They’re gonna shoot that pilot, and down comes that plane into the jungle and we had better not have any of our children left when it’s over, ’cause they’ll parachute in here on us. I’m telling you just as plain as I know how to tell you, I’ve never lied to you… I never have lied to you. I know that’s what’s gonna happen, that’s what he intends to do and he will do it. He’ll do it. What’s there being so bewildered with many, many pressures on my brain, seeing all these people behave so treasonous, it is just too much for me to put together, but, I now know what he was telling me and it’ll happen. If the plane gets in the air even. So my opinion is that we be kind to children and be kind to seniors and take the potion like they used to take in ancient Greece, and step over quietly because we are not committing suicide. It’s a revolutionary act. We can’t go back. They won’t leave us alone. They’re now going back to tell more lies which means more congressmen. And there’s no way, no way we can survive. Anybody … Anyone that has any dissenting opinion, please speak … Yes … You can have opportunity, but if their children are left we’re gonna have them butchered. We can make a strike but we’ll be striking against people that we don’t want to strike against. And what we’d like to get is the people who caused this stuff and some, there’s some people here are prepared to know how to do that … go in town and get Timothy Stoen, but there’s no plane, there’s no plane, you can’t catch a plane in time. He’s responsible for it. He brought these people to us. He and Deanna Myrtle. But people in San Francisco will not, not be idle over this. And not take our death in vain, you know … Yes, Christine …Christine [Miller]: Is it too late for Russia?Jones: Here’s why it’s too late for Russia. They killed. They started to kill. That’s why it makes it too late for Russia. Otherwise I’d said, “Russia, you bet your life.” But it’s too late. I can’t control these people. They’re out there. They’ve gone with the guns and it’s too late. And once we kill anybody, at least … that’s the way I’ve always … I’ve always put my lot with you. And when one of my people do something, it’s me. … Understand, I don’t have to take the blame for this, but I don’t live that way. They said deliver up Jjara, who tried to get the man back here. Jjara, whose mother’s been lying on him and lying on him and trying to break up this family and they’ve all agreed to kill us by any means necessary. You think I’m going to deliver them Jjara? Not on your life. No.Crowd: No! No!Unidentified Man: Is there any way if I go, that it’ll help?Jones: No, you’re not going. You’re not going.Crowd: No! No!Jones: Not going. I can’t live that way. I cannot live that way. I’ve lived for all and I’ve died for all. …Crowd: ApplauseJones: I’ve been living on a hope for a long time, Christine, and I appreciate– You’ve always been a very good agitator. I like agitation because you have to see two sides of one issue, two sides of the question. What’s those people gonna get done once they get through? They make our life worse than hell, they’ll make the Russians not accept us. When they get through lying … They told so many lies between there and that truck that we are, we are done in as far as any other alternative.Christine: Well, I say let’s make an airlift to Russia, that’s what I say. I don’t think nothing is impossible, if you believe it.Jones: But how we gonna air … How’ re you going to airlift to Russia?Christine: Why, I thought they said if we got in an emergency, they gave you a code to let them know.Jones: No, they didn’t. They gave us the code that they’d let us know of an issue, not us create an issue for them. They said if we … if they saw the country coming down, they’d agreed they’d give us the code, they’d give us a code. You can check on there and see if it’s on the code. Check with Russia to see if they’ll take us in immediately. Otherwise we die. I don’t know what else you say to these people. But to me death is not … death is not a fearful thing, it’s living that’s treacherous…Crowd: ApplauseJones: I have never, never, never, never seen anything like this before in my life. I’ve never seen people take the law … and do … in their own hands, and provoke us and try to purposely agitate and murder of children. There’s no use, Christine, it’s just not worth living like this … not worth living like this.Christine: I think that there were too few who left for twelve hundred people to give them their lives, for those people that left.Jones: Do you know how many left?Christine: Oooh, twenty odd … that’s, that’s small …Jones: … twenty-odd, twenty-odd…Christine: Compared to what’s here.Jones: … twenty-odd. But what’s gonna happen when they don’t leave. I hope that they could leave … but what’s gonna happen when they don’t leave?Christine: You mean the people here?Jones: Yeah, what’s gonna happen to us when they don’t leave? When they get on the plane and the plane goes down?Christine: I don’t think it’ll go down.Jones: You don’t think it’ll go down?Crowd: Yes it will…Jones: I wish I could tell you you were right, but I’m right. There’s one man there, who blames, and rightfully so, Eddie Blakey, for the murder, for the murder of his mother and he’ll sh… he’ll stop that pilot by any means necessary. He’ll do it. That plane will come out of the air. There’s no way you can fly a plane without a pilot.Christine: I wasn’t speaking about that plane. I was speaking about the plane for us to go to Russia.

_childDocuments_.review: This game didn't look like much when I first found out about it, but I like rogue-lites and it was just around two bucks, so I gave it a shot, and wow.The gameplay hook is addicting and good runs are incredibly satisfying. The gameplay seems very simplistic since you can't even manually attack, as all your attacks are cast automatically from whatever weapons and items you pick up during the run. There is a strategy element to building your character, as sub-par builds will not be able to keep up with the spawn rate of the enemies, which will eventually start to fill the entire screen. All you can do is keep dodging and weaving and collect the enemies' XP drops in order to level up and improve your build.It is in Early Access, but in just a little over a month after the EA release, new content and improvements have already been pushed. I really hope the developers keep supporting this game for a long time and keep adding content. It has huge potential. While it is a game that is great the way it is, the current content is quickly exhausted. After about 10 hours of gameplay I have unlocked everything and basically used every major build, which isn't bad at all for the game's price point, but I could also easily play this game for much longer if there was more to unlock or work towards.

_childDocuments_.review: - : This game gets you into a pleasant flow where you are playing almost subconsciously. If you want to play efficiently it is far from the idle game it seems to be. You can always be moving to the next thing that makes your run easier. Once you learn how things work you will be setting goals for yourself before you even start a run. - : Every time you think you have seen it all you discover another layer to the game that keeps you busy. The unlocks list keeps you busy without overwhelming you and there is always a new secret to discover. It’s honestly impressive how much content is in this game. The game also made me laugh about some of its surprises. It really likes to play tricks on you. - : The music and sound design is really good. I only noticed this once I started looking into its competitors. Since it has so much repeating sound it would get annoying really fast, but it doesn’t. - : all the weapons you get in the game are awkward to use at first. The fun comes in optimising how to play with them and seeing synergies with them. I have not seen any weapons yet that I didn’t like. The challenges for the unlocks also reward you for experimenting with all of them at least a couple of times.- : The first few runs I did were not that interesting and I honestly didn't see what people enjoyed about the game. The first time I got a chest that unlocked more than one upgrade and got much further I started seeing the “snowball” appeal that you also get in most roguelites.- : No spoilers but the “final boss” fight was a bit bland. It would have been nice if it had more than one stages.- : At some point you unlock a map if you pause the game which is useful to see pickups on the map that you missed but it quickly becomes cluttered. Would be nice to be able to zoom in.I was sick for a week and needed something simple to get through it and this game was perfect for the occasion. I thought I would get bored of it after a while but it just didn’t happen. I can honestly see now why people had this as their game of the year unironically. It’s deceptively good. You just have to get through the first few runs.

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivors is a Single-Player 2D Action Rogue-Like game where you survive waves of monsters.  Your goal is to survive as long as possible before death comes to you. The game is a major bullet hell with effects and everything flying around later in the game.Starting off you can play only a few Characters, eventually unlocking more with the Coins you earn while playing.  You will start into your first map at level one with only 1 weapon depending on the Character you decided to play.  Waves of enemies will come and try to kill you while sometimes dropping EXP to level you up.  Once you level up you will have a few choices of options of new Weapons or Passive Items you can choose 1 of them.   Every few minutes a boss enemy will spawn which will usually drop a chest or a better EXP Gem.  The chest has a chance to be 1, 3, or 5 items if you’re lucky enough, which is also used to evolve weapons this chest will normally just level up your current weapons.  Evolution is a mechanic you can do when you can combine a Weapon and a Passive item together to make a stronger weapon out of it, without spoiling too much to Evolve the “Whip” you need the Passive Item “Hollow Heart” however you need to get a max level “Whip” first before it can Evolve.  Once you got a max level “Whip” you need to kill one of those Bosses that spawn every few minutes and open the Chest which will Evolve your Weapon into a greater weapon.  I mentioned earlier you need a Weapon + Passive but there are a few cases you can evolve 2 Weapons together.After you finish your first Vampire Survivors run you’ll get coins, you can spend these coins in the “Power Up” section of the Main Menu (or buy a new character) and make you're next run a little bit easier.  There is a bunch of PowerUps you can decide to get that will enhance your gameplay and maybe you’ll end up beating your first run.Currently, as of making this review, there are 22 Characters you can currently play.  Each character has its own ups and sometimes downsides, they start with a different starting weapon with certain stats like decreased cooldown, or increased movement speed.  To unlock characters you either have to find them or unlock them through certain means.  After that when you go to start a game you will see the blacked-out character that you can purchase with coins.  All the characters are fun to play with their own builds you can try out that benefit them.At the time of this review, this game get’s constant and amazing updates the game creator is amazing and I suggest you buy this game and support it! This game has a pretty large player base and it’s a very fun and chill game to play too.  I personally feel like this game is way too good for the price it is at right now and should be increased.  If you like rogue-like, bullet hells this is the game for you! Hoping to see this game grow and improve over the next few years and can’t wait to see what’s to come.

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this review, I have gotten 93 hours out of a $3 purchase. I'm putting it down for now but I'm sure I'll be in the mood to pick it up again sometime after it hits full release. Easy recommendation.The game is fun when you're starting out because there's a lot to learn and unlock, and the game is great at giving you positive feedback and hitting those dopamine buttons. The game remains fun once you've mastered it because you can engage with it very easily and kind of zone out to; most of those 93 hours on this I had most of my attention on a podcast while I let my fingers do the motions of playing the game. This is great stuff, and the simple idea of "always be shooting" like this is brilliant in a way that will probably see a lot of iteration in future games.There are a few things I would like to see; for the moment their absence is acceptable under Early Access. Check the date on this; patches in future updates could easily address these minor complaints.- I want multiple save files. This is a mountain I would like to climb again. I like to race myself in other games that have a satisfying progression curve like this, try to get the most power in the fewest game attempts. I'd like to do that without removing the file where I've grinded out hundreds of eggs and maxed out all upgrades.- A high score list. You can measure on XP earned, enemies killed, money acquired, and so on. By character, stage, with/without eggs, with/without upgrades, etc. I want statistics. I want to chart that exponential growth. Let me make a graph, I love making graphs.- More weapon combinations. I want to combine Garlic and Clover. Magic Wand with Wings. Bible with Armor. More builds. More content. More more.- Update some weak weapons/characters. I won't name these specifically as that's super subjective.- Nerf Pugnala. IMO: Make her start with just one of her guns, make another character that starts with the other. Starting with two weapons is too good.The game's great, and it costs less than a coffee. The only people I would say should stay away are people who have a hard time putting games down; the game employs a lot of tactics to get its hooks into you. I found that enjoyable and engaging, but there are folks out there who might find that pushes on addiction triggers. It has the feel of a slot machine, and I image there are folks who would want to avoid that. If you're okay to engage with that kind of thing, you have no reason not to give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I spent 4,62 € for this game on sale including the DLC, out of pure curiosity to find out what all the hype and fuss is about, and... OH BOY! I have never become so quickly hooked to such a simple, primitive, crude, mindless, stupifying, weird and hilarious little game before! This is perfect for a quick fix of dopamine and to unwind after a stressful day at work. These endless waves of bizzare enemies, the mesmerizing patterns of projectiles spiraling outwards and scooping up the masses of crystals that gravitate towards the character emitting that satisfying crystal sound is all oddly relaxing, hypnotizing and so much fun!I find it interesting that the Developer Luca Galante -- according to Wikipedia -- applied visual effects from his programming experience for casino gambling machines in this game, such as for the elongated treasure chest opening animation. I have never been gambling in my life, but from playing Vampire Survivors I now have some understanding of how psychological reward effects, in particular flashy slot machines, can have on the human brain. But for sure it's better to be addicted to Vampire Survivors than gambling. However, I believe I will move on from this game soon enough, as it lacks depth, immersion and complexity for long term appeal.

_childDocuments_.review: In my Steam library, I have at least 10 great games that I haven't found the time to play yet and I am sure I'd love them - classics like Ori and the Blind Forest, Mark of the Ninja, also AAA titles like MK11 and Doom Eternal. All of those are taking a back seat because of this game.This freaking game. This lovingly crafted 3$ gem. For one, everything is so well balanced that for such a small game, even at 30+ hours of gameplay there's still stuff to do, and runs still feel fun. You wanna unlock all the achievements, you wanna collect all the characters and powerups. The other thing is, it is sprinkled with so many beautiful little touches - the secret characters and stages, the old school game references, the sometimes dumb jokes, the Italian names and puns (for the record I don't know any Italian but still really dig the whole vibe) - it all just feels very homey and nice. Also if you've got it during Early Access (which is still going on as I'm writing this), you get to follow the development of the game and really look forward to the next patch because it's gonna be actual new content.In the end, it is so unpretentious that it just feels like , like it's 2000-something and I just got Abe's Oddysee on a CD or discovered a flash game on Kongregate that I love. I'm not losing hour-long matches to salty 12-year-olds, I'm not farming for resources until 5 AM, and I'm not looking at complex character build charts to follow the latest meta - I'm just playing a video game for myself and enjoying it. And in this moment in video game history, that feels like nothing short of a miracle.
