_childDocuments_.review: Initially when watching videos of Vampire Survivors, I didn't really understand what the appeal was. For me it wasn't a game I enjoyed watching other people play and I think because of this, I wasn't wholly interested. Although I did buy it when it was still in Early Access for a later date, but also simply due to the fact 50% of my friends list was playing it.After being convinced by a friend, I finally gave it a try and I fell in love with it. The game is rather simple in terms of game play, pick a character, pick up items, evolve the items with other items and survive as long as you can.There are many stages, bonus stages and a large abundance of weapons and characters, so much so that there thousands of combinations you can go for. Plus with the Randomazzo cards, it just adds more elements to the game.For me the fun part was just trying to survive the 30 minutes and unlocking new characters. As quite the completionist, getting all the characters and weapons was just so entertaining to accomplish.I felt as if I couldn't stop playing the game until I'd 140/140'd the achievements.I do however have one gripe with the game and it might not be totally valid but I'd like to share anyway.Eventually, in most Vampire Survivors runs, especially when you know what you're doing, you just hit what I would call "Critical Mass" where you are effectively an untouchable god. To unlock certain characters and items you need to survive for 30 minutes for certain things. However once you know how to play the game and how to build, it's possible to reach "Critical Mass" in as short as twelve to fifteen minutes. Which at that point, you're literally just standing there, waiting for the clock to tick down. When you need to do this multiple times, it can feel a bit boring.Apart from that, the game is great. I like to go by the rule of £1 or $1 an hour, depending on your region, I paid about £4 for this and have nearly 40 hours in it. Truly unbelievable amounts of fun and an incredible game that everyone should at least try once, especially at this insane price point.9/10 I look forward to new updates and losing my life to it again soon.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to admit that this one put me off a bit at first. I mean, that cheesy art on the thumbnail coupled with assets that are clearly very “inspired” by  games doesn’t exactly scream “Game of the Year” to me.But that’s exactly what you have here. There’s a reason it was nominated for a bunch of awards when it was released in 2022. I still kind of wonder if that “reason” is some kind of charm spell hidden in the game’s files…I don’t mean that in any derogatory way, of course. I’ve played this game for hours and loved every second of it. (It was the first game I sank any meaningful amount off time into on my Steam Deck, for god’s sake.) It’s just that this is, on its face, a very simple game. Most of the player input, outside of menu navigation, is moving your character. Attacking and spell casting are both done automatically – the player only needs to position the character among the throngs of enemies for optimal obliteration. To me, when the enemies are coming at you in full force, it ends up feeling like I’m navigating a moving maze as I try squeezing through gaps in the enemy front. That is, until you get swallowed by the mob or Death himself comes for you and the level ends.And that’s kind of it. Don’t be fooled, though – the gameplay loop is addictive as ♥♥♥♥. There’s something about watching your leveled-up spells ripping through a hundred skeletons at a time that never gets old. Besides that, trying different characters and loadouts to see what is most effective kept me busy for a long time.If you’re looking for something entertaining to kill some time, you’d be hard pressed to find something better than this one. But, if you’re looking for something to really sink your teeth into, you might want to look elsewhere. Still, at this price, it’s probably worth picking up anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: In Vampire survivors, you take control of one of an increasing number of available characters and try to stay alive for 30 minutes. Between you and that objective stand literally thousands of pixelated monsters who will assail you from every direction. To help you defend against this virtually limitless number of foes, your character starts with one weapon and one booster stat progression (they’re different for each character). When defeated, most enemies will drop experience gems that you have to collect in order to level up. Upon gaining a level, you’re faced with a choice of 3 to 4 options including getting a new item (weapon or stat-boosting trinket) or leveling up an existing one.What sets Vampire Survivor apart from other action roguelikes is that you don’t have control over your weapons. They activate themselves at set intervals that depend on the type of weapon (some basic ones can fire several times a second, while more devastating ones can take much longer to recharge), their levels and other stats. With this defining feature, Vampire Survivors feels like a one-character auto-battler where you still have direct control of their movement. The actual battles may be tense but there’s little skill involved. The meaty decisions occur when you level up and this happens thankfully frequently enough (typically twice a minute).With its pixel graphics and gothic theme, Vampire Survivors looks like a Castlevania spin-off. Even the music would not be out of place in one of the Belmont family’s adventures. The whole presentation is not particularly sophisticated but holds itself together well.While innovative and fun for the most part, some aspects of the game design are annoying. For once, it’s not self-evident how to progress to the next levels. You must dig into the menu showing the unlockables to get it. Later objectives for bonus levels are similarly obscure. Another slight problem is that even though, on average, you level up often enough, there are still occasional stretches of time when all you have to do is move around and let your auto-firing weapons work for you, which is not terribly engaging and can even feel sedate.Still, with more than 100 unlockable items, levels, characters, and synergies between items that makes them evolve into new ones, the content proposition is generous enough to forgive those flaws, especially at that kind of price.

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivors is a 2D action game focusing on your choice of character surviving on levels with non-stop, escalating swarms of enemies. You must utilize your weapons to defeat enemies, level up, and acquire more weapons to defeat increasingly stronger and vaster amounts of enemies. Occasional power ups, mini-bosses, and varied wave patterns all pose challenges and opportunities.If I am honest this game is literally a diamond: compressed, self-contained, and immaculately cut to perfect form. Many of its mechanics and ideas are simple, yet complex, interweaving together into something understandable and captivating to play through. When you think it's done, it adds on just a little more, adding variety and nuance in an encouraging growth of player opportunity.Vampire Survivors definitely has 'retro' graphical appeal, being evocative of 80s and 90s gaming eras, minus some technical differences like scanlines. Its music is quaint and metronomic, fitting of the action without being problematic to the ears at all. The controls are quite literally the level of pong: all you do is move around, bobbing and weaving between automatic attack cycles. I found that strange at first, but it's actually very easy on the wrists and super comfortable to play with. I recommend using a gamepad/controller, as analog stick is supremely easier to work over 4-button keyboards.The gameplay systems are worth of academic study as a showcase of tapping into the core essence of ideas. It wastes no time nor energy on unnecessary complexity, instead letting simple parts create an engaging system. The game teaches you what it does, then adds on more piece by piece, making the experience of playing and progressing viscerally rewarding. This reads like an obvious "yeah, every game does that", but I wish to emphasize not all of them do it well. Vampire Survivors, to anyone familiar with its genre, does so exceptionally well.For 3$ this game executes its ideas better than most main studio brands I've encountered, and that's saying something. It could easily charge 10-15$, or more, depending on how far the developer wishes to push forward. So, even as an early access title, it's worthy of being looked at and tried out. You will definitely know if you like what it does in the first 2 hours, so refunding is a reasonable prospect.If you don't fall into the fugue state of just 'one more match' and wake up 8 hours later like me, of course.

_childDocuments_.review: I scooped Vampire Survivors in early access at a price point of $2.99, and since then I've always said it was a steal for the quality of and amount of content in this game, not to mention the consistent content updates and even a new DLC (which is phenomenal so far by the way)!!! Even since the price change and 1.0 release, I stand by that sentiment. I'd easily pay $10 for the base game, it's an incredible value.There's a seemingly endless list of characters, weapons, items, and stages to discover - with well over 60 hours clocked, I have yet to unlock them all.  It's full of fun little secrets and nods to its design influences (Castlevania and Final Fantasy shine through a LOT) that make it a joy to experience and pick apart for those details. There are so many evolution combinations of weapons & items that you're bound to find a build that fits your gameplay style. You wanna run around like a madman and mow down anything that might stand in your way? Done deal! Want to stand in one place and let the silly little enemies fumble their way to you (and to their deaths)? We got that too. The feedback loops of this game are the kind that're easy to sink several hours into without batting an eye. The pacing is great (and adjustable), with constant 15-30 minute progression loops will make you glance at the clock and wonder how it became 3AM, it was only 10:30 just a couple runs ago... Oh, and the soundtrack? Bangers ONLY. Not a single skip. I listen to it at work a lot, actually. (And it's another place where the Castlevania influences come through).This is definitely one of my favorite hidden indie gems that I've found on Steam in recent years. The developers clearly pour a ton of love into it - it shows in every update. I've recommended this to so many friends that I feel like a broken record, but Vampire Survivors really deserves it.

_childDocuments_.review: Full review (and video) available here:Vampire Survivors is perfect for anyone who wants to experience a 30-minute joy ride, going from slapping evil bats with a leather whip to wiping out legions of demons with single devastating strikes from God’s Own Bastard Sword and the Devil’s Sex Whip – all in less time than the least ambitious pizza delivery places.Sounds like a trip, right? And it doesn’t end there. On booting the game you’re shown a glorious retro splash page of a grimacing vampire, stoic tough guy, and improbably contorted woman. It makes me yearn for simpler times – sitting in my parent’s basement as a kid, no school tomorrow, eating a family-sized bag of Doritos with one hand and unpausing the family NES with the other, playing until the sun appears over the neighbour’s house in my idyllic American suburb. And I’ve never owned a NES. Nor a basement. And I didn’t set foot in America until my late 20s. Such is the raw power of that image.After navigating through the minimalist menus, selecting your stalwart corpse-to-be, and booting into the game, you’ll be transported even more into the past by the incredibly underwhelming start of the game.Oh, my dude just did a little whip thing. Did I press something? No, he just did it himself. Can I move him? Yeah, okay. Is that a bat? I guess I’ll move next to the bat so when my guy decides to do another little whippy it’ll kill it. That worked. Oooh, a shiny gem. Guess I’ll do it again?… Is this it?Vampire Survivors cares not at all for your modern contrivances, like attacking when you please. Or a tutorial. Or the controls. Or what to do. It’s called Vampire Survivors, you just survive the vampires you bloody idiot.You’ll work it out. Or die. Vampire Survivors doesn’t care which. I mean, you’ll be dying anyway, because this game does not coddle you for long. You’ll start out committing crimes against wildlife with a knock-off Indiana Jones prop, but those shiny gems dropping from the battered bats (which you’ll be compulsively collecting like the sticky-fingered goblin you are) are actually experience. And the gems start piling up.Every level, you’ll be given a choice of making your crappy starting weapon a little less crappy, or taking a whole new crappy weapon. Which you’ll use at the same time as your current weapon somehow. Don’t question it, it’s the magic of 80’s nostalgia (and possibly Medieval inbreeding). In 5 levels time you could have 5 more weapons if you’re not a wimp who chose support items, each whipping, stabbing, hurling, casting, and… bibling… all at the same time. That’s six slots for weapons, and six for not-weapons (if you’ve already picked and upgraded all the weapons or if your mother raised a coward).

_childDocuments_.review: It's cheap and addictive. Vampire Survivors is everything one might want to see in a quick, 30 minutes per session, roguelite (roguelike? Even if you can't survive the 30 minutes necessary, it uses upgrading and unlocking mechanics that last after your run. Unlocking weapons is a necessity if you wish to survive.100% achievements require levelling up character to levels 99-100 in a run, surviving under certain conditions, creating evolved weapons and finishing the levels already present (plus fighting some end level bosses). Completing all achievement is not necessary, but if you wish to unlock characters and items then you will get then naturally. With each update comes a couple of new achievements, so I will be coming back to it for a couple of days whenever they roll out.While still in early access, patches come out very frequently, so much so that I worry a little that the developer may be overworking themselves a bit. _childDocuments_.review: "98% of the ~75,000 user reviews for this game are Positive"The game is 3 dollars.Vampire Survivor can be described simply as 'A rogue-lite reverse bullet hell transparently homaging Castlevania.' The gameplay is relatively simple; survive for thirty minutes against near-infinite waves of monsters, collecting and upgrading weapons and passive modifiers to deal more damage and prevent anything from touching you.  This can be difficult at first, but the rogue-lite element of keeping the currency you gain through victory or death and applying it to unlockable characters or permanent passive upgrades will push you down the road to success and extreme replayability.Vampire Survivors is currently in Early Access which may turn some people off, but it's both 3 dollars base price and the developers are pouring constant attention into this game.  Since I purchased it (around a month and a half ago) there have been at least five major updates that add weapons, characters, maps, or other unlocks and the relevant achievements. This has culminated in at least 24 hours (at the time of writing) of gameplay even while attempting to optimize achievement unlocking.  Based on the documents they've shown and the space for additional content in-game, they aren't done, either.  It's a fantastic deal for the amount of time you can put into this.The game is also quite easy to get into, as all weapons are auto-fire the only thing the player needs to 'participate' in is moving the character around to not get hit or to collect items and experience, and selecting the level-up rewards.  There is some strategy in this, as all weapons have unique qualities and pair better with others, but it is not complicated to understand.  Certain weapons will become even strong with specific passive items, so the characters practically build themselves. It may look daunting when there are a hundred enemies on the screen and hundreds of numbers popping up, but it all boils down to a big game of tag.Speaking of simplicity, this game is great if you frequently stream for an audience.  Again, there is very little serious focus required for this game, so as long as you can move around a character it's an almost hypnotic experience watching, and you can easily burn half an hour each 'game' while you hang out with your chat and make better use of your audio.One last thing, it has been way too long since the gaming community received an official Castlevania game (I'm not counting Bloodstained) and the variety of sprites and art assets here absolutely scratch that itch.  Practically everything is a slight sprite edit away from a pre-existing weapon, monster, or character from the beloved series, and that is in no way a negative mark. On the contrary, Castlevania fans will probably find this more endearing, as they progressively unlock and discover additional references to the series. The color and design of everything in this game is top notch, completely fitting within the 'SNES era' confines the indie devs have set for themselves.I would definitely recommend this game to anyone that enjoys roguelites, castlevania, games they can 'turn their brain off' while playing, or achievement hunters. I look forward to the next patch!

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivors isn't your typical grandma--dodging-cars simulator. This game lets you unleash your inner monster hunter... in a surprisingly relaxing (or maybe terrifying?) way.  See, it depends on your perspective.  Some folks find the constant waves of enemies super chill, while others get a serious adrenaline rush as the screen fills with pixelated fiends.Whatever your poison, Vampire Survivors delivers. You've got a ton of weapon and gear combos to choose from, turning your character into a garlic-powered, holy-water-spraying monster-slaying machine (or something equally ridiculous). There are even new characters to unlock, each with their own unique playstyle.For the price, it's a steal. Seriously, you won't regret sinking your teeth into this one (vampire pun intended). Plus, there are achievements galore to keep you busy – perfect for those completionist gamers out there.Now, the only downside? The graphics are pure pixelated goodness. Some folks might miss the fancy 3D bells and whistles, but hey, the charm of this game is all in its simplicity. It's all about the fun, fast-paced action, and watching your character become an unstoppable force of monster-slaying fury.So, if you're looking for a unique, relaxing-yet-intense game with tons of replay value, Vampire Survivors is a must-try. Just be prepared for the possibility of waking up the next morning covered in garlic and holy water.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't feel like reading the whole thing? Down at the bottom is the conclusion and score given to the game! :)Vampire Survivors is the most addictive game of 2022, and it delivers a sense of accomplishment that can get you hooked. The progression system is a bomb that offers infinite possibilities. The gameplay combines the rogue-like aspects with those of an intense session of a bullet hell game. The game is fun due to the choices one makes while playing the game, the options being so vast that a round of the title will always be different from the next match. What upgrades you choose for your character determine if you become another coffin or can last until those precious 30 minutes. As time progresses, enemies come in more significant numbers, forms, and more powerful. Even death itself comes for you!The game has tricks for you to discover with the combination of upgrades and secrets you can uncover to your benefit. Once you get the hang of the game, you can keep playing for hours and hours as you become mighty enough to dispatch entire hordes efficiently! There is a lot of joy in optimizing your build as best as you can while enjoying the bloodbath that is destroying your enemies!The game features a lot of unlockables, to the point that you can play for a long time and not even unlock half of the things it offers. Characters exhibit meaningful differences and charisma that make them uniquely distinctive, and players discover their favorites as they play! There are a lot of power-ups and upgrades to learn that are incredibly fun to use and combine!The bad point of the gameplay is that for new players, it might need to be more apparent how progression and balancing skills work. At the same time, it can be irritating for those who want to have a more diverse experience. It is incredible to be so powerful that you can let your character sit idle and survive, thanks to your intelligent choice-making. Still, some folks won't like such a design.The sound in Vampire Survivors is as addictive as it's its gameplay! The gems you pick up make a sound effect that makes your brain feel good, and the numbers that pop up signify the colossal damage you are dishing out! The weapons and skills effects are also exciting as you see your abilities play out with good detail in the sound department.The music is retro-like, and the characters have their theme music, making choosing and playing them all the more gratifying! The excellent soundtrack gives the title a lot of atmosphere and immersion in the insane gameplay!Vampire Survivors is a game that has that retro look reminiscing games such as Castlevania. It has a lot of charm put into its presentation and a flair that gives each location a tone of its own. From decrepit forests to mysterious buildings, these places have a sense of dread and adventure. The spectacle of visuals is also a feast as electric bolts, axes, and attacks are displayed on the screen gloriously!The game was tested with an RTX 2060, 36 GB of ram, Intel Core i7-11700K - Core i7 11th Gen Rocket Lake 8-Core 3.6 GHz LGA 1200.This game will run efficiently on most hardware, so there is no need to worry about not having adequate specs. No crashes or bugs of any kind; it is a well-polished game!Vampire Survivors was the talk of 2022, and for a good reason: It shows that indie games can be as impressive if not more than big productions games if they are full of passion and originality! Asking for a mere five bucks becomes a must-have for any gamer wanting to enter into an addictive adventure! Survive, if you can!10/10  MASTERPIECEIf you enjoy and find the review helpful, please follow my curator StarsDeck!

_childDocuments_.review: It is three dollars.It's a pretty addictive little game for a whopping $3. The gameplay is extremely simple in that you only control the movement of your character and the weapons activate at set times which means I can hold my kid in one arm, and play this game with the other. There is some strategy however, as how you approach a mob without getting overwhelmed is important as well as what semi-random weapon combinations you choose.There are two upgrade paths that keep the game interesting. One is only for the items you get while playing, and the other is for purchases you can make to increase stats of your characters that carries over from game to game. The random element to the items you get while playing makes it so you have to figure out how to optimize each run depending on what you get. About the only thing I'd like to see in this game is some sort of dynamic music elements attached to each upgrade/weapon ala how Tetris Effect or Rez work as you get through a level, but that might add too much complexity and a soundtrack might require an increase in price.Is the game groundbreaking with an amazingly complex narrative? How can something so cheap (it costs 2,39€), something still in early access, something not yet fully content complete be this fun and addicting?!".At least that's what I kept telling myself as I kept playing. 46 hours later I am still having a blast with it. The developer keeps adding a ton of things with every new update, obviously as the game is still in early access, and even when they say "oh, sorry but this is a light update" you end up with new areas, new secret bosses, new evolutions, new characters and you feel like the dev is punking you.I am truly amazed by this game, as it is a simple yet well thought out experience at its core that doesn't get bogged down by grinding (you can grind tho if you like).I also appreciate the humor and references in it, which cover a lot of areas, not just other games, but also things like old anime shows or some real people (really easy to get if you're Italian).So yeah, I definitely recommend this to anyone who wants to have some fun leveling up while dodging enemies on the road to become a death machine vomiting projectiles and lasers and axes and crosses and daggers and whatever else to survive the onslaught coming your way.

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivors is a top-down bullet hell, except your character is the one causing the bullet hell.It's an incredibly accessible and addictive game where destroying an army of skeletons, ghosts, ghouls, bats, mummies, and hot werewolf boyfriends allows your character to level up, earn currency, and use that currency to permanently buff your character after a run is over.Leveling up allows the player to unlock new abilities, and buff existing ones. Finding treasure chests plays a slot machine animation to unlock yet more abilities and currency. It's this stress-less, dopamine-like rush that I acknowledge to be enjoyable, but I struggle to grasp a sense of challenge.It's interesting that the abilities in this game are entirely passive; i.e. lighting bolts strike at predetermined times, knives are thrown depending on where your character is facing, and eating garlic grants an AoE that constantly kills everything in close proximity. None of these abilities are active. The player simply navigates around the enemies, charge through when the time is right, and make decisions on what abilities they wish to equip.Overall, I enjoyed the time I spent playing Vampire Survivors, but I can't see myself being invested into it.However, for those who just want to relax and experience a well earned risk and reward game, I do recommend it :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is dangerously addictive. Sunk 3 hours into it the moment I bought it and it felt like an hour at most. Be prepared to keep starting new runs with no regard to how much time has passed.On a more serious note, this game is incredibly fun for those who enjoy building up a character through various weapons and abilities. You'll unlock new things as you go, and be able to upgrade them each run. There are permanent upgrades that can be unlocked as well. No two runs ever pan out the same way, with some ending near the start, and some taking much longer (in a good way).The scaling of enemy difficulty in each run feels incredibly fair, more so than almost any other game I've played. You'll know when you made the wrong decision for item grabs/upgrades when this scaling happens, allowing you to learn from your mistakes and find solid upgrade paths that extend your runs.I've been on the hunt for games like this, where you enter a play area and have to deal with enemies, and then earn upgrades and gear that you can improve over time. I might get some backlash for this, but I equate this game to a more involved "idle game" where you actually have to take control of the character, but the upgrade paths mirror that style of play a lot. This is exactly what I've been looking for, as I've been playing multiple idle games recently but nothing has scratched the itch of being able to take more control of the game and feel more fulfilled in progressing into higher levels.All in all, I highly recommend this game. For the price, you won't find much else that feels as worthwhile to play in this genre (at least as far as I know). Fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: [INTRODUCTION]Vampire Survivors was a huge surprise. I learned about the game this spring. The huge wave of popularity meant that it was pretty much inevitable to miss it when you're into gaming. I read articles about VS in various online gaming mags, watched few runs on YouTube, and the whole time i thought to myself:"People are actually paying for that?" Because, on the surface, VS looked like some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ low-effort mobile game.I knew that this genre might be fun, because i absolutely LOVED Crimsonland, but Crimsonland didn't have autofire, and despite being simple topdown shooter, Crimsonland had relatively smart enemies who tried to flank you or get in your six, not to mention freakin' motherload of extremely satisfying weapons and perks.I didn't understand how could someone find a game that looks like dumbed down Crimsonland enjoyable. A game with just few levels, few weapons that you're not even truly firing because they're all automatic, mobs that beeline towards your position without any hint of intelligence or tactics, i didn't get the Castlevania-ish estetics, i just didn't get any of it.Until i was slightly bored one day and found yet another article dedicated to VS spewing superlatives and praise.So i bought VS on Steam, absolutely convinced that i'm going to try few runs and refund.Then i actually tried to play it and got immediately hooked.[HOW DOES IT WORK]Vampire Survivors is essentially a mix of several genres. It's a sort of roguelike/topdown shmup/reverse bullet hell/rage game. You start with a character looking like a secret bastard exiled from the Belmont clan with a simple whip weapon (to this day i'm a bit surprised that Nintendo didn't sue yet). Then you're thrown into a level and... you try to survive. That's pretty much it. All the weapons are automatic, so the only thing you're doing is moving around or aiming.The game throws mobs of increasigly tough enemies at you. When they're killed, they sometimes drop experience gems.Minibosses and bosses can additionally drop chests. There are two categories of items. Weapons and powerups. During each level-up, you get a selection of random items. Either you can level-up existing weapon, get a new one, or get a powerup. You can have 6 weapons and 6 basic powerups. Weapon amount is capped at 6. You can actually get more than 6 powerups, but only as stage items (when your powerup slots are full, the level-up screen doesn't give you more powerups, but you can still pick them up if they're on the ground in the various stages). What's great about VS are the synergies between weapons and powerups. Each weapon is tied to a certain powerup item and when you fully level-up a weapon and pickup a chest dropped by a miniboss or boss enemy, you can "evolve" the weapon into its much more powerful version. At first, your arsenal is quite limited, but as you get further and further, more and more stuff gets unlocked. More stages, more weapons, more powerups, more synergies.And it's all extremely satisfying. At first, you're getting your ass handed to you. But if you keep at it, you're going to get better and eventually start understanding the various synergies, unlock more characters, try various builds - it's all extremely addictive. Vampire Survivors is a game that has a direct line into the reward centers of the brain. Imagine you're playin an oldschool RPG. You're thrown into huge openworld, running around, barely surviving on killing low-level enemies and selling the loot, VERY SLOWLY getting better and better. And after 20 hours, you finally save up enough cash to get better gear, skillpoints to get better abilities and THEN you go kill the first boss. You run around in the entry level area, one-hit-killing everything that up to that point posed no small challenge. It's satisfying feeling. Now imagine a game that's entirely based around giving you that exact satisfying feeling without the hours and hours of grind. That's Vampire Survivors. It's fast, and extremely rewarding. You get killed quickly (at least when you're newb), but you also level-up and get better quickly.VS is designed for short runs. Each stage is supposed to take 30minutes at maximum, after which a grim reaper spawns and kills you. When you level up sufficiently, you can kill even the grim reaper, but then the DEATH comes personally and kills you anyway. There are more characters to find, weapons to unlock, synergies to try, secrets to find, and you're having fun the whole time doing it.And the best thing is, Vampire Survivors is Early Access title, which means that there's still more stuff to come.[OUTRO]I would never expect spending 10hrs in a game like Vampire Survivors, much less a hundred. I have no idea how many runs did i do, because sometimes i just didn't quit the game after a run, i just alt-tabbed out and did something else, but there had to be quite a lot of them. I learned to do short VS runs anytime i had a bit of free time, but mostly before i went to sleep or when i was travelling somewhere (remote play). [VERDICT]I highly recommend VS to anyone who likes dopamine, to anyone who likes to get better at stuff quickly, to anyone who loves RPG "get better" mechanics but don't have time for playing RPGs. Vampire Survivors is a lot of fun, and it's a much deeper game than it looks on the surface. There's a lot going on under the hood, and the various interconnected gameplay mechanics are put together in such a smart and satisfying way, that it's hard not to get hooked.Vampire Survivors is a fantastic little gem of a game with price that doesn't reflect its quality AT ALL. For the amount of fun it delivers, it's dirt cheap.

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Survivors initially feels like a nice bite-sized adventure, something you can dip into every now and then for the pleasure of orchestrating a little mayhem as the heart of bullet hell rather than its recipient. The first few rounds, which usually last about ten minutes, may seem like little more than a fun waste of time, and then the path to the prize opens. A little extra power, a new level, new characters, and a satisfying sense of growth that leads to real chaos on the battlefield lead deeper into the game, with each new discovery building on the previous one in a way that's almost impossible to resist calling to start another run. Even when you're playing for fun rather than chasing a goal, there are so many characters and upgrade options that each game is different from the last, maintaining a constant balance between working on your favorite build, finding something new, and getting the best out of an item to level up when they're not what you hoped for. Vampire Survivors is a long slow game that never stops getting worse, maybe not the first in the genre it started, but certainly the best.

_childDocuments_.review: I am usually not into drugs. Especially hard drugs, but I don't know if I've ever experienced a drug that I've wanted to use all the time like this game. Vampire Survivors has found the perfect formula to make my brain excrete all the good chemicals. Dopamine, oxytocin, serotonin, endorphins, norepinephrine - you know, the good stuff. There's something about rogue-likes that just tickle my brain like that. I never thought I'd see the day where a game would take me to The Binding of Isaac highs. But well, here we are reviewing a game that in effect, does thisVampire Survivors is a game that's incredibly easy to pick up and play. It's very intuitive and simple to control. Each round can last anywhere from 5 (or less if you suck) to 30 (or more if you know how to beat a secret boss that halts your progress) minutes. It's great for people that are adults and have SOME self control. If you don't have self control it's very easy for falling into into your, "Eh, I'll just play one more round" instinct. The game is made up of such a simple but effective formula: see mob, kill mob, upgrade weapon, repeat - and that's it! there isn't even an action button. The only action you'll be doing is moving. This simple formula, coupled with a very tightly knit weapon upgrade system and a cast of Italian-named characters make this game such a joy to play.Story wise there's definitely not much going on. However, I love that you can start snapping a whip to a couple of bats (I see you Castlevania reference) to having an aura of deadly garlic and encircling bibles utterly destroy hundreds god (and devil)-like creatures every second. Definitely worth it to check out.In any case, my rating is:4.5 billions of bats out of 5 🦇🦇🦇🦇

_childDocuments_.review: If a game could make you c*m, this would do it.I started playing the game in my phone out of curiosity and dang I was hooked up. I only stopped because it was destroying my neck and eyes to play on a small screen so I had to get it here.Despite being super simple when it comes to gameplay (You just walked around, auto-shoots, and choose upgrades), it's super gratifying and fun and the amount of content and unlocks will keep you entertained for a long time.It's funny because it feels like it has like all the marks of a game that could have been incredibly predatory and full of microtransactions but they made all these addictive features, design and choices and then just made it a super cheap game with no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. It's perfect.It's the best game to get a dopamine injection right into your brain, either for a quick session or for a couple of hours because the game is also one of those that make you go "Just one more round". _childDocuments_.review: This game is way more fun than it has any right to be. It honestly should come with a warning for people with addiction issues. The gameplay elements are familiar, but made fresh; a combination of rogue-lite, TD, and bullet hell, with auto-firing weapons. There is a steady flow of unlocking upgrades and characters which keeps the gameplay fresh, while creating goals that motivate to play just one more round. It took 40 hours to get 100% completion, but more updates will add more content. The updates are regular and the devs are upfront about how the game will continue to progress. For $3, this is an absolute steal.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Survivors

_childDocuments_.review: For the price this game is being sold at, it is incredibly worthwhile. I've gotten, to date, 40 hours of play out of a one dollar simple auto-shooting horde game. _childDocuments_.name: Vampire Survivors

_childDocuments_.review: Before playing the game I'd never played a vampire survivors-like game, but I've fallen in love with this concept. Seems like there's a lot to sink your teeth into for completionists as well, excited to see how this game grows in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: At the 80 hour mark I've finally reached 100% achievements. The end is within my grasp...or so I think. Between arcanae, upgrades, and secret characters there's still far too much to explore and discover. I can't put the game down just yet!For such a simple concept, the amount of content is staggering. Every time I'd shut VS down after a run I'd think, no, I got to do one more. It's addicting like that, watching numbers go up and enemies die with all the chaos happening on-screen. With active updates aiming to add more to the game there's something extra to look forward to after you've messed with everything you could. Plenty of ways to break the game, especially at the endgame level. Cool concepts, or even the added challenge of finding different ways to take down Death. A panda that throws bombs around.I dunno, man, I played so much of this I started hearing gem collecting in my dreams. It haunts me. The music is great, and the sprites reminiscent of ye old Castlevania titles in the best way. There's not really any vampires, though, but there's just about everything else to fight. A giant ball of BONES.Queen Sigma is our sigma overlord.

_childDocuments_.review: Wildly addicting, with an insane amount of content for $4. So popular it created an entirely new genre of game clones. The developer also hired a team to start using the original funding to move towards a real game engine & hopefully will lead to a vampire survivors 2 or other genre-breaking game with equally crazy mechanics. Game eventually becomes a very relaxing experience after understanding all the mechanics, items, and how they work together. My advice on how to consume this game is to look the the list of challenges & slowly work through them. They help you understand how all the characters & weapons function, and slowly unveil more of the game to you over time so you're not initially overwhelmed. By the time you've completed every challenge you'll have infinite power at your fingertips, where even if you reset the game you should be able to complete runs fairly easy.Original Review--------tl;dr: arpg roguelite in a parody universe of castlevania. Better than Diablo Immortals.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has come a long way since its Early Access days on Steam, with a constant stream of free updates adding depth and content that's simply astonishing. And the best part? It's ridiculously affordable!The gameplay is deceptively simple at first—just move around and attack, easy peasy. But don't be fooled; this game will keep you on your toes as monsters swarm in from all directions. The Castlevania vibes are strong here, with a whip in hand and classic gaming horror creatures to face. Survive for 30 minutes, and you can count that as a victory.But where Vampire Survivors truly shines is in its progression system and weapon variety. Each attempt starts you off with a basic weapon, but don't fret—soon, you'll find yourself wielding a firehose of knives or summoning a colony of bats with garlic's power. The combinations are endless, and you'll be constantly making decisions on which items to use and how to modify your attacks. The satisfaction of creating an unstoppable barrage of firepower is unparalleled.The developer, Poncle, has nailed the balance of unlocks, ensuring you're never overwhelmed but always excited to try something new. The objectives provide direction and encourage experimentation. And when you accomplish them, the feeling of achievement is like a flood of dopamine.The game keeps subverting your expectations, turning everything you thought you knew upside down. It's a wild ride that you won't want to get off. The Xbox version has had some bugs, but they're getting patched, and I'm sure it'll be smooth sailing soon.I have to say, Vampire Survivors has quickly become one of my all-time favorites!

_childDocuments_.review: One day i saw this game for 2.39€ and decided to try it out. This is one of the games which give you the best bang for the buck! After playing for 44 hours and fully completed the game including all achievements and I can say that its an amazing game and really addictive however simple the concept is!It's a roguelike game where you start initially with some weapons and try to survive for as long as you can. However, with time, you get stronger with more powerups, the knowledge of builds and just experience (I guess) and can last longer and longer without dying. Maybe even beating the death itself! The game gets super satisfying with trying out new weapon and item builds and the arcanas. It's been an amazing and really fun game to play and it is really really underpriced. It provides way more fun and entertainment that the price. I'd say that it's a must buy game even without sale because it's legit awesome and totally worth it!Also, the achievements are somewhat tied to the progression so if you try to do a 100% achievement run, you'll actually 100% the game itself! Good luck surviving there fellow fighter! :))

_childDocuments_.review: Very simple premise: move around, avoid enemies, weapons attack automatically. Pick up xp gems to level up to get new weapons or improve the ones you have.On the surface it seems so simple it seems almost braindead and at first it kind of is. But as you understand the game better, and gain an understanding of how weapons and evolutions work, you're going to see the game really open up and allow for some interesting (and in some cases very powerful) builds.Lots of stuff to unlock, without making any of it too much a grind. And unlocking stuff feels like it matters.All in all, for the enjoyment I've gotten from this game so far it'd be a steal at twice the price and a bargain at double that.

Same few levels, and with little variation between characters.Hoping for some more content as the development progress. But all in all, very fun game.

name: Sonic Origins
detailed_description: Feature List About the Game The Blue Blur is back with an expanded multi-game collection of classic Sonic the Hedgehog games - Sonic Origins Plus! Sonic Origins Plus features the four beloved classic titles in Sonic Origins – Sonic the Hedgehog, Sonic 2, Sonic 3 & Knuckles, and Sonic CD with remastered visuals, bonus characters, added modes, challenges, behind-the-scenes content and more while adding significant improvements. This bundle also includes 12 Sonic Game Gear titles, previously released add-on content, playable Knuckles in Sonic CD, and for the first time ever, Amy Rose as a playable character in Sonic the Hedgehog 1, 2, Sonic 3 & Knuckles, and Sonic CD! With more content than ever before, this is the definitive way to experience these classic games! Classic Redefined Explore 4 classic remastered Sonic titles – Sonic the Hedgehog, Sonic 2, Sonic 3 & Knuckles, and Sonic CD in high-definition, with all-new opening and ending animations for each title! Classic and Anniversary Modes Spin Dash your way through numerous zones in Classic mode with the game’s original resolution and limited lives, or the new Anniversary Mode with unlimited lives in revamped widescreen HD. New Unlockables Complete missions and unlock Mirror Mode, new stages, challenges, behind-the-scenes content, a music player, animated shorts, special stages, and more! Game Gear Titles Play 12 classic Sonic Game Gear titles, including hits like Sonic Drift 2, Sonic Spinball, and Tails Adventure! New Playable Characters Play as Sonic, Tails, Knuckles or – for the first time ever – Amy Rose in Sonic the Hedgehog 1, 2, Sonic 3 & Knuckles, and Sonic CD! All-in-One Bundle Sonic Origins Plus includes the Classic Music Pack and Premium Fun Pack, which contain Extreme Missions, Mirror Mode, additional screen borders, new character animations in menus, added music from other Sonic titles, and more!

_childDocuments_.review: If you want all the main continuity Sonic 16-bit sonic games running in widescreen and at 60fps, this is the one. The games are here, they play as intended, and they are some awesome games. Fast, challenging, sometimes incredibly complex. A nice touch is the animations before and after games that give some continuity, and have a few nods to the background information given in the game manuals.I've yet to experience any issues with the software, and I think SEGA have done a good job getting this stuff together finally. Music licensing aside, the content is all there and there's even extra content in the form of using Knuckles in Sonic CD, or Tails in Sonic 1.It's good fun, and although Christian Whitehead's ports were the very best (having reverse-engineered the games essentially, and having things like virtual game boxes and cartridges,) the content within Sonic Origins works well enough that I would be happy for this to be the way for people to play to the old games for the foreseeable future. I'm hoping for Steam Workshop modding, but I can imagine SEGA being risk adverse in terms of people being able to publish things they would not want associated with their IP. Fingers crossed, though.Overall: Good job SEGA. You may not have an obsessive savant working on this, for whatever reason (I'm guessing it involves shareholders and corporate timidity,) but It's a very good package for the most important classic Sonic games. 8.5/10Optional advice: For Sonic CD, when at the title screen, access to the options/settings screen and select the JP/EU soundtrack. This is the original soundtrack, and because the past versions of the music were all sound chip music rather than CD audio, they will make more sense as remixes of the present music as they did not re-code the chip tune audio. I also happen to think that the Japanese soundtrack just sounds better, but nostalgia and personal taste will dictate what you prefer. If you've not heard the original, intended soundtrack though, give this a try. It very cool, and very 90s, which fits sonic perfectly.

_childDocuments_.review: 23/06/23 UPDATE (Sonic's Birthday)So, after a few patches and announcements I want to add the following:Finally, Sega fixed most of the problems with the collection, and gameplay-wise is pretty OK!. Not to mention the mod scene has grown exponentially and we can pretty much restore or fix anything we need.However, I would still advice to get it on discount or as a gift.But there's something else now: We finally got Amy, and... well, she's 11 USD (around $2000 ARS) alongside some 8-bit Sonic titles that are pretty good, but they only gave us the Game Gear versionsFor those who haven't played the Sonic GG titles, these are fine Sonic games, as long as you keep in mind that with it had some hardware limitaitons, so the titles aren't as good as the 16-bit counterpartsThat said, for some of these the game gear version is the worst one. I don't understand why Sega didn't gave us the Master System versions. The SMS had better resolution and screen, with pretty much the same hardware. I don't understand this decisionAt any rate, I would still advice against paying full price for the collection. You can find better fan projects to enjoy the versions of Sonic 1, CD, 2 , 3&K... and even the 8-bit titles:-Sonic 1 Forever / Sonic 2 Absolute-Sonic SMS Remake (S1 and S2 Master System)-Sonic Triple Trouble 16-bit-Sonic 3 A.I.R.**********************************************************************************************************Original Review:Sonic 1, Sonic 2 and Sonic 3 & Knuckles are some of my most beloved games in this franchise (with S3K being my favorite videogame of all the time). Sonic CD is kind of an interesting oddity, but still worth playing. Still, the point is that I know these games VERY well and I have a long history with themDo I think the games are worth playing here? Pretty much! These are good remakes of amazing games. The Widescreen alone makes it a lot more welcoming for new players. Although there are a couple of bugs due to SEGA's incompentence.Is this collection worth it then? No. there are better ways to play all these games.Why? Because Sega rushed things as always, made an incredibly confusing DLC pack for the Deluxe edition, buggy menues, messed with the AI code of Tails, added DENUVO (an anti-piracy software that causes a lot performance issues) and screwed up the possibility of doing more things with the groundwork Christian Whitehead and Headcannon already did.The games are as outstanding as ever, but they did NOTHING with them. They could have given us new in-game cutscenes for zone transitions. They could have re-done the level design for a "hard mode". They could have done a New game+ for each game. They could have added Mighty & Ray on all games and also Amy Rose.The animated cutscenes are breautiful, but they don't add anything new gameplaywise.If you're set on getting this collection, wait for a discount, don't pay full price for it. Or better yet, go play the S1, SCD and S2 mobile versions: these work A LOT BETTER and you could even play them on your pc (google Sonic 1 and Sonic 2 decompilation).And for Sonic 3 & Knuckles, Sonic 3 A.I.R. project is probably the best version of that game ever released, and has the level of quality I was expecting this collection to have.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic collection that goes above and beyond - It's not just a collection of poorly emulated ROMs like some of the other collections out there!! 100% recommended for any fan of 2D platformers. The best part about this particular collection is that it caters to purists who want to play the games how they were originally intended without any of the new features, and players who want enhanced modern versions of these titles. The individual games themselves have not aged, and the remastered versions (Anniversary Editions) play just as well as some of the best modern 2D pixelart games released nowadays. These versions feature new playable characters and new abilities that make the games even better.There's also tons of custom made Missions and unlockables (Movies, Illustrations, Music), as well as Mirror Mode versions of each game.I also really appreciate that this collection doesn't treat you like a baby with a stupid "rewind" feature or special "super easy story mode" difficulties. You've got to actually try to get through these games (though they really aren't that difficult to begin with).My only complaint is that the Steam Achievements are really dumb and easy. I wish it'd reward you for beating every game with every character, beating each of the mirror modes, S-ranking all missions, getting all the unlockables etc. Instead it rewards you for defeating an arbitrary amount of specific enemies (?!), and just S-ranking SOME of the missions. Not that it matters, it'd just make playing through the extra content even more fun if we had better achievements here.If you decide to purchase this collection, I recommend you play through the Mission Mode which is a really misleading name for a mode that allows you to play through all four games back-to-back as though they were one big adventure (which they are!). Ignore the achievements, just play the Mission Mode, then beat the custom missions, and then try out Mirror Modes and different characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Origins is a very; polarizing title to say the least. Between it being announced nearly  before it had a release date was quite an interesting move and the  and then on launch; it came out the Headcanon team came out and said they didn’t turn in what was released and weren’t too happy about it. Origins really didn’t have a lot going for it for existing fans; however what this collection was made for and marketed towards, parents who watched the Sonic Movie with their kids and wanted a way to replay classic games from their childhood; Origin was and kinda is perfect for that niche.I’ll cut to the chase; Sonic Origins is a good value in two situations; if you have a Steam Deck or just hate “setting up” emulators or fan ports of these games. However this only effects PC; if you’re on console this is a great value for a game; since there isn’t really any options. So lets talk about like; the game itself now right?Sonic Origins is a collection of 4 Genesis titles (+12  Game Gear games with Plus), under the Retro Engine, developed by Christian Whitehead, a legend in the Sonic space who needs no introduction; they’re all upgraded with full widescreen support in the Anniversary mode or you can keep the og 4:3 in Classic mode; “””new””” playable characters (Amy with Plus) and last but not least the new Story mode that was added to play all 4 games back-to-back in story order. Sonic Origins also comes with tons and tons of goodies that you can unlock with coins you find through out the game and honestly for new and old Sonic fans; it’s always nice seeing them bundle in concept art, music tracks, etc. While it isn’t as cool as Generations was; it’s still a neat touch for them to include  of 90s Sonic art and even new Classic Sonic art.With brand new animated cut-scenes to boot they are by far one of the best parts of this game; they are just usually eye candy to look at, and the Sonic CD intro was upscaled but it looks nice; sure as hell way better than what ever they did to Persona 3 Portables upscaling… sheesh.They all look really nice! I mean to be fair they didn’t change much in this port with the Mobile ports that came out before looked the exact same since they’re using the same engine; but I will say; the anti-aliasing enabled in game can look really weird? Not bad; just strange. They all control as you would expect; nothing really new here other than in all 4 games Sonic now has the Drop Dash. Like it or not it’s here to stay and it doesn’t seem it’s going away anytime soon. Sonic 3 doesn’t benefit that much from it since it was planned to be in it originally anyways, so it feels natural to put back in, Sonic 1 gets a much needed speed up with it, and Sonic 2 just feels even better with how already fast that game is. However; this and I’m not trying to oversell this to you; it  CD apart; since you can just find a semi-flat space in any level and just drop dash back and forth all challenge of finding a spot to Time Travel is just gone; while this makes the game better for a lot of people since it’s even less maze like and faster some people don’t like it and want to be able to disable it (you cannot in any of the games; either in Anniversary or Classic mode.)  but; alas we live in a post-Sonic Mania world and it’s effects will be here forever.Sonic Origins big improvement in the gameplay department I think benefits ‘em all; is the fact you can retry special stages using the coins you collect. In the case of Sonic 2 which stages I personally despise this was a life changing feature to make that game a lot more enjoyable getting all the chaos emeralds; so very very good move devs.By far the biggest downgrade and just lame-o feature is that Sonic 1, CD, and 2 are downgraded to the original Genesis versions; the biggest omission from all of them are multiple save files in each of em; so you can save progress between characters; since in Origins if you wanna change characters and mess around with someone else; you better be ready to restart the entire game! Only Sonic 3 has kept it’s save data system since it’s just already included in the game.As for the 100%? It’s not really that hard. The achievements for the most part are piss easy and you’ll get them as you play and beat each game; the only parts that suck are some of the challenges just kinda are not that fun and will take a lot of grind to get good at and beat the gimmick they’re hittin you with; and getting all the collectibles is something you’ll do while playing the games and doing all the missions.Honestly? The whole part that this collection is good and brings native widescreen and cool collectibles to the table is why it kinda hurts me to not recommend it; at least for PC, if you’re on console it’s a no brainer purchase if you’re a Sonic Fan; but since we’re here on Steam; yeah, it’s just not worth it to the other options you have on a computer, but if you want the easiest, no mods, cross saves for you Steam Deck already set up, to play all the classic Sonic games it really is a no brainer purchase; but I’d recommend saving your dollars for a better Sonic game.  Overall, I just; can’t recommend this for someone that is looking to get the best bang for their buck. If you’re a 100% nerd like me; Sonic 3 A.I.R has tons of achievements; just go for those instead of this.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me and never played the classic sonic games as a kid, this game is perfect for you. I've had such a good time playing through all of these games, and i'm planning on playing through them again. If you're a long time classic sonic fan, you'll find issues with the game, such as lives being removed from the game but most issues are fixed with easily downloadable mods. At the end of the day, these are still the timeless classics wrapped up in a nice package with quality life improvements such as widescreen and a better frame rate. Maybe buy it on a sale if you're unsure.Individual Game Reviews:Sonic The HedgehogThe game to start it all. If I'm honest, I really don't like this game. It's pretty boring thanks to it's level design, and it just makes me want to go play one of the other games in this collection. To make things worse, every zone has 3 acts, so the excruciating pain feels like it lasts an eternity. Also ♥♥♥♥ Labyrinth Zone. Sonic CDThe Black Sheep of the classic Sonic games. This game is weird as all hell, which is evident in it's level design. Sonic CD's level design encourages exploration to destroy generators and Metal Sonic holograms to create a "good future" for that zone. Oh yeah, there's time travel in this game. By passing a "future" or "past" sign and maintaining max speed for a couple of seconds lets Sonic time travel, changing the level's layout a bit and the zones music. This is a really cool concept, and it's a shame it never returned in any capacity. Sonic CD's soundtrack is a true bop and I recommend changing the OST from US soundtrack to JP in the game's main menu. What really holds this game back is most of this games zones are underwhelming, and the only zones I enjoyed were Palmtree Panic, Quartz Quadrant and Stardust Speedway. Also if you don't go out of your way to destroy generators and Metal Sonic holograms you can beat this game in about an hour. Sonic The Hedgehog 2This is what Sonic 1 should have been. They changed zones so that they now have 2 acts instead of 3 which is a more than welcomed change. Sonic 2 also has some of the best level design in any Sonic game ever, and the only zone I didn't enjoy was Metropolis Zone, mostly because it's the only zone in the game for some reason to have 3 acts. Super Sonic makes his first appearance in this game and he feels precise and fun to control. The special stages that you play to get the Chaos Emeralds were surprisingly fun to play, especially because of all the negative things I've heard about them. If you haven't played any of the classic Sonic games before, start here and play Sonic 1 later.Sonic The Hedgehog 3 & KnucklesSonic 3&k is two games put in one, Sonic the Hedgehog 3, and Sonic and Knuckles. Objectively, this is the best game in this collection. It took what Sonic 2 built, and improved on it. The zones in this game are iconic, Angel Island Zone, Ice Cap Zone, Sky Sanctuary Zone, actually, all of them are iconic. This is also the debut of Knuckles, which is cool. The games story is simplistic, yet conveys all it needs to. My only gripe with this game is some zones have dumb gimmicks that get boring after 2 seconds which completely ruin some zones, such as the fan dubbed "barrel of doom" in Carnival Night Zone, and the ghosts in Sandopolis Zone. Returning to Sonic 3&k is Super Sonic, and with it special stages. Although I enjoyed Sonic 2's special stages, Sonic 3&k blow them out the water entirely. Blue Spheres is such a fun mini game that really tests your patience and skill. After beating 7 special stages, you unlock Super Sonic, obviously. But what's unique about Sonic 3&k is you can then upgrade your Chaos Emeralds into Super Emeralds by completing 7 more special stages that are even harder. Doing this unlocks Hyper Sonic, which is just Super Sonic that is more sparkly and has a mid air dash ability. All in all, Sonic 3&k is regarded as the best classic Sonic game, and for good reason. Subjectively, I'd probably put this game equal to Sonic 2, if not a bit higher.

_childDocuments_.review: It's just an ok collection. It's worth the money to have an official way to play these games in a modern format.- First ever remake of Sonic 3 & Knuckles- 4 important games from Sonic's past, ranging from just ok to the best of the best.- Drop Dash was added to each game- Sonic CD's original intro and outros are accounted for and look great- Both Sonic CD OST's are readily available- Widescreen support- Mission Mode provides a nice bite sized challenge- A few of Sonic 3's music tracks were replaced due to copyright issues. The new (or rather, old) music in use here isn't bad, but the instrumentation could've used some work.- Denuvo Anti-Tamper- Sonic CD is still the same cramped game it's always been- Sonic 1 and 2 lock control of your character after a jump from a spindash or dropdash- Sonic 1 and 2's OST was not carried over from the superior Mobile versions- Story Mode offers little reason to play it, as it contains no different content from playing each game seperately. There is also no level select after completing it.- Without mods, the game looks blurry- The DLC is nonsense (I have to pay to pan the camera around the islands? Really?)- Quite a few bugs that are fairly easy to notice.- No online multiplayer support for Sonic 2 or 3- There's not really any difference between S1,2, and CD here and the ones that are on mobile.If you're looking for a more robust way to play these titles, seek out Sonic 1 Forever, Sonic 2 Absolute, Sonic CD Restored, and Sonic 3 AIR, all of which are fanmade versions of these games that contain more quality of life improvements over what's offered in Origins. That said, Origins is still a fairly good way to experience these games and I'm glad it exists.

_childDocuments_.review: After pre-ordering this game / collection for 68 AUD and getting every achievement as of now, I can safely say...I would've been better off using Emulators.This was my first time ever beating Sonic 1, 2 and 3&K (and first time getting the good end on CD) and although they are great experiences and I am a big fan of Classic Sonic, this collection pretty much blows, it's only pros being the widescreen gameplay and newly added cutscenes... which SEGA themselves can't even be thanked for considering that was the work of fans. And that's what you're going to begin to really realise, the heavy lifting was done by the fans while the lazy work came from, you guessed it, SEGA.To begin with, the keyboard controls are stupid and I want to sue whoever thought they were a good idea, If I hadn't had myself a controller, I might've sooner refunded the game. Secondly, people may defend this point as the games "staying true to the originals" which I can agree to disagree on but the whole menu's within menu's thing really sucked, having the options all the way at the museum for god-knows-what reason and then examples such as trying to change Sonic CD's Region Soundtrack, which took me longer than it should've, proving the menus really needed touch-ups in the first place. And the Origins menu was so underwhelming without even mentioning you had to PAY EXTRA to rotate and zoom a camera. (And the menu for the Illustrations and Music is Microsoft Powerpoint levels of quality).And the menus within menus leads onto my next point being: Wow, you really just half-assedly threw Christian Whiteheads work into the game with no extra effort. It would've been nice to make some minor improvements here and there but NOPE, apparently they can't do. There's also the missions, very cool idea and a good way to grind Coins... yet every level has these grey bricks just bloody thrown around the place. Normally I'd assume they couldn't change the levels... and yet they can place more enemies and ugly blocks... what is this???Also the mirror mode and boss rush are useless to me and probably to everyone else, the fact they make it an entirely different save/game for have a different Ratio Screen and flipping the world is stupid, just make it customizable. So if you haven't picked it up by now: SEGA does piss all to help in this games creation. Probably just threw this together so they could get more money in their pocket, and they really must love their money because they didn't want to waste a buck on trying to get Sonic 3&K's og soundtrack, I personally do not mind but fans obviously are dissapointed to see this and they must've known this considering they never got CW to port 3&K likely because of this reason up until this point. They claim they "composed new music" to fill in for the songs they couldn't use... when they literally use the unused music instead, yeah ok.Oh and didn't they mention adding an extra playable character or two? "how about we make Knuckles unplayable in CD" Yeah no, this review is long enough as-isNow if you made it through all my whining, here are some parts I DID like about this: Like I stated prior, the new cutscenes, missions and widescreen is so good, these games deserved these and being able to play these games in one neat collections is nice, it's because of this game I get to not only play all 4 games but I get to see all the good endings for myself, and pushing aside the roughness. these games are as fun as they'll always be, especially when played one after another.I like this collection of games, but they are really pushing the definition of a "remaster" and yet they're not the only ones, bad games and remasters seem to be occuring more frequently and it's sad to see SEGA go this direction too.Games like Sonic Mania (and maybe Sonic Generations) are what companies should be doing for their fans to celebrate milestones, but Sonic Origins is what companies think they can get away with nowadays.To conclude: I don't hate this game, I hate SEGA for allowing this great idea to become so terribly underwhelming.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a Sonic the Hedgehog fan ever since the first game released on the Sega Genesis back in the early nineties. I have fond memories of getting Sonic 2 for my birthday one year, and I also remember buying the rental copy of Sonic & Knuckles from my local mom & pop video store. I have a lot of fond memories of Sonic and this collection is an enjoyable way to relive those parts of my youth.There have been numerous Sonic compilations released over the years so what makes Sonic Origins different from the rest? For starters Sonic CD is included here which a lot of those early bundles lacked. There's also a Story Mode where you can start with Sonic 1 and play all of the games through in their canonical order complete with newly animated cutscenes tying each of the games together. Starting with Sonic 1 and going all the way through Sonic 3 & Knuckles collecting all the Chaos Emeralds as you go makes for a great challenge.The games are all in widescreen and built from the engines used by Headcannon for their ports of Sonic 1 and 2. Headcannon was not directly involved with the production of this compilation but their technology was used in Sonic 3 & Knuckles for pathfinding and other technical gobbledygook. You're getting a solid collection of Sonic's classic hits presented in possibly their most definitive editions.There have been some bad things said about the music in Sonic 3 & Knuckles, namely regarding the "Michael Jackson tracks" that had to be removed from the game for licensing reasons. In their place are the original compositions heard in the early prototypes for Sonic 3. They aren't done with a Genesis soundfont however so they sound a bit muddied. I personally would have preferred they use the Genesis originals instead of these weird covers but I'm certain there's a mod that fixes this. There's probably even a mod that puts the Jackson tracks back in the game!My favorite thing about Sonic Origins is the inclusion of the challenges for each of the games. Things like collecting X number of rings or beating a checkpoint within a certain time limit. It provides a nice bonus scenario mode that tests your skills at the classic Sonic games. For all the years I've been playing these games I was still thrown a couple of curveballs that took me numerous tries.Overall Sonic Origins is in my opinion a solid collection of games. Perhaps the asking price is a little steep, but that's nothing a Steam sale can't fix. Definitely mark this one for checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Origins is by far the best way to play and enjoy the classic Genesis games, even if I have a couple issues with the package itself. But the work put here to make the best version of these games that has ever been released is very obvious. I'm also writing this review assuming that most people looking at this may have already played these games before.The Sonic games in this collection, from what I can tell, go beyond simple ports/emulation of the originals and actually had a bevy of QoL features I had never considered but are very welcome.- The 16:9 versions of the games are beautiful and I love them.- Lives have been substituted by an Arcade-like credit system. Every life you would win in-game nets you one credit and those credits can be used to repeat special stages you fail at. - Sonic 2's biggest and only issue (for me) has also been fixed: You now get a dedicated button to turn into Super Sonic, rather than automagically transforming after getting 50 rings. THANK YOU.- Sonic 2's special stages also seem to run at a higher framerate and it is both a blessing and a curse. They are much faster paced, but I had to relearn how to play the harder ones. Still a ton of fun tho.- The new animations added to the beginning and end of each game are absolutely beautiful and I love them. They also help tie the games chronologically and create a "narrative" when you're playing Mission Mode.- WHAT DO YOU MEAN SONIC CD COMES AFTER SONIC 1?! I had legitimately never considered this.Cons:This is a very strong recommend from me, as someone who grew up playing these games. I just wish they would add the mod support from the Genesis collection into this so we could play romhacks too. Then this would be perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic set of remasters that feel great to play in widescreen. The new mission mode is fun and reminds me a lot of the extra missions from Unleashed and Generations, and the museum and coin feature is a great way to replace the outdated extra lives. I also enjoyed being able to replay special stages, and the great new animations for every game's introduction and ending.Issues I experienced:- Fell through a pinball flipper once in Sonic CD, didn't result in getting hit or death- A few (3 or so) gameplay elements got stuck in the floor or ceiling after being used in Sonic 2 and Sonic 3, didn't impede progress or result in getting hit or death- Experienced very minimal (1 second or less) stuttering, which only happened maybe 5 or 6 times in the whole time I played, and it only resulted in getting hit or death once- The instrumentation of the replacement tracks for Sonic 3 isn't very good- The level select and emerald count features after you beat the game are pretty much nonexistent, when they were present in the mobile ports- Customization features such as turning off spin or drop dash in Anniversary mode, or invincibility/extra life jingle toggle for Sonic 3 & Knuckles are lackingOther than that, my playthrough (All Achievements and 100% Museum) went very smoothly and was very enjoyable, I would recommend this game if you have any interest in playing classic Sonic.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid but flawed way to play the Classic Sonic games.I wanted to replay the Classic Sonic games recently. Whilst there are a countless number of ways to play each game, this collection went on sale for a pretty good discount recently so I decided to give it a try.I have some pretty big problems with it. Denuvo affects the performance of the menus pretty badly. The soundtrack in Sonic 3 is replaced and needs to be fixed with mods, and there are some minor changes to the games including the inclusion of the spindash in Sonic 1. However, whilst I'm sure that there are more definitive versions of each game elsewhere, I paid for the convenience of having all four games (five, if you count Knuckles separately from Sonic 3) in one place on my PC. The actual ports of the games are very solid outside of the minor changes. They bothered to include CD, which is one of my favourites and is often left out of Classic Sonic compilations and it includes both soundtracks. The new missions are a fun distraction. Amy being playable for the first time in all four games is really nice to see and there are some other cool goodies included like the selection of Game Gear games, concept artwork and brand new animated cut scenes.There's just too much this version does right for me to pass my nose up at it. Definitely do you're own research to see if this collection has what you're looking for but I'd personally recommend this, especially at a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: - Each game plays as good as their previous incarnations. The controls are as responsive as they should be.- , what more is there to say.- . Sonic 1 and 2 were previously offered in widescreen exclusively on mobile devices, however now they have a new home on proper platforms.-  that do justice to the original source material as well as providing a neat way of tying all of the games together.-  what more is there to say. It doesn't stop pirates, makes the experience worse for the end consumer, and requires an online connection to play.- . For the price the dlc is touted at, they are worthless to buy for anyone other than hardcore enthusiasts. The content they add should be in the game by default anyway, without the extra price.- While I understand Sonic 3's original music cannot be implemented,  in all honestly. However its more perplexing how a decision was made to replace the Super Sonic music with a cover/remix of the original theme.- . You are forced to play the games with drop dash enabled and in the case of Sonic 1, forced to play with spindash, even in the "classic" mode. The only game with decent options is Sonic Cd, and even then, those features were already options from the 2011 pc version. As well, there were missed opportunities to implement features that had even been in previous collections before, such as Sonic Jam's easy modes.- . This isn't much a problem for most casual individuals, but for the keen eyed it can be an annoyance to have a smoothed image on medium to large displays. - . The music throughout the games is muffled and sounds as if a low pass filter had been applied to it. Even at max volume it can be quiet compared to how it was in the originals.- . It frequently drops frames when even above the game's "recommended" requirements.- . The bindings are set to odd configurations with no other default options, forcing players to change them manually if they don't like them.- . You are forced to back out to the menu to change anything. Sonic Mania was the same in this regard but it's still a slight disappointment and inconvenience none the less.- . Your air control is removed in favor of a set arc. Why is this the case, I do not know.- . The variety in them is disappointing, often having mundane and boring objectives. The effort on these missions is clearly lacking, featuring grey blocks in preexisting levels as it's means to create these challenges. It's similar in quality to the extra content found within Sonic Forces, being superficial levels to inflate the game experience.- . This is an even greater disappointment when you realize that some of the images are low quality, especially the "harmony covers" which are taken from a 1996 screensaver and feature heavily compressed versions of said covers.- . The dpad controls for the museum are inverted for some ungodly reason, there is no option to use a mouse and there is no way to easily flip through pages in the manuals without having to exit the full view menu and flip 1 page at a time.
