_childDocuments_.review: The following review also considers the DLC for this game (as of 29th August 2022, should there ever be more).Sonic Origins is ok. Just ok. It does have what I really wanted, which was Sonic 1 and 2 2013 editions on a non-mobile platform, but it's bundled with CD, which...really had no need to be "here", since CD was perfectly fine remaining separate, especially when CD has no additional improvements. (I don't actually care for S3K all that much to be bothered by its inclusion.)The Good:- Mission Mode. Really liked this new spin on tackling levels. The Super Sonic challenge concept was especially really fun. Some of the missions seem extremely textbook given that I am a Sonic veteran, but the appeal to newer players to hone skills is certainly there.- Sonic 1 and 2 (2013) finally coming to non-mobile. It was downright criminal that it took this long. Honestly could have done without drop dash tho, I still don't think drop dash is very good as a concept.- The cutscenes are definitely well done and quite cute.- The fact that they snuck in a Spinball homage as one of the "islands". I'm a sucker for Spinball, so I can't not appreciate that.The Bad:- Denuvo. Unfortunately, SEGA got past the "complaining" phase and compromised only by removing Denuvo from Mania, while Forces still has it and Frontiers is about to. This is basically part of SEGA's host of bad decisions.- Frankly, the way the DLC was presented. You literally have no need for an extra 100 coins. You play all of mission mode once and get S ranks, you're nearly maxed and can buy almost all the unlockables. The missions that were in DLC could easily have been unlockables themselves. Big ball drop here.- I'm not gonna call this personally bad, because I don't mind, but Amy being presented as one of the characters in all the advertising and then not being a playable character. "New playable characters" is straight up false advertising, unless you want to call Knuckles + Tails "new". I can't ignore that as a flaw.- Delisting Sonic 1, 2, 3 and CD for this. Also another bad decision. CD didn't even need to be in this collection, period.- Shoving in drop dash for Sonic 1, 2 and CD. I'll even say it doesn't actually really belong in S3K either. These games did not need a move that the games aren't actually built for a lot of the time. (For the record, Sonic 1 having spindash is more acceptable, especially since it was built in to the mobile release).- CD being ported in with basically no changes. I'm going to call out something specific here: CD still has its own time attack mode built in, but also has the Origins-specific leaderboards, creating an odd redundancy. Oh, and the centisecond timer bug? Still in the game.The Ugly:- Boss Rush. Boss Rush is a nice concept, but it was executed badly, especially outside Sonic 1. There could have even been a time attack mode and a survival mode a la Robotnik's Revenge, or a specially designed boss rush level like Sonic 2 (2013) wanted to do. Huge missed opportunity. Instead, you have many bosses that do need a ring to go fast that have no rings or rings behind you so you have to waste time getting one, in exchange for other levels having rings, such as Final or Death Egg Zone. Very erratic difficulty scale, and it makes for an odd experience.- The leaderboards taking times from your first playthrough (by this I mean taking times from outside the My Data & Ranking section at all), even Super/Hyper times. Big error in judgement by whomever thought this was a good idea. Mania did this right. Even SONIC FOUR did this right. Why make this mistake here?- The coin system being utterly worthless very quickly. This replacing lives in Anniversary Mode was also not a good idea. Doesn't matter if I "have Classic Mode for that". Coins belong in Mario.- The Museum not having its own theme. Also a poor decision.- Mirror Mode. I have very mixed feelings about Mirror Mode, and I want to say it's good, bad, and ugly all at the same time. It's good for a mindfug experience. It's bad for IL runners because it's just an artificial reason for "more levels". It's ugly because no one actually wanted this, considering the time was better spent on other things...Overall, especially after the patch, the game is passable. It's not excellent, and plenty of bad decisions were made. The price isn't "bad" considering the work on cutscenes and the like, but for just the games it was worth halfish.Buy it at half price or less, and unless you also really like the missions, skip the DLC. Right now, save your money for Frontiers IF it turns out to be a good enough game. Try not to support SEGA's bad decision making if you can help yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a ethical responsibility to write a negative review for this compilation. the games look nice in widescreen and it's great to be able to see these on a marketplace. I like being able to waddle over to my computer after a long and exhausting day at work and just hit thoughtlessly hit the "play" button on this and play some old sonic games. The problem is, unless you're absurdly affluent and like throwing money away for no reason, there's no reason to purchase this. As a computer owner there are already ways to play these games in 16:9 on PC for a lot less than 40-45 dollars, and they have less bugs and have way more customization options than this offers. I don't need to tell you this since you've probably already read a bunch of reviews but go check out the decompiled ios/android ports of sonic 1, 2, and CD, and of course, check out either sonic 3 complete or sonic 3 AIR for a far superior experience than what this offers. So basically what you're spending money on here is the compilation goodies and the fact that this natively launches from the steam platform and you can collect achievements for it. The crappy part here is that the achievements are baby stuff. I felt pretty great about having all six chaos emeralds by the end of Spring Yard Zone in Sonic 1, but the game didn't give me any sort of pat on the back or reward for doing so. In fact, the inability to toggle infinite lives off in anniversary mode doubly makes it feel like there's zero incentive for playing these games at a higher level or trying to learn more about them. That sucks!The extras in the museum are sorely lacking. I remember Sonic Jam on the Saturn way back in 1997 having the original commercials for the games from japan and neat stuff like that. The museum offerings here are presented well and some of the art is in unprecedented resolution which is super cool but it's a lot of what you've seen already! It would've been nice to get some developer commentary tracks on levels, or maybe some options to configure custom playlists to enjoy while playing these video games. Yknow, some sort of offering that you can get here and not in other, superior versions of these widescreen ports.I don't need to mention the music, we all know its terrible, but I should mention that there is a mod to restore the original soundtrack already. I don't know if there was any way around this. Michael Jackson's estate is notoriously difficult to work with and probably wanted sega to pay out the ass for a game that came out like thirty years ago. I don't really blame them for not wanting to pony up the money. What I can blame them for is how awful the replacement music sounds. Custom playlists or new compositions from guest composers like Tee Lopes or something could have cool but instead we have Jun Senoue offering the worst-sounding "genesis" remixes of those godawful prototype tracks i've hated for decades. The situation sucks, but it certainly could've been handled in more thoughtful and creative ways. I also think it's cowardly of them to have done their best to hide the soundtrack replacement news until shortly before launch.Ultimately, don't buy this game. I bought it because I'm a stupid idiot and I like buying stuff because it makes me feel better about my dumb life. Go donate 40 dollars to an abortion fund or something and just google "sonic 1 widescreen android pc port" or something like that. Sonic is an anti-fascist and that's more in line with what he would want you to do, if he was real. I don't think he is though. (God I wish he was).

_childDocuments_.review: This is a collection of what many consider to be the best of Sonic the Hedgehog.  The games, for the most part, still hold up well.  The gameplay is still fast, & the cleaned up audio on most titles comes across wonderfully.  The dropping of lives & addition of the spin dash in all games in anniversary mode is a nice touch, as well as getting to play as Tails & Knuckles in most titles.  The coins earned in anniversary mode can also be used to replay special stages in the event of a loss.  The extra modes can also be fun, with mission mode having a selection of challenges, & mirror mode shaking the entire game up for veteran players. This does not feel like the definitive edition.  Sonic 1 & 2 are close to their portable versions, though still missing some things those titles had.  Sonic CD is practically just the Steam version, complete with missing Knuckles as a playable character.  It also uses the original cutscenes, rather than updating them along with all the new ones.  Finally, Sonic 3&K has the most problems, clearing being the odd one out.  It's audio quality is worse, it uses the beta/PC release tracks for stages 4-6, & the collision just feels off on so many points, coming across closer to the original Sonic 3 release.  There are so many small problems here & there that just add up.  As for the rest, the DLC is completely useless & not worth it, adding a ridiculously insulting ability to look at the island in the menu.  Not turn the camera to see around it or view the models, just to look at it. This list was incredibly simple, with the hardest challenge coming from simply beating the games.  No real challenge or meat to them, simply do a missions around each game, & unlock a number of items in the game's museum.  You don't even need to 100% the game to get them. This was a massive disappointment.  The games are all here, & a patch or two could fix some of the problems, but the lack of features to make the games worth playing again for old fans is noticeable.  As for newer fans, these ports have issues that could turn some of them away.  If it goes on sale, & these problems get fixed, then this could change.  As of right now, I really don't feel like it's the best or definitive way to play these games.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a Sonic fan for a long time. The first time I played a Sonic game was in 2006 with the Sonic Mega Collection Plus on the PS2. Because of that, a lot of my early memories with Sonic have been with the Genesis games. But there was one thing I could never do back then. Actually finish them. Either I had monkeys banging cymbals in my head back then or the games are just that difficult.Years later, probably 2012, I returned to the Mega Collection and learned of the save state feature, which I never knew about back when I first played it. With the save state feature, I was able to experience each classic Sonic game in full. But there was one minor problem. The save states took forever to load. That didn't hold me back from finishing the games and finally seeing those oh so satisfying credits roll by, but it broke the pace of the games to screeching halts. Because of that, I found it hard to return to the Mega Collection simply because the save states took so long to load. That was really it. Occasionally I'd load up a save and replay the final boss of each Genesis game, but it was not satisfying enough. I wanted to play through each game without worrying about lives and continues, without worrying about messing up a special stage, without seeing that dreaded Game Over screen cutting back to the title screen.With all that said, I believe Sonic Origins is the perfect way to experience the original Genesis era Sonic games. You have the widescreen support, no more lives system, the chance to retry special stages at the expense of the unique coins, the choice to play through each campaign as select characters, and the all new animated cutscenes that simply act to bridge the gap between each game. While I have replayed the Genesis games countless times and have had my irks with Origins adding stuff like the drop dash into every game, I don't mind it all that much.What's most important to me is that a new generation of kids will get to experience these games without the frustrating hassles of a retro gaming era so far removed from modern conventions. With this collection, I got to fall in love with each game all over again. And what I like most is that they are all conveniently in one single collection. Sonic 1, CD, 2, and 3&K work wonderfully when paired with each other in a single collection that urges you to play them in order.Oh yeah, this game passive aggressively posits CD as the second game, even though Sonic 2 released first. To be frank, I don't mind it. If it's what the writers at Sonic Team and SEGA want the classic games to be seen as, I'm all for it. The lovely animated cutscenes are done with such care as to give the information from the manuals without overbearingly adding too much lore that contradicts later games.As for my brief thoughts on each game.Sonic 1Absolutely classic. I love it to bits even though it wants to chew you up and spit you out. For the first entry in the entire series, it gets so many of the core mechanics right that it ages gracefully. Being a game from 1991, it becomes insanely unfair as it progresses. Honestly, I love it. And given the infinite lives that Origins throws at you, you can rest well knowing you will never have to be blasted back to the title screen.Sonic CDThis is quite a polarizing game. If you play it like any other Sonic game, you're simply not playing it the intended way. Each level is built to be large and sprawling, encouraging exploration. However that is antithetical to the Classic Sonic experience, since you want to go fast! As the second game in the collection, it challenges you to unlearn what you learned in Sonic 1, and that works really well as a teaching tool for the later games in the collection. The addition of new characters, Amy and Metal Sonic, is also great and makes CD essential playing.Sonic 2Perfection. With more zones than before, a better implemented special stage mechanic and the addition of Tails, Sonic 2 is one of the greatest platformers ever made. Sonic Origins' version of Sonic 2 borrows heavily from the mobile phone remaster of Sonic 2, which means an additional optional zone is playable, and you can have Sonic get a boost from Tails. The best version of an already amazing platformer. I highly encourage you try and win each special stage.Sonic 3 & KnucklesEven more perfection. Not more has to be said. Each zone is iconic, plays really well, and the game does a tremendous job at telling a story with just the in-game sprites and environments. The special stages are at their best, and the music top notch. Wait... the music?!! So yeah, the music in Carnival Night, Ice Cap, and Launch Base are different and vastly inferior to the original music tracks. I wholeheartedly refused to buy this game on console because at least on PC, I can mod the original music back in it's place. That's what I did for my game and I wouldn't have it any other way. Hopefully this review gets dated and an update adds the original tracks to the default experience. Overall though, replaying Sonic 3 had me with a big dumb grin on my face the whole time. I had never played a widescreen version of Sonic 3 before, so to finally be doing it fresh with the other classic games was amazing.I highly recommend this game to anyone that found the original games to be too difficult. It allows you to really appreciate the art in the games at a more relaxed pace, and the changes made are so minimal that you can easily mod the game to remove those minor irks. A very good collection.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 42.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: As a guy who has played this series since ALMOST the beginning (my first game was Sonic 2), this was kind of a given. As of my original review, I had finished Sonic 1 and started 2; as of this edit, I have since finished them all.I have not run into any control issues, but then again, I play this with a controller. I did play prior games (the old S&K collection, emulated versions, etc.) with a keyboard, but I'm terrible with keyboard controls for fast-paced games like this anyway, so I grabbed my Xbox controller. From the reviews on the keyboard controls, I'm glad I did...Anywho:Pros:-The infinite lives in Anniversary Mode, replacing "lives" with coins, which give retries on the special stages (THANK YOU, GOD). And are apparently also used for cosmetic things that are... only usable in the game, so maybe that's a "meh".-Spin dash in Sonic 1 (THANK YOU AGAIN, GOD). As I said, I started with Sonic 2, and I kept going for the dash by reflex when I first played S1 and went "hey, why isn't this working?"-Level restarting (OH HALLELUJAH), especially if you get stuck. Like getting caught between a star bumper and a spring in Spring Yard Zone in Sonic 1. (Also a way to cheese the emerald gain in Sonic 2, since the special stages are obtainable from the star posts, not the ring at the end. If you restart the level after getting one, and do that same star post again... you're going for two. And then three, and so on. I discovered this entirely by accident. Probably works similarly in 3, but haven't gotten that far yet.)-A somewhat more fluid moving special stage in Sonic 2 - innnnteresting...-Having now played through all of them (in anniversary mode, of course): Checkpoints at certain stages that ALSO SAVE YOUR SCORE. One of the troubles I always ran into playing the original Genesis games was that except for 3, none of them had a save feature, and even with 3, it always started at the beginning of the last zone you played, and also wipes your score to zero. The checkpoints in this game allow you to literally pick up where you left off.Meh:-I heard about it, and looked in the "museum" for the soundtracks... and saw the tracks for Carnival Night, Ice Cap, and Launch Base in Sonic 3 have been replaced with the ones from the Sonic & Knuckles PC collection from ages back. Fun fact: Those levels had music arranged/inspired/etc. by Michael Jackson... and then Sega found out who he really was. Oops! I mean, the replacements aren't BAD - well, Carnival Night's replacement in the Genesis MIDI version is pretty bad, actually - but when I first heard them in that collection about 20 years ago (God, I feel old), I was like "wait, what the hell happened?" (So was Yuji Naka about them being in this pack, apparently!) Launch Base particularly was a disappointment, the original Genesis version was my favorite track from Sonic 3 - the replacement, I remember reading a YouTube comment saying it sounded like a German military march. Make of that what you will.-They removed the freakin' options menu from Sonic 2. What, no sound test cheat modes? FOR SHAME. (The up-down-left-right-etc. one for Sonic 1 still works, though.)-Playing in widescreen aspect is great, but I admit I was kind of hoping for a Mania-style setup where the graphics had a "new-old" feel?-Moving from "cons" to "meh", since earlier I said there was no settings menu, I found it... it's in the "Museum" tab, so it's a little tricky to find. Ish.Cons:-A BIT sluggish in spots. Particularly the score count at the end of levels, and somewhat slower level transitions. (Maybe intended? Still a tad jarring.)-Occasionally getting stuck in less than ideal places - aforementioned example of being completely trapped and having to restart the level in Spring Yard in Sonic 1. I don't remember that ever happening before.-Not sure if this is intended, but... I notice the air bubbles are a LOT stingier in the water zones in Sonic 1. Particularly in Scrap Brain Act 3.-Sonic CD's special stages. It's not an Origins thing, it's a Sonic CD thing. They're the only thing worse than the Super Emerald special stages in S3&K. (And I HATE Blue Spheres!)-Price tag is a TAD steep... plus, the DLC is more music for the in-game player. Erm... okay? Not like we're going to use that much, but okay.All in all, it's... nothing spectacular - it's four oldies but goodies in one gift-wrapped package - but it's certainly enough to bring out the nostalgia.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If you've never played any of the original Sonic games on Genesis/Mega Drive and are willing to pay a premium to get a 16:9 remaster that's not as good as the fan-made options you'll probably be okay with this. Otherwise just don't bother (especially if you already have the originals).In a vacuum with no context I think this collection is actually fine? The issue is that they removed the originals when they released this to Steam. I want to give them the benefit of the doubt and assume they just did that because they thought this was going to be the definitive version but that's just not the case in my opinion. I'm glad that we finally have the widescreen mobile remasters of these games on Steam now but there's good reasons why you'd want the Genesis collection versions over this: the major reason being that this lacks workshop support where the old versions had it so you could easily download rom hacks without having to go through the trouble of patching it yourself. You also don't get the roms in a separate folder like you did with the OG versions so you can't use your own emulator if you want to. Not only that but to further rub salt into the wound the "classic" versions available in this version STILL ARE NOT THE ORIGINALS they don't even really try to hide that as there's Hidden Palace in Sonic 2 which is not a thing on the original Genesis version, there's also no slowdown and there's a lot of "bug fixes" in this version, so I'm not sure why you would even bother playing the 4:3 version outside of making a small minority of bosses slightly easier.It's not all bad though, I like that they removed lives as I feel like a big turn off to the originals is that they were really heavily trial and error based and with the small amount of tries you get before a game over I understand why people often dismiss the first 2 games. The 16:9 aspect ratio also really does help with a lot of areas and helps you see hazards way earlier (metropolis zone comes to mind) The animated cut scenes they added are cute and they dumped all the Game Gear games here which is nice. I don't think any of these really make up for the downsides though. Also it has Denuvo lol

_childDocuments_.review: (Originally written on June 24, 2022)Pre-ordered the deluxe edition, definitely not worth it. Origins is another example on why you should never trust SEGA for remastering any of their games in the future.Let's start with the good stuff first:Sonic 3 looks and plays flawlessly, no problems with gameplay whatsoever. You can tell this game was the one that got the most attention during development. Every character including Sonic's super forms have gotten new sprites for the various rotating platforms in 3. Cutscenes are fantastic as usual thanks to Tyson Hesse. The little islands are a very cute touch, very cool to see 3D versions of the islands for Sonic 1 (which you only saw in the 8-bit version) and Sonic 2 (which you only saw in the title screen background.) The premium art collection has a lot of concept art for both JP and US versions of Sonic 1 to 3, some I haven't even seen before. And finally the premium movie collection has the animatics for Mania Adventures and every cutscene in the story mode.And now for the terrible:The game is VERY blurry, due to a filter put on to combat inconsistent pixel sizes, which is  STUPID and nobody would ever have noticed. Disgusting low-pass filter on S3&K music, Jun's reworked prototype tracks sound like garbage (unfortunate cause I genuinely prefer prototype Carnival Night to the MJ version), Drop-dash is poorly implemented, which is crazy to even think about cause it's probably so easy to port in due to Mania also running on the Retro Engine. Physics are off in Sonic 1 and 2, and Classic mode STILL includes the spin-dash in Sonic 1 with no way to turn it off. Mods will definitely fix the game like always, in fact GameBanana already has a mod that brings back the MJ tracks. Premium music collection is a complete JOKE, it's just select tracks from the Sonic Generations OST and the Angel Island Zone remix from Super Smash Bros. Brawl.  Same goes for the Genesis music collection, various tracks are mislabeled or just outright not there. And finally, the way pre-ordering bonuses were laid out on the official Origins website was extremely convoluted for no reason. I never felt so robbed out of 5 extra dollars in my life. Only SEGA could achieve that.This was a highly anticipated re-release of the classics and just like Colors Ultimate, it fails on even emulating the originals. My overall rating for this disappointment: 5/10.My condolences go out to every developer for this game, excluding SEGA and Sonic Team.(EDIT: June 27, 2022)It's been 4 days since launch and already mods have improved the game drastically. The blur issue has been fixed, MJ's music has been re-added, Genesis music collection properly organized, and the physics for Sonic 1 and 2 alongside fixes for the Drop-dash in those games have been fixed. All of these fixes done so quickly by modders goes to show that Sonic Team is a shadow of their former self. With so many OG or newer but great developers gone, I highly doubt Frontiers will be even decent now that we know SEGA is still doing this ♥♥♥♥ behind the scenes.Overall rating for this game WITH the mods is 8/10. A great way to play all the OG classic games. However, I'm still not recommending this game. $45 USD just for the full experience is a HORRIBLE price tag. Look, I get that Mania was a standalone classic game so that's why it was $20 USD. But, these games are almost over 30 years old, and you could easily just pirate the ROMS and run them through KEGA Fusion or Sonic 3 A.I.R. At least make them cheap enough to stop the people who are pirating your precious old games and buy this. $20 USD for Deluxe, $15 USD for Standard. That's all this game needs.(UPDATE: November 23, 2022)I want the Steam Awards Badge.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like a lot of people really don't seem to understand just what Sonic Origins is....It always felt to me as if it wasn't really intended to be this massive collection of Sonic games like Mega Collection Plus or Gems Collection was. It was never meant to be anything beyond: "Hey, we're bringing the HD Remasters of Sonic 1 and 2 to PC, and here's CD and the never before seen an ACTUAL re-release Sonic 3 & Knuckles, all in glorious widescreen. Remade from the ground up in Sonic Mania's retro engine." Just giving us a nice refreshing take of 4 classic Sonic games packed with some neat things from Sonic's history that should surely reflect it's title as Sonic Origins.This should have been the explanation right? Well not quite. It seems like the higher ups at Sega didn't exactly know themselves how to market this game. As a result it is unclear to us the consumers, casual gamers and Sonic fans alike what this game really is. Couple that with the absolutely terrible price guide and "DLC" additions (which were all later included in the PLUS DLC) and it's very easy to understand why this title's reception is mixed. That being said, what is Sonic Origins. Is it a smash pack of classic Genesis games like the many collections we've seen for decades? Or not.This is a debate that I'm very tired of seeing because all of the people who know are overshadowed by the loud vocal majority that wants Knuckles Chaotix or Sonic 3D Blast to be included in this pack of remastered Sonic games. (I can understand why, Chaotix hasn't had a release at all and is probably the only 32X title worth playing in my humbled opinion.) If Sonic Origins seemed lackluster already, adding these games will honestly make things even worse. "Why is Sonic 1, 2, 3 and CD only in HD, why can't we get other genesis games in HD!?" Sure, if they had competent emulation developers who are able to reverse engineer the code on these old games and then modernize it for today's standards then SURE, games like Sonic 3D Blast or Chaotix would be a no brainer. However it just simply doesn't work like that. As stated previously the titles included in Origins were remade from the ground up. This is not your average Sega Genesis collection and should have been marketed as such!!Don't even get me started on the quality of the remastered games that we got... It just screams corporate meddling. Every game is full of it's own unique flaws and things that we haven't seen in other Retro Engine remakes. Which is another reason why Sonic Origins has a mixed reception but I want to talk about the elephant in the room. The PLUS DLC.I applaud them for listening to that loud majority that wanted more content for this game. I feel like it's especially beneficial to the game's reputation as a whole especially given it's strange launch price, this makes people feel as if they're getting their money's worth. Is what I would say if there wasn't another big elephant in the room, THE DIGITAL DELUXE EDITION. (Which I myself pre-ordered when it was available for purchase.) Do you know what we get in the Digital Deluxe Edition? More coins? - Yes.Music unlocked from the start?  - YesMore Content to unlock in the Art Gallery? - YesPlus DLC? - Ye- No. No?NO!? The game was a whole $15 extra dollars at launch for people who purchased the Digital Deluxe Edition why are those people not being compensated!? We paid $45 DOLLARS FOR THIS GAME. Okay so you give the people what they want, more content but at the same time you're ripping off the people who pre-ordered the Digital Deluxe Edition!? $55 DOLLARS TOTAL!?For a game that's being listed for $29,99!? Come on now. Originally I was content with whatever they offered for this game because I was just happy to see those retro engine ports of Sonic 1 and 2 being playable on more than just mobile phones. I was happy because Sonic 3 and Knuckles was FINALLY getting that treatment as well as being the only title to at this point has NOT seen a re-release since Sonic Mega Collection. If I had known that there was a possibility of this game getting a PLUS update and that THIS kind of strategy would be pulled I would have never pre-ordered it because ALL OF THE PRE-ORDER CONTENT COMES IN THE PLUS DLC! Sega, Sonic Team and their marketing team really dropped the ball on what would have been a decent collection of remastered Sonic games. Is Origins bad? No, not at all. I can tell there was some love put in to all this. While uncredited, part of Mania's dev team helped Sonic Team learn the Retro Engine. But with Orgins and it's troubled backstory, abhorrent marketing and business strategies makes this game just plain bad. Do not buy this title at a high price, wait for it to go on sale. Steam always has really good Sonic The Hedgehog sales and chances are you might even get a game bundled in if you don't have it already. Till then I'll be laying low til the price inevitably drops and I can purchase the plus DLC. (Too bad it's 1 year TOO LATE for me to get a refund.) I'll be playing the BETTER Sonic title that released last year, Sonic Frontiers which GAVE US FREE DLC ON THE SAME DAY THAT IMPROVED THE GAME IN WAYS ORIGINS COULD EVER DREAM OF. Do yourself a favor, wait for a sale. This collection can wait.So for now, this game's recommendation is a no from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Origins is, as far as I'm concerned, exactly what it set out to be. A collection of the four-ish games that defined what Sonic is at its core. And as the Sonic films have inspired a new generation of fans, the Blue Blur's history is now more accessible than ever!- Anniversary Mode is a life-saver for fans like myself, who have never had the skill to get far in retro games. Now that I don't have to worry about game-overs, I can properly explore the games without anxiety (or having to look up walkthroughs for Marble Zone.)- The many side-modes and time trial options allow for bite-sized gameplay sessions (which can also serve as training for the core game. Maybe someday I'll beat Classic Mode!)- The museum is a lovely collection of Classic Sonic music, videos and art (including, more surprisingly, every episode of Sonic Mania Adventures, and clips from the Sonic Symphony!) Part of me wishes they included entries from the 90s cartoons and comics... but as a fully Sega-approved collection, it's delightful.To wrap up, I especially recommend the game if, like me, you've been unable to get far in these games in the past. And even if you know these games inside and out, there's enough shakeups in the side-modes to get a fresher experience. In my opinion, Sonic Origins is Way Past Cool.

_childDocuments_.review: As a first timer to 3 out of 4 games in this collection, I've had a blast running through these games ^_^  - Sonic 1, though my least favorite, was still a good time. It's short, sweet and full of some fun levels and themes. Taking it slower and not rushing through levels made getting by the many obstacles less of a pain!- Sonic CD had perhaps my favorite soundtrack out of the 4,and I only listened to the JP soundtrack! Searching the past robot transporters wasn't worth it to me, so I just went for the time stones and I think it made for a much breezier experience   - Sonic 2 is a very lean, mean, thoroughly fun and succinct package! Levels are well designed and a great length; they're not as long as Sonic 3&K but not as short as 1 and CD,  While the special stages could get my goat sometimes, I really like how easy they were to access! - Sonic 3&K definitely encouraged more exploration; the other three games you could zoom through without a care in the world if you were good at dodging obstacles, but here it felt like while there was a lot of speedy moments, you also needed to take your time,  solve small puzzles and platform well to prevail. It felt different, but I enjoyed the more deliberate approach! And because I 100%-ed vanilla Mania's blue spheres both on PC and Switch before, tackling blue spheres here was like putting on a pair of warm slippers. :) That's just talking about the games themselves though. Talking about some of the features exclusive to Origins Plus: - Amy feels so fun to play! Her little double jump and the extra bit of safety her hammer provides when jumping into enemies is invaluable. - Anniversary mode is a blast. I love not having to worry about lives, and being able to restart special stages instantly made it easy to practice them and consequently, made  them way less frustrating then they might've otherwise been!- The widescreen aspect ratio is wonderful, and makes it way easier to see what's coming horizontally speaking! Helpful for Sonic 1 in particular. - The opening/ending cinematics were lovely, and were fun bookends to the experience! - As of the time of writing, I haven't yet played with mission mode much. I'm waffling as to whether or not to mess around with that. Saying all that, I know the current asking price can be a big ask for some. so if you're having doubts as to whether this will be worth it to you, you can't go wrong waiting for a sale.  For myself at least, I can say that this was a thoroughly pleasant experience that was worth the cost of entry :)

_childDocuments_.review: I never expected cancer to be a part of my story. I was a healthy, active guy in my mid-30s, working as a software engineer and enjoying all the things life had to offer. But when I started experiencing unexplained fatigue and a nagging pain in my abdomen, I knew something wasn't right.The diagnosis was a shock: stage 3 colon cancer. I couldn't believe it. How could this happen to me? I was young, fit, and had no family history of the disease. But as I sat in the oncologist's office, staring at the bleak statistics on the screen in front of me, I knew I had to fight.The next few months were a blur of chemotherapy and radiation treatments, hospital stays and endless rounds of medication. I lost my hair, my energy, and my sense of hope. The worst part was the isolation. I couldn't work, I couldn't socialize, I couldn't even go out in public without feeling self-conscious and vulnerable.One day, as I lay on my couch feeling sorry for myself, my younger brother came to visit. He had brought a gift with him: a copy of Sonic Origins, a collection of the Sonic classics from the 1990s that I had always wanted to play but never had the chance.I was skeptical at first. How was playing a video game going to help me with cancer? But as I started to immerse myself in the game, something miraculous happened. For the first time in months, I forgot about my illness. I was no longer a cancer patient, I was Sonic, a hedgehog running at the speed of light, saving animals from the evil Dr. Eggman.As I explored the two-dimensional, pixelated worlds of Sonic the Hedgehog, I felt a sense of purpose and accomplishment that I had been missing in my real life. I was using my mind, my reflexes, my problem-solving skills to overcome obstacles and defeat Eggman's contraptions. It was a welcome break from the constant worry and pain that had become my daily reality.Over time, as I played more and more of each game, I started to feel a sense of hope and determination returning to me. I began to think about the future, to set goals and make plans. I started exercising again, eating better, and taking care of myself. I even started to think about returning to work.And then, after what felt like an eternity, the day finally came when my oncologist declared me cancer-free. It was a moment of pure joy and relief, and I knew that I owed a lot of my recovery to the hours I had spent playing Sonic Origins.Looking back, I realize that the game was more than just a distraction or a hobby for me. It was a lifeline, a way to escape the darkness of cancer and find a sense of meaning and purpose in my life. It gave me the strength and courage to keep fighting, even when the odds seemed stacked against me.And now, as I stand here, a cancer survivor, I am grateful for every moment I spent playing Sonic Origins. It truly made a difference in my darkest hour.

_childDocuments_.review: As you can see, the game came out to some "mixed" reception, and I think the opinion of each person largely boils down to what their "relationship" to Sonic is.If you are a series veteran, there's not much to see here. All 4 games here have been available even in widescreen form one way or another (the 2011 remaster of Sonic CD was delisted from Steam just a few days before Origins came out, the ~2013 remaster Sonic 1 & 2 is available on mobile platforms – though you need a tablet with a proper controller to enjoy them, or jump through hoops to run Android apps on PC –, and Sonic 3 already had the fan-remaster called "A.I.R.", again, offering wide screen support), previous compilations like Mega Collection or Sonic Jam had better "museum" content, and "missions" are basically like various small custom ROM hacks.If you are relatively new to – or have an "on and off" relationship with – the Sonic franchise (maybe completing it once or twice over the years, but never getting the good endings etc.), Sonic Origins is a really great way to jump in now:- You can play the game with infinite lives, and even retry special stages, finally putting the chaos emeralds within reach for causals like me. You are still incentivised to explore though: collecting coin TVs (placed where extra life TVs used to be), or getting 100 rings gives you a coin, which you can use to unlock museum content (see below); retrying a special stage also costs 1 coin.- The game saves upon reaching checkpoints, so if you have just 5 minutes to play, you can. (The emulated versions, also delisted now unfortunately, also kind of had this option with save states: but a huge drawback there was that the temptation to "cheese through" the game, by saving e.g. during boss fights, was too high. Now you have the flexibility without taking *too much* of the challenge away.) Some of you might not care about this, but I really hate the fact that I can't play Sonic Mania unless I surely know in advance that I have 20-30 minutes to spare, because it only saves at the end of zones, requiring you to complete both acts in one sitting (which, depending on your age, or your ability to defeat bosses on first try, might be trivial, but for many of us, it isn't).- Missions are actually fun (and more accessible to "casuals" than ROM hacks) and not too hard (which again might be a con for veterans) – they are, in fact, a great way to practice situations you might come across while playing the main games, and they are also efficient coin sources (which, again, you need for retrying special stages).- All games have brand new intro and outro cutscenes, which are really well made. I enjoyed them a lot more than I thought I would!- The only part of the package that's truly disappointing, no matter how you look at it, is the museum mode. It couldn't really be more uninteresting, which is quite a feat considering they had 30+ years of material to gather from. Sonic Jam (the first major compilation of Sonic 1-3) came out like a decade after the first game (maybe even less), and it had a lot more interesting stuff in it.All in all, I'm having a lot of fun with this package despite already owning these games in other forms – but depending on your situation / priorities, you may or may not have the same feeling. I hope the above points will help you determine that.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever heard of a game where the developer had to save its integrity on Twitter and call out the publisher for how rushed, unfinished and buggy the final build of the game is? No? Well, then you're in for a ride.After Sonic 06, Sonic Boom Rise of Lyric, Sonic Forces and Sonic Colors Ultimate, SEGA released another game riddled with bugs and low quality. SEGA rushed this game and didn't want to delay it, because they thought it might be neat to release it on the same day Sonic 1 released, which is a nice homage, but they still don't get that a rushed product is a problem for the devs and the actual buyers. It is like using washing powder for your cake each time, wondering why it tastes bad.Now, before I get into it, I will mention the actual positive side.This game is great in terms of presentation. It is so nice to have the actual islands Sonic ventures on be visualized. They make the Sonic world seem way more connected. Furthermore, the cutscenes are still wonderfully animated. They clearly love the Toei Sonic style, and I wouldn't have it in any other way. While most of the cutscenes shown are only for the opening, others are for the start and ending of the games, which leads into a connected story.The mission mode is also pretty fun. I haven't played all missions yet, but it seems like each mission has its own stage, reminding me of Sonic Generations, and what can I say, they do their job in delivering some extra challenge.The last good thing is that you can retry special stages if you fail. Back then it was quite frustrating, but this way it actually is fun to hunt the Chaos Emeralds/Time Stones.Now, let's slowly dip our toes into the depths.The Sonic CD cutscenes weren't re-animated. I think it would be a nice novelty to keep the original cutscenes in the museum, unfortunately the game uses the old 4:3 cutscenes for the story itself too. That is quite inconsistent and makes it seem like a fan mod.Next is the drop dash, while it's nice to have the drop dash, I just cannot fathom how bad it is in this game. The drop dash in Sonic Origins is more of an instant spin dash rather than the actual drop dash from Mania. Meaning, you lack air control, you cannot redirect Sonic. That is quite frustrating to use. It is nice to have it, but the way they implemented it makes him feel like a car.Now.....the bugs. I would've hoped not to encounter bugs, since I rarely do, but in this game I actually got the most annoying and frustrating bugs possible. If Tails in Sonic 2 is flying whilst you jump into the Special Stage, you'd be able to hear his flying sounds the entire stage's time. Even worse was the fact that I beat Sonic 2's final boss, and when the end screen appeared, I started to realize I was softlocked. I couldn't continue in any way. I was stuck, waited 2 minutes and then just gave up, restarted the game and had to beat the final boss A G A I N. Next is Sonic 3. Sonic 3 is a mess. Next to Sonic changing into the foreground layer, even though during the cutscene he should've been in the background, he also clipped through multiple objects, through layers of the stages, leaving me softlocked a good few times, but they also completely messed with his physics. Sonic in this game is way too fast. He bonks his head against walls he never was intended to hit, ruining the flow of the stage. He also isn't able to reach the heights he used to. I wasn't able to reach, for example, a Special Stage because they messed with Sonic's jump, leading to him not gaining enough height.The DLC for Sonic Origins is such a cash grab. Remember when they tried to monetize Super Sonic in Forces? They literally just put a few missions in here, add an island camera view which should be in the base game, and rip the old models from Generations/Forces, put them in here, stiffly animating them. These extra 5 bucks should've been in the package, even the price is question worthy. Sonic Mania released for half of that and was more of a new game than this is. Hell, I'd even say it makes more sense to buy Sonic Mania and Sonic Generations instead, since you get the best out of both worlds with both being half original/half remake-type games.Also, where is the time attack mode? I mean....for a Sonic game there should be a time attack mode, where you can actually pick the stages and speedrun them individually, just like in Mania.Last, but not least, is a direct question. Where is the new character? You featured Amy so prominently in literally each promotional material, even the ending clearly hints at Amy maybe being playable, but she isn't. It feels like the devs really wanted to make her playable, but realized there wasn't enough time.Sonic Origins might be the 22nd way to play Sonic 2, but it is far from the best. SEGA should learn to stop using Sonic like a GTA free money glitch, 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: As a casual fan who'd only played the Sonic titles a handful of time, Origins was a fun way to play through this early part of the series. While I'm aware that this version launched with a number of glitches and issues I did not personally experience or at least notice any during my runs. Sonic 1, 2, 3 & Knuckles, and CD are all given a widescreen presentation as well as an Anniversary mode with the removal of the lives system, the ability to retry bonus stages, auto saving for all games, animated cutscenes and other quality of life features. There are also a number of short challenges to attempt for each game, boss rushes, mirror mode, and other fluff. While I didn't dabble in it myself, it appears you can also play through the original versions of the games, with the original lives system and without the widescreen adjustment.I was a fan of the removal of lives, particularly in Sonic 1 and 2 which could see you easily sent back to the beginning by running out of lives and continues. I do appreciate challenge but playing these titles as an adult, we don't have the amount of free time we did back in the day to do full game runs over and over hoping to make progress.You don't have save states or rewind, so completing the games still feels like a challenge, just not as punishing as before. Likewise, the ability to retry bonus stages using special coins earned from various challenges and things throughout the collection makes becoming Super Sonic and getting the good endings less of an ordeal- those bonus areas can be really unfair without it.I really enjoyed the widescreen presentation here, with the original pixel art of the games still being preserved and to my eyes, looking better than ever. Looks aside, Sonic and friends move fast to say the least, and any extra screen real estate in front of you keeps you from feeling blindsided by enemies, traps and pits, and makes the games more fun to play. There was a controversial decision made to replace some of the Sonic 3 music due to the infamous rights issues surrounding the title's soundtrack. It seems that they used music that was originally in the prototypes of Sonic 3, and just finished those up for this release, so there's still an air of authenticity about it. Without the nostalgia of the original music, it didn't make too much difference to me having this changed, and I think which piece of music is better really depends on the song. As to the games themselves, my relationship with Sonic has always been a little complicated. I never had Sega systems growing up, but was endlessly curious about the Genesis and the games I'd see advertised. On finally trying Sonic 1 many years later, perhaps on the Dreamcast of all places, I was underwhelmed. I've come around on it a bit, but it's certainly a rough around the edges game. Sonic 2 was much more my style, with a faster, more fun and more fair level design, a brisk pace, nice music and graphics, it was just Sonic but better. We even got a new friend, Tails the Fox, to accompany us on the adventure. Sonic 3 and Knuckles I've only now completed for the first time. While initially not a fan of the sprawling long stages, the game really grew on me, and I appreciated the creativity on display and the way they really pushed the system, and ultimately combined two games into one epic adventure. This title has the most replay value by far, and you could probably play the same stages many times and still find new areas and secrets. Sonic CD remains the odd man out of this group, feeling like a sequel to many of the worst aspects of Sonic 1, with some interesting visual and audio flash due to the CD format. Ambitious with multiple time periods to visit for each zone, and a focus on exploration, I found it impressive from a technical standpoint but ultimately boring to play, and eventually frustrating in the last third.This is clearly not the ultimate compilation that long time die hard Sonic fans were hoping for but for me, it works very well as an introduction to everything Sonic and may have become a little underrated at this time.

_childDocuments_.review: I've owned these games in multiple forms since the early 90s, and still play them regularly but I bought this package out of some strange sense of obligation since these were some of my favorite games as a kid and figured the new animations and challenge modes might make it worth the purchase. Hoped the games themselves would be solid versions, but I never did expect "Sonic 3 Complete" levels of customization. I'm really disappointed though, not surprised, but disappointed. I  expected the glaring issue of Sonic 3's soundtrack licensing preventing a full re-release, and thankfully modders have fixed that already.  Sorry if you're on console though I guess?  I didn't expect muffled audio throughout that sounds like 128kbps mp3, lots of weird physics bugs that I've never run into in other versions, removal of options that were in the mobile ports these are based on, and an almost complete lack of customization.  What if I want to play the harder Sonic 3 variants of some of these stages rather than the S3&K version?  Hell, what if I want to play the original S3&K version instead of the "Anniversary" version?  There are no options here.  Sonic Jam in the mid-90s on Saturn was much more fully featured than this 2022 game.  Not only did they completely remake the games for that new engine which resulted in smooth gameplay you wouldn't have got from emulation at the time, but they offered multiple difficulties and level layouts and the museum mode was gigantic compared to the one here.  Sega should have just released that game with some resolution bumps where it could be added!  I'll mess around with the challenge modes a bit longer maybe, but Origins will never be my definitive go-to version if I want to play through any of these games. And I say that even after modding Origins to a tolerable state adding back in the removed songs and applying a decent crt shader. The released version is an incompetent embarrassment and I feel bad for anyone stuck with this on consoles or experiencing Sonic 3 for the first time in this form. Sonic 1 Forever, Sonic 2 Absolute, and Sonic 3 AIR completely outclass Origins in every way and show the difference between passion projects and soulless nostalgia cash-ins.  I really wish this collection had been excellent, for us fans and for Sega.  Imagine if this had lead to other Sega series getting polished anniversary re-releases.  Shinobi, Golden Axe, Streets of Rage, etc.  Maybe the fans will come through there as well, Sega sure won't.

_childDocuments_.review: This was probably the most lukewarm compilation of Sonic games I have played, having played them since thee Genesis/Mega Drive days. Sonic 1 and 2 anniversary were actually quite okay and up to par with what is to be expected. The bosses were slightly tweaked for 16:9 and the sound quality and music all sounded very nice.Sonic CD was a middling experience albeit par, nothing out of what is to be expected. The main crux of the problem comes down to Sonic 3 & KnucklesThe sound quality for this game is atrocious. By no means for this price point with this few titles can this be overlooked. And I am not only speaking of the omitted OSTs from Stages 4-6, the entire game sounds like it was remixed through a pillow. I am not an audiophile by any means, but this was a step to far for me. That and the visuals being overall blurry makes this the weakest in the collection by a mile as it comes to remastering.As an aside, Blue Sphere now looks extremely smooth and they actually have it as a standalone mode, which is awesome for those who enjoy it. As for the extras...Mission mode is very meh. I didn't find a lot of the challenges that fun and it was really just given hoops to jump through to keep you busy for a little bit.The museum is actually very cool. I am not into extras like that usually, but this is definitely a shining point to the game as well. Overall this game at this price point is unacceptable, especially with the state of S3&K. Either wait for a sale or pray for a patch for this one,

_childDocuments_.review: A new popular trend among videogame publishers seems to be the removal of old games on digital distributions platforms, only to sell them again as part of a “new” collection afterwards – which is exactly what happened with , which launched after SEGA delisted previous version of the included classic  games. As such,  currently remains the only way to play these games on Steam, if you didn’t buy the older versions before. This would be less of a problem if  was worth its surprisingly high asking price of 29,99€ for the base game – but unfortunately, it just feels like a half-hearted cash-grab for fans and newcomers alike.On paper,  includes the first four main Sonic games, three of which originally released on the Sega Genesis () and one on the Sega CD (). However, while one might expect these original games to be emulated as part of the collection,  actually includes the 2011 () and 2013 () Retro Engine remasters by Christian Whitehead instead. As such remasters didn’t exist for  yet, the  team was tasked with creating one for  specifically.For purists, it has to be noted that despite the name, these “remasters” are more than just graphically enhanced versions of the original games, as  now includes the previously scrapped  for example. Notably for a franchise known for its soundtracks, some music tracks from  have also been replaced entirely . Unfortunately,  doesn’t offer the option to play the original games through emulation instead, which means that the actual origins of the series aren’t part of this supposed “Origins” collection - while there is a “classic mode” for each game, it’s essentially just an option for the original 4:3 aspect ratio.One of the new additions to these remasters is the “anniversary mode”, which mainly offers widescreen support as well as unlimited lives. This is also used during the new “story mode” of , which allows you to play through all four included titles consecutively, with new, very short (1-2min) cutscenes serving as a small narrative bridge between the games. Other news features of  include a really basic “Museum” mode featuring sketches, songs, etc to unlock, a “boss rush” (= fight against the game’s bosses in succession) and “mirror” mode (= world is flipped from left to right) for each title, as well as a “mission” mode – sixty standalone 2-3min challenges (e.g. destroy five enemies in a certain time) across the four games with different ranks to achieve. Overall, the new features of  are pretty standard inclusions for these types of anniversary collections and far from substantial enough on their own to warrant a purchase for dedicated fans.Oddly enough,  features a 10,99€ expansion pack (), which does offer the type of content that would make the base game more worthwhile for dedicated fans, such as offering Amy Rose as a playable character in all four games as well as Knuckles in ,  to accommodate his playstyle. Locking content that should’ve been in the lacking base game behind DLC just feels like a rude move, especially after the backlash SEGA already received when it came to the . All in all, as an anniversary collection,  is not offering many arguments for a purchase if you’re a dedicated  fan that already owns the games included in this collection in one way or another.On the flipside, I wouldn’t recommend  to newcomers to the series either - and I can say this especially because  has been my first  game as well. While the included games certainly had a huge impact on popular culture, they haven’t age particularly well in my opinion and might be more of an acquired taste these days. While the early outings of popular  rival Mario for example, such as the original  (1985), have certainly aged as well, I do consider them to be a lot less frustrating than what’s on offer in  – and I certainly wouldn’t have cared about beating them if I wasn’t granted unlimited lives through the “story” mode of this collections.My frustrations mainly stem from three things in particular: For one, while these classic  games want you to reach high speeds as you go through the levels, they also regularly punish you for doing so, mostly by placing obstacles and enemies in a way that are too hard to spot the first time around (e.g. buried enemies). To add to this, during some city zones in particular I periodically had a hard time making out what’s supposed to a non-interactable decorative element and what’s not. Second, the included  games occasionally include gameplay elements which are only used during one level but never properly explained – such as the infamous  during the Carnival Night zone of , an obstacle which needs to be controlled by holding up/down on the d-pad: a mechanic that isn’t hinted at or used anywhere else in the games. And third and final, there’s the boss fights – while I appreciate the game offering a lot of unique boss encounters, some of their hitboxes can be an absolute nightmare when figuring out the weak spots.Combined, these issues made my time with  a much more frustrating experience than I expected – while I quite enjoyed the visuals and music, I never felt quite in control of the flow compared to my time with all of the  platformers for example. That said, I do feel like offering a save state & reload system, similar to the one used in the  collections for example, would’ve been a great help in reducing some of my issues here. Additionally, it might’ve been a good idea to offer a more modernised  experience through the “anniversary” mode with more substantial additions to enhance the overall experience for new players than just widescreen options and unlimited lives. Ideally,  would’ve offered three game options – playing the original games, playing the originals games with slight enhancements (e.g. widescreen, save states) and a substantially modernised version for new players. Instead, there are none of the original games and only “remasters” with small enhancements, satisfying neither fans nor newcomers.Concluding, I’d only recommend  to either dedicated fans of the series who want to own the included games once more or newcomers who are as bullish about getting into a franchise by starting from the beginning as me – just keep in mind that these games are more than 30 years old by now and little is done to accommodate their age.

_childDocuments_.review: I pre-ordered this and was extremely excited for release day. Starting the game up on story mode and playing through the games seems fine enough, but between the all the bugs, compressed sounding audio, blurry visuals, Denuvo and the wholly uncalled for egregious and worthless DLC scheme straight up disrespects fans who paid full price for this game. Sad to say, after playing a bit for the past few days it's clear that what should have finally been the definitive way to experience the classic Sonic series but instead, Sega was looking for a quick payout just to arbitrarily release this thing on Sonic's 31st anniversary. The thing about this collection is, it's at the very least playable. That's why you see so many positive reviews mixed in with the bad. It's still the games you know and love and if viewed from a certain perspective they're fine  but notice how most of them still have some thing bad to say about it? Believe me, I want to love this game too. I stayed optimistic for a while before realizing how truly problematic this is not just for  release, but for the future of Sega and Sonic as a whole. Releasing a product in such a state when the people they contracted to assist making it knew about the problems and even asked if they could be allowed to fix them is shameful on Sega's part. It also sounds like they don't want to patch it post-release. This should not and cannot continue. It should not be allowed to be the industry standard.Sega needs to swallow their pride and stop interfering with the fantastic work studios like Headcannon are providing for them. We've already seen the potential in Mania and even the modding and fan game community. The answers are right in front of you. Please fix this.

I don't really feel like playing because of the keyboard issues, I just want to use the arrow keys as the movement keys. $45 for a game they're most likely going to leave in the dust like Sonic 06 is such a shame.Edit: Finally completed it after the update. Perhaps I was a bit harsh on it as it's not as bad as it seemed to me after a playthrough. Could use a few fixes here in there, with the jank hitboxes in Sonic 1 making me hit things that are above me, the disappearing platforms and objects in Sonic 2 after doing something, the cannons in Oil Ocean sticking me into the floor making me restart the level, the Death Egg sprite appearing after the Sonic 3 final boss when falling down and the copious amounts of times I've been crushed in Sonic 3 because I was Super/Hyper Sonic (however, I played a lot of Sonic 3 Complete so I forget if this was in the original game or not). This was super apparent however when I got crushed by the Sandopolis boss when I did the hold right trick on it with Hyper Sonic. Also lost my rings hitting a spike line in the Mushroom Hill boss fight after I defeated it, again, not sure if it was always there or a Sonic 3 Complete fix. The music all around was alright, some sounds didn't sound quite right and smooth, like the Emerald jingle after collecting a Chaos Emerald in Sonic 2, or in the Sonic 3 special stage after I got 100 rings, the music reset and completely messed up the speedup of the song. _childDocuments_.review: I want to say that I did not receive any crashes or performance issues like many others have said. The game ran perfectly fine for me, but when taking a look at task manager I can definitely tell that this game absolutely needs to be optimized.Starting with the positives, I'm a massive fan of the QoL changes. Lives are incredibly outdated and I love being able to play through these games without worrying about having to go all the way back to the beginning of the stage if I die. I'm also thrilled the Drop Dash is here from Mania and that it seems to be getting adopted as a mainstay in Classic Sonic's move set. It really helps keep the pace of the game up. This is also the first time we're getting Sonic 1, 2 and 3&K officially in widescreen. The version of Sonic 2 is also the newer one with the cut zone, previously only available on mobile. I haven't played much of them yet, but I really enjoy the mission mode. I loved that kinda stuff in the Mega Man Legacy Collections and I'm really happy we get something like that here.Unfortunately, the games aren't presented as cleanly as one might expect. There are complaints that the games are "blurry", which I don't think is necessarily the case. I was messing around with the settings and turned off VSync and turned on Anti-aliasing, which made the game SUPER blurry. But the games themselves, playing the game with the default settings, look pretty much like the Genesis games extended into widescreen. They don't really feel HD at all and it's unfortunate that it lacks the crispness I would have expected from a $40 release of games that have already been remastered before. Also, I swear that all of the sound in Sonic 3&K sounds muffled compared to the other games. Maybe it's just me. My ears got used to it.In the end, it's fine. I played through story mode. Knuckles isn't playable in CD for whatever reason, but I'm not a CD fan so that doesn't bother me too bad. None of the unlockables really matter. The new tracks for Sonic 3 are mid. Ice Cap Zone in particular feels drastically different without the original music. Wish they were able to get the rights or whatever, but it is what it is. The games themselves are still pretty solid. Probably not worth the price, especially if you already own the games here.Christian Whitehead absolutely should have been in charge of this project and it should have been $10-$15 cheaper. It is a bit of a disappointing collection, but the games themselves are still very good which is why I'm recommending it. At sale price.ORIGINS PLUS UPDATE:With the release of Origins Plus, the game has dropped in price, released a new character, and emulations of the Game Gear games are available. Amy plays fine. She's basically Sonic with a weaker drop dash and better instashield. The Game Gear games have never been great, but they're nice to have and speaking from experience Tails Adventure is a real gem. As a Deluxe edition owner, I kinda feel like I got screwed because of the pricing. Should have been free, but I can recommend Origins Plus even more now because of the cheaper price and extra content.

_childDocuments_.review: Checked out this game just awhile ago. Honestly, it's a pretty good introduction to the Sonic games. You're given plenty of QoL features like being able to retry the Special Stages and the prompts for how to play the games being readily available to you. These games are the remakes on mobile ported to PC alongside a brand new remake of the third game. The infamous section in Carnival Night Zone now has telegraphs for what to do so it won't result in you getting stuck at first. Though, it doesn't mean that it doesn't have anything for returning fans. The new version of blue spheres has some really great, detailed artwork for the menus and the stages that are introduced have some interesting challenges to take on. The Mission Mode albeit a few issues, works pretty well and has challenges that can be worth your while.  The cutscenes added to the games' beginning and end are pretty nice to see and have things left only in the Japanese manuals readily showcased in-game for newcomers and returning fans alike to check out. While Sonic 3 has new bugs here and there, the game still has a lot of new additions that make the game play much better than the originals. Outside of some optimization issues that I can't get into, I highly recommend this game. It's ultimately a collection with love and care put into making these games playable in one seamless experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game could've been an even greater, more definitive version of a Classic Sonic Collection. Christian Whitehead, Headcannon, animation studio Neko Productions and their director Tyson Heese clearly cared a great amount for their work on this product, but SEGA decided that a game that works is better than a game that works, and has even more careful, love and detail put into its entire structure and design. The Sonic games remastered by Christian Whitehead and Headcannon and implemeted by SEGA were hastily shoved into the port, being Sonic 1, CD, and 2, are missing minute and major fixes like audio and mechanics. The end result is a solid way to play Sonic 1, CD, 2, and 3&K all together, but it misses the options of Mania like turning on and off certain mechanics like Drop Dash, Super Peel Out, and more playable characters. Digging into the files of the game reveals cut content most definitely dropped because of SEGA's desire for more money, as opposed to a finished, fully cohesive release with attentive patches. It's clear that SEGA did the Challenges too since the quality is okay at best. All the work done by Christian Whitehead, Headcannon, Neko Productions and Tyson Heese is clearly presented with care, concern, appreciation, and love, for Sonic and fans. They have all the ingredients for the greatest Sonic experiences, but SEGA is an unmovable roadblock in this path. Overall, Sonic Origins is a great collection if you just want to experience Classic Sonic games all in one place in a 16:9 screen ratio, but there are so many more additions that could've made this a top tier collection of remasters.Buy this game when it's half off at $20, not at the overpriced selling point of $40.You can always get Sonic 1 Forever, Sonic 2 Absolute, and Sonic 3 A.I.R as a free alternative created by loving fans without the barrier of SEGA.I don't like SEGA's capitalistic, ignorant business practices so I don't recommend this game. Despite all the extra features, get the ROMs for free. If you really want all of the games in one place with extra features, then this collection is worth it on sale. Despite all my criticisms of the game and SEGA, this game is still a decent collection. It just could've been so much more.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:1. It's four of the best platformers of the 16-bit era.2. The new animated cutscenes are really great.The bad:1. The menus take forever to load. Playing 30-year-old games on an even moderately modern PC should be zippy quick, not slow as molasses.2. It's kind of expensive for what you get. Maybe if it included 3D Blast or Spinball or something, the price they're charging would be more justifiable.The notably odd:1. They replaced all the Michael Jackson songs from Sonic 3 with more generic songs, presumably due to a licensing issue. This can be fixed with a mod so it's more of a slight inconvenience than an actual problem, but still worth mentioning.2. The achievements are weird. For example, no achievements for getting all the Chaos Emeralds, in any of the games.Overall I'd say it's worthwhile if you don't already have these games. But maybe consider Sonic Mania instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always been a fan of the classic sonic games for multiple reasons. Each game creates a fun adventure with super fast speed and spin dash abilities. What's more they have allowed players to turn super form in any level in the games, with or without sound test or stage select. Also, the games have great music playing within the backgrounds. In addition, the special and bonus stages create mini-games for the players during the adventure, such as slot machines and labyrinth mazes. Furthermore, Sonic CD has incredible time-travel abilities that allow you to literally go to the past and create an amazing future with JP or US soundtracks. Additionally, Anniversary mode allows new players to play with INFINITE LIVES, RETRIES on the SPECIAL STAGES, in widescreen HD. Moreover, Classic mode provides a nostalgic feeling of challenging game-play with limited lives, continues, and opportunities. Plus, the game gear classics create a new 8-bit experience to players who never used a Game Gear before, including racing, pinball, and puzzle games. Finally, Sonic 3&K provides both Hyper forms and Blue Sphere challenges that make the effort worth it. I've always enjoyed the sonic classics, and I hope they will continue bringing more challenges as I take on each story in anniversary, classic, and mirror mode.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, a lot actually, BUTThe question being asked is: would you recommend this game to other players? My answer is a big NO.Dropping $40 isn't a big deal to me, but I understand many find that unfair, especially if you're on a budget. My biggest question is why does this even exist?! But before I get into that, I will explain why I bought it. I got it because of the widescreen, achievements, and the ability to easily mix and match mods without having to patch a dedicated rom. That's honestly it. Classic Sonic is a childhood favorite, literally, so this collection has something special for me.Now onto why I could not, and will not recommend this game. It's honestly a waste. It's a waste of money and talent. There are many iterations that exist for each of these games. I grew up with the original cartridges and the Sonic collection on PC many years ago and that did enough for me. The games have been available for pretty much every console ever, and I think you would save money if you just got them individually. Back in 2007 I got the lock-on for only 99 cents online!Honestly, I don't see how this is worth it for anyone, even for those who are new to Sonic. Just get each game one at a time, and see if you enjoy them. Why buy a $40 lifeless collection if you have no idea if you will even like a single game. This collection was clearly for people who already love Sonic, and love the classic games. But here's the thing, if you don't like just one of the included games, instantly the collection becomes a complete rip-off. Personally, I don't like Sonic CD at all, so already I'm screwed, but as I mentioned before, it didn't bother me.This collection is certainly nowhere near perfect. As many have stated, it's filled with bugs that certainly didn't exist in the originals, and there was certainly odd things that occurred that I know didn't happen in the originals. One thing that bothered crap out of me was the jumping felt off. If you were to jump and land and try to jump again the instant you landed, it doesn't register your input. I have no idea what's that's about, but that has costed me rings more than I can care to remember and certainly wasn't an issue I had with the original. As mentioned the physics felt a little weird as well.When this game was announced, I had no idea why people were so hyped up about it. It just looked like a lazy cash grab. Even from the trailer it didn't look special.In conclusion, honestly, do yourself a favor and just get the games individually. Don't waste your time with this piece of crap of a collection. It really has nothing special to offer for anyone.
