_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I'd say this is a solid package. 4 great games all in 1 package.(+) Coins & Museum================I really enjoyed the way coins are used (as weird as it is for a Sonic game to have them). As long as you have a coin to spare, you can retry a special stage. It's also pretty neat to use them in the museum. Speaking of, I really enjoyed the museum's content. I've watched the Sonic CD intro a lot since purchasing this game lol(+) Cutscenes================The new cutscenes are beautifully animated.(-) Price================Is this a great game? Definitely! Is it worth $40? Not really. Unless you really want to play this as soon as possible, I recommend waiting to get this game for a cheaper price. Also consider that there are better, more cost-efficient ways to experience these titles.(-) Sonic 3 & Knuckles Soundtrack================This version of Sonic 3 & Knuckles does not include the original game's Michael Jackson OST. Instead, those tracks have been replaced by new tracks based on the original game's prototype soundtrack. I personally like the original prototypes more than their Sonic Origins counterparts. The new Launch Base Zone theme is still really good (in my opinion) regardless. RIP OG Ice Cap though :c(+) Sonic 3 Boss Fight (Big Arm)================I really liked that they re-added Big Arm (final boss of Sonic 3 standalone) for the Launch Base Act 2 boss fight.(+) Extra Features================I've been enjoying the boss rush and mission modes. The missions aren't much, but they're cool to have. Now as for the boss rush... that's something I've always wanted in a Sonic game. It's amazing to see one finally added to a collection like this. I'm a bit disappointed that they didn't include the minibosses from Sonic 3 & Knuckles, but I guess it's pretty self-explanatory why they didn't do that.(+) Unlimited Lives================You get unlimited lives in anniversary mode. This has made Labyrinth Zone in Sonic 1 a lot less frustrating for me. Also, I was was more willing to experiment with momentum in different stages as a result (especially in Sky Fortress Zone in Sonic 2).(+) Overall Presentation================This is a great package for newcomers overall.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought Sonic Origins despite all of the negative attention it was getting. I'm a diehard Sonic fan, so take my review with a huge grain of salt. Disclaimer - I did install 2 mods to enhance my experience, one to fix the blurry textures and the other to restore Sonic 3's original soundtrack. Is Sonic Origins the best way to play these 4 games? No, it really isn't and that's super unfortunate. However, I found myself enjoying it a great deal even though it is far from perfect. It is a very convenient package and the games themselves run fantastic. I played with a wired Saturn controller and did not perceive any input lag. It's a shame because clearly there was SOME love shown in making Sonic Origins, they just didn't go 100% with it. For it to truly be the definitive way to play Sonic, they need to add a lot more content/features such as changing music/options on the fly or adding cheats/debug etc. The museum unlockables are bad. You can google/youtube literally everything that is in there. The museum should have had unlockable Game Gear/Master System games or something more worth while. I really love the new animations before and after every game, although I wish there were extended versions of them you could watch elsewhere. Also, the "Classic" mode of every game is a waste of time. To be clear; THERE IS NO "TRUE" CLASSIC MODE. What you get instead is a 4:3 cropped version of the base game. It's borderline false advertising. I know I was pretty negative, but I'm still going to recommend it albeit with the caveat that it's not worth full retail price as it currently stands.

_childDocuments_.review: This collection is a fine way to experience Sonic The Hedgehog's Origins (pun intended). Those are great and this is a fine way to experience what made people fall in love with Sonic from 1991 to 1994! There's plenty of control customization so you can have the control scheme you want (though I wish there was the option to have 3 jump buttons like on the Genesis to make revving up Spin Dashes quicker. I recommend this collection, though most people should wait for a sale before picking it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Check out screenshot #6. Couldn't even be bothered to make sure the rankings don't spell out "A S S" huh?Another potentially great Sonic game rushed out the door to meet Sonic's anniversary. Again. Another missed opportunity for an "OK" game to be great. Again. All they had to do was ride the wave Sonic Mania created, and the movies have done a lot to help the reputation get better.  It's cool seeing the series get a win every few years, but this isn't one of them.Not quite as bad as the GTA DE Trilogy fiasco, but this one is up there. Glitchy, unpolished, and rushed- with less features than Mania launched with, and a REALLY greedy price model.  And if they really can't use the original tracks from Sonic 3, they should properly communicate why. This was just lazy.Between the modding scene fixes/passion projects, and Whitehead and Headcannon, the fans care more about making a good Sonic game than Sega does. Some of those guys do what you can't or won't do for FREE. I used to love Sega, they tried out a lot of new things stuff, some would say too *many* things hardware-wise, to the point where they were competing with themselves AND competitors. But they always tried new things, they were inventive. They were cool. They cared.Today's Sega mostly tries to emulate past successes (sometimes literally) and does the same goofy, lazy (and now greedy) acts with the Sonic series time and time and time again. It feels like loving and rooting for a sports team that always loses, but your passionate fanbase keeps showing up for your games, loss after loss. Just in the hopes that maybe, just maybe the underdog will make a satisfying comeback. I've personally been waiting 21 years, and these chilli-dogs don't exactly taste like chili anymore.Is it realistically as bad as everyone says? No. The animated cutscenes and extra screen viewing space are really nice. But right now with the bugs, missing content and lack of features it just isn't worth the asking price. I'm waiting for more mod fixes, and, out of sheer curiosity, to see what Sega does about the poor reception. I'm not mad, I'm just disappointed.Hot air rant aside, mods can turn this into something really special. Something we should have gotten to begin with.

_childDocuments_.review: Should you buy Sonic Origins?TLDR:No, and you should probably boycott SEGA.First of all.. This game is online only. Which means you cannot play it without an internet connection. No steam deck offline play and no playing Sonic during internet outages, among numerous other things. This is a very anti consumer practise and it needs to be boycotted. This game should be playable offline.Next, Denuvo. Another anti consumer practise that needs to be boycotted... this is nothing but bloatware. 7gb for games that can seriously be no more than a few hundred mb...? How much junk have SEGA added to my system? How much anti cheat spyware crap is in this game? It uses 16gb of ram while in the menus alone, which leads me to complain about the fact the game lags on low end computers. This is where a game like Sonic Mania shines, you can tell it wasn't created as a cash grab by a half baked team, and was instead created by sonic fans such as Christian Whitehead and Stealth.That leads me onto my next complaint. Which is another anti consumer practise and ANOTHER reason to boycott this game (and SEGA as a whole)... When this game was released, SEGA delisted all the original roms, so there is now no easy legal way to obtain the original games on modern tech. This is just pure anti consumer, forcing people to buy the new inferior product, seriously, that's bad practise in every scenario and SEGA have fallen messes in my view, they are no longer a company that I will support if this is the practises they are pushing. Especially with them pushing NFTs on all their new upcoming games. They are here to extract cash at this point, and nothing more. Be aware of this when giving them your money.Now this delisting wouldn't be so bad if the "classic mode" in this game was actually classic mode, you know, the original games in their untouched original format? But guess what... "classic mode" is still the new rebuilt games. All SEGA have done is cut the aspect ratio down to 4:3 and give lives instead of coins.. which means "classic mode" has all the new mechanics (spin dash, drop dash, ect), and it has all the new glitches and errors.. therefore the games do not play the same as the true classic games at all. You would have thought dumping the classic roms in the game instead would have been easier, cheaper, and made more sense. But nope.Next (and this one isn't a big deal for casual players, BUT it is significantly important considering this is supposed to be a definitive collection of the classic games), the games do not play the same as the classics. There are changes in speed, timing and level design, which introduce new problems such as in Sonic 3; where if you reach max speed, you will be thrown into spikes and other obstacles that would never have hit you before on the original game because the level was designed around Sonics correct speed. The Sky Chase Act on  Sonic 2 is another example that really stands out. In this level all the badniks move at all the wrong times compared with the original game. There are also changes to the hitboxes, you can run into objects and be crushed in places where you would never have been crushed before, even when you aren't even within crushing distance. I've never been punished so much for going fast in a Sonic game... this is a serious issue for me, I hate it, and I don't think it can be fixed its a game flaw caused by multiple conflicting issues.I also have to say that the inability to have lives while on anniversary mode is ridiculous. Give us the option to swap those stupid coins for lives and continues, the coins mean nothing. This IS NOT the definitive way to play Sonic. This game is a half hearted cash grab in most respects. Love and care has clearly been taken in some places such as the new cut scenes which are awesome, but it is completely absent in others; such as the horrible music remakes, and severe lack of being able to move during a drop dash (EDIT: Roll lock has finally been fixed), not to mention the DLC cash grabbing.Price and downloadable content? The game is overpriced. It's a blatant cash grab by SEGA and its just not acceptable. They have stripped away parts of the game and then sold it back to the community, and as bad as that is, the DLC is also extremely over priced. £4 for some letterbox backgrounds? £4 for some songs...? Having to PAY TO ZOOM into the islands in the background?? These are all things should have been included by default. Sonic fans are being taken for a ride. £25 - £30 with ALL THE DLC and yes, maybe then you have a price worth paying... but £40 for everything is far too much considering it doesnt even have games such as Sonic Spinball and Knuckles Chaotix in the museum. The price of the DLC for what you get... it's pretty poor and very bad faith. (EDIT: and now to add insult to injury, SEGA are punishing their most loyal fans, pre order and deluxe edition owners of this game are now being charged a second time for DLC they already own if they want to upgrade to Sonic Origins Plus... and the games base price was dropped by £10 which means, if you didnt support SEGA on launch then you'll get more for less. SEGA could not get much more greedy, its pure cash extraction at this stage. The pre order and deluxe edition owners should have received this DLC for less than full price, if not free)Don't get me wrong THERE IS A GOOD GAME HERE. Mission mode is cool, and the new cartoon animations are brilliant, I really do like them! But if thats all you lack, then once again it's just not worth the price tag. There are far superior ways to play these games. The mission mode is little more than a rom hack.The new graphics truly are nice and Sonic 3 looks great, its by far the most noticeable change.Sonic 2 having the infamous Hidden Palace Zone is amazing too and its fantastic to finally have this on our systems, I love that it's finally accessible by default. But again £40 for that level and some mission modes? Sonic fans are being taken for a ride.Final take: Sonic Origins feels so good, yet it feels like its only 75% finished. It's not everything it could have been, and that 25% of lack luster cheapness and DLC cash grabbing isn't acceptable for a game of this magnitude. SEGA are killing their own product yet again with these stupid little things and its just greedy. SEGA really need to change their practises and update the game to its full potential.What has happened to the gaming industry? Its little more than an extortion racket these days, where you buy games broken and in parts and wait for updates on unfinished products, its a joke and this once again leaves a sour taste for the Sonic fan base and drops SEGAs reputation by another ton due to another fumbled release and cash extraction from loyal fans, I will never purchase another game on pre-order or even initial release thanks to the absolute mash of good and bad that this game is, I have yet again had my faith in SEGA (and the gaming industry as a whole) damaged and it's really starting to annoy me.This game has SO MUCH potential, continued support can make so much happen with this title and it could be by far the BEST sonic collection ever created. The menu is nice, the additional things like story mode are awesome! And as I said already, the new cutscenes linking the games together are incredible, it's old skool cool! But without at least adding additional things such as including the stripped out content (DLC) as standard, the game falls short. True DLC should have consisted of additional Sonic game remakes which could be added to the museum in game as time went on. Thats where the extra income for SEGA should have come from. (Not this double dipping they have tried to pull on everyone)Give classic sonic games the glory and respect they deserve and stop screwing around to squeeze money out of people! I'm sure many people would be happy to support SEGA and would happily buy additional museum DLC game remakes.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting collection for many reasons compared to SEGA's past attempts. First off, I'll preface this with the disclaimer that I do think it's a worthwhile purchase, but you should probably wait for a sale if you aren't a huge Sonic fan. The game is receiving updates to fix some bugs, and seemingly to even add new features. The game is only going to get better from here, and it'll get cheaper too, so there's no reason to get hasty with wanting to buy it right away. For example, in 1.0.4, S3&K had new cheat codes added to it that weren't there in previous versions, and fixed probably the most annoying bug in the game.The good:- 16:9 aspect ratio- Brand new story cutscenes- Mission mode- Gallery mode, featuring new concept art we've never seen before- For people who are not great at old arcadey games, the coin system makes the game a lot easier- Drop dash- Brand new remaster of Sonic 3 & Knuckles, which hasn't even received a port in years- The most beautiful remaster of Sonic CD's cutscenes we've ever had- Plenty of new, beautiful sprites for Sonic 3 & Knuckles, improving the presentation significantly, and making stage gimmicks like the Carnival Night Zone Barrel more intuitive- New act transitions for Sonic 3 & Knuckles- Improved S3&K competition mode- As of 1.0.4, new cheat codes for S3&KThe bad:- The high system requirements. This seems to be because of the main menu, which is rendered in real time and requires a modern GPU. This is a collection that was made with consoles in mind first, so the menu is really only an issue in the PC version for low end users. An entire demographic has been left out of playing this collection for a novelty that loses its charm after a few hours of play.- The confusing DLC situation and pricing. Personally I don't really find the DLC to be worth buying, and I think the base game is fine at $39.99. That's about $10 each for 4 amazing games, $8 for 5 games if you count Sonic 3 and Sonic & Knuckles as 2 different games. If you've already played these games and own them in other forms, however, it's going to be muddy as to whether you find that worth the price or not.- The bugs. Personally in my playthrough, I did not encounter a lot of issues. Occasionally there was the odd collision moment, but that happens quite a bit in the original genesis games as well, so it did not bother me that much. There was nothing that actually softlocked me or prevented progress. The only bug I encountered that was genuinely irritating was Tails' AI being broken in Sonic 2, however this was fixed in 1.0.4. - The half-baked Time Attack mode. Like Sonic Mania, there is an online leaderboard for every stage, which is great. However, there is no option to individually play these stages and try for a good time like in Mania, which feels like a huge missed opportunity. The mobile remakes of 1 and 2 had this, and CD even still has its own Time Attack mode in Origins, so it feels like a bit of a glaring oversight to me. The Time Attack mode is made even worse on the PC version, with hackers running rampant ruining it for everyone. It feels like there is little to no point to even trying to compete within the game when so many people are using hacks to ruin the fun for everyone, getting times of 0:0.00. - The sound design. This game has a number of oddities with it's sound. First of all, the music in the Genesis games have been remastered differently from the mobile remasters. The mobile games chose to remaster the music with different hardware, enhancing it from the genesis originals. The results are quite good, but they are not faithful. So, Origins chose the more faithful route, recording the Genesis music off of an actual SEGA Genesis. If you've never played the games on a Genesis or on an emulator with accurate sound emulation, this may sound weird and very wrong to you, but it is actually accurate to the original games. This is a creative decision that is going to be subjective for people. Aside from this, Sonic CD has audio mixing issues, with the volume of the cutscenes being different from the rest of the game. The 2011 remaster introduced looping segments to the stage music, but this version got rid of that and instead the songs stop and start again like the original SEGA CD version, which is a big step back from the 2011 version. Then, in Sonic 3 & Knuckles, that has a redone soundtrack, using the songs found in the old PC version of the game. Whether you like the tracks or not is subjective. Thankfully, the PC version of Origins has a robust modding scene, so you can easily replace these tracks if you don't like them. The one new song that really, really sounds bad, is the new Super theme. It sounds wrong, as it's not even using the instruments from 3&K, the drums are from 2, and the synth sounds wrong. The melody itself is good, and fan remixes have shown you can  make it work, it's just the choice of instruments that make it bad. It's a nice gesture from the team to make a new song for the game, but it just sounds bad. Thankfully, this can also be replaced with mods.All of that out of the way, SEGA has had a bad track record with previous attempts at collections. Old ones used faulty, inaccurate emulators that introduced issues and quirks that weren't in the Genesis originals. This remaster has quirks of it's own, but overall it is the best attempt at a collection SEGA has done so far. Most of the issues can be ironed out with patches, and you can use mods on PC to change bits you don't like, such as the redone soundtrack for S3&K. I do think this collection gets a bit too much flak for what it is. This is far from the worst attempt at a remastered collection out there, many of the flaws are exaggerated because people have this strange bias against Sonic games that they don't have for other franchises. Of course, I am not trying to write off the flaws of this collection, but to act like it is this huge disaster is taking things out of proportion. Sonic fans in general could stand to be more constructive when it comes to their feedback instead of writing everything off as massive flops to farm social media clout and approval from others.

_childDocuments_.review: This collection would still be a bit pricey (and the DLC would still be extremely penny-pinching) if these ports were flawless. Instead you're paying a premium for surprisingly feature-bare and buggy ports. There's little customization for the few features that are there, you can't do something as simple as play with the lives system and widescreen in the same playthrough, one or the other. You can't even say this is for authenticity, you can't ever turn off the spindash in Sonic 1, something even the atrocious Gameboy Advance port lets you do. Bugs are bugs, some are from previous ports, some are brand new. I haven't ran into anything game-breaking but its just so irritating when Tails constantly gets stuck off screen and rapidly spams the jump sound or when the rubble in Marble Garden Zone just doesn't stop falling for the entire stage when the drill robot digs at the beginning.As for added value, you can spend ingame currency to unlock art and music. Remember in Sonic Generations where you could set unlocked music on a per-level basis, including music that doesn't play in the game normally? Nothing like that here! You wouldn't want to play anything over our new awful Sonic 3 replacement tracks! Sit at the sound test! To help collect enough coins to unlocking this riveting content you can play a bunch of original missions developed by the geniuses at Sonic Team. Original may be overselling it since they're mostly obstacle courses of grey, ugly blocks that don't even try to match the tileset plopped over existing levels, you get vapid objectives like kill so many badniks. They have less substance than even Generations' missions and I would not recommend wasting the minor amount of time they would take unless you're really a fan of Sonic Forces' bonus levels. Each game has a mirror mode and a boss rush, exactly as it says on the tin. Though the boss rush has both lives and widescreen enabled, so it's clearly possible for the game to handle it but you're just not allowed to do it. Other than that you have some brand-new cutscenes between games to bridge those gaps. I have nothing negative to say about them, they're pretty and full of character. They were also officially uploaded to Youtube before the game's release, go watch them!Does any of this ruin these great games (and Sonic CD)? Or even mean that this version is bad? No, widescreen is very nice and it's good to see the 1 and 2 ports finally officially off phones, as well as an official port of 3&K. But at this price it's very difficult to recommend a package that's as barebones and flawed as this. I have to praise SEGA's marketing though, revealing the collection as Taxman and Stealth being involved, only to drop that most of the heavy lifting was being done by SEGA's internal teams months later is genius. _childDocuments_.review: Got this for 30 bucks, in my opinion the sweet spot for 4 remaked games. That's it, remaked, not remastered.The reason I say this is I have seen a lot of negative comments regarding lag input. I have played Sonic games all my life and while I'm not a speedrunner, I can tell rather than input lag is physics don't act as what I remember in my muscle. Bosses behave different in the hits, and that's very noticeable, you can't cheese some bosses like in the originals because they changed physics behaviours in some situations. Sum that to the fact I always played in PAL versions and the result is a quite different from what I'm accustomed.I'm not denying there could be input lag, there wouldn't be the decompilations if this wasn't true, but in my case I feel way more the 60 fps and changed physics than unresponsiveness. They are different games than the originals, they wouldn't behave the same even if you use the decompilation mod on them. So yeah, it's a new learning experience for me even if I have played these games all my life and I know them front to back. For instance, you know what a very bad, input lag ridden rendition of these games is? The mega drive/genesis classics before they patched it, and if you want to know how bad it was, try the Switch version which they left unpatched. That is truly straight unplayable.Edit: After clearing all games and all achievements, I stand with what I said. But the biggest change are special stages, the timing in my memory and muscle is absolutely off in special stages compared to regular ones. It took me several tries to finish some of them when I can do them without thinking in the mega drive, the augmented speed of the stage scrolling ♥♥♥♥♥ me up in my perception, but it was fun to get used to them rather than plow through them like I usually do. Sonic 2 special stages are the most changed, not only the speed but the depth and vision range is totally different.The only bad thing I see in this is the mentioned change in some music in Sonic 3, is not only that they sound worse than the originals but they feel really underwhelming compared to the rest of the soundtrack. It really stands out how they were leftovers of prototypes, they could have rearranged them to be on par with the rest. Still, this can be fixed through a mod, something I recommend and is easy to do. Could be worse.I didn't realize it had rankings of everything, included different modes but not special stages. This is something that will make me come back. Overall, the game is much better of what people makes, it's a good rendition but things are different, and you can always go back to emulators or the original consoles if the changes are so negative to you. This is good.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe that this game has not been criticised fairly. There are some problems but they are not completely disrupting my gameplay experience. I've played through the first zone and the first three missions of each game and I think the gameplay is quite solid, as if these games were the real deal. Widescreen, unlimited lives and the drop dash are nice luxuries to have in Anniversary mode. However, keyboard controls are not great and hard to change (jump is k by default and I cannot change it to the space bar). I think the prototype / PC collection music is a suitable way of dodging Michael Jackson's copyright strike, but the Sonic 3 & Knuckles music sounds low quality unlike all other music in this collection.The mission mode is very fun. I enjoy going through swarms of enemies in a certain time limit in slightly modified stages from each game. Why not bounce about in Metropolis Zone or jump across shifting platforms in Spring Yard Zone? As for the museum, it is just there for fans to enjoy extra content. Completing certain objectives gives a nice reward waiting for you in the museum.A Sonic Origins review will not be a Sonic Origins review without discussing its controversy. People have been blaming perfomance problems on Denuvo, the anti-cheat engine that this game uses (yes it is real: I looked at this game through a hex editor). However, I do not get any problems as I have a fairly decent computer (i5-10400F and GTX 1650 with 16GB of ram). If any of you aren't so lucky, try increasing the game's priority in Task Manager or ensuring that you are not using integrated graphics if you have a graphics card. As for DLC, it's just extra content for die-hard Sonic the Hedgehog fans. It just includes some extra cosmetic items including letter box backgrounds (for filling in the black space in classic mode), coins for buying items in the museum and extra music for the museum.Overall, I believe that this is the definitive way of playing the first mainline Sonic the Hedgehog titles in a modern way. In my opinion, some of the criticism this game received is unjustified. I hope there will be updates in the future to fix some problems.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Origins is an interesting throwback into the past, with a few curve balls that either help or hinder the experience. The original Sonic the Hedgehog, Sonic 2, and CD follow very closely with the old Christian Whitehead ports in Anniversary Mode, with some very small elements from more recent titles (such as the Drop Dash from Sonic Mania). Coins are in place of Lives, which do help with certain Special Stages, especially in Sonic the Hedgehog. Sonic 3 & Knuckles is the new port on the block, and while it brings many good changes, such as fixing some sprites and creating new scenes to better connect Sonic 3 and Sonic & Knuckles, there are some small bugs here and there, such as the beginning section of Marble Garden Zone Act 1, and a set piece in Sandopolis Act 2. These errors could be fixed in a future patch to potentially improve the gameplay experience, but aside from that, all of the games play great, and are all very well done ports.Now, down to the more debated aspects of the game: Music and Side Content. There are not many new music tracks to listen to, as many are the original tracks from their respective games. The only new tracks are the Menu music (a remix of the Sonic World theme from Sonic Jam). and the new(-ish) tracks for Sonic 3 & Knuckles's Carnival Night, Ice Cap, Launch Base, Super Sonic, and Credits theme. While the Menu track is somewhat serviceable (I do wish there were more original tracks or remixes for things such as the Museum or Mission modes, as the music can get repetitive), the new tracks for S3&K are a very interesting case. Tracks like Ice Cap and Launch Base are fine replacements to the original Genesis versions, and are very close to the versions present in the Nov. 3 Prototype. Carnival Night and the new Super Sonic theme, however, are either very muted (in Carnival Night's case) or very similar to Sonic the Hedgehog 4's soundtrack (which features poor Genesis soundfont replication). These are featured for only about a good 12 or so minutes (assuming 2 min per Act), so you don't have to wait long until the music comes back to the original tracks we know and love.The extras presented in this game are another mixed bag. The Missions mode is a neat little feature, providing some decently fun challenges that reward some easy Coins for your troubles. They're good tests for understanding how each of the playable characters work, and can be fun to speedrun. The Sound Test option is nice, with the optional DLC providing extra tracks from more Sega Genesis and even 32X games. The Museum option provides both some old artworks that we've seen before, as well as new concept artwork that we've never seen before. This is where you can also view the new cutscenes for the game, that now accompany each game (with CD getting 2 new cutscenes in addition to the originals), with bonuses providing a behind-the-scenes look at the storyboarded versions. S3&K comes a new Blue Spheres mode, which adds new spheres and layouts to test your skill (although it provides no Coins, more of just a bonus experience). While these are serviceable, I would have personally wished for more behind-the-scenes looks at the development of each game, either with more design documents, notes, or even videos of beta versions that we may have never seen before. And as I've said before, some new remixes for some classic tracks would be nice to have as well.With everything said, this is a very serviceable collection of classic games, with only a few small things hindering the overall experience. While some of the exrtas can be a little underwhelming, there's just a small amount enough of new content and insight into the development and history of these games. I would recommend this to anyone who would want to try and play through these games for the first time, or even the second or third time.

_childDocuments_.review: Great collection of 4 (or 5 technically) classic games that could have definitely used some more time in the oven. Some of the misconceptions in the reviews are a bit annoying though, so I'll clear them up:- Options menu is in the Museum tab, which is dumb- People are complaining about the "blurry' look of the games because of the fact that the "Anti-Aliasing" option in the settings have nothing to do with the actual 3D Island menus, the option is actually referring to the blur filter within the classic games themselves. TURN IT OFF.  It looks hideous and the option itself is extremely deceptive in its naming. The image looks significantly sharper and more properly scaled with the option off.- In order to get the (superior IMO) JP Sonic CD music in Story Mode, you need to actually boot Sonic CD up itself in the menus, go through Sonic CD's own soundtrack menu and switch the tracks, and then the changes carry overOtherwise, I've playing through Sonic 1 and partially CD, and I haven't really seen any serious bugs. The inclusion of Denuvo and its insanely high performance requirements is utter garbage though, unfortunately low-spec gamers might struggle to run this game (I tried running it on a i5-1135G7 + Intel Iris Xe and the menus were extremely heavy even at 720p, borderline impossible to access the games). The game runs like butter on my 3070ti + 10900k setup at least, but if it didn't that would be pathetic.Overall, I'd recommend it, with some patches and Denuvo removal it would probably be the best classic collection of the fantastic original games. This is A LOT better than the usual ROM-dump fare, despite the mixed reception.

_childDocuments_.review: It hurts me to post this. I love the classic Sonic games (especially Sonic 3 & Knuckles) and I thoroughly enjoyed myself playing through the story mode in this compilation. The animated cutscenes were beautiful and charming as all hell, the added enhancements to the games really do make them much better, and there's boat loads of content in the museum.But I cannot recommend this compilation because it has Denuvo anti-tamper. Not only do I always downvote any game with Denuvo because it's garbage and ruins the performance on any game it's implemented in (including this one, by the way) but Sonic games have always been about freedom and mods, and Sega is normally so cool about this. _childDocuments_.review: Sigh...After Mania was such a smash hit, I was hoping for Origins to be an utter slam dunk as well. I had a lot of hype going into this. The CW versions of Sonic 1 and 2 on PC, finally. Sonic 3 getting the same treatment FINALLY after Whitehead was denied doing so a decade ago, fancy new intro/outro animations for every single game to provide context for each game's story and a bunch of neat little extras, such as concept art, animatics, extra songs, etc.All of that sounded great, even if I think the price for it is way, way too steep for games that are nearing 3 decades in age. But where does it crumble apart? Behind the scenes is where it crumbles apart.Playing any game in Origins, you can immediately tell corners were cut. The physics, while remarkably close to the original games, still feel slightly off. For example, in Sonic 3's Launch Base Zone, you can't enter the pods if you're standing right next to them because your jump is just ever slightly too high. In Sonic 2, the Aquatic Ruin boss fight becomes weirdly difficult due to the aspect ratio, making it feel more like an oversight. In Sonic 1's Green Hill Zone boss fight, you can effectively cheese the boss by standing under the platforms (which wasn't possible in the original, you still had to dodge).The one thing that gets me though, is the music. Yes, I'm partially talking about the songs in Sonic 3, but I just mean the quality of the songs overall. Again, launching any game aside from CD, you can just hear the compression and crunch of every song. The quality of the songs is astoundingly low quality. It feels like they're using heavily compressed 128 kbps YouTube rips for every single song, and that's genuinely a shame. You don't need to be an audiophile either to hear the low quality, you can just immediately notice it as soon as it transitions from the Origins menu to the game.And of course, Sonic 3's changed music. Contrary to what others may think, I don't hate the replaced tracks. And if you don't know - they replaced the songs with compositions from Sonic 3's November 1993 prototype. Except, for some reason, they based the songs off of the MIDI compositions from the S&K collection on 1997. Zones like Ice Cap and Launch Base sound fine, if anything I think they genuinely recomposed the 1993 proto. ver of Ice Cap and cleaned it up, and it sounds legitimately wonderful, but Carnival Night Zone...god, it sounds awful.And then Sonic 3's Super Sonic theme they added. It's...awful. It sounds like something ripped out of Sonic 4. The baffling bit? They included the Unused Theme in the game's Museum Mode for Sonic 3's soundtrack. Why...couldn't they just...use that? It's just baffling. They can include it in the collection but apparently not use it in the game?I don't wanna keep going. Sonic Origins is a disappointment. I pre-ordered the Digital Deluxe edition by selling my CS:GO knife to buy it, and honestly - I kinda want my knife back now. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this is just proving that SEGA, after the success of Mania, is just going to start rushing and milking Classic Sonic games now. They've gotten so much flack in the past for their glitchy and rushed 3D games, it seems they'd rather take their time with those games, as seen with Sonic Frontiers being released 5 years later. If they want to get out Sonic games yearly now, it seems they're gonna basically use Blind Squirrel for shoddy remasters (unless Blind Squirrel can get their crap together) and Headcannon for Classic games, with random spin-offs in the off years, and, of course, the mainline 3D games every 4-5 years or so. I haven't even talked about my issues with the game itself and we're already off to a bad start.Back in May 2021, during the Sonic Central, it was announced that they were remastering the first 4/5 (Sonic & Knuckles wasn't announced to be by itself or part of Sonic 3 then), and I met it with a groan (not literally, I was in school and I didn't want to make a scene about a cartoon hedgehog). Don't get me wrong, these aren't bad games, heck, they're some of the best Sonic games out there (not Sonic 1), but I've never been as big for the 2D games as I've been for the 3D games, but I thought they looked good, so I was still a little excited. After that, radio silence for 11 months. Only info we got was that Sonic 3 and Knuckles was going to be wide-screen, which was a no-brainer anyways. Still, I hoped that the game would be good, and that we'd get more games than first shown.Weeks after watching the second Sonic movie with friends, (9/10 movie, if I must add) I began to think about the upcoming Sonic games. Frontiers had 2 trailers, second one being in December 2021, yet Origins didn't even have a proper trailer yet. As I began to wonder for a few days, a trailer came out showing the game. I was excited from what it showed us, and was looking forward to getting the game.Now, we encounter our first issue: price. How much would you pay for 4 remastered Genesis games, including 3 games which were free on mobile? I would personally pay around $20-30, but SEGA let greed go to their heads, and set the price at $40. Plus $5 DLC which should've been part of the main game. Then the next problem, delisting the other versions of these games on Steam. Why? Is it because they didn't want people to get confused? Or is it something more? Is it because you could buy those 4 games for $20 with those other versions? Possibly, but we won't know until someone says something. Then more silence, another trailer at Sonic Central 2022, then they announced they were changing Sonic 3 music (we'll get to that) and then the game came out. And from the get-go, this game was a dumpster fire.Never have I seen a game this divisive in the Sonic fan base. As long as I've been a Sonic fan, opinions have mostly been shared within the fan base: Sonic Mania is a godsend, Sonic Forces is a lazy rushed mess, Sonic 06 is a fundamentally good game ruined by glitches and Sonic's story, and Sonic Adventure 2 is the perfect Sonic game. But this game, I have seen so many fight about this game's quality, it makes Frontiers's discourse look civil. My take: I like Frontiers, I don't like Origins.Let's start with this: these games aren't bad, I mean, 1, 2, and CD are the Taxman ports, of course they're not bad. 3&K was remastered by Headcannon, one of the developers of Sonic Mania. These are all really good games at their core (yes, even CD, I don't think you guys know how to play the game right). They added the drop dash from Mania, added a mission mode, and the main menu has some really cool references to other games like Sonic Jam and Spinball. Museum is cool too, and gives you a lot of never before seen content. Plus there are some really cool cutscenes made by Tyson Hesse for this game exclusively.Positives end here, be warned if you don't like criticism.And to start it off, holy crap, this game is a buggy mess. Holy crap I've seen so many bugs from this game, and mainly from Sonic 3 & Knuckles. I've clipped through walls, been teleported to another position (Angel Island Act 1), seen items bug out, and plenty of other problems. People have also been having a weird bug with Sonic 2 Hidden Palace's boss just not going away after being defeated. I've even seen someone literally skip from Mushroom Hill to Hidden Palace. Sure it's a cool speedrun strat, but it's proving that they don't care about checking for bugs, they just wanted the games to get out as soon as possible. Point 2: Denuvo. End of statement.Then there's a lot of problems with each of these games they didn't fix. Sonic 1 has janky physics that don't work well with the drop dash. Sonic CD doesn't have Knuckles, even though he's in all the other games. Drop dash in Sonic CD makes time travelling too easy and broken. Sonic 2's Tails system is broken, as Tails makes the sound unbearable. Sonic 3 and Knuckles's insta-shield works really weird with the drop dash, making the latter harder to use. The physics of the game feel way off and too fast at certain points. Then they also changed a lot of the songs. Remember Ice Cap, one of the most iconic Sonic songs? They changed it's theme, because copyright. You see, back in 1993, when developing the game, they got Michael Jackson and Brad Buxer to help make some music for this game, which was great because it made such an iconic soundtrack, but also makes it hard for SEGA to rerelease Sonic 3 nowadays. For this game, they decided to get Jun Senoue to remaster some of the songs from the prototype version of Sonic 3. This also applies to Launch Base and Carnival Night, as well as some random songs as well. Don't get me wrong, these aren't bad songs, heck I like the new Super Sonic theme for Sonic 3 & Knuckles, but these changes didn't need to happenThen of course is the crappy DLC that should've been in the main game, and probably were until SEGA stripped it out to sell as DLC because that's something they would honestly do. Also, the blatant lies SEGA made in trailers advertising that new characters would be in this game (there isn't any new characters, unless you count the combo of Knuckles and Tails as a new character, and who does?). I would at least understand if they ported Mighty and Ray from Mania over to this game. What about the Chaotix, since they were in Knuckles Chaotix? But they don't do any of that. Heck, I would just take a sprite changed Sonic to Metal Sonic, I doubt that would be too hard for Sonic Team to do.Here's some of my personal nitpicks: You can't choose which Sonic sprite to use in each game. You can't choose which Sonic ability you want for each game. Sonic can still spindash in Sonic 1 Classic Mode, even though the spindash didn't exist yet. You can't play as Sonic and Tails in Sonic 1 even though you could in the mobile version. The settings menu is hidden away in the museum for no reason. Many songs in the sound test are mixed up, specifically Knuckles Chaotix. The animated cutscenes made by Tyson Hesse are only for the good endings and don't make sense if you got the bad ending. Game looks very blurry for no reason.There's so many other problems I have with this game, but I can't even state every issue with it. One of the biggest problems with this collection is that for someone like me, who has all of the Classic games in the first place, there isn't anything to entice me in this collection. Mission mode is fine and all, but that's the extent of this. If you've never played these games before, or you want this collection for nostalgia, then sure, go ahead and get them. I'm not your boss, do what you want with your life. The whole point of this review is to state that SEGA needs to get their acts together and stop rushing stuff out for the heck of getting it out faster, but I'm honestly not sure how they haven't gotten this message yet.

_childDocuments_.review: The price is absurd for what you're getting. They should not have reused the same engine for classic mode, and should do more than just recycle the old aspect ratio. Hell, I'd have been happy to pay that price just to be able to change colors of character sprites or use 'new characters' (as advertised...) sprites all together. _childDocuments_.review: This one hurts. So, so much.On paper, You got the guys who did the critically acclaimed ports of Sonic 1, 2, CD, and Sonic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥' MANIA heading up a collection of the four core titles of classic Sonic. It's on everything and it's easily playable, and with a bunch of nice little extras. Should have been a massive hit with fans, and a must-buy title for anyone.Instead, you get an overpriced, poorly managed collection that still misses features where it's just embarrassing. SEGA were the real ones who headed the collection, and while that doesn't sound strange, essentially it means they were the ones who decided to rip stuff out of the base game to make it DLC, and then hold off content that seemed to be made for the initial launch of the game, for a poorly made DLC pack a year later to... I assume remake the success of Sonic Mania Plus' release?It also means that SEGA decided to just toss in headcannon's ports of 1, 2, and CD in this without putting the effort in to make sure they all work properly. Headcannon technically did the ports, yes, but SEGA was the one who ruined them, same with 3K which was done specifically for this collection by Headcannon. Even with 2.0, there's still a lot of glitches that are present in the game and I can't keep stating this enough, THERE'S NO FULL KEYBOARD SUPPORT. I don't wanna hear "just use a gamepad, bro" when Sonic 3 HAS BEEN ON PC BACK IN THE 90S, it's not unheard of to play Sonic with a keyboard. You literally only need a D-Pad and two buttons, and it's still NOT IN THE GAME. Thankfully, there's Sonic Origins Ultrafix which came out not too long ago, and one of the first things in the trailer is full keyboard support among other nice changes to the game. Thing is, it came out over a year after the game came out. For that time, you got nothing unless you paid for a key rebinder.Because of this, specifically, it just makes the PC version of Origins such a joke. I would love to give SEGA my money for headcannon's versions of the classic titles, but they (SEGA) can't stop messing it up. They delisted the 2011 CD remaster off of Steam for this collection, and it completely stripped the features from that release in this. I wouldn't expect SEGA to do all the little tweaks that fans have done, but when there's such a massive and noticeable gap in quality, I can't help but recommend the fan decomps on PC instead of this collection, since wowee, I can use arrow keys and the enter key in them!I want to like this collection, and it should have been REALLY EASY to not mess up. But somehow, SEGA found a way to do it. Congrats. If you wanted to play the classics on your Switch or PS4 or something, then this collection is fine enough, it's good, even. But on PC, there's much steeper competition with easily accessible fan decomps in 1 Forever, 2 Absolute and 3 AIR, as well as CD Restored which you unfortunately have to track down or pirate since SEGA delisted the 2011 remaster.

_childDocuments_.review: As things are, I can't recommend this collection. I've spent way over 2 hours so I'm unable to get a refund, but it's taken me the whole game to reach Sonic & Knuckles only to discover there's a save corruption bug. The first time, I had no idea what had happened, and I thought I'd lost all of the progress made. Thankfully, I'd been backing up my saves to OneDrive due to using the mod manager, and as Cloud Saving was disabled, I was transferring my progress between my PC and laptop manually. OneDrive makes its own backups, so luckily I was able to retrieve one at the end of Sonic 3. Problem is, as soon as you enter Sonic & Knuckles, the game saves, you quit, and once you attempt to load it back up, you're greeted with an error saying there's a problem with the save. In other words - corrupted. It's good I can go back and keep the progress I've made before that happens, but it's still incredibly poor, and God only knows how this slipped through QA.A few others have run into this problem as well and despite reporting bugs to Sega Support, it's anyone's guess if any of the issues will get fixed. :( Because of this save corruption, I'm unable to finish the game, so I feel like it hasn't been money well spent! I've also discovered bugs that shouldn't even be in the games, and they certainly weren't in the original Mega Drive/Genesis versions either! Thank God I own the originals...Apart from this issue, I'm fairly happy with the collection. I certainly think much more could have been added though. And some things shouldn't be the way they are. I've yet to play the Game Gear titles, but even with the inclusion of Amy and Knuckles in Sonic CD, so many new challenges and achievements could have been added. Such wasted potential... Therefore, I don't see the point in going through the games as the other characters. Not any time soon anyway. Perhaps if there were achievements for playing as them...The missions are a nice little diversion, but there are a few that are frustrating and yet have a 3-4 star rating in difficulty when they should be 5! Others feel too simple. Likewise with some of the unlockables - there's some nice stuff there, but I feel the Premium videos could have been much better. The majority consist of test/line-drawing/storyboard animations of the cinematics. Would have been cool to have had some behind-the-scenes documentaries instead.And yes, there's also the issue with the original Sonic 3 music being absent. Thank God for mods, is all I can say! It's ridiculous though that we have to rely on modders and the fan community to fix many of the issues present! Story mode is cool with the inclusion of the new cinematics and how you'll go through each game one after the other. Anniversary modes are essentially the mobile remakes, which can be loaded onto PC for free anyway, so it feels rather cheeky to basically charge for them in this collection.Unless the game is patched and the save corruption bug is fixed, this review will be sitting with a negative rating permanently.
_childDocuments_.name: Sonic Origins

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointingly buggy for a collection of ports of games made 30 years ago. I have had the game crash several times when attempting to load the main menu. A bare bones museum. Sonic Origins has quite a number of things going against it. Still, even if you own these games a few times over, as I do, there is still something worth looking at here. There are many modes appearing in an official Sonic game for the first time, like the mirror mode. I find the missions to be quite entertaining. The story mode is a fun romp, not needing to worry about lives makes the experience quite relaxing. The ability to retry special stages is quite nice too. You can probably get about the same experience with a combination of different mods and ROM hacks, but I personally find it nice to have it all under one package. Which makes the state the game is in all the more disappointing. My recommendation is to wait for a sale, unless you are a die hard Sonic fan like me, in which case you probably have the game already.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Origins is quite a mixed bag of a product, but this collection does more harm than good.To start on the more positive side, the presentation is quite good with each game being represented on their own respective island on the main menu, which is pretty cute. The animated cutscenes produced by Tyson Hesse are outstanding, as well. As for the games included: each version of every game is... good enough, for the most part. Native widescreen support along with unlimited lives are natural additions to help sharpen the experiences of first-time players (like myself) and returning ones.Unfortunately, that's the best I can say about the package as a whole, as the rest of it is quite underwhelming.  There isn't much else to the collection besides that, outside of the museum, which does provide very engaging development artwork, but can otherwise be found online. The Mission Mode is a pathetic addition to the game that hardly contributes anything nor takes advantage of what each game has to offer and instead serves as nothing more than just another game mode. The worst offender for me was the performance: the game simply refused to launch properly most of time and would freeze up to several minutes in other instances.If you'd like to experience Sonic's origins, it'd be best to do so through other methods, as there exist decompilations of each game online that provide way more customizability. This collection simply doesn't do enough that previous releases have.
_childDocuments_.name: Sonic Origins

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good way to source the RSDK files needed to play superior versions of these games. Not to say there's no value in the collection itself, it's quite nice. I like all of the neat things in here for you to unlock, and the missions are very cool. This is a great buy for achievement hunters.These are not the original games btw, they do not behave exactly like the original games and in some cases are drastically different. Some are okay with that but the "Origins" title is almost false advertising. This should have been called "Sonic HD Collection" or "Sonic Remake Collection" or something. Not even the classic mode is faithful, they just cropped the remakes with no option to play the original Genesis versions of these games. Mainly because Sonic 3's original ROM cannot legally be distributed by Sega anymore due to copyright issues regarding the soundtrack that Michael Jackson and his collaborators contributed to. Still fun tho, even if the replacement songs in Sonic 3 sound terrible to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Sonic Origins

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Why did I pay for Digital Deluxe if I have to buy another DLC pack that should've been implemented when I originally paid for it?So here's my review on this game.Sonic 1 needs a lot of work done. It's extremely buggy and you'll roll down slopes that you're not supposed to (Ex, you'll roll down that one slope in Marble Zone and clip on the floor and stay rolling until you jump, then you go to the right and get hit by an enemy)Sonic 3 is worse. The hitboxes are insane. I've died countless times for seemingly no reason. I'm good enough to consider myself nearly perfect at these games and only die when I get cocky. But this port of Sonic 3 is horrendous. Yes, it's fun, but the hitboxes make it to where even if i run into the side of a spike that's pointing upwards or downwards, I'll take damage. I've even ran into one of those barrels and the space between it and the ground was less than a quarter of sonic's size and i ran into the side and instantly died because somehow it registered as a death even though i literally could have been stopped. The gap was so small that even if I rolled, I wouldn't have been able to fit through. Now for the music. The music needs to be the prototype. It sounds absolutely horrible right now. It just sounds like the PC version was converted into soundwaves that the Genesis can produce. The Super Sonic theme sounds like absolute garbage. They butchered the tune and might as well have just left it as the invincibility theme and it would've been 100 times better. In my opinion, they should've used the prototype super sonic theme. OR at the very least, used that garbage theme for super sonic, then used the prototype theme for hyper sonic. I don't even want to play sonic 3 again at this point unless I'm playing it on my actual genesis. Even the Sonic Jam port of Sonic 3 feels much better to play than this. I wish we just got a sonic jam remake, with remasters of every genesis sonic game with the game gear ports as DLC, and an open sonic world with the low poly models.Another bug I came across is the blue spheres. The music doesn't speed up as gameplay speeds up.This game should have been released later in the year and been worked on longer. What a wasted potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Sonic Origins

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game as a good excuse to replay the classic Sonic games with some quality of life enhancements. Needless to say it was that HOWEVER, it was not without its fair share of issues. I grew up playing these Sonic games and they will always be a timeless classic and have a place in my heart. The game features 4 games, Sonic 1, 2, 3, and CD. It offers 2 different ways to play the game, classic mode in the original 4:3 aspect or anniversary mode which is in the new wide screen 16:9 aspect and gives the player infinite lives. The anniversary mode gives us new cutscenes as well beautifully animated by Powerhouse Animation Studios and the long time sonic artist Tyson Hesse. As for the game play itself it is the classic games but given enhancements the original games didn't have. Sonic 1 lets you Spindash and use characters like Tails and Knuckles, Sonic 2 lets you fly as Tails unlike the original Sonic 2, and Sonic 3 is in wide screen like never before. Issues I've had with the game range from random crashes or performance issues. Another major issue is in Sonic CD you cannot play as Knuckles. This does not compliment how exploration based Sonic CD is and how explory of a character knuckles is. Another issue that while out of SEGAS control is still an issue is 3 stages from Sonic 3 has music replaced that is not the best sounding. While these issues are/were present, this is still a solid collection. I definitely would refer this to someone if they have never played the classic Sonic games. While the $40 price tag might drive people away, I think with how much things we're improved and added, it seems to be worth it. These games are so replayable and I find myself coming back to them on the regular.
_childDocuments_.name: Sonic Origins

_childDocuments_.review: i passed on this game last year because of all the bad things people were saying about it. i thought with plus that those issues would be ironed out, but no. _childDocuments_.name: Sonic Origins

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge Sonic fan. Sonic 3 & Knuckles is still to this day my favourite game of all time. It is hard to give any new comer a proper description of how good atleast this one title in the collection of four really is. We have made almost 30 years of progress in game design but the game still holds up well. I would probably not recommend it to anyone who is not a sonic fan and as such there probably is also no need to even recommend it as sonic fans will or will eventually buy the game. Currently many might feel it is over priced, nothing a special wouldnt fix. What is the fair value? That is up to the buyer.There are a few improvements for S3&K. Sonic now has more subtle animations when it comes to his rotation on the barrels in carnival night zone, probably added due to more storage. Super Sonic also benefits from this as his animations has also been fleshed out such as the rotation on the hydrocity lifts. Flashing sprites are replaced with transparent ones and special stages feels extra smooth.There are noticable flaws in the game. Physics are largely the same but swings in angle island swings you through spikes, the hydrocity air jets pushes you up making it impossible to get a specific 1-up. The special stage at the end of act 2 is unreachable because of the increased frame rate not allowing you to properly clip up the ledge. The large offence is the one everyone has heard about. The Jackson music is missing from Carnival Night, Ice Cap and Launchbase instead replaced by the pc midi and original proto type music. Not speaking of the package as a whole but with a few patches the bugs can be fixed. Sadly the music can't. Other than that I welcome the changes.
_childDocuments_.name: Sonic Origins

_childDocuments_.review: If you get it on sale I think this is a good package, the Anniversary mode is great for casual replaying of the Classic series. My casual ass loves being able to re try special stages too.It's not a perfect package and I think the most notable thing wrong with it is the price. Honestly, it's gone on sale I think twice now. It's sale price should be the standard price. Wait for a sale, don't buy it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm happy to have a collection with all of my favorite Sonic games, but there are a lot of glaring differences from the original.First off, the control changes made in Sonic 3 were the most noticeable, especially with Knuckles. This makes controlling him more frustrating and more clunky. I would much rather play as Sonic through the game. I'm not really keen on the removal of the life system in exchange for coins to as as continues on the Chaos Emerald stages as well. I feel like it takes away the high-stakes part which made it more exciting. However, I can see this being beneficial for newer players.I will probably stick to Classic mode for the games or just play the other official releases in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Sonic Origins

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, this game has a lot of problems and I understand that there are a ton of cheap practices in here, like locking oddly small things behind a paywall for a couple of change, but I love the classic games, especially these versions of them, that (all for CD) were unavailable on any platform that wasn't a mobile phone. And 3&K finally getting the same treatment. Whilst these are poorly slapped together & the overall package could've been more for the price, I think it was a decent enough collection of these classic games.It's good for what it is, but had so much more potential for what it could've been.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: I can easily recommend this game but only if you were to grab it on sale. For $40 at launch (or $45 if you wanted a island camera view), this was highway robbery. For a $20 price tag? I felt fine paying that. You get 4 of some of the most defining platformers of the 90s in widescreen. That alone made it worth it in my eyes. Also, it was quite easy to get 100% achievements in this game which was nice. Here are my scores for each of the sonic games included in this package. The only real bad things are the bizarre DLC and unlockables.  The unfortunate music issue with Sonic 3 is also a licensing issue.  Not sure why so many people are blaming Sega for that.

_childDocuments_.review: People gave this game some hate when it first came out, calling it a "lazy cash grab", but that didn't stop me from getting it, and I don't regret pre-ordering the biggest pack available. 40 bucks was steep, but this is an excellent way to experience the games.People say "Just get an emulator, it's free!" No, it should be more like $20, but that doesn't stop me from recommending the game! I have 100% Trophies and I don't regret sinking a couple hours into playing some awesome classics.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game to play it with the Ultrafix mod (which, yes, it's sad that such a mod even needs to exist in the first place, instead of Sega just fixing all the issues the game has themselves (and yes, it's even more sad that the game needs to be fixed in the first place, instead of just launching in a stable and polished state.)) and without all the issues that the vanilla game has it's actually a fairly good experience.This game has quite a few additions that I really like, like the coins, the menu islands, the missions and all the stuff added to Sonic 3.I actually specifically got this game  Sonic 3, since I was quite a bit tired of trying to figure out what mods to use to get the definitive experience out of Sonic 3 AIR, whereas here, I could just get it all within a single package.Other versions still offer a ton of customization so obviously this will never replace them, but I would recommend this game for just being nice simple versions you can pick up and play.......of course that is using mods. It is just one mod, yes, which is nice, but it isn't part of the vanilla game and especially on a Steam Deck it can be a bit of a process setting it up. I imagine most people would not wanna mess with mods.Also. this game uses Denuvo. and as of time of writing, it's had it 300 days longer than it took for Denuvo to get removed from Sonic Mania, and I am not very confident that they'll remove it from this game any time soon.Denuvo seems to really not like the Steam Deck, I assume it interprets each reboot as being a new device, causing you to get locked out after around 5 game starts, for 24 hours. (Which is why I'm writing this, I am currently locked out of the game, which I otherwise actually had a great time playing.)With all that being said, I don't think I can recommend this game as it is, unless you're willing to ♥♥♥♥ with both mods and Denuvo.Also honestly just pretend that the Non-Plus version of the game doesn't exist, Sonic Origins Plus doesn't feel like DLC, it feels like an update that you have to pay for, especially with Knuckles in Sonic CD being exclusive to that.I bought Sonic Origins Plus for 16€, but, if you're willing to put up with the above, I don't think 40€ is a terrible price either, I know I would've paid that, had the sale not started the exact day I wanted to buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sonic Origins

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about the package but overall I would say this is the definitive way to play the games in a modern form, I think the addition of the drop-dash and spin-dash add a lot to the movement and makes it much more enjoyable, looking at you Sonic 1, also the new intro/outro animations are pretty nice. However, there are some bad parts here, the removal of games from the Mega Drive Collection, limited options, and the hard bargain price for a port of really old games especially when there WERE better alternatives in terms of price and personal preference. There's a lot of good in this package but I think that it's a value to content preference, I think on a sale it's a fine enough purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: The classic ga,e are still fun to play, and are even more fun with the cutscenes. The intro still lags, but at least now the cutscenes are running clear. _childDocuments_.name: Sonic Origins

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Origins is a very accessible way of playing the classic 2D sonic games. I think its important to preserve old titles like these via remasters, or just nabbing the roms and loading them into emulators. Most of Sonic origins issues lie in the first 2 titles, sonics drop dash is tedious to use in the first 2 games as you cannot change direction while falling to the ground with a charged dropdash which takes the flexibility of a great ability, and just turns it into another spindash essentially. As for positives go, widescreen is a great addition as the older sonic games had somewhat unfair enemy placement and being able to see them coming sooner is a massive improvement. One other thing i dont see people address in their reviews, is that hyper tails is now in the game, not super tails, hyper tails. When you get all 7 chaos emeralds you can become super tails! and when you gain all 7 super emeralds, you can be hyper tails!! (hyper transformation hasnt changed since 3&k but still nice that we have an actual super form for tails) One other nitpick i have with sonic origins is that there is no steam workshop support, anyone who didnt buy Sonic 1-3 on steam before it was removed off of steam, wont be able to play with fantastic mods like sonic classic heroes, sonic 3&k complete, etc.In conclusion, i would say origins is a great way to replay the old 2d sonic games, but the price is definitely more than what id want to pay as these games are all around 25-30 years old. I really hope sega can compensate for the price by adding a unique campaign featuring unused zones like the wood zone, genocide city (minus the name), dust hill zone, and more.Long live hyper tails

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Origins is one of those collections that is very polarizing. For a lot of people, like myself, enjoy this collection because it fixes problems for all of the games (Consistent frame rate for Sonic 2's special stages, the infamous spike glitch from Sonic 1, and some of the hitbox issues from Sonic CD and 3&K), and are also happy to finally get a release of Sonic 3 & Knuckles after so many years of being the definition of a music licensing nightmare. For others, they absolutely hate the collection for changing the music for Sonic 3&Knuckles (even though the needed to do it in order to release this collection at all) and making the games easier by giving a retry function for the special stages (though they agree that it makes Sonic 2's special stages much easier), as well as the ability to turn off lives, and the lack of including Sonic 3D Blast, Dr. Robotnik's Mean Bean Machine, Knuckle's Chaotix, and Sonic Spinball (Though the music from those games are DLC). I can agree that I wish those games were included, but I also understand that they would have to rebuild those games in Christian Whitehead's Retro Engine which would take longer (Spinball and Mean Bean could be easy, the other 2 would need more time). I also like the fact that they added the ability to play without the lives counter. It was just an archaic game mechanic that added artificial difficulty. The ability to retry special stages is also really helpful, especially Sonic 2 with the god awful half pipe. All in all, I can recommend this to people who want to try Sonic 1-3&K. It might not be what purists call the "True Classic Sonic Experience", but it certainly gives more people of various skill levels the ability to experience the little blue hedgehog's roots.

_childDocuments_.review: You can watch the full coverage of the game here which shows every achievement getting completed. Part 1: Part 2: Part 3: Solid game that is optimized better than the Sega Genesis/Mega Drive Collection or SGMDC for short without mods from the Steam Workshop. Four of the Sega Genesis/MegaDrive/CD Sonic titles are here. Those omitted are Sonic 3D Blast, Sonic Spinball, Sonic 4 Episode 1 + 2 and Sonic Mania. Also I would feel that the Game Gear/NeoGeo games would be a welcomed edition if Sega got the means to put them into Sonic Origins. But as it stands you only get Sonic the Hedgehog 1, Sonic CD, Sonic the Hedgehog 2 and Sonic 3 & Knuckles respectively to round out the *Origins* of the Blue Blur and his friends and foes. While there are some glitches and such within the game. Overall, I felt its pretty solid throughout my playthroughs.  7 Hours or maybe even less you can speed through the whole Story Mode Campaign but aside from that with the premium DLC that I purchased from Fanatical you get extra Extreme Missions that would give a long time veteran some pause before completion but overall its entertaining. Extra Music + Extra Premium behind the scenes artwork and media is quite nice to see.MMV depending on how you feel SEGA pushed the product and those that worked on it. I feel that overall ST and its affiliates did a pretty solid job despite rumors and calls of it being a rushed job. To me its serviceable and enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: This one really hurts, especially as a long-time fan of the classic Sonic title, and as someone who's been wanting the remastered versions of these games on modern platforms for a decade now. While it's significantly better than the dumpster fire of Sonic Colors Ultimate, this collection is the definition of a mixed bag, and I really can't recommend it, especially at $40.It's not all bad: the new cutscenes are beautiful and charming. Some of the new modes are fun. The addition of the coins to restart Special Stages is a nice quality-of-life tweak along with the unlimited lives. And there are many great additions to Sonic 3 specifically, thanks to the efforts of Headcannon's dev team. At the core these are the same beloved games from the 90s.But for every pro in Sonic Origins, there are at least 10 cons. There are so many downgrades from the previous Retro Engine releases of these games, and Sonic 3 unfortunately was not finished in time. Granted, this has nothing to do with the team; there were very clearly a victim of Sega's crunch. (How this is still a problem after two decades is beyond me.) Here's just a couple of the problems:- Confusingly laid-out menus making navigation a chore. (Sonic CD's music is set to the US soundtrack by default and you need to go into the CD menu to switch it back, for instance)- Buggy implementation of the Drop Dash in Sonic 1/2- Remastered music from previous Retro versions is gone- Misleading classic mode that is just a cropped version of the anniversary versions with lives enabled instead of the actual ROM files- Numerous bugs and glitches, especially at launch. (While Tails's AI in Sonic 2 and some of the mislabeled music in the gallery was fixed, most bugs still remain.) None are game-breaking, but there's enough to become a huge annoyance, especially in Sonic 3's case- Lack of substantial bonus content in the gallery. There's a few new things, but most have already been released in other ways- Texture filtering that cannot be turned off- Need I even mention the hilariously awful replacement zone and Super Sonic music in Sonic 3?This was the easiest slam-dunk possible, and yet it still ended up like this. While I think it's a perfectly solid way to play these games on consoles (if you can find it on a good sale), on PC this collection is redundant, especially with the unnecessary inclusion of Denuvo that Sega loves to shove into their games. And with the old versions of these games now delisted, this is what you're stuck with in terms of "legal" means of playing these games. As much as I'd love to judge this collection on its own merits, the Retro Engine decompilations and Sonic 3 AIR are *much* better options to play the classic Sonic titles now on Windows. You can easily add the new additions from Origins, restore Sonic 3's music, and get so many more QoL tweaks that way, with no invasive DRM.I'm posting this review now with the recent announcement of Sonic Origins Plus which, while having some great additions, REALLY should've been in the base game. Amy really should've been there before, and locking Knuckles in Sonic CD behind DLC is an incredibly scummy move. Not to mention that they're only adding in the Game Gear titles (which you can easily restore into Sonic Adventure DX through the mod installer), when they could easily add in games that have never been re-released like Knuckles' Chaotix or the Saturn version of Sonic 3D Blast. Unless they go back and fix all the problems above and more, this won't be enough to save the collection.Man, these games deserved so much better...

_childDocuments_.review: Fun enough for me to 100% it. If you enjoyed these games originally, you'll enjoy them here with their new QoL updates.Comes with 4 games, (Sonic 1, 2, 3&K, CD) and a bunch of bonus content for them.-Native widescreen support. - Bunch of new cinematics and touch ups to the games. (I noticed some new animations and the such.) You can play through all 4 games in a row in story mode, turning the 4 games into one connected experience with new cutscenes.-Challenge modes/missions for each game. (Custom levels that revolve around completing challenges, like beat the obstacle course without touching any enemies. Boss rush, mirror mode, etc.)-The OG life system has been replaced with a currency system. You have infinite lives now, and 1up monitors now give coins that can be used to retry special stages and buy unlockables in the museum. Music, Art, Movies/animations. Surprising amount of stuff in there. Even the entire Sonic Mania animated series is in there.-All games have a save system now, and you can play as Knuckles in Sonic 1-3.Cons: I only have one. They had to replace the soundtracks for Carnival Night, Icecap, and Launch Base zones in Sonic 3. The replacement track for Carnival Night reaaaally sucks. Icecap is okay, but it doesn't hold a candle to the original. I honestly can't even remember Launch Base's new music. It wasn't very memorable unlike the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this objectively the best compilation of the Genesis Sonic games? Probably not. Is it a more than solid one? Absolutely! I really like the implementation of Tails, Knuckles, and Amy as playable characters in ALL the games (though I wish Amy wasn't DLC-only). Anniversary Mode is an amazing anti-frustration feature, letting you have infinite life coins for "Bonus Level Retries", for the older Sonic games cuz of some of those levels have some BS death/difficulty moments, especially the "0 ring" levels and bosses.The new animated movies for Sonic 1, 2, and 3+K is a nice touch. The Gallery, Museum, and Custom Challenges are also nice to haves. Native High Resolution is also nice.Main flaw honestly is that it's $30 is WAY overpriced for just the base compilation, and $40 even more so just for Amy and Game Gear Titles people likely won't touch. I miss when Sonic Anniversary and Gems Collection were actual good deals. Sonic Origins sadly ends up becoming a "wait for a sale" deal, but when it does go down to at least $20, it's great.That said Sonic Origins is still probably the best modern way to enjoy classic games especially with the different options to play Sonic 1, CD, 2, and 3 & Knuckles.
