_childDocuments_.review: Game seems to lack basic ingame methods of controlling characters with arrow keys, and is impossible to navigate out of ingame via the in game menu as it doesn't respond to escape, backspace or the enter key (the usual keys), or any other that I've found. Given this is a standard 2D platformer, controlling with arrow keys is the basic minimum I'd come to expect, and among the other issue It's basically impossible to play this properly. And yes, while there is a menu to rebind controls, it does not read arrow keys there either.This is amongst other minor issues, such as the game initially starting in fullscreen on a non-native monitor resolution (or refresh rate) causing the usual LCD resync delay and resizing of desktop windows, necessitating a change to borderless window in the options to make it stop doing that. And the default controls are rather confusing and all over the place, such as the default action being K of all things.These aren't deal breakers on their own, and the performance seems to be fine, but the impression I get was this was some sort of rushed console to PC port and doesn't have a great presentation, in addition to being impossible to play on a keyboard in a traditional way. This could be better.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a huge Sonic fan for two decades now and this collection is perfect. I'll be playing this until Sonic Frontiers comes out. It's a great time waster and a blast from the past. I remember first playing these games on the Sonic Mega and Gems Collections when I was a kid, so this really takes me back. Would I recommend it? Yes. There's one thing you need to do before you play it if you use NVIDIA hardware: Go to the NVIDIA Control Panel, Manage 3D Settings, Program Settings, and set the game to High-performance NVIDIA processor. It happens with a couple of games and it's easily fixable. The game was lagging at the startup until I did that

_childDocuments_.review: When I first opened this game, it lagged like crazy and messed up the resolution on my laptop but then I realised that it automatically runs from my integrated graphics instead of my GPU. Switching to my GPU totally fixed it so I thought that was worth mentioning if anyone else is having trouble making the game run well!This is the definitive way to experience the classic Sonic games, aside from a few minor nitpicks, and the drop-dash definitely makes the games so much easier and fun to play! I'm also really glad they removed lives and added coins instead since I'm pretty bad at the classic games lmao. Outside of the issues I mentioned before, the game runs flawlessly with no frame drops or lag. My biggest issue is with the key-bindings which are absolutely terrible and for some reason, it wouldn't let me change them to how I wanted them. Fortunately, the game is much better controlled with an Xbox controller so I won't be using the keyboard much. Some of the Sonic 3&K music is also vastly inferior due to it being a recreation of the prototype tracks, but the prototype tracks somehow sound so much more finished than the versions used in Origins.Overall, I highly recommend picking this up! But if you do, be sure to play with a controller!

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Origins is a fine collection. The only crimes it commits are the few 3&K tracks being mediocre (just fix it with mods) and the lack of new playable characters. Otherwise you get all of the beloved games packaged in a convenient bundle. There were virtually no glitches (minus the Tails sound effect one that has been fixed) and all the games played just fine. I cannot speak for how Denuvo actually affects performance, if it truly drops your fps I think you have more problems than just Denuvo. The real problem point lies in how Denuvo ruins the ability to purely play this game offline, as it needs to check the license occasionally through the use of an internet connection. But Im not gonna strike points off this game because of that. There is even a new version of Blue Spheres to play, and little extra missions that shake sections of levels up a bit.Now we get to the truly awful side effect of this game. Keep in mind that this does not make Origins awful, however it paints SEGA in an awful light. Delisting the games that were already on Steam is extremely anti consumer. This collection is not priced well, so doing that was just a true spit in the face. If you are looking to play these games in 16:9, with some extra features. This collection does the job and is great. If you are willing to mod it a little, its even better. But to the people that already own the originals on Steam? Just play the fan ports unless you want something official.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not as bad as some people make it out to be in their reviews but there are still some glaring issues.The biggest one for me is the image quality, for some reason the games don't look very sharp. It almost looks like like they scaled the game up to half the screen resolution internally, then used interpolation for the rest. I'm not sure if this is what they did but it still doesn't look very great.This is something you can actually fix by installing a mod (which is very easy) but come on, we shouldn't have to rely on mods to get an acceptable image quality.There's also a disgusting lack of customizability. When you play the game in anniversary/story mode you're forced to play with spin dash, drop dash, and infinite lives. Why can't we toggle these off? Why are all these settings are bundled together? Why can't we toggle things off?Drop dash is also another issue because it just feels... wrong. The way they implemented it feels rather inaccurate to Mania in all games except Sonic 3. This wouldn't be a huge issue to me normally because I don't even want to play these games with drop dash, but as I said we cannot really turn it off so... yeah...And of course there's also the issue with the music. I don't just mean the replaced music Sonic 3, there's a much bigger and serious issue going on here.In Sonic CD for example, the tracks have rather weird loop points, and they are clipping! Yes, literally clipping. How did they manage to mess it up when the 2011 CD release had it working perfectly? No idea.Sonic 3 is completely messed up too. The whole soundtrack seems to have a low pass filter applied to it which isn't something present in other games, nor it sounds actually good.And of course, they had to replace some of the music from Sonic 3 with their prototype versions because of legal issues. I love the original prototype tracks, don't get me wrong, but these replacement tracks somehow manage to be much, MUCH worse than those leaked proto tracks which is baffling.And yes, the issues with Sonic 3's music is also something mods can fix but I'm not going to give the game extra points for that.Outside these issues this is a good collection, and without them we would have had something fantastic in our hands. Finally being be able to play these games in widescreen in an official fashion is a blessing, the special stages are SO MUCH better here than in the Genesis originals, the option to be able to retry those is awesome, the entire recreation of Sonic 3&K here is super well done, and the menus are very pretty.I'm really enjoying the mission mode as well, despite it not being anything mindblowing. Same with the gallery I guess, there are some songs and concept art to unlock but it isn't going to hold your attention for too long.And, I mean, in the end, this is a collection if 3 fantastic games (and Sonic 1). Sure, they messed it up a bit but the games themselves are perfectly playable regardless.So... I guess in the end I think the collection is decent, just not $40 decent. It's nowhere near as big of a disaster as Sonic Colors Ultimate, so there's at least that.Also, apparently some people are having performance issues but idk it worked fine on my PC lolEDIT: Slightly updated after playing the game way more, and added some things about mods, but I still stand by most of what I said.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick OverviewThis is a very solid collection. A lot of love was poured into this and I enjoyed every moment of it. I've played this games dozens of times, yet Origins brought it new life for me. The biggest disappointment is the fact SEGA didn't want to shell out the cash for the MJ tracks for Sonic 3. That's honestly really annoying and stops this from being the definitive way to play Sonic 3. Also, the games are a bit soft looking, the pixels are crystal clear.The ControversyLets just get this out of the way first. I only recently became aware of the controversy, and completed the game well before discovering it. While I agree that the DLC and removal of previous versions is scummy, Origins is far from the "mess" people are making it out to be. In addition, people are trying to make it out to be another buggy release like Colors Ultimate, but this simply isn't true. Although that's more of a fault of the Sonic franchise's reputation. In addition, the crunch (even though the devs knew going in) is tough to hear. Especially since delays were a no go. I knew the delays for Mania and Boom 2 were just PR moves, but it hurts to see it. I honestly don't think anyone would care that much if Origins didn't release RIGHT on Sonic's 31st.BugsThrough out my 15 hours of play time I've only experienced 1 bug, and it was just a checkpoint activating before I got to it. The crushing collision for Sonic 3 also needs work. It's kinda annoying when I make a tight jump in Sandopolis or Ice Cap and die when I clearly could've made it.Extra Content made with Love.First off, is the islands. They look phenomenal. The fact that CD and 3 change as you progress in game is great. They also add an island for Sonic Spinball and 3D blast, was a welcome surprise. I would have loved this collection of the game. In addition Sonic World theme from Jam and Classic Collection gets a new fantastic remix for the menu music which hit me with a wave of nostalgia. New Blue Spheres stages were made for this game and they get their own little menu with unique pixel art, it was a nice surprise that was unnecessary but absolutely welcome. There were little tweaks added here and there to Sonic 3 that I appreciated. Extra animations to Super Sonic, and the fact Tails doesn't get annihilated in Angel Island Act 2 were welcome additions. Every little thing in this game, is made with love and intent. Lastly, the animated cutscenes, need I say more?DisappointmentsWhile I appreciate all the extra content. I kinda wanted a bit more. Firstly, the achievements are incredibly bare. It would help extend the play time if they were meant for more veteran players to give them a challenge. The missions, while welcome, are pretty easy (save for the DLC missions and that one Sky Chase Mission for Sonic 2). And again, no achievement reward for completing all of them. Also, the fact that content was needlessly locked behind a paywall is no bueno. After Sonic Gems collection, I was also hoping for some small unlockable games like the Game Gear titles or remaining two genesis games they have islands for... But, this collection is focused on porting the taxman ports of the classics as well as finally making one for 3 and K. Also, knowing the crunch the devs were under I'm not going to hold it against them. And honestly, what we have now is already a solid collection of Sonic's landmark "Origin" titles. But by far, the biggest disappointment is the soundtrack for Sonic 3. Really? REALLY? Opening Sonic 3 felt like an event, like seeing an old friend, or seeing the Mania announcement live. But as soon as I hit Carnival Night, my heart sank. The only Sonic 3 prototype song I liked, was Carnival Night Act 2. But it's remix here sucks. SEGA, you should've just shelled out the cash to put your best foot forward. Quit being cheap, it's frustrating. No wonder you keep digging Sonic into a deeper hole. Also, the games are a bit soft looking, the pixels are not crystal clear. Kind of annoying, but I didn't really notice it till it was pointed out to me. Still valid point.That's pretty much it, I put the conclusion at the beginning to make it more accessible for those looking for a quick answer. If you read it all, thanks. I'm interested to see what other's think of the game. I didn't mean for the review to be this long, but I'm really passionate about my favorite blue rodent. I've been with him since I was 4, and plan to stick around till I die. I hope the future is bright, but I'll believe it when I see it.(Edits:)- Added comment on softness of the games visuals.

_childDocuments_.review: This just barely makes the recommend list for me. For everything this collection does right (Drop dash + spin dash in all the games, widescreen, a new mission mode, the ability to play through all four games in one fell swoop.) there's something that's scuffed as hell (DRM, some minor audio bugs, the sonic 3 port being ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ raw, the menus lack polish, The lack of options for playing the games). At the end of the day, Everything I've experienced here is playable, but it really just makes me feel depressed that sega didn't take more time to make everything here as good as it possibly could be. If you've never experienced classic sonic and are looking for an official way to play these games, this would be the best way. On the other hand, the fan created efforts do a far better job. It's disappointingly fine.

_childDocuments_.review: *** Note: If you own this game, you need to install the Ultrafix mod. ***I was looking forward to this collection, but the execution is terrible. It has zero respect for the original games.Just looking at Sonic 1, they've changed a lot about how the game works. They included spin dash, even in "classic" mode. Spikes don't work the way they did in the original game. You can't hit Robotnik when he's entering the stage, you just pass through him. The hitboxes for various projectiles are different, right up to the electric balls in the final stage, so veteran players with muscle memory will die in places they wouldn't.These changes were all made intentionally to discreetly "improve" a classic game that these developers have no business modifying. They also delisted all their products that were selling the real version of the original games, so unless you purchased one of those games already, you can now only play this revisionist trash (unless you download a Genesis emulator and ROM for the original Sonic games).The changes they've made to these games show a complete lack of respect for the original work. Each game has a "classic mode" that describes itself as being the original classic game, but it's not true. They couldn't help but modify the original work and then pretend it's unchanged.The original Sonic established Sega as a brand, and it's the only reason they even have a company today. Yet they show it zero respect and make it clear they think they could have done it better, retroactively patching a game over 30 years later with elements of modern game design, even though the current developers had no hand in creating the original.If Sega thinks they can make a better Sonic game than the originals, then they should go do it: make a new game.Don't change the original games and pretend it's still the same game. And definitely don't bury all the real versions of the original games to force people to buy your new updated version. It's all so arrogant.tl;dr: If "classic mode" was the actual original game as advertised, I wouldn't have left a negative review. "Sonic 1 - Classic Mode" should be the same game that was on Genesis. No mechanical alterations. Any changes to the gameplay should obviously be optional and off by default. But they just couldn't help themselves.Edit: If you want this to be playable, look up the "Ultrafix" mod. It fixes every issue I found while trying the game out. I guess I don't need to refund now since the mod exists and I bought the game at 60% off. If you're set on getting this collection, then definitely wait until it's on sale, and make sure you get the Ultrafix mod.

_childDocuments_.review: This collection is absolute dogsh*t, play the de-compilations or the fan-made ports.-The animations were pointless and honestly a marketing scam (the opening cinematic and trailer marketed it as in-between zones, but it's only when launching the specific game and beating the game, that's it).-These games are unchanged from the mobile ports besides new visual/gameplay bugs that weren't in the remasters (Sonic clipping on-top of Tails' sprite when flying underwater, Tails behind Sonic in Blue Spheres does not jump on the Yellow Spheres, random stutters, etc).-There is no Time Attack despite the mobile ports having them.-The Toei animated cutscenes are upscaled and look beautiful, but the ending is sped-up like it was on Sonic Gems Collection on the GameCube/PS2, a collection that released back in 2005, it is 2022, the 2011 remaster had the correct speed with the sound effects from the JP audio.-Speaking of CD, the audio clips from Sonic and Amy are both gone, now they just either make the Time Stone sfx, or in Amy's case, pure silence, no yelp or giggle.-The bugs from the 2013 Sonic 1 and 2 ports are still present, as well as CD's mobile bugs despite being fixed on the PC/Console releases, AND this is all within a 10 year time span.-Classic mode isn't the original Genesis roms (the ones that got de-listed) DESPITE the game clearly giving the description "Play the game in its original form in 4:3", it's the same game on the Retro engine, but with a border and a life system, which leads to the next issue below.-THERE IS NO OPTION TO TOGGLE LIVES IN WIDESCREEN, CRASH BANDICOOT 4 LETS YOU DO THIS AND ITS A BRAND NEW GAME!!!!!!! -The time spent on the 3D Islands should've been spent on polishing up each of these games.-DLC is a total rip-off, do not buy it.-40 USD for the whole package when collections like TMNT: Cowabunga Collection exist for the same price (10+ games with alternative ports AND online multiplayer).-The original Genesis roms of Sonic 1 and 2 are NOW only playable on modern consoles via SEGA Genesis/Mega Drive Classics or SEGA Ages on NSO, with the original rom of Sonic 3 and Sonic & Knuckles being completely inaccessible.-The Retro Engine, albeit a great recreation of the original physics, does NOT work in Sonic 3's level design as intended, causing some noticeable bugs like dying from running past the screen (despite being able to do this just fine in the very original Genesis games), finishing certain levels when the boss is supposed to be coming down, etc. This engine works in Mania BECAUSE the levels were designed around said engine, these games were not.-Sonic 3 and Sonic & Knuckles are not given the option to play the games seperately, giving less accessibility for those who only like one game or the other.-The music in Sonic 3 has been partially replaced with the prototype/collection tracks, which sounds fine on paper because of legal reasons, but Jun Senoue managed to somehow make them sound worse than they ever have before (Ice Cap being the only exception), AND he managed to screw up the Super Sonic music via Sonic 4's soundfont, aka the one that pretty much all fans dislike heavily.This could have been the definitive way to play all of these classics on official software, but no, SEGA said: "Haha, you get crap with your sh*t." :)What a f*cking joke, Evening Star and crew deserved more freedom and control after making the best ports AND the best game in the last 10 years since Generations.SEGA you are the worst company in existence, and it's a fact. Atleast the Mega Man Legacy Collections (35 USD for two seperate packages combined totaling into 10 games) lacked as many problems despite emulating more games across multiple platforms (NES, SNES, PS1, PS3/X360/Wii).I am praying Sonic Frontiers turns out well, because if not I am done with buying games from this cursed franchise. I am okay with sticking to other forms of media.5/10, do better SEGA. P.S. we shouldn't have to rely on the modding communities to fix your broken games.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never written a comprehensive Steam review for a game, but then again, I've never been so pissed off by a game, either.Sonic Origins is the biggest letdown imaginable. Before I get into that, though, let's talk about the good parts of the game. The new Anniversary Mode lets you play through all four games with infinite lives. It's pretty well-known that lives, as a mechanic, kind of suck. They're a holdover from the era of arcade games, made to squeeze money out of you back then and to squeeze playtime out of you on consoles. Lives are replaced with Coins, which you can use to retry Special Stages or unlock art/music/video content in the new Museum.The cutscenes before and after every game in Anniversary Mode are, likewise, really cool! They clearly had a lot of heart put into them. Tyson Hesse and Powerhouse knocked them out of the park.The new Mirror Mode lets you play each game in reverse, flipping the screen and changing the game from left-to-right to right-to-left. This is a cool new touch that mixes up the gameplay for veteran players. It's neat.The also-new Mission Mode throws you into courses with set objectives. This is essentially identical to Sonic Generations' missions - you have set objectives (time, rings, etc.) and you're ranked based on how well you complete those objectives. This is... fine.That's the end of the good part of Sonic Origins. Now for the bad.Sonic 1, Sonic CD, and Sonic 2 are almost entirely unchanged from their mobile ports (and Steam port, in CD's case), with a few exceptions that I'll get to later. If you bought and played these earlier ports, though, you might notice something strange about Sonic Origins - namely, at launch, Sonic 1 and 2 on mobile devices were both 3$ a pop, and Sonic CD on Steam was 5$ before it was delisted. Origins is . If you're being  generous and want to bump the other two games' prices up to match CD's  price S3&K similarly, this game should be 20$ maximum. This alone is ridiculous. On top of that, there's a confusing and predatory-feeling bit of DLC that gives you exactly two pieces of meaningful content - 100 Coins (seriously?) and access to harder missions in Mission Mode. Sega's really going out of their way to nickel and dime you on this one.Sega also did a lot of advertising relating to "new playable characters", which is a flat-out lie. Tails and Knuckles have been playable in Sonic 1 since 2013, and Tails has been in CD since 2011. They couldn't even bother adding Knuckles to CD here, which would've been the easiest "new character" to add... but the promotional material and in-game movies focusing on Amy makes me think  who they wanted people to assume was playable. of the aforementioned "few exceptions" to the unchanged ports made the games  overall. Sonic 1 features the addition of the Drop Dash, except you can't turn around in midair after using it and jumping, so you can't chain it the way you can in Mania. Sonic CD has had Sonic and Amy's single, half-second voice lines removed for... some reason; the Drop Dash was added here, too, and it works much closer to Mania's version.CD has also had its entire Steam achievement list nixed in favor of Origins's mediocre "Play the game! Time travel once! Beat Metal Sonic! Beat the game!" ... and that's . Normally, I'd call this a nitpick, but CD's Steam port from  had a better achievement list. Why, Sega. Why.Sonic 2 has Sonic 1's halfassed Drop Dash, as well as at least two minor level layout changes - one in Metropolis 3 that makes a set of spikes borderline unavoidable (seriously!), and one that breaks Wing Fortress's intro. Good job, Sega.Sonic 3 & Knuckles is the most tragic case of all here. Sega contracted Headcannon (of Sonic Mania and Sonic 1+2 Mobile fame) to develop the remaster, which sounds all well and good... until you read  about how Headcannon was treated during development.S3&K's good features include the Drop Dash ( implemented this time, likely since Headcannon actually knows how it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ works), a bunch of additional rotation sprites for objects like the Marble Garden spinners and Carnival Night's barrels, and a few new flashy level transitions that add a lot of polish and heart to the game. Thanks, Headcannon.S3&K's  not present in the original game are numerous, to say the least. Its music hasn't been remastered at all; the tracks sound like low-quality playbacks of the Genesis tracks. It bears mentioning that this only stands out so much because the other three games  high-quality remastered tracks. The Special Stage music doesn't speed up to match Sonic's speed like it did in the original game, and the new Super Sonic theme is  to listen to, almost as bad as the original.Actually, none of the new music is good. I'm no Michael Jackson purist, either; I played Sonic 3 A.I.R. with all of the prototype tracks enabled, and they all sounded fantastic there. ; the tracks he wrote should've been arranged and programmed into the game by someone who's more familiar with Genesis sound synthesis. The tracks that made it into Origins are watered-down, inferior versions of the original, pre-MJ tracks.Miscellaneous annoying differences from the original S3&K include differing in-game physics (hold down when Marble Garden 1 starts and keep it held - the speed cap behaves differently so you fly into a wall, unlike in the original); the end of Act 1 signposts not falling in the same places, so they don't unearth monitors consistently anymore; a vine in Angel Island 2 forcing you to swing into spikes and take damage; an unnecessary vertical screen lock during Marble Garden 2's falling-ceiling section; and the Super transformation animation not halting you in midair, which cancels it in certain circumstances.I wanted to like this. Sonic 3, in particular, is one of my favorite games of all time; as it stands, though, I can't recommend this garbage fire of a "remaster" to anyone. Sega hasn't learned anything from their previous mistakes, and they've now stained Headcannon's reputation by forcing an unfinished product to meet an unneeded deadline. Mania was delayed on PC to add ♥♥♥♥♥♥ DRM back when it released - why couldn't Sega have done the same here to let Headcannon actually finish and polish their game?This is especially insulting given the runaway success of Sonic Mania. Sega didn't touch that game - they published it, sure, but Christian Whitehead, Headcannon, and PagodaWest were the actual . Sega themselves can't even handle rereleasing the ports previously released by Christian and Headcannon, let alone developing an actual ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Sonic game on their own, as evidenced by the past few years of blunders. It feels like Sega thought they earned some goodwill with Mania, thought "hey, people will probably pay big money for classic Sonic games even if we put zero effort in!", and released this ♥♥♥♥.Zero disrespect for Headcannon, by the way. Their work on Sonic 1, 2, Mania, and this 3&K port had a lot of love put into them - there's plenty of tiny fixes and details peppered into this port that weren't in the original. God bless you, Headcannon, and ♥♥♥♥ you, Sega.Go get a Sonic CD key online or something to play the superior PC port of that game, and go play Sonic 1 Forever, Sonic 2 Absolute, and Sonic 3 A.I.R. for the good PC versions of those. Don't let Sega scam you out of your money for this. I won't be coming back to Origins unless it gets major patches, whether official or unofficial, and major community mods to boot.What a cluster♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: What should have been a smash-hit celebration of the greatest games of Sonic's history is instead a lackluster collection of ports that are universally worse than even the mobile versions. This is currently one of the worst ways to play Sonic 1-3 or Sonic CD.- The game uses poor sprite scaling (likely linear/bilinear rather than integer) that makes the in-game graphics look blurrier than Mania or any of the mobile remasters. This does not appear to be a problem with any other platforms.- The UI looks astonishingly blurry on high-resolution displays, as if it was created for a 720p  display and then stretched with, again, poor filtering.- The sharp/smooth/CRT filtering options from previous releases have been completely removed.- There is no way to play the games in the widescreen "remastered" mode with the original lives system. You're required to either use the new coins system that removes lives as a mechanic or play in a letterboxed square.- The game does not obey Windows display scaling. Running in a borderless window will cause the game to take up a small chunk of the display.- The game has vsync issues. I get screen tearing issues owing to the game locking to 59fps instead of 60fps.- The music used for Sonic 3's Carnival Night, Ice Cap, and Launch Base zones are sharp downgrades from the prototype versions people thought we were getting. Sega directly stated these would use the original genesis soundchip, but they instead appear to be based on MIDI versions from the mid-90s PC collection. It's rough - Carnival Night in particular sounds like it's from a completely different system, terribly muffled/muddy and with a melody that's almost entirely absent due to poor mixing.- Bugs that were present in the original release of Mania have found their way back in, including bad Tails pathfinding. There are lots of scenarios where Tails will end up stuck on springs off-screen, producing terrible noises.- There are new and exciting physics bugs in Sonic 3 surrounding changing water levels and almost every stage gimmick.- Drop Dash locks your direction in Sonic 1 and Sonic 2, and the way it interacts with slopes in those games makes it basically unusable.- The DLC is a blatant cash grab, and would've just been cute add-ins for any other collection.- The game's encrypted with Denuvo, so while some of this can be fixed by mods (like sound files), expecting anything deeper is a tall order. For the price, the community shouldn't be expected to fix the game's shortcomings.I have a lot of other nitpicks (why are the options are tucked away in the Museum, why can you not change keyboard key binds, and why can you not move with the arrow keys?), but almost every one of these is a dealbreaker. This release is astonishingly buggy and rushed, and until/unless Sega addresses some of the many issues, this is just a worse way to play games you can already play just about anywhere else.I can't believe they want $45 for this.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing all of the games in Sonic Origins, I had to alter my review.  Avoid this game, unless you desperately want the widescreen presentation.  It's presented as the original Sonic games, but it is a buggy mess, and the game physics are definitely different and it frequently breaks things that are supposed to just work.  Can't go fast if the game dunks you into walls instead of that graceful slope designed to catch you. Additionally Sega has delisted secretary Sonic games to make you but this travesty at 4x the price. That said, there are several places you can still get digital copies, and there is a rich fan base that has modded many of the features of this game into other releases.   Personally, I own physical copies of all of these games. If you have a real system and don't mind spending the money, you can get an ossc and cables and hook up your Sega Genesis to a 4k TV and play then as they were intended without some weird corporate shenanigans.  I have hardware to play them in 4k and on the original systems.  To make matters worse, I payed extra to get access to the soundtracks, which are not the original, and are only available in-game.  So basically I payed extra for a sound test that had to be unlocked.In many ways the games are a lot easier here than the originals, and I don't consider that a bad thing.  Having extra player options, essentially, infinite lives, and saves for each stage.  Not to forget the 16x9 aspect, which increases the screen real-estate.  As far as I'm concerned, the game is a money grab and the most cynical re-branding of an original and beloved series.  There are five different editions of this game and they all should have been included as just one edition. Most of the added content is not new. And most of the digital Deluxe edition is a cosmetic change that most players would not know or care if they were missing.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic is back, but this time as a collection of older titles instead of something brand new. New Sonic games tend to have all sorts of issues, so surely a straight remaster of older ones would not? Well...Sonic Origins is a collection of four games: Sonic the Hedgehog, Sonic the Hedgehog 2, Sonic 3 & Knuckles, and Sonic CD. Each is presented in two formats: Classic Mode, which plays like the games were on their original platforms and then Anniversary Mode, which adds widescreen support and removes lives. Both have their merits, but the widescreen support added by Anniversary Mode absolutely elevates the experience and is easily one of the game’s best features.And yes, the games themselves are great. Fast and fun gameplay with a great mix of platforming, diverse level design with all sorts of interesting stuff to find, and just the right amount of challenge. I’ve always liked how freeform Sonic’s gameplay is and how open the levels were and these four games are no exception.The original game is perhaps the roughest of the bunch, but easily has some of the most memorable stages. The second game is the most difficult of the bunch, but has some of the best music. The third game has the most balanced gameplay of the bunch and honestly might be my favorite. CD is a bit of a weird one, combining some of the good aspects of the others, but I was not a fan of the time travel mechanic and boss fights; it’s probably my least favorite of the bunch.The question is then - do the changes made to these classics make the collection worth it? That’s a bit of an iffy one. On one hand, the package is a bit more expensive than I was expecting for a collection of four old games. With a $40 price tag, I wish the game had included even more classic Sonic games. For starters, Knuckles' Chaotix would have been an excellent addition, but Sonic Chaos, Sonic Triple Trouble, and the Sonic Advance games would have been great too.Quality of life is also an issue. These are old classics ported to modern platforms without the usual features we get with such releases, such as save states or the ability to rewind. I can do without the latter, but save states would have been super cool to have here and that is something that straight emulation does better than this collection.I also was not the biggest fan of whatever filter was used to scale these games up. It looks a bit blurry and nowhere near as crisp as I would have liked - even when messing around with settings like resolution and anti-aliasing (which I recommend you keep disabled). As it stands, it does take some getting used to.The collection does do good in its addition of new game modes though, including boss rush, mirror mode, and a mission mode that adds a bunch of new objectives. Not all of those missions land, but it’s a nice addition regardless. The museum mode is a nice touch too, allowing access to artwork, music, and videos.Perhaps the biggest issue with this collection though is how buggy it is, particularly on the audio front. In every game, I had audio cutting out too early, audio repeatedly playing even when not doing anything, muffled music, and in a few cases - the audio completely bugging out and playing nonstop loud and annoying sounds. And while I have not noticed any collision or physics issues - that also appears to be a common complaint.The collection is obviously a rushed job and you need look no further than the very devs that worked on it stating as such. Apparently there was some sort of disconnect there between the remaster devs and the actual finished product, leading to many strange bugs.I cannot give Sonic Origins a straight positive recommendation, but I also cannot say that it’s entirely negative either - this is why I wish Steam had something in the middle. On one hand, these are some absolutely solid classics and I am glad they are available on modern platforms, but on the other, the collection itself is lacking and there are quite a few technical issues on top of that.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: This was not worth the pre-order. The dropdash in sonic 1, 2, and CD does not work like it does in mania: instead, in one frame sonic does a spindash. This is significant because it alters how momentum works because you have to crouch to spindash. This does not feel right, I often notice dropdashes that would have worked in Sonic Mania often send me a different way than I expect. There is no reason for sega to remove the standalone versions of these games other than to artificially drive prices up for this and that is unacceptable having now played it. The price point of 40 dollars USD (or 45 dollars if you want the unlockables early) is bad as well, seeing as it was easy to get these games for around 10 dollars before the cleanse. There is also a noticeable lack of customization, and it is impossible to play with lives and have fullscreen or have the dropdash in 4:3. It is nonsensical as to why the player does not have control over this. Plus, the music in sonic three sounds awful. I get the micheal jackson tracks can't be used, but what happened here? The Sonic 3 prototype had these songs perfect on genesis. Using the MIDI versions from the PC release wasn't necessary. It makes these songs, which are entirely fine, sound worse than they should.For 40 dollars, you get a gimped dropdash, animated cutscenes that already leaked on twitter/youtube, and 3D backgrounds that do not add anything to gameplay. Knuckles is also not playable in sonic cd (for what reason? who knows, but is worth mentioning considering it cannot be that hard to add him). This is not worth it. Unfortunately, this is the only majorly accessible way (without piracy) to play these games (even buying the sega genesis classics collection in full will not get you sonic 1, 2, and 3 anymore). TLDR: Lazy ports (with exception to Sonic 3 and Knuckles, mostly) that are overpriced. Avoid this unless you MUST play classic sonic on pc. Even then, wait for a discount. The game as is feels empty and devoid of purpose. These games were already available and for a better price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is amazing. With a few drawbacks..I just finished marathoning every game on this 100% through the story mode. It was a blast, I loved every second of it!Of course, this is a rerelease of 4 (maybe 5 if you count S&K as a seperate game,) 30 old games. The price point of 40 dollars is quite steep, so does it do a good job compensating?Sonic 1, 2, and CD are the mobile ports, unsurprisingly. However, they've all been upgraded with the drop dash, making all of them a lot more fast pased and fun. However, I will note, I noticed a bit of input lag in the beginning, particularly Sonic 1, but it's not too game breaking and you can get used to it fairly quickly. As far as I know there is none in games following, and definitely not in S3&K. All of the games now have opening and ending cutscenes, and Sonic CD gets extra ones adding onto the existing ones in the original. They are all absolutely adorable and have a ton of charm, and some even add a bit of worldbuilding to the already established lore. However, these cutscenes are best experienced in game without spoilers. If you watched them on a compilation on YouTube, they definitely won't have the same impact.I've only dabbled a bit in mission mode, and haven't gone around to time attack yet, so I can't say anything about them yet, so please check out other reviews for information on those. As for the museum, it's great. There's a ton of fan-service, especially in the art section. I wish we had more historical videos in the videos section, but what we got was really cool, including animatics for the in-game cutscenes. The art has a ton of fanservice and is a blast to look through. There is a ton of art that hasn't been released to the public until now, and it's great stuff!I want to talk about S3&K. Of course, due to the problems with MJ, SEGA couldn't use the original music tracks for a few levels. Because of this, they used the prototype music, but instead of just ripping it and remastering it, they remade it from scratch. Unfortunately, the remade versions aren't up to par with the originals at all. Even some tracks that didn't need to be changed got changed, including the Super Sonic theme in S3&K, which got changed to a more light-hearted tune more in line with Sonic 2's Super Sonic theme, however, it uses Sonic 4 instruments, which is incredibly unfitting in Sonic 3. I'm sure there will be a mod fixing this eventually, but for now this is what we have.Also with a few scummy business practices, as for the digital deluxe release, and the delistings of the other older titles, I can understand why people would pass this up. What I'd say is, if you're a die-hard fan of the series, pick it up! It's great and I'd say you'll have a great time, and all of the little bonus content is amazing to discover as a fan If you don't care about Sonic all too much, I'd say you should still pick it up, but moreso when it's on sale. If you don't like Sonic at all, I doubt you'd get the game anyway.so, regardless whether you will buy/bought the game or not, I hope we all enjoyed Sonic's 31st anniversary and that the future for this beloved blue blur is bright! :D

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely disgraceful collection but I did not expect anything more since it was made "internally at SEGA"CONS:Most important - NO integer scaling, meaning all 4 games look just as blurry as Sonic CD 2011. What was the point of finally releasing the 2013 remasters on consoles if they look worse than when they did on mobile?Mission Mode is comprised of bite-sized, generically-designed levels that would make the most amateur platformers blush. I could tell it was made by Sonic Team cuz the mode features grey X-blocks like Forces and they're EVERYWHERE with no slopes in sightKnuckles isn't playable in CD (a primarily exploration-based game). Don't get me started on Amy - a character that's been promoted since the Archie Mega Drive days as part of Team Sonic. Then in Mania Adventures, then in IDW comics, and now here. So you'd think they would finally make her playable? Lol, you want them to make a NEW sprite-sheet (which they did back in CD 2011 for Tails)? You're asking for too muchNo customizations. After all these years, after fan projects like S1 Forever, S2 Absolute, S3 Complete, S3 A.I.R., OR EVEN Sonic Mania, our boys at SEGA couldn't be bothered to add the most BASIC options between all 4 games like fans do. No peel-out in S3, elemental shields in S1/CD/2, max control, Jam difficulties, can't disable the Drop Dash, no option to use lives/timeouts in Anniversary Mode or collect Tokens in Classic Mode, etc.Island Tour DLC just allows you to zoom-in on each island, not even rotate them. Money well spent. And that "animated characters on island" DLC? All of them are ripped from Gens/ForcesSuper Sonic isn't in S1. Now you might say "What are you talking about, obviously he isn't". Yeah, umm... except some Japanese promo images showed him in Scrap Brain. So I thought "Oh, so he, alongside a 7th Special Stage are in Anniversary Mode, nice bonus". And he isn't. You can only access him using cheats, just like on mobile. Is this a nitpick? Yeah, but maybe they shouldn't have blatantly lie to consumers, then The "Drop Dash" is a pure lie. What do I mean? It's actually a disguised Spin Dash animation that happens for a split-second? Doesn't sound bad, except the AGES version of S1/S2 natively added it to their ROMs. Oh! And in Origins it BARELY moves you after you execute it. Best part? S1/S2 have a fixed jump arc, so if you try to do this move in those games and jump, you won't be able to control yourself mid-air (think Castlevania)The Museum... god, remember those so-called "never-before seen concept arts" they promised? Well I'm here to tell you there are like 6 of them, everything else are Harmony covers and character sheets. The Video section has none of those cool 90s ads, promo videos or even documentaries, just a few pieces of the Sonic Symphony they threw in at the last hour, Origins' cutscenes and every episode of Mania Adventures (and their respective animatics). Both Normal and Premium sections offer very little content, especially if you pre-ordered the game which gives you a 100 Token bonus, you can literally unlock everything in under 2 hours. Not to mention it's complete silence, no remix of History or anything like that, no feeling of nostalgia. Just cynical, corporate silence as you browse what little they offer. Only ""new"" track here is a remix of Sonic World from Jam that plays everywhere except the Museum. ClassyS1/2/CD are straight mobile versions, so they haven't been touched up at all. Meaning the missing rolling SFX in CD hasn't been fixed, and the extended camera is still absentHorrible audio quality. Believe it or not, they REMOVED the remastered OSTs for S1, CD and S2 from mobile. Why? No clue. As for S3&K, y'know... the only new thing here, it isn't given the same treatment so its OST is really muffled, and ON TOP OF THAT, CD's 2 OSTs are super quiet and also in bad quality. How did they screw it up? idk, but it is hilarious Your Score in S3&K resets to 0 if you click the Restart button. This doesn't happen in other gamesThe music DLC (Chaotix, 3D Blast and Spinball) misnamed countless tracks. For example; Chaotix's bad ending theme (Destructive Power) is Door to Summer, while 3D Blast's Invincibility theme is the Menu theme. Incompetent? Very much. Funny? AbsolutelyNo Chaotix island. You might notice how Origins' gallery features stuff from Chaotix, 3D Blast and Spinball, the OSTs from those games they repackaged as DLC at the last minute, as well as the islands from Spinball and 3D Blast in the hub menu and... wait a second... where's the Island of Miracles from Chaotix? You telling me, the island from a game that is the closest to Sonic's gameplay of that era isn't here... but islands from 2 US-made games, one of which is a pinball spin-off made to promote a show that never aired in Japan, are here? Not only is this sorta insulting, I'm like 1000% sure it was supposed to be here as an Options island, they just didn't make a model of it in time, and plastered Options in the Museum of all placesScrewed up physics. Due to S3&K here clearly being made on Mania's engine, it had a lot of ramifications on the game's internal logic. Some stuff is cool like all elemental shields function how they did in Mania, making the bubble shield fun to use. Others... because the game now controls exactly like Mania, there are a LOT of collision/physics bugs that weren't present in the OG gameCD's ending animation. While the restoration team did really well with remastering the original opening, I... have no idea what happened with the ending. It looks like one of those interpolated anime clips. Worst part? It's sped up by 3x and there are no SFXs in the beginning, so it instantly plays the credits theme. The Gallery also plays it off-sync and it doesn't feature the bad ending version. Actually a jokeEven though I'm not one of those people that plays S3 and S&K separately, it's kinda absurd how they initially advertised this collection with those 2 games in mind. Final release? You can't play them separately. Oh wellThe new S3&K tracks. I don't know what sound chip Jun Senoue (same guy who composed S4EI) used but it sure wasn't a Mega Drive one. Tracks sound muffled, quiet and overall don't fit the game. It's especially insulting to CNZ Act 2, its prototype track is EASILY one of my favorite Sonic tunes... and Jun completely butchered it. They should've asked Yuzo Koshiro to recompose them. But you wanna know THE coolest part? Origins is made on Criware, meaning the audio is encrypted, meaning it'll be really hard to mod music in. Just a neat thing, y'know :)Denuvo. No need to explain, you already know the game runs poorly. Countless stuttering tooPROS:Cutscenes look great, but what did you expect from Tyson Hesse and Powerhouse, you knew they'd pull it off with flying colors. However they haven't animated any of the bad endings, meaning if you get one in any of the games, it would still play said game's true endingThe restoration group they hired to scan various pieces for the Museum and clean up the CD opening (not the ending) did a really good jobThe S3&K remaster, despite the collection's flaws, is alright. Nowhere near the level of AIR, which is odd cuz I know Stealth and his crew can do WAY better than this. At least it wasn't done by SEGAClassic games on PC, so your usual "Hope modders will fix it" mentality will continue yet again! You expect SEGA to do all the work? Pfftt, yeah rightNotice how all the collection's positives I listed were outsourced to 3rd parties and not done by SEGA? That should tell you how much they care. In the end you're left with:Sonic 1 (the Spin Dash is still present in the so-called Classic mode)Sonic 2 (with a horrible, downright game-breaking Tails AI)Sonic CD (they use leftover UI from the mobile version I kid you not)and Sonic 3&K (with its muffled, MJ-free OST)Happy 31st Anniversary, Sonic. _childDocuments_.review: Well well well, it appears that the internet is yet again too judgeful for a product which didnt deserve all the hate it recieved.....Let me explain to you why i chose to recommend this product despite its past negativity.When i was a kid i grew up playing the old sonic games with a collection called "sonic mega collection plus" (for the PC) which im sure most of you might be familiar with, it contained the original sonic games (except sonic cd which i was really eager to try out) from that point the classic sonic games (my favorites were sonic 1, 2 and 3&k) became my personal favorites and grew on me for the time being, ever since then i havent touched my beloved classics for a decade and unfortunately i handed over my bundle to my cousin which i regret to this day..... (plus computers dont really support CDs anymore so even if i still had it, it would still be useless)Fast forward for the announcement of sonic origins and i was rather thrilled to give it a shot, return back my childhood memories that filled me with joy, thanks to the new sonic movies and my introduction with sonic mania i was finally united with sonic after almost 10 years of not touching a single sonic game. but as you guys may assume i started developing hatred due to the internet's poor reception for the product's release, swearing to never buy it at its current state, i didnt wish to waste my hard earned money on a product filled with gamebreaking bugs.For months ive been debating with myself if i should buy sonic origins whenever i could and decided i would only do it when the game goes on sale, and that is excactly what i did.Let me tell you a bit about the experience i had with each game that was offered in the bundle (by the way i recommend you to get a controller to play the games, keyboard controls are a bit clunky)Sonic 1: the first entry in the series was actually very wierd for me at first, afterall i havent touched it in years,although it is still the slowest sonic game out of all the sonic games on the list, it was still fun but felt exausting clearing 3 stages with no innovation, but hey, it was the first game so i cant blame them.Sonic CD: This game i never tried before and was very eager to finally play it, many would call it "the black sheep" of the series as its generally very different than a normal sonic game, its essentially a sonic 1 upgrade but not fully understandable, i found the level design very odd and not very enjoyable, lets just say i didnt like the game and it made me sick, would never play again but im still happy i tried it and saw how a classic sonic game shouldnt be made.Sonic 2: now we get to the fun part, my second favorite game of this collection, this time sonic gets a new buddy named "tails" which really added flavour to the game and although his controls arent perfect, he is surly a great add on to the game, level design is very good with a sign of a huge progress from sonic 1, utilizing speed more than its previous installment.Sonic 3&K: And the cherry on top, the absolute king and the game that truly finished this collection with a great taste in my mouth is this masterpiece of a game, with the introduction of an actual story in the game, sonic 3&k suddenly gets more depth which would later follow to other games with much more complicated plots like the sonic adventure games which are heavily based on sonic 3&k's story.Plus, with me restoring back the MJ tracks to the game, it made the experience even more enjoyable (no stupid lawsuit will stop me from enjoying these goosebumping tracks >:D)So, what is the overall verdict of the product? Well after thinking about it deeply i came to a conclusion that at its current state, its a totally worth buying!and before you call me biast , heres why i think that way:1) I havent encountered a single bug/glitch as reported by many in the past, it appears that SEGA has indeed fixed the product and its now safe to buy, although i dont promise you that you wont encounter old school bs like bottomless pits and ingame mechanics which are still fairly annoying at times.2) The cutseens done for the game are absolutely gorgeous! the amount of effort and work that have been put to them are mindblowing, and with the introduction of story mode, these cutseens are connecting each and every classic in its place, creating a wonderful story.3) For those that claim that denuvo crushes the game's identity/ruins the game/doesnt allow mods/decreases performances ive got news for you, DO YOU GUY KNOW HOW MANY GAMES RUN ON DENUVO ANTI CHEAT? IF YOU DONT, HERES A FULL LIST OF THEM 4) And for those that miss the MJ tracks of sonic 3&k, just replace the horrible tracks with the tracks here For those that are still wondering if you should buy the bundle or not, it depends if you own previous classic sonic games or not, if you own them in any platform then i wouldnt recommend it, but if you are new to the franchise, looking for a quick escape with the timeless classics of the 90s or just want to add the classic sonic games to your game library, you should give it a go. (And if you worry about the price, just buy the standard edition or wait for a SEGA sale)Do i think this is the best classic sonic game bundle ever released? Of course not! do i condemn SEGA's decision with delisting all of the classic sonic games on steam? Absolutely! But do i think this bundle deserves all the hate it got? Not at all!But at last, Sonic origins is still worthwhile if you fit the categories, otherwise you are just wasting your money with a bundle which will get released a decade later.The classic sonic games will forever have a place deep in my heart as the games that truly defined my childhood and made me the returning sonic fan i am now, its not necessarily the bundle that made me this way, its the games i got to experience once more and keep them where they belong, proudly displayed in my games collection.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, you may have noticed some remakes or remasters of Sonic games, like Sonic Origins released recently with some added features, cutscenes and more. But that game has mixed reviews as that game is pretty much similar to Sega Mega Drive Classics on Steam, despite the added cutscenes, achievements and modifications.Why does this game have mixed reviews? Well, it appears to be pricey to have 3 of the original Mega Drive Sonic games merged into one - plus the Sega CD of Sonic CD game, but doesn't have some key improvements. For example, it doesn't appear to have a Classic Scanline screen or to make it look like you are playing on a CRT 1990s TV - like being back in the old school 1990s era. And it doesn't appear to have like HQx2 or xBRZ to smooth those staircase edges nor make Sonic look smoother for gamers who hate eye strains.Don't get me wrong, but the higher frame rates, Museum and Special Missions are ok. However, this game reminds me of the Sonic Mega Collection and Sonic Gems Collection for the GameCube which contains those classic Sonic games for the Mega Drive, Game Gear, Saturn and Arcade. Even the Sonic Mega Collection and Sonic Gems Collection contain some interesting archives and pictures of Sonic the Comic, and Sonic Coin-Op machines some of which were only released in Japan. But those archive collections, achievements and special missions should be only used as bonus features and focus on how to improve the general gameplay for those Sonic Classic games, as well as the remakes.Some gamers don't realise that having VSync on for Sonic Origins causes display lag and we got powerful GFX cards that won't cause screen tearing for playing remade 16-Bit games on an emulator - unless you are using xBRZ at a high factor or that. The Spindash for Sonic 1 segment for Sonic Origins and the Gold Coins used as Lives are ok, but that seems too feeble if you ask me. Also, Sonic 2 had some maps or levels removed as Mega Drive cartridge ROMs had limited storage.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh god what a let down this was.So first off, the game ran HORRIBLY, mainly suffering ALOT of slowdown whenever the game saved, started a level, came off from the main menu or entering a Special Stage; majority of the time pausing and unpausing would fix the slowdown but around Lava Reef in S3&K the slowdown would happen way more often, maybe it was because of Hyper Sonic? Honestly majority of these issues seem more than likely caused by Denuvo DRM, which from last time it was used in a Classic Sonic title (Sonic Mania) it ran horribly. So I was wishing they'd had some hindsight.The controls in Sonic 1, CD and 2 are all messed up. Main example being that the drop dash is implemented in a way where when you land you don't do the dash immediately and instead it keeps you vulnerable for a frame before doing a SHORT spindash. Alongside this when rolling your controls are locked to just jumping, you are incapable of doing ANY course correction or even changing the direction you're dashing with the Drop Dash.During Sonic CD specifically the sound effects are all sorts of messed up, what comes to mind first for it being the air timer and drowning being pitched up and out of sync. The goal post spinning and other sound effects also end up sounding like they're played through a botched emulator, maybe even an AtGames Mega Drive.In Sonic 3 & Knuckles, the most promising of the games in this batch, the music and sound effects sound really muffled or compressed at times, and the new remixes of the Prototype tracks are flat and out of key at points. And don't get me started on the special stages, I had gotten all 7 Chaos Emeralds by Marble Garden ACT 1, during which I was able to transform into Super Sonic fine. By ACT 2 my Chaos Emeralds had reset to 1 for some reason, in which I had to get all of them AGAIN. And even after that touching a Giant Ring would make me repeat the seventh Blue Spheres stage instead of giving me 50 rings, despite me already having the emeralds. This problem was fixed by Mushroom Hill ACT 1 though due to how the Super Emeralds work. Speaking of the Super Emeralds, using Hyper Sonic is a nightmare. So they never removed his rapidly flashing colour palette or screen clearing flash of white, infact they only made the screen flash worse by adding a hyper quick fade in/out.These experiences were all from one marathon of the Story Mode, and while the new cutscenes and visual additions to S3&K were great and fun, the problems listed above were enough to make my favourite games a miserable experience.Overall this is a pretty bad collection and remaster, bringing bugs and issues to already perfected versions of Sonic 1, CD and 2 (Mobile, IOS/Android) and a decent but buggy remaster of Sonic 3 & Knuckles, which supposedly according to Stealth from Headcannon on Twitter, is not what they handed SEGA fully.If I was to recommend this it'd be hopefully after the game gets patched, as I can see this becoming my main way to play these games if the launch wasn't botched.Instead I'd recommend the Mobile ports of these games and maybe emulating Sonic 3, I would recommend them all from steam but SEGA removed being able to buy the Mega Drive versions of these games a month or two ago to make way for this.Play Sonic 1 Forever, Sonic 2 Absolute, Sonic CD decompilled and Sonic 3 Angel Island Revisited if you want a PC widescreen Sonic experience, all of these require dumps of the payed versions of the games from mobile and a rom back up of Sonic 3, methods for obtaining a rom I cannot give as SEGA's official version of Sonic 3 & Knuckles no longer exists here, which S3AIR used.

_childDocuments_.review: Initial Reactions for Sonic 3 and knuckles (spoilers)I grew up with the Genesis Games and I even have the damn strategy guide for Sonic 3 when it first came out. I was a huge Sonic Fan and I would still be if this series was just treated with the respect it deserves from its creators. Instead, once again, for the THOUSANDTH time since we've all started playing sonic. "Just barely good enough" is Sega's motto when it comes to these games.The Good-Widescreen-Supposedly scales up to 4K, I have yet to even try that out-Coins are a good incentive to travel throughout the whole game and grab as many rings as possible-Super Sonic is Mapped to the Y Button like in Sonic Mania-Tails Helper Controls are nearly perfect-The camera controls seem to function better than the default controls in Sonic A.I.R, and you can now outrun the screen again. it's quite cool-Ice Cap Act 1 and 2 and Launch Base Act 1 use their prototype music without many changes...And the Bad- The Music does not start or stop correctly in stages. Everything has a strange fade-in and fade-out effect.- Special Stage Controls are tweaked, so if you're used to timing from S3/S3Air you will need to adjust- For that matter it's sort of difficult to use the sound effects from the special stage as a reference point for when you need to turn because of how delayed they are- The Special Stage music never speeds up as you play. So we went from S3 speed up too fast, S3K speeding up slower, and now S3K origins not speeding up at all... why?- Many Sound effects are seemingly added in all over the place for no good reason, It makes some parts feel like I'm watching a flash/youtube fan movie- Instead of letting you fruitlessly attack the first miniboss, they now arbitrarily lock you in place.- The Super Sonic Music is absolutely terrible and I would've rather them played the invincibility theme if it was going to be this bad- The Sonic 3 invincibility music is gone.. BUT they let you listen to it in museum mode for some crazy reason!- Absolutely no gameplay customization options whatsoever as far as I can tell (not surprised...)- Marble Garden's Crushers can now kill you from ALL SIDES rather than you needing to be under them... Ugh!- Marble Garden's swinging spikeball hitboxes are bigger for some reason?- A lot of things break really easily for the experienced players zipping through all the zones: Effects that are supposed to last for moments instead glitch out and last the entire level (For instance Marble Garden Zone when you first encounter the mini boss has debris falling and then it never stops if you run past it).- Carnival Night Act 1 and 2 and Launch Base Act 2 music is god awful which is weird because the prototype music that was recently dug up would've been perfect to use. Either they used the wrong versions or Jun just plain out screwed up.The worst offender of them all-They list and let you listen to the "unused music" for sonic 3 in the museum mode, which the community has already agreed on being probably the prototype super sonic music, but Jun made his own track for the game that screams sonic 4 levels of bad and you cant. turn. it. OFF.I'll update this as I go along but I really hope they fix the music up...Edit: So supposedly the entire game is built up as a modification of Sonic Mania. That's interesting but what's REALLY screwed up is sega took these ports and forced them to run alongside the hedgehog engine that powers their 3D games. They hacked into the sound engine part of the Retro engine that powers the game and... absolutely butchered it.So to break it down for you guys, and please leave a thumbs up if this makes sense...Sega used their 3D game engine to replace the perfect sound that these games had to begin with on the retro engine... and on top of denuvo you are running a 3D game engine at the same time as these 2D engines. This isn't some sort of "Haha technically..." or "Gotcha". This is what's actually happening, does it now make sense why the game runs like ♥♥♥♥?

_childDocuments_.review: …Yipes.Sonic Origins is like fitting a circle into the rectangle hole. After throwing away all of the rectangles. And taping shut the circle hole. But hey, they poured glitter onto the circle, so surely it MUST be worth it, right?I bought this game BEFORE the DLC came out, and I haven’t played it since. Why? Simple. It’s Sonic 1, 2, 3, and CD… and that’s basically it. What are its new features? A few cutscenes, some collectables and achievements, and small mini-challenges. Which are fine… in a vacuum. I paid $40 dollars for this?? I have Sonic 3 on Sega Mega Drive Classics, and the rewind and speed-up features along with the Genesis limitations made it instantly more fun and replayability due to easily accessible mods. And that was like… $5? Sonic 1, 2, and CD on Mobile are like $2 a pop. That’s $11 dollars! Even if you round up every game to $5, that’s $20! And the game is $40!…Or, it used to be.This is the thing that brung me to make a review. With the release of Sonic Origins Plus, the original game’s price lowered down to $30 so Sonic Origins Plus could take the original price of $40. Great, right? More things for the same price, where’s the downside?People who bought the original game, for $40, still have to pay 10 extra dollars if they want to enjoy the “full” experience. That is 50 dollars for $20 and a bunch of Game Gear games, most of the games in question being available in Sonic Adventure DX if they didn’t REMOVE it as a FEATURE.I could buy Sonic Frontiers with $50! I could (have) buy/bought all the Genesis games included in this collection along with Sonic Mania AND THEN SOME with $50! I could buy Sonic Mania, the Encore DLC, AND Sonic Generations for $50. At full price.If you like it, that’s fine. It just didn’t deliver for me personally.

_childDocuments_.review: Lifetime Sonic fan here. I was born in '92 and have been playing Sonic games ever since I was a small child playing our Sega Genesis (which our family still has!).Sonic Origins is, so far, an excellent Anniversary collection of the 4 definitive Sonic games.The new animations are phenomenal, and yes, CD fans, they kept the original CD Intro/Outro included (you just can't beat perfection). The music is all top-tier gold, and the collection of bonus content as well as all the missions and modes is a nice addition.I do have a few minor frustrations with this go-around of the blue blur's earliest adventures, but these should not deter anyone from grabbing a copy of this. - Cannot bind arrow keys for gameplay. This issue baffles me, I really don't even know what to say here. - The new CD intro with Amy is far too short, and includes a part of her character that should've been left buried: namely, Tarot cards. It serves no purpose and brings real world occultism into an otherwise fun and fictional franchise. I know how some people would react to me saying this, but I stand firm in my beliefs: Spirituality is important, and things like tarot cards can be very spiritually disastrous to play with, so I don't think it should have a place in a generally kid-friendly series. - In Sonic 1, I had a few issues with movement, surprisingly. When holding left/right movement keys and Sonic hits a wall or gets hurt, sometimes he doesn't move until you let go of the key and then press it again. Never had that problem in other versions of Sonic 1, so I'm not sure what's happening here.Don't let these issues keep you from enjoying this heartfelt, warm experience, they are extremely minor in contrast to the fresh experience that Origins offers. I highly recommend! ♥

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say Origins a very good collection as well as it runs smooth. I changed all my settings on my laptop to be high performance for the game but it didn't perform well until I actually went into the game and lowered the resolution down two notches. By far my favorite part of Origins is Sonic 3. I hear people complaining about the physics being wrong but I haven't had any issues with those and I think it plays very well. The new frames, sound effects, and added cutscenes create a whole new experience for me personally, You don't realize how smooth the game is until you enter a special stage or a blue orb stage. It's so incredibly smooth that it feels like a modern day sonic installment. My biggest complaint for sonic 3 and Origins in general is definitely the removal of MJ's tracks which include Carnival Night Zone, Launch Base Zone, and my personal favorite Ice Cap Zone. I wound up installing a mod to get all those tracks back because I couldn't stand the alternative themes. (There's also new music for super sonic but I thought it sounded better than the original.)As for the rest of Origins, I say it's all pretty good. Sonic is able to use all of his mania abilities and it felt a little out of place to be spin dashing and drop dashing in sonic 1. In sonic 3 I'm so glad they combined the temporary shield and the drop dash; they compliment each other very well. The extras (with the exception of challenges) feel kind of pointless and I don't really care much about them. Although if you like looking at old boxart, concepts and promotional material be my guest.I'd highly recommend this game to people who've never played these classics and I think it's a great way to jump back into the games for people who grew up with these games like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a HUGE Classic Sonic fan but this collection here is a giant disappointment and I'm gonna give out criticism on why I hate this collection. My main criticism about this collection is the pricing, 55 CAD is too much for four Classic Sonic games, especially when compared to Sonic Mega Collection which cost 20 dollars with 12 games. Sega even decided to delist the four Classic Sonic games on the digital store when the trailer came out and decided to lock some content behind DLCs such as extra missions and some island additions, That is very disgusting since it's a collection of four 30-year-old games. You even can't play as Metal Sonic or Amy Rose despite them being featured in the collection and can't even play as Knuckles in Sonic CD which is just very absurd and a big missed opportunity. Speaking of missed opportunities, It even sucks that Sonic 3D Blast, Sonic Spinball, and Knuckles' Chaotix aren't even in the collection despite them being available as soundtracks by DLC (Classic Music Pack). Sonic 3 and Knuckles is by far the biggest offender here in this collection, asides the glitches and bugs, one of the things about this version that made me upset is the fact there aren't any MJ tracks in this version especially Ice Cap as it's replaced by the earlier music from the beta version of Sonic 3, don't get me wrong for two things, The Sonic 3 Prototype music is very catchy and Jun Senoue is a great composer for the Sonic games, The Prototype music in here sounds awful, especially Carnival Night, therefore, wasting Jun's talents in remixing those beta tracks which is just very sad. It still didn't make sense to remix when they could just port the music from the Prototype version. I pretty much doubt if one of the updates will bring back MJ tracks and I'm not exactly sure why they can't get the MJ music to this version, probably it's the licensing issue. That music changed especially Ice Cap sure did give fans hard times.  While Super and Hyper Sonic finally got their own theme in Sonic 3K instead of using repetitive invincibly music but literally sounds like Sonic 4 music which doesn't feel right for Sonic 3K because of its instruments and it's a shame that it's not using the Unused version (But yet the Unused version music was used in the New Blue Spheres results). Going to Sonic CD in this verison:Remember how the 2011 port of Sonic CD, the music of it uses the unused loops in the Japanese OST but for unknown reasons, they decided to use the music based on the original version of Sonic CD in the Origins version which I also noticed on Day one when the collection was out. The US OST loops weirdly as it's also based on the original version of Sonic CD as well.Going back to Sonic 3 in this collectionAs we got the music out of the way, I even ended up getting those issues in S3K EVEN WITH PATCHES. I ended up getting soft-locked multiple times, the first time I got soft-locked in Carnival Night by a barrel (or should I say Barrel of Doom), and the second time I got soft-locked in the Knuckles Battle in Hidden Palace after defeating him. There have been many glitches in this version especially at Launch.There are still some things wrong with this collection,Classic Mode - Adding Classic mode in this collection sounds like a perfect idea on paper but it's executed poorly as it's just the remastered versions at a 4:3 ratio, Sonic 1 still has the spindash while the original Sonic 1 didn't have a spindash, Sonic 2 in Mystic Caves still takes you to Hidden Palace when falling in the infamous pit, and Sonic 3 still have Sonic and Tails fight Big arms while in the original S3K you don't unless if you play as Knuckles. Couldn't they just have it emulated using the original Sonic versions when using Classic modeAnniversary Mode - Nothing to say much about it but there is another missed opportunity for an option where you can turn on lives.The games (Except for Sonic 3K) don't even have save slots, instead, when about to play the game, a character select will just pop up, even the Mobile ports of Sonic 1 and 2 have file selects. Same thing with the Sonic CD 2011 remake where it even has file selection and options but in Origins, you can only change settings in the title screen (I even noticed it resembles the original Sonic CD selection in Origins)Sonic CD in Origins has voice clips removed, removing "I'm Outta here" and"Yes" voice clips, Classic Sonic being muted is pretty stupid. (If you are wondering, Classic Sonic has gone voiceless since Sonic Generations)In General, This collection is just worthless with big letdowns, This collection is not a definitive way to play classic Sonic games, if you want a better remaster of those Classic Sonic games, I recommend Sonic 1 Forever, Sonic 2 Absolute, Sonic CD 2011, and Sonic 3 AIR. Those remasters are way surpeiorI gotta admit that I really love the little animation cutscenes here, and it feels so nice to finally see Sonic 3 and Knuckles getting a rerelease officially although I'm better off with those fan remasters like Sonic 3 AIR and the original version of the classic Sonic gamesI would rate this collection a 2/10. I recommend not buying Sonic Origins. It's not really worth it.If there's anything I'm forgetting, let me know.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like the first four Sonic games? Then this is a great way to play them. Do you not like classic Sonic? Then this probably won't change your mind. It's not anything mind-blowing, but fans will appreciate the new cutscenes and extra presentation and gameplay gubbins. Finally having some way to play Sonic 1 and 2 on something besides mobile (officially anyway) is very good, not to mention having Sonic 3&K playable in widescreen at all. Mission mode is a neat little diversion, story mode seems like a good way to just blitz through all the games in one string, the new Blue Spheres levels are fun if you're into that, and the museum is a nice bonus. I also appreciate the new coins system, as it makes playing special stages less of a headache. For purists, they will like that the original versions are included for preservation's sake (though no way to play Sonic 3 and S&K separately? Bit of a nitpick, but if you're going to include the original roms, might as well add that extra bit, yes?). A lot of people may balk at the "new" music in S3&K, but I enjoy these beta tracks and I'm glad that their existence allows Sega to re-release the game finally. Music is subjective, yadda-yaddaDenuvo sucks but doesn't impact gameplay, and the DLC and pre-order nickle-and-diming sucks but ultimately doesn't take that much away from the core experience. Depending on your priorities, one might also find these games to be too old for the price tag, though I personally think the price was just fine for what I got (four not-unsizeable games with updated presentation and gameplay and a variety of side challenges).It's probably the definitive official versions of the first four Sonic games.
