_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended. Some points though.- Fantastic animations, Fantastic music- Game-play is fun even though it can be a little frustrating because of how reloading works. Press n hold reload, upgrades reducing time would be nice. A couple bosses could maybe use a checkpoint to them - Story was great  - Really wish there was more story though, only cause I loved it that much and wanted more.- Quests added nice bits of lore and some extra story. However rewards felt small. Though with everything you need, suppose the rewards don't need to be much else.- An epilogue would've been nice at least, ending felt far to abrupt but again, cause I'd love more story. A happy ending, something!10/10 Indie "Motorvania" game
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying the game so far, the gameplay is fun and the story is interestingThe boss battles are neither, as of now ive stopped playing due to how infuriating the bosses are to the point that I have no idea if they were even playtested at all. The bosses are not hard per say, but each fight is incredibly long and drawn out for the simple sake of it and a lack of variety in the bosses themselves does not make the length of the fight fun, each boss has pretty much 2 attacks (some even have 1) , 3 if you are lucky, and each fight can be minutes long. Coupled with 1 hit to die and no checkpoints makes an otherwise good game and absolute slog. Anyone whos played the game can likely guess what boss has caused me to quit playing, and I likely wont pick it back up until some sort of fix is introduced.Also also, the soundtrack is amazing everywhere but the boss battles, which doesnt help alleviate the tedium of playing one for the 15th time
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: The idea of a bike riding game alas flash games from the long ago was something that already sounded fun.But oh boy Laika is quite the experience.A terribly bittersweet story where some things I expected, others dont, but all of them ended up making me feel melancholic and excited to see it as unfolded.Fantastic soundtrack, each and every single one of the cassettes were a joy to find just to hear whatever tune they had.The art is beautiful, the scenery, the characters (Shaza my beloved) and the presentation was just on point for everything the game try to tell. Now gameplay wise, it was really fun and exciting, the bike gameplay really can carry a lot, but I do have some complains:- The metroidvania aspect feels like it wasnt fully embraced, you wont get much more mobility later than when you started, and when you do, its too late. Pretty much all places are accesible with just your gun and bike, which I think its nice but for a game that proclaims itself as is, I expected more.- I felt like it dragged a bit of its runtime, there was a small time between "midgame to endgame" where I had no side things to do until it was completed, then it continued, by that time I was a tad exhausted with it so I went and tried finishing things up. So overall a bit of weird pacing there.- The optimization is a bit lacking, aswell as settings for it, I would lag with too many (and sometimes just one) particles and animated cutscenes will lag behind aswell which was frustrating (they are few and are AWESOME). I could appreciate some fixing on that side but apart from that it was plenty playable. Now tl;dr I DO recommend LATB, I think it was a nice little interesting experienceIt will last about 20+ hours depending on how you do and/or completeI hope you like Laika as much as I did, and props to everyone involved (PD: I got the recomendation from Pazos god bless him (if you know, you know))
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Laika's gameplay is the real selling point. "Excitebike" with guns feels natural yet challenging-- it's hard to master but very rewarding every step of the way. Oftentimes I found myself revisiting old areas just to drive around and shoot things, unmotivated by any questline. I had never done that in a game before! The art direction & theming complete the experience, telling an emotional story about womanhood. The game has some problem points (sometimes lacked readability, control customization like 90% of the way there) but it's otherwise a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: This game suffers from serious visibility issues, which make otherwise great mechanics feel extremely underwhelming and frustrating. I'm honestly not sure how these issues could've slipped past anyone, and they unfortunately render the game borderline unplayable.Why am I still recommending the game then? Because the soundtrack absolutely slaps, and the game is almost worth playing just to experience it. I also hope that the previously mentioned issues will be patched. Please, I beg of the developer, it's not too late. A simple post-processing filter to highlight important information (namely the player and the ground) might be all the game needs, along with zooming the camera out a bit. It pains me to see a otherwise wonderful game be run down by an issue which has a clear path to amelioration.In conclusion, this game is great, but it feels like a bit of a prototype. If you're alright with some visual clutter and the ensuing confusion, it's worth a try, but in its current state, it needs some work before I can call it "good".P.S. Y'all know the connotation with the word "wanker", yes? I fear it may be misplaced, and if not, eek.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game unreservedly. It's got a compelling story with great characters, a convincing post-apo wasteland setting, excellent presentation and beautiful music. Furthermore, its unique gameplay twists set it apart from the more traditional "metroidvanias", offering a refreshing take on the genre.Alas, this (rather cool) motorbike gimmick proves to be the main thorn in Laika's side. The controls are a bit overwhelming, which results in a lot of clumsy unforced deaths. Combat is quite repetitive, which is further exacerbated by the "die and retry" design. Dying makes all the mobs respawn, which feels needlessly punishing at times. Bosses are a mixed bag, sometimes challenging for the wrong reasons (wonky design, repetitive wait-your-turn-to-attack patterns, etc.).In the end, I really wanted to explore the world and see the story through, so I decided it was worth toughing through the frustrating moments. If you feel you've got the resilience, go for it: rough as it may be, this game is unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, that might not be what you expected when you go to play it.The game has good writing with some interesting characters and what seems like a cool story. I played the demo of this for awhile some time ago. Playing it now with the full version and its good fun again. Now i understand a little more about it to :)It is part Bullet Time, part puzzle, part metrovania, part buggy racing game, part fighting, part platforming,etc...If you are looking for a Tony Hawk or Forza horizon style racing game this is not it. What this is though is a really fun game, with a great art design, cool setting and fun gameplay that has a wide variety of aspects.Sometimes you will be shooting enemies, other times you wil be trying to avoid them and or block them with parts of your Bike,etc.. At first I wasn't sure if this would be the game for me, but once I started to take it for what it offers and not what I was expecting, i started to really enjoy it.Fun game, try it out! I played about 3 hours of the demo to, so its not just the 1 hour steam is showing here on the full game :)Oh yeah and it also runs well on the steam deck to!

_childDocuments_.review: I used to love playing the Bike Race motorcycle mobile game. This feels like if they took that, suped it up, added some sick bullet-time gun-play and told a grim post-apocalyptic story. _childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good 20 hour game, is the short of it.Gameplay is incredibly crisp and I fell in love with it instantly. As many have pointed out, the free demo will very quickly let you will even like it. The demo allows like 2 hours of content, and the save is even loadable by the full game. While playing this game you will feel very damn cool. You will also feel like a massive fool at times. It's amazing when those two feelings are mere seconds apart, because despite having just killed a mob of enemies and successfully reloaded every single weapon, you have face-planted into the ground. Only demerit here with gameplay is the boss fights are a bit... underwhelming? They're not bad, but they are not very hard nor mechanically intense. A bit of a blessing and a curse, as on one hand I wanted a bit more, but on the other I'm also terrible at boss fights in most games. The only boss I had trouble with I figured out was the easiest with a silly cheese strat that made me feel like I was morphing into a cheese wedge.The music is beautiful. The only issue I have with the music is some locations use their own forced... not even soundtrack, but more like ambiance. Considering how long I was in some those areas, it can get kinda dull. However when in areas the cassette player is available, there's a total of like 1 hour of music when they're all unlocked. The music has found its way into my Spotify playlists, it's just beautiful.Visually, game is quite lovely. The artstyle is very pretty, and I at no point thought that something didn't look great. (Note my experience with the demo did have a strange graphical bug, but the full game didn't have it.) The only gripe I have here is the camera. Some places the camera will move to give a specific view of a zone, which is great most the time. However when backtracking, it can result in enemies you can't see. The atmosphere of all the locations is amazing. Characters can also get quite expressive too.Technically the game is quite sound. I got stuck in the ground only twice, and the second time was entirely my fault. I only encountered maybe a handful of bugs, with only one of them I could consistently cause. Besides the one I could cause every single time I wanted it, I encountered 5 gameplay bugs and a harmless UI bug. In total I got stuck in the ground twice, left the camera behind twice, and had the weird progression lock. (I did something very strange and I can easily see how that broke the game, exiting and loading fixed it.) The UI bug is sometimes a quest will be in the logbook twice, but it fixes itself and doesn't cause any instability nor loss of function.Progression wise the game is decent. There are massive jumps in capability spread throughout the game, and they all feel great. Only thing I wish is the game either was like 2 hours longer after reaching peak capability, or gave the capability a bit earlier. A New Game+ might also help this, as I would love to replay the game with all the tools at my disposal to see how cracked it would be. I only went grinding for resources once, but that's because I wanted to do it all at once. Normal gameplay provides an adequate amount of resources, especially if you don't want to upgrade weapons you don't use.Now the story. The story is terrible. No, not the quality, the content. The quality is immaculate, but this game is the only piece of media that's put me on the verge of crying. I will shamelessly admit that there was a point where I had to lie down because I couldn't see from teary eyes. It's a shame that the story will be such a small part of this review, because to me this was pretty big plus. It's terribly great, 10/10.Quests. There's a lot of fetch quests and running around the world. There is a fast travel system, but it isn't convenient all the time. I didn't find that awful as I liked moving through the environment, but I can see how players won't like backtracking and going to places they have been before for simple fetch quests. The rewards are also not great, but eh. I mostly did them for the world building and it making me plan routes through the map.Now, with being only a 20 hour game for doing most of the game's content (I am at time of writing missing just playing more blackjack and cooking more buffs... and dying a lot), the big question is replayability. The story isn't going to hit as hard, but the gameplay will still be crisp. I'm pretty sure runs could be done with a specific playstyle/weapon/goal in mind.I doubt it would ever happen, but if the developers came back to this game I would buy a DLC without any hesitation. A New Game+ would be welcome as well, as I mentioned with being able to play the whole game again with all the bells and whistles. I don't see the need for a boss rush, since the bosses are more of a story telling element than a gameplay one, but I wouldn't be against it as it would probably have wicked speedruns.It's a wonderful game of a coyote mom just trying her best. It's not a perfect game, but the things that make it wonderful easily outshine the bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I really wanted to love this one but I just couldn’t get over a few fundamental issues. I loved the music and art, and the relationship between Puppy and Laika seems so earnest. However, I ran into many QoL issues the deeper I got into Laika ATB. There should be a large balance meter visible at all times instead of when aiming with the reticle (the gear in the bottom right is great but the subtle red coloring when off balance is hard to see). Considering how minuscule Laika’s sprite becomes, it’s insane to me that this isn’t an option. It must be a nightmare for colorblind players. Also, this game is really not suited well for Steam Deck. Laika’s sprite just gets way too small to be seen well. It works better on a monitor or TV, but even then sprite size, on screen action, and how easily Laika becomes lost in the background makes it needlessly difficult to see where you are and how to land.The trial and error boss fights are a huge blemish on this game, too. Dying to a bad landing angle or to a stray bullet in the final phase of a boss is infuriating. I never felt like I was improving as I died again and again, and having to repeat boss fight phases over and over just to try something again is pure tedium. There are also mechanics that I just don’t think work well, such as wheelies to get across tightropes or shotgun propulsion. It all feels really random and inconsistent.Level design can be hit or miss, but I did like mastering sections in the moment. Going back across previously explored levels is really tedious, though, and the limited fast travel currency made me quite apprehensive to even fast travel.There’s obviously a lot of care and quality here, but the fundamental issues above made this game so frustrating I couldn’t bring myself to continue it.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I can't give this an universal PLAY THIS GAME recommendation because the gameplay I think will either delight you or frustrate you. So play the demo and see how you feel about it! If you like it at all - if the game is mechanically interesting, if you like the tone and the presentation of the world and its characters - you will find that the full game features much more of the same, developed richly and with great care.I could write a thousand-word essay why I love this game, but that's not a useful review. Instead, a summary!, both the quieter tracks as well as the many songs with full vocals, which create a gorgeous and thematically dense atmosphere throughout the game. It's extremely clear that the team is acutely aware of their strengths and go to great lengths to foreground the music in this game, with long quiet moments entwined in the gameplay that encourage you to sit and listen.The  is beautiful, detailed, and popping with personality. Background vistas are stunning and desolate. The small details on everything - toys for your kid, the art on casette tapes, the posters in the background, the snippets of personality in your quest journal and on item descriptions - give the impression of a lived-in world with history and feeling. It's not a "super dense lore" approach to storytelling like, say, a Souls game, but I think that's to its credit. It has just enough flavour to give you the sense of a world that these characters inhabit. in this game is fun and has personality. Laika's reluctant and grumpy and not very pleased to have to play the hero when all she wants is to protect her daughter. Is this a very well-established character trope? Yes. Does everyone still love it anyway? Also yes. Smaller characters are a bit more hit-or-miss with their writing but honestly everything works and it tells a great and emotional overall story. Can't complain. is a joy in this game, and I've rarely been happier to just drive from place to place - I only got bored after playing 30+ hours, I think? Every new area you open up has its own unique visual aesthetic, backdrop, etc., but it also has its own personality in how the terrain is designed for you to traverse. This presents constantly new puzzles, so when you're exploring a new area you are kept fully attentive and engaged in trying to understand how to move or spin or flip or jump through this landscape. You'll die a lot, sure. But you'll probably have a lot of fun while doing it. is probably going to be the big dividing factor. The core of it is motorcycle combat, where you're moving, shooting, and doing flips to shield yourself, reload, or refresh your bullet parry charge(s). You die if you take a single hit or land badly. This sounds exacting, and it is, but for better or for worse there's a lot of bloody giblets in the game that make it genuinely difficult to keep track of what's happening sometimes - leading to a small but significant degree of randomness in an encounter which can be frustrating. If you land six perfect shots with three reloads in the air, only to die because at some point one of your shots hit a dead enemy that flew in front of a live enemy (who then shoots you when you land), it's annoying! Or if you're parrying multiple bullets midair but lose track of which direction you're facing (and thus which direction you need to rotate to reload your weapon).The devs have done their best to make a game interface that is both clean and informative (your reticule tells you your relative orientation to the ground, as well as your remaining ammunition) but those are the remaining persistent issues that occasionally crop up. You'll eventually learn to play around them if you try enough! That said, the game makes an excellent effort to minimize frustration - lots of save points, and you lose half your currency on death which you can pick up as long as you don't run out of death-token-bags before recovering it, and even if you lose currency you accrue it so fast while just playing normally that I never needed to farm except when trying to 100% the game.The  of the game might put people off - it is very much post-apocalyptic grungy mad-max gory-dark in its writing. Not everyone likes that, and even as someone who is okay with it, the relentless tragic-ends to various side storylines can verge on rote. I will say I really really liked the story overall, but you could let that one person's tree be okay, at least! Not everything needs to be deathly awful! The  does have a few hiccups, particularly in the second half of the game where things speed up rapidly after a relatively slow, expansive first act. Not really a fatal issue in my opinion, and honestly a super hard thing to fix even in the best of stories/games.The  does risk becoming a bit mundane after a while - enemy types don't change much, and the starting weapon is so mundane-but-effective that I didn't really even upgrade it fully until the endgame. YMMV here, some might find it boring, but for me the evolving terrain layouts kept my brain occupied more than the gunplay per se - the traversal becomes a puzzle on its own, and enemies part of that puzzle and not so much opponents to be defeated.  is also a tad hit or miss.It's a game about a coyote mom on a motorbike with a gun. If that's not enough, a strong story, a world designed around a well-executed and innovative gameplay mechanic, and a stunning soundtrack should sell the case - as long as you're okay with the core gameplay conceit of playing as a coyote on a motorbike, shooting birds and dodging bullets while doing flips. A real diamond of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty rough. The flip to reload slows gameplay to a crawl -- permanently losing currency in a trial and error style game is too punishing. The story is amazing but is hampered by awful gameplay that is incredibly punishing. I found myself forcing myself to play the gameplay segments and hating them to get to the story I enjoyed.story = 10/10gameplay = 4/10controls = 2/10music = 9/10overall = 5/10Edit: To further clarify, this game is also incredibly inaccessible.I am colour blind -- I can scarcely tell where my character is pointing when the camera zooms and when covered in blood? GOOD LUCK, me! With one-touch death mechanics, lack of early game upgrades, and a learning curb more steep than Gungrave: Gore (which introduces 8 mechanics back to back, some of which don't work at all due to hitbox issues), this game has few mechanics, fails to communicate them, and then punishes you for failing to understand said mechanics.Two hours in and I am just getting this cooking things that is important? Backflips in different directions do different things?The backflip is perhaps the most annoying -- I have more often than not exhausted my ammo and died trying to flip on a smaller obstacle because I didn't want to go into a battle without ammo.Also, I have no currency due to trial and error learning, I can't even afford the guitar strings (I had to farm the single enemy outisde the gas station to do it). I am told having more viscera bags alleviates this but the thing is -- The game doesn't explain this or anything, really."You just want your hand held" -- No, I just want the game to communicate and introduce me to mechanics and give me a place to practice them. A "Death arena" where death wasn't punished but offered no award so I could practice would be great.A colour blind mode or palette change would be nice.More variety to approaching an obstacle would be nice -- I have no real options early game and towards mid-game I still have few options because I can't afford anything due to the Viscera bag death mechanic.All this, I discovered in two hours. I want to like this game, I want to have fun...But it's not rewarding and only punishes you for failure.Some changes -- A reload button Out of Combat.Backflip or front flip reloading and recharging your parry -- Or better yet, parry not having a cost mechanic associated but a very tight window to execute. Perhaps the bike's bottom should reflect projectiles in the direction its facing like a pong paddle, rewarding precise blocking? Maybe I should be able to plow into my enemy on my bike or drift slide into them to kill them comboing into a parry and killing two others with my loaded gun?There's just not a lot of interplay with mechanics other than "Move fast, read the screen that fails to communicate up/down/character facing when they're blood soaked and somehow juggle all these mechanics flawlessly or die instantly".I kinda wish I could ram into someone at speed with my bike and ramp off their body, do a flip reload while firing at a full screen of enemies, timing my flip to block projectiles. If the Viscera bag dropping was altered, a colour blind mode added, and a little bit of clarity on the screen were given I think this game might actually have some less irritating gameplay.Oh, and the worst part? The "Git Gud" fans that don't want me to be able to play.Piss off. I can't read the screen because everything smears together blandly when I kill something -- I want slightly less punishing gameplay so I can enjoy what you take for granted. If keeping the gate closed to other people is what makes you feel special than sod off.I've played games that are challenging. Dark Souls 2 was a lot of fun. It communicated mechanics, rewarded clever builds and strategies, and had more ways to approach problems than...Whatever this is trying to be. Oh and you drop currency on death! It adds tension. However the key difference is you have more tools and build upon what you've learned.This game? I can't even tell what's going on sometimes! I've died to invisible geometry! I died at spawn because an enemy just off-screen shot me and I lost a viscera bag! I once got stuck in a death loop and lost ALL my viscera and I couldn't figure out how to deal with more than 5+ enemies.The answer? I memorized their spawns and shot them from out of aggro range. Then proceeded to shoot the next checkpoint instead of activating it because I thought they were an enemy, overshot it, then died to an unknown enemy in the next screen and had to start over.What did I learn? I can't really tell because EVERYTHING BLURS TOGETHER BECAUSE I AM COLOUR BLIND. Every encounter is trial and error. EVERY ENCOUNTER.Also the bosses, especially the first boss, are really boring.Edit:For the love of god play this with a keyboard/mouse. It's night and day.Still not recommending it due to the colour-blind thing but it's more manageable. I am no longer dying due to control flailing.

_childDocuments_.review: Going into this game, I didn't have much expectations apart from how I liked the art style. Now, after finishing this.... extraordinary experience, I have some words.1.) _childDocuments_.review: Overall, Laika is a really interesting platformer with its driving, shooting, blocking mechanics. The narrative is overtly, and deliberately dark pretty much at all times but there's some really interesting elements, the main character has a fair amount of depth. And while it doesn't carry to all elements, the game tries to draw at least some of the game mechanics into the narrative itself, such as the character coming back to life.In more depth:Narratively the game really drew me in, exploring new areas was intriguing just to learn more about what was going on. Admittedly the dark tone is perhaps overdone, it almost becomes predictably and comically dark. When everything goes about as bad as can be, the tension in the darkness abates, essentially. The character is a little inconsistant, in that verbally she objects to her role, but is ruthless whenever not in player control. Desires a future without the conflict, yet has no interest in any solution but combat. But that may just be part of her personality. There's a few odd narrative moments. Like randomly pulling off a perfect disguise to a region we never see again, or the ending. I'll try to avoid spoilers, but essentially all hope is lost, then the final villain pulls a cartoonishly supervillain move to ruin their own master plan for no discernable reason. Oddly, I found myself more interested in the lore of my opponents than anything, and felt rather sorry for, most, of the birds by the end.The gameplay is a hard learning curve. In any situation other than your bike you move left and right with A and D, but on your bike pressing those will kill you. By the end, I'd gotten used to it though, but the game punishes any imperfection heavily. Here there are some mixed signals. The game uses a souls-like currency drop system (the currency is the entrails of your enemies, which is quite funny when you consider how many of the merchants like the birds... but accept their body parts as payment) so when you die, you drop half. Die too much as you lose it. This mechanic promotes careful, methodic play. The game otherwise promotes the opposite. You reload with a backflip, you need to build speed to ramp into place, it gives you checkpoints to get back into the action quick when you fail. This seems to promote, rush in guns blazing till you master it, and look good doing it. The screen can get a bit, cluttered and messy during combat though, which being as unforgiving as it is, feels questionable. Once you've become drenched in blood (the game does like its blood) it's hard to tell through the clouds of bird bits if you're going to land on your wheels, or need to do it all again.The soundtrack has some huge hits, all that needs said about that, love the OST... impressive how they managed to make me feel guilty listening to it. Really, the capacity for the game to make everything have dark undertones is impressive.

_childDocuments_.review: I would simply love to recommend Laika to anybody. Problem is, it's a game with very good story(which you wouldn't expect from a metroidvania) and very different style of gameplay than most. It's that sort of game where playing the demo is absolutely mandatory if you even think of buying the game. And if you do think you might enjoy it, please get the demo, get familiar with the controls and give it a try. Story is absolutely beautiful, same with soundtrack. Beícoli did absolutely incredible, and it's one of the games that is being carried by the soundtrack and few songs from which will be added to my normally listened songs.So, with the foreword already done let's get to the details. Game where you have a fusion of Trials Evolution, metroidvania and a shooter/platformer at the same time. When you first think of it like that it might seem like an absolute mess of a game. You'd be incredibly surprised how well the elements go together if you get used to the controls even a little bit. It takes a while, but when you do you feel like an absolute badass zooming past enemies, doing flips, comboing shots and weapons together for very cinematic shootouts. Characters you encounter are interesting, varied and each has a story you want to hear. I've been playing games for a big, if not major part of my life and Laika is one of the really few games that made me tear up. Story is really worth experiencing The world is really well done, with some fairly decent storytelling done by the looks of it alone. Although I'd also like to mention that Laika deals with many very... Sensitive topics so treat this as a small warning(?). There are some tedious moments in there, don't get me wrong(for example one of which is that, if you want to 100% the game you need to farm materials for weapon upgrades for example which can deter some players, although I've played through the entire game with almost basic, not upgraded equipment, so it's completely doable). Below I'll post a small pro/con list and a short TLDR:PROS:- Surprisingly good story.- Insanely good soundtrack.- Gameplay gets really fun when you get used to the very specific controls.- Very nicely done cast of characters and world.CONS:- Said specific controls can cause a lot of frustration in early stages so playing through a demo is absolutely mandatory.- Some areas are quite tough and require doing a lot of things at the same time which can build up frustration quite efficiently.(dashing, orienting your bike, shooting 3-4 enemies at the same time etc.)- I did hear about few, very rare glitches bugging some achievements, but developers are more than keen to help you with fixing your save if you get in contact through the official discord for example.TLDR:A game worth trying if you enjoy tougher gameplay or good story. If you enjoy both that's even more of a recommendation from me. It tells the story very nicely, has very good characters, doesn't overstay it's welcome and is just long enough to satisfy with the gameplay, and short enough to not make said gameplay too long for the story it's telling. If you'd ask me personally it's one of those "must play" games if you enjoy single players. It deals with some heavy topics very well. Complete recommendation from me. But it's one of those games you HAVE TO play the demo before you buy as it's really easy to get discouraged by the specific nature of the gameplay. Plus is, said demo is completely free, small to download and might encourage you even more to try this beautiful game.

_childDocuments_.review: 100%-ed this in less than a week... what a gameI understand that the controls may be frustrating to some people, but to me they're just so insanely clever and intuitive, and the gameplay feels very smooth once you master them. easily my favorite part of the game besides the story. I mean, backflip to reload, bike deflects bullets, using shotgun recoil for a boost? there's a lot of trial and error, but the game is also VERY generous with its checkpoints, meaning you won't have to travel for ages just to get to retry areas you struggle with.I thoroughly enjoyed my experience with this game, even though some parts were a bit of a slog & some of the boss fights are not really made to best utilize the unique control scheme. the story and beautifully animated cutscenes do make up for the less than good parts of the game imo, but that's not something I'm going to get into - you'll have to check it out for yourself!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Laika did not become one of my favourite games but it is a very solid game, still.Pros:* A story is engaging and rather interesting to follow. It's not very unpredictable and does not pose much of a mistery, though* Gameplay is mostly well balanced and soundly made* Graphics is quite good* Decent length* Soundtrack is great, Beícoli really is the best ;)Cons:* Disturbing themes, although presented rather muted, still are present (and are kind of the main point of the game)* Sudden difficulty spikes, some of the fights and specific location parts are much harder than all of the game* Questionable mechanics for loosing in-game money. You need to invest into buying new viscera bags right away, otherwise it'll be a lot of lost viscera and a lot of grind.* Not many choices to make. No consequences will be presented eitherNot here, not there:* Glitching gamepad because of steam gamepad settings enabled by default and game support for gamepad is native. I disabled steam gamepad support in steam's game settings and it went much better afterwards.* Despite the engaging story I didn't feel quite attached to most of secondary characters. But that might be a specific desicion by the authors to relay main character's detachment and inner emptinessAll-in-all, this is a good game and at least stands out with regard to gameplay. Totally worth completing.

_childDocuments_.review: Game-play:I found game-play to be inconsistent at times, but overall it was fine. The only similar game I've played is Ori and the Blind Forest, so I'm not familiar with the style. I found it somewhat easy to play, but hard to master. The bosses weren't very exceptional.Visual style:This game is incredible artistically. As an artist, both digital and traditional; I love the art style and visual design of the game. It certainly creates a unique feeling.Soundtrack:The soundtrack is extremely good, and builds on the atmosphere of the game and it even folds into the story of the game itself. It's also just really nice to listen to (I've used it for road trips and background music for drawing a lot).Characters:This game shines most in its characters. Each character has their own concerns, and not all of them view the player as a noble hero. The interactions Laika has with individuals across the wasteland are varied and interesting. Don't be surprised if you find yourself completing a whole string of side quests just to interact with characters more.I would, and did, recommend this game to friends and strangers. It deserves a lot more attention, and I would absolutely love to see more of this world in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh hello, chad who read negative reviews.Imagine this: you are riding along the promenade, the waning sun blankets the great beyond with a reddish tint, the sound and sight of the sea soothing your every senses, you hear the rubber wheel grinding the pavement, reminding of your presence in this world. Some effort is required to navigate the obstacles along the path, but that is fine, rhythmic, even. Nice and lonely, serene and hopeful. This is a very fine evening purchased with your time....except it isn't that fine. It was a bumpy ride, there are a million tiny annoying gameplay things that compound into a somewhat frustrating experience. Detours, retreads, backpedals, blindsides, accidents... all too common. Some segments are great, but many parts of the overall circuit are ultimately lacking. Yet, rear your head beyond the road and you are reminded of the phenomenal wasteland sights, interesting locals who invited you over for dinner to share their somber stories, and that nice bittersweet lady song echoing in the distance. Man, why? Why the finer things in life gotta suck? Why isn't the Lord more forgiving? Am I born with skill issue? This is not fai--Here comes the epiphany: Oh god, they ran out of money! The project is rushed! They are stretched thin! We've been riding in circles for the final hours! The end of the road still got some of that orange barrier lying around! No way! That blows! Curse this money driven world! Another greatness robbed from this plane of existence! Justice for coyote mum and her pup!Please fund a sequel, or an expansion. Buy this game. Endure it or let it sit in your backlog, idc. Give them yo monies.

_childDocuments_.review: I have very complicated feelings about this game. I understand the weight its narrative intends to convey, and it commits to a really unique gameplay style. I just think it's too cognitively dissonant to avenge the brutal murder of your puppy nephew and your brother by doing backflips on your motorcycle tony glock style.I think it might work for others, but for whatever reason, it didn't work for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mad this flew under my radar on release. _childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I keep coming back to the word "singular."  Laika stands completely alone in what it's doing.There's a pretty good Metroidvania in here.  The waypoints are a bit spread out, there were a few points in the midgame where I felt like I was backtracing a bit too much to tick every sidequest and exploration piece, and it's not always clear that you need an upgrade to get to location and that you're just not meant to be able to make that jump right now.It's got Excitebike in its blood.  Am I the age for NES nostalgia?  Absolutely.  It's great.It's got that excellent and fully present soundtrack.  Like something Darren Korb would do for Supergiant, not in its style, but in its exquisite prominence.It's got a protagonist and a world brimming with rage, worry, and sorrow, and yeah, I get feeling that way too.But this game is more than the sum of those parts.  It's brought everything together for, yes, a singular experience.  You should play this game, not only because it's excellent (and it is), but especially because there's nothing else out there like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited for this, but even I didn't think it'd be *this* good. The writing is superb and the relationships between Laika and her family are really grounded and sad. The combat is fun and in that range where it's pretty difficult to master. While you die in one shot, so does every other enemy apart from bosses, it leans itself to quick retries and usually checkpoints aren't far enough away that it's super annoying. I love the way that more enemies get added to the world as you go, it means that you have to rethink how to traverse a section of the map you've been through a bunch of times each time you reach a new major plot point. The bosses are fantastic and I've had a blast in each one so far. The game looks fantastic. This is just incredible, I haven't enjoyed a metroidvania this much in a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played this game for super long... but I think I can describe it pretty well for new players.  Did you ever have piano lessons when you were little?  You know how they made you play the same stupid song over and over and if you made one mistake you had to start again?  And you just played it over and over and over messing up until you got it right once and the teacher finally released you?  That's Laika.  Taking very imprecise controls, you must, through trial and error, memorize exact sequences of maneuvers and perform them precisely, in order, or you die and have to start over.  In one of the earlier areas you have to drive through a horde of angry, rifle-wielding bird people, and rapidly perform the following sequence of actions with no breaks in near-perfect order if you want to survive: Reflect bullet, front flip off jump to reload reflect, shoot bird, tilt back to block bullet, wait for second shot so your bullet doesn't collide with the bird's, shoot bird, backflip off jump to reload gun, shoot bird, tilt back to block bullet, wait for shot so bullets don't collide, shoot bird, reflect bullet, backflip THEN frontflip both within a single jump, shoot bird, shoot bird, reflect bullet.  Oh... and make sure to go left off the final ledge to reach the checkpoint instead of right like I did because if you go right you get stuck in a pit where you have to kill yourself to escape and your hard-won victory gets turned to ash.    Honestly... it reminds me of an old-style platformer like Mario or Megaman, except it's always on the hardest levels, and you're constantly running on ice.  If you like those kinds of games and you're patient enough you may enjoy Laika.  I mostly play strategy games, and I play Laika when I'm burnt out and I don't want to think, or I'm just bored with the same old same old.  It's challenging, but it's also mostly just tedious repetition.  It DOES feel cool when you finally, after an hour, execute the sequence correctly one time and get to see the next ten feet of the level before you meet more birds...    The artwork is pretty.  I feel like the game is trying to be edgy and hard core, but the fact the it's Happy Wheels with furries, and that I explode blood like I'm a Mortal Kombat fighter every time I tip my nose a little too far forward means that I simply can't take the game seriously.  However, I think that's also the only reason I'm able to enjoy it-if I was taking it seriously I would get too angry because I die every two seconds and I'd have to quit playing.    Conclusion?  I don't know.  I like the game and I'll probably play to the end.  It's nice to play something a little different.  Don't be fooled by the gameplay videos though-it may look awesome, but you're going to feel stupid a lot more than you're going to feel cool, and the cool feeling is very short-lived.  Despite it being a game where you ride a motorcycle, the race goes to the tortoise and not the hare with this one.  Slow, steady, and patient is what carries the day.

_childDocuments_.review: This game i believe to be the developer's magnum opus.The game is hand drawn and looks amazing for most of it, while the music isn't something i'd listen to it's still pretty good and it looks like a lot of effort was put into both, the writing and characters were great although some things are never addressed. _childDocuments_.review: Being a strange mixture of the motorbike franshise trials and a metroidvania i wasnt quite sure what to expect. While it took me a moment to get used to the system i quickly fell in love with it. Shooting is precise has style and every death felt very on my part. What really got me invested was the characters and world though, the soundtrack is gonna stick with me for sure. Had an amazing time. _childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: As a present, I got this game, and the Game is good, although mostly if you follow the main quests.My big grievance with this game is the padding with side quests which mean nothing, and that this game is a motorbike mobility based game in a metroidvania styled map. These two things, the quests and metroidvania with this movement makes the game longer than it should be, and making me want to finish the game already.Some sidequests are literally unfindable if you dont see the "Interact" button or look it up. Its actually really annoying and baffling that a Tree that I have to look for, is completely destroyed so I dont have a clue as to what to look for! But my character knows it seems like...The art is great, especially the animations and cutscenes. Although in some places it gets all over the place with hiding the road, hiding enemies, hiding bullets coming at you through foreground objects as well as the road. Sometimes its a wall, sometimes you can ride through it. Seaport did this the most, and Seaport in general sucks.The bosses however, also suck. They are boring. Creative but boring. The first and second boss were probably the coolest and thematicly in place with the game. But lighthouse boss (waiting around), pyramid boss (single attack), and final boss (Outdamaged) were a big letdown.One final thing I didnt like was the camera not going forward enough. It often gets taken control from me and I absolutely hate it. Cant see where im driving or shooting. Some birds shoot sooner than they are startled and having that extra camera leeway would be great.But it is a, good game. Its fine. Nothing too special. I would prefer it as a chapter based game rather than a metroidvania. The pyramid area is probably my most favourite area of the game because it felt like a level I was traversing. Maybe a bit like a zelda dungeon. Every other area didnt feel good enough as progressing the game, it felt it got easier with more upgrades/guns.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Laika: Aged Through Blood is one of those genre mash-ups that sounds like it shouldn't work, but it does. It took a while to get to grips with the gameplay style, but once it clicks, you'll find yourself settling into a strange flow. The story is absolutely top-notch too, one that I guarantee will stick with me for years to come. I cannot recommend this game highly enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: 100% recommend this game, even if it is at full price. Just buy and play it.I hyperfocused on it and lost a three-day weekend because of this game and it was worth every second.That said here's my more objective takes on it:- Controls take a little time to get used to but end up being fun. Dying is part of the experience and checkpoints are frequent enough that it isn't too frustrating.- Best way to play is Keyboard and Mouse. Controller is okay, but felt way more frustrating to me. Once you get the mechanics down it goes smooth, but yes, the one-hit-you-die part does make the learning part a little aggravating in the moment.But where Laika really shined for me was the music sound track and STORY. _childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of things to say about this game. More than I can reasonably fit into a Steam review. I would like to preface my review that I seldom play games just for fun. I wholeheartedly believe video games are an art form and an experience. Laika: Aged Through Blood caught my eye because of the art style and seemingly emotional story it had to tell. Laika’s (the main character’s) world is dark and gritty. Death can happen out of nowhere, typical of an apocalypse setting. You play as a woman whose family carries a curse where they cannot die and can act as a medium to the dead. It is because of your condition that you are pulled into being a pawn for your village. Death is far too great a threat in the wastelands, so everyone relies on you to do the dirty work for the village. The story revolves around trying to protect your village from an invasionary force of birds seeking to eradicate the surface dwellers and expand their empire. Surprisingly enough, the main story itself (as in the idea of “go here do task X and then come back and talk to person Y”) is one of the weakest parts of the game for me. Yet, that’s what makes this game so incredible for me.Where the game shines is the atmosphere and characters. The atmosphere is incredible. The aesthetics of the game are incredibly well-drawn and the animations are well-illustrated. But this is only surface-level praise. The designs and themes of the world play important roles. Your tribe is very much inspired by the culture of indigenous American tribes. The invasion force dons military uniforms similar to those of many Cold War Western nations. A lot of the game seems to be an allusion to colonialism. Your tribe rests their dead at a sacred grove, which you find out is being desecrated by the birds for resources. This happens while you try to spread your brother’s ashes in the forest, which evokes your fury. Laika wants every single one of these bird’s brains splattered across the ground- and so do you. It is at sections like this where worldbuilding shines the most. You truly begin to burn with hatred for these birds and everything they do. People keep dying in brutal and cold means. By the latter half of the game, you head over to a town where birds live. Quickly you realise that not all is well in their world either. Dystopian advertisements litter the streets where people are impoverished and broken. It’s a consumerist society that is propped up by the military. I believe this is an accurate depiction of contemporary America. Though the military is out committing acts of violence against different people of the world, their people are suffering. Towards the end of the game, you meet the leader of a resistance movement who explains to you that bird life isn’t glamorous. He is malnourished and poor- living in horrible conditions while the bloated wealthy class continue to live lavishly (sounding more and more like the US). In the aforementioned town, you see a bird that tried to recruit you to a pacifist movement. A movement of birds that couldn’t dodge the draft but instead now refuse to shoot. After this mission, I only started noticing some birds were wearing white bandages on their arms. If you drive up to them- they don’t fire. I immediately felt disgusted with myself. How many of these people have I killed indiscriminately? How many times did Laika perpetuate this cycle of violence? This little detail was so profound that one of the first things I ever did in combat was scan for these birds wearing white. The characters all accomplish their intended purpose. While many of the people in Laika’s village aren’t completely pleasant, you still kind of care about them in a way (some of them, at least). Any time someone dies, you can’t help but feel like it’s your fault. When there’s a chance of a character dying, I felt like rushing to aid them immediately. Your daughter, Puppy, gets lost and I felt like my blood was rushing when I thought she could have been brutally murdered by birds. Even a lot of the less memorable characters had interesting lines and storytelling. Laika’s character development is also particularly remarkable. She doesn’t seem to change all that much throughout the story until the very end, but that’s the point. She’s a woman who does what she has to to protect those she loves. Laika knows this won’t bring her to a bright path, but she believes that what she does now will create a better future for those who follow. Her story stops short, an explosion from a nuke that she detonates with her trusty revolver. Thus, the village is left without a Laika and Puppy is left without a mother. But the message is clear, she sinned and did the hard work so that her daughter wouldn’t have to. I think the game pointed to the fact that Laika wasn’t long for this world for a while yet I still wasn’t willing to come to terms with the ending. The game was phenomenal, but I still had some criticisms. Firstly, the most minor, there were some bugs here and there. Sometimes animations didn’t load or other odd happenings would occur. These are far and few between so don’t worry, the game is very polished. I don’t usually like souls systems in games (in this game, when you die you lose your money just like in Dark Souls). They’re very stressful and just mean that if you die you might just have to end up wasting time on farming more money. This game takes a great approach to this concept by letting you craft more bags that give you more chances to get your money back. So when you die, you’ll lose 50% of your money. If you die again, you lose 50% of what you had at that point. It’s not a perfect system but it didn’t make me want to rip my hair out like Dark Souls did. Sometimes enemies are behind resource containers which take the shot for you and make you waste double the ammunition. Also, you can shoot enemies multiple times. It’s fun to juggle them sometimes but god is it annoying in the early game when they block one of your precious limited bullets. This critique is a bit subjective but I feel like the game rushed to a close. The game was still expanding and then it just abruptly ended. It makes sense for the story, but I wish I could have spent more time with the villagers. Maybe that’s the point? You couldn’t spend enough time with them? I feel like you aren’t given enough time to get attached to the characters to truly weep for them when they pass. It’s certainly tragic when characters die but I didn’t bawl my eyes out like when I played Spiritfarer. They’re around for too short a time for you to truly cry for them (but you feel horrible that your actions got them killed). Lastly, I think the medium ability Laika has wasn’t utilised nearly enough. It was so emotional when she was dragging her brother’s corpse back home, speaking to him and getting his parting thoughts. Those moments were kind of sparse in this game and I think they actually would have been incredibly moving if they were utilised more often (though where they are utilised, it’s often with great impact and depth).Overall, this game is a work of art. I wouldn’t write such a massive review (this is even a shortened version for Steam!) on it if I didn’t find it impactful. Metroidvanias aren’t my type of game so I got annoyed by backtracking a lot, but the fact that I loved this game so much should be enough to show how incredible it was. The music is astounding, it’s one of my favourite video game OSTs of all time. Pair it with the tough and gruelling world Laika lives in and it just adds all that beautiful art to the rest of the game. My final verdict is a 9/10. Every bit of this game was made with love and care and it shows. The only thing keeping me from a 10/10 is that the game started to slightly rush towards the end and the fact that I’m not crazy about Metroidvanias (also that crab boss fight took four years off my lifespan). This game is worth every penny. Please, get it.

_childDocuments_.review: What if Excite Bike was also a metroidvania shooter? This is probably the most interesting metroidvania ever made, certainly the most interesting and original I've played. I love the overall presentation, despite the extremely grim tone. The art is simple but beautiful, the soundtrack is hauntingly atmospheric and heart-wrenching, and the unfortunately rare fully animated clips are amazing to behold. The game plays a bit like old Sonic games, often requiring route memorization of what order to kill enemies in in order to succeed. Respawn points are everywhere tho, so you're normally losing more than 10 seconds per attempt. That said, you can still explore with the weapons to find your own ways of doing things. I was very bad about remembering to use the parry mechanic, and mostly relied on the revolver (pro tip, the machine gun is super great if you continue spinning to reload). I felt it was hard, but forgiving. The narrative is incredibly grim, like anyone you meet could die as a result of you meeting them. If you can deal with that, and be willing to endure some try-try-try-try again gameplay, then I encourage you to try Laika out. Couple bits of criticism tho, the bosses aren't fantastic. I'm not sure what else they could have done with the motorbike-with-gun format but they can come off a lil meh. Also the ending is suuuper brief, sadly.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: One of, if not THE best game I've played in quite some time.The world is massive and full of little bits to find and uncover; from new weapons to characters you'll either help or massacre. Alot of my play time was just riding about trying to reach a box just out of reach, or find a way into an area that was blocked off. Or trying to help characters about the world with side quests ((Of which there are TONS))The combats a little weird at first, but once you get into it; you'll be pistol whipping, backflipping and boosting your way through hundreds of squishy bird soldiers with a grin as you collect their gibblets for currency!The story unfolds as you explore, do main and side missions and interact with characters throughout. Gradually teaching you more about this world, the people in it and Laika's history as well.. and it is a very sad tale. I genuinely felt sad and sometimes even a little misty at some of the story elements throughout the game.The only downside I'd say is some of the boss fights. They're a little short and a little simple for the most part. Dodge bullet of some sort, shoot obvious target point; repeat. But; that just gives more time for exploring and doing sick shotgun jump backflip reloads as you blow birds heads off before riding off in search of more around the map!I really, really hope we get a sequel some day that follows on from the ending of this game and gives us a little more closure
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: It's an excellent metroidvania, and certainly a highlight of the genre, sporting unique movement, refined action gameplay, and an absolutely stellar soundtrack. If you're unsure about whether or not it's for you play through the demo, and if you like it, pick up the whole thing. Absolutely worth it, even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Laika's a motorcycle metrovania style game that you can beat in 20 hours. But that twenty hours is one hell of a gripping story in a grim setting with depressing tones mixed with some seeds of hope. It's biggest strengths is the main gameplay itself, the moving story, and the wonderful music you'll listen to and unlock tapes of as you  play through. It's biggest weakness is some of the boss design being fights that drag out for quite a while where death has you refight the boss from the beginning every time you mess up. Thankfully not all of those fights are like this and there's plenty of stages to drive through between the big fights either.I left the game craving much more of the lore and world settiing. It was such a great experience that this review can't do it justice.

_childDocuments_.review: To get it out of the way, yes, this game is incredible and well worth the $20 asking price. I almost never write reviews for anything, but this game is an unsung masterpiece with a story so compelling that it kept me wanting more and left me reeling after completion. To memory only one other game has even come close to leaving me feeling this way, that being Undertale. The story is the aspect of the game that kept me hooked, and in a lesser game would be what makes it stand out, but due to how totally unique and masterfully crafted the rest of the game is, I can't say that it alone is what makes the game nor can I say that it is the de facto selling point of the game.Go ahead and skip this paragraph if you want to go in completely blind. I will be touching on the general story of the game and why I think it works so well....Laika is by far the most compelling protagonist in any game I've played in the last few years. And though overarching story describes the tale of a Laika as she battles against impossible odds to destroy a regime of fiercely militaristic, genocidal birds who seek nothing less than total annihilation of all land-dwelling life. Laika is special, however, because she can interact with the land of spirits, allowing her to speak with the dead before they pass on or even to come back from death herself. This is a more-than-sufficient story hook, but is actually the least compelling part of the narrative. What makes the game's story truly shine is in the characters, specifically Laika and her family. Their curse is hereditary, with immortality being passed from mother to daughter once the time comes. Perhaps by necessity, those cursed with undeath, if they even survive the sickness that precedes its inheritance, are raised as soldiers, not children, and are forced to bear children until one daughter grows to replace them. Until them, they are doomed to live out their life as a pawn of war, doing the grunt work that would be otherwise too dangerous for the mortal villagers. Additionally, each life lost and taken for an immortal makes them lose themselves a little bit, and with age memories of past lives twist and turn leaving their memory incoherent scramble of events. This is the curse that Laika bears, and that should she survive, her daughter Puppy will too. Laika lost many daughters before, and not wanting to endure the anguish of losing another child, Laika doesn't name her final daughter. She hopes that this will help her to not grow too attached to her puppy. It doesn't work. Laika never raises Puppy like a tool, as her mother raised her, and tries to keep her happy and insulated from the horrors of the outside world, but Puppy is curious and hyperactive, and due to the deaths of her sisters and best friend, had already lost her innocence. Even still, Puppy is a happy and optimistic child, but not without her misgivings. Death is always on her mind, and she's afraid of dying, and what would happen to Laika if she inherited Laika's immortality. It is through their interactions they love each other very much. Puppy even serves as Laika's moral compass. She is the only person left that gives Laika joy and purpose. The dialogue they share is often sad, sweet, and eloquently-written. In fact, the game's script is to the point and never overly verbose. ... Laika has an incredibly unique combat system, and while awkward at first, it keeps traversal and exploration and engaging. The impact of the weapons is satisfying, and combined with the corpse physics and (frankly comical amount of) spattered blood, the combat becomes incredibly meaty and satisfying as you learn to master it. Checkpoints are spaced apart fairly, and because  save for the rare boss encounter, both Laika and any enemy die in a single hit, combat can become a thrilling but erratic sequence of shooting, flipping, and maneuvering out of the way or even directly into enemy bullet spatter. Even still, learning to shoot, ride, reload and parry in while maintaining proper momentum and rotation of your character, while not too difficult due to future weapon upgrades, high sensitivity and bullet time, is still a bit of a learning curve, and is exacerbated by the fact that the starting revolver has only 2 bullets at level 1, so gunplay against 3 or more enemies takes a bit of practice at the beginning.Characters feature colorful designs, distinctive silhouettes and expressive body language and faces, and the game has crafted a beautiful but bleak post-apocalyptic landscape to explore and fight through. It has a beautifully colorful hand-drawn style that makes the backgrounds pop against the bold-outlined characters, and a masterfully written soundtrack that accentuates the silent beauty of the remainder of the world. The score is filled with plucky acoustics and surprisingly often features vocals from an in-universe singer. When in the wastelands you can collect cassettes and play them at your leisure. By comparison, the larger more story-significant areas and "dungeons", there will instead be an accompanying ambient track. The game is heavily elevated by its exemplary graphical and auditory presentation, and this in tandem with the fiercely emotional narrative was able to on several occasions jerk a tear from my jaded gamer eyes.While I adore this game, it is very flawed. Think of this as bit of a lightning round of gripes. For one, the game has some major issues with its pacing, both narratively and gameplay wise. A lot of my issues with the game's pacing gameplay-wise has to do with the game's at times microscopic instructions as to how or where to get to pivotal areas or questlines. This is combined with a fast travel system a la dark souls one where only a select few checkpoints, often inconveniently placed, are warpable, and with the exception of a particular key item, require consumables to even travel between and ONLY if you are already at another warpable checkpoint to begin. This led me to getting frustrated on occasion, but admittedly traveling the through the desert highways on my bike listening to some nice music was nice after a particularly intense encounter or story beat. The pacing is also a bit scattered narratively, but without getting into spoilers, one character taking her life felt rushed, underdeveloped, and ultimately tasteless. The climax, while good and thematic, felt rushed, sudden, and underdeveloped.Second and thirdly, the sidequests in the game are a cut above horrible. Just about every last one simply means travelling to a place to buy or collect an item for a character with no real useful rewards or satisfying narrative through line or conclusion. Also despite being technically being a metroidvania, your movement options and upgrades are few and far between and underutilized. There is one ability that is used for just one stage and boss or the odd interactable on the overworld, and another, by far the most fun ability in the game, which is used to its full potential but only unlocked in the very end of the game so it never has time to truly shine.My final issue is that almost every single boss in the game (and there are very few), is a frustrating mess in which you have to wait your turn to even hurt it, scripting most battles. Two bosses are autoscrollers, even. One of those is a three-part encounter. This boss design philosophy is confusing and antithetical to the rest of the hectic action of the game. There is only one non-turn based boss, but because of that, both of its healthbars can be depleted in around 15 seconds by a crafty player.It would be great if they weren't issues to begin, but the quality of the game in its entirety is great enough that I am willing to look past these issues. However, factoring them into account, I can't in good conscious give the game anything higher than an 8/10, two huge thumbs up, and a review an ninety minutes in the making.

_childDocuments_.review: My Little Review for Laika: Aged Through Blood :>Overall the game is very good the story is pretty straightforward but its impactful and it stays with you and it really makes it feel like your actions have some consequences (doesn't change the ending or anything), it also just made me cry like three times so if you want some feels yeah.  The gameplay is overall very fun and it feels fluid and it makes you feel cool in general.  The exploration is also fun the world is very pretty and has cool details.  The world also feels very fleshed out and rarely feels empty, although that could also partly be because the map isn't massive.  The fast travel and saving systems are also very nice.  Also this game has the most banger soundtrack ever written it fits the vibe so well and I unironically listen to all the songs outside of playing the game.  The music also comes in form of collectable cassettes you find in game which is very very cool.My main cons of the game are the following: The boss fights can feel a little underwhelming as they aren't too challenging and some are a bit annoying (its not awful but definitely not the highlight of the game) - however a plus to the bosses is the amazing cutscenes that come with them.  There are some bugs, for example I got stuck in a wall while using the dash on two separate occasions, and one time it just didn't put me into a required cutscene or just planned event so I had to leave and rejoin to get it to work.  Also as it is a metroidvania I wish it had more power ups that let you back track and go into areas you couldn't access without them.  There were a couple of them but there's only two meaningful movement upgrades, and they both do the same thing one is just a better version of the other.I fell in love with this game almost immediately because of the beautiful style and I stayed for the story and gameplay. Overall I would totally recommend the game it was a very enjoyable experience and in my opinion the pros heavily outweigh the cons.One more note I might be a little biased because I love metroidvanias and I'm kinda a sucker for post-apocolyptic worlds.I hope someone finds this useful :)

_childDocuments_.review: Great hook, awesome premise and incredible style, but in the end it doesn't actually do that much with it. Most of the bosses are pretty appalling design wise, they're a slog no matter how hard you find them. It sucks because they're supposed to be narratively significant, but the mechanics just feel tacked on,Narrative itself seems like it has a lot to say, but ends up shrugging all that off. There is a world where it can work, and there are elements that are interesting, but it fails to deliver in a really disappointing way. It's bleak for the sake of it, and the inclusion of SA felt especially tasteless, like it was shoved in last minute. (Its not a dark, depressing, edgy setting without DOMESTIC ABUSE and CSA amiright?)I really wanted to like this game, and I do like some parts. If you're into a fun, sometimes baffling metroidvania with unabashedly furry character designs, give it a shot! But if that's not enough to get you through it alone, give it a pass. Play Echo instead or something

_childDocuments_.review: Overall great & challenging game with a fantastic art style, a great soundtrack, and a very intriguing narrative dealing with dark, heavy themes of loss, death, coming of age, etc. It's not perfect and has some questionable choices (mostly in mechanics), but overall it's a really interesting game and I enjoyed my time playing it. Well worth full price and you'll be getting roughly 20 hours out of it if you do all of the quests, and a little longer if you achievement hunt.The aesthetic, artwork, and soundtrack are all top notch. I love expanding the soundtrack by finding new tapes, especially because there's a narrative reason for it. The soundtrack is SO good that even months after completing the game, I find myself listening to it now and then.The game controls decently well, but the floatiness/physics/knockback are all things that take a bit of time to get used to. I recommend just playing the whole game with a KB&M instead of a controller because precision eventually becomes an issue. I played the first half of the game with a controller (the rumble is really satisfying), but switched over to KB&M because of the shipyard, multiple small platforms with death pits, and the rope mechanics being exceptionally hard to deal with on controller.Some mechanics were implemented very well, such as the dash, parry, and shotgun jump. Other mechanics end up being unfun and frustrating, especially the ropes in the shipyard (you "snap" onto them really weird and balancing is a fight, I can't count the number of times I'd get to the end and because of this get quickly flipped over to my death, or would fall off the rope if the angle wasn't perfect and fall to my doom) and the boost having some inconsistencies. The combo counter is not displayed anywhere in the UI, and is only indicated by the screen becoming redder and hazier as you're shooting, which I don't like because it can be unclear if the area you're at is getting you close enough when you're going for the final combo achievement.Combat is enjoyable, but can get repetitive because of the one-hit deaths, the fact that all regular enemies are stationary, and the fact that you will be back tracking a LOT. A Caterpillar Made of Sadness is my favorite of all of the boss fights, taking full advantage of driving fast while navigating terrain and using tricks  The biggest problems with the bosses comes down to the later boss fights really being at odds with the run and gun fun of the rest of the game. I found the strategy that worked best and trivialized some of the subsequent boss fights was simply to take it slow and remain stationary, especially for the  boss that shoots upwards from below you and the  boss that has instant death pits on both sides of the arena platform. The final boss fight has basically no mechanics other than dodging and requires no strategy other than ride up one of the walls and spam as fast as you can, which was quite surprising. The fight felt way too quick and easy since it came directly after the instant death pit boss that could only be damaged during a short time window that followed completing some mechanics with the hook.The story is emotional, hard-hitting, heartstring-tugging, but also very depressing. The lore of the world is absolutely fascinating,  The side quests were a lot of fun, and you will be driven to complete them just by how great all of the characters are, rewards be damned. I do think the game gets a bit too gratuitous at times; the biggest example is the side quest
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Okay listen, I feel bad giving this a negative review because the art, music, character designs, world building, etc are all genuinely fantastic... but I would feel worse giving it a disingenuous recommendation after the miserable slog that is the last 30-40% of this game.They just stretched this cool concept of a moto-shooter metroidvania thingy wayyy too thin. The guns aren't distinct enough to feel different. The shotgun is the only real exploration tool you get in the whole game (the hook doesn't count, it's used in like 2 areas and will probably rubber-band your face into the floor). Hitboxes are inconsistent. Platforming feels clunky and frustrating when it's not at high speeds. Cinematic cameras will get you shot by off-screen enemies you otherwise would have seen. There's 6 bosses, and only the first 3 are fun, the rest are you wrestling against the clunky low-speed maneuvering in tight enclosed spaces (slow and confined are definitely what i think of when I think of motorbikes, yep). And the backtracking...dear god the backtracking... seemingly every side quest in this game is either (A) A fetch quest where you backtrack through a whole level to find mundane items like flowers or herbs, or (B) which is somehow even more boring... it just passively completes while you progress the main story.Longest 30 hours of my life.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I feel pretty mixed about this game, I LOVE the art, the music, the characters, (some of) the gameplay, but man some parts of this game are ROUGH.I think its a well made game for the most part, its stable, it runs well and has some really fun and unique ideas, but while it has very high highs, it also has some truly low lows. some of the decisions made for the actual gameplay are very questionable and/or frustrating.Like half of this game is a glorified fetch quest, someone asks you to go get something, you go out of your way to get it, you come back and get a crumb of engaging dialogue with an absolutely pitiful amount of rewards, and then they immediately ask for something else. repeat for almost every single side quest. The worst part is that when your initially exploring a new area quest items wont even spawn until an NPC asks for them, so you gotta drag your bike all across the dessert over again for every single quest. It can be incredibly monotonous, again for rewards that are almost always near worthlessThe other major issue I have with this game is the boss fights, I think the first couple are decent enough, but a lot of them have serious issues. These are fights where you have to wait for the enemies weak point to open up before you can damage them, have multiple phases, and you have only one hit point, with NO CHECKPOINTS.you have to restart the entire fight every single time you get by something, or even just land your bike wrong.The actual designs of the bosses are pretty cool, but I started dreading fighting them (The egg and crab can go to hell especially).I've complained a lot about this game, but I don't regret playing it and want to end this off with what I REALLY liked about this game.  I felt like this games overall presentation was overwhelmingly beautiful, from its gorgeous melancholy soundtrack, to its striking art style. The story and characters were also engaging, theres some particular moments that are very shocking and memorable. The gameplay (while still having some major issues) was very inventive and fun for the most part (doing 360s with your bike to reload is VERY cool)You should probably try out the demo before buying the game, should tell if you'll like this game or not.I had a lot of issues with this game, but I also don't think I'll forget about it anytime soon.I wish the best of luck to the devs at brainwash gang, you guys have made some really great and unique stuff!
