_childDocuments_.review: one of the marks of an excellent game concept is, upon seeing it, you think "duh! why didnt i think of that?" laika created that thought in my mind throughout the entire game, while managing to execute on those concepts perfectly.first, the gameplay. the concept of "2d run-and-gunning motorbike adventure" is not one i had ever thought of before, but now i wont be surprised if this game spawns an entire genre around it. the concept spawns so many brilliant and obvious in hindsight ideas like doing tricks to reload and putting your bike between you and the enemy to block, integrating the bikes movement into combat. this combined with the fluid controls and the quick respawns made every tiny encounter feel like its own puzzle, letting you combo between your weapons skills and movement to mow down hordes of enemies, all while looking and feeling like an absolute badass. the combat was difficult in places, requiring many many attempts to defeat some groups, but instead of thinking "this is unfair" after dying, i always thought about what went wrong and what to do differently the next time.a game with such brilliant gameplay could be forgiven for having a lackluster story, however laika knocks it out of the park in that front as well. the world of laika draws you in deep, letting you discover everything about what the world is like and how it got that way for yourself instead of outright telling the player. the game has some excellent twists even in its premises that prey on what people who play a lot of games will expect from their stories and plot elements, and pulls these false assumptions out from under you to create creeping realizations that had me taking breaks to process. the stakes are perfectly set, high enough to cause plot tension but not to high as to make the outcome predictable. my only gripe with the story is that the tensional and emotional climax happens at about the 2/3s mark, and is solved rather quickly afterwards. the finale has its own tension and stakes of course, but it isnt able to achieve the edge of my seat trembling that that event about 2/3s in created. perhaps the resolution to that event could have been moved to the finale to keep that anxiety up. the story is still beautiful and heart-wrenching and EXCELLENT as it is, it just sits at excellent rather than perfect for me personally.on top of the excellent plot and gameplay, there are so many more tiny details that make this game feel fleshed out and expertly balanced and overall loved. the little quest and dialogue details that could have been easily left out but add so much to the world and its feel. the cooking system and how it becomes an essential part of the game rather than just an extra boost. the soundtrack being diegetic and tied to optional unlockables, getting excited for each new cassette so you can hear more of the game's absolutely beautiful soundtrack. the fact that quest and item descriptions are narrated by laika herself, giving insight into her thoughts and additional lore that a bog standard description would.every part of this game feels expertly and lovingly crafted in a way you rarely see. i bought this game on sale for 16 dollars, but i would have GLADLY payed the full 20 for such an amazing experience. laika: aged through blood has quickly become one of my top games of all time, and i hope it will be one of yours too.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome artstyle and very flowy controls, but also very unforgiving at the start and with a few important rough edges. Once you get used to the bike + shooting it becomes very fun to traverse the (very big) map!Thing is, bike powerups come EXTREMELY late in the game, and oddly placed fast-travel points can make moving through the late/endgame a bit annoying to say the least.But all in all the game is a beautiful and bittersweet journey, if it hooks you. Writing is a bit shaky and kinda edgy sometimes, but Laika's main story and character makes up for it. Extra points for the beautiful animations and character designs, too.

_childDocuments_.review: Laika is not for everybody.It's grim, gory, vulgar and difficult. Try out the demo first and make sure you can get to grips with the unusual controls, and be ready for your death counter to reach the hundreds before the end of the game. If you've played either of them, the gameplay is essentially an open world Trials meets Katana Zero, with a demand for consistent acrobatic precision that brings back memories of Super Meat Boy's single-screen gauntlets.It's also the most motherly game I've ever played. I don't think I've even played any other game that brought the word "motherly" to mind but Laika sure did. So if you, like me, value new experiences above most else, then motorcycle platforming with guns and post-apocalypse dog motherhood will probably swing Laika over to being a worthwhile time. As long as you don't mind spending half an hour fighting a crab and repeatedly being called words I can't spell out in this review. (You can yell those words at the crab if it makes you feel better!)Huge bonus points for a wonderful soundtrack that, much like the rest of the game, feels unexpectedly fresh. Loads of acoustic guitars and vocals coat the otherwise brutal and dark scenery with gentle, somber, sometimes bittersweet vibes. I've been listening to it almost every day since I finished the game a couple of weeks back.In summary, if you're good with wastelands, swearwords, viscera and the desire to slap yourself in the face for perfectly executing a lengthy encounter with Keanu Reeves-like precision only to accelerate too hard, flip your bike, bump your head and get reset to the last checkpoint, then I can very much recommend Laika. It's not the sharpest game, but I genuinely love it for what it's going for.

I played 30 hours in five days, losing track of time just driving, flipping, and shooting. Its like a 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Good Game with potwential to be phenomenalPros:Art Style - Super sick very unique, you should be able to tell by the promo art if you will like itMusic - Phenomenal score, I usually hate this kind of folksy somber music but it fits the story and vibe of it allStory - If the story wasnt so enthralling i wouldnt hjave continued past some of the rougher parts. I struggled through certain sections because i was determined to see the story throughMixed:Mechanics - I really loved the trials style traversal but the one shot deaths were very frustrating at times i did end up turning on the setting so that iwouldnt die to a single pixel of my head touching a surface. A little too unforgiving to me.Deaths - Loved the death mechanic to revive but one shot deaths were a bit too intense at times i wopuld like to see maybe 3 hit points or something. i am not asking for the game to be easier just less tedious at times.Cons:Backtracking - I know its a metroidvania but getting back to a ability locked area sometimes was brutal to even get there and made me pull my hair out. _childDocuments_.review: The boss fights, which clearly have serious design flaws since the 3rd boss fight (Where Rock Bleeds). Zero error tolerance is not positive feedback for a game that requires multi-threaded precision maneuvering. Blaming players for their lack of skill is also not a good idea. The game has been out for over half a year now, and in terms of global achievements, the Swimcrab is at 33.2% and the Pope is at 29.8%. _childDocuments_.review: Words cannot describe how amazing this game is.I picked up the demo from my discovery queue because it had a neat animated trailer, and I loved it so much that for the next few days I was thinking solely of getting the full game.Once I did, i fell in love with the game unbelievably fast. I came in expecting a really good game, not a game that would immediately shoot to the very top of my favorite games list.The combat is shockingly smooth, engaging, and fun, the characters and their dialogue know how to get you to care for them more than you ever think you would, and the music is absolutely gorgeous, and despite me being someone that is typically very uninterested in music with lyrics, I fully intend on adding a ton of the songs to my music playlist(s).The game does *not* hold back any punches to get what it needs to get across through you, and there are many moments where I was just left in silence after witnessing what it had to throw. I don't even know what else to say. This game has been an incredible ride. (pun not intended)If you are reading this, do yourself a favor, and give the demo, at the very least, a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Laika: Aged Through Blood is one of the first games where I did 99% of what there is to do and kept wanting more, and while objectively there are issues with the game you can definitely point out - most of the quests in the game are fetch quests, the combat is extremely unforgiving and the bosses are not hollow knight level (they play more like bosses in Ori). I want to get those out of the way because to some they hear these things and deduce the game is not worth their time, ofcourse its their money and time however I think they would be sorely missing out. I'm a person who if I had known many of quests were fetch quests I would have never bought the game but thank **** I didn't when I bought this game.Laika is absolutely magical, the music, the art, the writing - its all so consistently amazing and coherent that I don't know how this game hasn't got more praise. The gameplay is as I mentioned earlier pretty unforgiving but its fun as♥♥♥♥, I've read other reviews saying it gets boring once your halfway through the game but to me the upgrading system, weapons you unlock aswell as how by progressing in the story every stage gets incrementally harder, so that your never breezing through places kept it fresh in my eyes. This game has become one of my favourites of all time, where this game gets it right - it gets it RIGHT.The only gripe I have is that once your done, your done. The story is absolutely amazing if a little overboard with the "you gotta remember this is a dystopia setting" tone but to me I cared about almost every single npc in the game. The writing is perfect. Play the demo, if that doesn't grab you by the collar then it might not be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has made me feel more emotion than any other game I have ever played, made me feel actual anger, sadness, and occasionally joy for certain characters. Even the side missions don't make you feel like you are going out of your way to complete them. 10/10 Story.(AND THE CUT-SCENES *mua* Chefs Kiss, Beautiful)The gameplay is fun and doesn't get too repetitive even towards the end because of the ever changing environments and access to new tools/weapons to help with traversal/combat. It also is a good challenge with the puzzles that you have to shoot your way through. Boss fights where a fun and challenging change to normal combat that kept me on my toes. 10/10 Gameplay

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't felt my heart sank playing a videogame in a while. There are a few games that have struck that bullseye, namely Oneshot, Undertale, Everhood, and Ori and the Blind Forest/Will of the Wisps, but those were a couple years ago. _childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cool game! Contrary to criticism I'm seeing, the gunplay and traversal are all very responsive and fluid, and relies pretty hard on good reaction times and figuring out good rotation. I'd say the block area of your bike is unclear at first since it seems to be slightly smaller than your bike, but other than that I'm finding this very enjoyable so far.There is one caveat in that the speed feels a bit sluggish at times, but I suspect there will be changes to that as I play more and upgrade my weaponry. This is SOMETHING of a metroidvania, after all, so there's bound to be some upgrades.The art is also positively gorgeous, the apocalyptic setting and desperation of the world reminds me heavily of LISA: the Painful RPG, but drawn by a far more accomplished artist. Characters are all memorable designs, ranging from a one-armed man playing guitar with his foot to the wisened old town chief in his wheelchair of bone and car parts.There's also an interesting mechanic where eating/cooking meals gives you timed buffs that do small things like increase combat rewards or combo multipliers.The level design is also fantastic, there's a clear intended flow at all times and some of the platforming challenges it asks are a good challenge. It makes it a point to never ask too much of you, always making it clear where you should be going. If anything, the level design only clashes in how gorgeous it is as you zoom by it. There were several moments where I just wanted to stop mid-combat and appreciate the background I was currently orchestrating a tornado of carnage through, but alas that momentary distraction would be enough to scatter myself to that tumultuous wind.Play this, it's quite good and if you're an artist you'll see a LOT you can learn from. This is a master class in effective use of art!
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game in 14 hours. The game starts off really fun and engaging, you learn more and more about the story, explore the map and learn new game mechanics, but i gotta say after a certain point i felt like the tempo really suffered. Once you have explored a majority of the map the quests kinda make you just ride along the same routes, and the fast travel points are pretty scarce. The good thing is you get to listen to the awesome soundtracks (which i even listened to on spotify on multiple occasions, just because they were so good and stuck in my ear). To fellow ultrawide gamers; the game doesnt support ultrawide so youre stuck with black bars, which kinda makes sense since it would be pretty broken to see further away.All in all, i recommend Laika. Its fun and sometimes just hard enough to get your blood flowing. 20 bucks is a good price for what you get IMO. The storystelling, atmosphere and music are all top notch.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: So much love clearly went into this game and there are so many things that are great. The art (both in the game and cutscenes) is gorgeous. Character design is wonderful. The lore is interesting. The tone gets a little dark in ways that are gratuitous, but I love the western aesthetics so I can overlook some edginess.I love collecting cassettes to expand the soundtrack, its an idea that more games should implement. It's a good incentive for people who love the game (who will enjoy some novelty in the repeating playlist) but easy enough to ignore if you don't care for completionism. The physicality of the cassette player in the menu is also something I love.Despite all there is to love, the game was just not fun to play. It did not take me 15 hours to figure that out (probably 1/2 of that was idling in menus, anyway), I spent a long time trying to push past that feeling because I was legitimately interested in the characters and story and wanted to know what happened. But ultimately the game beat me and I couldn't continue any further.My big gripe with the game is that the combat seems at odds with itself, which often drives players to more conservative, less fun strategies. I suspect when confronted with more enemies than their revolver had bullets, most players left the combat arena to reload because the places to do so in the arena were too dangerous or non-existent. The worst example of this is the .This could have been fixed pretty easily by making enemies slightly less accurate/not always approached at a straight line and then designing combat arenas around building and maintaining speed. Then make up for that loss of difficulty by making enemies more plentiful and let them move (oh yeah, with a few exceptions, enemies in the game are completely stationary). This formula has worked well for other movement shooters (eg Rollerdrome, My Friend Pedro). It's not the only way to solve the problem, but I do think it's the largest problem facing the game.That's the big issue that I feel must be addressed, because it's pervasive and pretty core to the game. Some smaller gripes I also had that did compound that problem:1. The soundtrack is very small and you can't find new tapes fast enough to keep the songs from getting old. It seems they only used a single artist, who is great but that made it worse by leaving the soundtrack with little variety.2. The game features SOO much backtracking. Normally I'd applaud devs for having very limited fast travel, but every time a side quest sent me across the map again, I felt hollow. This problem is exacerbated by the previous two: if combat was more fun or the soundtrack less limited, then going around the map so much would not be so painful.3. The control for turning the bike around was inconsistent, which got me killed in some key moments and led to quite a bit of frustration. 4. The rewards for side-quests were so bad. I did them anyway because I was motivated by the characters, and maybe that speaks for itself. But when they give me like 5 of a common crafting resource, I'd almost feel better receiving no reward.

_childDocuments_.review: A wholly unique take on metroidvania styled gameplay leaves much to be desired when even the most basic of gameplay actions require an incredible amount of finesse and delicate effort or you suffer instant death. In particular having to remember which direction to rotate your character (which is different depending on which direction your character is facing) just to reload two separate renewable skills that would have been mapped to a button in any other game, and all before you even make it to the first boss is, and I'm going to be clear here, way too much. A simplification of controls and primary gameplay actions would drastically improve the playability of the game, but its clear the developers wanted punishing instant-death hair-pin trigger-based gameplay and this is entirely at odds with the complete unstoppable bada $$ mad-max styled motor bloodsport theme the game has latched onto entirely.

_childDocuments_.review: First thing to say is this is not a pleasant game. It's very sad, very violent and it's very serious, nasty violence. The gameplay is fun and fairly original, with a reasonable but not excessive amount of challenge. The story and characters work fantastically well, on both the level of the overarching plot and also at the individual quest level. It's not even at a very high price point.I can make complaints - the map centre is frustrating to navigate around, the upgrades cost a bit too much given the campaign's playtime, objectives aren't always easy to spot - but really they're nitpicks, and they feel irrelevant even to me making them. _childDocuments_.review: I wish more games had this game's storytelling sensibilities. The way the world and the story aren't twisted to serve the player is just, mwah! There are things that are reveals, not because Laika just found out, but because everyone but the player already knows and it's uncomfortable to talk about. _childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game, there are so many positives, but I find it hard to recommend.  Let me explain.The gameplay, and this may be seen as a deterrent, mostly reminds me of Star Fox Zero.  For those uninitiated to that, let me put it simply; the controls WILL frustrate you.  It is a combination of the Trials motorcycle series, where you crash whenever your rider touches the ground, and a precision twin stick shooter.  Just like in Star Fox Zero, your movement and aiming are independent of each other, and it is extremely difficult to get your brain to put those two things together, especially when you die in a single hit.  Now, there are many checkpoints, and you are given a Shovel Knight-esque way to recover your loot to eliminate any losses, and the game provides you multiple ways to deal with enemies, but there are sections where I died so. many. times. trying to get my bike in the right spot while simultaneously dealing with enemies shooting at you.  Not only that there are foreground obstacles and other visuals to make it difficult to even see your bike, causing needless frustration.This makes it seem like a hard sell, so let me gush over the positives.  When that gameplay works, it feels awesome!  When you nail that difficult section, and deal with the bosses, it always feels satisfying, and you get that beating the dark souls boss moment when you get it right.  I did get better at the game, even though it wasn’t always clear to me at the time.  The story was engaging.  I did side quests for the story over the rewards, that was how much I was engaged.  The devs are unafraid to go there with a post-apocalyptic world, go back and forth with emotions, and portray relatable characters for the context.  If I was cursed with essentially being the gun toting grim reaper on a motorcycle, I would say many would act in the same way.  Also did I mention you get to essentially be a gun toting grim reaper on a motorcycle?The visuals are outstanding.  I loved how the world looks, and how well it connects with the story.  For a post-apocalyptic world they do a great job to make areas visually distinct and full of detail.  The music portrays the world to a bygone era before the apocalypse, but is done well and I enjoyed the contrast.There is a nice development of weapons with upgrades, and skills your bike acquires to expand the gameplay.  However, you acquire most of the upgrades very late in the story, and I can’t imagine doing some of the final segments without the rocket launcher, making them more required than optional.  One piece of advice, you may be tempted to backtrack; don’t.  I got frustrated a couple times on tedious fetch quests that were not worth it, save for ammo upgrades.  Most of the side quests are designed to be around the story area you are in, but if you forget, do not go back until you acquire easy ways to fast travel.  They can be done much more easily near the end game.  Most rewards suck anyways.At the price of 20 bucks and on sale for around 12, it makes for a solid but tempered recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe I kept this mostly spoiler free, as in no major reveals that aren't within the first 3-4 hrs of this game.Long story short, this is still an AMAZING GAME! But I give it a 7 / 10. You can read it below.Visuals - 10/10Starting off strong, I have to be honest about the art style. The very first showcase of this game in its trailer had an amazing 2D animation team and that alone captivated me immediately.While historically, and rightfully so, games that have amazing marketing animations rarely translate to the game this one does not disappoint. I can’t exactly explain how or why, but the in game style and the animation just goes SO hard. Every location is breathtaking, every character is so well designed, and the aesthetic is nailed the WHOLE WAY THROUGH. Laika, while it has its faults, is nothing short of an artistic marvel of a game. I would easily take screenshots and make them just static backdrops they’re so amazing. If you are a curator of artistic games, this one should easily make your collection. It gives me that SUPERGIANT GAMES feel, like how Hades is drawn and realized that hits me with really vibrant colors and a captivating use of heavy lineart variation. It is truly worth playing if not just for the sheer beauty of its art team.Sound - 8/10The sound design here, like any platformer, is quite good. They aren’t as complex as say a typical first or third person game would have to add a munch of music and folly to, but what it lacks in sound complexity it makes up for in its soundtrack. Beicoli does an amazing job at filling the role of a musical marvel lost to time, left with nothing but tapes for you to collect on your journey. At first I thought it would hinder the experience, having such a small collection of music at the start of the game, but boy was I wrong. It became a sweet little treat to add to this collection, finding a new music piece here and there to add to the in-game playlist. They fit the atmosphere so well, and while not all of them made my favorites they were a welcome addition to the otherwise barren wastelands. I gave this one an 8/10 because you can only do so much with sound in a scroller in my experience but for what it does it does it very well.Gameplay - 7/10I will admit, I am not a very good platformer gamer. I never really liked the meticulous timing and precise movement they required and that deterred me from a lot of what that genre had to offer. With Laika though, it was genuinely a fun and intriguing system! The first of its kind as noted as a Morovania, a play on metroidvania, where you have to control the orientation of your model, speed and angle all at once which can take a quick minute to get the hang of. It felt unique and relatively challenging at first, but when you did finally get the hang of it it was an amazing experience to master! From last minute parries, to daring flips and near-misses it feels so good for something so innovative for this genre. And while I praise it for what it achieves, I have it knocked down to 7/10 because it left me wanting just a little bit more than what it gave me. The system works mostly flawlessly, with a few minor challenges with how it registers overlapping paths and elevation. But even with that aside with a little learning, I felt a little cheated with the progression of abilities. Namely, the grappling hook. I think it was a missed opportunity to have it merely serve a situational purpose leaving it rarely ever used for things other than to pull a pillar, drag a head, or carry the ONE bomb area. When I saw it in the control menu I thought to myself, this would be so cool to be able to attach to a wall or ceiling and then use it to swing with momentum to reach new areas and such. You can imagine my disappointment afterward. I just think that extra touch could have added so much more not only to the depth of gameplay but also the level design, which is why I had to kick this one down a bit. Otherwise, I had the most fun in the final few hours with the nitro booster which added a whole new strategy to the game that was incredibly enjoyable. Despite it all, what IS here works well but it could have gone the extra mile and really dove into some untapped potential to be an amazingly unique game.Story - 7/10The story, while I am a sucker for the parent-child motif in a narrative, also left me wanting. That isn’t to say I didn’t enjoy it or that it wasn’t good, merely that I just wanted MORE. I wanted more dialogue from Laika and while I understand the idea that she's a short spoken, aggressive, and damaged individual I think it left her a little more underdeveloped than she could be. Things like more history on the blood curse, more about what Maya was like and what she learned before taking the role. Overall just more to really dive into these characters, the lore, and the setting. While environmental storytelling can do some of this, I think it missed a great opportunity for some good dialogue, character growth (or degradation), and some great story beats that could really hit harder on the heartstrings. Halfway through the game we got a good chunk of flashbacks and great information that had me tearing up, but after that there was a lot of missing immersion that could have truly driven this game home. My bias to the trope let me pass this with a 7 of 10, but for most others it’s probably a 6. But again, despite it all I did still enjoy the story. I just really wish there was more to it, or at the very least expanded more on what it has.Atmosphere - 9/10The atmosphere is absolutely amazing. It nails the wasteland vibe PERFECTLY. I love the nitty gritty survival depression they have here. It's consistent and uniform and I praise it for that. Nothing happens where the world or an area feels out of place. The world feels constantly oppressed but also lively with a smidgeon of hope. It reminds me so much of Mad Max and I love it for it. Everything from the need for resources, crafting, the grim uncertainty of its residents, and the wild biomechanical creature mutation stuff all felt right at home in this world and honestly, I want nothing more than to spend MORE time here. It captivates the mind and setting in a way that is both familiar and foreign in its own right.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game, though not that much emphasis on the "unlocking traversal options" kind of gameplay. One of those upgrades is also very situational, which is a bit of a shame. In general, it did not feel like a metroidvania to me.Thats not to say that it *doesn't* happen, and the other (still, very few...) upgrades do have a noticeable impact on traversal. Too bad one of them comes just before the end of the game.The core gameplay is still entertaining enough to have carried me to the end, and I did enjoy playing the game a lot.Controlling the motorcycle and gun at the same time, especially considering the reload and parry mechanics makes for a very engaging concept. Sure, one enemy is easy, but a group is harder. Later on, other types of enemies are introduced all of which require a bit more thinking to overcome. It doesn't take long until every encounter turns into a little mind game of its own - Who do I shoot first? Will they manage to take a shot off before they die? If they do, can I block it? Maybe it makes more sense to parry the shot, and save my bullets for someone else?Honestly, the more I played the game the more it reminded me of SUPERHOT.In SUPERHOT, the time-moves-only-when-you-move stuff makes it possible to plan out encounters just as I did for this game.However, unlike SUPERHOT here we only have bullet time, and only if you commit to taking a shot (i.e. while pressing down the trigger), *and* if you take too long to think of a plan, the shot will just go off and you waste a bullet. With the first gun only having two shots, thats a lot.To me, this is an improvement over SUPERHOT: Sure, you have some time to think, but not infinitely so. Thinking fast is rewarded, not least of which because you will probably fall on your face otherwise. Landing with motorcycle on top will kill you, so you more often than not need not only to win the fight, but have time left to land cleanly.Story beats are good but predictable, not much to say here.But the environment and atmosphere are top notch. The additional lore in sidequests also fleshes out the world well.Not going to go into this much more for spoiler reasons.Can definitely recommend getting this and giving it a go. Some caveats though:- Play on mouse and keyboard. The game is horrible on a controller, and I switched almost immediately, to immediate better results.- Getting to 100% is a chore, and I can't recommend it. The necessary items will need to be farmed, which is plain boring. Just play through the game normally, personally I also did all sidequests.

_childDocuments_.review: Ended up finishing the game. The core mechanics, visual style and music all held up. The overall game did not add up to the sum of its parts. Any time I played an extended session (which was most times) I could not get over how the traversal of the barren landscape felt like torture. Hold right or left until you get to the turn, and then DON'T MISS IT. I kept returning to my map to make sure I hadn't missed the turn like some horrible Google Maps heavy road trip. That would have already been a little annoying, since swapping routes was rare and easy to mess up, but then there's just birds every other corner you can't even see that will shoot and kill you instantly. This means for long stretches of time you have to mindlessly hold right or left while tense and ready for a bird to pop up out of nowhere so you can shoot it first. This is mostly what your experience will be playing Laika, driving around a wasteland as an immortal Uber Eats driver. That could even be a little more interesting, because then the game would be more built around it, but instead the game has you trying to find objects around the map for a cast of furries that all want a wild boar hide for their stuff. Unfortunately the fetch quests were important to me because the game comes out of the gate with incredible story and conflict, only for the story to fail to expand and end satisfyingly. The long stretches of waiting to arrive somewhere to get a thing for someone end up putting a lot of pressure on the story to be exceptional to be worth all the stressful driving, pressure it cannot live up to. Without the tedious, stressful traveling it would be a fine story, but after the final curtain I found myself wanting more out of it. The traversal wasn't all bad. Some places were challenging without being frustrating, and after multiple visits became fun tricks to smoothly nail without flipping and dying. Unfortunately most of the map you spend most of your time with is not interconnected in a way that makes it convenient, and instead requires roundabout, confusing routes to get to where you need to go. That means instead of revisiting sections of a reasonably sized, compact map with interesting locations you can learn to be excellent at, you will choose to use the paid-not-paid-annoying-fast-travel system. These are rare and allow you to cook, swap weapons, and teleport. Trying to return to your base is awful without a warp, but you'll often  need to travel a long way to get to a warp anyways. Fixing this wouldn't be helpful, since the actual problem is the repetitive and stressful driving you'll constantly be performing. It is boring, unchallenging nothing, and overly challenging at the same time. I finished the game because I hoped the end would make the grind worth it, but it wasn't and I can't go back and get my hours back.

_childDocuments_.review: The stellar music, visuals, and raw gameplay on display in Laika: Aged Through Blood have no business carrying a game  hard in today’s landscape.The immaculate vibes present throughout sections of the game are incredible. The cassette player (how the game conveys background music) has an assortment of music that can be described as nothing short of beautiful – some say it’s repetitive, however I disagree with this statement and posit this enables one to build up a layer of intimacy with the music; the player becomes familiar with what they hear, select favourites, and are encouraged to find more tapes if they start to drag in order to maintain musical diversity/freshness. The music dances between complementing and contrasting the dreary wasteland environment enough to the point where it  has my attention.The gameplay may be tricky at first, but is immensely satisfying to engage with and push the limits-of. As death is of little consequence, you are free to engage with situations at your own pace and in your own time. This allows you to soak in the rich atmosphere and stunning artwork to your heart’s content. Honestly, my initial hesitation of: “Oh it plays like one of those motorbike flash games” put me off to begin with, but once I got into the flow of things, I really saw how it shined above that preconception and how it does enough to be different and interesting. Once I REALLY got into it, I kept catching myself on a rhythm with my guns blaring having a grand old time alongside the soundtrack.The visual design on display is viscerally enchanting. Sheer eye-candy wherever you go – from region-to-region to cutscenes to set-pieces. I just love looking at this game, it’s great. It’s almost  good to the point where some combat settings tend to get cluttered, messy and unreadable with particle effects which may lead to the occasional fumble/death. The music and visuals go hand-in-hand to deliver spectacles and impactful scenes throughout the game.Music, sound effects, gameplay, story, visuals, everything on display is amazing. However, the underwhelming boss fights, bike upgrades, a kinda-shoe-horned parry system and story-mission length (man, some take way too long) pull the game down a few pegs. This game is not without flaws, but this is a good thing, it merely paves for future game titles by honing on what it does best.You should definitely try Laika if you catch it on sale. You'll feel the whole spectrum of emotions. Quite the package.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay I am editing (rewriting) my review. When I was playing in the beginning, some of the mechanics were not clicking with me (when I was just around 3 hours in). Add to that the UI could be really small on steam deck but thats not the game's fault. So when I wrote that review (while still recommending the game), I believe some of those frustrations crept in into the review. However once I got used to the nuances of the gameplay, holy hell this game is AMAZING. I am 20 hours in, and just cant put it down. I was already a fan of the story, art, music, and now that the gameplay has been clicking with me, I find it soothing to ride Where Our Bikes Growl, listening to music and shooting those bastard birds. I LOVE THIS GAME. Go get it. For me its a masterpiece. The mechanics, once you get the hang of them, let you combine traversal and combat moves together and soon you will be in a 'flow state', accessing previously unreachable areas by upgrades and experimentation. The story is beautiful, tinged with a certain sadness but the these 2D characters are just so amazingly written that you WANT them to succeed, even when you fully know that the world they live in is harsh and cruel. Kudos to the game's writers, they really went in and committed to the story, even when sometimes it gets too dark to handle. Laika is such an amazing character, she is stoic and fearsome, but at the same her vulnerability is obvious for anyone who knows her, because not only she's responsible for her village's safety, she's also a mother which keeps the stakes higher than I expected. Again, I am in love with this game <3

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal game that I highly recommend to anyone who likes metroidvanias. If you are curious how it plays, the best I can describe it as is like a cross between those mobile motorcycle games and a bullet hell lite, but with a story I genuinely enjoyed. I didn't really mess around with the cooking aspect much but at one point I crafted every recipe for the achievement, and was just a complete powerhouse for the duration of the effects and made SO much money. So definitely cook more than I did, it is worth it.The Reload system is unique and makes some fights a game of swapping guns lightning fast rather than reloading.At time of writing, I just completed the main story after spending most of my time going after collectibles and being a bit of a completionist. I won't spoil it but I want to say I appreciate the devs for writing a good story.The Soundtrack of this game is a HUGE draw. My wife quite literally bought the game because she got hooked to the soundtrack while I was playing. (much to my surprise, I just found out the soundtrack is available on Spotify!)Well done devs, I had a great time playing your game

_childDocuments_.review: Short answer; solid thumbs up.Art design, great, music even better, story/ world building/ general aesthetic, better again.The controls and game play are clean and fair, you never die because of bad luck or poor design (keeping in mind I've only beaten a couple of bosses, but based on what I've played so far the design is good).This game will appeal to 'pro gamers' and the casual crowed alike. Rather than have different skill levels to cater to all types of players the developer just allowed for generous respawns and a light death penalty. Better players won't have to respawn as much and worse players (like myself) are free to retry encounters without losing much progress at all.But when you do engage an encounter just right you feel like John Wick on a dirt bike. And again, if you're just looking for a casual experience, if you ♥♥♥♥ up an encounter, the respawns are very generous. But if you think you're good, go ahead and prove it, there is a lot of room here for genuine skill expression.

_childDocuments_.review: Recently I've found a lot of games that make something I am not even remotely interested(mainly any kinds of sports or racing) into things I enjoy. Laika: Aged Through Blood is one of them, and my god this is such a great game. It has an addicting core gameplay loop, a real eye-pleasing artstyle, fantastic soundtracks, and a brutal, gloomy story. All thanks to these elements combined, the game has easily become my favorite and currently the only motorbike that I actually enjoy. Of course it contains some issues that might dwindle the fun. The side quests are just glorified fetch quests, the visual effect sometimes can obscure the protagonist, and the map doesn't away depict correctly, just to name a few. The game is still a wonderful experience to play through.→: The main gimmick of the game is to ride through wasteland doing many stunts, while shooting all your enemies that conveniently just stand still on your path. I gotta hand it to the dev team. They really know how to make riding motorbike through various locations fun and cool. You perform a back-flip in the air to reload the guns and your front-flip to gain charge that allows you to deflect bullet with the bike(don't ask how it makes sense because of video game). Thus, players are encouraged to pull out some cool tricks. Every encounter with the enemies is a mini test to see how you juggle between back-flipping(reloading) and positioning. Time slows down when you hold the trigger, so you have plenty of time to readjust yourself.→: In addition to bike stunts, guns are as important and fun as you shoot them. Your trusty Revolver is jack of trade, able to get everything done with no trouble; Shotgun is the most interesting. Not only does it feel good to shoot, its recoil allows you to do back-flip everywhere you want; Crossbow boasts the highest ammo count and widest spread, easy to deal with multiple targets at once; Machine Gun is great for high combo and visceral(currency) farming because of its high fire rate; Sniper Rifle with magnifying glass gives you the most accurate shot; Rocket Launcher is risky to use, but all so satisfying to shoot back at those rocket launcher wielding a-holes.Another experience I love about Laika: Aged Through Blood is the feel of riding the bike. The thrill of biking-n-gunning is exciting, but the downtime between is equally satisfying. This is where the artstyle and soundtracks come into play. The landscapes are beautiful to behold. Each location has a distinct color scheme. The design of the background silently tells the story of the world, even the name itself is interesting. For example, in Where the Waves Die the background is an abandoned, dried up dam and a barren river. Near the end of the river we can see the bone of giant creatures, making me wonder what happened to this world, what cause the sea to recede so far away, and what would the creature look like when it were alive. The other part of the experience the cassette player. Laika: Aged Through Blood does the background music a bit differently than the usual. Players collect cassettes from different areas, and they are free to choose whichever song they want to play on the bike. Initially I was quite skeptical about this decision. Usually the soundtracks are made to fit in their designated areas, letting the player choose any soundtracks to play may break the immersion. It turns out that my worry is unwarranted. The soundtracks are not only amazing, but they also fit in every area perfectly. →Again, the artsyle and soundtrack are amazing.→I really, REALLY like each character design. I am a hopeless furry after all.→A grim story that depicts the cruelty of war.→Metroidvania style of abilities for more exploration.→Boss fights can be long and tedious, but I think they are good for this kind of gameplay.→: With how little way to upgrade yourself in the game, you can buff yourself temporary through cooking. Mixing up three out of fifteen ingredients to see what the potential outcome might be is a fun mini-game. And the buff you receive is nothing to scoff at, ranging from extra resource and currency gain, more deflect charges, extra ammo, to maximum bike magnet radius and 3x combo starter. These buff can help you overcome a lot of nasty situation in the late game.→: The concept is good, but I feel like the buff you get should be separated from the cooking system, and made into a standalone permanent upgrade system. Things like deflect charges, extra ammo, and magnet radius should be reworked into permanent upgrades either hidden in various areas or become motorbike upgrades you can purchase from the blacksmith. This design might address lacking a sense of progression, and also welcome some more interesting temporary buff like ammo efficiency (a chance to not consume ammo when shooting).The only problem I have towards the game is its side quests. They are not good. Almost every one of them is just a glorified fetch quest that wants you to travel to a specific location to collect a certain object. Other than some dialogues and resources you can get from exploring, there isn't any incentive to do them besides extending your playtime. Funny thing is, you will know which item is the aim of a side quest long before you have access to it. These items like flowers have a thicker outline than other, and it's slightly annoying that you cannot just pick them up and wait for the side quests to pop. It's a shame because I really enjoy the gameplay and I appreciate every opportunity to go out there and explore, if only the side quest were more interesting and rewarding.→The Meathook ability is lackluster. Its need to be more than just hook and pull things. Why not let us hook on to something and swing the bike across the ravine? That ought to fun and frustrating.→Maybe slow down the tutorial at the beginning. You need to give players enough time to practice before introducing new things.→Maybe reduce the blood splattering effect and explosion a little. Often time I find it hard to identify our protagonist due to all the effects triggering at the same time and at the same scene.中文小簡評→第一款我非常有興趣的特技摩托遊戲。→福瑞、劇情黑暗、玩法有趣、畫風美音樂佳，不愛都難啊。→特技摩托加上射擊，後空翻換彈、前空翻讓你可以反彈子彈，這些設計鼓勵玩家秀出酷炫的技倆。→六把槍各司其職，其中散彈槍特別好玩，他的後座力能讓你原地後空翻。→騎著摩托朝著遠方呼嘯而過，欣賞沿途末日廢土的風景，配上極其好聽的音樂，那種自在完全不輸特技摩托的爽感。→身為一位無可救藥的福瑞控，這遊戲的每個角色我都好愛阿。→劇情真的黑暗血腥，那個開場絕對會勾起你的興趣。→類銀河系惡魔成的技能設計與相連的地圖。→Boss戰設計尚可，或許會有點冗長，但配合遊戲玩法完全合理。→烹飪系統是少數你可以加強自己的選項任選三樣食材加再一起，可以煮出多種增益。概念很好，但是我覺得有些增益應該獨立設計成永久升級系統。→支線任務真的不行，大多數都是跑腿撿東西，獎勵不豐富，任務過程也不有趣。→鉤子這項技能很雞肋，應該要設計可以讓玩家盪過峽谷或抓住敵人加速前進。→開場的教學需要再緩點，應該讓玩家多練習幾次再介紹新特色。→噴血特效及爆炸過多，特別是在空中，容易把角色擋住。

_childDocuments_.review: This gets a 'maybe' from me, it has its moments of grace and some beautiful key art and music, but suffers from some truly frustrating and baffling design decisions that only serve to make the whole experience more of a let down.At its heart, the game is a splatformer where you will die many thousands of times due to the somewhat unfair accuracy (and bullet leading) of your enemies, coupled with any single mistake leading to you restarting the whole thing.This isn't necessarily bad, but there are many frustrating elements coupled with this that cause unnecessary frustration. Be it the soulslike bags you leave on death, forcing backtracking to obtain these if you head in the wrong direction (which is often in these very interwoven maps), or your enemies bodies blocking your shots - but not those of other enemies. The latter being quite important given you only have 2 or 3 shots at a time.The game isn't particularly large, but it outstays its welcome with constant and frequent backtracking to locations you have already visited multiple times to find new elements placed there, that you won't know are there until you happen upon them. Despite the maps size, it could still have done with being cut back in sections, especially the ship level that confusingly starts with a 7 minute unskippable cutscene with infrequent dialogue. I'm being critical here and I know, but I really enjoyed the game world and story and pushed through my constant frustrations with it until near the end, but I just can't bring myself to finish the last 5 hours, I'd rather let this one go.If you want to try this one, heavens do keyboard and mouse and not controller, the game is nigh impossible on a controller due to the accuracy needed with such minimal ammo for each weapon.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully presented game, that ultimately falls short of it's presentation. I wish there was a "sorta good, but watch out!" recommend option. The young, the old, the weak, the pregnant, the wounded, Israel intentionally strikes them without even the slightest care. Those who choose to stay get killed. Those who choose to leave still get killed on the extraction route designated by Israel itself. Those too sick ,too old, or too wounded who cannot leave shortly get killed. Bloody, even those who come to help the unarmed still get killed. _childDocuments_.review: I was completely enthralled by this game. Going in I expected it to be a few ours of entertainment, but it has exceeded that and rocketed to the position of one of my all time favourite indie games. The controls took a little bit to settle with me but once they did Laika is a blast, plus the soundtrack and story are amazingly written. _childDocuments_.review: Easily one of my favorite experiences playing through a game so far! Incredible visual style, a great emotional story with well written characters, awesome map designs that differentiate between areas well and are very fun to explore through, and it's impossible for me to ask for game play mechanics that are any better. I may be a bit biased coming from years of playing other motorcycle specific games, but the skill based combat and level navigation was super addicting and satisfying. Definitely not easy by any means, but for me nothing was too hard or frustrating that I would spend more than a half hour grinding any one section. Took me about 23 hours to beat the game for the first time, which could be quicker if you used fast travel more, but I didn't feel the need to because I had so much fun simply traversing through the map. I am super glad I found out about this game, and by the time I finished the demo I was hooked. I would absolutely recommend to anyone looking for a skill based game with a good story!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: 8/10 would recommend.- The gameplay take a while to get used to but once you do it's really fun. 99% of the game is spent on a moterbike, blocking enemy shots with it, doing flips to reload your guns and using the slow-motion to pull of sick-looking combos. The difficulty curve is gentle enough not to feel to punishing and in late game, traversing the world feels effortless.- The world is big and varied enough to be interesting but not so big as to take away from the fun.- The  is amazing. 10/10 combination of story, music and visuals. The OST is great and really adds to the feeling of the world. It is probably the main reason I am even writing this review. Because more people should experience it.A gripe I have with the game are the side quests. I wish they offered more information where to look for the items instead of just the general region. I'm not talking about map markers (that'd take away from the exploration) but rather description of what to look for. The quests themselves are also mainly fetch quests. I did them less for the gameplay and more for the "story". I put story in quotes because once again I come back to the atmosphere. The quests help bring a bit of hope to the wastelands and were really intrinsically motivated (especially since the rewards were irrelevant).Overall: good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is so very close to being an amazing game but there are a couple of flaws that make this game almost unplayable for me, as well as other problems that affect many people.The game is pretty unique and base gameplay loop is incredibly fun. You ride a motorcycle and it controls very similarly to the Trials games. The unique part is that you have a gun, and you have to turn around in your bike. Turning around is done by holding space, if you just press space you can parry enemy bullets. You shoot by aiming with the mouse, and pressing M1, holding M1 puts you in a bullet time to aim and react better. You reload your weapon, and refresh your parry by doing front and back flips. Yes, you can do it multiple times in a single aerial. Your bike also acts like a shield, turn the bottom of your bike towards enemy projectiles and you won't die. Very cool with tons of potential.The problem a lot of people are having is that they struggle to maintain focus on shooting all enemies, blocking multiple projectiles from different directions, reloading, refreshing parry, and still landing wheels down. People have asked for a mode where landing on your head didn't instantly kill you, and devs have said no. The main thing is that Laika's helmet is a skull, so it's white, but her bike is also white. When focusing not focusing on the bike (or people with poor vision) you can't easily and quickly tell what your angle is. Every end point of the shape Laika makes on her bike is white, so the best some people can do is put two of the white ends down and sometimes they end up on their head. They have tried to implement elements to help identify your positioning in air. The reticle has an arrow that shows the angle your head is at, and the arrow turns red when you are at a poor angle and will die, the ammo counter is in the shape of a revolver, and rotates as you rotate and will turn red at the same poor angles. The bigger issue is that your focus is almost never in the corner of your screen, as there is already an ammo counter on the reticle, the revolver is orange a color very close to red, so the revolver aspect is kinda negligible. If you know anything about the complexities of aiming, you'll probably know that you don't tent to focus on your reticle, but you focus on your target instead. Not only that, but often your attention is completely drawn away from aiming as you still have to block shots from multiple angles.To fix this, I've seen someone suggest a adding a red glow to the border of the whole screen when at a poor angle, which sounds like a good compromise that shouldn't be too difficult to implement, and can be a toggleable option. I'm not sure if I completely agree with a difficulty setting that removes an important part of what makes this game interesting and feel good to play. Not dying when landing poorly is kind of the whole point of Trials, and other similar games that this takes inspiration from, and adding it in can conflict with the artistic direction and intention. On the flip side, I don't think that some players who truly enjoy playing the game should be barred for a simple aspect of important info not being conveyed in a way that makes it quick and easy for them to interpret. Personally, I don't mind how the game currently is in this aspect, but this has been a large point of contention for a lot of players.The problem I have is that I want to play the game fast. Bullet time is a forced aspect, you have to enter it every shot as it automatically start on M1 press, regardless if you wanted to or not. Every time you enter it there is a zoom in effect to kinda help you focus on your shot. The zoom effect can cause shots that were aligned to miss as your angle gets shifted a bit from the zoom. This is further hindered by there being an accuracy penalty for not taking time on your shots. I want to make my shots without bullet time. I think that it plays into the badass feeling that the game seems like it's going for. Being able to full speed make two shots, do a flip, block a shot, and make another shot or two without the game deciding I didn't take enough time to aim so I should miss. I feel like if I can do an encounter without bullet time that I should be able to without relying on RNG to make my shots land, I should. This also affects farming for materials, you gotta shoot ore veins to mine it, but because of the aiming penalties you still gotta take the an extra second to aim your shot, the shot that you are making in a no-threat environment. I find it intrusive and it makes it really hard to continue to play the game. The game has the potential to be an incredibly fast paced experience but needing to stop for a full second to aim a shot that I've already aimed just feels like I need to slow myself down to play at the games speed, but every other aspect of the game tells me that it should be played at a faster pace. I would much rather have a bullet time be assigned to a different binding. It'll allow players to enter it when they feel like they need it, and when they don't need it that can clear the section faster.Honestly, if this one change was made then I could see myself not just playing through the whole game, but also potentially learning to speedrun the game. It genuinely causes me to not play the game, despite every other aspect being amazing. The art design, the music, the general gameplay, it's all great, but this one point I can't get over.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: A weird but sorely overlooked game with a gorgeous visual aesthetic, and an equally excellent soundtrack. The story oozes with an overwhelming sense of gloom that, despite its seemingly dissonant style of gameplay with funky motorcycle physics, fits perfectly. It's beautiful, really. The only big downside to the game is that it can be melodramatic at times, where scenes either don't have enough time to breathe or aren't set up in a way that gives you a chance to think over what's being shown to you.The gameplay is challenging yet forgiving, provided the person playing picks up on how its system works, and it has a satisfying puzzle-like loop with the way it combines combat and exploration. Every checkpoint and sequence is a puzzle that must be solved, and approaching it any other way will lead to guaranteed frustration. Mastery of the game's mechanics and being able to properly juggle the systems it throws at you really leads to a genuinely rewarding experience, but I can only imagine how many players are either not familiar with its gameplay style or how many players just aren't willing to understand it.I think this is going to be going way under most people's radar when it really shouldn't. If you've ever liked metroidvanias, enjoy a bit of a puzzle-like challenge, along with a thoughtfully unique experience with gorgeous visuals and music, you NEED to pick this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: This game tries to do too much. While the core story and mechanics drive the game there are several ancillary things that make the game kind of stumble. You will get upgrades that are maybe useful for one very specific spot but not really anywhere else. The first two weapons you get are the only ones really worth getting and upgrading because the others seem superfluous. Cooking is kinda pointless. There are side quests that just kind of throw in shocking subjects and are over with.But there's a core here that I really like. Laika as a protagonist is cynical about her place in a destroyed world and within her community but little moments of kindness break through and show her as a caring person with an awful lot in life. The mechanics of biking around may get a bit tiring by the end point but there's enough variation and a late stage ability that keep traversal interesting and fun. You'll crash a lot and combat is chaotic to a fault, but generous checkpoints and setpiece moments really carried this game into being one of my favorites of 2023.Also damn that sound track. Everybody's first reaction is "this doesn't match the game" but as it goes on the nuances of the vibe really bring together a unique mixture of aesthetics.

_childDocuments_.review: Come for the gameplay, stay for the music and the story.I must say that I will not be objective during this review because I absolutely loved it, maybe try out the demo before buying it, as the controls may not be for everyone, but if you like what you see in the demo, go for it, because the full game is even better.The story, while not too predominant in the game, mainly some quests, makes you build a "relation" with the people on the village, and you end up helping them not because of the rewards (that are mainly some crafting components) but because you actually want to help them.Moving onto the gameplay, there are 6 weapons and only one of them actually gives you a new ability metroidvania style, later in the game you get 2 abilities more, one situational and one that completely changes the mechanics, so if that is what you are looking for, maybe this game is not for you.The combat is challenging but having frequent save points makes it not frustrating. I must say there's a lot of backtracking in the game but the movement is quite satisfying so it's not really a pain.Lastly, the OST has some of the best songs that I've listened in games, and totally make going through the map a more fun experience, even if you don't like the game, give the music a try.All in all, if you are looking for a new and refreshing experience lasting around 15-20 hours, try the demo and if you like it, go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 4/5Laika: Aged Through Blood is a haunting and emotionally charged experience that delves deep into themes of sacrifice, survival, and the bonds that tie us together. Set in a dystopian world where humanity teeters on the brink of extinction, this narrative-driven adventure captivates players with its gripping story and atmospheric gameplay.- Compelling Narrative: Laika's story is a masterclass in emotional storytelling, drawing players into a world ravaged by despair and clinging to hope. The journey of Laika, a canine protagonist, as she navigates the horrors of a post-apocalyptic landscape is both heart-wrenching and poignant, leaving a lasting impact on players long after the credits roll.- Atmospheric World-Building: The game's atmospheric world is brought to life through stunning visuals and evocative sound design. From the desolate ruins of civilization to the eerie landscapes of a world reclaimed by nature, every environment feels rich with history and atmosphere, immersing players in its haunting beauty.- Emotional Depth: Laika: Aged Through Blood tackles weighty themes with a depth and maturity rarely seen in video games. Through its exploration of sacrifice, loyalty, and the enduring power of love, the game resonates on a deeply emotional level, prompting players to reflect on their own humanity and values.- Engaging Gameplay: While primarily a narrative-driven experience, Laika also offers engaging gameplay mechanics that complement its storytelling. From tense stealth sequences to heart-pounding action set-pieces, the game keeps players on their toes with a variety of gameplay challenges that enhance the overall experience.- Pacing Issues: Despite its many strengths, Laika occasionally suffers from pacing issues, with certain sections of the game feeling rushed or underdeveloped. This uneven pacing can detract from the immersion and impact of the story, leaving players wishing for more time to explore its richly realized world.- Limited Replay Value: Once players have experienced Laika's story to its conclusion, there is little incentive to revisit the game. While multiple endings and branching paths could have added replayability, the linear nature of the narrative limits its long-term appeal for some players.Overall, Laika: Aged Through Blood is a dark and gripping tale that stands as a testament to the power of storytelling in video games. With its compelling narrative, atmospheric world-building, and emotional depth, it's a must-play for fans of narrative-driven experiences and a worthy addition to any gamer's library.Check out my Laika walkthrough here:

_childDocuments_.review: The story of a woman making all the wrong decisions and losing everything in the goal of creating a better world for her daughter.I feel like this game would have benefited from being an RPG, or a movie. The story, character, music, setting themes, ETC is immaculate. I wish I could have had more agency there.  The tactile game play is weak, speaking as someone who loves it. (Go play cyclomaniacs 2 if you want to try out a better version of what this game is going for. It's a free flash game.)If you don't like the motorcycle mechanics immediately, you should know they don't get better as the game progresses. The developers needed to gate you off from specific locations for story reasons. So all forms of mobility up until the very end of the game are fixed in a way that hard limits emergent gameplay. As a result every time you unlock something new, you're instantly disapointed about how niche the use for it is. The grapple hook could be replaced with a key card, and the game wouldn't be much different.Inspite of that, I'd still highly recomend this game for basically everything else.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been thinking about Laika: Aged Through Blood because that game gives me some Feelings, and I'm usually very positive when a game does that. And it's true: I am, in general, positive on the game--mastering the mechanics is fun and the story hits hard despite being so larger-than-life. If that's all you wanna know, yes it gets a hearty recommendation with a small asterisk. Asterisk to follow, Both the gameplay and the story leave  on the table. First, it's a metroidvania, but you only ever get two abilities that impact traversal. Second, the story always pokes at the deeper implications of Laika's actions, but never quite confronts them.Story: Laika *gets people killed*, both directly and indirectly. But we never actually see the impact it has on her, besides making her more angry. *Does* Laika experience guilt? Or does Laika experience no guilt? The story implies that Laika experiences no guilt, but absolves her anyway. This is an okay direction to go. The implication is that the bad guys are so bad they need to be mowed down by the hundreds, and guilt is a useless feeling to have.So why does the story try to inject nuance there? Or actually, inject nuance and do nothing with it? The best scene in the game is (BIGGER spoilers)  It's a POWERFUL scene. This is the sort of scene where you EXPLICITLY lay out whether there is guilt over the action, or no guilt over the action, because either one is  with implications.Story doesn't do anything further with it.Gameplay: Once you master the controls, which ARE inherently interesting and are a requirement to get to the halfway mark, there really isn't much else to it. There's one new traversal method near the end which practically obsoletes the first, PLUS if you figure out how to abuse it, trivializes the reload mechanic the game insists upon.In a way, "figuring out how to abuse the new mechanic" does add one more complexity, but it comes at the cost of removing several others. But also... I'm not sure the other complexities added enough for a 16-20 hour game. There's a lot of repetition. By the time I got to the final area I was a bit tired of it all. The game's combat escalates, but not by as much as you'd think. The most interesting setpieces were the boss encounters, and there's only like five? of those.There were also a handful of design issues. One of the enemies jumps out of a box, but their hitbox does not activate when they appear. It's sometime during the height of their jump. But also sometimes bullets just miss the hitboxes of enemies despite passing right through their sprite.Still, I think it's worthwhile. For what they had, it feels like the game is a bit overly long, and if they had a little more story or more gameplay it might have justified the length. But it doesn't run SO much longer that it hurts the overall Feelings.

_childDocuments_.review: It is hard to choose the best indie game this year, I can't recall so many wonderful original high quality ones on just 1 year! And yet, Laika still shines among all them with its super polished gameplay, wonderful storytelling, beautiful soundtrack so characteristic in Brainwash Gang's games, original boss fights.And the riding... I have the same feeling I got playing the first Spiderman, when it didn't really matter what was the fastest route or the next mission to achieve, just wondering around was fantastic. And going across the incredible world of Laika on your motorbike is, by itself, incredibly satisfying. Then you manage to perfectly time an acrobatic jump with a shot-recharge-parry-shot combo and feel the king of the world. A game worth experiencing, a Top 3 (at the very least) indie game of the year, and an absolute steal for its price.

_childDocuments_.review: It's the  metroidvania with bullet time.While it does have a sprawling map, it only has 3 ability-gating upgrades, and just the general feel of the game causes me to want to call it metroidvania-like at best.This game will not be for everyone, even I was frustrated in the first few hours as I acclimated to the controls.  The controls are actually great, there is just a bit of learning curve to master them. The gameplay itself is working out how to approach each segment and is a bit trial & error (rotate my bike this way, shoot this enemy up top, then reflect the projectile of this enemy, then shoot the two down there). On a screen you'll probably fail at the execution a few times tweaking exactly how you want to approach the segment. Once you get past it, you'll immediately undergo the same situation again with the next segment, with different mob and track placement. As you master the controls, it can get a bit more free-flowing, but most of the gameplay is stop-start like that.  I think this game is at its best in sections like the boss in the mines where you are constantly moving one way, it feels faster paced when its like that, it would definitely be a more.. 'comfortable' experience if it were a straight up 2D sidescroller in this style.You'll die quite a bit from enemies that appear on screen too late to realistically react to them in time unless you already know that they're there.Backtracking in this game was a little more tiresome to me than a typical metroidvania.  Teleport points were spread out, and so i would have to repeat a lot of sections.  What made it worse was that the quest would suggest an area (and sometimes this was unclear too), but not tell you where in that area to be looking.  You may have explored that entire area already, and all you can do is go over the whole thing again.  It's tedious.  NPCs that you find on the map should also be marked for you to easily return to them.  The game does give you the ability to mark your map, so you can get around that at least.The music has had a lot of effort put into it, and works for the most part.  Rather than have specific tracks for areas, you have a looping playlist which expands as you find more cassette tapes.  I dislike this system and prefer biomes/areas to each have their own track, which gives an area a bit more character.  I would prefer the playlist as an additional feature where if i really want to hear a track, i can go into my tape player and mess with it.  As for the music itself, it isn't my style, but sounds quite modern and the sort of thing that might play in a t.v. shows emotional montage.  Tracks are vocalised, and have a 'jilted woman' and sometimes a 'travelling' vibe, which does fit biking around the gritty world as the female protagonist.  Not my cup of tea, but it works and on some level i do like and appreciate it.Laika was fairly enjoyable, sometimes tedious but quite impressive. _childDocuments_.review: It took me sometime to force myself to buy it, i knew it could be good or a fun game with pretty art.It broke all my thoughts after the end of the demo and where the game picks up from, alot of love has been put in this project and you can feel it for it's art, gameplay style, characters and tone. But i can't explain with just words on a screen how many things i felt during the story being told through bullets and blood,It takes effort to introduce a character, show how much they appreciate something at the same time you're burning it down.Even more a mother's rage, the only part you're not behind the trigger of a cycling gun chamber, Laika is.And a lot of courage to make the player bond with Puppy, to make them need to sleep and perhaps go check on the little kid every time you go back to upgrade weapons, fetch new quests and dust off again.Every time i shoot i feel the game is alive, impact marks, black and red lines while the bullet flies away and hits, the screen getting more red from the ongoing carnage of the grim biker and it's victims while i hear Coming Home or any of the 20 some bangers made for this game, i can't think of any other artist that could do what Beicoli did.Just go buy it or wait for a sale, go out there and make the wasteland red from their blood and maybe,just maybe, better times come when the blood dries, untill theres nothing left besides bones and shell casings.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Review from a Casual Gamer who just started playing indie games.My overall review on the game is its pretty fun, game goes by pretty quick. I beat most of the game in about 15 hours of game play, both main mission and a majority of side quests. Game play while seemingly repetitive is very satisfying. While its the same thing, the satisfaction of constantly juggling enemies with  a combo while reloading feels great. The story is grim and enticing, and was pretty impactful. I only have two complaints, which are a minor inconvenience, pale in comparison to the overall game. Story felt a little too edgy, characters cussing when the conversation is in a different tone, makes it feel like its out of place and just wants to add more cuss words. You can make a narrative feel dark without so much cursing. And the controls themselves are much better on keyboard and mouse than controller. I wanted this game to be on controller so the gameplay could be more relaxing, but man aiming on the controller is impossible, idk if its just me but mouse and keyboard felt MUCH better.Anyway, solid game 8/10, pick it up its noice.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, the idea seems awesome. Looking at the negative reviews, they all have the same complaints, which I agree with, so I'd highly recommend playing the demo prior to buying this.The game plays kind of like a Trials game with twin stick shooting. You start with a revolver with only two rounds. In order to reload, you have to perform a backflip. This gets very frustrating when you approach three enemies as their accuracy is deadly and you die in one hit. You'll find yourself performing backflips very often to reload your gun, one tricky thing about this while fighting multiple enemies is that killing an enemy will cover you in blood. Your whole character is pretty much a single blood of red and with how much is going on all over the screen, planning your next shot, you'll often times not realize which direction your character is facing and land on your head, killing you instantly. Speaking of landing on your head, you'll also find yourself sometimes taking jumps too quickly and hitting a high wall, killing yourself when your head hits a wall or ceiling too quickly. The game is a metroidvania and every encounter feels like a death trap on first approach. You reach some enemies with speed, not realizing they're there until you're already getting close. You'll find yourself dying very often in your first approach. After that, it's basically time to figure out the way to get through it without dying. I wouldn't even say the combat gets frustrating, but it makes every encounter just feel annoying and tedious. The worst however is when you reach an odd platforming section. Fortunately, there aren't many, but what finally made me give up on the game was a section I had to drop into an opening at just the right speed. If I went too slow, I would fall in the pit and die. If I went too fast, I would hit my head on the wall and die. If I tried to counter that and bounce my wheels on the wall so I don't hit my head, I still fall into the pit. The game has some great ideas, but the gameplay loop gets old really quickly. The combat isn't engaging enough to keep me interested. I had a lot more fun racing around but then you get frustrated with some oddly designed platforming sections. I feel like this game would have been much more enjoyable if instead of a metroidvania, the game was a lot more linear and focused on level design where you could build up speed to traverse the world and have some better placed enemies. I think of something like Ghostrunner where each area with enemies was thoroughly thought out and you would focus on finding an optimal path and just have to perfect your movements/attacks. This one is more of a big metroidvania map with enemies placed randomly. The soundtrack and world building is great. I'm sure the story is amazing considering all the positive reviews. However, the world traversal can get frustrating at times and the combat just feels tedious with a trial and error approach to me. I definitely think there's a great game in here somewhere but the level design and enemies just suck of a lot of the fun out of it for me. Again, give the demo a shot. If you enjoy the combat/platforming, I'm sure you'll really enjoy the game. But for me, it has too many flaws that unfortunately outweigh the positives for me to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're going to boldly proclaim that your game is a "TOTALLY NEW SUB-GENRE BRAH", then it needs to have literally nothing wrong with it. That's why everyone clowned on Death Stranding, because despite advertising itself as "the first strand type game" it had numerous design flaws. There are so many needlessly frustrating elements to this game's gameplay that it was honestly a struggle to motivate myself to keep playing.That being said, this game has an AMAZING story. The world, the characters, the presentation, the music, all 10/10, no notes. I kept going because I was genuinely invested in the story and wanted to see how it ended. Then, the ending came, and it sucked. It was a blue-balling, investment-robbing cop-out. All of the cutscenes in the game are way too short for no reason and don't have any time to breathe, but the ending cutscene is literally three seconds long with no dialogue before it boots you into the end credits. I was genuinely invested in what was going to happen, but it turned out to be the most inconclusive, unsatisfying ending I have witnessed in the last five years.This is an ok five-hour linear story stretched into an aggravating twenty-hour metroidvania for no reason. Pass this one up unless it's on sale like it was when I got it.
