_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, while I loved the setting, song, art and even the idea of the motorbike gimmick, handling the enemies, speed forward, and the motorbike orientation at the same time proved too difficult for me. Perhaps if there was an "auto-orient to ground" option somewhere, so people like me who can't handle this many things happening so far apart on screen might have a chance to enjoy the story could help, but unfortunately, at this point, I can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Laika: Aged Through Blood is visually interesting, mechanically satisfying but ultimately a let down with annoying scene changes that are too slow and often mean you are on top of danger before its visible or there will be some kind of effect happening around you (smoke, chunks of meat, explosions) that completely obscure your view during combat that make it impossible to tell if you are currently the right way up and going to land safely or are about to greet the floor with your face mid reload/parry reset.It's really a shame because a lot of the other things the game is doing are great but its enjoyment often gives way to frustration as you try to pixel perfect back-flip shoot three guys and then parry a fourth before landing the right way up on a postage stamp while being aggressively hounded by a team of snipers you need to take cover from.It has a world i would love to explore and a story that i want to know more about but the gameplay is so obnoxious it feels like a chore every time i jump back in for another go, maybe in time i will brute force my way to the end through sheer luck but as things stand it's not something i can fully commit my time to.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Laika is truly one of the games which I have played and can't tell whether it's good or bad. My feelings are mostly mixtured together. I can't help but mention that this game is pretty addictive, I was playing it for 7-8 hours for 3 days.But... let me also point out that this game (IMO) has a lot of drawbacks. Like, A LOT of them. I'm going to start with downsides. I'll list them and suggest my way of eliminating them:- Navigation through the map. Probably one of the heaviest downsides of the game. Most of the time, exploring the world, your eyes will be glued to the map, especially in the moments when you're trying to continue playing the main plot. The MOST frustrating experience you get once you take a lot of quests, you go for completing them, and not only you waste a lot of time just riding around, but also (most likely) you'll have to spend significant amount of time DETOURING to the fast travel point, so you can get back to the camp. I know, this is a game literally about riding a bike, but after some time it gets completely painful.: put more fast travel points around the map. Like... why not? Or at least make them openable for some amount of money or key item.- Respawning enemies. I remember reading someone's review and a person stated that most of the time you die because you flip off the bike. Respawning enemies are meant to make some "challenge" for you, but, like, as soon as you understand how to dodge them properly, they become annoying dolls all over the map. And you have to spend your precious time on them, otherwise you'll get killed.: not like it's a huge problem, but I see it more logical to remove enemies respawn. We know birds have a large army, but after Laika kills them, soldiers should take some time to deploy, right? Would've been much logical if they respawned only after you sleep in the camp.- The game is painfully linear. You only play how the game wants was intended to. Not that I'm too against of linear games, but why not add some choices that'll affect the main plot? SPOILERS AHEAD .: add some diversity, duh.- Side quests. Saved the best for last. WHY. THE. FUСK. DO. THEY. EXIST??? Look, I've been completing them for almost the whole game, hoping there'll be something good in the end. You waste your time riding in the wastelands, you come back to hand over requested item, and then you get fuсking 1 unit of useless material that you can get from the nearest to the camp lootbox. They're completely uninteresting and don't reward you. The only quests you really should complete are the remembering Laika's past and gathering the Wastelanders. That's it.: remove these fuсking side quests whatsoever. Or make some nice rewards for completing them.Speaking of advantages:- Can't help but mention the music. What a masterpiece at it's fullest. You know, sometimes not a single OST from AAA-games catches your attention and then you hear these OST from an indie game and immediately fell in love with them. I'm still listening to some soundtracks. My favorite is "Playing in the sun". Lovely.- Storytelling. Ah, storytelling. Full of grief, hopelessness, sadness, but also full of joy and anticipation of happiest future. Despite everything, storytelling is REALLY touching and deserves huge thumb up.- I loved the visuals. The world looks great, the surroundings look great, the animations after you kill bosses are just peak of perfection.- I still didn't decide whether it's good or bad, but the game is rather challenging to beat. Let it be an advantage. It requires some skill to complete this game - I liked that.As I said earlier, I can't give an overall rate for this game. IMO price for the game is a bit high. I loved this game. You may play it if you're ready for a challenge. Consider the risks yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: The soundtrack definitely sticks out among the crowd, a true work of passion just like the rest of the game. A tragic story that is hard not to love even if it pulls so hard on those heart strings. Not many games do you get the chance to grow attached to the characters but this one does it and you hate to see the looming darkness in the horizon. The game just works which is hard to say about most game releases anymore.There isn't a part of the game that I do not enjoy. The sound track fits the setting of the game rather perfectly. Difficulty is exactly where it should be so you don't just cruise through the game like its nothing. The story so far has been interesting and hope they continue it. All the bugs I ran into in the demo seem to have been fixed. Might not be the type of game for everyone but it was fun for me.Hardest part of the game is not making dumb mistakes that end up with you flipping your bike into the floor or a wall.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing. The characters, art, music, and story of this game are all so good.Flow of combat is extremely smooth, thanks to spectacular level design. I love so many of this games mechanics, like having to do a back flip to reload your weapon. I love reloading so much. Its so good.I absolutely recommend this game to whoever may be interested.I 100%ed the game in 26 hours, so you definitely get your moneys worth. Now go, wield an arsenal of weapons on your grief fueled coyote bike.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: When you launch the game, it gives you a warning that this game contains depictions of extreme violence, including against children, and boy does it not pull any punches. As you start the game you're tasked with locating your little daughter's best friend, who you find within the first 5 minutes of playing hanging from a tentpole, strangled in his own intestines, and mutilated beyond recognition. Make no mistake, the world these characters inhabit is incredibly cruel, unjust, hostile, and grim. Laika: Aged Through Blood is what the developers call a "motorvania"; a metroidvania style game where your main method of traversal is a motorcycle that you control in the same vein as the Trials games. It does add in the ability to shoot with a variety of different guns that you find across the world. The controls take some time to get used to, but most of the early game takes its time to teach you all of the basics. How to accelerate, how to tilt your bike, how to parry incoming projectiles, switch direction, shoot, reload, and more. It's also a metroidvania in the standard sense that as you upgrade your bike with more equipment, you gain access to more and more of the map. The game also allows you to upgrade your weapons so they allow you to fire more shots between each reload. On top of that there's also a cooking system where you can cook temporary buffs like increased resource amounts, wider magnetic range, etc.The art style of the game is beautiful and also utterly relentless when it comes to the depiction of a truly lawless, barren, hostile, post-apocalyptic world. No punches are pulled, no holds are barred. Several characters are missing various limbs or look grotesquely mutated from radiation poisoning, and when you shoot the enemy birds, they explode into a cloud of guts and viscera (which is also the primary currency of the game). The landscape is littered with enormous carcasses of formerly majestic creatures, and the rest is either a giant wasteland, a landfill, abandoned facilities, depleted mines, shipwrecks, or similar.The story is what I can best describe as depressive and . The world is ♥♥♥♥, Laika has lived a truly terrible life, afflicted with a curse that makes her unable to die, while she's seen multiple of her own children and her spouse die to illness or raids from marauders and mercenaries. Half of her friends have already whithered away, and she's doing everything she can to keep what remains of her little village alive against the oppressors. You sabotage their machinery, you kill their leadership, you destroy their monuments, but little does it matter, they just never stop coming. The music in the game is a selection of songs written specifically for this game by the developers' in-house musicians, and they really do set the appropriate tone for the setting: the soundtrack is sorrowful, melancholic, and gloomy, but also beautiful, with the acoustic guitar and wistful lyrics playing along as Laika races across the wasteland on her next adventure.The game is roughly 20 or so hours long, shorter if you skip most of the side-quests, and as an added bonus the savegame you create in the available demo also carries over into the main game, and the demo alone gives you almost 2 hours worth of gameplay on its own, so I suggest if you're on the fence about this game, check out the demo first, and continue playing if the gameplay and tone of the game is to your liking, because the tricky control scheme and bleak setting is going to be a hard sell for many.But it is without a doubt one of the best games I've played all year, and I whole-heartedly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: A somber, but beautiful game filled with loss and love. Its mechanics are absolutely stellar, and thought they can take a bit to get used to it makes navigating the world and combat feel spectacular. My only real complaints involve a few area specific gimmicks and a number of the boss fights, but they're brief enough to not be a bother. The game was genuinely just a wonderful experience, and even with a few moments of frustration, its story and character writing had me gripped enough that I was sobbing as the credits rolled. I can absolutely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: The idea of making a metroidvania twin-stick motorcycle game is incredible, and it's executed extremely well by Brainwash Gang. Riding the bike around the map, shooting enemies in slow motion, and doing backflips to reload never got old for me. Finding creative ways to deal with packs of enemies was a blast. You have situations where you'd miss a bullet on the enemy and end up having to find an unconventional way to clutch that, which was some of the most fun I had in this game.The story was incredible. I won't even attempt to summarize it here, but it made me cry several times. The art was also incredible, from the cut-scenes to the actual in-game art. Beautiful. Another one of my favorite parts of this game was the music. Every song fit so well for the game, and I was always excited to find another cassette.There were only a couple of things I didn't like about the game, but it feels very nitpicky. During some parts of the later stages of the game, you encounter groups of enemies that are very irritating to bypass, but that issue goes away pretty quick. I also wish there were more cassettes with a wider variety of music. Don't get me wrong, I loved the music; I just wish there was more of it.Overall, this game is a solid 9.5/10 for me. Laika: Aged Through Blood is one of my favorite indie games I've ever played and I highly recommend everyone reading this review go play it. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I played Laika for just a bit and it was sadly too much for me. This is a case where accessibility options are necessary, because I'm autistic and can suffer sensory overload. This is strange, because I beat plenty of very difficult games in the past such as Lies of P, Dark Souls 1, 2, and 3, or even Bloodborne. Sekiro was too much though. Laika hooked me in with its wonderful artstyle and compelling story, which was apparent from what little I played, but this game is overwhelming. I can't keep up with the difficult controls, having to worry about backflipping or frontflipping to recharge the deflect and reload my weapon. All the while dying in ONE HIT from any stray enemy bullet, and having to keep moving at a quick pace. It was sensory overload I don't think I quite experienced in a game before. This game, I'm sure, is something I would seriously love but the gameplay breaks my brain too much.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game, would recommend. Music, writing, and gameplay are all excellent. I could see some people complaining about the amount of backtracking or revisiting areas, but I personally loved the *vibe* of riding through an area, pulling off progressively cooler bike tricks and combat stunts. Speaking of vibes, I found the setting really engrossing- like Night in the Woods meets Mad Max meets those dirt bike flash games back from the late 2000s. Relative to other games, the checkpoint system means deaths are pretty low stakes- which lets the game really push the limits on difficulty without becoming frustrating.I would recommend m+kb for controls, felt much better than using a controller. Once I got the hang of it, I found it a joy just to move around in this game. Which was a great way to offset the story beats that are in equal part engrossing and often depressing.I played through the latter half of the game on Steam Deck (with m+kb plugged in) and had no major performance issues after some minor tweaks. I did get major slowdown initially, but disabling vsync in-game and in the Steam Deck settings fixed it (without introducing any noticeable screen tearing).One note for the devs (in they event they read this) - it'd be nice if the cursor had an additional arrow that indicates which way you're facing. Something like a semi transparent wedge that flips to the left/right side of the cursor, matching Laika's heading. Its easy to get turned around when changing direction midair, and looking at Laika can be misleading since you can aim behind you when driving. Without that visual feedback it can be hard to gauge how long I need to hold space to turn around when there's a lot going on. Having that cue that's always on top of everything (Laika can sometimes be obscured by particles, foreground elements, etc) would be a perfect solve with minimal impact on the game's look.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game, got a good 17 hours out of it, and enjoyed it most of the way through. It was quite challenging but it was always a fun time figuring out how to defeat large amounts of enemies or bosses. It can be called MotoX3M with guns but there's more than that to it, in general great game, I wouldn't recommend it to everyone but those that like this idea will love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fabulous game. Gorgeous, great soundtrack, extremely fun and rewarding mechanics, lovely deep story. I played through the entire game with a controller and that was enjoyable for me, though some may find it too difficult; mouse and keyboard seems significantly easier (you can move the reticule anywhere on the screen and shoot with less calculated accuracy) so I recommend that for anyone getting frustrated. I'm shocked this game is not more popular than it is. Truly a stunning piece of work, thank you to all those who put their time and effort into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best story driven game I have played ever. The genuine fear and attachment to some of these characters in unlike anything I've ever experienced before in a game, enough to push a grown man to tears. It's a fabulously done game and I sincerely hope, pray even, that this studio continues to work the magic they're making here because this is a masterpiece. Much love from the West, you guys, you did good here.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: The game evokes conflicting feelings.I'll start with the cons.1. Gameplay - an extremely controversial decision to tie everything into flash games about motorcycles. Either the main developer is a fan of these games, and therefore this option was imposed (it is not perceived as natural, no matter how you spin it for gun reloading), or this is an unsuccessful attempt to experiment. The difficulty in some places, relative to the average for the locations, is such that it is artificially inflated to hardcore for the sake of playing time. In particular, the birds at the last locator. The second turret was clearly staged on purpose, with the intention of making it more difficult. Well done, you made it more difficult. The moment where I cursed everything and used cheats, because this does not fit into any gates. What awaited me next was an incredibly stuffy crab boss, which even with cheats was depressing to get through.2. Artificially extended playing time. It can be seen that at some point, when the guys finally made a coherent and interesting game, the manager came and said “no, no, no, guys, of course you’re great, but we need gameplay time. I don’t care if it ruins the integrity, we have to hit to the price category and its requirements!" - and this despite the fact that in the very minimum passage there are 12 hours of game time. Man reported to senior management, well done. Got my salary. However, I think for everyone else involved it was not a pleasant experience, as is usually the case when interacting with managers. Stupid quests, when you need to do errands in the same location every other time, without being able to take several in one place - this is immediately a minus. This ruins everything because it literally pulls out the guts. But not for the birds, unfortunately, but for the player. If a manager or marketer is reading this, remember, buddy: let the game be more expensive and shorter, but be holistic and captivating until the very end. Not due to the fact that you personally showed beautiful statistics of potential sales and then kicked the player into grinding and timegates, but due to the atmosphere, characters, and plot that player empathize with.Now the pros1. The decision to replace people with anthropomorphic animals. Actually, a story about humans would not be interesting at all. An excellent solution with a specific target audience.2. The plot is excellent, it causes complete immersion.3. The characters are excellent, they evoke empathy and touch your heartstrings. Thank God, managers were not allowed here, apparently.4. Soundtrack - excellent, pleasant and thematic music, it immediately flies into your personal playlist.Questions1. Graphics. There is a feeling that the game was originally developed for one visual style, and then they suddenly chose another. This could be due to production costs or timing, or simply because the original artist was fired and another was hired. In general, the illustrations are excellent, but the difference from the first videos and the final ones is too great to simply ignore this fact.Total:Gameplay - 4/10Plot - 10/10Characters - 10/10Graphics - 10/10Soundtrack - 10/10Videos - 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: a very unique game, back flipping across the dunes while dome-ing birds with a sniper rifle backed by a stellar soundtrack and story more than makes up for sub par metroidvania world design and the lack of meaningful upgrades to the base traversal powers (the fact we have a grapple hook and cant use it to swing off terrain is tragic).
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun! The setting and music are very vibey and the story is great! But I HATE the crab boss. Screw that thing.In general Laika is pretty hard, but I wouldn't say unfair. The controls are unusual and the learning curve got me at the start. But once I got the hang of things - rushing through dilapidated buildings and shooting bird people felt so good! So yeah, you might get stuck in certain sections but when you preserver it really feels like you WENT through something and it's so rewarding!! Laika is a great game and easily gets my thumbs up... except the crab boss. Still have nothing but hate in my heart for the crab boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Really unique fun take on a metroidvania but with a motorbike guns and bullet time, do flips to reload, have some issues with it but half way or so through the game and mostly really enjoy it, emotional beautiful vocal songs and outstanding really detailed hand drawn visuals and animations and a semi interesting story which is a nice surprise for a metroidvania game.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game that gets brutal right off the bat.Gameplay is like the motorbike Trials games, with a metroidvania on top. It is a departure of the metroidvania genre so that could be either good or bad depending on your taste.I got lost quite a bit and I had to open the map often (but that may be just me).The only thing I didn't like is the fact that the last mission took a while to trigger for me. You have to wait for an event and I had nothing to do as I had done the side missions before.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, but a hard piece. This game kicks you in the guts and you ask for more.After Playing... fighting throught. My opinion stands. This is a tough as nails game, but far from unbeatable. It is an expierence. A Journey. And now after I finished the storyline, biting my fist from many many many frustrating deaths, which I rarely felt were the games fault, but my own for being a dumbass, I feel that emptiness that I always feel, when a good story comes to an end. I love it for what it is, but hate it for the heartbreak it gave me.I kinda hope, Laika's daughter gets a sequell, that is, if they keep the formula and mood. PS: I think those blackjack dealers are cheating ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: The wonderful soundtrack, world and narrative brought me in by the hand. I didn't have the heart to let go.my one gripe would be that at times it wasn't clear to me at the time that the game was trying to get me to use a specific mechanic during a couple segments, and as far as I'm aware [for some bosses] there isn't a checkpoint system for the more tedious bosses. The latter complaint should be more-so a difficulty option if it isn't already. It isn't terribly long. I went for most if not all of the objectives that you could and that clocked in about 20+ hours. Just know that some events can't be completed until after certain points in the main plot.I love this game man, and I wish more people knew about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: I completed this game a few months ago and it has stuck with me well after finishing the game, so much so that I have returned to leave this review. The music is simply amazing. I have listened to it many times after finishing the game. The story is beautifully tragic, the art and the cut scenes really enchanted me. I wish I could play this game over and experience it for the first time again.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Laika: Aged Through Blood was an amazing experience, from beginning to end, from the animations, to the combat mechanics, and especially the awesome music, there is little to complain about the game.Some things that I find off where the boss battles, where some were challenging and fun, other were somewhat frustrating, and some feel too easy from the point where you find them. There were some minor bugs, like one where while maintaining the trigger of the gun and interacting with an NPC caused the character to shoot said NPC and being stuck in a non-existent dialogue, were I had to exit to the main menu and play again, but other than that, I didn’t found anything game breaking.All in all, I think is an excellent game and I recommend anyone to try the demo and from there purchase the game if you like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Good music does not mean good music for a game, gameplay felt more enjoyable using the OST of Mad Max ( original one ). And in general this is a good description of the game: Tries to be more complex than it should be. Gameplay is fun when paccing is fast, but they force you to go back and fordward sometimes in slow and tedious gameplay in some bad designed levels and puzzles. A least it tries to do different things and at times it is really enjoyable and rewarding. There is a lot of possitve feedback and I am going to make a ¨I do not recommend the game ¨ just to showcase the problems I think the game has, but it can be great for the right personPS: Probably better on Pad ( With auto aim ) because on Keyboard &  Mouse it felt  weird
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm writing this review because for the first few hours, this game was comfortably on track to being one of my favorites ever. Right up there with Hollow Knight and Outer Wilds. But, disappointingly, it became a game I'm just never gonna play again because I can't be bothered to care and that sucks.Music and animation are easily the best part of the game, no notes there, but you might be better off just getting the ost and looking up the cutscenes.Game is Trials but with a gun, which is neat for a few hours but between the lack of comfortably accessible quick travel and the excessive bumps on the road, it becomes dreadful to have to go through the same areas over and over again because you just happened to get a new quest at that moment. This is made slightly better by you finally getting a movement upgrade way at the end because the game finally got bored of itself and needed to wrap everything up asap.Story is the biggest victim of this wherein the game has a phenomenal opening that quickly establishes a strong sense of "this world sucks and everyone is trying their best" and there's a tense undertone of clinging to hope even in hopeless situations to devolving into basic vanillafare edgelord junk in the second half that amounted to nothing but emotionally disengaging bitterness. It's like the writers weren't confident enough in how unsettling and hostile their setting and story already were and decided they needed to overcompensate by making it cartoonishly juvenile in its "Look, look! It's so messed up, right!!?"Story spoilers: Game's so edgy that, despite an absence of magical forces in general, there IS a spooky curse about the really scary subject of... menstruation... Yeah, we got magical periods at play, with every stupid beat that goes along with it right down to becoming expendable once your period magic is up and the only contribution you have left is to sacrifice yourself because you're basically useless now! No real reason for it, it's just messed up.Anyway, I really wanted to recommend this game because holy crap that opening was one of the strongest I've ever seen in a game, but it just really drags. It starts out like Mad Max: Fury Road but then wants to become Chinatown, except without actually understanding Chinatown beyond "haha it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥"
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty unique spin on the metroidvania genre. Unfortunately, it's plagued by some of the worst boss fights I've had the misfortune of experiencing. The bird pope was especially bad, but the crab made me outright quit the game. I don't care for the furry character designs; they could have been human and it wouldn't have changed the story. I didn't really care for the story either. It's gritty and gory, which I like, but there's no substance to it. Even if the ending is good, I'll never see it as the game never gave me a reason to stick around that for that long. The music was nice, but there's very little variety. I spent so much time listening to the same "sad girl" tracks on repeat that at some point, I had to put on a podcast to replace the music to keep me from losing my mind. I should have quit this game 2 hours in. I suffered through it for 10 hours. I wanted to finish it, but I'm done. The unskippable 9-minute cutscene of a boat slowly going from right to left was... yeah. I have no words. What were they thinking? This game is soft torture. It also doesn't run at 60 fps on the Steam deck; it barely reaches 45.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it. There isn't much replayability, but I'm glad I bought and played through. Beautiful game with a good, if sad and bittersweet story. Gameplay is somewhat hard in places, but well balanced.It took me about 20h, but I grinded a lot to unlock all the upgrades, and tried too long to get to places meant for later in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is outstandingThe visuals are gorgeousBest game sound track I've ever heardThe story and world is so captivating and gritty. Everyone is suffering but you can't help but get extremely attached to everyone and their relationships when you know nothing's ever going right.Controls and game play are fun and simple, yet You can master elements to make yourself bad-ass.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Its a great game! The story is great, the art is great, the music is great; all of it really!My only complaint is that there are a few bugs further into the game, some you probably wont encounter but there's a couple that stand outfor example as of the time of me writing this I got soft locked from progressing in the main story because a dialogue event wont trigger no matter what I do. I looked up the quests full details and my best guess is that I handed in a side quest to a character that's supposed to give me some sort of hint; I'm not sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful soundtrack and story combined with responsive and innovative gameplay. The game manages mature storytelling with compelling characters and a heartbreaking trama that at times brought tears to my eyes, but other times brought a warm smile to my face. Combine all this with a beautiful soundtrack by Beícoli, and you get the near-perfect narrative that this game has.My only complain is that the final stages of the game/story felt a bit rushed, and could have used a bit more time to let the situation sink into the player.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: Laika features a grim dark storyline with likeable characters. The grandmother-mother-daughter relationship was an endearing narrative which both fed into the overall dark narrative and contrasting it.After learning the controls, the game had a lot of cool moments driving and shooting with the bike. The metroidvania aspect is present, but rather slim.The athmosphere is great, as is the fitting soundtrack. Bonus points that the singer Beícoliappears in the game itself with a small but important story arc.The game is a raw diamond with some edges, but for me personally it is one of the best games I played in recent years, thanks to the fabulous combination of gameplay, naration, characters and soundtrack. It all comes together to provide a memorable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Laika: Aged Through Blood

_childDocuments_.review: A unique spin on a metroidvania by giving it the mechanic of the Trials games and also a gun. The handling of the bike and the shooting feels very solid, and it's very satisfying to pull off some of the maneuvers that you're able to when facing down large groups of enemies, blocking shots by angling your bike correctly, parrying shots to send enemies' bullets right back at them, while also firing off a few rounds yourself.All of this while given a beautiful art style and accompanied by a fantastic soundtrack that adds to the melancholic feeling of the rather grim world that you inhabit, fighting against a genocidal regime to protect your people and your daughter. Riding through the wastes and hopping over gaps while shooting birds to the soothing yet sorrowful acoustic guitar and vocals is quite nice.The story is quite good, but it is brought down by some issues, most notably the third act and the ending feeling rushed,.No spoilers but the final boss is quite a letdown and very anti-climactic, on top of being easily the least challenging boss in the game. However, the journey to get there is good, albeit a little bit melodramatic at times. And with some dialogue feeling a bit unnatural (though again, this is most notable during the final act).Overall, I'd say it's a game worth your time. I got about 20 hours trying to get every weapon/bag unlock and 100% it and I feel like most of it was well spent. The demo is pretty robust, letting you fight the first 2 bosses, so you can get a pretty good idea of whether or not you'll enjoy the gameplay loop or if the story grabs you. So give it a try if you're at all concerned before buying.

_childDocuments_.review: Laika is quite barebones beyond its main gameplay gimmick of being a metroidvania/excitebike hybrid. The artsy look of the game is neat, but it actually hampers the gameplay in many places. It's often hard to tell what's in the background and what you can ride your bike on. Foreground objects are placed in areas along with enemies, and this causes the player's bike and enemy projectiles to be obscured. Combine this with the fact the screen is often flooded with gore from enemies being shot to death, and that this gore gravitates towards the player and turns the entire player model red, and you have a situation where it's really hard to tell what's going on in a hectic situation, which can be frustrating when you die instantly from any damage. I have had many, many combat encounters play out where I successfully kill all enemies, but land on my head and eat dirt because my player model was covered in gore and the camera was too zoomed out to tell at a glance what direction my bike was facing.The game's difficulty curve is nonexistent. There's only one real hurdle, and that's the controls. You will die a lot trying to get them down, but once you do, they feel really nice and it's satisfying to traverse the landscape while fighting birds. The issue is that after this initial hurdle, there's no big difficulty spikes. Outside of bossfights, there are only four enemies, and three of them are stationary and shoot at the player. One of them only shoots in one direction and is shielded from attacks from one side, and one of them fires homing projectiles that are very slow and can be shot down. The only enemy that's really different is one that jumps out of a box and throws knives everywhere before hiding again. No enemies in the game are mobile, aside from bosses, and bosses move in very specific, very simple ways in their battle arenas. Half the bossfights are more platforming challenges than actual fights, and they tend to be somewhat long and lack checkpoints, which combined with all the other caveats I mentioned about the combat, makes them somewhat frustrating. I would say only 40% of my deaths in Laika felt fair.The main story has been praised for being really emotional and deep, but it's not at all. It's very simple and predictable, which isn't bad in and of itself. The relationship between Laika and her daughter Puppy is sweet, but it's so obvious that the game is trying to get you to connect with them so that Laika's death feels impactful when they inevitably kill her off. You may consider this a spoiler, but it's so obvious that one of these characters was going to die that I knew it the instant that Laika and Puppy spoke more than a couple lines to each other.Aside from the main story, there's a bunch of side quests that aren't deep in the slightest. They all boil down to finding some object for someone and then getting a few lines of dialogue and a small amount of extremely common crafting materials in return.The art of the game looks great. The environments look great. The character designs are very neat, but most of them aren't really used for much, and most characters have around three lines of dialogue a piece. The great art style, and the fact that the gameplay is very barebones in comparison, leads me to believe that most of the four years spent on developing this game was spent on hand-drawing all the environments and characters in the game, and I ultimately don't think this trade-off was worth it, in my opinion. I personally tend to play very mechanically deep and graphically simple games, so I might be biased here.Ultimately, I think you'll get just as much out of this game watching someone play it on Youtube or Twitch as you will playing it yourself. It leaves a very good first impression, but once the novelty of the art style wears off and you get past the initial difficulty hurdle, the game feels very mediocre.

_childDocuments_.review: "Laika Aged Through Blood" is not just a game—it's an expedition through loss, strife, and the thirst for redemption. It's a narrative that demands attention and a gameplay experience that urges mastery. For those ready to face its challenges, this game promises not only hours of engaging fun but also an emotional odyssey that will echo long after you lay down the controller.As the screen illuminates with the dire backdrop of a world scarred by zeal and ruin, "Laika Aged Through Blood" begins its poignant tale. Upon initiating this journey, I was immediately gripped by a narrative so profound and characters so fleshed out that my engagement was not only with the gameplay mechanics but also with the heart-wrenching plot that unfolded. What's remarkable is how the game amalgamates classic side-scrolling action reminiscent of Sonic with the gritty, mature themes of a post-apocalyptic setting. The developers have done a masterful job of crafting moments of intense action that are both fun and accessible, painting strokes of nostalgic gaming alongside innovative design—an absolute marvel called "motorvania."Amid the robust explosive gameplay and the graphic depictions that will jolt even the most desensitized gamer, there lies an artistic beauty in the desolation portrayed; a testament to the phenomenal art style and soul-stirring folk soundtrack by Beícoli. Each note and visual accentuates the thematic depth, lending gravitas to Laika's journey.The game's representation of violence is deliberate, impactful, but never frivolous. It reminds players that each burst of action serves the story, not just the thrill. And yes, while the disclaimer scenes caution the intensity of the content, the developers use these sparingly, respecting the narrative's serious tone and the player's sensitivity to such themes.In-game, my bond with Laika grew beyond the character on screen. The bike became an extension of her identity (and mine), and mastering its mechanics became synonymous with surviving and understanding this brutal world. The balance between high-octane motorcycle chases and the meticulous exploration and upgrading that defines the Metroidvania genre was struck with an almost artisanal precision.

_childDocuments_.review: Laika is a motorbike riding mother that takes out facist bird soldiers with revolver and other firearms. All weapons that Laika uses are reloaded by doing a back flip. While this mechanic fits well to the Elastomania like gameplay it can get frustrating to be doing back flips all the time, especially before upgrading magazine size of your weapons. This game has plenty of small things that had me frustrating me with the experience, but their weight got smaller and smaller as I got to unlock better guns and traversal options.- World navigation * This part of the game is what's most important of metroidvania, yet the game won't get grade A as navigating the game world is not easy. What makes this hard is how map system works. Only way you can acquire parts of map is by finding a certain npc hanging in that area and then buying a copy of map from him, meaning you can't see what all areas you have visited or not as map don't update upon visiting areas. What game also misses is some kind of travel log similar to Zelda:BOTW Hero's path system, meaning you can only rely on your memory what parts of each area you have visited.- Part of sidequest and rewards for completion * As world navigation ain't the best, tracking the route for completing part of the side quests is also a hassle, as part of them objective is located in one area but in reality you have to access it from another area. * For vast majority of side quests the rewards for completion are laughably small amounts of resources. I wish there would have been some money rewards, cosmetic unlocks or food recipes also as a reward. * At least one side quest is mandatory to complete, but it's not marked as main quest .-  feels like wasted potentialI wish that  would have been available for expanding moving mechanics and toss away flying enemy corpses. Right now it only ended up being used couple of times in main quest line and tore down few statues, making it very useless otherwise.Despite my review focuses mostly on few nitpicks that game could have improved upon, Laika: Aged through blood is a good metroidvania game filled with great storytelling, soundtrack and visuals. While I 100% agree with game's deloper Brainwash gang that game doesn't need dlc/ expansion, I partly wish we see a sequel for this great and grim experience on the future.Unless Elastomania like gameplay, extensive violence and/ or themes around leadership pressured pregnancy program, violence towards animals depicted as child, suicide and innuendo of rape are too hard for you, Laika: Aged through blood is great game I highly recommend to experience.

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to sum up this game I would call it Hotline Miami with furries on motorbikes. It's just as fantastic, with the same unique gameplay and the same fast-paced, one-hit-you-die style. The challenge mostly comes from its unique, creative mechanics, such as backflipping to reload your weapons.This is a BEAUTIFUL game. The thoughtful, melancholy music gives a sense of nostalgia and loss perfect for a post-apocalyptic, dystopian world like this one. All of the art is so well done, and the artist deserves MASSIVE kudos for making such beautiful levels that are also intuitive, that CAN'T have been easy to pull off. There's a ton of full animated cutscenes too, which is just so cool and so unnecessary that I can't help but appreciate that they were included.Perhaps the only criticism I could offer about this game is that some of the main quest felt a bit exposed and contrived, instead of a natural progression of the plot. Namely parts of the lighthouse arc. It's sad because the map was really clever, it just felt a bit tedious like a glorified fetch quest. Otherwise the plot is so good. This is a masterclass on storytelling. The worldbuilding is effortlessly weaved into dialogue, journal notes, and the story, giving me just enough information to fill in the blanks, while simultaneously never leaving me feeling lost or confused. And some of the emotional beats... Y'all I cried. God this is such a moving game.Cannot possibly recommend this game enough. I don't know if it's for everyone, the gameplay might be too frustrating for some people (notably enemies respawn when you die, so you really can't chip your way through a level and slowly progress. It basically all resets, and that can be incredibly frustrating). But if you like Hotline Miami I think this game will feel right at home to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Normally I don't review games until after I've finished them, but I'm making an exception here, cause I want to boost this game to as many people as I can while it's still fresh and new.This game invented a new emotion for me. Or a new genre. Or whatever you want to call it. I don't know what kind of desert magic from above Brainwash used to brew up this game's flow, but it WORKED. The amount of moments i've had where the game just clicks- -Jumping over a gap perfectly in sync with a small gap in the music, so I feel like i'm flying for a moment-Learning how to backflip just right so I can block a bullet and shoot back while landing safely-That AMAZING cinematic moment about 2 hours in. I can't even spoil it at all because it's soo cool-speeding along a deserted highway at 60 mph, playing in the sun. Yeah. You get it if you get it. Yes, the motor bike mechanic works. Yes, it feels polished. No, it is not bothersome. It is finely tuned and you will never find another game that tunes its platforming quite like this one. The world design from what I have seen so far is also extremely positive- certain areas and pathways remained blocked off at the start, as is typical for metroidvanias, but there is a VAST and WIDE amount of space you can still travel on your bike. It really feels like speeding uninterrupted through a massive wasteland.Now, I have a bad habit when it comes to video games of being strongly biased when it comes to their soundtrack. I have learned to put the gameplay first after much long thought, but LET ME TELL YOU. THIS GAME'S MUSIC IS SPECIAL! I don't even know how to begin. Beícoli did such an amazing job capturing the right mood that it feels otherworldly. A single acoustic guitar and a female voice will be your accompaniment through 90% of the game, and what else would you expect? You play as a lone woman travelling through the desert to save her people. It's her journey, and the music lets you know. And it is so, so, so beautiful, so many times over. Let me tell you, they took a big risk with the "cassette" music system- there's no way to skip as far as I know, and finding cassettes is supposed to be a big reward for exploration. If even a single song didn't live up to the standards it needed to meet for a player to be excited when it comes on or when they find a new one, it would be a problem.Needless to say, here it is not a problem. I am saving up all my viscera for that next cassette. I even skipped a map upgrade. 1200 soon baby, a few more birds.TL;DR this game is not a "cool concept". It's the real deal. If ANY of the "concepts" here look good to you, buy it as soon as you can, because all of them are realized. Peace.EDIT: you can skip cassettes after all. My point still stands.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's begin with the first thing people notice; Yes, the controls are different, you travel on a dirtbike, and have to keep your balance while also using it to shield yourself at times. Is it different? Yes. Is it a terrible idea? No.The game's art style is comic-style that is bright and sharp as a blade, but muted and has a feel that rolls with the theme of the story.After pushing through the frustration and anger, as all souls players will know, I can safely say I do not regret a single moment playing this game. The story is dark and maybe even a little hopeless, but it helps to focus your attention on why you choose to push on; is it for that character you like? Because it's your responsibility? Do it for Puppy?I loved how this game made me work for the story and how I often shed tears reading the dialogue and while the difficulty was frustrating it made the victories and rewards all the more sweeter.I would definitely recommend this game, or even the demo it has to see if it's for you. It'll be challenging, and difficult to adjust to, but if you push through, I think you'll be truly satisfied.

_childDocuments_.review: This game changed my life. I don't think I could emotionally handle a second play-through. Laika taught me things about myself, about motherhood, that I didn't think I could ever touch as a person, emotionally. I discovered that the incredible composer for this game, Beícoli, experienced both a miscarriage and the birth of a child while composing the game's soundtrack, and... even typing it nearly breaks me. I'll be listening to these songs for the next decade and humming them in my sleep. Best soundtrack of the year. Best writing of the year.The gameplay is fun enough, and there are some low points and high points, but the gameplay is not why this game is the greatest and most impactful game I've ever played. I understand why some people dislike it. If it doesn't resonate that way with you, it might feel... tedious. Or unfulfilling, or even mean. But for those that it does resonate with, you will not come out the other side of Laika the same.

_childDocuments_.review: The game opens its tutorial with a child that's been disemboweled and hanged by their intestines.Suffice to say; this is not a "everyone lives happily ever after" kind of story.Cue the tutorial: Accelerate with [L2]. You can turn, you can brake, there is no reverse.We only go forward, whichever direction that is.It is explained that you can reflect bullets with something of a parry system.Trick is you can only parry ONCE before you need to refresh it.How do you refresh it? Do a Front Flip.The tutorial then proceeds with you single-handedly taking on a military bunker with nothing but a dirtbike.Some way through you get back your character's two-shot revolver.Two shots is not a lot, especially when at least one room has 4+ enemies in it.How do you reload? Do a Back Flip.This game is mechanically designed to turn you into a flipping action movie badass. Getting shot at by half a dozen enemies and killing ALL OF THEM before you touch the ground again.That's the TUTORIAL.This game goes amazingly hard.Unskilled people may want to try an easier game, like Dark Souls 3.Soft people may want to try a less depressing game, like Demon Souls.My greatest enemy thus far is the seemingly random tailfires from my bike that instantly flip the back of my skull into the pavement. I can almost trigger them so frequently that I can climb vertical surfaces though, so there's that.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Summary: 9/10The controls are difficult to get accustomed to, but once I got into the flow of the game, I was rewarded with a challenging and satisfying gameplay experience. Death awaits around every bend, for both friend and foe.  Not a game for the faint of heart, as it does touch on some topics that some may find disturbing, but nonetheless this was a game that I enjoyed.  The Full Review:Laika: Aged Through Blood puts you in control of our titular heroine who explores the Wastelands mounted upon her steel horse.  The story begins with finding a friend of Laika's daughter having been brutally killed by the Birds, an opposing faction to Laika and her tribe hidden in the Wastelands.  You soon meet another ally who, on the brink of death himself, hands you your first weapon of the game, and thus sets in motion the story.  A story rife with death and bloodshed.  As you are constantly riding a motorcycle, you must navigate jumps and slopes while maintaining balance, all while attempting to shoot any Bird before they do the same to you.  You can block enemy shots with your bike, and even parry a bullet back at your foe, but if a single round connects with Laika, or you don't stick a landing, you're dead.  Fortunately, Laika's family has a "curse" that essentially makes her immortal, so suffering a fatal blow is not the end of your adventure and you revive at the last totem you interacted with. However, all enemies you've slain will respawn, so death is not without consequence. Adding to the challenge, you must back-flip to reload your gun and front-flip to recharge your parry ability.  The controls will take some getting used to, and will likely be a point of complaint for many players as it does feel counter-intuitive at first.  That said, mastering the controls and successfully maneuvering through a group of enemies all while spinning around on your motorcycle is oh-so-satisfying.  This was easily a highlight of playing the game for me.The art-style is also something I am fond of.  The overworld gives me an old-time-Flash-game kind of vibe, while still being beautifully detailed, and all the while is accompanied by perfectly atmospheric music.  And throughout the overworld you can find cassette tapes, allowing you to listen to these songs as you please during your ride through certain areas of the Wastelands.  Short animated cutscenes after boss fights or prominent story moments also added some nice flair to the experience.The main reason I am not giving this a 10 out of 10 is because I feel the story could have been deeper.  Don't get me wrong, I enjoyed the story, but learning more of Laika's family's "curse," why their tribe were forced from "Where All Was Lost," and more insight into the Birds' society and motivations for wanting to essentially wage war on the populace of the Wasteland, would have been interesting to see. You do get a healthy amount of world-building and backstory through the characters' various conversations and side quests, but I was still left wanting a little more after completing the story. Still a great game overall.  While I do think the dark tones and different control scheme might be a turn-off for some, it's these very things that made Laika: Aged Through Blood stand out to me.  I have much praise for the people who put their efforts into bringing this game to life, and would gladly welcome a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic title. I played the demo during one of the Steam Next Fest sessions, and was hooked after a surprisingly meaty demo. Definitely give the demo a shot as progress carries over and it's Trials bike gameplay with bullet-time combat in a grimdark setting. All the while playing as a bad@55 Wolf Mom. These thoughts are all scattered as I just finished the game and I am just dealing with the end of the journey.I have some gripes with the game. There were some bugs that can hinder progress in the game (which will probably get patched), for example, trying to rapidly go in and out of the "teleport" stations can cause the game to freeze sometimes. Steam Deck performance, where I played a majority of the game, is mostly fine save for a "water area". Also, bosses were interesting concepts, but I felt that most of them were just "survive as long as you can doing monotonous things". Visual clarity is sometimes an issue with picking up items for side quests or seeing your character (the icon on the crosshair helps at least). Lastly, progression, , and new weapons didn't feel as substantial or interesting. .Nonetheless, these issues are really minor compared to this game's many strengths. I am a sucker for Trials-style gameplay, and having that in a Metroidvania package and bullet time was an instant hook. The story is so dark, that I actually had to take breaks. So, the caution in the beginning is definitely good to include and be wary of certain things in the game. Combat is genuinely such a good time, enough that I just kept killing birds past needing to get their resources. Furthermore, it's also why I wasn't THAT bothered by the progression of the game. That's a very good sign and example of how crucial this foundation plays. The pacing of the story is somewhat fast if you just do the main story, with the ending feeling slightly rushed. However, the journey to that with doing all the side content really fleshes out the world, characters, and themes. Pairing an ultra-violent and ruthless "Western" nation against the poor village pups, coupled with themes of motherhood and coming-of-age make a uniquely, incredible female-centric story. I am really glad they decided to go with these because it is an important story and not something done too often, and while it's not the most subtle of stories, I do love the bits of environment storytelling and side quests pitted throughout the wastelands. I appreciate the dev team for going whole hog on the bloody and gorey "Happy Tree Friends-like" levels of violence. It matches the inherently dark and serious twists the story goes through, and I also appreciate the sparks of joy and hope - even though it's so few and far between. Going for 100% isn't particularly difficult as the last achievement I had to get was dying 1000 times, which I was lucky to be only 54 away when I rolled credits. Finally, the music is something I wouldn't normally listen to, but has now become part of my Spotify rotation. Beicoli absolutely nailed the the vibes and soothing, yet sombre vocals are approriate for the adventure. Hats off to them for such an impactful soundtrack because it 100% set the mood first whenever story beats happened and just going out and about.Overall, I am so happy that the Steam Next Fest allowed me to find this game, and I wish the devs continued success. These are the kind of games that inspire me to want to go into game dev because I see such a passionate project with some flaws but ultimately greater than the sum of its parts. Kudos! I am going to remember this journey for a long while.

_childDocuments_.review: Laika's gameplay is really unique, well designed and executed, although it takes some time to learn at the beginning. As a metroidvania it doesn't have too many traversal or other mechanics that interact with the map and therefore very few hidden locations, as upgrades usually just help you fight better. For optional content the game wants you to return to locations you've been to, usually for a fetch quest, which is really weak quest design but it is excuse to engage with the combat more so it's not that bad.The story starts out strong but gets worse as it progresses. Notably that the enemy bird empire is supposed to be evil but after they kill 2 people at the start of the game we never see them do anything bad again. In fact they don't do anything at all throughout the entire story (until the very end). Sure we see their aftermaths but in game the birds just stand around doing nothing while we go massacring all of them.The music is also absolutely beautiful. I listen to it on my phone now.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of emotional strength, even with the most powerful of stories that tackle a lot heart-aching topics, but I'll admit, this game did my emotions in. I was crying. The story is powerful in its expression, the music is heartfelt in its presence and the main character is just exceptional in her development as a whole. I'll remember this game for the year that's for sure.The game play does take some time to get used to and in my opinion can be an acquired taste. It is a metroidvania, but on a bike and traversing the terrain can be a bit of a chore sometimes, with a lot of times dying because of an incorrect landing on a bike, but once you get the hang of it, it becomes second nature in the controls and movement. The gunplay is where it really shines and is so, so fun! Bullet-time with guns and tricks make this for such a unique experience. But like the bike movement, the gun play takes time to get used to as well, especially combining the bike movement with combat. It takes some practice and trial and error, but is so worth it. There is a plethora of quests to be had that makes it lengthy as well and give a more in-depth about the story and environment. Overall, some tiny hiccups here and there with game play mechanics that can be a bit frustrating initially, but in my eyes and heart, it is an experience that must be, well experienced with an open heart to really feel the story being told.

_childDocuments_.review:
Laika: Aged Through Blood is a western-inspired motorvania set in a post-apocalyptic wasteland. It is the story about a tribe oppressed by occupant forces, and the personal story of a mother coyote warrior who descends on an endless path of vengeance to take back what her people lost.

Drive, jump and fight your way through the huge hand-drawn world on your trustworthy motorbike. Race through the wasteland and perform dangerous jumps, shoot enemies in slowmo and reload your gun by performing a backflip! Use skill-based power-ups and persist challenging battles against big bosses!

_childDocuments_.review: I have to admit: I don't know exactly why I enjoyed The Touryst so much. Maybe it's the gorgeous voxelized graphics, that strike a sweet spot between nostalgia and modern gloss. Maybe its charming retro feel, complete with naive dialogue that feels straight out of the 8-bit era or is it the arcade-shop where you can play arcade classics like F-Zero etc.? Matter of fact, I couldn't stop playing this little adventure until I'd beaten it to 100% so 4 Hours straight.Be warned that The Touryst comes with a few issues. It includes some very frustrating sections that feel like artificial difficulty, like the platforming rooms where you're prevented from rotating the camera. Also, it challenges you to complete 100% of the adventure, but pads it up with some minigames that feel "cheap" and not worth completing (Football / Soccer Game). However, it's hard not to forgive The Touryst's sins, when they come in such a neat little package. It also has some performance Issues and FPS dips here and there (Played on 144 FPS / V-SYNC ON).In terms of gameplay, "The Touryst" can be divided into two parts: an Adventure-Puzzle Platformer, and a Minigame collection. It urges you to explore the 8 islands, interacting with the locale and unlocking the secrets hidden away in the monuments. The game doesn't hold your hand "that much"; you'll lose yourself in the world with the amount of activity you can do on the islands. The highlight of the adventure has to be monuments, as they are a test of the mind. You might struggle with the camera... it can be a bit awkward with getting an ideal view while platforming especially when it comes to the glowing balls (You'll know what I mean once you play it).✔️ Voxelized Graphics (Love it but it depends on your personal taste)✔️ Soundtrack✔️ Puzzle's (If I can do it - you can do it as well)✔️ It feels "relaxing" to play and has a special charme to it ✔️ Dungeons✔️ Details (Coin Question Marks in Sand randomly for you to move over it in order to get the coins or DJ on the Beach playing different music depending on which Song you give him / select etc.)✔️ Optional Sidequests✔️❌ Too Short for its price-tag (this depends on your personal opinion if price is justified - got it for -50% off during Summer Sale 2022 and that's worth it for me)❌ Performance Issues (You see a few FPS Dips here and there which is not okay considering my specs (Specs down below)❌ Too Short for its price❌ It doesn't have much Settings in the Menu (not even Audio Settings?). I needed to use Windows Sound Mixer in order to lower the volume, like what?More Infos on the official Website:CPU: i9 9900k @3,60Ghz (STOCK)GPU: RTX 2080 Ti MSIRAM: DDR4 32 GB RAM @2667MHzOS: Win10Resolution: 1440p 32" 144hz Monitor @144 FPS

_childDocuments_.review: Digital Foundry is biased, I guess this could be called a great Xbox port, but it's not a "Superb Port" for PC.Because I like voxel graphics (3d pixels), this was an instant buy when I learned about it (just now). Normally, it should take 4-6 hours to complete the game, but for me, it took a total of 9 hours during 2 evenings.The first 2/3 of the game is excellent, fun, and intuitive. The last 1/3 of the game is confusing, random, and difficult. There are 8 small islands (overworlds), each with its monument puzzles (underworlds). It starts as a simple adventure game and ends with difficult-to-find boss battles. There are many mini-games (surfing, soccer penalties, 3 arcade games, quadcopter time trial, drum rhythm game), fetch quests, and collectibles.Reasons why it's a bad PC port:* menus and camera cannot be controlled with a mouse* volume levels cannot be changed* supports only 16:9 aspect ratio* supports odd resolutions (opens in 1024x576 window mode, no 1280x720 fullscreen mode)* game progress and graphic settings are both synced to the cloud (only game progress should, otherwise Steam Deck gets PC graphic settings and vice-versa)* some shadows (underneath building ledges) look like 1080p shadows, even at 4k resolution.

The game struck a perfect balance between the two for me.This is everything I want in my adventure games, I hope they not only make a sequel, but make it far bigger and grander.  Loved it!Money was pretty easy to come by which gates a lot of what you can do, I wish it had been tighter in that aspect.  It must be said that it is a very short game for the price though, get it on a deep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Naturally, this review comes from the 'Steam should have a neutral review' angle.The Touryst is a surface level fun little platformer with a few relatively simple puzzles thrown in. Until they aren't simple and require some very 'out of the box' thinking to solve. Generally progression is smooth but at times it feels as though the developers really didn't know how to make a cohesive answer to the puzzle and just left it as is. Additionally, there are a large number of segments that require your ability to use 3D platforming. Unfortunately, there is little thought into how this should be executed and some puzzles and movements feel almost like they're based on luck and not skill. This downfall is frustrating and confusing to a point. The whole game feels like a huge scope and a limited budget. As such, I commend the development team of throwing in so much content in such a limited way. You can tell scope creep really showed it's head here and the dev team dealt with it well.Overall I'd like to recommend the game, however, after finishing the story-line with approx 75% completion, I have 0% desire to return. The dev team deserves praise for what's on offer, unfortunately for me, it just isn't worth a revisit.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting game. I really like it, but prospective buyers should be aware of a particular quirk. The ramp up in difficulty reminds me a bit of Trine where to Platinum that game required me reviving gaming skills from an era long lost. It's crazy. I don't consider myself a great gamer, so hopefully most people will be able to get through it like I did. Just be prepared for difficulty to go from Very Easy to Very Hard with zero warning.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I liked the game. It's more kind of an adventure with tasks to fulfil, and lots of attention to detail. I mean, really, a lot of detail. At some point it is also a little bit jump&run, but exploration is kind of the main theme here. Go on vacation, and enjoy. The game is made for enjoyment, and it is rather nice to see games which actually bridge the entrylevel regarding gameplay skill.If you are looking for a platformer with more of an exploration theme, I recommend it. Don't go there if you can't appreciate details - like being able to dance on the dancefloor of the party, after setting all the equipment up.If you were looking to get this game at some point, I recommend getting it and enjoing it.You should play it with a controller and corresponding steam-input forced, and nothing will go wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not too far into yet but I'm liking it a lot. You get a lot of choices during the visual novel-like dialog segments and the characters are interesting, beautifully designed, and competently acted. Game got the aesthetic mostly right, love the art style but its 3D visuals leave some to be desired. Gameplay appears to be like that of the Swordcraft Story games, which is really cool.
_childDocuments_.name: MAGLAM LORD

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10: Worth it for visual novel/story and characters. Not so much for the combat/exploration. The visual novel/story aspect is quite enjoyable. The characters are typical anime stuff but done well. Having dialogue options to choose your own anime cliche response is a great aspect. It even gives you a little info on what character will like certain responses or if you're being "demonic", "cool" or "funny". Very much enjoyed this aspect of the game. The gameplay is a let down though. The field is too zoomed in for how quick you run around and considering you have a separate battle screen I'm not sure why they felt the need to zoom so far in (or make you move as quickly as you do). Being able to pull the camera back a bit further would be ideal. The hit boxes on the weapons feel way too small for trying to get the initiative going into battles. The battles themselves are simplistic which isn't terrible but it's stiff and doesn't flow well. There's a distinct lack of PC features though. I'm not a stickler for having every option under the sun but having 2 resolution options (720 and 1080) kinda sucks. More importantly though is the locked 30 fps. Not a problem for the visual novel aspect but it's very noticeable for field/battle movement; which as mentioned isn't too good already.
_childDocuments_.name: MAGLAM LORD

_childDocuments_.review: I'm redacting my whole original review because I thought it was too harsh. This game is fine, if a bit bland in gameplay. I'm just disappointed it isn't as good as Summon Night Swordcraft Story, which is a previous game attached to the studio most of Felistella's devs came from, Flight Plan. This game is very obviously inspired by that game series, and it's just not as good as that series. The game isn't bad, just not as good as the game that it's built to succeed the legacy of.BUT, there is a MAJOR problem with this game. The framerate is not only low, but incredibly unstable. I don't have a problem with 30 FPS in a slower paced game, but combat is actually decently speedy in this game, and if you do literally anything, the framepacing gives up and the game has a ton of microstutters that might as well add up to a macrostutter. It's like 200 grit on the eyes, even for 30 FPS games this is super jittery.
_childDocuments_.name: MAGLAM LORD

_childDocuments_.review: Here's a game with a battle system that basically takes the worst aspects of Tales and Star Ocean and runs with them: -Basic combos with only a small handful of skills (which aren't really made to chain together)-Low enemy variety with recolors out the wazoo-Attacks that come at you from off screen-Bosses that can't be staggered or combo'd at all-Non-existent level design that consists entirely of a bunch of square shaped areas connected together-Quests that take you to those same areas over and over again to farm enemies and materials, some of which take forever to drop the most basic thingsCombine all that with a story and cast that don't leave much an impression and you've got a game that you shouldn't give a second thought to playing.
_childDocuments_.name: MAGLAM LORD

_childDocuments_.review: A decent JRPG that gives you a resemblance of Summon Night: Swordcraft Story.Witty dialogue, pretty good VA, and character designs makes it a relaxing game with no doubt.Had a lot of chuckles while playing(or reading, you'd say) after a long day of work.My main gripe with the game, however, is its shallow, repetitive gameplay.Aside from maglam customization, there's nothing remarkable other than barebone skill system and hack-and-slash(which is exactly what you'd expect from this genre, but it could have been better).No progression carryover to your NG+ playthrough either, so there's little to no replayability unless you're a completionist.All in all, it was enjoyable. Consider this a dialogue-heavy RPG, and you get yourself a good treat. Other than that, there's not much to it, and I'd not recommend it if you value gameplay over dialogue and story.
_childDocuments_.name: MAGLAM LORD

_childDocuments_.review: Games like this make me wish there was a 'mixed' review option on Steam. Maglam Lord combines a handful of genres into one package, but I honestly wish it didn't. When the game is sticking to its visual novel elements, it’s pretty enjoyable.You can choose the gender of the Protagonist, choose your reactions and responses and build relationships with your party members. The game even offers you same-sex relationships, which boostered my enjoyment. The story is lighthearted and the characters are simple but still fun.Unfortunately this is only half of the game. The other half is a laughably bad action-RPG. The dungeon designs are dull and the combat is lackluster and poorly realised. The visual novel elements together with the story and characters really carried the game.
_childDocuments_.name: MAGLAM LORD

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game for when you want to turn off your brain and still be entertained. The 2D art is fantastic, and I'm really enjoying playing this big himbo demon lord and his interactions with the other characters. Although the battle system is kinda lacking, the focus isn't solely on it, so it's not too annoying, but it's a nice change of pace from it just being a visual novel. Still, the weapon customization and weapon triangle give it a bit of oomph, instead of just running into fights head first. I love it when games let me romance characters, and the dates being adorable really make me enjoy it. The only thing of note that I found really annoying was that in battle, there's this slow motion effect every time you hit an enemy, and at first I thought it was my PC having a stroke and dropping fps, but no, there was no fps drop. You get used to it after a while, but sometimes it can still be a bit jarring.So if you want a cute game that can make you chuckle, I'd recommend this game, but if you're looking for something battle focused and dislike visual novels, then I would steer away.

_childDocuments_.review: Like every review, the 2D part  of the game looks phenomenal. Visual novel aspects reminds me of Luminous Arc series. You get try to woo partners with a choice system. Art looks really good stylistically. Choice system lets you woo one character while not letting you woo the other.On the other hand, the 3D parts of the game probably need a lot of polish. Like watching a 3DCG anime, the 3D parts of it  make it stand out for the worse, comparing its 2D parts. Its like two teams mash together their respective project to created this game. Combo system is one dimensional. There is a single move-set for a type of weapon. They could have taken the parts Summon Night Story (GBA) combat system and that would have been better.  Every time your character hits an enemy, the action slowed the scene, which is very jarring. They should have probably put the resources into making this game 2D instead a mesh mash of 3D and 2D. This could have been Summon Night Story on the PC. I'm hoping they would take more time developing the battle system. i wouldn't recommend getting this game. _childDocuments_.review: A disappointing visual novel with barebones dungeon crawling.Most dialogue choices have no impact on the story; there are many possible love interests/partners but dating is extremely shallow and consists of picking a location your date may or may not like. Right before the final boss you pick your partner of choice, choose if it's a love interest or a good friend and get 1-2 extra lines after the ending.Dungeon crawling is just as bad: there are maybe eight enemy types and you see all of them in every dungeon, with different colour palettes. They even have the same weaknesses every time, which defeats the purpose of experimenting. Dungeons aren't random and every quest has the same map layout and boss rooms.I received this game as part of a bundle and I'm happy with what I got, but I wouldn't consider buying this even discounted. It's a shame because the soundtrack is catchy, the art gorgeous and the weapon customisation pretty enjoyable.

The combat is simple being toted as a spiritual successor to the sword craft summon knight games. This has that saturday morning anime feel. its a cozy game its easy to start and easy to finish. you can find "endangered species" characters that add quests or give you new gear options which is mostly just a hide and seek vibe, be prepared to check every nook and cranny of stages looking for them. or find a guide. Also the "dating" mechanic was adorable super cute I loved taking the different characters on dates it was simple not sexual and just cute. dating each of the characters gives you a chance to learn more about them getting more info on them and just really sinking you further into the immersion which I loved alot. reminded me alot of the fire emblem bonding mechanics. anyway if you like compile hearts games you will probably like this one. some people could call this a otome Kusoge.
