_childDocuments_.review: This low budget remake is my least favourite Yakuza game to date. The original was made between Yakuza 5 and 0 so you'd think it'd have some of the best gameplay in the series. Unfortunately, at least in this low budget unreal engine demake, the combat is Yakuza 3 levels of tedious. Every enemy has way too much health and all your styles feel useless and require no skill to use. It even feels like enemy AI has degraded to the point where they'll just stand around and watch you slowly tickle them to death one by one. Group encounters used to involve using throws and positioning to prevent getting ganged up on, even by small groups. Ishin enemies also stay grounded way too long? It's a weird thing to complain about but it makes the game feel cheap when you're doing your sword attacks on an enemy on the ground, not even hitting them, and they still take the damage. The gameplay feels like a cheap Yakuza unity engine rip-off made by one dude in his basement is what I'm trying to say. I could nitpick the gameplay all day long I hate it so much and I haven't even begun to talk about the horrible weapon upgrade system, free influencer DLC or the P2W garbage that you'd expect from an EA game. Even the story, the one element that you'd expect to be consistent is ruined by pandering to new fans of the series. Being a fanservice spinoff, most of the characters in the game are based off of pre-existing characters from the main series. However, for this remake they've changed who some of those characters are. Yakuza 1-5 characters are swapped out with yakuza 0, 6 and 7 characters but the roles that they play in the story are the exact same and they often make no sense. The graphics are a minor downgrade I'd say. Character models and environments are just a bit off, I also had some issues with LOD being really low upon entering a new zone but maybe that's just my computer. The worst offenders are the lighting and the blood effects. These look awful, the lighting is especially bad with large fires and candles. If you're looking for more Yakuza and you have played 1-6 just play those. Or Judgement I'm sure that's leagues better than this low quality remake. Worst part about this remake is that we'll never get the original game in english now. Most disapointing game I've played in years.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, Like a Dragon: Ishin! Kiwami!... lets start first with the gameplay.Ishin Kiwami's (I'm calling the game this since that's what it is in japan.) Combat is very similar to Yakuza 0 and Kiwami 1's combat, using the same style switching combat as those games, however in Ishin's case, it uses the different weapons that you have in your arsenal, those styles being Brawler, Swordsman, Gunman, and Wild Dancer.Brawler is very self explanatory, you use hand to hand combat to defeat your enemies, this style is mainly used as a defense style, as it has a parry mechanic that gives you invincibility for a short time, and you can equip whatever special weapon you have equipped at that moment, its also a very fast style, however the damage do you deal with said damage is not as great, which as I said earlier makes it more of a defensive style than a offense style.In Swordsman, you use a sword (duh), and can dish out slash damage to any foes in your way, you also have the added benefit of being able to block bullets as well, it terms of speed however its a slow style, but makes up for it through charge attacks and the different heat actions you can do, but overall its a decent style.In Gunman, you use a pistol, shooting foes with bullets and special bullets that deal different types of damage. This is one of the more spammable styles, as you can just keep spamming the attack button and sometimes the heavy attack button and pretty much kill anything as long as you keep your distance and they don't have armor.Wild Dancer is my personal favorite, using both the sword and the gun, you can make quick movements and do good crowd control, but with the lower damage, but the style has some of the more stronger (and cooler) heat actions due to them being heat actions that can target multiple at once, making it great for just normal brawling, and has good single target heat actions as well.Now I can't really talk about the combat without mentioning the Trooper Cards, as they went from being just a battle dungeon mechanic in the original game to being able to be used in any type of combat in this remake. Yes, these are broken, especially the very rare ones that represent characters from previous yakuza games, such as the Ichiban card and the Shinada card. However, as people have said, these are entirely optional, you can only use them in the battle dungeons and take them off when you get out of said battle dungeons, that's how I did my playthrough of the game even on Legend, but because of this "new" mechanic, bosses can also use special attacks from Trooper Cards, so it kinda feels forced at times, but again, it's your choice to equip them or not.Now to the story, the story of this game is good, taking place at the end of the Edo Period, you play as Sakamoto Ryoma (not kiryu) and explore the city of Kyo, and other stuff happens when you join the Shinsengumi and get closer to the one that killed Ryoma's father, the story is good but also remember that this isn't one to one to history, more of a original story based on said historical figures, and if you want to read more into them, then be my guest and look into Japanese history!City Exploration is the same as any other game in the franchise, explore, do a couple of minigames, do a couple of substories, and probably fight some ronin on the streets. However, this game also has a really infamous grind with crafting, eventually leading to doing battle dungeons the entire time.Of course this game is a remake, being remade in the Unreal Engine, this game is optimized very well on pc (after the patches that fixed the shader stutters) and with it the game looks pretty at times, this is also the studio's first time using Unreal Engine, and opting out of using the Dragon Engine for this remake. Unfortunate, but I feel like Unreal definitely makes this game setting feel more like that setting because of it.The music in this game is nothing but great, many tracks are remixes of songs from previous games including original songs, especially that final boss song. (Ishin Kiwami also added new remixes for 3 certain bosses, and also gave certain bosses their themes from previous games but not as cool as those remixes and sometimes just needing a why? looking at you Saigo and Katsura fight.)So overall, Ishin Kiwami is a decent Like a Dragon game, however I don't recommend this game at full price, wait for a sale that goes down to maybe 30 bucks, or play it through Game Pass, and don't even look at this game's awful DLC practices, being only able to be used once for a singular save file, and requiring a repurchase after said use. You also don't have to play this game for any canon reasons, as it doesn't really connect to any other Yakuza game in terms of the overall story, treat it as it's own thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Our journey of Yakuza games continues, only this time instead of jumping from Yakuza 5 to Yakuza 6 Song of Life, I decided to try out the remake of Ryu Ga Gotoku Ishin, also known as Like a Dragon Ishin!. Chronologically, this game was released in between Yakuza 5 and Yakuza 6, so it fits to play it before Yakuza 6.Like I said, this game is a remake of the 2014 Ryu Ga Gotoku Ishin. It's essentially the same game but with improved graphics, translated (original release was JP only) and some additional content.The story is based off the Bakumatsu era, the final days of the Shogunate period, and the turbulent period of Japan being mixed with western powers. What's interesting is that the character models that the game uses are the same as previous Yakuza games, but they don't have the same name. For example, Kazuma Kiryu is now Sakamoto Ryoma. I'll also mention that 95% if the characters in this game are based of the historical people that existed in real world. The events that happened in this game are based of the real events that happened during this violent period. I won't spoil much of the story, but this has to be one of the best written stories in Yakuza games. I liked the story so much that I got hooked on playing this, which is why I finished it a lot faster than previous games. So the story is well earned A grade.Gameplay is identical to other Yakuza games. You have adventure and combat mode, let's dig into combat mode first because it's the meat and potato of the game. The combat is surprisingly well made, with 4 different ways of fighting. So essentially, we are back to the Kiwami/Yakuza 0 system, which is my favorite combat system, as it adds so much variety to the game. I really liked the combat in this game, especially the crafting system that helps you improve your weapons further. The adventure mode is your typical sidequest hunting, wacky moments left and right, and of course, minigames. Minigames I would say are good, there's a lot of variety of them, from dancing, singing to gambling. There's also "sidestory" system. If you remember the Taxi sidestory in Y5, Hostess Club Management in Yakuza 0 or Majima's construction sidestory in Yakuza Kiwami 2, this is identical to that. Though the minigames and sidestories are great, I do have to say I still liked Kiwami 2 and 0 minigame better. I don't know, the management minigames in both of those games really hooked me. That isn't to say that minigames and sidestories don't deserve a praise in this game.Graphics are I believe done in Unreal Engine 4, and while sometimes they look a bit murky, I think the devs did an excellent job. The game looks visually beautiful.The music is interesting. It has some original music, but because they use character models from the previous games, some of the music is actually identical to... previous games. It's interesting to say the least.Throughout this experience, I would say, Like a dragon: Ishin! is so far, the second best Yakuza game ever made. Now keep in mind, I haven't played Song of Life and later games, yet, but so far, this game gets a well deserved second place. First place is still Yakuza 0.Overall great game, great remake, great story. A fan of Yakuza games should definitely check this game out. Fully recommend it. Now if you will excuse me, Song of Life is next on my list.

_childDocuments_.review: Stuttering issues have been fixed.Steam really needs to add a neutral/conditional rating for reviews.I can recommend this if you've played every other Yakuza and Judgement title available on Steam. As it stands, this game is absolutely not worth full price and there's better entries in the series available at a fraction of the cost, as well as the excellent Judgement games that are available for the same price. And that's not even bringing up how this game takes characters from all across the series and re-casts them as historical figures - having prior experience with the entire franchise is essential to enjoying Ishin to the fullest. You're either too deep in the RGG rabbit hole to pass this game up, or it's not worth playing yet.Okay, actual review - this game's an odd psuedo-remake of a 2014 PS3 game. Nearly everything remains intact save for some gameplay and story changes - some characters were swapped out for characters from Yakuza 0, 6 and 7, a famous scene was censored, the equipment upgrading system has been overhauled, and a magical card system that was previously restricted to a side mode was, rather controversially, made accessible in the main game. Said cards give stat bonuses, can be activated for buffs, and - crucially - let you fire ki blasts, chain lightning, levitating energy swords, and a full-on kamehameha.On one hand, this is a game set in late-1800s Japan that generally takes itself pretty seriously - not everyone wants to be able to summon a tiger, bear or volatile chicken during a boss fight. On the other hand, this is a series that has confirmed the existence of aliens, ghosts, deities and more in their universe, and regularly lets you punch them in the face. Meanwhile the series' superbosses can use space lasers, gigantification, teleportation, and pocket dimensions. Personally, I can stomach being able to deal anime damage in a game where my swords can be enchanted with fire, lightning and wind. They did give most of the important bosses some of these attacks, and while some are extremely powerful, they're all generously telegraphed and easily blockable. Getting hit by one is as avoidable as walking off a cliff, at most they just disrupt the pace of the fight.The game's story is great, but takes quite a while to ramp up. The final third of the game is where the story really kicks into high gear - that's not to say that the buildup to it is bad, but I found the side content to often be more engaging. Thankfully Ishin has some of the best side content in the series, and I wasn't left wanting for a good-quality distraction.Ishin's combat system is essentially a prototype version of what Yakuza 0/Kiwami 1 would use - 4 combat styles, each with their own uses, strengths and weaknesses. On a technical level they all feel good, but they lack the same punch, both figuratively and literally. The game really - and I mean REALLY - wants you to use a sword. Your barehanded melee damage pales in comparison to your sword damage, and while this can be compensated for with specific equipment setups, it's still linearly more effective to just build for sword damage. Punching doesn't set people on fire, swords can do that and more. Swords themselves are still fun to use, but aren't nearly as satisfying as simply punching something in other Yakuza games. Guns just... Exist. They have some cool special attacks but as a whole they're underwhelming. If I had to choose between being locked to a single fighting style from literally any other entry in the series, and the 4 styles this game gives you, I'd take the former in a heartbeat.Tl;dr play the other games first and wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of RGG you're gonna adore this game.Familiar faces recast in new interesting ways. A return to the old battle style from 0/Kiwami 1 with the added bonus of them perfecting the idea that each style should have its own theme. All the style themes come from the same composition, they're just different parts of the same track, so when you change styles it's a seamless transition from one part of the song to the next. Speaking of music, the old character themes remixed for this game are 10/10 oh my god.There's an in-game gacha for trooper cards, interesting ways to shake up combat but namely they're there to give you a smile seeing your favorite characters from the RGG series as a whole.The story is rock solid minus one strange scene near the ending that you'll just get no explanation for. It's honestly funny but nothing that compromises the story's narrative. It was the most fun I've had in a game in a long while, even if it did come with the occasional "Did you guys even play test this encounter?" gripe. The entire experience is so much fun to a longtime Yakuza fan, and the fanservice is exactly what I want from a spinoff like this. (As a side note for RGG completionists: this is the worst one to 100%. I did the math and you need a minimum of 6200 ryo. If you want to 100% this game, look up the chicken race strat.)

_childDocuments_.review: Ishin is a pretty solid entry into the I guess its now called "Like a Dragon" franchise now.TLDR the game is basically the entire cast of the various Yakuza games thrown into Feudal Japan. Its pretty fun sometimes recognizing familiar faces but with new personalities including our very own Kiryu...i mean Ryoma...I mean Saito...The world for once isn't Kamaraucho (though it might be where that plot of city ends up for all we know) but the enviroments still stack up pretty well. Most streets and side alleys feel just as lively and alive as they do in the busy city. Though you'll find a few paths that are always conspicuously empty save for maybe a combat encounter...almost like a hidden loading gate which brings me to probably my biggest problem with this game.its old. Like not very old but it is a PS4 era entry and it shows sometimes. I still can't tell if textures have been remastered for this port or not. I have a japanese copy i bought several years ago to play and tbh it seems mostly the same. Theres a few things here that wasn't in that version but most of it seems to be references and bonus material inspired by the other Yakuza titles.Now theres nothing inherently wrong with this in fact i'm glad they did it but what i am NOT happy about is the price point. Full price for a game thats several years old already? translating isn't cheap i'm sure but come on...Now theres another minor issue and thats the fact that the combat of the Yakuza franchise kind of feels goofy here in a setting where fights are frequently decided both historically and cinematically in 1 to 2 hits. The combat isn't bad but you will frequently confuse your razor sharp sword for a butter knife at times.The good parts of Yakuza are fortunately all still here. The story, the over the top violence of HEAT actions, the silly sidestories and the over the top characters are all still present and really carry the experience at times. The troop system they put in place is a interesting twist sure but i'm not a fan as i feel like it really clutters the hud.All in all Like a Dragon Ishin is good, its a fun idea and a fun game and i hope they do more outlandish ideas similar to it with the franchise going forward. It would be fun to see Kiryu and company in a variety of other scenerios and settings.But for this game don't pay the full price as its sort of a rip off.

_childDocuments_.review: The Yakuza game you play when you don't have a new one at the moment.For all intensive purposes, if you're here then you already like the yakuza series and dont know if this will be worth the time, being its own thing.When ishin first released, a little game known as Yakuza 0 was about to come out. so for reference point, anyone whose already played Y0 will notice most features of Ishin are the first iterations of what they found already. depending how deeply you take ishin, this will either make you feel right at home, or leave a lukewarm taste in your mouth as 0 is more or less all these gameplay refinements realized.Most notably the 4 different fighting stances you can use.You're given all 4 over the span of maybe 5 minutes without cutscenes. From what limited resources you have in tutorial land included, unless you just know to prioritize 1 of the 4, the first boss will clap your cheeks. Whereas Y0 gives you 3 over the span of an hour and lets you roam the main city and grind if you want inbetween. Tutorial land doesn't give you anything of note to do that'll keep you there longer than you need to be, as such, you'll rush to the first boss in order for the game to truly begin.Moreover, Ishin can easily be the most grindy game in the series. Even with 2 RPGs and a side game that wants to extend playtime, you will never feel like you're swimming in resources despite all your options. Unless you're playing ishin as a completionist and spending you're time making extensive use of ALL its features, you're going to be lacking in one way or another. it may be financially speaking, it may be statistically speaking, or even simply lacking good equipment.Having done 2 runs myself, once a blind casual run, and again with prior knowledge going out of my way to do even more than previously, it still feels like I could spend another 20 hours just trying to reach a variety of number thresholds before I feel like I can truly curb stomp whatever comes at me. There's simply too many features that revolve around doing repetitive tasks, or being situational and just so happen to do the right thing by accident. one of the biggest contenders for this is earning new moves. normal just upgrade yourself and be done with it, or level up a skill tree then you can learn the move if you find the trainer. in Ishin, you have to be the right level per style, find the master, fulfill the tutorial, then go through the skill tree to be able to unlock the move to actually be able to use it in a fight. leaving you in plenty of moments where you reach the threshold of a number of moves by the 7 hour mark but wont be able to use them till the 25-30 hour mark when you get the skill points to open it.one last example is "strikes of inspiration". depending on your stance you have to just know to setup the right situation to utilize a heat move, and eventually kiryu will have it trigger as it gives you one last QTE you need to land right in order for him to use the move, to then allow you the ability to unlock it, and then use the previously mentioned skill points on the skill tree just to check a box to then finally be able to start using them for real now.I've played ishin on multiple devices, once on xbox with just the base game and no DLC, and once on PC with all the DLC. So with that in mind, which should you get?Any of them. theres not any noteworthy difference between any version. HOWEVER, the DLC for this game is funky. the freebie DLCs' effectively remove a significant portion of the grind for early game and you can get through the story with them alone. that said, you can't even access them in game until you've already been given five across the ass and leave the tutorial land.Meanwhile the deluxe edition DLCs' are half assed. of all the DLC packs included in the deluxe edition, only the shinsengumi captains set is usable across multiple runs. everything else is 1 time use. and I don't mean 1 time use per run like in previous games. I mean 1 time use, period. meaning if you want to reuse any dlc that isn't already free. in particular the ability to use DLC characters like ichiban kasuga, you have to repurchase his pack every time you want to use him on a particular run. its genuinely upsetting.So really, just buy the base game, and snag the free dlc items you can get. you aren't missing anything worthwhile. just experiencing the game in its grindy glory.One last thing of note, Ishin probably has the worst karaoke minigame in the franchise based off what available on modern machines. its got nothing to do with the stylistic choices of feudal japan, but rather I've never found myself genuinely question whether or not my inputs are being read accurately before. the speed of the tracker fluctuates and jumps all over the screen between lines as opposed to a consistent one or two that it bounces back and forth as the notes appear. play any other games karaoke mode, then jump into Ishins' and you'll see what I mean. Its a sad day when a guy has to criticize a karaoke mode in yakuza.final verdict, 7/10TLDR: once the ball gets rolling, its great. However it take a while, and thats not for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally played this game using Google Translate after finishing Yakuza 0-7 but stopped at Chapter 3 due to translation issues. I'm so happy that I can finally enjoy this wonderful story and translation officially. Thank you so much for releasing this in the West and catering to your fans. This is easily one of my favorite Ryu Ga Gotoku games from a gameplay perspective but, I think, the story may be even better. The creative liberties taken with the historical fiction create a compelling narrative, memorable characters (even more-so thanks to nostalgia), and teach a lot about Japanese culture as well. As a fan of Rurouni Kenshin, this type of game has been a fantasy of mine since I was a child over 20 years ago and it delivers.I have played for 21 hours so far and I am only on Chapter 4 thanks to all of the side content this game has to offer. I imagine non-completionists may finish this story FAR faster than I will but I want to experience everything. I know that I should be trying to solve the murder mystery but I also have a farm to take care of, food to cook, and people to meet in town who need my help. My favorite aspect of these games are the little moments when you are interrupted by a side plot along the way to something else; these moments mirror life and immerse you in the world. I feel like I am a part of this world when I play; it is hard to put the controller down when you are busy being a real samurai who plays with a gamepad. I found myself in-game last night until 3:00 AM despite having work at 8:00 AM today. Every game made by this studio has that effect on me. When will other studios take inspiration from this series? These games continue to set the standard for what a "good" Action RPG is and I hope to see more Action RPGs from this studio in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR - Not perfect but if you love Yakuza then this game will make you happy. Just don't expect Lost Judgment levels of combat and fluidity, this is a glorified PS3 game.I took a lot of notes during my playthrough, mostly consisting of pros and cons. I will list them and go a little more into detail. Pros: • Combat feels and looks great. All of the animations feel like they had a lot of care put into to them. Each of the 4 styles are so different from each other and each have their strengths and weaknesses, can't say any felt bad to use, except maybe gunslinger which is really only good at long ranges and against non boss enemies. •Music is as usual top tier. Not much to say really except I felt this game had some of the best boss themes is the series. • Great selection of mini games. With this game being set in the late Edo period, there's a lot of opportunity for some unique mini games and I feel this game has a solid set of mini games that fit very well with the series and the time period it is set in.  • Trooper cards are actually pretty fun to use and I would argue almost necessary due to this game being pretty difficult at times. I like many others were worried before the game released if the cards would negatively affect the core game play, and I feel they don't. For probably about the first half of the game, trooper cards mainly consist of just buffs like heals or damage boosts but by around the late game you do get access to some of the more crazy cards. I always just looked at them as another move in my move set and not as a replacement for combat. • Generally the lighting is this game looks fantastic, especially during day time which is an area the Dragon Engine had trouble in. I did encounter some lighting bugs like flickering blood and unlit hair on Ryoma and some NPCS, these bugs were uncommon. • I just loved how colorful this game is. Again not much to say on this I just felt this game made amazing usage of colors throughout the whole game. • The story is good. Not the best the series has to offer but it's engaging. The game leads you to believe it is a very serious story but by the last few chapters it turns into a circus, not a bad circus but it gets pretty damn wacky by the end. Cons: • At launch the PC port was pretty bad, especially with the UE4 shader stuttering. This has since been fixed with Patch 1.03. Although I would still label this port as just serviceable. RGG has definitely made better ports than this.  • I would not under any circumstance attempt to 100% this game. I'd recommend just doing Main and sub stories, mini games, and at most maybe the battle dungeons. If you attempt to get 100% you will hate this game beyond belief, it is not worth it, don't do it, please. • I've always felt the bonds/friendships in this series are kinda boring and a waste of time, luckily most of the games don't have an egregious amount of them. This game has far far too many of them. This also makes trying to 100% a complete and udder chore. • The menus are kind of a pain to use if you're trying to do things fast. None of the menus go as fast you would like them to. With this game also being a RPG sort of, you spend a lot of time in menus, it's just something you have to get used to but you have to take it slow.  • You will be reading and skipping a lot of dialogue in this game and for some stupid reason you have to wait for every little animation to finish before you can skip. Some animations can take up to 6 seconds to finish so you just stare at people walking slowly or people getting up. Very annoying at times. • The camera is generally terrible. It's not as bad as some will lead you to believe but it sure does feel as if its working against you some times. • I only felt this a few times but some of the boss fights are pretty long and have no checkpoints, mix this with incredibly long unskippable qte's and you will get frustrated during certain boss fights when you die at the end and have to do all of that nonsense again. Like a Dragon Ishin is fun, would I say it qualifies as a remake? No, but for everyone now being able to play it for the first time in English, it's pretty tight.

_childDocuments_.review: You get to play a Yakuza game as a legendary samurai that triggered the biggest revolution in the Japanese history. One that led Japan, a country that has been isolated from the rest of the world for 250 years, into being a global superpower in only about half a century. Storywise, this isn't the strongest entry in the series, but the histocial flavour adds a very unique overall tone. The gameplay is just OK. They didn't bother refining the poorly aged aspects such as sprinting, camera, and the grinding curve. So it's best for you if you avoid this game if you don't have a strong stomach for aged games. Other than that this game is pretty fun. It's just as easy to have fun as any other RGG game.

_childDocuments_.review: The review will be split into two parts: The Actual Game and Misc.I've been wanting to get my hands on Ishin for a long time, but was unable due to the fact that there was no english localization. When I heard the news that a remake of Ishin was planned, including english localization, I was more than hyped.The Lore was great, a lot of plot twists and action sequences. I've experienced shock, tension, relief and I immensely enjoyed the game's lore. Acting on the characters was superb.The return to multiple styles is definetly a welcome change. Every style specializes in something else, Sword is for damage, Wild Dancer is for close ranged chip damage, Gunman is for long ranged chip damage, Brawler is defensive (kinda). I also love how the game rewards you with more experience points for things like using various styles, doing moves which are difficult to time and finishing an enemy with a heat action.Also to note is a drastic change in enemy behavior. You cannot combo enemies from behind anymore, they will turn around after 2 hits. Many say that this change is bad, but I think otherwise. My main complaint for Yakuza games in general is that they weren't very hard (I played on Hard). I didn't even utilize combos and had no issues beating most of the bosses. In Ishin however I had to reset 6 times, I actually felt challenged by the game (also played on Hard). Going for the back has been turned from "getting the boss healthbar down by 30%" to "getting a few unblockable hits in". Bosses also give you ample time to react when they break your combo, so you are not punished for going for the back. I like Ishin's combat a lot.This section will tackle side content. The yakuza usuals are here: gambling, karaoke, and most importantly: "Disco" makes it's long awaited return after Yakuza 0. I was happy to play it again. It also has your regular 2 longish side quests and a bunch of wacky and hilarious substories, along with, of course, an Amon fight at the end. -Slight graphical issues from time to time-Weapon smithing is, as of now, completely ridiculous with the prices that are set for certain weapons. -Ryoma sometimes has a very long recoil animation when knocked down-No special indicators for unblockable attacks, which would be welcome-The Penultimate Boss Fight was ass-The UI elements are very slow and janky and you need to wait a while before you can navigate the menus after entering themIt's time to move over to the negative part of the review. I absolutely HATE how they handled specific aspects of this game. I'll go over them quickly:This is absolutely unthinkable, especially for the most expensive RGG game to date. All difficulty levels should be avaliable from the get-go. I can understand things like cosmetic items, in-game boosts, but not a whole difficulty level, cmon now. Also bonus minus points to removing the tradition of unlocking the hardest difficulty by beating the game once.This means that if you redeem the DLC in one savefile and decide to start a fresh new game from the start, . It's a dirty practice, but most importantly, IT'S NOT MENTIONED ANYWHERE AT ALL.I honestly do not know the reason for this, since most if not all of the game is offline. This however makes it impossible to enjoy the game if for whatever reason you don't have internet access. Also if you lose internet connection after not saving, you will lose that progress.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed my time with this game. The story is your usual Ryu Ga Gotoku affair with twists and turns sometimes to the point its admittedly hard to follow this time around. The side content is plentiful and the setting is a refreshing departure, we don't see many games explore 1800s Japan. The voice work is as always top tier, zero possible complaints on that front. Yakuza (or I guess like a dragon now) games always set the bar for voice acting and nothing compares with just the incredible voiceover work. Ishin has no English dub for the people who care but why would you play a Yakuza game with a dub?My sole complain with this game is they didn't really do anything for the combat, the combat on this game just feels VERY dated after coming from games like Judgement, which is understandable since this game was made with their older engine years ago.Solid game, easily recommendable if you like Yakuza or find the setting interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: As a hardcore fan of RGG games, I've been waiting for a mere localization of Ishin but when I saw that they're going the extra mile to remake it on a newer engine I was filled joy but still a little hesitant.Hopefully what I feared the most didn't occur(game breaking bugs, visual glitches, performance issues, etc.)We got the same game with even more content and recent lovable characters added to it. Just let me say the soundtracks, minigames, bossfights, story(some parts) of ishin were just brilliant to say the least.However, RGG dropped the ball on some of the new design choices. The stylized aura is now just a simple flame, some small stuff in minigames, the design of some npc characters and the in-game lighting compared to dragon engine games are a bit disappointing.However, these are nothing compared to the stupidest idea of the RGG team since"rubber bullets": The freaking trooper cards and magician bosses. I know there were giant enemies and weird stuff before but bossfights are personal fights and the peak of every RGG game. To see your opponent get a laser beam out of his a$$ is just unacceptable. This sh#t belongs to Amon fights not story ones.Also the enemies take too many hits to die, making it a bit tiresome in most long battles. And f@ck the spear enemies and their hitboxes (you sometimes get hit even ehen you're behind them). Just hitboxes in general, are the worst they've ever been in this title.The ending is really weird, some of the substories are too short and simple and the in door lighting of character models look terrible (for the most part).But thanks to great mini games, soundtracks and iconic characters, I still enjoyed Ishin, which could've been 3 times better if not for the trooper magic BS.I wouldn't recommend this to a newcomer at all, just those who have played previous yakuza games and enjoyed them.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried giving this game a chance. I really did. Even after the 27 hours I spent on this damn game, I still had hope that something good came out of this so-called "remake," which is actually just an uninspired and rushed port to Unreal Engine 4.I'm going to list a bunch of issues that really brought this game down for me, and at this point, I really don't care if I'm nitpicking. I will include links for fixes for some of those issues throughout, and if you want a TL;DR in video form of most of those problems, here's a video by my friend, Samm O))):I tried the demo before early access came out, and I was greeted with tons and tons of stuttering. This is probably from shaders compiling in the background, which explains why it only happens for effects you see for the first time. Sure, it only happens on your first playthrough in most cases, but most players will end up playing once and leaving anyway, and that's a lazy excuse, but whatever, it's a month old demo and that may be fixed in the full game, right? (Wrong.)I went to the full game, and another problem: for some godforsaken reason, cutscenes were capped at 30 FPS. A choice probably borrowed from the console versions. Going from 120+ FPS to 30 in a few seconds was really jarring, and turns out they just forgot to uncap it. Later in the game, I got my Trooper Cards, and in all the battles after, I kept getting interrupted by them every single time, and the effects would also glitch out. I knew you could disable automatic activation, but no. Everytime I tried to, the menu would teleport to the bottom and not accept any inputs, no matter how much I wanted to change it. Now, I could've disabled Trooper Cards entirely, but I didn't for a reason I'll mention later. Another problem happened to me in the second half of the game, where the cutscenes would glitch out into flashing models and images. You can see examples of that in the video I posted at the start. It even happened for almost the whole duration of the cutscene after the final boss. Other issues include musical cues not being in sync with transitions, bad sound design (like in the cutscene after the final boss), NPC textures freaking out (even when they're not, they look really weird), or just any texture in general (steam in the bathhouse fight, textureless objects, weird faces and clothes, or just anything), some text that stayed untranslated, character animations not being in sync with the camera in cutscenes, inconsistent (or just plain bad) lighting, and a million other problems that either went unreported or I just haven't touched. Oh, god, where do I even begin?First of all, that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ugly sci-fi-futuristic font. Why!? Why would anyone choose that for a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ samurai game!? It's set in the 19th century, for god's sake. Thankfully this issue  and Second, those Trooper Cards designs. Most of the renders look like lazy photoshops. Hell, they are, because I can see leftover eraser marks in most. Some of the renders also go back to the PS2, and the faces from those outdated renders get plastered on newly rendered bodies. Not to mention that the cloned fire animations can have really ugly colors when combined. All of this comes together to create cards that look like they came from your usual low-budget Pay2Win tower-defense fantasy mobile game.Third, most of those shaders aren't doing the game any favors. The hair shader they use, most prominently. It looks like they have straws painted black and glued on. Sometimes, the game looks really good in cutscenes, but most of the time, it looks weird.Fourth, the lack of color, or just personality, in this remake. The original Ishin had a warm color filter, and it used its effects and color well. Now, it just looks like a straight Nintendo-hire-this-man port to Unreal Engine, which it is.Fifth, and this is the one about the audio, the stupid music changes. Spoilers for Ishin.Finally, the character recasts, which I'll be hiding for spoilers for both Ishin and Zero.The first thing me and my friends noticed is how sluggish and powerless this game makes you feel. Even after full upgrades and level 99, common enemies will take millennia to defeat. We're back to the only-one-healthbar ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ from 6, which makes your damage look super weak, which it is. See those Trooper Cards? They're the cause of all this. Every single upgrade in this game is useless, and every single element and attack in this game is nerfed so much to the point of feeling like molasses. Your damage in Brawler style, for example, is one pixel's worth, and that's being generous. You can fix that with either mods or cheating (which is completely justified here). Only cards upgrade your HP in a way that matters. The visual impact doesn't impact anything, and it feels like Ryoma's hands are feathers tickling the enemy until they die of boredom. Not only that, all bosses use the exact same annoying electricity effect, or the red blast. Another thing is that some enemies either don't do full combos like in the original game, or never ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stop, Bosses also never get knocked down. At all. They can escape your grab within 0.00443 seconds without fail, and some just can't be grabbed for the life of me. Skip this "remake" and play the original. They're asking 60 USD for a botched engine port of an actually good game. Do not give them money for this. It's an insult to the original, and a downgrade in every way.Thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon: Ishin is an action role-playing video game developed by Sega and released in Japan for PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, and PlayStation Vita in 2014. The game is part of the Yakuza series and is set in the historical era of the Bakumatsu period (between 1853 and 1868), a time of political turmoil and social change in Japan.The game follows the story of a former samurai named Sakamoto Ryoma, who is seeking revenge against the corrupt shogunate that killed his family. Along the way, he teams up with various other characters, each with their unique skills and abilities, to take down the powerful enemies that stand in his way.One of the most notable features of the game is its open-world setting, which allows players to explore the streets of Kyoto and engage in various side activities and mini-games. Players can take part in traditional Japanese pastimes like gambling, fishing, and even sword fighting competitions.The combat system in Like a Dragon: Ishin is also a major improvement over previous Yakuza games, with a new weapon-based system that emphasizes strategy and timing. Each weapon has a unique set of moves and combos, giving players plenty of options for taking down their opponents.The game's storyline is well-written and compelling, with a wide range of characters and subplots that keep players engaged from beginning to end. The game's graphics and sound design are also exceptional, with detailed character models and environments that capture the historical setting of the game.In conclusion, Like a Dragon: Ishin is an excellent addition to the Yakuza series that blends history, action, and open-world exploration to create a memorable gaming experience. Its engaging storyline, deep combat system, and breathtaking graphics make it a must-play for fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Ishin stands in a peculiar place, it is both a remake and a remaster at the same time. The added substories, combat balancing, quality of life upgrade and updated visuals are great but the game still feels like pre-Dragon Engine game. Ishin could have benefited a lot from Dragon Engine's fluidity and seamlessness. Nevertheless, Ishin is both an epic tale of Meiji Restoration and a fanservice for long time fans of RGG games.The game still feels great to play though, with the game even severely punishes you if you don't master the fighting styles to their strengths in any given situation. This alone makes Ishin one of the most challenging RGG game. But the added RPG mechanics with equipments, status effects, trooper card surprisingly make for variety of builds and can make for as much an enjoyable experience as without using those mechanics and make for an easier time if it's too difficult for certain players.The best thing about Ishin is how it tells its historical fiction. RGG takes huge loads of Bakumatsu history along with its historical people and spin them for a much more dramatic tale. One that is simultaneously about personal identities and bringing on a change of history. It is personal and grand at the same time along with an ensemble casts whose faces taken from mainline RGG games with diverse personalities and interests. You never really know who to trust or where the story will take you. Witnessing Ryoma's story of vengeance turn into a tale of discovering the truth and forging your own identity in a turbulent times is a remarkable experience. Kyo is also dense with atmosphere and things to do. A lot of substories found in Kyo are loosely based on historical people or historical events which make for a good learning opportunity, some of them also fleshes out certain organization that is just glanced over in the main story. There are however too much of friendship bonds with some of them take too long to progress but most of them still provide different scenarios and quite funny. The other standard substories are great tho, ranging from absurd, funny to genuinely sad. The biggest thing holding Ishin back is the grinding. Blacksmith level, styles level, materials for crafting required grinding and some of them are borderline too much. That said, the player is not forced to grind because the main story also gives you free weapons but playing in harder difficulties makes it harder to ignore the grind, especially how slow the leveling takes past level 70+. Still, Ishin is a great title. An experience that will be greatly enhanced if you are already familiar to Bakumatsu period, knowing when RGG goes off-script from the actual history to tell its own story is extraordinary. As a RGG game, it is one of top tier, even tho it could be better if it's a full remake. As a samurai game, it is still one of the best with believable pre-modern Japan atmosphere, full of details, enjoyable combat, and an engrossing story.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm starting to get really tired of how RGG Studio treats their older titles.This remake is nothing but an insult to all the fans of the series, whether you even realize it or not.It took nine years of fans outside of Japan asking for Ishin to be released worldwide, just for Sega and RGG to de-list the game from the Playstation Store and replace it with an inferior remake that no one asked for. The fact that they somehow managed to take a Japan-only Playstation exclusive and make it even less accessible than it already was is absolutely mind boggling. It  saddens me that now, the original game will most likely  be released worldwide and freed from Playstation exclusivity since the average player (understandably) has not played the original game, and does not know just how bad this remake actually is.Good :Two new karaoke songs (though only one of them is actually new, the other is just bakamitai for the fifth time)New substories (though they're pretty mediocre)Can change the haori of Ryoma and even all of the Shinsengumi captains whenever you want, no need to be in the post game.Mixed :Character recasts. They're just  for the most part, but I miss Baba as Todo, and I really don't like Shibusawa as Takechi. Han Joon-Gi is also a very unfitting recast for Yamazaki and it's very obvious that they lazily re-used the animations. Oryo is the only recast I think I actually liked more than the original.Bad :One substory was cutOpening movie was cutRhapsody of Chivalry was replaced with Town Bully from Yakuza 6 for some reason.The final cutscene involving a father and son in the present day looking at a statue of Ryoma and talking about him was cut from the game. It makes absolutely no sense why they would remove such an interesting and unique cutscene. Even Kenzan didn't have anything like that.Menus are strangely slow, takes like a full second after clicking something for it to appear. The menus were more responsive in the original Ishin.The combat is just worse than the original. Enemies have way more health since they rebalanced the game around the troop system rework and you can say goodbye to the wall bounding and back attacks signature of the original game (and many other older RGG games) because for some reason they thought giving every enemy hyperarmor was a good idea. Brawler style was also nerfed into the ground, practically making it a useless style. The damage is absurdly low and the parry buff does not last nearly as long as it did in the original. Bosses also love to immediately break out of grabs (or literally just can't be grabbed at all) unlike the original game.Who asked for the troop system rework? It feels like RGG was just desperate to find some new mechanic they could force into the core gameplay to have a reason to re-sell it to their Japanese fanbase. I find the argument that some people make that the troop cards are "optional" to be total BS and shows that they have no idea what playing the original game is like. Simply unequipping the cards yourself does nothing to make the game play like the original. The balance changes made to accommodate the troop system rework changed the combat for the worse as mentioned above. These magical abilities that bosses use now are not only unfitting thematically, they don't even add anything to the boss fights gameplay-wise. They were so lazily implemented that they just break the boss AI and don't act the way they would in the original game. Where they should often be performing long combos and follow-up attacks, they instead just favor using these lame magical attacks with long wind-ups and i-frames that really serve no purpose but to delay the fight. Tokugawa Yoshinobu will almost never actually do his follow-up attack after hitting Ryoma with a throwing knife, instead he'll just fire a giant laser beam at him like this is Dragon Ball and not a historical drama.The troop system rework also made grinding in general, but especially materials for Amon's sword (which isn't even as good as it was in the original; it no longer has the unique ability to create projectiles with every swing, now it just gives miniscule life leech that other weapons can have), even more tedious and take much longer. The best way to clear the last battle dungeon in the original Ishin with the troop cards takes about ten seconds to clear the whole room with four attack cards since they actually stack damage properly unlike the cards in the remake. Best way I could find to do it with the troop rework in Ishin Kiwami forced me to take them out one-by-one since the damage buffs didn't stack, making it a  slower process. Grinding was already a big issue in the original Ishin, and they somehow just made it even worse here.What the hell were they thinking with this atrocious blacksmith rework? Forging costs were increased so much it's actually insane. For example, the Bonbori Lantern used to cost 3 Ryo and 6000 Mon to forge, and now costs 116 Ryo 4600 Mon. That's an increase of over 30x the original price. WHY??? The reworked seal system is also some of the most asinine, RNG dependent ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of a game mechanic I have ever seen in my life. When enhancing weapons in the original Ishin, you would just sacrifice the weapon with the seal you want to use on another weapon and it would always work. There was even a small mini-game that determined how good the enhancement would be (which was not left to RNG at all). In Ishin Kiwami, the seals that come with gear you make are locked to that piece of gear, so you can't just dismantle it and use it on a different piece of equipment, you have to exploit a mechanic the game never informs you of, which is randomly getting an extra seal when making a piece of equipment. The best way to get the seals you want is to save your game, forge cheap weapons with an empty seal slot such as a bronze cannon over and over again until you get it with a random seal, reload your save and make that many cheap weapons minus one, then make the gear with the seal you want (which I had to refer to a spreadsheet some poor soul had to fill out to figure out what gear gave seals I needed for completion) and hope you get it. Then dismantle it to be able to use that seal on another weapon, then there's only a CHANCE that it will be added to the weapon when enhancing it with the seal. If it fails (which it has failed at a 2% chance of failing SEVERAL TIMES for me), reload your save, and then enhance with a completely different seal because the chance is pre-determined for some god forsaken reason, then try the seal you need again and MAYBE then it'll work. IN WHAT UNIVERSE IS THIS GOOD GAME DESIGN? I have 100% completion on both versions of Ishin, and the remake was FAR worse because of this.DLC is egregious. Nothing before launch said that the material pack DLCs were a ONE TIME USE. Not even once per save file. You can't even claim it again on a new save, you'd have to buy it again. Haori that were free in the original game are now locked behind DLC and the new difficulty is DLC.Why are there giant enemies like three times the height of Ryoma now? They're so strange and out of place.Amon is PATHETIC. In the original Ishin, Amon was one of the hardest fights in the series. Now he is the easiest. I did not even have to  to beat him. ON LEGEND DIFFICULTY.Censored QTE in the bath house fight with Saigo in chapter 2.Cutscenes are STILL locked at 30FPS.I absolutely dread to think about what they might do to Kenzan at this rate. It is one of their most important games because of the improvements and new mechanics that it brought to the franchise among other unique elements and they will likely throw that game away in favor of another terrible remake.TLDR: This is a vastly inferior, insulting version of the original Ishin that has nothing going for it apart from it actually being released outside of Japan.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the Like a Dragon / Yakuza series, short story:  buy.Though taking place in a different setting than most of the series and being set so far in the past, Ishin! has no problem at all feeding you a non-stop stream of varied content and things to do in a very busy, jam-packed fun open world.I will get the "meh stuff out of the way first.Combat:  The combat isn't necessarily bad, but feels dated and janky compared to many modern action games.  This is made worse by a frustrating AI that often times seems like it was programmed specifically to make you angry.  The various combat styles are not very well balanced, with the at least 2 of the 4 available not aging particularly well as the game moves forward.  All of this being said, I still would not call the combat anywhere near "bad" since it did keep me relatively engrossed for dozens of hours of gameplay.Story:  The story starts off very, very slow and takes quite a while to pick up steam.  You are given a metric ton of story background early on (thank goodness for the baked-in game glossary you can access at the touch of a button during dialogue) and it can be a lot to process and unpack.  I did not find myself really getting into the story until the final Act, but thankfully the myriad of side content did all the heavy lifting with keeping me entertained the whole time.Other than those two points, the rest of the game is really stellar.  I love the town layout, you are richly rewarded for exploring, chatting with locals and taking on mini games and I foun d myself spending entire hours-long gaming sessions simply goofing around with the optional content.Highly recommend, stellar game and glad we finally get to play a localized version in the US!

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon: Ishin! is a captivating spinoff from the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series that whisks players away to 1860s Japan. It ingeniously blends the series' signature traits with a historical samurai backdrop. In this game, you'll explore the vibrant town of Kyo, engage in thrilling real-time combat, and revel in an array of delightful mini-games.The story follows Ryoma, who finds himself caught in a maelstrom of political turmoil and imperial loyalist uprisings. The combat, although more intense and graphic, remains recognizable to fans of the series. Unique to Ishin is a captivating dungeon-crawling mini-game and the Trooper system, which brings an exciting layer to the gameplay.While still housing the series' trademark humor, the overall tone of the combat has grown more serious. Notably, Ishin introduces farming and cooking mini-games alongside the classic karaoke sessions and rhythmic challenges. The game strikes a clever balance by blending recognizable elements with the allure of history.Despite its higher price point compared to other Yakuza titles, "Like a Dragon: Ishin!" is a commendable experience that rewards players with a blend of the familiar and the novel. Whether you're a longtime fan or someone new to the series, the game's ambitious approach and skillful execution make it a journey well worth undertaking.

_childDocuments_.review: (This review is more for Like a Dragon fans. If you're new to Like a Dragon, go play Yakuza 0.)My favorite part of the Like a Dragon series is the plot and the characters. The endings are always explosive, and I always leave the game blown away. I did not get invested in this game's story. I think the biggest cause of this was the Like a Dragon characters cosplaying as people from 1800s Japan. The setting is really cool, and it's kind of funny watching Kiryu (now Ryoma) and crew navigate 1800s Japan. However, they went for a dead serious story instead of something more lighthearted, which made immersion impossible for me.In terms of substories, there are quite a few filler substories that I wish weren't there (go fetch me "X" 5 times, dull and boring), but aside from those substories are as funny as they always are. Nothing crazy.Gameplay stood up a bit better than the story thankfully . It's pretty standard brawler Like a Dragon gameplay (which I really like), but I was disappointed that all of the interfaces/graphics were the old PS3-era interfaces/graphics and not something more like this company's Dragon Engine. Why this game is not in the Dragon Engine is a mystery to me. 60$ is a high asking price for a remake if you're not putting considerable effort in (I got this 70% off), so keep that in mind if you're more graphically-focused.Also, maybe it's because I played on Legend, but this game did feel a little grindy. Burned through a few podcasts, which I never usually have to do for Like a Dragon games.Even my least favorite Like a Dragon game had a story that I loved, so I'm going have to give that title to this game now. It's my least favorite Like a Dragon game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a mediocre 2014 game with new, good and bad adjustments for 60 dollary doos. Yikes. (Wait for a sale.)Want a good Yakuza spin-off? Buy Lost Judgment.I love the Yakuza series, but LAD: Ishin is so painfully average. There was not a point where I cared about whatever was happening. So much talking and so many cutscenes, yet nothing of value is told.It's either: historical exposition, stating the obvious 3 times in a row or rarely actual interesting stuff (character conflict, motivations or banter).The protagonist is barely directly involved in the plot for most of the game. He either gets told what to do or tries to intervene too late.You have this "Avengers assemble" type of deal, with all these actors / characters from previous games together here and they barely interact or do anything.The plot twist is crystal clear from 2 hours in, so have fun chasing the obvious for 20 more hours. I must also note the main character, Sakamoto Ryoma, is so bland. He's this goody two shoes, always morally right. This might sound weird, since he's almost a copy of Kiryu Kazuma from Yakuza, but hear me out. Kiryu is a criminal, this is the card life dealt him. Constantly using violence and breaking the law, because he knows no better. He was raised this way and himself notes many times, isn't smart enough to find another path. You could say, he's a flawed character.Compared to Sakamoto, who's 100% right 100% of the time.About the main villan:I do love my boy Mine (Hijikata) here, character from Yakuza 3. He is given a lot of screen time and done justice. They did my boy right. Mostly because he's the only interesting character in the WHOLE game. He's got some ambiguity to him, you can never be sure what he's up to.Everyone else is so one note, you could read their minds.Select Wild Dancer style and mash X button. Not a SINGLE encounter in the main story and my encountered side stories requires any strategy. To boot, the other styles are complete garbage and not worth using.Now, I know none of Yakuza games had particularly advanced combat, but you could mix up your approach a bit. Ishin and Yakuza 0 are extremely similar to each other, so lemme compare them, as they basically released at the same time (2014 and 2015). In Yakuza 0, let's say you use the Beast style. It is most useful against groups of enemies, since your slow, wide attacks can't be interrupted. However, it's unhandy in fast 1v1 boss fights, but you COULD make it work in your own way just by attacking at the same time as the boss and trading damage. In most cases, it felt good to be this unstoppable tank. In Ishin, Brawler style is similar, but you cannot block or tank attacks from the bosses, because all of them (and most basic enemies) use a blade, thus knock you down before you hit them. This means you must constantly parry with strict timings and chip away with low damage, if you prefer the unarmed Brawler style.Or you switch to Wild Dancer style and ignore almost all mechanics. It's just boring. It feels unnecessary to use other 3 styles. Stunningly beautiful and as good as any Yakuza games. Overflowing with activities like dancing, singing and mahjong. Plenty of side stories, which are well written and funny, like having to translate a letter between lovers. Or some sort dance mob that would only happen in modern times, yet there it is. It's all so bizarre in the most fun way. Unlike Yakuza 0, you can enter most shops without a loading screen (wow, next gen, I know).Yet, there is an annoying delay to skipping lines of dialogue, that was fixed in Yakuza Kiwami 1 onward, but is present here for some reason. The line must play for like a half a second before you can skip (even if you hold auto-skip with R1+A buttons). I believe it all comes down to greed. This is not worth a full 60 bucks price tag.I did not like most of my time with it. I only finished it because I really love this series, but was kinda bummed in the end.There is definitely a bit of enjoyment to be had here, which would be fine if bought on sale.Story and combat are such a snooze-fest, I cannot be bothered with completing the good side stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: Ishin has a phenomenal atmosphere, a gripping story, and is really fantastic as a period piece in the Yakuza/Like a Dragon universe. However, this was all present in the original release of the game on Playstation, and this remaster is not a good port. Cutscenes are locked to 30 FPS, the combat and physics on Unreal Engine don't feel true to the series, and there were some highly questionable practices with the game's DLC (who puts consumable, repurchaseable item packs in a  game?) But by far, the Ishin remake has the worst grind of any game in the series for anybody seeking 100% completion. I have the platinum trophy for every game released on Steam so far, and I have never had an experience as painfully boring and anti-fun as with Ishin. Not only has the price of equipment at the forge been inflated to absolutely ridiculous prices, there is a dizzyingly long list of equipment seals you will never get your hands on without abusing the RNG that determines when they appear. If save scumming is the ONLY viable strategy for completing your game in any reasonable amount of time, something has gone terribly wrong.I love the Yakuza series, and it seems like it will be returning to glory with Gaiden and Infinite Wealth. If you really want to immerse yourself in the world of Ishin, then by all means do so. But I can't recommend it after so much of my time with it was spent completely ignoring that world in favor of endless menu navigation for that final, painful platinum.

_childDocuments_.review: I took my time yesterday to rush through the entire game and finish it so I could forever uninstall it.I have a lot of problems with the game, but let's start with the more positive stuff:-Soundtrack (for the most part) is RGG platinum, as always.-Ryoma's four fighting styles are unique and each serve to accomplish something (except one).-Not Kamurocho means a breath of very much needed fresh air.-Random goons are a bit more threatening because they wield blades.-The recasting of some of the characters was completely fine and I think people over exaggerated about it.-Imo, number one final boss fight. Literally best final boss.Now, for the bad...:-The DLCs in this game are super scummy, with the Ryoma helping kits being a bundle per save file, which is stupid because if you desire to play New Game again, you won't have these packs anymore and need to buy them again.-Speaking of DLCs, an entire difficulty is paywalled behind DLCs. Absolutely awful.-The game looks awful, GTA Remastered-tier graphics. And it's all because of...-Unreal Engine 4 instead of DE or even OE. What the people doing this remake were smoking, I have no clue.-The four fighting styles are very much not balanced: Brawler does no damage (and for the second time in RGG history, the Tiger Drop is basically worthless), Swordsman is far too slow in the early game, Gunman is OP once you get a decent gun and is very boring and Wild Dancer, while very much fun, is your only option against groups.-Dodging works only half of the time, I was getting hit constantly mid-dodge-Parrying has very bad frames and I would sometimes parry 2 seconds after the window would supposedly elapse-Enemies either have very big and obvious wind-ups, or they attack you frame one. Absolutely garbage.-The trooper card system exists outside of the dungeons. They work like Extracts from Judgment/Lost Judgment. In addition to this, they have the audacity of giving you really good cards for free with the Elite Troopers Bundle, and if you have DDE, you get even more busted cards. Now, normally this would be fine since you can have the argument of "just dont use them lolmao crybaby", but then you realize...-The bosses can pull special moves just like Ryoma can. I was BEWILDERED when Tokugawa (Daigo in this game) pulled a Kamehameha.-This leads to moments of frustration where the player might feel like it is absolutely necessary to use the trooper card system, which I don't think I need to tell you how bad that is.-The Dragon of Dojima skin is actual garbage, mish-mashing different parts from different Kiryus (Y5 face with YK1 suit and YK2 hair), and the animations for Ryoma do not fit Kiryu, who looks like he has disjointed bones.-The game is shoddy with optimization. I have a PC that runs Doom Eternal like butter, no issues with it whatsoever, so imagine my surprise when I get to the cutscene that introduces all the Shinsengumi captains only for the cutscene to lag so badly I HAVE TWO RYOMAS ON MY SCREEN! This doesn't even include random framedrop issues that just have no reason to exist.-God forbid you want to check the world map, because every time you exit the map the game freezes for one entire second.-You cannot 100% the game because of some internal issues so if you want to 100% the game, good luck.-21:9 is not supported, and you'll permanently have this border on your sides no matter what, even in cutscenes which was not the case in any other RGG title.Play LITERALLY ANY OTHER RGG GAME PLEASE. If you REALLY want to play this, install mods in the other RGG games so you can have a katana or something, don't bother with this trash can of a game. If you REALLY want to play Ishin, I suggest you put up with or learn japanese and then emulate the original.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a... controversial but still very good game.The good:Big, detailed, dense open world filled with tonnes of content. Loads of substories, sidestories/business management things, minigames, interesting objectives to complete etc.The combat is overall decent, and seeing the "cards" (which I'm sure were going to be in the original Y7 before it went JRPG) are quite fun.Fun environment, different and refreshing to Kamurocho, especially in its setting.Negatives:The graphics are enhanced in a strange way, everything has a blurry-like sheen to it and it cannot be fixed.Combat, though alright, is pretty unbalanced. The brawler style is entirely useless, and frankly if you are playing with anything but swordman you are playing it wrong. Gunman is easy to abuse, and wild dancer is better in theory than execution.Grind. Yeah, classic Y0/(Y7) style grind for equipment. Especially if you want to 100% it, Kiwami style.Story is a bit... wordy. I get its trying to tell a real Japanese story but with a weird twist to it, and blending historical events together in a conspiracy chain, but most of the plot is sitting around listening to blokes talk politics. Not quite as "bad" as Y7s story, but a bit boring. Its also hard to get invested in characters as there are so many, only a few get proper screentime.Honestly though, its a good game. In a similar vein to Yakuza 5- big solid game with refreshing new content, but a weak story (for different reasons) and a challenge to bring to completion. If you're a fan of Yakuza already, pick this up. If not... I wouldn't start here or recommend it on its own merit.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler Free ReviewFirst off god bless RGG Studios for not only bringing this game to the west but remaking it on unreal engine the game looks beautiful and is well optimized even for my 1050ti.That being said the game is a 1:1 copy of the original japanese version with only some few changes and nerfs to two of the combat styles.First off if you've played any yakuza game before or even played the original version of Ishin you will see some familiar faces here from previous yakuza games, mainly from yakuza 0. The community has had some mixed receptions of the character recasting, on which im on the side of agreeing with those not in favor of the new set of characters, I prefer the old ones in the original Ishin since the casting made more sense. As for the two styles that got nerfed which is Brawler and Gunman.Very little changed with one of brawlers dodge upgrades becoming now only usable in Brawler only unlike in the original where you can use the dash in all styles, while Gunman has had its fire rate nerfed quite a bit since it was just a tad bit op in the original.Now for the side content, there is a lot that has been added both new and old. The Karaoke minigame is back with a new song that some may recognize from the absolute meme it became, which is Bakamitai. We also have a new farming minigame with Haruka which is honestly a really nice change of pace after fighting some ronins. Overall you will never get bored in this game with the plethora of minigames and substories. Overall i really recommend the game to people who have already played a yakuza game.Also DO NOT BUY the booster pack/upgrade dlc, it is an absolute scam and my only gripe with this game the fact that its only a one time use, and is not even tied to a save file, yes you can only use it once then you'd have to buy it again. Honestly don't know what they were thinking with this, there was some already questionable dlcs at the past like with Lost Judgement where most of the powerups you get from buying the dlc is only a one time use.

_childDocuments_.review: I only recommend if you are a fan of Yakuza already, curious about Japanese History, or if it's on sale (primarily that).  For the first two: if you are into one of them or both already then fantastic it's for you.  For someone outside of Yakuza I won't recommend.  For starters, the combat offers 4 different varieties.   I only find 2 to be the most useful, being Wild dance and Swordsmen.  Gunman just doesn't feel all that fun and Brawler is useless unless you want to go through the training/grind to level it up.  The story is what you expect out of Yakuza: fantastic, emotional when it needs to be and funny when it needs to be.  the bosses are hit and miss but I feel that way for most bosses anyways.  Take it from someone who has never played the original from Japan, it is nice to see some of the characters I love playing in a setting that is not shown in other games, but they share the same personality as the main games.  Including some surprise characters I never thought they appear who I won't mention.  The sub stories are the main thing that drew me into Yakuza as Most of my playtime in open world games or Rpgs are the side quests, and boy does Yakuza has some great ones.  I hate to say that this one has very weak quests.  Only a small handful kept me captivated, with the feature of friendships, makes every other side story feel the same with sometimes no reward for your effort.  Another feature that I like to mention is the 2nd life which I really enjoyed when I want to do something outside combat (and I'm also a big fishing mechanic enjoyer).  It was very investing and I always kept coming back to do side things as cooking and paying rent.  Overall: It might sound I only say nothing but negative things about the game, but I had fun, a lot of fun even.  It's just compared to the other Yakuza games I've played (or played so far) I find this to be the weakest so far.  A very fun gimmick that gets repetitive later on is the best I can describe in just one sentence for Like a Dragon: Ishin!

I was actually shocked I sunk so much time into it because it seemed to fly by.The game has your typical convoluted, but super engaging Yakuza story, fun combat, and unforgettable comedic moments. Highly recommended for samurai fans*Mild Substory Spoiler*The highlight of the game for me is when your character is guilted into playing "house" with a group of children. He plays the mom, while others play the children, dad, and a local samurai. The child playing the local samurai comes into the house and starts demanding protection money. _childDocuments_.review: This game is generally pretty good.  The combat's a blast, the story has some really great moments, there are some fun new minigames, and the substories in these games never disappoint.  It was pretty fun playing as a character much like Kazuma Kiryu, just in a different time period.However, this game probably has the most scuff since Yakuza 4.  The game is basically a remaster of the original, which I wasn't aware of; I figured it'd be more modern and in-line with the current gen Dragon Engine games.  I didn't mind the blast from the past, but it was unexpected.  The game doesn't seem fully polished for PC, either; I'd get the occasional freeze, stutter, and at the worst of times, a flickering shadow glitch when there were cutscenes in certain buildings.  Not a game breaker, but it was disappointing.  Oh yeah, and the prerendered cutscenes were capped at 30 FPS!  Usually I'm not a snob when it comes to this, but it was pretty jarring when the rest of the game is usually played at 60 frames or higher.Overall, this game is solid.  It's pretty rough around the edges, but generally I'm happy ended up getting a port of this game.  I just hope that if we eventually get Kenzan, it gets the remake treatment instead of just a remaster.  I would GLADLY take more Like a Dragon swordplay!

_childDocuments_.review: Very glad to see this game finally released in the west. After almost 10 years, we finally get it in this pseudo upgrade/remake. While the visuals are a definite step up from the PS3 version it first released on, it doesn't compare to the visuals of the newest RGG titles like Lost Judgement and Yakuza: Like a Dragon. With that being said however, if you're a fan of the Like a Dragon/Yakuza games and their spin-offs, you know the deal with this one. Fundamentally, it plays similarly to Yakuza 5 and Yakuza 0, however there's a good amount of changes gameplay wise to make it feel distinct from both of those. So much so, I'd even recommend this game to those who don't regularly enjoy the series, as the gameplay and overall story play a lot more straight-faced than the regular Yakuza games. That isn't to say there is no humor in this one, there's still a lot of silliness in this one, but it doesn't pop up as consistently as it did in say, Yakuza 0. Lots of side content will keep you coming back for more and more, and most of it is very fun. As for the story, it's one of the better ones in the studio's work. It's a very loose historical revenge story/melodrama set in the end of the Edo period of Japanese history, where you play as the actual historical figure Sakamoto Ryoma infiltrating the Shinsengumi. A lot of the main characters are real people of the era portrayed as a lot of the same characters from the Yakuza series which is fun to see as you get a little hint of how they'd be characterized just based on which person from the series is taking their place. For example, Okita Soji looks exactly like Goro Majima, and he has some of the same tendencies and attitude, but is still different enough to stand as his own character. All that stuff said, Samurai games are not exactly everywhere so it's good to get this underrepresented historical time period in a very well told story that stays interesting all the way through. Great voice work as always, good writing, interesting characters, amazing soundtrack, and pacing is rock solid. The PC port needs some work however. Moving this game to Unreal 4 seems to have had some hiccups. Performance is fine, but not amazing, with some random dips in effect heavy moments like heat actions. The classic Unreal 4 stutter is still present as well, even if it's significantly reduced since the first patch that came out.  It's not an abysmal port by any stretch of the imagination, it's certainly playable all the way through without much hassle, more just something to be of note as these problems still exist nonetheless. If you are a fan of RGG games, you shouldn't even be reading reviews, you know you're going to love this game. If you're not an RGG fan and have interest in getting into the games or you've tried one or two and they didn't stick with you, i'd still say you should give this game a shot. It doesn't require any previous knowledge of any of their previous games whatsoever and has enough difference gameplay wise to stand out from the rest of their work. And for the 60 dollars, you're getting well over 35 hours of a really fun game, especially if you don't overlevel yourself like I did. I'd say this game is in the higher tier of RGG's work but behind their absolute best games like Yakuza 0 and Lost Judgment.
