Cutscenes are sadly locked to 30 FPS but the newly added ones with Harukas Minigame include 120 FPS Cutscenes (in my case, might be unlimited aswell).The 4 Styles are a pretty neat idea, being Fist, Sword, Gun and Sword+Gun. Sadly the Game "forces" you to use the Sword Style mainly because its the best for 1v1 (aka all Boss encounters). Sword+Gun is a fun style for building up a 99 Combo and clearing out waves of enemys. Fist is for the Gigachads who run Tiger Drop and Gun is pretty lame imo. Its a nice idea so you can clean up enemys from a distance but so far (being on the last Chapter) you only have to use it once to kill some enemys out of your range.It wouldve been nice to see I havnt played the original Yakuza Ishin so i cant tell whats new and whats old.tl;drGet it for like 30 to 40 bucks, cap FPS to 120 or below and expect some performance Issues during particle heavy cutscenes.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played every game in this series with an english translation. I really didn't like this one. The single biggest problem in this game is the combat and systems relating to it.TL;DR: if you just play the main story, you can have a good time with it. If you go for all substory completion (e.g. ) or -- god forbid -- 100% completion, you will probably hate this game.Every enemy feels like they have 2 or 3 times more health than they should have, you feel like you have 2 or 3 times  than you should have, and half the styles do garbage damage. I think they expect you to use the trooper abilities that erase squads, otherwise you're sitting there for an eternity mashing buttons.Getting good equipment to make your damage output  more favorable is locked behind a ridiculously tedious equipment grind. I sidestepped this entirely by buying a "light of heaven" sword from that one shady dude in town, then just using the swords given to you in the main story. Very little else ever felt even remotely worth it.In other game in this series, many of your moves have secondary effects, like stuns, guard-breaks, or knockdowns. There are very few moves in this game with those effects. Additionally, many enemies are immune to these effects (this is the hyper armor problem others have mentioned), so they'll face-tank your attacks and chunk your health bar.Every style feels like it has half the utility of a style in another Yakuza game. The reason for this is that they expect you to get that ability that lets you switch styles mid-combo, then use that for the whole game. Unfortunately, this system is nowhere near as fleshed out as it should be. Kiwami 1 did this  better. Brawler and Gunman feel very under-baked. Swordsman has a lot of counters, but they feel stiff and awkward to use, and sometimes seem like they just don't work. Wild Dancer has the most fleshed out moveset, but it's kinda just mash light attack then occasionally dodge.Then the dungeons. Oh my god, the dungeons. Don't even bother. They're only good for grinding materials, and they are so mind-numbingly boring. There's like 40 of them, and they get longer and more tedious the further you get.Finally, the "reward" () for doing all the substories . It's one of the worst in the series, and is just more of the same crap but with worse numbers. If you really,  want to do it, just download a save.I'm kind of amazed that testers played this game and said "yeah, this feels good". This game desperately needs a modder to come in and overhaul all these numbers. Unfortunately, because this is a new engine, the modding tools just aren't quite there yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon: Ishin is a welcome remake and localization of the original released back in 2014. However, its switch to Unreal Engine 4 has introduced bugs and performance issues that may take you out of the wonderful experience the game is trying to portray. Here are my pros and cons as a fan of the series and as someone who got 100% AchievementsOverall, Like a Dragon: Ishin is a fun experience as a long-time Yakuza fan and someone who already played the original Ishin. Much like the transition from the PS3-era games to Dragon Engine, the transition to Unreal Engine 4 leaves a lot to be desired. I hope RGG Studio listens to the community and apply the necessary fixes such as Shader Compilation to current and future games. As a fan, I'll give Like a Dragon: Ishin a 9/10 but critically, I docked some points for its monetization practices and the poor optimization. With all that said, to all my RGG kyodais around the world... tomorrow is yours!

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon: Ishin is a remake of the game of the same name that never got localized in the West. Releasing on the PS4, a lot of fans consider the original version of the game to be one of the best, if not the best Yakuza game in the series. With a lot of fan clamoring for a western release, RGG studios delivered a remake under the new Western name: Like a Dragon. In short, it's a phenomenal game, but so heavily flawed. Gameplay is fantastic for 3/4 styles and graphically the game looks great, but if you're someone who plays these games for more than just the story you'll need to be ready to hunker down and grind your head off.You have 4 styles: Brawler, Swordsman, Gunman, and Wild Dancer. Brawler is purely fisticuffs using moves that are fairly similar to Kiryu's Dragon style, Swordsman is a sword-only style that is slow but can be best used in single combat, Gunman is great at picking off targets from a range or those who are injured, and Wild Dancer combines Swordsman and Gunman into an agile and swift fighting package. Off the bat most players who have played the Yakuza series might gravitate towards Brawler, especially with moves like Komaki Tiger Drop being in his arsenal. Unfortunately however, Brawler ends up being the weakest in the game due to extremely poor damage scaling with the only fix being to stack a bunch of +Brawler damage slots in your armor that are not even remotely close to being easily obtainable. On the contrary, the most powerful one is Gunman by a country mile; its efficacy so great that they actually nerfed gunman in this remake, to make it from drastically overpowered to mildly. Wild Dancer is probably the best feeling overall due to it being very swift, having great mobility with multiple quicksteps, and even having decent single target damage due to a variety of heat moves and quick strikes. Swordsman being the odd one out, while great for single target damage, it feels very slow in comparison to everything else. Pack on the extra baggage of little duels in the game, swordsman's major strength isn't utilized enough and I felt like it was just better off as an armor destroying device or an easy way to stunlock certain opponents.Visually, the game looks phenomenal, but has its fair share of issues. Hair is completely messed up at times, showing grey for certain chunks thanks to lighting, certain interiors for in-engine cutscenes and substories have no shadows or natural light, post processing and motion blur are permanently on and require a mod to disable, as well as obvious texture clipping on certain models and animations. While some visual issues are always going to be present, RGG's first shot at the Unreal engine had these events occur far more often. Story wise, without giving anything away, this is one of the better stories in the series. It's a dramatization off of the real Sakamoto Ryoma with the added spice of RGG-style drama, and it's probably one of the best they've put out in a while. The Yakuza characters that depict the characters in-game are pretty great representations of their personality and motives, which makes it a treat for people who have played the previous games to guess what their angle is. However, as a remake goes, characters were replaced to modernize it. Some of the characters, like the Shinsengumi captains were replaced from their Yakuza 4/5 counterparts to those from Yakuza 0 and Like A Dragon, with some of them sticking out in an odd way visually. Other than that, it's well worth it for the story being told.As for progression, it's an oddball situation. If you want better weapons and armor, you either do Battle Dungeons or the Blacksmith. The Blacksmith allows you to upgrade gear, and Battle dungeons are your main source of materials to upgrade said gear (or if you're lucky in the dungeons, you might end up getting an upgraded item). However, if you're just going through the story, you are given gear at the end of certain chapters to keep you up to speed. However, if you're someone trying to finish the Battle Dungeons entirely or even 100% the game, the grind is the absolute worst in this game. Rare materials are extremely scarce and most only drop from the battle dungeons, so you'll probably be farming hours on end for what you need just to get a material to drop. Money is also a major issue with craftomg as Battle Dungeons pay out very little money unless you farm the very last dungeons, meaning your best course of action is to farm money elsewhere, with the most consistent big ticket winner is Chicken Races or Another Life. Both require waiting, Chicken races require luck and Another Life is just sitting around waiting for your vegetables, unless you spam manure. These money making techniques suck a lot of the interactivity out of the game and can take a very, very long time and combined with having to do Battle dungeons for specific materials, I wouldn't blame you for modding the game. Thankfully, Unreal Engine is very easy to mod and there's already a bunch of mods to cut down on farming tedium, such as increasing battle dungeon payouts, increasing drop rates, or even allowing vendors to sell rarer goods. If you're 100%ing the game, unless you want the absolute authentic experience, these mods only save you time.Now for the remake changes. As you would expect, Ishin changed some things from the original. Some are fine, some are not. For example, the Yakuza 5 style food boosts are gone, meaning you can't eat at restaurants for a damage, health, or heat bonus. Wild Dancer was nerfed with heat actions dealing less damage and Dragon god dance can't stunlock enemies as easily. Double shot seals used to be a 100% chance for 2 shots to be fired out of a gun at once, now reduced to 20%. Certain enemies were made into giant enemies, meaning they hit like a truck and you can't even use a good chunk of heat actions on them. Dungeons take significantly longer here than in the original as well. The most controversial one being the card system rework. Before, cards were only ever used in Battle dungeons, but now they're available everywhere (with the exception of training). This means you gain more health, can get buffs, and even do flashy magic based attacks anywhere, including in boss fights. Also some boss fights get that magic too now, regardless of whether or not you have those cards equipped. Overall the experience will be different than the PS4 game, so if you want to replay a remixed version of the original, this isn't the worst way to go.Overall, it's a great game, like RGG does normally. However, it's somewhat hefted down by bugs, odd design choices, and an extremely gruelling 100% grind. If you play just for the story, this game is surprisingly short with about 4-5 chapters being just a fight, some exposition, chapter end. If you're someone who wants to finish all the substories and fight Amon, this isn't going to be the worst grind but it certainly won't be the best. If you're a completionist, this game will become your own personal hell unless you get some mods to soften the blow.Overall, 7/10. Great game, grind aside. Grind included, it can be nightmarish. You have been warned.

_childDocuments_.review: The worst Yakuza experience currently available on Steam. Play literally any other Yakuza game for a fraction of the price, get this if you love the series and it's on at least a 50% sale.My biggest gripe with this game are the combat styles, aside from Wild Dancer (which is actually a great style) this game has a worse combat experience than all of the mainline Yakuza games. Brawler is massively underpowered and basically unusable throughout the game, even if you try to buff it by slotting in the Brawler damage increase seals it still does a fraction of the damage of every other style. Gunman is a single button spam style, it really has no combos and without a Pierce seal on your gun, it is unusable against armored enemies. Swordsman is the worst style I've ever experienced in a Yakuza game. Imagine the Beast style but it does less damage, has less range/aoe, and doesn't have the massive advantage of Beast's omnidirectional block and hugely reduced damage while blocking. It is absolutely miserable. The game has some other pretty serious issues with combat and combat related progression/mechanics. Heat moves in this game are more sparse than other Yakuza entries, for example, you have to level and acquire simple Heat moves you normally have as default for styles, such as the standard downed, grab and near a wall Heat moves. This game is also way more finicky when it comes to activating specific Heat moves with unique activation parameters, and even has enemies you cannot use Heat moves on at all. When you level a style to max you are able to "break your limits" and unlock the same exact leveling tree to progress through again, nothing new or exciting. The game also has a lot of really janky hitboxes, which I think contributes to the sketchiness of the Heat actions, but is also really annoying for combat. The enemy spear and two handed mace hitboxes really stand out.The crafting in the game is solid, although the economy of the game is a bit of a mess, they apparently nerfed the sell value of plates from the original and seem to have gone overboard. Without a ton of grinding (or exploiting) you don't really have the freedom to make many of the high level weapons to either try out different elements or the extra weapon styles, as the game doesn't have the usual activity aimed directly at making you money like most Yakuza games have now. It also effects your ability to enlist new troops as the best pull is a reasonably high sum for only getting 1 troop at a time, but the game gives you very solid troops for free. The Seal system is an absolute mess because the drop rate is hilariously low. When I finished the game having completed 97% of sub stories, every battle dungeon, and had capped out the diligence report for random encounter and sneaks by chapter 7, I had dropped 9 unique seals (I had a varying amount of those 9 but none over 7 total.) I think there are 30 or 32 total unique seals, and they're a powerful way to increase player power. It's very annoying to basically not get to interact with this system unless you use some of the goofy ways people are using to attain them, like spam crafting low level weapons just to disassemble them if they spawn with a seal. I love the Yakuza series and this was a huge disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series and Samurais in general when it was announced that Ishin was getting remade/remastered I was highly looking forward to it.  Luckily the game lived up to my expectations.  If you played other games in the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series you will likely enjoy this game, however I would recommend this game as your first game in the series.  Ishin makes a lot of references and nods to the main series, for example many of the characters themes are remixed in Ishin using traditional Japanese instruments.  If you have not played the other Yakuza games you would not get the references, and these references are some of the most enjoyable parts of the game.  I would recommend playing Yakuza 0 or Yakuza Kiwami 2 if you've never played one of the games in the series before.The main gripe I had with this remake is the squad/card mechanic that felt really shoehorned into the game, and is unfortunately necessary for bosses and certain areas in the game to restore heal and do high DPS.  However annoying it did not ruin the entire game and I would still recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Like a Dragon: Ishin!

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting take on Samurai class conflict with all of your favorite Yakuza characters.  There are a lot of returning themes you expect as well as some new ones that really help spice it up.  For example, you gain two types of experience:  one is based on whatever style you have equipped and one is general experience.  When you level up, you get training orbs and style orbs.  Style orbs are specific to that particular style, but training orbs can be used on any style, so you can develop as you wish.Virtue takes place of CP and is hyper useful as it controls several different mini-buffs that don't directly influence combat, but many things happening within the game itself.  You can cook, farm, sing karaoke, dance, fish, and so much more.  This is an amazing and addictive Yakuza experience that's unapologetically Japanese and I absolutely love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Like a Dragon: Ishin!

_childDocuments_.review: I have had a lot of fun, but this is once again a balance issue with the grind to difficulty ratio. Blacksmith levelling is crazy long and extremely costly. Gambling is the only way to make money quick but will require you to be extremely cheeky (save scumming). The second option is using mods to makes money less of an issueThe balance with difficulty vs grind makes no sense. Your only challenge - which is the 2nd to 3rd best way to get items and money is dungeons. They are the only "tough" fight you'll encounter during this game. The boss fights of each chapters are way way too easy. This is explained by the fact you have a gun fighting style - yes - smash one button all the time and evade once in a while. Especially efficient against non-armoured mobs and fighting stage with lot of distance. Otherwise Wild Dancer will make you practically untouchable and deal about 66% of the strongest stand Swordsman. Brawler is legit useless AF. Which feels like a let down!Overall those concerns makes the games average for the Franchise but still pretty good.The store is overwhelmingly heavy on the History of Japan and less about Saito Hajime and this makes some part of it kind of long. Are those parts important because they add context? Yes! If you're an avid reader and history buff, there's a lot of side quest that add a lot to the game experience. Overall 7/10!

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon: Ishin! is a fantastic spinoff in the Like a Dragon series. With excellent combat, a great atmosphere, and an interesting setting, Ishin has a lot to love about it. Moreover, the story is unique and not seen too often in video games; your knowledge of Japanese history will determine what you get out of the story, though. However, even though Ishin is a great game, it does have some issues. For example, despite being a remake, Ishin still controls like it came out a decade ago. Furthermore, the switch from the Dragon Engine to Unreal Engine 4 wasn't completely flawless; traversal stutter is more apparent than in previous Like a Dragon games. Still, even though Ishin has some problems, the story, combat, and atmosphere more than make up for its shortcomings. For fans of the Like a Dragon games, I'd highly suggest trying Ishin.

_childDocuments_.review: Lemme get something outta the way: The difficulty setting isn't paywalled. It's just paying for an early unlock, like hundreds of other games you probably paid 60 dollars plus a season pass for do these days, if you bought the deluxe edition. If you beat the game once, you unlock Ishin! difficulty without paying a cent. That's it. That's the answer.If you have a problem with this in all of the other games that do paying for early unlocks, then by all means, gripe about it. But it's not paywalled -- paywalling implies you MUST pay for something, not that it's an option for the sake of convenience.Anyway, it's a pretty standard UE4 port of a 9 year old PS4 game. Textures are facelifted, they used high-poly renders of certain characters instead of their lower-poly PS4 versions, and some of the character faces and voices have been replaced. I went in expecting a ton of problems and came out with only a few of them materialized, chiefly the micro-stutter on loading new effects, which I'm pretty sure everyone at this point knows is just shader compilation and will go away the more you play. Personally, I'm hoping for a patch from the B-team identifying which shaders are most common for pre-compilation, but I won't hold my breath, and neither should you.This game rocks. The combat's the best the RGG series has had since Yakuza 0, and that includes K2 and Lost Judgment. It feels like RGG's finally started to get the hang of the style system in a way that actively encourages players to switch styles depending on certain circumstances, instead of spending the entire game in Rush, Slugger, Snake or DOD (I don't even count Crane style in Judgment because of how absolute garbage it is). Giving access to Legend mode right off the bat is refreshing as heck, and enemies actually feel like they want you dead and will do everything they can to make it so. Wild Dancing through every encounter will get you killed real quick, and the game establishes right away that the mental challenge of recognizing what styles fit what situation is far more pronounced than it has been in most other RGG games up to this point.The story is pretty good, standard for RGG's storytelling style. You're introduced to the world, something bad happens that draws in Kiryu I Mean Ryoma against his will and you're dragged through an odyssey that involves meeting a diverse cast of crazy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and beating the ♥♥♥♥ out of them until they decide they like you enough to help you figure out who screwed you over. Rinse and repeat. There's nothing wrong with it that I've seen so far. Familiar faces everywhere, their personalities are also tied into the plot, and most of the voice work is unchanged from the original. If you like RGG, you'll like this. If you like Bakumatsu dramas, you'll like this. It's just the post-Yakuza 0 RGG cast putting on an Edo era play. You know, like they did that one time in River City Ransom.If you're just looking for a recommendation, that's about it, that's all I got to say, you can go on your way now. The rest of this review is a medium-length rant about peoples expectations for the RGG games, so you can skip this if you're already convinced.There's two things I wanna cover, and the first is the short one: 1) A lot of people don't seem to grasp that this isn't a mainline RGG game, and pretty much never has been nor was it ever intended to be, and even then, the expectation of quality from Sega or RGG Studio with any of these games seems incredibly skewed when coming from western gamers. Ishin is the equivalent of the Kiwami games: An update and release of something from a long time ago to give people the chance to play it in some form if their PS2 or PS3 is busted or they don't wanna eBay a disc where Mark Hamill voices Majima. It doesn't have the same amount of resources going into it as stuff like Yakuza 7 or Lost Judgment, and if you think this is unacceptable, I guarantee you you're gonna be disappointed by RGG Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name later this year, because it's gonna be the same damn thing. Cope with it and move on.2) Anyone coming to the RGG games expecting a tight, beautiful, ten-to-fifteen-hour AAA production is going to be, and will ALWAYS be, sorely disappointed. These aren't AAA games. These aren't even AA games. You're not paying 60 bucks for the realistic graphics or thousands of hours of multiplayer or film-quality voice work and motion capture, you're paying for an 80 hour soap opera action RPG where you get to bask in the incredibly violent animations, goofy side content, and Mahjong. If you aren't the kind of person willing to learn the rules of Riichi Mahjong, these games probably aren't for you.Okay, so that's kind of an exaggeration, but the point is that most people who whine about the RGG games being short or shallow or not top quality technical experiences do so while ignoring the literal hundreds of hours of side content packed into the games that the games just have. They just put it in there! It's there for you to play around with, to explore in an open world, to grind through because it's just THERE, and it's intentional and, most importantly, core to the experience. RGG Ishin is no different.I get it, okay: I'm a PC gamer too, as evidenced by me being here and dumping hundreds of hours into these stupid games. But you can't just completely ignore the history of the medium and somehow expect the PC gaming industry in Japan to evolve to the point of western PC releases in 1/4 of the time the west had to refine the art when throughout the entirety of home gaming Japan has focused almost exclusively on consoles and handhelds save for literal anime pornography. You want a short, polished poodle of a game, Sony's western dev houses are porting games to PC, and they're 60 bucks too, and they're short, linear cinematic experiences that'll probably make you happy. That's not a bad thing, that's what you're looking for. Play what you're looking for.As for me, I want RGG to stay a scrappy A-minus franchise that has systemic quirks that don't go away with most of the cash spent on the voices and likenesses of big-name Japanese celebrities who occasionally get caught up in drug scandals. I want them to keep putting in countless hours of goofy nonsensical side content with over-the-top situations played completely straight by the protagonists, while sticking to hard-hitting cheesy soap opera garbage for the main story. I want violent combat, I want pretty faces with clearly unrealistic limb sizes that manage to get the message across and I want raw ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ masculinity with rock hard abs and intricate, meaningful back tattoos.But I'm not gonna get any of that if RGG Studio starts spending its time kowtowing to western AAA release standards without any of the budget or time these corresponding games require. A little bit of gatekeeping isn't a bad thing, especially when it's focused on maintaining the quality of the experience instead of spreading the time and budget way too thin to create a viable product.These are a , and the sooner you understand that, the sooner you'll actually have a good time with them.

_childDocuments_.review: My first ever yakuza game and It leaves quite a lot to be desired. The game can be fairly clunky and have quite outdated level design, can clearly see that it was originally a PS3 game, and the story is abit all over the place with the majority of the side quests (substories) been very straight forward and having very little pay off. Also the grind to get the higher level weapons is atrocious and I would recommend nobody to bother going for it as the drop rates for certain items are terrible and it will taint your overall thoughts on the game.The minigames are very good and the main character is somehow very likable even though he is a very stoic and bland kind of person. I also found the combat to be surprisingly good and also surprisingly deep after getting some upgrades and new moves. A very sekiro lite kind of combat.  Overall I would give the game a 7/10 and would recommend it for it's setting and if you just want a decent game to play while you listen to a Podcast on the background. Perhaps I should of started with a different yakuza game as my first one but I am eager to try yakuza 0 later In the year.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 Wonderful game!This is another great spin-off game from RGG Studio. What I like about this game is that the gameplay is new and refreshing. You can use a sword, a gun or both at the same time.I was disappointed when I played the demo (because it was clunky and slow), but the full version is much better and smoother.  The story is amazing, the soundtrack and graphics are great. Right now, there are no cons that I'm facing (except that this game uses Denuvo, but that's another topic). It's a wonderful remake and I would recommend it to anyone interested in playing games from RGG Studios. The best thing about it is that you can jump right in without having to worry about the other games. That is not necessary. You'll understand everything from start to finish. Overall, and a message to Sega:I'm grateful that this game is available on PC, Sega. I hope you'll release more of your newer games on GOG (I'll definitely be buying there too).I'm also thankful that you will be releasing Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii will be released, in which Majima is the main character. Finally! I will also be checking out Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth. Those two games are the only thing missing. I'm looking forward to playing more of your older games. ^^

_childDocuments_.review: It's more Yakuza which is good, pick it up if you've run out of other entries to play but it definitely has issues:Port is iffy, pretty stuttery especially during heat actions, some cutscenes were flickering fortunately it never happened during the major story beats. Some enemy and boss movesets are a total crapshoot, difficulty overall feels like it was based on a dice roll rather than trending upwards. The Trooper Cards are perhaps the biggest issue with the combat either feeling like extreme overkill or downright necessary. The crafting system is frankly the most insulting grind I've ever seen in a single player action game like this, incredibly expensive and level-gated by an extremely slow experience system.The story is both predictable and nonsensical but not an enjoyable to laugh at kind of way.Soundtrack was kind of a hit or miss too, I heard remixes in marketing material that don't even show up in-game?I still enjoyed my time with the game but it'd really lost me by the final 2-3 chapters, don't see myself going back for another playthrough. It's nice to able to play this game without jumping through hoops but I really hope this isn't the standard that any potential future remakes are held to.

_childDocuments_.review: Trapped inside a mysterious laboratory and unable to remember his past, Derrick Cole discovers his extraordinary powers as he fights for survival against a determined military faction and a legion of seemingly invincible superhuman warriors. Breakdown is a science fiction thriller combining the best elements of shooters and fighters into a comprehensive first-person action adventure game. High-end, real-time rendered graphics reveal Breakdown's intense storyline and brings an unprecedented level of realism to the gameplay experience. The game features fierce hand-to-hand and weapons-based combat, challenging puzzles, surreal dream sequences, advanced AI, and massive, detailed environments for exploration.

name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition Experience the complete Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley experience in Tove Jansson’s beautiful, lively and melancholic Moomin world in Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley - Digital Deluxe Edition. Journey through the valley with the cherished keepsakes that Snufkin takes with him wherever he can: blooming flowers for his hat and a wooden mouthpiece for when he is lost in thought. Listen to the atmospheric original soundtrack inspired by the Nordic landscape; from harsh weather to unique stunning views of nature and wilderness, the melodies born in the hands and hearts the composer Oda Tilset containing tracks from the famous Icelandic band Sigur Rós. Skim through pages and pages upon concept art that came to life, never-before-seen places and environments, and musings from the team who created the game. Get a behind the curtain look on the techniques, philosophy and styles to make this game a storybook come-to-life, including characters, environments and fauna. The Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley - Deluxe Edition includes: - Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley - The cosmetic Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley Cherished Keepsakes DLC - The Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley Original Soundtrack - The Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley Digital Artbook About the Game Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley is a story-rich musical adventure game about Snufkin restoring the valley and helping the quirky and memorable characters and critters who call it home. A series of hideous parks have cropped up in Moominvalley, disrupting the landscape and its harmonious nature. As Snufkin you will distract police officers, pull out signs, and knock over misplaced statues as you vigorously try to restore nature and the inhabitants’ home while putting an end to the industrious Park Keeper’s plans… Experience a beautifully crafted and quintessentially Nordic game, brought to life with stories, emotions, and a melancholic atmosphere set in Tove Jansson’s vivid and beloved world of Moomin. You are invited to a wholesome experience for every age that combines open-world mechanics with puzzles, stealth, and melodic elements! GORGEOUS STORYBOOK STYLE BRINGING A WORLD TO LIFE Immerse yourself in a beautiful and imaginative world that captures the very essence of the Moomin stories; an extensive tapestry of graphical books and cartoons brought to life in a never-before-seen way. Experience the harmonious symphony with every footfall, elevated by music and melodies from the Icelandic post-rock band Sigur Rós. Befriend Moominvalley inhabitants as Snufkin with a few tunes from his harmonica. Wander Moominvalley with your heart open and your steps light. A CAST OF WONDERFULLY WHIMSICAL CHARACTERS Get to know a diverse cast of characters with strong yet whimsical personalities, depth, and complexity. Embark on a journey to not only find the cause of the hideous parks but to also discover and interact with the charming Moominvalley inhabitants. A MUSICAL ADVENTURE Explore a host of locations where the sun dips below the horizon, casting a warm amber glow across the meadows; where the scent of wildflowers mingles with the crisp breeze, carrying promises of untold stories and hidden wonders; and where you as Snufkin - with your hat pulled low and harmonica in hand - head out. Gain inspiration by exploring Moominvalley and by solving puzzles. Main features Set out on a cozy, story-rich adventure game in a gorgeous storybook art style Get the strict Park Keeper and his horrible parks out of Moominvalley with the help of your trusty harmonica, a bit of stealth, and the friends you’ll meet along the way Meet over 50 charming characters and creatures calling Moominvalley their home Experience narrative gameplay and a myriad of charming stories and quests involving the beloved characters inspired by Tove Jansson’s work Explore Moominvalley’s open world and solve musical and environmental puzzles along the way to uncover the happenings in the valley Immerse yourself in the beautiful soundscape of music and melodies composed in collaboration with Sigur Rós © Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley. Developed by Hyper Games. Published by Raw Fury AB. © Moomin Characters ™

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game as a gift.I've been watching Moomin in the last few months. I'm in my late 20's at this point, but I really enjoyed the old Moomin cartoon. This game is based around Moomin and follows the art style of the 90's cartoon.The biggest highlight of this game has to be the art style and the music. The art is drawn in a way to both resemble the cartoon, but it also has a feeling like it's a children's story book. It's very pretty and makes you feel very warm and happy. The game is complimented by a really relaxing and nice soundtrack to go along with the visuals. You'll often see amazing vistas and views that make you feel very fuzzy and warm.The gameplay itself is essentially an adventure game where you control the character with the mouse and have a few actions like playing musical instruments and jumping and finding ways to get around the environment. The gameplay isn't anything deep and all the puzzles are very simple to go through. The game does encourage you to explore around the areas as you can find "inspiration", which lets Snufkin, the protagonist of the game, increase his level with his musical instruments, which will also help as some puzzles require higher levels in the instruments. The game also has basic quests which will allow you to do a bit of exploration to find an item or solve a puzzle. None of this is particularly difficult.I haven't really discovered any bugs in the game. I think the collision of Snufkin can be a bit off if you're wandering around background objects, but nothing that's actually lead me to be stuck or softlocked. The game pretty much runs flawlessly and I have no complaints on a technical level.I find that the writing is really pleasant and cute. What I found surprising is that the game tackles the theme of nature, the issues with trying to "tame" and "control" that nature and even tackles things like the flaws of authority. Though the game doesn't paint the people behind that system of authority as evil, but instead as misguided, rather than trying to understand and appreciate nature. I think it's a good message to show.This game is more than likely made for a young audience. If you're a parent, I'd definitely recommend this game as a fun little adventure title. If you're a fan of the Moomin show or the novels or stories, this game is also for you. Personally, Snufkin was one of my favorite characters, so having a whole game just for him brought me a lot of joy.To the developers, I just want to say thank you for this experience. It's been a blast and this game's made me very happy!

_childDocuments_.review: To kick off, if you have no connection to the Moomin universe nor find the characters of Tove Jansson cute and charming, I highly doubt you will enjoy this experience. In contrast, if you have any of the previously mentioned things, you will have a great time. Hyper Games has managed to create a highly atmospheric and beautiful game that nails the art style of Tove Janssons’ later drawings of the Moomin universe to a tea, with wonderful and calming music to accompany you throughout the game.Aside from the audio and graphics that Hyper Games hit right on the head, it shall be said that this is what I would define as a high-quality family game. The gameplay is charming and fairly simple, and the length of the game itself is around 4 hours depending on how many of the optimal side quests you decide to do.  In my opinion this is the perfect length in terms of not getting bored of the said fairly simple gameplay.So, who exactly is this game for? Fans of the Moomin universe of all ages. If you have children, this is a high-quality game to sit down with and you can both enjoy it. If you are in my scenario which is early 20’s without children then this game is an evening or two where you can relax and enjoy the atmospheric world of Moomin.TLDR; Hyper Games made a good Moomin game and if you enjoy the Moomin universe, then play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the Moomins when I was growing up, so running around Moominvalley as Snufkin and restoring it to its natural glory was absolute nostalgic magic. The game is obviously gorgeous and all of the characters are, without a doubt, so precious and wonderful. Who doesn’t adore sassy little My or the sweetness of Moominmamma and Moominpappa? I loved every little second of this game, from the storyline of having to save the valley and our friend Moomintroll to exploring all over the valley, to playing as the coolest character of them all.That being said though, it was so short! I managed to complete the game and 100% it in just 6.4 hours. Considering the full game price of €20, I do feel that it’s a bit on the high end for the amount of gameplay you get and the fact that there is not much reason to replay the game either. I was fortunate enough to get it as a birthday gift but if it hadn’t been, I would’ve preferred to wait for a sale. 🌷
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Pleeeease please I implore to whomever this concerns, make the gazing scenes available as animated profile backgrounds in the points shop!! I am begging on my knees <3But to actually review the game; it was such an absolute delight to play. the art is so charming and lovely, the game play is fun and rewarding, and you get to run around as Snufkin playing a fruity little flute in ♥♥♥♥♥ little boots. 10/10 A+ Five stars
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: wished there was a way to revisit the valley after finishing the story though... overall great game, the music and art are beautiful! it was like reading a storybook to my daughter (quite literally). the woodies chasing snufkin around kept her entertained, i bet it was her favorite part. she sat down and watched til the end of my gameplay :))
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Snufkin is the childhood memory and nostalgia. A very chill and easy game to just spend few hours in a wonderfully crafted magical world while exploring it and meeting new friends.Gameplay is very simple, you just explore the surrounding while meeting characters and doing some tasks for them like bringing them stuff or solving some simple puzzles. The game is family friendly so it's not hard although some collectibles could be hard to find.There is progression though and it's related to you playing music. Playing an instrument makes other creatures follow you and help you.It offers a nice heartwarming story and really interesting atmosphere which differs greatly from american tales. It's heartwarming as I mentioned but at the same time a bit sad and weird which is a nice mix.All the environments are beautifully drawn and it's a real pleasure to explore them.Not much else to say about it. Very short but wonderful and unique adventure which is a must play for those who love cozy games.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's very easy for "cozy" games to just have monotonous gameplay that falls flat. This is not that! Short and sweet narrative driven questing game with gorgeous art and music. It was especially refreshing to find a cozy game that didn't lean so heavily on foraging and fetch quests. Lots of little adventuring puzzles and mini games throughout a truly immersive world. Nothing too complicated going on here, but not in a way that's boring. Felt like drinking a good cup of tea :)
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: You play as an anarchist, coming back home from a long journey, only to find your town completely ruined by the overly work-excited law enforcement. Your friend has gone missing and everyone needs your help to get everything back to it's chaotic, comfortable way.Love this game, hope to see more Moomin games in future. Bonus points for having Finnish as a select-able language.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclaimer, I am a huge fan of the Moomins. I was sceptical when I saw the game the first time, just worried the game would not be good and nervous the developers did not know about the Moomins well when making this game. I beat the game now including all the side quests.All my worries were unreasonable, it's clear the developers know exactly what the Moomin Valley represents and what its characters are like, with references from the Moomin books and TV-series. I was feeling at home playing this and excited when I met the main characters. Sniff being his usual scaredy-cat and greedy self, Little My being your feisty friend as I know her etc. Even my favourite character after Snufkin, Ninny the invisible child, is part of this game! The dialogue and conversations will make you smile or even laugh.You play as Snufkin, who just returned to Moomin Valley after being gone for Winter as he does every year. But everyone seem sad, the beautiful nature of Moomin Valley is turning into big parks by the Park Keeper, and Moomintroll is gone! Snufkin don't like the parks and will remove them, but most importantly he will look for Moomintroll - Just always two steps behind him.I'm so happy this game exist. I got emotional in the end and teared up. This is a good representation of the Moomin universe. I'm only sad the game is not longer, and that we can not enter the Moomin house.Thank you so much developers for making this ~~~!!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere created by the beautiful graphics and lovely music is perfect, but this was barely a game. You walk around and press a button, there are no choices or challenges. I grew up reading moomin, playing the games, watching the animated TVshow so I really looked forward to this game, but given how boring it is I can't recommend it. Maybe suitable for small children or those that just want to experience the movie-like story.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a Moomin fan this is an absolute must play. The game itself is super wholesome but not nothing special in terms of gameplay but its beautiful visuals and relaxing vibe are a pleasure for the eyes and ears. Meeting all the characters from Moominvalley put a big smile on my face and brought a bag full of childhood nostalgia. Play for it the feels not the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This game is EXACTLY what it's supposed to be, and does what it has to do gorgeously. It is a beautiful, soothing game, with its perfect amount of sadness and danger and adventure. The mini games are deeply satisfying, but this game excels really in aesthetic satisfaction. It's an acoustic and visual marvel. Playing this game as a kid is as satisfying as an ASMR experience for adults. Astounding
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, but def get it deeply on sale. It's short and there isn't much to do except play instruments to solve a couple puzzles and quests. It's a wholesome, short game that small children would even enjoy watching the story unfold. The music is very calming and the art style is gentle. If you need an anxiety chill pill in game form, this is a good pick.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Cute drawings, well-known characters, but everything else is boring. The gameplay mainly consists of stealth with park keepers, and occasionally pressing a couple of buttons with highlighted instruments. Why does the level meter even exist? The story is not Janissonian; Tove wrote about apocalypses and how the small creatures survive through them, whereas the game plot follows the typical struggle between "natural" locals and civilized invaders. The characters are shallow, few dialogues, press f to do the side quest.Not competitive, not plot rich, not congenial, well drawn.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Snufkin goes from wishing to locate his old friend to the Ted Kaczynski (pbuh) school of esoteric anarchoprimitivism, a route that can only lead one way. Ecoterrorism against the system on all levels. 10/10, but do rebind some keys to WASD before you play. The sound and artstyle is also inceribly wholesome.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: So far I had an absolute blast in Moominvalley and I will be back with a full review after I played it out and had the whole experience.It is such a relaxing game and yet so exciting. I had to be super stealthy and later after my first look I got chased and I had to flee so so fast! But for now - a quick first look: Ps: Little My for life! She the bestest!!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley offers a simple and relaxing experience. You explore beautiful surroundings, meet beloved characters, and complete various tasks. The gameplay mechanics are straightforward, ensuring easy navigation and interaction within the enchanting world of Moominvalley. Whether solving puzzles or discovering collectibles, each task feels integral to unfolding the charm of this beloved universe.Growing up watching the Moomins, I fondly remember the whimsical world and heartwarming stories that defined my childhood. This game captures that nostalgia perfectly, transporting you back to the enchanting Moominvalley with visuals and music that echo the original series.A delightful journey for fans and newcomers alike. If you're looking to relive magical memories, Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley is the perfect choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Having grown up with Moomin and friends in Sweden and Finland, I'm so glad to see this beautiful tribute to the world of Tove Jansson. It very much captures the mood of the books and other iterations, with whimsy, poignancy, and respect for the wonders of nature. Loving the Swedish translation so far as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly what I hoped it would be. You always have to be a bit sceptical about games made in an established franchise, especially if it's a "kids franchice" (even if calling it just that is selling Moomin short), and when it's also a fairly unknown developer, you have every right to be sceptical. But I'm so happy they got it right. A wonderful, cosy and wholesome game. Sigur Rós on the soundtrack fits so well and the artstyle is perfect. It's a bit on the short side (7.6 hours is not for a full 100% playthrough, i restarted a few hours in to get a collectable i missed so 4 to 5 for a blind playthrough is probably more correct), but honestly paying 20€ for a few hours doesn't bother me when the experience is so well executed. For what it's tryring to do, making a game about Moomin it's near perfect and I wouldn't mind a sequel down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: wonderful game. played it with my girl, and we loved it. gentle music, amazing artwork, and simple gameplay.also, extremely pleased to hear music from Sigur Ros, one of my favourite bands.highly recommend for a gentle adventure, in the perfect style of the moomin valley books and series, with familiar characters and a couple of new ones.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

They have greatly increased the life expectancy of those of us who livein “advanced” countries, but they have destabilized society, have made life unfulfill-ing, have subjected human beings to indignities, have led to widespread psychologicalsuffering (in the Third World to physical suffering as well) and have inflicted severedamage on the natural world. _childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I mostly purchased this because it's very nostalgic for me growing up in a nordic country (Denmark) and watching "Mumitroldene" in danish with my sister when i was a kid. As a stand alone game it's fine. It's obviously made for a younger audience which is fine, and it's extremely gorgeous to look at. Like all the animations and the painted background. Wowie. Though it is really short and easy, so if that's not in your interest, skip this one it's quite pricey for what it offers, but i enjoyed myself and got it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Such a sweet game! Didn't know much about Moomintroll before the game, but could fully appreciate the magical, sincere atmosphere nonetheless. Everything from art style to music is designed perfectly to encapsulate this serene, warm mood. This game is ideal for a weekend after a tough workweek when you want just to chill and vibe. Played together with my friend (as in, we played on separate laptops trying to follow the same quests), and we both loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the sweetest and most wholesome games I have ever had the pleasure of playing. You do not have to know the Moomins to play the game - I did not but still deeply enjoyed it. The ending genuinely moved me to tears with its kind and gentle message. The controls are intuitive and the puzzles simple but also varied enough that I was never bored of them, and was always curious as to what was around the next corner. I would recommend this to anyone who needs to take a break from the world and explore a place where everyone is welcome and the beauty of nature is paramount.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely relaxing, cozy and overall well put together Moomin experience for everyone. The graphics absolutely capture the charm and style of Tove Jansson's original works, and the gameplay and writing is fun and characterful. It's a short game at around 5~ hours to fully complete, but I personally enjoyed every last second of it very much. A strong recommend to everyone who likes Moomins or wants to experience their world in a video game form!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: As an illustrator myself, Tove Janssons work is so inspiring, so when I saw this game I just had to play it. Sadly though, I cannot give this game a positive review. Like many other negative reviews have said before, the game is gorgeous and the music is beautiful, and it has very cute animated cutscenes as well. However the game play is uninspired and the mechanics are lacking. Movement feel unresponsive as you have to wait for icons to pop up when jumping or pushing a rock. As a result I sometimes got stuck on a rock while jumping or had to replay the Groke sequence several times because the icons wouldn't trigger in time for me to move on.  The game play feels rinse and repeat having to do the same things over and over again, ( like removing the signs or luring the guards to the ghost). I'm planning to finish the game and hope I get to make some changes to this review. So far it reminds me of adventure games for kids in the 90s. Good to play with your little one's but feels very style over substance for adults who want a bit more from their games.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely delightful!  Relaxing music, beautiful water-color artwork, and fun puzzles.  Adorably spread chaos and anarchy while running from the police.  The only thing I don't like about this game is how short it is.  I really wish it was longer, but hopefully we'll get another installment of Snufkin's adventures.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Very "kind" and wholesome game with impeccable art style. It was drawn so well, in fact, that you can easily take many of the game stills and put them as a wallpaper - on your desktop or in your house. I sadly cannot say the same about the music, but it is easily equalised by an absolute masterpiece of a track "Just looking for warmth (feat. Sigur Rós)", listen to it even if you don't end up playing the game.It is rather easy in the difficulty department and suitable for children, which makes sense considering the source material. The puzzles and quests, however, are still stimulating enough for you to not get bored.Overall it was time and money well spent and I recommend this game to anyone looking for a chill beautiful game or nostalgic about Moomins.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Had an issue which made game unplayable but dev has provided a work around so updating my review. Issue was stuck in cut scenes, fix was to add -limit2kvideo to the launch options. I loved the Moomins growing up and as an adult I wrote an essay about Moomins and their creator Tove Jansson but my masters degree so it was real wish fulfilment to be able to step into the world I had spent so much time analysing. I am only a short amount into the game but I already love it. The game seems to be linear but don't let that put you off, enjoy the beautiful visuals, pleasant music, good storytelling and enjoy the journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I stopped playing for a while I started reading Moomin books recently and to my surprise when I came back to steam looking for a new game to play I found it in my wishlist and immediately bought it and played it. I loved every second of it and no moment was dull; the story, the visuals, the art & music exceptional 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely interactive story for Moomin-lovers. The artwork and music are beautiful. It has a very cosy feel with very basic interactions with the world, and cute things to collect e.g. . But I felt disappointed. This is a 5hr storybook, and an expensive one. A lot of effort and resource has gone into making this which is probably why it's expensive, but it's very short and it has little-to-no replayability. I haven't completed all the achievements but I feel no drive to go chasing them. For the price, I expect more. I expect more depth, more gameplay. I found my self comparing it to a game of a similar price, genre, and rivalling beauty that has given me over 60hrs of gameplay, and I'm not done with it yet. Unless there's going to be free updates with new maps and adventures in Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley, I am very unlikely to reinstall it.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I fancy the world of the Moomins, the game has some major flaws, that you should know before buying. Firstly, the concept of three instruments wielded by the protagonist is pleasant, it is a wasted potential for it to have available only one song per tool (apart from the drum, as the player can set the rythm himself). Songs are soothing but repetetive, and gaining new levels should allow Snufkin to enhance his repertoire. Very simple solution to very basic issue, rewarding the player with something more than just a level number in the corner. It screams out for Snufkin to be able to play anything else than just basic tunes, and sadly it's all you get from the start until the very end of your journey.First very irritating and irrational decision is to lock the gate of the fence, after you visit a certain character in her house . If you move forward with the plot, the gate closes itself forever, locking you out of the  on the map. Problem arose, when searching for findables and such, I wanted to make sure that I checked every corner, so I followed the same path only to find the closed gate. While you cannot get across or travel in any other way, the only way back is to follow the mundane path back, severly unsatisfied with how this was handled. I just cannot imagine what caused this decision, as this bring little help to non-existing problem from the player perspective, only causing irritation or confusion. For such a short total gameplay this adds just a substantial waste of time.Second, more major issue is that one chapter of the game takes place on an separate island. If you miss anything there before leaving, it is locked for you until next playthrough. You have to repeat the entire game, instead just allowing the player to visit the island after you finish this chapter, solely for the purpose of finding anything left behind. Again, . From the game-making mechanics it's a faux pas and laziness in execution, especially that this title should bring rather cozy couple of hours, devoided of such simple flops. Which brings me to the next issue below. As much I am not the "achievement dog", i'd imagine completing this game 100% is not to hard on the first and only playthrough, taking into account that the game itself is not difficult, so i wanted to do it just for pure pleasure. However, with the issue presented before, I cannot complete the game entirely unless making sure I sweep every leaf and corner on the location that i cannot get back to, and sadly several achievements simply did not pop out for me, despite of meeting the terms ( for instance). Bugs with such a short title is just sad, as there is no much things to get broken, compared to big titles on the market with multitude of variable factors. There is a thorn in my side on handling the ending. While it is not rare thing, to save player progress to the certain checkpoint and "travel back in time" after you reach the ending, to be placed just before final sequence, I was very disappointed that I could not travel across the Valley after . With massive part of the map being the dried river, the game begged to be able to finish the side quests or simply sightsee while the water is flowing again, especially that the player is never getting down to the ditches, so mechanic-wise nothing would change. You still travel across the bridges, logs and stones, and just like with the progress on the instrument playing, you receive no reward for your efforts. In conclusion from the perspective of the player, you receive:Quite ruined and not nice looking areas after .No visible reward for the final chapter (that could be achieved by putting some water in the dried river), just roll the credits and we're done. While the game has some unquestionable charm and quite funny moments, especially the Snufkin not giving a **** on some circumstances and having some mild "bad boy" outbursts - via dialog or actions - in contrast of his stoic nature, there is some missed potential with such a rich and vast world of the Moomins. The game has very short lifespan and there is nothing wrong with that. I have enjoyed shorter titles. But with the issues presented above you should totally . Prices of downloadable content is laughable as well in my opinion. Get only the standard game with substantial discount. Get ready for 2 playthroughs if you're a perfectionist. Otherwise I cannot promise that you will feel somehow allured and disappointed in the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend playing with a controller, as the PC controls are ass. But as for the game itself, all in all a fun experience and despite its short length, there's quite a bit to do considering how small the world is. Artstyle also looks FANTASTIC, absolutely beautiful, they nailed the magical Moomin vibe for once and it really stands out from anything else i've played. Finally we got the Moomin game we deserved, i've been waiting for something like this for a long time, as most Moomin games before were those kinda "educational" games for kids, whereas this actually can be called a video game. However, as i just said, it's very short, i finished it in 5 hours, so unless you're a huge Moomin fan like me (and basically every other Finn i know), i'd recommend waiting for a sale. P.S. as a fun fact i remember Snufkin being like my favorite character ever as a kid and i kinda wanted to be him so now my longtime dream came true too XD.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This game... It's very difficult for me to put my feelings into words to communicate how wonderful this game is. Have you ever wanted to wander through Moominvalley while meeting incredible creatures and helping the world? Don't look any further! Your dream has finally come true. It's not just a game, it's the whole world. It's filled with emotions and kindness.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: The art and music (Sigur Ros really hits the spot!) in this game are beautiful. The gameplay and narrative, unfortunately, are not as good. Does a Moomin game really need leveling up, stamina meter and stealth sections? The game shows you the Moomin valley and its denizens, but fails to do anything interesting with them, instead just giving you meaningless busiwork, doing fetch quests and solving trivial puzzles. A cozy and relaxing, but shallow and uninspired experience that conveys some of the beauty of Tove Jansson's work, but none of its sadness, creativity or wisdom.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: It's a sweet little game with a simple control structure - I played on Xbox controller and strongly recommend, as it made it easy to sit back and just chill. The story is relatively straightforward and the only real replayability comes from wanting to 100% achievements/collectables. But I'd definitely recommend it if you've got small kids, at a little over 4 hours if you take your time wandering around trying to find as much as possible, it's perfect for little attention spans.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say? Just a beauty of a game. Really love the artstyle, the story, the atmosphere, the characters & ofc the music. Its like being a part of the books, thanks to the familiar artstyle. Memorable moments in the game, just so chill. I recommend this game truly from my heart, really casual, a bit thrill & overall a masterpiece of a game. I want more of this, there's soo much more stories to tell in Moominvalley, would be amazing with sequels or DLC:s, this truly has the potential for telling more & broaden the horizons, really.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Plays perfectly on Steam Deck.Does a great job of getting across the atmosphere of Moonimvalley. The game play is definitely designed  more for kids (it's very simplistic, and the "stealth" sections don't have a fail state. This isn't a bad thing, I'm just pointing it out) It's short, and like the books and shows, a nice escape for awhile.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Great. True to the source material. Although the plots of individual quests will be familiar to any Moomin fan it's not unoriginal in the slightest. The source material pretty much allows for infinite retelling without it getting too tiresome. Beautiful hand drawn style full of soul. The enviromentalist ethos seems to be conveyed a little clumsily but personally I don't mind as its vague at best and doesn't force it too hard onto the player and most importantly seems to be in line with Snuffkin's character.Every single thing about this game seems meticulously crafted and builds perfectly into the calm yet rich atmosphere,
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This game was really made with love for Tove's art.  I never would have imagined that the Moomins could translate to the world of video games, but this is pretty much pitch-perfect.   It takes much of its inspiration, plot-wise, from Moominsummer Madness, but there are characters and scenes and artistic elements from many different books.  A short but memorable gaming experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: So far an OK experience, yet lesser than I hoped for.Despite the adoring, lore-accurate graphics, the game seems too generic - it lacks the Moomin spirit. I expected it to feel more like the old school Moomin games I played as a kid.The generic gameplay, mechanics and quest types does not come together as a memorable experience to me. Maybe my expectations are too high.Edit: Thanks to the developers for responding to this review.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Like others have said, this was a very beautiful game! If you are a fan of Moomin, I think you will enjoy the game to some degree and it would be worth the purchase. With that said, I do have some criticism:This game is definitely more suited for children, but even so, the game really doesn't let the player do much of the work at all. I feel like it's a stretch to call it a puzzle game. Everything you had to do was laid out for you. Despite the game teaching you the game mechanics (i.e. hitting the drum will move a frog) it will never stop reminding you how to use that mechanic (i.e. every time you see a frog, the game will instruct you to use your drum). One of the best feelings when playing a puzzle game is using what the game teaches you upfront and then being able to put two and two together later on. There are no hidden secrets behind rocks or corners (from what I've found): this game doesn't use previously obtained game knowledge to let the user explore a bit more and find things on their own. And in addition to this, the quests pretty much tell you exactly what you need to do in order to get the desired outcome.But is the story sweet and is the game fun? Yeah it is, but only because it's Moomin. And I like Moomin. Also they did an incredible job at making Little My annoying as all hell. Little sister vibes, Snufkin is stronger than I.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing! Loyal to the original stories but with twist of it's own. Art style is so cute and calming. I have been waiting for someone to make a proper Moomin -game for years and this is it! It felt so hearth warming to interact with the loved characters and they were written so accurate. I can never thank enough for making this game!  Much love from Finland <3
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: 4/10 Cute but unoriginal and unengaging.The graphics are cute, the music great. However, the story is sadly unoriginal: bits of the old animation plots are just recycled and mashed together without much in the way of cohesion. Snufkin's interactions with many of the valley's characters make it sound almost like he's meeting them for the very first time.Meanwhile, the map of the valley is designed like a dungeon, with claustrophobically narrow passages and tiny clearings in a dense forest.The puzzle elements are also exceptionally simple and painfully repetitive. While I wouldn't expect any kind of difficult challenge to be presented in a game clearly designed for small children, nevertheless the game as a whole was just too unengaging to merit a positive review.Nostalgia seems to be what's driving the review score so high for this game. Sadly, there isn't much else going for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: I believe that everyone's money is precious and £16 is for many people a lot of money.. The game's story, idea, and execution is lovely. I just cannot get behind.. people spending their money and receiving a product with a lot of issues.For many, you cannot change the resolution of the game (Mac but I heard some Windows users suffering with this too!), so many users are left unable to get this game working properly. For me? I am playing on a MacBook and the game is a square with massive bezels, the game is completely blurry due to the resolution making the art less than favourable. I can't appreciate the art that I can barely see.. so I have to play on my partner's windows computer which luckily didn't suffer from this bug. I feel this bug may be a laptop exclusive.Additionally the game stutters tons, even with v-sync on, on Mac! It really takes you out of the storybook experience, Snufkin himself behaves at times weirdly (if he stands on a rock I find he sometimes keeps switching direction and can't stop). I will change my review when the game is fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

Excellent graphics, peaceful music, nice puzzles and a wonderful atmosphere. I recommend it to all fans of the Moomins series but also to those who want to experience a relaxing adventure in a charming valley and forget about their worries for a while. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley

_childDocuments_.review: Still not the big, ambient-centric Moomin videogame that I dream but this was cute. Super easy and short (finished in 3.5 hours), a game obviously made for small kids in mind, but its a chill experience and a beautiful rendition to Tove Jansson work that she would probably loved. Mostly for Moomin fans only, but if this is your first time with the franchise I think its a decent start, if not a bit too shallow on parts.
_childDocuments_.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley
