_childDocuments_.review: Taiwanese developer Red Candle Games have already proven themselves as one of my favorite indie studios with Detention and Devotion (two horror games I hold in very high regard), and I was especially happy to see them still push forward with their next game despite the nonsense surrounding Devotion’s *continued* ban from storefronts. Branching out into making a Metroidvania with Sekiro inspired combat no less is quite a shift from their previous works though, and I was very curious to see how a team of their caliber would handle such a different projectNeedless to say, very satisfied with it. Nine Sols is fantastic, certainly drawing from the likes of Sekiro’s brutally difficult “parry or die” gameplay but adopting it to a 2D style incredibly well. It stands out on its own by forgoing a direct posture system in favor of its talisman mechanic (where you instead quickly attach bombs earned with parries to enemies), which gets so fun once your skills open up and makes for some of the most entertaining combat I’ve played of these type of games. The bosses in particular are really cool to fight against, initially seeming like insurmountable walls that gradually get more and more manageable as you memorize their patterns, until you can somehow effortlessly flow against their relentless attacks without even thinking. The final boss for the true ending is especially awesome in this regard, honestly one of the most rewarding I’ve fought in recent memoryBeyond just the combat, it further impresses with its unique “Taopunk” world-building and heavier narrative focus that’s a cut above many others in the genre. There’s not many Metroidvanias where I was as invested in the dialogue and characters quite like this one, Yi in particular was endearing as the main protag, and the story surrounding his vengeful path against the “Nine Sols” he once worked with was really interesting to follow, getting surprisingly heartfelt even. The game’s hub, the Four Seasons Pavilion, is nice too in how it encourages you to keep up with the other characters and watch as it changes in appearance the more items you bring to ShuanshuanThe game’s music is great and the handdrawn 2D art/animations for characters and environments is lovely, mixing beautiful aesthetics with grungy underground sci-fi machinery, and using detailed manga style panels for story moments that further add to the excellent presentationMap exploration was enjoyable too. It’s not really Hollow Knight level in that regard, but has solid variety and was fun to clear out areas looking for chests or optional bosses. Traversal is limited initially but also gets pretty good as you unlock stuff like air dash and double jump for platforming sections. The priority was definitely more towards its combat here, but still well done

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is AMAZING jades have a solid impact on game play and can change how you approach fights dramatically. _childDocuments_.review: imo 9 Sols is the best Metroidvania since Hollowknight. If you like the genre at all, but especially if you like HK you should play it. It has the same tight movement, gorgeous hand drawn characters and environments, subtle environmental story telling combined with engaging characters (more on that in a moment). There are some differences in abilities, but in both traversal and combat they are equally fluid. The main difference is 9 Sols trades the dodge/block-attack combat pattern of HK for parry-counter focused combat. Learning the enemy patterns is both intuitive and rewarding. The feeling of going from drowning to swimming in the harder boss fights is incredibly satisfying. Back to the lore, for once I read all of the lore and dialog as it comes up. I never do that in action games because it takes me out of the flow. Not only did I find all of it interesting enough to stop for, but they also placed most of the lore in very reasonable break points so it didn't feel disruptive.  The "cut scenes" are presented in a gorgeous semi-animated manga(or whatever the Taiwanese equivalent is) style which really lends itself to the overall feel. 10/10 game for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game to bits. It really is an amazing, unique experience. If you're reading this review, I urge you to give the game a chance.What I liked:The story was well paced and I truly became attached to all the characters. The exploration is only semi-non-linear. While you can sequence break, you'll mostly be guided along an "intended" path. I still found it very enjoyable to explore and to backtrack. The wide range of puzzles always kept me thinking, and backtracking never got too stale as I was often surprised with secret bosses and smart level design.The COMBAT is obviously the main focus of the game. I loved figuring out the patterns of regular enemies, and the bosses which often took hours to beat felt satisfying to learn and to eventually conquer. Each boss tested my skills and seeing my improvement was an amazing feeling. (devs please i need a boss rush)Oh and of course, the art and soundtrack are top notch.Response to criticisms:"The intro is too long" It really isn't. It's quite a standard introduction of the world, it's characters, and then a hook to begin the journey. The game has a story and it's going to introduce it properly. Similarly, "cutscenes too long and annoying." The cutscenes are well paced if you aren't rushing through the game. They give crucial and intriguing information on both the world and it's characters. The main reason you wouldn't like the cutscenes is if you aren't playing for the story. Otherwise, they're some of the highlights of the game."Combat is too hard, boring, unvaried, etc." This game is HARD. It has quite the learning curve in the beginning. You'll need to be learning from each encounter and adapting constantly. There's always a story mode if you want more of a steamroll experience, but on standard, you should expect setbacks for your mistakes. If you're finding the combat unvaried, you likely need to explore for side-grades. The combat is about learning and risks. If the game is feeling slow, you likely aren't pushing your abilities as far as they need to be. Complaints of the final boss are a completely joke. It's a culmination of everything you've learned thus far. You'll once again need to learn, improve, and push yourself to find more openings.Actual criticisms:A few of the hitboxes do linger for a bit.Some of the minibosses are paced quite badly. I often joke that one midgame boss in particular has a harder basic attack than the final boss For 100%ers, you can be locked out of certain achievements, and the game does require 2 playthroughs to fully complete.Some QoL and replayability features could be added.Conclusion:This is a good but tough game. Expect complex mechanics that demand your focus and accept the Ls that you'll inevitably take. Exploration is complimented by the level design and the whole game is well paced around the story. The art and soundtrack are amazing as well.Edit: THEY ADDED BOSS REFIGHTS THIS IS THE BEST GAME EVER

_childDocuments_.review: When I first played the demo of Nine Sols, i postulated that whatever year it came out, it would be GOTY. Now that the game has come out, I can indeed confirm - it's GOTY, barring, like, an absolute bombshell of a game dropping.It's, just. Like. Every single thing about this game is so good? The combat is what you come for and it feels -great- - fast, fluid, technical but not overly complicated, and the process of learning bosses and getting good at dodging, parrying, and countering their attacks just feels satisfying. It's the classic Dark Souls "get bodied the first time, become as gods by the time you defeat the boss" except, like, the game actually feels good to play, sorry Dark Souls fans I am not one of youuuu. Mob fights, especially with three or more in a room at once, can get a bit scuffed since the combat system is incredibly geared towards one-on-one fights, and the charged parry is a move I will never like or fully get used to - when everything is react-on-a-dime a move that takes like half a second to use just doesn't mesh well - but these are nitpicks on what was otherwise a beautiful combat system.Movement is great, a bit standard with your usual dash, double jump, etc. and the platforming rarely ever comes into focus save for one big stretch towards the middle, but it's fun enough to move around that I don't -really- care if I'm not being asked to do all that much else with it. Exploration is... a bit limited, as far as metroidvanias go, the game's fairly linear as are its areas but there's enough nooks and crannies with stuff hidden away and a handy helping of optional side-content that makes exploration rewarding all the same.Though even all that aside, the game's biggest success may be in its characters and writing. You don't know how nice it is to play a souls-like as a character who's actually, like, a character. Yi has personality, he has fun and funny interactions with the rest of the game's equally charming cast, the villains are all delightfully hateable and the banter between them and Yi is always a good time, there's more than enough of an emotional pull to the story and Yi's character arc throughout, he's just. Someone you want to help succeed even though his actions are often morally ambiguous. Helps that the lore and worldbuilding is pretty fascinating too, once it does start coming together the further you get in the story.And of course the game just looks beautiful - gorgeously animated, colorful and vibrant locales and quite a solid variety of them - though maybe a bit -too- much emphasis on cold, mechanical hallways that can look a bit too much like each other but whatever, it's fine, it fits the game's lore so I can't be too upset. The music's the only thing that strikes me as... not particularly memorable, more background music than anything, but there's a few boss tunes that stood out - which is probably for the best, since you'll be hearing some of these tunes a LOT.And there's a lotta bang for your buck here - it's a pretty meaty game, maybe not as much in map size as something like Hollow Knight, per se, but way above its level in raw challenge and packed with so much more story content, all of which I was delighted to experience. A good 25-30 hours to beat on standard difficulty, which is juuuuust right for me, I'd say.So yeah, uhh... sometimes a great game is just a great game and one I have no real reservations about recommending? You play as a kitty. Good kitty. Meow meow nya.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m writing this for my fellow weenie hut gamers. My metroidvania loving, Dark Souls hating pals who were drawn to this game because there’s a little kitty in it. A little kitty with a magic, glowy sword and a propensity for tearing the guts out of things. What could be better?! I’ll tell you: a game that doesn’t make you want to stab yourself with said magic sword.That was why, despite falling in love with the character/world design and animations as soon as I saw the trailer for this game, I was skeptical. I’ve gotten better at video games in the past several years. Hollow Knight pushed me to do so. You know what else it pushed me to do? Give up the game for over a year, and put it down for the second time just before the final boss (I like exploring in games, not bashing my head against a wall). I heard this game was hard, and while I could best Ender Lilies, I’m under no delusions that I am a Big Girl Gamer. I love video games, but some of them are just too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ brutal for me, and I want to have FUN while playing them.Then, by the grace of kitty gamer Jesus, Nine Sols blessed me with a gift: story mode. Story mode that you can switch to whenever you want! I didn’t want use it at first, but knowing that it was an option got me to take the plunge. So I did! I started Nine Sols, and my dodge-loving ass immediately had a hard time with the focus on parrying. But it was fine. The world was beautiful, the story had a strong hook, and I was a fuzzy little guy.I don’t know where exactly I was when I turned on story mode. I know I was being repeatedly stabbed in the face by a robot with a massive sword, but honestly, that describes a lot of my experience with Nine Sols so far. I immediately performed better. I could actually parry, where I was just rushing in with blind desperation before. Not all the time, but it was PROGRESS. I’ve seen a lot of talk about the dropping everything at death mechanic (which unfortunately you can’t turn off) giving people a heightened feeling of tension. Maybe it does, but in my case, it just makes me feel hopeless. That not only isn’t fun, but makes me perform FAR WORSE. If I could have turned the soulslike death mode off, I would have stuck with the original difficulty. As that wasn’t an option, story mode was a great alternative.There was another problem, though. After curb stomping the enemy that had given me so much trouble, I found that story mode was TOO easy. Therein lies the beauty of ~DIFFICULTY CUSTOMIZATION~! In Nine Sols, you can change how much damage you take, and how much damage you do. I set the damage I do back to its original value, and halved the damage I take, which is perfect for me. Fights aren’t a cakewalk, and I still die quite a bit, but I’m HAVING FUN. I’m exploring the beautiful world, seeing the story, kicking ass and having mine kicked in return. You can even bring back items to give to your own pet humans!You can look at other reviews for a more detailed breakdown of what you can expect from this game. The purpose of my review is to let people know that, if you’re drawn to this game, but are put off by the talk of intense difficulty, drowning in a sea of Git Gud, that isn’t the impassable barrier it is in most hardcore games. Red Candle Games has a place for us weenie hut gamers. It’s on a dying planet, full of robots who are ready to stab your face.

_childDocuments_.review: Of all games I have ever played in my 25+ years of living, few have resonated with me as deeply and quickly as Nine Sols has. This game is the best game of 2024 and it's not even close. Everything in this game is perfect, from the beautiful hand-drawn art, to the heartfelt story, to the fantastic fast paced combat.This game has the best combat I have ever seen in a game, feeling akin to games such as Hollow Knight and Dead Cells while taking a more defensive and patient approach to the souls-like metroidvania combat system.The game's story is confusing at first, but slowly begins to make sense over time, revealing a deep and enticing story filled with tragedies, sacrifice, and vengance. Without spoiling too much, the game follows Yi as he takes revenge on his former coworkers in an attempt to stop the project he concieved and helped make from destroying the world.The game's heavy emphasis on parries and counters make it feel unique yet familiar, with the best comparison I can come up with being bosses in Soulsborne games. The abilities are all intuitive and fun to use, with some being simple and common in other games, such as double jump and air dash. while others like the Tai Chi Kick and (spoilers) Unbounded Counter make the aforementioned combat exponentally better and more fun.UPDATESince my initial posting of this review, there have been two things I will quickly mention. first, the true ending brought me to tears. Second, this game has been nominated for several categories in the Steam Game Awards, so I humbly request that if this game interests you, vote for it in at least one category.Overall, this game deserves far more praise than it gets. I truly believe this is one of the best games of all time, and is more than deserving of a 10/10 from me. If you enjoy metroidvanias, this is a must have.

_childDocuments_.review: This is Red Candle's third game, but their first foray into the genre, which makes it even more impressive how realised of a vision Nine Sols is. The combat  is inspired by Sekiro but hardly dwells on it; parrying attacks is not how you defend, but also how you unlock your most powerful attack through the talisman system. The same core idea of parrying instead of i-frame dodging is moved to 2D and developed in a vastly different direction, making for an extremely engaging and reactive combat system.Combine that with an intriguing exploration that gives you quite a few mobility options right out the gate (preventing early game slog) and you get an absolutely essental Metroidvania. The strongest point, however, is the story. The game doesn't try to be obtuse and hide vital information in item descriptions or vague environmental clues; the story DOES open itself more and more as the game goes, but you never feel intentionally left in the dark. There are quite a bit of subplots and themes realised - all done with very few moving parts and just only a several core characters that are well written and more complex than they seem. The only downside is that after a VERY strong opening, the game leads you through two of its perhaps most boring zones with an industrial theme and (comparatively) little character. Thankfully, the following locations really bring out the promised "Taopunk" vibe in full force.It's also worth mentioning that the game has a few difficulty jumps. About 20% of my total playtime is due to attempting the same two bosses. The game is quite demanding at times, so  good reaction time is a must.

_childDocuments_.review: Bosses/player damage are way to overtuned to the point where it does not provide much challenge, but rather just adds unnecessary tedium. I think of those kind of games I liked the Messenger approach the most where you can at least control the tempo of the fight if you played aggressively enough (and in most of games with this kind of battle of attrition fights tbh). Here the tempo of the fight again is so overtuned that you have to go through very long chains of parries and animations until you have a reliable action window. This game is essentially a korean MMO of metroidvanias - high precision, high grind, but very very very very low skill ceiling.This, with the lack of the quick restart button and multiple phases makes the whole fights a "high risk low rewards" case. Am I supposed to grind for levels? Should I search for the tao fruits before facerolling bosses? Is it a megaman style combat where I'm missing something essential that will give me an advantage vs certain boss? Dunno, game puts no effort into explaining what it wants from me (I suppose its just a 'git gut' situation), and I dont want to bother either, I am so so so incredibly bored.Core game is much better outside of the bossfights, but it's not even metroidvania, you can only choose between first two bosses, and the rest of locations and fights are complete in a linear fashion, no optional upgrades, everything is linear and railroaded.Vibes and design: This game is a winner.The rest:Exploration and core play: Hollow knight wins hands downChallenge approach: Blasphemous wins hands downBossfights: Messenger, Hollow Knight, Ender Lilies, pretty much everything wins hands down (I would not even mention Rabi Ribi / TEVI that are like godlike piece of art compared to this: . It's not even such a high bar to pass tbh.Parrying mechanics: Grime wins hands down and the Final Performance boss fight is how I would prefer this kind of boss fights to be implemented:  So like 3/10 I guess?

_childDocuments_.review: "Heroes are forged in Agony" ... I Hardly ever write a review but ... I just fell so in love with this game that I forgot what reality feels like for a few days. In terms of how the game handles, you would fare better to expect it to be a 2D Sekiro than a metroidvania. The Gameplay is the best part for me as it genuinely explores Taoism and the philosophy of non doing, you can sense this in the fights, if you approach it in like any other beat em up or metroidvania or action game for that matter and simply do combos or button mash, you will get your ass kicked and most probably won't even win against the first boss, the key here is the art of being calm and keen observation and parrying opponents moves are so very well executed that it just clicks whenever you get a perfect parry. If you want to just experience the story and not want to deal with all this, there is an alternative mode as well called the story mode, but if you choose the standard mode, prepare to be ready to parry and be more observant and defensive. As for the Setting, without spoiling too much, the Taopunk genre is a first of its kind and it really works well. The Characters are really fleshed out (although not that many as in most metroidvanias) and the Story is riveting enough that you forego the addictive gameplay to see what the story is about. All in All, one of the best games I've ever had the pleasure of playing, Thanks to Red Candle. you have found a lifelong patron! and I will be following your works closely and hopefully there are more DLCs or other franchises like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Extraordinary game. Nuanced character writing facilitated by an excellent English localisation, A complex, haunting, and detailed world and story revealed by character conversations and lore from items with interesting designs, a confident, unique and beautiful art style, some of my favourite music in a game ever. Thoughtful exploration of the ways systems and leaders can fail. A morally ambiguous protagonist on a quest for vengeance against antagonists with sympathetic motivations who are nonetheless deeply contemptible.Enemy attacks are well telegraphed, and satisfying to parry. The difficulty is very high, but it feels fair to me. My skills and reflexes are not great, but I've found persistence to be rewarding in learning enemy attack patterns. When I die (which is frequently) it feels like my fault, not the game's. So far (about midway through), the game has consistently added new abilities that keep combat feeling complex and fresh. Changing my strategy with equippables and combat styles has resulted in significantly different gameplay experiences, sometimes providing the edge to get through a particular boss fight I was stuck on. I generally prefer 3d soulslikes over 2d because I find it is difficult to make movement, exploration and combat feel as nuanced in 2d, with only a few exceptions- this game and hollow knight are some of the only 2d soulslikes that feel rich and rewarding in the way fromsoft's games do. Making parry-based combat feel good and responsive is so hard, and it's amazing to me (as with hollow knight) that a fairly small team managed to make it feel so good.Issues I have with the game - There is a story mode, but I do still want a challange, so I wish there were more granular difficulty settings, e.g adjusting the parry window or slightly lengthening the duration the unbounded counter can be held. This is very minor as every time I've gotten stuck, I've been able to eventually move past the bottleneck after learning the boss. Very minor, rare grammar mistakes in the English localisation - this is extremely infrequent and doesn't detract from the overall excellent localisation. Fast travel unlocks late, which is fairly annoying, but fine once you eventually get it. It might have been nice to know early that I would get fast travel later, and I would have put off backtracking. The xp and skill based system is a little weird- I got the maximum number of skill points from killing enemies fairly early, and the remaining skill points can only be obtained through finding special items. Maxing out normal xp in this way feels demotivating, and I wish there was a way to respec, as a particular skill that would be really helpful on the current boss I'm fighting is fully locked off from me- I can't grind for it to help with the fight. Sekiro also had this issue, and solved it by allowing additional xp to be spent on very expensive damage upgrades- something like that would be cool. Linearity - so far the game is pretty linear. This is totally fine, but I wish that when I was stuck on a boss, there was a little more opportunity to go explore somewhere else and get stronger before coming back to it.  Also - I love Shuanshuan. I'd die to protect Shuanshuan. Great job red candle you made a perfect little guy.

_childDocuments_.review: In short: Nine Sols overall was a great game, smooth movement, combat and platforming. An engaging story and art that fits perfectly with the game. The progression felt nice to go through, going through the main bosses had a nice pacing along as you get on average 1 ability per major boss. You typically go into a new area - get an ability halfway through and fight the boss at the end, afterwards going back to the main hub area to look towards the next objective.One thing of note is that because the abilities don't come from the bosses, you can move onto the next area without before defeating the boss, which is nice as without this the game would be pretty much entirely linear.Though there are quite a few flaws, such as the start taking a while to get going, and nearer to the end the areas being unexpectedly short - with normal areas taking around 60 - 140 minutes with the later ones taking around 30.I feel fairly negatively towards how new abilities are obtained however, you end up going up to a save point and then it just, throws you into a tutorial area and you have the ability now. There's no build up whatsoever except for you seeing somewhere you can't get to in the nearby vicinity, this causes a weird "oh i guess i have this now" feeling to it. There's no ceremony to it just happens, and then it's done.My solution to this would be just simply, do it like Hollow Knight or Ori, make an actual build up, put it in the main world and make the tutorials appear the next time you save after collecting the ability.The Skill Tree and levels are interesting to see in a Metroidvania, overall don't have many complaints and think it merges well with the rest of progression. The combat in Nine Sols focuses on parrying, simply right clicking before an attack so you don't take damage, parrying grants Chi that can be used to do high damage moves. Thing I found most interesting about the parry is the imprecise parry where if you time it poorly you'll instead take "Internal Damage" which regenerates into normal health overtime. This allows the player to focus on other aspects of combat instead of purely on parrying.Healing is very limited, with only a couple of healing charges in your Pipe between save points. This is the reason why getting precise parries aren't a big deal as imprecise parries still prevent the largest consequence of taking damage - using up your very limited HP.I don't really have too much I can say about how enemies are as they are greatly varied. One problem I have with the enemies is that, for some reason some of the more complex and punishing enemies are put at the beginning of the game with midway having more relaxed and simple enemies. Late game enemies however feel just, not that fun to fight, as it just kinda becomes a parry fest then use Chi for a high amount of damage and if you let your guard down for a second you pretty much instantly die.The movement in this game is simply put, great, it feels and flows good, you're a tad floaty in the air but works for well combat later in the game. Dashing, wall climbing, ledge grabbing, and rope climbing all really work seamlessly with each other into a satisfying movement system.I personally found the story quite confusing mainly on how there's so many names that have to be remembered, you got the names of the Sols, NPC's, materials, factions and locations that it just sort of overloads the brain with information.Other than that I think the story is quite good, the Asian fantasy/mythology combined with Sci-Fi creates a unique and interesting setting that I personally have never seen done. Without too much detail, the story has the protagonist, Yi set out to get rid of the 9 Sols that inhabit the realm of New Kunlun. The Sols each control a part of New Kunlun such as the greenhouses/farming industry or the repository.Overall, I'd definitely recommend this game to anyone who wants a good Metroidvania to play with it's great combat, movement, exploration and story there isn't really many reasons I can think of that could make it be considered bad, even with the 30$ price tag.(If I didn't mention something, probably means there was no problems with it)

_childDocuments_.review: Nine sols is a metroidvania, souls like game.The game is 2d and everything is beautifully hand drawn. I played this game twice; one on standard mode for the true experience, and one in story mode for a more casual experience. Standard mode; it's how the game was meant to be played, you will be put to the test in skill and a lot of trial and error. But when you push through, the game feels very rewarding when doing every thing just right.Story mode: It lets you tweak how you want to play the game, so for anyone who isn't too good at souls like games like myself you can slightly adjust "some" things in the game to enjoy the story and exploration more. Which is very nice.The games main story was incredible, and the side stories to certain characters had a lot going for them as well. Nothing felt unfinished and everything ended with a satisfying conclusion. Also,I will say this too, go for those collectibles as you play, their are some great moments that come up from finding items.The combat in this game is tough, From the bosses to the small enemies, this game will not go easy on you. It's center of focus is to parry your opponents next move to gain an upper hand in the fight. At first, its a little tricky to get right, but man does it feel satisfying when you can pull off a perfect parry and attack. I will also say, the fights in this game are insanely fun and very challenging. Bosses are so unique and bring such a thrill to this game. The music in this game is something i couldn't get enough of, especially certain boss themes; their music went hard at times. The characters; i loved every single one of them. Their stories slowly being unraveled as the game pressed on just left me wanting to know more. It was that good. Nine sols gets a thumbs up from me without a doubt. It deserves its "overwhelming positive" reviews. The game is fantastic. If you like games that have a challenge to them with a good story, definitely pick this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first playthrough on Standard Mode, and I have to say that Nine Sols has quickly become one of my favourite games of the last several years at least. Yes, it's hard, but the difficulty never feels contrived or unnecessary. The deflection-based combat is incredibly satisfying. The main boss fights are fantastic, as you learn to parry, counter, and dodge every attack in a beautiful rhythmic dance. Notably, the final boss does present a HUGE (but completely fair) difficulty spike right at the end of the game. Nothing before it even comes close to the challenge it presents. It took me dozens of attempts over several days to beat it, but I was ultimately successful. I was never bored or overly frustrated during this process, because I could see my progress as every phase got easier over time, as I slowly mastered every move and combo in the boss's arsenal. Finally beating that boss was more satisfying than any other boss I've beat in recent memory. Much like Sekiro, you have to master the game's mechanics to be successful. You can't go respec into a broken build or farm levels. and you will likely max out your power progression well before the final boss. There is a good amount of variety available with the Jade and Spell Style options. There seem to be lots of viable loadouts, so I suggest just going with whatever works for you. Story-wise, I really enjoyed the narrative and truly cared about the characters. You can tell that the developers put a ton of thought and passion into the game's world and narrative. Overall, I have very few complaints and wholeheartedly recommend Nine Sols.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent, story driven metroidvania with tight, satisfying, clean combat and a dark and enthralling narrative.Story:The story hits hard at the beginning, continues to wallop you in the middle, and hits hard at the end. Many stories of an otherworldly type have a silent, dumb, naive, or amnesiac protagonist that has little context of what's going on around them, as a mechanism to explain the world to the player. This story has a protagonist with strong personality that is highly knowledgeable of the world around them, which allows for a large amount of mystery and intrigue as they react to the events of the game. You're constantly encountering snippets of information that tell you more about the world while drawing you in by raising more questions. This builds up into a satisfying payoff by the end where pretty much all of your questions are answered in a satisfying way.These snippets come in the form of environmental storytelling, written logs, well written graphic novel style dialogues, dramatic comic strips, and short but beautiful, artistic in-engine sequences. The narrative itself is extremely dark, thought provoking, and grey. It's very much front and centre, supplementing the brilliant gameplay, despite the gameplay being strong enough to do the talking for itself.The moment to moment narrative beats are tied strongly to the game's villains - the nine Sols. These characters are interesting, varied, and strongly characterised. The conditions under which you meet them is highly varied and non-formulaic, while also matching their individual characteristics. Insidious ones may trap you, flippant ones may not even be interested in your activities, etc... The boss fights are thematically appropriate and very cool.Gameplay:The game has hard combat and interesting platforming. It mixes tight parry-timing based melee combat with interesting traversal mechanics. It has a story mode for people who struggle more with this type of combat and want an easier experience. The combat feels punchy, elegant, and fluid. There's quite a lot of enemy variety and environmental hazards / constraints that keep it fresh throughout the game. There are a lot of set pieces such as getting locked in and assaulted, doing difficult platforming while under continuous sniper fire, having to be stealthy, or carrying out intricate platforming where the world around you is continuously phasing in and out of reality XDThe core combat is simple to learn and difficult to master, with a grindable, XP based progression system that enhances your core abilities and damage, exploration based upgrades that enhance your health, healing, and crowd control special abilities, and exploration based items of which you can only equip a few at a time that modify your abilities - like the charms from Hollow Knight.There's a lot of story and gameplay incentive to explore the world. The world is also filled with shortcuts that you can unlock after pretty much every major piece of platforming, which avoids frustration. There's also a fast travel system that slowly unlocks for you which is a great quality of life feature.Every zone is thematically unique, often rich in highly disturbing environmental story telling, and characterised by unique platforming or combat mechanics that always feel appropriate to the environment and Sol - such as traps, snipers, lava flows that must be avoided, respawning enemies, disappearing floors, etc...The bosses are hard, varied, and make you feel like a master of the game once you're on your 15th attempt and are dancing around their nuanced attack patterns like a boss. There's no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in the boss fights. They're very well balanced such that there is always a pattern or sequence of moves you can do to dish out damage while avoiding taking any, though actually doing so requires looking for the pattern and engaging with the game mechanics. They're also not as difficult as equivalent bosses in a game like Sekiro, which strongly inspires the combat style as the developers state.Overall:A very stylish, thoughtful, and enthralling game where I always wanted to learn more about the narrative and was perfectly happy to chop through thousands of dudes with my hands to do so. Would absolutely recommend to metroidvania fans, fans of good story in general and sci-fi in particular, people who liked Hollow Knight, people who are interested in east Asian culture (the Taiwanese developer used Taiwanese and Chinese artistic cues for the visuals, audio, music, and theming rather than western references leading to a very unique style for a game of this high a production value), and to souls-like enjoyers looking for their next challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: While your first impression of this game might be that it's a metroidvania it doesn't really suffer from the common occurrences like getting lost or not knowing where to go, or having to backtrack once you get more movement powers.The parry system is fun and done in a way that I think is more accessible to people that might not be used to playing timing centric games. A delayed/late parry will cause some internal/temporary damage to your character while a perfect parry will block all of the damage for example, so even if you're unfamiliar with an enemy or boss you can still make it through on imperfect parries alone. The game also offers a fair bit of customization with how you play and approach the combat with items you find and skills you can unlock.One of my biggest gripes with the game was fixed in a later patch, so if you're reading this review now you won't need to suffer through not having a detailed map before finding the areas chip as that is now unlocked from the start.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game with a high level of polish — one of my favorites I've played in the last decade. It's hard to think of a 2D platformer with better looking art than this. Music creates a consistently ominous mood in the level areas, while the boss fight themes are varied and range from aggressive, discordant themes (Jiequon's) to soaring, melodic string scores (Jie's). Nitpicks: mid-boss fights get redundant pretty quickly, and the writing suffers both from a seemingly poor translation and an overdose of names that are too similar to each other to keep straight — for example "Jie" sounds like a nickname for "Jiequan" even though the two are different characters. _childDocuments_.review: Good game.The bosses are easily the highlight of this. Regular combat is fine, but more strategically interesting than action-interesting. But the bosses, man. You'll go into one and die in five seconds, and the second time you'll survive six. But the thirtieth time you'll perfect-parry every attack like that scene from The Matrix and when you reach phase 2 you'll realise you're still at full health. That's a feeling nothing can compare to. One of the bosses, after beating, I was yelling at his corpse to get up and give me a phase 3. They're good fights!The setting/story is the other big draw. At the start it's just edgy which is fun in its own way, but it gets very emotionally deep as it goes on. And not just in word-dumps, the game pulls off a few tricks to make you grow to love the mascot kid just as much as the main character does. Well enough that it's my favourite hub area in any game I've played.I won't deny — with some of the bosses, after thirty deaths you might need something to keep you going, and that's when the game's aesthetics really deliver. The screenshots should make it clear the game looks pretty good to begin with, but the animations, designs, and the perfect-parry sound effect really keep things good. Especially the last one — much of the game's style is focused in your own actions. Parrying attacks, the cool-guys-don't-look-at-explosions talisman (which is your main source of damage!), the time-slow when you pull out your bow... everything's optimised for style, in a way that doesn't get old. You'll keep doing things because they feel cool to do, and that translates to having fun with the game.Plus there's a great end-credits song, which is always free points.Of course this isn't just a boss rush with story. It's a metroidvania. The exploring parts are... good. They're good! Unfortunately that's all they are, a 7/10 as opposed to the 9-10 of the previous points. You won't grow bored doing them, and the movement upgrades tick the boxes. But you'll rarely get excited finding something tucked away, the area unlocks are pretty linear and you don't get the fun of peeking into an area you can't visit yet, and there's nowhere that ever requires much of your platforming skills. The area gimmicks are good at least. This part doesn't detract from the game, but it's not why you'd play it.Negative points: not many, the game is a polished product. Lightning round: loading screens are too common, it's annoying you can't fast-travel between nodes and have to hop back to your hub then go back out, the mapping system has too many intermediate steps, can be easy to lose track of where you're supposed to go especially in the earlygame, a couple of bosses are easier and only took a few tries when I wish they'd take more. And no boss rush, seriously weird oversight. Let's hope for it coming in an update.All in all this is my current GOTY candidate for the year. And not because it lacks competition.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely amazing experience. Playing style-wise, it is Ori/Hollow Knight+ Sekiro, but this is not to eclipse its originality of the art and combat design, storytelling, and world-building: Unique style of 2D hand-drawn arts, challenging but fun combat with the offer of different styles of fighting, portraying an intriguing world infused  with futurism and Taoism elements, and an absolutely beautiful storytelling which brought tears to my eyes. My only negative comment was about the map and quest navigation in the game as I felt lost a couple of times during the game. Even if the quasi-open-world experiencing is what it is aiming for, if there is a place or a log that shows all the past conversations with NPCs so that I can check what are the hints that I have missed, that would be great. I also wished there was an option for NG+, if it is at all possible, since with the fighting system there are so many different ways I want to try to fight the bosses. Overall, this game was such a treat. Thank you, Red Candle Games.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: Nine Sols has the best combat out of any metroidvania I've played, and is comparable to Hollow Knight in terms of being one of the best metroidvanias I've played period. The characters are great, the artstyle is beautiful, and everything feels snappy and responsive.It's also really, really, really hard. As in "I just finished Elden Ring and the minibosses in the first few areas of Nine Sols are harder than most of the bosses in that game" hard. The game demands incredibly quick reactions and good pattern recognition from the first area, and appears to only get more difficult from there. Fighting two enemies at once is difficult, and any more than two is generally instant death. Even if you love parrying in games (I do!) you're going to get your ♥♥♥♥ pushed in more than once.If you love metroidvanias you'll probably love this game, but you have to know what you're getting into. No shame in turning the difficulty down.

_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: 4.5 hours flew by before I realized it. Once you feel like you've got a handle on the combat, they throw in a new mechanic that freshens it up. If the description didn't sell it, then the combat is definitely timing sensitive. Which makes the bosses such a fun time. They've got their own unique combat style that intensifies as the fight goes on. If that scares you, then the story mode is an alternative that's less demanding. The music is enjoyable, story captivating, and searching for secrets is rewarding. Also you start off with a grappling hook. So, I'd recommend.edit: I just finished the game. I only have one critique, but I would still recommend the game. My issue is the boss fight design. It seems like the first boss and the last boss are the hardest experience, and all the others are less demanding and fluff.         I ended up giving up and doing story mode for the last boss because the rest of the game doesn't prepare you for it. Not to spoil anything but the health and pace of the battle doesn't mirror the rest of the game very well; my damage felt insignificant with very few windows to retaliate. And yea, it is a "get gud" moment, but it killed the enjoyment for me to have a sudden spike in difficulty at the very end just for one achievement. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game and i really love it up until the final boss.  3 phases that are way harder than anything else in the game that does not prepare you is ridiculous. _childDocuments_.review: A tense, brutal challenge that manages to avoid ever feeling too "unfair" or "rage-inducing" (if you come at it with a patient mindset, that is).  The world is gorgeous, mysterious and a treasure to explore, although there is less returning to earlier areas for progression than I expected for a Metroidvania--plenty of chances to do that for optional content, though, so it balances out. The skill tree and jade system are both good (if unoriginal) ideas, but the former often feels too number-crunchy and niche while a number of jades feel useless. Perhaps they could have been folded into one system keeping the best of both? Either way, this is one of my favorites of the year so far, and I am absolutely gonna be playing it again and going for the True Ending soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: It's a relatively good metroidvania, so I wish I could recommend it as I had it on my wishlist since the earliest demo. But, the below combat notes were annoying enough that it made me really not enjoy playing the last third of it, finishing it just to put it down.- Double Jump comes really late in my opinion, but this isn't that big of a deal- The red move counter feels terrible in my opinion. As a hold for 1 second and release mechanic, you're constantly worried about holding it long enough if a red attack comes at you quickly. Something like "attack with parry held down" would feel way better as you know the move is going off, not guessing right before a devastating attack would hit you if you held it long enough or not. - Enemy attack animations where a sword or claw ends slightly behind them registers for a fraction of a second post-attack as if you're walking into the pointy end for fun if you get too close behind them after their attack. - Dodging through enemies doesn't always work, especially on bosses, if you're more than a pixel away. I'm guessing it calculates if you would move more than halfway through their hitbox, and bosses just have bigger hitboxes or something. - Enemies can ready a swing, and even if you dodge through right before the attack, they'll spin 180 instantly when unleashing it. If they spun after the first attack of a chain, I'd get it, but getting hit by the first move by trying to dodge through them is very annoying. - If there are tiny iframes when hit, I can't tell. I've gotten insta comboed by small enemies and bosses alike, especially if there are lasers I get knocked back into like the theater duo boss.

_childDocuments_.review: I really really wanted to like this game but no matter how much I throw myself at it hoping it’ll click I can't help but find myself getting increasingly aggravated by just kind of annoying game design that does nothing but punish the player for being bad at the game. I'm more than fine dying in an encounter a 100 times over because I'm still bad at the game, I'm fine with that because I want to get better and beat that encounter, what I'm not fine with is every time I die having to walk back through sometimes several screens worth of enemies and traps just to get back to the point where I died. Not only does this just kill any drive I have to play and kill any momentum I had because of it I'm constantly at risk of losing jin and money slowing me down even more. There's a lot of other little things I personally really didn't like whether it's the game taking close to ten hours to give me a fast travel, lots of enemies feeling like sponges, the map having next to no useful markers, lots of little pointless cutscenes or the lack of I frames when hit for a lot of attacks that should really have them but the short of it is I just really didn't enjoy this game unfortunately which really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks because the game has some absolutely beautiful art and the lore and story seemed super interesting. in all honesty it's another game I wish I could leave an “in the middle” review for because I can tell there's a fantastic game under these issues I have I just personally couldn't get past those issues. Maybe the game just isn't for me there's clearly many other people who love the game and won't consider anything I've said an issue but if you’re someone like me who doesn't enjoy frequent backtracking and lots of annoying little issues id avoid this game or at least wait until it's on sale. Hopefully someday I'll come back to this game and leave a more positive review.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best metroidvania I've played in years. Now before you buy this keep in mind that the combat in this game is not like hollow knight or messenger or most metroidvania. The combat relies HEAVILY on the parry system so if you're not a fan of sekiro or lies of P refrain from buying this. Parry is your best friend and dodging is the friend that you talk to once in a while. One of my favourite aspect about this game is that the bosses fights are immaculate. The music is kinda nice too.Long live apemen.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: Most fun I've had with a metroidvania since Hollow Knight. The main gimmick Nine Sols have that elevates it from its contemporaries is the parry-centric combat. There are two types of parry ala Sekiro, if you time your parry perfectly, you take no damage, if you slightly mistimed it, you'll take some recoverable damage, though you can't die from imperfect parry. Both types of parrying give a resource called Qi, which is where things get fun. You can use Qi to dash forward and put a bomb on your opponents that explodes after a short delay, and if you have the right upgrade you can hold down the Qi button to do even more damage. The experience of perfectly parrying every single enemy's attacks, dashing past them, and then walking away while they get blown to bits is pure dopamine, no matter how many times you do it. Aside from this, the game is also incredibly well animated and has a pretty unique aesthetic that combines cyberpunk with traditional Taoist symbolism, aptly named Taopunk. Nine Sols' weakest point is probably the metroidvania elements. The game is fairly linear despite how interconnected each zone is, and while the zones themselves are good, there aren't a lot of them. Rewards for exploration kind of suck too, early and midgame it’s mostly just cash, with all the good upgrades being back loaded into the last half. It should go without saying that the combat more than makes up for these deficits, however.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a really great metroidvania, the combat is amazing and the parry system works well. It is very story focused but the story is good, but the endings were a bit of a let down. All the main bosses were really unique and fun to fight. The side characters were great and each area felt distinct. The artstyle is top notch and the same goes for the soundtrack. I loved the home area and how it changed throughout the game.Enemy variety was kind of lacking, there's like ten enemy types with minor variations of them. There were a few bosses that were definitely way harder than the rest of the game especially the final boss. Probably my biggest gripe with the game is that you can only parry the direction you are looking unless you are in the air, this made some attacks feel really cheap and I didn't even realize this was a mechanic until the end of the game. I thought some hitboxes were broken but it was because of this mechanic that I thought that.It's definitely up there with the greatest metroidvanias but with a few minor issues8.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: I am delighted to give Nine Sols my strongest possible recommendation to anyone. As a fan of Sekiro and Hollow Knight, Nine Sols so perfectly takes inspiration from both of those to make a truly wonderful game. I have not yet completed the story as of writing this, but being the majority of the way through I feel now is as good a time as any to leave a review. All of the boss fights (to this point) are uniquely challenging and memorable, the OST and art design are absolutely gorgeous, and the combat is so buttery smooth. The parry mechanic is the bread and butter of this game, and you will be punished over and over again until you've mastered it. The parry mechanic is more forgiving than Lies of P, but only slightly more punishing than Sekiro via the internal damage mechanic (temporary damage taken from missing a parry, but can be recovered by perfect parrying, unlike NG Lies of P). This game perfectly fits the needs of both the Hollow Knight and Sekiro communities who are in desperate need of a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. I don't understand the bad reviews suggesting that the combat is unpolished and wonky when it is clearly not true. I have never felt cheaped out by the game. Almost every death I took was deserved. Some of those boss fights are among the most satisfying, coming from this genre, even more so than hollow knights. The exploration feels satisfying while having great level design in general. Now, the only nitpick I have with it is that for the most part it's pretty linear. I personally enjoy that more than looking around the same areas for hours trying to find the way to go. Hollow knight in comparison had a way more complex and incredible map layout while also having multiple ways to play the game. While Nine Sols lacks a bit in that sense it makes up heavily for it with its combat and also its story. Music  is amazing too, everyone loves that in a video game.Also, the Old boy homage was the highlight for me! I had a big grin the whole way through, haha!Played on standard mode. Finished the game at about 85%.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of 2D indie games like Hollow Knight, Dead Cells, and other Metroidvania's, but also like Souls-like games, this is for you. Very block/timing focused, very challenging. Combat is very satisfying, upgrades come in at a good pace and game never slows down enough to get dull. Music is great. Story is dark, interesting, and has a good mystery that still hasn't fully shown itself 13 hours in so far, looking forward to completing this. Also runs perfectly on the Steam Deck.Only complaint is that UI elements occasionally fail to communicate exactly where you need to be going. Many times I backtracked or wandered around the map aimlessly. Not sure if it's things that are lost in translation, but some sort of log with objectives would help a ton with this game. Make sure to keep an eye out for the '!' on the map, always check for those.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: Came here from the beautiful artstyle and interesting setting, stayed for the amazing gameplay, characters, and compelling story.This is my 2nd Metroidvania that I've ever played, and it's outstanding on all levels. It became one of my favorite indie games of all time and one of the best games I've played in 2024.The combat is fast-paced, smooth, and satisfying to master. Every ability that the game gives you is viable in any way in terms of exploration and combat. Some of the jades can be hit and miss in terms of viability, but it allows for room for experimentation with how you want to build your character.The bosses are very well designed in terms of visuals, mechanics, and personality/lore. The story, without any spoilers, is really good, and the pacing is well laid out. It kept me hooked from the beginning to the end.I know that the difficulty can be really hard sometimes, but if you look for openings for attacks, utilize your abilities, and practice the parry mechanic, you can overcome it! If you're really having a hard time, there is a story mode difficulty in which you can adjust the amount of damage you want to deal or how much damage resistance you want on yourself. I highly recommend this game, if you are a huge fan of metroidvanias/games that are challenging but yet satisfying to beat (similar to FromSoft's games and Hollow Knight) or just everyone who wants to try something new!Side Note: As of this right now RCG is now added Boss Replay/Boss Rush game mode and ported the game to consoles and added to XBOX PC Game Pass lineup. I highly recommend to all of the console or game pass people out there to try this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! The beginning can be a bit confusing, as it sends you all around the map, but things come together nicely by the end. The platforming and combat design are a lot of fun, although I had to get used to constantly parrying instead of dodging. The last boss and true ending were a blast! Overall, 4.5/5.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: Doesn't quite evoke the incredible sense of exploration and discovery that other metroidvanias provide but this game has the most incredible bosses out of any 2D game I've played, and is really only rivaled by Sekiro and Lies of P in that regard. If the bosses were a bit trickier they would probably be at the top (they're already plenty difficult, but a boss rush and harder version of each fight for masochists like me would be much loved)
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: I just played four hours of this metroidvania game.I am very impressed!It seemed obvious from the very beginning that the game would be able to deliver quality graphics in a hand drawn style, which it absolutely does. Very early in the game, expectations of a traditional metroidvania story setup are subverted by unexpected plot twists, leading into quite captivating world building and story content that is good for the genre. Then it turns out that the gameplay is pretty great. The combat system is a soulslike system with great rewards for people willing to learn the parry system, but you can get by with ambushing, brute forcing, dodging, and applying special skills in various situations as well. I do not parry in the Dark Souls games and never loved Sekiro due to the focus on unforgivingly difficult parrying, but I tend to parry in this game due to good telegraphing of enemy attacks and good balancing of the risks and rewards of parrying. Exploration has been open ended and often quite tense in the best possible way, due to sparse placement of respawning points, in a way that reminded me of the original Demon's Souls.The only problem with the game I could point to is an interface issue that should be fixable. When browsing shop lists, the information shown for the selected item inexplicably lags behind when you move up or down the list, for no good reason. The game is not verified for Steam Deck, but works great on my Steam Deck OLED, although I could easily increase the sub HD default resolution to 72op while maintaining a perfectly solid frame rate.I am looking forward to making serious progress in the game during our national holiday in Sweden in one more day, but I can already easily recommend the game for fans of the metroidvania genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: I see a lot of reviews calling this game a masterpiece. I was sceptical at first because I've been burnt by this sort of praise for a game before. But rest assured, this is no exaggeration. The soundtrack creates an ambience perfectly fitted to the uniquely stylised animation. The game play is incredibly responsive and in conjunction with the move sets of the monsters and bosses, can almost put you into a state of flow. This is all topped off by an absolutely captivating story of pain and sadness and love and loss. Genuinely, from the pit of my soul, this game is a masterpiece. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: Difficult. Polished. Simple. Engaging. A solid souls-like in another form.-Difficult - Punishing but every problem has a solution and every engagement a learnable pattern-Polished & Simple - No bugs, no overly sophisticated features or actions, knew what it was supposed to be-Engaging - Story was fascinating and characters deep. Probably could have added more meat to the story instead of souls-ing it because I was left wanting a little more structure to the chronology and places but it was still quite good.
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: *Update*- Post game, 100%'d review - idk if anyone will read this or not, I just need to write down my thoughts.Sad this is over, the final boss was a blast, the ending(s) broke me. Yet smh i'm desperatly hoping and praying for a continuation.The final fight was challenging and once you win and even redo it again (did it 3 times) it feels SO good. The music, the sols' themes and Yi's theme are absolutly phenomenal. I had to buy the soundtrack on steam as well, its full of gems.I took my sweet time to play the game (around 35+h), it does feel a bit short but there is just no downtime. I'm not good at Souls games but with perseverance it is doable 100% (played on normal), for those that want to chill more there is an easy mode, that from what I heard, is really good. At some point in the game, there will be a point of no return, have no fear, if you do in fact pass it you will be able to go back to that point after beating the final boss. Allowing you to 100% the game in a single go (and do the final boss few times for all endings).The story, themes and characters are brutally excellent and I think the hard hitting moments and the more "fluffy" ones do balance themself pretty well, a lot is optional (or quickly over) too if you're not into characters and relationship development (why).If you care about Yi and each npcs that form your circle, you will be in for a roller coaster of emotions. For your base to become a true home is one of the best feeling this game gave me.The combat is tight and feels right it took time to get used to but I had a lot of *click* moments, and there is a lot of thing that you can do to improuve Yi's abilities. Honestly the sekiro/parry system mix with metroidvania is chef kiss.The style and animations are also phenomenal and deserve the biggest praise, mixing taoism and cyberpunk aesthetics is not something you can find everywhere, and here it is gorgeous, from the backgrounds to the panels type cutscenes arts, it really is a beautiful game on that front as well.I will say it again now that I completed the game, the pacing and the discoveries leading to knowing and understanding the truth is impeccable.There are some questions unaswered, leaving to interpretation and as the game theme fits, it can be clear, that all questions do not need or have answers.Even if I desperatly want them with a continuation. Red Candle games, hats off to you.------------------------------------------------------------------*former incomplete review (did it just at the point of no return)Absolutly incredible, I do not want it to end. I did not finish it yet (but very close) and I gotta say it is one of my favorite games, period.The world, the characters, the music, settings and style all well executed and pulled off. And the story is beautiful yet tragic, the pacing and how you discover every little bits of the truth is so effective and clever.One of the best, if not THE best metroidvania/souls-like/sekiro(new) combo.I will keep looking at that Indie developper from now on. Red Candle Games, you cooked hard, thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, the game is not bad. _childDocuments_.review: - Smooth battle experience and very Sekiro-like. This game encourage you to parry rather than dodge, and after putting hours getting the sense of parrying, you'll be starting to enjoy the game. Besides, you will still hear the sexy sound of crash between swords even if you're sleeping. - Friendly game modes. For hardcore gamer, picking general mode fit your preference; while for those who just want to make their like easier, the game also provides easy mode where ATK and DEF are adjustable. With this mode my gf kill every boss with less than 5 dies... lol- Breathe-taking Music. The background music of several boss fights are very astonishing, deeply linked to the boss itself and also making you more on the vide to beat the boss.- Many cute kitties.  - Too little guidance in the first half of the game (though, still much compared with Hollow Knight). _childDocuments_.review: Beautifully crafted game with compelling characters, story, and game play.  It also rates very high on the frustration scale.  Something like Hollow Knight meets Elden Ring, be prepared to die hundreds of times as you go through unforgiving boss battles that require continuous precise timing as you slowly chip away at their health and various phases.  If that doesn't dissuade you, Nine Sols is incredibly fun and rewarding. 5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: This game is goated as hell, very difficult tho so if your idea of fun isn't struggling against a hard boss for more than 30 minutes until you finally get in the zone and have a wuxia style over the top back and forth with the boss and beat it then this game won't be for you, the exploration is pretty good, it's not as good as the all time greats but it's also not bad by any means, the platforming and movement is fluid satisfying and fun, the only way i could think to improve it is give the sprint more speed, as it stands it barely feels like you're going any faster, but so far it's probably my second favorite movement system in a metroidvania right after metroid dread, the combat is fun, responsive, quite fast and has many possible responses which is important to keeping a combat system fresh, it is definitely the highlight of the game, it really feels like you're playing through a wuxia duel with the more complex bosses once you get them down, this is the new standard for good metroidvania combat, i beg the devs for a boss replay feature i wish i could fight these bosses some more
_childDocuments_.name: Nine Sols

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. I'm not going to write much, as I'm sure you can find it elsewhere. _childDocuments_.review: As description said, it is a sekiro-like game, expect to be difficult (for me only the final boss was hard) and parry-based combat.The game is also story-heavy (for a metroidvania) and it is great! _childDocuments_.review: Nine Sols is an amazing game that leaves an impression that few games can. The story will draw you in emotionally and keep you hooked all the way to the end like a wild roller coaster. I sometimes struggle to find game lore interesting, but Nine Sols is a major exception. Nine Sols weaves story and lore together in a way that compels the player to seek information not immediately presented to them and the knowledge gained each time feels rewarding. The payoff of this combination is a high-stakes tale in a world that feels like it lives and breathes right in front of you.The gameplay can be demanding and requires developing some careful coordination and muscle memory, but will never present unreasonable challenges. The moments when you do start to understand an enemy's attack patterns and overcome those challenges is highly rewarding. You will feel like you can suddenly see and understand the numbers in The Matrix tear your foes down. 10/10 without a doubt and I am hungry for more.

_childDocuments_.review: Post 100% Edit: It's a rough slow burn, but its a nice gem. Post Ending Edit: The ending boss require you to have a really damaging build, preferrably all skills unlocked and most of the charms collected, because if you won't - you'll be stuck with whatever you have on you. Expect to get really bruised if you try to push yourself in this game, despite looking like Hollow Knight and wearing Sekiro inspiration on its sleeves it does not reserve itself to give you the breather room or options to deal with the enemies. ➕ Cute character designs➕ Really swift gameplay and story introduction➕ Interesting Blocking late parry trade system akin to Street Fighter chip damage style➕ Varied gameplay set pieces and enemy encounters🟣 There is not much room to actually enjoy its difficulty, its hard. It's not mechanically difficult but gameplay limiting difficult, you are tight on money, tight on XP and resources and you don't really have that many options when approaching enemies🟣 Despite being crowdfunded and having a 2+ years of development it lacks a bit of polish here and there, some animations feel unfinished (Edit: some animations got patched actually), some item descriptions need better translations and some cutscenes could really use a Skip or Cancel option (e.g. the Hacking sequences are not cancellable nor safe to use, it could really use some of that Cancel button magic).🟣 No beastiary or lore codex for its world. No quest logs ☹️🟣 The story is serviceable, but a bit rushed with its reveals.➖ A lot of the enemies feel like concrete slabs compared to your damage output, even if you follow the game's way of [Parry - Place Charge on the Enemy - Explode it], it will take a while to kill enemies. The player damage scaling crawls really really slow, and some bosses having Two or Three phases (some bosses can regenerate health indefinitely!) and one hit kill strings just make you feel miserable. First 2-3 hours of this game is pure torture, the game really pushes you to your knees before providing you story based upgrades (e.g. a Charged Attack or an Airdash).➖ Despite touting sekiro mechanics, i am not aware if there's a way to attack enemies poise. Your parry attacks won't stun enemies nor deplete their poise. The only way to stun enemies is to either break their shield with a charge attack or with a Remote Charge (by wearing a certain Talisman/Charm). I dont think the devs should have pushed their game marketing into Sekiro territory.➖ Most of the Skills and Talismans (The Charm system) are reduntant and don't really offer any difference to the gameplay style, most of them provide your character with some stat boosts for a really high price usage requirement and nothing much else.If you are not a fan of High Risk - Low Reward hard games, then your best bet to enjoy this game is to either cheese it by farming gold and XP to buy upgrades or to employ cheap safe tactics of dealing damage. Trying to take risk through the game by using dash i-frames or constantly parrying enemy attacks is not worth it - majority of the enemies and bosses have long attack patterns, regenerating health, lack of stun stagger windows, multiple phases and third party environment assisting their bloodlust towards you, don't push your nerves.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best metroidvanias ever made. Almost every encounter and boss was difficult, but fair and forgiving. Nine Sols didn't just borrow Sekiro's combat, but also Sekiro's design philosophy; every boss seemed like an impossible mountain to overcome, but the grueling process of learning the patterns led to near-flawless victories at the end. There is only one playstyle, with upgrades to different aspects here and there. The game demands mastery of it. You simply have to get good. What really surprised me was the quality of the story and storytelling. Much like Sekiro, the story is about the end of age and those who'd cling to it, wrapped not in Buddhism but in Taoism, something I knew nothing about before the game. Thankfully it explains everything you need to know without hiding necessary in text logs or item descriptions. The protagonist is flawed, fleshed out, and his character arc is great enough to drive the story. I was engaged the whole way through his revenge-plot-turned-redemption, tying into the Tao and the nature of self-improvement. How one can achieve immortality through selflessness and the love of those to remember us by.Hollow Knight weeps to be honest.

_childDocuments_.review: Like I'm sure a lot of people did, I came to this game looking for a metroidvania fix while I waited for Silksong to come out. Initially, I was coming to the game looking for an experience similar to Hollow Knight. There are two similarities: the metroidvania map exploration format, and the fact that you're playing as someone shorter than everyone else. If you're looking for a game to compare it to, you'd find a comfortable comparison in Sekiro, but a slightly more apt likening might be Lies of P. Both have mechanics centered around deflecting attacks in tempo with your enemies, but Lies of P allows for weaving dodging more easily into the mix. Similarly, Nine Sols challenges you to navigate your own way through the patterns of enemy attacks. Establish your own rhythms, find what works for you. There's a lot of different approaches to every enemy and boss, so one can really feel free to develop a combat style within the combat style the game sets out with. The game is extremely well paced. Exploration is the key to increasing your power, as long as I adequately looked around I never felt the need to grind at any point during my play through. Each new area, like any good metroidvania, forces you to learn new tricks and develop your skillset to meet new challenges. Each area feels different, even if there are some repeated enemy designs. For me, the primary highlight comes from the bosses. The bosses in this game are AMAZING. It may take a few attempts, but once everything clicks from their moveset to the range of their attacks every fight begins to feel like a dance. There's this amazing flow and impact each attack has, I just can't quite put into words how good the boss fights in this game feel. Some are better than others of course, but none really stuck out to me as bad. I loved the experience this game provided. The music, the atmosphere, the story, I really had a fantastic time. I came looking for something to tide me over until Silksong came out, and I ended up finding one of my new favorite games.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic Metroidvania for people that like good, difficult combat. While the music, art, and especially setting are wonderfully polished and unique, the story is good, and there is solid platforming and collectibles... the combat is the real selling point. If you loved Sekiro this game is pretty much a 2D version of it, with its own unique mechanics, but ultimately a heavy focus on timed parries and taking advantage of openings. Heavily Hollow Knight inspired (like most modern Metroidvanias), but it brings enough unique ideas and polish to the table that I can honestly say I hold it in the same high regard.Be warned the game is fairly difficult and there is a noticeable difficulty spike, especially for the final boss, but it isn't done in a frustrating way, and certainly feels rewarding to complete.

_childDocuments_.review: First time I've ever wanted to review a game, writing a few hours after letting the ending sink in. This was actually the first metroidvania I've sat down and completed in it's entirety (and will be going for 100% achievements soon). A phenomenal game start to finish, the combat mechanics and platforming do more than enough to make the experience enjoyable for the entire playthrough, it left me wanting to go back and start another playthrough immediately! The game is fairly difficult (the final boss especially), but if you can deal with a bit of trial and error in true metroidvania/soulslike fashion, then you'll enjoy the experience. I only have a few minor things I want to see added to the game. While I'd love dlc to get more out of this game and it's world, the base game is amazing as is and doesn't *need* anything added to it, as the gameplay and story are very well fleshed out. All I think it really needs to be perfect to me, is the ability to reload to certain story checkpoints to rematch specific bosses or complete quests/achievements you may have missed or messed up, and a boss rush mode to refight these amazing bosses easier (which they have shown interest in adding a boss rush mode after their focus on porting is done from what I've heard!)The atmosphere is extremely unique and beautiful, and the soundtrack was amazing (instantly added multiple songs to my personal spotify video game ost playlist). You can feel how much heart and soul the devs and artists involved in this game's creation put into it. Cannot recommend this gorgeous work of art enough. 100% recommend, easily one of my new favorite games of all time!
