_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - 3/10, tolerable story,  poorly designed game. Not worth your time or your money.South of the Circle is a walking sim that follows a linear story. The story is fine, I guess, but all the interactive elements are a detriment to it and it should not have been released as a video game.The flat colour low-poly graphics have a charm to them but are far from amusing enough to justify strolling at a snail’s pace to admire the view. Also there are a lot of visual errors and models constantly clip into each other.The story takes its sweet time taking off but eventually it does get decently captivating. I found the romance plot pretty generic but I wouldn’t necessarily call it bad. The characters are believable and well written. Except one. I could not bring myself to connect with the protagonist. Although a grown man, he would often behave like a nervous teenager which frustrated me as I was trying to keep the bloke alive. It is difficult for me to empathise with a character who keeps getting flashbacks to mild childhood struggles while in very dire circumstances during which he should be focused on surviving.I understand the game is trying to send a message (especially a feminist one), as it is not very subtle about it. This is fine when paired with an entertaining story, but in the first half when the narrative is still pretty “meh” it does feel like I’m being lectured by the devs.The biggest flaw of the game are the “choices”.  Instead of regular dialogue options you choose emotion based responses (confident, enthusiastic, shy, etc.). It is an interesting concept but executed terribly. The actual dialogue tends to barely if at all match the emotion you picked and often I struggled to get the main character to respond as I intended. Eventually I got to a plot point where I saw myself disagreeing with what my character was saying, regardless of what choices I picked. That’s when I realised that you don’t get to choose the protagonist’s responses, you can at best influence the tone in which they express them. Having the main character consistently say the opposite of what you want to say is very frustrating and makes you feel like you picked the wrong choice, which could have been entirely avoided if the devs didn’t dangle the illusion of choice in front of you for the whole game. At one point the game gives you a gun and implies you can shoot a person with it. Out of desperation to have any influence on the story I tried to kill the other person but the devs made it impossible. No matter how hard you try, the sights move away from the target.If the game was just the story then maybe, just maybe I could see myself recommending it at a discount, but all the vague and meaningless choices the game makes you believe you have make it a more frustrating than enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: So, this is my first negative review ever. Never expected it to be in a game that I mostly enjoyed.The game is beautiful, artistically. The characters are compelling, the voice acting GREAT, and the parallel storylines work really well in the context of someone stuck alone in the freezing cold, starting to allucinate. However, I take extreme issue with how the illusion of choice is implemented.Throughout the game, you are  (I tried sometimes to not respond, but I wasn't allowed; with one notable exception ) to choose the emotion that the main character feels whenever he intervenes in conversation. I did not expect these choices to have too much of an effect in the overall narrative, but I did expect them to shape the story in some way. However, I was dissapointed. In spectacular fashion. Spoilers ahead:If you want a visual novel with some choices which actually produce (small but significant and rewarding) changes in the overall story, with a great visual style, go play Pentiment. This game, I cannot recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a bit hard to decide on but I have to recommend this game if you are interested in the type of narrative games and such. Right of the bat, South of the Circle's soundtrack, plot, voice acting is outstanding. The struggles of insecurity, guilt, and bigotry within the environment and politics of academia portrayed is one of the most relatable and realistic I've ever seen. That being said, South of the Circle commit two of the worst crimes in its designs for a choice-based game. The most frustrating part about this game is that South of the Circle design the in-game choices as ambiguous as possible. Whereas other choice-based games at the very least give you one word to describe what the character is going to do. South of the Circle's choices are offered in the design of circles with different colors representing different emotions that the character will deliver the message/choice. More often than not, the character has said and done stuffs that I didn't want him to because the choices offered are extremely ambiguous. Not only that, it has kept me strictly playing "safe" by choosing the options that are shy and reserved because I didn't want him to say anything stupid at all. Spoilers:

_childDocuments_.review: At its heart, this is an interactive movie. And not a very good one at that. I’m over 90 minutes in, and so far, the entire plot involves 1) a guy struggling with his PhD thesis and 2) a ridiculously drawn-out love story. I was bored out of my mind. There is a 3rd story about a guy searching for help in an arctic tundra, but it takes a back seat to the others.The game lets you make dialogue choices based on your preferred emotion, but it doesn’t matter at all. Just for fun I let the game run itself by not pressing any inputs, and when the timer runs out, the game makes a choice for you. The response is the same, and nothing changes. You can literally take your hand off the controller/keyboard, and just watch.Well… not quite. There are other “gameplay” elements such as driving a car down a straight road, and moving a guy through the snow. Zero fun. I’ve played through lots of interactive FMV games, and walking simulators, but I’ve never experienced one where so little stuff happens.I can only recommend this to people who enjoy narrative heavy games with no consequential choices, along with a very slow burn plot. Otherwise, avoid. I stopped at 100 minutes in.

_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished South of the Circle, and I am, without a doubt, irredeemably frustrated.I'll preface this by saying that I actually put interactive storytelling above all else, and I believe that the medium is more relevant today than ever before. But the fact that this... this... this story had to be created as a game... well, that's indefensible in my eyes. I simply don't know what motivation, other than EU funding, warranted turning this story into a game.Make no mistake, I was deeply drawn in from the beginning of the story, and not just because I, like the protagonist, am called Peter and I work at a university. Not just because I am deeply concerned about the Cold War and all that it entails. Not just because it deals with serious issues, such as the office politics of the university, putting work before all private matters, or even the importance of dialogue. It is because it was supposed to be a game and it has not become one. I mean, I have played several "walking simulators" and I was perfectly fine, even moved by many of them.The graphics are captivating, with their stylized, flat, thirties-style visuals (WPA tourist posters came to mind). I loved the lifelike, sensitive and eloquent acting of the voice actors, I really felt I was in the middle of a real radio play. I loved every theme, from climate change to the feminist undertone of the work to the understated characterisation. But where does the player's role come in?Because it's a brilliant idea that the dialogues use various icons to that serve to 'direct' the protagonist, like a stage play. I'm also in favour of raising dramatic stakes by removing interactions at key poins even if the player wants to achieve something. But to have any interaction from the beginning to the end of the narrative be completely superfluous and weightless is a bridge too far. I cannot fathom what the player has done to be punished so, during this otherwise friendly three and a half hour 'gameplay'.  I can't see what prevented the makers from giving even the smallest decisions at least a bit of impact. And I really don't understand why the interactive medium was needed at all. For it is a great story that beautifully illustrates the difficult choices a compromising man makes, how we are bound by toxic masculinity even in the rareified air of Cambdrige academia, how we are at the mercy of our hearts and how we crave love and appreciation, and how the two can be at odds. But I will still not forgive myself for having to suffer through every interaction of South of the Circle. As much as I'm all for playing through the most narrative, cinematic, Davidcage-y video game possible, I wouldn't throw a stone at anyone for merely watching South of the Circle. Because while in a Telltale game I feel like every decision I make has weight, in a Quantic Dream game I'm involved in the plot, and in any indie adventure game there are exciting puzzles, dialogue trees, and tension, here in this game, that's sorely lacking. All of it.I can't help but feel that the use of the interactive medium in South of the Circle is completely unjustified, and I'm deeply annoyed that I have to press buttons to get to the end of the story, which if anything is what I've been conditioned to do since I was young. I suppose it could be said that this game is about how all your choices are inherently constrained, that physical, official and spiritual survival requires sacrifices, and that free will is the first of these sacrifices, but then again, you could have designed decision structures so that the player doesn't feel tortured all the time.So, in conclusion, I just want to say that digital gaming as a medium has every right to tell whatever story it wants to tell and I don't... okay, I moderately regret buying South of the Circle. That said, I maintain it's a textbook case for how narrative games can be diverted from their roots in play. And that is a cardinal sin.

_childDocuments_.review: So first things first, the biggest issue I had with the game was how it wasn't much of a game. And I'm not complaining about the visual novel aspect of it — I'm perfectly fine with text-based games and whatnot, but South of the Circle incorporated various interactions that made no sense and rather annoyed me as a player. For example, holding W or LMB to keep moving in a certain direction — there is no "playing" involved in that, so why not let me just click to the objective to move? And then there were minor associated issues like characters clipping through terrain and corners, being unable to turn your camera fast enough (since your character movement controls the camera) — all that is making you wonder why you give the player the tools to control the character /that/ much when they gain nothing from it. It doesn't make you feel involved in any way, it only bothers you to keep your finger aimlessly on the button for while trying to tell you that you're supposed to be enjoying the picturesque sights.And god, there are many. The game is visually stunning, I just think it could do with better interaction mechanics.Now on the subject of the story, the writing, dialogue are all great. Characters are well-presented, but — many will probably see this coming — the choice aspect is just off.So just to make sure we're on the same page here, you don't choose the specific lines but the emotions (to a varying degree) your character puts in them. Meaning if Peter is cornered to make a decision, he will have to, say, either agree to play along in a more panicky way on the one hand, resolute on the other. One major issue here is that there /does/ seem to be the intended way to progress through the story, and with Peter being the less masculine type (not putting this as a spoiler since it feels rather obvious from the first moments of the game and I love it), the less confident choices feel much more convincing. The bold ones feel misplaced, off — they're kind of along the lines of "confident complacency" at best.Which brings me to the next point, the overall plot. Which is where the spoilers definitely come in — do not click them unless you've completed the game:I realise this review's a bit weird, giving it thumbs up while mostly criticising it, and I do think that this has perhaps been rushed. Nonetheless, it's a great narrative experience, so if you dig these sort of games and aren't disillusioned to expect vital choices in this genre, it's a great pick — especially at this price.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: A meticulous, understated, and memorable little experience with excellent voice acting, atmospheric set design, and a solid soundtrack as the glue. This is essentially an interactive movie: a "walking sim" with very minimal exploration.There are many choices to be made but they are not in service of the plot. To be clear, this is not a "choices matter" game, at least it's not how choices are usually integrated into video games. Rather, your selections define your memories of the story. It is purely about roleplaying. But it's also about chance, because it's never clear how your choices—geometric shapes and colors—are going to manifest. Or maybe you do know how it's going to have to end? As the greatest statesman of our age has put it: "them's the breaks".People who like this kind of stuff will enjoy this game. That said, I feel the concept wasn't pushed as far as it could go. There's a purposeful restraint to the whole story that does right by its decidedly restrained characters but ends up skin-deep and rushed. Still, the designers are onto something here and I hope they get another opportunity to work on a fuller, richer game that builds on the 's potential.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: South of the Circle is an interactive fiction game set in the period of the Cold War. It is developed by State of Play who also made Lumino City. We follow Dr Peter Hamilton, a lecturer at Cambridge, who is working on his academic paper about the clouds and climate science. He meets Clara, who is also a lecturer at Cambridge, and together they continue to research the topic of his paper. Together, they discover radiation in the clouds and the source of the radiation is emanating from Antarctica.Peter is given the opportunity to go to Antarctica to continue his research however, the plane crashes. Floyd, the pilot, hurt his leg in the crash, so it is up to Peter to go in search of help.Throughout Peter's journey, the story transitions from the present to the past. Choices he made, his relationship with Clara, his family, and co workers.It is fully voice acted throughout and the quality is excellent. The story is compelling and it hooks you in from the beginning.Since the game is mostly interactive fiction, game play is minimal and almost complimentary. It involves making decisions about how Peter reacts to situations by his emotions. The responses range from shy, concerned, enthusiastic, honest to strong. The main character is moved around with either WASD or a controller.Keyboard and mouse can be used, however, I did find that using a controller was more intuitive and relaxing to watch the story unfold.Pros:* Excellent voice acting* Compelling story* Music is excellent and cinematic * Achievements (easy to obtain if achievements are checked prior to playing)* Trading CardsCons:* No mid level savingUnfortunately no mid level saving was quite a problem and it was such a shame to see how this affected the game, which took me just over 5 hours. Saving is done automatically by an icon in the top right corner and was sometimes difficult to see because of the white background of Antarctica. Although not quite sure, but I am assuming that most of the time it saved automatically after a "scene".Rating: 8/10 (would be more but no mid level saving - luckily the story is compelling)

_childDocuments_.review: "South of the Circle," set against the mid-Cold War era of 1958-1964, opens with a plane crash that foreshadows a fate already scripted. The game boasts a top-tier narrative, though its gameplay—limited to choices that ultimately don't alter the story—may divide opinion, resembling more a cinematic experience than a traditional game. To me, a game can be a vessel for storytelling, and in this light, "South of the Circle" shines brilliantly.The narrative unfolds through the protagonist's memories, which, like anyone's, are fallible and colored by personal values. The recurring interrogation scenes with the professor highlight this, as the protagonist repeatedly revisits his past, grappling with whether he stood up for Clara out of conviction or if it’s a reflection of his regret over betrayals.The player's choices seem inconsequential, underscoring the theme of individual helplessness against the sweep of historical currents. "South of the Circle" poignantly explores the inescapable societal forces that shape our inner shadows, silently steering our thoughts and actions. The predetermined ending, symbolizes the inescapable pull of the era, casting us onto the jagged rocks of tragedy and pain, revealing the subtle societal influences that quietly mold our identity and choices.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: The game plays out like a Film with time lapse of the present and past revealing parts of the story being told. You play as Peter, a shy/timid man who is a professor at Cambridge University. He is stuck in Antarctica trying to find rescue. as you try to find rescue you keep having flashbacks of Peter's life when he was at the university. Which led him to meet Clara. she's brave but also dismayed. The flashbacks story unfolds with Peter trying to write a paper for the university.(which isn't going well) Also the cold war is starting to kick off with protests of nuclear disarmament, possible threats from Russia. while at the same time discovering love. The gameplay is simple: you walk around and you click on objects to interact with this is also how you select the optional dialog. although you have optional dialog like offer games, These don't change the outcome of the story. But it doesn't take away from the feeling of being invested in the characters. And that comes down to the writing of the characters and the dialogue that goes on with them. There is a sense of realism and life in the different characters. which is really accomplished by the voice acting. The graphic design is very well blended with shapes, colors and shadows. The soundtrack is very much in tune with the mood of the story. all of this works very well together. to make a solid game. Now the biggest downside to this game is how the ending unfolds. Which I can't cover without containing spoilers.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: A love story against the backdrop of nuclear non-proliferation/disarmament? Hi, yes, it's me.Ok, so maybe this game is a bit of an easy sell for me, but South of the Circle is a beautifully stylized story-rich interactive novel. I say novel because it is less of a game and more a QTE narration of the love story between the two main characters during the Cold War. If you think the game looks pretty and the premise/storyline looks interesting, and you don't mind a more laidback experience, then this is a fabulous title to pick up. If you're looking for something heavily action-oriented, you will likely be disappointed. My only complaints about the game are that the QTEs don't seem to have a huge (any?) impact on the end of the game (though they do affect the immediate dialogue) and occasionally the camera angle veers into an awkward spot (though this normally only lasts a few seconds). The game took ~3 hours to finish and an extra hour to grab the two achievements I missed on my first playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has interesting thematic elements. The sound design is excellent. I even like the minimalist style. But it's irredeemably clunky in the way it switches from story element to story element. I hate being forced to control a character for 30 seconds with only one possible progression option. I'd rather watch a movie which is liable to be edited better or work in C story and other narrative elements. I can see people, especially narrative crafters, enjoying it as a study, but the lack of traditional gameplay is glaring.

_childDocuments_.review: : 3/5South of the Circle is a charming and well-told narrative experience rather than actually interactive game.: 4/5While I had some reservations about how the player interacts in the story, it was solid and definitely an order of magnitude more interesting than usual video game narratives. The characters are well thought out and the plot is interesting, using the back drop of the cold war to tell a character drama and mystery through the eyes of completely normal people. I really liked how the story touched me several times, especially by the end, when the conflict welled up between the main character's past and present.The pacing is too slow however, and an hour could definitely have been cut off while preserving the intended narrative.: 1/5 There is little gameplay to be found at all here, and what there is is rather just an excuse for the story to be sold on the Steam storefront instead of shown on a video site. It also felt very much like that the few decisions the player makes have little impact on the narrative, though they do change how some characters react to each other - this was at least satisfying to some degree. Sometimes it was impossible to tell what the characters were gonna say with the choices presented, and I would sometimes feel angry that the main character tells a completely different line than I intended when selecting a 'feeling'.: 5/5The game has a beautiful coherent artstyle, and a soundtrack of very high quality, hitting the precise notes to enhance the story at any moment. My only shortcomings with the presentation is a large number of instances where characters clip uncomely through the terrain and objects, and the faces of the characters were, while loyal to the artstyle, a bit too faint and don't convey emotions very well.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 6/10South of the Circle is a journey that pulls you in from the get-go, thanks to its captivating story and breathtaking soundtrack. The voice acting adds layers of depth to the characters, making you truly feel immersed in the experience. But as the tale unfolds, you can't help but feel a twinge of disappointment. The story, while intriguing, ultimately feels like it's missing something, leaving you wishing for more meaningful choices and a more satisfying conclusion. The narrative's cinematic qualities and stellar soundtrack make it seem like it would have flourished on the big screen, but alas, this is the only medium it can be experienced in. Still, there's no denying the unique charm of the game. It's flawed, yes, but it's also undeniably captivating. If you're willing to overlook its shortcomings, there's a lot to love here.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the visual style of the game and the "behind the scenes" design prototypes. But the game itself was more of a frustrating experience. No matter how you act, the outcome is the same and the story develops very slowly through constant jumps into memories. The most annoying element is probably the slow and clumsy movement, especially since you don't have any option to explore the environment and just need to keep pushing the button to move from point A to point B.I hope the developers will create a game in this visual style with a more interactive gameplay and more "open", explorable world. _childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure what to expect when I bought this game, but I've been pleasantly surprised.The writing, dialogue, and voice acting are all excellent. The art style reminds me of an old cartoon strip with a modern twist, which is really appealing. The only thing that slightly bothers me is the eyes—they're a bit too undefined and could use some color. They come across as a little creepy, though that might just be my personal preference.The writing, settings, and dialogue fit the era perfectly. It took me a minute to get the hang of the dialogue choices, but once I did, it felt intuitive. The vehicle controls, however, are a bit of a nightmare. If you've driven the Mako in Mass Effect 1, you'll know what I mean—it's like that, but worse.I haven't finished the game yet, but I'm really enjoying it. If you're looking for a relaxing day with a good story in an interactive novel format, this game is both engaging and calming to play.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: South of the Circle is actually a very intriguing and absorbing game, I didn't expect that.The developers were clearly inspired by "Firewatch" and "What Remains of Edith Finch" and for some reason I thought this game would be like Firewatch but in Antarctica. I forgot the trailers promising us a story about relationships and careers, set in 1960's cold-war Britain. The voice acting is great and the story is well-written. It was like actually watching a movie!Yes this Interactive Fiction is a typical walking simulator with minimal player agency but it is far from a simple FMV.Your choices do matter, but only in the context of the relationship.This is not a multiple-choice game with branching paths and endings, come on now.It all serves to immerse you and to deliver a gut punch in the ending.It is a beautiful game, the minimalist art style was competently used to give us an inoffensive 3D picture and convey the story well.Even the snowy regions did not flashbang blind me with all that white, unlike other games (like planet Hoth in SWTOR).This game is asking you to feel through it, asks what you would do.Stand by your convictions and principles or sooner or later break down after being chipped away at by friends, society and culture.I was steadfast in my beliefs and morals, yet the ending shows that it is not about us and this is not how the story went.Peter and Clara's relationship was beautiful to observe.If you did not understand the ending, it might feel like female schizophrenic gas-lighting. Short and beautiful game, with a bit confusing and cannibalizing liberal/feminist message about the cold-war 1960s.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game was beautiful. Magnificent. Gorgeous. Spectacular. Nobody half-assed a single element in this game. Everything from the music, the voice acting, graphics, scene transitions, pacing and plot, there was passion behind this. I can't believe I haven't heard of this game any sooner. The gameplay is similar to telltale, however that's not an actual issue. It doesn't let you choose which line to say, rather what emotion that comes out of you. At first it was hard to understand, but the more I was talking, the more I understood what each symbol meant. And even if you choose something different than someone else, everything just flows perfectly. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fa-nominal job everyone did.Pros- Music makes a scene 10x better when used correctly, and in no instance was music misused at all. Even the changes in music, either mid scene or transitioning, was a joy to hearVoice acting- top tier in my opinion. It felt real with the breathing and the breaks the voice actors took.Camera- In no scene did the camera feel out of place. For example, in the plane when the Russian and Floyd are talking, the focus is on them since Peter is sleeping. It's those little details that makes something so powerful yet surreal at the same timeSetting- Every set wasn't fully detailed like an arkham game for example, but it didn't need to be. From the snowy mountains to a city in the UK, it didn't need a whole bunch of details in the first place.Cons-I can't really say anything bad about the game. I mean 2 things that bugged me was the movement and the decision making.The movement I had to jerk a bit but it wasn't to the point where it was annoyingAnd the decision making. Again I liked that it wasn't sentences, however it did stump me here and there. But to get around that, just look at the timing and see when one option comes into play so quickly versus when another one does 1-2 seconds later.Overall: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ play this game if you want a rich story. I nearly shed at the middle. Fantastic job 11 Bit Studios. Fantastic job.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly decent story for a game and the art style is nice but there is no game in this. All of your choices in conversation seem inconsequential and the few times you get to move in the world there is literally a single path to follow. It might as well have been a TV series. The character movement through the landscape is, although clearly motion captured, occasionally shonky with limbs passing through objects. This could have been a stylish chose-your-own adventure but sadly its a single linear story that is slowed down by waiting for a button press after every sentence. Very disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, we all know what this is and what to expect: This is an animated movie where you occasionally click on the screen so you feel a bit more connected to the narrative. Call it "walking sim", call it "narrative experience" - whatever.I like to play these games occasionally, there are some interesting settings games like these explore and if you take them for what they are (=narrative experiences) they can be quite charming. The problem with this one is the ending. I don't mind downer endings (hi there, "Know by Heart") , I don't mind bitter sweet endings, I don't mind ambiguous endings (hello there, Pathologic) but this one is just muddled. In the last 2 minutes the narration pulls the rug from under you and tries to explain the twist in a sentence or two plus it leaves the rest completely unresolved. I loved the narration, the presentation, the music and the story but those last 2 minutes really left a sour taste, not because it did not give me what I wanted but because it felt so rushed, muddled and overall unfulfilling. If you want to experience a game that does the narration part better, try "Know by Heart" by Icepick Lodge. Any devs who want to dabble in this genre: A clean execution on well trodden paths is better than trying to risk everything for some narrative cleverness to make your work "stand out".
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I know it sounds unhinged, but you don't play this game for the gameplay, that is pretty basic and unremarkable. You click and hold circles, and you move around, don't get it if you don't like narrative games. This is a game you play for its story, and it's definitely worth it. You're following the same character in two different times in his life, alternating between scenes almost seamlessly. The different timelines have very different moods and settings and you don't have time to get "tired" of it before you switch to the other. They do join at the end too. Visuals are good, great voice acting, nice music, can be completed in about 3-4 hours with all achievements too. Yes, the ending is a bit odd, but if you give it some thought, it makes sense. Anyway, worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Finally found a new one! Kind of calm, mature, narrative game with fascinating story and extremely well voice acting. Genuinely I don't care anymore whether the story branches out to 10 different endings based on my choices. If not, well.. I still enjoy the ride and feel engaged deciding for the character. 'South of the Circle'  was a gem for me after playing mediocre games for so long.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Promising start but ultimately underwhelming. It was a nice concept, and I kept playing to see how the story panned out. The interaction is a bare minimum which is great if you just want to focus on the story. 6.5-7 out of 10. Recommend with reservations.The story in itself is quite simple, a bit predictable but certainly emotional. It could have really gone places but felt like it only scratched the surface of the characters and their relationships. And then all the choices you make don't seem to matter at all. Then at the end you are suddenly thrown an unreliable narrator twist which could have added a lot of depth and become a bigger feature in the game, but instead it just funnels everything back to the story the creator wanted to tell.    So the choices I made did not matter and it turns out the character behaved differently to the character path I thought I was shaping. And it crumbles down right at the end. Ultimately an unsatisfying way to finish the story, and quite rushed. Which was a shame because there was a lot of potential and a really nice concept but just never really delivered and then took over the story at the end so all your character choices meant nothing. Technically a few gliches throughout the playthrough. File verification/validation helped some. Other times character got stuck on a screen with no camera movement or any place to go - just pointless clicking everywhere. Quitting and reloading reset it and it progressed fine and presented a different path so no idea what happened.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Another outstanding game from State of Play. They're out here again with an amazing presentation for their games. I knew that they could do visuals and animations well having played Lume and Lumino City, they're previous games. But here the acting just elevates the presentation and story to just incredible levels. The combination of the voice acting, body language, and what little facial animation there is just works. It worked so well.Speaking of the story, it's absolutely lovely. It just sits with me and how it ended. At first I was puzzled and a little frustrated by the open nature of the ending. But after reflecting on it and basically spoiling myself online with the other choices, I think I love it. I liked that it dealt with themes of memory, love, and suspicion. And all of that was told well by the great pacing, dialogue, and actor performances. I really love how well this game told it's story.A few quick positive notes. I like the choice system they made here. The story itself is fairly linear. There is only one plot. But you can influence the moments in between by choosing the emotion of the lead. Doing that just adds a nice personal touch to the story telling and changes up some of the emotional impact of the scene. Another fun note is that the soundtrack is beautiful. Glad it's in my library now.Overall, I love this game. And I hope for more storytelling like this in more games.EDIT: I forgot to add that there is an e-book of the game's script as DLC for this. Provides a nice bit of context to that ending and the story as a whole

_childDocuments_.review: It's a visual novel with 2-3 options in dialogues, choices do not matter, regardless of decisive or unconfident answer the dialogue only varies in 1-2 lines and eventually, it leads to the same ending. I don't take it as an interaction game, the ending gives hope but still fogged, the idea is more clear.Playing this game reminds me of A Lion's Song by Mi'pu'mi Games and the Movie The Theory of Everything. All present a period in the last century in which women are looked down even in institutions of higher education. Their talent is not appreciated or respected and their names are to be removed if a report wants to be published or taken properly. What hits me is the man in the game actually insists on keeping the girl's name as a co-author, regardless of all the opposite voices, knowing he might lose in the effort he has put in the past 3 years. However at a certain point the girl said I thought you were different from other men and they broke up. Misunderstanding or fact, this game talks about unfair treatment of a woman  like (1) the girl gets the chance for higher education and care from her father only because his brother died in an accident (2) women get higher education but people only care how fast they type (3) once they get pregnant they might lose job. There's been progress in women's rights over the past decade but still much to be done.Player is constantly jumping between time, the places remind the same but you'll meet different times and people. Come to think about it after beating the game, it might be the guilt, or the regret the man kept in mind when he's desperate and in the last few hours. The ending is interesting as it seems all are tricked by their own country, all about politics and it is never clean. If you look today it's still the same. It's an okay game, can be slow sometimes, not much highlights but alright for the time and price.

_childDocuments_.review: South of the Circle is a profoundly engaging interactive narrative set in the Cold War era. I admire the game's narrative structure, particularly its adept unfolding of the story, seamlessly transitioning between past and present scenes. It features intriguing, ambivalent characters and delves into profoundly human questions surrounding memories, opportunism, the power of life choices, patriarchal inequality, academic complexities, and, of course, love. If you enjoy this type of game, then this is definitely for you. I had a truly great time with it!
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: South of the Circle takes players stands out within the visual novel genre with its distinctive art style and captivating music. Overall, the game offers an experience that is both enchanting and, at times, a touch perplexing.One of the standout features of South of the Circle is its simplistic yet incredibly unique graphics. The game dares to veer away from the conventional visuals seen in its contemporaries, opting for a style that is refreshingly minimalist. However, at times, this distinctive approach might feel engulfed by negative space, leaving players yearning for more substance in certain scenes.The true masterpiece lies within the game's musical score, which is nothing short of a roller coaster of emotions and seamlessly ties scenes together. The harmonious blend of the soundtrack is easily the most enthralling element of the narrative.Unfortunately, the weight of story choices doesn't translate into meaningful consequences. This could be a source of disappointment for those seeking a more impactful decision-making process. Furthermore, the ending leaves players with a sense of vagueness and dissatisfaction, a lingering feeling that contrasts with the otherwise positive impression the game leaves.Despite these minor drawbacks, South of the Circle remains a small gem within the story-telling genre. Its innovative approach to visuals, combined with its emotionally evocative music, creates an ambiance that is both rare and captivating.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: The cinemtagraphy is some of the best I have seen in a game. The story about sexism in higher education was powerful. However, it did not seem like my choices that I made in the story had an impact on the trajectory or ending of the game, which was a big dissapoinment. I am glad I played through it, even if I felt like it would be better suited for a short film format.

_childDocuments_.review: You are a climate scientist, studying clouds. This story flips back and forth across time, forcing you to face childhood demons and adulthood choices alike. This game is not about clouds, nor climate change. Hope that created some curiosity without giving any of the game away.A story about how men define themselves, no, how they let their work, define them. And place it first, before love itself. How they are so stupid to place love of their country above even love for the only woman who noticed them. Yep, it's a graphic novel, and this one lets you make choices of a sort, choices which all in the end may well come undone. International politics and a secrecy act destroys as much as it protects, lies. No, the Russians, are not coming, it was all a lie. Travel from Cambridge to the arctic circle, in a rather more deadly game that appears at the surface.Reminded me a little of The 39 Steps in it's plot and pacing, and Firewatch in the artwork, and pretty much every walking sim in the gameplay. A very well told story, not remarkable, just well told.If you enjoy this story, you have to check out this list of similar stories

_childDocuments_.review: When I started playing, I thought it is a walking sim. Linear, story-driven, get bits and pieces of story line from surroundings. No, it's not. Surroundings are empty (except first found item being a story spoiler). Then I thought it is an interactive movie. Choices, different routes, charters. No, it's not. Visual style is anti-movie, no details, no facial expressions, no scene depth. Then I realized that it is a book. Not an interactive book. Just a linear audio book with crappy illustrations.This "game" has zero gameplay. I've completed it in 3,5 hours. One hour of this time is main character walking (or driving) forward with nothing happening. Other 2,5 hours actors reading their lines. And sometimes player needs to push some buttons so the "game" can tell when player falls asleep.Maybe the story itself is thrilling and engaging? No, it's not. The romance between "strong female character" and sissy (main character) is predictable to the last bit. The other part is a "fight for your life" trip in the snow. And it's awful. Two men crash on a plane in Antarctic. Pilot broke his leg, so another one (main character) needs to bring help. He speaks with the pilot several times offering to get back to him, but pilot refuses. He does not need food, shelter or warmth. Once MC encounters a map. A paper map with a ship printed on it. And two adult men seriously discuss that this ship is their salvation. A picture of ship printed on a paper map. Really?Won't go deep into politics. Cold war bogus. Free democracies, evil soviets. Evil like in Red Alert, but not so funny.Spoilers ahead. Don't buy. Waste of time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes about 4 hours to complete.If you're the sort of person who loves literary novels and/or games that are really more movies where you occasionally have to push buttons, you'll love this "narrative experience".  This game is visually striking, has wonderful music, is very well voice-acted, and has an engaging story.  There's a bit of wonkiness with the models sometimes, but I didn't encounter any bugs more serious than minor visual glitches.  But...it's really not much of a game.  There are no puzzles to solve, no real choices to make, no resources to manage, nothing that makes it a game.Given 11bit's other offerings and the look of the game, I was expecting something where the point was to make difficult choices that had deep impacts on gameplay and/or the progression of the story.  But in this game, your choices are more illusory: you can choose whether to respond fearfully or angrily to someone else's demands, for example, or whether to introduce yourself by your first name or your title, but it doesn't seem to do a whole lot to change the overarching narrative or even the immediate conversation (I have done only one playthrough, ).  I was enjoying the game until I figured out that nothing I was doing was really changing anything--it is engaging visually, narratively, and musically.  I don't think this one is for me, but I think the people it is for will like it.

_childDocuments_.review: A really wonderful game/playablemovie. 3 hrs for a full play through and it kept me entranced to play it all in a single sitting. It's an interesting story with an interesting style, match cutting back and forth between earlier academia and the desolate snow that forms the background of the game art. The lightly textured art  still creates excellent backdrops for the very minimal gameplay - a mixture of walking forward and dialogue QTEs, but what really carries South of the Circle are some of the best voice performances I've heard in a game. _childDocuments_.review: BLUF: This is a novel in game format that was a relaxing way to spend a Sunday afternoon.No spoilers here: Welcome to a trip through memories to see how you got here. This is not my usual genre of play, but it was in a bundle package, so I played it cold without even looking at its store page. Pleasantly surprised, I spent 5 hours and completed the story.  The intertwining of the plot lines flowed naturally and did not seem out of place. Exploring the environment seemed to have been useful story-wise beyond getting all of the Steam achievements. The artistic ending is thoughtful and may not be everyone's cup of tea. _childDocuments_.review: South of the Circle is an interactive story game, where you make decisions in an intricate story that switches between two times in one man's life. The story is interesting and engaging, and the choices range from small, insignificant talking points, to large, very difficult decisions about love and war with seemingly very high stakes.Unfortunately, those very decisions are where the game fell short for my playthrough specifically. The story itself has some requirements on what happens, which limit what outcomes can come from your decisions. The game leads up to a large decision near the end of the game, where I personally made an honest decision that went contrary to the game's story. This ended with a section that felt unfair and forced the outcome I explicitly chose not to make. While this made sense in the context of the story, it felt like I was robbed of some agency and as though my decisions never really mattered.Nonetheless, the story that the game gave is still super interesting and unique, and poses questions that were extremely interesting to consider and watch play out. While I do believe that this story makes the game well worth playing, the shortcomings in the decision tree made the emotional impact fall flat at the climax of the story, making it not quite worth full price in my opinion. Others may make different decisions than I did, and therefore may be significantly more emotionally engaged at the end, so your opinion may very well be quite different from my own.

She helps him find his passion. The times are against Clara, when I next play Peter had better keep his promise. A beautiful and expansive world, great art work and music. I loved the game. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: South of the Circle was a very compelling adventure to play. Its story is very interesting, very well constructed. It gets a little bit repetitive and slow-paced a little bit before the ending of the story, and the ending is quite intriguing. There are no gameplay mechanics, its a simple point and click game, so it`s what you need when you just want to enjoy a new experience without getting any frustration. The graphics are very impressive and beautiful, the music is fantastic and perfectly adapts to the atmosphere of the game. It`s a good 9/10, I would really recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: "It could be ours, though. This beautiful thing. If you wanted it to be."An absolutely captivating little narrative experience. If you're one who has issues with games not having enough proper GAmEpLaY to warrant their existence then steer far away from this. You're in for the ride and making only slight emotional adjustments to the dialogue and intentions. This is not a choose your own adventure type thing nor are you making choices and affecting events much. It's a lightly interactive narrative experience, and a wonderfully carefully crafted one. Gorgeous use of music and camera angles and editing, this has some of the best cuts and scene transitions since Virginia and Sifu. Perfectly naturalistic dialogue and delivery, the characters are believable and human and I found myself engaged on both narrative levels. If you were bored (or angry) with games like Firewatch or Virginia or Oxenfree, then no, this is definitely not for you. But if you get swept up in narratives in video games, it's a lovely and mature and surprisingly delicate experience. Go in blind. Let it surprise you.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: South of the Circle is not a very good game and I cannot bring myself to finish it. Its story is uninteresting and its gameplay sucks. I do quite like its art style, but art style alone is not enough to carry a game. The gameplay consists of watching cutscenes, occasionally holing forwards, and making dialog choices. However, instead of choosing based on words or sentences, you choose colours and shapes, which makes it feel like I’m not actually making choices at all. I know at the beginning it shows how certain colours and shapes represented certain emotions, but I just don’t feel like it matched up well. It’s a system that sucks and makes it feel like a movie where I’m forced to click to continue rather than something interactive where I’m actually making choices. If the story were good, I would be fine with this almost nonexistent and tedious gameplay, but I really just don’t find myself caring at all about what is happening.

_childDocuments_.review: More movie than game, however the choice of emotion still gives some depth to the dialogue. Not a choose-your-own-adventure game, but totally worth the cost. I haven't finished the game yet but at this point even a bad ending wouldn't change my thoughts: get this game, treat it like a film, and you'll enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, South of the Circle was something tried to be like interactive, story-rich game with beautiful visual narration. But couldn't be a mix of them, interaction was low and pointless, story wasn't rich and didn't even had a end. And if you don't have a story, what is the point of the visual narration? We only left with beautiful.Yes, it has a very nice aesthetic, colour palette, film grain and scenery. I agree, by visual means, it is very good and pleasant watch it. I also like the "graphic design" of the objects and the choices.But this is not a game. This is not a "narrative experience". It is just a narrative. Choices doesn't matter, gameplay sucks. It is something between a walking simulator and cutscenes, still it could've been better. The repetitive build of the game bores you after a while and you know what is gonna happen. Storywise, I simply don't get it. Our character is smart enough to find a theory and become a professor at Cambridge, but stupid enough to don't understand international relations and office politics. If our choices didn't matter why did we even played the first game. We didn't even get a ending, just build for the current events and then nothing. Some scene changes were abrupt and by the last hour I just played it to finish it.I mean I am shocked by the ending, I didn't expect it to be this bad. This is one of the games I feel like I wasted my time, because it was a cliffhanger, but there is nothing else.Hope you can manage to develop your weak parts and create a good game using your visual style.

_childDocuments_.review: The main thing you do in the game is having conversations. But you can not choose what to say, instead you choose a symbos that represents a "mood", like "firm and strong" or "happy". But there is no telling what your answer will be. And a lot of times you only have one button to press, so no choice. _childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game. It worked flawlessly on my steam deck, so for those with a steam deck this does work well without any issues.The game itself was an excellent story with beautiful graphical style and fantastic voice acting throughout.If you enjoy linear, story driven games then you will enjoy this. _childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: I would argue that linear games with illusory choice are exactly as valid as games with branching decision trees and open worlds. The narrative exists to move the player's emotions. To do that, it has to be tightly paced, and directed, like a movie. A lot of the reviews say that it is basically an interactive movie. I don't have a problem with that. This game is gorgeous, has amazing acting, and a tense, tightly written story told through flashbacks and set pieces. I absolutely love this.
_childDocuments_.name: South of the Circle

_childDocuments_.review: I like the effort, but the final product just isn't there. The game is too short, the story confusing at times and the gameplay itself consist of never-ending autoscroller cutscenes. Sometimes the writing feels a little too woke for my liking as well.
