name: Little Goody Two Shoes
detailed_description: Dreaming Maidens: Pocket Mirror x Little Goody Two Shoes In these narrative-driven horror adventure games, you will find yourself using your wits to solve puzzles and explore rich environments full of charm and wonder. Your choices will determine your fate - try to discover as many endings as you can to uncover the truths to mysteries long forgotten! This bundle contains: Pocket Mirror ~ GoldenerTraum: a modern RPG puzzle horror game that will have you playing as a young girl who, deprived of her memories, finds herself embarking on a dreamy and frightening journey of self-discovery. Little Goody Two Shoes: a fairy tale horror adventure game with a dark twist. Follow Elise, an ambitious girl determined to become rich, as she attempts to escape her humble life and finds herself getting more than she bargained for… Little Goody Two Shoes Deluxe Edition Take Little Goody Two Shoes’ music anywhere you go with the Deluxe Edition! This bundle contains: Little Goody Two Shoes - a fairy tale horror adventure game with a dark twist. Follow Elise, an ambitious girl determined to become rich and escape her humble life in the village of Kieferberg. Official Soundtrack - The official soundtrack for Little Goody Two Shoes features 64 all-original tracks from the main game, including 3 unreleased bonus tracks. PLAY THE DEMO NOW! Try the demo today and enjoy the starting section of the game, where you explore Kieferberg and its mysteries, romance its bachelorettes and get a taste of the terrors of the Witching Hour... About the Game There once was Elise , a vibrant and ambitious young lass with a big dream – becoming filthy rich. In spite of this, the stars didn’t seem to have reserved our protagonist much fortune in life. Elise, who came from humble beginnings, had no choice but to spend her days away assisting her fellow neighbours with menial tasks to make a living. One day, Elise discovers a pair of beautiful shiny red shoes buried in her backyard – what a surprise! Bewitched, Elise embarks on a fearful journey that pulls her closer and closer into the heart of the mysterious Woods! Will Elise risk it all for the sake of a dream come true, or settle for her humble day-to-day life? The ending of this tale is yours to write… Little Goody Two Shoes is a horror narrative adventure game, set in a hand-painted fairy tale environment. There are 10 possible endings to fit your choices and actions in the game. But there’s more than meets the eye here, as you must also manage multiple aspects of Elise’s life in the village to stay alive. Remember, all decisions matter in this story! During the day, you will need to strengthen Elise’s bonds with her fellow villagers and work to make a living by playing fun minigames. But once the moon rises, make sure to keep Elise fed, healthy and sane in the multiple encounters with deadly foes as she makes her way further into the Woods. Kieferberg is a small and devout village, which means Elise will need to carefully navigate her relationships with the villagers to avoid arousing suspicion of witchcraft and be left to die in the Woods as punishment. At night, Elise can roam around the Woodlands, a mystical and phantasmagorical realm where enigmas and deadly enemies await as she tries to uncover its secrets. Through a limited day and night cycle Elise will need to carefully manage her needs if she wants to stay alive to finish her tale. Get struck by Cupid’s arrow and fall in love with the charming bachelorettes of Kieferberg. In this all-female cast of romanceable characters, unlock dreamy date scenes and storylines for each of them.

_childDocuments_.review: No game has stirred such conflicting feelings in me and shown me how limiting Steam's thumbs-up/thumbs-down recommendation system is. With that out of the way, I want to give this game its merits. The audiovisual presentation is second to none, matching 90's anime aesthetics with storybook illustrations to bring an unquestionably beautiful fairytale to life. The story manages to keep you on the edge of your seat—how far will Elise go to achieve her wish? What is she willing to sacrifice? In that sense, it manages to make you want to play further to find out. It is a pity, then, that the overall gameplay is absolutely miserable to go through. Don't get me wrong, here and then I do not dislike some difficulty in my games, but some sections made me wonder if anyone outside of the development team actually beta tested it.The day sections are fine. The minigames have a bit of a learning curve, and Kiss the Rat might require fiddling with the max FPS, but overall, it is fine. However, the Witching Hour segments. Never have I hated getting through a dungeon as much as I had during my time in the "Berry Forest" (Thursday and Friday's dungeon). I am sure whoever designed a certain dungeon absolutely loved getting lost in dark caves in Pokémon without Flash. Very sure of it. Oh, and also add lighting fast enemies, guess-based segments, and sometimes even lag if you've got a low end device. I dread playing through it again for other endings. No NG+ either. I don't expect to get what the developers did in Pocket Mirror for such a feature (I don't think it would work very well), but I'd like at least a "Story" difficulty that could tone down it all a bit?Look, I still recommend at least giving it a try, if only because it is quite rare to see an indie title with such production value and passion poured into it. Again, the music and art assets have a level to them that is mostly unparalleled, and Kieferberg truly feels alive. It is quite a shame, then, that the gameplay balance seems to have been an afterthought. Which, y'know, you'd think it would be important and all given it is a game first and foremost.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Goody Two Shoes

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most aesthetically stunning indie games to be released in recent years, Little Goody Two Shoes effortlessly blends up to half a dozen distinct artistic styles - 90s Japanese anime, classic RPG pixel art, pastel fairytale illustrations and even puppetry.It is also a magnificent mozaic of disparate genres - horror puzzle, RPG, resource management, classic arcade-style minigames, and lesbian dating sim,with each element meshing together to form a cohesive narrative structure that is incredibly effective in delivering the plot with gut-wrenching emotional impact.  The soundtrack is truly amazing as well, with more than 60 tracks ranging in atmosphere from heartwarmingly beautiful to deeply unsettling. My personal favorite would be 'Romantic Crepescule', which can only be described as a 'sunset in aural form'. The soundtrack also boasts 4 songs with Japanese lyrics, two of which were sung by Elise's VA, and the other two by Rozenmarine's VA. Their talent really manages to shine through! The story is a richly illustrated, beautiful-yet-horrific fairy tale which features as its protagonist an ambitious 18-year-old lass named Elise, who lives in a 19th-century German village called Kieferberg.A poverty-stricken orphan barely eking out a living as a lowly maid-of-all-work, Elise can only find solace in her three female friends (and potential love interests), plus a rather unfounded belief in her destiny of fame and fortune.Everything changes, however, when Elise learns of a local legend about a certain entity that grants people their deepest desire in exchange for a terrible price. Intrigued, Elise becomes increasingly ensnared in a dangerous web of greed and deceit, with paranormal disasters that may or may not be connected to her activities plaguing the townsfolk.The player as Elise must brave various otherworldly horrors in order to realize her wishes, while building up a romantic relationship with the love interests, earning her keep through menial odd jobs (represented by fun yet challenging minigames), and fending off accusations of witchcraft from the properly paranoid neighbors. Thematically speaking, the plot is as richly diverse as the aesthetics, covering such topics as LGBTQ romance (though Elise ends up marrying a man in certain endings, it is not her first choice to say the least), the poignant decline of small towns (Kieferberg is a picturesque village that is nonetheless slowly losing people due to a lack of economic opportunities and essential services), the bleak despair of poverty and social isolation (well represented in-game, which fuels Elise's determination to risk everything for a better future, despite the apparent perils), the ugliness of mob psychology (which rears its head whenever Elise is accused of witchcraft - a perfect scapegoat due to her social status as a poor orphan in a tightly-knit hamlet), and last but not least, the fine line between legitimate desires and unethical greed. Is it inherently wrong to wish for more? What is the price that you are willing pay for wealth and status? These are the questions that will continue to haunt Elise and the player, well after the ending credits roll. The romantic scenes are sweet and wholesome, with each love interest having a distinctive personality and a compelling backstory. Each of them has a different answer to Elise's unhealthy obsession with material wealth.Rozenmarine is a downtrodden beggar girl of a non-Christian faith with a meek, fatalistic outlook on life due to various hardships, yet somehow she manages to find happiness even in her extremely deprived circumstances - an attitude Elise could possibly learn from.Lebkuchen is Elise's dearest childhood friend and a nun-in-training at the local church, who serves as a pillar of their community through her selflessness and considerable moral authority. While her insistence upon putting the needs of the many before her own is slowly taking a toll on her, Lebkuchen persists due to a fundamental love for the community she belongs to, and the people who comprise it. After all, no individual is an island.Freya is Elise's friendly rival and the town headsman Gustav's daughter. One of the most gregarious, eternally-optimistic personalities in the game, Freya is attracted to Elise for the simplest of reasons - her beauty, elegance and assertive personality. She doesn't overthink things, and loves her life for what it is, intending to achieve success through hard work and shrewd harnessing of her innate talents - unlike Elise, who wallows in an emotional cesspool of bitterness and frustration.Elise can, depending on the player's choice, either embrace her lover's vision of a brighter future sans the satanic rituals, or persist in her dubious pursuit of easy riches and glory.As for the other elements of this marvelous game, the dynamics of daily village life are well-constructed to the point that Kieferberg itself can be considered a separate character, and the horror puzzles are, in their own way, hauntingly beautiful. Horror is mostly psychological rather than visceral, with each step of Elise's ill-advised quest fueling a growing aura of dread and suspense.  All of this eventually culminates in a denouement that can be either triumphantly cathartic or heart-wrenchingly tragic, with lasting consequences for Elise and her loved ones. While the game admittedly has many flaws, it is a miracle in itself that a team of a dozen developers or so managed to create such a delightful work of art on such a minuscule budget. I really do hope that Astral Shift receives the acclamation that it so badly deserves. Wishing you guys only the best of luck!!

_childDocuments_.review: Little Goody Two Shoes isn't a perfect game. You WILL have issues and annoyances here and there while playing. Despite this however, I still consider this game to probably be my favourite I've ever played. Let me get into why.-VisualsThe games visuals are top notch. But you don't need to take my word for it, you've seen the screenshots, and maybe even a trailer or 2.-SoundtrackThe games soundtrack is really beautiful. It generally (but not always) goes for a cosy and/or cheerful vibe. I listen to over 30 of the songs regularly, and the song Moon Bird, is one of my favourite pieces of music in general.-Narrative The game has a very solid narrative that will keep you pondering both about what's going on, and just how far things will go. You play as Elise, a maid of all work struggling to makes ends meet in the small German village named Kieferberg. Elise has wishes to become extremely rich, and will go to great lengths to make this dream come true. Just to what lengths will she go? Well, wouldn't you like to know? Meanwhile, the town of Kieferberg is very paranoid of witches, and many strange and absurd going ons is only further exaggerating this paranoia, and Elise's brash personality certainly isn't helping her avoid any accusations. -CharactersWhile there are many of residents of Kieferberg, the focus is primarily on Elise, and her 3 love interests, the optimistic and carefree Rozenmarine, the kind, cheerful and thoughtful Freya, and the sassy and caring Lebkuchen. But don't worry, this isn't a game where the love interests are only present while dating/pursuing them. They all got their own presence, moments and meaningful interactions outside of just dates/pursual. Overall their writing is extremely good! I felt really attached to all of them by the end! Although one critique I have is how the game ask you to start choosing who to date, before you really get to know 2 of the characters, leaving you without much basis on who you want to choose. (You can easily pursue 2 in one play through though, so it isn't a massive deal.)-AtmosphereThe atmosphere and vibe of the night sections are perfect, with lots of variety in environments. Art and atmosphere are clearly this dev teams strongest suit. But I'm quite bad at describing environments and atmosphere, you'll just have to take my word on this one. -Game playThe game play itself isn't particularly special, but it I wouldn't call it bad either. The game consist of 7 days, during the day you will: Work by playing mini games to make money so you can buy food, and/or other things. Go through story cut scenes, and go on dates. You do all of this while managing your hunger, your sanity, and how much the town suspects you of being a witch. Plus there is plenty of optional flavour dialogue that is different at every time of every day, via means of the talking to the village folk. At night you'll be typically entering the forest, and this is where the horror part of the game is. each night is different, but generally involves puzzle solving and/or avoiding death via various means. The night sections actually aren't very good gameplay wise lots of the time, but more on that later in the review. Overall, the game play is definitely more involved than your typical puzzle horror rpg maker game, but it isn't that much more involved.-The PuzzlesOne lesson the devs should of learned from their previous game Pocket Mirror, (which I also recommend) is that they aren't very good at designing puzzles. The devs didn't learn this lesson, nor did they get any better at designing puzzles. It honestly feels like they've gotten worse. The game has plenty of puzzles during the night sections, and most of the puzzle design in this game is ass. While the puzzles are typically bruteforce-able/stumble-able, so you won't get stuck too long that frequently, You will find yourself having to brute forcing/stumble your way to the solution through most of the puzzles, many puzzles you won't even realise how you were supposed to figure out even after "solving." Even many non-puzzle gameplay moments during the night aren't telegraphed what to do well and will result in you taking lots of damage/dying/getting stuck just cause it isn't clear what your supposed to do. The night sections are very atmospheric and beautiful, it's such a shame they are filled with these issues.-Bugs/GlitchesEven after the patch there are still a few intrusive bugs here and there. Nothing too crazy, especially after the patch, but you will probably have to deal an annoying bug like, 1-3 times. Such as Welma's shop not working during the final day, which is potentially a huge deal, as you can't go into the other shop once you enter town during this day, so if you don't have enough food to last the day you're screwed. Or another bug, where Interacting with the fish statue before Thursday with a certain item in your inventory will soft lock your game. Or how a certain note says has the completely wrong message after you've read it once. Again, it used to be much worse before the patch, but these bugs (especially the Welma one) are definitely problematic. Overall, I think Little Goody Two Shoes is an incredible game that despite its imperfections, is 100% worth your money and time. I do seriously consider this my favourite game I've ever played. The highs really are just that high for me. This game genuinely shifted the way I see video game narratives and how I think the best way to write them for my taste are.

_childDocuments_.review: So, at least a little bit of patience for it to come out!In that timespan, both DELTARUNE Chapters 1 and 2 released, both Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom released, even Hollow Knight released which means that for anybody who found Hollow Knight after release, I've waited for this longer than they've waited for Silksong. I've made friends, lost them, I've learnt so much about myself and my identity and gone from a child in middle school to an adult with a full-time job and college in that time.For this review, I wanted to make sure to write this review after seeing all it has to offer, so I just 100%ed all achievements for this game last night, and I want to talk about it and if it's worth a damn. I just also want to give a little context first.In July 2016, I found the game Pocket Mirror back when it was just a demo and got to check it out when the full version released shortly after. That game is a game I hold close to my heart, it was even a major factor in me later realizing I'm queer, so it's really important to me.Not too long later, the developers announced Little Goody Two Shoes. It was a bit clear from Pocket Mirror that there was still some things not really explained and would need to be addressed in a follow up, and this game is a prequel!I waited, and a lot of stuff happened and time passed. Yuzuki had a great remix of the Pocket Mirror soundtrack! I joined the official Astral Shift Discord way back when it was small in the start of 2018! There were some teases of some images of the game world and art, and it made sense that the game would take a long time to make. They had this awesome pin you could buy of Pocket Mirror! I missed my chance to buy it and was extremely saddened and wish I got one. Around 2019, we got some music preview and pictures of the main crew of characters and a livestream of working on some art. The game had a little teaser since it was getting some spotlight by Playstation. A while later, we got a look at the church interior! Yuzuki released an animation for Pocket Mirror that I was waiting for since 2018! That was neat! That was... 2021, I think? 2023, Pocket Mirror got a remaster; it was beautiful and it's on Steam! Added a little bit more content and completely remade all visuals, definitely recommend.And then the game released.I want to first say that of those seven years of waiting, I felt like the game was really justified in taking forever with the quality they were doing, but any game can end up like YIIK, so I was a little cautious. But then, opening the game, seeing that opening? Hearing that title screen? Playing the game?Well, here's my review on the game now.I guess the first thing to say is yes, the art is amazing, I don't have much to say here though jes' art is always wonderful. I just always watch the opening when I launch the game.The music is amazing. The title theme is so good, I've listened to it so much on loop. Red Ruby Shoes is amazing. Night Prayer is so lovely.The horror isn't that scary or anything, it's a lot ligher than most other games like this. Pocket Mirror had more horror factor to it if it's worth noting, but there is still some ominous atmosphere in this game. I just wouldn't say it's particularly frightening.And now, here's something I'm going to just be really critical about; the gameplay.So, to not spoil much, this game doesn't have too many puzzles compared to Pocket Mirror since it has other gameplay that fills up everything else. But when it does, they... really aren't that great. A massive amount of the puzzles in it are super cryptic and took forever to figure out and brought down the experience. I've played so many RPG Maker horror puzzle games, which this tries to emulate heavily, and I just... don't think this game does them well. A lot of other games like Ib or The Witch's House execute their puzzles a lot better because they put the clues and cues in pretty well and you're able to pick up on them. This kind of doesn't. I didn't use any guide for them, but I certainly did not like them. One of them even requires This issue wouldn't be too bad if it weren't for how bad the game is with some cases where you'll be punished hard enough to reload a save from a while back. It has heavy resource management and some areas and choices that force you to prepare for them, but if you somehow are short and didn't realize it, you may need to do a lot of replaying. For example, you need to balance food, but you can only work for certain times of the day and then as enough time passes, if you didn't prepare well enough, you may have to redo over an hour of content if you're unlucky just to proceed further. This happened to me near the endgame and it was not fun at all. And there's this one part that genuinely is BS, there's a missable task that will lock you out of a lot if you miss it but the game only lets you know you missed it if you continue and do another hour of playing. This also happened to a friend who was really into the game and they almost dropped it (but came back later and got to the ending). It's not much of a spoiler but if you want to be safe, As for the plot? I enjoyed it, especially as a Pocket Mirror fan and it's enjoyable without being one. It's hard to describe without spoilers. But one major factor of the plot is that the game is also part dating sim. And I'll be blunt. The dates are amazing and super ungodly gay??? It's really cute and beautiful and it was extremely memorable and I got really attached to some characters. It is unrestrained and lets the characters actually be little young lesbians and it's so cool for that, if you're like playing games for queer rep then this is going to hit well there. And I do just need to say, in seven years of waiting for this game I had no knowledge it'd be remotely queer and I think it's poetic that this game has so much good LGTBQ+ rep when the first game helped me so much in realizing I fall under that umbrella. I think the thing that just really hits me is that this game, despite how critical I am of its gameplay or feel that it didn't do something as well as Pocket Mirror, will be something that I know I'm going to think about for so many years going forwards, much like the original. The sights, the sounds, the beautiful CGs, the charm, the plot, the endings and the dating, it's all going to stick with me. The experience and days spent through all the tasks and slowly approaching the end curtain and all the build up there were a lot of fun and I just really feel so happy to have gone through this.So yes, without a doubt, this game was worth waiting over 7 years for. I'll wait another 7 if I have to for Astral Shift's next game. I really loved this, and I'm so glad to have seen it start from just the tiny demo with Pocket Mirror to now being a giant long and beautiful game and even get published by Square Enix. I'm just riding a wave of euphoria; I'm happy. I really am. I'll hold my memories close to my heart.Now please put out merch so I can buy it instantly... I'm begging you...

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to its release for many years, after Pocket Mirror in 2016 and the remake in 2023. It's the prequel to Pocket Mirror (I recommend you play it first, before LGTS), and is a horrific role-playing adventure game inspired by the 90s.You play the role of a young girl, Elise, determined to become rich and leave the modest world she grew up in.  She discovers a pair of magnificent shiny red shoes buried in her garden. Bewitched, the young girl embarks on a frightening journey to realize her dream, but there are many choices for the end. -Gorgeous gameplay, high pixel quality -Explore open world and adorable map (village, forest, house, etc) - Three charming girls romance dates  -Beautiful cinematics -Mini-games, story events, money-saving jobs, puzzles - Make the right choice otherwise suspicion, the village may suspect you of sorcery -Day cycle (morning, bedtime, evening, etc.) - Beautiful chara design and sprite character animations-You can skip dialogues, or reread the tutorials if you wish - Lots of creatures (goat, cats, dogs, monsters, ghosts or even strange creatures) - Find all  the golden girls - Heart sanity (if you run out of heart or food, game over)-Scary stories, scary to hunting down-Save too cute, especially the bird with the rose in his beak! -10 endings (many choices) -Cute achievements There are no negative things about the game, the developers work very hard for their long time.  I enjoyed so much this amazing game, it is extremely beautiful indie rpg game that I've never seen! such adorable and rich fairytale, Astralshift's work is always gorgeous!  I highly recommend you play it!

_childDocuments_.review: Completely captures the feeling of a fantranslated PS2 adaptation of a forgotten 90's shoujo manga. Almost dizzyingly textured & artisanal in its devotion to presenting this kind of rose-thorny traditional German folktale. Feels so genuine, inspired, fully realised in a way I desperately needed as a palette cleanser.For me to become completely convinced of its gameplay and narrative goals, I’d have to replay it with alternate routes in mind, which I’m not quite able to facilitate with my current limited free time - and Little Goody Two Shoes doesn’t exactly make going down these forks in the story particularly breezy. I don’t tackle games with completionism in mind these days but I find myself a little bummed about how much work I’d need to put into this if I wanted to see the stories I’ve missed. Nothing a timeline/"skip seen dialogue" update somewhere down the line can’t fix, please don’t make me watch a Youtube video.

_childDocuments_.review: For over a decade I have been playing RPGMaker/RPGMaker style games. I feel they are the most story rich games out there by far, and since that is what I look for in a game I eat them up! That's to say I've played dozens, but none of them are quite as quality as this one. Not to say other games are not great in their own rights, but the just sheer QUALITY oozing from this game at every corner is undefeated. Soundtrack, Designs, Graphics, Cut-scenes... this game really has it all. The developer has also clearly improved since their previous game ''Pocket Mirror'' which is I also highly recommend! A few weeks before ''Little Goody Two Shoes'' came out I was able to play through and 100% the achievements from Pocket Mirror. That game follows the story of Elise's (LGTS' Protagonist) daughter. You learn in ''Pocket Mirror'' that Elise grew up in a small village in Germany. She had to work for what she had, as she was not wealthy. Because of this Elise often dreamed of a more fortune-filled life. When she heard a rumor a demon in the woods could grant wishes, Elise sought him out and made a Faustian bargain with him. I had originally thought this snippet of lore in the game was just.. that: lore. Well, imagine my surprise when I saw this game was coming out! I was excited to play another game from this developer as I had really enjoyed my experience with ''Pocket Mirror''. I bought it a few days after it released and was able to 100% the achievements in this game as well. My thoughts after 24 hours in it? As I said earlier this game is phenomenal and exceeds in just about every category. The soundtrack is very intricate and perfect for every scene. There is one in particular named 'Devilish Carnival' that I listen to often even after beating the game because it is just SO good! It really charmed me as I was playing and I dug through the soundtrack on YouTube to find it. I also really like 'Ruby Slippers Mirage' which is so upbeat and fun. The designs are gorgeous resembling the early 90's anime art style, my favorite being Elise. The game also has 3 romance-able options (all female) for Elise which all have very stunning designs themselves. My favorite will always be Freya, though they are all pretty in their own right. The graphics are GORGEOUS and are revolutionary for RPGMaker games! There is not another like it with this much thought put into every pixel on the screen. Some items/objects/enemies are even in a more realistic art style to really put you on edge which I found fascinating when playing! Cut-scenes look like they're straight out of an anime. I remember booting up the game and just going "WOW!" from the opening. Of course, like all games it does have its own issues. I find them incredibly minor, but since this is my honest review I will still add them. The game takes course over a week (Sunday-Saturday) and if you do not do all of the side-quests on Wednesday & Thursday you will be locked out of 9/10 of the endings. This is a issue I find the most concerning: as you are locked into ONLY getting 1 ending of which I would consider a bad one. Side-quests are not important any other day and you don't have to do them at all if you don't want to. However, on Wednesday & Thursday if you forget to do certain things you just won't get the item you need to complete the game at its fullest. Which is incredibly unfortunate, and I hope is just a early release issue they change later on. To combat this I would recommend using multiple save slots and being very attentive. I was not aware of this issue and used only one save slot. Thankfully someone online shared their save file where I could play the other endings I was unable to see. If they hadn't though I don't know if I would've really wanted to replay the game to get the rest of my achievements. It was heartbreaking the moment I realized I was soft-locked after 10 hours of game play. Though I do think this will be changed in the future, I wish someone had warned me before I played. A simple mistake can ruin your entire run, which sucks. Again, I can't imagine this being a permanent issue. I wouldn't worry too much about it when playing.Other than that my complaints are pretty small. I think the mini-games you do as Elise works in the daytime are fun at first, but some are worse than others. 'Chop Chop Chop!' & 'It's Raining Apples!' are the mini-games I had the most fun with, but 'Kiss The Rat' & 'Chicken Frenzy' were just downright grating at times. Especially when you want to get to the next day quickly. I think if you could skip the working sections of the day and just get a flat 30 coins (which is the amount the lowest ranking on those mini-games gets you) it would be neat. Also, for all of the talk about the demon and the lead-up to him it was kind of odd to see he didn't have sprite art done for him like the other central characters do. I mean take Gustav for example, he has sprite artwork when he talks even though he isn't too relevant despite being Freya's father. He's literally just a town NPC! The demon also has artwork in the previous game the developer made so... why not in this game where he is arguably more important? He was my favorite design in ''Pocket Mirror'' so I was excited to see his new look... but nothing. Elise also comes across extremely mean sometimes even to her potential love interests. Which I get is the point since she is vain and petty: obsessed with fortune and all, but sometimes you'll be trying to say something nice on one of the romantic dates and Elise will instead say something mean. I'm nitpicking now I know, but these are things I genuinely thought about when playing. I have to nitpick to find bad things to say about this game in the first place, since it's genuinely just a really good game! I was very invested in this game. It's the first time I've been so invested in a RPGMaker game since my favorite game ''Fausts Alptraum''. Which I first played 5 years ago, so it has been a while. They are similar Faustian bargain stories with redhead bow wearing protagonists. I saw a lot of what I liked in my favorite game in this game, and some more even! So this game despite what I said above is really special to me. At first I hated Elise as I found her painfully naive, rude, obtuse and vain. Near the end though I realized I had come to really understand, appreciate and love her just as much as my favorite character Freya. In her own way, I think she is relatable. I was worried at first from her description in ''Pocket Mirror'' that she would be insufferable and hard to play as. However, I was delighted and surprised to learn she is quite funny at times and grows on you. I'm glad I gave her a chance by playing the game!If you are a fan of any of these: 90's anime, Lesbian romances, RPGMaker games, puzzle games, good soundtracks, dark stories, stylized games or story rich games then this one is definitely for you! Objectively this game is fantastic and will be the one to look up to for other RPGMaker game developers. We only get games like this every decade or so. So, will you accompany Elise on her journey to fortune? Will you let her sacrifice everything? Or will you make her realize just how much she truly has?

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Little Goody Two Shoes is a wonderfully crafted RPG-maker type horror/adventure game: it achieves excellence through its visual presentation and style, but leaves a lot to be desired regarding the puzzle segments, which actively detracts from the experience. As the indie title that it is I think you only need to be interested in this game visually and not be averse to the genre for a purchase to be completely warranted, LGTS is absolutely gorgeous and you notice the love and dedication that went into making this game, which is amazing. If you particularly like this aesthetic as I do, you're in for a treat and playing the game is a dazzling experience. Bonus points if you're also here for the yuri, of course!Unfortunately, for a game that has such a gorgeous presentation and flow, from the environments to all the menus, the characters, and every single little detail, the gameplay comes to an halt with the puzzle segments, which are of course needed and expected for game progression, but end up being chores most of the time until you memorize patterns and/or are proficient enough. It sounds fair, but it's actually more of a stump, and immersion breaking in such a way that it actively harms the experience. In no way I claim to be very good and patient at puzzles, but I 100% felt that the difficulty they presented was artificial, and only there to make the game longer, and as such I was just happy to *finally* clear them instead of genuinely satisfied I solved one.Regardless, I cannot shut up about how gorgeous this game is, and of course, the story, while typical of the genre, is well executed and engaging with how the game is presented, and the main characters are all appealing in their own ways, which is all you would need here I think. Try to go in blind if you can!As with everything, YMMV: I think the challenge presented through the puzzle segments was very poorly done but my frustration with them is not enough to detract me from playing the game, I was more interested in the aforementioned aesthetic, story, and characters. You should be also aware that the game has been patched with some very much needed quality of life changes, such as a Skippable Cutscenes option, so it is currently in a much better state than at release.The final verdict is that playing LGTS is an absolute must for people that are already interested in it for some reason and/or fans of the genre, that comes with a very big warning of frustrating puzzles (save as if you're playing a very old game & manage your resources and patience well!)Two last notes:— Lebkuchen best girl.— I cannot get out of my head how much Freya reminds me of Suiseiseki.

_childDocuments_.review: i don't think i liked it :(a richly illustrated nightmare fairy tale which warns of paranoid infighting and reaching for an unattainable ideal, broken apart by tedious and artificially difficult survival horror segments. i meet each hazard as intended and am often punished with unforgiving damage or by being taken to an instant game over, and while i fully accept that this very well might just be a skill issue on my part, it remains a significant hurdle that's barring me from engaging properly with the unfolding narrative.i'm not unfamiliar with the death-laden rpgmaker horror-esque titles which preceded LGTS and those it draws its inspirations from, its how it contextualises such flaws that becomes an issue. there are no "skip seen dialogue" options, with the fast forward made available to us after Elise's delayed inputs just slow enough to be annoying. on that note, bosses with instant death attacks have unskippable cutscenes prior making repeat attempts patronising. two core survival systems are made redundant within one of the in-game days. perhaps most tragically, the distinct visual style which once pleased the eye beings to blend into monotony and goes unappreciated after some hours.and like i'm sad about it! i wanted to like it! i really enjoyed how the story progressed and how my bond with my favourite lady bloomed and i liked the endings i've managed to get, but all these hiccups had me nearly just uninstalling early. it's a beautiful poetic horror title, but so many little things simply ended up overwhelming me.

_childDocuments_.review: First I'd like to say that I really enjoyed the demo when it came out and was very eager to play the full content. The art style and music (with some fun "anime opening song" to boot !), the unashamed old Shojo anime style that's not ironic or mocking the genre for a change, reunited in a German pastoral and rural environment rarely used in fictions, ...  Sadly I have to say that the more I was playing, the more a lot of annoying things, mostly relative to gameplay, just kept piling up until it felt so frustrating that I just wanted it to be over with. It really left a sour taste and it's a shame.The "Witching Hour" parts of the game were the main offender : confusing mini games, enemies that one shot you (and force you to go through cinematic you've already seen and can't always fast forward).Then after a while, the absence of fast travel between the protagonist's house and the town makes it for some boring and tedious running back and forth.It's more of a personal taste I admit, but I always found that having the player forced to do obvious bad choices to progress the story by making the character incredibly oblivious to the point of being unrealistic to be bad design (especially in horror/mystery games).All in all, I would say that I don't regret playing the game for like the first 2/3 hours, but then I would rather have looked some walkthrough or videos than force myself to finish the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite its overwhelmingly positive rating, I’m surprised there are only a few communities and forums this game has. I think this can be identified as a hidden gem game, you can definitely feel the developers poured their passion into it here, so I think it deserves a sincere review. Both positive and negative.First of all, the art style. Gods, it's gorgeous! It was the very first reason that got me to buy this game. If you like the way 90’s anime looks, you will love this game. Accompanied by beautifully animated sprites, along with a lush and colorful environment that really feels straight out of a fairy tale book! Even some of the items and scenes here are references to well-known fairy tales that we're all familiar with. Don't get me started on the soundtracks. I wasn't expecting that they would be composing any memorable soundtracks, knowing that this game is short (yes, this game is a bit short). The game proved me wrong, I suddenly found myself bobbing my head along with the soundtrack while I strolled around the village, and I was just 30 minutes into the game! It's a mix of a perky upbeat tune and a majestic but haunting melody, depending on what time of day you're in.I also love how the game tricks you into thinking you're playing a childish game, then proceeds to show its true colors as you progress through the story. At first, you'll be busy staring at a cute goat and a road full of mushrooms, but later that night, you'll be transfixed by a horrific image of an infant head attached with crawling legs, to the point where you'll be questioning yourself if you're still even playing the same game as before. As for the gameplay, it's very simplistic. The game progresses in a day-by-day manner (just like Persona), and those days are divided into six segments (morning, noon, dusk, etc.). Each action will cost a "segment.". It's up to you whether to spend it on dates or chores. Chores here come only in the form of mini-games, so don't go expecting a Harvest Moon-level kind of gameplay. Every last segment of the day is where the main challenge of this game lies. It will present you with several trials and puzzles that you need to undergo to progress to the next day. Money is also very very scarce here, it adds up to the fun and challenge that you must spend it very wisely. Otherwise, you'll find yourself struggling at the end of the game, unable to buy what you need for the final trial because you've already spent on unnecessary items in the last few days.However, despite its charms and wonderful story, I found a couple of bugs that soft-locked me in the game where it displayed the text box, then suddenly the controls did not work anymore? Forcing me to exit the game. There's also a part of the game where the shop doesn't let you buy things because somehow the menu is bugged. Not a big deal when you save often, but still, it's there.The game also has its minor infuriating moments sometimes. In some areas, you won't even know if that "thing" is just part of the scenery or an actual danger to your character. Hitboxes are rather weird sometimes too, like you are way distant from them, but even so, you still take damage. Despite its flaws, I just overlooked it because the story, art, and soundtrack are just so good. Especially the twist at the end.So, do I recommend this game? Yes. If you love story-driven games, 90's anime art style, catchy soundtracks, memorable villagers (that you won't mind talking to regularly), or a horror game that masquerades itself as a "cute" game, then yes, try it!

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: please hire someone to make good puzzles, not puzzles that make you wanna rip out your hair with every single step requiredI wanted to love this game so badly. The gorgeous artwork, the amazing soundtrack, the fun daytime events and minigames and the intriguing story (especially having played Pocket MIrror years ago) really don't leave much to be desired.But who thought the puzzles and design of the witching hours were fun? Every night just kept getting worse in terms of frustration and punishing deaths. Most cutscenes are NOT skippable so good luck replaying a part. I'm someone who saves a lot and on a lot of different save slots but even for me, I sometimes had to replay hours just because I was missing a dialogue to get a key... why are important items like that missable?The witching hours could have been the most amazing part of the game, yet they just pull it down so hard for me. If the gameplay at night was just a bit better and less frustrating, I'd easily give this game a 10/10. But like this? I'd probably settle with a 7/10, just because those nights make me not wanna finish this game and make it feel like a chore.Really disappointed. I'll probably still finish it because I love its universe and the overall design so much but the devs should really fix the difficulty spikes and make skipping cutscenes easier (some are skippable, some aren't).

_childDocuments_.review: Did not know this is a prequel to Pocket Mirror untill I had completed it, though it didn't harm the experience, but the games are linked.Reminds me of old, good RPG Maker horror games, if those had a budget. With the weaknesses and strengths attached. Though it's not so simple, but closest example I can think of. Make full use of the 20 save file slots. It is vital.Pretty much as anime as one can get, though that is clear from the pictures/trailer. Deal breaker for some. Does contain some tropes, like "clueless" protagonist, common in horror genre.Gameplay revolves around:A. Resource management by gathering items exploring/talking to people/doing mini-games for money for said items. Performance in minigames affects money you earn, this can screw you over if you aren't being carefulB. Date sequences with up to three seperate charactersC. Some lite puzzles/chase sequencesPros/Mixed/Cons:+ Absolutely stunning visuals, one of the best I've seen+ Great, at times haunting OST+ Fairytale-like theme works well+ Writing for the most part is quite good, especially for the characters you can romance+ Funny at times+ Fair full price and a steal on sale+ Has 10 endings (though some are far better than others, but expected from genre)* Minigames look fantastic, though a couple can be frustrating to S-Rank* Mixed feelings about the endings, pay-off for SOME of them wasn't there and I'm not sure they acknowledge each other in ways they should* I felt like some questions were left unanswered- Can lock you to bad/unsatisfying endings if you aren't paying attention to tasks available- Puzzles are not the best, taking you out of the experience sometimes, either by being really punishing or poorly made- While you can hold shift to fast forward most scenes/dialogue, replaying for different romance would still take some time- Weird design choices, such as replaying a mini-game for 5 coins, unclear meaning behind some available dialogue options, some poorly implemented puzzles...- Minor bugs, e.g. met one softlock, but it was avoidable after the factI'm used to these types of games so I managed to get a lot of endings on my first go without a guide, but someone less experienced may struggle. I recommend exploring thoroughly, being conservative with items and making full use of the different save slots.Overall, there were annoyances with the experience and not all endings were with the pay-off I had expected, but I was pretty happy with it at the end of the day. Will likely try out Pocket Mirror to get more of the story.

So why do I not recommend this game to other players then if I had such a positive experience with this game? Well, this game has a lot of flashing lights the further you get into this game and I've found myself dying a lot and encountering the flashing lights a lot, to which it no longer became an enjoyable experience. It DOES have a warning at the beginning of the game for those with epilepsy and I'm usually able to tolerate most games, but this was just too much. I encountered it past my 2 hours play time so Steam wouldn't refund me but I figured that I would put this warning up for those with epilepsy. It's a great game that I wish I could have enjoyed the rest of.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the rarest things in gaming is coming across a product that not only ticks every box in your book but also changes the way you think. I’m not gonna lie, what Little Goody Two Shoes was for me is nothing short of phenomenal. Filled with humor, creative ideas, fantastically put together story, wonderful sound design and hyper-interactive world. This is also a game that if not for a certain set of circumstances, I wouldn’t even take a look at. I’d find it in my Steam Queue, check it quickly and basically leave it there. But no, this time… I gave it a shot. And truly worth a shot this creation is, easily making its way to the Top 5 games I have ever played.Everything starts in a little village of Kieferberg, somewhere in medieval Austria. You play as Elise, a maid-of-all-work going through each day the only way she knows, by working herself into the ground while cursing everything the world stands on. Given the 90’s anime stylistic, retro sprites, relatable characters and soothing, pleasurable fantasy tunes, you can quickly get cozy with this title. The game just feels like this everyday cutesy story with tons of nice dialogues to read.Just as you relax and you seem to be getting your first grip on how the game’s world works, you get absolutely mauled by a much darker part of it. There are some supernatural happenings all around the place and they all seem connected to you, Elise. Naturally, this being medieval times, witchery accusations quickly start flying around, with most of them being thrown your way. Quite rightfully so, as Elise becomes part of something way bigger than she expects it to be. Despite diving into the unknown, she trusts her own abilities to finally make her wish of becoming rich and living a luxurious life come true.Things aren’t easy though, as nothing in life is ever free. Elise cannot just become rich in an instant. You oughtta prove that she is worth making that wish become reality by solving life-threatening puzzles, hiding the truth from the common folk and gathering items necessary for Elise to survive. All these while still maintaining a somewhat normal life as to not raise further suspicion of witchcraft in not-so-normal situations. While at first, it may seem like an easy thing to do, as the days go by, everything becomes more and more difficult and people around you become more and more nosey. Thankfully, there’s a bunch of friends to keep you company. You have Rozenmarine, a weird but kind traveler, to guide you through the process of how to make your wish come true. You have Lebkuchen, a devoted clergywoman, to trust you unconditionally, without asking too many difficult questions. You have Freya, a cheerful friend, to always have your back when you need it the most. While all three girls have a role to play in this story, only one of them can be chosen at a time. I also couldn’t live with myself if I haven’t mentioned Mr. Gustav here. Freya’s father and the mayor of Kieferberg, Mr. Gustav shares the cheerfulness of his daughter and helps with keeping the mood up, when life hits Elise the hardest. He's an honest man that cares about the village and all of its residents. He wouldn’t let any harm be done upon Elise or anyone else for that matter, which comes in clutch later on.Little Goody Two Shoes features multiple endings which, granted some are better than others, all provide you with this empty shell feeling you get after completing a great, compelling story. It was so good, there’s nothing left to do. What am I gonna do now? I have witnessed greatness. Yeah, at least 6 out of 10 different endings check all my boxes. I very rarely say it about games, but this one is worth replaying. Until you have seen all of the endings there is always a lot of more dialogue to read, side-stories to witness and feelings to be had.Simply put, a great story itself isn’t enough to justify recommending a product. Fortunately, Little Goody Two Shoes aces other areas as well. Since I already mentioned them at the beginning of this review, let’s just quickly break down what’s left to talk about. Because quite frankly, I could talk about them for hours and I only have around 8000 characters to use.Music is phenomenal. Soft and cheery tunes keep you engaged and perfectly fit the world that Astral Shift  has decided to create. Soundtrack drills into your head but doesn’t feel annoying at any point. You could listen to background ambient for hours and not get tired, especially that most of the locations have their own tunes, so each time you go to a different place, the background music changes ever so slightly, preventing repetition. Then… Witching Hours begin. The feeling of uneasiness and disconnection from anything that’s normal and comprehensible creeps in. It is perfectly captured and highlighted by the eerie background music that doesn’t really follow any usual rhythm, further inducing that…  feeling.But music itself is not all. All the little sounds, rumbles, voice acting, animal calls, even something so miniscule as SFX for moving across various menus fit very well together. This makes the entire experience not only believable and immersive, but also just worthwhile.Of course, there is also meat in this story and music sandwich. Said meat is gameplay. For most of the time you’re free to run around Kieferberg and its surroundings, talking with different villagers and earning money as a maid-of-all-work. In practice, this means a couple of mini-games in which you have to gather eggs, catch apples, cut wood and hit a rat with a stick. One aspect of LGTS that catches my eye is that almost everything in this world can be interacted with. You can literally touch every nook and cranny to witness Elise giving you her short and most likely annoyed description. The attention to detail is insane. To top it off, many different little side-stories can only be witnessed if you speak to certain people at certain time. When you’re finally done running around the town, sticking Elise’s nose in everyone’s matters, the night finally comes. Nights however… aren’t exactly what you might think they would be. We’ve talked about witchery and supernatural stuff going on already, haven’t we? Yeah, nights, or Witching Hours, as the game calls them, are when most of the action happens. This is where you have to fight for Elise’s life by solving puzzles and running away from the danger. While she’s awfully brave for a 19 year old, Elise makes the very sane decision of just staying out of harm’s way.So now that you know how to avoid certain death, you also have to solve various riddles in order to progress. Many different challenges await you, such as placing tiles in correct spots, standing on pressure plates in the right order or finding a phase of the moon based on hints scattered throughout a level.Some of them are easy, some of them require you to rewire your brain a little bit to understand what you’re supposed to do. It’s a perfect modern take on oldschool games’ idea of how to solve puzzles, by making you go around the level looking for clues on what to do.To me, Little Goody Two Shoes is a piece of art and possibly one of the best titles I have ever played - I enjoyed every second of it. To some extent, it changed the way I perceive things. Before LGTS, I disregarded many games without even giving them a shot, unless someone actually told me to play them. Little Goody Two Shoes made me realize that everything deserves a chance and sometimes… very rarely, but sometimes… you get to experience something truly amazing where you least expect it.

It always jumps in with amazing special effects & stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a gorgeous, delightful, devastating little game. I wanted to wait until I got all achievements to leave a review but I couldn't. This game switches from heartwarming to deeply heartwrenching, and I'm left here wanting more. I appreciate the horror relying more on atmosphere than jumpscares, which are annoyingly common in this genre of horror. The music is fantastic, the characters are interesting and the visuals are beautiful. I love the love between Elise and the girls, their romance feels genuine and it's easy to get attached to all of them. My only complaint is that starting over can feel really slow, but that's probably more of a me problem. 9/10, I absolutely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!! -Great Narrative-Beautiful Art Direction, 80s/90s Anime Art Style-Cool Level Designs-Good music -Smooth and Easy to understand mechanics and controls-Cute Character voice acting-Multiple Romance options-Multiple Endings-Fun minigamesCons-Some insta kills on certain levels can throw you off-food and health management is tight knit meaning you need to manage and budget cautiously-Slight backtracking to certain areas-Slightly confusing puzzles-Keeping suspicion down is kind of stressfulController is highly recommended when playing!!**I really love the story of this game and how it unfolds, the best part is that you can have multiple endings and save files so you can easily backtrack to another save if you want to experience a different outcome. The game offers a variety of gameplay mechanics. **There's a day and night system, where at the day you can talk to friends, townsfolk and do chores, explore places and enter special dialogues or discover locations. During the day, you can earn money by helping people and buy items like bread and berries in order to satiate hunger meter, sanity meter and Hearts or HP.**Night system where you enter the dark stages similar to persona but more lighthearted. There's mild jumpscares, enemies to avoid and puzzles to solve in order to progress to the next day. **The goal is to fulfill Elise's dream of leaving the town and you have to complete it within seven days. Time will only pass when you do chores or progress story. Not to mention, every night the story forces progression but side quests are meant to be done during daytime.**The art style is fantastic and there's a little bit of musical numbers in between which will give you a surprise. Cutscenes make it feel like an 80s/90s anime and it's pretty cool!**the puzzles for the game can be a bit trivial as it goes in line with trying to avoid enemies while you do it. there are save points in between areas that help but it kinda gets frustrating if you need to do a puzzle while an enemy might be waiting.A huge shoutout to my awesome noona gokidtiger for gifting me this game last christmas!!! I really enjoyed playing it and will comeback for more !!

_childDocuments_.review: I implore anyone interested in this game to keep in mind that Little Goody Two Shoes is all art, story, and character driven narrative. If a retro anime-styled, all-femme romance and a selfish teenager's descent into madness don't sound appealing, then please pour salt all over my review.Spoiler-free review to follow:I blind purchased Little Goody Two Shoes based on the art, description, and genre tags. This game is exactly what I was hoping it would be, so I am very happy with my decision! This is my first acquaintance with studio AstralShift-- although I had wishlisted Pocket Mirror, I never got around to trying it.To begin, I would like to draw a frame of reference for Little Goody Two Shoes as a game. I would say that the feeling playing LGTS gives me is something akin to Legend of Mana crossed with Yume Nikki. LGTS definitely has that PS1-era adventure game feel, yet it is skillfully modern in execution. The setting is obviously fairy tale Bavarian, yet doesn't feel overly contrived in its presentation. The accompanying soundtrack is symphonic, melodic, and moving. In my opinion, the music in the game is strong enough to stand on it's own, and I encourage anyone who has reservations about the game to start by listening to the OST. LGTS's art design features gorgeous sprites interacting with 2D, thoughtfully parallax-enhanced backgrounds. All the while, the character art hits straight out of 90's shoujo manga style in the best way. Furthermore, many sequences and interludes are deeply reminiscent of 90's and 00's Japanese animated media and visual novels. Fans of these mediums ought to be pleasantly assaulted with nostalgia.While LGTS is very much a story game, there is enough challenge in the gameplay to keep the player engaged. At times, the more frenetic sequences and puzzles have taken me multiple attempts to overcome, yet aren't punishing to the point of frustration. In regard to theme, the game leans heavily into sapphic romance, allegories, and psychological, surreal horror with a zesting of history. Learning to doubt one's community, the people closest, and even oneself are perhaps the most insidious notions explored in LGTS.I am not even close to finished with the game, so it is difficult for me to form critical opinions of the narrative plot or character development, but I will say that I wish LGTS could become fully voiced. I am fully aware that there are budget constraints with any project, and especially games such as this. However, I believe that the character interactions, particularly between the heroines, would be more immersive if acted out in full. Assuming LGTS is a commercial success, I would love to see a special edition or upgrade in the future that keeps the original voice talent, but expands on the scope.Regardless, I pray for the success of this game simply because I want to see more games like this. I absolutely adore the themes that LGTS explores, the presentation and the beauty of the experience. In the age of abject monetization of "anime" themed content, $20 USD for a polished game is a much needed breath of fresh air. To the developers: Thank you!

_childDocuments_.review: This game's art style is incredibly unique and has an incredible soundtrack. The game is well-written and well-made. However, the unskippable dialogues and the easily missable key-story events/items in the game make it sometimes frustrating - I had to redo an hour's worth of gameplay due to missing an item. Many items/events are easily missable, and some are integral for even a normal playthrough - as missing them will lock the player to the premature "bad ending." I think that the game lacks clear directions given to the player. I recommend pulling up AstralShift's spoiler-free guide on Steam and following it for the best experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't typically write reviews, but I think this is a special case of a game - a piece of art - so full of love and clear devotion from its developers that it truly deserves all of the praise and attention it can get.The story and especially the characters get you invested in a really satisfying way that got me emotionally invested almost immediately, with some fun mysteries to unravel that all tie nicely back into the main narrative. All three love interests especially are an absolute treat to interact with, definitely the highlights of the writing alongside Elise as a whole.Gameplay-wise, it's pretty enjoyable. I could see it feeling monotonous at times to certain people, but I never found myself falling into that kind of pit, and I think anyone who enjoys the RPG Maker horror-style of experience will find themselves right at home with the various puzzles and minor explorative elements (especially as LGTS lacks a lot of the... cheaper? aspects that I often see those kinds of games receiving mild criticisms for).Lastly, the art direction is simply sublime. Every single artist that contributed to this game, be it in the pixel artwork, the illustrations, the music, even the voice actors, absolutely killed it, and all of the different styles it goes for mesh together alarmingly well (I have to give HUGE props to the woodland in this regard). Every last thing Little Goody Two Shoes does comes together in this wonderful tapestry that I have nothing but the utmost respect and admiration to the dev team for achieving. Easily one of my favorite experiences in a long time, and one I won't forget.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of either Puella Magi Madoka Magic or Alan Wake II, you will probably enjoy this game, and if you are a fan both, as I am, it is a must-play. The art and music are absolutely incredible, the narrative is evocative and haunting, and the main characters are all compelling. The townsfolk have a surprising amount of characterization injected into them given just how many of them there are. There isn't a great deal I can say without spoilers, and while there really aren't any big surprises by the time you've played a bit, it's still better enjoyed blind. But it's worth every moment. I had such a good time. I have only two complaints: one, that the good endings were a little anticlimactic, and two, that there weren't any difficulty settings for the sake of accessibility. That stupid, godforsaken egg minigame...Anyway, ten out of ten, German witch lesbians now and forever. Corrupt that nun!

_childDocuments_.review: A really great game with nice graphics that we don't often see anymore. It also has a lovely soundtrack that I might listen to again occasionally. In terms of gameplay, it's pretty basic and plays better with a controller, as it shares old adventure games elements mixed with Visual Novels. The game is a slice of life with lesbian romances & elements of horror, but saying more than this would ruin the experience. It is "short" to "medium" length, as the game can be completed in 10h if you only focus on the "main" story, but the game has 10 different endings, among which 6 are variations depending on certain choices made. Still, an easy game to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the best indie games I've played:intriguing story, complex puzzles and I have a thing for 90s anime so I fell in love with the artstyle at the start. I will say that I think the story ran a little too long for me, and at times it was confusing to tie some parts together. The game has 10 endings that you can get at the end so it encourages you to do replays of the game. I'm not sure if I will replay this again as I think that I've had my fill the first time around. I'm not gonna lie though, towards the end of the game(thursday witching hour and friday witching hour; that moon puzzle..) the puzzles got confusing as hell for me, and it was frustrating trying to read guides to get through these parts of activating statues and running away from ghouls, etc. Maybe I'm slow or something; but this ♥♥♥♥ aggravated me to no end and in some forums people are like "pay attention to what is said in dialogue" and I did but those "hints" did not help me enough to get past these parts without going on youtube. Around this part of the game I was tempted to drop the game and not finish it. Basically never doing that ♥♥♥♥ again. Still, the game's great for people who enjoy visual novels.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was well worth the wait. Play this game without spoiling yourself, its worth it.I hope the game gets more publicity, because this game has so much love and care put into it, it deserves it.The devs deserve support on this game, lets give them some help!UPDATE: On the final day, HAVE YOUR FOOD BAR AT MAX, I LOST A LOT OF PROGRESS BECAUSE I DIDN'T HAVE ENOUGH STAMINA TO ENDURE THE CYCLE. Don't pull a me.:(UPDATE 2: This is the part where I give an honest take on the game: its not bad, but has a lot of flaws and nitpicks along the way of grinding the game out;1. NO FAST TRAVEL, NOT EVEN AFTER GETTING YOUR FIRST ENDING. This makes the game irritating to go through, having to run back and fourth back and fourth back and fourth to your house, it just gets sluggish and tanks the gameplay and feel of the game.2. Some parts of the game are not explained properly, like for the achievement of giving the right food to the girl every day, you don't realise that you have to press back to give her the food shes specifically asking for, but most players see this as just the game telling you what you should do for the next day, then you start to realise "oh, wait, I was supposed to feed her properly on the first day too-" and welp there goes your achievement do that on your next playthrough!3. Witching hours are very annoying, you just have to go through and wander around for the most part to solve some things. In the demo, I was looking for 20 minutes for the final key when it was in a bookshelf... 4. THE DREADED SNAKE WITCHING HOUR PUZZLES. Whoever thought it was a good idea to roleplay as a baby that got out of its crib at night as one of the puzzles, why? I also VERY ENJOYED THE MONSTERS THAT DEAL 1 and a half hearts of damage while annoying warping you all over the place while also being incredibly quick with little breathing room! (I will also bring up the moth puzzle in the second witching hour night, I got confused for a solid 30 minutes trying to interact with everything. Please update the game to make these a bit more obvious...)5. Refer to first update edit. I did not enjoy having to backtrack to get to the ending of the game over a stamina issue over saves.6. Repeatability is just very tedious and slow, which demotivated me to do the rest of the achievements (I decided to not cheat in the rest of the achievements I just gotta wait to see if they add fast travel, you guys should too, get the endings you'd like and wait.)7. Endings are a bit lackluster, you get a bit of dialog and they just mostly end abruptly. They're too short, some are sweet, but I would've loved to see more from them.8. Final day is just too bland, not even a final fight against the big bad... I would've loved an ending to fight against the main evil with your lover or something, that would've been a nice way to end it. No complaints to the art the art for the game was great like always!9. Some important characters just don't have portraits which bummed me out. The big bad? none! The secondary evil lady? NADA. I understand they don't show up most of the time in the story, but they're still important! 10. Sanity mechanic was only used for specific parts and was more of an annoyance than anything else. Sanity is only used for collecting Golden Girls, and being in darker parts of the overworld. Speaking of Overworld parts-11. THE ENDING RELATING TO THE CHURCH IS JUST DISAPPOINTING. When I watched and played the demo myself, I thought there'd be more to it, but it just ends up being a side ending thats very similar to another ending relating to the secondary evil character! What was the point of that evil creature in the first part of the secret when everything was related to Elise herself? How come there was 0 indication on the jewel puzzle? I read "I can't reach whats in there" so I think to myself "What if I used the broom?" NOPE! You have to place the jewel on the empty pedestal behind the hole????? EVEN ELISE WAS CONFUSED!Don't get me wrong, I loved the experience, you can see a lot of care put into this game, but honestly, I think the game should've been released in 2024 to add more to the game.I know I said too many negative things, but the artwork, the music, and the story was all sweet! Don't let these get in your way of the game, its still a great experience for your first time!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is an absolute masterclass in its various artstyles, and I personally believe it's worth playing just for the art. The music is perfect, the dating scenes are fun, the minigames for earning money are awesome. However, where the game falls flat for me is the story and gameplay.Let's start with the story - it feels like watching two trains slowly approaching each other on the same track. Everyone knows they're gonna crash hours before it happens and no one is doing anything. The story itself is good, but too simple for a 9 hour game. Mainly because during the first night, you're already going to have a rough outline what's going to happen at the end. And the story repeats the same rough outline for 9 hours with almost no major twists. It can be quite frustrating to play as a heroine who sees every single warning imaginable and just keeps going without thinking at all. Guess that's why she's wearing red all the time, red flags just seem like flags to her.The gameplay is again, too simple for a game this long. While the suspicion mechanic is fun, a lot of the choices in dialogue boil down to "Normal response" and "Yeah, I'm the witch and source of all your troubles, please, put a stake through my heart right now." The game features a lot of unnecessary repetiton, such as walking from your home to the city every single day, sometimes more than once. The puzzles are... sometimes not puzzles at all. Just walking around and pressing all the buttons available. They feel way too easy for the lenght of the game, just like the story. I'd like to see more building up on previously established mechanics - such as when the second time you go to the Crow's "fields". The designers could then place enemies in trickier positions and create exciting situations.I don't want to claim the entire gameplay was boring, or that there weren't interesting dialogues. Just that it felt like a game with 4 hours of great ideas stretched to fill a 9 hour game. As I said at the start, the game is still absolutely worth experiencing, it just feels bad that I can't call this game a masterpiece, when its art and music wowed me at every turn.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:As everyone else has been saying, the art and music are beautiful. The sound design is one of the best I've heard in this style of RPG. The horror imagery is fantastic, it's just the right amount of uncanny and stylistic. I LOVED finding the Golden Girls as well, my first ending their involvement didn't really apply but I'm working through endings where it will and I have an unreasonable amount of built up hype for it. I also really enjoyed the mini games visually and mechanically. The only disappointment I had with that was the rat game, and how often you're meant to play it to make money. It's probably the least fun out of all of them. Doable, but wish it wasn't so... Popular.Also... Whoever was on this team did their sapphic homework. This is the gayest thing I've seen all year, and it's NOVEMBER. EDIT: I forgot to mention in the initial review, my favorite part-- Like without question, my favorite part is when [SPOILERS] Elise gets her red shoes, dances to the square, and the reveal is that she's ACTUALLY singing and dancing. That blew my mind the first time I played through it, I was under the impression that it was a trope sing-a-long moment and knowing that it was reality REALLY grabbed me. Wonderfully done.The Not So Good:Some of the puzzles are frustrating. I can definitely tell that the devs put a lot of work into trying to figure out how to make things complex while still guiding the player in the right direction, and I would say that it was mostly successful. The big 'moon room' is probably (mechanically) the clumsiest. That one boss fight... The one with the three locks? That needs to be changed. I'm all for a punishing boss mechanically speaking because once I figured out how to handle the dodges I was set. And it gave me a very 'I DID IT' feeling, which is what you want. But I'm not sure how many people are going to be able to figure out the tricks to get through it. Apart from THAT, however, the 50/50 choice options you have incredibly unfair consequences if you get them wrong. You should not get one-shot for... Honestly, very vague options. Punished by having to repeat the mechanics? Sure. Halved health? You betcha. One-shot for that is unreasonable.As of November 7th only 16% of people have the achievement of defeating that boss. My First Completion, Ending #10 (MASSIVE SPOILERS): So I went into the game with the mindset of not romancing anyone on my first playthrough. I will be working towards all the endings but I wanted to do that one first because I figured it would be the shortest. I was purposefully avoiding the love interests and dialogue with them. I went on no dates. I had no hearts with any of the girls. And when I got to Aziel in the twisted church, it just... Picked Rozen? Which is fine, she's our 'they were roommates', she's with us most of the story anyhow. In that moment it makes sense.The first dialogue option in that fight was about a bracelet and a pine cone that I never received. The second, I made a lucky guess. And the third option was about 'fate' and 'purpose'. You're meant to choose 'purpose'. Which is kind of insane to me, maybe that makes more sense if you ACTUALLY romance Rozen but if you don't she's spouting about 'fate' left and right and that's all the context you have. So with that run, it one-shot me on the last lock and I had to do the whole thing all over again. I answered honestly a couple of times, too, on how I did plan to use her to get what Elise wanted. One-shot.The game needs you to have a romance with the girls for the 'Good Company' for its story, but it doesn't actually need you to romance ANY of the girls to get a conclusion for its story or mechanics. If you got Ending # 10, you'll know what I mean. So with that in mind, I don't know why the devs didn't consider that option with Aziel? Up until this point I had no trouble getting around with the decisions I made. I was getting to know the town and its people, not so much the girls, and it was really fun to play it that way. Getting the dialogue with them was so special and well thought out. I knew my ending was gonna be rough, I was making selfish choices and I was willing to sacrifice anyone to get there. That's bad karma in RPGs. ♥♥♥♥ me up, fam, tell me that I'm bitter and stone-hearted and only my mother could love me. ...If you got Ending #10, you'll know what I mean. But don't one-shot me when I have no context.It didn't ruin the game for me by any means, but it took me out of the moment. I'm looking forward to playing through the other endings and seeing how that goes.GLITCHES FOUND (will be updating, MASSIVE SPOILERS):1. When Apfel is lost and blindly walking around, you can glitch through to the right bottom corner and get to his side of the map. This isn't really a big deal, since he falls in the pit and it ends (so if you saved it's just a restart). At first I thought it was supposed to happen, the transition was so natural.

_childDocuments_.review: While I do recommend this game, I'll need to clear the air of some grievances.1. If you, like me, saw the trailer and thought there was a charismatic narrator to accompany the cut-scenes you will be disappointed to find out that spoken English is quite limited to what is essentially sound effects on dialogue boxes. The game looks amazing so you might think a lot more is going on in the game than there is. Temper your expectations and you'll have a great time, especially if you happen to be a lady that fancies intimate moments with other ladies. While I am not a lady, I still managed to have an overwhelming amount of respect for this game.2. The game is not afraid of locking you into a route that has only bad endings available at the end. So if you didn't make bread before Thursday, you have made a terrible mistake... this is not a joke. Also, it's important to know that there are exactly 3 happy endings in this game and coincidentally there are exactly 3 girls you can choose to date... let that sink in very thoroughly. Save early, save often.
