_childDocuments_.name: SUPER CRAZY RHYTHM CASTLE

_childDocuments_.review: I apologize for the formatting of this review, I don't normally review games but this one had so few and I felt it deserved a bit more feedback.I enjoyed this game quite a bit! It puts a new spin on the rhythm game genre. The songs are fun and always get stuck in my head, the games are interesting and challenging, but never too hard to complete, and the story was amusing. You can tell a lot of care and love went into this game with it's design and art direction. On the sad side, there are some issues I felt need to be addressed. (ENDING SPOILERS AHEAD) The fake ending was neat, but confusing. Fake credits role, the king laughs and "....what do I do now?" I thought to myself. My partner and I explored around, found the bunker, and did the extra demon levels. But how do we get those last two stars? How do we get the real ending? Oh, well, you were supposed to "know what to do" says The Traveler. Well, thanks to a well placed comment on a random Youtube video we found out you have to look at the screens behind The Traveler to know which levels to go back to. Maybe if we had played the whole game in one day, I would have remembered the random times we had seen them in those levels, and would have remembered on my own accord to go back and visit them. But alas, I did not play this all in one day and even if I did my memory is just not that good. That being said, I did find it very neat and cool to go back to those levels where, at one point, it didn't make sense to see this character there, only to have it make complete sense coming back at the end. It really ties the whole "Traveler" thing together, traveling through time and the game and such. But I will absolutely need that "long story" explained to me at some point! Anyways, we do all that stuff, play the end again, and...well, it was different, but it still didn't feel like a True Ending, unfortunately. In my opinion, if you're going to have fake credits role for a fake ending, you should have real credits role for a real ending. It puts the punctuation at the end of a well earned ending. Besides all that, there are some nit picky things I'd like to see addressed: The Darkness level should not be that hard to 3 star with only two people. I know it's possible (and I only know it's possible thanks to a Steam Forum comment), but it shouldn't be that hard to figure out and preform.I haven't 100% the whole game, and I probably never will, as that requires playing almost every song perfectly, a goal I find to be unrealistic for the average person. I think having a small one or two error buffer on each song to get platinum wouldn't hurt.That being said, do the doors at the end of the castle ever open? Are they just these big shiny doors that "just seem to not want to open" forever? If so, a design change would be helpful here, adding chains, barriers, or even a silly little sign that says "real fake doors" would be an improvement. Unless they open after you 100% or something, then something that denotes that would be helpful. I often found that I had a hard time remembering which trigger used which weapon, some sort of UI element to help remind the player would help ease this frustration. All that being said, I really did have a great time playing this game with my partner, and I recommend it to any fan of rhythm games, couch coop games, or party games. It's a solid 7.5/10, and if any additional content were to come out for this game, I'd happily play it.
_childDocuments_.name: SUPER CRAZY RHYTHM CASTLE

_childDocuments_.review: Up front I'm gonna say you should buy this game on sale, the gameplay is fantastic but the amount of gameplay is not worth $40.THAT BEING SAID.This game has a perfect mix of fun (but often very challenging) minigames mixed in with your standard 4 lane rhythm gameplay. These work in tandem to create a really aggravating but addictive loop of 'wow that was fun but i only got 1 star, i'll stop when i get 3 stars' and you'll be stuck there for a WHILE trying to achieve perfect gameplay.I've only played this game in a group (which I recommend) as the challenges are actually really difficult for 1 person to manage. _childDocuments_.review: I'm going to specify that I got this game with a heavy discount on the code. Yet I still feel ripped off. I am a solo player and rhythm game enthusiast. It is extremely rare that I ever use online multiplayer functions. I think I have only played two co-op games in my entire life. I went in solo, under the assumption this was bunch of music stages held together by a kooky storyline about a scamp of a king who likes to annoy people in his wacky funhouse of a castle.This unfortunately is not really a music game. It's a bizarre party game. Yes, the stages primarily incorporate music, but you can't really call it a rhythm game when a big part of gameplay is actually built around throwing a bunch of irritating obstacles in your way where you have to stop what you are doing, do the little challenge, and jump back into your combo. I guess I do not multitask well, because I found these distractions completely killed my groove, man! I can't seemlessly pick up a complicated note sequence after I've spent the last half minute throwing buckets of water on an overheating engine.While you can technically play the game solo, I believe from the hour I played that the stages are a lot easier the more people you have in the multiplayer with you. You have to clear the obstacles quick or you get an instant game over or run out of time to a certain amount of points, and it's only natural that's going to be easier the more hands you have. There are a bunch of other little things I really did not like:It forces you to download some application from Epic that's related to multiplayer even if you don't intend to go online. The dialogue is unskippable. Some bits and bobs have have a fast-forward (that isn't all that fast) but not all of it. I found the default button layout very awkward because they had to use three controller buttons as dedicated music buttons while reserving two buttons to act as an action and cancel action button for everything else. I suppose that is easily fixable with some controller remapping, but I did not bother because the fundamental problem is that Super Crazy Rhythm Castle is just not a good a rhythm game. This is not a game for music game fans. This more for the Mario Party crowd.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that functionally, this game is great. I don’t think my friends and I encountered a single bug with the game during our entire playthrough.Additionally:- Songs are varied in genre and difficulty in a very well rounded way.- The world hubs are, with few exceptions, well designed and we generally always knew where we were expected to go next.- The rhythm game mechanics are well polished.- There’s a good variety in the types of minigames that happen alongside songs.- The game design/aesthetic is cute and generally the screen/environment is pretty “readable”.- The length is good, and the bonus unlocks are reasonably obtainable.Unfortunately there are several issues that took away from our experience with the game:- The minigames are generally very poorly explained. This isn’t necessarily a bad thing, most are simple enough to not need any explanation, and trial and error can be really fun! But some of the mechanics are unenjoyably obtuse. Some levels have a nice intro to force you to trigger a mechanic before you can start, but some levels throw you in with 0 information.- Because of how involved some of the minigames can be, it often turned into 2-3 players playing the song the full time with 1-2 players handling the minigame and not playing a single note.- The writing is juvenile, disjointed, and presented so slowly that it’s a chore to sit through. There is occasionally a funny quip, but I found that most of the dialogue missed its mark. I think part of this is because of technical limitations with how they decided to display dialogue, but in the end it’s lackluster. Having to sit through stage intros with only a fast-forward button instead of a skip is excruciating for some of the stages.- The keyboard controls are a little rough. The semicolon is not allowed to be bound in the settings, so using wasd + jkl; is out.- The difficulty shift from regular to pro is extreme. I do wish there was something in the middle.- Releasing a held note too early counts as a miss, which is a bad design choice, imo. Make hit/miss count at the beginning and the hold count for points only. This makes some of the chording later in the game really aggressive.This may be worth it if you can share one copy between all your friends, but it’s certainly not worth $160 between four people. Ultimately, though, I wouldn't recommend this as the frustrations with the game outweighed the enjoyment in my experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly a very entertaining game.I started playing solo and then together coop with one of my friends. We both ended up finishing the game and hunting for coins and perfection. While over all reaching 140 coins in the music lab is rather pretty crazy, most songs and the 2 difficulty levels provided sufficient additional game value afterwards. There is also a hall room with a few levels just for PvP games, however, we did not really make much use of it, since all others options make much more fun.Most levels are literally made for coop-action, and playing solo (with a handdog, a bot filling that gap) makes it rather difficult to finish these particular stages (meat/nectar-level). Some tasks were in solo-mode also just rather random and sometimes a little bit annoying, while with two players those tasks started to make fun (more or less lol).Some stages require you to make up your mind first on how to finish them efficiently and eventually collecting 3 stars. While the main goal is still to play the music (more or less), every level still has its own stagging and perks. I am not gonna go into details here to avoid spoiling things.So the songs that you have played during the story mode get gradually added to your music lab, allowing you to play them over and over again. However, every finished level can always be replayed at any time, Having them in a lab makes it a lot easier though to just move from song to song. There is also a garage with special songs (all konami).It was interesting to see that the game was putting quite some stress on my 6800xt at wqhd. But apart from that it ran fine in sole mode - no probs whatsoever iirc. Coop-mode however was a different story. Most of the time it was fine, but there were here and there some issues. Lag/glitches/stuttering/ghosting of the music panel and tiles. Player characters stutter when moving around the map (this can be minimized by using alternative vsync for all players though). Also I dont understand why the tiles in the panel in the garage tend to lag/stutter that often - I think those lags are also very reproducible. As if those special effects (lights) are overloading the gpu or whatever.In general, its possible to beat the game in just a couple of hours. If you re goofing around, exploring or/and just trying to get all coins/stars, you will end up playing eventually 40-60 hours. The list of songs is very diversified. You will find many genres from metal, arcade, dubstep, k-pop over to rock and swing etc. Can I recommend the game? Hell yeah!Its literally crazy when you realize how fast and how many tiles come down, while you keep on pressing those buttons on your gamepad like nothing happened at all ! Scary and crazy at the same time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. There's really only one problem, and that's the price. If it were up to me, the game is worth $20. I wouldn't buy it if it isn't on sale for at least that much. But this is Konami, so... shrug.if you're looking for a hardcore rhythm game, this isn't it, but it's definitely not a walk in the park, especially if you play on pro. If you like figuring out what to do on your own, this game is great for that. On a blind playthrough, you'll have to play almost every level more than once if you want 3 stars. Almost every level has a unique gimmick, and you can really see the effort put into them. It's also really nice to look at, most parts are cute, but some are just downright pretty. I personally LOVE the silliness of the story, and the NPCs. I also ADORE the soundtrack. The variety is fresh, and I catch myself with some of the songs in my head. While the main campaign isn't very long, the music lab lets you play each song with no gimmicks, which adds a good bit more playtime. Almost all of the levels work completely normally in singleplayer, but for the ones that need another "player," The game has a solution that works pretty well. I would definitely recommend playing with friends just because it's a good time, but it's still worth playing even by yourself.Basically: It rules. If it's on sale, go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing and the fact it's almost completely flown under the radar is baffling and sad, because I genuinely think it's one of the best of the year. It's genuinely brilliant fun, very chaotic.I have do a couple of gripes, most notably playing this game with a controller can leave my fingers a bit sore if I play for too long. I wish the fast-forward cut-scenes option appeared for every cut-scene and skipped them entirely. And sometimes the puzzles are very unclear, though at the same time figuring out each levels bizarre gimmick is part of the fun, it can just take a bit sometimes.(I'd also love to see a practice mode akin to something like Guitar Hero had, getting to practice specific parts would alleviate some frustrations with getting those mint medals.)Regardless of all that, this game is oozing with charm, creativity and genuinely funny writing. The game-play is 9/10 times so much fun even when you're not playing the rhythm game. (Though honestly sod the recipes level, that 3 star was so hard to do in the short time limit.) And almost every song has been stuck in my head since first hearing, the soundtrack here is excellent.If you have even a passing interest in this game you should get it.
_childDocuments_.name: SUPER CRAZY RHYTHM CASTLE

_childDocuments_.review: THE best rhythm game I've ever played. But it's not a just an excellent rhythm game, it's chock full of puzzles and changes up the genre in a way that's unique every single level. I couldn't give this game enough praise because of both how catchy each song was but also how fun it was as a whole. I'd recommend it for every cent and more because it not only has a fully fleshed out campaign for solo/group play, but an entire party game's worth, flaunting 5 different ways to compete with your friends both with and without distractions!The songs never overstay their welcome and it takes many retries of levels to even begin getting annoying. Replayability is definitely a fun ride even if you know the twists and turns! There's even a pro mode for expert rhythm gamers, but that's not to say normal is easy! I've played a handful of rhythm games and even on normal I was definitely struggling to keep up with some levels (looking at you wheel). Knowing this, I'd recommend groups that are a little bit older since you can't progress until you've beaten each level at the minimum required score.That also goes for remote play, which this game does have. It goes without saying that bad connections are going to make precise rhythm games a nightmare so you would definitely need strong internet to host full online parties. Online is available too if everyone can get a copy and it works just fine!Solo is definitely doable but the experience is going to feel a lot shorter since you can beat the campaign by sinking in about 6-7 hours. That's not to say there's more content however, as there's challenge levels that are harder than the originals and many levels requiring you to play each song much better without distractions. There's definitely a lot to come back to after beating the main game!Overall, I'd give SUPER CRAZY RHYTHM CASTLE a 9.5/10 Must Buy! This is a genre defining game that spices up the rhythm format in every single way that makes it not only extremely fun for fans of rhythm games, but allows those less familiar with it to enjoy it's teamwork, puzzles, and crazy adventure!
_childDocuments_.name: SUPER CRAZY RHYTHM CASTLE

name: HARVESTELLA
detailed_description: HARVESTELLA, an all-new life-simulation RPG from SQUARE ENIX! Our protagonist awakens during the height of Quietus, a disaster that visits with the changing of each season – and a threat to all life. Lead a life of self-sufficiency with your vibrant house as a base and cooperate with allies to overcome various threats, all as you draw ever closer to the truth behind the disasters and the very world’s creation! Quietus The season of death that visits with the changing of the seasons. Plants wither. People cannot even walk around outside, due to the dust of death that fills the air. And each year, Quietus persists for longer and longer… World Nemea Town, where cherry trees bloom all year round. Shatolla, a seaside town home to a bustling tavern. Lethe Village, resplendent in the vibrant colours of the four seasons. The Holy Capital of Argene, cloaked in snow. Use the world map to travel to all these settlements and their respective dungeons. You will have to traverse beautiful, treacherous paths to reach the Seaslights – four giant crystals that govern the seasons. Daily Life Grow fruit, vegetables and crops in your fields to either sell or use as crafting materials. If you use the produce you’ve grown in your cooking, the food will grant extremely helpful effects for your adventures, such as HP recovery or temporary stat boosts! It might also be a good idea to take care of some plump cluffowl birds, dignified goat-like woolum, and a pet totokaku. Allies Shrika, a missionary searching for a new form of faith. Heine, a pompous gentleman mechanic. Asyl, descendent of the Wind poem people. And Aria, a mysterious girl who claims to have come from the future. Cooperate with – and sometimes clash with – your allies, including these characters among others. Reach a deeper mutual understanding by facing their worries and their way of life head on. Combat Overcome battles by switching seamlessly between jobs during combat – including the Fighter, adept with swift sword techniques, the Shadow Walker, which deals critical wounds with twin blades, or the Mage, specialising in magic attacks. When faced with a mighty foe, skilfully target their weak points to inflict the Double Break state and take them down in an instant!
about_the_game: HARVESTELLA, an all-new life-simulation RPG from SQUARE ENIX! Our protagonist awakens during the height of Quietus, a disaster that visits with the changing of each season – and a threat to all life. Lead a life of self-sufficiency with your vibrant house as a base and cooperate with allies to overcome various threats, all as you draw ever closer to the truth behind the disasters and the very world’s creation! Quietus The season of death that visits with the changing of the seasons. Plants wither. People cannot even walk around outside, due to the dust of death that fills the air. And each year, Quietus persists for longer and longer… World Nemea Town, where cherry trees bloom all year round. Shatolla, a seaside town home to a bustling tavern. Lethe Village, resplendent in the vibrant colours of the four seasons. The Holy Capital of Argene, cloaked in snow. Use the world map to travel to all these settlements and their respective dungeons. You will have to traverse beautiful, treacherous paths to reach the Seaslights – four giant crystals that govern the seasons. Daily Life Grow fruit, vegetables and crops in your fields to either sell or use as crafting materials. If you use the produce you’ve grown in your cooking, the food will grant extremely helpful effects for your adventures, such as HP recovery or temporary stat boosts! It might also be a good idea to take care of some plump cluffowl birds, dignified goat-like woolum, and a pet totokaku. Allies Shrika, a missionary searching for a new form of faith. Heine, a pompous gentleman mechanic. Asyl, descendent of the Wind poem people. And Aria, a mysterious girl who claims to have come from the future. Cooperate with – and sometimes clash with – your allies, including these characters among others. Reach a deeper mutual understanding by facing their worries and their way of life head on. Combat Overcome battles by switching seamlessly between jobs during combat – including the Fighter, adept with swift sword techniques, the Shadow Walker, which deals critical wounds with twin blades, or the Mage, specialising in magic attacks. When faced with a mighty foe, skilfully target their weak points to inflict the Double Break state and take them down in an instant!

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the main storyline, and still planning to enjoy the sidequests and other content in the game, I really wanted to just give an honest review here. In short, big recommendation for the game, for anyone who enjoys JRPGs (like Final Fantasy) with a dash of farming simulator life. Without getting into any spoilers, story-wise this game is a massive surprise, one that left me emotionally wrecked (in a good way) for the first time after finishing Nier:A years ago. Story is getting wilder and deeper and better the more you progress, and even the side quests feed into it well. The game starts off a bit slow first 10 or so ingame days, aka few irl hours, and the dialogue/setup of everything at the start is pretty cringe. However, the more you play, the more you'll enjoy it. The charm of this game is massive, and you can sink hours into it, or just focus on the story and ignore the farm stuff completely. PROS:- Immersive, large world with relatable characters- Story that will make you question...everything- Interesting new twists on classic JRPG job system- Interesting side stories- Ability to cozy up on your farm and just chillCONS:- in order to progress stuff on the farm, you DO need to do the story, which is unskippable, so if you don't care for that, beware- starts kind of slow- animation lock on some of the skills can make combat difficult for wrong reasonsFor me, definitely worth the price and I'm only stopping the praise so I can go back to play :)

_childDocuments_.review: I read a review stating that all the negative reviews were people that were only 3 or so hours in.  I gave it 14 hours hoping the game would pick up, and it never does.  The farming mechanics are just unnecessary, the return you get on planting seeds is around 5%, and most of the seeds you have are from rewards rather than purchasing them from a merchant.The combat is pretty bad for an ARPG.  At best you get a basic attack, a dodge (for some jobs) and a few special abilities that do just a little more than basic attacks.The job system, equipment and other supporting RPGmechanics are just as basic as everything else.  You don't get multiple weapons, you just upgrade the ones you have (linearly I might add).The story starts off with your pretty standard and uninspired 4 elements and main character with amnesia.The animation is very chunky, particularly during dialogue.  Reminds me of early 3d games.On the plus side, it ran at a solid 120 fps, so that's cool I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so I've reached the point where the game really starts to open up now. It's a shame there's so many negative reviews with less than or around 2 hours, because you haven't even seen the "real" game yet. This is a really fun game. While it's not exactly what I expected, I'm still having a blast with it.First and foremost, this is not a farming sim like Stardew Valley or Story of Seasons, this is a JRPG with farming sim elements to it. The game is leaning more towards being story and side quest driven than just being a traditional farming sim where you do nothing else than just tend to your farm. Your progress will be directly linked to the story, you have to play it in order to progress and unlock more stuff for your farm as well.Story is alright. It's not bad by any means but it's also not groundbreaking. It's good enough to keep me invested and wanting to see where it leads. The side quests surprised me though. They offer some pretty good additional story content and made me care about some of the otherwise bland characters. Plus the quest rewards are pretty good when you're trying to build your farm.Now the farming itself. I'll go ahead and just say that it's nowhere near as good as Stardew Valley. I'd put it somewhere between Rune Factory 5 and Story of Seasons (PoOT). It is satisfying enough though and you can put some good amount of time into this, just not right away. You'll have to unlock most of the stuff that makes the farming fun by doing certain quests, which I don't want to spoil here. To get more of these quests you'll also have to progress the main story. So yeah, farming is good, just not right away. It'll take you a good amount of time to get a good farming experience, which is probably the worst part and the reason for a lot of the negative reviews. Be prepared to put A LOT of hours into this before you have evrything unlocked to have a great farming experience.I also like the fighting system. Again, it's not that great in the beginning, but it starts to shine once you unlock more jobs and skills. You can switch between jobs on the fly and during combat, making fights more fun and engaging. Combat is not too simple, but also not too complicated. They found the right balance here imo.There's a lot to do during your average day in Harvestella, but time is limited, as is usual in this type of game. Time is the most valuable currency and you'll never be able to do everything you want in a day. You'll be forced to leave dungeons right before you reach the boss in order to not black out because the clock strikes midnight. Also, if you die in combat the day ends immediately. So make sure you do all your chores before you head into any battles. On top of that, you'll have to manage your stamina by eating food. If you run out of stamina, you can't do anything, not even swing your sword. So bring food with you if you head into any instances. This might sound rough and too hard, but I'm enjoying having to perfectly manage my time and properly prepare when heading out.A lot of people complained about the graphics, and I agree to a certain extent. The game uses the exact same graphics as the Switch, just with a better framerate and improved resolution. The game can look somewhat ugly in certain areas, but will look really pretty in others. My opinion on this is mixed. There's plenty of videos and screenshots to judge for yourself.Also, small side note, the soundtrack is really good.So, is this a fun game? Yes, definitely. Without any doubt.Is this worth 59,99€ (or the equivalent in your currency)?If you are into both JRPGs and farming sims, yes. Otherwise, no. They're using the same price tag as the Switch version. If this was a PC only title it would probably be somewhere around 40€ or 45€.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been having so much fun with this game. I get really overstimulated by other farming games that throw way too much at you at all times, and where some have argued that Harvestella is not nearly in depth enough with its farming, it is exactly at my level(:I also have a lot of fun with the combat although not all the jobs are to my tastes but that's the point of having options, right?Fun story, lovable characters, beautiful fantasy scenery - if a bit simple. The dialogue is fun and I find myself going out of my way to talk to NPCs (looking at you, old lady yelling at the sky in Nemea) Whether I'm on a grand adventure or collecting twigs in the forest, this holds up. Not once have I felt like a side-quest was a slog.Easily and quickly one of my favorite games ever.Edit:Having finished the game, I just wanted to add that this is officially my favorite game of all time. I wish there were a little more to do in terms of post-game content and the ending itself seemed a little too quick to resolve for all the build-up, but I'm so happy with my overall experience that half of this particular critique/nitpick comes from a place of just wanting more reasons to keep enjoying it.Also, the music is incredible! _childDocuments_.review: Harvestella is a delightful little farm rpg that does its best to ride the coat tails of the studio that made it.  All the functional aspects are there and the framework is (mostly) solid but it gets very shaky as you stack the story on top of it.  To start, the farming aspect is wonderfully simple.  It never gets too complex from start to finish and some of the food designs were cute and fun.  My favorite being moonfruit and nitro pineapple.  Finally perfecting your farm will require you to 100% the fairy orders which is basically 100%-ing the post game as well which is a tad annoying.  I would have preferred the farming aspect be completely unlocked 70-80% so you can focus on the story from there on.Regarding the combat, it manages to function enough to be engaging.  Skills are tied to a stamina system that will ensure you either conserve stamina or be an absolute glutton with food to regain it.  The best skills are at the end of your skill tree though i found myself rarely using most of them.  Shadowblade’s was my favorite.Regarding the story.  Its…somewhat engaging.  Halfway through, your just playing the generic hero, but after that, it gets heavy quick.  Not super heavy but understandably heavy.  Wont go into spoilers but its pretty existential.  Then again, most SE rpg’s tend to be.  I loved the idea of the seth/omen but there is a major contradiction near the end i had with them and the big bad.The characters are endearing.  Each with their own issues that range from revenge to rehabilitation, survival, religion, and acceptance will take place on some of them.  You can even “romance” one of them but i use that word VERY lightly.  The game uses the term “partner” and it sticks.  Your not lovers.  You act more like roommates.  So your romancing is basically asking them to split the rent with you.  One of the weakest parts of this game.  Lastly is the story.  While I wont delve into specifics.  The story started to lose me around Chapter 7.  When all the supposed pieces started falling into place, so did my interest.  One of the biggest elements isn't even a part of the main story.  Its a side dungeon and its not even fully explained.  The story also does little to expand on its most confusing elements and you can feel the lack of focus on the writing team.  This game was not a priority and it shows HEAVILY.All in all, it’s a decent product but wait for a sale.  This IS NOT a $60 game.  $30 for sure.  Not enough quality was put in for it to warrant that large price tag as this game looks like it would have been big in the early PS3/360 era, not when it did release.

_childDocuments_.review: --New Review after 27 Hours of Playing the Game--You can read my original review below on my original impressions about the game. Some of it still holds true even now but I can also tell you what has changed in my opinion.I do recommend this game now, especially if you're looking for a Rune Factory-Like game. Harvestella follows heavily into the vein of Rune Factory, while feeling a lot more like a Final Fantasy game.If you looking for a Farm Simulation game, with strong singular community interaction, and changing things on a local scale... this game isn't really for you.If you are looking for a good jRPG, with reliable combat and responsive controls. This game isn't really for you either.If you want a interesting story, with interesting game elements, and is "farm-sim lite", then YES this game is for you. Harvestella is a whole lot of different things, and some of those elements clash from time to time. It has it's charms, but still feels...like it could just be so much more.If I had to rate it:Graphics: 9/10 (While the design direction is certainly unique, there are often weird graphic anomalies during cutscenes)Music: 10/10 (Outstanding, and possible the best thing about this game.)Story: 7/10 (Oddly paced, and sometimes nonsensical. The main story is understandable and easy to follow, but some of the side quests seem forced and rather... odd. Like shallow and lacking depth at times.)Voice Acting: 3/10 (@Square Enix: WHY IS IT ONLY DURING COMBAT!?!? BAD!)Combat: 5/10 (No active dodge, until you skill into it. Even then no benefit for dodging. You can completely skip certain fights by just using the orbs you craft. 2-4K Damage is enough to instant kill most enemies. You yourself, the character, may as well not even engage in melee combat. You will be targeted first, you will die first, and you will hate it.)Controls: 6/10 (Janky, unexpected, and undersirable.)Overall I'd rate this game a 7 out of 10. It has elements that saves it, but other elements that are dissatisfying. For a AAA Game company like Square Enix to deliver a game that lacks REASONABLE COMBAT, when they have MANY MANY games where they did it well... it's infuriating. This game tries to be a LOT of things. Some of those things it does well, others... not so much.--Original Review after 4 Hours Playing the Game--First I would like to say that I want to like this game, I really do. But for a Company like Square Enix, I expect better. This game has so many other part-time farmer/warrior games that came before it (Rune Factory series being a prime example), all made by studios with smaller budgets, and less resources than Harvestella... and yet somehow they all managed to make something better than what Square Enix gave us.The Character Creation is rather anorexic, only giving us the option to change Eye Color, Hair Color, and Skin tone. I won't get into body types, because it's all just rather laughable, and truly just a meme worthy joke, that they could have not even bothered at all.Voice acting is... minimal. It's all pretty much just background noise, and doesn't occur in the important parts of the games... which is literally the cutscenes...which is where we've been taught to EXPECT voice acting.Art direction is...rather typical for Square Enix. It actually doesn't stand out, and is almost expected. Also, the design choices seem to have been the source of the issue where the player character doesn't have greater customization, because they choose to do CHARACTER ART of your character.Animations are clunky and not fluid, and even trying to farm the land can be more of a chore than it needs to be. It quite literally locks you into a position when using the hoe, watering tool, or hammer. Even combat is just such an immense hassle. You're committed to an action, and there is no active dodge at all. Like the story so far is interesting, but at the same time feels lethargic. In other games there is depth to the relationships, not only with the main cast, but also the rest of the community, and you can build friendship with even the lesser characters. In Harvestella, you're kind of removed from the community, and there is no depth to the relationship of your immediate neighbors, let alone the broader community.I don't know, I really expected more from Square Enix on this, especially for having to pay $60. The game feels janky, and despite having a polished appearance, really needs more work on the basic fundamentals of character controls. There just seems to be a lot of bad decisions of Square Enix's part, and the game feels like it needs more time than what they gave it. I'd almost rather go back to playing Stardew Valley, Rune Factory, or even other games that feel less like a cash grab.

_childDocuments_.review: I am so disappointed since I was really looking forward to this game. The UI ruined it for me. Mouse scrolling seemed to not be an option for anything. If you have any sort of specialized mouse, it will likely not be of much help. _childDocuments_.review: I usually buy games on sale but I went ahead and splurged and got this right away because I am a Square Enix fan from the days of yore. I went in hoping for a revolutionary game - a Final Fantasy quality story with Harvest Moon level farming, I'd pay any price!!! Well... this isn't that but it does deliver with an interesting story. I've played almost every farming sim out there and none have gripped me with the story the way this one has. The side characters are interesting as well, having intriguing backstories, and so you're excited to have the next bit of dialogue with them - rather than some generic small talk. It's also a nice bonus that they give you a few dialogue options to pick from in conversation... it's no Fallout level of choice, but the options felt different enough to be fun and let me feel like I had a hand in shaping my generic player character's personality.My complaint would be the wonky controls in the farming area - it makes you wonder if the designers ever played a farming game before? Come on! We have the Harvest Moons, the Rune Factories, Stardew, all the crafting and building games available that have done it right... make the farming less clunky, please! There is no need to lock the character in a weird seed-planting gesture after planting a seed. But, all and all, the farming is just a short chore you do before going out to do rpg fighting, exploring, and experiencing more of the story, so I can put up with it - but yes, it's a missed opportunity for something fun rather than a clunky chore. If you like story games, you'll want to give this one a try. If you like farming sims... buyer beware. ^^

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is an absolute dumpster fire, this is evident as early as the first combat encounter. Animations for everything are stiff and emotionless. General movement and combat feel loose, cheap, and generally lacking a sense of weight. Zero voice acting an hour into the game, with a practically 480p prerendered cutscene being used an intro. UI prompts look cheap, and have no confirmation sound, making them feel like a placeholder asset that was never replaced. Default confirmation button for controllers is "B/CIRCLE", which makes sense with Nintendo controllers on the switch version, but not on PC. You can switch this option to be "A/CROSS", but it should definitely be the default.This is not a $60 product. Far from it. Even $20 feels like pushing it, with how downright cheap initial presentation and gameplay looks and feels. Only play this if a sale drops it down to $5 and you grow tired of playing RF4S or Stardew for the sixteen thousandth time. RF5 is better than this, and that game is also too much of an asking price at $50. At least that game has a dodge button.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid farming sim/RPG hybrid in the vein of Rune Factory.  The world design and story is a thousand times better than the latest Rune Factory, though whether you enjoy the actual gameplay more or less than Rune Factory is going to depend pretty heavily on taste.  I like it more, but I'm sure a lot of people will like it less. There's a lot of crafting, and the crafting elements all tie back into either weapons or the food system, which is used for combat.  Unlike some sims, you actually do need to eat some kind of food or your stamina won't recover, which is a pretty cool touch.  Weakest point for me is that while there are plenty of devices and so on that you can construct, your actual farm itself has basically zero customization.  The customization options for the main character are also pretty lacking - you can't even wear class outfits in cutscenes, which is a bizarre decision to me. People who like the post-game grind from Rune Factory will probably be a bit disappointed because it doesn't seem like there are any hardcore options for weapon customization - upgrades are very linear.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the naysayers reviewing this game, Harvestella is absolutely fantastic. From the farming feeling fluid and satisfying, to the exploration giving the RPG feel. _childDocuments_.review: First and foremost I just wanted to say I am a little glad this game got a good few negative reviews because it meant that the key shop I bought this from lowered it's price significantly and I was able to pick it up earlier than I anticipated.Going into this I want to try and not compare this game to any other franchise and just treat it as it's own individual game.HARVESTELLA from the opening for character creation it's shallow, you get to pick a skin colour, a hair colour, an eye colour, a voice for your character (which I think is either broken or just never used) and then pick your name it's simplistic but for this kind of game it works it's not the most HD 4K ultra realistic graphic game I've seen but it works.As for the opening cutscene and story, it's a nice and vast array of the colour pallet and makes the games aesthetic pleasant on the eyes. As for the story it's generic as it gets.The farming portion is quick and snappy you don't need to go through about 3 menus just to get to the one item you need, Hold one button and press another and swap between whatever items you need which is a plus, the only tiny problem I have with the farming so far is the hoe, to plant seeds you need to tilt the ground twice but aside from that pretty good.Combat: Like any other RPG you beat the crap out of any enemies in your way so you don't die and get EXP for your trouble. It's all freeflow and no turn based fights here.From what I've played so far, it just honestly gives me I am Setsuna (with farming and only with snow sometimes) vibes all around, the calming nature of the town you're in, the music and the visuals.Fundamentally the game runs smoothly at 120FPS at max settings with no crashes or anything game breaking as of yet which is a major plus. Some animations are a little wonky but hopefully this gets fixed in a future update.Now the main problem I have with all of this, is the developers mind set and the Nintendo Switch, this game is the exact reason as to why no game in 2022 should be developed for multiple systems while only have the switch's limitations in mind as far as I'm aware the switch is such a niche market and devs should stop trying to put games like this on there cause it's setting them up for failure. Had this game moved to the other side of the spectrum where it was developed for PC and then ported around it would have been a lot better and there would have been much better visuals and maybe more customisation.Considering the £50 price mark at the moment for a switch game on PC it definitely isn't worth it right now, a sale would be the best to wait for.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is wonderful so far. The slew of negativity is completely unwarranted. It is a bit slow to start, but that's true for most JRPGs and farming sims alike. No, it's not Final Fantasy. No, it's not Stardew Valley. If that's what you want, then yeah, move on. It's closer to Rune Factory, but if the plot was a little more serious and the combat took precedence over the farming. I'm reviewing this before completing it just because a lot of the current criticism is unfair  and I wanted to help balance it out. Thus far, the writing, world-building, and characterization has been fantastic. It's been a very long time since a game's cast and story has caught me so entirely, but here I am, invested in the lives of random NPCs. The farming is simple but fun, and it expands as you progress. The art is gorgeous. The combat is enjoyable and the job system keeps it entertaining and fresh. Also, the animals are so fricken cute. The only thing that I found underwhelming was fishing, which is thoroughly uninteresting, though I don't see that as game-breaking. This game is awesome, but if you don't like JRPGs or story-heavy games, you're going to be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, its basically final fantasy with a small farming mechanic that takes 4 minutes at the beginning of each day.The dungeons are hard and require quite a bit of grinding, the bosses are equally hard.The people complaining about the price must have never owned a gameboy, an snes orSega Genesis.The amount of effort in the art and the fact that this game came out with barely any bugs. That cant be said for really any new releases in the last 4-5 years.Also people saying its too pricey dont understand economics or even game design.If $1 represents 1 hour of gametime and a game allows for 100 hours of game play, than a 59.99 dollar price tag is more than enough to pay for development.The other complaint stems from this unwillingness to play as a feminine character. Which brings me back to gameboys, snes’s and sega. You dont modify an rpg character back then because you are that character, I point to Cloud from FF7. You are Cloud, noone else. You wear what he wears. In this game you can be male female and everything in-between but you are still Ein. Its basically pokemon, you can be a girl or a boy but you are still the default up until customization was introduced which has been recent.Thats all the negative down votes Ive seen.The game is good, its hard to put down. There’s a lot of socio-politcal commentary in it, for example you save a Siren from trafficking in one quest. This is Final Fantasy, not a life sim.

_childDocuments_.review: If you play this game as the first one of its type, you might not know, but this game is just a fast cash grab by copying and fusing games like Rune Factory and the Ateliere Series.Why am I making this harsh description? Simply because it is such low grade quality in comparison to other established games on the market.Let me give examples: The game asks you in the beginning which languages you want for voicelines, but except the attack-type-moaning there has not been a singular voiceline for the whole tutorial and a little beyond. Even if such a grand and wealthy studio like Square Enix doesnt have enough time to record all voicelines, they could simply do the trick like in Rune Factory 5 where they just have some general small voicelines just to color the text with fitting sound. This game has nothing.Charakter Creation is simply a joke. It lets you choose barely anything and dont get me started about the male character template, that ... _thing_ is simply unaceptable to represent anyone. I know this game was primarily made for the female audience, but it would have been a better decision to not put any male character in, like in the Ateliere Series, then to have THAT... But then comes the story telling, far aside from the standards that Square Enix itself has set, this games tutorial is simply unbearable. You get to make choices that simply change nothing. NOTHING, not even a singular textline difference! And until you are done with the story tutorial, you are given freedom of movement, where you have to run towards your story markers but there is actually no freedom as the game forces you towards the goal by simply cutting of any other direction you might wanna look at. Lets not talk about how low-grade the logic of the NPCs are, or boderline forced the whole situation is... Its worlds logic was butchered and the setting forced to get the gameplay barely integrated into the story...Honestly the word "forced" seems to be the essence of the game. But its not all that bad, the visuals and music are as great as one knows it from Square Enix and the fighting system is probably good if you advance the story a bit. But why bother with this game, when other games have both good visuals, music AND Worldbuilding... especially when the gameplay itself is barely different.

_childDocuments_.review: The environment looks pretty, if a little barren here and there. While the story is your rather predictable four-elements dungeon set-up, it is enjoyable and welcoming to people of all kinds. I like the farm economics, it's simple, but relaxing--and you can go and break that up with fun quests, typical fantasy combat, and of-course, fishing. If I had one critique, it's that they didn't put enough into animating the characters. They're all cheap stock animations(really, really bad robot people animations), and they're the same for every character. I know that asset reuse is important and saves time--but if you're gonna copy-pasta it across the board, at least find someone on your team with a VR kit and mocap some actual human expressions. I also have mixed feelings about the lack of a skip feature, I like the inability to skip forcing me to watch the story content, I actually think that's a great thing--watching the doctor complain about me dying for the 10th time--eh, that got really boring. That having been said, I opened the game, set my 1 hour timer, and I wasn't able to put it down. I've really enjoyed the game as a whole so-far, and with the exception of one really spectacularly focused camera perspective putting a giant low-poly cliff with heavily optimized generic ground texture on a rule-of-thirds corner during a key dramatic scene--I think this is a lovely game. I don't think it's a $60 lovely game, but if the story and gameplay come through, I'd be happy to pay $40 for it.UPDATE: So far the story has carried through, I've been really impressed with the world design given some limitations. Again, this game would be hard-pressed to compare to other similarly priced titles, so I still feel that the price was a little high, but I don't regret the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: After 40+ hours of Harvestella, I honestly think that this is one of the best farming sims and it might be my favourite JRPG to release this year. In the way that Rune Factory 1 revolutionised the genre by adding dungeon crawling to the time honoured Harvest Moon format, Harvestella actually does something different and takes the concept further, giving you a massive story driven JRPG quest with hours of charming side-stories and intriguing character story arcs on top of the farming stuff. And the farming stuff is actually refreshingly simple and restrictive in a way that actually makes the game better than its contemporaries. A lot of reviews complain about this, but I think its actually one of the game's greatest strengths because it fixes one of the genre's biggest issues: Pacing.In RF4 and RF5, the games give you TOO MUCH time and freedom to do what you want. You can easily craft 100 strawberry milkshakes by the start of Summer and never have to worry about RP and end up spending every day from morning to midnight. The games have stopped being punishing in any way and I end up burning out before the first year is over. In modern farming sims RP/stamina is no longer a resource you have to manage, dungeon crawling isn't something you need to prepare for and actually advancing the calendar takes forever because you can do so much in a single day. Harvestella fixes this pacing issue in a number of clever ways. Cooking and crafting takes time. At first this sounds incredibly restrictive, but its actually a great way to push the calendar forward instead of burning out on the game within a single game month. You actually have to allot days to certain activities like "today I'm going to mine ore, tomorrow I'm going to save my stamina and do the dungeon." You can advance the calendar by just crafting all day and feeling like you still accomplished something even instead of feeling like you have to go and do 10 more chores before going to sleep. I can't emphasise how refreshing it was to be in that mindset, after being in the "I need to spend 30 minutes on each calendar day to maximise my time and I have 7 days until this crop ripens" mindset for so many years.Questing also takes time. Not only are there a metric ton of sidequests and character quests in the game, but the fact that moving on the world map takes time means that you have to pick and choose your activities. Maybe there are 3 quests you need to do in Nemea, and 4 quests you need to do in Shalotta. It'll take you several days to complete them because of the time it takes to travel. This isn't wasting your time playing the game, its just moving the calendar forward so you can quest as an alternate activity while your crops are growing. The game gives you more tasks than you can possibly do in a single day, so take your time, let your crops grow and sit back and enjoy the story.This is where it really shocked me. The story is actually really good and is a driving force for playing the game. After the first 2 chapters show you the ropes, the game takes off the rails and gives you the freedom to explore the world, visit the three other cities and assemble your JRPG party in any order you want. Each town has a lengthy storyline where you'll recruit companions and tackle the dungeon, but each is wildly different. And each one has tragic consequences for the characters involved that give them reasons to join you on your journey. I want to be as vague as possible because the game has done such a good job at hiding what the plot is actually about until you play it. The twists in the story are simultaneously set up well in advance while also being ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crazy so its something you have to see for yourself.Each town has hours of side quests to tackle, most of them being character driven little dramas. For example, one quest has you helping out a girl at the orphanage who doesn't want to be adopted. Another quest has you reunite a woman with her amnesiac fiance. Another quest is about a woman pretending to be a man's granddaughter in order to steal his wealth. Each quest comes in multiple parts and can take you across the world to complete, helping the world feel more alive as everyone's got their own hopes and dreams that you can help accomplish. The quests remind me of NieR's quests although most end in a happy ending instead of a murder suicide, though a rare few do end in surprisingly sad and tragic ways.Each companion and certain other important characters also get lengthy 10 part story arcs that will take several in-game weeks to complete, and they don't end up being as straight forward as they initially seem. Cres' goal to cure an incurable plague doesn't have the outcome you might expect and Hien's initial story of showing off his submarine to the local kids ends up being a tragic tale of loss with an obscene twist at the end. Again, I don't want to say more, but the story surprised me in its quality and quantity.Weakest part of the game for sure. You can get by mostly by mashing and chugging juice but the boss fights are fun and there are a ton of different jobs to level and skills to learn. The game is fun enough as it is, though it could be way better. The game has FOEs and dungeon events like in Etrian Odyssey but the events can't kill you and the FOEs/FEARs don't chase you far enough to be a threat. Still, blows Rune Factory out of the water in every way so if that's your comparison point, its still a plus.Its a game that gets better the longer you play it. Its simple in a good way, like a throwback to the Gamecube/PS2/DS era of games before things got too complicated and you had too many things to worry about on your farm. The story is weird and all over the place in a good way, where the story goes after you gather your party and visit the 4 major towns isn't exactly a surprise, but its a surprise how far the game takes it. Just play the game for yourself, accept that this isn't Rune Factory or Stardew Valley and its doing its own thing and enjoy the ride.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of both FF14 and games like Stardew, this is a perfect balance of combat/story/side quests. The incorporation of this games version of limit break makes the encounters more interesting and I am so glad you can save at any point in time around the auto save times. _childDocuments_.review: Fair warning, this is not a cozy farming game. It is in fact a fully-fledged, party-based JRPG with a (big) farming part. The farming part is well realized and fun and there is a lot to do in it alone. But to progress you need to play the story as well, which takes a lot of time doing main-, party-member and side-quests that all come with extensive, non-voiced dialogue. So if you are just in the mood to do some farming and ignore the “social” and dungeon crawling parts, this is not a game for you. In Harvestella you will always go back and forth between farming, dungeon crawling and story bits. That said, all the parts of this game are well made and work together hand-in-hand. For example, everything you need for healing life and stamina is made by crafting which is done with components you grow on your farm. There are obstacles in dungeons like broken bridges that need to be repaired with components created during the farming parts. Farming is your usual affair of breaking down rocks, collecting wood in the wild and planting and watering all kinds of seeds during the four seasons. Some stuff can be automated later in the game. Earned items can be sold for money, used in crafting or invested into farm and weapon upgrades.Combat is pretty simple and reminded me of MMORPG combat where you mostly dodge area of effect attacks shown with red circles and lines while spamming standard and special attacks that are on a cooldown. There are twelve different character classes that all come with their own special abilities. Three can be equipped at once and freely changed during combat. You only control the main character Ein who can be female or male, while party members engage on their own. The story itself is surprisingly deep - if you are into convoluted anime-stories - but the presentation itself is probably the biggest downside of the game. While the graphics and artstyle are pretty, it shows that this was made on a tight budget. There is tons of non-voiced dialogue transcribed in mildly animated ingame-cutscenes. The character animations repeat over and over, there are maybe a dozen of different animations for character interaction. The same goes for the music. While the music itself has some great tracks, they loop way too often over the play-time of 60-100 hours - depending on how much stuff you want to do in this game. It doesn’t help that some of the dialogue, especially the minor side-quests, is overly long. It really hampers the pacing of the game. I’d say, if you really focus on doing all the side-quests, Harvestella is ⅓ farming, ⅓ dungeon crawling and ⅓ dialogue/cutscenes.The game runs great on the Steam Deck, but it doesn’t show video cutscenes which happen mostly at the beginning of a new chapter. There are only a few of them, but it’s still a big oversight and can hamper the enjoyment of playing this on Deck. I also had one part very late in the game where I just got a black screen after a cutscene and I had to play that part on my PC instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I for one, am happy with this game. I enjoy roaming the dungeons. It's a bit PSO-esque which is fine by me. I'm 70+ hours in, and haven't beaten the story yet because it just keeps coming.  I've been blown away by the quality of the stories being told in this world.  I've enjoyed them all, even shed a few tears over them. Those who think the battles aren't difficult haven't gotten far enough.  It seems easy enough at first, but it doesn't stay that way.   While I love farming sims,  I'm glad they made the choice to streamline it. This is a visual novel on steroids and if I had to do more on the farm it would be tedious. There's lots of cooking and gathering if you like that kind of thing, the garden is reasonable, and the critters are cute .  Even though it's simplistic, I'm impressed by all the neat stuff I've unlocked so far. Don't be turned off by negative reviews from people who have barely scratched the surface. If you like farming sims and jrpg's, this is an Isekai Life story worth trying out.

_childDocuments_.review: Allow me to make the decision on getting this game far easier for a very specific subset of old gamers out there like me: do you love old SNES Quintet games like Soul Blazer, Illusion of Gaia, or Terranigma? Stop reading now and buy this game. It feels like something that fell out of an alternate reality where super unique action RPGs with close, personal stories on a grand scale are still being made. If you loved those games then you know that ‘feel’ they had and how hard it’s been to find ever since. Harvestella maybe aiming for a farming/RPG hybrid but manages to become something far greater in the process for folks looking for a type of game that has long been lost.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: A game that is both comfy, relaxing, and yet extremely gripping in its story and world building.This is not farming meets final fantasy.This is Nier Automata meets farming.If Nier Automata left you wanting more, play this game. If you like good stories, play this game.The side quests aren't boring fetch quests. Each one has a genuinely interesting story that left me actually wanting to know what came next.Character/personal quests are split into small, bite-size chunks - you can complete them at your own pace without getting locked into an hour-long cutscene gauntlet or dungeon. In fact, just about everything in this game moves at your pace.You can take a break from the world-shattering story to do some farming for a few days, weeks, seasons, YEARS if you're so inclined. And then you can pick up the story or quests wherever you left off. Farming is only as complex or simple as you want it to be. Combat is similar - it's hack and slash-y, facetank everything and use your homemade potions and meals to restore HP/Stamina, but you can minmax if you want with accessories/buffs/resistances.I'd highly recommend this game to anyone who wants a really cool JRPG with a bit of cozy farming on the side. Contrary to how Harvestella was advertised as the opposite (farming with RPG on the side - wrong!!!).

_childDocuments_.review: Last edit afterSince the game is getting bad reviews because "the character isn't male enough" and other (in my opinion) crapy reasons... _childDocuments_.review: Harvest Moon's last few releases have made me drastically lower my expectations for this entire genre. When the early review for this game came out, this game looked like it would just be another rushed cash grab, and I thought I would just skip this one.On release, I saw a streamer playing it and having fun, so I caved and bought it, but kept my expectations low. I've been pleasantly surprised. I've honestly enjoyed this more than the recent Harvest Moon, Rune Factory and Story of Seasons games. This game makes me feel nostalgic where other recent releases have fallen short.I think it's really pretty and relaxing, I like the character art, the music is great. The game is also a lot bigger than I thought it would be. I don't disagree with criticisms - character customization is sad for 2022, most of the villagers are bland...but those haven't stopped me from enjoying the adventure. I think there's a lot to love here. And kudos to the devs for actually listening and making some changes before full release.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Yes.40 something hours into the game and I still haven't finished story. This is what I wanted from Rune Factory 5. A jRPG with farming elements. It started out as expected. Generic protag. I was surprised to see they had hair and eye color changes. Considering games of this genre usually have amnesiac pre made protag A (and B if we're lucky). Even more surprised the color changes reflected in the character profile screen. Just because the name says Harvest in it doesn't mean it's the same line as Harvest Moon or Stardew Valley. You'll be really disappointed if you go in thinking like that. Look at Rune Factory for reference instead.The start is slow and clunky and I was worried that it was a representation of the rest of the game. However I was pleasantly surprised when all the new elements they gradually gave me actually enhanced the gameplay. Everything you unlock feels really rewarding. Side quest, character story quests, farm levels, new recipes... etc. I am drowning in things to do. As a person who loves completing things they got me with the little jewels representing how far I am on character story and things like turning in food/fish for money and recipes and other fun stuff. Nothing is perfect, the battle system is pretty simple but I mean it wasn't boring. I enjoy the telegraphed attacks. FEAR mobs have little gimmicks and I think that is cute as heck. Dungeon progression is actually really nice. I prefer slowly exploring and making shortcuts to go back to where I was before. Instead of just bum rushing through to get to the boss and being done with it. Planning it around my days is half the fun.The skill tree is very small and easy to understand. But man it's good enough. I'm tired of complicated skill trees with too much to think about. I want to focus on my farm! Which by the way I was three months in before I realized I had unlocked another big part of the farm. They got me acting like a little kid finding new things every day. I expected a pretty basic story that was just good enough. However they have made the dialogue for the story and side stories charming enough where I can stay interested regardless of the generic NPC models. Bless them for focusing more on world building than pretty characters. For this type of game, as a long term Rune Factory series fan, I never care about the models much. They would all be blocks of polys back in the DS days, so seeing Squenix art with their stylized models made me happy but it was more like a bonus. So what if they have static facial expressions? That's what the art on the bottom right is for. No voice acting? I guess it was depressing they didn't at least put some well timed reaction noises. I would have liked a "ahh is that so?" or some chuckles/giggles here and there, maybe an exaggerated "EH!?". But voice acting isn't really necessary here. Treat it like a visual novel. All in all it's not the best this genre can do but Square is definitely taking it a step in the right direction. I much prefer this to RF5 in almost all aspects.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to point to my hour count, I've had a hard time figuring out if I -liked- this game for most of my play time, only after a friend asked my thoughts on it, I found it is a resounding 'no'. I will chalk this up to the promise of a mystery and a list of goals that give me bonuses carry me through a game that I eventually described to said friend as 'flavored paste'.The game is half JRPG, and half Farm Sim, and it is incredibly milquetoast in both respects.The combat is basic, You have basic attacks and then special attacks.There are different jobs, you can have 3 equipped to switch between in combat, but they're all some basic flavor of melee or ranged, some have elements/damage types attached to them, you hit enemies with elements/damage type they're weak to to do more damage, For bosses if you hit them enough with what they're weak to you get MORE damage, If you hit them with more than one type they're weak to you get to do MORE MORE damage.When you kill stuff you get exp to all jobs you've equipped, that you can spend on the skill tree for it to unlock more special attacks, up to a max for 4. The best thing about this system is each job has 2 items that can give buffs to any job, most of them fall into phys damage, magic damage, break gauge(the boss weakness bars), and crit. Sounds good right? Unfortunately the best part of the combat, the skill tree, is incredibly vague on what the upgrades to your special attacks do. So if there is a special attack called "Slash" and you go to look at "Slash II" to see what it gives you, it just says something like "Acquires Slash II". Ooookay? Do I get more damage? How much more damage? Does it give more range? Does it reduce cool down time of this skill? No idea! Hope you like looking at wikis, because you're going to start seeing a theme.Okay, so we've got our skills, and we can level up, this is a JRPG, so we get equipment too, right?Other than a weapon, the only swappable gear in the game is for the main character are two rings.Yep.2.So what can these rings do?They can increase defense or attack, protect you from debuffs, or give you more Job EXP. Rings can have multiple slots, and you can make a device to make combine rings and kinda make custom gear with the abilities you want. There are multiple levels for each of the ability, even for the status defense items... but good luck figuring out what the difference is between similarly named ones. What does stomach ache guard do? How is it different from Indigestion?? No, I'm not joking, those are the ACTUAL names for the skills. You would think you can l just look at the ring and it will tell me what it does. No. Short of the defense/attack that you can actually change your stats, if you look at the ring, it just tells you something like "Stun Guard III" You know... the name of the skill. Guess where you have to go to find basic information about your gear?? Did you guess a wiki? I knew you would, you're smart like that, that's why I like you.Here's the thing, I can get through bad or bland game play for a good story.Unfortunately the main story starts of with your basic amnesiac with a bit of a mystery tease and then dives into some wild mental backflips by the end I wish I hadn't paid as much attention as I did. I'm not going into any specifics here. Maybe if I had gone in with a "This is parody" mindset and just laughed at it.Side quests are sub basic and a bunch of people being needlessly difficult because they have to drag out this quest chain for 3 more quests. Most of your interaction with your party members are done through the seasonal dungeon they're attached to. After that you have little side quests to get closer to them and a few other NPCs. They are all of similar quality.I think part of the problem I had is 99% of the choices during dialogue give the same response, and I don't mean, there is like a few about a paragraph of different text but the over all leads to the same result, no. The answer that immediately follows sounds like it could answer either reply same regardless of your choice. For example:The village mayor asks you to make some mouse repellent and your choices are:'Sure.'or'Don't you have any in the village?'And the line directly after you answer is:'The one we have is a little weak. We're going to need something extra strong.'Which leaves the other half of the game. The farming.Just like every other farm sim, you have your farm land, you have rocks and wood on it, you break it up and then hoe the land, plant your seeds, water, wait, profit. You start with 1/9th of the field you can get, not counting the two special fields you unlock later.Unlike other games, there is no reward for processing food, meals don't make them more valuable, turning a fruit into a juice doesn't change the price. After you unlock all of your field, max out your barn/coop and buy the extra inventory bags there is no reason to make more money except to buy seeds. I managed to unlock the max size of everything in spring of year 2, and the most infuriating things is it is not large enough because all of your processing machines HAVE TO BE PLACED ON FIELD TILES. You also unlock different types and colors of fences... again, that can only be placed on field tiles! That's it. That is all of the depth of the farming. You can't increase the level of the soil, if you want better quality crops you'll have to do fairy requests, we'll talk about that soon. There's nothing makes it special, nothing that makes it worth continuing to farm once you're maxed out on money, hell, I'd even say once you have the upgrades and a stockpile of food, there's no point to continue to bother with it.This is BAFFLING to me as a long time player of a variety of different farm sim games like Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley, and Rune Factory.I would even put money on being able to beat the game without bothering with upgrading any of the farm.Half of this game is a farming game.That does not make a compelling case for it's The only thing I was having fun with was doing all of the fairy quests. Each seasonal dungeon you free a fairy that give you what would traditionally be your farming tool upgrades, you do the things they ask they upgrade different areas to give you better quality crops, or crafted item recipes. It's basically a to-do list. They are not worth doing past the first half for the rewards.Once you beat the game you can marry one of your party members, I did not do so. Full disclosure, I did not beat the game. I got to the last dungeon when said friend asked me if I like it, and after thinking back on it, I would have been better off doing some mod for another farming sim rather than the 130 hours I poured into this game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're on the fence between this and a game like Stardew Valley, buy Stardew. If you already have Stardew, just start a new save instead of buying this. Combat is lame, the farming is boring, the story is boring. Farming is clunky and not remotely satisfying. Combat has no dodge, no block, just exchanging blows and job-switching to use magic or physical attacking. Switching jobs has a significant cool down for some reason, so don't ever expect to handle a battle in a dynamic way.You get to choose between Male, Female, and Nonbinary but don't worry, no matter what you choose your character wears the same outfit: hot pants and go-go boots with a fantasy flair, side ponytail, and wide birthing hips. Customizing you character is nothing more than swapping colors. Your inventory is "full" and won't let you collect any new items, even of the same type that you don't have full stacks of, if every slot in you backpack is full.The majority of this game's dialogue, and by majority I mean 99.99%, is text only. Some party members talk in combat but that's about it. I'm glad I bought this on sale, I'm mad I even paid half price for this bland nonsense. Want a RPG experience? Any other game will do. Same if you're looking for a farming game, the farming in this game is limited and less immersive than the oldest Harvest Moon titles.A $60 price tag for this game is a crime. It's not worth $20.

_childDocuments_.review: For years now, Square-Enix has been trying to make a good A tier original IP game. The games they've released have mostly been middling mediocrity. But finally, they've released a game that I'd actually call "decently good".  First things first though, is actually set expectations, because in usual fashion, SE's marketing did an absolutely terrible job. Harvestella is a JRPG first, and a farming simulator in a somewhat distant second. Neither are particularly deep, but the JRPG portion is a proper (A)RPG with a full job system, dungeon diving, and overarching story that is surprisingly compelling, while the farming portion is just the player plopping a few veggies & fruits in an expandable (but still limited) area, and tending to 2 specific types of  animals, all this so that you can have ingredients to cook food that you'll use as supporting items for the aforementioned dungeon diving. The audio for the game is...interesting. The music is pretty good, kinda reminiscent of Nier Automata's. The voice acting, by contrast, is almost non-existent. If the simplistic farming hinted at it, the lack of VA exposes the fact that this game had a low budget to work with. The story does lose a lot of it's impact when the only times you'll ever hear a character talk is in random grunts and shouts. Ofc, that's likely leading you to the question: "If it's that obviously low-budget, then why is it priced like a marquee game?", and the answer to that leads to why, I think, Square-Enix has been unable to make their lower-tier efforts stick: pricing misalignment. This game, like a lot of others in their catalogue, is way overpriced for how underbudgeted, and how unproven, it is. This game would be a FAR EASIER pill to swallow if were somewhere closer to 40$/€ base price than within spitting distance of AAA pricing that it is now.   But I'm digressing there. the TL;DR for this review is: Low-budget JRPG with simple farming sim bolted in, compelling story but overpriced, rec'd when on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:  A soulless Rune Factory wannabe that's mechanically very basic. Only get it if there's huge discount >70% or get Rune Factory instead.The action part is super basic; you can't customize your stats, the only thing equip-able is your jobs (skill sets) and accessories. There's no weapon crafting and customization, and the same goes with your armour. As your party members, the only thing you can do is upgrade their weapon. That's it. They don't receive EXP, they just automatically have the same level as you. Fighting enemy is just tapping one button, with the occasional skills & evasion (only in some jobs). Oh, and don't forget to eat because stamina won't regenerate on empty stomach.As for the farming part, just imaging Harvest Moon in the early days, but worse, especially the animal part and the equipment. You can only get a chicken coop and a barn, and you need to purchase said two types of animals from a merchant. Unlike Rune Factory where you can capture almost any monster, this feels very basic and not fun. As for the farming equipment, there's no upgrade. You can only level up your farming skills, but only through grind quests after you unlock the required characters. This is just a blatant way of extending play time.Crafting is very basic. There's only two crafting: item crafting which use items gathered from exploration and cooking, which is use your farmed crops and gathered materials. Most of the times, you craft items to help exploration (e.g. fixing bridge), and some damage items.As others said, the action and farming part feels like independent of each other. Farming is just for making money and getting ingredients for your food, which is basically your potion. Exploration is OK. Nothing special, nothing bad.Then, the graphic, audio, and story is what you expect from a 3rd party game that's also released on Switch: graphic feels like PS2 era with fancy effects, audio is of typical budget JRPGs, and story is filled with all sorts of common tropes and character types of anime world, that's heavily sugar coated so the game is playable by kids.All in all, this game is a soulless husk of a chimera of two game genres, that's filled with the most boring flavour that you can find.
