_childDocuments_.review: This is game is absolutely worth the time. I've played most Rune Factory & Harvest Moon games, and a plethora of JRPGs (& more tbh). PROs: Graphics are some of the best for farming sims I've found, the art is gorgeous. It has no platforming characteristics, so no gliding or climbing etc. Definitely a casual walk-the-path type of explortation. That said, the battles are still fun and take a little skill to dodge attacks. The quality of life mechanics are well done. Lots of teleportation and farming mechanics to save time like Area of Effect watering of plants, sprinklers and rain even in the summer. The menus are organized and make side quests and story quests super easy to follow and remember if you decide to ignore them for a while. I'm not a big side quest person, but these side quests are suprisingly endearing and even have a major character show up in them sometimes. The game is long, the story is pretty deep. The rendering for characters, livestock, crops and enemies is top-of-line high definition. The music is beautiful, sounds like a Final Fantasy game.CONs: My biggest gripe is the MC's art doesn't show up during dialogue, & they don't speak at all outside of the player choosing responses. And the games has you choose A LOT of responses. I wish so badly MC art showed up and had different emotions, like Rune Factory & Fire Emblem games. Also, character customization includes non-binary, which is great, but the visuals only allow you to choose an androgynous look that leans slightly masculine or feminine. Then you get to choose eye color, hair coor and a deep or high voice. If they have the MC character art & voice acting like Rune Factory, combined with just a little more character customization, it would be absolutley perfect. Along that same vein, the game could do with a lot more voice acting. Especially for the romance options. And lastly of course, more polished running and exploration like climbing etc. I'm hoping for these types of improvements in future installments.Also since many want to know, the romance options all have thier own menu in the main menu that allows you to keep track of doing all 10 of their events. There could definitely be more to them, but they aren't bad. Hopefully will imporve more in later installments.Really excited to see where Squarte Enix takes this series bc there is a TON of potention and this is a pretty solid first installment.

_childDocuments_.review: While not a game I'd recommend to everyone, I found enough to enjoy in Harvestella to give it the thumbs-up. The dungeon crawling is basic but satisfying, with enough variety available to keep the moment-to-moment gameplay interesting. What stood out to me personally was the cozy storytelling. I often found myself feeling as though I were some sort of fantasy-genre wandering therapist while playing Harvestella, going from town to town just listening to people's problems and helping them work through their baggage. So if that's something that appeals to you I would recommend checking the game out.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that I believe will be very divisive in its current state. You'll either love the atmosphere and the potentiality of the game, or you'll be relatively unimpressed and lose interest quickly. I currently *don't* recommend this game if you're looking for a polished gem of a life-sim RPG, but I do recommend still checking out the game IF you are willing to give it a chance to become polished. I plan to revisit this review at a future date. Character creation is really limited. Bonus points for including Non-Binary on the gender selection screen, though, bravo! This doesn't change anything in the game beyond how people refer to you in dialogue.The first few hours of the game, are on tutorial rails, limiting where you can go, and what you can do. Quests and events will constantly railroad you into following orders. It takes a bit for the game to open up and let you explore things more freely.Stamina, Hunger, and Time management are all core systems of the game, but I feel like they need better tuning. Time still feels like too much of a crunch, though the current length of day  feels much better than what we had in the demo. The day, however, still doesn't feel like its enough. The progress of an in-game day feels like the older entries of the Harvest Moon series, you feel sleepy by 10PM, by midnight you gain the "Very Sleepy" debuff, and then you pass out, netting yourself a Drs fee. Stamina is consumed by running around non-combat areas, and can easily drain your entire stamina bar if you aren't paying attention. Combat and looting nodes also drains stamina. Hunger then comes into play; You eat something, and it starts the slow regeneration of your stamina. This then drains your hunger/belly meter over time. With Combat, you can switch between 3 Jobs in battle. These are upgraded via the Job Board and accrued Job Points. You eventually gain AI party members, but their AI feels clunky. The game uses an active combat system, but still feels like it's turn based  at times, where there are attacks you cannot dodge if they are cast by the enemy. Most melee attacks are easy to deal with, being easily out ranged. Melee combat is relatively button mashy. Mage's casting time feels horribly slow, so I can't see myself using it outside of having to for certain enemy types. Farming feels like an afterthought until you have access to more recipes, I have yet to explore this more. Pros:Well optimizedQuick load timesGreat artInteresting character designNon-Binary as a choiceGreat musicInteresting story premise, world setting, and atmosphereCons:Many systems that need tweakingNot great on MKB controlsWeak or odd dialogueParty AI feels unreliable and painfully slow to react in combat, sometimes not reacting at allControls use a Japanese control scheme, which can take a little time to acclimate toNo option to change controller inputs or prompt/button style.

_childDocuments_.review: Harvestella takes place in a pre-industrial setting similar to Earth, with one big exception being the presence of magical implements called Monolites, which ease and improve the life of all inhabitants in various ways. The world is plagued by both ferocious monsters that roam outside the Monolite’s areas of influence, and also a continent-spanning plague called Quietus, that periodically withers crops and causes mortal sickness to people.Companions mostly feel one-sided and never evolve their personality at any point, their quests a boring slog consisting of “talk to this NPC in 14 different locations to suddenly be best friends forever”. Your dialogue choices will never have any consequence, and are there only to give you the illusion of developing a character, while the story is on a fixed track for 99% of its runtime - no choice and consequence whatsoever.As far as world design is concerned, Square Enix still proves to have a solid grasp of art direction: beautiful landscapes that feel varied and evocative are present throughout the adventure; combined with the solid soundtrack, one may even find some solace in their beauty, between one mind-numbing chore and the next. Dungeons and locations do feel thematically-unique enough to have their own “mood”, if you look past the same NPCs copy-pasted 35 times; yet, they’re not as intricate as one would hope or expect.The world is divided into various locations, either settlements or dungeons, that you can reach through a world map initially traversed on foot, and later on with mounts and even vehicles. Overall, there aren’t more than two dozen locations overall, which is rather miserable for a 70+ hour JRPG; in fact, a lot of side-quests will recycle the same places, enemies and NPCs ad-nauseam because of how small the world is.Dungeons are divided into floors, connected by fast-travel beacons you can unlock and use as shortcuts, since finishing an entire dungeon in a single day, before you’re forced to go back to sleep, is almost impossible. The way this game manages time is a standard for farming-sims, but days are far too short for how slow the pacing of everything is; this leads to even more wasted time to backtrack.Exploring cities, dungeons and the overworld map are all worthwhile things to do, as many hidden chests, some of which behind devices or obstacles you’ll need specific consumables to overcome, contain rare materials or unique recipes to collect. But… guess what? You won’t need those recipes anyway, and while those rare mats can give a good buck early on, they become redundant from mid-game onwards. This means exploration, on paper, is worthwhile - but 80% of the time it’s actually redundant. Fights are in real-time, and will see you, alongside two companions, pitted against a variety of monsters and machines. The variety of foes is initially good, however becomes redundant and recycled the more the game advances. Remember how in FFXII there were 600+ unique monsters? Yeah, that was back when devs still gave a damn. You’ll have an array of ranged and melee classes to dynamically swap on the battlefield, each with their own abilities (up to four) and different elements to exploit foes’ weaknesses. Progression of classes is grindy, as only those you equip will get XP from kills, meaning that to level up all classes equally, you’ll have to get some serious grinding done, as it takes hundreds of foes to gain even a single level at later stages. But here’s the good news; you won’t need to do that, since all melee classes are simply worse than ranged ones, and as long as you have a class combination that has all elements, you’ll be good to go with just three of them. Bosses evolve as fights go on, and can be “broken” by hitting them with an element they’re weak against, thus increasing the damage they take for a while and also enabling your companions’ special moves, which give them invulnerability while executed, but not to yourself, so yes, you can actually die while watching your companions performing some overly-long attack animation. Boss design isn’t bad, but isn’t good either: most of the time, you’ll win if you have enough consumables, or lose if you don't; there’s no heal cooldown, so you can spam 129 fruit juices in a row and be immortal - vegan power!Your farm initially consists of a single plot of land to till, water and sow; it can be expanded when you both have enough money and materials, at a dedicated trader. Depending on season, different plants will grow with different times and terrain types needed; you’ll need to stockpile in the right season, if you want to have enough to make the more complex food recipes later on. Despite various utility skills that can make farming quicker and more convenient, or implements like automated sprinklers, the whole farming component remains a drag: it’s slow, clunky, and never feels satisfactory. It’s all in all, the same as buying healing and mana consumables at a shop, but with extra, longer steps that add nothing to the gameplay formula other than filler. Just spam the cheapest crop and resell everything for money to buy upgrades, or make the simplest available foods as consumables - you don’t need anything more than that.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all as I see this being mentioned by many negative reviews:My 6 year old 1070 runs this at 120fps@4k without getting over 70° - so please don't speculate on spectacular real graphics. Its buttery smooth with no stuttering and clear distance, much unlike the gameplay you can now see in different Let's Plays or streams. Loadtimes are non existant thanks to a m.2 SSD while the switch takes 3-5s depending on the area you travel to.For gameplay:This is your typical JARPG with focus on storytelling and progression behind an off-battle activity to buy progress items. Here: Farming.Up to a certain point exploration and gathering was really time consuming, but teleporting just unlocked which will save hours per day in the future. No complains there anymore.Battle is easy, enemies will let you know you're underequipped quickly and hit like a truck - we talk ~10% of your max health per hit. Brute forcing is possible as the Dash Ability allows for a quick dodge but has no i-frames to rely on.Story is mysterious and progressing slowly, per usual for an JRPG. Even thou dubs only exist mainly in dungeons and daily activities, progression would take even longer if everything was voiced.Is it worth the money so far for 4.5h of playtime for me?. YesAs always for a console port: Please play with a controller. The layout is pretty nice except for showing right trigger actions on the left side of the UI. Thankfully Steam allows for easy re-configuration of controller buttons for certain games, same as the Switch does.Many of the first day negative reviews where based on:A) about the priceB) about the male designC) about the binary optionA) None of those had played the game past the tutorial. (2hrs and less to be able to refund)I retract my statement from above. The full price is worth it, even if you are not totally into JRPG.B) None of those evidently knew what an "art-style" is, Many games are designed like this, especially games developed by a japanese Team.C) None of those had a reason besides their own victimhood and/or their ego being hurt as they were not catered design that fit their personal bubble. It's a choice you can but do not have to make. It will NOT affect your gameplay.If you enjoy story driven ARPG Games with a side flavor of farming - read: RF4 or other similar games you'll be fine. Compared to other games that partially can be compared with this;Story, graphics and material progression was worse. Farm management was hell, with every machine taking up a crazy amount of space.Story, inventory management and general grind loop as well as QoL was worse.:Of course, better in the farming aspect, but QoL only comes from mods. It's base functions are tedious, but enjoyable in their repetiveness. Story revolves around one place and their people and can't compete with the moloch that is a JRPG that has world story, party memeber storylines and town-storylines. Battle "exists".:Now we are talking: for example Ryza 1's beginning was slower. Getting materials and crafting was more tedious but the storyline was better (so far and imho)At this point the reviews of people that actually played the game get through and time will tell how this game fares. Personally I estimate an 100+h game for myself.Even though Harvestella is nearly 5 times as expensive as SDV, the experience so far is reasonable for that pricetag. I paid the same for PS5 AAA Games and got less out of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Harvestella is a JRPG first and farming sim second, so temper your expectations coming in. I say that because most farming sim games that I have played while having a story are not really the main focus but rather the relationship you have with characters in the town and of course your farm. Instead this game focuses a lot on the story and the party members you gather in your journey. This game has multiple towns and for each town you will only really get to know the two party members that you get in each town. You unlock their own stories based on how far you are in the story and not by socializing with them(talking or gifts). Story:I enjoyed the story and like true JRPG fashion it goes to places especially on its last act. The characters are fun enough especially the interaction between them which is helped a lot with great portraits. Combat:Combat is average at best, you will have access to multiple jobs unlocking more as you progress the story. The main problem of the combat though is the lack of any dodge or blocking mechanic, while you can unlock an ability to dash it doesn’t stop you from getting damaged and it's mainly used to move away from an aoe attack. It’s not that bad if you are just going through the dungeon avoiding the boss mobs but once you do start fighting them it will just end up being a battle of attrition as there is no way to avoid being damaged . Farming:There are a couple of things that I liked that they have done here and one of them is how they handled your tools. They don’t take up any inventory space and it's easy to access and I also like the way you upgrade them by doing orders. Without spoiling anything, orders are given to you by characters that will help you in the farm as you progress the story and they will also add different biomes and also a bit of more life in your farm. You have a universal storage which is great, you don’t have to worry about what chest you put that one material in, and you don’t need to have the materials in hand to craft or cook it will automatically take from the storage. Although if you want to process ingredients like making mayo or spices you still need to have the material in your inventory which is a weird design choice.Controls:So i played this game using M/KB and immediately i noticed that the game is made for a controller but i got used to it and it wasn’t too bad but i definitely recommend a controller if you have one.Music:The combat music, funny moments, the sad moments, the serious moments. I love all of them, definitely one of the highlights of this game for me.OverallOverall i enjoyed this game and definitely recommend this for those who like JRPG and farming sim.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of the familiar Square Enix elements: quirky characters, an interesting storyline, job classes like fighters and mages, and crystals. What makes this game a little different is that it has farming, crafting, cooking, and fishing elements. It is a relaxing game. If you are an experienced player, do not expect a challenge but do expect to have a relaxing time raising crops and killing enemies. What it sets out to do, it does well. It has a gorgeous soundtrack, the graphics, while certainly not bombastic, do well to underline the gorgeous world and the core game mechanics are fun.I do not think it deserves the negative reviews and a mixed reception. It is a good game, but one where you should be aware that it is its own thing. Not the next big farming life social simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR RatingGraphics : ♦♦♦◊◊Story : ♦♦♦♦◊Voice : ♦◊◊◊◊Crafting : ♦♦♦♦♦ (You don't have to have the needed items IN YOUR BACKPACK!)Farming : ♦♦♦◊◊Overall : ♦♦♦◊◊------------------------(Will update this later, but as of right now I'm only 9 hours in and onto a secondary city)As Harvestella was marketed out in my perspective... It seemed like it would be a combination of Atelier and Stardew Valley with a fantastic graphics. That's not what I would say that we've gotten... The game starts slow and pushes you to get through the first 3 chapters before opening up the world for Ch. 3a, 3b, and 3c + side quests. The graphics reflect that of the main platform this title was made for (Nintendo Switch) and it shows... from flat foliage to very bland backdrops. The farming leaves much to desire as the economy revolves around you farming and selling anything that isn't nailed down and this comes with dwindling usage as crops give 1/pc per plot and seeds are hard to come by in the wild (They don't drop with crop harvesting). Crafting, however, can be enjoyable as it doesn't require much and the crafting materials span your backpack as well as your storage box. Combat is mediocre at best with very little strategy involved past utilizing weaknesses and a stagger meter (for bosses). For whatever reason, there's VERY little voice acting... The most I've heard is from battle starts/ends.Honestly, it's not even close to being a great life-sim game and even worse at a $60 USD price point.BUT, if you're a fan of FF-level character art, JRPGs, and can appreciate a good sprinkling of crafting & farming... This game will hit the spot for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a difficult game to recommend. _childDocuments_.review: I'm not much of a "leave a review" kind of person but this game gets some weird ones so I wanted to throw my two cents into the void.TL;DR: I'm an experienced player in farm sims, farm RPGs, and jRPGs and Harvestella has far surpassed my expectations and become one of my favorite farm RPGs I've ever played, beating out Rune Factory 4 for me. Though it is lacking in romance or festivals, the other systems are interesting and keep me engaged. Farming is well designed and progression is linked to the main story to keep you moving forward. Combat is fun if a bit shallow but that's to be expected to be honest, it's not like RF has the best combat either. It got such middling reviews from others that I wasn't sure I'd like it, but genuinely it has really won me over and I'm enjoying my time with it.Up front, the tutorial is a bit long, but once you get through the first few days the game opens up immensely. The story and characters are wonderful, but are definitely more in line with a traditional jRPG than say, Rune Factory is. The farming system feels limiting at first but also opens up immensely with story progression. I like that there are a good amount of options for processing goods, upgrading farming skills (rather than your tools), some basic animal ranching, and new types of farm plots without overwhelming you. I find it easy to balance between doing tasks on my farm and handling quests and dungeons.For combat, the job system is fun but unobtrusive. I like playing around with the different classes. For the most part, combat is not very challenging, but I did have a boss or two give me some trouble.I love the sidequests in each town and the way the stories continue. I love the unique situations in each town and the way the story is unfolding (I've completed the Spring and Summer towns, and am now in the Winter one).There are little hidden treasure chests and collectibles around each town. Dungeons are fun to explore. Everything feels well paced to me. I like that there are areas you can't access immediately and have to come back to as you upgrade your exploration tools.My biggest complaint is the lack of romance and festivals, a staple in a farm RPG. It's such a shame the art direction for all the story characters is so cute but you can't romance anyone. But even then, there are enough sidequests, character story events, and main story events that I don't feel like the towns are empty. Personally, if you're on the fence, I say give it a try. If you're not sure, wait for a sale. Just go in knowing the first hour or two is pretty hand-holdy (which if you're familiar with Story of Seasons titles, you know they have a bad rep for lengthy tutorial sections) and then you'll be free to start exploring.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game that I feel appeals to a lot of different types of players. It's got a nice story, beautiful graphics, fun jobs. I will say though, I expected the crafting/gathering to be the main priority of the game and while it IS important and you WILL be doing it every day, it really only consumes a handful of your time, the majority of your time is spent running around going through the story and battling. Overall though this game has sucked me in and I think it will suck you in too if you're looking for an RPG with meaningful crafting/gathering tied into it.

_childDocuments_.review: Harvestella may be a jack of all trades, master of none, but I have really enjoyed my time playing it. If you like aspects of farming, RPG, quests, crafting, fishing, cooking, achievements, and more with a dedicated storyline, I think you would like this game. I 100%'d the game in Switch and did it again on Steam. The achievements are quite reasonable if you're looking to put in some time if that's something you're interested in.The story can take a bit to wrap your head around, but I enjoyed it. You have a main storyline but also character storylines that can be progressed depending on how far you are into the story. You can do these as you go or come back to them and you won't miss any; same with the general side quests. If you're just starting out, I recommend doing these for good money, seeds, and materials.You get some customization over your farm and your options continue to expand as you play and unlock sort of in-game achievements for more recipes, areas of your farm, or upgrades. The game also encourages you to revisit old areas that you can unlock more in later.I really struggled with the combat of the game for a bit, but I eventually got it down. I wish it were a bit clearer which of your skills - as you're using them - applies which typing and which of the break bars stood for which typing. This isn't something you typically need to worry about until some end-game bosses. You can build your party around their bonuses (e.g. I selected two party members who gave good magic bonuses), select jobs that complement these, and equip rings to boost your stats (and can later combine rings if they have available slots or compatible stats). Its unfortunately not worth grinding for rings as they have low drop rates, but you can get some good scripted drops that should suffice plenty.I really enjoyed the music of the game, especially in the Coral Shrine. The models and general art style doesn't blow me away, but the character portraits are too notch and really help convey what the characters are saying (which is why I was so disappointed that Story of Seasons: Pioneers of Olive Town did away with them).The end game can get a bit grindy, particularly if you're farming for materials to upgrade everyone's weapons or max out job classes, but I didn't mind it too much (and I typically don't care for grinding much in games). You can also get a ring to help with job points gain which helps a good bit. I recommend using some guides if you really want to max out everything and find the best places to farm materials or find things to help you do so.If you're not sold on the game, it frequently goes on sale and that's a good time to pick it up! The first couple hours can be a little slow (I played the demo originally and wasn't sure if I would get the game), but I find it expands pretty quickly from there.

_childDocuments_.review: Harvestella is the quintessential example of the maxim of “More than the sum of its parts.” Each specific part of the game it self leaves something to be desired. Often these issues are even easy fixes but ultimately keep every specific part of the game one of the worst within its genre. Yet, I genuinely loved it, loved playing it, even as most of what I will say here sounds like me ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about it.Harvestella is sold on the idea that its Stardew valley with final fantasy like elements. This is totally untrue, the farming sim aspect is really secondary to the JRPG core. The farming itself can be astifying, the games crops are beautiful as is their meals and I will say if you invest time into any of the farm sim system it will pay dividens. This is no stardew in the sense of there being money traps like animals early on. If you invest in your farm it will pay back. However, strictly none of it is needed. A friend of mine barely farmed outside of paying for upgrades to their own player and the materials to make healing serums. No instead this is a JRPG with a farming system really loosely tacked on. The story barely addresses it, the story vibe and side quests feel less about meeting your community and relaxing on at the farm, instead it feels more like Nier Replicant but if the farming in that game was more expansive. This has its positives, it does something with its side quests that only really Nier and the Witcher I trust to really do, almost all of them follow evolving story lines with the same characters in problems related to your previous. Sometimes the writing is boring, sometimes its surprisingly meaningful, but usually it will invest you when you're on side quest 3 on a side quest chain. Honestly the Nier Replicant  comparison is so apt it hurts. Both in its main story which is much more concerned with the secret scifi elements, which to be fair is the strong part of the narrative, than the low key farming world. Frustrating part is, the real time combat just isn’t good either. The game is in desperate need of a dedicated dodge button and mechanic, there is something like it for specific jobs, but it barely works and is super finicky. As is the hit boxes for enemy attacks, many are just, if they preform the animation, the damage is dealt. The mechanics are decided by smartly switching jobs, who your team mates are, and slamming juice when needed. All of that is decided at the start of the dungeon crawl, within it, its mindless. It reminds me of old mmo combat, but without the multiplayer aspect to keep its life going.Then there is the Cozy Town elements key to games like stardew valley are sadly stripped down. You get your party members whose stories can be really compelling (Dainthus, Aria, Emo) to horrendous (Istania, Brakka, Unicorn) and sadly the romance elements while the characters are compelling feels like an afterthought. The Town never gets to really be a character like in the genres cousins, and could do with tighter focus.  Not to mention bugs, like despite trying for days never catching a single legendary fish, the weird AI bugs on the FEARS especially, whom seem to only notice, you and reset if you manage to have your companions tank for a few seconds. (Rendering my favorite class, Avenger, useless in the end game)Despite all of this, it comes together to be addictive and compelling in weird ways. Maybe its the beautiful look of the game, the compelling scifi elements. The Omen who are just kinda awesome in concept and execution, the whole second act of the game. It all just comes together and makes me smile. More than anything I wish this game could get a sequel to just tighten up things with small changes. Maybe set on Lost Gaia trying to recolonize it. Focus on the one town your making, add a dodge button to the combat. Have building up the town with your farm actually part of the point of getting up each day. Harvestella is good despite each part separated out failing, but failing in such redeemable ways it begs for a second try. Tragically, seems like this game is bound to be a forgotten game in its genre.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR;  RPG first, farming sim second.  Combat is basic, no dodge or block though has range of weapons and minor skill trees for each, plus you get up to two party members to adventure with at a time(total of 8 to choose between).  Found it fun, can be grindy but with charm and decent story compared to similar games. Not worth starting price of $60.--To emphasize, this is mainly a Action RPG game first before it is a farming sim, the story and characters have more relevance than the actual farming mechanics.  That is not to say it is completely ignored, but compared to others where farming is the primary concern, it does fall short.  To add to it, the combat is basic as can be, offering minimal variation of fighting enemies which can be described as "Use the weapon enemy weak to, then move back and forth to avoid hits... or tank hits and eat food.", which sums it up.  However the boss battles do up the ante big time, having full mechanics similar to a MMO and even a break gauge/bonus break to increase damage with teamwork, that is where real fun in combat came in... though compared to the other bits, does not take much to be better.With those pieces alone it would be a mess of a game, however combined it does come together as a fun experience where you are taming a farm, growing and expanding your land while also going on adventures around the realm.  It is something that may not satisfy most people that want a intricate farming sim or intense fast paced combat, but if able to handle the bit of jank of both, the gameplay loop itself of working to fund your food and equipment for your journey is pretty good.Another point to mention is lack of character customization, which is minimal at best.  I had hoped for eventually unlocking more but seems all get is at the beginning, though do get some "outfits" based on job/weapon using, it changes back during cut-scenes.Story wise, it is similar to what a normal FF game would be.  Something bad happens, you are amnesiac and something special about you.  It can be cliche with main story albeit with a darker tone than most farming sims, but the side stories do have a real world element to them that enhances the charm and brings it more down to earth, trying to resolve issues people deal with in life, especially regarding saying goodbye.To wrap up, it's a decent game for what it is, a basic RPG Action where you do simple farm work for money to fund equipment upgrades, food to heal and even work towards marrying someone if choose to.  It has interesting enough story with some more sad tone than happy happy joy joy.  Biggest recommendation can do is, don't go in expecting epic combat or intense drama/tension or the most innovative farming ever, cause it's not any of that.  But it all wrapped up together what it is, is a fun little bundle to enjoy some simple times, before you go off to save the world... Or chill in the forest and enjoy the jam.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my 2022 game of the year. I went into it expecting a light-hearted farming sim with some RPG elements to spice up the daily gameplay loop. What I got was a gut wrenching story of grief and humanity set in a phenomenally interesting* world.*True to the JRPG genre, it's also sometimes confusing. I'm a huge fan of lifestyle sim games like Stardew Valley, and in that regard there is a bit to be desired. The farming is not nearly as in depth as something like Stardew, the seasons are simplified, the actual growing process is dumbed down. The only real means of "automation" of the process comes from sprinklers and certain in-game progression. Otherwise you are always constantly harvesting and replanting your crops yourself. With the way the time/stamina system works, there comes a point in the game where this is your entire day unless you have meals ready to go to restore your stamina. Romance is an afterthought. Each main character has their own quest line throughout the game, but these are universally personal stories for each of them that ends in self discovery. The romance aspect is tacked on to the end, much much later in the game. Despite these shortcomings compared to other entries in the genre, this game has everything else you'd be looking for in a farming sim.I'm also, however, a huge fan of RPGs, and that's where this game really shines.  Each of the combat jobs plays uniquely enough to feel interesting, and the implementation of the weakness and break system makes party building enjoyable and dynamic. Throughout the late game, as I was hunting down specific optional bosses, I was constantly changing which jobs I used and which characters I took with me in order to accommodate my target's weaknesses. The quests throughout the game are also incredible. Nearly every single storyline drew me in and more than a few of them made me cry. I can't possibly overstate how well written this game is.I made the choice to 100% this game. I would simply like to warn you ahead of time that if you, too, make that choice, you are in for a grind. I saw the achievement to earn 1,000,000 dollars well before I was finished with upgrading my farm. I still had to upgrade every character's weapon all the way, and that's not even getting into side things like inventory upgrades or, god forbid, buying seeds for farming. I will admit that this specific point is kind of a double-edged complaint. In a game like Stardew, farming (haha get it?) for this sort of cash wouldn't even be a problem. I think that's because, though, that's the point of Stardew. Making money over time through tediously managing a farm and everything around it  However, Harvestella is a JRPG with farming sim elements, not the other way around. There is a story. There are chapters. There is an inherent sense of progression that is wholly different from other genre games. So this sort of grind fits and makes sense in a JRPG but feels incredibly disjointed from a farming sim.I mean, it says it up top. Recommended. This is my game of the year. I absolutely freaking love it, even the grindy farming bits. Do yourself a favor and play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty game with seemingly outdated graphics, clunky combat, shallow writing and world building, and disappointingly little farming.Unless fixed, I would not recommend this game.Breakdown -Character Creation:Starting with the most obvious, it’s cool that Square Enix has added a Non-Binary option. Wonderful! Except that it feels superficial and like they just added it to create good media and gain more customers. The creator itself is very limited in all aspects (also, they didn’t add a gender neutral voice, it’s really choosing between male and female).Story/Dialogues:It’s shallow. The dialogue choices are not unique or different. All the choices boil down to the same thing and have no impact on the actual dialogue (which is not unique to this game, but it still urks me). All the responses are “Don’t feel sad” or “We can do this!”, there are few, if any, witty or fun responses. None of the dialogue choices, for me, felt genuine or thought out. ALSO! I’m annoyed that there is no voice acting! The characters actually have voiced lines while out and about in the world (each character has like one or two, but the point still stands). So I’m confused why they didn’t just voice the dialogue itself.Story wise, it felt the same. None of the ‘disastrous events” felt dangerous or urgent. The characters talk about all sorts of trouble, but we never see it in the actual gameplay. I could’ve spent the first in world year just plotting along happily through each dungeon if it weren’t for mechanics and abilities locked behind each part of Chapter 3.My biggest gripe is the cutscenes. After defeating some bosses, you expect some long cutscene and the characters to have an emotional moment, no? But, unless something went wrong for me, the bosses die in a short clip and the cutscene sort of, just, ends? No explanation, no victorious quote, no nothing. It just cuts to the characters in another place, some unknown time after the battle. It feels like the main characters just defeating a common shmuck and called a day! Where are my epic; “We just defeated a really powerful enemy, yay!” moments? It just ends. And I actually had to get up from my chair and take a break the first time it happened cause it disappointed me so much.Gameplay:It’s alright. The general controls aren’t too bad, except the camera keeps giving me motion sickness. The combat is clunky. The job system is cool and interesting conceptually. But in reality, is clunky as well. The dodge (step) skill doesn’t work half the time I press the trigger (they probably should have added some sort of animation canceling to it) and it doesn’t actually dodge anything. It just nudges the character slightly in one direction. I do like the enemy weakness system, it adds a little spice (a little) to an otherwise pretty monotonous and boring combat.Farming wise. It feels shallow and rushed like several other things in this game. I’m also sad about the lack of farming in a game advertised as a farming game. The profits feel so minute that it feels better to farm a load of monster parts and sell those then spend the time caring for the 20 grilla profit carrops. (I did all the math). So unless that is changed, it’s better just to do all the side quests which give you 1,000 grilla pretty much for every one and get all the farm upgrades in a few days compared to the weeks it would take to make that much with crops.Again, several parts of farming are locked behind Chapter 3 events, which is not a bad thing. But when you are reliant on farming and home-made food for money and curatives, it gets very slow and boring.All in all, the game feels rushed and shallow. I’m going to continue to play it however, in hopes that it gets marginally better down the line. I hope some of these issue are fixed, because this game as so much potential.Note:I’m writing this after completing Chapter 3 of the story and just around 15 hours of gameplay. I’m not sure if these issues are universal, but they are what I have found and had a problem with. I hope this helps.

_childDocuments_.review: Main pro: combining these 2 genres is addicting as a fan of bothMain con: the story can take less than a year to complete so you'll want to either make slow progress or make sure you get everything you need in each season, unless you want to grind out completions post-gamePros:- the dungeon setup is smart considering there's a day/night cycle - as you advance in dungeons, you can make shortcuts so you can easily get back to where were you, so you can explore dungeons one step at a time and always be back home for nightfall- you can fast travel home anytime- I enjoyed the plot and characters although there is a potentially controversial part of the plot but it moves on after that- the combat classes are really fun to play around withCons:- not enough depth - I could've beat the game within year 1 but I still had seasonal things to do in year 2. I would want a game like this to last 2 years so you don't have to be on top of getting all the seasonal stuff the first time around- combat is okay - it's mainly button mashing, it's hard to dodge enemy attacks especially in slower classes, and strong enemies will aggro on you so you have to be leveled up enough to tank hits against those opponents- conversations & side quests can drag on sometimesI would definitely recommend taking your time with the game and maybe looking up seasonal things so you don't miss anything the first time around. I also don't feel this game is worth the sticker price, I bought it on sale and am very happy with it.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I only paid half price for this game and I still don't think it's worth it. The appearance and game mechanics are sterile. I would recommend Rune Factory 4 Special over this in a heartbeat. I'll probably finish the game since I've spent almost 60 hours in it so far, but it's kind of hate playing at this point. Pros: The world building and lore is pretty interesting (albeit confusing) once you get into the game a bit. The Seaslights are beautiful and haunting in appearance from a distance. There is a very cute mount you can purchase. Cons: Everything else is very generic and overall the locations feel sterile. Everyone looks the same, even the PC has the same face and eyes as most other characters and there is very little customization.  Pretty much everything is on rails. You can somewhat choose what order to do things in, but even that is limited. The options the cut scenes give you don't feel like they make an impact and sometimes the followup dialogue is geared toward the one you didn't pick, so you know that the choice was just an illusion and makes no difference. There is a scene where you are ganged up on and my party would've been able to handle them with no problem but a cut scene triggered.  There are several instances where I would've been able to fight my way out of a situation and the game wouldn't let me.  And I say this as someone who usually avoids combat and prefers the life/farm sim parts of games.   This has been said in other reviews but I'll reiterate it here: the farm sim portion of the game feels like an afterthought. Having to put maker machines on your coveted farmland is an asinine choice and I hate it in every game that implements it this way.  Essentially the annoyance compounds with every additional piece that wasn't well thought out by the development team.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a farming sim.This is a JRPG with farming elements. And as that, it is wonderful. The characters are loveable and I care about them, the world is interesting and has just enough little things that remind me of early Final Fantasy to feel charming, but not enough to feel boring or derivative. I thoroughly enjoyed learning more and slowly unravelling all the mysteries in the world.The gameplay was... fine. It wasn't revolutionary, or amazing, but it was still fun to play, and especially the farming felt very satisfying. Where the game, in my opinion, struggles a bit, is with pacing. The story starts out extremely slow, and while that might be nice to get attached to the world and the characters, the way it took quite long to even get to know all the characters meant that it was a bit of a drag in places. Towards the end, on the other hand, the story was basically moving at breakneck pace, and I felt like the farming part was just a chore instead of some welcome relaxation between exploring and fighting and new revelations. I found it very hard to stop following the story to do my farming and keep up my equipment. That's honestly a minor issue, compared to the good parts of the game, in my opinion, so it didn't detract from my enjoyment a lot.Overall, though, I still enjoyed the game a lot. I would recommend it, but it's a prime candidate for "Wait for a good sale".

_childDocuments_.review: I just wanted to grow crops and this game made me fight God (not really but it feels like it).This review is from the POV of someone who desperately craves farming/life sims and does not play many action adventure games.Harvestella is more of an action adventure JRPG than a farming/life sim, and it does neither super well.It is plagued with many little annoyances that keep it from reaching greatness. However, I still had fun and think it doesn't deserve so many negative reviews. My biggest gripe about this game is STAMINA. Everyone complains about the time moving fast but I had no problem with time management. I did, however, struggle with stamina. You use stamina for everything: sprinting, planting, fighting, gathering. Out of stamina? Your character makes a pathetic whine and now you can't sprint or pick up that rock on the floor. Out of stamina during battle? Your character becomes a striking dummy and you cannot attack. You MUST eat food. Food, other than giving various buffs and healing your HP, replenishes some stamina. As long as you have something in your "belly gauge" or whatever it is, your stamina will slowly replenish (and I mean very slowly). People may say, well don't sprint everywhere but I gotta go fast. The other problem with the dependency on food is that you end up hoarding most of your crops to cook food. Unlike other farming games, your crops are not the main source of income early to mid game. Yes, you can grow a ton of crops for money later, but in the beginning your farm space is tiny, seeds are pricey, profit is low. Upgrades will take everything you have. You will be poor. And if you struggle with combat or stamina management like I did, you will need those crops to make food. You cannot buy necessary ingredients for dishes to cook, you will have to grow a lot of the ingredients. To be honest, this was my biggest struggle with this game. I like to grow in bulk and throw everything in the shipping bin; don't do this.The combat is necessary for progression of both the story and farm but you can face tank most of it by using a lot of juice/ food. It is not difficult. The most difficult thing about the combat is the animation lock keeping you from moving out of things or using an item. Noticeable in the late game, if you get hit by one thing... be prepared to get stunned inside 3 other attacks that destroy your HP. There isn't really a combat dodge, some classes have a dash. The allies in your party cannot be controlled. They are sometimes useful and sometimes confused on what to attack. They will most likely not pull aggro on enemies. So if you're playing a ranged job you will still be tanking. Doing companion quests will give you party buffs. Playing the classes are simple. You mash one button and have 2 other abilities unique to each class. There are elemental weaknesses that you can take advantage of, classes have their own elements and you can only carry 3 classes and 2 party members. You can also craft some battle items to help. I didn't really use them but if you want to break bosses a lot then you probably need them.Main story is pretty good. It's pretty stereotypical JRPG writing but I enjoyed it. I was pleasantly surprised by some of the side quests and conversations. This game is not voiced. This is not a problem for me but it is a problem for most. The only voices are NPCs during battle or when you walk by them. Honestly, the voices become so repetitive they become annoying.  Also, you cannot skip cutscenes so be prepare to read everything or mash a button to skip. Farming/life sim things: You cannot customize yourself, your house, or your farm. You "create a character" by changing your hair and eye color which doesn't change. You will wear the same outfit in all the cutscenes. You can only craft and place fences on your farm plot but it takes away space from growing things or placing machines. Machines (like to make feed, mayo, juice, etc)  take all day and can only be placed on your farm plot. Romance is not really a thing. You can choose a life partner at the end of the main story but all relationship quests are platonic. There is a special cutscene with your chosen life partner at proposal but that is it. They will live on your farm and do nothing but repeat voice lines when you enter/leave your house. Animal raising is bare minimum. There is choice of fantasy chicken and fantasy llama you buy from a vendor. They give you items if you make sure their silo has food in it. So you actually read this whole thing. If none of this bothered you. Buy the damn game and play it. It may not be $60 worthy with all the little annoyances to some people (and I was one of those ppl in the beginning) ... but I did get my money's worth in playtime. I completed all of the main story, side quests, and companion quests, I have over 60 hours. And I'm still working on maxing out all of my farm and weapons, completing the deep dungeon, finishing up all the food turn ins, collecting all the dolls, getting the secret classes, and catching all the legendary fish. Theres so much to do that I'm still learning surprises about the game. There were a lot of strange design choices in making this game, but it is obvious there was still a lot of love put into it.

_childDocuments_.review: More than meets the eye! I was someone who played the demo for Harvestella on my switch and fairly quickly felt apprehensive about paying $60 to play it.Then, my husband gifted it to me and I decided to give it more time before making up my mind on the matter and I am so glad I did. I really enjoy Harvestella! I was expecting it to have more farming elements and more relationship building, which isn't really prevalent in the first several hours of the game. (It has a lengthy intro.) Only to find out, it does have the relationship building with characters that are important to the plot. It isn't like traditional farm/life sims where you bring them gifts, but you do side quests for them instead, unlocking more of their story in the process. This game is primarily a JRPG with some light farming, more than anything. It has skill trees and different classes. One thing I decided I like about it to is that it incentivises cooking, unlike a lot of farming Sims. The combat can drain your health fairly quickly even with the step dodge, so you just eat a meal that gives you Stat boosts and bam! You're good to go! TLDR: it's worth $60 to me if you like action JRPGs, farming life sims and Square Enix's crazy narratives.

_childDocuments_.review: Update around 10 hours: Tentative yes at the current asking price. Definite yes on sale. If you want to like it, you probably will. If you don't want to like it, you probably won't. There is a basic albeit not great "dodge", but there's still quite a lot of unavoidable damage. Once you unlock the save points, you can save or teleport home at any time pretty easily--the "return" consumable thankfully gets relegated to emergency escapes. Once you unlock the kitchen and fermenting barrel, HP and stamina get quite a lot more manageable. Tip: Think of it less as a Dark Souls "dodge everything" kind of game and more of a Diablo "get ready to chug potions" kind of game and it'll go much smoother. -----------Original review:Initial impressions:Cons:-Character creation is a joke: the male has a long ponytail and still looks female; there's no hair styles or features to pick from; the only thing you can change is your skin tone, hair color, and eye color.-Incredibly generic fantasy tropes. Mysterious girl? Check. Save the world? Check. Main character amnesia? Check.-Incredibly long prologue. At least 20 minutes before you even get to the farming tutorial, which is the first time you really get to do anything but read.-Can only rest in your own bed. Not that inn on the opposite side of the continent. That takes several hours of your in-game day to trek back to.-Farming seems to be an afterthought to the ARPG side, which is the opposite of what you'd expect from a game with "Harvest" in the title.-I've "heard" that the first 10 hours are a blast and then the game starts working against you/stops respecting your time after that.-Sprinting uses stamina. A lot of it. And there's no dodge.Pros:-Graphics and artwork are beautiful. If only RF5 looked this good.-Basic movespeed is appreciably fast-paced.-Watering can is possibly the best implementation of one yet.-Jobs! If you like Square Enix job gimmicks, you'll like this.-The overworld map is actually pretty nice and I don't mind travelling "large" distances like this as opposed to spending hours walking through filler zones.-The port runs great. There's no mouse icon for the menus, but it works for everything else.

_childDocuments_.review: Like Rune Factory before it, Harvestella is a Niche within the already Niche farming sim genre. I appreciate that it tries to bring a somewhat more mature theme, more complex story, and more depth than its contemporaries. While the juggernaut that is Square Enix is the publisher, the developer of Harvestella is Live Wire, founded in 2018, only a handful of games under it's belt, and 20 employees. Harvestella appears to be their most ambitious game yet. I bring this up not excuse any shortcomings of the game, only as information on the developer is sparse and absent from the Steam page!The combo of action RPG and farming works really well for, evidently, a small group of players and allows the game to be enjoyable despite excelling at neither aspect. Fans of the genre can see the potential and Harvestella is a step towards that potential, but still a long way for maximizing it.The combat could use more depth and a higher skill ceiling. The farming and crafting aspect could have a longer and more balanced progression to match the length of the narrative. The dungeons could do more, in terms of gameplay, to differentiate from each other and be less linear. Every aspect of this game has been done far better elsewhere, but Harvestella is the best example I've come across of these elements combined.The art  is gorgeous. The 2D portraits for characters and sprites for items in particular are best in class, if not particularly abundant. The use of colour and style makes the environments breathtaking and unique despite the low poly models and low res textures. Even though I'm certain that I selected the male protagonist, I constantly forget that I did so. The character customization is all but absent and I am very suspicious that there is really only one protagonist model.The music is the most skillfully executed aspect of Harvestella. The OST is top tier and the use of vocals and choir to cement an atmosphere in cities and dungeons is done with mastery and is something I haven't experienced much elsewhere, if at all. The composer is quite accomplished in games and Anime and it shows.Lack of voice acting for the story is disappointing. Each character has a few battle lines and maybe a greeting or two in JA/EN. The VA did a great job on those so it's a shame there isn't more of it, considering how much dialogue there is.There is a lot of narrative and dialogue. The story is intriguing enough but it is fairly generic JRPG. Enjoyable but forgettable. Some of it is very well written and can be quite clever. Though I can see that some may find it too tongue in cheek at times. My only complaint with the narrative by far is the overabundance of side quests where all you do is observe some children learning some life lesson or "help" their caregivers do parenting. Those stories are fine on their own, I just got frustrated with it being so prevalent.The relationship quests are a facsimile of social links from the Persona games. Where you have ten short quests/character development scenarios for each party member. They stretch a bit thin but overall are a mix of passable to good character stories.The recommendation goes to those who are already ingrained or are curious of this niche. A niche that struggles to have high quality titles but nonetheless can be the upmost enjoyment for those it speaks to. I pray Live Wire and/or Square see this as enough of a success to make a sequel or spiritual successor that builds upon the concept, refining the constituent elements to be par with the best of their respective genres.

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely gave this game a fair shake, but it never really clicked for me. I can see the appeal of Harvestella to some people, but I am not one of those. In my opinion, it winds up being both a mediocre farming sim, and a so-so RPG with half-cooked combat, in a rather bland world. Graphically, the game looks not much better than a Playstation Vita title, and the lack of variety amongst the NPCs also betrays the limited budget the team surely had. The music is halfway decent, but with all the dialogue (that I've seen) being text-based, and with unskippable cutscenes, there is just a certain dryness to the presentation.The combat system is very uninspiring. The job system is a great thing and I am always a fan of those, but it's not remotely as deep as I would like. With enemies frequently having unavoidable direct damage attacks, combating bosses is usually just a matter of consumables. If you made/bought enough to heal, you will win. Maybe this was just a poor next game choice after 100+ hours of Elden Ring. It felt like getting out of a Bugatti and into a Honda Civic. A Civic will get you from Point A to Point B but the journey will be unmemorable. I didn't want to finish this journey. 6.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: Still fresh in and could easily change my mind with more time, but I'm DIGGIN IT.Farming is as good as I need it to be, combat feels simplistic (but fine) this early but looks like it will get much more interesting with the 12 jobs (classes) you can mix and match for your character, the quests aren't too weak to be bland or too drawn out to get boring and laborious (so, just right), and the characters are great with AMAZING dialogue and writing.I'm not sure I can put my finger on what exactly I'm enjoying so much about Harvestella. I think it's the overall dynamic and pacing along with the well balanced diversity of activities. There's always something to do and something toward which you strive.I hope I update this as I put in some more time.

_childDocuments_.review: I have now completed the game and am pleasantly surprised at how much I enjoyed it. I was fully engaged and immersed in the story.There were some firsts that I experienced in the most positive sense:1. THERE IS NO STRUGGLE WITH STORAGE. Kudos to the developers for implementing this feature that every game I have played so far, does not address.2. The game ran perfectly on my laptop. My laptop didn't even get warm after hours of playing. I didn't experience any crashes, bugs or glitches, NOT ONE. This is a first as every game I have played so far fries my laptop, and is full of bugs and glitches. Again, respect to the developers for enabling me to have the stress free gaming experience that I have always wanted.3. I loved the farming tools and appreciated the fresh approach to farming.With character customisation, judging by how unique and varied the dungeons and world are, I suspect that they simply ran out of time, then made the excuse that the character is non-binary. I don't buy it! Non-binary does not mean that there is only one look, which is female. It comes with all different features, shapes and sizes.Whilst the lack of character customisation didn't detract from my enjoyment of the game, it will affect the re-playability of the game for me. Normally, I would play both genders, but there is no point here as they look exactly the same. The only difference is that the male comes with child-bearing hips. It's disappointing, to say the least.What I am hoping for, is that there is a continuation of the game, either through updates or DLC. Also, I hope that the developers take note and address the character customisation issue by giving us more choices, male, female, non-binary, hairstyles and body types. Please, let us customise our character fully. This would turn an extremely good game into an extremely brilliant game.Is it worth the money? From the way it ran so smoothly on my laptop, free of bugs and glitches, and the amount of enjoyment I got from it, I would have to say yes, I am so glad that I purchased this game.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty terrible overall. It's an attempt to incorporate two gameplay systems, but rather than complimenting each other, they mostly compete for the limited time you get allocated each day. The trailer implied that you find seeds during your adventures, but in reality you buy 99% of them at shops. It's not the worst farming system, but it's hardly enjoyable. You spend a lot of time repeating the same thing so that you can expand your farm and do more of the same at a larger scale. The game itself takes a moment to mention how the whole farming thing is a joke. Unfortunately, you do really need the money you earn from it to upgrade weapons.To make things worse, there are four seasons at the end of which your farming progress resets and you need to replant everything with a different set of plans. You also need to keep a lot of the harvest from earlier seasons to cook recipes in the off-season. This hits you pretty hard economically and you barely have enough money to reinvest in the first year. After the first year you suddenly break out of the poverty cycle and grow your farm a lot, but that's just a lot more time you spend every day watering dirt. You can craft stuff that helps automate things, but the best, labour saving-upgrades are such ridiculously end-game items that I doubt anyone would actually benefit from them before uninstalling the finished game.Combat is really bad. It makes the sort of janky and experimental stuff we saw on PS2 look like a polished gem. In a lot of ways, it's just hitting X until things die. There's little skill involved, it's all entirely level based. If you select a ranged class, get ready for mobs resetting half-way through the fight because what little AI there is can't path-find to you on a flat surface. Your companions can spend half the time just standing idle like muppets and you can't rely to them to even finish off a near-death mob.The story is weak, keeps pulling random crap and doesn't make a lot of sense overall. It feels like filler content. There's lots of side-quests, which mostly involve running between point A and B to read dull writing. I think by the time you hit your third or fourth cheesy subplot with someone getting amnesia, you can tell that nobody really cared. Speaking of reading, the game actually had voice over. But it's so rare and random that it shocks you to suddenly hear voice outside of the three lines characters speak on repeat in battle.

_childDocuments_.review: After about 3 hours of play, I will say that I don't have anything serious to complain about, and if you know what you are getting with this game, I would recommend it. The visuals (graphics, art style, character designs) are gorgeous, and the music is very well done. The game reminds me a LOT of FFXIV in many of the design and setting departments. The game is quite literally half farming, half RPG, all Square-Enix. It looks, feels and plays like FF mixed with Stardew Valley. The customization is definitely lacking, but you don't even get any in most FF or Square games, so that is a small issue for me. The characters are well made and look cool enough for me to not care. The only issue I had was the fact that the controls and options are a little bare-bones and simple. The video options consist of little more than brightness, resolution and window type. You can customize mouse and keyboard controls, but not gamepad controls, which is very odd. Also, the camera sensitivity, even at max speed, is pretty slow, and your audio/video/control options are basically non-existent.The game-play is not terribly paced, and there is definitely story and characters. So far, it is kind of playing out like a Star Ocean narrative. I really like the character designs, and I am a huge fan of the art style, character images in-dialogue, and the setting. There is an over-world map, surprisingly, and it is really nice looking and well designed. The map also works well with the time system. You get a home base, with a farm plot. The farming is basically what you would expect, and it looks like you will be able to upgrade and expand the farmland as you play.All in all, I was really looking forward to this game, and like I said, if you know what you are getting, you will enjoy it. It is basically a higher budget Stardew with better graphics and mechanics, given the Square-touch.I do hope that eventually they improve or expand on the settings and options, and hopefully they add more customization and there is some kind of romance mechanic added. As of now, I don't think there is any type of relationship mechanic going on. Again, I am only about 3 hours in, so there is plenty of room for reveal and twists. I am okay with paying full price as I am a Square fan and enjoy RPG and sim games. Supporting the devs here on this one is worth it, and increases the likelihood of patches and DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: While the game is a little rough around the edges, it is still an enjoyable one. Harvestella is a mix of a single player rpg and farming sim. While the farming portions aren't ground-breaking, they can still stand fairly well on their own. As for the story, it can be a bit jarring at times but alright if you stick with it. The music score really elevates this from a good game to a great game. Harvestella feels like a sleeper hit.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: I saw some of the bad comments about this. To be honest, I think a lot of people were thinking, with a name like Harvestella, it would be more geared towards farming. Honestly, I did as well. I got the game regardless because I knew if I didn't like it within two hours, I could just ask for a refund. The story at the start was kinda meh. I could have honestly skipped the cut scenes no problem. There is no character customization really. I feel like no matter what you pick, your character looks female. I wish there was more aspects of customization because I just didn't like the two choices given. Once you get past the second chapter, everything really picks up. I love the music in the game. It is flawless. The regions are beautiful. It runs very well. I have it maxed out on FPS and graphics. The upgrades to the farm you can get are worthwhile. There are only chickens and a sheep that does the job of a sheep and a cow in other farm sim games. With the farm, there's expansions available you get after completing parts of chapter three that make it more beneficial. Once you get your partners, I feel that the relationship system is kinda blah and I skip over most of the dialogue, but I love the characters overall and their designs. Some of the job classes stink, but some are great, but that's with any personal preference or game to be honest. The NPC quests are boring and I skip those as well. Otherwise, I'm enjoying the game very much. The combat system is good if you know how to use the classes. I wish there was a dodge mechanic but there is a dash you can use to dodge moves. It can be challenging at times, which makes it better. You can't just rush in to dungeons and there are puzzles that have to be completed and some challenging enemies. I love the grinding aspect and I feel this game was meant for someone like me. It reminds me a bit of Rune Factory and I honestly can't stop once I start playing for the day. I highly recommend this game to Rune Factory fans or people who want to try something a bit different. This game is not full proof, but it's honestly beautiful with amazing music I could listen to for hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I completed the game before winter arrived. While the combat mechanics were decent, managing class levels proved to be quite cumbersome. As I progressed, I found myself facing increasingly challenging enemies, particularly in the mid-game.One aspect I wished for improvement was the involvement of my partners in combat. _childDocuments_.review: Harvestella is a game that was an unexpected surprise for me.I had just originally regarded it as a more by-the-numbers part farming/part action RPG and not stand out in any particular way, but a handful of friends giving it high praise convinced me to check it out. What I got was an adventure that reminded me of the enjoyment I had playing the original release of NieR years ago.In terms of gameplay, the system has a lot of push and pull to maintain, in regards to stamina/time management. You are able to do some farming activities (plant crops / water / use ingredients to create food)  which then give you the stamina and HP to explore dungeons. This is all balanced out more with the cycle of time, where you cannot play as much as you want, you are limited by the time remaining in a day (which fortunately the game autosaves after each day), and eventually you either are pushed to go to bed or you will fall asleep out in the world and be returned home (with a small penalty of money/lost time the next day). The clock also determines your access to shops/NPCs/etc., so personally I was able to schedule out a general loop of what I'd do per day, which would shift based on sidequests/which shops I needed to visit, etc. This supports being a very pick up and play style game (especially on Steam Deck, which runs well and I used the entire playthrough), so good for small chunks, you can even max out what you can do in a single day in ~15-30 minutes. So I had a fun time building out my schedule, improving my attributes to be able to do things faster and consume less stamina which ends up giving me more leeway to do other tasks later. It's a satisfying gameplay loop, especially since there's no real "timers" to be concerned about other than the seasons changing and your crop availability to change with them. You very rarely are "forced" to do certain tasks, other than when the story calls for it, which makes it a very chill experience. Want to just farm/gather materials? Go for it! Want to see how much of a dungeon you can explore in a day and do some sidequests? Up to you! The freedom and lack or urgency does seem counter to certain story beats, but you are free to farm/gather what you need and prepare before embarking on a journey.The story for the game is worth seeing through to the end, it is hard to describe without approaching potential spoilers, though. Just will mention that unraveling both why the world is the way it is with Quietus as well as your character's role, is quite an adventure, especially as you are revealed more and more of why things are the way they are. It is both a mixture of a general air of sadness with a mixture of hope and perseverance (which just gives a small idea of what to expect). For sidequests, there a *lot* of them, which mostly consist of the usual "Get [x] number of [y]", "talk to [person] in [town]", so unfortunately while they are basic (aside from having to manage your time appropriately), the writing of them gave a lot of laughs, existential crises, and all of the feelings in between. Even the party member sidequests stand out, and I did appreciate that not everyone's story does really wrap up with a neat bow and be like "hey their problem is totally fixed and everything is A-OK, thanks to you, the protagonist!" The only recommendation is that since there are a lot, it's best to group them up based on location and knock out multiple events, which does lead to a lot of talking and cutscenes (where you can see more of the writing and you also get some fun dialogue options as well).The soundtrack is full of both pleasant farm-tastic tunes as well as high energy dungeon themes that really stand out. I feel some of the music you hear a lot while exploring was fine in general, but certain themes around bosses and specific areas really just make me wish the soundtrack was more widely available for people to listen to (thanks Square-Enix >:(  ). Check it out if you can find it, they did some great work for this.Overall, I think this is a game that went under the radar for many people and really deserves some attention, or at least a better look than "ah just another standard JRPG". I'm not sure what the developers will work on next, but I look forward to see their next project. This new IP does not appear to get in the same realm that the NieR franchise did, but I feel it's hitting the same highs with making you really think through certain situations and how you would handle them. I wish I could be more specific, but Harvestella is definitely a game that stands out as one of the best RPGs of the past few years. Strong recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is very lackluster for a AAA SE game.. They really  missed a chance for a great combination of a FF style game with a Farming sim. _childDocuments_.review: When someone I love dearly came down with a sickness that left them bedridden, I began looking for games to play for them that would hopefully cheer her up. She loves her cozy games, and she always let me watch her play them -- it was a great way for us to spend time together. So I buy Harvestella on a whim; it had Square Enix's name on it, so I trusted it. We didn't get to play it together like I intended since we found other ways to pass time, but I went on to play this nonetheless. Boy, am I happy I did! I was expecting a cozy farming game to sink a few hours into like Sun Haven. What Live Wire delivered was an incredibly emotional slow burn of a story with an even more incredible soundtrack that ranges from relaxing and upbeat to hauntingly beautiful, as can be expected from a game published by Square Enix. Additionally, each environment is so unique and just straight up attractive to look at and walk around in. The artists did an incredible job stylistically. I thought that the lack of voice acting would be a turn off, but for me, it actually gave the game some really nostalgic charm.I loved every twist and turn of this journey, going so far as to complete every quest! Every time a story had left me sobbing (and trust me, I sobbed a LOT playing this game), it also gave me a hand back up and ended in a way that left a smile on my face. Each of the main cast is memorable, and having completed the game, I genuinely feel as if I'm saying goodbye to some very close friends. I can't wait to revisit them down the line! My biggest gripe with the game is that character customization leaves MUCH to be desired, but I think the few gripes I have with the game can be attributed to the games low budget or the fact that it was made for the Nintendo Switch. I'm not too well versed in the Switch, so I'm not sure about its capabilities. Still, what this game has to offer greatly outweighs whatever small gripes I have. It is sad that this game didn't get the marketing it needed to succeed, but hopefully with time, the game will become more popular and Square Enix will give Live Wire what they need to make a Harvestella 2! Until then, this is an absolute gem of a game and I will be eagerly keeping my eyes open for more like this.It's hard to explain, but this game has been pretty therapeutic for me. So if you are on the fence about this game, just give it a go like I did! Dive on in, you won't regret it!
