_childDocuments_.review: I'm having fun with the game. So I recommend it. It's pretty, dramatic, and sounds great, like most Square games. The only thing that bugged me at first, is the time constraint put on you to get things done before you have to sleep. But I totally get that there has to be a stop point to advance some story elements, as well as have crops grow, sell goods, stores open, etc. Other games handle this mechanic different. I think I remember some let you work your land and kill stuff in the dark if you feel like it. This is a more advanced story and isn't going to let you do that. You get used to getting into a routine, and there are areas that have bridges and ladders to repair for shortcuts to come back to. So you aren't stuck trying to rush an area each subsequent time. Also, for leveling purposes and farming/crafting supplies, you're going to want to repeat areas and grind mobs a lot anyway.I think the game has way more to offer than it's getting credit for, from reviews I've read. I almost didn't buy it, but am glad I did. I haven't even unlocked anything but the basic harvesting and two job classes, because of trying to explore every nook and cranny available before bedtime, while still watering the plants!Everyone is entitled to their opinions. I suggest at least buying on sale and trying it out. Set a timer and refund if it's not your style. Don't go by the 'mixed' reviews. 9/10 - Minus 1 point because I want the day just a teeny bit longer, so I can plant one more carrot..
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: This game is deeply mediocre and just barely worth recommending; I would -not- pay full price for it.Let's get the two major flaws out of the way.  If they're deal breakers, I'd just move on.  If not, I do have good things to say, which I'll wrap up with.First and foremost, the character writing is abysmal, in the sense that it seems like everyone is holding the idiot ball all the time.  The overall story and themes are actually quite interesting, but every single character is licking the windows or sniffing glue at every opportunity.  A handful of basic questions could solve most of the game's quests before they even begin - and there are a whole lot of quests.  I was constantly frustrated to discover that I had to sit through yet another unskippable cutscene.  A large portion of my gameplay was just mashing circle to continue while watching Netflix on another monitor.Second major sin, the RPG elements are laughable.  In short, there's no challenge and no player choice.  The game does have the window dressing of an RPG, in the sense that there are numerous classes to develop with XP and job points.  However, equipment is trivial - one weapon, one upgrade path, no options.  The job system is utterly linear.  Your AI-controlled party members are useless.  They won't engage with foes until you attack first.  I played primarily as a caster and killed things with one charged attack all game long; my party never did anything unless I was brawling with a 'FEAR' enemy, a sort of miniboss that has more health.  FEAR enemies I defeated by just... drinking juice.  Not dodging attacks, not exploiting elemental affinity, not the useless 'break' system - just chugging dozens of bottles of juice, which I could make infinitely thanks to lots of veggie farming.  There's a system where you break two enemy vulnerabilities and press a thumbstick to fire off an ally's attack, which I was aware of, but only got to use once because everything just died too quickly to get a double-break off.That said, I'm criticizing the RPG elements of the game harshly because the game is just an awful RPG.  However, the farming elements are quite tightly designed.  There's some slimming down of the usual farming sim formula in ways I appreciate - not having to run and fill up your watering can, for instance, or having a single set of tools that become more potent when you complete X number of tasks around the farm rather than a process of upgrading tools by forging new ones.  Overall the farming, fishing, cooking, etc felt streamlined, but still meaningful.Another major upside is the graphics.  I was consistently impressed with the visuals, including the character visuals and costume design.  The visual tone is consistent throughout, and considering the breadth and scale of the plot that's an impressive achievement.I bought Harvestella expecting it to be an OK RPG alongside an OK farming sim.  It turned out to be an abysmal RPG, but quite a good farming sim.  The high points were exploring the numerous environments the game presents, and the low points were the individual character stories and the entire combat system.
_childDocuments_.name: HARVESTELLA

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely having a good time with the game so far. As of now it is nothing groundbreaking and nobody can deny that it certainly has its issues, but I feel like people are too harsh on this game.Pros:- Beautiful art direction! The illustrations look stellar. Even basic items get incredible looking artworks. The character models ingame look fine, but are nothing special - the environments are a feast, though; whenever I enter a new area I just stare for a moment.- Incredible OST!The music is just so lovely. It fits the sceneries and battles perfectly. One of the best sounding video game music I have heard in a while. Sucks that it's not easily available on Youtube or streaming platforms, though.- Good writing!Personally I enjoy the writing; it's simple and to the point, yet it helps the characters shine, bringing their personalities and little quirks to life just fine.The characters all seem intriguing so far and I want to see where the game takes them!- Interesting story?So far, the plot keeps me just interested enough to want to keep playing and find out what's going on. It's nothing too fancy yet, and thanks to the common amnesiac MC trope, your character knows nothing of what's going on at first - and NPCs can't be assed to explain a lot of it, either. Guess it works, though - I want to find out what they're talking about.- Good balance of gameplay...?This is definitely a hotter take, looking at reviews, but I enjoy the balance of farming and doing other things. Maybe it's because I get overwhelmed by your typical farming game and prefer my A/JRPGs over stuff like Stardew. Here I get both, with just the right amount of farming for me personally.People who mainly eye this game for the farming sim - you probably won't be happy here if you're not at least staying for the RPG. Because that what it seems to be first and foremost.Cons:- There's no voice acting. At all.I can't believe there's no voices except the occasional repetitive battle voice line. That's definitely a letdown.- Controls are janky af.I heard it's rough on kb/m, but I play with a controller 95% of the time, so I didn't care when I heard it. Controller feels off as well, though. It's not plain bad by any means - it just feels a bit stiff, sometimes, a bit unresponsive other times, and especially in combat the controls get in my way more often than not. You're better off leveling up to get tanky and bring tons of consumables to just survive through fights out of spite than trying to wrestle with your controls.... Might also partly be since I never touched an XBox controller in my life and there's no way to get Dualsense button prompts, unless I'm mistaken. Which takes me to the battle system - being able to change jobs mid battle is really cool! The rest is... well, fine. It mostly sucks that it's tied to such unresponsive controls, because battles feel like they're supposed to be busy; a quick exchange of blows, that's just being held back by its controls.On another note, I don't get the complaints about the character customization - or rather, lack thereof. To be fair, I never expected anything to begin with, unlike others maybe. Rune Factory doesn't let you customize your character either, but nobody's talking about that when drawing the comparisons between the two franchises...You don't get a lot of customization here, and personally, I couldn't care less. I know this kind of game would have been perfect for creating your own character for a lot of people; personally I was only disappointed for a moment, before I shrugged and just moved on. At least your character's party illustration will match the hair and eye colors you picked, which is a very nice touch! As of now, I can't think of anything else to say; will update this as I continue the game.This game was 70 bucks here; as of now, I don't quite feel that's justified. I would happily pay 50, hell, maybe even 60 bucks for it and feel satisfied. Seeing this get sold as an AAA game, though... it's a bit steep for what it is, for sure. So maybe wait for a sale, if you haven't followed some walkthrough on Youtube and aren't absolutely convinced you will love it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game. I played the demo on switch and then saw it was coming to Steam and despite mostly negative reviews all siting the same thing, I decided to take the plunge. It's not perfect, I especially don't like having to teleport home while I'm in the middle of a dungeon just because the game tells me I have to, or I can't do a part of a quest because it's too late. But seeing the farm grow every day and doing the morning tasks and then getting back to where I was doesn't take long. It's a good mix. I'm enjoying the characters and the serious, wait never mind this isn't serious at all slice of life feel of the side quests, and the rewards you get feel plentiful and makes it worth doing them. Although there are too many I feel, but I guess it makes the world and towns feel more alive. The combat can be fun, and the second main boss fight showed how dynamic the combat can be. At the same time it's a little clunky and I feel like I take too much damage when fighting tougher enemies and there isn't any armor or anything you can make or buy that makes you feel like you are getting stronger or rewarding you for working hard or playing optimally, if there is a high level enemy, you just gotta wait until your number is higher than theirs, or engage in the fight and hope it hits your teammates who take marginally less damage and hope it doesn't reset. So far, the rewards for winning tough fights aren't really worth it anyways, so it's easier to just ignore them and come back later. I may enjoy this game, but I can see parts that not everyone will. As someone who didn't expect an amazing farming sim, and came in with low expectations due to others, I can still see a lot of positives. I love the music and I think the world and the towns are very pretty. I enjoy the farming aspect a lot and don't feel punished by doing something sub-optimal. However I don't think it's worth 60 dollars, but if it's a game made by a 3rd party publisher/developer and it's on Switch, it's going to cost 60 dollars. But still, I am here to put in my positive review to fight off the negative reviews of people who didn't even play the game.Also, I don't care about the customization, the fact my characters illustration changes to match my hair color and eye color shows they put more effort into character customization than most other JRPGS. That's good enough for me.Don't even consider the Switch version it plays look doodoo compared to a good PC, but that goes without saying.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because seemed really interesting. The trailer and pictures will make you believe the game is focused around the "Harvest moon-esque" Features of the game. While there is a full farming there, there is also an amazing, rich and deep story line, amazing combat and class system, as well as actually interesting and engaging characters. I love RPGs and I love games that seem to be off peoples radars. This is one of those. With that said, its hard now at days to find an RPG that will really suck me I used to back in the day of SaGa Frontier, Valkyrie Profile, Wild Arms Grandia, Lunar Legend and Star Ocean. But Harvestella did it. And its something I have and will highly recommend others give a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Game itself is ticking just about every box I could ask for. Id give this a 10/10 if it weren't for 2 things holding it back, one of them I'd consider to be pretty major. 1. This is minor, but the voice acting is bare minimum. This is only a personal gripe for me2. Character customization is an absolute joke. They mentioned inclusivity, when in actuality you get non binary or female options. There is no actual masculine options. Your hair is tied to body type, larger body gives longer hair and smaller body gives the tied up version. All armors are non binary that lean pretty heavily on the feminine side, at least from the 4 I've seen so far. If they let us have actual customization options for our characters and not just color combos for hair, skin and eyes I'll be happy and this review will change. Until then it's a 6/10. With the lack of options dropping it by 3 and the lacking VA being a 1.Overall, if you're looking for an adventure with housing/farming that lets you dungeon crawl this is a great pick. If you're wanting to build your character to how you want, then this ain't it. And hopefully square is reading through the reviews to put something in the game. Obviously the models exist as a shop keeper has the male body options, and there's dozens of hair styles, and even some beard options. No reason for them not to let the player have access to them.

_childDocuments_.review: Harvestella is quite a typical JRPG but with a bit of weird real-time battle system. Attached to it is a cozy little farming sim that is tied to story progression as well as ridiculously engaging in its own right. Along the story, you'll meet several characters that all measure up to the usual stereotypes and do so with varying effectiveness. You'll also engage in a lot of sidequesting, with a couple of great storylines—and some not so great. In the end, the fate of the world is, of course, at stake (that's really not a spoiler). All in all, the ingredients of Harvestella makes for a game that seems very lacklustre and stereotypical. However, it's definitely more than the sum of its parts. I LOVE this game. It makes me all fuzzy and warm inside. I had a ton of fun playing through it and looking back at it fills me with joy. Harvestella is just such a complete package. It's been a long time since any one title has engaged me as much.I highly recommend Harvestella if you like farming sims with a story. I also recommend it if you like JRPGs in general, and ones with active combat in particular. But you have to expect much of the genres' shortcomings, perhaps even be one of those that, like me, gets a kick out of them.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Final Fantasy game with a bit of farming on the side.I recommend getting it on sale.I am a huge fan of the farming genre, but this is not a Rune Factory type of game like they marketted itself to be, which is why so many people felt betrayed and are giving negative reviews.This is by no means a bad game, just that it's too expensive for what it is, but it's to be expect from a JRPG.- There is a very deep relationship system, but no overworld relationship building.Your relationship growth with them feels a lot more organic than you can imagine, I'm just sad it takes you finishing the main story to "marry" your favorite partner.Also, there is no divorce, so either make multiple saves, or decide your favorite before making a choice.I ended up choosing a late game partner. Or early game if you get what I mean? xD- The combat system is hit and get hit.The combat system for yourself feels quite deep, there is many classes and fun ways to play the game, plus two secret reward classes to collect.However, you can't dodge damage unless it's scripted damage, AKA marked on the ground. Which can be very annoying and frustrating.- Farming is for cooking, not sellingMaking money in this game is not hard, but the crops you grow are more for you to cook and fight, most money I made was from raising animals and selling the extra items they hold.Selling crops don't make you enough back unless they are tree crops to justify buying, growing and selling.The profit margin is too low.There is exceptions like Nectarine, but you take so long to unlock it, that you will understand what I mean.- The item collection and crafting are very deepThis is actually SUPER ironic.All items mark what they are for:Crafting, cooking, selling.And believe them when they say such, I hoarded the selling itens thinking they could be used for something, and after 60h I can tell you... they are used for what they claim, and that's it, you have no reason to hold onto it, like, really no reason to.- Fishing in this game is very time consuming and not really rewarding.You throw the line, it bites, you pull, that's it. It's just time consuming and has no mini-game, it's just an automatic fishing that was added like it was an afterthought.How I know this? Because Square and Nintendo are infamous with how good their fishing minigames are, so the lack of any shows the lack of planning for it. They add fishing to games that don't need fishing, why wouldn't they add a proper fishing minigame to a game that needs it?- 100% Completion is actually fun!Aside from Fishing, the 100% completion challenge of this game not only is fun, but it's actually super rewarding!You unlock classes, itens, scenes and other things!So it feels really rewarding to do it, even if sometimes it's annoying (AKA Fishing), or hard (100F challenge thing).So my final rating of this game as a stand-alone:8/10But as a farming type genre:6/10This is a JRPG game with farming aspects, it's not a Rune Factory game, and people will need to accept this to enjoy this lovely game.Still not worth the $60 price tag though lmao

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not saying the game is bad, I'm saying I wouldn't recommend it.The game has no idea what it's trying to be. Is it a collect-a-thon? Yes kinda. Is it a time management RPG like Atelier? A little, but Atelier exists and does it better.Is it a farming game like Harvest Moon, Story of Seasons, Stardew Valley, or even Rune Factory? No, not at all.Is it a dungeon crawler or action RPG? No not really, and there's tons of other games that do it better.I would've played more, and will probably pick it up again once it hits a lower price but right now it's not worth it.If you want farming, play one of the games I previously mentioned. If you want action combat, just play something else. Harvestella is trying to do everything at once and ends up doing nothing well, which is a shame cause it controls well and looks pretty.And we got the 'Non-Binary' option in there for the kids.

_childDocuments_.review: First: This is *Absolutely* NOT a farming sim or "life sim".  The "farming" elements have squat to do with the story or gameplay.  It's bland RPG that they shoe-horned in farming elements to capitalize on Stardew valley craze.First: Farming is *extreme* low profit compared to everything else in the game.Cooking is *ZERO* profit.  Yep.  The finished product of cooking is worth the Exact same as materials.You could, and probably should, skip all the farming elements.As for the rest:Is it bad?  No.Is it good?  No.Combat is mid...Classes are a joke.  Other than the mage class, there isn't any real difference.Enemy Weaknesses/resists are a joke.  They are being spammed with "resists" and "weak" where you can't tell who's doing what, and most of the symbols are indistinguishable from one another.  "But you can switch classes to exploit weaknesses"  The problem with that, is groups will have different enemy with different weaknesses, and they'll all be dead before you can figure out who is weak to what.  And there is a timer on how often you can swap classes.So, it all boils down to: Fighter, or Mage.  Mage is *incredibly* slow, but takes no damage if you have allies.Practically all fights are extremely easy to avoid.Leveling and gear, as far as I can tell, are inconsequential.  Thus, you could skip the combat part as well.Story is decent enough.  No voice acting.  Very sedate.Overall, It's a low-to-mid game that fit my needs perfectly: I wanted to play something that wasn't bad to distract me from work when I need a break, but wasn't so good as to distract me from work when I needed to work.It's not something I *want* to play, but it's a good way to mindlessly de-stress.Sure as **** not worth $60, which is the only reason for the negative review.  Regardless of the length of playtime, this is worth, at most, $20.Naming this "Harvestella" and labeling it a "farming sim" and "Life sim" is just a spit in the face of all players buying it for such.

_childDocuments_.review: *Recommend ONLY IF ON SALE!!! This game is NOT a full-price (USD $60) value. Artistically, it's a beautiful game. Graphics, music, backgrounds, character art - no complaints in any of those areas. Story?  Quite interesting, some neat ideas, lots of side-quests had entertaining story as well, with only a few exceptions. (lighthouse quest chain)Gameplay? Not so much. The farming is basic, but serviceable. What really brings the game down is the COMBAT. You can't dodge most enemy attacks like you would expect to in an "action RPG" style game. There are obvious "red damage zones" painted for large spells that you can avoid, but that's all. Some classes have a "dash step", but it isn't usable as a dodge and takes a LOT of stamina to use. Also, your NPC allies generally won't tank hits for you - most enemies will ignore them to target you instead, and kiting is generally ineffective. They also do fairly weak damage... If you get your NPC Allies between you and larger "Elite" foes (FEARs), acting as a wall? The FEARs ignores NPC Allies, and eventually just despawn & reset. This leads you to just face-tanking even the toughest enemies & bosses, and spamming healing items to get through the fights. The only "strategy" or "skill" in fights is identifying and using the correct elements to do more damage and break defenses. All major fights become a DPS race against your supply of healing foods & (gallons of) juices. Overall, if you enjoy a good story with interesting twists, great art/music, and are willing to slog through mediocre combat mechanics to witness the story..... watch for a good sale. I felt for the story, it was worth the price at 50% off (USD $29.99). Such a shame, if the combat had been enjoyable, it would have been a much better game ....

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying Harvestella. The features are mostly solid and well executed, though (the job system aside) they seem to lack in depth. The game seems to lean more heavily on the RPG/story side over the sim side, and while unvoiced, the delivery of said story has been good so far. The music is good across the board, sometimes even great and the game absolutely looks beautiful, especially when it comes to the environments. The biggest let-down so far is the combat itself, which, while the different jobs feel like they each have their unique identity and are definitely fun to experiment with, is decidedly lacking in a lot of ways. Hits feel like they lack meaningful impact, even when the numbers are high, outside of specific skills that do knock-back or stun effects. I also feel the lack of a proper dodge mechanic and while some jobs can unlock something of the sort, it just doesn't feel good to use and there are no I-frames that I can tell. This is felt especially in combination with somewhat poorly telegraphed monster attacks in general combat situations, though boss attacks tend to be a bit better. Monster attacks also seem to hit quite a bit further than the animations seem to communicate a lot of the time, making the lack of a dodge even more glaring.Cooldowns on job-switches and skills seem on the long side even with the appropriate reductions unlocked on the job board and, in the case of job switching, it seems unnecessary to have to deal with them when you switch jobs outside of combat, making it feel somewhat like the game punishes you for planning in advance by switching to a specific job before initiating combat. As being successful in combat is fairly dependent on using the right jobs to make use of monster weaknesses, unless you are grossly over-leveled, this often leads to wasting time either in battle by running circles until a switch becomes available or out of battle by waiting to initiate until everything is ready to go. It is also a little painful that unequipped jobs don't progress, making getting them up to par when you need them feel frustrating at times.Lastly, some enemies (especially some of the early ones) keep being recycled across zones that otherwise have a vastly different look/feel, diminishing the zone identities and making new zones quickly become unexciting when you just run into the same slime/horse/etc. again and again. The farm aspect of the game is pretty satisfying, especially when it comes to the mechanics. Things like watering the crops feels good from the get go (no frustratingly inefficient watering can to deal with at the start) and harvesting goes pretty fast too, with satisfying sounds. There is some tool/skill progression to feel that you are 'getting better', though it doesn't feel very extensive as of yet. The fact that eating helps you regen your stamina pretty much indefinitely makes it so you won't have days where taking care of your crops eats through the stamina needed to do anything else in that day, the way you encounter in most games of the genre, so I haven't felt forced to end a day before I did everything I wanted to due to stamina constraints.The farm animals are super adorable, and the buildings and area look amazing. The farm also leaves some opportunities for exploration locked until you unlock specific crafting recipes and such, so it keeps it fresh and interesting. It's one of my favourite locations in the game.That said, the progression in this part of the game is largely tied to a wash-list of small tasks along the lines of "harvest x amount of y" and "cook x times" and slows down to a crawl fairly soon when those required amounts per task get higher in combination with needing to finish more tasks for the next milestone, which can be a little frustrating (especially when said tasks also include season bound crops).Profit margins on crops and processed/cooked goods are also pretty poor, and processing crops takes up quite a bit of (in-game) time either inactively (by sitting in a processor until the next morning) or actively (cooking can really eat up time if you want to do it in bulk). So it feels like it takes forever to earn money this way, especially early on, not so much because the crops and other products sell for little, but because seeds and other services are expensive in comparison, and by far the biggest part of my income so far has been from quest rewards, as the pay from those IS good and they tend to give you good amounts of various seeds as well. However this has as a side effect that it feels like the farm is really more of a side to the RPG, and the point where I run out of side-quests (and food deliveries) looms heavily in the not-so-far distance.Fishing is pretty shallow, only requiring you to cast your line in a fishing spot and press a button when something bites. Fishing spots tend to come with a nice scenic camera angle and the fish each have a pretty picture and a nice little blurb of flavour text when caught, but both the fishing itself as well as the fish are decidedly unexciting most of the time. (The exception for me is the Octopus Traveler, which deserves an honorable mention as it made me laugh the first time and still makes me chuckle every time it has come up since). It also doesn't pay huge bucks, but using up the last few hours each (ingame) day to catch and sell some fish has certainly helped to pay for farm expansions, buildings and weapon upgrades, so there's that.All together I've found that while certainly an enjoyable experience across the board, nothing Harvestella brings to the table justifies the 60 euro pricetag over the amount most indy titles cost. So, while I do recommend this game, I would advice to wait for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely incredible and can only get better with impending DLC.This game suffered from some early bad press because of the inclusion of non-binary and weak character creation. It’s a shame because this game should not be slept on.ProsSurprisingly interesting story, quite outside the norm of the genre.  The twists, turns, and discoveries keep the world exploration interesting and make me want to learn more about this world.Job system. Always a welcome addition. The jobs are interesting and all provide different play styles and bonuses. Once you learn how to optimize your load out, you can hit some really cool power spikes and take out tougher enemies.Side quests are actually interesting and well written for the most partTool upgrades feel very rewarding and farming doesn’t feel like a chore as a result. Especially the watering and gathering upgrades.Managing dungeon progression vs time of day actually leads to you making some interesting choices. Do you risk trying to make it to the next save point? Can I make it home before I pass out? Do I have enough stamina to kill an enemy up ahead?  Did I even remember to do all my chores before I got myself into this mess?ConsParts of combat need to be optimized. A dodge/guard button and the ability to animation cancel would make the combat feel much more dynamic. There are some abilities that will lock you in place for 3-4 seconds while an enemy starts and finishes a cast in that duration. Hoping for DLC or a patch that fixes this.While the game boasts a long play through time, I’d love more post game content to keep me wanting to farm year over year.A number of the characters look extremely young, especially in the context of you eventually making them a domestic partner. This is pretty normal for the genre, but makes me personally feel creepy and not want to develop their bond.Character creation. Has to be mentioned. The game needed a couple more body types and hairstyles. The female model looks amazing, the male model is too androgynous in its default build. It looks great in most of the job outfits, but it will be difficult for some players to imagine themselves in the MC’s shoes.Overall, I was pleasantly surprised by this game. It boasts an extremely long play time, especially for the story, and in my opinion was worth every bit of the retail price. The game only continues to get better with more time played.

_childDocuments_.review: So, currently I am 18 hours in. Might as well do something fun while not sleeping, right? So, I'm going to start by saying I'm not even through the first year. So i'm not knowledgeable about everything. I'm about to finish the first month/season. I've completed a lot of story, and so far that's where most of my time goes. Farming feels like more of an after thought in this game. It's easy, and convenient enough not to take a lot of time. But it's also your main source of income. So before you set out to quest for the day just collect/sell, harvest/water crops then head out. The graphics are nice to me, the characters while not many unique models, are memorable in the questlines. And I'm enjoying the quests. Pros: I enjoy the story, the characters have some depth to them. You have ideas about them and their history but don't fully know until following certain quests.Pretty graphics. Are they Unreal Engine 5? Nope, but they're nice either way.Music is beautiful. It's basically more story than farming, so it's kinda like half of a final fantasy game?Haven't found any groundbreaking bugs or anything.Cons: The character customization sucks admittedly. You have like 2 hairstyles, and you can change your skin/eye color. That's about it. Definitely should be more for a game made in 2022, but hey, not enough for me to downvote a game.For those hoping for a game based around farming like Stardew, it's not really. I mean, it might be later on? But for the most part right now it's the first few minutes my character wakes up in the morning then I'm off to quest/follow the story. There needs to be more ways/more efficient ways to get money since the focus isn't farming. I've made enough to scrape by, but that's been basically enough to upgrade my gear and buy the kitchen add-on for the house.Kind of a personal gripe, but I don't like that you can't decorate the house you live in. Part of the charm of those other farm sim like games. Creativity.Thoughts? I'm looking forward to seeing what happens in the future for this game. If we get dlc? Added maps, crops, etc. Maybe mod support. I'm enjoying the journey however, and I know the price might be off-setting to some, but I'd say give it a try if your wallet can handle it. Otherwise wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is bland. The story, the art, the fighting system—all bland.Story: There's nothing unique about this game that sets it apart from others. It features the typical JRPG "I can't remember anything" protagonist with a farming paint job. The story is boring, and the tutorial is excessively long. Three hours in and still on a tutorial? Why does such a bland game drip-feed gameplay features so slowly? "Go here, talk, go there, talk, you can't do this right now." I can't even skip the cutscenes. Side quests are uninteresting, following the same "go here, talk, go there, talk" pattern with the occasional "fight this monster." It doesn't help that most dialogues are bland with meaningless choices.Art & Music: All character models look the same regardless of gender, except for the old people/fat people stereotypes. Why aren't there different clothes for the male model of the protagonist? Also, the character reverts to the default "fighter" class outfit for cutscenes. The music is nice, but it becomes old and repetitive quickly. Nothing I would go out of my way to find and add to a playlist.Gameplay: From what I've seen of the fighting system, it's boring and not very engaging. I'm not looking for Souls-strat-sweaty level gameplay here, but coming from Square Enix, I was hoping for something more engaging. Most fights involve face tanking and button smashing. The class system is interesting, but I can't pick my job right off the bat, and I had to slog my way through an uninteresting story to unlock more.Forgot to add: No voice acting? For a $60 game and no voice acting????I got this game on sale for $29.99, and even then, I feel like I wasted my money.

_childDocuments_.review: I kept hoping if I kept playing the quests would become more interesting.  70 hours in now, and I feel I'm almost close to completion, yet I don't even want to load it back up to do so.  You seem to spend 95% of your quests helping children with mundane things like squabbles with friends, or collecting sticks for snowmen.  It made the game feel anti-climatic at every turn.  I enjoy the fighting style, and being able to switch and level up different abilities, but the game is lacking content.  I don't mind doing numerous side quests for t he kiddos in t he beginning, but when almost everything is maxed out, and I'm still going from town to town settling children's squabbles in near end game, it leaves the player feeling a bit empty or unaccomplished.  I felt myself skipping a lot of dialogue because of this, and the fact that all of the NPCs share the same features!  It's almost impossible to tell characters apart for side quests unless they have the alert above their heads because most of the NPCs look exactly the same.  Just google some gameplay before purchasing.

_childDocuments_.review: Harvestella, What to say about the game.  I think most people reviewed it on the demo or early on.  I myself never did that as I wanted this game to be a new experience.    Some people would say Robocop or terminator 2 is a Scifi movie.  And I would say this game is clearly scifi.It is ironic as I played Triangle strategy before this.  Awful game, but relevant here as many stated it was great for all the text in the game and story.  Harvestella, should be classified as a Visual Novel with gameplay in the world.  The game is a must play for side quest.  I would say the side npc stories are the best in the game and better than most games.  On par with some good Elder Scroll quest but for our generation not grandpa’s.  The main cast has stories that are similar in growth to say Tales of Arise.  The ruler guy in that story for an example went from being a ruler to learning how to be a leader.  This game toons follow similar paths.  The combat is so so, actually looks a lot like FF stranger of paradise.  Saying that, itha sa few mobs and most things die so fast that combat is not really a star of the game but something you can do or enjoy.The zones are good. Lots of love when into the areas.  Many reminded me of Tales of Zesteria.  Speaking of that….  The music no one would deny it has a great opening song.  Harvestella soundtrack is great and relaxing.I did the farming it was nicer than Rune Factory 5.  Still not my mega cup of tea.  I wish they added a real blacksmith crafting, clothing or woodworking.  I would recommend this game for the stories and side quest alone.  All else is frosting on top, to enjoy and extend your time in the world.

_childDocuments_.review: PLEASE DON'T BELIEVE THIS BAD REVIEWS.The game is amazing, it's a farming simulation game with touches of RPG. It's the classic Harvest Moon and Rune Factory style. Even Stardew Valley or Animal Crossing. People is treating the price of this game like if it was an indie game and it's not, it's better.It's full of tiny details everywhere. It's NOT A PORT. It goes amazing on PC, 0 errors, full 60-120 fps. Runs perfect. Quick menus and quick movement for harvesting things in the maps where you explore. Animations for picking up materials aren't necessary when the game tries to make it dynamic and quick but still super relaxing and chill. It's cute as hell. And you can inmers yourself into the story of the characters very well with tiny quests that are adorable and let's you know more about your surroundings.The story is really misterious and looks really cool, much more better than any story from any other farm gaming I've played. The animations could be better, but if this game has it's roots on the other games from the same guys, I am Setsuna, Lost Sphear and Oninaki, it's their style.Personalization is poor, but it's like Rune Factory: you have this protagonist and that's it, and this doesn't make the game less better and interesting. I would like to change at least the hairstyle but it's not something that bothers me. Graphics are so beautiful, the music is AMAZING. It has the same level of quality of any AAA game like Nier of FF. I don't understand what people expected from this game and why the bad reviews. It's a full game not an indie, that's why it's that price, and I think it's very fair. I've paid more for an indie game that only gives me 5 hours of gameplay like Stray (the cat game). =/ And that's overpriced.This game deserves every inch of love you can give to it, because it deserves it. It's really beautiful and I'm so happy! Because I've always wanted something more dynamic and into this kind of style for a farming game. I don't know if you can date or not, if you can then it's perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a comparison, this is Dark Cloud 2 meets Harvest Moon. This is not Stardew Valley level farming focused. Farming, quests and combat skill all need to be worked on simultaneously; do not simply focus on one aspect of the game at a time as it will greatly reduce the overall immersion and will cause you to stall and have to go back to work on neglected areas. Love how polished the graphics and audio are, although for a AAA game I would've liked to have seen more voice acted lines to help with character growth. I will call this game a niche gem, but if you are unsure I would wait for a lower price point, although again I am happy with the purchase at full price. I suspect it is at least a 50 hour game as 15 hours only got me through the first Spring season.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely difficult to recommend. It's not a BAD game, but it's certainly not a $60 game. Not to mention the marketing for this missed the mark entirely, so most people are going to pay for a $60 game just to realize they didn't get what they expected. This game would be better priced at $20-30. You can already get some deals on this game if you shop around, but it's still pretty pricey.Price aside, it really feels like it lacks polish. I actually am enjoying the game quite a bit despite it's flaws, but it's really hard to understand why the game shipped in this state. Square Enix might have playtested this game for bugs, but I feel like they never asked the playtesters if the game was actually fun to play. There are SO many minor inconveniences and inconsistencies that make the game less enjoyable. For example, a lot of back and forth for quests that could have just been handled in cutscenes. The weird thing is, some quest cutscenes move you to the locations involved in them, but other quests will make you walk small distances over and over instead.Farming in this game feels like such an afterthought that I don't know why they even bothered, and why the game was both named and marketed for it. It's very uninteresting and super basic. I'm a huge fan of Stardew Valley, but the farming in this game just feels like a terrible time-sink rather than an enjoyable or relaxing activity.A lot of people complained that there is no voice acting in cutscenes. This does sometimes make the game feel a bit less alive, but it's not a huge issue for me. Honestly, I'm more annoyed that they did SOME voice acting for characters in the field. Once you gain the ability to harvest multiple crops at a time, hearing the same voice line 10+ times in 30 seconds is a bit annoying. They should have made more voice lines or none at all. Or even just a cooldown after hearing a line.Graphics wise, the game has a great style to it that I feel is appropriate. My only gripe is that some of the animations look extremely stiff and awful. When you get started with farming, you have to use the hoe twice per square. This animation is EXTREMELY robotic and unnatural. This becomes less of an issue later with the farming skills, but still. Running around with my weapon out is also generally pretty bad looking.I wanted to hit "Yes" for recommending this game, but my conditions for who I would recommend it to are too narrow. If you can pick the game up for cheap, go for it. I would never recommend spending $60 on this. Even if they fixed the issues I have with the game, it will never be worth $60...but it would be really nice if they patched it up a bit anyways. (They probably won't, though.)

_childDocuments_.review: Harvestella seems like a game that two different people with two different ideas worked on separately, then combined their half-finished games together to make a complete(only so far as 50% + 50% = 100% mathematically) product and Harvestella was the unfortunate outcome.Don't get me wrong, it has good points to it. However, for a FARMING game, the farming is not one of them.The farming, which you assume looking from the outside is its primary draw works differently when you interact with its features. Tilling the soil and planting crops locks you in a single direction for a few seconds, only allowing you to strafe side to side at a slower pace. This only lasts long enough to be inconvenient, then you're released from it as you begin to adapt to the change. The watering and harvesting of said planted crops is not like this. You can walk around freely as you water your plants. This makes the single-direction lock seem to serve no purpose outside of frustrating the person playing the game. It also has a stamina system that you can regenerate by eating food to increase a "fullness" meter. This doesn't serve much purpose other than to place some minimally effective limit on the characters actions. More like they saw stamina systems in other games of the genre and just copied the idea, but very poorly.The combat within the game, which is honestly what you'll do the most, is likewise rather under cooked outside of the major boss fights. It's just a series of button mashing against mobs in the world. There's no real technique or strategy outside of the occasional use of, at most, 4 skills that do special damage. Creatures run at you, you run at creatures, and you stand face to face beating each other up until one of you dies. There's no real dodging or blocking. Sure, you can run away from an attack but you'll get hit a lot regardless. There's just defense stats and higher HP to tank more damage.If you're a dedicated mouse and keyboard gamer, then don't even bother looking past this line. This is a controller game. The control scheme for mouse and keyboard is atrocious. It may actually be the worst control scheme I've ever seen for mouse and keyboard. Going back to my earlier anecdote, it's like two different people created half the UI, then just stuck their halves together. Different windows have different controls. Some use WASD, some use the arrow keys, some use mouse. Have fun dealing with sub-menus that change what buttons do what regularly.The game actually looks quite pretty though. The environments are what you'd expect from a square enix title. Very high fantasy with fantastical landscapes and huge crystals jutting out of the ground, for some esoteric reason. The character art is likewise very beautiful. It's one of the things I love the most. The music is awesome though. It's very soothing and very enjoyable to listen to. I could turn the game on and simply let it run in the background so I could listen to the music.I looked forward to Harvestella when I first found out about it but I bought it with the expectation that it would be a Farming and Life Sim. It is not those things, or at least it's not very good at those things. It's a JRPG where you can plant some vegetables to cook food for your travels, which is your main source of healing to recover your HP after getting hit in the face repeatedly.Strongly do not recommend to anyone that exclusively plays mouse and keyboard. Save your money and sanity.To all others, I would recommend you buy an actual JRPG and a better farming game. You'll very likely save money and get more hours of entertainment from it.

_childDocuments_.review: Well it's not a perfect game, far from it.The goods:Firstly the art style, music and just general maps and settings are beautiful as you'd expect from Square enix.It's a relatively chill and forgiving game, (there are some buts to this later)It's very intuitive with what it's trying, farming, combat (but again...more butts)The story i've got to with so far is that of most jrpg, it's chapters and littered with side quests which keeps you busy.For a change the time per day ratio is actually workable! Seriously i don't know why so many modern farm games hate you to have time to enjoy a day!The mehs:The farming is..not really fun, maybe it improves but it's really not at all a priority you go out water, box the plants then go on your day.The combat is also like the farming..it seems so basic and not fun or satisfying which for Square enix i was hoping more dazzles and cool powers but really it isn't. Basically you get "jobs" to swap between and get more when you get more party members, basically copying their powers..so not really unique. (again maybe later on it could get better)The story has been okay but i'm struggling to keep up as the pacing has been a little fast, like for the first 10 days i'd wake up to something happening (not that it's a issue) but it can throw of my enjoyment.The leveling up and combat difference is a pain, i would love a dodge button or a block button..but nope, it's more reminicent to a ff14 where you just take the pain as you spam attack and click on special powers when you can. It's again not a fun combat system even with the npc party members it don't matter, you die, it's end of day for you.   The bad:So it may just be a me issue but the avatar models have been very generic and really don't stand out, the npcs are just boring, compare it to dragonquest npcs and you'll know what i mean, as for the avatars of the party members it's again not really nice to look at, which for square enix who have some of the best and most iconic designs for characters its a bit meh. The avatar creation is also quite..limited...as in you only get 2 body types, (male/female)  hair color and eye color.The money making is kinda boring, and i'm sure if i spent time to dedicate to find out whats worth doing to make money it'd be fairly easy to cheese. So far, farming, adventuring/killng or fishing have been the only forms of income from the shipping box.So all in all:It's not a bad game, it's far from a bad game..but it's not worth it's price tag. It's story seems great so far, Maybe it's a game where a long investment of time is needed to really enjoy it. But i'd highly suggest not comparing or imaging rune factory games before going in.  I'd say wait for a sale before buying.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not one to write reviews of a game often, but this game definitely deserves it.It mixes together two of my most favorite genres: RPGs and Farming games. It's as if Final Fantasy and Harvest Moon or Stardew Valley had a Baby :)What first made me fall in love was the amazing artwork and the appealing character design. After playing a couple of hours I can also say, that the gameplay is very well designed an though through. It feels fluent in the farming, RPG and combat aspects. All packed in a so far great story! Especially the combat system, which makes you feel your character evolves with experience, giving different jobs you can play for mixing things up to your liking, but still not feeling clunky in the beginning before you reach a certain level of experience or need to unlock this specific skill you need is a well designed feature. The combats are not too easy either, but not as hard as to make you think you have to grind levels a lot to defeat certain bosses (up to the point I played until now that is :P).And if you need a break from fighting you have a lovely Home to tend to with a variety of possibilities: Growing crops, processing, animal handling, cooking, fishing and more. And here as well the system is very well thought through and feels fluent in handling. Square Enix never seems to fail my expectations and they really deliver games of quality rather than half done bug-shows as a lot of other developers do these days.

_childDocuments_.review: Without spoilers, I'll just say that Harvestella somewhat starts as you'd expect from a Rune Factory game: you, a random farmer/hero to be, awake without your memories in a strange town by a strange person, but unlike most farming sims, I noticed immediately even in the demo that Harvestella had a slightly more somber tone. Now this isn't constant in the game, there's plenty of lightheartedness and humor and brighter colors until you hit Quietus, a day between seasons that marks nothing but death for the people of this world and the day you awake to, or certain areas farther into the story. If you thought Square Enix's prints weren't visible enough, the story in the second half of the game goes even more Square Enix.So I'll be honest, I was genuinely curious where the story was going from the start. I made my little guesses, been proven wrong as the story went, made new theories, and discovered I was at least half right in parts. It was a fun ride that truly picks up once you get through the prologue, however...maybe this is a consequence of me hyperfixating so hard I said ♥♥♥♥ off to sleep, but there were times near the end where I struggled to make a little sense of the timeline regarding the sci fi elements (like I said, it's a Square Enix game). I wouldn't be surprised if to some, it feels convoluted, but I can at least say that the hints and events earlier in the game are made and done with these things in mind so they don't just feel like ass pulls either. I could still understand most of it, but certain details I basically had to just chuck into the mental trashcan because it wasn't worth trying to wring my brain out for it. Maybe it might make more sense to me after some proper sleep, when I don't have a cold (or at least I hope it was just a cold) and I replay it, but I feel like that's still important to say.The story is the biggest part of this game, by the way. It's an RPG first, a farming sim second.I'll be blunt, I have no idea why some people think the graphics look bad. I could be biased-- I'm not new to farming sims, both pure and hybrid, and most of them do not have graphics to the level Harvestella does. Rune Factory 5 makes this look like the Sistine Chapel's ceiling in comparison. I can to some degree see what someone might mean when they say it looks like DS game, but only in it's stylization, not actual quality. A game like this would look so bad on the DS, not even Pokemon with it's simple style and chalky looking 3D models could look crisp on that thing. I will say that I don't know how it looks on switch, but I think it looks fine, even beautiful on PC. The character models look simpler compared to the environments, but is that even a bad thing? And they're still well made on top of that, so...yeah. I really don't have anything else to say here, it's a nice looking game and I am genuinely confused. Moving on.So this is probably what might be putting a lot of people on the fence besides it's pricing, so I'll say what I said above. RPG first, farming second, and so the farming is designed to reflect what this game is trying to do: make you self sufficient.You're an adventurer, on the quest to save RPGland, so how are you gonna stock up? With so much food and drinks in your bag, every NPC will think you're trying to run the most primitive and inefficient food truck ever. In this game, farming is a means of supporting your adventure. Not saying you can't make some profit from it (the game doesn't force you to continue the story if you want to take a break, the opposite actually), but you WILL want to stock up on veggies and for cooking, because outside of a Double Break skill from one party member, there isn't any other way to heal yourself or your party but with food and drink. (Tip btw: you can create two types of effective healing potions with the fermenting barrels by putting either hermit's root or wise man's root into them which you'll even get for free from doing Cres' stories. You're welcomed.)To be honest, I don't mind this approach to farming because I feel like it fits with the game, and on top of that, the way they handled making farming feel more efficient and quick actually makes a smooth and relaxing experience to me and there's parts I wish were even in more pure farming sims. There's no need to refill your watering can and neither do you have to upgrade it yourself. You get four fairies on your farm after saving the day at each Seaslight (basically these giant crystal-like growths that gives the world seasons) during the first part of the story, and each of them come with goals to complete as you farm and adventure (basically objectives like harvesting a certain number of a specific crop or do a certain amount of quests in a specific city, nothing all that challenging and you'll probably do just casually playing the game). After you complete a certain amount, they reward you with stuff like upgraded fields or processors, or even tools. The ores in the game are mostly for crafting useful items you can use on your farm, in dungeons, or upgrading your party's weapons, so with all that in mind, it makes sense why the developers probably didn't want to pull the string too thin with tool upgrades. All of this together, I think, makes farming feel simple in a good way to me. Even animals won't die if you neglect feeding them, but they're affections can still go down if they're ignored so pet those fluffy babies so they can keep giving you some quality eggs and milk.I genuinely loved the party in this game, mostly their interactions during break times (basically you go near the save points in the dungeon, eat some food, and depending on the dish, you might get a Tales of- adjacent skit) where the characters chat with each other (you also get dialogue options during these to feel included) and the main story. Each party member (+1) gets their own personal stories that are like special side quests for the purpose of learning more about them and deepening your bond with them. Although there's some I feel wasn't as good as others' (Brakka), it's still solid enough and I liked their interactions a lot in the other means I mentioned (also Brakka). So what I'm saying is, even at their bottom, they're still charming enough to the point that I'm currently trying to see how they all react to confessions. A shame you can only gift a ring to one.Heine and Dianthus best boy and girl btw.So I actually like the idea of the romance being held off until you finish the game. The idea that you've journeyed and thought seemingly impossible enemy after seemingly impossible enemy while strengthening the bonds with a certain someone through their stories during is a genuinely sweet thing to me and I see where they were going with it. I wouldn't change that for a sequel, to be honest, because if expanded, I can see it being kinda unique to Harvestella, to help set it apart from other farm sim or farm sim adjacent games.I hesitate somewhat to finish this section because I just finished the game and haven't really soaked up this part of it yet, but just in case, I'll say this because the developers do seem to actually read criticism so who knows, but-- I think it would go a long way if there were extra character stories for after marriage/partnership. They don't have to be a lot, so long as they're strong. I love the cutscenes for giving them the ring, I love these characters in general. But I think a page can be taken from the likes of Story of Seasons: Trio of Towns, with maybe little stories centered around your new lives together. Just a bit of fluff maybe. Something to just make the player's heart feel all warm and fuzzy, ya know?So yeah, I loved this game, from start to finish. It's not perfect, but the bumps on the road feel more like little pebbles that can easily be polished up for future games.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely title. Enchanted graphics. Stylized look to things. Incredibly detailed portraits. Dense illustrative design for dungeons, interiors and even the world map.This game is an evolution of the genre, its own game, an enjoyable dungeon crawler and an expansive adventure title.With lovely music, long requested QOL improvements for the genre, smooth animations and performance. _childDocuments_.review: After making it through the first dungeon, my first impressions on this game are good. It started out slowly but by the time you get to the first dungeon it picks up. First off, the story in this game is more than what you see in other farm sims. So if you are going in thinking this is just a farm sim I would change those expectations. The story is engaging and the characters are pretty good. There is alot of mystery so far and alot of questions about the world that need serious answering. Combat is interesting, with a job system and more thought put it than you would expect for a farm sim.As for the farming sim part of the game, it is not super fleshed out yet, but I am still in the first spring. No leveling up seeds like RF5 and only certain characters have friendship levels. Upgrading tools so far seems to be based on fulfilling quest requirements, which involve basically shipping stuff and renovating the farm. Planting and harvesting are basic right now, though I expect it to broaden as I make my way through some more. I have not yet started any animal husbandry though the NPC for it was just unlocked. Cooking in this game is good once you unlock it and the art for the dishes is amazing.  Overall this is a good mix between jrpg and farm sim. If you are expecting Stardew Valley levels of farming, this is not the game you are looking for, but if you want to do some farming while enjoying a good story I would pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a Farming Sim game.Pros: Great graphics, interesting characters, enjoyable storyCons: - Not a "Farming Sim" game. It's a hack and slash adventure RPG with a farming mini game you play for a few minutes each game day.- It's a hack and slash game with pretty lame hack and slash mechanics. No dodging / blocking. Dashing to kind of dodge works sometimes but uses energy which you need for everything else in the game so it feels pretty restrictive. hit / run / hit / run / heal / hit. It's tedious.- No character customization at all- No cut scene / dialog skip button. Replay-ability is absolutely 0 if this isn't fixed. - Story pacing is awkward juxtaposed against the farming element. Every game day one of your companions is on the verge of death somewhere in the world with monsters about to eat them. On your quest to save them you run out of energy and just go back to your farm to sleep and then farm a bit for a week before you finally go save them. The high stakes of the story and the "farming sim" feature just don't mesh together at all. It really feels like they made an adventure hack and slash RPG and then decided to add a farming element after the fact.Overall if you like JRPGs you should get some entertainment out of the game. Not at all worth 60 usd. buy it 60% off.

_childDocuments_.review: C+ / B- or perhaps 5.5/10. Not worth $60.This game is plagued by mediocre writing, uninspiring characters who are difficult to care about, and grammatical errors (I seriously don't know how this is even a thing in 2022). As many have mentioned, this is a JRPG with farming elements (read: added as a grinding mechanic). However, the game plays, reads, and feels like a game that would have been designed over a decade ago by a non-native English speaking developer working on their second game. This is not a triple-A production, nor is it worth a triple-A price tag. I'd rate what you get at $20-$30. Buy it on sale, or better yet, not at all. I received this as a gift from a friend, so I will play through the entire thing. I am perhaps 50-60% complete at 55 hours, in fall of year one.Pros:- Pretty character portraits- Cute worldCons:- Story is uncompelling and offers you no reason to care about the world- No voice acting.- No character customization.*- Unskippable "cutscenes."***Character customization is as follows:Choose Male / Female / Non-binary (This is no effect on model or anything in game)Choose Male or Female model: All males have one haircut, all females have one haircut.       - Select one of five skin tones. - Pick hair color. - Pick eye color.Choose a voice: Male / Female. **At no point does your character speak!** This is only for yelling as you attack.There are 12 jobs in the game, each with its own costume. You cannot change your clothing out of combat, despite models already being in the game. You have one uncustomizable costume for out of combat, and then you automatically wear your job costume in dungeons or combat.**Cutscenes are merely camera locked character interactions, not actual videos. Every time you interact with a character on a quest or side quest, these occur. They cannot be skipped. If you wish to play through the game a second time, you must re-watch all of them. There is no auto-progress setting for text, you must click confirm to move to each new speech panel.I will alter my review if the game gets better by the time I finish it.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on sale for 30$, and overall I would say it was worth the price if you like games in the same genre such as rune factory or if the mashup of "final fantasy + farming sim" appeals to you as it does to me. I think at the full price of $50-60 it would be a bit harder to justify, primarily due to its overall simplicity and lack of depth of its core features.Additionally, while I personally don't consider it enough of a deal-breaker to warrant a negative review- I would actually *not recommend* this game for children of religious families. Several themes, so-called 'protagonist' companions, and many lines of dialog clearly stray from what is required by the fantasy narrative into full-on anti-religious bigotry. The game world includes a religious cult clearly modeled after the catholic church, which are depicted as evil, oppressive, simple-minded, and superstitious. All of these instances become especially notable in stark contrast with the inclusion of beings of supernatural origin, such as magical fairies, in the game; This is a strong indicator that the writers purposefully decided to overlook the presence of their own supernatural elements in game, and cherry-pick their disdain towards the more real-world religious elements (i.e. implying people are stupid for thinking god exists, while literally standing right next to magical fairies and a unicorn.) I almost always overlook these types of themes in games, especially eastern ones, but had to highlight it this time because it was so pervasive. Being respectful of others doesn't just include the color of their skin.Moving on, pros and cons:PROS:+++ 2D Artwork is excellent, UI is good. 3D environmental visuals and shaders look really good stylistically, even though it was made to run on that overpriced potato console the nintendo switch.+++ Music is really good, I would think some FF music enthusiasts would happily purchase the OST.++ The style of the overworld map could be the new gold standard for similar games in my book.++ combination of final fantasy elements with a farming game work out very nicely.++ The game's core strength is in its variety of features and its presentation. + The story & character arcs are 'decent' I would say, but not great. The initial mystery and intrigue of the game world is soiled a bit by a lackluster and unoriginal 'reveal'. Not bad, but they could've done a lot better.  + story and farm progression is well-paced and doesn't pressure you much. getting knocked out in combat is not punishing at all. Several quality of life elements such as easy teleport points all combine into a very casual enjoyable experience.Cons--- Anti-Religious themes and dialog far exceed the levels required to meet the narrative into what is clearly promoting bigotry and disdain for religious peoples outside of the game itself.-- Absolutely *none* of the core features have any depth: combat, class system, crafting, fishing, farming, animals, quests, npcs, relationships. None of it has any depth or complexity. -- Romance options are non-existent. The ability to court and marry your favorite npc character(s) is a pretty big draw for fans of the genre and it's not present here. - All cutscenes are non-skippable, and there are a lot. This will be a big deal for less patient people.- The game gives you 3 fake gender choices for your character: male, female, and non-binary. Every option looks female. - This is a nintendo switch game. All of the 3d models are hyper simplified to run on decade-old hardware. Visually, the worst part of the game is the 3d character models; specifically the NPC townsfolk. This gets overshadowed slightly by the quality of 2d portraits, but I can't help but think a game by square enix asking for 50$ on the regular could have afforded to make some genshin-level character models for the pc release and not reused the same 5 townsfolk npc models for every single quest.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR better than expected, but its not stardew valley or rune factory. Its final fantasy farmingIll get the elephant in the room out of the way first, the non-binary option in the character select screen is completely useless, except for a line near the end that if i say it would massively spoil the plot of the game. TBH i would say the writing of the game fits the male avatar a lot better than the female avatar, and i get the sense that the character customization was shoehorned in 2 months before launch. If they just stuck with the male avatar and gave him a bit more personality, i would rate this game about.4% higher than i will since the bulk of the writing and other characters REALLY carry the game.The writing and the story is really good, and it feels like it belongs in a fully fledged Final Fantasy game than a FF/farm game, but it does really fit well within the confines of the gameplay. the supporting cast have a persona- like story path where you hang out with them for story beats, support them with choices, and when you complete each story beat, they grow stronger, which is an intensive to go thru the story. most side quests are generally 3 quests deep that spans roughly 3-4 in game days, so you dont have to rush to get them done all in one day. and they do reward free seeds for the farm, which really helps in the early game. i never expected so many gut punch and depressing stories in a farming sim, but it makes the stories that have a happy ending and the overall plot feel much more impact fullThe gameplay is not turn based like older FF, but is more of a hack-n-slash with a few special moves mixed with avoiding telegraphed attacks. You do have a stamina meter that you need to keep an eye on if you want to dodge or use special attacks, and if your character is hungry, you dont regen stamina. you can keep your character full by making meals in the kitchen (when you unlock it) at the farm with the ingredients you find/grow. you also can make drinks that act like healing potions with the fruits and veggies you find/grow as well, so you dont buy potions, you grow them.The farming part starts off slow in the beginning, like all other farm sims do, but thru the story, side quests, mining, fishing, and growing crops, you can expand the farm slowly with the money you earn. you have to be careful near the end of the month through, since each season is one month long, and if you still have crops in the field when the games "quietus" event comes, the crops will die. you also have to make machines for the farm to process the ingredients you grow to make food, which usually takes a day to completeThe quietus day usually comes at the end of the month,. and usually opens up a dungeon on the farm where you can get crafting materials for machines and your weapons, and gives a bit more xp than normal dungeons, so its important to go as far as you can in the dungeon during quietusThe farming aspect does feed into the questing aspect, which in turn, feeds into the farming aspect, which makes a satisfying loop of trying to get farm work done and enough supplies to go dungeoning that day, which in turns makes each check point in the dungeon more satisfying.Overall, a pretty solid game, great story, really damn good writing, and satisfying game loop. though if your looking for a farm sim like SDV, you will be disappointed. id give it a 8.8/10. id enjoyed my time with it but i dont blame you if you wait for a sale, since there is alot of great games coming out this season

_childDocuments_.review: Let me clear up the huge misconception:THIS IS NOT A FARMING SIM LIKE STARDEW VALLEY.THIS IS A JRPG.If you come into the game with the mindset of a JRPG, this is a good game. I'll be honest that reading through the description I thought it would be heavier on the farming aspect, but this is primarily a JRPG.I have played pretty much all the farming sims like Harvest Moon, Story of Seasons, Rune Factory, Stardew Valley, My Time At Portia/Sandrock, etc.. I would say Stardew Valley is heaviest on the farming aspects with a sprinkle of combat and quests. Rune Factory I would put in the middle with a pretty decent farming system but also very heavy on the story, quests, and combat. Harvestella is heaviest on the story, questing, and combat, with farming being more of a side thing you do.As for the main complaints I have seen:NO CHARACTER CUSTOMIZATION!There is almost no character customization, which is pretty typical for most JRPGs. I'm surprised they even let you do any customization. If you want to insert yourself and make your own character, this game is not for you. Doesn't seem to be any way to change your clothes too besides switching classes in combat. I don't mind this as I'm used to it, but I know this is a turn off for some people.THERE'S NOT ENOUGH TIME!I have not had any issues with time coming from other standard farming games with time systems. There is plenty to do in one day and there are so many ways to fast travel that it makes me wonder if people played more than a few hours. You get ways to fast travel a few hours in and it is very easy to craft an item that will take you home from anywhere. Stamina is super easy to get back with even the most basic of foods. I think people are confused and think you're supposed to clear dungeons in one go - that's not the case. You should be spending multiple days, that's why there's shortcuts you unlock along the way in dungeons.FARMING IS TOO SIMPLE!As I mentioned before, this is a JRPG first.THE GAME IS TOO EXPENSIVE!This is the only main complaint I agree with. As this is a Switch game, I was surprised to see it priced at $60 like a AAA title. While this is clearly a labor of love and worth more than a $20 indie game, this does not feel like a full AAA release. I would say it would be fairly priced at $40. If you love JRPG's, then this is still a good buy at $60, but if you're on the fence I would wait for a sale.I recommend getting this game if you like JRPG's, but do not buy it expecting a Stardew Valley type game.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m recommending this game, but with some big reservations.  I’d give it a neutral review if I could. It does a lot of things right, but it screams “low budget” in some pretty obvious ways.First, it’s a JRPG + life sim, but it doesn’t do either particularly well.  This game could have been a chance to appeal to both JRPG lovers and sim lovers, but instead I’d recommend it only for the niche audience that likes both.  The systems are fun and addictive, but overall pretty shallow.  For example, the character customization and growth is weak for an RPG, and the relationship system is weak for a life sim.The combat leaves a lot to be desired as well.  It’s not terrible, but limited dodge/movement, no blocking, and 0 cooldown on healing items means that the intended way to approach tough fights is to just spam chug drinks to heal your way through them.  This is made more obvious by the fact that your NPC allies seem incapable of moving out of telegraphed AoE attacks, so you’ll spend most tough fights just healing them.  Despite all this, the job and break systems are enjoyable enough for the combat to be addictive despite its flaws.  It’s fun to explore the job systems and try out different classes for different enemies.The generic NPCs and side quests are probably the game’s weakest point.  Pretty much every sidequest requires you to talk to X number of people in town, go to a location (which ends in a fight 90% of the time), then travel back to the location where you picked up the quest to complete it.  The NPC models are also unapologetically recycled like crazy, so get used to seeing the same models everywhere in the game.  The writing can be entertaining for some of the quests, but the reused models and lack of voice acting ultimately makes them feel flat.The farming is probably the element I enjoyed most despite its simplicity.  Planting, watering, and harvesting can be done relatively quickly, and the farm animals are adorable.  It’s rewarding to see your farm capabilities grow as you gather each of the faerie NPCs, and all of the processing stations give you some variety regarding which products and crops you can grow.Ultimately it could have been a great game if it had a higher budget or was in development longer, but it’s overall a fine game that will appeal mostly to players that like both JRPGs and farming sims.  If you like only one of these genres, I’d probably stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely scratches the farming sim itch for me and the story ain't half bad either. Took about 60 hours to complete the story and planning to put more in to get all the achievements.Pros:- Looks very nice and runs great on PC. Played the demo on Switch and I prefer having graphic fidelity + good frame rate over it being portable.- Extensive story with a good variety of dungeons, reminiscent of Rune Factory games.- The music is bloody amazing! I loved all the remixes they made of the main theme.- Decent farming sim, with a good selection of crops- Enjoyed some of the character side quests- Variety of classes for combat- Don't need to grind too much for items/moneyCons- Story dungeons does start to drag near the end, grinding the story to a standstill at points (especially chapter 6-7).- Combat is very simplistic and doesn't really offer as much free movement as I would've liked.- The time system feels a bit too fast but you eventually get used to it- Sprinting taking up stamina, which forces you to eat constantly (some may enjoy this type of mechanic but I just found it irritating when trying to get through dungeons)- Side quests got repetitive very fast and most of them were forgettable.- While I do like the majority of the character quests, I would've preferred they shortened it because some of the scenarios didn't really progress the character development/story.Overall I enjoyed the game a lot as a farming sim and RPG hybrid, with it being one of the more polished Square Enix titles I've played. It really feels like a blend of Rune Factory (farming sim), Xenoblade (Story) and Nier (music) while doing it all to various degrees of success. The story could definitely be pushed further as it feels like a pretty standard JRPG plot and the combat could use some tuning to make it feel smoother, but ultimately, it was an experience that was worth its price tag.
