_childDocuments_.review: The protagonist wakes up amid the mysterious phenomenon known as Quietus, in which toxic dust fills the air and threatens the lives of humankind, but is unable to remember who they were or how they got there. (Cliché, but at least there’s a far more interesting reason for the amnesia than usual.) A whole bunch of other WTF stuff happens and the protagonist has no choice but to try to figure it all out if they’re ever going to have any kind of “normal” life.      • I didn’t personally confirm this, but according to others, the game doesn’t play well via keyboard.      •  involves: JRPG-style main story and sidequests, JRPG combat, farming, fishing, gathering/mining (mechanically the same), animal caretaking, collecting, crafting, and cooking.     •  is real-time action-oriented, but slow-paced compared to others. HP and stamina gauges to maintain. No random encounters; enemies are on the field and can be avoided by dashing. Only story-related enemies lock party into an isolated grid. Player has no direct control over party members. Party members cannot heal, so that is solely the responsibility of the player. If party members are defeated, they revive themselves after a bit of time passes. No “Game Overs”; if the player is defeated, they appear back at their home with the local doctor lecturing them about being careful. Player can switch job classes during battle to have access to different abilities and elemental attacks.     • There is no difficulty setting, so ? Probably not. That’s just my opinion though. General fights are easy enough, but some of the bosses can be fairly hectic. A more casual gamer might need to level up significantly in order to survive boss fights. Optional bosses can be very time-consuming.    •  is available post-main story. There are eight human main characters that are conveniently all single and available for the protagonist to romance. The player can only romance one character; sorry, my fellow polyams. After the partnership commences, that character moves in with the protagonist. It is not particularly romantic and is definitely not a focus of the game.    • 3 possible . 2 bad endings & one good/true ending.    • Lots of mysteries to figure out.     • Extremely addicting. Messed up my sleep schedule. Had dreams about it.    • Upon completing parts of the main story, faeries come to the protagonist’s farm, and I like their system of unlocking things that improve the gameplay.     • I really appreciate items being clearly marked in their descriptions as “used in crafting/cooking” or “to be shipped for money.” Otherwise, I hoard everything not knowing it won’t be useful later in the game. (An exception being juices and jams. For some reason, they’re labeled as items to sell, but some juices/jams are needed for a few recipes.)    • Items/ingredients don’t need to be in direct inventory for crafting/cooking or when going to the smith/builder. Items/ingredients can be taken from storage. Super convenient.    • I like the “secret” thing you can do during Quietus (when the player can’t do much of anything). Spoiler:     • Very pretty settings throughout the game. An autumn themed forest, a cherry blossom town, a beautiful beach town, and a frosty winter town. The water is pretty.    • Lovely, beautiful music.     • The confirmation button on the controller can be changed in settings. As this game was also released for the Switch, I’m glad they put in this option, because using what I consider the “cancel button” for confirming is odd. Every game on the Switch uses “A” for confirm, which is where “O” is on a PS4 (or 5) controller. That’s the cancel button.    • Criticisms of organized religion and blind faith.    • Philosophical narratives on what it is to be human and the worth of humanity’s salvation/preservation.    • Character creation is disappointing. Very limited. (Though, at least there’s a non-binary option for pronouns.)    • Even though the sprinklers hover in the air, you can’t plant seeds directly beneath them.    • Several instances of “repair bridge” prompts being left in Japanese. That’s sloppy work for a AAA company.    • I encountered a bug with the jumping ability. I don’t know the trigger, but at one point my character couldn’t jump like she was supposed to. Had to restart the game to fix it.    • While there are a decent amount of NPCs with darker skin, not a single one of the main characters is dark-skinned. There are eight human main characters and couldn’t even get a token.    • While there are random NPCs that are referred to as “they/them,” none of the main characters or even important side characters are non-binary. I always find this situation weird when devs give the player the option to be non-binary for their character, because it means they’ve acknowledged the existence of trans people, but are still unwilling to put them further into their story.    • During the “Return to Sender” sidequest, an NPC refers to Castle Lewis as the Castle of Illusion even though people outside of the main characters don’t know that’s its true name.     • Illogical and asinine decisions/reactions from grown-a$$ adult characters. This happens repeatedly throughout the game in sidequests and even by some of the main characters. It’s different when little kids make unwise decisions due to their inexperience and naivety, but grown-a$$ adults doing completely nonsensical or downright dumba$$ things is a weak excuse to further a plot point. The most common example is an adult character running off into a dungeon by themselves for whatever reason despite having no fighting skills; it’s like they have no sense of self-preservation whatsoever and that’s horribly unrealistic. What you need to take away from this review:  The most common reason for negative reviews for this game was people b!tching about wanting one genre and not the other. You have to be a fan of both JRPGs and farming sims or you won’t have a good time with this game. Understandably, people get cautious about getting hybrid games because a lot of times they're poorly designed. I feel like this is  an example of that. I feel both genres were integrated very well for this game. Everything unfolds at steady pace for more casual gamers to adjust to JRPG elements, if they’re unfamiliar. The only issue might be the difficulty of combat, but otherwise, I definitely recommend this game to people who enjoy both genres.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite a slow start, not quite being the farming sim on the box, and clear budgetary constraints, Harvestella manages to be more than the sum of its parts, making for one of the most unique, moving and interesting JRPG experiences I’ve had in recent memory. If you like stuff like Nier/Automata’s worldview and environmental ‘feel’, with writing that feels like it could at times be by Yoko Taro crossed with Kojima, phenomenally atmospheric music with elaborate battle themes, Persona-style social links, Xenoblade-esque extensive intertwining character side quests, Virtue’s Last Reward/999-style asides and exposition, 13 Sentinels-style  sci-fi themes, Rune Factory-lite farming mechanics, hack and slash dungeon crawling with pretty decent light puzzle mechanics, please give this a shot, or at least wishlist it for a sale. It’s the sort of game which would have probably been lauded as a truly one of kind 3DS or PS2 era title. Unfortunately, the $60 price tag and being a Switch port (and square seemingly just not sending out review codes) I suspect led to a lot of people glossing over it, and the direct comparisons to farm/sim contemporaries don’t really do it a lot of favors especially early on. After completion I would have easily paid $60 had I not been apprehensive about the quality, but for most the $40 price point is probably better.Just a really genuinely special game with some rough edges and a lot of heart.

I like being able to fight and change jobs and being in for the long haul with options of how to play when I sit down. A big part of these life sims for me is the story and romantic aspects which I haven't gotten to, so we'll see, but so far, I'm enjoying this as a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic JRPG + Farming Sim. Coming from FFXIV and Stardew-like games, I wasn't sure if I'd like a game like this. However, it's absolutely amazing. Please, do not let the *mixed* reviews bug you, almost none of them are from people who have gotten past the tutorial chapters.The game really opens up after Chapter 2-3, and my pesonal to-do list in the game is a mile long. :DSome of the pros:+ Love love love the characters thus far. They feel pretty fleshed out and real, once you get to know them. Dialogue is a bit cheesy sometimes but I don't mind it.+ The sidequests with townsfolk are pretty enjoyable. A comfy mix of humor and Trauma, along with decent rewards for doing so.+ Big fan of certain QoL things, like being able to pull crafting/cooking materials directly from your storage instead of needing them on your person, or not having to stand still while watering crops. Makes the farming/crafting aspect feel a lot more fluid.+ The classes are fun and I can see the FF bleeding into the class flavor. Haven't had a chance to play everything, but I really like the Mage and the Pilgrim.+ The collectible systems really start to pop up as you complete Chapter 3. Very Happy. Dopamine go brr.+ The simple fishing minigame is a nice break from the hell of Stardew fishing. Put the rod in, wait, pull it in and get a fish. Is it basically just a loot box? Yes, but it's chill gameplay. + The world map is explorable and also has little secrets! I won't spoil but there is more there than just the big stuff, but that comes later. :)+ The actual farmsim part is on par with Stardew. Not sure what the in-game will look like, but the plants, season rotations, daily maintenance, sprinklers, etc., are on-par with other games in that vein.+ The music is stellar. Every bit as awesome as one would expect. + I like the character art in dialogue.Now, the cons:- Not much character customization. Hair color, eye color, and gender [male, female, nb]. I'm personally okay with the options, but you may want more.- Your outfit is fixed. Apparently this is normal in many JRPG games [and other SE games]. Hopefully they add this in some capacity later? Each job/class *does* have different outfits, but you always revert to the default when you're not in combat areas [like dungeons]. This can be a bit jarring when you first start.- I think menus and inventory management could use a bit more love, but it's not *super* lacking. Definitely something that I think will improve with time, provided the game receives updates after launch.- The combat can feel a bit samey sometimes, but the boss fights are very cool and very much feel like ff encounters (down to the aoe markers, lol).Overall, I very much recommend this game. I find it worth the $60 price tag, but ymmv. Worst case, wait until a Winter sale and grab it then, you won't be disappointed. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Its a cozy JRPG with some farming attached to it. The focus is on the rpg side more so than the farming side.Stories for NPCs are told via sidequest and so far i have enjoyed them all. Most of them are chain quests actually. The farming aspect is more on the simple side but at least i was never pressed for time or have i ever run out of stamina. The main story so far is very well told and the music is really good! Personally i love the art direction however it is a switch game and it shows. considering the time i invested and still going to invest i feel it was worth the money. There is a lot of content for players available if one gets past the first 2 or 3 hours. I think ppl that liked older harvest moon games or prefer a more story focused title with sim elemants will enjoy what harvestalla has to offer.Edit after 30ish hours:If you are over the age of 30 and crave a good old fashioned JRPG think 90s early 20s, this is it. Seriously, the story is so well done, the side quests are so well done, the characters are so well done. This is by far the most Jrpg or the Jrpgs that i played in the last 3-4 years. Think of the farming as a fun side activity that you can spend hours with (such as chocobo breeding) or just spend enough time to get money and health potions (drinks). Its really is the JRPG side where the game really really shines.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally make reviews before finishing the game, but there has been a lot of negativity in some reviews and in the discussions, so I wanted to give you an idea of why I am so addicted to Harvestella.Background: I like JRPGs and Farming sims, but I can be rather critical of poor ones, which seem to float around more recently.Pros:+Great balance between quests, adventure, and farming+The story (even small characters) really shines+The world thus far oozes with personality+Well stylized art+Fantastic sound track+Pretty well thought out character progressionCons:-Mediocre Switch port (lack of quality settings, graphical limitations, controls)-Combat is rather simplistic (though still good for farming sims)-Farm is not fully customizable "Cons" I have read people say that I don't think are issues:~Can't manually save until a couple days in (saving at night early on is more than sufficient)~Lack of character customization (Never super appealed to me and I'm used to Harvest Moon/ Story of Seasons, with no options)~Mediocre game for 60$ (Console games go for 60$ for over a decade, if you can't afford games, wait for a sale)Overall, the simple yet rich story from all of the characters really gives this game a charm. Mechanically, it isn't perfect. The combat gets kinda spammy and some of the animations take too long, but the FFXIV AOE circle dodging is fun. The combat is better than Rune Factory imho. The farming is also solid and the events with the main characters are what I always wanted from a farming sim. Basically, this game isn't perfect, but it is a beautiful, well written, and fun farming adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: So, very early impressions, but here are my thoughts for anyone who is thinking about buying now...TLDR: Good game, it appears to have been developed primarily by Live Wire, not SE (Live Wire is a more indie team, 11-50 employees, solid track record though) so don't expect a triple-A title. If you're not a hardcore fan of JRPGs and farming/life-sim type games, wait for a sale ($30 would be reasonable value imo).For any who want details, so far, this feels like a very good game, best production values I've seen in farm/life sim games, and its most directly comparable to Runefactory. The game looks great, the music is great, and the combat is probably the best I've experienced in the genre. Unfortunately, the game has very little voice acting, not sure I've heard anything outside of combat/exploration, and I'm unimpressed with the English voice over. I'm still early into the story, but I like what I've seen so far, its more typical of a JRPG than a farming life sim (disclaimer: I'm a fan of that). So, we've gotten a well developed fantasy world with lore, factions, and interesting party characters. Unfortunately, the more minor NPC's are generally underdeveloped compared to something like Runefactory or Stardew (nameless npcs, reused models, no backstorys, etc). I'd say Harvestella builds a more interesting world, and Stardew builds a more interesting community, imo.As for the farming gameplay, I'm still making up my mind on that. At this point it feels workable, nothing special compared to something like Stardew, but deeper than what I saw in Rune Factory 5. I'm not far into the game, so I'm very open to my opinion changing.It's also overpriced at $60, Square Enix and farm/life sim fans like myself will probably get $60 worth out of it, but for anyone else, I'd say wait for it to go on sale for like $30/40. Don't expect a triple-A title with this one, it wasn't actually developed by SE, but by Live Wire, an indie dev known for Ender lilies. That said, this game feels more like a double-A title (SE may have pitched in on development), but still has probably the best overall production values and writing I've seen in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've put a good 30 hours into this game and honestly, it's nothing special? I love games like Harvest Moon and Stardew Valley, and I love Final Fantasy, but this attempt at making a hybrid just comes off flat. It feels like two mediocre games merged into one, except even they are quite simple.The farming side is basic. Just two animals you can add to your farm, basic upgrades and crops you can unlock. It feels separate from the RPG side except for the food you can craft that can heal you or provide buffs in combat, but even that could be replaced with basic potions. The JRPG side has a generic storyline with generic characters and terrible writing. There are job classes, but these are again basic with just a few special moves. The combat itself is a button mash. The side characters and 'romance' questions are boring. The farming and JRPG side just don't complement each other at all.The whole game feels cheap and rushed. Parts of the game haven't even been translated properly. There's no animations for actions like mining. I really WANTED to like this game, but 30 hours in, I can't be bothered to see it through to completion. If you're really curious about this one, now's the time to try it while it's on sale. It's not worth full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I need a 'Maybe' option to go with the Yes/No on recommendations. I like this game, but I'm not gonna lie - I did expect more, somehow. - You will have a slow start - every farming sim I have ever played is a slow start. So it takes time to get more seeds, expand your farm's capabilities, etc. Some upgrades are tied very much to the main storyline, so getting that upgrade on watering, or the ability to destroy those larger rocks? Painfully slow. - Character creation seems very limited. I'm not sure anything would change with the gender selection, TBH.- The intricate cutscenes you usually get from Square aren't here. Ditto voice acting.- Developing character relationships - again, just not quite the depth you'd want, very scripted. It feels like it leans a bit more towards visual novel, but less options.But... I am enjoying working my way through the storyline, trying to figure out the secrets behind the Seaslight, Quietus, etc. I've got the three Seaslights done, waiting to see what's next as there's been a fair but of foreshadowing. And typically, I pick up farming sims as pleasant timewasters - they're usually kind of relaxed, low-key, repetitive. It has got that chill, stress-relieving aspect. And the artwork is pretty.So my overall opinion? It's not bad, but it is limited, and they could have done better. If you want a farming sim with a mysterious backstory, go ahead. If you're after the sort of JRPG that wows you with its intricate gameplay, don't pick this one. And either way? Maybe wait for the price to go down. I would be more put out if this game hadn't been a Christmas gift.

_childDocuments_.review: Comment the first:  Play this game with a controller, not M&K. If you're not used to Switch controls, there's an option to switch cancel/confirm, and it will fix the issue you will otherwise have. If you are a fan of slice of life / farming / japanese rpgs (all 3. you must like all 3.), you will probably love this game. I love this game. This is not Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley, or Rune Factory. It is in the same genre as those games, but it is definitely its own beast. Does spending about a half hour doing a quest that's mostly just talking to people (in which you reconcile a father and his teenage daughter after a fight over what she's going to do with her life) sound like a good time? (This quest does not exist; it is an example and about on the same level as a fair number of quests.) To me? Yes, yes, yes, yes, yes it does. But I recognize not everyone shares that opinion. The farming loop is good; the mechanics of farming itself aren't tedious. Combat is action-RPG, you don't control your party members, player skill comes in in choosing the proper job/ability for the enemy in front of you. A couple of the boss fights are pretty novel, but the mechanics are easy to figure out. The puzzles are easy but not braindead. The story is better than anything I've played in the genre, by far hands down no question, but it isn't as good as your pure-RPG with a story focus might be. It's good, I love it, but it's pretty cliche and a lot of the story time is padded out with REALLY mundane slice of life stuff (which I enjoy). If "love and the power of friendship saves the world" isn't your jam, give it a pass. If you're looking for cozy and heartwarming and good-cry (my first tears appeared at about the twenty minute mark), you will disappear into this game and nobody will ever see you again.If you enjoy the genre, it's a good entry, especially given you get like a PARTY and choices in combat and actual abilities instead of just swinging a sword. And an RPG story, even if it's not SE's best storytellers (which imnsho are those behind Endwalker, so if you hate THAT take my opinion here with a grain of salt). I mean it's a farming game what do you want.

_childDocuments_.review: I am about half way through Harvestella. When I first saw this game, I saw what looked like a fresh jrpg gaming experience so bought it almost immediately. I saw the mixed reviews others gave too. Personally I think this game is a gem. It is a classic japan gaming experience that has used time elements very well. The graphics are older school but it is lovely to look at. The gaming experience is top notch. It is a game with a combination of RPG and Farming type elements, with a world map you can actually ride a mount around on!Like other games there is the main quest line and  about 36 side quests from what I read. You must do the side quests they are stories within themselves and have had me sobbing at the stories that unfold. The game tends to be gentle in nature it is not hardcore. The rpg elements are minimal to tie in with the farming elements which are minimal too. So not difficult to master. Even though the character customization is simplified too, I dont know why anyone would want a different character to play with while playing this game, as the one given is  perfect :) I like the combat in this game it is fun and easy to master. The creatures in this game you fight are awesome and original looking by the way. The game has a day/night time element which has been done superbly in my opinion. There is 30 days that last about 20-30 minutes per day depending on what your doing. Then there is 4 different seasons (120 days) that affect what you farm and the fourth one which is winter, I have a funny feeling I cant grow normal crops due to it being winter. It will be a fun challenge to try survive without my usual crops and i like this element in games very much. Also each 30 day ends with a natural phenomenum called the quietus. This is a period where you cant function in the world properly so you have to stay housebound while it passes. You have to remember to stop farming during this period or you lose all your crops. Its like a lockdown like coronavirus lockdown was in our lives but in the game. I knew Harvestella was going to be a great game and I wasnt wrong. Even if the graphics are not superior this is a classic of a game that everyone should play. The farming is fun and not intrusive and you dont have a gigantic farm to manage so its nice to work with. Its like a toned down final fantasy game with farming as well. A new concept for me and im definitely enjoying it. The game is meant to be between 40-80 hours to complete everything unless your a speed gamer!

_childDocuments_.review: (((TL,DR: Most negative reviewers didn't get far enough to even know what they're reviewing. If you like farming/RPG hybrids like rune factory, harvest moon, or stardew, this game will probably be for you, but you're going to want a controller.)))Let's get this out of the way first. Most of the negative reviews are coming from people who couldn't wait more than 3 hours worth of playtime to complain about why it wasn't good enough. Until you complete chapter 2 (Which most negative reviewers probably didn't) The game will have you go to bed at 10pm, and hold your hand to a small extent, to which it will let go and let you stay out late into the night afterwards.Yes, the game isn't perfect, it's not a perfect Farming sim, and it's not a perfect Arpg. But the combat can be mildly challenging and also decent fun if you switch up your classes mid combat to take advantage of element types. The farming is fun, and does get better as the story progresses and you unlock the task book which will grant things like food processors, automated sprinklers, and higher levels of tool efficiency related skills. I've seen quite a few complaints about how the farming is lacking QOL features of other farming games, and as a Harvest Moon/ Rune Factory veteran I honestly don't know what they're on about as it's much more fluid than either title's previous entries from the get go. It's a simple system that works, and is fast and efficient as you don't want to invest too much time into your farm (although with latter farm expansions, you could spend the majority of an in game day tending to it)I won't try to defend the abysmal player character select choices or lack thereof, but the characters you meet along your journey are slightly above mediocre, they have stories and relationship levels, and although I'm still unsure if this game has any level of actual romance to it, the game DOES give you flirty options and some characters flirt back. Still too early on for me to know though. REGARDLESS: Even just being  "Okay." These characters are leaps and bounds more in depth than traditional farming sim games. I have enjoyed my time with a few select characters so far, and was interested enough to visit some characters further to learn more about them. The story as a whole (So far) Is not amazing, but interesting enough for me to want to learn more.I have played almost every major Japanese made/ inspired farming game in the last 20 years, and most are often very low budget, or are early access garbage. Rune Factory 5 left a particularly bad taste in my mouth. And while this game is not perfect, it hurts to see a game in this genre get so many negative reviews when it is obviously a step in the right direction and a decently well made one. you're not going to find farming sims that look, play, or sound as nice as this every day, and I'm sure some of the negatives to this game could easily be reworked in an update or mod.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually a fan of fighting-action games. Or rhythm games, despite being a musician. Hi Fi Rush combines both in a way that simply works, bringing out the best of both genres and slathering copious amounts of charm all over it, from the music, to the art direction, to the writing. Combat is clean and makes you feel like a badass when you pull off combos (which are only dependent on a few buttons; not 7 or 8 like most - the real meat is keeping your wits and deciding what to do, and keeping up with the beat). The story is unique and engaging, and there were multiple sequences I laughed out loud. If you like games, whether or not you think this one is for you, I still highly recommend you try it.THAT SAID - I do still have a couple of minor complaints, nothing experience ruining. Not all cutscenes are skippable, especially when the antagonists talk to you while you're controlling Chai (your character), which can be annoying for replayability. Not to mention audio and video can occasionally desync for some cinematics. I'm not a fan of how important using your companions is for getting higher scores, I get from a thematic standpoint this is important to highlight how much you depend on your friends, but over the course of my playtime I didn't get to a point that summoning them felt fluid while focusing on my own positioning and attacks. It feels gross that the meta often involves spamming them, it's a little discordant with the strategic intent that you need them to help with certain threats.There's also a couple of minor story beats I find a little...stupid? Most of the stupid is good. Silly, charming, hilarious. But every once in a while a character does something that doesn't make a lot of sense. It's not nearly as bad as it could be, though, and most of these instances don't require a lot of mental gymnastics to rationalize. They just feel out of place without properly leaning into the characterization they portray.The game is imperfect - so what? It's frighteningly close, much closer than most large studios achieve nowadays. I laughed out loud a few times, I actually got emotional over the ending, and I found myself enjoying a kind of experience that I don't typically take to. Hi Fi Rush benefits greatly its commitment, its passion, and its style - and I would still love it if it had a hundred more issues. It just *works*, and I will forever remember it as one of my favorite titles. So yeah - give it a try :>

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 Masterpiece!This game is amazing. It was shadow-dropped at the same day it was anounced.When it came out, it only cost €30. On sale, you can get it for less than €20 which is fine. You know, most games these days cost 70-80€. And these games (not all, but most) are lifeless, boring and stuffed with microtransactions. Plus, you're forced to be online, and if the servers go down, you're doomed. (Basically, you're throwing your money out the window and wasting your time too).So it's great that there are developers still making full single-player games these days. And it doesn't have to be a high budget game. As long as the game is fun, that's the most important thing.The soundtracks, gameplay, story and locations are fantastic. The characters are also funny and amazing.I think this cel-shaded art style looks cool (That's why I bought the game, Lmao. You got my attention. XD) and I would love to see more games like this in the future. It's a refreshing change from these hyper-realistic games. It feels like I'm watching a western animated series (there are also a few references to well-known anime and cartoons). It's also not a normal hack-and-slash game like any other. It's also challenging because you are rewarded more if you attack the enemies to the rhythm of the music.Overall:Anyway, this game is really fun and it's great to support games like this that come out without announcements (like showing fake trailers that look different than the final product, usually a downgrade) or rumors/leaks (where many people post misinformation and have high expectations, only to end up disappointed and upset). So, I want to thank Bethesda for releasing this game on Steam, Bethesda. I really hope you release a sequel to this game. ^^

_childDocuments_.review: I can honestly say I haven't played a game as good as Hi-Fi Rush in years.The game oozes charm. Everything moves to the beat, whether that's you, the enemies, obstacles, or just stripes of paint on the walls.Just dashing to the beat in each level feels so satisfying. I rarely play rhythm games, so I expected to beef it hard, but it's almost impossible not to tap your toes to the beat each level.The story isn't bad either.Greedy corporation wants to use AI to take over the world. Gee, hit a little too close to home for anyone else?Characters are funny and witty, kind a reminds me of a Marvel movie if it didn't take itself too seriously.Lots of meta humor, jokes about if the main character were to star in a video game, stuff about their character tropes being too on the nose. It's stuff I'd normally find a little "meh" but for some reason, it all just seems to work in the world they've set up.The music is phenomenal, both the licensed tracks and the original score.Combat feels great and since everything's on beat even advanced combos and parries feel easy and satisfying to hit.Pick this one up. I can honestly say I feel more like myself since I've played it.The world just seems brighter somehow.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi-Fi Rush is a stylish, energetic, joyous blast of a video game. This surprise hit from Tango Gameworks takes on the concept of a rhythm spectacle fighter and masterfully executes it. It's just plain fun to pull off flashy moves to demolish your foes, all in sync with the music. The only con I have is the platforming can be annoying at times, but that's a very minor flaw. Otherwise, this is one of those games with so much passion and creativity poured into every part of it that it's extremely hard not to love.The game is also very newbie-friendly. Combos aren't very long or complex, there are many visual indicators to help you sync with the rhythm, and you aren't punished for being off-beat, instead you're rewarded for good timing. This is greatly appreciated, as I am not very good at rhythm games or spectacle fighters, yet it was easy for me to get into a groove with Hi-Fi Rush.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastically crafted game.The levels are bright and colourful with lots to explore. Combat is very fun, with lots of options, high skill ceiling and so much cool stuff to do. The enemy variety is just right with a large cast of fodder, leader and boss enemies all with their own own mechanics. It reminds Kingdom Hearts two with the over-the-top action and spectacle.The story is very fun with a fun cast of over-the-top characters, jojo references and humour. It reminded me of the cartoons I watched as a kid like Jackie Chan Adventures or American Dragon in the best possible way.Oh and if you're a fan of rock you'll love this game, the soundtrack is great with a mix of some popular tracks and original soundtracks. There is also a bunch of post game content that I haven't finished yet.All in all, this is an absolutely amazing game.Edit:Being 40 hours into the game now I think I should highlight the few cons I have with this game.- The platforming is a bit janky, Chai doesn't really have any air mobility so you will regularly find your self missing very short jumps unless you double jump (at which point you risk overshooting).- The progression was a bit weird, I hadn't unlocked all the combos/abilities by the end of my first playthrough which to me is odd. (For clarity had about 70% of the combos and 3 specials)- There is a lot of unskippable dialogue/tutorials. There should be more options to skip scenes and tutorials you have already seen. - Rhythm Master difficulty has this tiny issue where the meter stats half-way down rank C each fight, which results in RNG situations where where you're fighting shielded enemies and have to hope that they attack in the first 2 seconds so you can parry them, otherwise you instantly lose the fight.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, buckle up, music lovers, 'cause "Hi-Fi RUSH" is about to take you on a wild ride through sound town! This game is like your favorite mixtape come to life, with beats that'll make your head spin and visuals that'll blow your mind.First off, let's talk vibes. "Hi-Fi RUSH" is all about the music, and oh boy, does it deliver. From electronic bangers to chill beats, every track is a journey through sonic bliss. The gameplay is simple yet addictive—just tap to the rhythm and ride the waves of sound like a pro DJ.Visually, this game is a feast for the eyes. Neon lights, pulsing colors, and trippy effects come together to create a sensory explosion that'll leave you craving more. It's like being at a rave without ever leaving your couch.But it's not all about the tunes and visuals—there's a surprising amount of depth here too. With different levels to conquer and challenges to beat, "Hi-Fi RUSH" keeps you coming back for more, striving to reach that perfect score and unlock new tracks.So, if you're looking for a game that's as hip as your favorite vinyl collection, look no further than "Hi-Fi RUSH." It's the ultimate fusion of music, style, and pure fun. Turn up the volume and let the rush begin! 🎶🎮

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game; 9/10+ Fantastic, colorful, dynamic art style & animation+ Engaging and unique rhythm based combat+ Banging soundtrack+ Solid difficulty and pacing, especially at higher difficulty levels+ Actually well placed quicktime sections* Not too long* Totally linear* Not especially replayable for the average player* Passable character writing- Platforming is sluggish and takes getting used to; judging depth is difficult at times- Story is a bit cliche and wasn't very engaging to me- Combat can devolve into repetitive optimal strategies of repeating the same combos over and over- Parrying is very op; just mashing the button in time with the beat will block 90% of attacks from fodder and most larger enemiesNot perfect, but very close to it as far as games go. The gameplay might need some balance tweaking, and the platforming some general improvements to feel and momentum. But otherwise, very much worth your time, especially given how short and densely packed of an experience it is.

_childDocuments_.review: My game play time of 10 hours is what it took me to go through the campaign on Normal while focusing on collecting, with no post-game play.Not only is the game play absolute fire, the humor is the best! Reminds me of Borderlands kind of humor, but with its own style. I found myself chuckling quite a bit, and all the characters were very thoughtfully made. Performing combos will get a crowd to cheer for you, making the combat and music even more enticing! There was a healthy balance of combat, platforming, and rhythm sections. There is also post-game work to do. My only complaint is that outfits unlock only at the end of the game for post-game use. It's nice in that you're invigorated with a fresh look, but I personally would have liked to customize a bit earlier.The only warning I have: Your head will start to bob without you knowing it while you play. You probably won't realize it until you leave the game and you sit there for a second still bobbing your head. If you have a loved one next to you, they are not immune and will also start to bob. As I type, I'm reminded of the rhythm and am back to head bobbing. You've been warned.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. If you like 3D hack-and-slash games and like rhythm games, this one is probably for you. Even if you have terrible rhythm (like me), you'll probably still enjoy it. The main mechanic is to hit enemies on the beat of the music of the game, which is excellent, by the way. Between fights I'd be bobbing my head to the music, and during fights I was pumped.The art is in such a refreshing style and I love it. The story is long enough that you can feel satisfied, but not so long that it overstays its welcome. Most of the characters are pretty memorable and enjoyable to fight against.I think the only thing that I disliked is that certain parts of the game required split-second precision to progress. However, I felt the game doesn't punish you too harshly when you fail. Overall, this game that dropped out of nowhere definitely earned its accolades.

_childDocuments_.review: Have not played much, but so far the visuals and gameplay are winning over the few negatives, and those negatives don't apply to everyone. They are:1: Character customization doesn't unlock until AFTER you complete the game. I understand this is sort of like a Streets of Rage system where they intend people to go back and replay the levels once complete to try and get higher scores or find new things, but I am willing to bet for most people the game will be a one and done, so not letting them do customization until after the game is complete is weird. (this is even with Dthe Deluxe version, where aft er the first stage you can change clothing items from what you get out of the Deluxe stuff, but the rest of the customizations available in the game still seem to be locked until completion)2. Not a gripe for most people, but while the game supports Ultrawide in gameplay, it does not in cutscenes. I know it CAN do UW in cutscenes since you can HEX edit the EXE file to allow it or use the UuuClient to force it, but if those ways allow for it and the game works fine with it, then it should be in by default.3. Might just be a game design thing, but jumping feels weird because you seem to lose al forward momentum as soon as you reach the apex of the jump, and just drop straight down. There is a double jump and air dash you can use for movement and platforming, but it still feels really off to just halt your forward momentum at the height of a forward jump, which has messed with my head a few times and made me miss some jumps.Other than that though, so far it's really fun, and as I said, those 3 complaints won't apply to most people and aren't enough to keep me from recommending the game.UPDATE: Love the combat, HAAAAAAAAAAATE the platforming, mostly because of how wonky the jumping is with it's lack of forward momentum. That coupled with the camera makes it more difficult than it should be to judge jumps.UPDATE 2: I still dislike the platforming and still like the combat. I found that fully maxing the controller sensitivity makes the game feel better because I felt the camera rotation was just too slow by default. Also, I am annoyed by how much screen tearing there is in cutscenes even when I try to mitigate it with V-Sync, Freesync or a combination of both. And despite running at a locked 141 fps (it's easy to run, have my game capped at 3 fps lower than my refresh rate), possibly because of the animation style, the game just doesn't always look completely smooth.UPDATE 3: It's been weeks and I haven't been able to get myself to play further. I think that I enjoy the platforming and moving through the levels so little it's not enough to get me to play it more... Keeping it as a recommend because I know it's a good game, even though I don't know if I personally will ever care enough to keep playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game slaps.It's a hack-and-slash where instead of hacking and slashing you're bashing robots over the head with a guitar to the beat of an absolute banger soundtrack of licensed and original music (though there is a streamer mode with just the original music).It's a short romp (10ish hours if you're just playing the campaign and not doing post-game stuff) that is short enough to introduce new mechanics so it never feels "samey".It offers a challenge with combat that makes you feel powerful when you get into a flow state with the beat. It has consistently fantastic boss fights, all of which are unique in their own way. The final boss is damn difficult too.The characters are likable, and you see how they develop as individuals, teammates, and friends.It has puns, visual gags, physical comedy, callback jokes, and an overall light-hearted tone, albeit with realistic and serious stakes in the fairly straightforward storyline. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Hi-Fi Rush is one of, if not the best new game released by a big studio I've played in nearly 10 years. It's a rhythm hack-and-slash game with aesthetics and writing that reminds me of videogames and cartoons from the pre-2010s, and that statement may be an insult coming from some, but from me it's one of the highest compliments I can give anything in the entertainment space.i felt like this could have come out in like 2003-2005 on the PS2 and it would have fit right in. The fact it came out in 2023 shows me that the old-school style not only still works, but is still remembered fondly by at least someone in the industry who knows how to recreate it. And words cannot describe how thankful I am for that.The story is pretty dang good for what it is. It's not trying to be this super-serious story like Last of Us, God of War, CoD, etc., instead it goes for a more goofy cartoony and honestly just fun style that has really felt like a lost art form for the better part of 10 years. Like, I've seen plenty of games and films attempt it since 2013, but very few of them hit the nail on the head as they instead go for some new style of cartoony that... most of the time just feels bland and boring in comparison. This game feels very much alive and kicking. And by the way, the soundtrack is awesome and if there's any chance of that getting a store page on Steam, I need to know about it immediately.The gameplay is also pretty dang smooth. Like maybe Devil May Cry smooth. The fact that I can screw up the timing and still play is a godsend for an action-focused game such as this, and there are a few cases where I wish other action-rhythm games did the same. And thankfully, there's still an incentive to try to match the beat as doing so will cause enemies to sometimes drop health pickups or energy pickups during combat, which is a great counterbalance to removing the punishment for being off-beat.Now, when I played I only encountered one or two bugs, the main one I found was on the first level when you take the second "shortcut" the camera became stuck in place while my character was not, so I had to back out to the main menu and restart from last checkpoint to progress. It worked fine since then.Hi-Fi Rush is a masterpiece, a modern classic, and definitely a contender for my GOTY 2023. I never could have expected a magnificent game like this to come out when every other company just pushes out the same boring overdone hyper-realistic hyper-linear hyper-monetized overly-politicized creatively-bankrupt criminally-underpolished crap to add to the monotonous gray hodgepodge that is currently the AAA game industry. The industry should take some notes from Hi-Fi Rush, honestly.
_childDocuments_.name: Hi-Fi RUSH

_childDocuments_.review: Hi-Fi Rush is a delightful game made with a lot of heart. The story is straight-forward and lighthearted with a few emotional beats sprinkled in towards the end. The writing is standard fare: female characters are perfect, men are idiots, but it is written such that it isn't grating. Gameplay is simple without being simplistic and leaves a lot of room for skill expression. The game's art style and visual direction for both gameplay and cutscenes is a breath of fresh air in the earth-toned landscape contemporary design is stuck in. Characters move fluidly and expressively with a lot of personality. The vocal performances in English are outstanding, There were very few bugs, and those that I encountered while playing were introduced in the latest patch. Once, my character was shoved out of the combat area and could not return inside which bugged the rest of the enemies for the remainder of the tower-up arcade mode. Second, the completionist achievement would not unlock despite having completed all challenges and content for the game.  Beyond these two very minor inconveniences, the game is extremely well polished.In all, I would definitely recommend this little gem. Easily one of the best titles published by Bethesda. Tango Gameworks made a winner with this one and deserve all the praise in the world for it.

_childDocuments_.review: On paper, a game that mashes rhythm gameplay with stylish hack and slash like DMC and Bayonetta wouldn't have got my attention. The game doesn't punish you for missing attacks on the beat, but the once the beat clicks, it makes combat feel very fluid and fun.The game feels alot more approachable than Bayonetta and DMC due to the concept of everything moving to the beat as this makes timing dodges, parries and attacks very manageable. The game also provides tons of visual cues and aids to help you keep in time with the beat. That being said, alot of the latter levels and fights pretty much demand you have a decent sense of rhthym. The story is pretty straightforward but that's fine. The game has a very charming setting and characters which make it a fun experience and the game doesn't take itself seriously. Just have fun and enjoy the ride.I think my only real criticism is the lack of a proper lock-on feature. The game is largely fine without it but there are a handful of battles where I really wished it was an option.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic from start to finish. While I experienced some launch week bugs, the game was so fun that I ran back my lost progress and enjoyed it just as much on the second playthrough.Comparisons to another recent rhythm platformer, No Straight Roads, are apt here. Once again, gameplay is on cue to the beat, the soundtrack is killer, and puns and references abound to carry a coming-of-age story against a fortified megacorp that you break down boss by boss. But that's mostly where the comparison ends: while NSR was more of a cooperative Jet Set Radio-infused platformer, HFR is a focused single-player experience that draws comparisons to Ratchet & Clank and much earlier titles like Comix Zone or Viewtiful Joe's cell-shaded-and-dithered visual style.HFR is also mostly on the rails from start to finish, with minimal exploration to speak of even in postgame. Carrying the experience instead is absurdly good writing, great music, extremely satisfying combat, and a cast of charming characters that would fit right into a Persona game. The standard gamut of upgrades to health, special, combo enablers, and buffs round out the typical 3rd person action loop in a satisfying way without distracting from gameplay. Accessibility options, well-demonstrated gameplay features, optional tutorials, and the ability to continue playing at any of the game's generous checkpoints are also extremely appreciated on week one of launch.And, most importantly, the beat-based combat is crisp and feels great. It feels a little stiff at first even on controller, but more options open up to weave in combos, dashes, parries, specials, and support abilities. All of which build into a satisfying mixture of activity that remains challenging without becoming overwhelming on both the player and the game's own engine.My only complaint other than week-one bugs is that some of the later encounters contain telegraphs and context cues that fall a little flat and are difficult to read on a first attempt. I hit the game over screen more than a few times because a mechanic or expected action simply wasn't visible to me, though the generous checkpointing and continue system let me figure these situations out quickly.Overall: on a first play, expect good fun for about 10-15 hours, which for the price of admission and quality of gameplay on offer, is worth it.Edit to add: RIP Tango Gameworks. Wish y'all the very best on what you do next. <3

_childDocuments_.review: It's Ratchet and Clank meets rhythm combat, to the extent that you're collecting gears from items you smash and most enemies are robots. I had to double check that this was a Bethesda Softworks IP, developed by Tango Gameworks (ZeniMax > Xbox Game Studios), what a weird and neat game to spawn from a developer known for gritty DOOM-and-gloom games.It's fantastic, while short. The game lives up to being a fun combat rhythm game. The immense attention to detail in the world and the characters, literally everything moves and fights to the beat of the music. Matching the beat during combat is really satisfying and rewarding, but at the same time punishes you for slipping off-beat. Combat happens in controlled cells that are very obvious allowing you to explore the level freely between the combat areas. Tons of secrets and hidden areas to explore, easter-eggs and comedic side-commentary from worker droids.My gripes with the game revolve around hard to complete button combos, can't really tell if you got it right. Perfectly timed enemy attacks every time you try to finish your combo. Some levels have hard to track beats or the beat is kinda lame, the track used in the final two levels was by far the best. Some combos will launch you up and over the object you're trying to attack. Some of the QTE's will drive you mad even though they're just some side objective. About half of the boss fights felt strategic using block and solid attack timing, others were just button mashing like the final boss.Note: If you're having trouble with timing, try disabling the low-latency option. As weird as it sounds I was more used to regular latency on my controller so the low-latency setting was messing me up.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game as much as anyone else (and feel like it's honestly a steal at 30 bucks). The art design is gorgeous, the characters are charming, the story is engaging, and the combat is some of the best fun I've had in a game in a very long time.But I will mention a few rough spots, because the game is not flawless:1. Platforming is clunky. I don't know if the controls just are not well suited for it, or if the cel shaded environment makes it hard to judge distance (or maybe both), but you will find yourself missing platforms way more than you should. Each time you miss a jump, the game takes a small chunk of your health and puts you back at the beginning of the segment. For one off accidents, it's not too punishing. But when you miss a jump several times in a row right before a difficult fight, it's more than a little frustrating.2. Most of the world moves to the beat of the music. This is not a complaint obviously, but it makes the fact that a few things don't do this stand out, and make for a frustrating couple minutes. My main example of this would be , which I've had to sometimes repeat 20 times in a row to get right.3. The UI was very clearly designed for use with controllers. It's still usable on PC, but there's some minor annoyances like no button mouseover indication. If you're like me, you'll end up just using WASD+E to navigate menus.The following isn't a complaint, but a PSA:  Despite the bright and cheerful appearance, combat can be pretty punishing. I'm no novice to rhythm or action games, but even on normal difficulty, some of the later fights required multiple repeats to get through.

_childDocuments_.review: Really neat gameplay concept that makes me realise gitaroo man should of received a sequel. The game does suffer from some boring writing, however i did enjoy the characters that you meet and join your group later on into the game.As for the game itself, i enjoyed it. Im a big fan for action games and it was nice to see something involve a new style and put rhythm into the mix, as mentioned before one of my very beloved games gitaroo man which was a rhythm game back on the PS2 followed very similar ideas that this game shares, its almost as if the game was taken as inspiration at parts.The whole style of this game, the vibrant and expressive characters, and the great level design make this a game a nod towards previous rhythm games that have come in the past that should be revisited. For an action game it doesn't equal to capcom or bayonetta level of combat but its enjoyable with the addition of trying to stay in sync with the music to reach higher score points and fun with staying in flow with the beat playing.My least favourite part of the game being the platforming and that seemingly feeling a bit janky and weird at times where i would find myself overjudging or propelling myself in the complete wrong direction when trying to climb up to the next area. I'm not sure if I wanted the same thing but with faster, more intense music, or the same thing but with a more compelling narrative.If the developers of gitaroo man ever find me, please take into consideration that more rhythm games should be made.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi-Fi Rush is a proper joy to play all the way through, no strings attached . It is a *damn* fun game, that wears its genre and medium with pride - it is a videogame-ass videogame that feels like developers from the PS2 and GameCube era were plucked from the past and made to make a game today. Which is at least half-true, as Tango Gameworks is comprised of ex-Clover and PlatinumGames employees. One of the finest Character Action games out there, the combo depth is insane. Chai practically plays like Nero from DMC4/5, and Tango's DNA comes through strong. Never gets too overwhelming though, game does a very good job teaching its mechanics without being too handholdy. Game trickles plenty of new and exciting things over its runtime, and it all blends very well together. Enemy variety is good, no one battle feels the same. Minor complaints: the lack of a "reset camera behind player" button can get annoying in platforming segments. The lack of a dedicated lock-on button is annoying (especially for Devil May Cry and Bayonetta veterans), but there aren't any directional inputs and the auto lock on swing feels pretty accurate, so you can get by without one. It feels a little too easy to maintain an S combo rating and not as satisfying as you'd hope - double and triple S ratings would be appreciated, or make the S combo rank harder to hit and maintain. The lack of a taunt button isn't really an issue, but having one would be pretty on brand for this game, and especially for Chai :)Slightly more major complaint: Higher difficulties aren't meaningfully different from lower difficulties, just tighter rhythm timing, higher enemy HP, and enemies do more damage. Wave compositions and enemy behavior isn't any different, and boss movesets remain the same, so replays on different difficulties can get repetitive.That aside, Hi-Fi Rush is a fantastic game, and we need more of it, and of AA cheaper games in general. Must play.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute delight from start the finish.Featuring great style, and refreshing blend of action and rhythm gameplay, I have a fair bit to mention here.Starting off with the+++Positives+++EVERYTHING, is tied to the beat and rhythm of the game!Character animations, platforming, combat, the option to go off-beat exists but it's nowhere near as rewarding or efficient.It's also surprisingly easy to get into, having enough destructible objects laying around means you're practising attacks in some form, and stretches of land mean you're most likely dashing in rhythm to go from point A to point B faster.Besides rankings and slower animations, there's no real downside in messing up the beat too much either, it's very friendly but rewarding to master.The style of this game is just a delight.Striking comic book aesthetics to accompany a goofy adventure with fun characters, followed with humour that actually gets a good chuckle out of me quite often, it's just fun!The music, while pretty good, actually goes a step further with streamer mode.Streamer mode gets rid of any licensed songs and replaces them with new OST, and in a lot of cases I think these songs work way better.And at half the cost of a standard AAA game, I have no reason to say you shouldn't buy this at full price.Game's a bargain as is, lasting roughly 10+ hours, and it's mostly just all quality stuff.Now onto the---Negatives---The enemies covered in armour are anti-fun.They require an ability to get rid off their armour, but usually it takes multiple hits to get rid of it before you can actually deal any damage.The problem is that this ability without any upgrades, is kinda a bit long, and once you get rid off the the armour, the enemies themselves are usually nothing special.Not bad, just not great either.Having the option to replay stages after beating them would've also been nice, but you have to beat the game to do this.I get why, as there is some post-game content, and new side areas you couldn't get to your first time through, but all the same I would still like to be able to go back.And finally, my last complaint is related to one of the last few stages so this'll be a minor spoiler but not enough to make me say "avoid this".>>>Conclusion<<<Hi-Fi Rush is a game that I found to be an absolute delight and one I'd highly recommend to others.Even if you don't think you'd like rhythm games, I still recommend you keep an eye on this, the game really does do a good job of getting you into things.Just a whole lot of fun and well worth your money.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been an absolute gem. Combat with mechanical depth for it to challenge if you want to be a master, and becoming quick and snappy once you have hit the rhythm and flow state, combined with a colourful and easily enjoyable cast of characters (even the villains. Very easy to love for different reasons). The story, while not breaking new ground, never needed to as the depth of the story is in the characters, and it tells a beautiful tale of growth, acceptance, redemption, and culminates with a splendid emotional payoff and a glee-inducing final confrontation. The soundtrack (as you would hope for a game about rhythm matching) is filled with fantastic head bopping and foot tapping songs, which are accompanied by well made and satisfying audio responses with on beat actions. Tight writing with quippy and fun dialogue crowns this experience, with slight small details producing a whole that is more than the sum of these small parts. I implore you to always be on the lookout for small details, both visually and audibly.Even if you cannot keep a rhythm, they give constant visual hints and clues on how to maintain on time, and if all else fails then there's the option for a non-intrusive beat keeper that gives a much easier to follow cue. If you approach this game impatiently, you may not get as much out of it, as it is no button masher like most hack and slash titles. It runs on a combo system, but patience and forethought can get you so far.Would recommend to anyone and everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Seriously, I say this as someone who hasn't liked previous action games they've played in some parts due to my inexperience and other parts the games themselves, but this game? This game that combines rhythm and stylish hack and slash combat nails the experience of an action game? Perfection from two seemingly unrelated sides that end up making quite the pretty coin. Game brings the difficulty and high score systems both genres are well known for and blends them together into this addicting experience that rewards the player for getting better and better at it's mechanics; both with big numbers AND significant cool factor. Even beyond the amazing gameplay, the game's story, set pieces, visuals, and of course the music are all top notch. With a style that feels reminiscent of a time when developers opted to make unique and stunning looks before it got washed away in a hyper-fixation on realism that has caused so many games to become dated by today's standards. Top it off with a simple, yet effective story that knows what it's trying to do and does it well. There's no grand morale to be gain here, just lovable characters, beautifully hate-able bosses, and plenty of funny side characters all over. This is the kind of game people will be talking about in 10 years time for being a diamond in the sea of rough sea of mediocre game launches of the past year or so.All of that said I did have a FEW moments of frustration. Certain enemy types in the mid to late game tilt a little too hard to the side of threatening and become flat out annoying with a lot of your options being made suddenly very limited and is only made worse by the game occasionally throwing something completely new at you that is just plain painful (Something that became VERY apparent in Track 8, Chorus 9). Combine this with a admittedly lackluster customization system that feel less "Pick your playstyle" and more "Here's a set to make ONE thing of your build Crazy strong" given that your skills can take up to 3 of your 5 max slots to get the best version of that skill, you might find yourself with not a lot of room to really "customize." Even if you did have that room though, the game prices a lot of upgrades fairly high and don't payout enough of the Gears needed to buy them to really experiment much so if you're only going to be playing for the story and don't want to delve into post game content, then there's not going to be much to sink your teeth into. Still, everything there is but a footnote on my overall experience with the game. It's the few, tiny imperfections that come with every game, the things that you'll go "Yeah this game's great but F*** this thing in particular." In no way was anything I just said enough for me to not recommend this game. Hell it's only here to give anyone reading this some idea of where this game may fall short and hopefully bring back some reasonable expectations, since some may see the Overwhelmingly Positive reviews and think "There's gotta be something wrong with this game." If you're interested it all, it's worth your time and money. You'll get more out of it the more you stick with it and commit to the game fully, but even as a single playthrough experience, it is a breath of fresh air in this day and age. Worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally do reviews prior to beating a game, but I'll make an exception here. Hi-Fi Rush is good. Straight up good. Gameplay is Devil-May Cry meets Rhythm Game (more so than dmc5's light rhythm mechanic) with bits of jrpg storytelling mixed with classic level design you would expect to find in playstation titles like Ratchet and Clank. The core combat is extremely solid, exactly what you would expect from a hack-slash action title like a devil may cry title, where matching your attacks to the beat of soundtrack powers up and speeds up your attack animations. While for some it may be hard to get the rhythm mechanic down at first (I notoriously struggle with them) the game makes every effort to make it as easy for you as possible, from enemies attacks also timing to the rhythm (allowing you to make so slick parries and dodges once you get the beat down) to visualizing the beat throughout the level design. Certain parts of the level are ALWAYS moving to the beat of the sountrack, the protagonist snaps to the music, there are visual and audio cues when you nail the timing, you even have the option to enable a visual representation of the beat at the bottom of screen for ease of use if necessary. Now just that alone would not have sold me on the game. But it absolutely OOZES style as well. From your main weapon being a guitar, to the anime and jrpg inspired design, the beautiful color palette and a wonderfully done fully voiced dub. I don't think there is a single line of dialogue that isn't dubbed, and all of it was cast extremely well. It feels extremely fresh and nostalgic at the same time.

_childDocuments_.review: This might be the most "how do you do, fellow kids?" game I've ever played. It is aggressively obnoxious with possibly the most unlikable protagonist I can remember. The whole game is a noisy mishmash of conflicting ideas; There is constant pandering to boomers with the early 2000s aesthetics and music, combined with zoomer speak, dead memes, and dated cultural references. I feel like this was portrayed as a character action game with rhythm elements, but instead it's more like a rhythm game with free movement. While the gameplay is competent, I think I enjoyed watching the spectacle of the animated cutscenes more than actually playing the game. While the game is clearly a callback to "the good old days" of cartoony aesthetics and punky art styles, it just comes off as pandering to me. Games like Jet Set Radio and Devil May Cry worked because they were innovative on top of embracing the aesthetics and music of their time, while this game's designs and references are all over the place. Missions all use original tracks but they sound like corpo-rock background tracks which only peak when you hit S rank. This was clearly trying to emulate Devil May Cry 5's music implementation and yet none of the music come close to the rush of "Devil Trigger," instead being inoffensive and sanitized royalty free-sounding tracks. In fact, there's a streamer mode that replaces the licensed tracks used for bosses with even more of this borderline elevator music. The only memorable licensed tracks are by Nine Inch Nails and The Prodigy and yet I would've been fine with never hearing "The Perfect Drug" or "Invaders Must Die" ever again with how much they've been licensed in the past. As for the bosses, the only one I liked was the first one. Shortly after parrying is introduced, mandatory parrying sections are included in boss fights (and enraged mini-bosses in between). The worst of this is Korsica's fight, which is just a series of Simon Says QTEs. Normal rhythm games are engaging even for people who aren't musically inclined (or who don't even play video games [even my literal boomer Dad liked Guitar Hero]), because failure usually only comes from massively flopping on harder difficulties. Hi-Fi Rush instead takes the path of making mandatory Simon Says sections requiring a 100% success rate to pass that part of the fight. Maybe it was just because I was playing on Hard difficulty, but the precise timing required on top of the 100% success rate really ruined most boss fights for me.If this game was instead a strictly character action game where you could freely switch between party members, it probably would've been a GOTY nominee for me. It's a shame that your team members are regulated to assist movements, akin to a tag team fighting game, because those elements aren't integrated well either. Certain enemies require multiple assist calls to break their shield or weapon before you can even attack them, including certain bosses with really specific hitboxes. Aiming these can be a pain and usually just slowed down fights, on top of fights already being slow because of the rhythm elements. It's also really strange that they went with assists instead of swaps because there are sections where you do get to play as other characters.Hi-Fi Rush isn't a bad game but I wouldn't recommend it. The way that the character action elements are combined with the rhythm elements are like combining ramen noodles with chocolate; they're great on their own but don't mesh well together. There's occasionally memorable fights and cool animated sequences, but you have to get past the terrible protag and combat rhythm elements that ironically ruin the rhythm of the combat. I think most of the praise for this game comes from the contrast it provides with the mess that the modern video game industry is: here you have a complete game that works at launch with unlockable cosmetics, versus many modern games launching broken and still having season passes, battle passes, and cosmetic DLCs. I get what the developers were trying to do, but it feels out of place and out of time in a bad way.

_childDocuments_.review: Even if it's not perfect by any stretch, hi fi rush is a fun little rhythm action game reminiscent of combo action games like DMC and the like.The art style is a super pretty comic book style that runs as smooth as butter in gameplay, while cutscenes offer that gorgeous purposefully-low-framerate style that just makes everything pop in the most amazing way.The game is a combo action game, meaning plenty of smacking enemies all over the place with memorised combos for high scores, or alternatively using the same 2 combos over and over again and still getting an S rank.The game isn't very challenging even on hard mode, but the bosses are half difficulty spike and half bullsh!t spike. As long as you can keep the beat and mash dodge/parry, you can deal with anything the game throws at you.The writing is really marvel/borderlands, meaning that everyone is the snarky ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and there's plenty of "explain the joke as it happens" cringe. Thankfully it's not totally insufferable here, and a lot of the humor actually lands. The characters are all archetypes, but they're entertaining enough, although as a footnote a lot of the actors sound really bored with the material.The biggest flaws with the gameplay are threefold:1: The jumping is absolutely atrocious. It rockets you straight up into the air and gives you little to no distance, even with an aerial dash. Trying to do fast paced platforming (or hell, even slow paced platforming) with it is a complete and total nightmare.2: There are so many particle effects being vomited onto the screen at any given time that enemy telegraphs might as well be invisible. Trying to pick out that one tiny split-second star sticker that tells you you're about to be flattened and react to it is like trying to pick out a specific rainbow pebble in a fishtank.3: Some enemy attacks have to be parried in order to kill them, but the timing for the parry sequence doesn't gel with the stage's actual beat, and basically requires you to tune out the music for a moment to get it right.What's most disappointing though is that the music in this rhythm game isn't very memorable. Only a couple songs in the whole soundtrack really stuck out to me, and of those one was a song I've heard before, and one was a remix of a song I've heard before. Compared to other rhythm games I've played recently where the soundtrack was just bangers on top of bangers, a lot of the tracks in hi fi rush are just atmospheric grunge-rock fluff that all blends together into a smoothie of denim and stupid haircuts. Despite all that though, it's an enjoyable little romp at a decent price, especially for bethesda. It's worth it if you want a game to relax with for a few hours that's actually upbeat and colorful for a change.

_childDocuments_.review: Update for the closing of Tango:I wholeheartedly still recommend you find a way to play Hi-Fi Rush, however, if you can find a way to not pay for it, that would probably be for the best. Microsoft Games Studios is going down the drain so fast it's hard to keep track of their bad decisions. 10 years ago they used to brag about their studio acquisitions, but I guess the prize for putting out the best game they had on XBox in 2023 is to close the studio and call the whole thing a failure. TF are y'all doin' over there?------------------------------------------------I didn't like The Evil Within, which these guys made. I hated Sunset Overdrive, which this game initially reminded me of in it's release trailer. But THIS game is OUTSTANDING.It's "T for Teen" Devil May Cry with musical combat that actually works, and I've tried a fair number of musical combat games where it certainly did NOT work. Presentation goes hard, the plot is entertaining without being obnoxious (despite how it might look in the trailers), and  it takes 15 hours to get through on the first run (though replayability is high, there's more to the game after you hit the credits). Why they dropped this out of the blue and are only asking for 30 bucks is beyond me. If this is a AA game, they need to make more, and these guys need to do whatever they want for the foreseeable future. If you like beat-em-ups like DMC, Bayonetta or God of War, this one is certainly worth a shot.The surprise action hit of the year, and a firm contender for GOTY. 5 outta 5. Until I saw Shinji Mikami's name in the credits, I kept wondering why this game was giving me the same warm and fuzzy feeling as action games like Viewtiful Joe. For all you older cats who say a lot of "videogames these days..." statements, this one should already be in your library.
