_childDocuments_.review: My favourite game to be released last year. I played this on release but I'm bad at getting round to reviewing things. I'm reviewing it now in light of... recent decisions made by Microsoft, which I'll come back to.I'm a Nine Inch Nails and Black Keys fan (and what a cracking choice of a Prodigy song) so I was drawn in from the trailers and bought this on release. The animation is fantastic, with endearing character design, it has an engaging story poking fun at corporate greed while keeping it lighthearted and comedic, and a wonderful original soundtrack fitting in perfectly with the licensed music. The audio works SO WELL with the visuals, everything syncs to the beat visually (and I mean everything, industrial machinery, lights, characters), it's incredibly satisfying when you get into the rhythm and improve as you go through the game. Excellent combat design with a nice variety of combos and upgrades. The team really worked together well on this.As a side tangent, I'm a musician but only played a couple of other rhythm games before this; in a way I kind of feel like this would be great for beginner musicians getting used to the idea of rhythmic playing, at least in 4/4 haha.It's also a refreshing to have a game without micro-transactions, isn't live service, isn't a huge time-sink (not that there's anything necessarily wrong with that, but it's hard for lots of people to find the time to commit to very long games), just 10 hours or so of main playtime for the main story, but at the same time with lots of replay-ability and extra content, some of which the devs have added since release. I haven't managed to come back for the completionist on this but I really want to when I find a good time for it, I would love to get fully immersed in this again. A real throwback to a time when games didn't have in-game predatory micro-transactions and were fully complete on release. Hi-Fi Rush is clearly made by a passionate team that really care about what they're making. A shining example of how to make a successful high quality game that people really want to engage with. This model is, in many ways, what people didn't even realise they were missing in today's climate.Absolutely incredible game, 10/10.And that's where my review should end. Unfortunately, Microsoft/ XBOX don't seem to know when they have an absolute gem. In their words, Hi-Fi Rush was a "breakout hit" for them. Go to Tango Gamework's Twitter and you see them retweeting all the various awards Hi-Fi Rush has won. Matt Booty from XBOX says "we need smaller games that give us prestige and awards", the day after... _childDocuments_.review: You'll notice most reviews have only like two hours in before giving a glowing review. Well, there's a reason for that. The game starts fine with a great looking art style, amazing soundtrack, and interesting fun characters. After the first two or three stages, I too thought this was an amazing game. Then I played six more stages and felt the enthusiasm get sucked out of me. This is a game where your mileage will vary quiet a bit. If you are looking for a rhythm based simple beat'em up with light platforming elements you'll be very happy. If you are looking for a fluid exciting action game you are going to be left feeling lied to.The first design decision I really want to call out that just disrupts the flow of the game is an over reliance on partner abilities to fight enemies. Before you can interact with an enemy you need to hit them with a specific partner attack, sometimes multiple times. These partner attacks are on cool down, this means that fights often feel like you spend a decent amount of time flailing around dodging and parrying before you are actually able to engage in the fight. It's much akin to a more obnoxious version of what the Ninja Theory DMC did with the red and blue attacks. It's not hard to deal with, avoiding everyone for the opening section of a fight isn't hard, it's just a tedious chore.In fact let's address the comparisons to games like Devil May Cry and Bayonetta. The similarity is that you explore an area a bit, get locked in a combat room, and then get scored at the end of that combat room. You can also by new unlocks from the shop with gears you picked up in the stage. That's about where the comparisons end. Both DMC and Bayonetta give you access to new individual moves as well as combos, Hi-Fi Rush only gives you combos and supers. This has an unfortunate consequence of making everything you do feel rather same-y as every string starts with the same weak or heavy attack and the difference between doing most combos is string length and a slightly different ender. Some combos end in the air or do a little better job with crowd control, but by and large it feels rather lacking in variety. This simplicity was likely done to keep the rhythm game aspect simple, but it also means if you come in expecting something as rich as like Devil May Cry 5's combat system you are going to be disappointed. The game seems to be really proud of it's call and answer parry system which is this mechanic where you are locked in place and shown a series of button prompts for parrying and/or dodging. Then after it's shown what to expect the enemy lunges at you and you have to hit those buttons in a rhythm. It looks great, it plays fine enough at first, but eventually it just becomes yet another sequence that isn't very fun yet the frequency of them increase as you keep going. It all feels like just another way to have more quick time events.The ratio of chore to fun just gets worse the longer I play and at this point I feel myself checking out because I'm just not having fun. I came in expecting something more action oriented, but so many of the tedious design decisions just interrupt flow of the game and they keep getting tacked on the longer the game runs. I really wanted to like this game because it looks and sounds great, but there's no depth of combat that I usually need for these kind of things to sustain interest.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi-Fi Rush is a rhythm hack and slash. And I must put an accent on . Pretty much everything is on the rhythm. Hits you cause are on the rhythm, hits you receive are on the rhythm, environment is on the rhythm, cutscenes are on the rhythm, everything.You could think that this would be some sort of tedious design, but it actually flows really well as a game mechanic for a hack and slash, and even becomes somewhat of a meditative experience when you're in combat and trying to get the best combo.Furthermore, everything can be parried (after unlocking), you can even block magma balls and huge robot hits with no problem - as long as it's on the beat. The gameplay is the best part of the game, and if it wasn't so good, I doubt I would've managed to finish all the achievements in this game.The game also has a significant number of platforming sections. This is where I feel that the game has some issues, you have access to a double-jump and an air-dash, but the jumping mechanic doesn't feel solid, and using all the jumps and dash doesn't really feel as if it will get you too far.This game is pretty much based on soundtrack and sound design. To start with the most surprising point, this game has songs from Nine Inch Nails and The Prodigy, unsuspected, yet welcome, and other artists. But if you want to stream this game, you also have an option for a soundtrack which shouldn't get you into DMCA trouble. Which is pretty great in case you want to not have your VOD nuked.But back to the point, this game is on the beat. All the attacks, yours and the enemies', and the environment, is on the beat. Every stage has a different track, and the environment and combat will mold around it. You will see jumping bins, boards, fences, shrubs, just in rhythm with the beat. The story is linear and lacks any choices which can be done to actually affect the ending. The story itself is corny, but in the good kind of way, and the characters are varied in their own right.There is some character progression for the main character, going from a solo act to a team player, and the story itself serves the game sufficiently to also provide comedy and even dramatic moments.I 100%'d this game, and it was a complete ride. It took me about 8 hours to do one playthrough, and then I clocked in 61 hours to reach the final challenge to unlock 100%. All in all, some achievements are ridiculously difficult, and some are ridiculously tedious, and some are both. The biggest offenders are the "Don't get hit during X boss fight" achievements. There are a few of these, and in some cases, legitimately attaining this challenge would imply redoing a level completely, which can mean up to 20 minutes of gameplay extra if you rush to the boss. Furthermore, the difficulty challenges must be done individually. As in, there are 12 sets of levels and 5 difficulties. To get all the achievements, you will need to get S rank on all the difficulties, so you could be looking at doing each stage twice, at least, for each difficulty. This is where the brunt of the hours went.I thoroughly enjoyed the game, and for 30 euros, it's a solid choice. The style is amazing, the story is charming and everything just feels complete - compared to other titles in this world where you pay 60 or even 70 dollars and then you become a slave to season passes and battle passes.

_childDocuments_.review: Every aspect of this game feels like being a kid again watching Saturday morning cartoons. The art style is reminiscent of something like Ben 10 and the humour is fun. The dialogue is witty and well written, I found myself smiling almost the whole time when I played it and I surprisingly found myself caring a lot about the main cast. The story isn't that deep but is still fun and surprisingly heartfelt at times. Chai is your typical overconfident protag who has to learn how to work as a team and the crew you acquire along the way have their respective tropes but they are all still brimming with personality and I found myself loving all of them and feeling a little something when they all came together in the end for the final battles. The gameplay is also amazing, I think the best way to describe it is Devil May Cry combos mixed with a rhythm game. Its bright and colourful, but can also get really complex towards the end with its combos. It's easy enough for a casual player to pick up but has a lot of great challenge for people who may want to put in the work to master the controls. I also want to mention how effortlessly diverse the cast is. I know it might seem a bit dramatic, especially when talking about a game as lighthearted as this, but I think it is worth giving the team props for. I feel like companies often avoid diversity in their cast because they think it needs to be complex and dark but really, it can be as simple as treating your non-white characters like the rest of your cast. This games has multiple POC characters on both the hero and villain team and all of them are very distinct and memorable. The fact they aren't white isn't ever brought up in game, they are just written to be as wacky and interesting as the rest of the cast. all in all, very fun game, highly recommended.edit: F*ck you Microsoft

_childDocuments_.review: I do like much of it, but I just can't recomend it to most people. A shame, since it had great potential, and I love a lot of parts of this game, but at the end of the day.. there are also just several parts that are frankly terrible and completely ruin it and just turn some moments into pure frustration.Inputs don't work, when I started I noticed my attacks just weren't working sometimes, my character would stop responding to attack inputs for a few seconds randomly. Changed default windowed mode to fullscreen and it fixed that one, but there's some other control bugs in the game that show their heads sometimes, that was by far the most common and biggest, but not the only one. Hence in part why I'm playing on keybaord instead of with my controller. So some pretty bad and major input bugs. This might be the gamble on this game, does it work for you or not? And are the issues you have fixable or not? Don't forget you can't test out too much given steams return policy of just 2 or so hours of game open time.Blocking works ok during battles ussually, but many enemies have cinematic moments they force you into before you can kill them where they play a beat to you, and then you need to counter it by playing it back. So these are basicly mandatory methods to continue through the game, but several of these don't match up with the games beat, several of them don't even match up with their initial timings, the attack itself uses different timings than the notice beat they first gave, changing the tempo, sometimes just shifting an extra quarter second gap between a note or two...  Some of the quick time events also require you to basicly tap keys in a given order quickly, that only show up just before you must press, ok... but this sucks when they have nearly identical images for keys, and they all show up on the same path, or randomly on screen, so you can't tell what a given key is by peripheral vision, I love guitar hero, dance dance, etc... but imagine if all the arrows or beats coming down the path were in the same color, and there weren't any clearly marked out lanes for the different beats, you have to carefully look to see what each one is, but only have amoment to identify and respond to it. Sure, you can tell the shift button from the left click, but the shift and space are the same rough shape, as are left and right mouse buttons. With controllers you might have varied colored icons there to help? But on keyboard as I played this the UI made this just a horrible minigame moment you're forced to deal with in the middle of boss fights, that is literally worse than the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ flash or cheap games random people have made, it's hard to believe just how bad this was set up and designed.Fifth main boss, the financing guy, to beat him you must tap specific buttons, lmb or rmb in sequence and quickly as it comes down a track. A single track, no top/bottom or left/right. So you must identify wich one purely by it's icon... both using the same color and shape, just one has the orange bit on the right, the other on th left, icons not even that big to easily see though... and if you want the timings right it's hard to look ahead at the ones coming and only press and identify right as it hits the end point. This ♥♥♥♥ right here had me nearly just quit the game, a lovely music and cool boss battle, again completely ruined by the stupidest of design decisions and mistakes by throwing in a random mini game that wasn't at all well designed. At least put them on different tracks, or color them differently, or make it be between lmb and shift or E or something else that can look different at a glance from eachother.Everything goes too the beat... until it doesn't, and that happens a lot. The background at first animates to the beat, and the music matches the beat... in the first level quite well. Going forward, you start finding some levels where the enviornment and visuals don't really show the beat at all. Certain testing rooms in the second main zone of the game come to mind where literally zero elements animate to the beat, just a few that animate randomly, not too the beat.Similarly certain enemies especially in their forced parry events don't always follow the beat, like... completely ignore it sometimes. Or some characters like using korscika or whatever her name was, her quick time event thing doesn't care about the beat, lots of little moments pop up where the beats just not actually used, or trying to follow it actively hurts your ability to play. Similarly the music, in some locations doesn't match the games beat. Every song should clearly use the same tempo and beat the game tries to pretend it's got... but some don't, and if you try to play with those songs as the guide you will get screwed up. I think the best example of these problems, is that at multiple points in the game, I suddenly faced moments where it felt like the game was just randomly scrrewing me and killing me or throwing me back a save pissing me off badly for no reason, and my answer was to just turn off the music, and ignore the enviornment or anything else that tried to convey a beat or sense of rythim or music, and to only rely on visuals like directly matching the enemies attack visual, rather than the inacurate pre beat notice they gave before the attack, or the music of games overall beat since those don't sync up or match with stuff always. And for a music rythim game, turning off the music and ignoring the rythim to get the timing on quick time events or stuff that you are forced to get through to continue the game... ya that's a really bad thing. These popped up often enough to really pull me out of the game and keep me from really just falling into that zone and loving it.Final boss just ruins the idea of rythim as well. To defend against him you pretty much need to be able to see and hear certain queues. But they are often far too damn quiet, or small, so you basicly aren't allowed to use any real attacks of your own, since far to often when I did attack, my own attacks audio overwelmed his to the point I couldn't hear it, and my attack visuals covered him to the point I can't see what he's doing. But he isn't easily staggered so there's no safety just because I got a first hit or two in, it basicly turned into constantly dodging around at a distance just calling in allies to wittle him down, rather than going in and fighting and parrying and dodging myself, since a lot of his attacks just don't stand out enough. Many other larger enemies have louder obvious sounds before you must parry, he has a lot of different attacks with different sounds, some are damn quiet. Some enemies have giant obvious signs like razing a giant sword before a swing, he has a few more obvious ones, but is a smaller character using tiny hand sized drones flying around him that like to attack as well. Some of these sounds and queues are quiet or small and just get lost if you are doing anything yourself, and he can do these attacks almost anytime, so finding safe times to get close, and not just be dodging... It just involved slowly dodging while trying to use allies to get staggers to jump in, and then get out and try to dodge/block for a bit without any attacks till it built back up... but it just got really messy and felt like luck as often as not. In the end when I did beat him, it felt like 80% luck since that time he just didn't end up randomly attacking right after I got an attack or two off very many times. Still couldn't use any longer combos or anything, only the shortest at most, but even those were enough to overstay his stun/safe times in many previous fights and get me killed when he punished me for them. And if I just play it safe doing almost nothing... those attempts took sooooo long to wittle his health , that I just got tired and made mistakes after awhile, or missed some queue. _childDocuments_.review: It's like a 7/10 for hack n slash gameplay but a straight 10 on charm and style.Getting my criticisms out of the way first - there are much better games out there in this genre.  I'm positive if you played this right after DMC or Bayonetta, you'd feel the lack of polish.  Clear visual feedback during a fight is especially lacking.  What just hit me?  Did I successfully block that attack? Better take a precious half-second to check my health bar and sure. What combo am I in?  I thought I was in the uppercut combo but the game is acting like I'm in the middle of something else.  Why is my support character attacking a different target than the one I thought I selected?  All of these things add up to make the game feel imprecise.  You don't feel fully in control and it's easy to start  rhythmically button mashing.Pacing in the early game is also a chore.  It felt like I hit a tutorial every 5 minutes until I finished the first level.  I was close to walking away at this point, and I would have missed out if I did.There are zero games out there that do this genre this way.  The cutscenes are an absolute delight - endlessly clever and funny.  It felt like the old days of gaming where every cutscene was reward.  The gameplay feels clunky at first but once a song comes on that you jive with, your whole body syncs with the rhythm. It's infectious.It's worth a buy but a more refined sequel would likely blow it out of the water.

AAA gaming is in a hell of a state right now as many great industry people are being let go to maximize profits. _childDocuments_.review: This game is the embodiment of you playing video games after middle school when you were a kid and then had the omega brain idea of creating a character action game with your favorite songs as the background theme.Fantastic battle-rhythm combo system, awesome visuals and level pacing, a plot not too convoluted but engaging enough to follow through, characters that are unique while not wearing you down with extreme tropes, it's hard NOT to find an aspect of the game that isn't appealing to anyone who saw a THIRTY-DOLLAR video game made in the year 2023. The game does an incredible job teaching you the mechanics throughout the story, and mastering combos and new moves, while may take some time, feel so satisfying, especially as the soundtrack and crowd starts rocking out harder to your style meter.Exploration feels great as well, finding secrets and power ups to help you rock out harder during the more difficult combat sequences that ramp up later in the game. That and having silly NPC interactions makes traversing through each level a fun experience, and barely feels like you're just wasting time going from Point A to Point B.My only honest complaint is when the action gets way too crazy, it's hard to keep with all the mechanics that can occur (musical ques from enemies, visual blips to attack, etc.), but the game gives you just enough room for recovery and to reassess the room, allowing you to get back onto the beat and back into combos. Whether you're a fan of the classic PS2 character action games, you love NIN, or if you're looking for a lovable gang of doofs to do sick smoking style combos with, Hi-Fi Rush offers a grand experience at a ridiculously affordable $30. Would highly recommend to anyone, and would also recommend petting 808 at any given chance.

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest surprise this year so far and we're only in January. Outta nowhere, Tango releases a game that blends DMC and Bayonetta with BPM and Hellsinger, and whaddya know, those are all some of my favourite games! The gameplay is so fun, so easy to pick up but wanting to do cool combos makes you push yourself, and the game has more than enough tools for you to practice and learn in. Dedicated combat practice rooms with settings to change to practice that one specific situation with combo lists make it easier than ever to get really good. The art design absolutely pops off with the cell shading, dragging me all the way back to Jet Set Radio with a new soundtrack. Characters are relatively shallow but entertaining and funny, and the whole game is set in a pseudo-punk revolutionist kinda space. Music from NiN and other artists alongside original scores that mix together as the world moves to the beat, it seems to last around 10 hours on hard, and it's not even full price! (It's also on game pass!) Give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: The Definition of a perfect gameNow I know what you're thinking: "A perfect game? Really Mouse? You think this is a perfect game?" And to that I say, Yes! The combat feels funky fresh whereby you have to hit enemies to the beat of whatever song is playing in a level, the looks and details give off PS2 era love and attention to details, the game is STILL getting new content a whole year after its release and even if the new content doesn't give you a reason to come back to it, the gameplay loop is just top notch. A main complaint I see about this game is that the characters are "Too Annoying" or they're "Le Epic Cringe" for a game made in this current decade. The thing is though, the reason the characters are the way they are is that the whole vibe of the game is to not take it seriously. I mean come on. You have a guy running around beating robots with a makeshift guitar made out of scrap metal and you expect me to take it seriously? No! And that's why the characters work so well for me. They're not meant to be taken seriously and even the characters in the game know this. And that's why it works! Everyone from Robbie Daymond to Erica Lindbeck to God mother f**king ROGER CRAIG SMITH did a fantastic job in bringing these characters to life with their witty personalities and A+ voice acting. I love this game with all my heart and it showed me that games don't need to be hyper realistic to be good. Sure graphics are important. If you're intending to emphasise emotion then you obviously need to have the characters look semi decent. But the gameplay, the additional end game content, the replayability of this game has shown me that not everything is about graphics and if the game is just down to Earth and fun, then you have a perfect game of fun high octane actionIf you've been holding off playing this game and you've come across this review, let this be the one to help push you over the metaphorical edge in buying this game. You will not regret it.

He accepts his flaws, becomes a team player, understands empathy better, and worked his way from a no-skill rock-star wannabe to a fantastic "on-the-beat" combatant with guitar skills pending. _childDocuments_.review: One of those games that's just damn fun. I've always thought a rhythm hack and slash would be awesome, and this is just exactly that. Having dodges, parries, and combos all to the beat of the music is hella satisfying, especially if you're a gamer and a musician like myself. Is super fun and can be quite challenging at times, and some of the fights involve pretty complex rhythms and such that you have to deal with. My biggest complaint is just that it's a little short - I got 11 hours - but usually when that's the worst thing about a game it means it's pretty damn good. Plus, there's quite a bit of after-game content I've yet to try out. Gameplay is definitely the best part of this, as the combat is super well done, but there are a lot of other amazing aspects of the game - the artstyle is awesome, mostly taking on a comic book look, even occasionally switching to 2D animation for some of the cutscenes (with some cool transitions). The story is super fun and charming, and all the characters are unique and well played, with some pretty solid character development and such. Overall, I definitely recommend, especially on sale as it is as of writing this - but I still recommend at full price, as it's not too expensive to begin with. Just overall a very well polished, solid game that does exactly what it set out to do and more. And just in general, hella fun.

_childDocuments_.review: HiFi Rish is one of the best games I've ever played in my life. It feels tailored made for me as a person. The game has a GameCube/PS2 style charm that can't be overstated and I wish more games would experiment with. The gameplay is top-tier. Rhythm is important for combat but not required. But if you can master it, you'll feel like a god as you destroy robots with the power of rock and friendship. The music is gold. Whether the licensed tracks or the original recorded ones, the soundtrack shines in every conceivable way. I love the characters, the look, the sound, the world, the gameplay, and the progression. I've bought and beaten the game twice (Xbox/PC). I will buy the physical edition when it drops. And I will sing the praises of this game forever more. Tango Gameworks deserves all the praise and accolades they can possibly get. The fact that Microsoft shuttered the studio only a year after it gave them one of the best games of all time is a crime. I hope all the developers find a new home where they are deservedly appreciated for their talent and creative vision. I wish them all the best. And I hope that Microsoft executives always have a tiny pebble in their shoes that they can't seem to find. Long live Tango Gameworks, long live HiFi Rush.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi-Fi Rush is a brilliant rhythm beat-em-up up that is flashy, fun, and feels good to play. The game rewards you for playing on the beat, and doesn't mercilessly punish you for messing up. Its a fun world to just exist in, where everything, even random objects in the world bounce to the beat of the music. Everything from Chai's walking to an NPC's idle pose bounces along to the music, which is useful to help you keep rhythm. You play as Chai, a goofy wannabe rockstar who gets a new robotic arm that due to a defect, lets you sense the music in everything. Helping you are a great cast of characters who jump in and help you smash robots to take down the evil corporation. Fight fun and unique bosses, wear fun a goofy clothing, get ranks and scores in your performance, and bop along to the catchy tunes as you fight.-Gameplay - 9/10Music - 10/10Graphics - 10/10Effects - 10/10Controls - 9/10Game Performance - 10/10-Overall - 9.5/10. Play this game if you enjoy satisfying musical games, even if you suck at keeping rhythm like I do.
